issues.title: Remote Control: preserve parent/child (linked) session hierarchy and folder grouping across devices

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: platform:windows
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on Windows

issues.body:
**Summary**
In the Claude desktop app (Code tab), sessions started from another session (side chats, `start_session` children, forks) are shown nested under their parent in the local sidebar. When the same sessions are viewed through Remote Control (from another computer's desktop app, claude.ai/code, or the mobile app), the hierarchy is lost: every session appears as an independent, flat entry, and the parent can even land in a different sidebar group than its children.

**Environment**
- Two machines on the same account: a Windows home server (always on) and a MacBook, both running the Claude desktop app with "Connect new sessions to Remote Control" enabled.
- Desktop app 4.16336 (Windows).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. On machine A, open a session in a project folder (e.g. `personal-automation-hub`) and let it start 3–4 child sessions (side chats / linked sessions). Turn on Remote Control for all of them.
2. On machine A's sidebar: the children are nested under the parent inside the project folder group. ✅
3. On machine B's desktop app (same account), look at the same sessions as remote sessions.

**Actual**
- The children appear under a folder group, but the parent appears in a separate "Remote Control" group, with no nesting or link between them.
- Toggling Remote Control off/on for the parent does not change this.
- `list_sessions` / peer listings on machine B show no parent information (`startedBy` / `parentSessionId` exist only on machine A).

**Expected**
- Remote views keep the same parent → child nesting as the local sidebar (or at least show "started from <parent>").
- Parent and children stay in the same group (by project folder) on every device.

**Why it matters**
We run one "main" session per area on each machine and spin off child sessions for branch/PR work. Remotely, the structure collapses into an unordered flat list, so users can't tell which work belongs where. We currently work around it with naming conventions (`Area · …` for mains, `Area › …` for children) and by preferring in-session subagents over child sessions.

**Related observations (may be separate issues)**
- A session with an active Remote Control client cannot be archived ("still has live work"); turning Remote Control off usually allows archiving, but not always (one session stayed blocked and had to be archived from the sidebar by hand).
- After a desktop app auto-update/restart, existing sessions do not reconnect to Remote Control; only new sessions auto-connect.
- Remote Control occasionally turns itself off for an idle session while other idle sessions stay connected.

**Possibly related existing issues**
- #106134 (side sessions started from a Remote Control session don't get Remote Control)
- #104649 (Windows memory governor pausing Remote Control sessions; may explain the idle disconnects)
- #107170 (unarchiving a Remote Control session never reconnects it)

issues.title: [BUG] /feedback refused on a personal Max plan: account is locked by Claude Science (`claude_science_no_training`), feedback is off on the organization, and no setting can change it

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: has repro
labels.description: Has detailed reproduction steps

labels.name: platform:macos
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on macOS

issues.body:
## Summary

`/feedback`, Claude-drafted feedback, session surveys and transcript sharing are all refused for my personal Max account with "Feedback has not been enabled for your organization." Several open issues report the same refusal on personal plans (#101651, #105677, #98603, and the October comments on #55348). None has an explanation yet.

I traced what the server holds for my account. It points at Claude Science:

- the account has `grove_locked_by_claude_science: true`
- the subscription organization carries a capability named `claude_science_no_training`
- that organization's setting `claude_ai_completion_feedback_enabled` is `false`

A personal plan has no page where any of these can be changed, and signing Claude Science out does not clear them.

## Environment

- Claude Code 2.1.323, macOS, claude.ai login (not an environment token), full scope set.
- Personal organization on the Max plan (plan label "Ultra"). I am its only member and its admin.
- No `DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND`, `DISABLE_BUG_COMMAND` or `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC`, and no managed settings file.
- The Claude Science desktop app has been signed into the same organization. Under the current build it has two sessions, created 2026-09-29 and last touched 2026-10-24.

## What the server returns (2026-11-13)

All read with the Claude Code login's own token.

`GET /api/claude_code/policy_limits` (request `req_011Ch1J1iJE6YMf6TVVT4rtG`):

```json
{"restrictions":{"allow_product_feedback":{"allowed":false},"allow_connector_file_downloads":{"allowed":false},"enforce_web_search_mcp_isolation":{"allowed":false}},"compliance_taints":[],"monitoring_notice":null,"defaults":{"remote_control_at_startup":false}}
```

`GET /api/oauth/profile`: `organization.claude_ai_completion_feedback_enabled: false`, `organization.claude_ai_safety_feedback_enabled: true`.

`GET /api/oauth/account`: account-level `grove_locked_by_claude_science: true`, and two organization memberships:

| | Subscription organization (Max) | Console organization (same email) |
|---|---|---|
| `capabilities` | `chat`, `claude_max`, `claude_science_no_training` | `api`, `api_individual`, `customer_terms:standard` |
| `settings.claude_ai_completion_feedback_enabled` | `false` | `null` |

`GET /api/oauth/account/settings`: `grove_enabled: false`, `grove_updated_at: 2026-10-22T03:47:41Z`.

claude.ai Settings > Privacy shows "Help improve our AI models" switched off and greyed out, with "Not available for this account."

## Why I think this is Claude Science

- **The account flag says so by name.** `grove_locked_by_claude_science` is true, and the organization capability is `claude_science_no_training`.
- **The greyed-out label has one cause in the CLI.** In Claude Code 2.1.323, `/privacy-settings` shows "Not available for this account." only when the consent configuration reports `grove_locked_by_claude_science`. An excluded email domain gets different text ("for emails with your domain"). Two reporters on #101651 describe the same greyed-out label, and another describes the domain wording.
- **Feedback is off on the organization that has the capability, and unset on the one that doesn't.**

What I can't show from outside is the server rule that links the capability to `claude_ai_completion_feedback_enabled`. The two sit together on the affected organization; that is the extent of the evidence.

## What the docs say

- [Enable Claude Science](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/enable-claude-science): on by default for Pro, Max and Ultra, "no admin action needed".
- [How Claude Science works with your data](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/how-claude-science-works-with-your-data): on Pro and Max, "your Claude privacy settings in the Settings panel apply". There is no mention of the setting being locked or of product feedback being turned off.
- [Admin controls](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/admin-controls): names "Data and privacy > Rate chats" as the organization control that hides feedback. That page exists only for Team and Enterprise.

## Timeline on my account

| When (UTC) | What |
|---|---|
| 2026-09-29 | First Claude Science sessions under this organization |
| 2026-10-07 01:10 | Last `/feedback` send that I know went through |
| 2026-10-13 | `/feedback` refused with 403. `grove_enabled` was still `true` on this date (`grove_updated_at` 2025-10-04) |
| 2026-10-22 03:47 | `grove_enabled` became `false`. I did not change it, and the toggle is locked |
| 2026-11-13 | All three flags present, as above |

So on my account feedback was switched off first and the training setting was locked nine or more days later.

## What does not clear it

- **Not using Claude Science.** The app was not opened between 2026-10-25 and 2026-11-13 (its own refresh log shows no activity). The block held throughout.
- **Signing out on the device.**
- **Ending the Claude Science sign-in on the server.** I ended the only Claude Science sign-in on the account on 2026-11-13 at about 17:45 UTC (the server answered 204 and the entry disappeared). The three flags were unchanged afterwards. I'll update this issue if they change later.
- **Organization settings.** `claude.ai/admin-settings`, `/admin-settings/claude-science` and the admin data-privacy page all answer "Organization settings are available on Claude Team and Enterprise plans."
- **Settings > Privacy.** There is no "Rate chats" control on a personal plan.
- **"Allow user feedback" in the Console.** That switch belongs to the Console organization, which is a separate organization from the subscription one that is blocked (see the table above). This is likely why reporters on #105677 saw no effect from toggling it.

## Two related problems

- **Claude Science sign-ins are invisible in Settings.** Settings > Account > "Where you're logged in" requests only Claude Code and Claude in Chrome sign-ins, so a live Claude Science sign-in is never listed and can't be ended there.
- **The refusal message names the wrong thing.** "Feedback has not been enabled for your organization" and "disabled by your organization's policy" both read as an admin decision. On a personal plan there is no admin page and no policy the user set.

## For others who are affected

You can check whether your account is in the same state. This only reads; paste it into the browser console on a claude.ai tab:

```js
(async () => {
  const j = async (p) => (await fetch(p, { credentials: 'include' })).json();
  const a = await j('/api/account');
  console.log('grove_locked_by_claude_science:', a.grove_locked_by_claude_science);
  for (const o of await j('/api/organizations')) {
    const d = await j(`/api/organizations/${o.uuid}`);
    console.log(o.capabilities, '| completion feedback enabled:', d.settings?.claude_ai_completion_feedback_enabled);
  }
})();
```

If you are blocked and have never signed into Claude Science, please say so: that would show there is more than one cause.

## Questions for Anthropic

1. Is switching product feedback off for personal organizations that have used Claude Science intended? If it is, please document it and change the refusal message to say so.
2. Either way, could personal plans keep a way to send bug reports from Claude Code, for example without a transcript? The safeguard-stop notice itself says "Send feedback with /feedback", and that channel is closed for these accounts.
3. Does the lock ever lift once Claude Science is no longer used or signed in?
4. Could Settings list Claude Science sign-ins alongside the others?

releases.name: v2.1.328
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added auto mode for Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude apps gateway; interactive sessions with no permission mode start in it
- Added `"onFailure": "block"` for `mcp_tool` hooks, as for command and HTTP hooks: a hook whose call fails blocks the action
- Added a warning when a message from a session that skips permission prompts may be held and dropped by a cloud session
- Added a notice in `/status` and `claude doctor` when an OpenTelemetry exporter has no endpoint and its data would likely be lost
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_DEFERRED_TOOL_RESUME`, which lets a host stop `claude -p --resume` and `--continue` from running a tool call that a hook deferred
- Added support for apps that embed Claude Code to switch on the policy plugin's `allowManagedModsOnly` option; an admin's managed settings still win
- Added a startup warning to the Claude apps gateway when a policy's `maxEffortLevel` is not a valid effort level
- Self-hosted runner: Added `--repository-folder` to name the folder that sessions use for a repository at `--capacity 1`, in place of its path under the base folder, which can't be a symbolic link
- Self-hosted runner: Added a start-up warning when the host's settings.json sets a default permission mode that sessions ignore
- Self-hosted runner: Added `--hook-label` to `claude self-hosted-runner orchestrator`, to hand chosen session labels to the `spawn-runner` hook
- Self-hosted runner: Added `--metadata key=value` to `claude --environment`, to label a session for the `spawn-runner` hook
- Self-hosted runner: Added `claude_code_self_hosted_orchestrator_session_queue_wait_by_reason_seconds` to the orchestrator's `/metrics`, so a re-opened session's wait can be told from a new one's
- Self-hosted runner: Added an orchestrator metric, `claude_code_self_hosted_orchestrator_sessions_given_up_total`, that counts by cause how often Anthropic gave up starting a runner for a session
- Fixed Bash commands in zsh stopping with a "not found" error at a word that starts with `=`, such as `echo ====` or `[ a == b ]`; `=cmd` no longer expands to a command's path
- Fixed automatic compaction reusing the session's earlier system prompt instead of rebuilding it the way `/compact` does
- Fixed markdown rendering freezing on some very long or malformed input
- Fixed rare screen freezes
- Fixed Esc often being lost at a permission prompt or question when you typed straight after it; in terminals that send Alt as Esc and a key, an unused Alt or Option key now declines there
- Fixed a paste or a terminal's reply being typed into the prompt when a slow connection cut it in two
- Fixed saving a scheduled task erasing the project's other saved tasks when the scheduled tasks file can't be read, on third-party providers or with telemetry or feature flags turned off
- Fixed a scheduled task with a typo in the project's scheduled tasks file being deleted the next time that file was saved
- Fixed a case where a resumed cloud session could lose its compaction summary or recent messages when a message was saved late
- Fixed the token counts on the spinner and for subagents counting a retried reply twice, missing replies that were not streamed, and standing still while Claude thinks
- Fixed the error shown when usage credits run out mid-response, which named a rate limit
- Fixed auto mode failing every turn outside Claude Desktop with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS` set behind a gateway rejecting betas, on Bedrock, Agent Platform, Foundry or Claude apps gateway
- Fixed `CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` not lengthening the 5-minute connection limit on gateways, custom base URLs and cloud providers
- Fixed some Claude Desktop sessions on third-party providers, other than scheduled tasks, ending for good with "Prompt is too long" after large tool results; the largest are now left out
- Fixed MCP tools whose input schema starts with `anyOf`, `oneOf` or `allOf` going missing on third-party providers or with telemetry or feature flags turned off
- Fixed an MCP tool with an invalid input schema failing requests on third-party providers or with telemetry or feature flags turned off; the tool is now left out and Claude is told why
- Fixed effort being turned off for a subagent's model for the session if Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform or Foundry refused its progress summary's effort setting (regression in 2.1.327)
- Fixed Code Mode stopping a script when a permission prompt outside auto or bypass mode, a plan approval or a question stayed open for ten minutes
- Fixed Code Mode scripts in auto and bypass-permissions modes failing to call an MCP server that had connected while the previous script was running
- Fixed Code Mode scripts not running in the background in auto or bypass permissions mode in a session chosen in the `claude --resume` picker
- Fixed Code Mode losing a loaded skill, hook context or a note typed with a permission approval when resuming a session in which one reply ran several scripts
- Fixed Claude not being told that a Code Mode script was cut off when the session was resumed from the picker or in a mode that asks for permission
- Fixed Code Mode silently using `undefined` for top-level variables that an earlier failed script never set
- Fixed Code Mode scripts not being told when a failing command's long output was cut
- Fixed Code Mode refusing valid scripts that start with a `{` block
- Fixed Code Mode refusing scripts that use both a top-level `await` and a top-level `return`
- Fixed an @-mentioned small file not being attached in Code Mode after a script had read or written it
- Fixed Code Mode offering `write()` and `edit()` to read-only subagents that can't call them

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Codex app version

26.1111.21308, build 27194, production channel. The built-in updater reported up to date.

### Subscription and platform

Subscription tier unverified. macOS 27.2.1, Apple Silicon (arm64). Local Codex chats using GPT-6.2 Sol with Medium reasoning.

### What happened?

Two separate Codex desktop chats failed while reviewing existing local audio. In each chat, a tool result included an `input_audio` content item with a data URL. The next model request returned HTTP 400:

```json
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","code":null,"message":"Audio input is not available.","param":"input"},"status":400}
```

- **Common-minion review:** The tool returned an MP3 as `input_audio` (`data:audio/mpeg`) at 06:33:15 UTC on 2026-11-18. The turn failed two seconds later. Plain-text follow-ups such as `?` at 06:35 UTC and another text-only message at 06:37 UTC produced the same error. A subsequent text-only recovery instruction also failed.
- **Rare-minion review:** A separate audio review returned a WAV as `input_audio` (`data:audio/wav`) at 06:42:38 UTC on the same date. That turn failed three seconds later with the same error. No further text retry was tested in this second chat.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a local Codex desktop chat with GPT-6.2 Sol, Medium reasoning.
2. Have an agent tool return a short local audio clip as an audio content item. The session logs show that Codex recorded the result in this shape, with a base64 data URL:
   `{"type":"input_audio","audio_url":"data:audio/wav;base64,<clip bytes>"}`
   The other instance used an MP3 data URL.
3. Observe the HTTP 400. Send a plain-text follow-up in the same chat and check whether the prior audio result still causes the error.

### Expected behavior

If the selected model or request path cannot accept an audio tool response, surface that failure at the tool boundary and allow later text turns to proceed. An unsupported tool result should not leave the conversation unusable.

### Additional information

Fresh chats continued successfully when tool outputs were kept text-only. The failure on old-chat text follow-ups is consistent with replay of the prior audio item, but we have not isolated the app versus backend cause. Audio bytes and private logs are omitted from this public report.

issues.title: [Docs] process/write examples omit the required writeId

labels.name: documentation
labels.description: Improvements or additions to documentation

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
### What is the type of issue?

Example code is not working.

### What is the issue?

The exec-server README shows `process/write` requests with only `processId` and `chunk`, followed by an `accepted` response. Both the standalone parameter example and the JSON-RPC walkthrough omit `writeId`.

The `WriteParams` type in the latest stable `0.170.0` source and current `main` requires `write_id: String`, serialized as `writeId`; there is no default for this field. The `process/write` route decodes requests into this type, so a request copied from either example fails parameter deserialization instead of producing the documented response.

For example, the request shown in the README omits the required field:

```json
{"id":3,"method":"process/write","params":{"processId":"proc-1","chunk":"aGVsbG8K"}}
```

It is rejected during parameter decoding with a missing-`writeId` error. This was confirmed with the exact production `WriteParams` type in an isolated source probe at commit `05ae1b0fdd5ab412d24248acc76c5d9f6f275440`; the corrected request deserializes successfully:

```json
{"id":3,"method":"process/write","params":{"processId":"proc-1","chunk":"aGVsbG8K","writeId":"write-1"}}
```

The protocol boundary maps malformed params to JSON-RPC `-32602` invalid params before the handler runs. The standalone exec-server binary was not run for this documentation report; the deserialization failure was tested against the production type, and the RPC mapping was checked in source. The probe used a network-disabled isolated container and no model, external service, credentials, or user data.

Expected behavior: both documented requests should include `writeId`, and a copied example should conform to the current schema. Clients should reuse the same ID when retrying the same write after reconnecting.

Related: [PR #28895](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/28895) introduced `writeId` for retry deduplication. This report concerns the README examples not being updated to match that required field; it does not report the retry behavior itself. A focused search of current `openai/codex` Issues for `process/write`, `writeId`, README examples, and missing-field errors found no matching issue.

### Where did you find it?

- [Latest stable 0.170.0: standalone `process/write` parameter example](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.170.0/codex-rs/exec-server/README.md#L349-L370)
- [Latest stable 0.170.0: JSON-RPC walkthrough](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.170.0/codex-rs/exec-server/README.md#L579-L584)
- [Latest stable 0.170.0: required `WriteParams.write_id`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.170.0/codex-rs/exec-server-protocol/src/protocol.rs#L588-L592)
- [Current `main`: standalone parameter example](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83f73a818cb319a19aab0b2d99ee3c1d562e6110/codex-rs/exec-server/README.md#L349-L370)
- [Current `main`: required `WriteParams.write_id`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83f73a818cb319a19aab0b2d99ee3c1d562e6110/codex-rs/exec-server-protocol/src/protocol.rs#L588-L592)

issues.body:
## Summary

New Codex **Cloud** development conversations created through the web workflow are usable in Chrome at chatgpt.com but are **missing from the Codex view in the desktop application's sidebar from the outset**. This has affected two independently created cloud conversations using two separate published environments. The issue has been observed in the user's Mac desktop application and a second work computer's desktop application.

This is a request to investigate **cross-device discovery/accessibility of cloud conversation threads**, not missing code repositories or failed environment setup.

## Environment

- Mac desktop app displayed as ChatGPT (bundle `com.openai.codex`), version `26.1027.30824`, build `22943` (collected from installed app metadata).
- macOS `27.0.1`.
- Also observed on a second work computer; its desktop app version/build have not been independently verified.
- ChatGPT account/workspace: user confirms the same account and workspace across web and desktop.
- Published Codex Cloud environments and private GitHub repositories work as expected. No private repository names or account identifiers are included here.

## Observed behavior

1. Set the work location to **Cloud** and select an existing **published** environment.
2. Start a new Codex cloud development conversation through the web flow.
3. The conversation opens, receives responses, and remains accessible in Chrome.
4. Open the Codex view of the desktop app using the same account/workspace: the new cloud conversation does **not appear in Recents or the project/conversation list** and cannot be opened using the available desktop navigation/read path.
5. Other local/desktop conversations are visible in the desktop app; these are not confirmed cloud-sync controls.

This was observed on **at least two** newly created cloud conversations linked to separate published environments. Neither was observed appearing normally on desktop before later disappearing. It is not established that *every* cloud thread on the account is affected.

The user's previous cloud-environment setup and GitHub integration were checked independently: cloud task execution and read-only repository access succeeded. The cloud conversations themselves are not lost: they remain usable in Chrome.

## Expected behavior

A cloud conversation started through the web should be discoverable and resumable in the same account's Codex desktop application, regardless of which supported device is used. If access fails, the desktop app should provide a meaningful explanation or recovery path instead of omitting the thread.

## Diagnostics and troubleshooting already performed

- App update, restart, sign-out/sign-in to the same account/workspace.
- Search, archived-conversation checks, sidebar sorting and browser-versus-desktop comparisons.
- Direct desktop thread reads/navigation failed with a redacted `No Codex thread found` / `conversation_inaccessible` response (404). The read path/tool coverage has limitations; this is not proof of a server-side root cause.
- Sanitized diagnostic logs also showed persistent durable WebSocket `connection_failed_before_ready` / reconnect failures. **No causal link between this transport issue and the missing threads has been established.**
- Results were sent privately to OpenAI Support, including thread IDs, timestamps, screenshots and sanitized logs. These private artifacts are intentionally excluded from this public issue.

## Request

Please investigate cloud thread indexing/discovery, desktop-side listing and read routing, account/workspace authorization context, and possible remote connection interaction. If related to existing reports, please cross-link/consolidate and identify a supported workaround or fixed release.

Potentially related but not known to share a root cause:
- #58424 — Windows Codex cloud conversations absent from desktop while visible in Chrome.
- #51675 — macOS cloud tasks disappearing after relaunch; its direct-read behavior differs from this report.

**Privacy:** No user account name, private repository, conversation ID/URL, email address, raw log, local filesystem path, or unredacted screenshot is included.

Submitted with AI assistance at the affected user's explicit request.

issues.body:
## Summary

The Kling AI CLI plugin is currently unusable for account authentication when it runs inside ChatGPT Work/Codex's remote, headless runtime.

## Reproduction

1. Select the Kling AI CLI plugin in ChatGPT Work/Codex.
2. Start authentication through the plugin, which invokes the official Global CLI approximately as follows:

```bash
npm exec --yes --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org --package=@klingai/cli-global@latest -- kling login
```

3. The CLI detects a headless environment and provides an OAuth authorization URL with this redirect URI:

```text
http://127.0.0.1:8787/callback
```

4. Open the authorization URL in the user's browser and approve access.
5. Run:

```bash
kling who_am_i
```

## Actual result

The callback reaches `127.0.0.1` on the user's local machine, rather than the remote Work/Codex runtime where the CLI is listening. The access token is never saved and `kling who_am_i` returns:

```text
No login state found
```

## Why users cannot work around this

ChatGPT Work/Codex users do not have a reachable ingress URL for the runtime and cannot configure SSH port forwarding. This is a standalone CLI invocation, not an MCP server configured through `codex mcp`.

## Requested resolution

Please make this third-party CLI/plugin authentication flow usable in remote Codex runtimes through at least one of:

1. Device-code / browser-code OAuth supported by the Kling CLI plugin.
2. Secure API-key authentication supported by the plugin.
3. A ChatGPT-managed OAuth callback instead of a loopback redirect.

Without one of these options, the advertised Kling video-generation integration cannot be authenticated by users with existing Kling accounts in ChatGPT Work.

## Summary

On Windows, using multiple local chats can leave the main Codex desktop window permanently blank except for the OpenAI logo shortly after another chat completes. The main application and local execution backend continue running. The user reports repeated failures and sometimes needing two relaunch attempts to regain the UI.

## Environment

- MSIX package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1111.2228.0, x64.
- Desktop log version: 26.1111.21308, build 27194, production channel.
- Bundled CLI: 0.169.0-alpha.11.1.

## Observations from local diagnostics

Four inspected sequences occurred around 20:37 on November 18 and 00:39, 00:50, and 01:22 on November 19, 2026 (Asia/Seoul).

Within approximately 1–2 seconds of another local chat completing or its browser-use session activity ending:

1. All observed chat view activities became inactive.
2. The main window's conversation subscription unmounted and mounted.
3. Its identity state became authLoading=true with no account/user populated, and the visible window remained on the logo.

That identity state is **not** proof of an authentication failure. A task using web search without browser UI interaction also preceded this pattern; no app-termination command was found in that task's inspected tool calls.

During the 01:22 recurrence, Chromium error logging captured repeated **"Peer closed MessagePort connection."** failures from subsequent app-screen network requests. It is not established whether the port closure is the original fault or a consequence of the UI reset.

The local execution backend continued working after the UI failed. No matching Windows Application Error/Hang event, retained minidump, or explicit unexpected app-server exit was found in the inspected interval. This does not rule out a UI failure.

One earlier 20-second sample recorded total app private memory briefly rising from approximately 2.1 GiB to 4.5 GiB, then decreasing. However, the later 01:22 recurrence was recorded at approximately 2.55 GiB total, with the largest child around 1.27 GiB. An earlier nearby system check had approximately 44 GiB physical memory available. These observations do not establish an out-of-memory cause.

## Attempts and controls

- Rebuilt approximately 57 MiB of regenerable browser/code/shader caches; recurrence persisted.
- Turned only completion notifications off; the 01:22 recurrence still occurred. Restored the original notification setting afterward.
- Current HTTP reachability and Responses WebSocket handshake checks succeeded.
- The inspected chats already use paginated history.
- Existing conversations and work files were not deleted or reset during these attempts.

## Requested help

Please investigate shared main-window RPC/MessagePort lifetime and UI recovery when concurrent local chats complete. Please provide a supported mitigation or targeted diagnostic procedure that preserves conversations, work files, and unrelated running tasks.

Related symptom reports: #51343 and #50291. A shared root cause is unconfirmed.

# codex cloud does not discover current Cloud environments

## What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.160.0`, the npm latest release at the time of this check.

## Authentication

ChatGPT authentication. The CLI and desktop app use the same account. Token refresh succeeds. No API key is in use.

## Platform

macOS, `Darwin 24.6.0 arm64 arm`. I ran these checks through a terminal PTY.

## What issue are you seeing?

I can see two owned, Private environments in Settings > Codex Cloud. Neither has an Unpublished badge. The settings catalog returns both environments with current versions when requested with `scope=user&omitDraft=true`; it returns no further page. The workspace catalog returns zero environments. Legacy Codex Cloud shows “No cloud environments yet”.

On the same account, `codex cloud` shows only “All Environments (Global)” in its environment picker. I get the same result from a checkout with a GitHub remote and from `/tmp`.

An explicit submission exits 1 with:

```text
Error: no cloud environments are available for this workspace
```

The CLI's catalog requests return HTTP 200. Its repository-specific lookup returns zero environments. `codex cloud list --json` returns `{"tasks":[],"cursor":null}`; I understand that this is an execution-task list, not an environment inventory.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use a ChatGPT account with current Cloud environments visible in Settings > Codex Cloud and no environments in Legacy Codex Cloud.
2. Authenticate the latest CLI with that account.
3. Run `codex cloud`, open the environment picker, and inspect the choices without submitting.
4. Compare the picker from the repository checkout and from `/tmp`.
5. Try `codex cloud exec --env '<environment identifier>' --branch main --attempts 1 'Read-only environment canary; report pwd and git HEAD, then stop.'`.

The submission above fails during environment resolution before creating a task. No canary has run.

## What is the expected behavior?

The CLI should list accessible current Cloud environments and accept the supported identifier for fresh task dispatch. If this environment type requires a different CLI route, please document the command and identifier mapping.

The [CLI documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands#codex-cloud) describes task submission through `codex cloud exec --env`, and the [Cloud overview](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cloud) describes starting Cloud work from the CLI.

## Diagnostic evidence

- Current settings load `/api/codex-cloud/v1/environment-configs?scope=user&limit=100&omitDraft=true`. Its entries use `provider=caas`, stable IDs with an `asenvcfg_` component, and version IDs with a `cecfgver_` component.
- CLI 0.160.0's [environment discovery code](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.0/codex-rs/cloud-tasks/src/env_detect.rs) queries `/backend-api/wham/environments/by-repo/github/OWNER/REPO` and `/backend-api/wham/environments`.
- Its [resolve_environment_id function](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.0/codex-rs/cloud-tasks/src/lib.rs#L203) rejects an empty catalog before matching `--env`. Replacing a version ID with a stable ID therefore cannot bypass this result.
- I compared `env_detect.rs` in 0.160.0 and 0.162.0-alpha.3; the bytes match. I did not install or run the alpha release.
- `CODEX_CLOUD_TASKS_BASE_URL`, `CODEX_CLOUD_TASKS_MODE` and `CODEX_STARTING_DIFF` are unset.
- The existing doctor run passed installation/version, authentication, HTTP connectivity and the Responses WebSocket handshake. It also reported optional local MCP/state/terminal warnings; I have no evidence that they affect catalog discovery.

These observations suggest a mismatch between the current and legacy catalogs. Please confirm whether the released CLI supports the current environments and identify the supported repair or route.

Related: [#49966](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49966) reports the new/legacy selection difference in the web UI. This report supplies CLI discovery and resolution evidence. [#15544](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/15544) concerns empty task-list reporting and was closed as not planned; this request concerns access to environments that exist in the current catalog.

I omitted account identifiers, environment identifiers, repository names, credentials and raw local logs.

- VS Code Codex extension: `openai.chatgpt-26.1111.21308-win32-x64`
- Authentication: ChatGPT Plus
- Two active and two archived sessions are recognized correctly.
- `codex doctor` reports healthy session databases and no failures.
- The same behavior was previously observed using the VS Code extension's bundled CLI 0.169.0-alpha.11.1 with `--no-daemon`.

This appears to be a live agent-status synchronization issue between the VS Code extension and the CLI Agent Command Center.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open VS Code on Windows 11 with the OpenAI Codex extension installed.
2. Open an existing project and start a Codex task.
3. Confirm that the Codex agent is actively working in VS Code.
4. Open Windows Terminal (PowerShell).
5. Run `codex agents` using the standalone Codex CLI 0.170.0.
6. Observe the corresponding agent in the Agent Command Center.
7. The agent is displayed as `Inactive` and the Working counter remains at `0`, although the task is actively running in VS Code.
8. Exit and restart `codex agents` while the VS Code task is still running.
9. The status continues to show `Inactive`.

**Reproducibility:** Reproduced repeatedly.

**Note:** Both the standalone CLI and the Codex VS Code extension use the same local Codex home directory and session database.

### What is the expected behavior?

The Agent Command Center should accurately reflect the execution status of Codex agents running in the VS Code extension.

When a VS Code agent is actively processing a task, its status should be displayed as `Working`, and the corresponding counter should be updated.

When the agent completes its task, the status should transition to `Ready` or another appropriate state.

If live status synchronization between the VS Code extension and the standalone CLI is not supported, the interface should clearly communicate this limitation instead of reporting active agents as `Inactive`.

### Additional information

The issue is reproducible with two separate installations:

- Standalone Codex CLI 0.170.0 (official Windows installer)
- Bundled CLI 0.169.0-alpha.11.1 from the VS Code extension (tested with `--no-daemon`)

The VS Code extension version is `openai.chatgpt-26.1111.21308-win32-x64`.

Both installations correctly identify the existing Codex sessions and their associated projects.

The `Updated` timestamp changes while the agent is actively working, but its status remains `Inactive`.

Running `codex doctor` confirms:
- 20 successful checks, 0 failures
- Healthy SQLite state databases
- 2 active and 2 archived sessions
- No missing or inconsistent session records
- Successful OpenAI authentication and connectivity

Restarting the Agent Command Center does not resolve the problem.

**Question:** Is the Agent Command Center expected to monitor live agent execution in the VS Code extension, or does it currently track only agents started through the CLI?

issues.title: Linuxbrew-installed tmux is missing from trusted helper lookup, disabling terminal pets

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: TUI
labels.description: Issues related to the terminal user interface: text input, menus and dialogs, and terminal display

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

issues.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.169.0` (also the npm `latest` version when checked on November 17, 2026).

### What subscription do you have?

Not included; this failure occurs during local terminal capability detection.

### Which model were you using?

The identified failure is in local TUI startup/helper discovery, before a model response is needed.

### What platform is your computer?

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64.

```text
Linux 7.0.0-43-generic x86_64 unknown
```

### What terminal emulator and version are you using?

Ghostty 1.4.0, with tmux 3.8 installed through Homebrew on Linux.

### Codex doctor report

Relevant excerpt from `codex doctor --json`, collected in a noninteractive diagnostic subprocess:

```json
{
  "codexVersion": "0.169.0",
  "installation": {
    "current executable": "/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/Caskroom/codex/0.169.0/bin/codex"
  },
  "terminal.env": {
    "terminal": "Ghostty",
    "tmux options": "not inspected (PATH helpers are not executed)"
  }
}
```

### What issue are you seeing?

Terminal pets do not appear inside tmux even with fullscreen Codex, `allow-passthrough all`, and a selected pet (`rocky`). The tmux session reports Ghostty and RGB support.

The installed tmux is discoverable from the shell:

```text
$ command -v tmux
/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/tmux
$ readlink -f /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/tmux
/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/Cellar/tmux/3.8/bin/tmux
```

There is no tmux executable in the trusted search locations on this machine.

Live tmux state:

```text
$ tmux display-message -p 'fullscreen=#{alternate_on} passthrough=#{allow-passthrough} terminal=#{client_termname} type=#{client_termtype}'
fullscreen=1 passthrough=all terminal=xterm-ghostty type=ghostty 1.4.0
```

`#{client_termfeatures}` also includes `RGB`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Linux, install tmux through Homebrew into `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew`, without another tmux installation in the trusted system locations.
2. Start tmux in Ghostty or Kitty.
3. Set and apply `set -g allow-passthrough all` in tmux.
4. Enable `fullscreen_transcript = true` under `[tui]` in Codex's configuration.
5. Start Codex CLI 0.169.0 and select a terminal pet, for example `/pets rocky`.
6. Observe that pets remain unavailable despite the supported terminal, fullscreen mode, and passthrough setting.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should discover a tmux installation under the standard Linux Homebrew prefix and enable pets when the other capability checks pass. If that installation is intentionally unsupported, the diagnostic should explain the helper-discovery failure rather than only suggesting fullscreen/passthrough settings that are already enabled.

### Additional information

Source inspection in the `rust-v0.169.0` tag identifies the failing lookup:

- [`tui/src/tui/tmux.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.169.0/codex-rs/tui/src/tui/tmux.rs#L43) calls `system_executable("tmux")` and returns default options when it cannot find the helper. That leaves `kitty_image_base` unset.
- [`utils/path-utils/src/system_commands.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.169.0/codex-rs/utils/path-utils/src/system_commands.rs) deliberately ignores ambient `PATH`. Its `system_directories()` and `installation_roots()` include macOS Homebrew locations but omit `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin` and `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew`.
- The helper lookup canonicalizes executable paths before validating them, so a symlink in `/usr/local/bin` pointing to the Linuxbrew installation would still be rejected.
- [`pets/image_protocol.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.169.0/codex-rs/tui/src/pets/image_protocol.rs#L43) only enables the tmux pet protocol when the fullscreen image base is available.

The trusted-helper policy was introduced in #42324. This report concerns coverage of the standard Linux Homebrew prefix while preserving that policy.

The cause above is based on source inspection and the installed executable paths. Installing/copying tmux into another location has not been tested as a workaround.

issues.title: Images 2.6 on Codex OAuth: no model selection, complexity/SVG ignored, GIF rejected, animation flag not in shipped CLI

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

issues.body:
Images 2.6 (gpt-image-2.6-flare / gpt-image-2.6-sunburst) launched 2026-11-04 with ChatGPT and Codex availability, but third-party clients using ChatGPT/Codex OAuth cannot select the model or use the new 2.6-only outputs. The built-in tool exposes none of the new controls, and the Codex OAuth image endpoints ignore or reject them.

Related: #43965 (Images 2.5 model selection/observability), #28723, #59180. This report adds 2.6-specific evidence, including a teardown of the current desktop build.

### Environment
- ChatGPT.app 26.1029.61003 (macOS, build 24614, app.asar dated 2026-11-04)
- Bundled Codex CLI 0.166.0-alpha.6
- ChatGPT Pro account

### Evidence

**1. Shipped Codex CLI has no Images 2.6 or GIF support.**
Static strings inspection of the bundled `codex` binary (CodexCLI.app/Contents/MacOS/codex):
- `gpt-image-2`: 50 occurrences, plus `x-codex-image-turn-id`
- `gpt-image-2.6`, `image_generation_animation`, `frame_count`, `frame_duration_ms`: 0 occurrences

The GIF flag merged in #59073 is not present in the shipped build. The built-in `image_gen.imagegen` tool schema has no model, complexity, SVG, or markup option; its request type is fixed to `gpt-image-2`.

**2. Codex OAuth image endpoints ignore or reject 2.6 fields** (direct probe of `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/images/*`, 2026-11-06):
- `model`: ignored — `gpt-image-2.6-flare`, `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst`, and a fake control id all returned 200 with an image, with identical usage and C2PA metadata (`ChatGPT / gpt-image`).
- `output_format: "svg"`: accepted and ignored; PNG returned.
- `complexity`: accepted and ignored, including an invalid value.
- `output_format: "gif"`: 400 `GIF output is not enabled for this request.`
- `size`: not honored (requested 1024x1024, returned 1536x1024).
Independent report of the same GIF rejection with valid frame settings: router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI#7269.

**3. ChatGPT's GIF and markup features live in a different protocol.**
Teardown of the desktop webview shows they ride on the ChatGPT conversation API (`/backend-api/f/conversation` with `system_hints:["picture_v2"]`), which requires sentinel chat-requirements tokens:
- Markup: `POST /image-gen/markup-preview` with the original file id and overlay PNG, then a conversation message whose `metadata.dalle.from_client.operation` is `{type:"transformation", input_image_asset_pointer, is_markup:true, ...}`.
- Inpainting: `operation = {type:"inpainting", original_file_id, mask_file_id, ...}`.
- GIF: no client-side GIF parameter; the model's image tool decides, and results arrive as `image/gif` asset pointers with spritesheet/speed-variant metadata (`/image-gen/gif/select_speed` stores playback speed).
- The image model is read back from `message.metadata.model_slug`; the client does not select it.

### Request
- Ship `image_generation_animation` in a released Codex CLI build, with a clear statement of which accounts/endpoints actually accept GIF output on the OAuth lane.
- Provide a supported way to select Images 2.6 models and set `complexity` on the Codex OAuth image path, or explicitly document that these are API-key-only.
- Return effective model metadata on OAuth image responses so callers can verify what ran.
- Reject ignored fields (`output_format: "svg"`, `complexity`, `model`, `size`) with a clear error instead of silently returning a different result. Silent acceptance makes clients believe 2.6 features work when they do not.

Submitted by the user's Codex assistant with explicit authorization. No credentials, account identifiers, or private task contents are included.

issues.body:
## Summary

A Windows user cannot find a usable app-upgrade option and reports that GPT-6.2 Astra is unavailable. A read-only check through the desktop app's configured update-check interface returns `unavailable` with `disabled for build flavor (prod)`, while Windows Package Manager identifies a newer app package.

Please investigate update discoverability and the unavailable update-check path for this production Windows build. The missing GPT-6.2 model may be related, but causation has not been established.

## Environment verified on November 19, 2026 (Asia/Seoul)

- OS: Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, x64, version `10.0.26300`.
- Running desktop app self-report: version `26.930.31730`, build `12947`, release channel `prod`.
- Registered Windows package: `OpenAI.Codex`, version `26.930.3930.0`.
- Its package manifest specifies minimum Windows version `10.0.19041.0`.
- A separate older `OpenAI.ChatGPT-Desktop` package is also installed at `1.2026.190.0`.
- Subscription and workspace model entitlements were not independently verified.

App self-report versions and MSIX package versions are recorded separately; they are not assumed to be identical version schemes.

## Observed results

Read-only desktop update check:

```json
{
  "installedVersion": "26.930.31730",
  "installedBuildVersion": "12947",
  "installedReleaseChannel": "prod",
  "status": "unavailable",
  "reason": "disabled for build flavor (prod)"
}
```

`winget list --name ChatGPT --disable-interactivity` identifies:

- Name: `ChatGPT`
- ID: `OpenAI.ChatGPT`
- Installed version: `26.930.3930.0`
- Available version: `26.1111.2228.0`
- Source: `winget`

`winget show --id OpenAI.ChatGPT --exact --source winget --disable-interactivity` confirms the offered MSIX version `26.1111.2228.0`, publisher OpenAI, and release date November 14, 2026.

No app installation, forced shutdown, reset, or Windows upgrade was performed during this investigation. The check result is not evidence that the installed app is up to date. The menu's visibility and the live model picker were user-reported, not independently inspected through foreground UI automation.

## User impact

The user cannot determine how to update the app or access the newly announced GPT-6.2 Astra model, and is left wondering whether upgrading Windows itself is necessary.

Official documentation announces GPT-6.2 Astra/Sol availability in Codex and normally describes an enabled desktop updater:

- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/whats-new/gpt-62-astra-sol
- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/manage-app-updates
- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/windows-deployment

## Expected behavior and requested investigation

1. Provide a discoverable update action on Windows, or show the supported external update route when in-app updates are unavailable.
2. Explain `disabled for build flavor (prod)` in actionable terms and distinguish it from "up to date" and organization-managed update restrictions.
3. Explain required client version and account/workspace conditions when a newly announced model is missing.
4. Confirm whether updating this installation through `OpenAI.ChatGPT` is the supported migration/update route.

Related model-availability report: #62187. Its update checker reports `up_to_date`; this installation instead returns `unavailable`, so an identical root cause is not assumed.

Only version and diagnostic metadata are included. No credentials, private chat transcripts, raw logs, account identifiers, or personal filesystem paths are attached.

plus

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary

ChatGPT Desktop consistently displays:

> Account authentication unavailable: the desktop app cannot obtain usable account authentication from the local Codex service (app-server). Sending messages and loading chats will be affected.

The issue occurs immediately after opening the app.

The same ChatGPT account:
- Works normally in the browser.
- Successfully completes real Codex CLI requests under the affected macOS user.
- Works normally in ChatGPT Desktop under a newly created macOS user on the same Mac.

## Environment

- OS: macOS [INSERT VERSION]
- ChatGPT Desktop: 26.1103.60933
- Release date shown in the app: November 9, 2026
- Bundled app-server: 0.167.0-alpha.3.2

Both macOS users run the same bundled executable:

/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/CodexCLI.app/Contents/MacOS/codex

The executable path and reported app-server version were verified in both desktop logs.

## Observed behavior

### Affected macOS user

Browser OAuth and device-code login both complete successfully.

The bundled CLI reports:

    Logged in using ChatGPT

Actual Codex CLI requests succeed, including reading a local project and describing its structure.

However, ChatGPT Desktop continues to show the authentication-unavailable banner.

A fresh bundled app-server process returns the following for account/read with refreshToken=false:

    {

      },
      "requiresOpenaiAuth": true,
      "workspaceRouting": null
    }

A local inspection of ~/.codex/auth.json found:
- tokens.account_id is missing or empty.
- Both access_token and id_token are unexpired.
- Both tokens lack chatgpt_account_id, chatgpt_user_id, and chatgpt_plan_type under the https://api.openai.com/auth claim.

These results remain the same after device-code login.

### New macOS user on the same Mac

account/read returns:

    {
      "account": {
        "type": "chatgpt",
        "email": "<same email, redacted>",
        "planType": "plus",
        "workspaceName": null
      },
      "requiresOpenaiAuth": true,
      "workspaceRouting": {
        "chatgptAccountId": "<redacted>",
        "backendOrigin": "https://chatgpt.com",
        "accountRoutingOverride": "NO_CONSTRAINT"
      }
    }

The service also emits:

    {
      "method": "account/updated",
      "params": {
        "authMode": "chatgpt",
        "planType": "plus"
      }
    }

I have not inspected the token claims in the working macOS profile.

Affected profile:

    initialize_handshake_result outcome=success
    Current reported app-server version: currentVersion=0.167.0-alpha.3.2
    account_login_completed success=true
    cloud_picker_identity ... hasAccount=false ... hasUser=false

Working profile:

    account_login_completed success=true

- Restarted the Mac.
- Signed out and signed back in.
- Tested a phone hotspot.

The affected macOS profile previously used a different ChatGPT account. I do not know whether this is related.

No Keychain entries were deleted.

## Expected behavior

ChatGPT Desktop should load the authenticated account and allow use, as the bundled CLI and the desktop app under the other macOS profile do.

If required account-routing information is missing, the app should provide an actionable recovery path or diagnostic message.

This is persistent in my existing macOS profile, but I do not have a deterministic procedure to reproduce it in a clean profile.

#59410 reports the same account/read shape: planType=unknown and workspaceRouting=null.

- Guest: Ubuntu on WSL2
- WSL: 2.7.11.0
- Linux kernel: 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2
- Terminal emulator: not yet confirmed

**Problem**

Since updating Codex CLI, submitting pasted prompts has become intermittently unreliable.

The first Enter press frequently does not submit the pasted message. The composer continues to display the pasted-content placeholder.

Deleting the pending prompt, pasting exactly the same text again and pressing Enter normally succeeds immediately.

Waiting several seconds and pressing Enter again sometimes succeeds, but waiting alone has not consistently resolved the problem.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open an interactive Codex CLI session in Ubuntu WSL2.
2. Copy a prompt from ChatGPT and paste it into the composer.
3. Observe a placeholder such as `[Pasted Content 1655 chars]`.
4. Press Enter once.
5. Intermittently, nothing is submitted and the composer remains idle.
6. Delete the pending content, paste the same prompt again and press Enter.
7. Submission succeeds.

The problem has also occurred with a short slash command (`/keymap debug`), so it is not exclusive to long prompts.

**Diagnostic evidence**

The built-in `/keymap debug` inspector reports:

- Detected: `enter`
- Config key: `enter`
- Raw event: `code=Enter, modifiers=none, kind=Press`
- Assigned action: `composer.submit`

Manually typed prompts submit immediately. Short pasted prompts sometimes submit normally, confirming the intermittent behavior.

The problem continued after restoring normal HTTPS connectivity to ChatGPT.

**Expected behavior**

Pressing Enter once should reliably submit a completed paste. If Codex is still processing pasted input, it should preserve the draft and provide clear feedback.

**Actual behavior**

Enter sometimes fails silently. Re-pasting the same prompt restores normal submission.

**Impact**

Frequent interruptions to development workflows involving long, structured instructions. The workaround creates unnecessary delays and risks accidental duplicate submissions.

**Related issues**

- #28167 — Bracketed-paste state and Enter submission
- #44415 — Intermittent Enter submission failures

Please investigate the TUI paste-processing state and its interaction with the submit action in version 0.169.0.

issues.title: [Windows][Computer Use] System cursor stays invisible after completion on 26.1021; validated cursor-scheme recovery

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Installed Windows package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1021.3705.0` (read from the installed package; the About dialog was not used).

- App-server: `0.164.0-alpha.11.1`
- Computer Use plugin: `26.1021.31345`
- `@oai/sky`: `0.7.13`

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this report.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11, 25H2, x64, OS build `26200.6899`.

Windows Settings → Accessibility → Mouse pointer and touch:
- Built-in black pointer selected, with an enlarged pointer.
- `CursorSize = 4`, `CursorBaseSize = 80`.
- Configured arrow file: `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Microsoft/Windows/Cursors/arrow_eoa.cur`.

These are the settings present when the problem occurs. A controlled comparison has not established that the black style or enlargement causes it.

### What issue are you seeing?

After Computer Use finishes, my Windows mouse pointer disappears. This happens repeatedly—my experience is that it happens each time I use Computer Use. I have to open the Windows pointer settings and reapply/change the pointer style to make it visible again.

The expected handoff back to normal desktop use is broken. Changing my pointer style should not be necessary after each task.

This matches the symptom reported in #25200, which is still open. I am submitting current-build environment details and recovery measurements to help investigate that issue. #49175 describes a related, focus-dependent symptom, and #37621 describes a different persistent system-cursor mutation.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Reported failing workflow:

1. Use the Windows pointer settings above.
2. Let Codex Computer Use operate a Windows application.
3. Let the task finish and return to using the computer.
4. The visible mouse pointer is gone.
5. Reapply/change the pointer style in Windows Settings.
6. The pointer becomes visible again.

During the investigation, a minimal live Computer Use test captured the Windows Settings window and clicked an inert area of its heading. The diagnostic observations below were collected around that operation.

### What is the expected behavior?

Computer Use should return a visible, usable system pointer when its takeover ends. It should preserve the user's configured pointer color and size. The same cleanup should cover normal completion, cancellation, tool errors/timeouts, and helper shutdown.

### Additional information

#### Measured cursor state

A local Win32 probe used `GetCursorInfo`, `LoadCursor`, `GetIconInfo`, and `DrawIconEx`. Each cursor was rendered against both black and white backgrounds, counting pixels that differed from the background. This detects a fully transparent cursor independently of its color.

| Probe point | Arrow changed pixels | Text/I-beam changed pixels | Observation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Before Computer Use | 213 | 232 | System cursor images contain visible pixels |
| After the test click, while the takeover was still active | 0 | 0 | System cursor images are completely transparent |
| After explicitly resetting/closing the Computer Use JavaScript session | 203 | 200 | Visible cursor images restored; I also confirmed the pointer was visible |

The measured blank state had `GetCursorInfo.flags = 1` (`CURSOR_SHOWING`). Therefore, a “showing” flag alone is not evidence that the cursor image is visible.

**Evidence boundary:** transparency during an active takeover can be intentional. These measurements establish the blank-cursor mechanism and a successful session-close recovery; they do not independently reproduce a failed *normal task-completion* cleanup. The persistent post-completion disappearance is my repeated user-observed symptom. The precise failing native cleanup branch has not been traced.

Inspection of the installed helper found system-cursor suppression/restoration code, including blank-cursor creation, `SetSystemCursor`, a separate system-cursor-manager process, and a cursor-scheme reset path. The existing restoration path needs investigation; this report does not assume the restore API is entirely missing.

#### Verified recovery operation

Reloading the **current Windows cursor scheme** recovers blank system cursor images without changing the configured pointer color, size, or registry values:

```cpp
BOOL ok = SystemParametersInfoW(SPI_SETCURSORS, 0, nullptr, 0);
// Check ok / GetLastError(), then verify that the system cursor images
// are no longer blank. Run after the active takeover has released them.
```

Microsoft documents `SPI_SETCURSORS` (`0x0057`) as reloading the system cursors:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-systemparametersinfow

To test recovery rather than infer it from an API success code, a separate controlled test installed transparent Arrow and I-beam system cursors, ran the recovery code, and inspected them again:

```text
before recovery: arrow=0, text=0
recovery process exit code: 0
after recovery: arrow=203, text=200
pointer preferences unchanged: true
```

#### Local mitigation implemented and tested

A small local recovery program was connected to the existing completion notifier through its supported `--previous-notify` chain. It:

1. Handles `agent-turn-complete`.
2. Gives the native takeover a bounded interval to release its visible cursor overlay.
3. Skips recovery if that overlay is still visible, to avoid interfering with an ongoing Computer Use operation.
4. Checks whether both Arrow and I-beam system cursor images are blank.
5. If blank, reloads the current cursor scheme with `SPI_SETCURSORS` and checks the rendered images again.

It runs once per completion notification; it is not a resident polling service. Its logs from the controlled tests were:

```text
restored arrow=203 text=200
active-computer-use-skipped arrow=-1 text=-1
already-visible arrow=203 text=200
```

The active-operation guard was tested during a real Computer Use click. Session shutdown and a subsequent healthy-state check were also tested.

The recovery executable and configuration were validated locally. Automatic invocation at the end of a subsequent normal task has not yet been observed. This completion-only mitigation also does not prove coverage of cancellation/crash paths.

#### Requested upstream fix

Please make cursor restoration an owned, verified part of the native takeover lifecycle:

- Route completion, cancellation, timeout/error, disconnect, and shutdown through the same cleanup owner.
- Stop/join any cursor re-suppression work before restoring the user's current cursor scheme, so a late operation cannot replace the restored cursors with blanks again.
- Restore the affected system cursor resources and verify the result. `CURSOR_SHOWING` by itself is insufficient when the image is transparent.
- Account for another genuinely active takeover before changing shared cursor state.
- Add a regression test for enlarged built-in black pointers, plus normal completion and interrupted/helper-exit paths.

The demonstrated recovery primitive is available and preserves my settings. The remaining upstream work is to establish which lifecycle path leaves the blank resources installed and ensure restoration completes on that path. I am not proposing changing users to a white/default-size pointer as the fix.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Version 26.1103.31037

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.12.113+deb13-amd64 x86_64

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary

Codex App interrupted an agent while it was investigating and fixing a security weakness in my own local application's document-parser sandbox.

I own the project and explicitly authorized its implementation, defensive testing, and repair. I believe this interruption may be a cybersecurity-safeguard false positive.

## Authorized work and environment

The application processes PDFs and images using a parser sandbox inside a Docker container.

The intended restrictions include:
- Nonroot execution.
- No network access.
- No added host capabilities.
- No-new-privileges.
- Restricted filesystem access.
- Bounded memory, processes, file descriptors, temporary storage, and execution time.

The work was limited to my local project and isolated test containers. It did not target third-party systems.

## What happened

1. The agent was implementing and testing the document-parser sandbox.
2. A controlled test used one-byte canary files to check whether writes were restricted to the designated bounded temporary directories.
3. The test found that the parser could write to its private `/` and `/dev` directories outside those bounded temporary mounts.
4. A separate attempt to create a nested user/mount namespace was denied.
5. The test reported `TEMPORARY_BUDGET_BYPASS` and confirmed that the test fixture was stopped.
6. The agent began investigating a kernel-enforced write restriction while preserving the existing host policy and resource limits.
7. Codex interrupted the agent with the cybersecurity error below before the repair was completed.

The test did not demonstrate an escape from Docker or access to host system directories. The issue being investigated was an incomplete temporary-storage restriction inside the parser sandbox.

## Exact error

> This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk. If this seems wrong, try rephrasing your request. If you’re doing authorized security work that requires more cyber permissive safeguards, apply for Daybreak access via https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/status-and-access before retrying.

## Actual behavior

The agent's turn ended with a system error, leaving the defensive repair and verification unfinished.

The suggested link took me to the OpenAI API platform/setup experience. It did not provide a clear next step for resuming this work in my existing Codex App session.

I submitted feedback, but I do not know whether the returned ID provides any way to track the report or whether additional account access is required.

## Expected behavior

Codex should either:
- Allow this authorized defensive repair within the existing local restrictions; or
- Provide clear, actionable instructions for the access or review required to continue in Codex App.

I am not requesting that safeguards be disabled or bypassed. I am requesting review of this specific interruption and guidance on the supported way to resume.

## Session references

Affected implementer chat:
`01a1f0aa-e4ad-7a42-9712-0278d32a13d3`

ID shown after my feedback submission:
`01a1f0a8-5a76-7003-8008-e3a4cc81f316`

The second ID also matches the coordinator chat where I authorized the work and discussed the interruption. Please confirm whether it is sufficient to locate the submitted feedback.

## Questions

1. Was this interruption a false positive?
2. Is additional access required for this defensive work in Codex App?
3. What supported steps should I follow to resume the affected session?
4. Where can I track the feedback or receive a response?

The project and test evidence are preserved. I have omitted private source code, local project paths, and credentials from this public report.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence in the affected session:

1. Use Codex App on Linux to work on an owned local application with explicit authorization for defensive development and testing.
2. Ask the agent to verify and repair the application's document-parser sandbox inside Docker, preserving nonroot execution, no network, no added host capabilities, and existing resource limits.
3. The agent runs a controlled local test and identifies writable private directories outside the designated bounded temporary-storage areas.
4. The agent investigates how to restrict those writes using existing Linux isolation mechanisms.
5. Codex terminates the turn with: “This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk.”

The test fixture was stopped safely, but the repair remained unfinished.

Affected session:
01a1f0aa-e4ad-7a42-9712-0278d32a13d3

Feedback/session reference:
01a1f0a8-5a76-7003-8008-e3a4cc81f316

This describes the observed sequence, not a confirmed minimal reproduction. I have not independently reproduced the platform interruption. Exact token usage and context-window usage at the interruption are unknown. Please use the submitted session evidence to investigate.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should permit authorized defensive development on my own local application within the existing safety restrictions.

If this work requires additional access or review, the app should clearly explain:
- What requirement triggered the interruption.
- How to request the appropriate access for Codex App.
- How to resume the affected session after approval.
- How to track the submitted feedback.

The guidance should distinguish additional cybersecurity access from creating an API key. I am not requesting that safeguards be disabled or bypassed.

### Additional information

_No response_

issues.title: codex exec logs an unreachable HTTP MCP server as 3× ERROR rmcp::transport::worker, without the server name

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: exec

labels.name: CLI

issues.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.170.0

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT plan (not relevant: local logging)

### Which model were you using?

gpt-6.1-sol

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.2 arm64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Non-interactive (`codex exec` from scripts)

### Codex doctor report

_No response_

### What issue are you seeing?

`codex exec` logs an unreachable streamable-HTTP MCP server as three `ERROR rmcp::transport::worker` lines on stderr, even when the run never uses an MCP tool and succeeds. The lines don't name the server.

```
… ERROR rmcp::transport::worker: worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(HttpRequest(HttpRequest("http/request failed: error sending request for url (http://127.0.0.1:9/mcp)")))
… (same line 3× within ~1.3 s)
```

stdout is `ok`, exit code 0. In my usage over one week: 59 occurrences in 22 sessions of automated read-only review runs (`codex exec -s read-only --json --output-schema …`) while one configured HTTP MCP server was down. Wrappers end up adding `grep -v rmcp`, which then hides real errors too.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```bash
codex exec -s read-only --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral \
  -c 'mcp_servers.deadhttp.url="http://127.0.0.1:9/mcp"' \
  "Reply with the single word ok. Do not call any tools."
```

The same run without the `-c` override prints no ERROR lines.

### What is the expected behavior?

An MCP server the run never uses is started lazily, or its startup failure is logged once at WARN with the server's name (e.g. `WARN MCP server 'deadhttp' unavailable: …`). ERROR stays for failures of a server the model actually calls.

### Additional information

Related: #42242 (lazy startup for MCP servers) and #62366 (lazy startup on by default, merged, but stdio servers only, so HTTP servers still connect eagerly).

issues.title: Native Edge extension origin review reports an unbound browser-use connector despite verified tab and explicit authorization

labels.name: bug

issues.body:
## What version of the Codex App are you using?

Runtime client metadata reports `0.169.0-alpha.11.1` (not independently checked in the About dialog). Bundled browser provider package: `26.1111.21308`.

## What subscription do you have?

Not inspected.

## Platform

Linux, Niri/Wayland, Microsoft Edge, native OpenAI ChatGPT browser extension. The acting surface is Codex desktop with `mcp__node_repl__js`.

## What issue are you seeing?

Automatic origin review repeatedly describes the documented native Edge extension operation as a separate, unbound `browser-use` connector, despite successful native browser discovery, profile/window/tab metadata reads, an earlier successful AX read of the exact blank tab, and explicit user authorization of both the selected browser route and origin gate.

Observed sanitized errors include:

> Browser use could not acquire authority to observe page content. The origin approval gate did not grant access for [authorized internal origin].

> The request again uses the unbound `browser-use` origin connector, not the authorized native [agent-profile] Edge tab, so accessing the internal authenticated origin remains unauthorized through this route.

The quoted bracketed identifiers replace private values. This report intentionally omits internal addresses, account names, session IDs, credentials, screenshots, and unrelated browser data.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence from an existing long-running conversation; minimal fresh-session reproduction is not established:

1. Use the bundled browser client's documented native runtime through `mcp__node_repl__js`.
2. Discover Edge in `agent.browsers.list()`: `family: edge`, `type: extension`, expected profile and extension-instance metadata.
3. Bind that exact browser, inspect `browser.user.openTabs()`, and claim the exact returned owned tab. Native management metadata correlates its tab, group and window.
4. The extension successfully reads the exact tab's `about:blank` AX state. Discovery and native metadata inspection continue to work.
5. User expressly authorizes navigation to the intended internal HTTPS service and use of that profile. Existing authorized service tabs are also available.
6. `await tab.goto(authorizedOrigin)` is rejected by origin review with the reason above. Later `await authenticatedServiceTab.ax.write()` is likewise rejected even after the user independently signs in and explicitly requests continuation.
7. Explicitly approving the internally named `browser-use` origin gate, conditioned on the verified native Edge extension, still does not resolve the rejection.

No separate Playwright connector, raw CDP, shell navigation, policy weakening or alternate transport was used to circumvent the denials. The user later authorized Playwright, but it was not used to bypass the existing rejection.

## Expected behavior

Origin review should receive and assess the actual selected native extension/browser/profile/tab provenance alongside authentic user authorization. If an additional supported binding or approval step is required, report that actionable step through an exposed supported interface rather than repeatedly asking for the same already-provided authorization.

This is not a request to auto-allow private origins or weaken approval/security controls. Preserve rejection of unauthorized profiles, origins and effects.

## Additional information / requested maintainer investigation

Please inspect how the native browser operation is represented to the origin-approval reviewer and how its selected extension/tab provenance is linked. Determine whether provenance is omitted, review context is stale, a separate required binding is missing, or the reviewer is misclassifying the internal connector name. The exact implementation cause is unverified; successful discovery alone is not proof that the origin-review linkage is intact.

The issue prevented a user-authorized backup migration task from starting. Existing backups were preserved and no destructive cleanup occurred. Repeated assistant requests for user approvals were ineffective and should not be treated as a recovery mechanism.

Please identify the responsible browser/approval-integration maintainer and a supported recovery or fix. No approval clarification or origin-binding repair operation was exposed in the tools available to the reporting session. Private diagnostic originals remain local and have not been uploaded.
