Updates `express` from 5.1.0 to 5.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

v5.3.0

Highlights

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @​cuishuang in #7459

  • Upgrade qs to ^6.16.0, which fixes CVE-2026-2391 (GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), CVE-2026-82417 (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) and CVE-2026-82562 (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx): arrayLimit bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled isBuffer - by @​davetashner in #7057 and #7478, and @​cyphercodes in #7305

  • Upgrade proxy-addr to ^2.0.8, which fixes CVE-2026-90711 - by @​lazerg in #7474

🚀 Improvements

  • Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. req.fresh previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by @​Cherry in #7366

    // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
  res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
  res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
});

  • Improve HTML structure in res.redirect() responses when HTML format is accepted by adding <!DOCTYPE html>, <title>, and <body> tags for better browser compatibility - by @​Bernice55231 in #5167

  • When calling app.render with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by AkaHarshit in #6903

    app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected

  • Upgrade content-type to ^2.0.0, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker Content-Type parsing/formatting in res.send()) along with a behavior change: res.send() now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a Content-Type that fails to parse. type-is is upgraded to ^2.1.0 as part of the same change - by @​blakeembrey in #7234

    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
// -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8

  • The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as Error.cause and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's parent/original) are no longer swallowed - by @​Nitin-Mohapatra in #6464

  • Upgrade content-disposition to ^2.0.1, which changes the Content-Disposition header emitted by res.download(), res.attachment(), and res.sendFile(): file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by @​blakeembrey in #7233

    res.attachment('user.html');
// before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
// after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html

... (truncated)

Bumps [@simple-git/argv-parser](https://github.com/steveukx/git-js/tree/HEAD/packages/argv-parser) to 3.0.0 and updates ancestor dependency [simple-git](https://github.com/steveukx/git-js/tree/HEAD/simple-git). Release notes

Sourced from @​simple-git/argv-parser's releases.

@​simple-git/argv-parser@​3.0.0

Major Changes

  • df13aeb: Remove the vulnerabilityCheck export, use parseArgv(...tokens).vulnerabilities and parseEnv(env).vulnerabilities instead. Each vulnerability now also carries the configKey or envKey that triggered it.

Minor Changes

  • df13aeb: Add the allowConfig and strict options. Configuration keys outside the built-in list of known-safe keys (SAFE_CONFIG_KEYS) and the keys named in allowConfig now emit a one-off SIMPLE_GIT_UNLISTED_CONFIG warning, or are rejected when strict: true is set. Known-unsafe keys can now be permitted individually through allowConfig, and environment variables through allowEnvironment, deprecating the unsafe.allowUnsafe* options that only covered configuration keys or environment variables (they continue to work as before).

  • a996f0f: Thanks to @​manus-pi and @​eliteaja11-dev for submitting CVE proposals that contributed to these changes.

    When the recommended checks are enabled (with unsafe.recommended: true or strict: true), HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME supplied through .env() with a value other than the one in process.env require allowUnsafeConfigPaths (or naming them in allowEnvironment), as git reads the global configuration from $HOME/.gitconfig and $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config in the same way as GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL. Passing the inherited value through is unaffected, and neither is removed from the inherited environment.

    parseEnv accepts the inherited environment as an optional second argument, used to compare HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME against.

    isGuardedEnvKey is now exported from @simple-git/argv-parser, identifying the environment variables (GIT_* and the others git reads, such as EDITOR and PAGER) that simple-git removes from an inherited environment.

  • c8ee6bb: Vulnerability reports:

    With thanks to @​manus-pi, @​manus-use, @​ba-am, @​mspiq, @​hoseinenddev, @​freyesperales, @​dalberrt, @​zer0d4y5, @​gamster01, @​humaneBicycle, @​Hama1cco, @​eliteaja11-dev, @​Cone-Tester, @​Figo5, @​MalwareEZ, @​zachariah-mithani, @​shaswata56, @​Akokonunes for submitting CVE proposals that contributed to these changes.

    • allowUnsafePager will now catch setting a custom binary in git grep --open-files-in-pager.
    • allowUnsafePager now also covers interactive.diffFilter, the shell command that git add -p and the other --patch commands pipe their diff through.
    • new (deprecated on arrival, prefer allowConfig) allowUnsafeSendEmailConfig option covering the sendemail.* keys that git send-email runs as commands, reads as files or uses to turn off certificate verification (sendmailCmd, toCmd, ccCmd, headerCmd, smtpServer, smtpServerOption, smtpSSLCertPath, smtpSSLClientCert, smtpSSLClientKey, aliasesFile and mailmap.file, including their per-identity sendemail.<identity>.* variants), and the imap.tunnel, imap.host and imap.sslVerify keys used by git imap-send.
    • new (deprecated on arrival, prefer allowConfig) allowUnsafeWebServerConfig option covering the instaweb.httpd, instaweb.modulePath and instaweb.gitwebDir keys used by git instaweb.
    • new (deprecated on arrival, prefer allowConfig) allowUnsafeBrowser option covering the browser.<tool>.path, browser.<tool>.cmd, man.<tool>.path and man.<tool>.cmd keys used by git help and git instaweb to open a browser or man page viewer. browser.<tool>.cmd and man.<tool>.cmd were previously covered by allowUnsafeCommandBinaries.
    • new (deprecated on arrival, prefer allowConfig) allowUnsafeSignatureTrust option covering gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile, gpg.ssh.revocationFile and gpg.minTrustLevel, which decide which signatures pass verification.

  • df13aeb: Add templateArgv, isTemplateStringsArray, remoteUrl and refName for building a git argv from a tagged template literal, where every interpolated value is treated as untrusted data. simple-git uses these for git.cmd.

prs.title: chore(deps): adjust workspace dependency pins and update simple-git
prs.body:
## Summary

Follows up on #30321 by adjusting workspace dependency pins, version-scoped root `overrides`, and Stage 2 sandbox `Dockerfile` sub-package versions, and updates `simple-git` from `3.36.0` to `4.0.2`.

## Details

- Updates `simple-git` from `3.36.0` to `4.0.2` in root `package.json`, `packages/cli/package.json`, and `packages/core/package.json`.
- Adjusts workspace manifests, root `package.json` `overrides` (using version-scoped keys `minimatch@^11.0.0`, `brace-expansion@^5.0.0`, and `es-module-lexer@^3.0.0` where legacy major versions coexist), and Stage 2 of `Dockerfile`:
  - `@grpc/grpc-js`: `1.14.6`
  - `@hono/node-server`: `2.1.6`, `hono`: `4.13.16`, `jose`: `6.2.13`, `express-rate-limit`: `8.7.1`, `qs`: `6.17.0`
  - `@opentelemetry/core`, `@opentelemetry/resources`, `@opentelemetry/sdk-metrics`, `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace`, `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base`: `2.11.0`
  - `import-in-the-middle`: `3.5.3`, `es-module-lexer@^3.0.0`: `3.0.3`
  - `glob`: `14.0.3`, `minimatch@^11.0.0`: `11.0.2`, `brace-expansion@^5.0.0`: `5.0.12`, `@isaacs/nonrecursive-glob-match`: `1.0.2`
  - `basic-ftp`: `6.2.3`, `ip-address`: `10.7.5`, `systeminformation`: `5.33.18`, `tar`: `7.5.22`, `undici`: `7.30.1`, `ws`: `8.22.0`
- Regenerates `package-lock.json` (synchronizing `basic-ftp` and `uuid` override resolutions) and `packages/vscode-ide-companion/NOTICES.txt`.

## Related Issues

Related to #30321

## How to Validate

1. Run `npm ci`, `npm run check:lockfile`, `npm run build`, `npm run bundle`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npm run lint` across workspaces.
2. Verify `git diff --exit-code packages/vscode-ide-companion/NOTICES.txt` after `npm ci`.
3. Run unit tests:
   - `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/services/gitService.test.ts src/telemetry/sdk.test.ts`
   - `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/extension.test.ts src/config/extensions/github.test.ts`
   - `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-a2a-server`
   - `npm test -w gemini-cli-vscode-ide-companion`

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [ ] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any)

prs.title: fix(core): match commandPrefix and commandRegex rules against the top-level command argument
prs.body:
## Summary

This pull request updates `buildArgsPatterns()` in `packages/core/src/policy/utils.ts`
so patterns generated from `commandPrefix` and `commandRegex` match only the
top-level `command` argument in serialized tool arguments. It also wraps
`commandRegex` in a non-capturing group `(?:...)`, updates
`compileArgsPattern()` to run the nested-quantifier check on the authored
pattern, and updates `docs/reference/policy-engine.md` and unit tests to reflect
the new behavior.

## Details

Tool arguments are serialized with `stableStringify()`, which prefixes each
top-level key-value entry with a `\x00` delimiter while omitting that delimiter
from nested objects and array items. Previously, `buildArgsPatterns()` emitted
`"command":` without the leading `\x00` delimiter and concatenated `commandRegex`
without grouping.

This change makes the following technical updates:

- **Top-level argument anchoring (`packages/core/src/policy/utils.ts`):**
  `buildArgsPatterns()` now prefixes patterns generated for both `commandPrefix`
  and `commandRegex` with `\x00`, ensuring matches occur only at a top-level
  `command` property rather than inside nested structures or string values.
- **Scoped alternation for `commandRegex` (`packages/core/src/policy/utils.ts`):**
  `buildArgsPatterns()` now wraps `commandRegex` as `\x00"command":"(?:${commandRegex})`
  so top-level alternations (for example, `ls|pwd`) remain scoped to the
  `command` value.
- **Authored-pattern validation (`packages/core/src/policy/utils.ts`,
  `packages/core/src/policy/toml-loader.ts`):** `compileArgsPattern()` now
  accepts an optional `authoredPattern` parameter (defaulting to `pattern`) and
  runs `NESTED_QUANTIFIER.test(authoredPattern)`. `loadPoliciesFromToml()` passes
  `rule.commandRegex ?? argsPattern` (and `checker.commandRegex ?? argsPattern`
  for safety checkers) so the `(?:...)` wrapper added by Gemini CLI does not
  trigger false nested-quantifier rejections on existing quantified rules.
- **Documentation (`docs/reference/policy-engine.md`):** Documents the `\x00`
  top-level delimiter in `stableStringify()` output, updates the `argsPattern`
  example to `\x00"command":"(?:git|npm)`, and clarifies `commandRegex`
  start-of-command alternation behavior.
- **Tests:** Updates expectations in `policy-updater.test.ts` and
  `safe-regex.test.ts`, and adds coverage in `utils.test.ts`,
  `toml-loader.test.ts`, and `shell-safety-regression.test.ts` for top-level
  anchoring, `commandRegex` alternation scoping, and quantified `commandRegex`
  compilation.

## Related Issues

## How to Validate

Run the policy unit test suite, typecheck, and linter against the updated
files:

1. Run the policy tests in `@google/gemini-cli-core`:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/policy/
   ```
   Expected result: all 16 test files (450 tests) pass.
2. Run TypeScript typechecking and ESLint:
   ```bash
   npm run typecheck
   npx eslint packages/core/src/policy/ docs/reference/policy-engine.md --max-warnings 0
   ```
   Expected result: zero type errors and zero lint errors or warnings.
3. Verify edge cases covered by the new unit tests:
   - `commandPrefix` and `commandRegex` match when `command` is the top-level
     argument and do not match when `"command":"..."` appears inside a nested
     object, array element, or another top-level string argument.
   - `commandRegex` with top-level alternation (for example, `ls|pwd`) matches
     only at the start of the `command` value.
   - Quantified `commandRegex` expressions (for example, `(?:ab)+`) continue to
     load without triggering nested-quantifier rejection.

prs.title: fix(core): keep ASK_USER for shell commands with unresolved expansion
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR keeps the `ASK_USER` decision for shell commands whose arguments bash
rewrites before they run. `PolicyEngine.applyShellHeuristics()` classifies a
command from its unexpanded text and upgrades the default `ASK_USER` decision to
`ALLOW` when the command is read-only. When the text contains brace expansion,
parameter expansion, ANSI-C or locale quoting, arithmetic expansion,
substitutions, or unquoted globs, bash runs a different argument list than the
one that was classified. With this change, those commands keep the confirmation
prompt, and the decision matches the arguments that run.

## Details

The change adds one helper, one early return in the policy engine, and one
condition in each `isStrictlyApproved()` function. It doesn't add dependencies,
change `shellParse()`, or modify runtime shell flags.

- **New helper:** `hasUnresolvedShellExpansion(command)` in
  `packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts` walks the tree-sitter-bash syntax
  tree through the existing `parseCommandTree()` path.
  - It reports `simple_expansion`, `expansion`, `ansi_c_string`,
    `arithmetic_expansion`, `command_substitution`, `process_substitution`, and
    `brace_expression` nodes, plus the `$` token followed by a `string` node
    that tree-sitter-bash 0.25.0 produces for `$"..."`.
  - It checks the unquoted text of `word` and `concatenation` nodes for `{a,b}`
    and `{a..c}` groups and for `*`, `?`, and `[...]`. Text in `raw_string` and
    `string` nodes and backslash-escaped characters are literal, so `'*.md'`,
    `"{a,b}"`, `\*.md`, `{}`, and `{id}` aren't reported. Tilde expansion isn't
    reported, because the existing path checks already handle it.
  - It returns `true` when the parser isn't available, parsing times out, or the
    tree has errors. It returns `false` when the configured shell isn't bash, so
    PowerShell behavior doesn't change.
- **Policy engine:** `applyShellHeuristics()` calls the helper right before the
  known-safe upgrade. When the helper returns `true`, the decision stays
  `ASK_USER`, and a debug line records it:
  `Command contains unresolved shell expansion, preserving ASK_USER`. The `DENY`
  early return, the workspace and Git checks, and YOLO handling are unchanged.
- **Sandbox approval:** both `isStrictlyApproved()` functions
  (`sandbox/utils/commandUtils.ts` and `sandbox/utils/commandSafety.ts`) apply
  the helper only to the `isKnownSafeCommand()` fallback. A command whose root
  tools are all in `approvedTools` stays approved, because that list is an
  explicit approval.
- **Unchanged:** explicit `ALLOW` rules, rules with `commandPrefix` or
  `argsPattern`, and the `plan`, YOLO, and non-interactive modes.

The following table shows example decisions with the default `run_shell_command`
rule in the `default` and `autoEdit` approval modes.

| Command                                                 | Before  | After      |
| :------------------------------------------------------ | :------ | :--------- |
| `echo {1..3}`                                           | `allow` | `ask_user` |
| `ls *.md`                                               | `allow` | `ask_user` |
| `ls ${d:-/etc}`                                         | `allow` | `ask_user` |
| `ls "$HOME"`                                            | `allow` | `ask_user` |
| `echo $'x'`                                             | `allow` | `ask_user` |
| `ls -la`, `find . -name '*.md'`                         | `allow` | `allow`    |
| `ls '*.md'`, `echo "{a,b}"`, `grep -E 'a{1,3}' f.txt`   | `allow` | `allow`    |
| `ls *.md` with an explicit `ALLOW` rule for shell tools | `allow` | `allow`    |

**Behavior change:** read-only commands that use unquoted globs, brace groups,
or variables, such as `ls *.md`, now show a confirmation prompt instead of
running automatically. Quoted arguments keep auto-approval. If you want these
commands to run without a prompt, you can add an explicit `ALLOW` policy rule.

**Tests:** this PR adds 117 tests. They only ask for a policy decision or a
boolean result, and they never run the commands.

- `policy/shell-argument-expansion.test.ts` (new): 70 tests with the real
  parser, the real `NoopSandboxManager`, and a temporary workspace, in the
  `default` and `autoEdit` approval modes.
- `utils/shell-utils.test.ts`: 40 tests for the helper, including syntax errors,
  a parse timeout, an unavailable parser, and PowerShell.
- `sandbox/utils/commandUtils.test.ts` (new) and
  `sandbox/utils/commandSafety.test.ts`: 7 tests for both `isStrictlyApproved()`
  functions.
- `policy/policy-engine.test.ts`: the existing `shell-utils` mock in this file
  doesn't load the parser, so it now also mocks `hasUnresolvedShellExpansion` to
  return `false`. No assertion changed.

## Related Issues


## How to Validate

You can validate the change with the unit tests and with a short interactive
check.

1.  Install the dependencies:

    ```bash
    npm ci
    ```

2.  Run the focused suites:

    ```bash
    npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- \
      src/policy/shell-argument-expansion.test.ts \
      src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts \
      src/sandbox/utils/commandSafety.test.ts \
      src/sandbox/utils/commandUtils.test.ts \
      src/policy/policy-engine.test.ts \
      src/policy/shell-safety.test.ts \
      src/policy/shell-safety-regression.test.ts \
      src/policy/shell-substitution.test.ts
    ```

    Expected result: all tests pass. Some `shell-utils.test.ts` tests are
    skipped on Linux and macOS because they only run on Windows.

3.  Run the static checks:

    ```bash
    npm run lint
    npm run typecheck
    ```

    Expected result: both commands exit with code `0`.

4.  Optional: check the behavior interactively on Linux or macOS.
    1.  Start Gemini CLI in a test folder with `--approval-mode default` and
        `--debug`.
    2.  Ask Gemini CLI to run `ls -la` unchanged. It runs without a confirmation
        dialog.
    3.  Ask Gemini CLI to run `ls *.md` unchanged. The **Confirm Shell Command**
        dialog appears, and the debug console shows
        `Command contains unresolved shell expansion, preserving ASK_USER`.
    4.  Ask Gemini CLI to run `ls '*.md'` unchanged. It runs without a
        confirmation dialog.

Edge cases that the tests cover:

- Quoted text stays literal: `echo '{red,green}.txt'`, `cat 'file{1,2}.txt'`,
  and `awk '{print $1}' f.txt`.
- An explicit `ALLOW` rule without `argsPattern` keeps `allow`.
- PowerShell returns `false` for any command.
- A parse error, a parse timeout, or an unavailable parser keeps `ASK_USER`.

Local results on Linux (Node.js 26.1.0): the full `@google/gemini-cli-core`
suite passed (8,955 tests, 57 skipped), and a run that mirrors CI (clean,
install, build, lint, typecheck, all workspace tests, bundle, and a bundle smoke
test) passed.

- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any)
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:

prs.title: feat(acp): support mid-turn steering over ACP (_session/steering) (#30048)
prs.body:
Fixes #30048

### Description
Historically in ACP mode (`gemini --acp`), external editor hosts or agent orchestrators had only two options during an in-flight prompt: wait for the entire multi-tool turn to finish or abort the pending turn (`this.pendingPrompt?.abort()`), discarding all completed work. Meanwhile, the interactive TUI mode already supported mid-turn user steering natively.

This PR implements the ACP steering extension proposal (`_session/steering`), enabling clients to inject guidance directly into a running agent turn at tool-execution boundaries without cancelling the session.

### Changes
- **Capability Advertisement**: `GeminiAgent.initialize()` now advertises `_meta.steering = { supported: true }`.
- **RPC Routing**: Added `_session/steering` and `steering` handlers in `acpRpcDispatcher.ts` delegating to `Session.prototype.steer()`.
- **Boundary Injection**: `Session` queues steering text hints and injects them via `formatUserHintsForModel()` at tool-call wave boundaries alongside tool response parts.
- **Idle Behavior Handling**: Supports standard outcomes (`injected`, `promptRequired`, `startedNewTurn`, `failed`) based on session state and `_meta.steering.idleBehavior`.
- **Lifecycle Management**: Guaranteed cleanup of `this.pendingPrompt` to ensure accurate idle vs. generating detection.
- **Testing**: Added comprehensive unit test coverage in `acpRpcDispatcher.test.ts` and `acpSession.test.ts`.

prs.title: fix(acp): standardize token usage tracking and quota metadata (#24280, #27985)
prs.body:
### Description
This PR resolves two token tracking discrepancies in ACP mode:
1. **Preserve `PromptResponse.usage` on cancelled turns (#24280)**: Previously, early aborts or cancellations returned `{ stopReason: 'cancelled' }` without `usage` or `_meta`. This caused ACP clients to lose token usage metrics on cancelled prompts. Cancellation paths now return `buildPromptResponse('cancelled')` with preserved turn usage.
2. **Track cached and thought tokens in model quota metadata (#27985)**: Per-model quota breakdowns in `_meta.quota.model_usage` previously only tracked input and output tokens, omitting cached and thought tokens. We now track all four token dimensions (`input`, `output`, `cached`, `thought`) across all models and multi-turn tool loops.

### Changes
- `packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.ts`:
  - Updated `modelUsageMap` type to include `cached` and `thought` tokens.
  - Added `cached_tokens` and `thought_tokens` to `_meta.quota.token_count` and `_meta.quota.model_usage`.
  - Added helper `recordTurnUsage()` to ensure tokens parsed before abort are preserved.
  - Updated abort and `AbortError` return paths to return `buildPromptResponse('cancelled')`.
- `packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.test.ts`:
  - Added unit tests for mid-stream prompt aborts, immediate aborts, `AbortError` handling, and multi-turn multi-model token accumulation.

prs.title: ⚡ Bolt: optimize tool argument and error message sanitization hot path
prs.body:
* 💡 What: Pre-compiled regular expressions (`KEY_WITH_DELIMITER_REGEX`, `SPACE_SEPARATED_REGEX`, `FILE_PATH_REDACT_REGEX`) and pre-computed normalized sensitive key patterns (`NORMALIZED_SENSITIVE_PATTERNS`) at module scope in `packages/core/src/utils/agent-sanitization-utils.ts`.
* 🎯 Why: Previously, `sanitizeErrorMessage` re-compiled multiple regular expressions via `new RegExp(...)` on every call, and `sanitizeToolArgs` re-normalized `SENSITIVE_KEY_PATTERNS` for every property key of every object passed to it, causing significant CPU and GC overhead on the hot path for tool call execution and error handling.
* 📊 Impact: ~8.2x speedup (825% performance improvement / 88% runtime reduction) for sanitization calls (reduced execution time from 3,323ms down to 402ms for 50,000 operations in benchmarks).
* 🔬 Measurement: Benchmarked 50,000 iterations of `sanitizeToolArgs` and `sanitizeErrorMessage` with nested objects and sensitive parameters.

issues.title: Pasted PDF is counted at its encoded size in the context estimate and triggers an unnecessary compaction (620k estimated vs 31k real)

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Pasting a PDF into the prompt triggers an immediate automatic compaction because the context estimate counts the PDF at roughly its encoded file size, not what it costs the model. A 1.9 MB PDF added ~620k to the estimate but ~31k real input tokens.

Similar to #2936 (images), closed in April; this is the PDF/document case.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.114-0

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start a session on `gpt-6.2-astra` with the `long_context` tier (tokenLimit 922000).
2. Work until the context is ~200k (estimate `conversationTokens` ~202k).
3. Paste a 1.9 MB PDF into the prompt (attachment type `file`) and submit.
4. `session.compaction_start` fires 10 ms after `user.message`:
   `trigger "threshold"`, `currentTokens 845092`, `conversationTokens 821857`, `tokenLimit 922000`.
5. Compaction is applied: 276 of 283 messages removed, ~41k tokens left.
6. `session.usage_record` for the call carrying the PDF: `inputTokens 234816` (previous call `204065`), so the PDF cost ~31k real tokens.

### Expected behavior

The compaction threshold uses the attachment's model token cost (~31k here), not an estimate from the raw or base64 file size. No compaction at ~235k of 922k.

### Additional context

- macOS (Darwin), arm64, zsh; terminal: xterm.js inside tmux
- The ~620k estimate ≈ the base64 size of the file (1.9 MB × 4/3 ÷ 4 chars per token)
- Evidence is in the session's `events.jsonl`: `user.message`, `session.compaction_start`, `session.compaction_complete`, `session.usage_record`

issues.title: store_memory offers user scope when user-level memory is unavailable; every user-scoped store fails with 404

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`store_memory` offers `scope: "user"` even when user-level preferences are not available for my account. Every user-scoped store then fails with HTTP 404, while repository-scoped stores work. The only client-side switch, `/memory off`, turns off both scopes, so I can't keep repository memory and turn off only the user scope that fails.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.113; also the runtime embedded in the VS Code 1.146.0 agent host (1.0.108-0)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Use an account where user-level Copilot Memory preferences are not available, and work in a repository where repository memory is.
2. Start a session with memory enabled (VS Code agent host, or `copilot --enable-memory`).
3. Note that the `store_memory` tool's `scope` parameter allows `["repository","user"]`; `copilot -p "..." --enable-memory` reports the same.
4. Have the agent store a personal preference, so it calls `store_memory` with `scope: "user"`. It fails within about a second:
   > Unable to store memory: the memory endpoint was not found. User-scoped memories may not be enabled.

   Tool telemetry: `operation=storeMemory`, `source=service_api`, `scope=user`, `httpStatus=404`.
5. With the same account and host, `store_memory` with `scope: "repository"` succeeds (HTTP 201), and repository memories load into the prompt normally.

### Expected behavior

When user-level preferences are not available, the runtime should:

- Leave `user` out of `store_memory`'s `scope` values and out of the memory guidance in the system prompt. It already does this for repository scope when there is no repository context ("Memory storage correctly limits available scopes when no repository context is present").
- Show user scope as unavailable in `/memory show`, as 1.0.107 does for repository scope.

Separately, it would help to be able to turn off only one scope (for example user scope) in `/memory` or `/settings`, rather than all memory with `/memory off`.

### Additional context

- macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- The client can't tell me why user scope is unavailable (my personal scope choice, my plan, or organization policy); it only infers "may not be enabled" from the 404.
- Workaround: a personal custom instruction telling agents not to call `store_memory` with user scope. This relies on the model following it.

issues.title: ACP: a failed session/request_permission is recorded as a user denial and silently ends the (sub)agent's turn

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Copilot CLI 1.0.114, `copilot --acp`, Linux (WSL2).

When the ACP client answers `session/request_permission` with a JSON-RPC error, the CLI records the permission as `{"kind": "denied-interactively-by-user"}` with `decisionSource: "unattended_fallback"`. The tool result says:

> Permission denied because no permission response path was available. Configure an interactive permission response path, or try an alternative that does not require this permission.

The agent loop then handles it as a user rejection: the turn ends right after the tool result, with no further model call. A background subagent goes idle with an empty final message, `read_agent` shows an empty turn, and the parent gets no report. The message tells the model to "try an alternative", but the model never gets the chance.

In `-p` mode the same unattended fallback records `denied-no-approval-rule-and-could-not-request-from-user`, and the model receives the error and keeps going. That is what ACP should do too.

This shows up in practice with T3 Code, which fails `session/request_permission` once its turn has settled while background subagents keep running (pingdotgg/t3code#23552). Every background subagent that needs one approval after that point ends with an empty reply. This happened to all background review subagents in our sessions, with gpt-6.2-sol, claude-opus-5.5 and claude-haiku-5.5.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.114.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

The script below is a minimal ACP client. It asks a parent agent to start one `general-purpose` subagent that runs `sleep 25` and then reads a file outside the working directory. With `T3EMUL=1`, it approves `session/request_permission` until the parent has finished its turn, then answers with `{"code": -32603, "message": "ACP agent requested input without an active turn"}`.

```
T3EMUL=1 python3 acp_repro.py bg background gpt-6.2-sol xhigh
T3EMUL=1 python3 acp_repro.py sync sync gpt-6.2-sol xhigh
```

| Subagent model / effort | Mode | Permission outcome | Final message of the subagent's turn |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| claude-haiku-5.5 / default | background | `denied-interactively-by-user`, `unattended_fallback` | empty |
| gpt-6.2-sol / default | background | same | empty |
| gpt-6.2-sol / xhigh | background | same | empty |
| claude-opus-5.5 / default | background | same | empty |
| gpt-6.2-sol / xhigh | sync | approved | full answer |
| gpt-6.2-sol / xhigh, CLI started with `--allow-all-tools --allow-all-paths` | background | no request needed | full answer |

The subagent's events (`~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl`) show `permission.completed` → `tool.execution_complete` (success false) → `assistant.turn_end` → `subagent.completed`, with no model call after the denial.

<details><summary>acp_repro.py</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal ACP client: asks a Copilot CLI parent to launch one subagent, then inspects its events.

Usage: T3EMUL=1 acp_repro.py <label> <background|sync> <subagent-model|default> <effort|default> [extra copilot args...]
Every session/request_permission the CLI sends is approved (allow_once) and logged with whether a
session/prompt was in flight at the time.
"""
import json
import os
import shutil
import tempfile
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time

label, mode, model, effort, *extra = sys.argv[1:]
t3emul = os.environ.get("T3EMUL") == "1"  # fail permission requests after the parent turn, like T3 0.1.10
parent_done = threading.Event()
cwd = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=f"acp-repro-{label}-")
# Outside the cwd and outside the trusted temp dir, so reading it needs a permission.
target = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="acp-repro-outside-", dir=os.path.expanduser("~")), "target.txt")
open(target, "w").write("REPRO-FIRST-LINE 42\nsecond line\n")

proc = subprocess.Popen(
    ["copilot", "--acp", "--model", "claude-haiku-5.5", *extra],
    cwd=cwd, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True, bufsize=1)
lock = threading.Lock()
pending = {}
prompt_active = threading.Event()
perm_log = []
next_id = [0]


def send(obj):
    with lock:
        proc.stdin.write(json.dumps(obj) + "\n")
        proc.stdin.flush()


def call(method, params):
    next_id[0] += 1
    rid = next_id[0]
    ev = threading.Event()
    pending[rid] = [ev, None]
    send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": rid, "method": method, "params": params})
    return rid, ev


def reader():
    for line in proc.stdout:
        try:
            msg = json.loads(line)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if "method" in msg and "id" in msg:
            if msg["method"] == "session/request_permission":
                opts = msg["params"].get("options", [])
                allow = next((o for o in opts if o.get("kind", "").startswith("allow")), opts[0] if opts else None)
                title = (msg["params"].get("toolCall") or {}).get("title")
                perm_log.append((time.strftime("%H:%M:%S"), "after-parent-idle" if parent_done.is_set() else "parent-active", title))
                if t3emul and parent_done.is_set():
                    send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": msg["id"], "error": {"code": -32603, "message": "ACP agent requested input without an active turn"}})
                    continue
                send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": msg["id"], "result": {"outcome": {"outcome": "selected", "optionId": allow["optionId"]}}})
            else:
                send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": msg["id"], "error": {"code": -32601, "message": "not supported"}})
        elif msg.get("method") == "session/update":
            u = msg["params"].get("update", {})
            if u.get("sessionUpdate") == "agent_message_chunk" and "LAUNCHED" in json.dumps(u.get("content")):
                threading.Timer(1.0, parent_done.set).start()
        elif "id" in msg and msg["id"] in pending:
            pending[msg["id"]][1] = msg
            pending[msg["id"]][0].set()


threading.Thread(target=reader, daemon=True).start()


def wait(rid_ev, timeout=600):
    rid, ev = rid_ev
    ev.wait(timeout)
    return pending[rid][1]


wait(call("initialize", {"protocolVersion": 1, "clientCapabilities": {"fs": {"readTextFile": False, "writeTextFile": False}}}))
sid = wait(call("session/new", {"cwd": cwd, "mcpServers": []}))["result"]["sessionId"]

task_args = {"agent_type": "general-purpose", "name": f"repro-{label}", "description": "Repro read file",
             "prompt": f"First run the bash command `sleep 25`. Then use the view tool to read {target}, then use the bash tool to run `wc -c {target}`. Reply with the file's first line and the byte count."}
if model != "default":
    task_args["model"] = model
if effort != "default":
    task_args["reasoning_effort"] = effort
task_args["timeout"] = 0 if mode == "background" else -1
prompt = ("Call the task tool exactly once with exactly these JSON arguments, then end your turn with the single word LAUNCHED. "
          "Do not call read_agent or any other tool, and do not wait.\n" + json.dumps(task_args))

rid_ev = call("session/prompt", {"sessionId": sid, "prompt": [{"type": "text", "text": prompt}]})
if mode == "background":
    parent_done.wait(120)
    time.sleep(85)
else:
    wait(rid_ev)
print(f"[{label}] parent prompt finished {time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}; session {sid}")

events = [json.loads(l) for l in open(os.path.expanduser(f"~/.copilot/session-state/{sid}/events.jsonl"))]
sub = [e for e in events if e.get("agentId")]
first_turn = []
for e in sub:
    if e["type"] == "subagent.completed":
        break
    first_turn.append(e)
final = [e["data"].get("content", "") for e in first_turn if e["type"] == "assistant.message"]
decisions = [(e["data"]["result"]["kind"], e["data"].get("decisionSource")) for e in first_turn if e["type"] == "permission.completed"]
tools = [e["data"]["toolName"] for e in first_turn if e["type"] == "tool.execution_start"]
print(json.dumps({
    "label": label, "mode": mode, "model": model, "effort": effort, "extra": extra,
    "subagentTools": tools, "permissionDecisions": decisions, "clientPermissionRequests": perm_log,
    "firstTurnFinalMessage": (final[-1][:200] if final else None),
    "t3emul": t3emul, "completed": any(e["type"] == "subagent.completed" for e in sub),
}, indent=1))
proc.terminate()
shutil.rmtree(os.path.dirname(target), ignore_errors=True)
shutil.rmtree(cwd, ignore_errors=True)
```

</details>

### Expected behavior

- A failed or unavailable client response is classified like the `-p` fallback, not as an interactive user denial.
- The error goes back to the model and the turn continues, so the subagent can try another approach or report what it could not do.
- If the turn has to stop, `subagent.completed` and the `read_agent` result say why, so the parent does not get a silent empty turn.

### Additional context

- OS: Ubuntu on WSL2 (Windows 11)
- Client: T3 Code 0.1.10 (`acpRegistry` provider); also reproduced with the standalone client above.
- Workaround: start the CLI with `--allow-all` so no permission request reaches the client.

issues.title: A session started in an unselected iTerm2 tab keeps the plain look because a late color reply is dropped

labels.name: area:theming-accessibility
labels.description: Visual themes, colors, dark/light mode, contrast, screen readers, i18n/RTL

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

At startup, the CLI asks the terminal for its foreground, background, and palette colors and waits about 2 seconds. When the answer comes later, the CLI draws its plain look for the rest of the session: thin lines around the input box, a sidebar without its header buttons, and different colors. It ignores the late answer and doesn't ask again.

iTerm2 answers late whenever the CLI starts in a tab that isn't selected. It sends replies for a tab that isn't on screen in batches once a second, so the colors arrive about 2 seconds after the CLI asks. Recordings of the terminal traffic showed the answer 1.997 to 2.000 seconds after the question, so each start wins or loses by a few milliseconds.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.114 (also seen on 1.0.111 through 1.0.113)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. In iTerm2 3.7.2, open a new tab and run `sleep 5; copilot --session-id $(uuidgen | tr A-Z a-z)`.
2. Within 5 seconds, switch back to the previous tab, so the new tab isn't selected when the CLI starts.
3. After about 15 seconds, switch to the new tab.

The session shows the plain look, and its log in `~/.copilot/logs` has `queryTerminalColors: failed to assemble colors (bg=failed, fg=failed)`. With `--session-id` the CLI missed the answer on every start; without it, the miss is intermittent.

### Expected behavior

The session gets its normal look once the terminal's colors arrive, even after 2 seconds. For example, the CLI could apply a late reply, or ask again when the tab first gets focus.

### Additional context

- macOS 27.2.1 on Apple silicon, iTerm2 3.7.2.
- With `--session-id`, 5 of 5 starts in an unselected tab missed the colors on 1.0.114. Without it, 3 of 24 missed them on 1.0.111, and 4 sessions missed them this morning in normal use.
- A CLI started in the selected tab got its answer in about 65 ms.
- Running `/settings theme github` and then `/settings theme default` in an affected session fixes it, even while its tab is still unselected. The log then shows `queryTerminalColors: detected ... ansi=16/16`, and the normal look returns.
- Starting with `"theme": "github"` doesn't avoid it. That session also showed the plain look and logged the same failure.

issues.title: Organization-managed models show no reasoning-effort controls or context capacity in /model

labels.name: area:enterprise
labels.description: GitHub Enterprise (GHE/GHES) support, org policies, and enterprise settings

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
## Summary

With a GPT model configured through **GitHub’s organization-level custom-model settings**, Copilot CLI can select and use the model, but the `/model` picker shows `—` for both **Context** and **Reasoning** and does not offer reasoning-effort choices.

This concerns organization-managed models served through Copilot, **not locally configured BYOK providers**.

## Environment

- Copilot CLI **1.0.114**
- macOS arm64
- Organization-managed GPT model using the **Responses API**, with Thinking enabled in the organization configuration
- Fresh isolated CLI profile, without local model-capability overrides

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a GPT model in GitHub’s organization-level Copilot custom-model settings, using Responses API.
2. Start an interactive CLI session and select that model through `/model`.
3. Observe the Context and Reasoning columns, and try Right/Tab to adjust the available settings.
4. Submit a simple prompt, then run `/context`.
5. Compare with the corresponding GitHub-hosted model in the picker.

## Actual behavior

- The organization-managed model selects successfully and answers normally.
- Its picker row shows `—` for Context and Reasoning; Right/Tab does not expose the corresponding controls.
- The model catalog contains the configured token limits, and `/context` shows the available capacity correctly.
- Starting a fresh process with `--reasoning-effort low` or `high` is accepted, with the selected effort confirmed in request diagnostics and usage records.
- The corresponding GitHub-hosted model exposes working reasoning-effort and context controls in the picker.

## Expected behavior

- Display the organization-managed model’s configured context capacity.
- Offer its supported reasoning-effort choices and apply the selected value.
- If a setting is unavailable, explain why rather than showing an unexplained dash.

This does not require offering multiple context tiers for a model with a fixed capacity; that fixed capacity should still be visible.

## Related

- #4960 — Enterprise-managed model-selection failure, marked fixed in 1.0.95. Selection works in this reproduction; the missing capability display and effort controls remain on 1.0.114.
- #4953 — Also reports missing Context/Reasoning information, but primarily concerns encoded-ID selection. This reproduction does not require an embedded slash in the provider-side model name.

The exact responsibility between catalog capability metadata and CLI picker handling is not yet established.

issues.title: Linux/WSL: Entra MCP browser sign-in stalls silently when `xdg-open` is missing, and `/mcp` Authenticate shows a URL that fails with "State mismatch"

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

This issue was split out of #4017 at a maintainer's request. It isn't #5250 either: there's no OS broker here, and the CLI logs `Entra broker not eligible; using the browser OAuth flow {"broker_available":false}`.

I retested on **CLI 1.0.114** on WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 with an Entra-protected remote HTTP MCP server (the Azure DevOps remote MCP, `https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>`) and no stored token. The browser flow itself now works. When a browser opens, Entra SSO completes, the loopback callback reaches the CLI, and the CLI logs `MCP OAuth tokens saved`. The token falls back to file storage under `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/` because there's no Secret Service, and a restart reuses it. Device code (Ctrl+G) now shows a code. Each flow uses a per-flow random loopback port, so the "fixed callback port" I described in #4017 doesn't apply on 1.0.114.

Two problems remain, plus one on the app side.

**1. When `xdg-open` is missing, sign-in stalls with no URL and no visible error**

A stock WSL Ubuntu install has no `xdg-utils`, though `wslview` is installed. The launch fails, and the failure is logged only at DEBUG:

```
[DEBUG] [rust:mcp_client::oauth_flow] Entra broker not eligible; using the browser OAuth flow {"server_url":"https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>","broker_available":false,"force_device_code":false}
[ERROR] Opening browser for ado-direct authentication...
[DEBUG] [rust:mcp_client::oauth_flow] failed to open OAuth browser {"error":"Spawn { command: \"xdg-open\", source: Os { code: 13, kind: PermissionDenied, message: \"Permission denied\" } }"}
[ERROR] Requesting access token for ado-direct...
```

The `PermissionDenied` error is misleading because no `xdg-open` exists on `PATH`. I suspect `execvp` returns EACCES from a Windows-interop `PATH` entry. The CLI doesn't print the authorize URL or fall back to `$BROWSER` or `wslview`. The user sees only:

```
! MCP server 'ado-direct' is taking longer than expected to connect.
! Gave up waiting for MCP server to finish starting: ado-direct. Startup continued without it; it may still connect.
```

After that, the CLI contacts `login.microsoftonline.com` about every 6 s indefinitely, and the server stays `pending`.

**2. `/mcp` → server → Authenticate shows a URL whose callback is rejected**

While the startup flow is pending, choosing **Authenticate** shows:

```
A browser authorization is already in progress for this server. Open the URL below to complete it.
If your browser didn't open, copy this URL manually: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/v2.0/authorize?...
```

The displayed URL is identical to the startup flow's URL, including `state` and `nonce`. But the action also starts a new flow: `session.mcp.oauth.prepareFlow` runs again. When I complete the displayed URL in the browser, Entra and the `vscode.dev/redirect` hop succeed, and the loopback callback reaches the CLI. The CLI then rejects it:

- With a working browser opener: the callback page shows **"Authorization Failed — State mismatch - possible CSRF attack"**.
- After the `xdg-open` failure in (1): the callback returns **HTTP 404 Not Found**. Replaying the same callback URL from inside WSL with `curl` also returns 404, which rules out WSL localhost forwarding. Nothing is logged.

If I skip Authenticate and open the startup URL directly, sign-in succeeds, even about 70 s after startup "gave up waiting". So the only URL the UI ever shows is one that can't complete. Without a working `xdg-open`, the user has no way to sign in from the UI. That matches my original #4017 symptom: the browser reports success, but no token is stored.

**3. App sessions on a WSL host have no sign-in path**

In GitHub Copilot app 1.4.2 (Windows) with sessions on a WSL host, the host was still running bundled CLI **1.0.104-0** (`copilotd` 1.0.5) and didn't update to 1.0.114. A new session lists the server's tool names, which may come from the tool snapshot cache. Every call fails:

```
MCP server 'ado-direct': MCP server "ado-direct" requires authentication. Sign in through your MCP client's authentication settings.
```

No browser opens on Windows, and I found no sign-in action for the server in the app. The Windows app log shows only `session/mcpServerStateChanged` actions with `translated_event_count=0` and no auth-related action. If this is already fixed in a newer host, please say which `copilotd` or CLI version to wait for.

### Expected behavior

- If launching the browser fails, show the authorize URL in the session immediately, log the failure at WARNING, and fall back to `$BROWSER` or `wslview` on WSL.
- When Authenticate runs while a flow is pending, either keep the pending flow's `state`/`nonce` valid or display the new flow's URL. Never show a URL the callback will reject.
- App sessions on Linux/WSL remote hosts should surface MCP OAuth-required in the app with a Sign in action that completes the flow. Opening the Windows browser works: WSL localhost forwarding delivers the callback to the host process.

### Affected version

- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.114 (linux-x64 release tarball, `--no-auto-update`)
- GitHub Copilot app 1.4.2 (Windows), with its WSL host serving sessions using bundled CLI 1.0.104-0

### Environment

- Windows 11 + WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel 6.18 (microsoft-standard-WSL2)
- No `xdg-open` (`xdg-utils` not installed); `wslview` present; `BROWSER` unset
- No Secret Service (`org.freedesktop.secrets`), so MCP tokens fall back to `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/`
- Server: Azure DevOps remote MCP, `type: http`, no `oauthClientId`

### Steps to reproduce

1. On WSL Ubuntu without `xdg-utils`, with no stored MCP token, run:
   `copilot --log-level debug --additional-mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{"ado-direct":{"type":"http","url":"https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>","tools":["*"]}}}'`
2. Observe "taking longer than expected" and no URL. The log shows the `xdg-open` spawn failure.
3. Open `/mcp` → `ado-direct` → **Authenticate**. Copy the displayed URL into a Windows browser and complete sign-in.
4. The callback returns 404 (or "State mismatch" if an opener exists), and the server stays unauthenticated.
5. Control: put an `xdg-open` shim on `PATH` that hands the URL to the Windows browser, and restart without clicking Authenticate. Sign-in completes and the server connects.

**Workaround:** install `xdg-utils`, or put an `xdg-open` shim on `PATH` that calls `wslview`, and don't click Authenticate while the startup flow is pending. That fixes the standalone CLI only. For app sessions on a WSL host, I still use a local stdio proxy that adds a bearer token from `az account get-access-token`.


(These details we created using GHCP attempting to repro another bug/fix.)

issues.title: Background sub-agent `agent_idle` notification is held for 60 s while another background task runs, even when the main agent is idle

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Setup: the main agent starts sub-agents with the `task` tool and `mode: "background"`, often several at the same time. It then ends its turn and waits for each sub-agent's `agent_idle` notification before it calls `read_agent` for the result.

When a background sub-agent finishes while another background task is still running, the CLI holds its `agent_idle` notification. It releases the notification after 60 s, or when the last other background task finishes, whichever comes first. If no other background task is running, the notification arrives at once.

The CLI holds the notification even when the main agent is idle and has ended its turn to wait for the result. The result is ready, but nothing happens for a minute.

My main agent coordinates several child sessions. It runs code reviews in background sub-agents, often several at the same time. In 13 of these sessions, 98 of 239 background results reached the main agent 55 to 65 s after the sub-agent finished. Each 60 s hold happened while another background sub-agent was running. The holds added about 3 to 7 minutes of idle time per session. Often a child session also waited for the result, for example for a go-ahead to merge its PR. I also ran the same jobs as child sessions, which report by message. That setup had no gap and finished noticeably faster.

`read_agent` with `wait: true` isn't affected. It returns the result within 0.05 s.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.106. Session logs from 1.0.99-2 and 1.0.102-0 show the same delay.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. In an empty folder, run:

   ```bash
   copilot -p 'Make exactly two task tool calls in one response, both with agent_type "task", model "claude-haiku-4.5" and mode "background": one named "slow" with the prompt "Run the shell command: sleep 150; date (use initial_wait 200). Reply with its output only.", and one named "quick" with the prompt "Run the shell command date and reply with its output only.". Then end your turn immediately. Do not call read_agent for "quick" until you receive a notification that it is idle. After that notification, call read_agent once for "quick", then wait for "slow" with read_agent wait: true and timeout 300, and reply DONE.' \
     --model claude-haiku-4.5 --allow-all-tools --log-level all --log-dir ./logs
   ```

2. In the session's `events.jsonl`, compare the `subagent.completed` time for "quick" with the time of its `system.notification` (`kind.type == "agent_idle"`):

   ```
   12:01:25.669Z subagent.completed   quick
   12:02:25.743Z system.notification  quick   (60.07 s later)
   12:03:56.833Z subagent.completed   slow
   ```

   In 4 runs, the gap was 60.057, 60.072, 60.077 and 60.085 s. Sometimes the model calls `read_agent` early, even though the prompt tells it not to. Skip those runs.

3. To compare, change the prompt so that the main agent calls `read_agent` for "quick" with `wait: true` at once. The result arrives 0.007 to 0.05 s after "quick" finishes, in 5 of 5 runs.

The debug log shows the decision to hold the notification when "quick" finishes. After that, the log shows only telemetry until the CLI releases the notification:

```
12:01:25.670Z [DEBUG] [rust:native_notification_delivery::implementation] Notification settlement inspected an empty executable queue {"active_immediate_completion":false,"queue_resume_requested":false,"idle_deferred":true,"has_running":true,"has_batch":true}
12:02:25.673Z [INFO] [rust:native_notification_delivery::implementation] Agent "quick" (task) has finished processing and is now idle.
```

### Expected behavior

When the main agent is idle, the CLI should deliver a finished background sub-agent's notification at once. The main agent can then act on the result.

I understand the reason for batching. But when the main agent is idle, the hold only adds delay. Any of these changes would fix the problem for me:

- Deliver the notification at once when the main agent is idle. Keep batching only while a turn is in progress.
- Hold notifications for a much shorter time, such as a few seconds, to group sub-agents that finish at almost the same time.
- Make the hold time a setting.

Today the only workaround is to make the main agent wait in `read_agent` with `wait: true`. But while it waits, it doesn't see messages from its child sessions or other notifications.

### Additional context

- OS: macOS (darwin-arm64)
- I ran the repro headless with `copilot -p`. The same delay happens in interactive sessions that the GitHub Copilot app hosts.
- I couldn't find an environment variable or setting for the 60 s hold.
- I can share the debug logs from the repro on request.

issues.title: macOS sandbox prevents backend integration tests from connecting to servers started by the tests themselves

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Allow TCP connections within the sandbox

### Proposed solution

## Summary

The macOS sandbox’s host-filtering restrictions prevent a common backend testing pattern: _start a local server, connect a test client to it, and verify its response._

Direct localhost TCP connections are blocked even when:

• The server was started by the sandboxed command itself.
• Both server and client run inside the same process.
• The server binds only to `127.0.0.1`, using an OS-assigned free port.
• `allowLocalNetwork` and `allowOutbound` are enabled, and `127.0.0.1` is allowlisted.

This is a general backend-development limitation, not specifically a Java or Gradle problem. It affects tests that exercise real client/server communication, including local API servers, protocol implementations, and service fixtures.

## Environment

• Copilot CLI: 1.0.114
• macOS: 26.7.3, ARM64
• Command sandbox enabled with host filtering

## Relevant configuration

```json
{
  "sandbox": {
    "enabled": true,
    "userPolicy": {
      "network": {
        "allowOutbound": true,
        "allowLocalNetwork": true,
        "allowedHosts": ["127.0.0.1"],
        "blockedHosts": []
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Minimal reproduction

The essential behavior can be demonstrated without a build tool, test framework, external dependency, or internet connection:

```python
python3 - <<'PY'
import socket

with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as server:
    server.settimeout(3)
    server.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    server.listen(1)
    address = server.getsockname()
    print(f"Listening on {address}", flush=True)

    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as client:
        client.settimeout(3)
        client.connect(address)

        connection, _ = server.accept()
        with connection:
            connection.sendall(b"Hello World")

        with client.makefile("rb") as response:
            assert response.read() == b"Hello World"

print("Client/server test passed")
PY
```

The server and client intentionally run in one process. The listening socket’s backlog allows `connect()` to complete before `accept()` is called.

### Expected behavior

There should be a supported way for sandboxed tests to connect to local servers they start, without disabling the entire sandbox or abandoning remote host filtering.

This need not mean granting unrestricted access to every service on the host. A scoped permission, isolated loopback environment, or explicit opt-in with documented trade-offs would address the testing requirement.

### Actual behavior

Binding and listening succeed, but the client’s direct connection is rejected:

```
PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted
```

A standalone IPv4 socket probe confirmed this bind/listen-versus-connect distinction.

Allowlisting `127.0.0.1` does not permit the direct connection when host filtering is active. Proxy-mediated access is not equivalent: ordinary socket clients and many test frameworks do not route their local TCP communication through an HTTP proxy.

## Impact and requested capability

Running backend integration tests is a routine part of implementing and validating changes. Currently, this restriction can force developers to disable sandboxing for precisely the commands that execute application code and its dependencies.

Please provide a supported way to run local client/server integration tests while retaining sandbox protection and remote host filtering.

Related discussion: #5390. This request concerns the broader testing capability, rather than only Gradle daemon startup.

### Example prompts or workflows

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.title: /model shows no reasoning effort for providers.json (BYOK) models

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A model defined in `providers.json` never gets reasoning effort levels, so `/model` shows `—` in the Reasoning column and the effort can't be changed there. This happens even when the model declares `capabilities.supports.reasoningEffort: true` and the provider honours every level.

The effort itself works: requests go out with `output_config.effort: "medium"`, and `--reasoning-effort low|high|xhigh|max` changes it. What's missing is the list of levels on the resolved model. Two things follow from that:

- `/model` has nothing to offer.
- `effortLevel` in `settings.json` is ignored for these models, which matches the help text saying it applies only to "models that support it".

From the SDK types (`@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.34), the picker reads `Model.supportedReasoningEfforts` and `Model.defaultReasoningEffort`. `ProviderModelConfig` has no equivalent field. A BYOK model can only set the boolean `capabilities.supports.reasoningEffort`, and the runtime doesn't turn that into a list. `metadata.supportedReasoningEfforts` isn't used either.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.113 (also seen on 1.0.112), macOS arm64.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Create `~/.copilot/providers.json` pointing at any Anthropic-compatible endpoint that serves a reasoning model:

   ```json
   {
     "providers": [
       { "name": "gw", "type": "anthropic", "baseUrl": "https://gateway.example.com", "apiKey": "…" }
     ],
     "models": [
       {
         "id": "claude-sonnet-5-5",
         "provider": "gw",
         "modelId": "claude-sonnet-5.5",
         "maxPromptTokens": 1000000,
         "maxContextWindowTokens": 1000000,
         "maxOutputTokens": 128000,
         "capabilities": { "supports": { "reasoningEffort": true, "toolCalls": true } },
         "metadata": {
           "supportedReasoningEfforts": ["low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"],
           "defaultReasoningEffort": "medium"
         }
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

2. Run `copilot`, then `/model`. The model shows its 1M context, so the file is read, but Reasoning shows `—`. Built-in models in the same list show `← Medium →`.
3. Over the SDK, `session.model.list` returns the model with `capabilities.limits.max_context_window_tokens: 1000000`, but no `supportedReasoningEfforts`, no `defaultReasoningEffort`, and no `capabilities.supports.reasoningEffort`. `providers.config.read` shows all of those fields were saved.
4. Set `"effortLevel": "high"` in `settings.json` and send a prompt. The provider still receives `output_config.effort: "medium"`.
5. Run `copilot --model gw/claude-sonnet-5-5 --reasoning-effort high -p "hi"`. The provider receives `"effort": "high"`, so the runtime can send it.

### Expected behavior

A BYOK model that supports reasoning effort should be able to declare its levels, and `/model` and `effortLevel` should use them. That could be:

- `supportedReasoningEfforts` and `defaultReasoningEffort` on `ProviderModelConfig`, mirroring `Model`, or
- inheriting the levels from the `modelId` catalogue entry when `capabilities.supports.reasoningEffort` is true.

### Additional context

- `modelId` appears not to bring over the catalogue model's capabilities or limits for `providers.json` models. With `modelId: "claude-sonnet-5.5"` and no explicit limits, `/model` shows 128K, not the catalogue's figure. The docs say `modelId` lets the CLI "use that model's capabilities and limits".
- The SDK types describe BYOK reasoning efforts as possible ("BYOK providers can define additional levels"), but no field exists to define them.
- Related to #2725, which is about the picker filtering levels for a built-in model. This one is about a custom model getting none.

issues.title: ACP: zero-turn sessions (empty or slash-command-only) never persist events.jsonl and fail session/load with -32002 after client restart

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

issues.body:
## Summary

When Copilot CLI is used as an ACP external agent in Zed, sessions sometimes never get their `events.jsonl` written to `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/`. After restarting Zed, reopening such a thread fails with:

```
ACP request failed {"method":"session/load","error":"Resource not found: Session <id> not found (-32002)"}
```

This happened 3 times in a row this morning. The session directories exist (with `workspace.yaml`, `checkpoints/`, `files/`, `research/`), but `events.jsonl` is missing, so there is nothing to resume.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 27.2.1 (arm64, Apple Silicon)
- Zed: 1.28.1 (Copilot installed from the ACP external agents registry, id `github-copilot-cli`)
- Copilot CLI: npm package `@github/copilot@1.0.113`; the bundled `@github/copilot-darwin-arm64` binary reports `1.0.114` via `--version` (verified this is also what a clean `npm install @github/copilot@1.0.113` ships, so the version display mismatch appears to be in the published package itself)
- Install location used by Zed: `~/Library/Application Support/Zed/external_agents/registry/npx/github-copilot-cli/`

## Timeline & evidence

Three consecutive sessions created between 09:35 and 10:00 local time today all ended up without `events.jsonl`:

| session | events.jsonl |
|---|---|
| `3dc0a34a-4ff3-473c-8005-2506f70cc5ec` | missing |
| `53bcd828-71f1-4bf2-819d-bec37345122e` | missing |
| `5735b891-2fde-4ef1-aa15-5bf85c2393aa` | missing |

Sessions created before (e.g. 11-08, 11-12) and after (10:11, 10:14) the incident window have non-empty `events.jsonl` and load fine.

At creation time of each broken session, the CLI log (`~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`) shows:

```
[WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::api_session_options_update] Failed to reload managed hooks after enabling managed settings {"error":"no hook session for session id <id>"}
[WARNING] [rust:events_engine::host_delivery] event was not delivered to its registered session host {"error":"GenericFailure, no session host is registered for session <id>"}
```

and on the next Zed start:

```
[ERROR] [rust:acp::connection] ACP request failed {"method":"session/load","error":"Resource not found: Session <id> not found (-32002)"}
```

During the incident window the CLI process was restarted frequently (6+ PIDs within ~25 minutes) because Zed was restarted repeatedly.

## What I verified

1. **Zed is not at fault for the load failure.** Spawning the exact binary Zed uses with `--acp` and sending `initialize` + `session/load` for one of the broken session IDs reproduces `-32002` outside of Zed.
2. **The same binary works correctly standalone.** A full ACP cycle (initialize → session/new → session/prompt → kill process → relaunch → session/load) succeeds: `events.jsonl` is written and the session reloads.
3. **Not a version mismatch on my machine.** A clean `npm install @github/copilot@1.0.113` ships a binary that also reports `1.0.114`.

So the bug seems to be that under some conditions (possibly rapid ACP client restarts / session host re-registration, per the `no session host is registered` warnings) the CLI creates the session directory but never persists `events.jsonl`, and the session becomes permanently unrecoverable.

## Expected behavior

- Sessions created via ACP are persisted reliably, or
- If persistence fails, session creation should fail loudly instead of leaving a broken shell directory, and/or `session/load` should handle a directory-without-events more gracefully.

## Workaround

Running `copilot` directly in the terminal has not shown this problem; only the ACP path through Zed is affected.

type.name: Feature

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

I maintain [prismantis](https://github.com/NahumLitvin/prismantis), a reply renderer for Claude Code that also ships for OpenCode and Codex. It draws some fenced blocks as colored terminal pictures: mermaid xychart and pie charts, quadrant grids, mind maps, kanban boards, and a ```figure block for hand-drawn text diagrams.

A Copilot CLI plugin covers most of a port: a `sessionStart` hook or rules file for the note, a command for `/prismantis`. But the transcript renderer has no hook. An extension can add tools, commands and a canvas, not change how a block in a reply draws, so a chart block shows as source. Mermaid has no renderer at all in the CLI.

### Proposed solution

Let an extension or plugin register a renderer for a fenced block language. The CLI passes it the block text, the width and the theme colors, and it returns styled lines (ANSI is fine), drawn in place of the default code block. Returning nothing keeps the default.

OpenCode ships this as [`registerCodeBlockRenderer`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/7828491cc9d8e482eda4f7ca7bb2287fdbecca00/packages/plugin/src/tui/context.ts#L555), and prismantis draws its charts there through it.

### Example prompts or workflows

"Chart replies per hour for east and west" gets an xychart block back. With a registered renderer it draws as a two-line chart in the transcript instead of eight lines of mermaid source.

### Additional context

Related to custom themes (#1504): a renderer would take its colors from the active theme. Happy to test against the prismantis renderers.

issues.title: Startup reports disabled MCP servers as “blocked by policy” and repeats the warnings

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Description

Copilot CLI displays organization-policy warnings at startup even though every configured third-party MCP server is explicitly disabled through `disabledMcpServers` in the user settings. The same pair of warnings appears twice during startup.

### Environment

- Copilot CLI: **1.0.101**
- OS: **Windows**
- Shell: **PowerShell**
- MCP configuration includes user-configured and plugin-provided servers.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have third-party MCP servers configured.
2. Disable all of them through the CLI, persisting their names in `disabledMcpServers`.
3. Start a new interactive CLI session with an account for which the CLI reports that third-party MCP servers are disallowed by organization policy.
4. Observe the startup warnings.

### Actual behavior

Startup displays:

```text
Third-party MCP servers are disabled by your organization's Copilot policy. Only built-in servers are available.

9 MCP servers were blocked by policy: ...
```

Both messages appear twice in the observed startup. Every server named in the warning is already explicitly disabled in the user settings.

### Expected behavior

- Already-disabled servers should not be counted as servers blocked by policy at startup.
- An unchanged policy notice should not be repeated during startup refreshes.
- If a general policy notice is intentional, it should be clearly informational and distinguish organization restrictions from user-disabled servers.

### Investigation notes

Read-only inspection of the locally installed **1.0.101** bundle found:

- In `cli-main.js`, `reloadMcpServersExclusive()` passes the configured server map to the policy filter without disabled-server settings. Disable settings are handed to the native lifecycle afterward.
- The interactive initialization path emits the general policy warning based on policy allowance, without checking whether any third-party servers are enabled.
- The general and filtered-server warnings have no deduplication at these emission points, allowing repeated initialization/reload calls to emit them again.

These observations explain the reporting behavior; **they do not establish that disabled servers are launched**. The exact trigger for the second initialization/reload has not been identified.

### Related issues

- github/copilot-cli#2567 - incorrect startup "blocked by policy" reporting in a different configuration scenario.
- github/copilot-cli#4907 - repeated MCP lifecycle notifications.

issues.title: Background Agent MCP Connections Destroyed After Text-Only Turn

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

MCP tools in background agents (launched via the `task` tool) are unreliable. The CLI framework destroys MCP transport connections after any turn where the LLM produces a text-only response (no tool calls). This means background agents that depend on MCP tools intermittently fail with `"Not connected"` or `"Connection closed"` errors - even when the MCP server is healthy and reachable.

This is a blocking issue for using custom agents with MCP servers in background mode. Any non-trivial agent workflow that involves MCP tools will eventually hit this bug because the LLM occasionally produces a text-only response before making a tool call (~10% of the time with default prompts, 100% when the system prompt encourages reasoning before acting).

The bug does not affect standalone agent invocations (`copilot --agent <agent> -p <prompt>`) or the parent session's own MCP connections - only background agents.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.35

### Steps to reproduce the behavior


### Prerequisites

- Python 3.10+ with `aiohttp` (`pip install aiohttp`)

### 1. Add the attached server

```py
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("repro-mcp-server", port=8099)

@mcp.tool()
def fast_tool(query: str) -> str:
    """Returns immediately. Echoes the query back. For testing MCP transport reliability."""
    return f'{{"status": "ok", "query": "{query}"}}'

if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run(transport="sse")
```

Save to `~/.copilot/repro_mcp_server.py`

This is a minimal MCP SSE server that exposes a single `fast_tool` which immediately echoes back its input. 

### 2. Create the agent definition

Save as `~/.copilot/agents/repro-test-agent.agent.md`:

```markdown
---
name: repro-test-agent
description: "Minimal agent for reproducing background-agent MCP bug."
mcp-servers:
  repro:
    type: sse
    url: "http://localhost:8099/sse"
    tools: ["*"]
tools: ['repro/*']
---

You are a test agent with a STRICT protocol. You MUST follow this exact sequence
for EVERY request:

Turn 1: Reply with ONLY this exact text: "Processing request." — absolutely NO
tool calls on this turn.
Turn 2: Now call the requested tool.

CRITICAL RULE: You are FORBIDDEN from calling any tool on your first turn. Your
first message MUST be pure text with zero tool calls.
```

The system prompt forces a text-only first turn. This simulates the natural LLM behaviour of reasoning before acting, which triggers the bug deterministically.

When run, the background agent produces "Processing request." on turn 1, calls `repro-fast_tool` on turn 2, and returns `{"status": "ok", "query": "test-bug"}`.


### Expected behavior

I expect that MCP tool calling is reliable for any background agent session.

### What actually happens

The agent produces text on turn 1. The framework fires internal `response` and `messages_snapshot` events which tear down the MCP transport. The agent either never gets a turn 2, or turn 2's tool call fails on a dead connection.

Debug log signature (`~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`):

```
[DEBUG] response (Request-ID null):
[DEBUG] Ignoring event of kind: response
[DEBUG] Ignoring event of kind: messages_snapshot
[ERROR] MCP transport for repro closed
[ERROR] MCP client for repro closed
```

**Repro rate: 3/3 (100%)** with the included agent definition.

### Intermittent variant without special system prompt

The "text first" system prompt makes the bug deterministic, but it also occurs naturally. With a neutral system prompt ("call the tool and report the result"), the LLM occasionally produces text before a tool call. In testing:

- 2 failures out of ~20 background agent invocations with neutral prompts (~10%)

### Non-background agents are not affected

- `copilot --agent <agent> -p <prompt>` (standalone mode): MCP survives across turns. 0/15 failures.
- Parent session MCP tools: text-only turns do not destroy connections.
- The bug is specific to background agents spawned via the `task` tool.


### Additional context


### CLI log: standalone agent (works — MCP survives)

```
copilot --agent repro-test-agent -p 'Call repro-fast_tool with query "standalone-test".' --allow-all-tools
```

```
09:24:25.374 [ERROR] Starting remote MCP client for repro with url: http://localhost:8099/sse
09:24:25.402 [ERROR] MCP client for repro connected, took 27ms
09:24:25.533 [DEBUG] Adding tool: repro-fast_tool
09:24:27.996 [DEBUG] Making Anthropic Messages streaming request with messages: [
09:24:32.836 [DEBUG] response (Request-ID null):        ← LLM response arrives
09:24:40.914 [DEBUG] Tool calls count: 2                ← includes tool_use
09:24:40.915 [DEBUG] Permission request (kind=mcp)      ← tool executes
09:24:40.971 [DEBUG] Tool invocation result: {"result":"{\"status\": \"ok\", \"query\": \"standalone-test\"}"}
09:24:40.997 [DEBUG] Making Anthropic Messages streaming request  ← turn 2 (report result)
09:24:43.433 [DEBUG] response (Request-ID null):
09:24:43.434 [DEBUG] Ignoring event of kind: response             ← event fires...
09:24:43.434 [DEBUG] Ignoring event of kind: messages_snapshot
                                                                   ← but NO MCP teardown
```

### CLI log: background agent (fails — MCP destroyed)

```
copilot -p '...launch background agent...' --allow-all-tools
```

```
09:19:17.426 [INFO]  Started background agent with id: bug-repro
09:19:17.486 [INFO]  Custom agent "repro-test-agent" invoked
09:19:17.545 [ERROR] Starting remote MCP client for repro with url: http://localhost:8099/sse
09:19:17.573 [ERROR] MCP client for repro connected, took 27ms
09:19:17.664 [DEBUG] Adding tool: repro-fast_tool
09:19:17.666 [INFO]  Found 1 MCP tools from server 'repro'
09:19:17.671 [INFO]  Custom agent "repro-test-agent" using tools: repro-fast_tool, view
09:19:18.074 [DEBUG] Making Anthropic Messages streaming request  ← child agent turn 1
09:19:20.632 [DEBUG] response (Request-ID null):        ← text-only "Processing request."
                                                         (no "Tool calls count" line)
09:19:20.715 [INFO]  System notification: Agent "bug-repro" has finished processing
                                                         ← agent treated as DONE after text-only turn
...
09:19:54.619 [DEBUG] response (Request-ID null):
09:19:54.621 [DEBUG] Ignoring event of kind: response             ← same event as standalone...
09:19:54.623 [DEBUG] Ignoring event of kind: messages_snapshot
09:19:54.629 [ERROR] MCP transport for repro closed               ← ...but HERE it kills MCP
09:19:54.629 [ERROR] MCP client for repro closed
```

Note: both modes fire `Ignoring event of kind: response`, but only the background agent path destroys the MCP transport afterward.
