issues.title: Stdio MCP server fails to connect when `server/discover` times out: legacy `initialize` fallback on the same connection is rejected with -32022

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Summary

When a stdio MCP server takes longer than ~10 s to start, Copilot CLI gives up waiting for its `server/discover` probe and sends a legacy `initialize` **on the same stdio connection**. A server built on the MCP Python SDK 2.3.0 then processes the queued `server/discover` first, locks the connection to the 2026-07-28 protocol, and rejects the `initialize` with `-32022`. Copilot CLI reports the server as failed and does not retry, even though both sides support 2026-07-28.

In the same situation, Claude Code (2.1.308) and the MCP Python SDK client re-probe with `server/discover` and connect successfully.

## Environment

- Copilot CLI 1.0.103 (linux-x64)
- MCP server: any stdio server on `mcp` (Python SDK) 2.3.0 with a slow cold start. Observed with `analytics-mcp` 0.8.0 (Google Analytics MCP server) and `serena-agent` 2.1.0.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Save this as `slow_server.py`:

   ```python
   # /// script
   # dependencies = ["mcp==2.3.0"]
   # ///
   import time

   time.sleep(12)  # simulate a slow cold start

   from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer

   server = MCPServer("slow-start-repro")


   @server.tool()
   def ping() -> str:
       return "pong"


   server.run("stdio")
   ```

2. Run `uv run --script slow_server.py < /dev/null` once so the dependencies are cached.
3. Start Copilot CLI with the server:

   ```sh
   copilot -p "List the tools of the slowrepro MCP server. Do not call them." \
     --additional-mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{"slowrepro":{"type":"local","command":"uv","args":["run","-q","--script","/path/to/slow_server.py"],"tools":["*"]}}}'
   ```

## Actual behavior

The server is not connected. The log shows:

```
[WARNING] [rust:rt_mcp_connection] MCP server connection failed {"server_name":"...","raw_error":"failed to initialize MCP client: JSON-RPC error: -32022: connection is serving the 2026-07-28 protocol; the initialize handshake is not accepted({\"supported\":[\"2026-07-28\"],\"requested\":\"2025-11-25\"})"}
```

Frames captured between Copilot CLI and the server (seconds since spawn):

```
 0.007 C->S {"id":0,"method":"server/discover","params":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion":"2026-07-28",...}}}
 9.797 C->S {"id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25",...}}
13.813 S->C {"id":0,"result":{"supportedVersions":["2026-07-28"],...}}
13.814 S->C {"id":1,"error":{"code":-32022,"message":"connection is serving the 2026-07-28 protocol; the initialize handshake is not accepted","data":{"supported":["2026-07-28"],"requested":"2025-11-25"}}}
```

Servers that normally start within 5 s also hit this right after the machine boots (cold disk cache, many processes starting at once). In that case, `/mcp reload` or restarting Copilot CLI connects them.

## Expected behavior

The connection succeeds over 2026-07-28, as it does when the server starts within the timeout. Any of these would work:

- When the fallback `initialize` gets `-32022` and `data.supported` contains a version the client supports, re-probe with `server/discover` at that version. The MCP Python SDK client does this (`mcp/client/_probe.py`: "The fallback handshake itself can be answered with -32022 … That code is itself positive modern evidence … so it triggers one re-probe at a mutual version instead of failing the connect."), and so does Claude Code.
- Accept a late `server/discover` response that arrives after the fallback was sent.
- For stdio, restart the server process before falling back, so the fallback does not share a connection with the unanswered probe.

## Workaround

Make the server start faster than the probe timeout. In our case the venv is read-only at runtime, so `.pyc` files were never written. Installing the server with `uv tool install --compile-bytecode` brought startup down to ~3.5 s, and Copilot CLI then connected over 2026-07-28. This still fails occasionally right after the machine boots, as described above.

issues.title: Extensions don't start for sessions created with `create_session` until the user switches to them

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A session created with the session management tool `create_session` starts with no extension processes. Its model has none of the extensions' tools, none of the skills extensions register, and no extension hooks. Extensions start only when the user first switches to that session in the Sessions sidebar or with `/resume`, or when `/restart` restores it. Sessions the user starts directly, and prompt mode (`copilot -p`), load extensions within a second or two.

A created session is meant to work without the user watching, so it can spend minutes on its task without the tools it was asked to use.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.108-1 (also seen in 1.0.105, 1.0.106, and 1.0.107)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Turn on session management tools (`sessionManagementTools` in `~/.copilot/settings.json`).
2. Add a user extension, for example `~/.copilot/extensions/probe/extension.mjs`, that calls `joinSession({ tools: [{ name: "probe_ping", ... }] })`.
3. In session A, ask the agent to call `create_session` with the prompt "Search your tools for probe_ping and say whether it exists." Stay in session A.
4. Session B reports that `probe_ping` doesn't exist. The process log has no extension launch for B's session ID, and B's `events.jsonl` has no extension events.
5. Switch to B in the sidebar. The log shows `Registering foreground session: <B>`, then `Session changed (<A> → <B>), reloading extensions`, followed by extension bootstrap lines for B. Send B any message; `probe_ping` is now available.

### Expected behavior

A session created with `create_session` gets the same extensions as any interactive session from the moment it's created, since the host supervises it and it is meant to work without the user watching.

### Additional context

- macOS on Apple silicon (arm64).
- Over two days on one machine, 10 sessions created by other sessions received their extensions between 36 seconds and 26 minutes after creation, each time when the user first opened the session.
- `copilot-sdk/docs/extensions.md` says `joinSession()` "attaches to the user's current foreground session", which may explain it.
- Possibly related: github/copilot-cli#5164 (switching sessions in the sidebar starts a set of extension hosts per session).

issues.title: MCP OAuth (interactive): authorization code is received and the success page is served, but the code->token exchange never runs — server stuck "Connecting"

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

For a remote HTTP MCP server using Entra ID OAuth (Azure DevOps remote MCP,
`https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>`), the interactive CLI completes the browser
round-trip but never exchanges the authorization code for a token.

Observed with Copilot CLI running **inside WSL2** (Ubuntu 26.04 on a Windows 11
host). I have not tested native Windows or native Linux, so I cannot say whether
this is WSL-specific — see the note at the end.

Observed sequence:

1. On startup the CLI auto-connects, gets the expected `401` with
   `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.dev.azure.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/<org>"`.
2. Metadata discovery and dynamic client registration succeed — a registration
   record is written to `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/<key>.json`, with
   `authorizationServerUrl`, `clientId: aebc6443-996d-45c2-90f0-388ff96faa56`,
   `redirectUri: http://127.0.0.1:41003/`.
3. The CLI logs `Opening browser for <server> authentication...` then
   `Requesting access token for <server>...`.
4. I complete the sign-in. The browser lands on
   `http://127.0.0.1:41003/?nonce=<nonce>&code=<code>` and **the CLI's own
   callback page renders** ("Authorization Successful"). So the code reaches
   the CLI's listener.
5. Nothing further happens. The TUI stays on "Authenticating: <server>" /
   "Connecting to <server>...". No `<key>.tokens.json` is ever written, and no
   log line is emitted after this point.

The `<key>.verifier` file is **not** removed. Per the runtime's own state
machine (`MCP OAuth token exchange completed; saving tokens` ->
`MCP OAuth tokens saved; clearing code verifier`), a surviving verifier means
the exchange never completed successfully.

The MCP transport worker meanwhile keeps cycling:

```
[ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed,
  when Client(OAuthChallenge { www_authenticate_header: "...oauth-protected-resource/<org>",
  response: McpOAuthHttpResponse { status_code: 401, ... } })
```

### The failure is in the CLI, not the environment

I reproduced the identical flow manually with a small script — **same client ID,
same scope, same `vscode.dev` relay, same loopback pattern** — and it succeeds
on the first attempt:

```
TOKEN EXCHANGE: HTTP 200 SUCCESS
  scope        : https://mcp.dev.azure.com/Ado.Mcp.Tools https://mcp.dev.azure.com/.default
  token_type   : Bearer
  expires_in   : 4102
  refresh_token: present
```

Driving the MCP server with that token also works:

```
[initialize] HTTP 200   serverInfo: {"name": "AzureDevOps.Mcp", "version": "1.0.0.0"}
[tools/list] HTTP 200   tool count: 43
```

Writing that token into `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/<key>.tokens.json` in the
CLI's own schema (`accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `expiresAt`, `requestedScope`,
`scope`) makes the server connect normally. `grant_type=refresh_token` renewal
against the same endpoint also works.

So tenant config, consent, scopes, app registration, the `vscode.dev` relay,
loopback reachability and the MCP server are all confirmed working. The only
step that fails is the CLI's own code->token exchange.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:
   ```json
   {"mcpServers":{"ado-remote-mcp":{"type":"http","url":"https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>"}}}
   ```
2. Start `copilot`. It auto-connects and begins the OAuth flow.
3. Run `/mcp auth ado-remote-mcp`, press `c`, open the URL, complete sign-in.
4. Browser shows the CLI's "Authorization Successful" page.
5. `ls ~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/` — no `.tokens.json`; the `.verifier`
   remains. The TUI never leaves the connecting state.

### Expected behavior

After the callback is received, the CLI proceeds to `exchanging_code`, stores
the tokens, clears the verifier, and connects the server.

### Additional context

- **No diagnostics are available for this step.** `RUST_LOG` is accepted but
  produces no additional output, and the process log contains nothing at all
  between the callback and the stall. The runtime has specific failure strings
  (`ExchangeResponseFailure`, `failed to clear OAuth code verifier after
  authorization failure`) but none reach the log file. Surfacing the token
  endpoint's response on failure would make this self-diagnosable.
- `ctrl+g` (device code) does not help: `mcp.dev.azure.com` advertises no
  device-code support, so the CLI logs `Server does not support device code
  flow - falling back to browser` and retries the browser path.
- The callback arrives as `?nonce=<nonce>&code=<code>` with **no `state`
  parameter** — `vscode.dev/redirect` consumes `state` (the CLI encodes the
  nonce in the state fragment). If the handler validates `state`, that may be
  relevant. Unverified.
- Possibly related: #4994, #5192, #4695 — all ACP-mode or cross-session reuse.
  This one is plain interactive mode on first sign-in.
- **Environment caveat (WSL2).** This was only observed with the CLI running
  inside WSL2; I have not reproduced it on native Windows or native Linux, so I
  cannot confirm whether the platform matters. Two WSL-specific points, both
  ruled out as causes:
  - WSL has no browser launcher by default (`xdg-open`/`wslview` absent), so the
    CLI's `Opening browser...` step is a silent no-op until `BROWSER` is set.
    That produces a *separate* earlier symptom (no prompt at all). After adding a
    launcher the browser opens correctly, and the stall described above persists.
  - Windows→WSL loopback forwarding works. An independent listener inside WSL
    received the browser's redirect on `127.0.0.1` (including the follow-up
    `favicon.ico` request), so the callback path itself is sound.

issues.title: MCP OAuth (Copilot Desktop app): non-first-party HTTP servers cancel host-token then never launch the "runtime browser flow" they deferred to — no auth, no error, no popup

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: This issue has been added to our internal issue tracker

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
Describe the bug
In the GitHub Copilot Desktop app, remote MCP servers configured with "type": "http" that are non-first-party (e.g. Atlassian, incident.io) fail to authenticate. Toggling the server off/on in Settings produces no browser popup and no visible error — the server simply never connects.

Affected version
Desktop app shell: v1.0.15 (latest, confirmed via in-app update check)
Bundled Copilot CLI engine: v1.0.69-0 (AppData\Local\github-copilot-sdk\cli\1.0.69-0\copilot.exe)

Steps to reproduce
Add a non-first-party remote MCP server with "type": "http" and a url in mcp-config.json (e.g. https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2)
Enable it via Settings → MCP servers in the Desktop app
Toggle it off, then on again
Observe: no browser window ever opens; the server stays disconnected with no user-facing error

Expected behavior
A browser window should open for OAuth consent, as it does for the raw copilot CLI and for local-type servers wrapped in npx mcp-remote.

Actual behavior
~/.copilot/logs/github-app.<pid>.log shows this single log line and nothing further:

github_app::session::manager::mcp_status: MCP OAuth non-first-party server; cancelling host-token so runtime browser flow runs server_name=<server>
```

This line repeats on every toggle attempt (confirmed 43 occurrences across multiple sessions for both atlassian and incident.io), but there is no subsequent log entry anywhere indicating the "runtime browser flow" it defers to is ever actually invoked — no browser-launch attempt, no OAuth URL, no error surfaced to the user.

## Root cause hypothesis
This behavior appears tied to the MCP host token-injection OAuth rework shipped in copilot-cli v1.0.66 (2026-06-30 changelog entry: "Added runtime telemetry for the MCP host token-injection OAuth flow, recording when an OAuth broadcast is emitted to the host and how the host responds (token or cancelled)"). For non-first-party servers, the host correctly identifies it should defer to a client-side browser flow and cancels its own token injection — but that deferred browser flow is never triggered inside the Desktop app shell.

## Workaround
Reconfiguring the server as a local type wrapping npx mcp-remote bypasses the broken Desktop-app host/browser-flow handoff entirely, since mcp-remote runs its own independent OAuth implementation:

```json
"atlassian": {
  "type": "local",
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["--yes", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp"]
}
```

This works reliably. Native "type": "http" does not, for any non-first-party server, in the Desktop app.

## Additional context
Possibly related to #2536, but distinct: that issue is about the raw copilot CLI's "Opening browser for X authentication..." log line firing and a browser genuinely opening, just re-registering (DCR) on every launch. In this Desktop-app case, the browser-flow deferral log line fires but no browser-launch attempt is ever logged afterward — a different failure point entirely (host→client handoff, not CLI OAuth caching).

issues.body:
## Description
When reloading MCP servers with `/mcp reload`, the CLI correctly terminates the existing stdio MCP server child process before starting a new one. However, running `/clear` (start fresh session) spawns a new stdio MCP server process without terminating the previous session's MCP server process, leaking orphaned processes over time.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Start a session with a stdio-based MCP server configured (e.g. a custom `*.exe` MCP server).
2. Confirm the server process is running (e.g. via Task Manager / `Get-Process`).
3. Run `/clear`.
4. Observe: a new instance of the MCP server process starts, but the previous one is still running.
5. Repeat `/clear` multiple times — orphaned process count grows unbounded.
6. Contrast with `/mcp reload`, which correctly stops the old process before starting the new one.

## Expected behavior
`/clear` should terminate/clean up MCP server child processes from the previous session (or reuse them) before/while starting the new session's servers, matching the behavior of `/mcp reload`.

## Actual behavior
Old MCP stdio server processes are left running indefinitely after `/clear`, accumulating over repeated use (observed 22+ orphaned exe instances in one session).

## Environment
- Copilot CLI version: 1.0.82
- OS: Windows
- MCP server type: stdio-based custom MCP server

issues.title: Expose stable runtime turn IDs to built-in plugins

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
## Problem

Browser Use needs one exact agent-owned turn identity at both ends of a turn so it can return only the User Tabs claimed by that turn.

The current integration does not provide that correlation:

- MCP `tools/call` may contain `_meta["com.github.copilot/turnId"]`, but only when an SDK caller supplied the optional, caller-controlled `clientTurnId`.
- Built-in Copilot CLI and Copilot App sessions can issue MCP calls without that field.
- `agentStop` carries the session identity and timestamp, but not the agent turn identity that produced the corresponding MCP calls.

A timestamp is not a turn identity. Delayed or reordered hooks force built-in plugins to infer which turn stopped, or to fall back to session-scoped and idle cleanup.

Related Browser integration work: #397 and #398.

## Request

Expose the agent loop's real, opaque turn ID through a new agent-owned field on both:

1. every final MCP `tools/call` request made by that turn; and
2. the matching `agentStop` payload.

The Copilot CLI built-in-plugin path and the Copilot SDK session path should both expose the turn ID already owned by their respective runtimes. The built-in plugin should not generate, inject, or remember this ID through `preMcpToolCall`.

This should be a new field rather than a compatibility extension of `clientTurnId`:

- `clientTurnId` is optional and caller-controlled;
- `agentTurnId` is always agent-runtime-controlled and identifies the actual executing turn;
- no equality or fallback relationship between them is required.

Proposed field names and payloads follow.

### MCP tool call

```json
{
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "browser-use/manage_user_tab",
    "arguments": {
      "action": "claim",
      "tabId": "candidate-tab-id"
    },
    "_meta": {
      "com.github.copilot/agentTurnId": "agent-turn-opaque-id"
    }
  }
}
```

The agent runtime, not a hook or plugin, stamps this field after hook metadata processing so a hook cannot accidentally remove or replace it.

### Agent Stop

Command-hook payload:

```json
{
  "hookEventName": "agentStop",
  "sessionId": "session-opaque-id",
  "agentTurnId": "agent-turn-opaque-id",
  "timestamp": "2026-11-18T05:00:00.000Z",
  "stopReason": "end_turn"
}
```

The `agentTurnId` in `agentStop` must be exactly the same value stamped on MCP calls from the turn that emitted that Stop event. It must not be looked up from whichever turn is current when the hook is delivered.

## Browser Use outcome

With this contract, Browser Use can directly correlate:

```text
tools/call(sessionId, agentTurnId)
...
agentStop(sessionId, agentTurnId)
→ cancel/drain that turn's Browser work
→ return only the User Tabs claimed by that turn
```

This removes the need for Browser-specific generated turn IDs, timestamp-to-turn lookup, cross-process lifecycle locks, and replay/cleanup bookkeeping while preserving exact per-turn User Tab reclamation.

## Acceptance criteria

- A built-in Copilot CLI integration test asserts that MCP calls and `agentStop` receive the same agent-owned turn ID.
- A Copilot SDK integration test asserts the same behavior for an SDK-created session without `clientTurnId`.
- Tests cover multiple MCP calls in one turn, two sequential turns, and a delayed Stop from the earlier turn.
- Tests verify that `preMcpToolCall` output cannot remove or replace the agent-owned field.

issues.title: Organization-managed GPT models do not defer MCP tools despite Responses API and toolSearch enabled

labels.name: area:enterprise

issues.body:
## Summary

Organization-managed GPT models load all MCP tool definitions upfront, even when tool search is enabled and the model uses the Responses API.

The same underlying model defers tools when accessed through GitHub’s hosted offering or a directly configured external provider using Responses.

This becomes expensive with large tool definitions: a separate organization-managed Sol test consumed **236,905 actual input tokens** for a simple “Reply OK” prompt that required no tools.

## Environment

- Copilot CLI **1.0.110**, macOS arm64.
- Custom model configured centrally through **GitHub organization settings**, not local BYOK.
- Selected model: `<org>/<key-name>/gpt-6-luna`.
- Organization configuration:
  - **Responses API**
  - Tool calling, Streaming, Vision and Thinking enabled.
- CLI setting: `"toolSearch": true`.
- MCP server setting: `"deferTools": "auto"`.

## Reproduction

1. Configure an organization-managed GPT model using Responses.
2. Connect enough MCP tools to exceed the tool-search threshold. Our test used 48 synthetic MCP tools.
3. Start a fresh interactive CLI conversation and select the organization-managed model.
4. Ask it to call one known synthetic read-only tool.
5. Inspect the `turn tool surface resolved` diagnostic.
6. Repeat with hosted and directly configured models.

## Results

Same tool inventory and underlying GPT‑6 Luna model:

| Connection | API | Total tools | Deferred tools |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Organization-managed | Responses | 49 | **0** |
| GitHub-hosted | Responses | 49 | **49** |
| Direct external Gateway | Responses | 49 | **49** |

The total includes one native function. All three cases successfully called the requested tool and returned its result.

The organization-managed case reports:

```json
{
  "tool_search_enabled": true,
  "model_tool_calls_allowed": true,
  "opted_out": false,
  "client_path": false,
  "builtin_path": false,
  "generic_path": false,
  "deferred_tool_count": 0
}
```

## Expected behavior / question

Organization-managed models should support on-demand tool loading where the model and endpoint support it, or clearly explain why tool search is unavailable despite being enabled.

Could the organization-qualified model ID or catalog `family: "custom"` be preventing selection of the Responses tool-search path? Is there a supported way for an organization administrator to enable this capability?

## Related

- microsoft/vscode#323699 — Capability propagation problems on the organization-managed model route; concerns Vision, not this exact behavior.
- github/copilot-cli#4613 — Earlier eager-loading regression, marked fixed in 1.0.105. This organization-managed case reproduces on 1.0.110.

labels.name: area:authentication

issues.body:
## Summary
On Windows, `copilot-keychain-chunk.*` entries appear to accumulate in Windows Credential Manager without being cleaned up. Once the per-user vault is full, **every** application on the machine fails to store credentials, which broke an unrelated tool's login.

## Observed
- Windows Credential Manager contained ~180 `copilot-keychain-chunk.<hash>.<uuid>.<n>` generic credentials (about two thirds of all entries in the vault).
- `CredWrite` from an unrelated process failed with Win32 error 8 (`ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY`, "Not enough memory resources are available to process this command") even for a ~1 KB blob. Free RAM was not an issue.
- An unrelated CLI that stores its OAuth token in Credential Manager then failed with an error mentioning "OS keyring is not reachable ... Not enough memory resources".
- After deleting all `copilot-keychain-chunk.*` entries (vault went from 265 to 83 entries), writes succeeded again.

## Suspected cause (inference, not confirmed)
Secrets are split into chunks, and when a secret is rewritten or refreshed (for example MCP OAuth tokens), the previous chunk set is not deleted. Failed or interrupted writes may also strand chunks. The middle UUID segment looks like a per-write version id.

## Suggested fix
1. On write: write the new chunks, update the index or pointer, then delete the old chunk set only after success.
2. On startup: sweep and delete any `copilot-keychain-chunk.*` entry not referenced by a current index.
3. Surface a clear warning when a credential write fails with a resource or quota error (related: #5399).

## Environment
- Windows 11
- Multiple MCP servers configured (several using OAuth)
- Not sure whether the writer is the CLI or the desktop app; both may share this storage code. Please re-label or transfer if this is the wrong repo.

issues.body:
## Summary
Add a way to be notified when startup MCP initialization has settled, i.e. every configured MCP server is either `connected` or `failed`.

## Motivation
With several MCP servers configured (filesystem, docling, figma, browserbase, playwright, atlassian), startup takes a while and some servers fail (e.g. OAuth challenge, timeouts). Today there is no signal for "startup done":

- `hooks.sessionStart` is documented only as running "when a session starts or resumes", not after MCP initialization settles.
- `notifications` / `beep` only fire on idle turns and attention requests.
- Live status is only visible in-session via `/mcp list`; `copilot mcp list` shows configuration only.
- Logs in `~/.copilot/logs` contain warnings/errors but no clear "all servers settled" line.

So users cannot tell when it is safe to start prompting that relies on MCP tools.

## Proposal
Any of:
1. A new hook event (e.g. `mcpStartupComplete`) with a payload listing each server and its status (`connected` / `failed: <reason>`).
2. Extend `notifications` / `beep` to fire once when MCP startup settles.
3. Document whether `sessionStart` waits for MCP initialization, and expose per-server status to hooks.

## Environment
Copilot CLI 1.0.109, macOS

### Describe the bug

## Describe the bug

Since **1.0.109**, `/mcp auth azure-devops` for `https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>` opens the native **Microsoft account broker window (OneAuth)**. That window **blocks copy and paste completely**. 2. Run `/mcp auth azure-devops`.

### Expected behavior

For Entra MCP servers, provide either:

as a fallback or as an opt-in setting (for example, honoring `COPILOT_ENTRA_DISABLE_ONEAUTH`).

labels.name: area:non-interactive

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

`copilot --acp` never connects to a running IDE, even when it is launched from the editor's own integrated terminal, in the same workspace, with a valid IDE lock file on disk. The interactive CLI in the exact same terminal attaches within ~1 s.

Contrast from the same machine, same version, same second, same workspace:

**Interactive `copilot`** — `~/.copilot/logs/process-…-13896.log`:

```
20:27:58.429Z [WARNING] Failed to parse lock file …\0173da6b-….lock: SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input
20:27:59.083Z [ERROR] Connecting to IDE MCP server: Visual Studio Code (C:\Users\hersh\Develop\patioz-api-fastify)
20:27:59.151Z [ERROR] Connected to IDE MCP server: Visual Studio Code
20:27:59.175Z [WARNING] [rust:mcp::client] MCP server advertises list-change capabilities but refused
                       subscriptions/listen … {"server":"Some(Implementation { name: \"ide\", version: \"0.0.1\" …})"}
```

**`copilot --acp`** — `~/.copilot/logs/process-1794513585531-30960.log`:

```
19:59:45.538Z [INFO] Starting ACP server (stdio)
19:59:45.623Z [INFO] [rust:acp::serve] ACP server started (stdio mode)
19:59:45.623Z [INFO] [rust:acp::serve] ACP server started, waiting for requests
```

…and nothing else. No lock-file scan, no `Connecting to IDE MCP server`, no `ide` MCP client at all.

The lock file was present and valid the whole time:

```json
{
  "ideName": "Visual Studio Code",
  "pid": 19300,
  "isTrusted": true,
  "socketPath": "\\\\.\\pipe\\…",
  "scheme": "pipe",
  "workspaceFolders": ["c:\\Users\\hersh\\Develop\\patioz-api-fastify"]
}
```

### Consequences

1. **No IDE status.** The "Visual Studio Connected" indicator the interactive CLI shows never appears, so an ACP host cannot tell whether the agent has editor tools.
2. **No IDE tools.** The `ide` MCP server (diagnostics / `openDiff` / selection / editor navigation) is absent from the ACP session's tool set, while it is present in the interactive CLI's. ACP sessions are therefore strictly less capable than interactive ones in the same terminal.
3. **No IDE-client registration.** The session never goes through `registerTrustedIdeExternalClient`, and its `client_name` is `github/acp` with `vscode.metadata.json` `origin: "other"`. Combined with VS Code's discovery gate (`readinessFiles = ['events.jsonl', 'workspace.yaml', 'vscode.metadata.json']`, and `_nextScanAt = this._hasJournal ? Date.now() : Infinity` in `copilotSessionDiscoveryWatchers.ts`), a freshly created ACP session — which has only `workspace.yaml` — is never listed in the Agents window, not even under "External", until the first message produces a journal.

## Affected version

```
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.109.
win32-arm64, Windows 11 (build 26300)
```

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Open VS Code (any version that publishes `~/.copilot/ide/*.lock`) on a folder; confirm a non-empty lock file exists for that window and `isTrusted: true`.
2. In VS Code's integrated terminal, run `copilot` → it reports **Visual Studio Connected** within ~1 s, and its log contains `Connected to IDE MCP server: Visual Studio Code`.
3. In the same terminal, same cwd, run `copilot --acp` and drive it over stdio:
   ```json
   {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":1,"clientCapabilities":{"fs":{"readTextFile":true,"writeTextFile":true}}}}
   {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"session/new","params":{"cwd":"c:\\Users\\hersh\\Develop\\patioz-api-fastify","mcpServers":[]}}
   ```
4. Compare `~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`: the interactive process has the two `IDE MCP server` lines, the ACP process has none.
5. Optional: check the ACP session's tool list — `ide`-provided tools are missing.

## Expected behavior

One of these, in order of preference:

- **`--acp` performs the same IDE discovery as the interactive CLI.** The ACP process is started by a terminal that belongs to an IDE window whose lock file advertises the cwd; there is no ambiguity to resolve, so the existing `discoverIdeWorkspaces` / `connectToIde` path could run unchanged and simply make the `ide` MCP server available to ACP sessions. This mirrors what the interactive CLI already does at startup.
- **An explicit opt-in**, if silently attaching is undesirable for a headless server: e.g. `--acp --ide` (or a `COPILOT_IDE=1`-style switch), defaulting off, so containerised/unattended ACP hosts stay untouched.
- **ACP-native alternative:** since the editor is normally the ACP *client*, accept the `ide` MCP server from `session/new`'s client-supplied `mcpServers` under a reserved name (e.g. `copilot-ide`) and document it, so ACP clients that are editors do not depend on lock files. Note this does **not** cover the editor-integrated-terminal case, which is the reproduction above.

Whichever is chosen, the behaviour should be symmetric: the same workspace, the same IDE, the same terminal should not give the agent a different tool set depending on `--acp`.

## Additional context

- **There is no configuration knob today**, which is part of the request: `copilot --help` exposes `--acp` but no `--ide` / `--attach-ide` / equivalent, and a scan of the bundled `cli-main.js` finds 135 `COPILOT_*` environment variables, none of them IDE-related. So a user cannot work around this.
- This is **not** about the `/code` handoff. `/code` (VS Code 1.146+ "Continue a Copilot CLI session in VS Code") goes through the Copilot SDK / Agent Host and `session.create`; it does not traverse ACP. The gap here is specifically the ACP server.
- ACP capabilities observed on 1.0.109, for completeness: `loadSession: true`, `sessionCapabilities: { close, list }`; `session/new` returns `{ models, configOptions, modes, sessionId }`.
- Related, but different: #4143 (CLI should inherit MCP tools from a connected VS Code instance — assumes the connection exists), #1868 (document `/ide` for IDEs beyond VS Code), microsoft/vscode#335215 (external agent sessions only discovered at startup).
- Suggested areas: `area:non-interactive`, `area:mcp`, `area:tools`.

issues.title: Delegated `task` children cannot authenticate HTTP-OAuth MCP servers: `<server>/*` gets 401, explicit refs work only on claude-fable-5.1 and only for some servers

issues.body:
ustom child agents launched with the native task tool cannot use HTTP-OAuth MCP servers reliably. Two symptoms from the same cause, observed across ~30 delegated runs on 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-12:

1. <server>/* wildcard on an OAuth server → requires authentication in the child. The agent host opens a fresh connection per declared server when a child starts. For HTTP servers it attempts a host-delegated OAuth handoff that never gets a response, falls back to browser OAuth it cannot complete, and sends the request unauthenticated:

The identical three lines are logged for atlassian (https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp). The parent session calls both servers successfully; the stdio testrail server (env-var credentials) works from every child.

2. Explicit <server>/<tool> references behave differently by model and by server. With tools: [..., atlassian/atlassianUserInfo, atlassian/getJiraIssue, ...] (no wildcard): on claude-fable-5.1 the child discovers the tool via tool_search_tool, calls it, and succeeds (7/7 for one agent, 1/1 each for two more profiles). On gpt-6-luna the same agent file discovers the same name and then declines to call it ("no callable invocation interface"), 0/6 attempts — even after instructions explicitly required an attempt. Models were harness defaults; no model override in any failing run. With tools: [..., mabl/get_current_user] on claude-fable-5.1, the child discovers the name and calls it, and the host returns Tool 'mabl-get_current_user' does not exist. So explicit Atlassian refs reach an authorized path that explicit mabl refs do not.

Secondary: tool_search_tool inside a child returns tools not in the child's tools list (e.g. atlassian-executeDestructive, Postman-MCP-*), consistent with #5191.

Affected version:

Agent host copilotVersion 1.0.103-unstable.r41379698026.g3219c66 (from session events), VS Code agent-host client (vscode-agent-host), Windows.

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

Configure https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp and https://mcp.mabl.com/mcp (both HTTP OAuth) in .vscode/mcp.json; authorize both in the parent session.
Child A: tools: [read, search, vscode/toolSearch, atlassian/*] → delegate via task, ask it to call atlassianUserInfo once. Observe requires authentication.
Child B: tools: [read, search, vscode/toolSearch, atlassian/atlassianUserInfo], instructions "discover then call exactly once; a name-only discovery result is not evidence it is uncallable". Delegate with model: "claude-fable-5.1" → success. Delegate with default gpt-6-luna → refuses without attempting.
Child C: tools: [read, search, vscode/toolSearch, mabl/get_current_user], model: "claude-fable-5.1" → Tool 'mabl-get_current_user' does not exist after discovery listed it.
Check ~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log for the three-line sequence above for each server at child start.
Expected behavior:

A child inherits the VS Code session's MCP OAuth state for every configured HTTP server (or the host-delegated OAuth handoff succeeds), so <server>/* and <server>/<tool> behave the same from a child as from the parent, independent of model. If children intentionally cannot use OAuth-only HTTP servers, that should be documented so declarations can be designed around it.

Additional context:

Workaround we are using: explicit <server>/<tool> references plus model: "claude-fable-5.1" for Atlassian; for mabl, switching the server to its documented x-api-key header auth (https://help.mabl.com/hc/en-us/articles/48563261741204) so the connection no longer depends on the OAuth handoff. Atlassian's equivalent API-token mode is not enabled for our site, so the model pin remains the only Atlassian path.
Question: is the tool definition actually attached to the model after discovery for explicit refs? Session events record the discovery result but not the per-turn tool list, so we cannot distinguish "model declined an undefined function" from "host did not bind the definition".
No credentials, tenant identifiers, or ticket content included; log lines are redacted as the host prints them.

issues.body:
## Problem

On macOS, a keychain prompt keeps appearing for the `copilot-mcp-oauth` service even after choosing "Always Allow":

> security wants to use your confidential information stored in "copilot-mcp-oauth" in your keychain.

The prompt names `security` (`/usr/bin/security`), so the CLI reads the item through the `security` tool.

## Observation

Keychain Access showed about 50 separate `copilot-mcp-oauth` items in the login keychain (kind "application password"), each with a different hashed account name. Their modified dates are spread over every day from 2026-09-30 to the current day, with several created or modified on the same day. The login keychain has no auto-lock timeout (`security show-keychain-info` reports `no-timeout`), so locking does not explain the repeated prompts.

"Always Allow" adds `security` to the access list of one item only. If the CLI creates a new item (or deletes and re-creates it) whenever a token is stored or refreshed, the new item has no grant, and the prompt returns. Old items are also never removed.

## Expected

- Update an existing item in place, so a previous "Always Allow" persists.
- Remove items for tokens that are no longer used.
- Alternatively, store the OAuth tokens for all MCP servers in a single item, so one grant covers them.

## Environment

- Copilot CLI 1.0.99-2, GitHub Copilot app
- macOS, login keychain
- Several remote MCP servers using OAuth (Atlassian, Jama, GitHub)

Related, but a different symptom: #4203

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

A plugin in the Agent Plugins format can't connect to a remote MCP server whose authorization server only accepts pre-registered clients with an exact redirect URI, such as Looker's managed MCP server. Copilot CLI supports this in user and workspace config with `oauthClientId` and `auth.redirectPort`, but not from such a plugin, and a plugin server that carries those fields is dropped without a warning.

### Proposed solution

1. For Agent Plugins plugins, read Copilot's OAuth options from `plugin.json` → `extensions["com.github.copilot"]`, which Agent Plugins 1.1.0 reserves for client-specific data, merged into the server of the same name in `mcp.json`:

   ```json
   "extensions": { "com.github.copilot": { "mcpServers": { "looker": { "oauthClientId": "my-registered-client", "auth": { "redirectPort": 35731 } } } } }
   ```

   When agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec#7 adds OAuth fields to the spec, read those too.
2. Warn when a plugin's MCP server is skipped, naming the file and the field, instead of dropping it silently.

### Example prompts or workflows

- A company plugin for Looker: people install it and sign in on first use, without editing `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`.
- The same for identity providers that require exact redirect URIs (Okta, Entra ID, Keycloak).

### Additional context

Copilot CLI 1.0.109, Linux arm64. Plugins installed from a local marketplace into a throwaway `COPILOT_HOME`, then `copilot mcp list --json`:

| Where the OAuth fields are | Result |
|---|---|
| Agent Plugins `mcp.json`, on the server | Server missing from `copilot mcp list`, no warning |
| `com.github.copilot/mcp.json` or `.mcp.json` | Ignored; only the `mcp.json` server loads |
| `plugin.json` → `extensions["com.github.copilot"]` | Ignored |
| Legacy plugin (no Agent Plugins `$schema`), `.mcp.json` | Loaded with `oauthClientId` and `auth.redirectPort` |

The dropped server was `{"type": "streamable-http", "url": "https://looker.example.com/mcp", "oauthClientId": "my-registered-client", "auth": {"redirectPort": 35731}}`. The Agent Plugins schema allows only `type`, `url` and `headers` on a remote server, so a plugin that validates can't carry these fields. Our workaround is a stdio proxy in the plugin that does the OAuth itself.

Related: #1491, microsoft/vscode#319440 (VS Code has no callback port setting; its agent host passes `oauthClientId` to the runtime but not `auth.redirectPort`).

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On Windows, the automatic (OneAuth/WAM) MCP sign-in requests the token through `https://login.microsoftonline.com/common`, even though the server's protected resource metadata advertises a tenant-specific authorization server (`https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0`). For a **single-tenant** Entra app registration, Entra refuses `/common`:

```
AADSTS50194: Application '<app-id>'(<app name>) is not configured as a multi-tenant application.
Usage of the /common endpoint is not supported for such applications created after '10/15/2018'.
Use a tenant-specific endpoint or configure the application to be multi-tenant.
```

The CLI surfaces this only as:

```
Microsoft Entra sign-in for https://<server>/mcp failed: ENTRA_CONFIG: the authenticator rejected the configuration [code 2002, tag 7q6cl]
```

and the tool call fails with `MCP server "<name>" requires authentication`. As a result, **every interactive session** has to run `/mcp auth <server>` again. 1.0.105 did not have this problem.


### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.108 (also reproduced on 1.0.107; 1.0.106 not tested). Works on 1.0.105.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Host a remote HTTP MCP server protected by a **single-tenant** Entra app (`signInAudience: AzureADMyOrg`), returning `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://<server>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"`. The metadata lists `authorization_servers: ["https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0"]` and `scopes_supported: ["api://<app-id>/access_as_user"]`. VS Code and Copilot CLI client IDs are pre-authorized on the app.
2. Add it to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` as `{"type": "http", "url": "https://<server>/mcp"}`.
3. Run `/mcp auth <server>` once; this succeeds and tools work.
4. Exit and start a new interactive session: `copilot -i "call <server> tool X"`.
5. The tool call fails with "requires authentication". The debug log (`--log-level debug --log-dir ...`) shows:
   ```
   [rust:oneauth] [OneAuth:0003:Error:7q6cl:ff000000] (Code:2002) Access denied for the resource.
   [rust:rt_identity::auth::oneauth] OneAuth acquisition failed {"error":"ENTRA_CONFIG: the authenticator rejected the configuration [code 2002, tag 7q6cl]"}
   ```
6. The Windows event log `Microsoft-Windows-AAD/Operational` shows the real error for the same request: `GetTokenSilently ... AADSTS50194 ... Request: authority: https://login.microsoftonline.com/common, client: aebc6443-996d-45c2-90f0-388ff96faa56, ...` (the log also notes the account id is empty).

Observations:
- Repeating step 4 with `npx @github/copilot@1.0.105`: the first session opens a browser sign-in; a second session reuses it silently and the tool call succeeds. No AADSTS50194 events.
- Non-interactive `copilot -p` on 1.0.108 succeeds silently from the state saved by `/mcp auth`; only interactive startup fails.
- Unsetting `COPILOT_ENTRA_AUTH_AUD` (cf. #4796) does not help.
- `COPILOT_ENTRA_DISABLE_ONEAUTH=1` just changes the error to `ENTRA_UNAVAILABLE ... disabled by COPILOT_ENTRA_DISABLE_ONEAUTH`; there is no fallback to the saved sign-in, so `/mcp auth` is still needed every session.
- The MCP config has no setting for the authority/tenant (`oauthClientId`, `oauthScopes`, etc. exist), so there is no client-side workaround.

### Expected behavior

The silent sign-in should use the authorization server advertised in the protected resource metadata (the tenant-specific authority), or the tenant of the account saved by `/mcp auth`, instead of `/common`. Sessions after the first `/mcp auth` should connect without prompting, as in 1.0.105. If silent sign-in fails, the CLI should fall back to the saved sign-in or report the underlying AADSTS error rather than a generic `ENTRA_CONFIG` code.

### Additional context

- Windows 11 (build 26300), x64, Entra-joined, PowerShell 7
- Server: remote HTTP MCP server on Azure Container Apps, ASP.NET Core + Microsoft.Identity.Web, single-tenant app, token v2
- Making the server's app multi-tenant would avoid `/common` being refused, but widening the app's audience just to work around the client isn't a good option for us.
- Trace/correlation IDs and full debug logs are available privately on request.

issues.body:
### Summary

Copilot Connectors that are connected and working in an interactive CLI session don't show up in sessions started with `copilot --acp`. An ACP client gets the user MCP servers from `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` and the built-in GitHub MCP server, but no connector tools.

### Environment

- Copilot CLI 1.0.106 (ACP, bundled by the ACP client [T3 Code](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code)) and 1.0.108 (interactive and `-p`)
- linux-x64
- The `connectors` setting is not set in `~/.copilot/settings.json`, so the default (`true`) applies.
- The same account and machine were used in every mode.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect the Slack and Work IQ connectors (these were the two I tried).
2. Run `copilot`, then `/mcp`. The **Installed** tab lists `Slack` and `Work IQ` as **Connector / Connected** with tool token counts (about 29.4k and 7.5k tokens).
3. Start a session from an ACP client (`copilot --acp`) and ask the agent which tools it has. It has none with `slack` or `workiq` in the name; the only MCP servers are the user servers and `github-mcp-server`.

### Expected

Connectors connected for the signed-in account are available in ACP sessions, the same as in interactive sessions. If that isn't supported, the docs should say so.

### Actual

ACP sessions get no connector tools, and the logs show no warning or error. ACP sessions are the only way to use the CLI from an ACP client, so connectors aren't available there at all.

### Additional observations

- `copilot -p` (1.0.108) also has no connector tools. A run with `--log-level debug` sends `connector_client_operation` telemetry, so connector loading appears to start, but a tool search for `slack|workiq` returns `No tools found`.
- Workarounds don't fit well. Adding Slack's remote MCP server (`https://mcp.slack.com/mcp`) to `mcp-config.json` fails in ACP with `Client registration failed: Authorization server does not support dynamic client registration`. The connector exists to handle that sign-in.

### Related

- #5347: connectors fail in interactive sessions but load in `-p` mode (a different loading path).
- #5049: a plugin that's enabled in the CLI is unavailable in ACP mode.
- #1255: ACP support for MCP config passed with `session/new`.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A session made with `create_session`, which the user has switched to and which another session then closes with `close_session`, can't be reopened in the same CLI process. `/resume` fails with:

`Failed to switch session: Error: Failed to associate local session <id> with its built-in plugin host`

Relaunching the CLI, or opening the session from a new CLI process, lets it reopen normally.

A created session that the user never switched to reopens normally after the same close. After the failed attempt, at a later switch between sessions, the CLI starts an MCP server process for the session that didn't open and leaves it running.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.108-1

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Turn on session management tools (`sessionManagementTools` in `~/.copilot/settings.json`). Our setup also had user extensions and one remote MCP server; we haven't tried without them.
2. In session A, call `create_session` twice to make sessions B and C.
3. Switch to B, then back to A. Don't switch to C.
4. In A, call `close_session` for B and for C.
5. Run `/resume` and pick B. It fails with the error above.
6. Run `/resume` and pick C. It opens.

When A closes B, the log shows `Cleaning up session <B>: Session closed via sessions.close`, then `Failed to apply session management settings: Error: the Copilot SDK reported a failure: RPC error -32603: Request session.management.configure failed with message: The destination session is not available`. Closing C logs only `Closing session <C>`.

### Expected behavior

A session closed with `close_session` can be reopened with `/resume` whether or not the user had switched to it.

### Additional context

- macOS on Apple silicon (arm64).
- Seen twice on 2026-11-08 with different sessions. Both times an MCP server process for the session that failed to reopen was still running afterward.
- Related: github/copilot-cli#5380 (created sessions start extensions only when the user switches to them) and github/copilot-cli#5164 (switching sessions leaks MCP servers and extension hosts).

labels.name: area:mcp

issues.body:
### Summary

Every **interactive** CLI session prints:

```
[WARNING] Connected Connectors could not be loaded; existing local and self-hosted MCP servers remain available.
```

The same CLI version, same account and same working directory load Connectors **successfully** in non-interactive (`-p`) mode. So this appears to be specific to the interactive session-startup path, not to the account's Connectors configuration.

### Version

`1.0.105` (linux-x64, Node v24.22.1). `CONNECTORS` feature flag resolves to `true` for this account, so Connectors are enabled and failing rather than disabled.

### Observed behaviour

The warning appears on every interactive startup in all five of my retained session logs (2026-10-29, 2026-10-30 x2, 2026-11-02, 2026-11-03) — 100% reproduction rate, going back as far as log retention allows.

The emitting code is byte-identical between 1.0.103 and 1.0.105 (`reportManagedConnectorFailure` in `cli-main.js`), so this is not a recent regression — it just looks like a long-standing failure.

### Not reproducible headlessly

I ran, with debug logging enabled:

```
copilot --log-level debug --log-dir <dir> --allow-all-tools -p "reply with OK only"
```

twice — once in an empty `/tmp` directory, once in the large git repo where the interactive sessions fail. **Neither run produced the warning.** Both emitted `connector_client_operation` telemetry and completed Connector loading cleanly.

### Why that matters for diagnosis

Looking at `beginManagedConnectorLoad` in `cli-main.js`, interactive sessions appear to take a different branch from headless ones:

```js
let r = t.authInfo === void 0
  ? { apply: s => n.currentAndApplyToSession(t.nativeSessionId, s),
      current: s => n.currentForSession(t.nativeSessionId, s) }
  : void 0;
```

When `r` is set, the code applies session credentials and races them against an `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`, with failure paths that throw `"The active GitHub account changed while loading Connectors"`. Headless `-p` runs supply `authInfo` and skip that path entirely. That session-credential/timeout branch looks like the likely culprit.

### Main request: the failure cause is unobservable

The underlying exception is only logged on the failure path:

```js
T.warning(r);
T.debug(`Copilot Connectors session integration failed: ${k(n)}`);
```

Since the failure reproduces *only* interactively, and `--log-level debug` is most naturally exercised via `-p`, there is effectively no way for a user to capture the real error. I could not obtain it despite the failure occurring 100% of the time interactively.

Concretely, it would help a lot if:

1. The underlying cause were logged at `warning` level alongside the user-facing message (or at least included in it), rather than only at `debug`.
2. The user-facing warning distinguished "timed out", "account changed", and "server error", since the remediation differs wildly.

### Possibly related

I am simultaneously seeing `GET /copilot_internal/managed_settings` return `422 Validation Failed` on this account (filed separately). Connectors sit on the same managed/enterprise settings surface, so these may share a root cause — though the Connectors failure clearly predates the 422 by at least a week.

### Impact

Local and self-hosted MCP servers continue to work, so impact is limited to Connectors being unavailable plus a startup warning on every session.

issues.body:
Copilot CLI 1.0.105 on macOS (Apple Silicon), signed in with an Enterprise Managed User account whose organization policy sets `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`.

The CLI sometimes hangs indefinitely at startup or on `--resume`. It has happened repeatedly over the past few days.

- The server policy is fetched successfully (`serverFetchFailed=false`).
- About 30 s later the log shows `Managed MCP policy application exceeded its settings settlement deadline; independent enforcement continues` (logged twice).
- Nothing is logged after that. Only 1 or 2 of the 11 configured MCP servers (5 stdio, 6 HTTP) are started, the UI never becomes usable, and after about 2 minutes all connections to github.com are closed. I waited more than 3 minutes before killing it.
- On resume, the session also logs: `Plugins required by your organization admin could not be checked… Error: Managed settings could not be confirmed`.

It happens intermittently with the same configuration. Starting with every `--disable-mcp-server` flag usually works, but it isn't tied to a particular server, because turning them back on one by one didn't reproduce it.

CLI processes left running from closed terminals seem to make it more likely, but stopping them doesn't always fix it.

Logs available on request.

labels.name: area:non-interactive

labels.name: area:mcp

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Starting Copilot CLI, including `copilot --acp`, with every user MCP server off for that process only, without listing each server name and without editing `mcp-config.json`. A client that starts `copilot --acp` as a worker needs this so a person's own MCP servers do not reach that worker.

### Proposed solution

One flag, for example `--disable-user-mcps`, that skips every server from the user MCP config for that invocation. `--disable-builtin-mcps` already covers the built-ins and is the pattern to copy. State in `--help` that `--acp` honours it.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. `copilot --disable-user-mcps` in a directory whose user config has many local servers, when this run should not start them.
2. `copilot --acp --disable-user-mcps` from a client that speaks ACP and wants the same empty user roster.
3. `copilot --disable-mcp-server docs` remains the way to drop one named server and keep the others.
4. `copilot mcp disable docs` remains the way to persist that one server as off across later runs.

### Additional context

Measured on GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105 (npm `latest` on 2026-11-02), macOS 15.7.4 (24G517), Darwin 24.6.0 x86_64, throwaway `HOME`, not signed in.

`copilot mcp list` showed `docs (local)`. `copilot --help` and `copilot --acp --help` list `--disable-mcp-server <server-name>` (one named server), `--disable-builtin-mcps` (built-ins only), `--enable-mcp-server <server-name>` and `--additional-mcp-config <json>`. None turns off every user server. `copilot mcp enable` and `disable` persist a per-server setting.

Not observed: whether a user server actually starts under `--acp`. Unsigned in, `initialize` succeeded and `session/new` returned `Authentication required` before any server command ran, and adding `--disable-mcp-server docs` produced no ACP frame within 7 seconds. Please confirm how `--disable-mcp-server` behaves under `--acp` in a signed-in session.

Nearby but different: #3380 asks to skip repo MCP files, #768 and `/mcp disable` persist one name, #3582 is about a `"disabled": true` property being ignored.

### Describe the bug

The built-in `web_search` tool fails intermittently (more than half of calls over the last ~9 days) with:

```
MCP server 'github-mcp-server': MCP request failed: Transport send error: Transport [...StreamableHttpClientWorker<...RawCapturingReqwestClient>...] error: unexpected server response: HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout: [HTML error page omitted]
```

Every failure happens at **~121s**. Successful calls take between 32s and 115s. This points to a fixed **120s gateway timeout** in front of the remote MCP endpoint (`https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/mcp/readonly`). The web search backend (Bing searches plus answer synthesis) often runs longer than that limit.

### Evidence (from local `~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl`, `tool.execution_start` → `tool.execution_complete`)

| 2026-10-22T00:58:11Z     | 42.4  | OK  |
| 2026-10-22T12:39:50Z     | 121.2 | 504 |

issues.title: Windows: elevated session creates .mcp-writer.lock that non-elevated sessions cannot open (open_lock, os_error=5)

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On Windows, if an **elevated** (Run as administrator) session is the first to create `%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\.mcp-writer.lock` and `.mcp-writer.binding`, all later **non-elevated** sessions fail to start MCP servers:

```
Failed to start MCP Servers: Error: Shared writer storage I/O failed. (operation=open_lock, os_error=5)
```

**Root cause:** The two files are created with a protected DACL:

```
.mcp-writer.lock  OWNER RIGHTS:(IO)(F)
                  NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM:(F)
                  BUILTIN\Administrators:(F)
```

Two problems combine:

1. The `OWNER RIGHTS` ACE has the **inherit-only (IO)** flag, so it does not apply to the file itself. Only SYSTEM and Administrators get access.
2. When an admin account creates a file from an elevated process, Windows sets the default owner to `BUILTIN\Administrators`, not the user.

A non-elevated token has `BUILTIN\Administrators` as deny-only, so opening the file returns `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (5). Changing only the owner to the user does not fix this, because of the IO flag. Other files in `~\.copilot` inherit the user ACE from the parent and are not affected.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.103

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure at least one MCP server.
2. Delete `%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\.mcp-writer.lock` and `%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\.mcp-writer.binding`.
3. Start `copilot` in an elevated terminal, then exit.
4. Start `copilot` in a non-elevated terminal.
5. See `Shared writer storage I/O failed. (operation=open_lock, os_error=5)`.

### Expected behavior

The same user can open the files from both elevated and non-elevated sessions. Possible fixes:

- Grant the current user SID explicitly.
- Apply `OWNER RIGHTS` without the inherit-only flag, and set the owner to the user SID.
- Do not use a protected DACL. Inherit the ACL from `~\.copilot`.

### Additional context

- OS: Windows 11 Pro, local admin account with UAC enabled
- CPU architecture: x86_64 (AMD64)
- Terminal: Windows Terminal
- Shell: PowerShell 7.6

Log excerpts:

```
[ERROR] [rust:copilot_runtime::shared_api::event_log] Failed to retry MCP servers after OAuth listener registration: {"error":"Shared writer storage I/O failed. (operation=open_lock, os_error=5)"}
[ERROR] Failed to start MCP Servers: Error: Shared writer storage I/O failed. (operation=open_lock, os_error=5)
[ERROR] [rust:mcp_engine::session_lifecycle] Failed to initialize MCP host: Shared writer storage I/O failed. (operation=open_lock, os_error=5)
[ERROR] [rust:copilot_runtime::shared_api::lifecycle] Scheduled queue processing failed after retry; queue drain abandoned {"error":"Message(\"Shared writer storage I/O failed. (operation=open_lock, os_error=5)\")"}
```

**Workaround** (from an elevated shell):

```
icacls %USERPROFILE%\.copilot\.mcp-writer.lock /grant "%USERNAME%:F"
icacls %USERPROFILE%\.copilot\.mcp-writer.binding /grant "%USERNAME%:F"
```

Related, but a different cause: #4998 (macOS stale `.mcp-writer.binding`).

issues.title: macOS: Entra-broker MCP servers fail at startup: concurrent sign-ins rejected ("sign-in is already in progress") and rejected cached token not recovered

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On macOS, two Entra-protected remote MCP servers (Azure DevOps remote MCP at `https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>` and the WorkIQ plugin at `https://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/mcp`) fail to connect at session startup. The failures happen in the native Entra account-broker path that 1.0.95 introduced.

The logs show two separate problems.

**1. Concurrent broker sign-ins are rejected instead of queued**

When both servers need a token at startup, both call the account broker at the same time. The CLI's broker wrapper allows only one interactive request per process and throws for the second request. The second request is not queued:

```
[ERROR] Signing in with your Microsoft Entra account (account broker)...
[ERROR] Signing in with your Microsoft Entra account (account broker)...
[WARNING] Entra token acquisition failed {"server_url":"https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>","error":"Entra broker error: Error: A Microsoft sign-in is already in progress. Complete or cancel it before trying again."}
[ERROR] OAuth authentication failed for ado-remote-mcp: MCPOAuthError: Microsoft Entra sign-in for https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org> failed: Entra broker error: Error: A Microsoft sign-in is already in progress. ...
```

Which server fails depends on timing. The `/mcp` reconnect hits the same collision. The guard is in the broker plugin's `acquireTokenInteractive`, which throws when `this.interactiveRequest` is already set.

**2. Startup cannot recover from a token that the server rejects**

At startup the cached WorkIQ token returns HTTP 401. The CLI then asks the broker for a new token, and the broker returns the same token. The connection fails:

```
[WARNING] the Entra account broker returned the rejected access token {"server_url":"https://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/mcp"}
[ERROR] OAuth authentication failed for workiq: MCPOAuthError: Microsoft Entra sign-in for https://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/mcp failed: Entra broker error: the broker returned the rejected access token
```

This repeats on every new session. A token that the broker issued about 30 minutes earlier, and that WorkIQ accepted then, was rejected in the later session. The 1.0.101 changelog says *explicit* sign-in recovers from rejected cached tokens. The automatic startup and refresh path does not recover. While the WorkIQ request holds the broker, it also blocks the ADO request (problem 1).

The tenant enforces a Conditional Access sign-in frequency policy. Other Entra clients on the same machine report AADSTS70043. I suspect this is why tokens that are still within their lifetime get rejected.

### Expected behavior

- The CLI queues or serializes concurrent broker sign-ins across MCP servers instead of failing them.
- When a server rejects the token the broker returns, the startup and refresh path bypasses the broker's cached token (for example with a forced refresh or a claims request) or falls back to interactive sign-in. It should not fail the connection.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.103

### Environment

- macOS 27.0.1 (Apple silicon)
- Microsoft Enterprise SSO extension (Company Portal) installed
- Remote HTTP MCP servers: Azure DevOps remote MCP (`mcp-config.json`, no `oauthClientId`) and the WorkIQ plugin (`workiq@work-iq`)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the Azure DevOps remote MCP server and install the WorkIQ plugin.
2. Sign in to both once, then wait until the cached tokens are rejected (in this tenant, roughly 30 minutes or more).
3. Start a new `copilot` session.
4. Neither server loads tools. The logs show the errors above.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Cross-project session browsing and first-class non-git project folders (consolidates #17842, #16116, #15192)
issues.body:
The earlier requests for this (#17842, #16116, #15192) were auto-closed by the stale-issue bot as not planned, with a note that new issues are welcome if the need is still real. It is, so I am consolidating them into one.

My workflow: many small project folders on one machine. Some are git repos, several are intentionally not (tooling, docs, synced folders). OpenCode already stores the launch directory on every session, so the grouping data exists. Three things make it hard to actually use:

1. The session picker is scoped to the current directory. There is no way to browse or search sessions across projects without cd-ing into each folder first. A comment on #16116 notes that `listSessionsGlobal` was added to the internal API for CLI and TUI builds, but no client surfaces a grouped-by-project view, and the Desktop app has no global list at all.

2. Non-git folders get inconsistent treatment across clients. Their sessions sometimes pool under a global project, and Desktop has had reports (#29621) of non-git directories not appearing even though their sessions exist. A directory containing `opencode.json` or a `.git` directory should be treated as a local project, as requested in #15192.

3. Renaming or moving a folder on disk orphans its sessions. A stable project marker (an id stored in `opencode.json`, or re-association by path) would let sessions follow their project.

What would solve most of this:

- A cross-project session view: an `--all` / global mode on the session picker, grouped by project, in both the TUI and Desktop.
- `opencode.json` as an explicit project marker for non-git folders.
- Re-association of sessions when a project directory moves.

Thank you. OpenCode is otherwise the nicest session model of the terminal agents I use, and these gaps are the only place I still lose conversations.

issues.title: acp: every session method hangs forever on Windows (Bun fetch starved by the /global/event SSE stream)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/ide-acp
labels.description: Editor integrations and ACP

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
### Description

On Windows, `opencode acp` completes the `initialize` handshake, but every method that goes through the embedded SDK (`session/new`, `session/list`, ...) hangs forever — no timeout, no error, no log progress. The TUI is fine.

Root cause: Bun's `fetch` on Windows never completes a request once the process holds an open streaming HTTP response. The ACP server keeps a long-lived SSE subscription to its own embedded server (`acp/event.ts`, the `global event connected` log line) through the same SDK client that `session/new` uses for its 5 concurrent HTTP calls (`loadDirectorySnapshot` in `acp/service.ts`). Those requests are never dispatched, so the RPC hangs. Reproduces on 1.15 → 1.19.6, with a clean config, clean data dir, and `--pure`, with or without a system proxy.

Minimal repro of the runtime bug (bun 1.4.2 / 1.4.4 on Windows; node 23 on the same machine finishes in 12ms):

```js
const sse = await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:23457/events")
;(async () => { const r = sse.body.getReader(); for(;;){ const {done} = await r.read(); if (done) break } })()
const rs = await Promise.allSettled(
  Array.from({length: 5}, () => fetch("http://127.0.0.1:23457/x", { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(8000) })),
)
// bun: 5x rejected (timeout, requests never reach the server)
// node: 5x fulfilled
```

Notes:
- not proxy related (`NO_PROXY` makes no difference), not origin-pool related (different origins starve too, `Connection: close` is ignored)
- not server related: node server + bun client fails, bun server + node client works
- an open streaming response is enough — the body does not even need to be consumed
- `node:http` in the same bun process is unaffected

Possibly related: #7112 (windows-specific, Zed agent window never loads), zed-industries/zed#65624.

### Plugins

oh-my-openagent (reproducible with `--pure`, so unrelated)

### OpenCode version

v1.19.6 (also verified on 1.19.4, 1.19.1, 1.19.0, 1.18.35, 1.17.10, 1.16.2, 1.15.13)

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows: `opencode acp` (any 1.15+ build)
2. Send the ACP `initialize` request over stdio — responds fine
3. Send `session/new` — never responds

### Operating System

Windows 11 Pro 26100 (build 26300)

issues.title: server: every location load re-subscribes file watchers on / and each home-directory ancestor

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.name: area/core
labels.description: Agent loop, tools and config

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/macos
labels.description: macOS

labels.name: platform/linux
labels.description: Linux

issues.body:
## Summary

Each time the background service loads a location (a project or worktree directory), it subscribes file watchers on the filesystem root (`type=entries`, no ignores) and on every ancestor directory up to the user's home, plus the global config directories. The same set is subscribed again for every location and for each request span, so a busy service logs hundreds of identical `watcher subscribe` lines per minute.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.0 (`opencode --version`: v2.3.0)
- OS: Darwin 25.6.0 (arm64)
- Terminal: Ghostty
- Shell: fish
- Install/channel: latest (release)
- Active plugins: 35 third-party plugins (names withheld); none of them touch the file watcher.
- Model: Claude Opus 5.5 (Global), as reported by the harness

## Reproduction

1. Run the background service (`opencode serve --service`) with several projects or worktrees nested under the home directory.
2. Open sessions in two or more of those directories, or let subagents create worktrees there.
3. Search `opencode.log` for `message="watcher subscribe"` with `role=server`.

## Expected Behavior

A location subscribes watchers for its own directory, and shared parent or global directories are subscribed once per service, not once per location and request.

## Actual Behavior

- Each location load logs these subscriptions:
  - `watcher subscribe path=/ type=entries ignores=0`;
  - one entry per ancestor (`/<home-root>`, `/<home-root>/<user>`, and every intermediate directory);
  - the global config and install directories.
- The identical set repeats under different `http.span` values within the same second (for example spans 315, 322 and 337 at one timestamp).
- In one busy two-minute window the service logged between 264 and 952 `watcher subscribe` lines.

## Additional Context

- Seen on every location load throughout a day of normal use, so it reproduces consistently.
- Watching `/` with `type=entries` and no ignores looks wider than needed. If each subscription holds a native watch, the count grows with every location the service loads.
- No workaround tried.

issues.body:
### Description

On Windows 11, when I ask the agent to run two shell commands in the same step, one of them never starts:

Command failed: Write-Output REP-ONE: failed to spawn
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe: 拒绝访问。 (os error 5)

The other call in the same step completes normally. Serial shell calls have never failed for me (dozens of commands today), and exit code is still 0 even when the tool call fails.

Controlled run: 6 rounds of the same prompt, 2 shell calls per round. 12 calls total, 6 succeeded, 6 failed, and every single round had exactly one failure. Which one fails is random (sometimes the first, sometimes the second).

This is not specific to the desktop app. `opencode run` from a clean process tree (both apps' pwsh processes fully gone) reproduces it, and the desktop app and the CLI share one `opencode-pty` daemon, so I believe the race is in the daemon's spawn path. Two pty daemons were running at the time (service.json shows protocol: 9, different instance ids), and the error appears from both clients.

Things I checked that are not the cause:

- The App Execution Alias itself works: spawning "...\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe" 10 times in a row from a plain shell succeeded 10/10.
- Concurrent AppX activation is fine: 6 Start-Process of the same alias at once succeeded 6/6.
- No process buildup: Get-Process pwsh showed a single process while calls were failing.
- Not the command text: the failing command is a bare Write-Output.
- Not other agents or terminals: keeping a non-opencode pwsh alive changes nothing (test passes).
- Not PATH: removing both WindowsApps directories from PATH before launching does not help, the daemon still tries the alias path, so it does not resolve the shell through PATH when spawning.

Workaround I use now: keep shell calls serial, do parallel work inside one command (ForEach-Object -Parallel, Start-Job, Start-Process). Starting the daemon over makes single calls work again but parallel calls still fail.

### Plugins

None

### OpenCode version

2.3.2 (desktop 2.3.2.0, CLI opencode v2.3.2)

### Steps to reproduce

On Windows with Microsoft Store-installed PowerShell 7 (pwsh.exe resolved via AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps), start an OpenCode session (either desktop app or opencode run).

Ask the agent to invoke the shell tool twice in parallel in a single turn, e.g.:
Please execute the shell tool TWICE in parallel in this single turn: 1) shell command 'Write-Output PARA-ONE' 2) shell command 'Write-Output PARA-TWO'. Do both simultaneously.

Observe the tool results: exactly one shell command succeeds, while the other fails at process spawn with:
failed to spawn C:\Users<user>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe: 拒绝访问。 (os error 5)

### Screenshot

### Operating System

Windows 11 (build 26100)

OpenCode Desktop built-in terminal / Windows Terminal (using Store-installed PowerShell 7, pwsh.exe)

issues.title: read: AGENTS.md lookup follows symlinks out of the project and re-injects instructions already loaded
