labels.name: platform/nix
labels.description: Nix or NixOS

issues.body:
### Description

When the read tool reads a file through a symlink, the nearby-`AGENTS.md` lookup walks up from the link's target instead of from the path inside the project. If the target is in another tree, the walk never reaches the session directory (the `stop`), so it keeps going and injects every `AGENTS.md` above the target.

In `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/read.ts` the walk starts at `dirname(fs.resolve(target))`. The filter after it drops files whose directory contains the session directory, comparing resolved paths. A project whose own `AGENTS.md` is a symlink into that other tree gets that file injected again on every such read, although it's already in the startup instructions. The ledger in `SessionInstructions` only knows earlier read-time injections, not the startup ones.

On our host, project skills and memory files are symlinks into a config repo (`~/dev/xai/.agents/skills/x/SKILL.md` -> `/etc/nixos/agents/nikita/projects/xai/skills/x/SKILL.md`), and the project's `AGENTS.md` lives there too. In one day, reads of those files re-injected the project's `AGENTS.md` 61 times in sessions that already had it, and the user's global instructions file, which happens to sit two levels up at `/etc/nixos/agents/nikita/AGENTS.md`, 21 times. It has happened every day since at least 2.2.x.

Walking up the path as the model gave it (still resolving each found file to dedup), or skipping files that are already in the session's startup instructions, would avoid both.

### Plugins

none needed (seen with cursor-opencode-provider and our claude-compat plugin)

### OpenCode version

2.3.2 (same code on `dev` 47fcf735)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Make `store/proj/AGENTS.md`, `store/AGENTS.md` and `store/proj/skills/s/SKILL.md` outside the project.
2. In the project, symlink `AGENTS.md` -> `store/proj/AGENTS.md` and `.agents/skills` -> `store/proj/skills`.
3. Start a session in the project and have it read `.agents/skills/s/SKILL.md`.
4. A synthetic message injects both `store/proj/AGENTS.md` (the project's own instructions, already in the system prompt) and `store/AGENTS.md` (outside the project).

As a test in `packages/core/test/session-instructions.test.ts`:

```ts
it.live("a symlink into another tree injects no AGENTS.md from above the link target", () =>
  Effect.gen(function* () {
    const location = yield* Location.Service
    const dir = location.directory
    const store = yield* Effect.promise(() => fs.mkdtemp(path.join(path.dirname(dir), "store-")))
    yield* mkdir(path.resolve(store, "proj", "skills", "s"))
    yield* writeAgents(path.resolve(store, "AGENTS.md"), "store-instructions")
    yield* writeAgents(path.resolve(store, "proj", "AGENTS.md"), "root-instructions")
    yield* Effect.promise(() => fs.writeFile(path.resolve(store, "proj", "skills", "s", "SKILL.md"), "skill"))
    yield* Effect.promise(() => fs.symlink(path.resolve(store, "proj", "AGENTS.md"), path.resolve(dir, "AGENTS.md")))
    yield* mkdir(path.resolve(dir, ".agents"))
    yield* Effect.promise(() => fs.symlink(path.resolve(store, "proj", "skills"), path.resolve(dir, ".agents", "skills")))

    const session = yield* Session.Service
```

issues.title: Feature: Hold-spacebar push-to-talk voice input (like Claude Code)
issues.body:
## Feature Request

**What:** Hold-spacebar-to-record voice input, like Claude Code has. Hold the spacebar down to record from the microphone, release to transcribe and submit.

**Why:** Claude Code has this feature and it's a major UX advantage for hands-free coding. You can dictate code changes, ask questions, and give instructions without typing. The current keybind system only supports press events, not hold-and-release, so this can't be done via a plugin.

**Current workaround:** I built a plugin that registers a `voice_transcribe` custom tool and a `/voice` command. It works but requires typing `/voice` each time, which defeats the hands-free purpose.

**How it could work:**
1. On spacebar key-down, start recording from the default microphone (ffmpeg/avfoundation on macOS, pulseaudio on Linux)
2. On spacebar key-up, stop recording, transcribe (local whisper or API), and inject the text into the prompt input
3. User can review and hit Enter to submit, or just auto-submit

**Implementation notes:**
- The TUI keybind system currently only handles key press events, not hold-and-release. This would need a new keybind type or a dedicated voice input subsystem.
- Transcription could use whisper-cpp (local, no API key needed) or an API. Local is better for latency and privacy.
- macOS has avfoundation for mic access; Linux has pulseaudio/alsa. Both work with ffmpeg.
- The spacebar is currently used for `dialog.mcp.toggle` and `plugins.toggle` in dialogs, so the hold-to-record should only activate when the prompt input is focused and empty (or always, with a different key if there's a conflict).

**Related:** This is similar to what Cursor and Claude Code both offer. It's becoming table stakes for AI coding tools.

issues.body:
- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

## Feature: first-class local push-to-talk dictation with active-chat routing in the TUI

I'd like OpenCode to support **local, offline push-to-talk dictation** as a first-class feature (or with enough plugin API support to make it reliable): hold a hotkey, speak, release, and have the transcript inserted/submitted into the chat that was active when recording started.

### Why this is different from the existing voice requests

Related issues (#33300, #35219, and the now-duplicated #53977) ask for voice input in general. This request is specifically about two hard parts that a normal plugin cannot currently solve well:

1. **Hold-to-record without hold-aware keybinds.** OpenCode's keybind system handles key *press* events, not key-down/key-up. The workaround is a global evdev listener (e.g. Right Alt) outside the TUI. A first-party implementation could expose press/release keybind events or a small voice-input subsystem so plugins don't need root-adjacent `input`-group access.
2. **Chat routing.** If the user switches tabs or apps while speaking, the transcript must still land in the chat that was active when recording *started*. Today this needs a localhost bridge that writes a short-lived target (session id/title/project) and calls `opencode api POST /api/session/<id>/prompt` on delivery.

### Reference implementation

I maintain a working kit for Arch/Hyprland that implements exactly this flow, and would be happy for the OpenCode team to use it as a reference point:

**https://github.com/Rocketkid300/opencode-voice-kit**

How it works:

- `whisper.cpp` (`opencode-voice` crate) transcribes locally — no API key, no cloud, no audio uploaded.
- A global Right-Alt evdev hotkey handles push-to-talk (no TUI hold-keybind support needed).
- A small Python bridge on `127.0.0.1:4096` reads a short-lived `target.json` written by the TUI plugin and delivers the transcript via `opencode api` to the originating session; it falls back to `wtype` only when there is no active chat.
- The TUI plugin shows live state in the prompt footer (`● voice`, `REC 2.4s`, `transcribing`, `sending`, `error`) and exposes `/voice on|off|restart|toggle` plus `Ctrl+Alt+V`.
- Routing state contains only session IDs, titles, and project directories — never audio.

It is tested on Arch Linux + Hyprland with OpenCode v2 and is fully offline (the only network access is the one-time local model download).

### Request

Please consider either:

- building this into OpenCode (local STT, push-to-talk, active-chat routing, footer state), or
- exposing plugin API hooks for hold/release keybind events and for injecting a prompt into a specific session, so community implementations like the one above don't need a separate evdev listener and localhost bridge.

Benefits: hands-free/accessibility support, privacy (no cloud), and lower latency for long prompts. This is becoming table stakes in AI coding tools.

issues.title: desktop: session tabs are lost after a PC reboot (strip pruned before the bundled server registers)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/desktop
labels.description: Desktop app

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
## Description

After a **cold reboot of Windows**, the Desktop app opens with an empty session tab strip. The sessions themselves are intact (they are in the sidebar / session search), and pulling the app apart shows the tab state was written to disk — so this is not "state never saved": the strip is pruned on startup and the pruned (empty) list is written back, so the tabs never return.

The strip survives a normal "quit + relaunch" of the app. It is lost on a real machine reboot, which is also the path an auto-update takes (`background service starting { reason: 'missing' }`).

## Plugins

None (no plugins configured in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`).

## OpenCode version

2.3.2, desktop, windows x64 (channel `latest`). Also seen on 2.3.0 before the update.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In Desktop, open several sessions as tabs.
2. Reboot Windows (cold boot).
3. Start Desktop.
4. The session tab strip is empty; "Recently closed" still contains older entries.

## Screenshot

N/A (tab strip is simply empty; no error is shown).

## Operating System

Windows 11 10.0.26300.9974

## Terminal

Desktop app, no terminal.

## Additional context

The tab strip is persisted per window in the desktop's `drafts.sqlite` (`%APPDATA%/ai.opencode.desktop/drafts.sqlite`, table `state`):

- `opencode.window.<id>.dat | tabs` (JSON array of `{type:"session", server:"sidecar", sessionId}`)
- `opencode.window.<id>.dat | tabs.info`, `tabs.recent`, `tabs.panes`, `tabs.closed`

Right after a good start these keys hold a full strip (28 entries in my case, updated seconds after launch), so the write path works.

The startup timing looks like the trigger. From `logs/<timestamp>/main.log` (`<user>` and paths redacted):

```
[09:56:54.224] (main) main window visible { window: '...' }
[09:56:54.227] (main) starting v2 background service
[09:57:01.247] (main) v2 CLI background service starting { reason: 'missing' }
[09:57:02.827] (main) v2 CLI background service ready { version: '2.3.0', url: 'http://127.0.0.1:28894' }
```

and from `renderer.log` of the same launch:

```
[09:57:05.003] [warn] [server-request-queue] server thrashing detected [object Object]
[09:57:05.897] [debug] [tabs] update persisted session info [object Object]
[09:58:04.688] [warn] [server-request-queue] server thrashing detected [object Object]
```

In the renderer, the strip is filtered against the currently known servers and the filtered array is written back immediately:

```ts
M(() => {
  if (!tabsReady() || !infoReady() || !serversReady()) return
  const keys = knownServerKeys()               // servers.list + plugin servers
  const next = tabs.filter((tab) => keys.has(tab.server))
  if (next.length !== tabs.length) for (const tab of tabs) if (!keys.has(tab.server)) { dropInfo(tab); dropPanes(tab) }
  setTabs(() => next)                          // persisted right away
})
```

`server.list` in `opencode.global.dat` is persisted as `[]` — the bundled `sidecar` server is only added at runtime when the background service registers. So if `serversReady()` becomes true before the sidecar is registered (a cold boot, where the service is `missing` and needs ~8 s, is exactly that window), every tab is dropped and an empty array is persisted. When the sidecar appears a moment later there is nothing left to restore.

There is a second, related path: tabs whose session cannot be resolved are removed for good (the `abandon` event), which is the same symptom when the session lookup races the server start.

"Recently closed" (`tabs.closed`) is kept separately, so the only recovery is reopening tabs from there by hand.

Happy to test a build that waits for the bundled server (or that never prunes servers it has not seen yet) before rewriting the strip.

issues.body:
### Description

A tool result made of a single text part is sent as an array while the process is live, but as a plain string after a restart or `--session` resume. The text is identical; only the shape changes. The prompt-cache prefix ends at that item, so everything after it is re-sent uncached.

- Live: `packages/ai/src/tool-runtime.ts` L81–82 (`_legacyResult` branch) keeps `{ type: "content", value: [text] }`, which `lowerToolResultOutput` (`packages/ai/src/protocols/open-responses.ts` L641–651) sends as `"output": [{ "type": "input_text", ... }]`.
- Rebuilt: `toolResult` in `packages/core/src/session/runner/to-llm-message.ts` L114–130 collapses a single text part to `{ type: "text" }`, which is sent as `"output": "..."`.

On GPT-6.2 Sol this costs about 8–11k uncached tokens per restart. For example, one request read 30,464 of 39,070 prompt tokens from cache, where a request with an unchanged prefix would read about 39k. It happens on both the WebSocket and HTTP transports, and with other plugins' transforms disabled. 1.x sends a string in both cases.

Making both paths produce the same `ToolResultValue` should fix it. A test could compare a request built live with the same request rebuilt from stored state.

### Plugins

Any plugin tool that returns a single text part (seen with `@fro.bot/systematic`'s `systematic_skill`)

### OpenCode version

2.3.2 (c0ad18b); these lines are unchanged on `dev`

### Steps to reproduce

1. `opencode run --model openai/gpt-6.2-sol "<prompt that calls a plugin tool returning a single text part>"`
2. `opencode run --session <id> "<follow-up>"` (new process)
3. Compare `function_call_output` for that `call_id`: an array in the last request of step 1, a string in the first request of step 2. `cached_tokens` for the step 2 request stops at that item.

issues.title: [FEATURE]:Desktop: upgrade /btw into a docked side-chat panel with its own composer, history, and quote support
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

### What I want

`/btw` already exists in the desktop app (`Ask a side question` — "Get a one-shot answer without adding to the conversation"), but it is a read-only, one-shot side tab. I would like it to become a real side chat: a docked right-side panel with its own composer, follow-up questions, and persistent history — and with the quote popup able to feed it.

### Current behavior

- `/btw <question>` (or the `Ask a side question` command) opens a tab titled `/btw`. The panel shows one question and one answer, with Copy / Retry.
- The panel is read-only: it has no input box, so I cannot type a follow-up there. Every new question needs another `/btw ...`, which means another tab.
- Each tab keeps a single Q&A pair, and the store comment says it is "kept until its tab closes" — close the tab and both the question and the answer are gone (#50879).
- Nothing in the panel can carry the text I just selected in the timeline; I copy-paste it by hand.

### Proposed behavior

1. **A real side chat, docked.** `/btw` opens (or focuses) a right-side panel that stays open while the main conversation continues. Inside the panel there is a composer of its own: type a follow-up, get an answer, keep going in the same panel. Collapsible, remembers width and open state per session, restores after restart.
2. **History in the panel.** Consecutive Q&A pairs stay listed and scrollable in the panel, so a follow-up does not need a new tab and nothing is lost when the panel closes. Keep Copy / Retry per answer.
3. **Each question is still one-shot context.** The side chat keeps its own minimal context — what I explicitly attach plus, at most, the panel's own earlier turns. It must not inherit the main thread. Show a small context/token badge, and let me detach an item.
4. **Quote → side chat.** In the quote popup (the one introduced in 2.2.0), add a third action next to send / comment: "Ask in side chat". The quoted text plus my note becomes the side chat's next question. Dragging a quote into the panel does the same.
5. **Keybind and setting.** Toggle the panel from the command palette and a keybind (e.g. `mod+shift+B`). A setting can turn the docked panel off, falling back to today's behavior exactly.
6. **One panel, many threads (optional).** If several `/btw` conversations are open, host them as sub-tabs inside the docked panel rather than competing tabs in the side region (see #60233).

### Why this is cheap

Everything needed already exists: the side tab region, the per-session `chats` store inside the `btw` built-in plugin, the quote popup and composer note API, and the plugin panel registry (`Panel`, `ctx.layout.open(..., { background: true })`). This is turning a fixed one-shot tab into a panel with a composer and history, plus one more action in the quote popup.

### Acceptance criteria

- `/btw` opens a right-side docked panel; the main thread keeps its own context, apart from explicitly attached quotes.
- I can ask a follow-up inside the panel without opening a new tab, and the earlier Q&A stays visible.
- Quote popup → "Ask in side chat" → that text appears in the panel as the next question.
- Panel width, open state, and per-session conversations survive restart and session switching.
- Answers remain readable after the panel is closed and reopened.
- Turning the new panel off restores exactly today's behavior.

Related: #50879 (btw answer unrecoverable once its dialog closes), #60233 (sidebar tab UX), #56065 (side-question keybind does not enter /btw mode).

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, the OpenCode pre-push check can stall during Turbo hashing when run from a linked Git worktree. Official `dev` at `56dc95bff5f002321a12de5bbbe2783cd0c87e2a` pins Turbo 2.10.2 and runs `bun run check` from `.husky/pre-push`. The typecheck stage invokes Turbo.

## Reproduction

From a linked worktree checked out at that official commit, install with `bun install --frozen-lockfile`. Run the following from the worktree root in PowerShell (this is a dry run and does not push anything):

```powershell
$env:GIT_DIR = git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir
Remove-Item Env:GIT_WORK_TREE -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
bunx turbo typecheck --dry=json --concurrency=3
```

On the same Windows x64 checkout with Bun 1.4.4, Turbo 2.10.2 completed in 5.9 seconds without the explicit `GIT_DIR` and was still running after 30 seconds with the hook-style environment. The latter command was terminated after the timeout. In the original pre-push hang, Turbo's child Git status commands traversed dependency directories instead of using the linked worktree root. This affects contributors pushing from a linked worktree.

Expected: the same task graph completes with the Git hook environment. Related report: [vercel/turborepo#15081](https://github.com/vercel/turborepo/issues/15081). The fork is testing a pinned Turbo upgrade in [OpenCode.My#14](https://github.com/joe-ieta/OpenCode.My/pull/14).

As a comparison on the same unmodified official checkout, Turbo 2.11.11 completed the same dry run with the hook environment in 2.2 seconds. The test used its native executable directly with --skip-infer to prevent Turbo selecting the workspace's pinned version.

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: status/repro-simulated
labels.description: Reproduced with a simulated model or mock

labels.name: area/providers
labels.description: Providers and model lists

issues.body:
### Description

Gemini 3.x models on the Vercel AI Gateway provider (`vercel/google/gemini-4-neon`, `vercel/google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview`) fail most tool-calling turns with:

```
Error: reasoning start before end: reasoning-1
```

The session stops and does not recover.

OpenCode sends these models to the gateway's Anthropic Messages endpoint ([`vercel-ai-gateway.ts#L242`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.3.2/packages/ai/src/providers/vercel-ai-gateway.ts#L242)). For Gemini, that endpoint streams overlapping content blocks:

```
content_block_start  0  thinking   (thought summary)
content_block_start  1  thinking   (signature only)
content_block_stop   1
content_block_start  2  tool_use
content_block_stop   2
content_block_stop   0
```

The Anthropic Messages protocol passes the overlap through unchanged. `Lifecycle.reasoningStart` and `textStart` ([`lifecycle.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.3.2/packages/ai/src/protocols/utils/lifecycle.ts)) track open fragments in a set and do not close the open one. The session runner allows one open fragment and throws ([`publish-llm-event.ts#L181`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.3.2/packages/core/src/session/runner/publish-llm-event.ts#L181)).

#45789 and #50685 fixed this error class for OpenAI Responses and for AI SDK providers. #50685 states: "Native `@opencode/ai` protocols already normalize these boundaries through their lifecycle helpers (#45789)." But #45789 added the normalization inside the Responses parser, so the Anthropic Messages protocol does not normalize these boundaries. Any Anthropic-compatible server that overlaps blocks ends the session.

Related: #36892, #43312, #50662.

### OpenCode version

2.3.2

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run:

   ```sh
   opencode run -m 'vercel/google/gemini-4-neon#low' "Read the files in this directory, then summarize them. Plan carefully first."
   ```

   This failed with `reasoning start before end: reasoning-1` in 2 of 2 runs, in a directory with two small files.

2. To see the stream without OpenCode, run:

   ```sh
   curl -sN https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/messages \
     -H "authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
     -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
     -d '{"model":"google/gemini-4-neon","max_tokens":8000,"stream":true,
          "thinking":{"type":"adaptive"},"output_config":{"effort":"low"},
          "tools":[{"name":"shell","description":"Run a shell command","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"command":{"type":"string"}},"required":["command"]}}],
          "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"First write one short sentence saying what you will do. Then call the shell tool with: ls -la"}]}' \
     | grep '^data:' | cut -c7- \
     | jq -rc 'select(.type|test("content_block_(start|stop)")) | "\(.type) \(.index) \(.content_block.type // "")"'
   ```

   This printed overlapping blocks in 3 of 3 runs.

### Operating System

macOS 27.2.0 (arm64)

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Desktop mode with a dual-model auto review -> fix loop

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.description: Desktop app

issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

**Request.** A built-in desktop UI mode that runs two different models against the same change automatically: one model reviews, the other fixes, and the loop repeats until the reviewer is clean.

Typical flow:

1. Start the mode on the current working tree (or a branch/PR), pick a reviewer model and a fixer model.
2. The reviewer reads the diff and produces structured findings (file, line, severity, problem, suggested fix).
3. The fixer applies fixes for those findings.
4. The new diff goes back to the reviewer.
5. The loop ends when there are no blocking findings, a round limit is reached, the usage budget is spent, or the user presses Stop.

**Why it belongs in the UI.** The value is supervision: a round timeline, the findings list with `file:line`, a per-round diff, and buttons to accept or revert a round or stop the loop. Doing this today means copying findings between sessions by hand.

**What exists today and why it is not enough:**

- `/review` is a single prompt that runs in the current session with the session model. It does not fix anything and does not re-review.
- `/goal` keeps the agent working toward an objective, but there is no reviewer role and no model separation.
- Subagents and per-agent models exist, so a scripted loop is possible, but it needs a custom command or plugin, and there is still no UI for rounds, findings, or stop conditions.
- #1047 asked for a review -> fix -> review loop with subagents in 2025; it was closed by the stale bot, not implemented.
- #63631 (advisor tool) is related but different: it lets the working model consult a second model, not a persistent reviewer/fixer pair with a visible loop.

**Suggested minimal shape:**

- A "Review & fix" mode with two model pickers (reviewer / fixer) and a max-rounds setting.
- Reviewer output as a machine-readable findings list, rendered in the UI.
- Stop conditions: clean review, max rounds, token budget, manual stop.
- Optional: require approval before each fix round or before committing.

Version: OpenCode desktop 2.3.0 (Windows).

issues.body:
## Summary

On OpenCode Desktop, GUI plugin parts (`./gui-experimental`) are only loaded from the app's **own sidecar server**. When the user connects to a **remote** server, that server's plugins are listed under **Settings → Extensions → Plugins** but never get a GUI: the row has no on/off switch, and none of the plugin's contributions appear (command palette, titlebar pill, side panel, session-header slot). Installing the *same* plugin on the desktop machine (`This computer`) makes its GUI work, which confirms the cause.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.2 (desktop app and its bundled `opencode-cli`); remote server 2.3.1
- OS: macOS 13.7.8 (x86_64); remote server Linux 6.x (x64)
- Terminal: not applicable (desktop app)
- Shell: /usr/bin/zsh
- Install/channel: release (updater reports `up-to-date` at 2.3.2)
- Active plugins: remote server global `opencode.json` → `@inf-studio/collab@0.5.3` (ships server, `./tui`, `./gui-experimental`)

## Reproduction

1. On a remote server, install a plugin that ships `./gui-experimental` (bundle present: `dist/gui-experimental.cjs`).
2. In Desktop, connect to that server (server picker shows `This computer` plus the remote entry; remote is selected).
3. Open **Settings → Extensions → Plugins** → select the remote server.
4. Look at the plugin row, and search the command palette for the command the GUI part contributes.
5. Control: install the same plugin version on the desktop machine's own server (`This computer`) and repeat steps 3–4.

## Expected Behavior

Either the remote server's GUI parts load, or the row says GUI parts are unavailable for remote servers. The docs say the app "loads GUI entries from its own background server", and a plugin row normally shows "a switch that turns its GUI off".

## Actual Behavior

- Remote server: row shows name + icon only — **no GUI switch**, no version, no error text; no contributions anywhere.
- `This computer` with the same plugin: the GUI loads and its contributions appear (so the bundle and the plugin are fine).
- Server side is healthy for the remote plugin:
  - `GET /api/plugin` → `{"features":{"server":true,"tui":true,"gui":true},"state":{"status":"active"}}`
  - `GET /api/plugin/gui?id=<id>` → `401` without the desktop credential (expected; the main process holds it)

## Additional Context

Cause, read from the shipped app (`app.asar` → `out/main/host-*.js`, minified):

- the plugin host subscribes credentials for one endpoint: `D = () => pe()` (the local sidecar URL), and its `subscribe-credentials` branch uses `D()`;
- its credential helper only serves the sidecar: `ie(id)` returns local credentials for `id === 'sidecar'`, with a remote branch that the GUI host never calls;
- plugin enumeration then runs `client.plugin.list()` → filter `features.gui && state === 'active' && source.type !== 'builtin'` → `client.plugin.gui({id})` against that same endpoint.

So a remote server's plugins are enumerated elsewhere (the settings list) but their bundles are never fetched.

Suggested resolutions:

1. Load GUI entries from the server selected in the app (the bundles are already served there; the window already has `servers[].client` authenticated), or
2. Document the limitation and state it in the settings row, so plugin authors do not chase a GUI that cannot load.

Workaround in use: install the plugin on the desktop machine's own server and read remote data through `MountedSession.server.client` (the plugin's GUI then works while sessions live on the remote server).

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Let plugins check whether an action is already allowed without asking the user to approve it.

For example, a plugin might need to decide whether it can share information from a session. If sharing would need approval, the plugin can leave the information out. Just checking should never open an approval prompt.

The plugin API's `permission.assert` opens a prompt when the current rules require approval. OpenCode already has an internal check that answers this question without creating a request. prs.title: refactor(core): Code Mode files use the environment of the path they resolved
prs.body:
**A Code Mode program now reads and writes a file through the same route.**
In Code Mode the agent's program touches files through a `Bun` object (`Bun.file(...)`, `Bun.write(...)`). After #64774 its writes went through the environment of the path they resolved, but its reads, stats and deletes still went through the session's environment. Today those are the same environment, so nothing a user sees changes.

❌ **Before**
1. `Bun.write("notes.txt", ...)` writes through the environment of the resolved path.
2. `Bun.file("notes.txt").text()`, `stat()`, `exists()`, `delete()` and `Bun.Glob` go through the session's environment.
3. One file, two routes. They agree only because a session has one environment.

✅ **After**
1. Every file operation in Code Mode's `Bun` uses the environment of the path it resolved.
2. Nothing in it asks for the session's environment any more, so that is dropped from the services a Code Mode run needs.

🟰 **Behavior change:** none.

```diff
- host.files.read(handle.target.absolute, range)                        # the session's environment
+ handle.target.environment.files.read(handle.target.absolute, range)   # the file's own
  # same for stat, exists, delete, glob, and the checks before a write
```

📊 **Proof**

A new test runs a real Code Mode program with every resolved path placed in an in-memory environment, while a file of the same name sits on disk.

| The program… | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| writes `one`, then reads it back | ❌ reads the disk file | ✅ reads `one` |
| deletes the file | ❌ deletes the disk file | ✅ deletes the in-memory one; disk untouched |
| globs for the deleted file | ❌ finds the disk file | ✅ finds nothing |

The new test fails without the source change: 2 pass after, 1 of 2 before.

👀 **Read:** `packages/core/src/codemode/tool.ts` and `packages/core/src/session/context.ts`, where the environment is removed from the services handed to a Code Mode run. `Bun` looks its services up at run time, which the type checker does not track, so a leftover lookup would only fail when a program runs. There is none in `packages/core/src/codemode`. The existing test's setup moved into a shared helper so both tests use it. A wildcard glob through another environment is not covered by the new test, only a literal one. The rest is routine.

<sub>🔍 Follow-up to #64774 · no user reports · no flag: refactor with no behavior change</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`: no type errors
- `bun test test/tool-target-environment.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 2 pass, 0 fail
- `bun test test/tool-execute.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 37 pass, 0 fail
- `bun test test/tool-model-policy.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 7 pass, 0 fail
- New test against the previous source (with the environment still provided): fails, the program reads and deletes the disk file

</details>

prs.title: docs: add /goal command reference
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes #64805

### Type of change

- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The native `/goal` command shipped in v2.2.1 (PR #59437) but has no docs page. `/docs/goal/` returns 404, and `/docs/commands/` only covers user defined commands, so the built in command is undocumented and people install third party goal plugins instead. This adds a Goals page and puts it in the docs sidebar under Configure, right after Commands.

The page covers:

- starting a goal with `/goal <objective>`, including the 4000 character limit, optional surrounding quotes, and that a new objective replaces the one the session already has
- `/goal pause`, `/goal resume`, `/goal clear` and bare `/goal` for status, with the error each one answers with when it does not apply
- the automatic progress review that runs when the session would go idle, the five verdicts it can return, and what each one does
- the reasons a goal stops: user interrupt, server restart, the 50 round limit, three stalled rounds, 30 minutes idle while it waits on background work, a failed session, and a review request too large for the model
- where the goal shows in the terminal and in the desktop app

Source read for the behavior:

- `packages/core/src/plugin/goal.ts`: the command parser and subcommand handling, `MAX_OBJECTIVE`, `MAX_ROUNDS`, `MAX_STALLS`, `WAIT_LIMIT`, the idle hook, and the verdict handling
- `packages/core/src/plugin/goal/judge.txt`: the review prompt, the verdict shapes, and the rules it follows
- `packages/schema/src/goal.ts`: the goal state and its three status values
- `packages/tui/src/feature-plugins/prompt/goal.tsx` and `packages/gui-plugins/src/goal/renderer.tsx`: the status labels and the pause, resume and clear actions

Files changed:

- `services/site/src/docs/content/goal.mdx` (new)
- `services/site/src/docs/lib/navigation.ts`

`llms.txt` and the sitemap are generated from `docsSections` in `lib/navigation.ts` (`services/site/src/docs/lib/llms.ts`, `lib/sitemap.ts`), so the new entry is listed there without another edit.

### How did you verify your code works?

Not with the full build. Bun is not installed on this machine, so I did not run `bun src/docs/script/build.ts` or `bun typecheck`. The `check-docs` workflow builds the docs for this change, and its run is waiting for a maintainer to approve it.

What I did check, with a script over the changed files:

- the frontmatter keys match `services/site/src/docs/frontmatter.ts` (`title` and `description` only)
- the new nav slug `goal` resolves to the new content file, and every nav slug in `docsSections` still has a content page
- code fences are balanced, code blocks are `text` fences like the sibling pages, and the page adds no internal links, so the link check has nothing new to resolve
- no prose uses em dashes or double hyphens

### Screenshots / recordings

This is a new docs page, so a screenshot needs the docs build served locally, which I could not run here.

### Checklist

- [ ] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

Implemented with AI assistance and reviewed by the account owner.

prs.title: refactor(core): read tool calls its filesystem functions directly
prs.body:
**The read tool had two ways to read a file. Now it has one.**
After #64774, the read tool's filesystem service had no dependencies and only forwarded to plain functions, which the same tool already called directly for skill files. This removes the service. Nothing a user sees changes.

❌ **Before**
1. The read tool asks for a filesystem service at setup.
2. For a normal path it calls the service, which forwards to a plain function.
3. For a skill path it calls that same plain function directly.
4. The read tool's tests replace the service with a fake that returns canned results, so the real read code never runs in them.

✅ **After**
1. The read tool calls the plain function for every path.
2. The service, its interface and its layer are gone.
3. The read tool's tests run the real read code over an in-memory filesystem.

🟰 **Behavior change:** none.

```diff
- reader = ReadToolFileSystem.Service            # forwards to read(...) and files.list(...)
- reader.read(target.environment.files, path, ...)
- reader.list(target.environment.files, folder)
+ ReadToolFileSystem.read(target.environment.files, path, ...)
+ target.environment.files.list(folder)
```

📊 **Proof**

| Read tool tests | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| What answers a read | A fake returning canned results | The real read code over an in-memory filesystem |
| Paging, binary detection, folder listings | Asserted the arguments passed to the fake | Asserted on the real output |

Source is +6 −30 across four files; the rest of the diff is the test file. No new test: the existing 40 read tool tests now cover the real code path. The suggestion-ranking test was checked by deleting the sort it covers, which makes it fail.

👀 **Read:** `packages/core/test/tool-read.test.ts`, the `files` wrapper at the top. It turns `\` into `/` before the in-memory filesystem, which only understands `/` paths, so the tests behave the same on Windows. Windows unit tests do not run on pull requests, so that has been traced by hand and not run. Four expectations changed because the fake had hard-coded them: three media `uri` values are now the real file URL, a folder entry ends with the platform's separator, and the "not a file" message is the one the real code produces for that case. The rest is routine.

<sub>🔍 Follow-up to #64774 · no user reports · no flag: refactor with no behavior change</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`: no type errors
- `bun test test/tool-read.test.ts test/tool-read-filesystem.test.ts test/session-instructions.test.ts test/tool-target-environment.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 91 pass, 0 fail (after the first commit)
- `bun test test/tool-read.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 40 pass, 0 fail (after the last commit)
- With the sort in the suggestion ranking temporarily deleted: `bun test test/tool-read.test.ts -t "ranks same-folder"` fails, then passes again once restored

</details>

Addresses #60313 (Linux restart not verified live), #60191 (passkeys fail fast; no real passkey support). - **User agent:** Fixes #55730. - **Permissions:** Fixes #61238, Fixes #61609, Fixes #54044 (a configured or agent deny refuses every call; the tools stay listed, as on `dev`, and draft #64789 hides them; #53294 and #56869 are closed duplicates). - **Agent tools:** Fixes #61625, Fixes #64217, Fixes #55795. only their service workers stay. - A tab stays agent-driven until the person acts in it; there is no 30 s hand-back. - The pane may open by itself for a file the agent shows, or a web page with `focus: true`; prs.title: feat(mcp): trust private-network server certificates on first use
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Part of #40111. Stacked on #60039 (per-server `tls` config); once that lands, this diff is just the first-use flow.

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Trusting a private-network MCP server's self-signed certificate becomes a first-use decision instead of up-front TLS config:

1. The first connect to an `https` server at a private IP fails with the presented certificate — fingerprint, subject — and the command to trust it.
2. `opencode mcp trust <url>` shows the certificate's subject, validity, and fingerprint and asks for confirmation. `--yes` skips the confirmation (required without a terminal); `--force` is only needed to re-pin after the certificate rotated.
3. The pin is stored per project in a new `mcp_trusted_host` table (new migration). Later connects are pinned by fingerprint, so a rotated certificate fails the connection instead of being silently accepted, and certificates without IP SANs work because the fingerprint is the identity check.

The trust hint is only added for actual TLS verification failures (self-signed, expired, alt-name, and the Node-style codes); network, protocol, and HTTP failures keep their original message. Hostnames never qualify — the IP literal in the config is the trust boundary, not DNS. An explicit `tls` config takes precedence.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/core/test/mcp-trust.test.ts`: private-host classifier, per-project store, first-use → trust → reconnect, rotation → re-pin with `--force`, and an appliance certificate without IP SANs.
- `packages/server/test/mcp-trust.test.ts` (end-to-end over HTTP), `packages/cli/test/mcp-auth-choices.test.ts`, 56 TLS tests, 92 schema and 10 protocol tests.
- `tsc` clean in schema/core/protocol/client/server/cli; `bun run migration --check` passes.

prs.title: feat(mcp): support per-server TLS trust for remote MCP servers
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Part of #40111

Related: #23506, #14696, #26862, #1694

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Adds an optional `tls` block to remote MCP server config, so a server with a self-signed or private-CA certificate can be trusted for that one server without changing verification anywhere else (no `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`):

- `ca_file` / `ca_pem`: PEM CA bundle, from a file (with `~` or workspace-relative paths) or inline, or both.
- `fingerprint`: pins the exact certificate the server presents, like an SSH host key. OpenCode compares the presented certificate against the fingerprint and then uses the fingerprint as the identity check for the connection. Name matching is deliberately not enforced: LAN appliance certificates often omit the IP SAN a hostname check would require (a self-signed `CN=OPNsense` with no SANs is the common case), and the fingerprint already identifies the certificate.

The TLS options are scoped to the fetch used by that server's transport. A missing CA file or a fingerprint mismatch fails the connect with a specific error instead of the first request. Docs: new "TLS Trust" section on the MCP servers page.

### How did you verify your code works?

- 56 tests in `packages/core/test/mcp-tls.test.ts`: unit coverage for PEM/fingerprint/path validation, plus integration tests that connect a real MCP server over TLS with fixture certificates, including a new appliance-style certificate that has a CN and no SAN (the case a name check rejects).

prs.title: feat(core): auto-update plugins written as name@latest
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A plugin written as `name@latest` now updates on its own. Everything else keeps today's behavior: checked, shown as outdated, and installed with `opencode plugin update`.

```text
"foo@latest"                       → checks on startup + every 24h, installs, hot-reloads
"foo", "foo@^1.2", "foo@next"      → notify only (unchanged)
"foo@1.2.3"                        → pinned, never checked (unchanged)
```

- An update reloads the plugin through the existing reload path, so there's no restart.
- If a newer version fails to load, the running one already stayed in memory, but the broken one stayed newest on disk and a restart loaded it. Now that version is marked rejected (`Npm.reject`), so a restart loads the previous one, for manual updates too. Its files stay until they expire, since the npm cache is shared by every location and process that may still run it, and it's only rejected if it's still the newest under the install lock.
- Each `@latest` plugin gets one automatic attempt per check (24h), so an update that fails isn't retried on every reload.
- Disabled plugins aren't updated.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New supervisor test: with updates available for `x@latest`, `x`, `x@^1.0.0` and `x@next`, only `x@latest` is updated, and only once.
- New npm test: rejecting makes the previous install current, keeps the rejected files, and does nothing unless the given version is the newest.
- `packages/core` supervisor, reload and npm tests pass, and so does `bun run check`.

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(app): bundle OpenMono as the default mono font
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

OpenMono becomes the app's bundled default font for code and for the terminal. It replaces IBM Plex Mono (code) and JetBrainsMono Nerd Font Mono (terminal). OpenMono is built on [Iosevka](https://github.com/be5invis/Iosevka); its terminal icons come from [Nerd Fonts](https://github.com/ryanoasis/nerd-fonts).

- `monoDefault` and `terminalDefault` are `"OpenMono"`. A stored font choice does not change: an empty value follows the new default, and a typed name (the old defaults included) still goes first, with OpenMono as its fallback.
- The files are the app build of OpenMono Nerd 1.000: no ligatures, every character one cell wide, in Regular, Bold and Italic. Regular covers weights 100 to 599 and Bold covers 600 to 900.
- The app's `@font-face` rules take the name ahead of an installed OpenMono, which has ligatures.
- The `@font-face` rules state the font's typographic line metrics (ascender 965, descender 285, no gap). Without them macOS reads the files' `hhea` table (descender 220), and inline code backgrounds and terminal rows become 17px instead of 18px. The overrides can go if the font's `hhea` table ever matches its typographic metrics.
- Settings › About › Third-party notices lists OpenMono and the Nerd Fonts icon sets with their licenses.
- Bold Italic is not bundled. The app's own code never asks for it; a terminal program that does gets the Italic file made bold, as it got a slanted Bold before.

**Terminal redraw**

The icons are now a file of their own, so an icon that the terminal draws before that file arrives stays a missing-glyph box, because the canvas only redraws rows that change. The terminal now draws every row again when a font file finishes loading; `draws terminal icons whose font file arrives after the first paint` in `e2e/regression/terminal.spec.ts` holds the icons file until the terminal has painted, and fails without the redraw.

**How the files load**

Each style has a text file. The icons are the same in every style, so all styles share one icons file. Text and icons have no character in common, and `unicode-range` decides which file a character needs:

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "OpenMono";
  src: url("/assets/OpenMono-Bold-text.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 600 900;
  unicode-range: U+20-2387, U+2500-25FF, /* … */ U+F882-1FBE7;
}

/* One rule like this for each style, all with the same file. */
@font-face {
  font-family: "OpenMono";
  src: url("/assets/OpenMono-icons.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 600 900;
  unicode-range: U+23FB-23FE, U+2630-2665, /* … */ U+F0001-F1AF0;
}
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  app[App starts] --> text["Regular text, 100 KB"]
  code[Bold or italic code] --> styles["Bold or Italic text, 100 or 112 KB"]
  term[A terminal opens] --> icons["Icons, 1.06 MB, one request for all styles"]
  icons --> redraw[Terminal draws its rows again]
```

**File sizes**

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code font that loads with the app | 46 KB | 100 KB |
| Font that loads when a terminal opens | 1,061 KB | 1,061 KB |
| Mono font files in the build | 2,252 KB | 1,373 KB |

- Added to `packages/app/public/assets`: three text files (100 KB, 100 KB, 112 KB), `OpenMono-icons.woff2` (1,061 KB) and `OpenMono-OFL.txt` (4 KB).
- Removed: the two JetBrainsMono Nerd Font files (1,061 KB and 1,047 KB), the three IBM Plex Mono files the build took from `@ibm/plex` (145 KB), and the `@ibm/plex` dependency of `packages/app`.
- The build's mono fonts are 878 KB smaller than on `dev`.

**Feature flag**

No flag guards this change. The app does not read the flag registry, because the client must not depend on Core. A flag would also need both font sets in the build. The earlier default-font change (#44876) shipped without a flag. A user who wants another font types its name in Settings › Appearance.

**How to refresh the font files**

```sh
cd packages/app
bun script/openmono.ts <app-nerd build folder>
```

The script copies the three text files, the Regular build's icons file and the license. It copies nothing and says why when the icons files of the build's styles differ in code points, outlines or horizontal metrics, or when the build's `unicode-range` values or copyright lines differ from the ones in the app.

**Known limits**

- Safari ignores the three metric overrides. In the web app there, inline code backgrounds are 17px tall instead of 18px.
- A bold italic terminal cell uses the Italic file made bold by the browser.

### How did you verify your code works?

- The DevTools protocol reports the rendered font of code blocks, inline code, diffs and shell output as `OpenMonoNerd-*` from the app's `@font-face` rules. A canvas has no such report, so the terminal's text, symbols and icons were checked in an element with the terminal's font. The test machine has OpenMono installed, and the same family name in a page without the rules resolves to the installed font.
- Icons in regular, bold, italic and bold italic text all come from the one icons file, with no system font, and the page requests that file once.
- A session with code only requests the text files. The icons file is requested when a terminal opens.
- Code block, paragraph and shell output heights, inline code height and the terminal cell (8.4px by 18px) are the same as on `dev`.
- The screenshots use the e2e mock server on macOS. I did not check a live shell, the packaged desktop app, Windows or Linux.

### Issue for this PR

No issue. This follows the release of OpenMono 1.000.

### Type of change

### What does this PR do?

The website and the docs (`services/site`) set their mono text in OpenMono, Anomaly's typeface, built on Iosevka by Belleve Invis (SIL OFL 1.1). The files come from the OpenMono 1.000 build.

- **Family name.** `"OpenMono"` in CSS, with the metric-matched stand-ins renamed to `"OpenMono Menlo"`, `"OpenMono Consolas"` and `"OpenMono Courier"`. The previous family name is gone from the service, and `test/fonts.test.ts` now fails if it comes back.
- **Same letters as Desktop.** `src/docs/assets/fonts/OpenMono-{Regular,Bold,Italic,BoldItalic}.woff2` are byte-for-byte the text files that OpenCode Desktop bundles (no ligatures, every character one cell). `script/openmono.py` subsets them for the web, as the previous script did.
- **Layout does not move.** Units per em, advance (600), ascender, descender, line gap, x-height and cap height are identical, so every size, weight, tracking, line height and the fallback overrides stay as they are. Of the 1,320 characters the site served before, the upright styles change the shape of C, c, G and the letters built on them (29 characters, terminals 0.002 em longer). The italics slant 11.8° where they slanted 12°, and their C, c and G terminals move 0.02 em. `⥈` and `⬰` are now one cell wide.
- **Weights.** Unchanged: Regular draws 100 to 500 and Bold draws 600 to 900. Section titles keep their 0.2 px stroke as the stand-in for Medium.
- **Ligatures.** Off, as before: the source has none and the subsets keep only `ccmp`, `locl`, `mark` and `mkmk`.
- **Cyrillic.** OpenMono has Cyrillic, so the Russian and Ukrainian pages now set mono text in OpenMono and not in the system font. It is a file of its own (`cyrillic`, Regular and Bold) so those pages fetch 18 kB and not the whole `rest` file. The italics have no Cyrillic file: no page sets Cyrillic in mono italic, and two more faces put the docs stylesheet over its 30 kB budget. It is at 30,701 of 30,720 bytes.
- **Settings.** `monoFontRevision` goes to 3, so a mono font saved on the development server resets to OpenMono once.
- **Credits.** `humans.txt` credits OpenMono, Iosevka by Belleve Invis, and the licence. `src/asset/fonts/OpenMono-OFL.txt` carries the copyright lines of the build.
- **Link cards.** `script/og.ts` renders its four cards (`/product/browse`, the changelog release card, and the two legal documents) with the new files. `src/asset/og/release.jpg` is captured again from this branch; inside the card's crop it differs from the old still only by the font. The two legal stills stay: those pages have changed since the stills were made, so a new capture changes more than the font.
- **Brand rules for agents** (`/brand.md`). One new rule: turn OpenMono's code ligatures off, because the released family has them on and OpenCode shows none.
- **Terminal captures.** `script/capture-assets.ts` records the Terminal screenshots and product video cuts with VHS and an installed font. Its default is now OpenMono Nerd, the terminal family: the status marks come from the font, and arrows and the ellipsis are one cell wide. VHS draws each cell on its own, so neither family shows ligatures.
- **Badges.** The 160 `-mono` badge files are not redrawn. Their text is outlines, and only the C of OpenCode differs, by 0.002 em: 0.02 px on the 20 px badge and 0.05 px on the 44 px one.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Regular Latin (preloaded on every page) | 19,084 | 27,280 |
| Bold Latin | 18,700 | 26,880 |
| All served files | 193,076 (8 files) | 296,972 (10 files) |
| Source files in the repo | 250,508 | 424,316 |

The Latin files are larger because the build stores accented letters as full outlines, not as components.

**Feature flag.** None. The site reads no flags, and a typeface cannot be half on: both families would have to ship. The gate was the font's release, and OpenMono 1.000 is out.

**Refresh the fonts** after a font build, from `services/site`:

```sh
uvx --from 'fonttools[woff]==4.60.1' python script/openmono.py path/to/app-nerd
```

**Follow-ups**, after this merges:

- Export the 13 OG Studio cards again, with their 13 videos and 153 locale cards (`src/asset/og-studio/manifest.json`). They are made by hand in OG Studio and are not part of this PR.
- Capture `src/asset/og/privacy-policy.jpg` and `terms-of-service.jpg` again, as a change of their own.

prs.title: refactor(core): file tools use the environment of the path they resolved
prs.body:
**The file tools now ask the path they resolved where it lives, instead of assuming the session's one environment.**
An environment is where files are read and commands run: the local disk, or a remote workspace. Today a session has exactly one, and every tool captures it when the tool is set up. This is groundwork for letting a single tool call reach a different machine than the session's own. Nothing can do that yet.

❌ **Before**
1. A tool turns a path into a target: an absolute path plus what to ask permission for.
2. It then reads and writes that path through the session's environment, which it captured at setup.
3. So "which machine does this path live on" has no place to be answered. It is always "the session's".

✅ **After**
1. A tool turns a path into a target, and the target carries its environment.
2. `read`, `edit`, `write` and `patch`, and the services they write through, use the target's environment.
3. Path resolution still hands every target the session's environment, so the answer is the same as before. It is now answered in one place.

🟰 **Behavior change:** none.

```diff
- environment = session's environment            (captured when the tool is set up)
- target      = resolve(path)
- environment.files.read(target.absolute)
+ target      = resolve(path)                    (target.environment = session's environment)
+ target.environment.files.read(target.absolute)
```

**The live object on the target is a step, not the end shape.** A target should stay a plain value that names where a file lives, and one filesystem should take that name and route to the right place, so call sites read `files.read(place)`. That needs a list of environments to look the name up in, which does not exist yet. This PR does the part that is needed either way: no file tool assumes the session’s environment any more.

**Not yet through the target.** These still use the session's environment or the host directly. They are identical today and each needs the same treatment before a target can point anywhere else:

| Still on the session or the host | Where |
|---|---|
| Running the command | the shell tool; only its working-directory check moved |
| Search | `grep`, `glob` |
| Formatting after a write | `edit`, `write`, `patch` |
| Finding nested `AGENTS.md` after a read | `read` |
| A move between two environments | `patch` assumes both ends share one |
| Code Mode's file reads | its writes already go through the target |
| Image and video tools, MCP | untouched |

📊 **Proof**

The new test points every target at an in-memory environment, while a file with the same name sits on disk, then runs the real `write`, `read`, `edit` and `patch` tools.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| The in-memory file ends with the last edit | ✅ |
| The file on disk is untouched | ✅ |
| The diffs the tools report, and the permission preview, show the in-memory content | ✅ |

The test fails without the change: pointing any one of three reads back at the session (the preview read in `write`, and the read after the write in `edit` and in `patch`) fails it, each on its own assertion.

👀 **Read:** `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/patch.ts`. Each pending update now keeps its target beside its content, so the write, the move and the formatting pass each use the right file’s environment. The formatting pass walks the same files in the same order as before. `FileMutation` and the read tool's filesystem service no longer depend on the environment, so their layers build from nothing. The rest is routine.

<sub>🔍 First step of the multi-machine plan · no user reports · no flag, because nothing behaves differently</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

From `packages/core`:

- `bun typecheck`: no type errors
- `bun test test/tool-target-environment.test.ts` (new): 1 pass, 0 fail
- `tool-read` 40 pass · `tool-read-filesystem` 42 pass · `tool-edit` 21 pass · `tool-write` 10 pass · `tool-patch` 43 pass
- `file-mutation` 9 pass · `file-access` 7 pass · `file-access-path` 22 pass · `session-instructions` 8 pass · `tool-execute` 37 pass
- `tool-shell`: 96 pass, 2 fail. The two (`conditional substitutions respect once` and `respect always`) fail the same way on `dev` without this change on the Mac they ran on, with `wait: pid … is not a child of this shell`.

</details>

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #60883

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

A new session starts as a draft, but the draft route mounted neither the session screen nor the side region. Review and every session-scoped panel were therefore unreachable until the first message created a Session.

This mounts the shared session screen and side region on the draft route. The draft already carries its workspace directory, so the existing screen can bind to it without a second layout or a new workspace-scoped panel API. Panels opt in with `Panel.drafts`; Review opts in and reads the draft's workspace. The draft reserves its session id before the first message, so the Review tabs keep the same key when the draft becomes a Session and stay open. Session-only lookups stay unchanged unless the caller passes `{ drafts: true }`.

The draft side region is desktop-only, and Review still requires the draft's project to resolve.

- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Hi folks, hope you're all doing well! Thanks a lot @ngbrown for the clear report with the redacted response shape, and for the mock repro in the thread, that made this easy to pin down.

Native compaction failed with `Invalid compaction response` whenever the session had a live instruction update in it, and this PR lets those updates come back through compaction.

`packages/ai/src/protocols/utils/responses-compaction.ts` calls `/responses/compact` for OpenAI, Azure and xAI, decodes the returned window with the `Response` schema, and turns each item into a `Message` that the next request replays.

**Before**

1. A session gets an `AGENTS.md` change, so `lowerMessages` sends it as `{ type: "message", role: "developer" }`.
2. Compaction runs and `/responses/compact` returns that developer message inside the window, as the API docs allow.
3. `Response` only accepts message items with role `user` or `assistant`, so decoding fails.
4. The whole compaction fails with `provider.invalid-output: Invalid compaction response`, even though the HTTP status is 200.

**After**

Same through step 2.

3. `Response` also accepts message items with role `developer` or `system` whose content is text parts.
4. `toMessage` turns them into `Message.system(...)`.
5. On the next request `lowerMessages` sends that system message back as a `developer` message with the same text, so the window replays as it came back.

The change is one new variant in the `Response` union and one branch in `toMessage`. I took `system` along with `developer` because the compact output schema lists both roles for input messages. A developer message holding an image or file still fails decoding, since `SystemMessage` only holds text and OpenCode never sends one like that.

One thing I'd love your take on: `SystemMessage` has no `providerMetadata`, so the item `id` and `status` of a developer message are dropped and the replay sends it without them (user messages keep theirs). That seemed fine to me since input message ids are optional, but happy to change it if you'd rather keep them. Any feedback or tips are very welcome!

prs.title: feat(plugin): let permission hooks add deny rules
prs.body:
Adds the `permission` hook `experimental.rules`. A server plugin can now add deny rules for an agent in a session. Before, a plugin could only change one request's decision in `evaluate`: the agent was still offered the tool, skill, or MCP server, and only the call failed.

```ts
await ctx.permission.hook("experimental.rules", (event) => {
  if (event.agent === "plan") event.deny({ action: "webfetch", resource: "*" })
})
```

## Contract

- **Deny-only.** `event.deny({ action, resource })` appends `{ action, resource, effect: "deny" }`. Core keeps the list. `event`, `event.rules`, and `event.session` are frozen copies, so a hook cannot allow, edit, reorder, or remove a rule, or remove another hook's deny. Extra fields on the argument (such as `effect: "allow"`) are dropped.
- **Where the denies go.** After the agent's rules and the session's rules. Evaluation is last-match, so a hook deny wins over every configured `allow` or `ask`, and a configured deny stays final. `evaluate` hooks do not run for a request a hook deny refuses (same as a configured deny).
- **One ruleset.** `Permission.rules(hooks, { session, agent })` is the only place that builds an agent's rules in a session:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[agent rules] --> R[Permission.rules]
  S[session rules] --> R
  H[experimental.rules denies] --> R
  R --> E[Permission.configured: ask / assert / allows]
  R --> L[SessionContext.select: tools, Code Mode, skills, MCP]
  R --> U[automation run: Code Mode check + unattended scoped rules]
```

- **Event fields.** `sessionID` and `agent` to choose what to deny; `rules` (the effective configured rules) to avoid duplicating a deny that already applies; `session` (the session's own rules) to tell a per-session grant from an agent default. Nothing else.

## Other `Permission.merge` calls

- `authorize` in `packages/core/src/automation/code.ts` keeps `Permission.merge`. It reads the configured rules only to find scoped `ask` resources to prompt for. A hook adds no `ask`, and every check there goes through `Permission.Service`, which applies hook denies.

## Cost when no plugin registers the hook

- `Permission.rules` calls `hooks.has("permission", "experimental.rules")` first: one `Map.get` miss and an empty `some`. It then returns the same merged array as before. No event, copies, or freezing happen.
- `configured` now uses `agents.select` instead of `agents.resolve`, because the event needs the agent ID.
- No caching.

## Failure behaviour

- A deny that is not two strings dies with `A permission "experimental.rules" hook added an invalid deny: …`.
- A hook that throws (Promise) or dies (Effect) propagates the defect.
- Both fail the permission check, the step's listing, or the automation run. Nothing proceeds without the deny. This matches `evaluate`: hook failures are not caught there either (`permission` hooks have no failure channel in `PluginHooks`).
- Plugins load asynchronously. Nothing waits for them; until a plugin registers the hook, rules are built without its denies. The docs state this limit.

## Feature flag

No flag. The change adds plugin API only: without a registered hook, behaviour is identical to `dev`. The `experimental.` name carries the stability promise, as for the other `experimental.*` hooks.

## Not included

- No change to `evaluate` (no `experimental.approved` / `approvedSave` fields), no `requireConfiguredAllow`, no `deniesAll`, no wildcard move to `@opencode/schema`, no Code Mode or browser changes.
- Subagent descriptions (`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/subagent.ts`) still filter by the agent's own rules, as on `dev`.

## Related

- #61824 adds `experimental.review`, which decides one request after the rules settle on `ask`. This hook works earlier, on the ruleset, and only denies. The two do not overlap.
- First consumer: the desktop browser plugin in #63002, which switches to this hook once it merges.

prs.title: feat(core): choose tools and Code Mode placement from the session's model
prs.body:
**Chooses tools, and which of them go into Code Mode, from the session's model, in one hard-coded function, and lets a tool declare a separate Code Mode form.** The Code Mode placement is behind the opt-in `full_codemode` flag; with the flag off, only rules 1 and 2 below apply and tools are placed as on `dev`.

## Model tool policy

`modelTools({ model, websearch, fullCodeMode })` in `packages/core/src/tool/model-policy.ts` returns `{ hidden, direct }`. It runs in `SessionContext.select` with the model the user selected (session model → agent model → default), in the same pass that filters tools by permissions. The `experimental.model.resolve` hook still runs in `load`, so Copilot "auto" routing is unaffected.

1. **GPT models use `patch`; other models use `edit` + `write`.** Always. Same predicate as before; it moves here from `patch.ts`'s `context` hook.
2. **`websearch` is hidden** when web search is off or no provider is available. Always. Moved from `websearch.ts`'s `context` hook.
3. **With `full_codemode`:** `read`, `write`, `edit`, `patch`, `shell` and `websearch` are allowed in Code Mode. GPT and Anthropic models get them inside Code Mode, with `glob`, `grep` and `webfetch` hidden (scripts use `shell` and `fetch`). Other models, and sessions without a model, keep them as top-level tools.

`Tool.snapshot(permissions, { services, tools })` skips hidden tools and puts a tool in Code Mode only when Code Mode is enabled, the tool allows it, and the policy doesn't keep it direct. The policy can only keep tools direct; it never moves a tool in.

## `options.codemode`

`options.codemode` is now `boolean | { pinned?, description?, input?, output? }`:
- `false`: never in Code Mode; always a top-level tool (as on `dev`).
- `true` or unset: allowed and preferred in Code Mode; the policy may keep it direct.
- An object: same as `true`, plus overrides used only for the tool's Code Mode form. `pinned` moves in here; top-level `options.pinned` still works but is deprecated.

With `full_codemode` on, the built-ins register `codemode: { pinned: true, description, input? }` (`websearch`: `true`); with it off they register `codemode: false`, as on `dev`. `shell`'s Code Mode form drops `background` and uses the 10-minute default timeout.

`Tool.Info` takes `<Input, Output, CMInput, CMOutput>`, so `execute` is typed against both forms; tools without overrides have exactly `dev`'s types.

## Plugin API

- `editor.add/list/get/update` and `ctx.tool.list()` all use plain `Tool.Info`; overrides are visible on `options.codemode`. Editing `description` in `update` changes only the direct form.
- `execute.before`/`execute.after` events carry `info?: Tool.Info` (undefined for unknown names) and `codemode: boolean`; `Tool.Context.codemode` is set for calls from a Code Mode script.
- Input repair now repairs against the form being called, so fields that only exist in a Code Mode input are no longer deleted.

## Other changes

- The Code Mode catalog cache keeps the 5 most recently used tool sets per location (was one slot), cleared on any registry change.
- MCP instructions follow the tool snapshot: no mention of `execute` when Code Mode is off; the "Code Mode no longer available" message says tools are now direct; the worktree hint names whichever tool exists.
- `packages/core/src/tool/AGENTS.md` notes that the Abattoir model tools page mirrors this logic and must be updated with it.

## Known open items

- The policy uses the selected model, but `experimental.model.resolve` in `load` can switch models afterwards; the tool set then follows the selected model, not the resolved one.
- The `explore` agent denies `execute`, so with `full_codemode` on, GPT/Claude explore sessions lose `glob`/`grep`/`webfetch` without gaining Code Mode.

📊 **Proof**
- New `tool-model-policy.test.ts` (rules per model family, websearch, the flag, and `SessionContext.select` end to end); Code Mode override, pinned and cache tests in `tool-registry.test.ts`; Code Mode input repair in `tool-input-repair-integration.test.ts`; four-parameter typing in `promise-tool.test.ts`.
- Before the rebase: `typecheck:tsc` 33/33, lint clean, and schema, plugin, core, sdk and server suites pass. CI runs on the current head.

---

Fixes #57711

Related: #55087

Public API: `Tool.Options.codemode` accepts `{ pinned?, description?, input?, output? }` overrides and top-level `pinned` is deprecated; adds `Tool.Context.codemode` and `info`/`codemode` on tool execute hooks (backwards compatible)

prs.title: refactor(codemode): thread PsychoScript runs by program complexity
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Stacks on #64437 (base branch `codemode-rust`).

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

This changes how PsychoScript runs programs, not what they can do or see. There are no new APIs. `PR.md` gains a Threading section with the same content for when the crate moves.

**Compiling is sized by nesting, not source size.** Parsing and compiling recurse once per syntax level, and the parser has no guard of its own.
- `nesting::bound` scans tokens for an upper bound on nesting. It is conservative by construction: a `/` that may be a regex or a division, or a byte it can't place, makes the rest of its line count raw (every opening bracket, no closer). Source it can't tokenize counts raw to the end.
- A program compiles on the caller's thread when it fits the 512 KB budget, however long it is. A deeper one compiles on a thread sized to its bound: 1 KiB per unit in release builds and 16 KiB in debug, over the measured worst of 819 B and 12.9 KB (`bench/examples/stack_probe.rs`).
- This applies to `execute`, `program`, `execute_async` and `resume`.
- Running needs no native stack for deep syntax, and built-in callbacks are VM frames, so a run stays where it is driven, with one 512 KB budget. Call depth matches the reference exactly: 10,000 levels at one frame per level, 5,000 at two, 3,334 at three, in release and debug.

**Long runs as futures leave the executor.** In `execute_async`, `run_async` and `run_resumable_async`, a stretch of compute longer than 1 ms stops at its next safe point and finishes on a worker thread of the run's own. The next stretch starts on the executor again. Host code never runs on the worker; it is handed back to the executor in the same order:
- `HostFunction` calls, including the work a synchronous one blocks on (`Returned::Block`), during which the run's other host calls keep being polled;
- starting async functions and `DurableFunction`s, and the first poll of their futures;
- `Namespace` `resolve` and `keys`;
- accessors such as a streaming body's `cancel`.

Dropping a run while it is on its worker brings it back first, so its calls are cancelled on the executor. A suspend works the same either way. Blocking `execute` and `Program::run` never use a worker.

To move between threads, a run's state is `Send` (`Arc` instead of `Rc`, byte buffers behind an uncontended `Mutex`), and a run owns its module list and source.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, round-trip conformance, all four generators with a clean tree, and `bash test262/run.sh` (13444/13444) all pass.
- Conformance runs every case both blocking and as a future.
- `tests/offload.rs` covers sync, blocking, pending, async, durable and namespace host code during offloaded stretches. Without the hand-back, 13 host calls ran on the worker; with it, none do. It also covers a streaming `cancel`, and dropping or suspending a run that is on its worker.
- Scanner tests cover 19 regex-versus-division and other disguises of deep nesting; deliberately deep programs on a 1 MiB caller thread end with a diagnostic.
- Instruction counts against the base: the nine bench programs are within ±0.5%. Plugin event: `reducer-padded.js` −9.1% (no thread), `reducer.js` +1.5% (the scan). See `bench/RESULTS.md`.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #56729

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`ShellTool` forks its completion observer into the plugin activation scope. When `Plugin.activate` rebuilds the shell plugin suffix, that scope closes and the observer is interrupted, so a background shell that finishes afterwards never notifies its Session: the Job and its persisted background marker survive, but the Session receives nothing and the marker is never acknowledged.

The shell plugin now reclaims persisted shell backgrounds when it is activated:

- For each marker it waits on the Job (immediately available when the Job already finished).
- It replays the same notification as the normal observer, using the Job's recorded output/error for completed jobs.
- It acknowledges the marker afterwards.

Jobs from a previous process are unknown to this process, so they are left for the existing restart recovery path. Delivery stays deduplicated by the persisted notification ID, so a reclaim that races a live observer still produces one notification, and `completeBackground` is idempotent. The observer itself stays owned by the shell tool; this only covers the lifetime gap between activations.

- [x] Bug fix

### Issue for this PR

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

The Console watch loop guard holds a session's wakes after 20 since the user's last prompt, and that count never decays. A session watching something busy (all of a member's Slack mentions, say) stops waking for good after 20 and stays stuck until someone prompts it.

This resets the count when an update arrives 30 minutes or more after the session's last update, woken or held.
