prs.title: feat(core): run image generation as a background job
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Image generation now runs as a background job on the server, the same way video does. `POST /api/experimental/generate/image` returns an ID right away, the server makes the request and stores the images as blobs, and `GET /api/experimental/generate/image/:id` reads the job.

```text
before: POST /generate/image → waits 10–60 s → { images: [{ data: <base64>, mime }] }
after:  POST /generate/image → { id: "image_…", status: "running" }
        GET  /generate/image/:id → running | completed { blobs } | error { reason }
        GET  /blob/:id → the image
```

**How it works.** `ImageGeneration` (`packages/core/src/image-generation.ts`) mirrors `VideoGeneration`, minus the lease and polling. Image providers answer in a single request, with no job ID to check later, so the server that took a job makes the request itself:

```text
start    check the model makes images (unknown models still fail with 404)
         save image:<id> as running in kv, fork the request in the server's scope
request  done   → images to blobs → record = completed (only if still running)
         failed → record = error "failed"
cancel   stop the request if it's local → record = error "cancelled"
wait     wait for the local request, else reread the record every 5 s
every 5s drop records 24 h after they finished
         a job still running 31 min after it started → error "unknown" (its server stopped)
```

**The tool.** `experimental_image_generate` now starts a job through the service and gets a `track` step like the video tool: wait, copy the blob into the workspace with the extension of its real format, post the notice. After a restart, an image that finished before the server stopped is still saved. One that was mid-request is reported as cancelled, as before, because its request died with the process.

**Plugins.** `ctx.experimental.generate.image(...)` becomes `image.create(...)` and `image.get({ id })`, matching the client. I updated the plugin docs example.

**Trade-offs:**

- **Breaking for experimental callers.** The old route returned base64 images inline. Anything calling `client.experimental.generate.image` or the plugin method has to switch to create-then-get. The one external user I know of is OpenChamber's opt-in image tool; their desktop app pins its own server version, but their web and VS Code builds would break once users update.
- **A server that stops mid-request leaves its job running for up to 31 minutes.** Without a job ID there's nothing for another server to pick up, and marking it failed sooner would need a heartbeat. Images take seconds, so this is rare.
- **Not on workerd.** Blobs need a local disk, so the image routes fail there like the video routes do.

Also raised the notice timeout in `tool-video-generate.test.ts` from 10 to 20 seconds. Its first status check and the wait each run every 5 seconds, so under load it could miss.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Live against xAI (`grok-imagine-image-2.0`) and OpenAI (`gpt-image-2`): both jobs completed and their blobs downloaded as a JPEG and a PNG; an unknown model still returned 404 `ModelNotFoundError`.
- `image-generation.test.ts`: a job completes with its blob, a cancelled one reports `cancelled`, and one whose server stopped fails with `unknown` after the deadline. 10 reruns passed.
- `tool-image-generate.test.ts`, `session-execution.test.ts`, `generate.test.ts`, the video tests and `test/plugin` in core: 755 pass.
- `packages/server` generate, video and schema-error tests, `packages/plugin` and `packages/client` tests pass.
- `bun run check` at the root, and `tsc` in core, plugin and server.

Not covered by a test: the restart path that saves an image which finished before the server stopped.

### Screenshots / recordings

None.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #63892

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

On Windows, a shell command that uses Microsoft Store PowerShell 7 stops before it can run. Process creation fails with OS error -1073283067 (0xC0070005), so the caller gets no command output, in a project directory and in a temporary directory. The same commands still run under Windows PowerShell 5.1. Pipe-mode creation passes PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST to CreateProcessW and retries without a job when that attribute is refused. The retry matches only Win32 error 5. A packaged executable reports the same refusal as 0xC0070005, so the original spawn failure is returned unchanged.

create_process_refused_job treats both 5 and 0xC0070005 as a job-list refusal, and the Windows spawn path uses it to choose the jobless retry. When either code comes back from a job-backed attempt, the process is created again with no job attribute. A unit test covers both codes, the signed value -1073283067, that same code read from an io::Error, and non-matches for Some(2) and None.

prs.title: fix(ai): chunkTimeout counts model output, not keep-alives
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue filed.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A streamed `anthropic-messages` call through Zen went silent partway through a tool call for about 30 minutes and never errored. The model had stopped producing output, but the connection kept sending `: keep-alive` comments and Anthropic `ping` events, and those reset `chunkTimeout`:

- Native HTTP route: `RequestExecutor` wraps the raw response body in the chunk timer (`withBodyTimeouts` in `packages/ai/src/route/executor.ts`), so any bytes reset it, comments included.
- AI SDK route: `wrapSSE` already ignores comments, but every SSE event resets the deadline, `ping` included (`packages/core/src/aisdk.ts:68`).

Fix: `chunkTimeout` now resets only on events that carry model output.

- `http.ts`: model routes send with `chunk: false`, so the executor skips its byte-level chunk timer, and run the chunk timer on the framed stream instead. SSE framing already drops comments, empty events and keepalives. The header timeout and whole-request deadline stay in the executor, and every other request keeps the byte-level chunk timer. When the chunk timer fires, it raises a retryable read `TransportError` with code `Timeout`, as before. The default doesn't change.
- `anthropic-messages.ts`: `ping` is no longer one of the SSE event names the framing keeps, so it never becomes a frame.
- `aisdk.ts`: `ping` events don't move the deadline.

Side effects:

- `document` and the other non-SSE framings (`lines`, Bedrock event stream) now bound the time between frames, not between byte reads. For `document`, the chunk timeout covers downloading the whole body.
- With `includeRaw`, a named `event: ping` no longer shows up as a raw event.

### How did you verify your code works?

New tests:

- `packages/ai/test/http-timeout.test.ts`:
  - A stream that sends only `: keep-alive` and `ping` past 15 minutes now fails with the read timeout.
  - A stream that sends a text delta every 10 minutes for 30 minutes completes.
- `packages/core/test/aisdk.test.ts`: the heartbeat test now also sends `ping` events and still has to time out.

Each new test fails when the fix it covers is reverted.

### What does this PR do?

Adds a `configDir` setting to the Claude Agent provider so another Claude config folder can be used. It can also be a list of folders, and OpenCode moves a chat to the next account when one hits its usage limit before showing any output.

```jsonc
"claude-agent": {
```

issues.title: pi-durable: permanently delete a conversation from storage
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add a way to permanently delete a conversation from pi-durable storage, e.g. `harness.deleteConversation(id, ctx)`: it refuses (or aborts first) while a run is active, then removes the conversation's entries, docs, inbox items and scheduler state from the store.

### Why?

We host pi-durable for end users (SQLite storage, one harness per process). When a user deletes a conversation we can drop our own index row and files, but the message history stays in the durable store forever: in 1.2.0 the store is append-only and the only removal I could find is for inbox items (`removeInboxItem`). So "delete" only means "nobody can look it up any more", which is a weaker privacy guarantee than users expect, and the store only ever grows.

Deleting rows from the SQLite file ourselves would depend on the internal schema and break on upgrades.

### How? (optional)

A storage-level `deleteConversation` implemented by each backend, plus a harness method that checks the live run state, evicts the conversation from memory (rooms/subscriptions get a terminal "deleted" signal), and calls it. Tombstoning the id so a later `submit`/`entries` fails with a clear "not found" error would keep callers honest.

### What do you want to change?

If not, I'd like a way to admit new work in the same Harness while old work stays held, then release one chosen item without releasing its peers. The hold needs to survive another reopen.

### Why?

After restoring a store, we want the operator to choose which eligible work resumes. On `@earendil-works/pi-durable` 1.5.2, submitting a new input in a separate conversation also settled the unselected old input as `unanswered/interrupted` (retries disabled; no second provider call for the old input). Withholding and reinstalling a custom definition instead released both tasks of that kind.

[Runnable reproducer](https://github.com/markdlabrecque/automaton/tree/a869060d5baf25e0bd850cfb3f27dfb3e3e7e1a1/investigations/selective-recovery): temporary SQLite, controlled process kill, faux provider, no credentials.

### How? (optional)

A hold at scheduler reservation time seems like one option. The tool waits tracked in #12026 look useful for cooperative tools, but I haven't found a host control there for an already-interrupted generation. Is there an existing seam you'd recommend?

issues.title: Managed installs can run Pi on the distro Node.js, which a distro update can break

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Managed install (pi.dev installer), 1.5.2, CachyOS x86_64_v4. After a system update `pi` printed only

```
node: error while loading shared libraries: libsimdjson.so.36: cannot open shared object file
```

and exited. The distro cause is separate and already reported (CachyOS/distribution#641): their
`cachyos-znver4` nodejs build still links `libsimdjson.so.36` while `simdjson 2:5.2.0` ships `.so.37`.

The Pi half: this managed install reused the distro Node.js (preflight is `command -v node` plus a version
check, and Arch has no installer Node method), so `~/.local/share/pi-node` never existed and the managed
launcher's `exec .../node_modules/.bin/pi` resolved `#!/usr/bin/env node` to the broken system `node`.
`pi update` was unreachable in that state, so the install could not repair itself. Re-running the installer
"fixed" it by downloading a standalone Node.js, which is exactly the state a managed install should have
been in from the start.

### Why it matters

A managed install pins every dependency except the one that runs them. Any distro Node change - soname
bump, an old Node, package removal - takes Pi down with an error that mentions Pi by accident only.
Repro without any distro bug: install Pi in a container using the distro Node (so no
`~/.local/share/pi-node` exists), then remove or replace that Node. `pi` dies; `pi update` cannot run.

### Expected behavior

Two fixes are in this repo; https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12304 implements them:

- `pi update` smoke-tests the staged release with the Node.js running the update rather than the Node.js
  the launcher will use next (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/pi-node/current/bin`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pi-node\current` on
  Windows). Related: #12048 fixed the same assumption on Windows.
- After a managed update, report when the install has no Node.js of its own and point at the installer,
  instead of leaving a bare loader error for the next distro touch.

The larger fix is in `install.sh` / `install.ps1`, which are not in this repository: a managed install
should always provision the standalone Node.js it already knows how to download, and the launcher should
exec it by absolute path rather than rely on the shebang. (Adding it to PATH globally would repeat #10519,
so it should stay scoped to Pi's own process.)

I have the change written and tested; per CONTRIBUTING it needs `lgtm` before the PR can stay open.

issues.title: Codemode batching hides skill reads in the tool UI

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Problem

Codemode encourages batching independent tool calls. When an agent reads `SKILL.md` through `tools.read()` inside a codemode call, the conversation displays the codemode call instead of the direct `[skill]` read. This makes skill activation harder to see and inspect.

In Pi 1.5.2, `dist/extensions/codemode/tool.js` defines the prompt guideline: “Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.” The agent followed this guidance to batch a skill read with a documentation read.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a session with codemode enabled and a discoverable skill.
2. Ask the agent to read the skill and another independent file.
3. Have the agent batch both calls using `codemode` and `tools.read()`.
4. Compare the tool display with a direct `read` of the same `SKILL.md`.

## Actual

The batched read is presented as a codemode call. A direct read is displayed as `[skill]` with its line range and expandable content.

## Expected

Skill reads remain visible and expandable as `[skill]`, including when batched. Alternatively, route skill reads through direct read calls, including a parallel tool-call array of 1–8 calls where supported, while retaining batching for other work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A skill read is identifiable and expandable in the conversation when other independent reads run in parallel.
- [ ] Codemode guidance does not encourage hiding skill reads behind a single opaque tool display.
- [ ] Add a regression test for the chosen behavior.

## Notes

The `read` tool still executes inside codemode; the reported issue is presentation and discoverability, not a failure to load the skill. The 1–8 parallel tool-call array is a proposed alternative; its availability in every client is not verified.

### What happened?

The application clutters home directory on Linux with its configuration/state directory. Right now the `~/.pi` directory is a mess that doesn't work well for people who checkout dotfiles in a home-level Git repo, people who don't like cluttered home, people who prefer to keep state on different partitions, etc.

Since we're talking about an AI agent, here's what GPT-5.4 has to say:

>  For Linux, pi should ideally move from:
> 
>  - ~/.pi/agent/...
> 
>  to:
> 
>  - config → ~/.config/pi/agent
>  - sessions/state → ~/.local/state/pi/agent
>  - cache → ~/.cache/pi/agent
> 
>  while continuing to read the old location for compatibility and migrating users automatically.
> 

>  Practical directory split
> 
>  A sensible mapping:
> 
>  - ~/.config/pi/agent/settings.json
>  - ~/.config/pi/agent/keybindings.json
>  - ~/.config/pi/agent/models.json
>  - ~/.local/state/pi/agent/sessions/...
>  - ~/.local/state/pi/agent/auth/... if auth is persistent state
>  - ~/.cache/pi/agent/... for any rebuildable caches


P.S. I'm aware of https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/534, and the difference is that my issue asks you to use appropriate locations not just for configs, but for data and other files as well.

2. See the `~/.pi` being created

It should follow the standard and configurable Linux locations for config, state, cache, etc. instead of polluting user's home directory.

issues.title: Read Tool: Crashes the process if the abort signal fires during a specific window

labels.name: bug

labels.name: untriaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

While `read.execute` is running, the whole process crashes if the passed signal is aborted between line 207 (MIME type detection) and line 46 (`yield* handle.createReadStream`) in `dist/core/tools/read.js`. No extensions are in reproduce code with SDK core read tool.

The actual output on crash:
```
$ node repro.mjs
node:events:505
    throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
    ^

AbortError: The operation was aborted
    at stream.<computed>.AbortError.cause (node:internal/streams/add-abort-signal:47:22)
    at module.exports.addAbortSignalNoValidate (node:internal/streams/add-abort-signal:53:5)
    at addAbortSignal (node:internal/streams/add-abort-signal:38:25)
    at ReadStream.Readable (node:internal/streams/readable:360:7)
    at new ReadStream (node:internal/fs/streams:258:3)
    at FileHandle.createReadStream (node:internal/fs/promises:408:12)
    at Object.readLocalFileChunks [as createReadStream] (file:///home/vscode/.pi/agent/install/releases/1.5.2/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/tools/read.js:46:23)
    at async selectLinesFromStream (file:///home/vscode/.pi/agent/install/releases/1.5.2/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/tools/read.js:156:22)
    at async file:///home/vscode/.pi/agent/install/releases/1.5.2/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/tools/read.js:241:35
Emitted 'error' event on ReadStream instance at:
    at emitErrorNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:170:8)
    at emitErrorCloseNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:129:3)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:90:21) {
  code: 'ABORT_ERR',
  [cause]: DOMException [AbortError]: This operation was aborted
      at new DOMException (node:internal/per_context/domexception:76:18)
      at AbortController.abort (node:internal/abort_controller:579:18)
      at Immediate.step (file:///tmp/pi-repro/repro.mjs:9:65)
      at process.processImmediate (node:internal/timers:574:21)
}
```

How it actually happened (explanation by Claude Opus 5.5):
---
The whole pi process crashed during a codemode script. One nested call in a `Promise.all` failed (grep on a path that didn't exist). codemode then aborted the sibling `read` calls. One of those reads had its signal aborted before `readLocalFileChunks` reached `handle.createReadStream({ signal })`. Node then emits `AbortError` on that ReadStream on a later tick, after the `for await` has already received the error and finished. Nothing handles that `'error'` event, so the process exits.

### Steps to reproduce

Running the script below with `node repro.mjs` reproduces the crash in most runs. If it doesn't, adjusting `ABORT_COUNT` within the range 3-10 should reproduce it (it depends on timing, so reliable reproduction is difficult).
```js
// repro.mjs
import { createReadTool } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
const read = createReadTool(process.cwd());
const ac = new AbortController();
read.execute("repro", { path: "repro.mjs" }, ac.signal).catch(() => {});
const ABORT_COUNT = 3;
let n = 0;
const step = () => (n++ < ABORT_COUNT ? setImmediate(step) : ac.abort());
// abort a few event-loop turns later, i.e. while fs.open/stat is pending
step();
```

[Just a reference]
Claude Opus 5.5 explains the cause and suggests a fix below.

- The signal is already aborted when `createReadStream` is called, so the stream is destroyed in its constructor and its `'error'` event is deferred to `process.nextTick`.
- The `for await` iterator still receives the `AbortError` through `eos()`, which also attaches a temporary no-op `'error'` listener.
- Because `readLocalFileChunks` passes `autoClose: false` (so `autoDestroy` is false), the iterator's `finally` calls `cleanup()` and removes that no-op listener. The deferred `'error'` is then emitted with no listener. With `autoClose: true` the crash does not occur. (Node v24.22.1, `createAsyncIterator` in `lib/internal/streams/readable.js`, `eos()` in `lib/internal/streams/end-of-stream.js`)
- Suggested fix: add `signal?.throwIfAborted()` before `createReadStream` in `readLocalFileChunks`. This fixed it in a local plain-Node test.


### Expected behavior

The aborted read rejects (or returns early) and the process keeps running.

### Version

pi 1.5.2, Node v24.22.1, Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) in WSL2

issues.title: [fullscreen] Large transcripts re-render every frame; every resize re-emits the whole transcript (1 core saturated)

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
> 🤖 Drafted by the reporter's local pi agent from measurements we collected together; the reporter verified the repro with `pi -ne` (no extensions). Disclosed per CONTRIBUTING.md.

## What happened?

On Windows 11 / Windows Terminal / **2 logical cores**, working in a session with a large transcript
(current session file ~1.6–2.4 MB) makes the TUI stutter badly on window resize and when scrolling.

Measured inside the pi process (wrapping `process.stdout.write` + sampling `process.cpuUsage()` deltas over 5 s windows):

| Scenario | pi process CPU | stdout written |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `regular`, each resize 120×30 ↔ 209×51 | **5.2–5.8 s CPU per 5 s window** | **3.9–5.2 MB per resize** |
| `regular`, scrolling | 3–5 % of one core | ~10–120 KB / 5 s |
| `fullscreen`, scrolling a large transcript | **66–101 % of one core** | ~30–360 KB / 5 s |

On a 2-core machine, 66–101 % of one core is 25–50 % of the whole machine spent on the render path, which is what
shows up as stutter. Switching `tuiMode` from `fullscreen` to `regular` removes most of it.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Windows Terminal, `tuiMode: "regular"` (default), resume a session with a large transcript
   (a few thousand entries / ~1.5–2.5 MB `.jsonl`).
2. Maximise → restore → maximise the window a few times (each resize with a large transcript).
3. Observe the stutter; confirm by measuring bytes passed to `process.stdout.write` and `process.cpuUsage()` deltas.
   With `tuiMode: "fullscreen"`, scrolling the same session saturates one core continuously.

## Expected behavior

Render and emit work should scale with the **visible viewport**, not with the total transcript size — both for
per-frame rendering and for resize.

## Version

pi 0.85.1, node 22.23.2, Windows 11 26100, Windows Terminal, 2 logical cores.
Only difference between the rows above is `tuiMode`.

## Additional context

- `createChatViewport()` places the transcript document inside `new ScrollView(document, { follow: "end", ... })`,
  and on resize the whole transcript appears to be re-emitted at the new width (3.9–5.2 MB per resize).
- The numbers were collected with one locally loaded panel extension that wraps `process.stdout.write` and samples
  `process.cpuUsage()`; that extension's own components render in **0.1–0.2 ms/frame** (instrumented), and the CPU burn
  also appears in windows where it renders nothing.
- Re-validated with **`pi -ne`** (no extensions): resizing with a large transcript still stutters → not extension-caused.

issues.title: Threshold compaction fires far below the window when the selected model is virtual
issues.body:
**What do you want to change?**

`AgentSession._checkCompaction` should skip the threshold check when the context window is unknown.

With a virtual model selected, `_modelForMessage()` returns `undefined` (it calls `getPhysicalModel()`, which returns `undefined` for virtual models), so `contextWindow` falls back to `this.model.contextWindow` — the virtual model — which reports `0`. `shouldCompact(tokens, 0, …)` is then true for any non-negative estimate and any reserve value.

**Why?**

With a virtual model selected (registered via `pi.registerVirtualModel()`), any zero-usage, error, or aborted assistant message — including the placeholder left behind when a routed turn is aborted with Esc — makes the next prompt emit `compaction_start` with `reason: "threshold"`. Two sessions on a 1,048,576-token model compacted at 271,663 (25.9%) and 562,025 (53.6%) tokens, while the user was actively working.

Two sibling paths already handle this case, which is why I think it is an oversight rather than intent: `_exceedsCompactionThreshold()` returns `false` when `model.contextWindow <= 0`, and `getContextUsage()` uses `_limitsModel()` instead of `this.model`. The same unknown window is why the footer shows `ctx —` for a virtual selection.

**How?**

In `_checkCompaction`, resolve limits the way the sibling paths do — the physical model from `_modelForMessage()`, or `_limitsModel()` — and return early when the window is unavailable or `<= 0`, mirroring `_exceedsCompactionThreshold()`. I would add a regression test with a virtual model reporting a zero window.

Repro is three steps: select a virtual model registered by any extension, press Esc during a turn so the last assistant message ends `stopReason: "aborted"` with zero usage, then send any prompt and watch `compaction_start` fire with `reason: "threshold"` well below the real window.

I would like to submit this as a PR.

issues.title: Session resume fails on OpenAI-compatible providers: empty toolCall id/name gets persisted, causing 400 missing field tool_call_id

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

# Session resume fails on OpenAI-compatible providers: empty toolCall id/name gets persisted, causing 400 "missing field `tool_call_id`"

## Summary

When a model behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint emits a malformed tool call with an **empty id and empty function name**, pi persists the broken message pair (assistant `toolCall` with `id: ""` / `name: ""` + a `toolResult` with `toolCallId: ""`) into the session JSONL. Every subsequent LLM request that replays this session history is rejected by the OpenAI-family API with:

```
Error: 400 BadRequestError
{"error":{"message":"Invalid JSON data: Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[215]: missing field `tool_call_id` at line 1 column 484235","type":"invalid_request_error","code":"json_parse_error"}}
```

This makes the session **permanently un-resumable** on OpenAI-compatible providers (`pi -c`, `pi -r`, auto-continue all fail once the broken entries enter the active branch). The only current escape hatches are starting a new session or hand-editing the JSONL.

## Environment

- pi-coding-agent / pi-ai / pi-agent-core: **0.73.1**
- Node v24.11.0, Windows 11
- Provider: OpenAI-compatible endpoint via `openai-completions` API (e.g. agnes-3.0-flash, but any OpenAI-compatible model that can emit a bad tool call — e.g. via LiteLLM proxies — is affected)

## Root cause

Traced through the installed 0.73.1 dist:

1. **pi-ai, `streamOpenAICompletions`** — when streaming deltas arrive without an `id` (and the model sends an empty `function.name`), pi creates a `toolCall` block with `id: ""` / `name: ""` instead of synthesizing a fallback id or sanitizing the name.
2. **Tool runner** — looks up the tool by the empty name, fails, and records `toolResult { toolCallId: "", toolName: "" }`. Both entries are then persisted verbatim into the session file.
3. **`transformMessages` (pi-ai)** — passes empty ids through: the orphan-tool-call check (`existingToolResultIds`) actually *matches* `""` to `""`, so no synthetic result is inserted and the empty id flows into the next request.
4. **`convertMessages` (openai-completions)** — emits `tool_call_id: toolMsg.toolCallId` (= `""`) and `function.name: ""`, which the OpenAI-family deserializer rejects (400 `json_parse_error` / `missing field tool_call_id`).

Note this only surfaces when the *next* request is sent to an OpenAI-family API; the same broken session on a lenient provider may not fail, which makes it hard to diagnose.

## Proposed fix (defense in depth)

1. **Sanitize at stream time (pi-ai, OpenAI-completions parser):** when a tool-call delta/block ends up with an empty `id`, synthesize one (e.g. `call_${crypto.randomUUID()}`); if `name` is empty, keep the tool call but mark the block so the runner produces a clean error result (or drop the block if arguments are also empty). This prevents broken data from ever entering the session file.
2. **Sanitize at request build time (pi-ai, `transformMessages` / `convertMessages`):** before sending, repair any remaining empty `toolCall.id` / `toolResult.toolCallId` pairs by pairing a tool result with its preceding assistant tool call and generating fallback ids. This makes already-corrupted sessions resumable without file surgery — no session migration required.
3. (Optional) A `SessionManager` migration pass on load for existing v3 session files containing empty tool-call ids.

Any of 1–2 fixes the user-visible failure; 1 is the root-cause fix, 2 is the robustness net.

## Workaround (user side)

A pi extension using the `context` event can repair empty ids in the message list before every LLM call, and a small script can rewrite the corrupted JSONL entries (backing up the file first). With that in place, sessions stay usable, but broken entries keep accumulating in session files — so an upstream fix is still needed.

## Verification of the diagnosis

- Reproduced end-to-end: session containing the two entries above → `transformMessages` + `convertMessages` output contains `tool_call_id: ""` → OpenAI-compatible endpoint returns exactly the 400 in the summary.
- After repairing the two entries (non-empty matching ids), the same session replays cleanly through the OpenAI-compatible provider for the full 215-message context.


### Steps to reproduce


1. Run any session against an OpenAI-compatible model.
2. The model emits one tool-call response with an empty tool-call id and empty function name while still sending arguments (observed: `tool_calls: [{ id: "", function: { name: "", arguments: "{...}" } }]` — some providers/models/proxies produce this on truncated or malformed output).
3. pi executes the tool: no tool matches the empty name, so pi writes a `toolResult` with `toolCallId: ""`, `toolName: ""`, content `"Tool  not found"`, `isError: true`.
4. The session continues normally for that turn (the error result is shown in the TUI).
5. The **next** request that replays the full history → 400 `missing field tool_call_id` (and/or `invalid tool call: function name must not be empty`).

Minimal reproducing session tail (anonymized, 2 entries are enough):

```jsonl
{"type":"message","id":"e2","parentId":"e1","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"toolCall","id":"","name":"","arguments":{"command":"echo hi"}}],"api":"openai-completions","provider":"openai","model":"any","stopReason":"toolUse","usage":{"input":0,"output":0,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0,"totalTokens":0,"cost":{"input":0,"output":0,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0,"total":0}},"timestamp":1700000000000}}
{"type":"message","id":"e3","parentId":"e2","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"","toolName":"","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Tool  not found"}],"isError":true,"timestamp":1700000001000}}
```

Resume the session (or just send the next user message) with an OpenAI-family provider → 400.

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Version

0.73.1

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

For the regular openai-responses API, Pi currently serializes context.systemPrompt
as a developer or system message inside input.

I would like to add an explicit compatibility option that can instead serialize
that prompt in the top-level Responses instructions field. The current input
behavior would remain the default.

### Why?

Some Responses-compatible gateways only inspect the top-level instructions
field. When it is missing, they may inject their own default agent prompt even
though Pi already supplied a system prompt inside input.

This can cause the gateway prompt to override or interfere with Pi's dynamic
system prompt.

### How? (optional)

Add a systemPromptFormat option with input and instructions values.

The instructions mode would move the existing system prompt to the top-level
field rather than copying it. Empty prompts would remain omitted, and request
sampling parameters would retain their existing final override behavior.

I have a local implementation and tests ready.

### What happened?

I had a session running in a git worktree and another process removed that worktree (post-merge cleanup). After that, every `codemode` call in the session failed:

```
Script failed
Wall time 0.0 seconds
Output:

Script error:
Script sandbox failed: ENOENT: process.cwd failed with error no such file or directory, the current working directory was likely removed without changing the working directory, uv_cwd
```

`bash` in the same session handles it correctly:

issues.title: pi-env: `kill_tree` can kill an unrelated process that reused a command's pid

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?
On Unix, pi-env's `kill_tree` falls back to `kill(pid)` when the group kill fails. The group kill fails once the command has exited and been reaped. A late timeout, cancel, kill or `kill_all` can then SIGKILL an unrelated process that got the same pid. I found this by reading the code; I have not seen it happen.

### Steps to reproduce
Not reproduced end to end; pid reuse is hard to force. The fallback alone: start a child that is not a group leader and call `kill_tree(pid)`. The group kill fails and the bare pid is killed. Details are in the AI-labeled comment below.

### Expected behavior
Signal only the process group. Every command already starts in its own session.

### Version
`main` at ff8721f178

I have a small fix with a test and can open a [PR](https://github.com/peterkc/pi/pull/2) if you want one.

<hr/>

**AI-assisted analysis.** Written with Prime Agent.
Assisted-by: prime-agent:claude-opus-5-5

`kill_tree` (`packages/env/daemon/src/sys/unix.rs:347`) sends `kill(-pid)` and, if that fails, `kill(pid)`. The fallback came in with [ba03e03f2d](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/commit/ba03e03f2d24d8b08156d7fd798fe8d9a4ed91c4). Since [b48c675a91](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/commit/b48c675a912f7852810e5f8c9f8ca6887b5b851b), the exit grace can last much longer while the client is slow, so the window is wider. Example fix: https://github.com/peterkc/pi/pull/2

<details>
<summary>Diagram: how a late kill reaches a reused pid</summary>

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as pi-env daemon
    participant C as command (pid 4242, own group)
    participant U as unrelated process
    C->>D: exits
    D->>C: reaps pid 4242 (group 4242 is gone)
    Note over U: the system gives pid 4242 to U
    D->>D: late timeout, cancel, kill or kill_all
    D-xC: kill(-4242) fails: no such group
    D->>U: fallback kill(4242) sends SIGKILL
```

With the fix, the daemon stops after the failed group kill.
</details>

issues.title: pi-durable: truncate or delete one conversation's entries (Tx.truncateConversation)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Problem

A Session can hold many conversations: forks, ownerless roots, task-owned children. There's no way to remove one conversation's entries without removing the whole Session. We need that to honor a user's delete in an app where each chat can fork.

Our setup is one Session per platform chat. An owner's branch is `conversation.fork(entryId)` inside that Session. When the user deletes:

- **a source chat that has live forks,** the forks still read its entries through `parent.at`, so we keep those entries. Its entries after the latest fork point belong to no one else, but we can't remove them.
- **a fork,** none of its own entries are read by anyone, but they stay in the Session until the whole Session is deleted.

So "delete" becomes "hide" until the last related chat is gone. That breaks our guarantee that a deleted chat can't be rebuilt.

Removing the rows directly in `Storage` isn't safe while the Session has an owner. The owner caches entries, conversation tails and scheduler indexes in memory, and fencing it to clear that cache fails a running turn on a sibling conversation. Other state also names those entries: the conversation's `pi.agent`, `pi.live` and `pi.usage` revisions, its tasks, and its submissions.

## Proposal

`Tx.truncateConversation(conversationId, { after: EntryId | null })`, a write on the Session line:

- It removes the conversation's own entries with id > `after`. `after: null` removes all of them.
- It also removes the document revisions, submissions and task records that name those entries.
- It's refused when:
  - any fork's `parent.at` is past `after` (a fork still reads that range), or
  - a task of the conversation is live.
- It's adopted into the owner's memory like any commit, so watches, tails and indexes stay consistent without fencing.
- A new `Storage` method performs the removal in the same transaction as the commit marker, so custom stores (ours is Postgres) can implement it.

That covers both cases:
- A deleted source with forks: `after` = the latest `parent.at` among its forks.
- A deleted fork with no forks of its own: `after` = its `parent.at`, which removes all of its own entries. The conversation record could then be retired too, so `scanConversations` stops listing it.

## Version

1.5.2

issues.body:
**What happened?**

While running pi with the `radius` provider and the `recursive/flint` model, the provider request failed with HTTP 402. Pi surfaced this to the user as:

```
Error: 402 Payment Required: Describe-file request failed
If this looks like a pi bug, /bug sends a report to the developers.
```

**Error details captured in the session transcript**

- provider: `radius`
- model: `recursive/flint`
- url: `https://radius.pi.dev/v1/messages`
- status: 402, statusText: `Payment Required`
- error: `{ "message": "Describe-file request failed" }`

The failed assistant turns ended with `stopReason: "error"`, empty content, and zero token usage; the request failed at the gateway before the model generated a response.

**Context**

- The failure followed an agent turn that attempted to read an image file through the bash tool; the conversation then carried image content into the next request, which failed at the gateway file-handling step.
- Flint is configured as free in the models store (zero input/output cost), so a payment-required failure is unexpected and may be gateway-side billing, quota, or file-handling behavior.

**Related upstream issues**

- 402/429 with Retry-After surfaced as a fatal empty turn with no retry.
- Retry handling ignored server Retry-After delays.
- Radius gateway accepted models with missing pricing fields, producing NaN costs.

**Ask**

- Is the `Describe-file` step part of the gateway request pipeline, and should a 402 of this shape be treated as retryable or billing-related rather than fatal?
- Should the resulting empty-turn failure be surfaced differently so long-running sessions can recover?

`ExtensionUIDialogOptions` (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/types.ts:116`) to carry
`blocked?: BlockedStatus | false`, so an extension can open a picker without telling terminals and
dashboards that a human is needed.

## Why?

We run pi inside Herdr: Herdr-Core keeps the terminals alive, Herdr-App shows them. Terminals
report program status over OSC 7501, and Herdr turns that into `working` versus `blocked` —
blocked meaning stopped because a human is needed. pi emits that status from
program-status-reporter.ts, and it is what lights a pane up.

Concretely: pi-background's `/bg` lists jobs and opens one's log. With more than one job it asks
which one, and the picker alone puts the pane in "Needs you" until I choose or press Esc — while
I'm only reading output. That state should be reserved for where pi cannot continue without an
answer: a permission prompt, or a question the model asked. A view I opened myself with a slash
command is not that, and every false alarm makes the real one worth less.

I assumed it was pi-background's bug; it isn't. `showExtensionSelector`
(`interactive-mode.ts:2865`) defaults to `{ kind: "question", message: title }` for every
`select()`, and `ExtensionUIDialogOptions` offers only `signal` and `timeout` (`types.ts:116`). No
extension can say "this picker is navigation, not a decision" — jobs, models, themes, sessions,
tools all report the same thing.

## How? (optional)

- Add `blocked?: BlockedStatus | false` to `ExtensionUIDialogOptions`.
- In `showExtensionSelector`, use
  `opts?.blocked === undefined ? { kind: "question", message: title } : opts.blocked`, and skip
  `setBlocked` entirely when it is false.
- `confirm()`, `input()` and `editor()` keep their current defaults.

Small in code, broad in effect: one conditional covers every current and future picker, and
`blocked` keeps meaning "a human is required" for everything that consumes program status —
terminals, dashboards, notifications, agent supervisors.

Happy to send the PR if you agree this belongs in core.

issues.title: Let an extension say who a prompt came from (an origin on prompt() / sendUserMessage(), kept on the user entry)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add an optional, opaque `origin` to `AgentSession.prompt()` options and to `pi.sendUserMessage()` options. pi would pass it on the `input` event and store it on the user message entry it creates. pi itself would not interpret it.


### Why?

A host that relays text into a session (a web UI, a Telegram bridge, a scheduler) knows whether a human typed it or a job produced it. Extensions that gate risky actions on "the human approved" need that fact, and today there is no way to pass it. `input.source` only says `interactive`, `rpc` or `extension`. `pi -p TEXT` also reports `interactive`, so a cron job's prompt looks like typing.

The workaround is to emit an event on `pi.events` just before the send and match it by text. That breaks when the send never reaches the `input` handlers: an earlier extension returns `handled`, or pi refuses the prompt during compaction. The marker then waits around and can match a later identical prompt. From an extension, `pi.sendUserMessage()` returns nothing and reports failures only as `extension_error`, so the host cannot even tell that its send was dropped.

### How? (optional)

`options.origin?: Record<string, unknown>`, threaded through `prompt()` into `InputEvent` and persisted as a field on the user message entry, so it survives resume and fork. A transform from an `input` handler would keep the origin. I'm happy to implement it.

issues.title: compaction.modelOverrides are ignored for the routed model when a virtual model is selected

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

I have a router extension that registers a virtual model (`hybrid/auto`) and routes between Qwen3.8-27B (131K window) and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (64K window). While setting up per-model compaction settings for it, I traced how Pi resolves them and found something that looked a bit off.

Compaction takes the context window from the routed model, but reads `reserveTokens` and `keepRecentTokens` from `this.model`, which is the virtual model. So an override keyed by the physical model never applies. Here's `_exceedsCompactionThreshold` on main (5f89cc0):

```ts
return shouldCompact(
	estimateProjectedContextTokens(projection, this.sessionManager.getBranch()).tokens,
	model.contextWindow,                                    // routed model
	this.settingsManager.getCompactionSettings(this.model), // virtual model
);
```

`prepareRequest` passes `route.model` in as `model`, so a single call ends up mixing the two. The same `this.model` lookup happens in `_checkCompaction` (line 3122), manual compaction (line 2946) and `_runAutoCompaction` (line 3268).

This looks related to #12035, which hits the same `_checkCompaction` path, but for the window instead of the settings.

### Steps to reproduce

I worked these out from the code and haven't run them as a standalone repro yet.

1. In `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, set `compaction.reserveTokens` to 16384 and `compaction.modelOverrides["<provider>/<physical-model>"]` to `{ "reserveTokens": 4096 }`.
2. Load an extension that registers a virtual model whose `route()` always returns that physical model, and select it.
3. Fill the context. Compaction triggers at `contextWindow - 16384`.

### Expected behavior

Compaction triggers at `contextWindow - 4096`, the override for the model that actually serves the request.

I think the fix is to read the settings from the `model` argument in `_exceedsCompactionThreshold`, and from `_limitsModel()` in the other three. `routedModel` is only set after the first response though, so `prepareRequest` would need to pass `route.model` through to `_runAutoCompaction`.

For now I'm keying the override by the virtual model name (`hybrid/auto`), which does work. Let me know your thoughts!

### Version

1.5.2

issues.title: Tool order depends on registration order, so the same tools can bust the prompt cache
issues.body:
### What happened?

`getCurrentTools()` in `utils/transcript.ts` returns tools in insertion order, and a tool that is removed and added again goes to the end of the Map. So when tools show up after the session starts (MCP servers connecting or reconnecting, `tool_search` loading tools, extensions registering late), the final order depends on who finished first. Same tool set, different bytes in the request, and the provider writes the whole cache again.

On providers without `supportsMidConvoToolChanges` (Bedrock for example) every one of those is a full cache write, and with a big prefix that gets expensive. I hit it a lot with 3-4 MCP servers that connect at different speeds.

### Steps to reproduce

Quick way to see it without MCP:

```ts
const a = getCurrentTools([sys({ toolsAdded: [x, y] }), sys({ toolsRemoved: [x] }), sys({ toolsAdded: [x] })])
const b = getCurrentTools([sys({ toolsAdded: [x, y] })])
// a = [y, x], b = [x, y]: same tools, different request
```

In a real session: two direct MCP servers that take different times to connect, run a few sessions on Bedrock, and compare the tools array of the requests. The order changes between runs and `cacheRead` drops to 0 on the request where it changed.

### Expected behavior

The same tool set always serializes the same way, no matter in which order the tools arrived. Sorting the resolved list by name would do it (one cache miss when you upgrade, then stable).

### Version

1.4.0, same on main (cc9c52310)

Happy to send a PR for this one too.

issues.title: Mouse wheel scrolls prompt history instead of transcript in fullscreen on Windows + Zellij

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

Mouse wheel in fullscreen mode scrolls through the editor's prompt history instead of the conversation transcript when running inside Zellij on native Windows (Windows → Alacritty → Zellij → Pi).

Direct terminal (no multiplexer) works correctly. Linux with tmux also works correctly.

**Root cause:** `TuiAltScreen.beforeTerminalStart()` writes mouse DECSET sequences (`?1000h`, `?1002h`, `?1006h`) before `ProcessTerminal.start()` calls `process.stdin.setRawMode(true)`. Windows ConPTY silently consumes these sequences while stdin is in cooked mode, so the multiplexer's inner pane never enables mouse tracking. Zellij then falls back to emitting `ESC[A`/`ESC[B` arrow keys for wheel events on alternate-screen panes, which the editor interprets as history navigation. I made a PR #9655 already, please review.

**Fix:** Move the alt-screen entry and mouse DECSET writes from `beforeTerminalStart()` to `afterTerminalStart()`, after raw mode is active. I'd like to submit a PR for this.

**Environment:** Pi 0.85.1, Zellij 0.45.1, Alacritty 0.17.0, Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200), Node 22.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82f73340-89d6-490d-9f55-534e6efee08b

### Steps to reproduce

Mouse wheel in fullscreen mode scrolls through the editor's prompt history instead of the conversation transcript when running inside Zellij on native Windows (Windows → Alacritty → Zellij → Pi).

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Version

0.85.1

issues.title: feat(coding-agent): add assistant message transformers

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## What do you want to change?

Add `pi.registerAssistantMessageTransformer(fn)`. It lets an extension rewrite a display copy of each assistant message before `AssistantMessageComponent` lays it out. Returning a message without `thinking` blocks removes the thinking row and its spacer. Session and model data are untouched.

[Patch](https://github.com/ARQAWA/pi/compare/v1.4.0...thinking-label-sdk): 9 files, about 100 lines including tests.

## Why?

We use an extension that collapses tool calls into one summary line through `registerToolRenderer`. Collapsed tool rows render zero lines. With thinking hidden, every model step still renders two rows: a blank spacer and the `Thinking...` label. A turn with ten tool steps looks like this:

```
Thinking...

Thinking...

Thinking...

Read 7 files · searched 19 times · ran 9 commands
```

Most of the visible transcript becomes repeated labels.

Current APIs cannot remove these rows:

- `setHiddenThinkingLabel("")`: the label is styled before `Text` receives it, so the empty label still renders a blank row.
- `registerMarkdownTransformer` returning `""` for `assistant-thinking`: the block renders empty, but `updateContent` already added spacers from the raw content. This is the same gap as #8154.

Spacers are decided from raw `message.content` before any render-time hook runs. So the hook has to run before layout.

## How?

`updateContent` applies registered transformers to a `structuredClone` of the message, then runs the existing layout unchanged. A throwing transformer is skipped, like Markdown transformers. Streaming and history rendering both pass the transformers.

Tests cover layout without thinking, throwing transformers, and mutation isolation. `npm run check` passes.

Requesting `lgtm` to open a PR.


issues.title: durable: calibrate compaction retention to reported context usage
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Fix skipped compaction in `pi-durable` when reported context usage exceeds the threshold but character estimates are below `keepRecentTokens`.

### Why?

A useful analogy is that one Han character is often closer to a subword in Latin-script text than to a single letter. Counting both as one character hides this difference: CJK text can use substantially more tokens per character, with the exact ratio depending on the model and content. A fixed divisor such as 4 or 3.5 can therefore substantially underestimate its token count. Using this estimate for retention while using provider-reported tokens for the threshold creates incompatible budgets, causing the skipped compaction described below.

With a 64,000-token window and 32,000-token reserve/retention, a CJK-heavy tool run reached 49,824 context tokens while local estimates were only 23,704. `selectCut()` returned no cut, so generation continued until truncation. The same mismatch remains on current `main`. Related report: #2562.

### How? (optional)

Reuse `estimateContext()` to calibrate entry estimates before range selection. Ignore usage invalidated by later context edits, and select only cuts with a non-empty prefix. Keep the existing tool-pair rules and compaction API.

The [implementation](https://github.com/neavo/pi/compare/eb326d265ae0b88489a6d10319307780df827cdf...codex/fix-compaction-usage-budget) includes six regression tests. The related compaction, recovery, and context tests pass (132 total), including compaction before a tool run's next generation. `npm run check` passes. `./test.sh` stops at the existing Windows `spawnSync npm ENOENT` in `scripts/local-package-install.test.mjs`.

I would like to submit this fix. Please approve with `lgtm` if this scope is acceptable.

issues.title: bash tool: tool_execution_end carries no exit code, only isError

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## What happens

With `pi -p --mode json --no-session --tools read,bash` (v1.5.2, checked today on Ubuntu and macOS), the `tool_execution_end` event carries **no exit code** for bash calls:

```json
{"type":"tool_execution_end","toolCallId":"...","toolName":"bash","result":"...","isError":false,"durationMs":41}
```

`ToolExecutionEndEvent` in `dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts` confirms the shape: `type`, `toolCallId`, `toolName`, `result`, `isError`, `durationMs`, `parentToolCallId`. There is no `exitCode` / `exit_code` anywhere in the event, and no CLI flag that asks for it.

## Why it matters

Anything that reads a pi trace and wants to know **whether the command actually succeeded** can only see `isError`, which is the tool's own error flag and not the process exit status: a command that exits 3 (a real, meaningful failure for the caller) arrives with `isError: false` as long as the tool itself ran. On a real 1045-line trace with 15 completed bash calls, no call could be credited as "the source proved it" because the reader demanded `exit_code == 0`; adding `exit_code: 0` to the same 15 calls made all 15 readable. So downstream harnesses have to either trust `isError` (losing the distinction between "ran and failed" and "did not run") or ignore pi traces entirely.

## What would fix it

Add the process exit code to the event for tools that run a process:

- `ToolExecutionEndEvent.exitCode?: number` (absent when the tool did not run a process, which is already how `durationMs` is treated);
- same key in the JSON mode output, so a trace is self-describing;
- keep `isError` as it is (the two answer different questions).

Non-breaking by construction: the field is optional and absent for tools that do not spawn a process.

issues.title: durable: allow cancellation handlers to wait on signals and deadlines
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Let cancellation handlers in pi-durable save their progress and wait for a signal or deadline.

After Stop, a parked tool could request cancellation of a remote job, save its cancellation checkpoint, and wait for confirmation. If the host closes and reopens, the same task would pick up the cancellation without restarting normal execution.

### Why?

Requesting cancellation doesn't always mean the remote job has stopped. A host may need to wait for confirmation before releasing resources or treating the operation as finished.

I want that wait to survive host restarts, while keeping the task's existing ownership and the conversation’s busy state.

### How? (optional)

Extend the existing sleep and signal mechanisms to cancellation handlers, with separate cancellation checkpoints and signal delivery. Leave durable task joins and new owned children out of this change.

Related: #12026.

I'm willing to implement this change.

issues.title: `openai-responses`: omitting `strict` makes Copilot-hosted models fill optional tool arguments

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

`@earendil-works/pi-ai` 1.3.0 sends no `strict` field on `openai-responses` tools
when the model's catalog entry has no `compat.supportsStrictMode`. The GitHub
Copilot endpoint then decodes the schema strict-like, and every declared optional
property comes back populated: `""` on gpt-6-luna / gpt-6.1-sol / gpt-5.3-codex,
and invented values on mai-code-1.1-flash (`{"provider":"openai","model":"gpt-4o-mini"}`).
Tools that reject an empty id fail with an error; tools that treat it as a real
filter silently return wrong results.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `POST /responses` to `https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com` with
   `model: "gpt-6-luna"` and a single tool whose `parameters` declares two
   optional string properties, no `required`, and no `strict` key.
   The returned `function_call.arguments` is `{"provider":"","model":""}`.
2. Repeat with `strict: false` on the same tool definition.
   The arguments become `{}`.
3. Through pi: `builtinModels().complete(model, context, { onPayload })` shows
   `tools[0]` carries no `strict` key. Setting
   `model.compat.supportsStrictMode = true` for the same model makes pi emit
   `strict: false` and the arguments become `{}` again.

Each step reproduced 3/3 times. The same requests through the plain `openai`
SDK, with no pi in the path, behave identically, so this is not argument
post-processing in pi.

### Expected behavior

Optional tool properties should be omitted rather than filled. The catalog
entry for `github-copilot` ships 18 `openai-responses` models and none sets
`compat.supportsStrictMode`, while `openai` sets it on all 44. With the flag
missing, `openai-responses.js` (`model.compat?.supportsStrictMode ?? false`)
skips the `strict` field entirely, whereas the `openai-completions` path
(`compat.supportsStrictMode !== false`) already sends `strict: false` by
default — which is why the same models behave correctly on completions.

Catalog source: `packages/ai/catalog/providers/github-copilot.*` (`dist/providers/data/*.json`
is generated). The same gap appears in xai, opencode and meta, observed from the
shipped data only — I did not run those.

### Version

1.3.0

issues.title: Reduce SQLite storage writes: update only changed columns in the task upsert

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

The task upsert in the SQLite storage does ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET with all six columns (conversation_id, kind, status, abort_requested, background, record) on every task transition. I'd like it to update only the columns whose value actually changed.

### Why?

SQLite rewrites every index named in SET even when the value is the same. I traced one prompt (2 model calls + 1 tool call) on 1.5.2 and on main: ~123 dirty 4 KiB pages for ~8.8 KB of real data, 72 of them in pi_tasks and its indexes.

We run pi-durable where storage is billed per page written (Rivet actors, same on Durable Objects), so this is most of our storage cost per prompt.

### How? (optional)

One extra read per commit to get the stored columns, then SET only the ones that differ (inserts unchanged). No schema change, stored rows are identical.

I tried it: 123 -> 84 pages per prompt (-32%). Storage conformance suite passes (66/66 on main) and abort / background / kill -9 + resume / parked tool scenarios match the unpatched run row by row. Happy to share the patch and the trace scripts, or open a PR.

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add an `auto_retry_decision` event, fired in [`_prepareRetry`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/43472ddb6a6ad9e9bdd74aaa97b22c22cb3e4283/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts#L3924-L3964) after pi computes its backoff and before `auto_retry_start`. It carries `attempt`, `maxAttempts`, pi's `delayMs`, `errorMessage` and the failed `message`. A handler may return `{ delayMs }` (still capped by `retry.maxAgentDelayMs`) or `{ action: "stop" }`. The last handler that returns a value wins, like [`cache_warming_decision`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/43472ddb6a6ad9e9bdd74aaa97b22c22cb3e4283/packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/runner.ts#L1135-L1156).

### Why?

Many providers state the wait only in the error text, e.g. OpenAI's `Please try again in 10.384s` ([openai-node#1477](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/issues/1477)) or Groq's `Please try again in 1.969s` ([continuedev/continue#2343](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/issues/2343)). With the [defaults](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/43472ddb6a6ad9e9bdd74aaa97b22c22cb3e4283/packages/coding-agent/src/core/settings-defaults.ts#L18-L22) (2 s base, 3 retries), pi's backoff ([`retryDelayMs`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/43472ddb6a6ad9e9bdd74aaa97b22c22cb3e4283/packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts#L149-L153)) retries after 2 s, 4 s and 8 s, so a server that enforces a 20 s window fails the turn after three retries that all land inside it. When the window is hours long, the three retries are wasted and the turn fails anyway.

#2366 was closed with "we don't interpret rate limits as it's brittle", and a later comment there asked for a way to "intercept the message and do something with the default backoff timer". This is that hook: pi still interprets nothing, and the parsing lives in an extension for the providers its author uses. (#7134 asked for `retry_after` support in core and was auto-closed.)

Today a retry reaches an extension only as the failed [`agent_end`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/43472ddb6a6ad9e9bdd74aaa97b22c22cb3e4283/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts#L1372-L1373), and the one way to stop it is [`ctx.abort()`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/43472ddb6a6ad9e9bdd74aaa97b22c22cb3e4283/packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/types.ts#L374-L375), which also ends the run. Nothing can change the delay. #9829 (extensions can't see per-attempt retries) was auto-closed.

### How? (optional)

I have a prototype on `6f7f7f2` (the cited files are unchanged on `43472dd`): a new `emitAutoRetryDecision` in `runner.ts` written like `emitCacheWarmingDecision`, about 20 lines in `_prepareRetry` ("stop" undoes the attempt the same way the exhausted-budget branch does), the types and exports, and a short section in `docs/extensions.md`. Six new tests in `agent-session-retry-events.test.ts` cover a delay override, the cap, stop on the first and on a later attempt, no handler, and a throwing handler. `npm run check` is clean.

One open point: the session event `agent_end.willRetry` (what interactive mode reads) is computed synchronously while `agent_end` is emitted ([`_willRetryAfterAgentEnd`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/43472ddb6a6ad9e9bdd74aaa97b22c22cb3e4283/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts#L1265-L1279)), before `_prepareRetry` runs, so it still says `true` when a handler stops the retry. The prototype documents that rather than moving an async hook into the `agent_end` dispatch; I'd like your preference.

I could implement it myself if this gets an `lgtm`.

issues.title: Navigating the session tree adds the branch's prompts to Up-arrow history again

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

I rewind with `/tree` (double Esc) a lot, and I noticed that afterwards Up-arrow history is full of repeats. Every navigation adds the prompts of the branch I land on to history again, even though they are already there.

With five prompts p1..p5, history is `p5 p4 p3 p2 p1`. After going back to p4:

```
p3 p2 p1 p5 p4 p3 p2 p1
```

After going back to p3:

```
p2 p1 p3 p2 p1 p5 p4 p3 p2 p1
```

So the prompt I usually want after a rewind (the one I just sent, to tweak and resend) ends up behind copies of older prompts, and history is capped at 100, so the repeats push real entries out.

Both tree navigation paths (the `/tree` selector and the extension `navigateTree` action) re-render the chat with `renderInitialMessages()`, which passes `populateHistory: true` and adds every user message on the branch to editor history. That is right at startup, but on navigation the prompts are already in history. `addToHistory` only skips a repeat of the latest entry. The rebuild after compaction (`rebuildChatFromMessages`) already re-renders without populating history.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `pi -ne`, send a few prompts (or open any session with several).
2. Press Esc twice on an empty editor, pick an earlier user message, choose "No summary".
3. Clear the editor and press Up a few times.

I reproduced it on main in tmux with an empty agent dir and a session of five prompts, so no extensions were involved.

### Expected behavior

Navigating the tree leaves Up-arrow history as it was. Fix: #12280.

### Version

1.5.2 (main at 05fd3fbda0)

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): smoke-test managed updates with the launcher's Node.js
prs.body:
## Problem

A CachyOS system update replaced `simdjson 2:5.1.1` (`libsimdjson.so.36`) with `2:5.2.0`
(`libsimdjson.so.37`) while its `cachyos-znver4` `nodejs` build still links `.so.36`. `node` stopped
starting, and with it `pi`:

```
node: error while loading shared libraries: libsimdjson.so.36: cannot open shared object file
```

The distro bug is reported separately (CachyOS/distribution#641). The Pi part: this managed install had
reused the distro Node.js, so `~/.local/share/pi-node/current/bin` never existed, and the managed
launcher's `exec .../node_modules/.bin/pi` fell through `#!/usr/bin/env node` to the broken system
`node`. `pi update` was unreachable as well, so the install could not repair itself, and the output named
nothing Pi-related.

The installer half (always provision the standalone Node.js for a managed install, and exec it by absolute
path instead of via the shebang) lives in `install.sh`, which is not in this repository. This change is the
half that is here.

## Change

- `pi update` smoke-tested the staged release with the Node.js that happened to be running the update
  (#12048). Resolve the standalone runtime the launcher actually uses (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/pi-node/current/bin`,
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pi-node\current` on Windows) and verify with that when it exists, so the check reflects
  the next launch.
- After a managed update, say when the install has no Node.js of its own and point at the installer,
  instead of leaving the user with a bare loader error the next time the distro touches `node`.

Only the environment of the update's own smoke test is touched. Pi's Node.js is not added to the user's
PATH, which is what #10519 objected to.

## Tests

Three tests in `test/package-command-paths.test.ts`:

- a managed update with a standalone runtime verifies through it (a runtime that cannot start fails the
  update and leaves `current-version` unchanged); this test fails on `main` without the source change,
- a managed update without a standalone runtime prints the note,
- a managed update with one does not.

`npm run check` passes. `vitest --run test/package-command-paths.test.ts` (Node 22.23): 45 passed, 2
failed; the two failures (`config-selector` built-in extension cases) also fail on `main` in this
environment.

I did not open an issue first, which CONTRIBUTING asks for. This is a concrete proposal for the part that
is in this repo; say the word and I will open the issue with the installer-side findings and close this.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): tree navigation no longer re-adds prompts to history
prs.body:
Closes #12279.

**Problem.** Both tree navigation paths (the `/tree` selector and the extension `navigateTree` action) re-render the chat with `renderInitialMessages()`, which renders with `populateHistory: true`. Every navigation therefore adds the prompts of the branch it lands on to Up-arrow history again. `Editor.addToHistory` only skips a repeat of the latest entry, so with prompts p1..p5:

- before: `p5 p4 p3 p2 p1`
- after going back to p4: `p3 p2 p1 p5 p4 p3 p2 p1`
- after going back to p3: `p2 p1 p3 p2 p1 p5 p4 p3 p2 p1`

History is capped at 100, so the repeats also push older entries out.

**Fix.** `renderInitialMessages()` takes `{ populateHistory?: boolean }` (default `true`), and both tree navigation paths pass `false`. Startup and session switches still fill history from the session. This matches the rebuild after compaction (`rebuildChatFromMessages`), which already re-renders without populating history.

One consequence: navigating to a branch whose prompts were never rendered in this process (one written by an earlier run and not on the branch pi started on) no longer adds those prompts to history. History is otherwise filled only from submitted prompts and the startup branch, so this follows the existing rule.

**Validation** on main `05fd3fbda0`:

- New tests in `test/interactive-mode-tree-navigation.test.ts`: tree navigation re-renders with `populateHistory: false`, and `renderInitialMessages()` populates history by default and not with `false`. Both fail without the fix.
- In tmux, with an empty agent dir and a session of five prompts, rewinding twice with double Esc: before, history grows to the lists above; after, it stays `p5 p4 p3 p2 p1`.
- `npm run check` passes. In `./test.sh` the only failures are unrelated to this change:
  - The find tool tests fail because fd is not installed here and `PI_OFFLINE=1` prevents downloading it.
  - The pi-env tests need cargo, which is not installed here.
  - One `auth-storage` test also fails on main; chord's `state-fuzz` timed out under load and passes on its own.

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

issues.body:
## What would you like to be added?

In the Web Shell (Qwen Code Desktop and the standalone `qwen serve` web mode), the composer's workspace-selector chip is only rendered when a workspace context is active or when no session is attached:

```ts
// App.tsx, v0.27.2
const workspaceContextActive = effectiveSessionContext?.kind === 'workspace';
const composerWorkspaceSelectEnabled =
  workspaceContextActive || connection.sessionId === undefined;
```

In a **live session** (attached session, context `kind === 'live'`) the chip is hidden, so the `Cmd/Ctrl+T` view-navigation shortcut (introduced in #14179, being extended in #15931) is a silent no-op in the most common view — an active session in the primary workspace. There is no way to open the workspace picker from an active session; the only way to start a session in another workspace is to leave the current session first.

## Why is this needed?

Multi-workspace setups: while working in a live session it is useful to start the next session in a different workspace without navigating away. The app already supports the outcome — choosing another workspace from the composer starts a new session there (`switchWorkspace` → new session) — so enabling the chip for live sessions only removes the guard.

A one-clause change looks sufficient:

```ts
const composerWorkspaceSelectEnabled =
  workspaceContextActive ||
  connection.sessionId === undefined ||
  effectiveSessionContext?.kind === 'live';
```

Standalone/projectless sessions would stay hidden, as the existing comment intends ("An attached projectless session hides it again").

## Context

- Umbrella issue #13175 ("keyboard shortcuts for Session Overview and Split View") was closed 2026-10-29 by #14179 (part 1, shipped in v0.27.2); the remaining hotkey set is in progress in #15931 (part 2).
- Neither PR covers this enablement: both only modify the capture-phase `keydown` listener in `App.tsx` (verified in their diffs; #15931 additionally adds a `data-web-shell-workspace-select-trigger` test attribute to `WorkspaceSelector.tsx` without changing visibility).
- We currently work around this with a local post-install patch that appends `|| <ctx>?.kind === 'live'` to the same expression (verified in the 0.25.1 → 0.27.2 builds); an upstream fix would make the local patch unnecessary.

issues.body:
## Deferred PR-watch review follow-ups (from #17665)

PR #17665 (managed GitHub PR-watch + bound-session private injection, slice 1) was squash-merged as `8a96777248`. The round-7 review posted one Critical (R7-1, the watch lane missing the `repoFilter` allowlist — fixed and merged) and **deferred 15 non-blocking findings** under the convergence posture. This issue tracks them so they are not silently lost. Several were triaged during the review round and have draft fixes/tests prepared; each still needs to be verified and landed post-merge. None is a blocker for the merged slice.

### Gate / CI blast radius
- [ ] `.github/scripts/managed-agent-gate-scope.mjs` — the managed-suite gate misses the file(s) that actually mount the `channel` entry point (the top-level registrar `packages/cli/src/commands/register-top-level-commands.ts`, beside `commands/channel.ts`). Add the pattern + a `managed-agent-gate-workflow.test.js` row.
- [ ] `.github/scripts/managed-agent-gate-scope.mjs` — `packages/channels/github/` is in the managed blast radius but `packages/channels/base/` is omitted, although the managed adapter imports runtime values from it (e.g. `fitInboundText`). A base-only change would not select the managed suite. Add `/^packages\/channels\/base\//` + a meta-test row.

### Adapter watch behavior + witnesses
- [ ] `packages/channels/github/src/managed-github-adapter.ts:857` — the watch pass's stalled-instance guard (`this.instanceStalled`) has no witness. Add a test.
- [ ] `packages/channels/github/src/managed-github-adapter.ts:1101` — no test covers a head move that coincides with a failed CI read. Add a test.
- [ ] `packages/channels/github/src/managed-github-deps.ts` — when the CI aggregate is decided by the legacy combined-status source, the failing context names (`data.statuses[].context` in that same response) are discarded. Include them in the failed-check evidence (mirror the check-runs path: dedupe + budget + `namesIncomplete`).
- [ ] `packages/channels/github/src/managed-github-adapter.test.ts` — CI-read assertions in the watch block are counts, and the fake `getCiStatus` returns one head-independent body for every ref, so no test witnesses that the correct head's checks are read. Make the fake head-aware and assert the read ref matches the observed head.

### Client / production wiring
- [ ] `packages/cli/src/commands/channel/managed-channel-client.ts:252` — `retirePrWatchBinding` treats any 404 (including `channel_not_found`) as a successful retire. Only `pr_watch_binding_not_found` should be idempotent-success; rethrow other 404s.
- [ ] `packages/cli/src/commands/channel/managed-github.ts` — nothing pins that the wiring reaches the adapter, and the dep it sets is optional-and-silent, so the single line that turns PR-watch on in production has no witness. Add a wiring test.

### Java control plane / tests / design docs
- [ ] `ManagedChannelAdapterController.java:95` — no shipped producer creates a PR-watch binding, so the watch pass only runs against hand-seeded rows. Confirm this is the intended slice-1 scope (binding creation is via the internal `pr-watch:create` route; no UI producer yet) and document it, or track the producer as a later slice.
- [ ] `ManagedPrWatchService.java` — a guard "can never fire because the route already rejects the same field at the same value." Verify whether it is genuinely unreachable dead code (remove) or deliberate defense-in-depth (keep + comment). Do not remove a load-bearing guard.
- [ ] `ManagedPrWatchServiceTest.java` — the release test's comment says the release is justified by a *replay* against the pinned Session, but since round-5 added `requireTargetSession` before the cross-binding replay, a CLOSED/moved pinned Session is refused before any harness replay. Correct the comment (or strengthen the test) to match that reality.
- [ ] `ManagedPrWatchServiceTest.java` — the test claims to "pin the exact regex the Harness enforces" but pins a private Java copy of `HOSTED_UUID_REGEX`. It currently matches the TS `HOSTED_UUID` (`hosted-file-history-protocol.ts:108`) exactly; strengthen the test to read/compare the authoritative TS regex so future drift is caught.
- [ ] `ManagedPrWatchService.java` + `docs/design/2026-11-17-managed-github-pr-watch-bound-session.md` (+ `.zh-CN.md`) — the design docs' description of the staged-row release must match the actual round-5 behavior (revalidate the pinned Session first; release only when it is dead/closed/moved or a refusal proves non-commit; outcome-unknown keeps it pinned). Correct both language versions if they overclaim.

### E2E rig assertion strength
- [ ] `scripts/run-managed-pr-watch-e2e.mjs` — the four "PRIVATE-ONLY: no public comment" checks only witness that the fakes answer 404 to unmodeled requests (postComment dropped), not that the adapter never attempts a public post. Assert the fake recorded zero postComment attempts.
- [ ] `scripts/run-managed-pr-watch-e2e.mjs` — a check cannot fail: `fakeControlPlane()` initializes `admitted` from `opts.preadmitted ?? []` and P1 passes no options while `inj` is `cp.state.injects[0]`. Make the assertion falsifiable.

## PR-watch 评审延期跟进项（来自 #17665）

PR #17665（managed GitHub PR-watch + bound-session 私有注入，slice 1）已 squash 合入 `8a96777248`。第 7 轮评审发布了一条 Critical（R7-1，巡检路径漏 `repoFilter` 允许列表——已修复合入），并在收敛姿态下**延期 15 条非阻断发现**。本 issue 跟踪它们以免静默丢失。其中数条在评审轮已分诊并起草了修复/测试，仍需合入后逐条核实落地。均不阻塞已合入的 slice。

### 门禁 / CI 影响面
- [ ] `managed-agent-gate-scope.mjs` — 漏掉真正挂载 `channel` 入口的文件（顶层注册器 `register-top-level-commands.ts`，与 `commands/channel.ts` 并列）。补模式 + meta 测试行。
- [ ] `managed-agent-gate-scope.mjs` — `packages/channels/github/` 在 managed 影响面内但漏 `packages/channels/base/`（managed adapter 从其导入运行时值，如 `fitInboundText`）；base-only 改动不会选中 managed 套件。补 `/^packages\/channels\/base\//` + meta 行。

### Adapter 巡检行为 + 见证
- [ ] `managed-github-adapter.ts:857` — stalled-instance 守卫（`this.instanceStalled`）无见证，补测试。
- [ ] `managed-github-adapter.ts:1101` — 无测试覆盖 head 移动恰逢 CI 读失败，补测试。
- [ ] `managed-github-deps.ts` — CI 聚合由 legacy combined-status 决定时，丢弃了失败 context 名（同一响应的 `data.statuses[].context`）；应纳入 failed-check evidence（镜像 check-runs 路径：去重+预算+`namesIncomplete`）。
- [ ] `managed-github-adapter.test.ts` — watch 块 CI 读断言都是计数，fake `getCiStatus` 对任何 ref 返回同一与 head 无关的 body，无测试见证读的是正确 head 的 checks；使 fake head 感知并断言读取 ref 与观测 head 一致。

### Client / 生产接线
- [ ] `managed-channel-client.ts:252` — `retirePrWatchBinding` 把任何 404（含 `channel_not_found`）当成功 retire；仅 `pr_watch_binding_not_found` 应幂等成功，其余 404 重抛。
- [ ] `managed-github.ts` — 无测试钉住接线到达 adapter，且其设置的 dep 可选而静默，生产开启 PR-watch 的那一行无见证；补接线测试。

### Java 控制面 / 测试 / 设计文档
- [ ] `ManagedChannelAdapterController.java:95` — 无 shipped producer 创建 PR-watch 绑定，巡检只对手工播种的行运行。确认这是 slice-1 预期范围（绑定经内部 `pr-watch:create` 路由创建，尚无 UI producer）并记录，或把 producer 列为后续 slice。
- [ ] `ManagedPrWatchService.java` — 某守卫「永不可达，因路由已在同值拒绝同字段」。核实是真死代码（删）还是有意纵深防御（保留+注释）；勿删承重守卫。
- [ ] `ManagedPrWatchServiceTest.java` — release 测试注释称释放由对钉住 Session 的*重放*证明，但 round-5 在跨绑定重放前加了 `requireTargetSession`，CLOSED/移走的钉住 Session 在任何 harness 重放前就被拒。更正注释（或强化测试）以符合实际。
- [ ] `ManagedPrWatchServiceTest.java` — 测试声称「钉死 Harness 强制的精确 regex」却钉私有 Java 副本 `HOSTED_UUID_REGEX`；当前与 TS `HOSTED_UUID`（`hosted-file-history-protocol.ts:108`）完全一致，强化为读取/比对权威 TS regex 以捕获未来漂移。
- [ ] `ManagedPrWatchService.java` + 设计文档（中英）— staged-row 释放描述须符合 round-5 实际行为（先复核钉住 Session；仅当其死/闭/移走或拒绝证明未提交才释放；结果未知保留钉住）。若过度声明则更正双语。
