issues.title: web-shell activity E2E: priority order and unread-clear cases fail intermittently at file scope, pass in isolation

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/development
labels.description: Development experience

labels.name: scope/testing
labels.description: Test frameworks and cases

issues.body:
## Summary

Two cases in `packages/web-shell/client/e2e/web-shell.activity.spec.ts` fail intermittently when the file runs as a whole, and pass when run alone. The failing case varies between runs. Both failures involve the 12-day-old `old-unread-result` fixture row and the priority section's unread membership/order.

Found while sweeping the specs affected by #17733. Attributed there to a pre-existing flake rather than that PR's change; filing separately so the lead is not lost.

## Evidence

All runs on the same machine, same checkout, `--project=chromium --workers=1`. "Base factory" means `packages/web-shell/client/e2e/utils/mockDaemon.ts` restored byte-for-byte from `838e15098e` (sha256 `6cbad625…`); "head factory" is `4ae844886d` (sha256 `3acee6c3…`). The two differ only in cloning `standaloneSessions` and `midTurnMessages`, which `activity.spec.ts` never passes.

| # | Scope | Factory | Result |
| - | ----- | ------- | ------ |
| 1 | 22-spec sweep, 143 cases | head | **1 failed** — `:521` activity ranks attention… |
| 2 | `activity.spec.ts` alone, 15 cases | head | **1 failed** — `:521` (same case) |
| 3 | `:521` alone (`--grep`) | base | 1 passed |
| 4 | `:521` alone (`--grep`) | head | 1 passed |
| 5 | `activity.spec.ts` alone, 15 cases | **base** | **1 failed** — `:580` activity clears shared in-memory unread state… |
| 6 | 22-spec sweep, 143 cases (re-run) | head | **143 passed** |

An earlier 143-case sweep at `838e15098e` also passed. CI on `4ae844886d` runs these `@smoke` cases and both smoke shards plus the aggregate are green.

So: the base factory fails too (run 5), the failing case moves between runs (`:521` vs `:580`), each case passes in isolation on both factories, and a re-run of the identical sweep is green. That rules out the #17733 delta and points at order/timing dependence inside this spec.

## Failure signatures

`:521` — priority order. Expected the secondary workspace's `unread-result` at index 5; received it last:

```
    "unread-result",
    "pinned-result",
-   "unread-result",
    "old-unread-result",
    "running-task",
+   "unread-result",
```

`:580` — after "Clear read chats", priority row count stays at 5 instead of 4 for the full 20 s (42 polls). The next assertion in that case expects `old-unread-result` to be gone.

## Leads

- **Priority order is arrival order, not a recomputed sort.** `activity-model.ts` builds the section as `snapshot.priorityKeys.flatMap(...)`, so the order is whatever order keys entered `priorityKeys`. The `:521` expectation encodes one particular interleaving of the two workspaces' unread state becoming visible. The case waits for `toHaveCount(8)` and then reads the order immediately, which does not wait for the secondary workspace's key to settle into its final position.
- **A local-calendar-day cutoff sits next to a 12-day fixture offset.** `activity-model.ts:201-203` computes `cutoff = startOfDay(snapshot.activatedAt) - 6 days`, and the fixture builds `old-unread-result` at `12 * 24 * 60` minutes before `Date.now()` (`activity.spec.ts:69`, offsets via `stamp()` at `:35-47`). Rows outside that window are excluded from `recent`, so this row's placement depends on the priority path alone — and the window edge moves with the local day, not with elapsed test time.
- **Both failing cases are about shared in-memory unread state.** `:580`'s own title says so, and `:521`'s symptom is unread ordering. Worth checking whether unread state or `priorityKeys` carries across cases in one worker.

I did not isolate which of these produces the failure, so treat them as leads rather than a diagnosis.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd packages/web-shell
npx playwright test --config playwright.config.ts --project=chromium --workers=1 \
  client/e2e/web-shell.activity.spec.ts
```

Run the whole file, not a single `--grep` case — isolation hides it. It is intermittent: expect to need several runs, and expect either `:521` or `:580`.

## Suggested direction

Make the order assertion wait for the settled state rather than reading it right after the count settles, and/or make the fixture's day offsets independent of the local calendar day so the 7-day window edge cannot move under it. Neither is attempted here.

## Limits

Chromium only, Linux only, single worker. I did not run the visuals config, other packages, or a multi-worker configuration, and I did not bisect when this started.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 概述

`packages/web-shell/client/e2e/web-shell.activity.spec.ts` 有两条用例在**整文件运行**时偶发失败、单独跑则通过，且失败的用例在不同轮次间漂移。两次失败都牵涉 12 天前的 `old-unread-result` 夹具行与 priority 区的 unread 归属/顺序。

在为 #17733 做受影响 spec 扫描时发现，已在该 PR 归因为既有 flake 而非其改动所致；单独立 issue 以免线索丢失。

## 证据

同机同检出，`--project=chromium --workers=1`。「base 工厂」指把 `mockDaemon.ts` 按字节还原为 `838e15098e` 版本（sha256 `6cbad625…`），「head 工厂」为 `4ae844886d`（sha256 `3acee6c3…`）。两者只差对 `standaloneSessions` 与 `midTurnMessages` 的克隆，而 `activity.spec.ts` 从不传这两个 override。

| # | 范围 | 工厂 | 结果 |
| - | ---- | ---- | ---- |
| 1 | 22 spec 扫描，143 用例 | head | **1 红** — `:521` |
| 2 | 仅 activity.spec.ts，15 用例 | head | **1 红** — `:521`（同一条） |
| 3 | 仅 `:521`（`--grep`） | base | 1 绿 |
| 4 | 仅 `:521`（`--grep`） | head | 1 绿 |
| 5 | 仅 activity.spec.ts，15 用例 | **base** | **1 红** — `:580` |
| 6 | 22 spec 扫描，143 用例（重跑） | head | **143 全绿** |

`838e15098e` 上更早的一次 143 扫描也全绿。CI 在 `4ae844886d` 上跑这些 `@smoke` 用例，两个 smoke 分片与汇总均绿。

即：base 工厂同样红（run 5）、失败用例在漂移（`:521` vs `:580`）、两臂隔离都绿、同一扫描重跑全绿。这排除了 #17733 的 delta，指向该 spec 内部的顺序/时机依赖。

## 失败签名

`:521`——priority 顺序：secondary workspace 的 `unread-result` 期望在第 6 位，实际落到末位。

`:580`——点了「Clear read chats」后，priority 行数在整 20 秒内（42 次轮询）恒为 5 而非 4；该用例下一条断言正是 `old-unread-result` 应消失。

## 线索

- **priority 顺序是到达顺序，不是重算排序。** `activity-model.ts` 用 `snapshot.priorityKeys.flatMap(...)` 构造该区，顺序即 key 进入 `priorityKeys` 的顺序。`:521` 的期望编码了两个 workspace 的 unread 状态可见的某一种交错。用例在 `toHaveCount(8)` 后**立即**读顺序，并未等 secondary 的 key 落到最终位置。
- **本地日历日截断紧邻 12 天的夹具偏移。** `activity-model.ts:201-203` 算 `cutoff = startOfDay(snapshot.activatedAt) - 6 天`，而夹具把 `old-unread-result` 造在 `Date.now()` 前 `12 * 24 * 60` 分钟（`activity.spec.ts:69`，偏移由 `:35-47` 的 `stamp()` 生成）。窗口外的行被排除出 `recent`，所以该行只能靠 priority 路径出现——而窗口边缘随本地日期移动，不随测试耗时移动。
- **两条失败用例都与共享内存 unread 状态有关。** `:580` 标题即如此，`:521` 的症状是 unread 顺序。值得查 unread 状态或 `priorityKeys` 是否在同 worker 内跨用例残留。

我没有隔离出究竟哪一条导致失败，故以上只是线索、不是诊断。

## 复现

```bash
cd packages/web-shell
npx playwright test --config playwright.config.ts --project=chromium --workers=1 \
  client/e2e/web-shell.activity.spec.ts
```

要跑**整文件**，别用单条 `--grep`——隔离会掩盖它。它是偶发的：可能需要多跑几轮，且可能红在 `:521` 或 `:580`。

## 建议方向

让顺序断言等待状态 settle，而不是在计数 settle 后立即读；并/或让夹具的日偏移与本地日历日无关，使 7 天窗口边缘不会在其下移动。此处均未尝试。

## 限度

仅 Chromium、仅 Linux、单 worker。未跑 visuals config、其它包、多 worker 配置，也未 bisect 起始时间。

</details>

prs.title: feat(managed-agent): clarify Web UI parity and wire local terminal
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a central **Managed capabilities** dialog with all 35 audited daemon-only surface groups, English and Simplified Chinese explanations, search, and an explicit tracker for every group. This distinguishes a tracked gap from a permanent product decision instead of leaving users with an unexplained missing control.

Corrects the capability matrix against the routes that actually exist, including side-query/recap support and archived Session export, while preserving the distinctions between durable Session worktrees and the daemon's narrower reset, branch, handoff, and persisted-attestation contracts.

Enables the existing terminal and required tool-measurement support for local Managed deployments. The local front door now relays Managed terminal upgrades through the existing single ACP dispatcher, with strict path matching, primary/loopback and Host/Origin checks, selective handshake forwarding, initial-byte relay, and shutdown cleanup. The standalone gateway reuses the same relay rather than maintaining a divergent implementation.

Design documentation: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/managed-web-ui-17717/docs/design/2026-11-19-managed-web-ui-parity.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/managed-web-ui-17717/docs/design/2026-11-19-managed-web-ui-parity.zh-CN.md).

## Why it's needed

Managed Web UI hid a large number of daemon-only surfaces without saying which gaps were temporary or intentionally excluded. Several parity rows also contradicted mounted routes, and durable worktree storage obscured important differences in the daemon's operational contracts.

The terminal itself already had the Java admission, ticket, Runtime, and UI code, but local `qwen serve --managed` did not enable or dispatch it. Wiring it through the established local front door makes that existing feature usable without introducing another WebSocket listener or conflating Java's one-time terminal ticket with the daemon bearer token.

The inventory records the choices requested for this implementation, rather than silently making new product exclusions: Memory stays with #13396; Agents, Extensions, Hooks, Channels and Scheduled Tasks stay with #16546; the remaining groups stay with #15084 for separate reviewed decisions.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. From both a full-shell new Session and an existing Session (including host-session-only presentation), open **Managed capabilities**. Expect 35 groups in five categories, English/Chinese reasons, and explicit issue ownership. Search locally and confirm that opening or filtering the inventory creates no Session and makes no new backend request.
2. Build and launch a same-revision local Managed runtime. Open a shell-capable Session after provision and expect `capabilities.terminal: true` and a visible Terminal action. Request a ticket, verify a 101 handshake using `qwen-ws`, run a harmless command at the Workspace cwd, and verify resize and closure.
3. Attempt to reuse a consumed ticket. Expect HTTP 401 rather than a 101 upgrade. Also verify that browser Authorization, Cookie and identity/signature headers are not forwarded to Java, and that primary/loopback, Host and Origin violations are refused before any Java upgrade occurs. Ordinary ACP and unrelated upgrade routes should retain their existing behavior.
4. Check the matrix against the actual routes: BTW/recap cite the mounted side-query surfaces; archived Sessions can be exported; durable Managed worktrees are not mistaken for persisted attestation, ownership-transfer reset, post-create branching, or work-carrying handoff.

### Evidence (Before & After)

**Before:** a static baseline review and focused regression confirmed that there was no central Managed capabilities entry, local terminal deployment options were not enabled, and the unified local front door had no Managed terminal upgrade route. The baseline global runtime-download attempt failed before launch, so no unsupported claim of a completed baseline E2E run is made.

**After (the capability inventory and creation are verified in real Chromium; terminal Group D is still incomplete):** the independent final browser run at `f8b464a6de` observed five categories, 35 unique groups, 35 tracked statuses and issue links, zero owner mismatches or malformed rows. Search/empty-state restoration, focus entry/return and query reset also passed. After an initialization-idle baseline, opening, searching and clearing the dialog produced zero new same-origin requests and zero console/page errors.

![Managed capabilities, real Chromium on f8b464a6de](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17717-validation/managed-capabilities-dark.png)

With the required Workspace selected, real Session creation returned HTTP 202, `status: accepted` and `replayed: false`. The earlier creation-response timeouts were traced to the harness leaving **Choose a Workspace** unselected, so no create request had reached Java. The earlier capability assertion was not a request issued by this static dialog: its exact excess request was `GET /workspaces/%2Ftmp%2Fqwen-17717-postmerge-QI7mut/sessions/live-state` during initialization; the settled rerun retained the zero-request assertion. These were evidenced harness corrections, not production-code changes made to hide a failure.

![Terminal entry visible while model provisioning fails; this is not a successful terminal session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17717-validation/terminal-entry-provisioning-failed.png)

The second image proves only that the Terminal action became visible. The provisioning model Turn failed with `Hosted Harness model authentication is unavailable`, and the harness then stopped while waiting for an obsolete composer placeholder before requesting a ticket. No current-tree ticket, 101/`qwen-ws`, PTY command, resize or replay result was reached. Do not interpret this image as terminal execution proof.

These images are from `f8b464a6de`, not relabeled as `6e76965c76`; the later upstream change is limited to unrelated goal-marker tests, mock support and bilingual design records. Earlier pre-merge terminal successes remain historical evidence and are not substituted for current terminal verification. The final task closed its four observed listeners; its remaining tracked durable worker was separately signalled and the final tracked process/browser lists were empty. The report also records the module's local verification budget as exhausted (734 seconds including assembly), so remaining terminal/CI/manual verification is explicitly pending rather than being retried without limit.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Linux, Node v26.12.1, JDK 21 and Maven 3.9.11 with a task-local Maven repository. Local build/typecheck/bundle, focused Vitest and Maven tests, and an independently driven real Java/Worker/Chromium stack using task-owned temporary directories.

Post-merge root build, typecheck and bundle: all passed on the audited merged tree (`bg_626f35d4`, exit code 0).

Focused TypeScript verification after merge: CLI passed 247 tests across 6 selected files (1020 unrelated declarations in those same files were skipped by the filter); Web Shell passed all 265 tests across the Managed capabilities dialog and Sessions page files. These are focused tests, not claims of a complete repository test run.

After refreshing the task-local sibling SDK installation, the merged-tree Java `ManagedAgentApiContractTest` passed 25 tests with zero failures, errors or skips; Checkstyle passed across all Java modules.

The upstream workflow meta-test, including the changed `sdk-java.yml`, passed all 79 selected tests in the merged tree.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: terminal dispatch is a deliberately narrow exception before daemon bearer verification because Java authenticates its one-time terminal ticket independently. It remains restricted to the Managed deployment, exact raw terminal path, primary listener and loopback, after Host/Origin checks. Handshake forwarding excludes browser credentials and private identity/signing headers. Both socket directions and shutdown cleanup are covered by focused tests and a real terminal path.
- Not validated / out of scope: full CI, the complete Java suites and MySQL profiles remain CI gates. Missing/malformed/cross-Session ticket cases, persistence across same-data-directory restart, reconnect/scrollback replay, per-header audit through the real upstream, `--open` browser cleanup, and the model provisioning Turn are only claimed where the independent report explicitly verifies them. The 35 currently tracked daemon-only surfaces are explained and assigned, not newly implemented or permanently excluded. SSH, resident, extension and repository-wide worktrees remain out of scope.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: no new OpenAPI route or migration. Local Managed startup explicitly rejects `QWEN_SERVE_ACP_HTTP=0` because the terminal needs that dispatcher; the ordinary daemon's ACP opt-out is unchanged. A local terminal is a human shell, not a model tool: an authorized operator can run arbitrary commands as the server OS account without per-command model approval and without container isolation. The user guide documents that trust boundary.

prs.title: fix(core): delimit JSONL records after interrupted appends
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Keeps complete JSONL records readable after an interrupted append leaves a partial, unterminated tail. Legacy asynchronous and synchronous appenders now inspect the final byte and, when needed, include a leading newline in the same buffer as the next record. Existing partial bytes are not rewritten or presented as valid JSON, while normal newline-terminated files retain their original byte format.

The tail probe is best-effort for append-only files: an `EACCES` or `EPERM` failure preserves the original append behavior rather than making read permission a new requirement for writing. Other probe failures still propagate, and opened descriptors are closed on every path.

## Why it's needed

Resuming a session after a partial write could glue the next complete record onto the damaged tail. That new record then disappears during parsing, its children point to a missing parent, and session recovery degrades history even though the later records are present on disk. The reported session showed exactly this chain from a glued physical line to `degraded_history`.

This PR addresses the writer side of that failure. Reader-side salvage of already-glued records is intentionally handled separately in #17756, so this PR is linked with `Part of #17747` rather than a closing keyword.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Confirm ordinary transcript appends are unchanged, and that an existing empty file receives no spurious leading newline.
2. Start from a JSONL file with a valid parent record followed by an unterminated record. The next complete record should begin on a new physical line, subsequent descendants should resolve their parents, and the original partial bytes should remain visibly incomplete.
3. Deny only the read probe with `EACCES` while leaving append permission intact. A complete record should still append with the original newline behavior, proving the added inspection has not regressed append-only files.
4. Exercise the real CLI scenario with isolated `QWEN_HOME` and `QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR`: create a six-record session, interrupt the following write with Linux `RLIMIT_FSIZE` and `SIGXFSZ`, then resume once more. With the final bundle at `85319df31d`, this left a 137-byte partial tail, then yielded 12 readable complete records, one remaining partial line, no glued double-UUID record, and no parent-chain gap. Both `node dist/cli.js serve` `/load` and `/context` returned HTTP 200; recovery was `{"kind":"clean","canContinue":false}`, and no `History gap:` replay notice appeared. All 11 checks in the verification harness passed.
5. Expected local gate results: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/utils/jsonl-utils.test.ts src/services/session-writer-lease.test.ts` reports 200 passed and 2 skipped; `npm run build && npm run bundle` completes successfully.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for appearance: there is no UI or visual behavior change. The evidence image is an actual terminal rendering generated from the final real-CLI verification log, not a mock transcript or a before/after UI comparison.

![Real CLI verification: 11 passed checks, clean recovery, and zero parent-chain gaps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/issue-17747-write-side/verification.png)

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Linux host; Node 24 for the build and tests; `node dist/cli.js` plus isolated daemon and a local mock OpenAI endpoint for E2E; no live model calls.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Every legacy append performs a bounded one-byte tail probe. Read-denied files intentionally retain the original append behavior, so this protection is available only when the tail can be inspected.
- Not validated / out of scope: Existing truncated JSON content is not reconstructed. Reader-side salvage belongs to #17756. This PR does not introduce a universal cross-process append lock or route all transcript writers through the writer lease. Verification focused on the affected core paths and the real interrupted-append chain on Linux; broader suite failures and the CLI timeout observed during review are not claimed as full-repo green runs.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None. Public signatures are unchanged and well-formed JSONL files are written exactly as before.

## Linked Issues

Part of #17747

Related: #17756 (independent reader-side salvage).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 此 PR 的内容

当一次追加被中断、留下不完整的无换行尾部时，保持后续完整 JSONL 记录仍可读取。legacy 异步和同步追加路径现在检查最后一个字节；如有必要，将前置换行与下一条完整记录放入同一个 Buffer。已有的半条记录不会被改写或冒充合法 JSON，正常以换行结尾的文件仍保持原始字节格式。

尾字节探测尽力兼容只写文件：`EACCES` 或 `EPERM` 探测失败时保留原追加行为，不把读权限变成写入的新前提。其他探测错误仍向上传播，所有已打开的描述符都在退出路径上关闭。

## 为什么需要

部分写入之后恢复会话，可能导致下一条完整记录直接粘到损坏尾部后面。新记录因此无法被解析，其子记录指向不存在的父节点，会话恢复把历史降级，尽管后续完整记录仍在磁盘上。原报告正是从这种粘连物理行走到 `degraded_history` 的过程。

本 PR 负责这一故障的写入侧。已经粘连的记录的读侧抢救有意由 #17756 独立处理，因此本 PR 使用 `Part of #17747`，不用自动关闭关键词。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 确认正常 transcript 追加不变，并向已有空文件追加时没有多余的前置换行。
2. 构造含一条有效父记录及一条无换行半条记录的 JSONL 文件。下一条完整记录应从新物理行开始，后续子记录应能找到父记录，原有半行字节仍保持不完整。
3. 只对读取探测注入 `EACCES`，但保留追加权限。完整记录应按原换行语义成功追加，证明新增检查没有破坏只写文件。
4. 使用隔离的 `QWEN_HOME` 和 `QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR` 复跑真实 CLI 场景：创建六条记录的会话，用 Linux `RLIMIT_FSIZE` 和 `SIGXFSZ` 中断下一次写入，再恢复一次。在最终 bundle（`85319df31d`）上，故障留下 137 字节半行，随后读出 12 条完整记录；只剩原本那一条不可解析半行，没有双 UUID 粘行，父链缺口为 0。`node dist/cli.js serve` 的 `/load` 和 `/context` 均返回 HTTP 200，恢复为 `{"kind":"clean","canContinue":false}`，replay 中没有 `History gap:` 提示。验证 harness 的 11 项检查全部通过。
5. 本地门的预期结果：`cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/utils/jsonl-utils.test.ts src/services/session-writer-lease.test.ts` 为 200 passed、2 skipped；`npm run build && npm run bundle` 成功。

### 前后证据（Before & After）

外观无变化：没有 UI 或视觉行为变更。证据图由最终真实 CLI 验证日志生成，不是 mock transcript，也不是界面改动的前后对照。

prs.title: feat(memory): opt-in stable extraction window for prefix reuse
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds an **internal, default-off experiment** for #15493. Today the managed auto-memory extractor reads a sliding `last 40` CURATED history tail that is re-derived on every run (`captureCacheSafeParams` -> `getHistoryTailShallow(40, true)` -> `buildAgentHistory`), so the request bytes after the extractor's constant system prompt change on every appended turn and a provider prefix cache can never be reused.

With `QWEN_CODE_MEMORY_EXTRACT_STABLE_WINDOW=1`, the extractor instead pins a start index into the parent's CURATED history once per extraction **epoch**. Every run sends `curated[windowStart..]`, sanitized exactly as today (`slimCompactionInput` then `buildAgentHistory`), with the task prompt at the tail. Because the start does not move inside an epoch, consecutive runs send a byte-identical history prefix and only the appended turns / task prompt are uncached.

- Cursor gains optional CURATED-coordinate window state (`epoch`, `windowStartCurated`, `coveredCurated`, `windowHeadHash`, `windowEpochId`) beside the existing RAW `processedOffset`. Offset semantics are unchanged; raw offsets are never used to index curated history. Pre-experiment cursors keep working.
- A new epoch seeds its start no later than the last covered curated index, so turns no completed run extracted are never dropped by a rebase. The 40-entry tail remains the fallback when nothing has been covered yet.
- A parked #13004 slice is proven against the material actually sent rather than assumed to be inside the window. With a coverage cursor the seed already sits at or before the last covered index, so the parked turns are normally inside; a first or rebased epoch can seed at the last-40 tail, which may sit after them. In that case only the unproven residue is appended after the window entries — the pinned prefix bytes stay unchanged, the common case appends nothing, and the owed turns are extracted exactly once instead of being silently settled.
- Epochs rebase only on structural invalidation: session change, process restart, an in-place history rewrite (compaction / clear / rewind / branch, wired through the existing boundary hooks), a shrunken history, or a changed head entry. `coveredCurated` advances only after a run made genuine progress.
- The window is deliberately unbounded between structural invalidations: #15493 keeps growth bounding as the session-compaction policy's decision, so this experiment never re-slices to a newer "last N" to fit a budget. Since the extractor input is a subset of the main session's history (and is slimmed further), main-session compaction bounds it.
- The parent's curated history is materialized once, at extraction execution time, through a provider closure passed from both trigger points (`LlmClient` and ACP `Session`); the per-turn scheduling path never materializes or copies it.
- No settings schema change, no default change; the env key is a project-`.env` exclusion (same pattern as #13571). The flag-off path is byte-identical to main (planner called with the same arguments; cursor keeps exactly its three old fields; `EXTRACT_TAIL_ENTRIES = 40` assertion untouched).

## Why it's needed

See #15493: on one deployment (0.25.1, implicit prefix caching) the first request of each extraction run had a median of 64,318 input tokens with 6,272 cached (~10.0% hit); 710/1,096 runs cached only 5K–9K tokens — exactly the extractor's constant system prompt. The main session on the same provider reaches 95.2%, so the provider is not the limiting factor: a window whose first bytes move on every append cannot be reused, no matter how its contents are filtered.

This is the extractor-owned append-only prefix requested in #15493, and it is deliberately complementary to borrowing the parent's rendered system prompt (explicitly out of scope in the issue): the extractor keeps its own system prompt and tool surface, and keeps the #12951 sanitization win.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. With the flag unset (default), confirm the extraction request path is unchanged: the planner receives the same cache-safe tail, the cursor is written with only `{sessionId, processedOffset, updatedAt}`, and the `EXTRACT_TAIL_ENTRIES === 40` assertion stays green.
2. With `QWEN_CODE_MEMORY_EXTRACT_STABLE_WINDOW=1`, run two consecutive extractions with new turns completed in between; the second run's `extraHistory` must start byte-identically with the first run's, with only appended turns after it.
3. Force each rebase path (session switch, process restart, `setHistory` / compaction, truncate, head-entry change) and confirm the epoch increments, the seeded start is never later than the last covered index, and a failed run does not advance coverage. A rewrite of an interior curated entry that preserves the array length and the window-start entry must also start a new epoch (the manager boundary supplies the changed identity); plain growth must not.
4. Confirm the extractor still gets its own system prompt, 5-tool surface and `restrictReadsToMemoryPaths`, and that no parent-only instruction or project file enters its input.
5. Let a cadence skip park a #13004 slice, then run a long following turn: the parked turns must reach the extractor exactly once. The same must hold when the flag is enabled after a skip with no prior window cursor, and in both cases the window entries stay first so the reusable prefix is unchanged.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Synthetic harness over the real window helpers (60 turns / 120 curated entries, 8 runs, +2 turns per run, real extractor system/task prompts):

| metric | sliding 40-tail | pinned epoch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| adjacent-pair cacheable fraction (median) | 11.9% | 90.0% |
| overall request-byte reuse across 8 runs | 10.5% | 81.4% |
| total cold bytes | 757,886 B | 203,464 B (-73.2%) |
| previously-sent history bytes reused on the last pair | 39 B / 87,920 B | 140,643 B / 140,643 B (100%) |

Automated verification on the PR head: focused core memory suites 97/97 pass across the five touched files, including a real manager -> extractor -> planner integration pin (flag-on-from-start parked-slice control, the coverage-less-cursor branch that fails without the fix, and an epoch-identity pair: an interior in-place rewrite must bump the manager generation and reseed, while append-only growth must keep the epoch, the pinned start and the old prefix byte-identical), plus the three fixtures that keep coverage from advancing without genuine progress and keep the window across no-op / flag-off runs; the existing #13004 cadence case passes 2/2; scoped eslint/prettier clean; the epoch-identity case is red on a no-op generation bump (M13 mutant) and green with the real wiring. CLI env-key suite 54/54 passed on the prior tip. Core-scoped `tsc --noEmit` passed on an earlier tip, but no typecheck or full build was rerun after the final commit — repo-wide checks are left to CI.

Not measured: a live provider prefix-cache run and extraction fact-quality comparison (the design doc's paired-run acceptance remains open; that is why the flag stays default-off).

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--: | :--: |
| Linux | ✅ |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js v26.8.2, local unit runs only; no sandbox.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk: a missed rebase point leaves a stale prefix cached; correctness is unaffected (only a cache miss), and every rebase seeds at or before the last covered index so no unextracted turn is skipped. Cursor state is additive/optional, so rolling back to the old build is safe.
- The window intentionally grows with the session within an epoch (bounded by main-session compaction). Very long epochs can therefore produce large extractor inputs until compaction rebases the epoch; that trade-off is the point of the experiment and is measured by paired runs, not capped here.
- Out of scope: sharing the parent's rendered system prompt, extractor tool-surface changes, sanitization/selection policy changes, persistent extractor conversation objects, making the experiment default-on, and any growth cap/budget (bounding long-session growth remains a compaction-policy discussion per #15493).
- Not validated: live provider cache-hit percentages and memory-content quality; those require paired runs and are deferred to the experiment's follow-up.

## Linked Issues

Refs #15493, #13612, #13004, #13571, #12951.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

背景：#15493 中已量化——提取器每次 run 都从滑动的"最近 40 条"重建请求，因此系统提示词之后的前缀每次都变，前缀缓存只能命中那 5K–9K 的系统提示词（中位命中 10.0%，主会话对照 95.2%）。

本 PR 是一个**默认关闭的内部实验**：把窗口起点按"epoch"钉在父会话的 curated 历史里，同一个 epoch 内起点不动，每次只追加新 turn，任务提示词放在尾部，因此相邻两次 run 的历史前缀逐字节一致。session 切换、进程重启、压缩/清空/回退、历史缩短或头部改写时显式开启新 epoch，并用"覆盖偏移"保证不会跳过任何没被成功提取过的 turn。

#13004 被跳过（parked）的切片不再假定一定被窗口覆盖，而是用实际要发送的内容做覆盖证明：有覆盖游标时窗口起点本来就不晚于最后一次覆盖的位置，切片通常就在窗口内；首个/重建的 epoch 可能从最近 40 条尾部起种，因而排在切片之后。这种情况下只把"未被证明覆盖"的剩余部分追加在窗口条目之后——被钉住的前缀字节不变，常见情况不追加任何东西，被欠的 turn 恰好被提取一次，而不是被静默结清。

原始 `processedOffset` 仍是 RAW 坐标，窗口状态单独用 CURATED 坐标记录；40 条尾部路径和 `EXTRACT_TAIL_ENTRIES=40` 完全不动，默认行为零变化。开关为 `QWEN_CODE_MEMORY_EXTRACT_STABLE_WINDOW=1`，与 #13571 一样不进 settings schema、禁止项目 .env 开启；不做增长上限（增长边界属于压缩策略，见 #15493），因为提取器输入是主会话历史的子集且经过进一步瘦身，主会话压缩会先发生。

与 issue 中明确列为 out of scope 的"借用父会话 system prompt"是互补关系：提取器保留自己的 system prompt、工具面和 #12951 的净化收益。合成 harness 实测相邻请求可复用前缀中位 11.9%→90.0%、8 次 run 总冷字节 −73.2%；另有 manager→extractor→planner 的集成用例钉住 parked 切片路径与 epoch 身份（内部就地改写必须换 epoch 并重种，纯追加必须保持前缀逐字节一致）。真实 provider 缓存命中率与记忆质量对比仍未测，因此默认保持关闭。

</details>

controls, no-loss of the unextracted tail, an unchanged flag-off path
(including the 40-entry assertion), readability of a pre-experiment cursor,
and the absence of size-driven rebases on a large window. Refs #15493,
#13612, #13004.

* fix(memory): carry unproven parked slices in the stable extract window

The stable path sent only `curatedHistory.slice(windowStart)` and assumed the
window covers every parked #13004 slice. That holds once a coverage cursor
exists (the seed is never later than the last covered curated index), but a
first or rebased epoch without coverage seeds at the last-40 tail, which can

resolver's own guard only compares the window-start entry: an in-place rewrite

can force the rebase. Nothing crossed the manager boundary to pin that wiring

Drive the real manager -> extractor -> planner seam with the flag on:

prs.title: feat(qqbot): let the agent send a local file to the chat
prs.body:
## What this PR does

It lets the agent hand media back to a QQ chat. A new per-channel switch, off by default, exposes four tools that each take an absolute local path: one sends a file, one an image, one a video, and one a voice message. The channel checks that the file really is a regular file inside the session's workspace or the system temporary directory (symlinks are resolved and refused when they escape, paths with more than one hard link are refused, and the opened descriptor is re-checked), then uploads it through the platform's chunked upload path and sends it as a rich-media message. The image, video, and voice tools also check the file's magic bytes and its per-kind soft limit before any upload, so a file the platform would render as something else — a GIF, a WebP, an over-limit image — is refused with a pointer to the file tool instead of being quietly downgraded to a file card. Every send reuses the turn's reply anchor and message-sequence counter, so media sent mid-turn stays in the same reply chain as that turn's text; when the reply window has closed it falls back to an active message, and when active messages are disabled it reports the refusal instead of dropping the media or silently replacing it with text. Upload failures are reported to the model with the platform's error code classified, so a retryable part failure can be retried and a daily-limit rejection is not.

## Why it's needed

An agent working in a channel could read a conversation and write files, but had no supported way to deliver one to the user: images, videos, and voice messages could come in, and text could go out, but a report, a generated archive, a chart, a short clip, or a voice note produced locally had to be retrieved by hand from the machine. The tools close that gap with the same ownership rule as the other adapter tools — a tool is only offered to sessions of the channel that registered it. The platform renders an image, a video, and a voice message differently from a file card, so the sender picks the form the user should see instead of every artifact arriving as a download.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Enable the new file switch on a QQ channel and, from a session in that chat, ask the agent to send a file it created inside the workspace; a file card should arrive in the chat and the send should belong to the same reply chain as that turn's text. Then confirm the boundary: a path outside the workspace and outside the temporary directory is refused, a symlink pointing outside is refused, a file over the size cap is refused before any upload, and with the switch off the tool is not registered at all. In a chat where active messages are disabled, force the turn's reply window to close and confirm the tool reports the refusal rather than sending text. Then ask the same session for a generated PNG, an MP4, and a WAV (or MP3/SILK/OGG): the chat should receive an image message, a playable video, and a voice bar, each still in that turn's reply chain. Hand the image tool a GIF or a 21 MB PNG and confirm it is refused before any upload with the accepted formats and the file-tool fallback named, instead of arriving as a file card.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — channel-side tools, no TUI change.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only; the platform upload and send paths are exercised with a mocked HTTP layer. Local verification at this head: `file-tools.test.ts` + `api.test.ts` 85/85, `send.test.ts` + `events.test.ts` 368/368, `tsc --build packages/channels/qqbot` exit 0.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the tools hand a local file to the platform under the bot's own identity, so they are opt-in per channel and bounded to the session workspace, the temporary directory, and a per-kind size cap (20 MiB for files, 20 MB for images and voice messages, 30 MB for videos); the path and format checks are the security-relevant part.
- Not validated / out of scope: a real end-to-end send against the live QQ platform. The accepted format lists come from the platform's documentation, which disagrees with itself on image and voice formats (the file-type table says `png`/`jpg` and `silk`, the overview text also lists `gif`/`webp`/`bmp` and `mp3`/`wav`/`ogg`); the design follows the table for images and the wider list for voice, and a format the platform rejects comes back as its own error with a fallback to the file tool. The bilingual design document is at `docs/design/2026-10-25-qqbot-outbound-media.md`.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; the switch defaults off and the change adds a new option and tool rather than changing existing behaviour.

## Linked Issues

The adapter-tool pipeline these tools are exposed through landed as #14348 (now in `main`); this branch has `main` merged into it, so the diff contains only the outbound-media increments.

prs.title: feat(i18n): add Arabic support for CLI and Web Shell with RTL layout
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This pull request adds complete Arabic language support across both the command-line interface and the Web Shell, including right-to-left layout support in the Web Shell and exported HTML transcripts.

In core and the CLI, Arabic is registered as a shipped language option in the shared output language table and settings schema so it appears alongside existing locales in interactive language selection, slash-command completions, daemon feature advertisement, ACP integrations, and automated locale checks. A full Arabic locale catalog is included for CLI prompts, commands, tool display names, and subscription quota notices with all six Arabic cardinal plural forms.

In the Web Shell, Arabic is supported across transcript views, standalone gates, Managed agent views, slash-command subcommand completion, local command hints, toast notices, settings dialogs, and the service-worker offline fallback. Right-to-left rendering is driven automatically from the resolved UI language via document and portal direction attributes, Radix direction context propagation, conversion of layout-directional CSS and Tailwind utilities to logical properties, mirrored pointer-drag resize deltas and horizontal arrow-key navigation, flipped directional chevrons and back arrows, RTL-aware sticky DataTable pinning and Switch thumb travel, and explicit left-to-right preservation for code blocks, diffs, terminals, structured spreadsheets, charts, left-to-right plan dependency topology graphs, and interactive waiting games. Interactive-only Arabic translations are stubbed out of the read-only transcript export bundle while keeping transcript-reachable Arabic strings available in exported HTML documents, and the document export bundle budget has been updated to match the measured size.

## Why it's needed

Arabic-speaking users previously had to fall back to English in both the terminal CLI and the browser Web Shell, and Arabic text inside the Web Shell rendered inside an English left-to-right shell chrome with unmirrored spacing, borders, popovers, drawers, and directional controls. Adding full Arabic catalogs, CLDR six-form pluralization, and full RTL layout mirroring makes both interfaces natural and usable for Arabic users without inflating read-only exported HTML transcripts with interactive-only UI strings.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Switch the CLI UI language to Arabic via settings or `/language ui ar`, and verify locale normalization for regional and POSIX variants such as `ar-SA` and `ar_EG.UTF-8` while confirming unrelated prefix neighbors like `armenian` do not map to Arabic. Confirm CLI menus, `/language` choices, tool display badges, and multi-form quota messages render in Arabic, and model output language settings recognize `Arabic` alongside existing options.
2. Open the Web Shell in standalone or embedded mode with Arabic selected via `?language=ar`, `/language ui ar`, `/settings`, or browser locale, and verify both the root container and the portal root carry `lang="ar"` and `dir="rtl"`.
3. Inspect key RTL surfaces in Web Shell: the sidebar docks on the start side and widens when dragging its resize handle leftward, popovers and tooltips open on the mirrored side, the floating artifact drawer slides from the left edge, the docked right panel widens when dragging its divider rightward, horizontal tab and timeline arrow navigation follows RTL order, directional back arrows and collapsed chevrons mirror visually, switches slide leftward when toggled on, and DataTable sticky leading/trailing columns pin to the right and left edges respectively.
4. Confirm code blocks, diffs, terminals, spreadsheets, ECharts, and left-to-right DAG plan dependency graphs remain legible with intentional left-to-right structural geometry while user messages isolate mixed-direction text cleanly.
5. Export a conversation to HTML while using Arabic and verify exported transcripts render localized status labels and RTL direction without pulling interactive-only Arabic dictionaries into the read-only transcript bundle.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Automated verification after the final edits confirmed green workspace builds, TypeScript typechecks across all packages and integration tests, zero-warning strict linting, CLI i18n checks showing 1976/2005 Arabic keys translated with zero missing keys, clean read-only transcript bundle builds within the updated byte ceiling, and passing unit/DOM tests covering core output-language consumers, CLI language/quota behavior, Web Shell Arabic pluralization, non-collision locale normalization, build-boundary separation, and RTL layout/resize/drawer/table behavior. Live browser screenshots were not captured locally in this turn.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local Node 22 macOS verification covering workspace builds, strict ESLint, TypeScript typechecks, Prettier formatting, CLI locale validation, and Vitest unit/DOM suites. Playwright browser E2E, integration suites, and Windows/Linux hosts remain to be validated in CI.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Adding Arabic to the shared core output-language table affects downstream consumers across core goal verification, session title generation, the settings JSON schema, the CLI language registry and `/language` command, serve settings/feature routes, ACP integration, and the i18n check script; all downstream consumers were verified against the build, typecheck, and existing/expanded unit tests. In Web Shell, keeping synchronous translator lookups splits Arabic strings into transcript-reachable and interactive-only modules so read-only HTML exports grow by 47,120 measured bytes (including RTL runtime wiring) rather than carrying all interactive copy. Broad logical CSS/Tailwind refactoring across Web Shell components relies on automated CSS, ref-compat, and DOM suites locally and benefits from Playwright/visual spot-checks in CI.
- Not validated / out of scope: VS Code IDE companion host-chrome strings outside the embedded Web Shell remain English and Simplified Chinese only and were left untouched as requested scope focused on CLI and Web Shell; terminal RTL rendering behavior depends on the host terminal emulator; full Playwright visual tests and non-macOS runners were not executed locally; an unrelated pre-existing timing race observed in the Managed local-files bridge test suite also reproduces identically on the untouched base commit.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None. English remains the fallback locale, existing partial-catalog behavior for Russian is unchanged, and existing language configuration values continue to work without migration.

## Linked Issues

None

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

本 PR 为命令行界面（CLI）与 Web Shell 增加了完整的阿拉伯语语言支持，并在 Web Shell 及导出的 HTML 对话记录中支持从右到左（RTL）的镜像布局。

在 Core 与 CLI 部分，我们将阿拉伯语注册为共享输出语言表及设置 Schema 中的内置语言选项，使其能够同步出现在交互式语言选择器、斜杠命令补全、守护进程特性声明、ACP 集成以及国际化校验脚本中。同时新增了完整的 CLI 阿拉伯语翻译词典，覆盖交互提示、命令说明、工具显示名称以及包含全部六种阿拉伯语基数复数形态的订阅配额提示。

在 Web Shell 部分，阿拉伯语已全面覆盖对话记录视图、独立认证门槛页、托管 Agent 视图、斜杠命令子命令补全、本地命令提示、Toast 通知、设置面板以及 Service Worker 离线回退页。系统会根据解析出的界面语言自动在根容器与 Portal 根节点设置 `lang="ar"` 与 `dir="rtl"`，并通过 Radix 方向上下文向下透传；同时将具备方向语义的 CSS 与 Tailwind 样式统一改造为逻辑属性，在 RTL 模式下镜像处理侧边栏与右侧面板拖拽调整宽度的方向符号、横向键盘方向键导航、返回箭头与折叠尖角图标方向、Switch 开关滑块位移动画以及 DataTable 固定列的吸顶方向；对于代码块、Diff、终端、电子表格、图表、有向无环计划拓扑图和等待小游戏等需要保持物理从左到右结构的内容，则显式保留 LTR 排版，并对混合方向的用户消息采用双向隔离渲染。为避免导出体积膨胀，仅交互界面使用的阿拉伯语词条会在导出 HTML 构建模式中被独立存根剔除，仅保留只读记录所需词条，并依据实测字节数同步更新了导出运行时大小预算。

## 为什么需要这个改动

此前使用阿拉伯语的用户在 CLI 与 Web Shell 中只能回退到英文界面，且 Web Shell 中的阿拉伯语文本会直接嵌入英文 LTR 界面框架里，导致边距、边框、弹出层方向、抽屉滑出方向以及箭头图标方向均与阿拉伯语阅读习惯相反。通过补充完整的阿拉伯语词条、CLDR 六形态复数规则以及全套 RTL 镜像布局，两个端都可以为阿拉伯语用户提供自然完整的使用体验，同时保证只读导出的 HTML 文件不会被仅用于交互界面的翻译文本拖累体积。

## 审阅测试计划

### 验证方式

1. 在 CLI 中通过配置文件或 `/language ui ar` 切换界面语言为阿拉伯语，并验证 `ar-SA`、`ar_EG.UTF-8` 等区域/POSIX 标签的规范化解析，同时确认诸如 `armenian` 等共享前缀但不相干的词不会被误识别为阿拉伯语。检查 CLI 菜单、`/language` 选项、工具名称徽章、订阅配额多复数形式以及模型输出语言 `Arabic` 的显示与设置是否正常。
2. 在独立模式或嵌入模式下通过 `?language=ar`、`/language ui ar`、`/settings` 或浏览器语言切换到阿拉伯语打开 Web Shell，确认主根节点和 Portal 根节点均带有 `lang="ar"` 和 `dir="rtl"` 属性。
3. 验证 Web Shell 中的核心 RTL 交互与布局：侧边栏停靠在起始侧且向左拖拽分隔条时加宽，Tooltip 与 Popover 在镜像侧弹出，窄屏下的浮动右侧抽屉从左侧滑入，宽屏停靠下的右侧面板向右拖拽分隔条时加宽，水平 Tab 与时间轴导航遵循 RTL 方向键顺序，返回箭头和折叠箭头图标完成水平镜像，Switch 在开启时向左滑动，DataTable 固定首列与操作尾列分别吸附在右侧和左侧边缘。
4. 确认代码块、Diff 视图、终端、电子表格、ECharts 图表以及计划 DAG 拓扑图依然保持清晰的从左到右结构方向，同时包含阿英混排的用户消息可正确自动隔离文本方向。
5. 在阿拉伯语环境下导出 HTML 对话记录，确认导出文档可正确呈现本地化状态文案与 RTL 排版，且仅交互场景使用的阿拉伯语词典未被打包进只读导出产物。

### 对比证据

在最终修改完成后，我们已完成全仓工作区构建、全量 TypeScript 类型检查、零警告严格 ESLint 检查、Prettier 格式化校验、CLI 国际化脚本校验（阿拉伯语共翻译 1976/2005 项，缺失关键项为 0）、导出 HTML 运行时体积校验以及核心模块、CLI、Web Shell 与 VS Code Companion 相关单测和 DOM 测试验证。本次在本地未额外截取实时浏览器界面截图。

### 测试环境

|     系统   | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 运行环境说明

基于本地 macOS 与 Node 22 环境完成了工作区构建、严格 ESLint 检查、TypeScript 类型检查、Prettier 格式检查、CLI 语言校验与 Vitest 单元/DOM 测试；Playwright 浏览器 E2E 测试、集成测试及 Windows/Linux 环境需由 CI 进一步验证。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：在核心公共输出语言表中新增阿拉伯语会影响目标校验、会话标题生成、设置 JSON Schema、CLI 语言注册及 `/language` 命令、daemon 设置与特性路由、ACP 集成以及 i18n 检查脚本等下游消费方；上述全部下游消费方均已通过构建、类型检查以及原有与新增单测的验证。在 Web Shell 中，为保持同步翻译读取契约，我们将阿拉伯语词条拆分为只读记录与交互界面两个模块，使导出 HTML 运行时资产实测净增 47,120 字节（包含 RTL 方向控制逻辑）而不会引入大批量交互文案。组件库及各页面级样式大量改造为 CSS 逻辑属性与 RTL 镜像规则后，本地已通过 CSS 规则、ref 兼容与 DOM 单测验证，建议 CI 中结合视觉回归进一步复核。
- 未验证 / 范围之外：VS Code 扩展宿主侧外部框架文案未在本次范围内，仍维持英文与简体中文（其中嵌入的 Web Shell 本体支持阿拉伯语和 RTL）；终端层面的双向文字排布效果取决于用户所用的终端模拟器本身；全量 Playwright 视觉测试及非 macOS 平台尚未在本地运行；在 Web Shell 全量测试运行中观察到的 Managed 本地文件桥接测试条目存在一处上游基线提交已引入的无关竞态失败（我们的改动未涉及该目录）。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。英文继续作为兜底语言，俄语既有的部分词条策略保持不变，现有语言配置无需任何迁移即可继续使用。

prs.title: fix(web-shell): refuse background-work deletion in the dialog for any row
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The delete dialog now refuses to delete a session with running background work whether or not it is the session this client is attached to, matching what the sidebar row already does. The attached-session rule is unchanged: that session is deletable once nothing is running. Clicking a refused row now names the reason in the dialog hint: the danger button is disabled in that state, so the row click is the only place the refusal can reach the user. Only the attached row's wording says "the current session"; any other row reuses the existing background-work refusal string. That hint follows live state rather than the click: it names whichever rule blocks the row now, disappears once the row is deletable again — without waiting for another click — and stays quiet while a delete is running or an outcome or a live error holds the slot. Those texts are rendered nowhere else in the dialog, so a later refusal must not be able to take the slot from them — and a transient load error must not mute it for good, so the hint mirrors the error rather than latching it. The load error and the delete outcome keep separate slots — sharing one let a recovering list clear a failure the user had not read yet. The guard is renamed so its name no longer claims a narrower scope than it has, and the rule itself now lives beside `hasLiveWork` as one shared helper that the row gate, the eligibility check and the dialog all call — it takes each caller's own notion of "current" rather than deriving it from an id, because the sidebar compares workspace-qualified identity. The Session Overview card gate is a fourth delete path and deliberately stays stricter, so it keeps its own expression; the design records that difference.

The design document is reconciled in both languages: its Solution section still described the dialog's guard as a current-session block while acceptance criterion 4 already promised the dialog refuses background work without that qualification.

## Why it's needed

Follow-up to the review on #17676 (merged). That change widened the sidebar row's Delete gate to refuse background work on any row, but left the dialog's guard scoped to the attached session. The two entry points therefore disagreed about a non-attached background-only session: the row refused it, while the dialog kept it tickable, kept it in the request, and sent it. The delete route has no idle guard, so confirming ended the background work the row was advertising as running.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Open the Web Shell against a daemon with at least two sessions. Have a session that is **not** the one you are viewing run a long command in the background (any background shell, e.g. a ten-minute sleep) and let its turn finish.
2. Open the delete dialog. That session's row must render disabled and must not be tickable. Before this change it could be ticked and deleted.
3. Tick that row while it is idle, then start background work in it from elsewhere. The row must become unchecked, stop being counted in the hint, and be absent from the delete request — while any other ticked row is still deleted.
4. The session you are attached to must stay deletable when nothing is running in it. Clicking a refused row must name the reason in the hint — the background wording for another row, the "current session" wording for the attached one — and a successful tick must clear it so the selection count is readable again.
5. Leave that refusal on screen and let the background command finish. Without any further click, the hint must stop asserting the refusal and the row must become tickable again. Filtering the refused row away and clearing the filter must not bring the refusal back either. If the session list fails once and then recovers, the refusal must be able to speak again afterwards — and a delete that failed while that error was showing must keep its failure text through the recovery.
6. Confirming a delete while a refusal is showing must show the delete's outcome, not the older refusal. Clicking a blocked row *while the request is still running* must leave the hint on that request's progress and then its failure — and clicking one *after* a failed delete must leave the failure text in place, since the dialog renders it nowhere else.
7. In the sidebar, a session that shares an id with the one you are viewing but lives in another workspace must keep its Delete action while both run a turn, and lose it once it has background work.

Commands, copy-pasteable from the repository root:

```
cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/components/dialogs/ client/components/sidebar/ client/session-catalog/ client/components/SessionOverviewPanel.test.tsx client/i18n.test.ts client/visual-capture-contracts.test.ts
cd packages/web-shell && npx playwright test client/e2e/web-shell.background-turn.spec.ts client/e2e/web-shell.session-live-state.spec.ts client/e2e/web-shell.composer-usage.spec.ts
cd packages/web-shell && npm run typecheck
```

Observed on this branch: 2039 unit tests passed across 81 files, 13 Playwright tests passed across the three specs, typecheck exited 0, ESLint and Prettier clean.

The acceptance case ticks a non-attached row plus another row, turns the first one busy, and asserts the row renders disabled and unchecked, the hint counts one rather than two, and the request carries only the other id. Removing the background term from the guard turns exactly that case red. Each new behaviour has its own witness: dropping the expiry effect, freezing the reason at click time, keeping the refusal through a delete confirm, and swapping workspace-qualified identity for a session id in either sidebar gate each turn exactly one named case red.

### Evidence

Staged against a live daemon: a probe session in the daemon's primary workspace ran a background shell with its turn finished, so the only work left was background work.

Clicking that row leaves it unchecked and names the rule in the hint, while another row stays ticked:

![Refusal named in the delete dialog hint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r2/refusal-hint.png)

152 seconds later the background command ended. With no further click the hint stopped asserting the refusal, and the row ticked normally — the count is readable again and the guard did not latch:

![Tickable again once the background work ended](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r2/tickable-after-expiry.png)

A second pair, same live page and daemon, with the delete failed at the network boundary so no session is actually removed. Before the fix, clicking the background-busy row after the failure replaced the only statement of what went wrong:

![Before: the refusal takes the failure's slot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r4/before-fix.png)

After the fix the failure text stays, and the refused row is still untickable:

![After: the failure keeps the hint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r4/after-fix.png)

A third pair stages a transient load failure: the primary workspace's session list is failed at the network boundary, then a real catalog change makes it refetch and recover. Before the fix the stale error stayed in the hint forever and clicking the background-busy row said nothing:

![Before: a transient error mutes the refusal for good](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r5/before-fix.png)

After the fix the hint clears when the list recovers, and the refused row names its rule again:

![After: the refusal speaks again once the list recovers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r5/after-fix.png)

A fourth pair covers the two-owner case: the list fails while its stale rows stay on screen, a delete fails on every row, then the list recovers. Before the fix the failure text was lost to the recovery:

![Before: error recovery clears the delete failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r6/before-fix.png)

After the fix the failure keeps its own slot and survives:

![After: the delete failure survives error recovery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r6/after-fix.png)

The row's disabled rendering already existed for the attached session; this extends which rows reach it and makes the refusal expire with the state it describes.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment

Unit tests and the three Playwright specs run locally on macOS against the repository's mock daemon. The screenshots above come from a Chromium session driven against a live local daemon, with no page errors.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a session with background work can no longer be deleted from the dialog until that work finishes. That is the intended refusal — the delete route closes the live session unconditionally — and it matches the sidebar row and the Session Overview card.
- Not validated / out of scope: the pre-existing difference for a **turn** running in a non-attached session (the row offers Delete, the card refuses it) is untouched and remains recorded as a separate policy decision in the design.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No new translation keys — the existing background refusal string is reused.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/web-shell-delete-dialog-background-guard/docs/design/web-shell-sidebar-background-work-indicator.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/web-shell-delete-dialog-background-guard/docs/design/web-shell-sidebar-background-work-indicator.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to #17676.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

删除弹窗现在对**任何**有后台工作在跑的会话都拒绝删除，无论它是否为本客户端所连接的那个——与侧栏行内已有的行为一致。当前会话的规则不变：无工作时仍可删除。点击被拒绝的行现在会在弹窗提示区说出原因：该状态下危险按钮是禁用的，点击行是拒绝唯一能触达用户的地方。只有当前会话那条文案才说「当前会话」，其他行复用已有的后台工作拒绝文案。该提示跟随活状态而不是那次点击：它说出当下阻断该行的那条规则，行恢复可删后即消失——不必等下一次点击——并在删除进行中、或结果与仍然存在的错误占着这个位置时保持安静。弹窗别处不再渲染那些文本，所以之后的拒绝不能把它们挤掉——而一次临时的加载错误也不该把提示永久闭嘴，因此提示镜像错误而不是闩住它。加载错误与删除结果各占独立的槽——共用一个槽时，列表恢复会清掉用户还没读到的失败信息。判据同时改名，不再让名字声称比实际更窄的范围；规则本身以一个新的共享 helper 放在 `hasLiveWork` 旁边，行内闸门、资格判断与弹窗都调用它——它接收各调用方自己的「当前」判定而不是从 id 推导，因为侧栏比的是带工作区限定的 identity。Session Overview 的卡片闸门是第四条删除路径，且刻意更严，因此保留自己的表达式；设计文档记录了这条差异。

设计文档两版同步自洽：Solution 段仍把弹窗判据描述为「当前会话」的拦截，而验收标准 4 早已无限定地承诺弹窗拒绝后台工作。

## 为什么需要

这是 #17676（已合入）评审的后续。那次改动把侧栏行内 Delete 闸门放宽到对任何行都拒绝后台工作，却把弹窗判据留在「仅当前会话」。于是两个入口对「非当前 + 仅后台」的会话给出不同答案：行内拒绝，弹窗却仍可勾选、仍保留在请求里并发出去。删除路由没有 idle 闸门，确认后就会结束该行宣称正在跑的后台工作。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

1. 打开连着 daemon 的 Web Shell，至少两个会话。让一个**并非**你正在查看的会话在后台跑一条长命令（任意后台 shell，例如十分钟 sleep），并让它的回合结束。
2. 打开删除弹窗。该会话的行必须渲染为禁用且不可勾选。改动前它可以被勾选并删除。
3. 在它空闲时勾选它，随后从别处让它开始后台工作。该行必须变为未勾选、不再计入提示计数、并从删除请求中消失——而其他被勾选的行仍会被删除。
4. 你所连接的会话在无工作时必须仍可删除。点击被拒绝的行必须在提示区说出原因——其他行是后台文案，当前会话是「当前会话」那一条——而成功勾选后必须清除它，让选择计数重新可读。
5. 让该拒绝提示留在屏幕上，等后台命令跑完。在没有任何进一步点击的情况下，提示必须停止断言这条拒绝，该行必须重新可勾选。把被拒行过滤掉再清空过滤，也不得让拒绝复活。若会话列表失败一次随后恢复，之后拒绝必须还能重新出声；而在该错误显示期间失败的删除，其失败文案必须挺过这次恢复。
6. 在拒绝提示仍在时确认删除，必须显示删除的结果而不是那条更早的拒绝。在**请求仍在进行中**点击被阻断的行，提示必须留在这次请求的进度、随后是它的失败信息上；在**删除失败之后**点击被阻断的行，失败文案必须原地保留——弹窗别处不再渲染它。
7. 在侧栏里，一个与你正在查看的会话同 id、但位于另一个工作区的会话，在两者都在跑回合时必须仍保留 Delete；一旦它有了后台工作就必须失去 Delete。

命令，可在仓库根目录直接复制执行：

```
cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/components/dialogs/ client/components/sidebar/ client/session-catalog/ client/components/SessionOverviewPanel.test.tsx client/i18n.test.ts client/visual-capture-contracts.test.ts
cd packages/web-shell && npx playwright test client/e2e/web-shell.background-turn.spec.ts client/e2e/web-shell.session-live-state.spec.ts client/e2e/web-shell.composer-usage.spec.ts
cd packages/web-shell && npm run typecheck
```

本分支实测：81 个文件共 2039 个单测通过，三个 spec 共 13 个 Playwright 用例通过，typecheck 退出 0，ESLint 与 Prettier 干净。

验收用例勾选一个非当前行与另一行，让前者变忙，断言该行渲染为禁用且未勾选、提示计数为 1 而非 2、请求只带另一个 id。从判据里去掉后台项，恰好让这条用例变红。每条新行为都有各自的见证：去掉失效效应、把原因冻结在点击时、让拒绝穿过删除确认、以及把任一侧栏闸门里带工作区限定的 identity 换成 session id，都恰好让一条具名用例变红。

### 证据

对着真实 daemon 造景：在 daemon 主工作区里放一个探针会话，回合已结束、只剩一条后台 shell 在跑。

点击该行后它保持未勾选，提示区说出这条规则，而另一行仍保持勾选：

![删除弹窗提示区说出拒绝原因](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r2/refusal-hint.png)

152 秒后后台命令结束。在没有任何进一步点击的情况下，提示不再断言这条拒绝，该行也能正常勾选——计数重新可读，闸门没有锁死：

![后台工作结束后可再次勾选](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r2/tickable-after-expiry.png)

第二组对照，同一个真实页面与 daemon，删除在网络边界被置为失败，因此没有真的删除任何会话。修复前，失败之后点击那个后台忙碌的行，会把唯一说明出错原因的文本替换掉：

![修复前：拒绝挤占了失败文案的位置](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r4/before-fix.png)

修复后失败文案原地保留，被拒的行仍不可勾选：

![修复后：失败文案保住提示位](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r4/after-fix.png)

第三组对照造的是临时加载失败：在网络边界让主工作区的会话列表失败，再用一次真实的目录变更让它重取并恢复。修复前，过期错误会一直挂在提示里，点击后台忙碌的行什么也不说：

![修复前：一次临时错误把拒绝永久闭嘴](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r5/before-fix.png)

修复后，列表恢复时提示清空，被拒的行重新说出自己的规则：

![修复后：列表恢复后拒绝重新出声](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r5/after-fix.png)

第四组对照覆盖「两个写入方」的情形：列表失败但旧行仍在屏上，此时删除对每一行都失败，随后列表恢复。修复前失败文案被这次恢复清掉：

![修复前：错误恢复清掉了删除失败信息](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r6/before-fix.png)

修复后失败信息有自己的槽，挺过恢复：

![修复后：删除失败信息挺过错误恢复](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17713-validation/pr17713-r6/after-fix.png)

行的禁用渲染本就存在于当前会话，本次扩大哪些行会走到它，并让拒绝随它所描述的状态一起失效。

### 测试过的系统

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### 环境

单测与三个 Playwright spec 在 macOS 本地、对着仓库自带的 mock daemon 执行。上面两张截图来自驱动 Chromium 对着本地真实 daemon 的会话，无页面错误。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：有后台工作的会话在该工作结束前不能从弹窗删除。这正是意图中的拒绝——删除路由会无条件关闭 live 会话——且与侧栏行、Session Overview 卡片一致。
- 未验证 / 不在范围：非当前会话里正在跑**回合**时的那条既有分歧（行提供 Delete、卡片拒绝）本次不动，仍作为单独的策略决定记在设计文档里。
- 破坏性改动 / 迁移说明：无。不新增文案键，复用已有的后台拒绝文案。

prs.title: fix(tui): backport ink #1031 so a rows-shrink clears the frame
prs.body:
## Why

The append-only Static path (`ui.useTerminalBuffer: false`) swallows transcript lines. `ui.useTerminalBuffer: true` / Virtualized History is unaffected — it repaints the viewport and does not keep content in the terminal buffer.

Two reproductions:

1. **Terminal rows shrink**, columns unchanged (Android/Termux soft-keyboard toggle) — one line lost per toggle.
2. **While the model is thinking** — the same swallow, with no resize at all. This is the more general trigger: it shows the resize is not the root of the defect.

## Root cause

Two defects in the bundled `ink` (pinned `7.0.3`), both on the frame-erase path. `resized` compares width only, so a rows-only change never redraws at all; and when a redraw does happen, the erase is anchored to the wrong end of the frame.

`clear()` and `render()`'s inline erase both move the cursor **down to the bottom of the previous frame** first (`buildReturnToBottomPrefix` → `cursorDown(previousLineCount - 1 - cursorPosition.y) + cursorTo(0)`) and then erase upward. `cursorDown` **clamps at the last terminal row and does not scroll**, so whenever the frame reaches past the rows remaining below the cursor — a tall frame while Thought streams, or right after a rows shrink — the cursor lands short of the frame bottom and the upward erase runs past the frame's top into the transcript above. That is the eaten line, and it is why (2) exists with no resize involved.

## What

Ports the three required parts of `vadimdemedes/ink#1031` (`c8002843e`, merged 2026-09-21, unreleased — 77 commits past `v7.1.1`) onto the vendor state:

- `build/cursor-helpers.js` — add **`buildEraseFrame`**: with a cursor shown, locate the frame **top** relative to the cursor and erase **downward** (`cursorMove(0, -min(cursor.y, previousLineCount - 1))` + `cursorTo(0)` + `eraseDown`); no cursor falls back to `eraseLines(previousLineCount)`.
- `build/log-update.js` — expose `getCursorPosition` on both renderers (via `previousCursorPosition`; after a flush `cursorDirty` is already cleared and `cursorPosition` is stale) **and route both `clear()` paths through `buildEraseFrame`**. Also `build/log-update.d.ts` for the new `LogUpdate.getCursorPosition` type.
- `build/ink.js` — track `lastTerminalHeight`, and extend `resized` with the rows-shrink-with-cursor arm.

Additionally, and beyond #1031: that change routes only `clear()` through `buildEraseFrame` and leaves `render()`'s inline erase — `returnPrefix + ansiEscapes.eraseLines(previousLineCount) + str + cursorSuffix`, hit whenever a frame is re-rendered with changed output — on the same clamped path. Both of `render()`'s inline-erase sites are routed through `buildEraseFrame` here as well, so trigger (2) is not left half-fixed.

`patches/ink+7.0.3.patch` is regenerated in full from the `npm pack ink@7.0.3` baseline (1397 lines / 22 files).

Both reproductions run through the same code path: a Thought stream emits static output, so `renderInteractiveFrame` takes its `hasStaticOutput` branch and calls **`this.log.clear()`** — the function this PR rewires to `buildEraseFrame`. So the fix covers the no-resize trigger as well, not only the resize one.

Fixes #12449.

## Validation

Behaviour, A/B, same pty harness (`ui.useTerminalBuffer: false`, first frame gated on the `ESC[?2026h` sync marker), rows-only `TIOCSWINSZ` 34x100 → 20x100:

| build | bytes | erase sequence | cols-only control (34x80) |
| :-- | --: | :-- | --: |
| stock 0.24.3 | **0** — never redraws | — | 1802 B |
| + this patch | **893** | `ESC[?25l ESC[2A ESC[1G ESC[J` — erase **downward** from the frame top | 1742 B |

The cols-only control still redraws fully, so the new arm fires only on the rows path. Gate instrumentation on the patched build: `w=100 h=20 lastW=100 lastH=34 cur={"x":2,"y":2}` — the gate opening shows the redraw happens; the sequence above is what shows the erase is correct.

Patch integrity:

- `git apply -p1` against a pristine `npm pack ink@7.0.3` applies clean.
- The resulting tree is byte-identical to the tree the behaviour was validated against (`diff -rq` clean).
- 22 files, matching the upstream change's file set.

Harness note: run it under `pty.fork()` (the child must acquire the pty as its controlling terminal). With `subprocess` + `start_new_session` no `SIGWINCH` is delivered, `resized` is never entered, and both builds read 0 bytes — a false green.

prs.title: feat(channels): add Microsoft Teams extension and host ingress
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a Microsoft Teams channel extension for personal conversations, explicit group mentions, channel-thread isolation and ordered final-text replies. It supports standalone operation and an application host using the same protocol code.

Hosts can call `createTeamsIngress(name, credentials, acceptInbound)` without constructing a bridge, router, channel or listener. It returns only `handleWebhook`; the Microsoft SDK authenticates and normalizes each Activity, and success waits for acceptance. TeamsChannel delegates to the same verification path. Execution and send hooks remain separate from HTTP ingress.

## Why it's needed

Teams users lack a native channel provider. Application hosts need durable acceptance and ownership checks without copying Teams protocol logic or modifying inference core.

## Reviewer Test Plan

- Verify private messages and trusted bot mentions execute; ordinary group text, wrong bot/tenant, bad serviceUrl, and invalid signature/audience/issuer/expiry do not.
- Set another bot's `Connections__*` environment registry: explicit Teams credentials must remain authoritative, including audience and issuer validation.
- Block or reject the acceptance callback. HTTP success must wait, and persistence failure must be retryable. Original actor/thread/target must survive concurrent requests.
- Verify exact-event cancellation and revocation suppress output, including empty/oversized completed results. These results become bounded notices through the ordinary ChannelBase cancellation and send path.
- Base 0.23.0 supports hosted operation only; 0.26.1 supports standalone and hosted operation. One physical host-provided base instance is required.
- Run the actual release script for a new version, pack/install the manifests together, and confirm the current exact base peer follows the release while the tested legacy peer remains supported.

### Evidence

Focused package tests, repository build/typecheck/bundle, release-script tests and independent compiled SDK/Fastify verification are reported in the verification comment for the current source revision. Independent checks cover the new ingress on both supported base versions, existing channel behavior, completed-result/cancellation races, and an actual release consumer installation.

JWT tests use temporary RSA keys and local JWKS lookup through the real SDK verifier. Connector/UserToken clients are controlled recorders. This demonstrates protocol and host behavior, not live tenant delivery.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--- | :--- |
| macOS | Local build, package, SDK/host and release-consumer verification |
| Windows | Local verification not performed |
| Linux | CI results are recorded separately |

Node 22.23.1, Microsoft Agents SDK 1.9.1, Fastify 5.11.3.

## Risk & Scope

- Standalone scheduling/dedup is in memory. Durable acceptance, execution recovery and delivery retry policy belong to the host. The standalone ingress itself neither queues nor deduplicates.
- No changes to inference core, ChannelBase or built-in provider registration. Publication and registry inclusion remain maintainer decisions. Untested base versions are not declared compatible.
- Not validated: real tenant app installation, Microsoft JWKS/Connector network, actual agent tools, and end-to-end CLI extension loading. The global CLI baseline was unavailable; built CLI smoke is tracked separately. National clouds, attachments, Graph history, cards and scheduled delivery are outside this proposal.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/teams-channel/docs/design/teams-channel.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/teams-channel/docs/design/teams-channel.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Refs #15618. This remains a draft proposal; it is not merged or published.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

通用 Teams 扩展支持私聊、群显式 @、帖子隔离和顺序文本回复。新增独立 `createTeamsIngress`，无需临时 Bridge/Router/Channel，也不启动监听器；同一 SDK 验签路径等待宿主接收完成再 ACK。显式认证连接隔离宿主环境配置，空白/超长确定结果沿正常取消与发送保护处理，发版脚本同步当前 base peer 并保留已验证 legacy peer。

持久化、恢复与重试策略归宿主；插件不绑定特定应用或数据库。未改推理核心、ChannelBase 或内置注册表。合成 SDK/Fastify、取消竞态和实际包安装证据与真实 Teams 租户验收分别记录；维护者接受、合并和正式发布仍待完成。

</details>

prs.title: feat(core): copy .worktreeinclude paths into new worktrees
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds support for a repository-level `.worktreeinclude` file: a committed, gitignore-syntax list of ignored paths that are copied from your main checkout into every worktree the CLI creates.

A `git worktree add` checkout contains only tracked files, so gitignored local state — `.env`, `appsettings.Development.json`, local certificates — is absent. This PR reads `.worktreeinclude` at the repository root (one pattern per line, `#` comments, blank lines skipped), matches those patterns against git's own ignored set, and copies the matches into the new checkout while preserving directory structure.

Patterns are only ever matched against `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard`, never expanded from disk. That keeps tracked files, `.git` internals and paths outside the repository unreachable by construction: the worst a committed pattern can do is select a file git already lists as ignored. The listing is recursive, so a pattern naming a fully-ignored directory selects the files inside it rather than a directory entry that can't be copied.

The copy runs on both creation paths — `createUserWorktree` (the `--worktree` flag, the `enter_worktree` tool, and `agent` worktree isolation) and `setupWorktrees` (Agent Arena) — so one committed file covers every worktree family. It is non-fatal throughout: a missing or unreadable file, an oversized one, or an individual copy failure leaves the worktree usable without those files. The file is capped at 1 MB and 10,000 patterns because it is committed input that anyone with push access can change, and each pattern costs time against every ignored file.

## Why it's needed

Agents working in a worktree routinely need local, never-committed files — an API key in `.env`, a machine-specific dev config — and today every new worktree requires manual setup or a custom provisioning script. Running several isolated agents in parallel multiplies that cost. This is the last unimplemented item from the worktree design's advanced list (the `.worktreeinclude` row in `docs/design/worktree.md`), and it is tracked as #10584.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

In a scratch repository that ignores `.env` and `.local/`:

1. Create `.env`, `.local/top.txt` and `.local/sub/deep.txt` in the main checkout, plus a `.worktreeinclude` containing `.env` and `.local/`.
2. Create a worktree (`qwen --worktree=one`, or `createUserWorktree('one', 'main')` directly).
3. The new checkout contains all three files with the source contents; a gitignored path not named in the file (try `secrets/*.json`) is absent.
4. Delete `.worktreeinclude` and create another worktree: nothing is copied and the worktree still succeeds.

The new integration test file pins those four outcomes plus a negation (`!config/example.json`), a tracked file named by a pattern (not copied twice / not selected at all), the size cap, and a `.worktreeinclude` that is a directory.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: `packages/core/src/services/gitWorktreeService.ts` copied only untracked files in `setupWorktrees`; `createUserWorktree` copied nothing. After: both paths copy the resolved `.worktreeinclude` set.

```
$ cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/services/gitWorktreeService.worktreeinclude.integ.test.ts \
    src/services/gitWorktreeService.test.ts src/services/gitWorktreeService.symlinks.integ.test.ts
 ✓ ... (13 tests) / (41 tests) / (15 tests)
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  69 passed (69)
```

`npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/core/tsconfig.json` and `npx eslint` on the touched files pass.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

macOS only. Windows and Linux not run locally; the copy path is plain `fs` with repository-relative paths from git, and CI covers the rest.

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit and integration tests only (real `git` against temp repos).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a committed `.worktreeinclude` lets anyone with push access decide which ignored files a clone copies into its worktrees. The blast radius is bounded to gitignored files that already exist in the source checkout, but a pattern reaching a large ignored tree (a build cache) would copy it per worktree with no size limit. That tradeoff is documented in the user docs' Limitations section.
- Not validated / out of scope: symlinks among the ignored files are copied as whatever `fs.copyFile` does with them (the link target's contents), not recreated as links. Worktrees created before a line is added do not retroactively receive the file.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Without a `.worktreeinclude`, behaviour is unchanged.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #10584
