prs.title: feat(managed-agent): render DingTalk managed replies as editable cards
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This adds the H5e slice of the Managed Agent channel work: a managed adapter that supports cards now renders one reply delivery as a single provider-native card and edits that card as the remaining segments arrive, instead of posting plain text messages. DingTalk is the first card-capable provider; email, GitHub and WeCom keep today's text behavior unchanged.

The card path is built entirely on the existing delivery contract. The segment plan, the per-segment write-once receipts, the claim budget and the partial/unknown recovery are untouched. The first segment creates the card, each later segment applies a full-snapshot update that appends its text, and every segment still receives its own receipt — a card segment's provider message id is the card's deterministic track id, the durable handle that resolves the card for editing. Rendering is gated three ways: the adapter declares card support, the operator configures a card template id, and the transport provides a card send. When the accumulated card body would exceed the provider's content bound, the delivery falls back to the text path for that segment and the rest of the tail, so the card carries the prefix it can hold and the remainder arrives as ordinary messages — each segment still gets one truthful receipt, and nothing is silently truncated. A failed or ambiguous edit resolves visibly as rejected or unknown and never triggers an automatic second send, exactly like a failed text send.

There is no change to the record bodies, the closed key sets, the successor rules, the Java control plane, the SQL schema, the OpenAPI document or the claim protocol. "Edit" here means the provider-side update of a card the delivery already owns, issued through the same claim → send → receipt pipeline as a send; editing a settled delivery record remains forbidden by the H5 contract.

Review-driven hardening keeps the card path honest about delivery: the managed card client requires a positive delivery verdict (an unreadable or unconfirmed answer is ambiguous, never an `accepted` receipt for an undelivered card), while Legacy callers of the shared client stay tolerant; the proxy egress buffers the response body before destroying its dispatcher so proxied card sends actually work; completed and terminally-settled deliveries prune their persisted card body instead of retaining it until eviction; a definitive card refusal no longer evicts the conversation's live webhook; `cardTemplateId` is declared in the channel's management fields so an editor can enable cards, and a configured-but-unusable id is announced once rather than silently disabling cards. The adapter-facing `receipt` return is widened from void to the settled delivery view (the Java endpoint already returns it) to drive the prune-on-delivered; callers that ignore the result are unchanged.

## Why it's needed

Card-style surfaces are the remaining H5 slice that makes managed channel replies usable in chat products that expect structured cards. Text-only replies lose the grouping and editability the provider already supports. On the managed DingTalk path the gap was concrete: each segment was a session-webhook text message whose provider message id was a local random UUID, so the adapter held no provider-side handle it could ever update. DingTalk has a real interactive-card API and the Legacy channel already uses it; this slice brings that capability to the managed path without inventing a second delivery source or bypassing the segment ledger.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The load-bearing surface is the adapter and its transport, exercised by deps-injected suites against a fake DingTalk card endpoint (no live provider is a merge gate, mirroring the DingTalk adapter slice). Run from each package directory:

- `cd packages/channels/dingtalk && npx vitest run src/managed-dingtalk-adapter.test.ts src/managed-dingtalk-deps.test.ts src/managed-state.test.ts` — the card loop (create once, edit per later segment, accumulated body concatenates back to the reply, overflow falls back to text and persists the switch, restart resumes the same track id, an evicted progress entry sends the tail as text and never re-creates the card), the discipline (definitive refusal → rejected, ambiguous → unknown, neither re-sends; a pre-send persist failure abandons the delivery and rolls back both the outbound entry and the card map; an orphan card segment replays its receipt or settles unknown), the gates (no template / cards false / no card deps all keep the text path), and the transport (createAndDeliver vs updateInstance endpoints, the IM_ROBOT sender target, token cache/early-refresh/401-retry, permanent vs transient errcodes, proxy dispatcher use and teardown).
- `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/commands/channel/managed-dingtalk.test.ts` — the command hands the parsed robot credential to the transport so the card send exists.
- Regression baseline (unchanged surfaces): the DingTalk managed stream/heartbeat suites, the channel-base contract suite, the core channel record/operations/authority suites and the CLI channel funnel suite stay green.

A mutation sweep disabled eight load-bearing rules in turn (capability gate, template gate, first-segment overflow check, accumulated overflow check, deterministic track id, eviction-safe text fallback, progress pruning, rollback snapshot copy); each produced a real test failure (all eight killed), confirming the witnesses are load-bearing rather than trivially green.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-user-visible TUI change; the managed adapter is an experimental explicitly-selected entry and the card surface is provider-side. Behavior is pinned by the deps-injected suites above.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment

Local workspace build (`npm run build`), vitest per package, Node 22 with an enlarged heap for typecheck. No live DingTalk tenant; the card transport is verified against a fake endpoint in the deps.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a single interactive card cannot hold every reply (the provider caps card content), so an over-long answer renders its prefix as a card and its tail as text messages within the same delivery. This is a rendering fallback inside one delivery chain — same delivery id, same ledger, same claim/resume protocol — not a second delivery source, and each segment still gets one truthful receipt. The alternative (truncating the card body while receipting every segment as delivered) would make receipts claim content the user never saw, so it is rejected.
- Not validated / out of scope: a live-tenant DingTalk smoke (real card template + stream inbound) is a follow-up, not a merge gate; card rendering for email/GitHub/WeCom; card metadata in the public read model (needs closed-key, Java, SQL and OpenAPI work with a contract version bump); streaming/finalize card surfaces; group cards (the managed path admits private chats only). No new adapter, no attachment kinds beyond inline staging, no proactive sends, no H6 automation, no public resend mutation, no WebShell mirror routes, no change to how the model is driven, and no Legacy behavior change.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The persisted adapter state gains an optional card-progress map; a state file without it still validates, so an upgrade loads existing state unchanged. Adapters without the declaration or a configured template are byte-for-byte on the text path.

Design documents (both languages, complete and synchronized): [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/managed-channel-h5e-cards/docs/design/2026-11-18-managed-channel-card-surfaces.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/managed-channel-h5e-cards/docs/design/2026-11-18-managed-channel-card-surfaces.zh-CN.md).

Implements #17716 (H5e card-style segmented channel surfaces). DingTalk interactive cards (private chat) land here; the live-tenant smoke and card rendering for other adapters remain follow-up under the same slice. Parent #12827 (Stage H extension runtime), under #12380.

本 PR 补上 Managed Agent 渠道工作的 H5e 切片：支持卡片的 managed 适配器现在把一次回复投递渲染成一张 provider 原生卡片，并随剩余分段到达而编辑这张卡片，不再发送纯文本消息。DingTalk 是第一个支持卡片的 provider；email、GitHub、WeCom 保持今天的文本行为不变。

记录体、闭合键集、后继规则、Java 控制面、SQL schema、OpenAPI 文档与 claim 协议均无改动。这里的「编辑」指对一次投递已拥有的卡片做 provider 侧更新，通过与发送相同的 claim → send → receipt 管线发出；编辑已落定的投递记录仍被 H5 契约禁止。

卡片式界面是 H5 剩下的切片，它让 managed 渠道回复能在期待结构化卡片的聊天产品里真正可用。纯文本回复丢掉了 provider 已支持的分组与可编辑性。在 managed DingTalk 路径上缺口很具体：每段都是一条 session-webhook 文本消息，其 provider message id 是本地随机 UUID，适配器手里没有任何可更新的 provider 侧句柄。DingTalk 有真实的互动卡片 API，Legacy 渠道也已在用；本切片把该能力带到 managed 路径，而不另造第二条交付来源、也不绕过分段台账。

承重面是适配器及其传输层，用注入 deps 的套件对假 DingTalk 卡片端点验证（真实 provider 不是合并门，与 DingTalk 适配器切片一致）。从各包目录运行：

- `cd packages/channels/dingtalk && npx vitest run src/managed-dingtalk-adapter.test.ts src/managed-dingtalk-deps.test.ts src/managed-state.test.ts` —— 卡片循环（创建一次、之后每段编辑、累积正文拼接复现回复、溢出回退文本并持久化切换、重启恢复同一 track id、被逐出的进度把尾部以文本送达且绝不重建卡片）、纪律（确定性拒绝 → rejected、含糊 → unknown，两者都不重发；发送前持久化失败放弃投递并回滚 outbound 条目与卡片映射；孤儿卡片分段重放其回执或落 unknown）、门（无模板 / cards false / 无卡片 deps 都保持文本路径）、传输（createAndDeliver 与 updateInstance 端点、IM_ROBOT 发送者目标、token 缓存/提前刷新/401 重试、永久与瞬态 errcode、代理 dispatcher 的使用与销毁）。

- 回归基线（未改面）：DingTalk managed stream/heartbeat 套件、channel-base 契约套件、core 渠道 record/operations/authority 套件与 CLI 渠道漏斗套件保持全绿。

变异 sweep 依次禁用八条承重规则（能力门、模板门、首段溢出检查、累积溢出检查、确定性 track id、逐出安全文本回退、进度剪枝、回滚快照拷贝），每条都触发真实测试失败（八条全部被杀），证明见证是承重的而非 trivially 绿。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A —— 非用户可见 TUI 改动；managed 适配器是实验性、显式选择的入口，卡片界面在 provider 侧。行为由上述注入 deps 的套件钉住。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

本地 workspace 构建（`npm run build`）、按包跑 vitest、Node 22 并为 typecheck 加大堆。无真实 DingTalk 租户；卡片传输对 deps 中的假端点验证。

- 主要风险/权衡：单张互动卡片装不下每一条回复（provider 限制卡片内容），所以超长答案把前缀渲染成卡片、尾部在同一投递内以文本消息送达。这是一次投递链内部的渲染回退——同一 delivery id、同一本台账、同一套 claim/resume 协议——不是第二条交付来源，每个分段仍各得一条真实回执。另一种做法（截断卡片正文却把每段都回执为已送达）会让回执声称用户从未看到的内容，因此被否决。

prs.title: feat(telemetry): record OpenRouter routing backend and generation id
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Records two OpenRouter routing attributes on the `qwen-code.llm_request` span: `openrouter.provider`, the backend that actually served the request, and `openrouter.generation_id`, the `X-Generation-Id` response header. Both are read from the raw wire — the response headers and the un-normalized response body or SSE chunk — because the OpenAI converter builds a fresh response from a fixed field whitelist and drops them before telemetry ever sees them.

The non-streaming path now takes its completion through the SDK's `withResponse()` so the raw `Response` is reachable, falling back to a plain await when the client does not expose it. Writes go through a new `GenAiExchangeController.recordResponseAttribute`, which refuses to touch a finalized attempt or a handle from another generation.

## Why it's needed

OpenRouter rotates requests across backend providers, and which backend answered is often exactly what explains a difference in speed, cost, or output quality. OpenRouter reports that decision on every response, but today an external observer of Qwen Code's telemetry can see that something answered via `openrouter.ai` and never which backend. Issue #14629 asks for the two values, and both halves are needed for the routing decision to be usable: the provider for the immediate answer, the generation id because it is the key to OpenRouter's own per-generation cost and latency lookup.

The attributes are vendor-prefixed rather than folded into `gen_ai.provider.name`, which already means the gateway/protocol provider (e.g. `gcp.gemini`); overloading it would silently change the meaning of an emitted field.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Point a config at `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` with telemetry enabled and run a prompt; the `qwen-code.llm_request` span should carry both attributes. Without an OpenRouter key, the behavior is covered by unit tests: header capture, body/chunk capture with first-non-empty-wins, and the hostname gate that keeps a non-OpenRouter endpoint from emitting either attribute even when its payload carries the same field names.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible or TUI change; this only adds span attributes.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   N/A  |

Unit tests only; no live OpenRouter traffic was exercised.

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests only.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the non-streaming path now goes through `withResponse()` instead of a plain await. Mocked and proxy-compatible clients that lack the method take the same await path as before, and the existing suite covers that fallback; a client whose `withResponse()` resolves an unexpected shape would now fail where it previously succeeded.
- Not validated / out of scope: not exercised against live OpenRouter traffic, so the upstream contract (that `provider` appears on every chunk and `X-Generation-Id` on every response) is taken from the report rather than re-verified here. Full `npm run build` was not run; the core package typecheck, eslint, and prettier are clean on the changed files.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. New span attributes are additive and only emitted on an OpenRouter hostname.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #14629

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

在 `qwen-code.llm_request` span 上记录两个 OpenRouter 路由属性：`openrouter.provider`（实际服务该请求的后端 provider）与 `openrouter.generation_id`（响应头 `X-Generation-Id`）。两者都从原始网络层读取 —— 响应头，以及未经归一化的响应体或 SSE chunk —— 因为 OpenAI converter 会用固定的字段白名单重建响应对象，它们在进入遥测之前就被丢弃了。

非流式路径现在通过 SDK 的 `withResponse()` 取得补全结果，从而能拿到原始 `Response`；客户端没有该方法时退回普通 await。写入统一走新增的 `GenAiExchangeController.recordResponseAttribute`，它会拒绝向已 finalize 的 attempt 或属于其他 generation 的 handle 写入。

## 为什么需要

OpenRouter 会把请求轮转分发到多个后端 provider，而究竟是哪个后端应答，往往正是速度、成本或输出质量差异的原因。OpenRouter 在每个响应里都会报告这个决策，但今天观察 Qwen Code 遥测的外部系统只能看到「某个后端通过 `openrouter.ai` 应答」，看不到是哪一个。

属性采用厂商前缀，而不是并入 `gen_ai.provider.name` —— 后者已有确定含义（网关/协议 provider，如 `gcp.gemini`），复用会静默改变一个已发布字段的语义。

## 评审验证方式

把配置指向 `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` 并开启遥测，跑一次提问，`qwen-code.llm_request` span 应同时带有两个属性。没有 OpenRouter key 时，行为由单测覆盖：响应头采集、响应体/chunk 采集（取第一个非空值）、以及 hostname 门禁 —— 即使非 OpenRouter 端点的 payload 里有同名字段，也不会发出这两个属性。

Before/After：不适用，没有用户可见或 TUI 变更，仅新增 span 属性。

仅在 macOS 上跑了单测；未使用真实 OpenRouter 流量验证。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险：非流式路径改用 `withResponse()`，不再是普通 await。缺少该方法或被 mock 的客户端仍走原来的 await 分支，既有测试覆盖了该回退；若某客户端的 `withResponse()` 返回了非预期结构，原本能成功的请求现在会失败。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：未对真实 OpenRouter 流量验证，`provider` 出现在每个 chunk、`X-Generation-Id` 出现在每个响应这两点取自 issue 报告而非本轮复验。未运行完整 `npm run build`；core 包的类型检查、eslint、prettier 在改动文件上均干净。
- 破坏性变更：无。新增 span 属性是纯增量的，且只在 OpenRouter hostname 下发出。

</details>

auto_merge.commit_title: feat(telemetry): record OpenRouter routing backend and generation id (#16495)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* feat(telemetry): record OpenRouter routing backend and generation id

An OpenRouter request is answered by one of many rotating backends, and
which one served it is usually what explains a difference in speed, cost,
or output quality. OpenRouter reports that decision on every response --
`X-Generation-Id` as a header, `provider` as a top-level field in both the
JSON body and every SSE chunk -- but neither survived into telemetry: the
converter builds a fresh response from a fixed field whitelist, and the
pipeline never looked at the raw Response outside the non-SSE guard.

Record both on the llm_request span as vendor-prefixed attributes,
`openrouter.provider` and `openrouter.generation_id`. They are read where
the wire data still exists and gated on `isOpenRouterHostname`, so a strict
OpenAI-compatible endpoint that happens to use the same field names cannot
emit them. `gen_ai.provider.name` already means the gateway/protocol
provider, so it is not reused for the backend.

The non-streaming path now takes the response through `withResponse()` to
reach the headers, falling back to a plain await when the client has none.
Writes go through a new `GenAiExchangeController.recordResponseAttribute`,
which keeps them off a finalized or foreign-generation attempt. The
streaming path reads `provider` from the first chunk carrying one and stops
looking, since the field is present from the first chunk on.

Verification: 384 tests pass across pipeline.test.ts and
gen-ai-request.test.ts, covering header capture, body/chunk capture with the
first-non-empty rule, the non-OpenRouter gate, and the finalized/foreign
handle guards. Two mutations were used to confirm the new cases fail
without the code: dropping the hostname gate reddens the two gate cases,
and returning `undefined` for the header read reddens the header case. Full
`npm run build` was not run; typecheck, eslint, and prettier are clean on
the changed files.

* test(telemetry): make the generation guard and OpenRouter scopes observable

The case named 'refuses a handle from a different generation' took a handle
from one controller and wrote it through another, so the check it exercised
was handle.controller !== this: deleting the generation comparison left all
47 cases green. Split it into two cases and drive the generation one on a
single controller, where a retry advances the generation and the stale handle
is the only thing that differs. Removing that comparison now turns the new
case red.

The non-streaming OpenRouter block sat inside describe('executeStream') even
though it calls pipeline.execute(), which reported it under the wrong path;
its httpResponse helper moved to file scope for both describes to share. The
endpoint check in the streaming loop is also invariant, so resolve it once
before the loop instead of once per chunk.

* test(telemetry): reach the controller guards these two cases name

Both new cases were named for checks the suite could not discriminate.

A handle from another exchange whose attempt is still open carries the same
generation, so deleting `handle.controller !== this` left the suite green:
the earlier case used a fresh exchange at generation 0, where the
generation check answers first. Assert on the receiving span instead, so a
leaked write is visible.

The OpenRouter capture returned early for a missing controller, but every
case installed the live fake handle. Add the telemetry-off state —
`reportOpenAiRequest` returning undefined on an OpenRouter endpoint — and
assert the completion still comes back.

Both were verified by mutation: removing either guard turns the matching
case red.

* test(telemetry): assert no attribute is recorded for an undefined value

The 'ignores an undefined value' case used toEqual({}), which ignores keys
whose value is undefined. Deleting the guard in recordResponseAttribute left
a { 'openrouter.provider': undefined } entry on the span and the test still
passed, so it did not cover the guard it is named after. toStrictEqual fails
in that case.

* chore(ci): give the integration typecheck the same heap ceiling as the build

tsc -p integration-tests/tsconfig.json runs with Node's default heap and
aborted at about 2 GB on the self-hosted runner, so the no-AK integration
gate failed before any test ran. The build script already asks for 6144 MB.

* chore(ci): drop the redundant heap flag from typecheck:integration

Reverts 5df507f60. The no-AK gate already wraps this script with
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 via `env` on the self-hosted
pool, and scripts/tests/no-ak-integration-ci.test.js pins the script to
the bare tsc invocation. Hard-coding a second, larger ceiling inside
package.json overrode the fleet predicate for every lane and broke that
pin, reddening the unit-test lane.

---------

prs.title: feat(web-shell): quote selected message text into the composer or a new side task
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a "Quote to composer" action to the text-selection popover in the Web Shell transcript: selecting a fragment of an assistant reply or a user message now offers, alongside the existing "Copy plain text" and "Copy Markdown" actions, a way to quote the fragment into the active composer. Clicking it inserts the fragment as an inline chip at the end of the composer, followed by a line break so the user's follow-up command starts on its own line; when the prompt is sent, the chip serializes to a single-line `<quoted-message>fragment</quoted-message>` fence inside the prompt and is carried through the existing reference-annotation machinery (`inputAnnotations` with `reference.kind === 'quote'`), so the quote survives send and session reload.

The quoted fragment is normalized before insertion: all whitespace runs (including newlines) are collapsed to single spaces — the chip is a single inline editor range — bidirectional embedding/isolation control characters are stripped, and the length is capped at 4000 characters. Each chip is identified by a deterministic hash of its text, so the same quoted fragment always produces the same tag id.

This PR also adds an "Ask in side task" action to the same selection popover (shown only while side tasks are available for the current session). Clicking it creates a new side task for the session and places the selected fragment in that side task's composer as a quote chip, reusing the same inline-chip mechanism — so when the user submits their prompt, the chip serializes to the same `<quoted-message>fragment</quoted-message>` fence exactly like quote-to-composer. Nothing is sent automatically: the user writes the question on top of the chip and submits it themselves. The chip is inserted exactly once, when the child session has connected and its transcript has settled empty, in whichever order composer-ready and session-empty are observed; a per-session delivery registry makes the handoff race-free and prevents a duplicate chip across pane remounts and effect re-runs.

The actions are available wherever a composer exists (the main chat and split-view panes). Read-only and embedded transcript views do not provide the actions, so the buttons are hidden there. UI strings are localized in English and Chinese.

## Why it's needed

Follow-up prompts often need to reference a specific part of an earlier reply. Today the only options are copying the selection to the clipboard ("Copy plain text" / "Copy Markdown") and pasting it manually, which loses the signal that the fragment is a quote of earlier context. Requested in #12682.

"Ask in side task" follows up on the same need: side tasks exist to ask questions about the current conversation without cluttering the main thread, and asking about a specific fragment should not require copying it and pasting it into the side task composer, which loses the quote semantics and chip formatting. Requested in #16964.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start the dev server (`cd packages/web-shell && npm run dev`) and open a chat session with at least one assistant reply.
2. Drag-select a fragment of the reply text — the selection popover appears. Before this PR it offers only "Copy plain text" and "Copy Markdown"; after, it additionally offers "Quote to composer" (and "Ask in side task" while side tasks are available).
3. Click "Quote to composer" — an inline chip with the selected fragment appears at the end of the composer and the menu closes.
4. Press Enter to send. The user bubble renders the chip, and the POST to `/session/:id/prompt` carries the fragment as a `<quoted-message>fragment</quoted-message>` line in a `type: 'text'` prompt block plus an `inputAnnotations` entry with `reference.kind === 'quote'`, `reference.value` = the normalized fragment, `reference.serialized` = the `<quoted-message>fragment</quoted-message>` fence.
5. The same flow works when selecting a fragment of a user message; the buttons are absent in read-only/embedded transcript views.
6. In a session where side tasks are available, drag-select a fragment and click "Ask in side task" — a new side task tab opens and its composer shows the fragment as a quote chip; nothing is sent (no prompt POST for the side task).
7. Type a question in the side task composer and send it — the prompt carries the `<quoted-message>fragment</quoted-message>` fence and the `reference.kind === 'quote'` annotation, the same serialization as quote-to-composer.
8. While side tasks are unavailable for the session, the popover does not offer "Ask in side task".

Automated coverage: `packages/web-shell/client/utils/quoteReference.test.ts` (normalization: whitespace collapsing, bidi stripping, 4000-character cap, tag shape), `packages/web-shell/client/utils/askInSideTaskDelivery.test.ts` (delivery registry: register-before-request and request-before-register orderings, single delivery across pane remounts and quote re-requests, empty session ids ignored, sessions independent), four new cases in `SelectionCopyMenu.test.tsx` (ask button hidden without an ask action, shown with one, click passes the selected text and closes the menu, disabled for image-only selections), two new cases in `App.test.tsx` (the ask action provisions a side task tab carrying the raw selection as `initialQuote` and sends nothing; no ask action is exposed while side tasks are unavailable), plus the Playwright before/after scenario from the evidence below.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Playwright run against `npm run dev` with the mock-daemon e2e harness (Chromium, 1280x720), selecting the word **bold** from an assistant reply:

Before — the selection popover offers only the copy actions:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4ekuct25/qwen-code/evidence/pr-12682/assets/web-shell-quote-2026-10-14/1-before-popover.png

After — the popover additionally offers "Quote to composer":

"问这个侧边任务"操作是同一需求的后续：侧边任务用于在不打扰主线程的情况下询问当前会话，而针对特定片段的询问不应依赖复制再粘贴到侧边任务输入框——那会丢失引用的语义和芯片格式。本操作响应的是 #16964。

prs.title: feat(core): mark quota-exhausted fallback models terminal for the session
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Extends the opt-in model availability ledger (introduced in #17377) so that a fallback model which fails with a permanent quota exhaustion is recorded as terminally unavailable for the rest of the session, instead of being re-probed on every later turn. The fallback chain already skips models the ledger marks unavailable; this change adds the permanent-quota signal that feeds the ledger's terminal state, which survives turn boundaries and is cleared only when a new session starts. Transient capacity errors keep their existing per-turn skip-and-re-probe behavior, the primary model is still attempted on every request, and with the tracking setting disabled the fallback chain behaves exactly as before. The setting description and its generated schema and localized copies are refreshed to describe the session-permanent skip.

## Why it's needed

A permanent quota error (a free-tier quota, an allocated quota, or a token-plan quota that names a future reset time) cannot succeed until the quota resets, which may be days away. Today such an error on a fallback is classified fail-fast, which the fallback eligibility check excludes, so the exhausted model leaves no ledger trace and is tried again on every subsequent turn — spending a request and latency on a foregone conclusion each time. Recording it terminal lets the chain skip it for the whole session, reaching a healthy fallback directly.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

With the tracking setting enabled, drive a primary capacity failure into a fallback chain where the first fallback answers with a permanent-quota body and a later fallback serves. Confirm the first fallback is attempted once, recorded unavailable with reason quota, and then skipped both on a second request in the same turn and on a request in a fresh turn (the terminal mark survives the turn reset, unlike a transient capacity mark which is re-probed next turn). Confirm a fallback that fails with a transient capacity error is still re-probed on the next turn, and that with the setting disabled no terminal mark is written and the chain re-probes as before. A permanent real-socket test exercises this end to end through a local OpenAI-compatible server, the real SDK, and the real ledger, pinning the server-side request log so the skipped fallback is observably absent on later requests. Each predicate signal and the wiring branch is mutation-witnessed (removing it turns the matching test red).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-user-visible core behavior behind an opt-in experimental setting (default off).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local unit and real-HTTP integration tests (Node 24); core typecheck, lint, and the settings sync gates green.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the terminal-quota predicate must not permanently skip a model that could recover. It is narrowed to the explicit permanent-quota signals (the two fail-fast quota classifications, the insufficient-quota permanent provider code, and the reset-time quota message); transient capacity, auth, moderation, and other permanent-but-non-quota errors are not marked terminal.
- Not validated / out of scope: skipping an unhealthy primary at the chain entry; the prompt-vs-silent policy action map from the preview; cross-session health sharing; flipping the setting default. A quota-metric error that names no reset time stays on the per-turn re-probe path by design (its permanence is ambiguous).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The setting stays opt-in (default false); gate-off behavior is byte-identical.

Design documents: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/model-availability-terminal-quota/docs/design/2026-11-19-model-availability-terminal-quota.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/model-availability-terminal-quota/docs/design/2026-11-19-model-availability-terminal-quota.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Builds on #17377 (merged).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

扩展 opt-in 的模型可用性台账（#17377 引入），使因永久配额耗尽而失败的 fallback 模型被记为本会话剩余时间终态不可用，而不是在后续每一轮都被重新探测。fallback 链本就会跳过台账标记为不可用的模型；本改动新增喂给台账 terminal 态的永久配额信号，该态跨轮边界存活、仅在新会话开始时清除。瞬时容量错误保持既有的「本轮跳过、下轮重探」行为，primary 模型仍每个请求都被尝试，关闭跟踪设置时 fallback 链行为与之前完全一致。设置描述及其生成的 schema 与本地化副本同步刷新，以描述会话永久跳过。

## 为什么需要

永久配额错误（免费层配额、已分配配额、或指明未来重置时间的 token-plan 配额）在配额重置前不可能成功，而重置可能在数天之后。今天这类错误落在 fallback 上会被分类为 fail-fast，而 fallback 资格检查排除 fail-fast，于是耗尽的模型不留任何台账痕迹、后续每一轮都再被尝试——每次都为早已注定的结果浪费一次请求与延迟。把它记为 terminal 让链在整个会话内跳过它，直接到达健康的 fallback。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

开启跟踪设置，构造 primary 容量失败进入 fallback 链：第一个 fallback 返回永久配额 body、后续 fallback 服务。确认第一个 fallback 仅被尝试一次、被记为不可用且 reason 为 quota，并在同轮第二个请求与新一轮请求中都被跳过（terminal 标记跨轮重置存活，区别于瞬时容量标记下轮重探）。确认瞬时容量失败的 fallback 仍下轮重探；关闭设置时不写 terminal 标记、链按之前重探。一个永久真实 socket 测试经本地 OpenAI 兼容服务器、真实 SDK 与真实台账端到端验证，钉住服务器侧请求日志，使被跳过的 fallback 在后续请求中可观察地缺席。每个谓词信号与接线分支都有变异见证（删除即对应用例转红）。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A —— 非用户可见的核心行为，位于 opt-in 实验设置之后（默认关）。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### 环境（可选）

本地单元与 real-HTTP 集成测试（Node 24）；core typecheck、lint 与设置同步门绿。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/权衡：terminal-quota 谓词不能永久跳过一个可能恢复的模型。它被收窄到明确的永久配额信号（两个 fail-fast 配额分类、insufficient-quota 永久 provider code、重置时间配额消息）；瞬时容量、鉴权、审核、及其它永久但非配额的错误不被记为 terminal。
- 未验证/范围外：链入口跳过不健康 primary；preview 的 prompt-vs-silent 策略动作映射；跨会话健康共享；翻设置默认值。未指明重置时间的 quota-metric 错误按设计留在每轮重探路径（其永久性不明确）。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无。设置仍 opt-in（默认 false）；gate-off 行为逐字节不变。

设计文档：[英文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/model-availability-terminal-quota/docs/design/2026-11-19-model-availability-terminal-quota.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/model-availability-terminal-quota/docs/design/2026-11-19-model-availability-terminal-quota.zh-CN.md)

## 关联 Issue

基于 #17377（已合入）。

</details>

prs.title: test(web-shell): pin the goal marker double-click guard and refresh its design record
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Closes out the loose ends left by the sidebar goal markers feature after it merged, in one branch rather than several. It started as three documentation-and-witness items. Review then added a fourth — an E2E witness for the clearing transition — and writing that case exposed a fixture-ownership defect in shared test infrastructure, which this branch also fixes.

First, the design document's status line still announced the feature as a proposal. It now records the landed state and the merge it came from, plus the two decisions review changed along the way: the completed-goals-hidden rule lives in one shared visibility predicate read by all three surfaces, and the goal projection coexists with the separate artifact-count projection that landed on main in parallel rather than being folded into it. Everything below that line still describes the design as written, except the validation plan, which this PR corrects to match what the tests actually exercise.

Second, the document's validation plan listed a rejected `status` field on the goal-changed notification. That field does not exist — the same document's design decisions section explains why it was dropped. Both language versions now describe the checks the suite actually exercises (version, session id, unresolvable session) and point back at that decision. A review item then caught that my first rewrite still implied the handler's ownership clause was covered: it is not, because the only foreign-session case sends an id `resolveEntry` cannot resolve, so `!entry` short-circuits first. Both versions now state outright that the ownership clause has no test witness today.

Third, the marker's double-click guard was the one marker behavior with no test witness. A case now sits beside the existing Enter-guard case and pins it.

Fourth, the clearing transition — the one a maintainer most wants to see proven — had no E2E witness either. A case now drives it through the notification path: mutate the goal away, bump the catalog clock, and the marker must disappear on its own without a reload. Writing it exposed a fixture-ownership defect in the shared e2e scenario factory: the factory stored the caller's session array as-is, so a case that mutates a session after install was also mutating the module-level fixture every later case reads. The clone now happens once at construction, beside the sibling field that already cloned, and the factory's own contract is pinned by a new unit test.

Review then pointed out that the new case repeated the older transition case's scenario block verbatim, and that the duplication is load-bearing: the live-state feature is what enables catalog polling, so an edit applied to one copy would leave the other silently not polling and failing as an opaque locator timeout. Both cases now share one file-local scenario helper and one goal-transition helper. Checking that premise uncovered a defect that had been sitting in the spec unnoticed: the 250 ms poll interval both copies advertised was inert, because the resolver accepts only values of at least 1000 and otherwise falls back to a 5 s default. The helper now advertises the smallest honoured value and documents the floor, which also made both transition cases about three seconds faster.

## Why it's needed

The status line is what a maintainer reads first when planning the next slice; leaving it at "proposed" invites reopening finished work. The stale `status` mention contradicts a decision recorded in the same document, so a reader implementing against the plan would add a validation surface the design deliberately refused. The double-click guard is load-bearing: without it a marker double-click both opens the session and starts a row rename, yet removing it kept every test green — exactly the gap the post-merge review named. And the fixture alias was a live trap for the next author: any new transition case written in this file's style would silently pollute the fixture for its siblings, in the same worker and across retries, and would have to rediscover the rule from a comment.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

For the double-click guard: run the marker suite and confirm the new case passes, then delete the marker's `onDoubleClick` line and re-run — only that case should fail, which is what makes it the guard's witness rather than a duplicate of the click case. Re-measured on the current head: `1 failed | 9 passed` with the line removed, `10 passed` with it restored, production file restored byte-for-byte (sha256 matched).

For the clearing transition: run the markers spec and watch the fourth case. It asserts the running tone first, pins two markers before the clear, then requires the target marker to reach count 0 while the row itself stays listed and one marker survives. Those survivor assertions matter: the marker locator is a descendant of an ancestor-filtered row locator, so a bare count of 0 would also be satisfied by the whole row unmounting. Both transition cases build their scenario through the same file-local helper; deleting the live-state feature from it reds the repaint case every time. The clearing case is timing-dependent under that same mutation — a slower, non-live-state catalog refresh can also remove the marker near the 30 s boundary — so it witnesses the behavior rather than isolating the polling path. With the feature present it settles in about a second.

For the fixture ownership fix: run the new contract test, then remove the `structuredClone` call in the scenario factory and re-run. Exactly the three `sessions` ownership cases should fail (`3 failed | 4 passed`) while the other four stay green — one holds `scenario.sessions`, mutates through the held reference and asserts it is still the same array (the property the notification path depends on), and three cover the other cloned collections. Reverting any one of those three clones reds exactly its own case, `1 failed | 6 passed` each. The pairing is the point: the fix removes the alias without breaking post-install mutation. Restored byte-for-byte afterwards (sha256 matched).

Because the factory is shared, the sweep matters more than the new cases alone. Every spec that passes one of the cloned fixtures or mutates it after install was enumerated (24 files) and run locally: 23 of them, **148 tests**, single worker. One run hit a single pre-existing intermittent failure in the activity spec, attributed with a matched-scope base/head A/B and filed as #17791; the run records are in the round comments. The remaining file is the visuals suite, which uses its own Playwright config and is covered by its own CI lane; I did not run it locally. This sweep is not redundant with PR CI — the pull-request lane runs `@smoke` only, so the 57 non-smoke cases in that set (91 of the 148 are smoke-tagged) get no pre-merge signal. The full suite does run in `e2e.yml`, but on pushes to `main`, nightly and on demand, not on pull requests.

For the notification wording: compare the validation plan against the design decisions section and the handler — all three should agree the payload carries only a version and a session id. The plan should also say the ownership clause is untested, not imply it is covered. Confirm the Chinese twin says the same.

For the status line: confirm it names the landed state and merge, that the two listed decisions match the shipped code, that it scopes the "as written" claim to exclude the validation plan, and that nothing outside the status line and the validation plan changed.

The repository's formatter reports no changes needed on the touched files, ESLint is clean, and the package's `tsc --noEmit` exits 0. As an independent final gate, an isolated real daemon driven through a real browser passed **18/18** checks — including the goal sidecar relocating into the archive chats directory on real disk, the archived catalog still projecting the goal, and the marker disappearing after a clear.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible surface changes. The double-click guard already existed; this PR only pins it. The clearing behavior also already worked; the new case proves it, and the factory change alters test-fixture ownership only.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  N/A   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local vitest (marker suite 10 cases, factory contract 7 cases), local Playwright on Chromium (markers spec 4 cases, plus the 148-test affected-spec sweep), the mutation checks described above, and an isolated real-daemon run against a real browser.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: no production code changes. The diff is two documentation corrections, nine added test cases across three files, and one behavior change in shared **test infrastructure** — the e2e scenario factory now clones every caller-supplied collection that its routes mutate in place: `sessions`, `standaloneSessions`, `midTurnMessages` and `gitRemotes` — the last one counts because an accessor hands the array itself to the add/remove routes. A fifth such collection, `allocatedSessions`, is factory-built and cannot alias a caller; fields that routes only reassign wholesale replace the reference and need no clone. That factory change is the only item with reach beyond its own file, which is why the affected-spec sweep above was run rather than just the new cases. The mutation checks temporarily removed a production line and a factory call and restored both byte-for-byte; the shipped guard is untouched.
- Not validated / out of scope: the third post-merge review item is a calibration of the merged PR's own description (its "never a wrong state" claim is stronger than "faithful to the journal", because the runtime can journal a pause it then declines to adopt). That is a wording fix on the merged PR's body, not a code change, and is handled there. Re-journaling on non-adoption would be a runtime-side change and is deliberately not attempted here. The contract test does not add a nested-field leak case: no spec in the suite mutates a nested session field in place, so that case would be speculative.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

Both carry the same landed state, the same two decisions, the same corrected validation wording and the same follow-up pointer; the historical sections are unchanged in both.

<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

把侧栏目标标记特性合入后留下的尾巴在一个分支里收掉，而不是开好几个 PR。起初是三项文档与见证工作。评审随后新增了第四项——清除转换的 E2E 见证——而写这条用例时暴露了共享测试基建的夹具所有权缺陷，本分支一并修掉。

其一，设计文档状态行仍宣称该特性是提案。现在记录已落地状态与来源合并，并补上评审期间改变的两处决策：完成态隐藏规则收在一个共享可见性谓词里、由三个界面共同读取；goal 投影与并行落到 main 的另一套 artifact-count 投影**并存**，并未合并成一套。该行以下内容仍按撰写时的设计描述，**验证计划一节除外**——本 PR 把它更正为测试实际覆盖的范围。

其二，文档的验证计划列了 goal-changed 通知上被拒绝的 `status` 字段。该字段并不存在——同一文档的设计决策段解释了为何弃用它。双语两版现在描述套件实际覆盖的校验（版本、会话 id、无法解析的会话）并回指该决策。随后一条评审意见指出我第一版改写仍暗示 handler 的归属子句已被覆盖：并没有，因为唯一的外来会话用例发的是 `resolveEntry` 解析不出的 id，`!entry` 先短路。两版现在直接写明该归属子句目前没有测试见证。

其三，标记的双击守卫是唯一没有测试见证的标记行为。现在在既有 Enter 守卫用例旁补了一例钉住它。

其四，清除这一转换——维护者最想看到被证明的那一个——同样没有 E2E 见证。新用例走通知路径驱动它：把目标改写成无、推进目录时钟，标记必须自行消失而不靠重载。写它时暴露了共享 e2e scenario 工厂的夹具所有权缺陷：工厂原样保存调用方传入的会话数组，于是 install 后改写会话的用例同时改写了后续每个用例读取的模块级夹具。克隆现在只在构造处发生一次、与早已克隆的兄弟字段并列，工厂自身的契约由新增单测钉住。

随后评审指出新用例逐字复制了既有转换用例的场景块，且这份重复是承重的：live-state 特性才是目录轮询的开关，只改一份副本会让另一份静默停止轮询，并以不透明的定位器超时失败。两条用例现在共用一个文件内场景 helper 与一个目标转换 helper。核实该前提时又查出一处一直存在于该 spec、双方都没注意的缺陷：两份副本宣称的 250 毫秒轮询间隔是 inert 的——resolver 只接受不小于 1000 的值，否则回落到 5 秒默认值。helper 现在宣称真正会被接受的最小值并写明该下限，这也让两条转换用例各快约三秒。

## 为什么需要

状态行是维护者规划下一片工作时最先读的东西；留在「提案」会让人重开已完成的工作。过时的 `status` 提法与同一文档记录的决策相矛盾，照计划实现的人会加上设计明确拒绝的校验面。双击守卫是承重的：没有它，标记双击会既打开会话又触发行重命名，但删掉它所有测试仍绿——正是合入后评审点名的缺口。而夹具别名是给下一位作者留的活陷阱：任何按本文件风格新写的转换用例都会静默污染兄弟用例的夹具（同 worker 内、以及重试之间），还得从注释里重新发现这条规则。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

双击守卫：跑 marker 套件确认新用例通过，然后删掉标记的 `onDoubleClick` 那行再跑——应只有该用例失败，这正说明它是该守卫的见证而非点击用例的重复。已在当前 head 复测：删掉后 `1 failed | 9 passed`，还原后 `10 passed`，生产文件按字节还原（sha256 一致）。

清除转换：跑 markers spec 看第四条。它先断言 running 色调、钉住清除前有两个标记，然后要求目标标记计数归零，同时该行仍在列表中、且仍存活一个标记。这两条存活断言是关键：标记定位器是祖先 filter 行定位器的后代，裸的计数 0 也会被整行卸载满足。两条转换用例经同一个文件内 helper 装配场景；从其中删掉 live-state 特性，repaint 用例每次都会转红。清除用例在同一变异下则取决于计时——一条更慢的、非 live-state 的目录刷新也能在 30 秒边界附近摘掉标记——所以它见证的是行为，而非隔离轮询路径。带该特性时它约一秒内就稳定下来。

夹具所有权修复：跑新契约测试，然后去掉 scenario 工厂里的 `structuredClone` 调用再跑。应恰好三条 `sessions` 所有权用例失败（`3 failed | 4 passed`），另外四条保持绿——其中一条持有 `scenario.sessions`、通过该引用改写并断言它仍是同一数组（通知路径依赖的性质），另三条覆盖其余被克隆的集合。分别还原那三个克隆，各自恰好其对应用例转红，各为 `1 failed | 6 passed`。这一对才是重点：修复消除别名，同时不破坏 install 后的改写。随后按字节还原（sha256 一致）。

因为工厂是共享的，扫描比新用例本身更重要。已枚举所有「传入被克隆夹具」或「install 后改写它」的 spec（24 个文件），本地跑了其中 23 个：**148 个用例**，单 worker。其中一次运行命中 activity spec 的一条既有偶发失败，已用同范围 base/head A/B 归因并立 #17791；运行记录见各轮评论。剩下一个是 visuals 套件，它用独立的 Playwright config、由其自身 CI 车道覆盖；我没有本地跑它。这一扫描不与 PR CI 重复——PR 车道只跑 `@smoke`，所以该集合里的 57 个非 smoke 用例（148 个中有 91 个带 smoke）拿不到合入前的信号。全量套件确实在 `e2e.yml` 里跑，但触发是 push 到 `main`、每晚与手动，不在 pull request 上。

通知措辞：把验证计划与设计决策段、handler 三方对照——三者应一致地认为载荷只带版本与会话 id。计划还应写明归属子句未被测试，而不是暗示已覆盖。确认中文孪生版说法相同。

状态行：确认写明已落地状态与合并、两处决策与已发布代码一致、「按撰写时描述」的声明已排除验证计划一节，且状态行与验证计划之外没有任何改动。

仓库格式化器对改动文件均报告无需改动，ESLint 干净，包级 `tsc --noEmit` 退出 0。作为独立终门，隔离真实 daemon 经真实浏览器驱动通过 **18/18** 检查——含 goal 侧车在真实磁盘上搬入归档 chats 目录、归档后的目录仍投影该 goal、以及清除后标记消失。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A —— 无用户可见界面变化。双击守卫本就存在，本 PR 只是钉住它。清除行为本来也正常；新用例是证明它，工厂改动只改变测试夹具的所有权。

### 测试平台

| 操作系统 | 状态 |
| :--: | :--: |
| 🍏 macOS | N/A |
| 🪟 Windows | N/A |
| 🐧 Linux | ✅ |

### 环境（可选）

本地 vitest（marker 套件 10 例、工厂契约 7 例）、本地 Chromium 上的 Playwright（markers spec 4 例，外加 148 用例的受影响 spec 扫描）、上面各处变异检查，以及隔离真实 daemon + 真实浏览器的一轮运行。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：不改生产代码。diff 是两处文档更正、跨三个文件的九条新增用例，以及共享**测试基建**的一处行为变化——e2e scenario 工厂现在克隆其路由会就地改写的每一个 caller 集合：`sessions`、`standaloneSessions`、`midTurnMessages` 与 `gitRemotes`——最后一个计入是因为访问器把数组本体交给 add/remove 路由。第五个此类集合 `allocatedSessions` 由工厂自建，不可能别名调用方；只被整字段重赋的字段只是换引用，无需克隆。工厂改动是唯一影响超出自身文件的一项，这也是上面要跑受影响 spec 扫描、而不只跑新用例的原因。变异检查临时删过一行生产代码与一次工厂调用，两者均按字节还原；已发布的守卫未被改动。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：合入后评审的第三条是对已合入 PR **自身描述**的校准（其「绝不会出现错误状态」比「忠于日志」更强，因为 runtime 可能记下一个随后拒绝采纳的 pause）。那是已合入 PR 正文的措辞修正、不是代码改动，已在那里处理。非采纳时重新记日志属 runtime 侧改动，这里刻意不做。契约测试没有加嵌套字段泄漏用例：全套件没有任何 spec 就地改写会话的嵌套字段，加了属投机。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

auto_merge.commit_title: test(web-shell): pin the goal marker double-click guard and refresh its design record (#17733)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* docs(design): mark the sidebar goal markers design as landed

The status line still said "proposed" after #17515 merged as c98108ee13, so a
maintainer planning the next slice from this document would reopen finished
work.

Both language versions now record the landed state plus the two things review
changed: the completed-goals-hidden rule collapsed into one shared
hasVisibleGoal predicate read by three surfaces, and the goal sidecar coexisting
with main's separate artifact-count sidecar rather than being folded into it.
They also point at #17731 for the single candidate the final review bounded and
ruled out. The rest of each document keeps describing the design as written on
2026-11-17, unchanged — the status line is corrected, not the historical record.

* test(web-shell): pin the marker double-click guard and correct the notification payload

Two non-blocking items from the post-merge review of #17515, addressed here
rather than in a third PR:

- The marker's onDoubleClick guard was the one marker behavior with no witness:
  nothing dispatched dblclick on it, so dropping the line would let a marker
  double-click both open the session and bubble to the row's rename handler
  with every test still green. One case beside the Enter guard now pins it.
  Removing the guard reds exactly that case (1 failed | 9 passed), and the
  production file was restored byte-for-byte afterwards (sha256 match).
- The validation plan still listed a rejected `status` field on the goal-changed
  notification. The payload carries only { v, sessionId }: the design decisions
  section already says a status field would add a validation surface with no
  consumer, and the handler checks v, sessionId and ownership only. Both
  language versions now describe the real checks and point back at that
  decision instead of contradicting it.

* docs(design): stop claiming test coverage the ownership clause does not have

The validation plan I rewrote in the previous commit said the goal-changed
handler ignores "unowned sessions", which reads as a covered case. It is not:
the handler gates on `!entry || !this.ownsSession(sessionId)`, and the only
foreign-session case in the bridge suite sends an id that resolveEntry cannot
resolve, so `!entry` short-circuits and ownsSession is never consulted. Deleting
the ownership clause would keep the suite green.

Both language versions now say "unresolvable sessions", which is the branch the
suite actually exercises, and state outright that the ownership clause has no
test witness today — recording the gap rather than hiding it behind wording.

Pinning the clause instead was considered and rejected for this PR: ownsSession
is a constructor parameter defaulting to () => true, not a BridgeOptions field,
and createAcpSessionBridge only accepts BridgeOptions. Injecting a real
ownership callback would mean widening the production construction surface or
hand-building the bridge through a long positional parameter list; either
belongs in a change scoped to the bridge, not to a design-record correction.

* docs(design): scope the "as written" claim so it does not cover the section I edited

Audit of the previous commit found a contradiction I introduced: the status line
said the sections below describe the design as written on 2026-11-17, while the
same branch had rewritten the validation plan. The claim now excludes that one
section and says it was corrected to match what the tests actually exercise.

Also dropped "shipped" from that sentence: the double-click case is added by this
branch and is not in main yet, so calling the suite "shipped" would overstate
what has landed. Both language versions carry the same scope and the same
wording.

* test(web-shell): cover the goal-cleared repaint in the markers E2E spec

The validation plan's E2E bullet promised "clearing removes it", but the spec had
three tests and none of them cleared a goal, so the transition a maintainer most
wants witnessed had no E2E assertion. Adding the case makes the bullet true
instead of narrowing it.

Driven exactly like the existing repaint case — by-reference mutation of the
scenario session plus a sessionCatalogVersion revision bump, no reload — so it
asserts the notification path rather than the load path.

It asserts presence rather than a starting tone: goalSessions is a module-level
fixture that the repaint case mutates by reference, so the initial status depends
on test order. The first attempt asserted `running` and failed with `attention`
for exactly that reason; the case is about the marker disappearing, not its tone.

Markers spec: 4 passed (was 3).

* test(web-shell): give each mutating markers case its own fixture and pin the survivors

Two review items on the clear case, both confirmed against the code:

- createWebShellDaemonScenario keeps overrides.sessions by reference, so
  `target.goal = undefined` stripped the goal from the module-level goalSessions
  for every later test in the worker. Both mutating cases now pass
  structuredClone(goalSessions). With the fixture no longer shared, the clear
  case can assert its starting tone again instead of weakening to mere presence.
- activeMarker is a descendant of an ancestor-filtered row locator, so
  toHaveCount(0) is equally satisfied when the row itself unmounts. A refetch
  that dropped goal-less sessions would have kept this @smoke case green while
  the user's session vanished from the sidebar. The case now also pins the row
  still being listed and the other goal-bearing row keeping its marker.

Witness for the second item, using a mutation that drops only the harness
session once it has no goal (so the other three cases are unaffected):

- with the survivor assertions: 1 failed | 3 passed, failing on
  `row(page, 'E2E Harness Session')).toHaveCount(1)`
- with those two assertions ablated, same mutation: 4 passed — the vanished-row
  regression is admitted

The mock and the spec were restored byte-for-byte afterwards (mockDaemon.ts
sha256 c63da610… matched, git status clean for it). Baseline after restore:
4 passed.

* fix(web-shell): clone the e2e session fixture in the factory, not at each call site

The previous commit put structuredClone at the two call sites that mutate a
session. That left the alias where it is created: createWebShellDaemonScenario
stored overrides.sessions as-is, while its sibling goalsByWorkspace already
cloned. A third binding — openSidebar's default parameter — still handed the
module-level fixture over by reference, so the next author writing a transition
case in this file's style would pollute the fixture again and have to rediscover
the rule from a comment.

Clone once at construction, next to the existing goalsByWorkspace precedent, and
drop both call-site clones and their duplicated three-line explanations. The
constraint that matters is preserved: installMockDaemon still holds the scenario
by reference and routes still re-read scenario.sessions per request, so the
twenty-odd specs that mutate it after install keep working.

Adds the unit test this factory lacked. e2e/** is excluded from vitest, so the
contract is pinned in client/mockDaemon-fixture.test.ts: the caller array is not
handed back, an in-place mutation stays out of the caller fixture, one scenario's
mutation stays out of a later scenario over the same fixture, and the scenario
array is still exposed by reference for post-install mutation.

Mutation witness: removing the factory clone reds exactly the three ownership
cases (3 failed | 1 passed) while the by-reference case stays green — the fix
does not break the property the notification path depends on. Restored
byte-for-byte afterwards (sha256 6cbad625… matched).

Verification: contract test 4 passed; markers spec plus three representative
post-install-mutating specs (bind-session-pr, background-turn, split-persist)
23 passed; web-shell tsc --noEmit clean after rebuilding @qwen-code/sdk, whose
stale dist was producing two unrelated errors in files this change never touches;
ESLint and Prettier clean.

* test(web-shell): reuse the shared session factory and pin the pre-clear marker count

The new fixture-ownership test built its session by hand and cast it to
DaemonSessionSummary, leaving out fields the real summary carries. A shared
factory already exists for this — client/test/sidebarHarness.ts exports
makeSidebarSession, four sibling suites use it, and an earlier review round on
the merged feature PR asked for exactly this delegation. Repeating the
hand-rolled fixture in a new file would have invited the same finding again.

The clearing case explained its survivor assertions with "2 before the clear,
1 after", but only the 1 was asserted. Pin the 2 as well, so the parenthetical
is an executed witness rather than a claim, and a fixture or render regression
fails at the baseline instead of after the mutation. The sibling first case in
this file already pins the count for the same reason.

Verification: contract test 4 passed, marker suite 10 passed, markers spec
4 passed. Both mutation witnesses re-measured on this head with byte-exact
restores — removing the marker's onDoubleClick gives 1 failed | 9 passed,
removing the factory clone gives 3 failed | 1 passed with the by-reference case
still green. Because the factory is shared, all 22 non-visuals specs that pass
a session fixture or mutate scenario.sessions were run: 143 passed, single
worker. web-shell tsc --noEmit, ESLint and Prettier clean. Isolated real-daemon
rig 18/18.

* test(web-shell): share the live-state wiring between the two goal transition cases

The clearing case repeated the repaint case's scenario block verbatim — 19
identical lines — and the duplication is load-bearing rather than cosmetic:
workspace_session_live_state is what enables the live-state hook, so a future
edit applied to one copy would leave the other silently not polling, and that
case would fail as a bare 30-second locator timeout with nothing naming the
missing capability. Both cases now build their scenario through one file-local
helper, and the find + assign + revision bump goes through a second one.

Checking the review's second premise turned up a defect that had been sitting
here unnoticed: the 250 ms interval both copies advertised was inert.
resolveSessionLiveStatePollInterval accepts only safe integers >= 1_000 and
otherwise returns the 5 s default, so the cases were polling at 5 s while
claiming 250 ms. Advertise 1_000 — the smallest honoured value, as
composer-usage.spec.ts already does — and record the floor in the comment so the
next reader does not inherit a knob that does nothing. Repaint drops from 19.9 s
to 16.0 s and clearing from 19.6 s to 16.9 s.

Verification: markers spec 4 passed; Prettier, ESLint and tsc --noEmit clean.
Removing the capability from the shared helper reds the repaint case in 4 of 4
runs. The clearing case is timing-dependent under that mutation (3 failures, 3
passes over six measurements): the isolated run passed at 49.6 s against 35.3 s
when it fails, so a slower non-live-state refresh can satisfy it near the 30 s
boundary. It witnesses the behavior, not isolation of the live-state path, and
with the capability present it settles in about a second. Every mutation
restored byte-for-byte (sha256 ce4db2ba… matched).

* test(web-shell): close the fixture-ownership contract for every collection routes mutate

Review pointed out that the factory still aliased standaloneSessions and
midTurnMessages while the new comment and contract test framed the fix as a
fixture-ownership contract. The standalone create/patch routes unshift and
index-replace the first, the mid-turn route pushes the second, so a caller
sharing either array across cases would see one case's writes in the next.
Nine specs do pass standaloneSessions, but every site builds a fresh inline
array, so this is a trap for the next author rather than a live leak — which is
why it belongs with the contract meant to prevent it.

Enumerated the class instead of fixing two instances: the only in-place writes
to scenario collections are sessions, standaloneSessions, midTurnMessages and
allocatedSessions. The first three come from overrides and are now all cloned;
allocatedSessions is factory-built, and the only nested writes are on the
factory-built state literal. The clone-site comment names that set explicitly
rather than implying every caller-supplied array is owned.

Also corrects the shared-helper comment in the markers spec: it promised a
missing capability makes the case fail as an opaque timeout, but measurement
showed the clearing case is timing-dependent under that ablation. It now states
which case fails deterministically and which may still pass.

Verification: contract test 6 passed. Per-field witnesses — reverting the
standaloneSessions clone reds exactly its own case, reverting the midTurnMessages
clone reds exactly its own case, each 1 failed | 5 passed, both restored
byte-for-byte (sha256 3acee6c3… matched). ESLint, Prettier and tsc --noEmit clean.

prs.title: feat(web-shell): commit only the selected files from the commit view
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The Web Shell commit view can now commit a subset of the dirty files. It lists every uncommitted file with a checkbox, preselects all of them, and sends the selection with the commit. Unchecked files stay in the working tree, and work the user had already staged outside the selection stays staged instead of being swept in.

Underneath, the shared commit helper and the daemon commit route gained a `paths` option next to the existing `all` flag. The dialog no longer uses `all: true`; it always sends an explicit selection, and refuses to commit when nothing is selected instead of letting git fail on an empty pathspec.

Renames are handled explicitly: either half of a rename selects the pair, because git only records the rename when the deletion and the addition land in the same commit.

## Why it's needed

The commit view always committed everything. A single session that produced two unrelated changes (a bug fix and a refactor, say) could only be split into clean commits from a terminal, which defeats the point of having the dialog. The issue asks for per-file checkboxes so the Web Shell git workflow matches what the CLI already allows.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit and route tests cover the new behavior; no manual UI session was run. Reproduce the original gap by opening the commit view with two dirty files and pressing Commit — before this change both files are in the commit, after it only the checked ones are, and unchecking all of them surfaces a "select at least one file" error instead of a daemon call.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no screenshot or recording was captured for this run.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Tests and lint run locally on macOS from a linked worktree; no `npm run dev` session.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the dialog now depends on the diff listing to build a selection. If the list is empty or fails to load, it refuses to commit rather than falling back to committing everything, so a broken diff route blocks committing from the dialog (the CLI is unaffected).
- Not validated / out of scope: no manual UI verification on a running daemon, and no full `npm run build`. `packages/cli` typecheck was not run (fresh worktree reports unrelated TS6305 on unbuilt workspace dependencies); `packages/core` typecheck passes. `packages/web-shell` typecheck reports only the 12 known stale-SDK errors, which are identical on `origin/main`.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. `all: true` keeps its previous semantics.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #8446

prs.title: feat(live-voice): add configurable turn_detection for realtime session.update
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Live Voice now negotiates a turn detection mode that the selected realtime model actually supports. When `experimental.liveVoice.turnDetection` is unset or empty, the session defaults to `server_vad` for qwen-audio realtime models and keeps `semantic_vad` for all other models, preserving the existing omni realtime behavior. The default is resolved from the effective realtime model — the model that actually goes on the wire — so `provider:modelId` selectors such as `dashscope:qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus` also receive the correct default. A new enum setting lets users override the mode with `server_vad`, `smart_turn`, `smart_turn_v2`, or `semantic_vad`. The Host client applies the model-aware default inside its session layer; the daemon resolves it during credential resolution (and it can be overridden there via experimental.liveVoice.turnDetection).. An invalid setting value is a configuration error that makes Live Voice unavailable without taking the daemon down at boot. The `null` push-to-talk mode from the previous revision is removed: with no server-side VAD nothing commits the input audio buffer on this path, so the mode could connect but never answer; making it viable requires a client-side commit trigger, which is separable follow-up work.

## Why it's needed

Fixes #17000. The qwen-audio realtime family rejects `turn_detection.type: 'semantic_vad'` — the value both realtime clients hardcoded — so Live Voice fails at `session.update` with `Unsupported turn_detection.type` even though the WebSocket handshake succeeds and the session reports ready. Users with a qwen-audio realtime route cannot use Live Voice at all. The server's own default for these models is `server_vad` (visible in `session.created`), which is what this PR now sends.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the focused checks locally (all executed on macOS against this revision): `npx prettier --check` on the changed files, `npx eslint --max-warnings 0` on the changed TypeScript files, `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/cli` and `packages/qwen-live`, and vitest on the three touched test files — 47 + 40 + 85 = 172 tests pass. `npm run generate:settings-schema` was run and the regenerated schema is committed; re-running it produces no further diff.

For the behavioral claim, configure a `realtimeOnly` route for `qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus`, resolve the credential through the fixed resolution path, and open a Realtime WebSocket to the derived endpoint. Sending the old hardcoded `semantic_vad` in `session.update` is rejected by the server (Arm A below); sending the resolved `server_vad` is accepted with `session.updated` (Arm B); an explicit `smart_turn_v2` override is also accepted (Arm C). A reviewer should additionally confirm that the default keys off the effective wire model (unit test with a `provider:modelId` selector), that an invalid value degrades to `provider_config` unreadiness instead of crashing app construction (the boot read is now wrapped; there is no dedicated test harness for the boot path itself, so that part is covered by inspection), and that the Host client still sends `create_response: false`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Non-UI change: wire transcripts against the real endpoint instead of screenshots. Probe run 2026-11-12 against `wss://token-plan.ap-southeast-1.maas.aliyuncs.com/api-ws/v1/realtime`, model `qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus`, voice `longanqian`; the credential (including `turnDetection: server_vad`) was resolved by the fixed code from a real user configuration. API key redacted.

Arm A — before (old hardcoded value), sent `session.update`:

```json
{
  "type": "session.update",
  "session": {
    "modalities": ["text", "audio"],
    "model": "qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus",
    "voice": "longanqian",
    "turn_detection": { "type": "semantic_vad", "create_response": true, "interrupt_response": true },
    "input_audio_format": "pcm",
    "output_audio_format": "pcm",
    "input_audio_transcription": { "model": "qwen3-asr-flash-realtime" }
  }
}
```

Server response:

```json
{
  "event_id": "event_IfXcIZ1DBBSxKxYaapbDi",
  "type": "error",
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "invalid_value",
    "message": "Unsupported turn_detection.type: 'semantic_vad'. Supported values: server_vad, smart_turn, smart_turn_v2. Use turn_detection: null for push-to-talk mode.",
    "param": "session.update"
  }
}
```

Arm B — after (resolved default), sent `session.update`:

```json
{
  "type": "session.update",
  "session": {
    "modalities": ["text", "audio"],
    "model": "qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus",
    "voice": "longanqian",
    "turn_detection": { "type": "server_vad", "create_response": true, "interrupt_response": true },
    "input_audio_format": "pcm",
    "output_audio_format": "pcm",
    "input_audio_transcription": { "model": "qwen3-asr-flash-realtime" }
  }
}
```

Server response:

```json
{
  "event_id": "event_Fig5L9JqDchGYudRRCa6P",
  "type": "session.updated",
  "session": {
    "id": "sess_VsEhTzNuX85X9poHbhAih",
    "object": "realtime.session",
    "model": "qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus",
    "modalities": ["text", "audio"],
    "voice": "longanqian",
    "output_audio_format": "pcm",
    "input_audio_transcription": { "model": "qwen3-asr-flash-realtime" },
    "turn_detection": { "type": "server_vad", "threshold": 0.5, "silence_duration_ms": 800 }
  }
}
```

Arm C — explicit `smart_turn_v2` override: the server answered `session.updated` (`sess_DnapvOkZdHsXOk3zdHdVF`) echoing `"turn_detection": { "type": "smart_turn_v2", "threshold": 0.5, "silence_duration_ms": 3000 }`.

Speech turns with real microphone audio after the accepted update: **not tested** (requires interactive audio input); everything above was observed live against the real endpoint.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment

Node + pnpm workspace install; focused vitest, tsc, eslint, prettier; live WebSocket probe from macOS. Full preflight/build/e2e were not run locally; fork CI is pending maintainer approval (`action_required`).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: qwen-audio realtime sessions now receive `server_vad` instead of a value the server rejects; omni and all other models keep `semantic_vad`, so existing working setups are unchanged, and the override setting is opt-in.
- Not validated / out of scope: end-to-end speech turns with real microphone audio (the probe verifies `session.update` acceptance only); boot-path degradation is covered by inspection, not a dedicated test; full CI has not run locally (fork PR); push-to-talk (`turn_detection: null`) is removed from this PR and needs a client-side input-commit trigger as separable follow-up; `smart_turn`/`smart_turn_v2` are accepted by the endpoint but not exercised with real speech.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none for existing configurations. The unreleased `null`/empty-string push-to-talk behavior from the previous revision of this PR is removed; an empty string now means unset (model-aware default), consistent with the other `liveVoice` fields.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17000

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的作用

Live Voice 现在会协商所选 realtime 模型实际支持的轮次检测（turn detection）模式。当 `experimental.liveVoice.turnDetection` 未设置或为空时，会话对 qwen-audio realtime 模型默认使用 `server_vad`，对其他所有模型保持 `semantic_vad`，从而保留现有的 omni realtime 行为。默认值根据生效的 realtime 模型——即真正发送到服务端的模型——解析，因此诸如 `dashscope:qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus` 的 `provider:modelId` 选择器也能获得正确的默认值。新增的枚举设置允许用户以 `server_vad`、`smart_turn`、`smart_turn_v2` 或 `semantic_vad` 覆盖模式。两个 realtime 客户端都应用同样的模型感知默认值：daemon 的 Live Voice 会话与 Qwen Live Host 会话，其中 Host 客户端刻意保持 `create_response: false`，因为其编排器负责响应创建。非法设置值属于配置错误，只会让 Live Voice 不可用，而不会在启动时拖垮 daemon。上一版中的 `null` 按键说话（push-to-talk）模式已移除：在没有服务端 VAD 的情况下，此路径上没有任何机制提交输入音频缓冲区，该模式能连接却永远无法应答；要使其可用需要客户端提交触发器，属于可分离的后续工作。

## 为什么需要

修复 #17000。qwen-audio realtime 系列拒绝 `turn_detection.type: 'semantic_vad'`——这正是两个 realtime 客户端硬编码的值——因此即使 WebSocket 握手成功、会话报告就绪，Live Voice 仍会在 `session.update` 处以 `Unsupported turn_detection.type` 失败。配置了 qwen-audio realtime 路由的用户完全无法使用 Live Voice。服务端对这些模型的自身默认值是 `server_vad`（在 `session.created` 中可见），也就是本 PR 现在发送的值。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

在本地运行聚焦检查（本修订版已在 macOS 上全部执行）：对改动文件运行 `npx prettier --check`，对改动的 TypeScript 文件运行 `npx eslint --max-warnings 0`，在 `packages/cli` 与 `packages/qwen-live` 中运行 `tsc --noEmit`，并对三个改动的测试文件运行 vitest——47 + 40 + 85 = 172 个测试通过。已运行 `npm run generate:settings-schema` 并提交重新生成的 schema；再次运行不会产生新的差异。

对于行为性结论，配置 `qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus` 的 `realtimeOnly` 路由，通过修复后的解析路径解析凭据，并向派生的 endpoint 打开 Realtime WebSocket。在 `session.update` 中发送旧的硬编码 `semantic_vad` 会被服务端拒绝（下方 Arm A）；发送解析出的 `server_vad` 会被接受并返回 `session.updated`（Arm B）；显式 `smart_turn_v2` 覆盖同样被接受（Arm C）。审阅者还应确认：默认值以生效的线上模型为准（含 `provider:modelId` 选择器的单元测试）；非法值降级为 `provider_config` 不可用而不是让应用构造崩溃（启动读取现已包裹 try/catch；启动路径本身没有专用测试 harness，该部分仅经代码审视覆盖）；Host 客户端仍发送 `create_response: false`。

### 证据（前后对比）

非 UI 变更：以真实 endpoint 的线上转录代替截图。探针于 2026-11-12 对 `wss://token-plan.ap-southeast-1.maas.aliyuncs.com/api-ws/v1/realtime` 运行，模型 `qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus`，音色 `longanqian`；凭据（含 `turnDetection: server_vad`）由修复后的代码从真实用户配置解析。API key 已脱敏。

Arm A——之前（旧硬编码值），发送的 `session.update`：

```json
{
  "type": "session.update",
  "session": {
    "modalities": ["text", "audio"],
    "model": "qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus",
    "voice": "longanqian",
    "turn_detection": { "type": "semantic_vad", "create_response": true, "interrupt_response": true },
    "input_audio_format": "pcm",
    "output_audio_format": "pcm",
    "input_audio_transcription": { "model": "qwen3-asr-flash-realtime" }
  }
}
```

服务端响应：

```json
{
  "event_id": "event_IfXcIZ1DBBSxKxYaapbDi",
  "type": "error",
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "invalid_value",
    "message": "Unsupported turn_detection.type: 'semantic_vad'. Supported values: server_vad, smart_turn, smart_turn_v2. Use turn_detection: null for push-to-talk mode.",
    "param": "session.update"
  }
}
```

Arm B——之后（解析出的默认值），发送的 `session.update`：

```json
{
  "type": "session.update",
  "session": {
    "modalities": ["text", "audio"],
    "model": "qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus",
    "voice": "longanqian",
    "turn_detection": { "type": "server_vad", "create_response": true, "interrupt_response": true },
    "input_audio_format": "pcm",
    "output_audio_format": "pcm",
    "input_audio_transcription": { "model": "qwen3-asr-flash-realtime" }
  }
}
```

服务端响应：

```json
{
  "event_id": "event_Fig5L9JqDchGYudRRCa6P",
  "type": "session.updated",
  "session": {
    "id": "sess_VsEhTzNuX85X9poHbhAih",
    "object": "realtime.session",
    "model": "qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus",
    "modalities": ["text", "audio"],
    "voice": "longanqian",
    "output_audio_format": "pcm",
    "input_audio_transcription": { "model": "qwen3-asr-flash-realtime" },
    "turn_detection": { "type": "server_vad", "threshold": 0.5, "silence_duration_ms": 800 }
  }
}
```

Arm C——显式 `smart_turn_v2` 覆盖：服务端返回 `session.updated`（`sess_DnapvOkZdHsXOk3zdHdVF`），回显 `"turn_detection": { "type": "smart_turn_v2", "threshold": 0.5, "silence_duration_ms": 3000 }`。

更新被接受后使用真实麦克风音频的语音轮次：**未测试**（需要交互式音频输入）；以上所有内容均为对真实 endpoint 的实测观察。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### 环境

Node + pnpm 工作区安装；聚焦 vitest、tsc、eslint、prettier；从 macOS 发起的实时 WebSocket 探针。完整的 preflight/build/e2e 未在本地运行；fork CI 等待维护者批准（`action_required`）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：qwen-audio realtime 会话现在收到 `server_vad`，而不是服务端拒绝的值；omni 及其他所有模型保持 `semantic_vad`，因此现有可用配置不受影响，覆盖设置为可选项。
- 未验证 / 范围之外：使用真实麦克风音频的端到端语音轮次（探针仅验证 `session.update` 被接受）；启动路径降级仅经代码审视覆盖，无专用测试；完整 CI 未在本地运行（fork PR）；按键说话（`turn_detection: null`）已从本 PR 移除，需要客户端输入提交触发器作为可分离的后续工作；`smart_turn`/`smart_turn_v2` 被 endpoint 接受，但未用真实语音演练。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：对现有配置无破坏。本 PR 上一版中未发布的 `null`/空字符串按键说话行为已移除；空字符串现在表示未设置（模型感知默认值），与其他 `liveVoice` 字段保持一致。

## 关联 Issue

修复 #17000

</details>
