prs.title: fix(serve): pin remote-access admission and non-REST shutdown drain (#17712)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Closes the three deferred coverage/documentation gaps tracked in #17712 and fixes the production shutdown defect the new drain coverage uncovered:

1. **`remote-access` listener end-to-end admission pin.** A new `enableRemoteAccessListener` fixture pins the interface list to loopback, enables the listener through the real `POST /remote-access/enable` management route and reveals the remote bearer, then drives the actual listener: 51 streams admitted, the 52nd refused with the exact listener-scoped body (`scope: "listener"`, `listener: "remote-access"`, `limit: 51`), the refusal attributed in the real daemon access log with `reason=listener`, the primary listener still admitting, `byListener['remote-access']` counted, and the remote deep-health pair reading 51/51. This mirrors the existing `local-control` clamp pin, so both pairing listeners are now pinned end-to-end.
2. **Shutdown drain coverage for the counted non-REST surfaces.** A new pin opens a generation stream, an ACP SSE stream and an initialized ACP WebSocket (three counted slots), then asserts `handle.close()` resolves and every slot returns to baseline — open non-REST streams neither hang shutdown nor leak their shared slots. A second pin opens a raw upgraded ACP socket whose peer never reads or answers close and asserts shutdown still resolves and frees the listener.
3. **Stalled-peer scope note.** `docs/users/qwen-serve.md`'s scope note and the design's Constraints section now state the bound explicitly: a peer that stops reading stalls writes on non-REST surfaces with no reaper to reclaim the slot; the stream holds its cap share until its lifecycle ends or shutdown force-closes it, and the shared cap bounds how many such slots coexist. The design's open question is recorded as resolved by decision: reaper coverage stays REST-only (heterogeneous lifecycles make a per-surface writer-stall reaper a separate design), with the documented bound plus the new pins instead.
4. **Shutdown force-close reaches upgraded sockets (production fix).** `serve-app-lifecycle` now tracks every accepted socket from the `'connection'` event and the close force timers destroy the survivors, so an upgraded ACP socket whose peer never answers a close frame no longer hangs `handle.close()` — it previously rejected with "The serve listener did not confirm shutdown." Tracking from `'connection'` rather than `'upgrade'` keeps Node's no-listener fall-through to the request handler intact: a sole `'upgrade'` listener would park handle-less-profile upgrades instead of answering the hidden 404 (a regression the first tracking attempt introduced and CI integration caught). A unit pin in `serve-app-lifecycle.test.ts` asserts that fall-through survives while no transport owns upgrades. The same sweep lands on the Local Control pairing listener (`local-control/service.ts`), whose `close()` previously hung `disable()` and the daemon drain over a non-answering upgraded ACP peer; a service-level pin asserts `disable()` resolves within a bound over such a peer.

## Why it's needed

#17662 unified admission and occupancy across every long-lived surface, making the shared cap the only backstop for surfaces the writer-stall reaper does not cover. The `remote-access` pairing guarantee previously rested on code symmetry with `local-control` rather than a pin, and the stalled-peer bound was implicit. Both gaps were deferred during #17662's review and tracked in #17712. The shutdown defect in item 4 is the same failure shape #17502 fixed for REST streams, reached through upgraded sockets that `closeAllConnections()` alone does not touch.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- From `packages/cli`: `npx vitest run src/serve/server.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false -t "(clamps the remote-access listener|shutdown force-closes counted|shutdown reclaims an upgraded)"` — expect 3 passed. Mutation witnesses: removing the `remote-access` clamp from `resolveSseAdmissionCaps` reds the first pin (52nd stream admitted with 200); deleting the `for (const socket of this.openSockets) socket.destroy()` loop from the lifecycle force-close reds the upgraded-socket pin ("The serve listener did not confirm shutdown."). Removing only `server.closeAllConnections()` is **no longer discriminating** — the loop already destroys every socket it reaches, witnessed green; restoring an `'upgrade'` listener in `bindServer` reds the fall-through pin in `serve-app-lifecycle.test.ts` (handshake timeout).
- Regression selection: `npx vitest run src/serve/server.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false -t "(Unified SSE admission/occupancy|Deferred #17502 review pins|T2.9 SSE writer idle timeout|SSE reaper arming|HTTPS SSE eviction force-close|records an unfinished drain)"` — expect 31 passed; plus `src/serve/remote-access.test.ts` and `src/serve/serve-app-lifecycle.test.ts` (17 passed), and `src/serve/local-control/service.test.ts` (27 passed).
- Docs: read the qualified scope note in `docs/users/qwen-serve.md` and the resolved open question in `docs/design/sse-unified-admission-occupancy.md` / `.zh-CN.md`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: no test drove the `remote-access` listener's admission path; shutdown behavior for counted non-REST streams was unpinned, and a non-answering upgraded peer made `handle.close()` reject; the scope note implied non-REST surfaces always end with their lifecycles. After: the pins green with the mutation witnesses above; shutdown resolves and frees the port for a non-answering upgraded peer (real-daemon SIGTERM drive); the hosted-harness hidden-404 upgrade fall-through is preserved (CI integration shard red→green across the tracking fix); the bound is documented in the users guide and the design (EN/ZH).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

## Risk & Scope

- Production change is confined to shutdown force-close: `serve-app-lifecycle` and the Local Control service `close()` (connection tracking plus destroying survivors); no wire, API or admission-semantics change, and Node's upgrade fall-through is preserved and pinned. The pins exercise real listeners and the real management routes in-process (`runQwenServe`), with the interface list pinned to loopback for determinism on hosts without a usable LAN interface.
- Not validated / out of scope: a per-surface writer-stall reaper (deliberately deferred by decision, recorded in the design); Windows/Linux locally (Linux unit/integration shards green in CI).

## Linked Issues

Closes #17712. Refs #17554, #17662, #17502.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

关闭 #17712 跟踪的三个延后覆盖/文档缺口，并修复新 drain 覆盖暴露的生产 shutdown 缺陷：

1. **`remote-access` listener 端到端准入钉。** 新夹具 `enableRemoteAccessListener` 把接口列表钉到 loopback，经真实 `POST /remote-access/enable` 管理路由启用 listener 并 reveal 远程 bearer，然后驱动真实 listener：51 条流准入、第 52 条以精确 listener 范围正文拒绝（`scope: "listener"`、`listener: "remote-access"`、`limit: 51`）、拒绝在真实 daemon 访问日志中以 `reason=listener` 归因、主 listener 仍准入、`byListener['remote-access']` 计数、远程 deep-health 对读 51/51。与既有 `local-control` 钳制钉对称，两个配对 listener 现在都有端到端钉。
2. **新计数非 REST 表面的 shutdown drain 覆盖。** 新钉打开生成流、ACP SSE 流与已 initialize 的 ACP WebSocket（三个计数槽位），断言 `handle.close()` resolve 且所有槽位回基线——开着的非 REST 流既不挂死 shutdown 也不泄漏共享槽位。第二条钉打开一条对端永不读取、永不回应 close 的裸已升级 ACP socket，断言 shutdown 仍 resolve 并释放 listener。
3. **停滞对端范围注记。** `docs/users/qwen-serve.md` 范围注记与设计约束节现在明确边界：对端停止读取时非 REST 表面写入停滞、无回收器回收槽位；流持有其 cap 份额直到生命周期结束或 shutdown 强制关闭；共享 cap 约束此类槽位同时存在的数量。设计开放问题记录为按决定决议：回收器覆盖保持仅 REST（生命周期各异使逐表面 writer-stall 回收器成为另一个设计），以文档化边界加新钉代替。
4. **shutdown 强制关闭触及已升级 socket（生产修复）。** `serve-app-lifecycle` 现在从 `'connection'` 事件跟踪每个已接受 socket，close 强制计时器销毁幸存者，因此对端永不回应 close 帧的已升级 ACP socket 不再挂死 `handle.close()`——此前会以 "The serve listener did not confirm shutdown." 拒绝。从 `'connection'` 而非 `'upgrade'` 跟踪保住 Node 无 listener 时回退 request handler 的语义：sole `'upgrade'` listener 会把无 transport profile 的 upgrade park 住而不答 hidden 404（第一版跟踪曾引入该回归、被 CI integration 抓住）。`serve-app-lifecycle.test.ts` 的单位钉断言无 transport owns upgrade 时该回退仍在。同一清扫落到 Local Control 配对 listener（`local-control/service.ts`）：其 `close()` 此前会让 `disable()` 与 daemon drain 在不回应 close 的已升级 ACP 对端上永久挂起；服务级钉断言 `disable()` 在此类对端上有界 resolve。

## 为什么需要

#17662 把准入与占用统一到每个长连接表面，使共享 cap 成为回收器未覆盖表面的唯一兜底。`remote-access` 的配对保证此前靠与 `local-control` 的代码对称性而非钉；停滞对端边界此前是隐式的。两者在 #17662 评审中延后并跟踪于 #17712。第 4 项的 shutdown 缺陷与 #17502 为 REST 流修掉的是同一故障形态，只是经由 `closeAllConnections()` 单独触及不到的已升级 socket 到达。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

- 在 `packages/cli` 下：`npx vitest run src/serve/server.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false -t "(clamps the remote-access listener|shutdown force-closes counted|shutdown reclaims an upgraded)"`——预期 3 过。变异见证：从 `resolveSseAdmissionCaps` 移除 `remote-access` 钳制使第一钉红（第 52 条流 200 准入）；从 lifecycle force-close 删除 `for (const socket of this.openSockets) socket.destroy()` 循环使 upgraded 钉红（"The serve listener did not confirm shutdown."）。仅移除 `server.closeAllConnections()` **不再具有判别力**——loop 已销毁其触及的每个 socket，实测绿；在 `bindServer` 恢复 `'upgrade'` listener 使 `serve-app-lifecycle.test.ts` 的 fall-through 钉红（handshake 超时）。
- 回归选择：`npx vitest run src/serve/server.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false -t "(Unified SSE admission/occupancy|Deferred #17502 review pins|T2.9 SSE writer idle timeout|SSE reaper arming|HTTPS SSE eviction force-close|records an unfinished drain)"`——预期 31 过；另加 `src/serve/remote-access.test.ts` 与 `src/serve/serve-app-lifecycle.test.ts`（17 过），以及 `src/serve/local-control/service.test.ts`（27 过）。
- 文档：读 `docs/users/qwen-serve.md` 限定后的范围注记与 `docs/design/sse-unified-admission-occupancy.md` / `.zh-CN.md` 已决议的开放问题。

### 证据（前后对比）

前：无测试驱动 `remote-access` listener 准入路径；计数非 REST 表面的 shutdown 行为无钉，且不回应 close 的已升级对端会使 `handle.close()` 拒绝；范围注记暗示非 REST 表面总随生命周期结束。后：各钉绿且带上述变异见证；真实 daemon SIGTERM 驱动下不回应升级对端的 shutdown resolve 且端口释放；hosted-harness hidden-404 upgrade 回退保住（CI integration shard 随跟踪修复红→绿）；边界在用户指南与设计（EN/ZH）中文档化。

| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |

## 风险与范围

- 生产改动仅限 shutdown force-close：`serve-app-lifecycle` 与 Local Control service 的 `close()`（connection 跟踪加销毁幸存者）；无 wire、API 或准入语义变更，Node 的 upgrade 回退被保住并有钉。钉在进程内（`runQwenServe`）驱动真实 listener 与真实管理路由，接口列表钉到 loopback 以保证无可拥 LAN 接口机器上的确定性。

prs.title: perf(core): compact the inline memory and first-request prompts
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Shortens the main session's file-based memory policy while keeping the instructions for saving, updating, and forgetting inline. A fresh session omits an empty memory catalog. Clearing the last entry still supersedes existing catalog snapshots on live and resumed requests. The base system prompt drops repeated generic tool examples and compresses the guidance for consequential actions. Dedicated model formats and the explicit generic-example override remain available.

## Why it's needed

A typical first question carries the resident policy even when it involves no memory change. The approach evaluated in #17784 also introduced an extra policy-loading step on explicit memory turns. Keeping the write contract inline reduces the first request without requiring that step.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Send the same fixed ordinary question to fresh sessions with empty memory. Check the first outgoing main request and add up the provider input reported by every request in the turn.
- Save, update, forget, and recall an isolated synthetic preference. Verify the saved topic, index, and reply. Compare each scenario's median whole-turn input against the baseline.
- Start with an empty catalog, save an entry, delete the last entry, and resume the session. Restore the same entry and confirm each new request sees the current catalog.
- Check the dedicated tool formats, the explicit generic-example override, and the authorization rules for consequential actions.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Base `477dc9d214`, candidate `74df3b3630`. Five paired runs per scenario used identical synthetic inputs and initial memory state in fresh isolated sessions, with alternating run order. Main and side calls used `qwen3.8-max`. Real background extraction used `qwen3.8-flash`. All 219 requests returned complete provider input usage. Whole-turn input sums the main, side, and background calls.

**The first main request for the fixed ordinary question fell from 12,950 to 11,540 provider input tokens in all five pairs, a decrease of 1,410 tokens (10.9%).**

| Scenario | Whole-turn input median, base → candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ordinary first question | 42,112 → 47,122 | +11.9% |
| Save memory | 38,986 → 46,599 | +19.5% |
| Update memory | 39,844 → 36,016 | −9.6% |
| Forget memory | 53,037 → 48,412 | −8.7% |
| Recall memory | 26,344 → 18,529 | −29.7% |

**All five scenario medians are within the 30% increase limit.** The ordinary first-question whole turn still used more input because its background extraction median increased from 29,162 to 35,582 tokens, outweighing the first-main reduction. One ordinary pair increased 40.9% when extraction went from three to five requests. That pair is included in the median. The extractor persisted inferred preferences from the one-off synthetic question in four baseline sessions and five candidate sessions, with six topic files written in each arm.

All candidate save, update, forget, and recall fixtures passed the disk and answer checks. The save median went from three to four requests. In three candidate runs, the model read the index and wrote the topic and index in separate rounds. No memory-policy skill was loaded. Controlled CLI and ACP checks also verified the empty catalog, clearing the last entry, session resume, and restoring the same entry.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Build, bundle, type check, 2,188 focused tests, and controlled CLI/ACP checks passed |
| Windows | CI |
| Linux | CI |

## Risk & Scope

Model tool choices and background extraction can affect whole-turn usage. The comparison above includes both effects. Existing memory files and settings are compatible.

[English design](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/74df3b3630d8d448a1459ad137598896a0ff77c0/docs/design/auto-memory/compact-inline-memory-prompt.md) · [简体中文设计](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/74df3b3630d8d448a1459ad137598896a0ff77c0/docs/design/auto-memory/compact-inline-memory-prompt.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Revises the approach evaluated in #17784.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 改动

缩短主会话的文件式记忆策略，保存、更新和遗忘规则继续内联。新会话省去空目录快照。删除最后一条记忆后，最新清空快照会覆盖较早的目录，在线请求和恢复会话都适用。基础系统提示词移除重复的通用工具示例，精简高影响操作说明。模型专属格式和显式启用通用示例的入口继续可用。

## 背景

普通首问也要携带常驻策略。#17784 评估的做法还会让显式记忆操作多一步加载规则。精简内联规则能缩小首问输入，同时让写入规则直接可用。

## 审阅测试计划

### 验证步骤

- 在记忆为空的新会话发送相同固定首问。检查第一条主模型请求，并加总该轮每条请求的 provider 输入。
- 保存、更新、遗忘和召回一条隔离的合成偏好。核对主题正文、索引和召回答复，分别比较各场景的整轮输入中位数。
- 从空目录开始，保存一条记忆，删除最后一条后恢复会话，再重新添加同一条记忆。确认新请求使用当前目录。
- 检查模型专属工具格式、通用示例的显式开关，以及高影响操作的授权规则。

### 前后对照证据

基线为 `477dc9d214`，候选为 `74df3b3630`。每个场景五组配对，各组采用相同的合成输入和初始记忆，在全新隔离会话中交替运行两个版本。主模型和旁路请求使用 `qwen3.8-max`，实际后台提取使用 `qwen3.8-flash`。219 次请求均返回完整 provider 输入用量。整轮输入加总主模型、旁路和后台请求。

**五组固定普通首问的首个主模型请求均从 12,950 降至 11,540 token，减少 1,410 token（10.9%）。**

| 场景 | 整轮输入中位数（基线 → 候选） | 变化 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 普通首问 | 42,112 → 47,122 | +11.9% |
| 保存记忆 | 38,986 → 46,599 | +19.5% |
| 更新记忆 | 39,844 → 36,016 | −9.6% |
| 遗忘记忆 | 53,037 → 48,412 | −8.7% |
| 召回记忆 | 26,344 → 18,529 | −29.7% |

**五个场景的整轮输入中位数都在 30% 增幅上限内。** 普通首问整轮输入增加，是因为后台提取输入中位数从 29,162 升到 35,582 token，抵消了首个主模型请求的节省。有一组后台提取从 3 次增到 5 次，整轮输入增加 40.9%。该组已计入中位数。后台提取把一次性合成题目推断为长期偏好，基线发生于 4 个会话，候选发生于 5 个会话，两边各写入 6 份主题文件。

候选的保存、更新、遗忘和召回用例均通过了落盘和答复核查。保存的请求数中位数从 3 次变为 4 次。三组候选先读索引，再分两个回合写入正文和索引。评测中没有加载记忆策略 Skill。受控 CLI 和 ACP 验证还覆盖了空目录、清空最后一条、恢复会话和重新添加同一条。

### 测试平台

| 平台 | 状态 |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | 构建、打包、类型检查、2,188 项定向测试和受控 CLI/ACP 验证通过 |
| Windows | CI |
| Linux | CI |

## 风险和范围

模型工具选择和后台提取均可影响整轮用量。以上实测已计入两项影响。现有记忆文件和设置兼容。

[英文设计](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/74df3b3630d8d448a1459ad137598896a0ff77c0/docs/design/auto-memory/compact-inline-memory-prompt.md) · [中文设计](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/74df3b3630d8d448a1459ad137598896a0ff77c0/docs/design/auto-memory/compact-inline-memory-prompt.zh-CN.md)

## 关联

调整 #17784 中评估过的方案。

</details>

prs.title: fix(sdk-java): preserve assistant callback UUIDs
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The legacy Java SDK passes each complete assistant message's envelope UUID to its content callbacks when present. If the envelope has no UUID, each block keeps its existing ID. Streaming callbacks keep an explicit non-null `message_id` and otherwise use the stream event UUID.

## Why it's needed

Applications that use the callback ID to associate content with the envelope that carried it currently receive a null ID in both modes, even when the CLI supplied a UUID.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

For each mode, send two assistant envelopes with distinct UUIDs and texts through an SDK session. Confirm that the text callbacks arrive in order and each carries the UUID of its own envelope. For a complete message without a UUID, give the text block an ID and verify that the callback retains it. For a stream event containing both fields, verify that the callback receives the explicit `message_id`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Both regression cases delivered the expected text on the baseline and then failed with two null callback IDs. Both passed with this change. The local Maven SDK suite reported 455 passed and 10 skipped, with zero failures or errors. Checkstyle and packaging passed. One run with `CI=true` hit a loopback TLS timeout in an existing test. The final local run passed that test. N/A for UI screenshots.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Tested locally |
| Windows | Pending upstream CI |
| Linux | Pending upstream CI |

### Environment (optional)

macOS arm64, OpenJDK 17.0.18, Maven 3.9.12. The regression uses the actual SDK session and decoders with a fixture transport.

## Risk & Scope

- Standard CLI stream events supply only a UUID. That UUID can differ across events within one assistant message.
- Local coverage used the SDK fixture transport. The upstream Java matrix and daemon integration workflows are pending.
- Callers can read the supplied UUID from the existing callback field. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17656

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 改动内容

旧版 Java SDK 将完整助手消息的外层 UUID 传给内容回调。缺少外层 UUID 时，各内容块保留已有 ID。流式回调优先使用显式提供的非 null `message_id`，否则使用该事件的外层 UUID。

## 改动原因

应用可以使用回调 ID 将正文关联到承载它的外层消息。目前即使 CLI 提供了 UUID，两种模式下的回调 ID 也都为空。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

在两种模式下分别通过 SDK 会话送入两帧，每帧采用不同的 UUID 和正文。确认正文回调按顺序到达，每个回调携带自己那一帧的 UUID。再给缺少外层 UUID 的完整消息设置文字块 ID，验证回调保留该 ID。给流式事件同时设置两个字段，验证回调收到显式的 `message_id`。

### 证据（修复前后）

基线的两条回归用例都收到了预期正文，随后因两个回调 ID 均为空而失败。修复后两条均通过。本地 Maven SDK 套件 455 项通过、10 项跳过，零失败或错误。Checkstyle 和打包通过。有一次启用 `CI=true` 的运行在一个既有测试中遇到本机 TLS 连接超时，最终本地复跑中该测试通过。无界面截图。

### 测试平台

| 系统 | 状态 |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | 本地已验证 |
| Windows | 待上游 CI |
| Linux | 待上游 CI |

### 环境（可选）

macOS arm64、OpenJDK 17.0.18、Maven 3.9.12。回归测试使用真实 SDK 会话及解码器，传输由测试夹具提供。

## 风险与范围

- 标准 CLI 流式事件只提供外层 UUID。同一条助手消息内的多个事件可以各有不同的 UUID。
- 本地验证采用 SDK 的测试传输。上游 Java 矩阵及守护进程集成工作流待运行。
- 调用方可通过现有回调字段读取收到的 UUID，无需更改配置或迁移。

修复 #17656。

issues.body:
## What happened?

After using CodeWhale in GNOME Terminal and exiting, the terminal profile keeps CodeWhale’s Nord light colors instead of restoring the previous profile colors. The background becomes `#ECEFF4` and the foreground `#2E3440`, while the palette remains Solarized. The terminal looks inconsistent outside CodeWhale.

Expected: CodeWhale restores the terminal’s previous background, foreground, and palette on exit, or leaves the existing profile colors untouched.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In GNOME Terminal, use a profile with the Solarized palette and a non-Nord background/foreground (for example Solarized Dark).
2. Configure CodeWhale with `theme = "custom:nord"` and a theme file containing `surface_bg: "#ECEFF4"` and `text_body: "#2E3440"`.
3. Run `codewhale` in that GNOME Terminal profile.
4. Exit CodeWhale normally.
5. Observe that the GNOME Terminal profile background/foreground remain the CodeWhale Nord colors instead of the previous colors.

## Codewhale version

`codewhale 0.10.2 (ff466b2ed0bf)`

## Where did it happen?

- TUI (terminal interface)

## Operating system

- Linux

## How did you get Codewhale?

- npm

## Provider and model

`deepseek / deepseek-flash`

## Terminal and shell

GNOME Terminal 3.44.0 using VTE 0.68.0; `TERM=xterm-256color`; `COLORTERM=truecolor`; `/bin/bash`.

## `codewhale doctor` (optional)

Not included; no relevant failure was observed.

## Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

- CodeWhale theme: `~/.codewhale/themes/nord.json` defines `surface_bg: "#ECEFF4"` and `text_body: "#2E3440"`.
- GNOME Terminal profile currently reports:
  - `use-theme-colors=false`
  - `background-color=rgb(236,239,244)` (`#ECEFF4`)
  - `foreground-color=rgb(46,52,64)` (`#2E3440`)
  - palette still Solarized (`#002B36`, `#FDF6E3`, etc.)
- CodeWhale’s binary contains OSC 11 handling (`crates/palette/src/osc11.rs`), and its logs show terminal probes for `\x1b]11;?` and `\x1b]10;?`.
- OpenCode 2.2.5 was also used under the same GNOME Terminal profile and has an identical Nord light background/foreground, so the exact writer is not fully isolated. Cross-reference: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/63977
- The request is that the application setting OSC 10/11 restores the previous terminal colors on exit, or preserves the existing profile colors. A regression test for terminal color restoration would help.
- Workaround: reset the GNOME Terminal profile colors with `gsettings`.
- I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate.

## Isolation steps not yet completed

1. Test whether `printf '\033]111\007'` and `printf '\033]110\007'` restore the dynamic background/foreground.
2. Reproduce with CodeWhale alone, then OpenCode alone, to identify which process writes the profile colors.

issues.title: Secret redaction runs on every model request and is slow on ordinary text

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: os:windows
labels.description: Windows-specific behaviour

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
Before each model request, `prepare_model_bound_request` (`crates/engine/src/client.rs`) passes every tool result in the conversation through `redact_model_bound_secrets` again, so the redaction cost is paid on every call and grows with the session. Redaction itself is slow on ordinary text: on a 2.8 MB mix of this repo's source, `Cargo.lock` and JSON files, one pass takes about 317 ms here (release build, Windows 11, i7-9700), roughly 9 MB/s.

I have a change ready in `crates/sanitize/src/redact.rs` that brings that pass to about 127 ms (about 2.5x) without changing any masking rule or any output. The old and new code give byte-identical results on every text file in the repo and on fuzzed input, and the existing sanitize tests pass.

Since this sits next to the credential handling that CONTRIBUTING asks to discuss first: would you take a PR for it?

issues.title: opencode-zen: free model rows are dead ends in Codewhale — the gateway checks an exact payload and TLS cipher list (429 FreeUsageLimitError)

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: os:linux

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
### Before you start
- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. Closest closed issue: #6705 (different problem — stale curated wire list).

### What happened?

`opencode-zen` lists Zen's free model ids in the model list — `codewhale model list --provider opencode-zen` returns 50 rows, 11 of them `*-free` (`hy4-flash-free`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, `beam-free`, …) — and `docs/PROVIDERS.md:998` documents the free rows as supported `/chat/completions` models. Every request to one of them fails with the provider's client-scoped refusal:

```
Rate limit exceeded: Free usage limit reached. Free models work in OpenCode (https://opencode.ai);
subscribe to OpenCode Go to keep going: https://opencode.ai/go; … automatic retry stopped
```

The same key and the same model id work in the official OpenCode CLI at the same minute, so this is not a credential or account problem: the entitlement is scoped to the first-party client. Codewhale already recognises the message (`opencode_go_hint`, `crates/engine/src/llm_client/mod.rs:469`), but the catalog surface still offers the rows, so the user selects a model and hits a dead end after the turn has started.

Expected: the free rows work from Codewhale the way they work in the OpenCode CLI with the same key.

### Request

Please make the free OpenCode Zen models work from Codewhale on the `opencode-zen` route.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the Zen route with a key via `OPENCODE_API_KEY` (documented fallback env var, `crates/config/assets/provider_descriptors.json` → `opencode-zen.env_vars`).
2. `codewhale exec --provider opencode-zen --model hy4-flash-free "hi"` (same in the TUI: `/provider` → OpenCode Zen, `/model` → a `*-free` row).
3. The turn ends with the quota-window error quoted above (classified `llm_quota_window`).

Plain curl, same key, outside Codewhale — the same refusal, so it is not a Codewhale request-shape bug:

```bash
curl -s https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"hy4-flash-free","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}],"max_tokens":8}'
# HTTP 429
# {"type":"error","error":{"type":"FreeUsageLimitError","message":"Free usage limit reached.
#  Free models work in OpenCode (https://opencode.ai); subscribe to OpenCode Go to keep going: https://opencode.ai/go"}}
```

Control — same key, same model id, same minute, official CLI:

```
opencode run -m opencode/hy4-flash-free "hi"    # normal answer; the session row records
                                               # {"id":"hy4-flash-free","providerID":"opencode"}
```

`GET https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models` with the same key returns 200 and lists the free ids, so the key is valid and the catalog is reachable.

### Verified 2026-11-18: what actually gates the free rows

#### How it was measured

The `opencode` provider's `baseURL` was pointed at a local HTTP capture server through `provider.opencode.options.baseURL`, and one `opencode run -m opencode/hy4-flash-free` was made through it. The captured request (all headers and the full body) was saved and then replayed byte-for-byte against the real endpoint with three clients, using the same key and no proxy:

| Client | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `bun` `fetch` | captured request, byte-for-byte | **HTTP 200**, streamed answer from `hy4-flash-free` |
| `curl` 8.23.0 with OpenSSL defaults | captured request, byte-for-byte | HTTP 429 `FreeUsageLimitError` |
| Node 26 `fetch` (OpenSSL) | captured request, byte-for-byte | HTTP 429 `FreeUsageLimitError` |
| `bun` `fetch` | same headers, simplified body (short system prompt) | HTTP 429 `FreeUsageLimitError` |

#### Correction to the first hypothesis

The first reading of that table was "a TLS fingerprint that only Bun can pass". That was wrong. A second round of measurements with a plain `curl` isolated three independent conditions, all reproducible with standard command-line flags:

1. **Payload.** The system prompt (61 901 characters) and the `tools` array (11 870 characters) must be the client's own, byte for byte. Only the user message (`messages[1].content`) and the model id may change. Truncating the system prompt, dropping `tools`, or keeping a single tool returns 429; changing only the user message returns 200.
2. **TLS cipher list.** The gateway checks both the order and the exact set of suites: TLS 1.3 in the order `AES128 → AES256 → CHACHA`, then this exact TLS 1.2 list:

   ```
   ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-SHA:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-SHA:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA:AES128-GCM-SHA256:AES256-GCM-SHA384:AES128-SHA:AES256-SHA
   ```

   With OpenSSL's default order the request returns 429 even with a valid payload; with the lists below it returns 200. The two curl flags are `--tls13-ciphers` and `--ciphers`. Set separately, either flag alone still returns 429 — both are required.
3. **Session id.** A real `x-opencode-session` id captured from the CLI (`ses_` + 24 characters) is required. A randomly generated id of the same shape returns 429.

Not required: the API key, an `Authorization` header, a proxy, `x-opencode-client`, `x-opencode-project`, `x-session-affinity`, `x-session-id`, or a particular header order. The free tier answers anonymous requests. `wget`, Python `ssl`, `openssl s_client` and 11 `curl-impersonate` profiles (Chrome 100-136, Safari, Firefox, Edge) all return 429 with an otherwise identical request, which is why the first hypothesis looked like a transport fingerprint; the cipher-list comparison shows the check is narrower than that.

#### Working example

The payload is captured once from a real CLI request via the `baseURL` override described above and saved as `free-payload.json` (about 104 KB on disk, about 32 KB gzipped). Replace the session id with a freshly captured one. Note that this route is `https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1/chat/completions`, different from the `/zen/v1` route used in the original reproduction above.

```bash
jq -c --arg q 'Say hi in one word' '.messages[1].content = $q' free-payload.json \
| curl -sN https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'User-Agent: opencode/latest/2.2.0/cli' \
    -H 'x-opencode-session: <real-session-id-from-cli>' \
    --tls13-ciphers 'TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256:TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256' \
    --ciphers 'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-SHA:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-SHA:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA:AES128-GCM-SHA256:AES256-GCM-SHA384:AES128-SHA:AES256-SHA' \
    --data-binary @- \
| sed -n 's/^data: //p' | grep -v '^\[DONE\]$' \
| jq -r 'select(.choices[0].delta.content != null) | .choices[0].delta.content' | tr -d '\n'
```

Observed on 2026-11-18 with curl 8.23.0, no key and no proxy: `hy4-flash-free` answered with a single-word greeting, `glm-5.3-flash-free` answered `pong`. A control request with the same payload and the same session id, but with neither cipher flag, returned HTTP 429 with `Retry-After: 78867` seconds. The 429 is the per-IP free-tier limit, so wait for that window instead of retrying in a loop; this is a rate limit, not a ban.

#### Caveats

The payload is tied to client version `2.2.0`: if the server-side prompt changes, a fresh capture is needed. The session id may expire and needs to be captured again. These measurements describe an intentional client gate; whether Codewhale should reproduce a first-party client is a maintainer decision.

#### Implication for the fix

Codewhale has to reproduce the exact payload, carry a valid session id, and present a matching cipher list. Changing the User-Agent or adding `x-opencode-*` headers alone is not enough.

### Codewhale version
`codewhale 0.10.3 (dev)` (built from a git checkout)

### Where did it happen?
TUI (terminal interface), CLI command (`codewhale exec`)

### Operating system
Linux

### How did you get Codewhale?
Built from a git checkout

### Provider and model
`opencode-zen` / `hy4-flash-free` (also `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, `glm-5.3-flash-free`, `beam-free`, … — 11 free rows in total)

### Possible cause (not verified)
`client_user_agent()` (`crates/engine/src/client.rs:331`) sends `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; codewhale/<version>; +https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale)` on every route, so the provider can distinguish Codewhale from the OpenCode app. I did not test whether a different User-Agent changes the result: that would mean impersonating the first-party client, and whether this project should do that is the maintainers' decision, not mine.

Update 2026-11-18: verified above — sending the first-party User-Agent alone does not change the result. The exact request body, a real session id and the matching TLS cipher list are all required. Whether Codewhale should impersonate the first-party client remains the maintainers' decision.

issues.title: Provider failures: the diagnostic log has no cause, and the error card drops the typed code

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: area:install
labels.description: Install, npm wrapper, release artifacts, Homebrew, winget, Docker, Nix

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
When a provider request dies after dispatch, the cause survives as English prose in two places (the session record and `codewhale receipts`) and **never reaches the diagnostic log**. The prose is also the only machine-readable form there is: no receipt field, no log field, no structured tag.

1. **The session record keeps prose, not a cause.** `turn_outcomes[].error` holds a sentence; the `Provider request receipt` carries `outcome: "open_failed" | "incomplete"` and `coverage: "missing"` but **no cause field**, so a consumer must regex English to tell a header stall from a mid-stream read drop from a proxy reset. `codewhale receipts` re-renders that same sentence, so it inherits the same limitation.
2. **The diagnostic log holds neither.** `~/.codewhale/logs/tui-*.log` records `engine turn completion settled status=Failed` and nothing about the reason: a grep for every provider failure family returns **zero** hits across 62 log files, while the settlement line appears 463 times.
3. **The rendered card drops the typed code.** The card is prose composed from the raw provider string; the typed `code` the envelope already carries (`llm_network_error`, `llm_timeout`, `llm_server_<status>`, …) never reaches the reader, and neither does `RequestTransmission` (`NotDispatched` / `Rejected` / `OutcomeUnknown`) — the one field that answers "did the provider see it".

None of this is a retry-policy complaint, and none of it says the cause is lost — `receipts` proves it is not. It is a "the evidence is not where a support reader looks, and is not structured where a tool could use it" complaint, and it is cheap to fix.

**Stated up front so nobody has to discover it:** `codewhale receipts <id> --format json` already returns the cause (verified live, quoted in § Defect 1). This issue argues the log and the card should carry it too, not that it is unavailable.

---

## What is measured, and how

Two corpora, both from one operator's machine:

- **Session records** — `~/.codewhale/sessions/*.json`, 610 files, 2026-09-15 → 2026-11-12. Each carries a `journal` (`message` + `system` entries) and `turn_outcomes[]`.
- **Diagnostic logs** — `~/.codewhale/logs/tui-*.log`, 62 files, 2026-11-05 → 2026-11-12, 8.4 MB. These files are appended to while a session runs, so the counts below are a snapshot; `Completed` drifts upward between reads while `Failed` stays at 15.

### Where the failures actually are

`turn_outcomes[]` with `status: "failed"` across the whole corpus: **180 records, every one carrying an `error` string**. Grouped by cause:

| Cause (verbatim leading text) | Count | First seen | Last seen |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Provider returned an empty response` | 44 | 2026-10-05 | 2026-10-26 |
| `Upstream idle timeout exceeded` | 26 | 2026-10-06 | 2026-11-02 |
| rate-limit / 429 family | 25 | 2026-10-18 | 2026-11-06 |
| `Provider stream connection dropped…` (transport read) | 12 | 2026-10-10 | 2026-11-12 |
| auth family | 10 | 2026-10-xx | 2026-11-09 |
| `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason` | 5 | 2026-10-23 | 2026-11-06 |
| `Network error: Request failed: error sending request` | 2 | 2026-11-12 | 2026-11-12 |
| `Provider usage settlement failed…` | 2 | 2026-11-11 | 2026-11-11 |
| `Request timed out after 0ns` | 1 | 2026-11-12 | 2026-11-12 |
| other (tool, policy, quota, malformed provider text) | remainder | | |

### What survives into the log

Zero. Across all 62 files:

```
$ grep -c "Provider stream connection dropped" ~/.codewhale/logs/*.log   → 0 in every file
$ grep -c "error decoding response body"        ~/.codewhale/logs/*.log   → 0
$ grep -c "error sending request"               ~/.codewhale/logs/*.log   → 0
$ grep -c "did not receive response headers"    ~/.codewhale/logs/*.log   → 0
$ grep -c "Upstream idle timeout"               ~/.codewhale/logs/*.log   → 0
```

What the log *does* contain is the bare settlement line — `engine turn completion settled status=Failed` — 15 times in the same window:

```
394  engine turn completion settled status=Completed
 54  engine turn completion settled status=Interrupted
 15  engine turn completion settled status=Failed
463  total
```

Attributing each `Failed` to the nearest preceding log line gives: 4 × usage-receipt retention, 3 × snapshot prune, 4 × tool failures, 1 × proxy refusal, 1 × turn stall, 1 × session retention, 1 × nothing. The provider failures above are not among them — they did not write a line at all.

### What survives into the session record

Free text only. For a `Provider request receipt` with `outcome: "open_failed"` or `"incomplete"`, the full key set is:

```
source_accounting, accounting_error, session_id, turn_id, request_index, request_id,
source_id, route, primary, transmission, coverage, physical_requests,
physical_requests_dropped, prefix_check, reused_preparation, wire_observations,
wire_observations_dropped, usage, usage_reported, outcome, transport_retries,
elapsed_ms, cache_attribution
```

There is no `error`, `cause` or `failure_class` field. `accounting_error` exists but is `null` for these. So the only machine-readable statement about a failed request is `outcome` (3 values) and `coverage` (`missing`); the cause lives exclusively in `turn_outcomes[].error` as English prose — and that prose differs by code path, so a consumer has to string-match on sentences that are periodically reworded (see § "Why the prose is not a stable key").

---

## Defect 1 — the diagnostic log has no cause for a failed turn

**Claim, verified against `28b755f6e`:** the failure branches that build the user-visible card have no `tracing` call at `warn`/`error` level, and the one line that does settle a turn carries the status but not the cause.

Where the two cards are actually built:

- **Stream-open failures** — `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop/model_step.rs:424` calls `initial_stream_error_user_message(...)`, then the `Err` arm runs to `model_step.rs:~486-536` and returns `TurnOutcomeStatus::Failed`. That file has exactly two `tracing` calls: `:577` `tracing::debug!` (target `provider_response_diagnostics`) and `:637` `tracing::warn!` (child usage settlement). Neither carries the error.
- **Transport-read failures** (`Provider stream connection dropped…`) — built at `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs:5073` via `stream_read_error_user_message(&message, any_content_received)`, in the same shape, also with no `tracing` call.

The umbrella settlement line does exist — `crates/engine/src/core/engine.rs:7961-7968`:

```rust
tracing::info!(
    target: "engine.turn",
    status = ?status,
    event_sent = turn_complete_event_sent,
    "engine turn completion settled"
);
```

(Quoted verbatim from `engine.rs:7961-7968`. The `error` value exists in scope two lines above and is **not** included.)

`info` with `status` — and **no error**, **no route**, **no provider**, **no transmission state**. So the log says a turn failed and cannot say why, which is exactly the question asked after a crash.

**The `debug` line does not rescue this, and that is measured, not assumed.** `crates/runtime/src/runtime_log.rs:137-139` builds the file-subscriber filter as `EnvFilter::try_from_default_env().unwrap_or("info")` — so `debug` is dropped by default. In 62 log files / 8.4 MB:

```
grep -c "parent model response settled"  → 0
 grep -c "provider_response_diagnostics"  → 0
 grep -c "engine turn completion settled" → 463
```

That is: the `info` settlement line reaches the file; every `debug` diagnostic does not. Raising `CODEWHALE_LOG_LEVEL`/`RUST_LOG` to `debug` would surface `provider_response_diagnostics` — but it still would not carry the error text, and the default install never sees it.

**What already works, and must be stated or this issue is wrong.** `codewhale receipts <id> --format json` **does** return the cause, because `session_receipt` reads `turn_outcomes[].error` and renders it as a `TurnFailed` action (`crates/engine/src/receipts.rs:142-172`, `:1887-1902`, with `bounded(&redact(...))` for secret hygiene). Verified live against a real session:

```
$ codewhale receipts <session> --format json | jq '.actions[] | select(.tool=="turn" and .status=="failed") | .error'
"Network error: Request failed: error sending request"
"Provider stream connection dropped while reading the response body. …"
```

So the gap is narrower than "the cause is lost", and the honest statement is: **the cause survives in the session record and (truncated) in `receipts`, and never reaches `tui-*.log`.** A reader who knows to run `receipts` gets the prose; a reader tailing the log — or reading a log shipped by someone else, which is the usual support case — gets `status=Failed` and nothing else.

`receipts` also bounds the sentence: `MAX_ERROR_CHARS = 160` (`crates/engine/src/receipts.rs:50`), and the live output shows the cut — 52 chars for the short one, exactly 160 plus an ellipsis for the long one:

```
52   Network error: Request failed: error sending request
160  Provider stream connection dropped while reading the response body. Some output had already
     streamed, so Codewhale is surfacing the warning instead of replayin…
```

The truncated tail is where the distinguishing detail lives (`Details: Stream read error: error decoding response body`). So `receipts` gives a *recognisable* cause, not a complete or structured one — a third reason the structured field belongs in the envelope and the log.

**Why the log gap still matters.** `receipts` prints the same free-text `turn_outcomes[].error` sentence, so it inherits the instability described in § "Why the prose is not a stable key" — it can say what the sentence says and nothing structured. It also cannot be grepped across a fleet of sessions without re-implementing the sentence matching. And `not_recorded` / `omitted_actions` mean `receipts` may itself be bounded away from the failure.

**Why there is still no cheap workaround inside the log.** `codewhale_runtime::logging::warn` is stderr-only and gated on `CODEWHALE_LOG_LEVEL` (`crates/runtime/src/logging.rs:106-113`); it never reaches `tui-*.log`. Only `tracing::*` at `info`+ does. Several sibling diagnostics in the same file use `logging::warn` (`turn_loop.rs:5018, 5045, 5097`), so setting `CODEWHALE_LOG_LEVEL=debug` still leaves nothing durable.

**Suggested direction.** One `tracing::warn!` (or `error!` when the turn ends) at each failure-card site, carrying the fields the envelope and receipt already have: `code`, `category`, `transmission`, `provider`, `model`, and `http_status` when present. No new event, no new persistence, no behaviour change — the neighbouring `tracing::error!(%error, "provider usage has no durable acknowledgement")` at `turn_loop.rs:4858` is the shape to copy.

---

## Defect 2 — the card drops the typed cause and the transmission state

`crates/engine/src/llm_error_envelope.rs:21-24` sets `envelope.message = display_message`, overwriting whatever the typed mapping produced. The typed `code` survives on the event (`ErrorEnvelope::code`), and `apply_engine_error_to_app` stores only `message` and `severity` into the transcript cell (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/apply.rs:232`). So the reader sees prose and the machinery keeps the code — the two never meet.

Six distinct failures, as the operator sees them:

| Layer | What the operator reads | Says the layer? | Says "provider saw it"? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-dispatch (DNS/TCP/TLS/proxy) | `Connection failed before request dispatch: …` | yes | yes, implicitly |
| Post-dispatch, transport read | `Provider stream connection dropped while reading the response body. … Details: Stream read error: error decoding response body` | no | no |
| Post-dispatch, request send | `Network error: Request failed: error sending request` | no | no |
| Header stall | `SSE stream request did not receive response headers after Ns; request outcome unknown` | partially | says "unknown" |
| Local idle/timeout ceiling | `SSE stream idle timeout after Ns — no data received (bytes_received=…)` | yes, it's ours | n/a |
| Upstream status | `Server error (503): <provider text>` | yes | yes |

The vocabulary to fix this already exists and is 15 codes wide:

```
llm_quota_window, llm_rate_limited, llm_quota_exhausted, llm_server_<status>,
llm_network_error, llm_connect_before_dispatch, llm_timeout, llm_auth_error,
llm_authorization_error, llm_invalid_request, llm_model_error, llm_content_policy,
llm_context_length, llm_parse_error, llm_other
```

and `RequestTransmission { NotDispatched, Rejected, OutcomeUnknown }` at `crates/engine/src/llm_client/mod.rs:370-374`.

**Suggested direction (composition only):** render a short tag from `code` and the transmission state beside the message — e.g. `provider stream read failed · outcome unknown · resend to continue`. Keep `message` as the detail line. No new types.

---

## Why the prose is not a stable key

The failure sentences are reworded often enough that no consumer can depend on them, which is the concrete argument for Defect 1's structured field:

| Phrase | Present at `28b755f6e`? | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Provider returned an empty response` | **no** (only in a test fixture) | 44 historical failures carried it |
| `Upstream idle timeout exceeded` | **no** (only in a taxonomy test) | 26 historical failures carried it |
| `SSE stream request failed after HTTP/1.1 fallback` | **no** | the fallback error now goes through `h1_fallback_error` (`stream_entry.rs:215-238`) |
| `Request timed out after 0ns` | replaced | now `… (provider request exceeded its transport budget; exact duration not recorded)` — `da201bac8` |
| `Provider stream connection dropped` | yes | `streaming.rs:390-411` |
| `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason` | yes | `chat.rs:1732` |

Both rewordings are good on their own — `da201bac8` stopped fabricating `0ns`, and `21c8f86c4` named determinate rejections instead of calling them `internal`. Together they mean the sentence text is not an API, while nothing else carries the same fact.

---

## Corrections to my own earlier counts (so a reader can reproduce)

My first pass over `sessions/*.json` counted **substrings**, which over-counted badly: agent transcripts quoting the failure text, earlier analysis sessions quoting source code, and one conversation describing the same error three times all inflated the numbers. Recounting only `turn_outcomes[].error` — a field the engine writes, never a transcript — gives the 180-record table above. Raw substring counts (e.g. 480 × `error sending request`) are **not** occurrence counts of the fault and should not be read as such.

The distinction matters for one claim I am *not* making: I cannot show that every one of these 180 was recoverable by a single follow-up message. I can show the weaker, verifiable thing: every failure class above except rate-limit and auth was followed in the same session by further successful turns, so the session's work continued.

---

## How to reproduce the counts

A maintainer cannot run my classifier, so here is the exact method. It reads fields the engine writes, never transcript text.

```sh
# Count of failed turns across every saved session.
# -s (slurp) is required: without it jq drops files mid-stream on this corpus.
jq -rs '[.[] | .turn_outcomes[]? | select(.status=="failed")] | length' \
  ~/.codewhale/sessions/*.json          # → 180

# The same records, one cause sentence per line, grouped by leading text:
jq -rs '.[] | .turn_outcomes[]? | select(.status=="failed") | .error' \
  ~/.codewhale/sessions/*.json \
| sed -E 's/^(.{0,40}).*/\1/' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
```

Two things a reader must know to reproduce these numbers honestly:

- **`-s` matters.** Without slurp, the same one-liner printed 42, 192 and 180 on three consecutive runs over an unchanged directory. The corpus contains multi-megabyte session files, and non-slurped `jq` appears to stop early on this input set. Use `-s`, and expect the total to drift upward while the session doing the counting is itself being saved into the same directory.
- **No deduplication.** A turn that failed twice counts twice. That is intentional: the claim is about how often a reader is left without a cause, not how many distinct faults exist.

Field path: `turn_outcomes[].error` on the session document root, written by `SavedTurnOutcome` (`crates/engine/src/session_manager.rs:2092`).

**The "other 53" bucket is not a junk drawer, and deliberately not expanded.** It decomposes into tool failures, provider plan-quota exhaustion, malformed provider text (`ERROR` alone), a wall-clock ceiling, and a handful of one-off rejections. None of those are transport failures, and none would change the two defects above; expanding them would pad the table without adding an argument.

**What the numbers do not prove.** They are one operator's sessions, from one provider, on one machine, over 59 days. They do **not** establish a rate, a frequency per turn, or that a typical user sees this. They establish only that the failures are common enough in one real corpus to justify a diagnostic line — which is the whole claim.

---

## What this issue does not ask for

- No change to retry policy, defaults, or `[retry]`/`[stream]` semantics.
- No replay of anything after dispatch. The unknown-outcome stop (`92b4900d1`) stays as is.
- No new persistence format — the fields proposed for the log already exist on the envelope and the receipt.

---

## Deferred: the replay knob

The obvious next ask — "give me an opt-in knob that replays these" — was pulled from this draft because its central premise does not survive review:

> **The premise, and why it is wrong.** A header stall or a post-dispatch `NetworkError` means *the client saw no bytes*. It does **not** mean the provider produced no completion. The provider may have generated and billed the entire answer while the client was gone. That is precisely the case `92b4900d1` exists for (`docs/CONFIGURATION.md:2914-2917`).

Two smaller blockers found while checking it, worth recording here so they are not rediscovered:

- `ErrorEnvelope::recoverable` is not a "resend hint". It drives offline-mode / turn-liveness (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/apply.rs:177-198`) and headless exit status (`exec_error_event_is_fatal` = `!recoverable`, `crates/engine/src/exec_events.rs:206-214`). Repurposing it would change `exec` exit codes and CI behaviour.
- `[retry]` merges **whole-table** per profile (`crates/runtime/src/config.rs:10181`: `retry: override_cfg.retry.or(base.retry)`), unlike `[stream]`'s per-key merge (`:10187`). Any new `[profiles.x.retry]` opt-in would silently discard the base `max_retries`. Also, `crates/config/src/settings_schema.rs` defines **no** `retry.*` keys at all, so `/config` and `config set` cannot reach a new key without schema work.

If it is ever proposed, the honest framing is "replay when the client received no bytes, accepting that the provider may already have billed a completion", with per-attempt cost accounting — not "replay when the provider cannot have answered", which is not knowable.

---

## Related

- `92b4900d1` (2026-11-02) — "stop replaying inference with unknown outcomes". The policy this issue leaves alone.
- #6184 (**open**) — "Engine silently freezes mid-run: user messages are persisted but never answered; no error, no log line, no crash entry". Closest open neighbour; Defect 1 may belong with it.
- #6796 (closed) — "Retry attempts are invisible". Addressed the *retry* banner; the *failure* record is still missing.
- #6843 (closed 2026-10-08) — determinate rejections labelled `internal`. Why prose can be a poor key, and proof the wording moves.
- #6699 (closed) — no retry when the SSE request never received headers.
- #7045 (closed) — SSE retries capped by the stream-open window; HTTP/1.1 fallback returned raw HTTP errors.
- #5769 (closed) — network errors stopping the engine; closed as working-as-intended, which is why this issue is scoped to diagnostics rather than recovery.

## Environment notes (anonymised)

- The local proxy refuses connections on a six-hour cadence (01:54, 07:54, 13:54, 19:54 local), self-heals within ~2 s, 17 times in the 7-day log window: `net: local proxy refused connections; requests go direct until it returns`.
- That window is the environment this issue is written from: a flaky edge, a third-party OpenAI-compatible provider, a model that streams reasoning. Nothing in the report depends on the provider's identity.
- One `Provider plan quota exhausted` cluster (2026-11-09) is the provider's own weekly limit and is not a defect.

issues.title: TUI: full-screen erase + repaint on every window focus flashes on terminals without DEC 2026 (gnome-terminal/VTE)

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: os:linux
labels.description: Linux-specific behaviour

issues.body:
## Summary

On every window focus gain (selecting the terminal window), the TUI erases the entire screen (`CSI 2J`) and repaints it from scratch, wrapped in DEC 2026 synchronized-update markers. On terminals that do not implement DEC 2026 (gnome-terminal / VTE < 0.76), the erase lands before the repaint, producing a visible flash/glitch on every focus. The repaint is byte-identical each time — nothing on screen changed.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run codewhale (v0.10.2) in gnome-terminal (VTE 0.68) with any theme whose background differs from the terminal's default background (e.g. a light custom theme over a dark terminal background).
2. Switch away from the window and back (focus out, focus in).
3. Observe: a brief flash of the terminal's default background over the app surface on every focus-in.

## Expected vs actual

- Expected: focusing the window causes no visible redraw.
- Actual: full-screen erase + repaint on every FocusIn; visible flicker when the terminal ignores DEC 2026.

## Evidence

Captured over a pty with terminal emulation (xterm DA answers, focus events `CSI I` / `CSI O` sent explicitly). The FocusIn frame begins:

```
ESC[<1u ESC[>1u ESC[?1007l ESC[?1000h ESC[?1002h ESC[?1003h ESC[?1015h ESC[?1006h ESC[?2004h ESC[?1004h ESC[?2026h ESC[?25l ESC[r ESC[?6l ESC[H ESC[2J ESC[36;46H ESC[1;1H ...
```

i.e. mode re-setup (mouse tracking, bracketed paste, focus reporting), `?2026h` (begin synchronized update), cursor home, `2J` erase, then a full repaint, ending with `?2026l`.

Measurements (120x40 cells):

- Idle output: 0 bytes (diff-based rendering — nothing redraws while idle).
- Each FocusIn: ~6.7 KB full repaint; two consecutive FocusIn frames are **byte-identical** (redundant).
- FocusOut: 61 bytes.
- `synchronized_output = "off"` in settings removes the 2026 markers but keeps the identical erase + repaint.
- The app never issues a `DECRQM` (`CSI ?2026$p`) capability query — it emits `?2026h/l` unconditionally.

## Root cause

The focus handler unconditionally erases and fully repaints on FocusIn and relies on DEC 2026 to make it atomic. VTE ignores DEC 2026 until 0.76 (user's terminal: gnome-terminal 3.44.0 / libvte 0.68.0, Ubuntu). The erase therefore renders immediately with the terminal's default background, followed by the streamed repaint — visible as a flash. With a light theme over a dark terminal background the flash is very prominent.

## Suggested fixes

1. Detect DEC 2026 support via `DECRQM` before relying on it, and on non-supporting terminals either skip the erase or use a damage-only redraw.
2. Skip the erase entirely when nothing changed — the FocusIn repaint is redundant; diff-based rendering already achieves 0-byte idle.
3. If mode re-setup on focus is intentional (terminals may reset modes), keep it but drop `2J` and repaint only changed cells.

## Environment

- codewhale v0.10.2 (ff466b2ed0bf)
- gnome-terminal 3.44.0, libvte-2.91-0 0.68.0 (Ubuntu)
- Terminal default background: rgb(23,20,33); custom light theme background: #ECEFF4

Possibly related: #6728 (idle CPU regression).
