issues.body:
## Summary

A local bookkeeping admission failure ends the turn **before the provider request is sent**, with the model never called:

```
Turn failed: provider source admission failed: usage publication has no reserved native journal slot
```

This contradicts the 0.10.3 changelog entry at `CHANGELOG.md:505`: *"Turns no longer fail on a cost bookkeeping error... The turn now continues, the receipt keeps the accounting error, and the status line says the cost is uncertain."*

That promise was implemented for the **settlement** path only. The **admission** path, which runs earlier, was never made non-fatal — and it is still fatal on `upstream/main`.

## Observed

Four admission failures between 13 and 15 November 2026, in three different sessions, on `0.10.3 (dev)` built from `5af8a9a24`:

| When (UTC) | Session |
| --- | --- |
| 2026-11-13T20:56:01 | `f80a14df…` |
| 2026-11-15T02:18:35 | `c6d6e81d…` |
| 2026-11-15T03:40:00 | `da9cbd26…` |
| 2026-11-15T15:04:01 | `c6d6e81d…` |

Recorded in `turn_outcomes[].error` with `status: "failed"`.

The turn is what is lost, not the prompt: the prompt stays in history and the next message continues from it. Verified in the same session — the failed turn's prompt is retained and answered by the following turn. What the operator pays is a dead round trip, not retyping.

## Root cause: the usage journal's capacity path contradicts itself

This is not an owner-mismatch race. The immediate trigger is visible in the log, and it lines up with all four failures:

```
2026-11-15T15:03:52.792468Z  WARN codewhale_engine::cost_status:
    native usage journal is at capacity; this request continues without a retained receipt
2026-11-15T15:03:52.793015Z  WARN codewhale_engine::tools::subagent::engine:
    child refusal receipt was not admitted
    error=usage publication has no reserved native journal slot
2026-11-15T15:04:01.367856Z  INFO engine.turn: engine turn completion settled status=Failed
```

Seven capacity warnings in the log window; every admission failure follows one within seconds:

| Capacity warning (UTC) | Turn failed (UTC) | Gap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-11-13T20:56:01.736 | 2026-11-13T20:56:01.912 | 0.18 s |
| 2026-11-15T02:18:33.174 | 2026-11-15T02:18:35.642 | 2.5 s |
| 2026-11-15T03:40:00.255 | 2026-11-15T03:40:00.419 | 0.16 s |
| 2026-11-15T15:03:52.792 | 2026-11-15T15:04:01.367 | 8.6 s |

The code path, in `crates/engine/src/cost_status.rs`:

1. `prepare_observed_kind` calls `reserve_retention_slot()` before building the record.
2. `reserve_retention_slot` checks the per-owner cap (`MAX_RUNTIME_USAGE_RECORDS_PER_OWNER = 256`). At capacity it logs *"this request continues without a retained receipt"* and returns `Ok(())` — **before** `slot.active.store(true)` and **before** inserting the slot into `native_slots`.
3. `prepare_observed_kind` continues, builds the record with that same (still inactive) slot, and calls `retain_runtime_usage_record(owner, &record)?`.
4. `retain_runtime_usage_record` checks `proof.slot.active` — false — and returns `WouldBlock` with *"usage publication has no reserved native journal slot"*.
5. That error propagates out of `admit_dispatch`, and the turn fails.

So the capacity handler says "continue without a receipt" and the very next call makes it fatal. The two halves of the same function disagree.

## Why it is a defect and not a policy

- **Nothing was dispatched.** Unlike a stream drop or a timeout there is no unknown provider outcome — the request never left. Nothing was billed, nothing was generated, no duplicate risk exists.
- **It is local.** The provider, the network and the model are irrelevant; a journal slot is Codewhale's own bookkeeping.
- **The behaviour is documented as fixed for this class.** The settlement branch honours that (`turn_loop.rs`: `tracing::warn!(%error, "provider usage settlement failed; the turn continues")`). The admission branch does not. Note the admission path was added in `ccc087723` (2026-11-02) and the later `bc3ad117e` (2026-11-07) fixed only the settlement path; it never touched `model_step.rs`.

## Still present upstream

Checked against `upstream/main` at `b107c4996`, 350 commits ahead of the build that produced these failures:

- `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop/model_step.rs` still returns `TurnOutcomeStatus::Failed` with `provider source admission failed`.
- `crates/engine/src/cost_status.rs` still has the `WouldBlock` "no reserved native journal slot".
- The three commits that touched `model_step.rs` since the build (Auto-Review intent, RunOrigin minting, DeepSeek parity) do not change this block.

Updating the binary does not fix this.

## Suggested direction

Make the capacity path and the retention call agree. Two options, either is small:

1. **Skip the retain when reservation declined.** Have `reserve_retention_slot` report that it declined (at capacity), and have `prepare_observed_kind` skip `retain_runtime_usage_record` for that record — the handler already decided the request should continue without a receipt.
2. **Make admission non-fatal, like settlement.** Log the admission failure with its code and let the request proceed with cost unknown. The turn is what produces the usage the journal is trying to record; failing it to protect the journal is backwards.

Option 1 is narrower and preserves the existing retention semantics. Independently of either, the capacity branch is worth a second look: 256 records per owner is reachable in a long session, and the branch currently drops retention silently for every request past the cap even when it does not fail the turn.

The `AlreadyExists` guard ("usage source was already admitted") may deserve a fatal path — that one signals a real double-admission bug — but it should be a distinct variant, not shared with a capacity or retention-slot condition.

**Scope note: this block has three fatal returns, not one.** The same pre-dispatch section also fails the turn on a `NativeUsageOrigin::runtime` construction error ("provider accounting admission failed") and on `bind_dispatch`. All three are local bookkeeping that runs before dispatch, so a fix should decide the class rather than patch the one message string this report happens to contain.

## Related

- #7328 — the logging/card defect for provider failures (commented there about this one).
- `bc3ad117e` — made the settlement path non-fatal; this issue asks for the same on admission, or for the capacity path to stop contradicting itself.
- `ccc087723` — added the admission path.
- `CHANGELOG.md:505-509` — the 0.10.3 changelog entry this contradicts. (0.10.3 is not tagged; the latest release is v0.10.2.)

issues.title: Named-turn undo reads the whole turn store twice before forking

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
## Summary

`/undo` with a `turn_id` resolves the named anchor by loading every turn and every item of the thread, then calls the generic fork preparation, which loads the same turns and items a second time. A fork of a 200-turn thread opens 400 turn files where the depth-based fork opens 200.

## Environment

Codewhale 0.10.2 at commit 6391f4f307040851fca29d679d3c05a985828a54, local runtime store, 200-turn conversation (400 stored items).

## Expected behavior

The named-turn path already has the turns and items in memory when it resolves the anchor; the fork preparation should reuse them instead of re-reading the store. One whole-store pass per fork.

## Actual behavior

Both operations ran against the same 200-turn thread at the same commit. File opens were counted per phase.

| operation | turn-file opens | item-file opens | wall time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| depth-based fork (drops 100 tail turns) | 200 | 598 | 379 ms |
| named-turn undo (drops turn 100 and later) | 400 | 1,000 | 601 ms |

The named path reads twice as many turn records and about 1.7x as many item records for the same thread.

## Root cause

`fork_dropping_user_turn_in_sessions_dir` first calls `list_turns_for_thread` and `prepared_items_for_turns` to resolve the turn id through `fork_cut_for_user_turn`, then calls `prepare_fork_at_user_message_in_sessions_dir`, which calls `list_turns_for_thread` and `prepared_items_for_turns` again (crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:13037-13051 and :13120-13160).

## Suggested fix

Pass the already loaded `turns` and `items_by_turn` (or the resolved cut index) into a preparation variant, for example `prepare_fork_at_cutoff_in_sessions_dir`, so the preparation does not re-read the store. The public depth and named-turn paths can then share one preparation that takes the loaded prefix.

## Impact

Every named-turn undo pays two full store passes instead of one. On stores with tens of thousands of items — the case the one-pass item helpers were introduced for — that is seconds of avoidable reads per undo, and it also extends how long the global admission guard is held.

issues.title: bug: a session whose late-usage ledger hits 1 MiB can no longer be saved at all — compaction fails and the transcript stops persisting

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:install
labels.description: Install, npm wrapper, release artifacts, Homebrew, winget, Docker, Nix

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
## Summary

Once a session's late-usage ledger reaches its 1 MiB bound, **every save of that session fails** — checkpoint, snapshot and completed-commit alike. Compaction dies with `Making room failed: late usage ledger exceeds its size bound`, and the conversation stops being persisted while it keeps running in memory.

A bookkeeping sidecar should not be able to stop the transcript from being saved.

## Provenance — not a stale binary, not two processes

Checked before filing, because the first hypothesis was "an old binary kept running after an update":

- Installed binary: `codewhale 0.10.3 (dev)`, commit `5af8a9a24`, built **2026-11-11 00:08 UTC**.
- The affected process started **2026-11-13T23:49:19Z** — two days *after* the build. It is the new binary.
- One `codewhale` file on disk: `/home/f2/.cargo/bin/codewhale` is the only hit; `/usr/local/bin`, `/usr/bin` and `~/.local/bin` have none.
- The ledger file itself was last written `2026-11-14T23:44:57Z`, i.e. by this process, not carried over from an older build.

So the failure is produced by the current binary and the current code, not by a leftover process.

## Observed

Session `c6d6e81d`, workspace `~/Documents/Shared/Research`, 1488 messages. The ledger `.late-usage/c6d6e81d….json`:

```
records      941
size         1,048,490 bytes
bound        1,048,576 bytes (1 MiB)
headroom     86 bytes
avg record   ~1,114 bytes
overflowed   true
unresolved   0
```

86 bytes of headroom, and one new record is ~1,114 bytes — so **every** further append fails, permanently. There is no pruning of settled records anywhere in the code to make room.

The log, 16 November:

```
14:51:25  WARN compaction: context compaction failed             auto=false
14:51:25  WARN persistence: persistence write failed             what=completed-commit:c6d6e81d…
14:51:34  WARN compaction: context compaction failed             auto=false
14:51:34  WARN persistence: persistence write failed             what=completed-commit:c6d6e81d…
14:56:02  WARN persistence: persistence write failed             what=checkpoint:c6d6e81d…
… 184 checkpoint failures carrying the same error, through 15:11 …
15:11:06  WARN persistence: persistence write failed             what=checkpoint:c6d6e81d…
```

Counts from that one log file, so a reader can reproduce:

```
184  persistence write failed what=checkpoint:c6d6e81d…   error=late usage ledger exceeds its size bound
  2  context compaction failed                            error=late usage ledger exceeds its size bound
```

The session document was last written at **14:50:16Z**; at the time of filing the clock was **15:11Z** — 21 minutes of turns running in memory only. A crash or a close loses that work.

One caveat, stated so the numbers are not over-read: three earlier checkpoint failures on **14 November** carry `error_kind=StorageFull` — a full disk, a different cause. Those are excluded from the counts above; every 16 November failure carries the ledger message.

The two compaction failures are manual (`auto=false`). The save failures are not: they are on the ordinary checkpoint path, so **the session is not being persisted at all** — not just compaction.

The only thing that clears the ledger is deleting the session (the `codewhale-session-deleted-v1` tombstone). While the session lives, the file can only grow.

## Root cause — three independent mistakes line up

**1. A hard 1 MiB cap with no eviction.** `MAX_LATE_USAGE_LEDGER_BYTES = 1024 * 1024` (`crates/engine/src/session_manager.rs`), and `write_late_usage_ledger` rejects anything larger with `InvalidData: late usage ledger exceeds its size bound`. Nothing prunes settled records; the file only grows.

**2. The cap is fatal to the session save.** `flush_pending_usage_admitted(&id)?` is called with `?` on all three write paths — checkpoint, snapshot and completed-commit. So a ledger write failure aborts the save of the conversation itself.

**3. The degradation path is already dead in this state.** `write_late_usage_candidate` has a fallback that writes a smaller "overflowed" ledger — but only `if !original.overflowed`. This ledger already has `overflowed: true`, so the fallback never runs and the error propagates unconditionally.

The three together produce a hard lock: the ledger cannot grow, cannot shrink, cannot be marked overflowed again, and the save cannot proceed.

## Why this is not #6842 or #7348

- **#6842** owns the *growth* — bounding the replay index while preserving spend deduplication (and it explicitly warns that truncating the fingerprint set can double-count money). It does not mention the 1 MiB bound, the size-bound message, or that hitting it blocks persistence; checked the body, no occurrences. This issue is about the *coupling*, not the growth.
- **#7348** owns the sibling defect one layer up: the in-memory journal cap (256 records) failing the *turn* before dispatch. This one is the on-disk ledger failing the *save*. Different cap, different file, different consequence.

The shared principle is the one the 0.10.3 changelog already states for settlement — "Turns no longer fail on a cost bookkeeping error" — and that `bc3ad117e` implemented for the settlement path. Persistence never got the same treatment.

## Confirmed in current upstream

Checked against `upstream/main` at `b107c4996` (2026-11-15), **350 commits ahead** of the build that produced this:

- `MAX_LATE_USAGE_LEDGER_BYTES = 1024 * 1024` — unchanged.
- `flush_pending_usage_admitted(&id)?` — still fatal, at all three save paths.
- `write_late_usage_candidate` — same `if !original.overflowed` guard.
- No `records.retain` / `records.clear` / `records.pop` anywhere in the ledger code — no eviction added.

Updating the binary does not fix this.

## Suggested fix

Make the ledger write non-fatal for persistence, and give the ledger a way out of the corner:

1. **Do not fail the save on a ledger error.** Log it with its code, write the conversation, and let the receipt say cost is unknown. Same shape as the settlement path already uses (`tracing::warn!(%error, "provider usage settlement failed; the turn continues")`). A local accounting sidecar must not block transcript persistence.
2. **Make the degradation path reachable.** The `overflowed` fallback only fires once; after that the ledger is stuck. Either allow rewriting a marked-empty ledger when the bound is hit, or drop settled records that are provably no longer replayable — the same trade-off #6842 is deciding, which is why this can be a small, safe slice rather than a redesign.
3. **Surface it once, not every save.** 184 identical checkpoint warnings in twenty minutes is noise; one operator-visible notice naming the ledger and the remedy is enough.

## Workaround for an affected session

The ledger is a per-session sidecar, `~/.codewhale/sessions/.late-usage/<session_id>.json`. Moving it aside (`mv … .bak`) makes the next save succeed again. That file is the spend-dedupe record, so the cost of the workaround is that a replayed usage receipt for this session can be counted twice — which is exactly the risk #6842 is deciding about. It is a stopgap for a stuck session, not a fix.

## Related

- #6842 — owns bounding the usage replay index without losing spend deduplication. This issue is the failure-mode half.
- #7348 — the same "bookkeeping must not block the product" principle, at the turn-dispatch layer.
- `bc3ad117e` — made usage-settlement failure non-fatal for the turn; persistence still lacks the equivalent.
- `CHANGELOG.md` 0.10.3 — "Turns no longer fail on a cost bookkeeping error".

issues.title: bug: the TUI freezes for the whole next turn when a save-snapshot is requested as a new turn starts

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: area:install
labels.description: Install, npm wrapper, release artifacts, Homebrew, winget, Docker, Nix

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
## Summary

When a turn ends and a new turn starts within milliseconds, the TUI freezes for the **entire duration of the new turn** — keystrokes are ignored, nothing renders, and the only way out is to close the terminal. In the session below the freeze lasted **209 seconds**, and the same session recorded it twice more at 541 s and 848 s.

The visible message afterwards is:

```
Session <id> could not be saved (resource busy). Recent work may not be saved.
```

That message is a symptom, not the cause: `resource busy` is the fallback error string the UI uses when its session snapshot does not arrive.

## Mechanism

1. A turn settles. The TUI's turn-complete handler requests a snapshot from the engine (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs`, `engine_handle.get_session_snapshot().await`). The await is **unbounded** — no `tokio::time::timeout`.
2. The engine serves `Op::GetSessionSnapshot` only from its run loop between turns. `handle_send_message` awaits the whole turn inline, and nothing inside the turn loop drains `rx_op`. So while a turn runs, the snapshot request sits in the 32-slot op channel.
3. If the next turn starts before the snapshot is served — which happens when the message is already queued — the UI blocks until that turn finishes.

The UI event loop is a single async loop: while it awaits the snapshot it does not poll the terminal, so input and rendering stop. That is the freeze.

The codebase already knows this hazard. `get_subagent_settlement` on the same handle carries the warning:

```rust
/// Query after the active turn settles, without competing with events.
/// The caller must keep draining events and bound this future: an active
/// turn can be awaiting provider/tool work or a full event channel.
```

`get_session_snapshot` has no such note, and the turn-complete call site does not bound it. The startup path uses the same method **with** a timeout (`LAUNCH_SESSION_SYNC_WAIT = 2s`, `await_engine_session_sync`), so the bound exists in the codebase — it is simply missing here.

## Natural control experiment

One session (`2a4365be`, workspace `~/`, 16 November) produced four identical `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason` failures within 15 minutes. Only one froze:

| Failure | Next turn started | Warning | Freeze |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 18:54:29 | **+0.02 s** | 18:57:59 | **209 s** |
| 18:57:59 | +375 s | same instant | 0 s |
| 19:06:33 | +8.3 s | none | 0 s |
| 19:09:12 | +31.9 s | none | 0 s |

The only difference is whether a new turn started before the snapshot could be served. Same error, same session, same binary — freeze only when the next turn starts immediately. The user reproduced this live: the third failure did not freeze.

## Timeline of the 209-second freeze

```
18:54:29.929  turn 4156686f  phase=idle
18:54:29.944  turn completion settled status=Failed   (stream closed before [DONE])
18:54:29.966  turn 6a12cd4b  started                  (+22 ms)
              … UI awaits get_session_snapshot(); engine is inside the new turn …
18:55:07.188  turn 6a12cd4b  phase=streaming the model response
              … nothing in the log for 172 s …
18:57:59.786  turn 6a12cd4b  settled status=Failed    (same stream error)
18:57:59.798  WARN terminal session source no longer matches; checkpoint retained
```

The warning fires the moment the snapshot is finally served — and it no longer matches, because the engine's source has moved on. The UI then reports `Session … could not be saved (resource busy)`.

So the sequence is: the stream error is what makes the new turn end; the snapshot request is what makes the UI wait; the mismatch is what produces the misleading "not saved" notice.

## Not caused by the old workspace-lock issue

The "resource busy" wording is the same string the workspace-lease refusal used, so it is worth ruling out: this session ran in `~/`, its log shows the delegated-store read-only warning at startup (the known legacy-store case), but the save failure here is not a flock — no `Resource temporarily unavailable`, no coordination-lock line at the time of the freeze. The text comes from `snapshot_error.unwrap_or_else(|| std::io::ErrorKind::ResourceBusy.to_string())` in the same turn-complete handler.

## Frequency in one month of logs

`terminal session source no longer matches` appears **15 times across 7 log files** (9–16 November). Four have a measurable freeze:

```
848 s   tui-2026-11-14-4002283.log   turn eebd894f
541 s   tui-2026-11-15-55504.log     turn 93494e2e
209 s   tui-2026-11-16-880180.log    turn 4156686f
 69 s   tui-2026-11-13-1149827.log   turn 1443f6d1
```

The 848 s case is confounded by the separate late-usage-ledger defect (#7356) in the same session; the other three are clean (zero ledger failures in their logs) and share the exact signature above.

Underlying stream errors: **9** `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason` across 6 sessions since 10 October (10, 14, 18 ×2, 21 Oct; 16 Nov ×4). That error is separate — it is the trigger, not the freeze.

## Still present upstream

`upstream/main` at `b107c4996` (350 commits ahead of the reporting build) has the same unbounded call at `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:3906`; the turn loop still does not drain `rx_op`. No open issue covers this: #6184 is the engine going silent, #7328 is missing failure causes in the log, #7356 is the ledger blocking saves. This is the UI blocking itself on a busy engine.

## Suggested fix

Bound the await and keep the loop alive:

1. Wrap the turn-complete `get_session_snapshot()` in `tokio::time::timeout` — the same 2 s used by `await_engine_session_sync` is a reasonable start. On timeout, keep the checkpoint (already done today) and skip the completion commit instead of blocking.
2. Or serve `Op::GetSessionSnapshot` while a turn runs — it reads session state, but the engine is single-threaded, so this likely needs the snapshot to be published out-of-band rather than computed on demand.
3. While here, make the refusal say what it is: `resource busy` reads like a lock, and it sent at least one operator looking for a stale process. A sentence naming the pending Engine snapshot would have saved that search.

Option 1 is the smallest change and removes the freeze entirely; the snapshot will still mismatch sometimes, which is already handled.

## Reproduction

Not deterministic, but the conditions are simple: with a message already queued, let a turn fail with `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason` (or any fast failure), so that the failure's turn completion and the queued turn start land within the same few milliseconds. The UI then stops responding until the next turn ends.

## Related

- #7356 — late-usage ledger blocks session saves; the 848 s case overlaps with it.
- #7328 — provider failures leave no cause in the log.
- `CHANGELOG.md` 0.10.3 — "Turns no longer fail on a cost bookkeeping error"; the same principle applies to a UI that must not block on a busy engine.

issues.title: zh-Hans TUI: /status labels misaligned, and English left in tool cells, /help, /diff and the composer

labels.name: area:mcp

issues.body:
I ran a debug build of `main` (4b8a30009) with `LANG=zh_CN.UTF-8`, which selects zh-Hans, against a scripted mock provider, and read the TUI output with `tmux capture-pane`. These are the zh-Hans problems that showed up on screen. #7299 already covers the ASCII punctuation in the pack and the `Locale::ZhHans` branches outside it. The items below are separate from both.

### Misaligned columns

- [ ] **`/status` label column.** `push_row` in `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/config/status.rs` pads labels with `{label:<16}`. That counts chars, but a CJK label is two columns per char, so each row's value starts in a different column:
  ```
      路由:              deepseek · mock-model · 思考 auto
      项目文档:            无项目文档
      MCP:             已配置 0 个
      上下文窗口:           已使用 3.4%（4407 / 128000 token）
  ```
  Expected: every value starts in the same column, as in English.

### English text on zh-Hans screens

These strings are hard-coded English, so every non-English locale sees them in English:

- [ ] **Tool cell subtitles.** `exploring_label` in `crates/tui/src/tui/tool_routing.rs` builds `Reading {path}`, `Listing {path}`, `Listing directory`, ``Searching for `{pattern}` `` and `Listing files`. On screen: `✓ ▷ 读取 完成 · Reading 中文 目录/笔记 📝.md`.
- [ ] **Activity summary row.** `tool_run_summary` and `activity_family_summary` in `crates/tui/src/tui/history/tool_run.rs` join the translated parts with ASCII `, ` and `: ` and append raw tool names. On screen: `浏览了2个文件, 1次搜索: explore, file search`.
- [ ] **`/help` and the command palette.** `216 entries`, `(aliases: /qingping)` (`views/help.rs`), `aliases: …` and `{} shown / {} entries` (`command_palette.rs`).
- [ ] **`/diff` summary.** `summary: 2 files, +3 -1, 2 hunks` and the per-file `1 hunk` (`crates/tui-kit/src/diff_render.rs`).
- [ ] **Composer context preview.** `↳ [git] git status · resolved on send` and `[mention] 笔记 · resolved on send` (`file_mention.rs`, `git_mention.rs`).
- [ ] **`/status` window source row.** `目录: models.dev live · 9070 offerings · fetched 2m ago · 云端事实: off` (`status.rs`, `model_picker.rs`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the TUI with `LANG=zh_CN.UTF-8`, or with `locale = "zh-Hans"`.
2. Run `/status` and `/help`.
3. Send a prompt that makes the model call `read`, `grep_files` and `file_search`.
4. Type `@git` in the composer. Run `/diff` after a file edit.

milestone.title: v0.10.3
milestone.description:
Corrective release and exact-candidate qualification. Release scope approved November 5, 2026.

Keep history/undo and compaction continuity, login/model selection, worker durability and safe retries, bounded input/output, runtime responsiveness, and supported installation/client qualification here. Use release-blocker for the unresolved repair/qualification gates. Use status:awaiting-release for source fixes that are landed but still need final verification and shipment; do not close them merely because main contains the fix.

Broad refactors, optional features, full historical audit sweeps and unqualified optimization claims move to the later planning milestones. This replaces the previous all-refactors-for-0.10.3 umbrella scope; unfinished requirements are deferred, not completed or discarded. Confirmed release-critical defects must not be hidden by a future umbrella target.

Freeze the final source and binaries, finish the required platform/client evidence, then run final validation. Provider spend, signing and publication retain their separate approvals. No due date or published release is created by this milestone.

issues.body:
## Summary
`codewhale auth chatgpt` completes the browser sign-in, but then fails with:

```
error: ChatGPT token signature or identity claims failed verification
```

`codewhale auth status --provider openai-codex` afterwards still reports `active source: missing`.

## Environment
- CodeWhale 0.10.2 (ff466b2ed0bf), installed via `npm i -g codewhale` (latest on npm)
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300, Git Bash, Node via nvm4w
- No proxy / custom CA env vars

## Steps
1. `codewhale auth chatgpt`
2. Sign in on auth.openai.com in the browser (callback to `http://127.0.0.1:1455/auth/callback`)
3. Terminal prints the error above; no grant is stored.

## Checks already done
- Clock skew vs auth.openai.com is ~15 s
- `https://auth.openai.com/.well-known/jwks.json` and `openid-configuration` are reachable (HTTP 200)
- The error string appears to cover several failure paths in the binary (unknown/invalid verification key, audience mismatch with the registration, missing `chatgpt_account_id`/subject), so it is unclear which one is hit.

## Request
Please make the error say which check failed (signature / audience / identity claim), or document the account/plan requirements for `auth chatgpt`.

prs.title: feat(providers): add UberLLM as a bundled descriptor row
prs.body:
## What and why

Adds UberLLM as a bundled compatible-host descriptor row, in the same shape as the Opper row (#7131) and the Runcrate row. UberLLM is an OpenAI-compatible gateway with one key for models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, Kimi and others, usually below list price (per-model prices: https://uberllm.dev/models). `/provider` uses `UBERLLM_API_KEY`, `https://api.uberllm.dev/v1` and `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` as the bootstrap model. Model ids are `vendor/model`. Its `GET /v1/models` is public, so the row uses `public_models_endpoint` discovery like Runcrate and Wafer; the live list stays the model authority, and billing stays Unknown in the omission ledger. No new ProviderKind or compiled model roster.

I work on UberLLM.

Files: the descriptor row and its test (`uberllm_is_a_descriptor_row`, bundled count 16 -> 17), the compatible-default count and omission row in pricing coverage (count 16 -> 17, "thirteen" -> "fourteen" non-Baseten compatible defaults, one review sentence and one route), the EN and ZH provider docs, and the two `docs/PROVIDERS.md` entries in `web/data/agent-docs.generated.json`. CHANGELOG and credit files are left to maintainers, as CONTRIBUTING asks.

## Where this came from

Provider addition, no issue needed. Same shape as #7131.

## How I tested it

- I did not run cargo locally (no Rust toolchain on this machine), so CI is the first run for `descriptors.rs` and `default_coverage_tests.rs`.
- `python3 scripts/check-provider-registry.py`: "Provider registry drift check passed."
- `cd web && node scripts/check-facts.mjs`: "OK — committed facts.generated.ts matches workspace".
- `web/data/agent-docs.generated.json` regenerated with `deriveAgentDocs` from `web/scripts/docs-sources-lib.mjs` is byte-identical to the committed file.
- All three edited JSON files parse.
- Endpoint check against the live service: `GET https://api.uberllm.dev/v1/models` answers 200 without a key and lists `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`; a keyed `POST /v1/chat/completions` with the default model (including a `json_schema` response format and a tool-call round trip) answered normally.

## Checklist

prs.title: fix(models): keep MCP tools with null-default optionals on the Moonshot route
prs.body:
## What and why

On a Moonshot (Kimi) model, an MCP tool from a Python server is dropped from the request whenever it has an optional parameter such as `limit: int | None = None` or `filters: Filters | None = None`, so the model never sees the tool.

FastMCP and Pydantic v2 write that parameter as `{"anyOf": [{"type": "integer"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null}`. The provider-neutral `sanitize` collapses it to `nullable: true`, and `normalize_kimi_compatibility` restores the `anyOf` but carries `default: null` into the integer branch, where `validate_mfjs_default` rejects it (`InvalidDefault`). For a `$ref | null` union the collapse is skipped and `default` stays beside `anyOf` (`InvalidKeywordValue`). Either way `project_tool_schema` returns `Omitted`.

This drops a `default: null` from a node that already admits null (`nullable: true`, or an `anyOf` with a `{"type": "null"}` branch) before the union is rebuilt. It removes the incompatible default annotation while preserving accepted values and optionality.

## Where this came from

Bug fix, no issue. Found while testing Pydantic-shaped MCP schemas against the Moonshot projection; the existing `kimi_parameters_restores_registry_collapsed_nullable_anyof` covers the same path with a hand-written `anyOf` that has no `default`.

## How I tested it

`kimi_parameters_accepts_pydantic_optional_with_null_default` runs the production two-stage path (`sanitize`, then `sanitize_for_kimi_parameters`) on both shapes and validates the result with `validate_mfjs_parameters`; it fails on `main` and passes with the change. `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/models/src/schema_sanitize.rs`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-models --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` are clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)

- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it)

prs.title: fix(snapshot): roll back partial file-scoped restores
prs.body:
## What and why

When a file-scoped restore fails after earlier checkouts or removals, undo can report failure while leaving those changes in the workspace. This PR uses the existing safety snapshot to roll back attempted checkout batches and completed removals. Recovery stays within those paths and preserves newer contents it detects. The error identifies any incomplete recovery and includes the safety snapshot ID. Directory pruning, when requested, runs after a successful restore. A failed checkout can still leave empty parent directories it created.

## Where this came from

Refs #6559 (F02-10). Thanks to @7jrxt42BxFZo4iAnN4CX for reporting partial restores, and to the maintainers for identifying the remaining file-scoped case.

## How I tested it

- `CODEWHALE_DEV_NEXTEST=0 bash scripts/dev-test.sh snapshot restore` — 20 passed, 0 failed, including a late removal failure and a Git checkout that failed after writing part of a batch.
- Ran the new regression on the unpatched base and confirmed it failed because a file remained overwritten after the restore returned an error.
- `bash scripts/preflight.sh --check` — passed.

prs.body:
## What and why

The six remaining hard-coded English strings from #7304 now come from the locale packs. All 15 packs get the new keys, and English output is unchanged byte for byte. zh-Hans uses full-width punctuation as in #7299 / #7314. (The `/status` label column from the same issue already shipped in #7314.)

| # | Surface | zh-Hans before | zh-Hans after |
|---|---------|----------------|---------------|
| 1 | Tool cell subtitle (`exploring_label`, `tool_routing.rs`) | `读取 完成 · Reading src/foo.rs` | `读取 完成 · 正在读取 src/foo.rs` |
| 2 | Collapsed activity row (`tool_run.rs`) | `浏览了2个文件, 1次搜索: read file, search` | `浏览了2个文件、1次搜索：read file、search` |
| 3 | `/help` count and aliases (`views/help.rs`) | `216 entries`, `  (aliases: /qingping)` | `216 个条目`, `  （别名：/qingping）` |
| 3 | Command palette (`command_palette.rs`, `traits.rs`) | `aliases: image, media, fujian`, `1 shown / 1 entries`, `3 / 9 matches` | `别名：image、media、fujian`, `显示 1 个 / 共 1 个条目`, `3 / 9 个匹配` |
| 4 | `/diff` pager and edit cards (`diff_render.rs`) | `summary: 2 files, +3 -1, 2 hunks`, per file `1 hunk` | `摘要：2个文件，+3 -1，2处改动`, per file `1处改动` |
| 5 | Composer context preview (`file_mention.rs`) | `[git] git status · resolved on send` | `[git] git status · 发送时解析` |
| 6 | `/status` window source row (`status.rs`) | `目录: models.dev live · 9070 offerings · fetched 2m ago · 云端事实: off` | `目录: models.dev 实时 · 9070 个可用模型 · 2 分钟前获取 · 云端事实: 关闭` |

Notes per item:

1. `exploring_label` takes the UI locale. The card picked the `find` verb by checking whether the label started with the English word `Searching`, which would break once the label is translated. `ExploringEntry` now carries a `search` flag set from the tool name (`grep_files`, the only tool that produced that label). I removed the comment sentence that this change made false.
2. List and clause separators and the `clause: families` join are pack strings (`ListSeparator`, `ActivityClauseSeparator`, `ActivityFamilies`). Tool family names stay as they are: they are tool identifiers, and the existing `a_collapsed_run_summary_names_what_actually_happened` test requires `read file` in every locale.
3. `/help` alias suffixes, the slash-menu alias hint (`widgets/mod.rs`, same string) and the palette count and alias text are pack strings. `shed_to_width` in `views/help.rs` also treats `（` / `）` as parentheses and ` （` as a field joint, so a narrow `/help` still drops the whole zh alias field and never cuts it in half.
4. `codewhale-tui-kit` does not depend on `codewhale-localization`, so `render_diff_bounded`, `render_diff_window`, `search_diff`, `search_diff_from_origin` and `diff_row_for_origin` take a `DiffSummaryLabels` (its `Default` is the current English text). The TUI builds it from the pack, and the diff pager rebuilds it in `set_locale`.
5. `pending_context_previews` takes the locale, and the git and file previews use one pack string.
6. The config group reads text through `StatusMessages`, so the new keys are added there and in `config_policy_messages.rs`. The age uses the existing `SessionsTime*` strings, whose English text matches `cloud_facts::age_label` (`just now`, `2m ago`, `3h ago`, `1d ago`). The group still builds as `codewhale-portable-config`.

Not changed: the row labels in `/status` still use an ASCII `: ` (`目录: `) like every other `/status` row. A cloud-facts state other than `off` still reads `cloud_facts::label()` in English. Other English nearby that the issue does not list is also unchanged: the git mention label `working-tree diff`, `use /attach for media bytes`, and the `1 file +3 -1` header from `diff_summary_label`.

Closes #7304

## How I tested it

The machine locale is `zh_HK` (`LANG=zh_HK.UTF-8`), which makes the English-asserting `/status` tests run in zh-Hant. So I ran the TUI tests with `LANG=en_US.UTF-8 LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8` through `scripts/with-hermetic-test-home.sh`.

prs.title: fix(engine): avoid rereading history for named-turn undo
prs.body:
## What and why

Named-turn undo loads every source turn and item to resolve a tail-relative depth, then delegates to depth-relative preparation, which loads the history again. Long sessions pay an extra whole-history read while undo preparation holds the admission guard.

Reuse the loaded records through the existing `prepare_fork_from_cutoff`. Resolve the anchor with the shared user-turn indexing rule and use the anchor itself as the cutoff and receipt, preserving removal of the selected turn and everything after it. Source capture, external-executor rejection, workspace/store ownership checks and the session lease remain in the existing preparation flow.

The shared fallback retains its existing retained-prefix item reads. This change removes the named path's redundant complete preparation pass; the evidence below measures turn-file reads rather than wall-clock speedup.

## Where this came from

Refs #7355. Thanks to @soarkit for tracing the duplicate reads and providing the file-open benchmark that made the extra pass visible.

## How I tested it

```sh
CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CODEWHALE_DEV_NEXTEST=0 bash scripts/dev-test.sh engine -- \
  named_turn_undo_reads_turn_store_once_and_drops_anchor \
  fork_at_user_message_ fork_at_user_turn_ \
  saved_checkpoint_validation_and_forks_preserve_history \
  abandoned_backtrack_fork_leaves_no_session_document --test-threads=1
bash scripts/preflight.sh --check
git diff --check
```

- Negative control with original production code and the same regression: `test result: FAILED. 8 passed; 1 failed`. The regression failed exactly at turn-file reads: **10**, expected **5**.
- Fixed code: `test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed`. The fixture includes three user turns, an intervening compaction and an unrelated thread; it verifies one turn-store scan, the dropped range and receipt, the retained prefix, and source preservation.
- Final preflight: `preflight: OK`, including rustfmt. `git diff --check` passed.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] Formatting passes and tests cover the changed behavior
- [x] Existing undo behavior is preserved; no new user-facing feature requires a registry row

prs.title: fix(tui): recapture focus without erasing the viewport
prs.body:
## What and why

Ordinary window focus recovery currently erases the viewport before repainting it. On terminals that ignore DEC 2026, this exposes an intermediate blank screen. Separate focus recapture from explicit clear requests: restore terminal modes and margins/origin, then repaint the viewport, including blank cells, without `CSI 2J`.

Resize, suspend, theme changes and external terminal handoffs retain clear-and-redraw recovery. A queued clear takes precedence over focus recapture. The draw still runs once, preserving the per-frame hyperlink registry and cursor handling.

Full repaint recovery remains intentional. Ratatui's cell directives can cause one additional ordinary diff before settling; this change does not promise less repaint traffic.

## Where this came from

Refs #7343. Thanks to @scripting-drafts for the detailed report and control-stream diagnosis. This addresses the ordinary-focus erase path; it does not establish zero redraw or native GNOME Terminal visual behavior.

## How I tested it

Focused TUI tests, including the new recapture regression and existing focus, cursor, mode-recovery and resize coverage:

```sh
CODEWHALE_DEV_NEXTEST=0 bash scripts/dev-test.sh tui -- \
  focus_recapture_repaints_cells_without_erasing_the_viewport \
  focus_gained_forces_terminal_viewport_recapture \
  focus_loss_defers_frames_until_focus_or_input_returns \
  focus_loss_defers_frames_only_on_vte_terminals \
  focus_loss_keeps_painting_inside_tmux_even_under_a_vte_host \
  recover_terminal_modes_emits_expected_csi_sequences_with_gating \
  frame_cursor_is_hidden_during_diff_then_positioned_before_reveal \
  cjk_composer_cursor_and_mouse_geometry_agree_in_compact_and_wide_frames \
  g3_resize_clear_and_failure_are_inside_synchronized_output
```

`test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5830 filtered out`.

- `cargo fmt --all` and `bash scripts/preflight.sh --check`: passed.
- `bash scripts/dev-cargo.sh build -p codewhale-cli --locked`: succeeded for clean main and the fix.
- Real offline PTY comparison at 80×24 and 120×40, synchronized output off/on, three focus pairs per case: clean main emitted 12 whole-screen erases across 12 FocusIn events; the fix emitted 0. Mode recovery, synchronized-output gating and input liveness remained functional; all four fixed runs exited 0.
- VTE-path deferred-resize control: no output while unfocused; returning focus applies the pending resize and retains both clears, matching clean main. Input remained live and the run exited 0.

Actual before/after terminal recordings and replay instructions: [before/after recordings](https://github.com/laozidabo/Codewhale/tree/409c73df1c3304a17a6a6eb86c20b52e7121fc14).
These capture real PTY bytes in isolated offline sessions with synthetic inputs. They are control-stream evidence, not a native GNOME Terminal rendering test.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (`c4195348f`).
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior.
- [x] Feature docs/registry considered: existing behavior bug fix; no new command, provider or feature flag.

issues.body:
Hourly Extension Tests can exhaust Boat memory after runner setup succeeds.

Two scheduled runs failed `checks-node-extensions-shard-3` with exit 137. Boat reported that a process needed more than 7,428 MiB RAM plus 6,143 MiB swap:
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44459817245/job/135344291352
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44466669217/job/135366698620

The shard runs mixed extension batches with two concurrent config groups. A recent all-Blacksmith hourly run passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44452942906. This is runner memory exhaustion, separate from the sandbox-start limit fixed in #201116.

Keep mixed extension batches on their existing Blacksmith route; spend the existing quota-bounded Boat allowance on file-bounded extension shards. Preserve all tests, concurrency, deadlines, manual/retry routing, and the maximum 20 Boat starts per run.

issues.title: Qualify PostgreSQL cron finalization and pool reuse across in-process restarts
issues.body:
The existing PostgreSQL Gateway cron fixture covers graceful process exit and crash recovery, but does not prove the in-process restart path waits for an interrupted run's blocked finalizer while retaining its process-owned PostgreSQL bridge pool.

Add one real-process test using the existing fixture: hold the model response, lock its running receipt from an independent PostgreSQL client, request a public in-process restart, observe cancellation and the blocked database update while readiness drains, then release the lock. Require the same process with a new boot identity, exactly one interrupted receipt/history outcome, a successful fresh manual cron run, unchanged cumulative bridge-worker starts, and no tagged PostgreSQL connections after final shutdown.

Maintainer-requested continuation of the PostgreSQL audit. Test-only scope: no production, SQLite schema/version/DDL/migration, persisted format, durability/retention, config, or public API changes. This covers manual cron execution and bridge-worker reuse, not automatic retry policy or preservation of individual database backend PIDs.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/201245

issues.title: refactor(test): consolidate plugin-update cohort setup
issues.body:
## Summary
Consolidate repeated plugin-update cohort setup in the CLI persistence tests.

## Problem to solve
Four test blocks repeat the same runtime versions, installation root, environment, and cohort initialization. Changes to this shared setup require editing each copy while preserving the distinct rollback and persistence scenarios.

## Proposed solution
Use one file-local helper for the repeated setup. Keep every existing case, assertion, fence, guard, await position, and cleanup path. Create fresh runtime objects for each call.

## Alternatives considered
Keep four copies, or move the helper into shared test infrastructure. A file-local helper matches the current consumers without adding a shared abstraction.

## Impact
Developer maintenance only; no user-visible behavior change. This is the requested code-reduction work, not a claim that a flaky test was repaired.

## Evidence/examples
The repetitions are in `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-plugins.persistence.test.ts`. The candidate removes 31 net test lines without changing production code. Focused validation is in progress.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?
Yes.

### Summary
A Matrix rich reply can activate a mention-required bot using a bot mention present only in the quoted message. The quoted fallback also remains in the current agent body, despite separately hydrated reply context.

### Reproduction
Alice sends `@Claw can you help?`; Bob replies to Alice with only `I already solved it.` The Matrix event contains the normal leading plain-text quote and an `<mx-reply>` HTML fallback with Alice's bot link, followed by Bob's current text. Supply no current `m.mentions.user_ids` and no bot thread participation.

On main0b818fd563d75e2a9c9230ad4ccbee11894b5862, the production mention resolver scans the fallback HTML and returns `wasMentioned=true, hasExplicitMention=true`; the real shared mention gate returns `shouldSkip=false`. The body-selection helpers retain the old quoted question as current text. Removing the fallback gives `wasMentioned=false` and `shouldSkip=true`; a fresh bot link in the authored suffix still gives a positive mention.

### Expected behavior and impact
A quote-only reply to another human should not count as a new explicit mention. Preserve genuine authored mentions, independently hydrated quote context, relation metadata, and ordinary authored blockquotes. In mention-required rooms, this avoids unwanted bot turns and passing the previous question as newly authored text.

### Evidence and limits
Local synthetic event fixtures exercise production body helpers, mention detection and shared mention gate. Full handler/transport adoption, a homeserver and model responses have not been tested. This is currently a source/function-level reproduction, not a live-delivery claim. Matrix rich-reply fallback format: https://spec.matrix.org/v1.10/client-server-api/#fallbacks-for-rich-replies . The mention behavior is inferred from OpenClaw's current gate contract, not specified directly by Matrix.

Bounded searches and changed-file inspection found no matching fix among25 open candidate PRs. #168054 and #186324 share owners but address coalescing/gallery handling; #16941's genuine HTML-mention compatibility must remain.

Environment: macOS arm64 source checkout; Node24.22.2/pnpm12.15.0. No provider needed for mention preparation.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`@openclaw/whatsapp` 2026.11.5 no longer writes the outbound `Sending message -> …` and `Sent message <id> -> <redacted jid> (<ms>ms)` log lines (nor the structured `sending message` / `sent message` records) that 2026.11.3 wrote for every send. Is this removal intended? Operators who use the gateway log as delivery evidence lose it on upgrade.

### Steps to reproduce

Found by inspecting the published packages before upgrading (not by running 2026.11.5 in production):

1. `npm pack @openclaw/whatsapp@2026.11.3` and `npm pack @openclaw/whatsapp@2026.11.5`, extract both.
2. Search each for the fixed string `Sent message `.
   - 2026.11.3: `dist/.setup/send-*.mjs` contains
     `outboundLog.info(\`Sent message ${messageId} -> ${redactedJid}${hasMedia ? " (media)" : ""} (${durationMs}ms)\`)`
     together with `Sending message -> …`, the reaction and poll equivalents, and structured `logger.info(..., "sent message")` records from the `web-outbound` module logger.
   - 2026.11.5: no match anywhere in the package. The send module only calls `logger.warn` and `logger.error`.
3. The same fixed-string search over the `openclaw` 2026.11.5 core `dist` and `@openclaw/codex` 2026.11.5 also finds nothing, so the line does not appear to have moved.

### Expected behavior

A successful outbound WhatsApp send leaves an info-level record in the gateway log carrying the message id and the redacted recipient, as in 2026.11.3 and earlier, or the release notes name the replacement source of that evidence.

### Actual behavior

In the 2026.11.5 package there is no info-level record of a completed outbound send in the WhatsApp send path. The 2026.11.5 release notes do not mention the change. The inbound line and the monitor's `auto-reply sent` record are still present.

### OpenClaw version

Running 2026.11.3; comparing against the published 2026.11.5 packages (core, `@openclaw/whatsapp`, `@openclaw/codex`).

### Operating system

macOS (Apple silicon), Node 26.

### Install method

npm global install; WhatsApp plugin installed through the plugin manager.

### Model

Not model-specific.

### Provider / routing chain

Not provider-specific.

### Additional provider/model setup details

None.

### Logs

Not applicable: the report is about log lines that are no longer emitted. The 2026.11.3 format was:
`Sent message <message id> -> sha256:<12 hex> (<n>ms)` from subsystem `gateway/channels/whatsapp/outbound`, on the trace of the turn that sent it.

Questions:
1. Was the removal deliberate (log-volume reduction) or a side effect of the send-path refactor?
2. If deliberate, what is the supported way to get per-message send confirmation (message id, redacted recipient, time) out of the gateway: the `message_sent` hook, a delivery ledger, a log level or flag?

issues.title: [Bug] Source build cannot boot: dist/extensions ships JS without openclaw.plugin.json manifests or assets, so plugins.entries.* fails validation (exit 78)

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish
labels.description: Thin issue quality; more reproduction proof or environment detail is needed.

labels.name: impact:other
labels.description: This issue has meaningful maintainer-visible impact outside the owned taxonomy.

issues.body:
## Summary

A source build of this repo produces a `dist` that **cannot boot**: `dist/extensions/<name>/` gets the extension JavaScript but not its `openclaw.plugin.json` manifest and not its `assets/` directory. `openclaw.json` `plugins.entries.*` resolves against those manifest paths, so config validation fails and the gateway exits `status=78/CONFIG` before it ever binds its port.

Nothing in the build output or the docs says the source build is not bootable.

## Environment

- Source checkout at `bff0b597d` (package version `2026.11.5`), built with the repo's own `scripts/tsdown-build.mts`
- Node 24.22.3, Ubuntu Linux x64
- Comparison target: the published npm install of `2026.9.37` (`81da850`) on the same host

## Observed

Manifest coverage across `dist/extensions`:

| tree | extension dirs | dirs with `openclaw.plugin.json` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| source build, `bff0b597d` | 83 | **3** |
| published npm install, `2026.9.37` | 65 | **64** |

One extension, `a2a`, side by side:

| source build | published install |
| --- | --- |
| `api.js`, `channel-plugin-api.js`, `index.js`, `runtime-api.js`, `setup-entry.js`, `setup-plugin-api.js` | `api.d.ts`, `api.js`, `assets/`, `channel-plugin-api.js`, `index.d.ts`, `index.js`, **`openclaw.plugin.json`**, `package.json` |

`openclaw.json` on this host lists 51 `plugins.entries.*`. Validation resolves those entries against the manifest paths, which do not exist in the source build.

## Reproduction

1. Build from a source checkout of `bff0b597d` using the repo's build script.
2. Point a gateway at the built `dist` (`node <checkout>/dist/index.js gateway --port <port>`).
3. Observe config validation fail and the process exit `status=78/CONFIG` with no listener on the port.

Journal in our run: service started 22:01:47 MST, state upgrade completed 22:02:13, config validation failed 22:06:26, process gone, port never bound.

## Why this is worse than a plain startup failure

The failure happens *after* the upgrade path runs. In our attempt the new binary had already:

- copied 7.3 GB of state across 58,337 files,
- migrated the agent databases v19 → v24,
- stamped `lastTouchedVersion` / `lastRunVersion = 2026.11.5` into `openclaw.json`.

So reverting the binary alone does not recover the host: the older release then refuses to start with *"this OpenClaw binary is older than the config last written by OpenClaw 2026.11.5"*. Recovery required restoring `openclaw.json` and the pre-upgrade database copies as well. A packaging error that fires before the port binds still costs a state migration and a full restore.

## Expected

Either the build produces a bootable install-style layout (copy each extension's `openclaw.plugin.json` and `assets/` into `dist/extensions/<name>/`), or the build/docs state explicitly that a source build is not bootable without a separate packaging step.

Manually staging the manifests into `dist/extensions/` is a workaround, not a fix: it changes the artefact, so any hash recorded before staging no longer describes what boots.

## Impact

Anyone validating a branch from source on a real host hits a non-obvious exit after a state migration, and the natural conclusion ("my change broke boot") is wrong. We lost an apply window to it.

Environment note: this report is from a third-party operator testing a patch, not a maintainer.

issues.body:
### Summary

When `hooks.status` (or `openclaw hooks list` without `--agent`) refuses because several agents are configured and none is the implicit owner, include the configured agent IDs in the error, and consider a way to list gateway-wide plugin hooks without picking an agent.

### Problem to solve

With two or more agents in `agents.entries`, none marked `default: true`, and no explicit `agents.defaults.systemAgent`, calling the gateway method `hooks.status` without `agentId` returns `INVALID_REQUEST`:

```
Multiple agents are configured, but this Gateway request has no explicit owner. Set agentId to one of the configured agents.
```

`docs/cli/hooks.md` now documents that `--agent` is required in this setup, which is fine. But:

1. The error does not say which agent IDs exist. `AgentSelectionRequiredError` already carries them (`error.agentIds`, `src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts:60-75`), but `resolveAgentIdOrRespondError` (`src/gateway/server-methods/agent-id-shared.ts:30-52`) only forwards `error.message`. A client has to make a second call (for example `agents.list`) to recover.
2. Plugin-registry hooks are gateway-wide (the handler adds `registry.hooks` to every report, `src/gateway/server-methods/hooks-status.ts`), yet listing them requires naming an arbitrary agent.

Steps (v2026.11.5):

1. Configure two agents, for example `agents.entries: { main: {...}, helper: {...} }`, with no `default: true`.
2. `openclaw gateway call hooks.status` (no params), or `openclaw hooks list`.
3. The call fails with the message above and no list of valid IDs.

### Proposed solution

At minimum, pass the IDs as structured error details (`errorShape` already accepts `details`):

```ts
// src/gateway/server-methods/agent-id-shared.ts
params.respond(
  false,
  undefined,
  errorShape(ErrorCodes.INVALID_REQUEST, error.message, {
    details: { code: error.code, agentIds: error.agentIds },
  }),
);
```

and print them in the CLI hint (for example "Pass --agent <id>. Configured agents: main, helper.").

Optionally, accept `agentId: "*"` on `hooks.status` and return `{ agents: { <id>: report } }`, with plugin hooks listed once since they are the same for every agent.

### Alternatives considered

Calling `agents.list` first and retrying with an ID works, but every client of every agent-scoped gateway method has to reimplement it, and the error already has the data.

### Impact

Affected: multi-agent setups without a default agent, and tools that call agent-scoped gateway methods.
Severity: annoying.
Frequency: always, in that setup.
Consequence: an extra round trip, or a confusing error for CLI users who don't know the agent IDs.

### Evidence/examples

Related but different: #126360 (ambient callers that have no agent to pass). This request is only about telling an explicit caller which IDs are valid.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance

### Additional information

The same `resolveAgentIdOrRespondError` helper is shared by other agent-scoped gateway methods, so the `details` change would help all of them.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When `chat.history` replaces a transcript message larger than 128 KiB with the `[chat.history omitted: message too large]` placeholder, the placeholder keeps `__openclaw.id`, `runId`, `seq`, `idempotencyKey` and the tool identity, but drops `__openclaw.transport`. A client that finds its own inbound message by the channel `messageId` (`__openclaw.transport.messageId`) can no longer find that message once it is large.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Send a message over a channel that records a transport `messageId` (for example the bundled A2A channel), with a body that makes the stored user message larger than `CHAT_HISTORY_MAX_SINGLE_MESSAGE_BYTES` (128 KiB). A2A caps extracted text at 64 KiB, so use a text part plus a structured data part, or any channel without that cap.
2. `openclaw gateway call chat.history` for that session.
3. Compare the entry for that user message with a normal-sized one.

### Expected behavior

The placeholder keeps the small identifying metadata, including `__openclaw.transport` (`channel`, `messageId`), the same way it already keeps `id`, `runId`, `seq` and `idempotencyKey`.

### Actual behavior

`__openclaw.transport` is missing from the placeholder. Only `idempotencyKey` is left, so a client has to rely on how the idempotency key is derived from the `messageId`.

From the v2026.11.5 source:

- `src/gateway/chat-history-budget.ts:112-148` (`buildOversizedHistoryPlaceholder`) rebuilds `__openclaw` from an allowlist (`toolOutput`, `id`, `runId`, `seq`, `idempotencyKey`, `turnBoundary`, `transcriptPosition`) that has no `transport`.
- `src/gateway/session-transcript-record-parser.ts:281-294` (the transcript parser's oversized placeholder) keeps only `idempotencyKey` and `__openclaw: { truncated: true, reason: "oversized" }`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (first seen on 2026.11.3; code unchanged on `main` as of 2026-11-19)

### Operating system

macOS 27

### Install method

npm package

### Model

N/A (not model-dependent)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A (not model-dependent)

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

_No response_

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: clients that read `chat.history` and match messages by the channel `messageId` (for example to find the turn their own inbound message started).
Severity: annoying; the client loses its anchor for that turn.
Frequency: always, for any message over 128 KiB.
Consequence: the client cannot locate its own large message in history.

### Additional information

Suggested fix: keep the two short transport strings in the placeholder.

```ts
// buildOversizedHistoryPlaceholder
const transport = asOptionalRecord(metadata.transport);
const keptTransport =
  transport && (typeof transport.messageId === "string" || typeof transport.channel === "string")
    ? {
        ...(typeof transport.channel === "string" ? { channel: transport.channel } : {}),
        ...(typeof transport.messageId === "string" ? { messageId: transport.messageId } : {}),
      }
    : undefined;
// ...
__openclaw: {
  // ...existing fields...
  ...(keptTransport ? { transport: keptTransport } : {}),
  truncated: true,
  reason: "oversized",
},
```

Both fields are short strings, so the placeholder stays within the byte budget that `replaceOversizedChatHistoryMessages` already checks. A matching change in the transcript-record parser's placeholder would make the two paths consistent.

issues.title: [Bug]: Discord native command continuations fail on active conversation targets in 2026.10.5

issues.body:
### Bug type
Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
Discord native command continuations can fail in 2026.10.5 before reaching an active conversation run because a session reader admitted for the slash-source session is reused to read the conversation target.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run the published 2026.10.5 package with Discord native commands enabled.
2. Start a normal agent run in a Discord conversation.
3. Submit a native `/steer` command targeting that active conversation. The native command has a per-user slash-source session while the active run owns the conversation session.
4. When target-slot adoption is skipped because the conversation already has an active owner, the continuation retains its source reservation and fails during the initial restart-recovery session read.

PR #177451 now includes a deterministic isolated regression through the real `admitReplyTurn` and `runReplyAgent` paths, with SQLite-backed source admission and a separate active conversation owner. It reproduces the exact failure on the affected release without a Discord or model API request.

### Expected behavior
The continuation should read the conversation target and steer its existing run while preserving the slash-source reservation and its currentness checks. This Discord workflow worked before our upgrade from 2026.10.4.

### Actual behavior
Discord reports `Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.` Gateway logs recorded the shared failure twice after the upgrade:

```text
Session read differs from its original admitted target
```

The real-admission regression reproduces the same error on the unmodified 2026.10.5 source. `runReplyAgent` passes the source operation's cohort reader to its initial read of the different target session. `assertSessionEntryCohortScope` correctly rejects the mismatch before steering runs.

### OpenClaw version
2026.10.5, official npm package; source reproduction at `1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8` (`v2026.10.5` / `release/2026.10.5`). Last observed working installation: 2026.10.4.

### Operating system
macOS 27.0, arm64; Node.js 26.10.0.

### Install method
npm global; updated using the native OpenClaw updater.

### Model
Provider-independent failure before inference. The isolated regression uses a synthetic backend and does not call a model.

### Provider / routing chain
Discord native interaction -> OpenClaw native command dispatch -> reply admission -> conversation target read -> failure before backend steering.

### Impact and scope
The native active-target continuation failure is reproduced on the affected release. The operator has now narrowed the initial broad report: the same native `/status` command works in a parent channel but fails inside a thread. Other commands have not been established to share this parent/thread split; this does not prove that every slash command fails or shares this root cause. We also reproduced the distinct direct `/status` auth-selection failure already tracked in #169213 and #169319.

The parent/thread difference is consistent with per-session conditions: direct status reaches the auth guard when its target has a saved auth override, while the continuation defect requires a separate source reservation and an active target. Unbound threads keep their own conversation target rather than using the parent session. The follow-up tests compare parent, public-thread, and private-thread routing, plus real direct-status behavior for an unpinned parent and a pinned thread. No live parent/thread acceptance of the patch has been performed.

PR #177451 includes a registry-driven adapter routing audit covering registered specifications, aliases, dynamic skills, ordinary dispatch, argument menus, model pickers, direct status, plugins, denied senders and source/target isolation. It also compares real Client interaction routing for parent, public-thread and private-thread fixtures. Destructive command effects and live Discord delivery are outside that isolated routing check.

The review follow-up adds a nine-cell source-authority matrix: one current-source success plus abort/release pairs before the initial read, during the target read, during steering preparation and during asynchronous backend preparation before the final queue effect. It uses real admission/runner/injection authority checks with a synthetic final backend effect. The awaited-preparation regression exposed a released source resolving instead of rejecting; the follow-up carries source currentness through the existing steering owner. A separate isolated test captures real parent/thread status plaintext and presentation output while asserting both complete stored entries remain unchanged. The broader follow-up passed 293 selected tests across seven files in 118.53s, including all nine source-authority cases and all six status regressions. After coherent test-case extraction, the two affected suites passed all 263 tests (235 runner and 28 Discord plugin-dispatch). Candidate `8cf6137a8a927f19c3a696fbe88524d1477cf917`; current checks and hosted-review state are recorded in the PR. The CI repair preserves the existing same-owner steering path when an optional target key is absent; all 304 selected tests and the session-accessor boundary guard pass locally on this head. Hosted CI now passes on this head, including both previously failing jobs and the final CI gate ([run 39301725615](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39301725615)); ClawSweeper revision 2 completed on exact head `8cf6137` at 18:41 UTC on October 19, with no concrete findings; it requires production-backend/native Discord acceptance and a maintainer delivery decision before merge.

### Additional information
Native command configuration and the saved auth-selection fields were unchanged by the upgrade. The first post-update status error preceded our later cleanup of an empty slash-session row.

Current main has replaced this older command-admission architecture in #175837. This report concerns the still-published 2026.10.5 implementation and a narrow repair for `release/2026.10.5`; it does not assert that current main still has the same continuation bug. The existing status issue remains the tracking issue for that separate failure.

The repair remains under review in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177451. The later live update below records successful local candidate deployment and four positive native checks. Production source-revocation acceptance and the maintainer decision between a stable correction and the next stable release remain open.

## Controlled 10.4 → 10.5 causal comparison (October 19)

Two independent upstream changes are isolated:

- Direct status: [`af55058459c8cfab7b9430218138eba7b16cce6c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/af55058459c8cfab7b9430218138eba7b16cce6c) (#166985) adds the saved-selection identity guard. The pre-existing status loader supplies a cloned entry alongside the original store entry. With the same compatible synthetic credential and saved pin, actual published 10.4 returns a full card; published 10.5 throws the exact `SessionWorkStartInvalidatedError`. Removing the guard in isolated 10.5 restores the card; forwarding its verbatim declaration/call into 10.4 reproduces the error. A 10.5 control fixes only snapshot coherence while retaining the guard and succeeds. An unpinned 10.5 control also succeeds. All six cells preserve both complete durable session rows and attempt zero network requests.
- Busy-target steering: [`45908445e13f8b910d3ffc192260fec9eee07e1f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/45908445e13f8b910d3ffc192260fec9eee07e1f) (#166703) adds the erroneous retained-reader handoff. The real native-key resolver, `/steer` handler, SQLite source admission, busy-target adoption and runner succeed on exact 10.4 source. Unmodified 10.5 throws `Session read differs from its original admitted target` with zero injection. Deleting only the initial target read's fifth argument, `getReplyOperationSessionReader(providedReplyOperation)`, restores exactly one injection on 10.5. The cohort guard remains intact; the same 10.5 fixture and backend adapter are used before/after. All three cells preserve the target owner, retain the source reservation, and perform zero new model runs or queued fallbacks.

The status cells exercise actual published helper/auth-store/session-store/model-selection/rendering code; the original 10.5 owners byte-match the installed package. issues.body:
## Summary

A `openclaw message send --channel discord ...` invoked as a short-lived CLI process can still be running long after Discord has created the message. Callers with a process deadline (a `spawnSync`/`execFile` timeout) kill the CLI mid-flight and see a timeout error even though the send succeeded. With a 60s caller deadline, 13 of 18 timed-out attempts had already delivered.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.3 (1391f7c), macOS (arm64), local gateway running.
- Sends issued by automation via the CLI: `openclaw message send --channel discord --target channel:<id> --message <text>` (text only, no `--media`, no session key).
- Caller kills the child at 60s (`spawnSync <bin> ETIMEDOUT`).

## Observed timing

Discord message creation is observable independently of the CLI via the gateway's own ingress rows (`channel_ingress_events`, `lane_key = channel:<id>`, ms epoch). Across 18 adjudicable timeout attempts, 13 had an ingress receipt 13–53s after the attempt started, while the CLI was killed at 60s. So Discord had the message with 7–47s still to go in the process lifetime, and the remainder was post-send work and/or process linger.

Recent successful sends:

| ledger row (attempt start) | Discord message created | bookkeeping row written |
|---|---:|---:|
| T | +13.6s | +21.0s |
| T | +11.3s | +41.1s |
| T | +12.8s | +41.7s |

The message exists ~13s in, but the per-send bookkeeping completes up to ~30s later.

CLI cold start measured on the same host with `--dry-run` is ~2.8–4.2s, so the kill is not a startup problem.

## Code observations (installed dist, read-only)

- The bundled Discord plugin's outbound adapter is `deliveryMode: "direct"` (`@openclaw/discord/dist/outbound-adapter-CO2BRlRl.js`), so `sendMessage` in `dist/message-XBWiTWA6.mjs` takes the direct branch: Discord REST plus all post-send work run in the spawned CLI process. The CLI cannot select the gateway route for Discord.
- The post-send work after the platform send includes `mirrorDeliveredPayloads` (transcript append with a writer fence), `persistQueuedPostSendState`, delivery-queue lease handling (`PLATFORM_SEND_OWNER_LEASE_MS = 6e4` in `dist/delivery-queue-storage-BoTQv3qb.mjs`), outbound audit terminals, and delivery commit hooks (`dist/deliver-CkUxL8GZ.mjs`). These write to the shared `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite`, which the long-lived gateway is also writing; `OPENCLAW_SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS` is 5s per write.
- The launcher (`openclaw.mjs` → `dist/entry.js`) does not call `process.exit` after the command resolves; process exit waits for the event loop to drain, so open handles can extend lifetime past completed work.

## Impact

- Any caller with a deadline can kill a send that already succeeded and then retry it, duplicating alerts. Receipt-less callers cannot distinguish "delivered" from "failed".
- 46 such timeout rows accumulated over five months in one installation; recently 2–5/day during alert bursts.

## Requested fix

One or more of:

1. Make direct-mode CLI sends exit deterministically once the platform send is acknowledged and remaining bookkeeping is either finished or durably queued (bounded post-send work).
2. Allow Discord sends to opt into the gateway delivery route so a caller deadline cannot abort an in-flight delivery.
3. At minimum, bound the post-send bookkeeping with a hard deadline and report the delivery result before it.

Happy to supply more timing logs or a repro harness (e.g. a script that spawns the CLI with a short deadline and compares the ingress receipt timestamp).

issues.body:
## Environment
- OpenClaw: 2026.10.7 (157d8c2), upgraded 2026-10-27 17:03 (GMT+8)
- Node v24.22.1, Linux x64, systemd user service
- Discord single account configured as `channels.discord.accounts.main` (no `default` account exists)

## Regression 1: heartbeat fails every ~31min with SessionBindingError after upgrade
**Pre-upgrade**: zero occurrences in 6 days of journals.
**Post-upgrade**: every ~30min since 17:12, same triple each cycle:
```
2026-10-27T17:12:42.825+08:00 [diagnostic] message dispatch completed: channel=unknown sessionId=unknown sessionKey=agent:main:main source=replyResolver outcome=error duration=18ms error="SessionBindingError: Session binding owner changed for discord:default"
2026-10-27T17:12:42.829+08:00 [heartbeat] failed: Session binding owner changed for discord:default
2026-10-27T17:06:01.290+08:00 Delivery failed (discord to channel:1478191291455246476): Error: Discord bot token missing for account "default" (set discord.accounts.default.token or DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN for default).
```
Local root cause: cron jobs whose `delivery` block lacks `accountId` (legacy shape `{"mode":"announce","channel":"discord","to":"<id>"}`) now resolve to account `default` instead of the single configured account. The gateway registers a `discord|default` conversation row for the target channel and the main session's replyResolver trips over it on every heartbeat wake. Workaround applied: `openclaw cron edit <id> --account main` on the 3 affected jobs → errors stopped immediately (zero SessionBindingError across 2+ heartbeat cycles after fix). Suggested fix: when no accountId is given and exactly one discord account is configured, resolve to it instead of a nonexistent `default`; and/or skip creating binding rows for accounts that fail token resolution.

## Regression 2: liveness warning / event-loop starvation during model_call
**Pre-upgrade**: zero liveness warnings in 6 days.
**Post-upgrade**: 3 warnings within 3 hours, all during `processing/model_call`:
```
2026-10-27T18:00:19.099+08:00 [diagnostic] liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,event_loop_utilization interval=74s degradedFor=74s eventLoopDelayP99Ms=74289.5 eventLoopUtilization=1 cpuCoreRatio=0.111 active=1 work=[active=agent:main:discord:channel:...(processing/model_call,q=1,age=94s last=model_call:stream_progress)]
2026-10-27T19:23:12.119+08:00 [diagnostic] liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,event_loop_utilization,cpu interval=118s degradedFor=119s eventLoopDelayMaxMs=117641.8 eventLoopUtilization=0.996 cpuCoreRatio=0.927 active=1 work=[... last=model_call:started]
```
Accompanied by fetch-guard starvation:
```
17:47:41 [fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 5000ms (elapsed 22718ms) timer delayed 17718ms, likely event-loop starvation operation=fetchWithSsrFGuard url=http://192.168.50.166:11434/api/tags
17:49:37 [fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 5000ms (elapsed 54184ms) timer delayed 49184ms ... same url
```
Context: LAN ollama provider (`models.providers.ollama`) was configured; its host is currently down (ping 100% loss; TCP connect succeeds then empty reply — host up, service dead). The recurring `/api/tags` probe through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` delays timers by up to ~88s per attempt while cpu stays low — smells like something synchronous inside the SSRF guard path (DNS resolution? blocklist check?) rather than the fetch itself. Pre-upgrade journals show no such probes/warnings with the same config and the same dead host. Workaround applied: removed the ollama provider → liveness warnings and fetch-timeout lines stopped immediately.

## Impact
- Discord replies/receipts visibly delayed while the loop is starved.
- Heartbeat wakes failed every ~31min → proactive checks silently dead.

Happy to provide full journal excerpts or the sqlite conversation rows if useful.
