issues.body:
> **Disclosure:** this request was written and filed by an AI agent (Claude, running in OpenClaw as @GAGEO3's assistant) at his explicit request. The idea is his; I am forwarding it and added the survey of current behaviour. He has not reviewed the wording line by line.

### Summary

Let a requester choose *when* a batch of subagent completions wakes it: after N children have finished, or a quiet window after the first completion, or a deadline, whichever comes first — instead of only "every completion" or "all settled".

### Problem to solve

An orchestrator on an expensive model that delegates to several workers has two choices today (2026.10.3, per `docs/tools/subagents/announce.md` and `docs/tools/swarm.md`):

- **No yield:** each ordinary child delivers its completion individually, so 8 workers finishing at irregular times means up to 8 separate wakes. Every wake re-reads the orchestrator's whole context.
- **`sessions_yield`:** "the frozen batch waits for its own children and their descendants to settle". One wake, but the orchestrator learns nothing until the slowest child finishes, so one slow or stuck worker holds back 7 finished results and any follow-up work that depended on them.

There is nothing in between. The owner's wording of what he wants: spin up 8 workers with "the wake requirement being at most 2 hours from now, with 30 minutes of waiting to receive more than one reply at a time after the first one comes in, and automatic waking after 3 or more agents reply regardless of time frame."

### Proposed solution

An optional wake policy on the batch, for example on `sessions_yield` (or as a default under `agents.defaults.subagents`):

```jsonc
sessions_yield({
  wake: {
    minCompleted: 3,            // wake as soon as 3 children have settled
    settleWindowSeconds: 1800,  // or 30 min after the first completion, to collect stragglers
    maxWaitSeconds: 7200        // or 2 h after the yield, whatever has (or has not) arrived
  }
})
```

Suggested semantics:

- The requester is woken at the **earliest** of: all children settled; `minCompleted` reached; `settleWindowSeconds` elapsed since the first completion in the batch; `maxWaitSeconds` elapsed since the yield.
- A partial wake delivers **all results finished so far in one turn**, plus a list of the children still running (run id, label, elapsed time), so the requester can decide to wait again, steer or cancel.
- Children that are still running are **not** cancelled by the wake or by `maxWaitSeconds` (that stays the job of `runTimeoutSeconds`). They form the remainder of the batch; a further `sessions_yield` waits on them under the same or a new policy.
- Omitting `wake` keeps today's behaviour (all settled).
- Each result is delivered exactly once across partial wakes.

### Alternatives considered

- **Collector children + `agents_wait`:** returns at the first completion or a timeout capped at `waitTimeoutSecondsMax` (600 s), and the requester's turn has to stay open and loop. That is still a model step per return, and on CLI backends a long open turn runs into the no-output watchdog.
- **A cheaper "lead" subagent in the middle** that absorbs the irregular wakes and reports up once. This works today with nesting and is what we will do meanwhile, but it adds a model, a context and a failure point purely to implement a timing rule the gateway could apply without any tokens.
- **A scheduled automation that polls `subagents`** and wakes the requester by rule. Possible, but it is per-user scaffolding, and it races the built-in completion delivery.

### Impact

- Affected: anyone running an orchestrator/worker split, especially with a costly orchestrator model and 5+ workers of uneven duration.
- Severity: medium (cost and latency, not correctness).
- Frequency: every fan-out.
- Consequence: either many full-context wakes of the most expensive model, or finished results sitting unread until the slowest worker ends.

### Evidence/examples

- `docs/tools/subagents/announce.md`: "After `sessions_yield`, the frozen batch waits for its own children and their descendants to settle."; "ordinary siblings retain their individual completion delivery."
- `docs/tools/swarm.md`: "`agents_wait` provides the same first-completion boundary: it returns as soon as at least one requested run completes, or when the bounded timeout expires."; `waitTimeoutSecondsMax` default 600.
- Related, broader, closed as stale (not as fixed or rejected): #150598, whose rule 3 ("Coalesce and dedupe. N completions arriving together should surface as one summary decision point, not N wake-ups") is the same need. This request is the narrower, configurable form of it.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

### Additional information

Observed on OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (59cb447), Linux, claude-cli runtime for the orchestrator. Should stay backward compatible: no policy means current behaviour.

### Summary
`openclaw hooks enable` / `disable` refuse to run while the local Gateway owns the state, although `docs/cli/hooks.md` describes hot-reload behaviour for exactly that case and `openclaw config set` applies the same change to the running Gateway without a restart.

### Problem to solve
With the Gateway running (2026.11.1, 4ffdd20, Linux x64, systemd user service):

- `openclaw hooks enable <hook>` fails with `This operation requires exclusive offline state ownership` (exit 1, nothing written).
- `openclaw config set hooks.internal.entries.<hook>.enabled true` succeeds against the same running Gateway, logs `[reload] config hot reload applied (hooks.internal.entries.<hook>)`, and the hook fires on the next event.
- `docs/cli/hooks.md` ("Enable a hook") says: "The running Gateway reloads the selection in `hybrid` mode." That reads as if the command works while the Gateway runs.

In code, `src/cli/hooks-cli.ts` runs enable/disable through `runWithLocalStateOwner({ method: "hooks.enable|disable", onForeignOwner: "refuse" })`; the refusal text comes from `src/cli/local-state-owner.ts`. Unchanged on main as of 2026-11-11.

I understand that offline state ownership is deliberate (see #195309). This request is about the dedicated command being stricter than the supported online path, and the docs pointing the other way.

### Proposed solution
Either of these, in order of preference:
1. When a running Gateway owns the state, route the mutation through the existing `config.set` / `config.patch` RPC for `hooks.internal.entries.<key>.enabled` (and `hooks.internal.enabled` where needed), and keep the local write when no Gateway owns the state. Hot reload already handles the rest.
2. Minimum: make the refusal name the online alternative, e.g. `Gateway is running; use: openclaw config set hooks.internal.entries.<key>.enabled true`, and align `docs/cli/hooks.md` with the actual behaviour.

### Alternatives considered
- Use `config set` directly: works today and is our workaround. The request is to make the dedicated command and its docs consistent with it.
- Stopping the Gateway to run `hooks enable`: works, but costs a restart that the config path shows is unnecessary.

### Impact
Operators follow the docs, hit the refusal, and either restart the Gateway unnecessarily or edit config by hand. The error message gives no hint that an online path exists.

### Evidence/examples
1. Gateway running, managed hook present in `~/.openclaw/hooks/<hook>/`.
2. `openclaw hooks enable <hook>` gives `This operation requires exclusive offline state ownership`.
3. `openclaw config set hooks.internal.entries.<hook>.enabled true` gives `[reload] config hot reload applied (hooks.internal.entries.<hook>)` in the Gateway log; the hook fires on the next matching event, no restart.

Related: #195309 (offline-ownership refusal wording for `memory status`), #197086 (status output does not show hook selection).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?
No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information
Filed separately from #197086 on purpose, so that a design decision on this one does not hold up the status fix.

🤖 Investigated and drafted by kumo (AI agent) on behalf of @bitfroest.

issues.body:
## Summary
On **2026.11.5** (e13cf15), Node v24.22.2, Linux x64 (Ubuntu, systemd user service, default Node runtime), the Gateway's spawn broker keeps dying after about 1–2 days of uptime and **is never restarted**. From then on, every brokered spawn fails with `Spawn broker is unavailable` until the whole Gateway is restarted. That includes exec, stdio MCP startup, claude-cli backend turns, cron script triggers and the SQLite read-only worker.

This looks related to #173222 (owned map stuck at 256 dead PIDs → `request capacity exceeded`), which was closed on 2026-10-15. Three of our five incidents start with exactly that signature. The newest one has no precursor at all.

`docs/gateway/background-process.md` says: *"After the broker first becomes ready, broker loss fails affected commands rather than rerunning them; later commands use the restarted broker."* In practice no restarted broker ever appears. No `spawn broker ready` line is logged until the Gateway process is replaced.

## Incidents (same host, 9 days)
| First failure (CT) | Gateway uptime at failure | First signature |
|---|---|---|
| 11-10 23:06 | ~1 day | `Spawn broker is unavailable` (then `request capacity exceeded` on 11-11) |
| 11-12 22:26 | ~1.7 days | `stdio startup cleanup did not confirm closure \| Spawn broker request capacity exceeded` |
| 11-16 04:53 | ~1.4 days | `Spawn broker request capacity exceeded; stdio startup cleanup also did not confirm closure` |
| 11-18 21:35 | ~24.5 h | `Spawn broker is unavailable` (no precursor) |

Every incident lasted until a manual Gateway restart. The longest unattended outage was about 43 minutes, on 11-18.

## Latest incident: logs (trimmed, hostname removed)
Last healthy activity, then the first failures. Nothing was logged in between for broker exit, signal, or crash:
```
21:35:22.860 [agent/cli-backend] cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5 activeSessions=2
21:35:23.4xx [ws] client connected ... (x8, gateway-client backend operators)
21:35:27.494 [process/supervisor] spawn failed: runId=neat-sable:78a0cbfd2ffc reason=SpawnBrokerError: Spawn broker is unavailable
21:35:29.312 [process/supervisor] spawn failed: runId=clear-shell:78a0cbfd2ffc reason=SpawnBrokerError: Spawn broker is unavailable
21:36:12.449 [bundle-mcp] failed to start server "<stdio-mcp-1>": Spawn broker is unavailable; stdio startup cleanup also did not confirm closure, so restart the Gateway before retrying | ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE
21:36:12.524 [agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli ... error=Spawn broker is unavailable; ... | ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE
21:46:12.643 [gateway] database page-cache warm failed (state): Error: SQLite read-only worker failed to start (executable /usr/bin/node, cwd ~): Spawn broker is unavailable
22:01:00.540 [process/supervisor] spawn failed: runId=isolated-completion-... reason=SpawnBrokerError: Spawn broker is unavailable
... (84 such lines until restart)
22:18:46.137 [gateway] spawn broker ready pid=...   <- only after the Gateway process was replaced
```

## Ruled out
- **Kernel OOM**: no OOM or kill entries in `journalctl -k` for the window.
- **systemd-oomd**: idle, with no entries. Host has 121 GB RAM, about 26 GB used.
- **No broker exit/crash log line**: the broker disappears silently from the Gateway's point of view.

## Expected
1. Broker loss gets logged with its exit code/signal.
2. The Gateway respawns the broker (as documented), or at least fails the health check so supervisors can act.
3. Owned-map entries for exited children get reaped (the #173222 regression?).

## Workaround we're using
An external systemd timer greps the Gateway journal for repeated `Spawn broker is unavailable` / `request capacity exceeded` with no later `spawn broker ready`, then runs `openclaw gateway restart --safe --preserve-definition`.

Happy to capture broker state live (Inspector, as in #173222) the next time it happens, if that helps. Tell us what you'd like collected.

issues.body:
### Summary

Allow operators to configure the SQLite header-probe deadline for managed updates through `update.sqliteHeaderProbeTimeoutMs`, without editing installed bundles or disabling file classification.

### Problem to solve

This is an enhancement on top of the batching/splitting fixes, **not a report that their original all-path timeout still exists in 2026.11.3**.

During an upgrade driven by 2026.11.1 on Linux/x64 (Node 24.22.1), the old worker received 313,386 paths (~42.5 MB JSON) under one 10-second deadline. The unchanged probe timed out after 10.56 s. A complete cold-cache profiling pass took 30.52 s with no read errors, while a warm pass took 6.52 s. This led to a temporary installed-bundle workaround.

2026.11.3 already batches 4096 paths and splits timed-out batches; current main also scopes updater database discovery to declared plugin resources. Those fixes address the observed size problem. The remaining request is an explicit, supported operator control for slow storage/process startup, including the final single-path probe. We have not reproduced a new header timeout on 2026.11.3.

### Proposed solution

Add an optional positive integer `update.sqliteHeaderProbeTimeoutMs`, defaulting to 10000 ms:

```json
{
  "update": {
    "sqliteHeaderProbeTimeoutMs": 30000
  }
}
```

- Deadline is per worker invocation, including retries/split batches; it is not a total update deadline.
- Apply it consistently to update engine admission/database discovery and migration filesystem capture, including late single-file classification and worker serialization.
- Resolve it at the existing update/config owner and pass a scalar explicitly; no live config reads inside the header worker, no process-global override.
- Preserve existing batching/splitting, isolated execution, no-follow/regular-file guards, complete-result validation, and failure behavior.
- No `0`/unlimited/skip-check mode. Standalone backup keeps its existing default unless its own contract is explicitly extended.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Keep automatic batching/splitting only:** good default, already implemented; a final individual probe still has a fixed deadline.
2. **Delete the check or classify only by extension:** unsafe for managed/opaque SQLite stores with nonstandard names; full archive creation needs consistent SQLite handling and WAL/ownership checks.
3. **Increase the hard-coded constant:** changes all installations and gives the operator no durable control.
4. **Patch dist locally:** overwritten on update and difficult to audit.

### Impact

Affected: operators of managed installations on slow or heavily loaded storage.
Severity: operator-control enhancement; no current-release timeout failure claimed.
Frequency: environment-dependent.
Consequence: avoids unsupported bundle edits when a bounded longer probe is necessary. A larger value intentionally permits longer waits before timeout/splitting.

### Evidence/examples

Related prior work: #187150 / #187197, #194239, #193970, and #172857. Earlier reports #194850 and #194452 concern the historical whole-tree budget; this request does not reopen that fixed behavior.

Implementation will include schema rejection of invalid values, default preservation, override propagation through actual worker/archive boundaries, and unchanged incomplete-result failure.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

### Additional information

A separate post-install SQLite WAL-publication verification failure was observed after the header stage passed; this setting is not proposed as a fix for that separate failure. No private state, credentials, file paths, or recording contents are included here.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A Control UI stable update from 2026.11.3 to 2026.11.4 spent hours validating/activating, left the Gateway unavailable during the incident, and recorded a SQLite-lock failure publishing the predecessor-stop receipt; SSH intervention was needed to finish recovery.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Actual behavior

This is one observed incident, not a minimal or repeatable reproducer. The operator started the stable update through Control UI → Settings → Updates on an existing npm-global installation with a systemd user service. After more than three hours, the Gateway was unavailable and update status showed `offline-maintenance` blocked.

The failure report records `validating` for 9027.67 seconds (~150 minutes) and `activating` for 4468.76 seconds (~74 minutes). Candidate admission checks passed. Candidate Doctor lint exited 0 with 14 deferred advisory inspections; the subsequent `openclaw doctor` exited 1 with `Predecessor stop receipt publication could not be verified. database is locked`.

Rollback refused because the shared SQLite database had changed since its snapshot and restoring it would discard later writes. Package recovery was marked unverified. These failure records coexist with later recovery/readiness records; they should not be interpreted as a single instantaneous health status.

### OpenClaw version

Starting CLI: 2026.11.3 (`847611d`). Target and candidate safety-check updater: 2026.11.4. After recovery, CLI and live Gateway RPC were verified as 2026.11.4, build `d843d6af39a42cd3c30084edbeabeece732fd93a`.

### Operating system

Ubuntu/Linux; incident OS release was not captured in the supplied evidence.

### Install method

User npm-global installation (`~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw`), systemd user Gateway service. Update initiated through Control UI Settings → Updates, stable channel. Approximately 253 GiB available at snapshot-space preflight; this was not a disk-full failure.

Current shell Node: `v24.22.3` (read-only `node --version`, 2026-11-16). Incident Node version is not independently established by the retained local evidence inspected for this report; candidate node-runtime admission passed.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Additional provider/model setup details

The reported failure is in the updater/Gateway handoff, not an observed model request. Later model-login trouble was restored through unspecified steps; credential deletion and any causal connection to this update are unproven.

### Logs

Minimal excerpts from the retained update report and bounded failure JSON (private paths omitted):

```text
Update safety checks ran in the candidate updater (2026.11.4).
Admission checks: config: ok, database-schema: ok, node-runtime: ok, plugin-availability: ok.
Phases: requested (38.12s) → staging (499ms) → validating (9027.67s) → activating (4468.76s)
candidate-doctor-lint: exitCode=0; errors=0; warnings=14
openclaw doctor: exitCode=1
Predecessor stop receipt publication could not be verified. database is locked
SQLite contention call site: Error: database is locked
  at runExistingOpenClawStateWriteTransaction
Databases changed after snapshot capture: $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite;
restoring the backup would discard later writes. Current databases were preserved.
package-backup-retention: exitCode=1
Installation recovery is unverified
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No raw log attachments. The excerpts above were checked against the retained update report and bounded diagnostic JSON. Additional timing/process observations below come from the operator's incident/recovery summary, not a new reproduction.

### Impact and severity

One observed affected Ubuntu installation; the update blocked normal Gateway use and required SSH recovery. One incident is documented; recurrence rate and broader prevalence are unknown. No database loss is established. The rollback guard explicitly preserved later writes.

### Additional information

#### Observed activity and uncertainty

Earlier samples showed filesystem traversal through retained workspace/build artifacts, then a SQLite-header worker doing disk reads. A later sample showed the main updater using approximately 99% of one CPU core while other cores were idle. The last reported handoff messages concerned previous-Gateway verification and service-command ownership, but the last message is not proof of the blocking location.

The scanning hypothesis is unconfirmed. The recorded SQLite-lock error does not establish the cause of the earlier hours of CPU activity. This report does not conflate the incident with the separate `Invalid string length` SQLite-classification issue.

#### Recovery (operator-reported, not instructions)

The operator sent exactly one SIGINT to the updater and confirmed the updater/controller and direct children had exited. Status was then `publication-complete` but still failed with `post-update-failed`. SIGINT may have contributed to the final outcome; the available evidence does not exclude that possibility.

Backup existence was checked, but verification details were not recorded. The operator ran `openclaw update repair --no-restart` once as the installation owner, without sudo. Recovery reported Gateway restart/verification and finalization with warnings. Subsequent CLI and live Gateway RPC checks verified 2026.11.4. No raw SQL, database restoration, lock deletion, forced kill, or manual npm replacement was reported. Retained incomplete captures are not claimed as verified backups.

Recovery warnings included unfinished Codex data/settings migration with old data retained, deferred agent database-path repair, retained runtimes because an unrelated process's cwd was inaccessible, an unavailable tool-allowlist entry, and unresolved auth identity with the profile unchanged. Latest status reported repair finalization succeeded and superseded some warnings; not every warning was independently rechecked.

#### Desired outcome and investigation request

No grounded known-good timing baseline or deterministic reproducer is available, hence the `NOT_ENOUGH_INFO` fields above. The desired behavior is bounded update completion/failure, useful progress diagnostics, and restored availability without SSH rescue. `publication-complete` should not be confused with end-to-end success.

Please investigate prolonged validation/activation CPU activity; writer contention while publishing the predecessor-stop receipt; handoff/cancellation behavior while maintenance blocks Gateway access; and progress reporting. This report does not establish a full root cause or a released fix.

#### Related reports checked

- #193094 documents prolonged validation on 2026.10.8 → 2026.10.9 with SIGKILL; this incident instead reached 2026.11.4 activation and includes the predecessor-stop receipt error and a single operator SIGINT.
- #197083 documents a WAL-publication witness failure on 2026.11.1 → 2026.11.3, not the same recorded receipt-publication error.
- #200022 is a closely related 2026.11.3 → 2026.11.4 automated package-backup-retention report with matching build and generic failure/recovery shape; it does not include the timing, receipt-lock excerpt, or intervention sequence here. Whether it represents the same underlying defect or incident has not been established.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Setup's `config.set` flow reports completion and an optimistic hot-application hint without surfacing that plugin configuration was saved but deferred, leaving the previous configuration active.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed sequence on one running Gateway, not a new production reload test:

1. Keep admitted turns open after they have resolved tools from an external plugin that does not declare `reload.turnHandover`.
2. Through the `openclaw` Setup tool, make an authorized change to registration-captured plugin configuration. In this incident the change was an OAuth callback URL, under `plugins.entries.<plugin-id>.config.oauthCallbackUrl`.
3. Observe Setup report the configuration update as done, with “Change will apply without restarting the gateway.”
4. Inspect the saved value and the native plugin's effective configuration separately. The value is saved, but the active plugin still lacks the setting and its Connect control remains disabled.
5. Inspect Gateway logs and the administrator `plugins.inspect` retention result. Automatic application was deferred during prepare, and the previous plugin configuration remains active.

The retained-work guard itself is not claimed to be defective. Resolving a tool factory can legitimately retain its plugin before tool execution.

### Expected behavior

Setup should distinguish successful persistence from confirmed runtime application. For a deferred edit it should report **“Saved; waiting to apply”**, preserve the saved revision, and surface the reason/application condition without claiming active application.

This is the behavior already implemented for Gateway configuration RPCs and Settings by [#196570](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196570). The affected runtime includes that merged fix.

### Actual behavior

The Setup reply was:

```text
[openclaw] running: config.set
Updated plugins.entries.<plugin-id>.config.oauthCallbackUrl. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.
[openclaw] done: config.set
```

The path above is redacted; the wording is otherwise preserved. Setup did not disclose saved-but-deferred application or that the old configuration remained active. Subsequent read-only checks found the saved callback but an unchanged native connection control.

The source path also returns `applied: true` from the persistent-operation wrapper without consuming a runtime-application receipt. That is a source finding, not an additional field asserted to have appeared in the visible reply.

### OpenClaw version

`2026.11.3`, source checkout `98b4d8e10a8cb2da0dab06c831e241f8884f3a60`.

The decisive Setup/CLI files cited below are byte-identical to public commit `e230abd098ed970c30a9812813d2a77b5e80640a` (the merge of #196570). The inspected runtime includes that commit by ancestry. The relevant paths were also unchanged between this checkout and the then-current `origin/main` `0b818fd563d75e2a9c9230ad4ccbee11894b5862`.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0, arm64; Node.js 26.12.1.

### Install method

Native source-checkout installation, launched as a managed macOS LaunchAgent with Node and the built `dist/index.js` Gateway entrypoint. Relevant built modules predated the serving process startup; the Gateway PID was unchanged across the read-only diagnosis.

### Model

`clawrouter/openai/gpt-6.1-sol`

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw → ClawRouter → OpenAI.

### Additional provider/model setup details

No provider fault is attributed. The demonstrated boundary is Setup's configuration mutation result versus the Gateway's actual application state.

### Logs

Gateway log, timestamp and offset preserved:

```text
2026-11-10T22:23:02.211-06:00 [gateway/reload]
config reload deferred: PluginRuntimeApplicationError:
Plugin operation failed during prepare:
Plugin <plugin-id> reload is waiting for retained work, calls, or previous-generation cleanup;
the previous plugin configuration remains active.
Gateway generation 2: replacement not applied.;
retrying automatically after admitted work and cleanup settle
```

A later administrator inspection of the live instance returned:

```json
{
  "generation": 2,
  "acceptingCalls": true,
  "replacementPending": false,
  "disposing": false,
  "total": 9,
  "omitted": 0
}
```

Eight references were active `work` references with reason `prepared-generation-lease`, attributed to four runs; one additional 10 ms-old reference had unknown attribution during the inspection. No predecessor field or failed-cleanup record was returned. These are acquisition facts, not proof of a leak, stale lease, or actual tool execution. Session IDs, run IDs, hostnames, URLs and credentials are intentionally omitted.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Source-backed ownership chain, pinned to the public commit whose files match the affected runtime:

- [Setup's config mutation helper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e230abd098ed970c30a9812813d2a77b5e80640a/src/system-agent/operations-execution-helpers.ts#L287-L314) calls `runConfigSet` without a `localStateOwner` or runtime-application receipt.
- [The CLI configuration entry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e230abd098ed970c30a9812813d2a77b5e80640a/src/cli/config-cli.ts#L88-L102) takes the direct writer path when that owner is absent.
- [The writer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e230abd098ed970c30a9812813d2a77b5e80640a/src/cli/config-cli-runner.ts#L543-L565) saves configuration; [its success hint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e230abd098ed970c30a9812813d2a77b5e80640a/src/cli/config-cli-runner.ts#L595-L616) comes from static hot-reload classification, not observed application.
- [The Setup wrapper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e230abd098ed970c30a9812813d2a77b5e80640a/src/system-agent/operations-execution-helpers.ts#L277-L284) emits `done` and returns `applied: true`.
- In contrast, [the Gateway configuration response owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e230abd098ed970c30a9812813d2a77b5e80640a/src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.ts#L192-L234) explicitly reports saved-but-deferred outcomes and preserves the persisted configuration in structured details.

This identifies the missing feedback path, not an introducing commit. No focused isolated regression test or new production mutation was run for this report.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: one observed operator using Setup to configure a native CRM connection on a busy Gateway.
- Severity: configuration feedback is misleading at an onboarding-blocking boundary; the callback is saved but connection setup cannot proceed on the active configuration.
- Frequency: observed once, followed by repeated read-only confirmation that the saved and effective states differed.
- Consequence: the operator receives a completion message without the runtime dependency needed to explain or safely recover the still-disabled workflow. No data loss or unintended CRM mutation was observed.

### Additional information

This is a narrow remaining Setup feedback gap, not a duplicate assertion that every loaded plugin is always retained:

- [#195478](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/195478) describes the earlier registry-wide retention problem.
- [#196570](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196570) is merged and is present in the affected checkout. It narrows retention to resolved/invoked capabilities and gives Gateway config RPCs/Settings deferred-application feedback. The Setup/direct-writer route above still does not consume that outcome.
- The plugin's lack of handover opt-in does not authorize bypassing retained work. This report requests truthful saved-versus-active feedback, not forced release, concurrent generations, or interruption of admitted turns.
- Regression status and introducing change: `NOT_ENOUGH_INFO`.

Suggested isolated regression coverage, not executed here: resolve a non-handover probe tool, hold its turn, change registration-captured configuration through Setup's approved `config.set`, and assert that the result exposes deferred application while the old runtime remains active; then release the holder naturally and verify eventual application. Include an unused/denied-tool control that acquires no plugin work retention.

issues.body:
### Summary

A completed automation run should keep a bounded record of what it actually produced — stdout/stderr plus the payload's returned value — and Run history should let an operator expand the row to read it.

### Problem to solve

Script-payload automation runs retain only the string their payload returns as `notify`. stdout/stderr are discarded, so an operator cannot see what a run actually did or why it produced nothing.

Verified on 2026.11.5 (Linux arm64) with controlled probe jobs (one run each, then removed):

- delivery mode does not affect capture: an announce job and a not-requested job stored identical 212-character summaries
- there is no short cap: a 2000-character return value was stored in full
- stdout/stderr are not retained: an 800-character stdout line left no trace
- a run whose payload returns NO_REPLY stores a null summary (intended silence sentinel)

Consequence: silent runs cannot be audited, so a missed alert is indistinguishable from a healthy check, and Run history has nothing to expand for these jobs.

### Proposed solution

- Retain bounded stdout/stderr alongside the payload's returned value (default 8 KB with an explicit truncation marker), coordinated with the byte caps proposed in #200047.
- Keep the existing NO_REPLY behaviour: a run that returns the silence sentinel should still store no summary.
- Redact: pass captured text through the existing secret-redaction path before persisting; store a hash-only summary when redaction is not possible.
- Control UI: expanding a Run history row reveals an Output panel for every payload kind (script, command, agent), reusing the existing transcript viewer where possible.
- CLI: `openclaw automations runs <id> --verbose` prints the recorded output for each run.
- Opt-out: `automations add --no-capture-output` for payloads that intentionally handle credentials.

### Alternatives considered

- Log inside each script: every automation reimplements rotation and formatting, and the output is not visible where the run is displayed.
- Live tail only (#186888): useful while running, nothing remains afterwards.
- Reading gateway logs: on this host journald keeps no files, so past runs cannot be audited from logs.
- Reusing the delivery summary for all output: preserves the current conflation and leaves capture, privacy and byte-retention policy unresolved.

### Impact

Affected: operators of script-payload automations, especially ones that stay silent on success and only speak on failure.

Severity: Medium — execution is unaffected, but post-hoc verification is blocked.

Frequency: Every run; in the reported setup two jobs run 48+ times per day.

Consequence: silent runs cannot be audited, alert history cannot be reconstructed, and each new automation needs ad-hoc file logging before it can be trusted. Expanding a Run history row gives no information for these jobs.

### Evidence/examples

Environment: OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15), Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit (arm64), Node 24.22.2.

Controlled probes, each a temporary script job run once and then removed
(`terminal_summary` length read from `task_runs`):

| job             | delivery      | payload return      | stored summary |
| ---             | ---           | ---                 | ---            |
| probe-announce  | announce      | notify = 200 chars  | 212 chars      |
| probe-nodeliver | not-requested | notify = 200 chars  | 212 chars      |
| probe-long      | not-requested | notify = 2000 chars | 2000 chars     |
| probe-silent    | not-requested | notify = "NO_REPLY" | null           |

- A script printing an 800-character stdout line stored none of it; only the declared
  `notify` value is persisted.
- Delivery mode made no difference to what was stored. The announce probe's run was
  marked failed (no delivery route in an isolated session) and still stored its
  212-character summary.

Related: #186888 (live output while running), #200047 (run history byte cap),
#168687 (diagnostics not rendered), #165903 (heartbeat transcript unavailable).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

### Additional information

Implementation sketch (triage only, not a full design):

- Capture: wrap payload execution so combined stdout/stderr and the returned value are collected before the delivery decision is made.
- Storage: write into the existing run detail record field already used for `terminal_summary`, so retention and byte caps from #200047 apply unchanged.
- Redaction: reuse the existing secret-redaction path; fall back to a hash when text cannot be safely stored.
- Opt-in/out: `--no-capture-output`, default capture on.
- API/CLI: include output in `cron.runs` payloads; add `--verbose` to `automations runs`.
- UI: Run history row expansion renders an Output panel for all payload kinds.
- Tests: stdout retained; truncation boundary; secret redaction; capture disabled stores nothing; NO_REPLY still stores nothing.

issues.title: Concurrent turn in a busy session aborts with 'SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite' (SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError)
issues.body:
## Summary

When a new message arrives in a session while a long-running agent turn is still in flight, the turn can fail with:

```
SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <sessionId>
```

The underlying error is `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` (or `ReplaySafeTranscriptConflictError`). The whole turn is aborted and the user sees a generic "Your request couldn't be completed" message.

This is a concurrency bug in the SQLite transcript store: two concurrent turns (or a turn plus a side question) in the same session mutate the same append-only event sequence, and the optimistic-concurrency check that guards the rewrite path trips even though neither writer corrupted the transcript.

## Reproduction

1. Open a session that runs a long task (observed: 20–30 minutes of tool work).
2. While that turn is still running, send another message into the same session (observed with `/btw`, but it is not specific to that command — a plain message triggers it too).
3. The in-flight turn aborts with `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` and the user gets "Your request couldn't be completed: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for …".

Observed session keys:
- `agent:xiao_dudu:telegram:xiao_dudu:direct:7044906239` (runId `qizi-19-1795062289160`, in flight 1601s → failed)
- `agent:main:telegram:main:direct:7044906239` (runId `qizi-15-1795061267225` → `ReplaySafeTranscriptConflictError`)

## Diagnostic evidence

The conflict is detected by the append-only history guard in the prompt-cache boundary check:

```
[prompt-cache] cache read dropped 196762 -> 256 runId=qizi-15-… request=1 for minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash
via boundary-aware:anthropic-messages;
historyRewrite(message 728 (assistant) differs from the previous request; history must be append-only;
changed fields: content.type, content, envelope.role, envelope.timestamp, envelope.runtimeContext,
envelope.runtimeContextCarrier, envelope.other["runtimeContextCarrierRetained"], envelope.api, …);
requestGapMs=33971908 promptTokens=294853
```

The guard is correct in principle — the session transcript really did change between the snapshot read and the rewrite. The problem is that a legitimately concurrent turn is treated as corruption, so the in-flight turn is killed instead of being serialized, retried, or re-read.

Relevant code paths (dist bundle, 2026.11.5):
- `session-message-rewrite-domain-*.mjs` / `session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write-*.mjs` — the guarded rewrite operation
- `session-mutation-conflict-error-*.mjs` — `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` / `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` ("SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for …")
- `session-transcript-locked-write-*.mjs` — locked write path
- `chat-transcript-persistence-*.mjs` — `rewriteAssistantTranscriptMessageByIdempotencyKey` / `replaceEvents`, the callers that hit the guard

## Notes

- The session data itself is not corrupted: `session_transcript_index_state.needs_rebuild` is 0 and `transcript_rewrite_watermarks` generation matches the indexed leaf for the affected sessions, so no repair is needed after the failure.
- Frequency on one production machine: 3 occurrences on 2026-11-17 and 6 on 2026-11-18 across 3 different sessions.

## Expected behavior

A concurrent turn should not be reported as transcript corruption. Either:
- the concurrent write is serialized (per-session write lock / queue) so the rewrite re-reads the current snapshot, or
- the conflict is retried against the fresh generation, or
- at minimum the user-facing message explains that a turn is already running in this session, instead of surfacing an internal SQLite error.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash / run failure

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On 2026.11.5, an ordinary channel user message (not a command, not a directive) that is recorded into the transcript while an agent turn is running still invalidates that turn's commit and kills it with `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` ("SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <session-id>"); the finished answer is discarded and the user gets the generic "couldn't finish this reply" notice.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15), Telegram direct chat, built-in `openclaw` embedded runtime.
2. Send a request that produces a long turn (in my case 107 s and 313 s; the agent runs `exec` against a remote host, several tool round-trips).
3. Before that turn finishes, send one ordinary chat message in the same chat (no `/` prefix), and optionally a `/status`.
4. The turn dies at commit with `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError`; no reply reaches the user.

Both incidents below were reproduced with this shape; the first occurred twice in one morning on the same session.

### Expected behavior

The running turn should complete and deliver its answer, with the later message retained as pending input for the next turn — which is what already happens when the later message is not admitted into the transcript until the turn settles (`session_pending_inputs` shows that mechanism exists).

Per #194451, a context-bearing append inside a started turn's commit window is the known failure. PR #201271 (merged to `main` 2026-11-18) addresses it for command exchanges recorded through `recordDeliveredCommandExchange`. The appends observed here are ordinary channel messages (`idempotencyKey: channel-user:v1:…`), which that change's file list does not cover, so the ordinary-message path looks unaddressed. I could not test `main` directly; this report is 2026.11.5, which predates that merge.

### Actual behavior

**Incident 1** (all times UTC, gateway journal):

```
02:54:48  inbound user request; agent turn starts (lane=main, embedded runtime)
02:59:29  inbound Telegram update (follow-up message)
02:59:50  inbound Telegram update (follow-up message)
02:59:54  user row appended to transcript, idempotencyKey=command-input:[...] ("/status")
03:00:00  lane task error: lane=main durationMs=311209
          error="SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <session-id>"
          errorName=SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError taskKind=turn
          sessionKey=agent:<agent>:telegram:direct:<peer>
03:00:00  Embedded agent failed before reply: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite
03:00:01  message dispatch completed ... outcome=error duration=313013ms
```

**Incident 2**, earlier the same morning:

```
00:06:16  agent turn starts
00:07:33  plain user message appended mid-turn
          idempotencyKey=channel-user:v1:76b4a98a… ("Ok to restart as needed for the fix")
00:07:56  /status row appended mid-turn
00:08:03  lane task error: lane=main durationMs=106877
          error="SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <session-id>"
          errorName=SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError taskKind=turn
00:08:05  message dispatch completed ... outcome=error duration=108850ms
```

The transcript rows written inside the commit window in a third sample of the same shape: `toolResult` rows at 02:59:32 / 02:59:38 / 02:59:42 / 02:59:48, then a `user` row at 02:59:54 (`/status`). Turn results and the inbound row are interleaved, so the exact single mutating append is not separable from this log level; the plain channel message in Incident 2 is unambiguous.

Same error class, same session key prefix, on the previous stable releases (2026.11.2 / 2026.11.4) for a different agent's Telegram direct session:

```
2026-11-12 16:53:08  durationMs=40667
2026-11-13 12:15:26  durationMs=541557
2026-11-16 08:35:15  durationMs=77454
```

Not context-pressure related: the affected session reports `contextTokens=1048576`, `totalTokens=437488`, `contextBudgetStatus.route="fits"`, `compactionCount=0`, and neither failing run contains a provider error.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (e13cf15), npm install, stable channel

### Environment

- OS: Linux 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 (x64)
- Node: v26.12.1
- Runtime: built-in `openclaw` embedded agent harness
- Channel: Telegram, direct chat, polling (isolated polling worker)
- Model: `ollama-cloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud` (1M context)
- Agent session: ~13.5k transcript events; long `exec` tool turns are normal for this agent
- Delivery: default; no client tools, no approval prompts in the affected turns

### Additional context

The user-visible result is a false failure: the turn's work is complete and the answer exists, but it is dropped, and the copy says "⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply". Retrying works, which suggests the answer is replay-safe and could be rebased onto the newly appended rows — the same conclusion reached in the #194451 discussion for the WebChat replay-safe variant.

Related: #194451 (command path, fixed on `main` by #201271), #192522, #176235 (backgrounded exec completion injecting a user turn, same conflict on the cron path), #148280 (self-conflict on a slow tool).

Happy to test a candidate build against this exact session and report back.

issues.body:
## Summary

On an explicit restart, the Gateway logs `gateway is draining for restart` and then sits in systemd's `stop-sigterm` state for the **full `TimeoutStopSec` window** (5m30s here) before being killed. Two periodic tasks keep firing once per minute against resources that have already been closed, each logging a failure and apparently never unregistering their timers.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1), Linux, Node 24
- systemd `--user` unit from `openclaw gateway install`, `TimeoutStopUSec=5min 30s`
- 17 plugins loaded, no channel plugins with long-lived connections

## Observed

```
19:36:59  [agents/subagent-registry] subagent run sweep skipped: gateway is draining for restart
19:36:55  [health]   refresh failed: Gateway health refresh owner is closed
19:36:56  [plugins]  workboard lifecycle sync failed: Error: Gateway request entry is closed
19:37:55  [health]   refresh failed: Gateway health refresh owner is closed
19:37:56  [plugins]  workboard lifecycle sync failed: Error: Gateway request entry is closed
19:38:55  [health]   refresh failed: Gateway health refresh owner is closed
19:38:56  [plugins]  workboard lifecycle sync failed: Error: Gateway request entry is closed
19:39:55  [health]   refresh failed: Gateway health refresh owner is closed
19:39:56  [plugins]  workboard lifecycle sync failed: Error: Gateway request entry is closed
```

`systemctl --user show` during this period:

```
ActiveState=deactivating
SubState=stop-sigterm
TimeoutStopUSec=5min 30s
```

The unit became `active` again at 19:41:35, i.e. only once the stop timeout had elapsed and systemd escalated. The subagent sweep, by contrast, correctly notices the drain and skips itself — so the drain flag is reachable; these two tasks just don't consult it or don't clear their interval.

## Expected

After the drain begins, periodic tasks whose owning resources have been closed should unregister (or check the drain flag as `subagent-registry` already does), so the process can exit promptly instead of waiting out `TimeoutStopSec`.

## Impact

Every explicit restart costs ~5 minutes of downtime rather than seconds. With `Restart=always` this also widens the window described in #144976, where a stop that exhausts the drain window is followed by an unrequested restart — these two timers look like a plausible way to exhaust it.

## Notes on related issues

- #144976 — slow drain followed by unwanted auto-restart; this report may be one cause of the slow drain, but the symptom is different.
- #101720 (closed) and #128948 (closed) — timers outliving their owner in other subsystems; same shape, different components.
- #153153 — `TimeoutStopSec` too small on installed units; here the timeout is already 5m30s and is fully consumed.

This was observed while restarting to recover from #152965, so the two came up together, but they are independent: the hang reproduces on a plain restart regardless of what prompted it. Filing separately as offered in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/152965#issuecomment-5751556093.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a multi-user Gateway, the Control UI session observer chooses its utility model and credential per agent only. It ignores the session owner's linked model account. When the agent-level auth order points at a deliberately unusable profile, every observer digest for that agent's sessions returns 401, and the observer turns itself off for the run.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Multi-user Gateway with roles. A non-default agent (call it `team`) has primary `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`. Its per-agent auth order for `anthropic` is one placeholder API-key profile, invalid on purpose, so sessions without a linked account cannot fall back to shared credentials.
2. Each user runs the agent on their own Anthropic credential, connected to their user profile. `utilityModel` is unset for the agent and in defaults, so the utility model auto-derives to `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`.
3. A user with a linked account runs a dashboard chat on that agent. The session observer is on (the default).

### Expected behavior

The observer's utility call uses the session's effective provider and auth profile. The docs already describe this for dashboard titles: "For dashboard titles, automatic utility derivation and the regular fallback use the effective session provider and auth profile" (docs/gateway/config-agents/models.md, `utilityModel`). Failing that, the observer should skip model digests when it can't use the session owner's route.

### Actual behavior

The chats themselves work on the users' linked accounts: every `claude-opus-5-5` call for these sessions returned 200. Every observer digest for the same sessions went to `claude-haiku-4-5` on the agent-level placeholder profile and got `401 authentication_error: invalid x-api-key`. After 2 failures the observer logs `session observer disabled after consecutive failures` for that run.

Observed over one day: 197 `claude-haiku-4-5` 401s and 0 successful `claude-haiku-4-5` calls, across 5 sessions owned by 3 users, with 32 `session observer disabled after consecutive failures` warnings.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.7 (c074824)

`main` reads the same today:
- `src/gateway/session-observer.ts` resolves the model with `resolveUtilityModelRefForAgent({ cfg: deps.getConfig(), agentId })`.
- `src/gateway/session-observer-completion.ts` prepares it with `prepareModel({ cfg, agentId, modelRef, useUtilityModel: true })`.

Neither call passes the session's owner or auth-profile selection.

### Operating system

Linux 6.8 (Ubuntu host, Docker container)

### Install method

npm global install, run in Docker

### Model

anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 (auto-derived utility model); sessions run anthropic/claude-opus-5-5

### Provider / routing chain

Gateway -> Anthropic Messages API directly (no proxy or router). Agent-level auth order for `anthropic`: one placeholder API-key profile. Sessions use each user's own connected Anthropic credential.

### Additional provider/model setup details

- The agent's role uses `modelPolicy.sourceAgent: <agent>` and `sessions.others: "none"`.
- Workaround we use: `agents.entries.<agent>.utilityModel: ""`. This turns off the observer's model digests for that agent; preamble headlines stay.

### Logs

```text
[model-fetch] response provider=anthropic api=anthropic-messages model=claude-haiku-4-5 status=401 elapsedMs=109 dispatcher=reused contentType=application/json
session observer disabled after consecutive failures {"sessionKey":"agent:<agent>:dashboard:<id>","consecutiveFailures":2,"error":"Isolated completion failed with stop reason error. | {\"status\":401,\"code\":\"401\",\"errorType\":\"authentication_error\",\"message\":\"401 {\\\"type\\\":\\\"error\\\",\\\"error\\\":{\\\"type\\\":\\\"authentication_error\\\",\\\"message\\\":\\\"invalid x-api-key\\\"}}\",\"provider\":\"anthropic\"}"}
```

### Impact and severity

- Affected: multi-user Gateways where users run an agent's sessions on their own linked model accounts.
- Severity: low to medium. Observer digests never appear for those sessions, and the logs fill with 401s.
- Frequency: always, on every observer digest for those sessions.
- Consequence: no status digests, and the 401 noise hides real auth problems.

### Additional information

Related: #195172 (who pays for unattended utility-model calls). We did not observe the following; it comes from reading the code. If the agent-level order held a real shared credential instead of a placeholder, the same path would send every user's observer calls to that shared credential rather than to the session owner's account.

issues.body:
## Operator problem

An operator who wants to rewind, fork, or switch a session's transcript first needs to know _where_ they can jump to. The gateway already exposes the canonical, read-only `sessions.branches.list` RPC — "Lists transcript DAG tips available for branch switching" — but there is no CLI surface for it. Today the only way to see a session's branch points is to hand-craft a raw gateway RPC call (or use the Control UI). The sibling mutating verbs (`sessions.branches.switch`, `sessions.rewind`, `sessions.fork`) also have no CLI, but they are admin writes; this request is scoped to the safe, read-only listing that any operator can run to inspect a session's checkpoint tips.

## Existing-solutions preflight

- `openclaw sessions list` lists _sessions_, not the transcript DAG tips of a single session.
- `openclaw sessions tail` streams trajectory progress, and `openclaw sessions compact` summarizes; neither lists branch/rewind points.
- A plugin cannot close the gap cleanly: branch listing must resolve the session row through the gateway's own authorization/projection path (incognito, sharing, operator boundary), which lives behind the canonical `sessions.branches.list` handler rather than a public client helper. Reimplementing that resolution outside the CLI would duplicate the gateway's `session-row` projection and authorization logic.

## Bounded outcome

Add a `sessions branches <key>` CLI subcommand that forwards to the canonical `sessions.branches.list` RPC and renders the result.

- Accepts a session `<key>` plus the shared gateway options (`--agent`, `--url`, `--token`, `--password`, `--timeout`, `--json`).
- `--json` emits the raw `{ branches: [...] }` envelope.
- Text output lists each branch tip with its active marker, `leafEntryId`, `messageCount`, and `headline`; an empty list prints a clear "No branches found" line and exits 0.
- A failed RPC exits non-zero.

### Non-goals

- No `sessions branches switch`, `sessions rewind`, or `sessions fork` CLI verbs (admin writes; separate, higher-risk surfaces).
- No changes to the `sessions.branches.*` RPC contract, schema, or authorization.
- No new root command; `sessions` already exists.

## Canonical owner and decision surface

- Canonical method: `src/gateway/methods/core-descriptors.ts:239` (`sessions.branches.list`, family `sessions-rewind`, `operator.read`).
- Handler: `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-rewind.ts:80`.
- Params/result schema: `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions.ts:693` (`SessionBranchSchema`) and `:702` (`SessionsBranchesListParamsSchema`).

This change is a pure surface: it only forwards the `<key>` + `--agent` into the RPC and formats the already-defined `branches` rows. No gateway, schema, or authorization logic changes.

## Acceptance

On current main `240d0ac7e9d3db4501c193dc09efe8d42261aa38`:

1. `openclaw sessions branches "<key>" --json` round-trips through the running gateway and prints the `branches` array.
2. `openclaw sessions branches "<key>"` prints one human-readable line per branch tip (active marker + entry id + message count + headline), or "No branches found for session …" for a fresh/unforked session.
3. `openclaw sessions branches "<key>" --agent <id>` scopes the read to the owning agent.
4. A gateway failure exits non-zero; invalid `--timeout` is rejected before dispatch.
5. Unit tests cover forwarding params, empty vs. populated output, terminal-control escaping, JSON envelope, and non-zero exit.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this? — Yes

**Version:** 2026.11.5-beta.1 (d7e4557), Control UI dashboard chat, agent tools in code mode.

**What happens:** `exec` → `ask_user({questions:[…]})` without `awaitResults: true` returns `{status:"waiting", reason:"pending_tools", pendingToolCalls:[{id:"bridge:callValue:1"}]}`. If the agent then ends its turn (after one `wait` that is also still waiting), the owner never gets an answerable card and the answer never reaches the agent. In one conversation this happened three times in a row. Each time the owner had to reply in text before the agent re-sent the question. The same call with `awaitResults: true` blocked and returned `status:"answered"`.

**Expected:** one of: `ask_user` blocks by default; a pending card survives the end of the turn and its answer is delivered on the next turn; or the result tells the model explicitly that ending the turn will cancel the question.

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, after a fresh `openclaw plugins install`, the plugin loads successfully on the **first** gateway start. Every subsequent gateway start/restart fails to load **all** plugins (third-party *and* official bundled extensions) with:

```
Error: Plugin source changed while preparing its reload; retry after the edit finishes.
```

This persists until the plugin is uninstalled and reinstalled again. I have verified with full filesystem snapshots that **zero files change** between a successful load and a failing one, so the receipt comparison appears to be a false positive rather than an actual file mutation.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Home (build 10.0.26200), x64, NTFS
- Node.js: v26.13.0
- OpenClaw: 2026.10.9, 2026.10.10, and 2026.11.2 — **all three affected** (installed globally via npm)
- State dir: default `C:\Users\<user>\.openclaw`
- Gateway: `openclaw gateway run --task-supervisor` via per-user Startup login item
- Plugin path contains **no symlinks/junctions** (verified via `lstat` reparse-point check on every path segment)

## Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install -g openclaw@2026.11.2`
2. `openclaw plugins install @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin@2.4.10` (any plugin with a build pipeline likely works; see below — official bundled extensions are affected too)
3. `openclaw gateway start` → plugin **loads successfully**
4. `openclaw gateway restart` → plugin load fails with the error above
5. Every further restart keeps failing. Only `openclaw plugins uninstall <id> --force && openclaw plugins install <pkg>` makes the next start succeed again — then the cycle repeats.

## Evidence that no files actually change

Full-tree snapshot (ino, size, mtime_ns via `os.lstat`) of the plugin project taken immediately before and after a failing `openclaw gateway restart`:

```
Snapshot A: 45593 files
Snapshot B: 45593 files
Changed: 0   (added: 0, deleted: 0, modified: 0)
```

Additional checks on this machine:

- `fs.fstatSync(fd, { bigint: true })` on the plugin entry file is fully stable: 20 independent open+fstat cycles → zero variance; also stable with 2000 file reads interleaved between two fstats.
- The official **bundled** extension `reef` (never modified, lives in the npm package's own `dist/extensions/`) fails with the identical error during `openclaw doctor`:

```
failed to load doctor contract for reef from D:\...\openclaw\dist\extensions\reef\doctor-contract-api.js:
Plugin source changed while preparing its reload; retry after the edit finishes.
```

- Since bundled extensions are also affected, this is not specific to the third-party plugin or its content.
- No `OPENCLAW_*` env flag in `dist/plugin-generation-*.mjs` disables the check (only `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS` appears).

## Observed throw sites (2026.11.2 dist, for reference)

- `plugin-generation-artifact-*.mjs`: `sizeBytes !== file.sizeBytes` and `contentHash !== expected.contentHash` receipt mismatches
- `plugin-generation-source-lookup-*.mjs`: `FsSafeError("too-large")` and `position !== sizeBytes` during read

I could not pinpoint which comparison fails, because the logged error swallows the underlying `FsSafeError` code (`too-large` / `path-mismatch`) and the failing file path — the gateway log only shows the generic message with the plugin entry point. Logging the cause chain here would greatly help diagnosis.

## Impact on Windows

- Every gateway restart permanently breaks all plugins until each one is reinstalled.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` does not help — it stops the gateway and its own plugin loads hit the same error, so the repair cannot complete.
- When the failure happens during a boot-time load, the gateway child can exit entirely (`Gateway child failed`, exitCode=1) and the supervisor does not relaunch it, leaving the gateway down.

## Workaround currently in use

Reinstall the affected plugin while the machine is idle, then start the gateway; do not restart the gateway afterwards:

```
openclaw gateway stop --force
openclaw plugins uninstall openclaw-weixin --force
openclaw plugins install @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin@2.4.10
openclaw gateway start
```

This restores the channel on the first load, every time — consistent with the receipt being regenerated correctly at install time and then mismatching on all later loads.

## Related issues

- #160959 (open): the plugin generation capture mechanism (#144252, shipped 2026.9.6) has known problems with large dependency trees — the failing plugin here bundles a full `openclaw` SDK copy (~45,600 files), the largest external plugin layout I have seen
- #141933 (fixed 2026.9.8): the same fs-guard pattern produced unbounded false "Memory source changed while indexing" retries — this looks like the same guard family false-positiving on the plugin side
- #167531 / #167516: capture performance fixes for many-small-file plugins

## Request

1. Log the underlying cause (`FsSafeError` code + failing file path) when this error is raised, so the mismatching step can be identified.
2. Investigate why the load-time receipt comparison disagrees with install-time data when no file has changed on disk (suspects: bigint stat serialization round-trip, path normalization/case differences between install and load, or hashing a different input set in the two phases).

Happy to run any diagnostic build or share additional logs.

### Summary
`openclaw update` from 2026.9.9 → 2026.11.3 fails reproducibly. The candidate gateway fails the `startupz` verification (`candidate-startup-failed`, reason `runtime-verification-failed`) and the updater safely rolls back to 2026.9.9 each time. The installed version never changes.

### Environment
- OpenClaw: 2026.9.9 → attempting 2026.11.3 (npm global)
- Platform: macOS (darwin 25.5.0)
- Node: 24.16.0
- 50 enabled plugins, all at 2026.9.9

### What happens
- Candidate gateway boots, reaches `cli.bootstrap.plugin-plan` (~7s) and `cli.bootstrap.webhook-readiness` (~10s), then **exits with code 1**.
- Step `candidate-gateway-startup` → exit 1; failing check `startupz`.
- `stderrTail` in the failure JSON is truncated — the actual exception is never surfaced. **How can I capture the full candidate-gateway stderr?**

### Ruled out (4 attempts)
- NOT system load — a retry under idle load (1-min ~5) failed identically.
- NOT a timeout — `openclaw update --timeout 240` failed identically (exit code 1 is a crash, not a hang).
- NOT one specific plugin — disabling the `slack` plugin cleared its `config: warn` admission but the candidate still exited 1.

### Suspected
Possible runtime/plugin-API incompatibility: the 2026.11.3 runtime may crash loading a 2026.9.9 plugin. Note `@openclaw/whatsapp` plugin update is gated ("requires plugin API >=2026.11.3") — a chicken-and-egg with the runtime.

### Diagnostics
A sanitized diagnostics bundle (`openclaw-diagnostics-*.zip`, generated by `openclaw triage`) is available — happy to attach or share it.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When the stored OpenAI ChatGPT (Codex) OAuth access token has expired and OpenClaw refreshes it while the host has no network (DNS lookup or connect fails), the sign-in is lost. The refresh fails with `getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN`, and the stored refresh token is replaced by the failed-refresh marker. When the network comes back, OpenClaw does not retry the refresh: the profile reads as "not configured", and the user must sign in to ChatGPT again, although the refresh token never left the host.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in with OpenAI ChatGPT OAuth (profile `openai:default`) and let the access token expire (or seed an expired profile in an isolated state directory).
2. Without network (for example `unshare -rn`, or Wi-Fi off), run `openclaw models status --probe --probe-provider openai --json`.
3. Restore the network and run the same command again (the evidence below used a loopback recording proxy to see whether a token request is sent).

### Expected behavior

Step 2 reports a temporary failure and keeps the profile. Step 3 retries the refresh with the stored refresh token.

### Actual behavior

Step 2 fails with "OpenAI Codex token refresh error: getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN. Please try again or re-authenticate." and the stored refresh token is replaced by the failed-refresh fence (expiry 1). Step 3 fails with `Auth profile "openai:default" is not configured for openai`, and no request reaches the token endpoint.

### OpenClaw version

main at 9c37f54204558bd3e146a9e300ef2ac82a88a75d (2026.11.3)

### Operating system

Linux; the code path is platform-independent

### Install method

Source checkout (main)

### Model

openai/gpt-6-astra (any model routed through the ChatGPT OAuth profile)

### Provider / routing chain

openai (ChatGPT OAuth subscription profile, Codex runtime)

### Additional provider/model setup details

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

```text
$ unshare -rn openclaw models status --probe --probe-provider openai --json
"error": "Isolated completion preparation failed: Auth lookup failed for provider \"openai\": OAuth token refresh failed for openai: OpenAI Codex token refresh error: getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN. Please try again or re-authenticate."

# network back, simulated: a new namespace with loopback only, through a recording proxy on
# 127.0.0.1:18999 that logs each CONNECT and answers 502 (openclaw = node scripts/run-node.mjs
# in the checkout); the proxy logged no CONNECT
$ unshare -rn sh -c 'ip link set lo up; node proxy.mjs proxy.log & sleep 1;
    HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:18999 HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:18999 openclaw models status --probe --probe-provider openai --json'
"error": "Isolated completion preparation failed: Auth lookup failed for provider \"openai\": Auth profile \"openai:default\" is not configured for openai."
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

See the linked pull request.

### Impact and severity

Affected: users signed in with OpenAI ChatGPT OAuth whose host loses the network while a refresh is due (laptop sleep or travel, Wi-Fi drop, DNS outage, VPN reconnect).
Severity: Medium (blocks every OpenAI request until the user signs in again).
Frequency: Always, when the refresh runs during the outage.
Consequence: A short network outage turns into a manual ChatGPT sign-in; unattended agents stay down until someone signs in.

### Additional information

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196055 fixed the same failure for MCP client OAuth: a refresh that fails before connecting is reported as not attempted, so the sign-in survives. The OpenAI ChatGPT refresh reports every transport rejection as an unknown token response, which writes the terminal failed-refresh fence.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In the Control UI sidebar, a session and the visible child session it spawned are rendered as unrelated sibling rows when both belong to the same custom group (folder). The parent/child link exists in the data (sessions.list returns parentSessionKey and childSessions correctly) but the sidebar does not show it. When the child finishes, its completion announcement is delivered into the parent chat, so the operator sees a long report about work that never ran in the conversation they have open, and concludes that sessions were mixed up.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In the Control UI, put session A and session B in the same custom group (Move to group, e.g. group X).
2. In session A, have the agent start a long task in a separate visible session (sessions_spawn with visible=true). The new session B gets parentSessionKey = A and joins the same group.
3. Look at the sidebar: A and B appear as two flat rows inside group X. No indent, no expand arrow, no child-count badge on A, no hint on B that it belongs to A.
4. Let B finish (in my case B also hit a model fallback). B completion is announced into the chat of A.
5. Open A: it now contains a long report about the work done in B, as if A had done it.

### Expected behavior

Child B is shown nested under its parent A (or at least B shows a child-of-A cue and A shows an N-child-sessions cue), whether or not they share a group. Completion announcements that come from a child session are visibly labeled with the originating child (name plus link), so the parent chat does not look like it did the work itself.

### Actual behavior

Flat list, no lineage cue. Data side confirmed with sessions.list (sanitized): A.group=X, A.parentSessionKey=main session, A.childSessions=[B]; B.group=X, B.parentSessionKey=A. So the relationship is correct in the gateway and is lost only in the sidebar projection. This matches the note in #147603 that the tree promotes categorized dashboard children to the group top level instead of nesting them. Operator impression: sessions are mixed up, the folder (group) view does not show parent and child.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)

### Operating system

Windows 11 Pro

### Install method

npm local install (app\node_modules\openclaw), Gateway on Windows

### Model

claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5-5 (fallbacks: agy-cli/gemini-3.8-flash-low, openai/gpt-6-astra)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> claude-cli -> Anthropic (not provider related)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not provider related: this is a Control UI session-tree projection problem. A model fallback did happen during the child run (openai/gpt-6-astra to agy-cli/gemini-3.8-flash-low), so the announcement text came from a different model than the parent, which made the confusion worse.

### Logs

```shell
sessions.list excerpt (sanitized, ids shortened, group renamed X):

key=agent:main:dashboard:A  group=X  parentSessionKey=agent:main:main  childSessions=[agent:main:dashboard:B]  status=running
key=agent:main:dashboard:B  group=X  parentSessionKey=agent:main:dashboard:A  (no childSessions)  status=running

sessions.list data has the lineage; the Control UI sidebar rendered A and B as flat rows in group X.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: Control UI users who organize sessions into groups and use visible spawned sessions
Severity: Medium (UX friction, misleading, no data loss)
Frequency: every time a visible child shares a group with its parent
Consequence: operator cannot tell which session did what and treats it as a sessions-mixed-up bug

### Additional information

Related issues, all different from this one: #147603 (asks for persistent spawned sessions as independent peers), #190978 (delegated work hard to follow, feature), #194762 (child-count badge anchored to the wrong row), #137107 (nested groups), #150054 and #136467 (new chats nested under the current one). Here the child IS a real spawned child and the gateway data has the link, but the sidebar drops it when the pair is grouped. Workaround (untested): keep parent and child ungrouped, or ask the agent which child session a report came from. Reported from a Windows deployment by the operator.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On Windows, `openclaw gateway start` blocks for the full 90-minute startup deadline even after the managed Gateway child has already exited with a fatal startup error. The service health waiter has a 90-second `stopped-free` early-exit grace on win32 and returns, but `postStartCheck` awaits it in `Promise.all` together with `waitForGatewayHttpReadiness`, whose only exit is the same 90-minute `deadlineAt`. The CLI therefore appears deadlocked although the service is definitively down, and the operator sees no failure for 1.5 hours.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows 11, npm-global OpenClaw 2026.11.5, Gateway installed as a Scheduled Task.
2. Make Gateway startup fail fatally. In this incident the agent database was left at schema 27 while 2026.11.5 requires 38, so the task's gateway process exited after ~20 s with exit code 78.
3. Run `openclaw gateway start` (manually, or from an agent/watchdog).
4. Observe: the CLI process tree stays alive for the full startup deadline; `openclaw gateway status` concurrently reports `Service is loaded but not running (likely exited immediately).`; no Gateway child and no listener exist on port 18789.

Observed on 2026-11-19 (local UTC+8): `gateway start` attempts at 11:40:01 and 11:42:00 were still alive at 12:04 (20+ minutes), with only 0.17–29.8 s of CPU and no listening sockets. They had to be killed with `taskkill /T /F`.

### Expected

When the managed service runtime is `stopped` and the port is `free`, `gateway start` should fail within the existing 90 s stopped-free grace and print the child's startup error (including the `openclaw doctor --fix` guidance for the schema mismatch). At minimum, cancel `waitForGatewayHttpReadiness` when the health waiter returns a terminal stopped/failed outcome, or `Promise.race` the two waits instead of waiting for both.

### Actual

`waitForGatewayHttpReadiness` polls `/healthz` and `/readyz` every 500 ms until `deadlineAt`, independently of service/runtime state, and its only cancellation path is an external abort signal. `Promise.all` then keeps the CLI alive for the full deadline.

### Source (read-only inspection of packaged 2026.11.5, e13cf15)

- `dist/gateway-startup-timing-BGts4IhB.mjs`: win32 `deadlineMs = 3 * DEFAULT_UPDATE_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS`; `DEFAULT_UPDATE_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS = 1800000` in `dist/update-run-timeouts-Byb-PlTk.mjs` → 90 minutes.
- `dist/lifecycle-C9JvC1Vv.mjs` (`postStartCheck`): `Promise.all([withCommandProcessScope(() => waitForGatewayHealthyRestart({ ..., deadline: l, timeoutMs: i })).finally(() => l.dispose()), waitForGatewayHttpReadiness({ config, port, attempts: c, deadlineAt: s, delayMs: 500, signal: getAsyncWorkSignal() })])`, where `s = performance.now() + resolveGatewayStartupTiming().deadlineMs`.
- `dist/restart-health-Cb8MkGvo.mjs`: `WINDOWS_STOPPED_FREE_EARLY_EXIT_GRACE_MS = 90000`; returns `stopped-free` after ~90 s when runtime is stopped and the port is free (`if (... o >= _ && p.runtime.status === "stopped" && p.portUsage.status === "free")`).
- `dist/restart-health-probe-Uc_1Nf6c.mjs` (`waitForGatewayHttpReadiness`): loop exits only on success, on `e.signal` abort, or when `performance.now() >= e.deadlineAt`.

There is no `--timeout`/`--wait` option on `openclaw gateway start` in 2026.11.5 to bound this.

### Logs

```text
2026-11-19T11:40:21.969+08:00 ERROR OpenClaw agent database <state>\agents\main\agent\openclaw-agent.sqlite uses schema version 27; stop active agents and run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to schema version 38 before using it.
2026-11-19T11:42:21.580+08:00 ERROR OpenClaw agent database <state>\agents\main\agent\openclaw-agent.sqlite uses schema version 27; stop active agents and run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to schema version 38 before using it.
```

```text
$ openclaw gateway status
Runtime: stopped (state Ready, last run 78, last run time 2026-11-19T03:42:16Z)
Connectivity check: failed
  connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:18789
Service is loaded but not running (likely exited immediately).
```

Processes observed at 12:04 (killed manually):

```text
PID 8372 (node, started 11:40:01) -> PID 3280 (node, started 11:40:01)
PID 2444 (node, started 11:42:00) -> PID 13120 (node, started 11:42:00)
CPU: 0.19 s / 29.8 s / 0.17 s / 11.0 s
```

### Impact

- The operator and any automation treat the CLI as hung/deadlocked and wait 90 minutes (or kill it), while the real fatal error is already known and printed elsewhere.
- This masks the actual recovery step (`openclaw doctor --fix`) and delays service restoration.
- After the agent DB was migrated v27→v38 with `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`, the Gateway started normally and `/healthz` and `/readyz` returned 200, so the wait behavior is purely a failure-path defect.

### Related

- #166004 (Windows scheduled-task Gateway readiness timeout)
- #170956 (Windows restart/update reliability)
- #194580 (older agent schema refusal / service parking; this incident bypassed parking because the schema mismatch is fatal but the CLI wait hides it)
- #153899 (Gateway drain waits out the full stop timeout; the same restart here also spent the full 300 s drain budget)
