issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

An unfinished built-in Goal remained `active` and displayed **Pursuing goal** after `sessions_spawn` failed on a retired plugin inventory and the enclosing run settled successfully, with no observed continuation owner.

This issue is scoped to the **Goal's disposition after that failed launch**, not a general repair of plugin hot reload or every Goal stall.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

The [Automatic continuation contract at the affected commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/954f1a4fea0fd69ff0f951c9ebf7f2af79b86f33/docs/tools/goal.md#automatic-continuation) says that normally completed built-in turns check the active Goal and queue a hidden continuation, while terminal errors and timeouts pause the Goal.

After this failure settles, the unfinished Goal should either retain a verifiable continuation through an existing execution owner or move to an explicit non-active state with an actionable reason. It should not remain unqualifiedly **Pursuing goal** with nothing admitted or scheduled to advance it. This report does not choose automatic retry versus explicit pause.

### Actual behavior

One production incident was observed on 2026-11-09 in a Control UI webchat session using the built-in OpenClaw harness:

| Time (UTC) | Direct observation |
| --- | --- |
| 17:07:56 | The user resumed an unfinished Goal. |
| 17:19:24 | Gateway logs recorded a plugin replacement and successful config hot reload. This precedes the inventory refusal; the exact retired inventory identity was not captured. |
| 17:25:17 | A requested final reviewer launch failed during `sessions_spawn` model verification with `Plugin inventory has retired; begin a new plugin operation.` No reviewer was admitted by this call. |
| 17:25:25 | Audit recorded the enclosing `agent.run.finished` as `succeeded`; runtime diagnostics recorded `session.ended` with `status: success`, `stopReason: stop`, no abort and no timeout. |
| Subsequent investigation | Session status was `done`, Goal status remained `active`, and the UI still said **Pursuing goal**. There was no unconsumed queued/interrupted input or saved scheduled continuation for this session. |

The three collector children admitted during this run had already ended and been collected. The failed final launch did not create another child. The parent had retained a work checkpoint with final review and later acceptance still outstanding; retaining that checkpoint did not establish a continuation.

The session's goal-state history showed no intervening user Stop/Pause, new completion, or later pause event. `abortedLastRun` was `false`, and the Goal record had no configured token budget. This was not a recorded `length` ending or timeout.

### OpenClaw version

`2026.11.1`, running Gateway build and clean installed source at `954f1a4fea0fd69ff0f951c9ebf7f2af79b86f33`.

Not retested on a newer main revision. No last-known-good version or introducing commit is established, so regression status is unknown.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0, arm64; Node.js v26.12.1.

### Install method

Managed native source-backed installation; Gateway running as a macOS LaunchAgent.

### Model

Exact provider model identifier intentionally withheld from the public report. The effective harness was the built-in OpenClaw harness, not Codex, Claude Code, or another external harness. Model-specific causality is not established.

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw built-in harness → ClawRouter → OpenAI-compatible Responses API. The observed refusal occurred in the reviewer's model-verification step before that child was admitted, not as a recorded provider request failure.

### Logs

Sanitized excerpts from separate records for the same enclosing run. Account, session, run, tool-call identifiers and local workspace paths are omitted; the records below are not presented as one original payload.

`sessions_spawn` tool result:

```text
sessions_spawn could not verify the selected model: Plugin inventory has retired; begin a new plugin operation.
```

Audit outcomes:

```text
2026-11-09T17:25:17.576Z  tool.action.finished  sessions_spawn   failed  tool_failed
2026-11-09T17:25:17.586Z  tool.action.finished  dispatch_action  failed  tool_failed
2026-11-09T17:25:25.022Z  agent.run.finished                   succeeded
```

Selected fields from the runtime `session.ended` event:

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "aborted": false,
  "externalAbort": false,
  "timedOut": false,
  "idleTimedOut": false,
  "timedOutDuringCompaction": false,
  "timedOutDuringToolExecution": false,
  "timedOutByRunBudget": false,
  "stopReason": "stop"
}
```

Separate persisted metadata observations: `session.status = done`, `goal.status = active`, `abortedLastRun = false`. Old cancelled input records were not counted as queued work.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The operator's screenshot showed the green **Pursuing goal** strip and an elapsed-age display. Private conversation context is not attached. The independently inspected server-side records above establish the stalled state beyond the UI indicator.

Source investigation boundaries, pinned to the affected build:

- [Goal eligibility](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/954f1a4fea0fd69ff0f951c9ebf7f2af79b86f33/src/auto-reply/reply/goal-continuation.ts#L122-L174) rejects several outcomes, including error-bearing payloads, and returns a boolean.
- [Initial-turn continuation caller](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/954f1a4fea0fd69ff0f951c9ebf7f2af79b86f33/src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-result.ts#L407-L433) and [follow-up caller](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/954f1a4fea0fd69ff0f951c9ebf7f2af79b86f33/src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.ts#L368-L395) do not expose that boolean as a recorded decline reason.
- [Lifecycle Goal pause](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/954f1a4fea0fd69ff0f951c9ebf7f2af79b86f33/src/config/sessions/session-run-lifecycle-projection.ts#L449-L474) applies to failed/timeout/Stop terminal classifications. The observed enclosing run was classified successful.
- [Spawn model-verification boundary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/954f1a4fea0fd69ff0f951c9ebf7f2af79b86f33/src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn-plan.ts#L88-L120) converts a model-choice preparation exception into the observed tool error.

**The exact check that declined continuation in this incident remains unproven.** In particular, the presence of a last tool error does not by itself prove that the final `EmbeddedAgentRunResult.payloads` contained `isError: true`. The hot-reload timing also does not establish the exact inventory owner or an introducing commit.

Existing focused eligibility tests were run on the affected checkout:

```sh
corepack pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/goal-continuation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 \
  -t 'preserves an existing continuation, failure or approval owner'
```

Result: exit 0, 9 passed, 74 filtered skips. This confirms current exclusion behavior, including the error-payload case. It is not an end-to-end reproduction of this production incident or proof of its decisive gate.

### Impact and severity

- Affected observation: one built-in Goal in a Control UI webchat session.
- Impact: unfinished review/acceptance work stopped while the UI continued to advertise pursuit; the operator had to notice and investigate.
- Frequency: one observed incident; repeatability and prevalence are unknown.
- No data loss or unauthorized effect was established. No operational recovery was executed as part of the investigation.

### Additional information

A deterministic reproduction has not been established. The production sequence above is directly observed; the regression scenario below is a proposed experiment, not an executed reproduction.

#### Bounded acceptance criteria

1. Establish an incident-shaped Gateway regression: an active built-in Goal, a required `sessions_spawn` refused before child admission because its inventory retired, all earlier children settled, no queued user input/approval/other continuation owner, and an otherwise normally settled parent. Include the preceding hot-reload boundary where needed to reproduce the actual failure.
2. After settlement, assert a concrete disposition: existing-owner continuation under current admission, or an explicit non-active Goal state with a reason. Do not accept `goal.status = active` with no continuation owner as success.
3. Preserve existing Stop/Pause, goal replacement/completion, budget/usage limits, queued-input precedence and genuine child/tool/approval waits. Do not replay completed or uncertain side effects to recover the Goal.
4. Make the tested disposition observable enough to distinguish a legitimate wait from a dropped continuation. Do not claim a fix solely from the existing eligibility tests passing.

No periodic watchdog, parallel pursuit scheduler, blanket acceptance of error payloads, automatic model/account switch, or broad plugin-lifecycle redesign is requested.

#### Related reports and fixes

- #167477: retired inventory persisting across later callers after hot reload. This report does not claim the inventory defect itself is new.
- #190427: already-completed children's requester settle wake fails inside a retired inventory. Here the final child was never admitted, and earlier collectors were already settled and collected.
- #195482: an unstarted background-exec completion event is dropped on self-held plugin-replacement admission. No such exec-event drop was established here.
- #187898: Goal visibility/continuation after a required child's quota failure; that incident had a future recovery job. This incident had a pre-admission spawn refusal and no saved continuation.
- #186928: active Goal loses continuation after `stopReason: length`. This incident recorded `stopReason: stop`.
- #192988: native-harness child-return/restart custody. This incident used the built-in harness and did not cross a Gateway restart.
- #187069: merged background-exec completion lifetime fix. Its merge commit `ae8db06778136216807e802080f40a2f5b3f3cc9` is an ancestor of this affected build. This is not a report that the earlier fix was missing or a claim that it caused the incident.

issues.body:
**Bug type:** Regression (worked before, now fails)

**Beta release blocker:** No

**Summary**

Since the bundled Codex moved to `@openai/codex` 0.169.0, `scripts/package-mac-app.sh` fails on main when it stages the runtime with the Codex plugin. The runtime portability check rejects `codex-voice-host`:

```
error: Nonportable LC_RPATH in .../runtime/lib/node_modules/openclaw/node_modules/@openai/codex-darwin-arm64/vendor/aarch64-apple-darwin/codex-resources/voice/bin/codex-voice-host (16777228:0:0x00): @loader_path/codex-voice-host.runfiles/_main/_solib_darwin_arm64/voice/native_link_macos_aarch64
```

`stampDesktopRuntimePlugins` already strips one leftover Bazel rpath from this binary (`@loader_path/../../_solib_darwin_*`). 0.169.0 added a second one (`codex-voice-host.runfiles/...`) that the strip does not match. 0.170.0 still ships both, on arm64 and x64.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Check out main (seen at 36ee3b3d1dc) on an Apple silicon Mac with Xcode selected.
2. Run `ALLOW_ADHOC_SIGNING=1 SIGN_IDENTITY=- OPENCLAW_SKIP_MLX_TTS=1 BUILD_ARCHS=arm64 scripts/package-mac-app.sh`.
3. Wait for "Staging official plugins codex" and the runtime verification after it.

**Expected behavior**

The app packages and the bundle is ready.

**Actual behavior**

`verify-mac-runtime.mjs` stops with the `Nonportable LC_RPATH` error above and packaging exits 1.

**OpenClaw version:** main (2026.11.5)

**Operating system:** macOS 27.2

**Install method:** source build (`scripts/package-mac-app.sh`)

**Impact and severity**

Source and dev Mac builds can't be packaged, even on branches that don't touch packaging. Release builds are not affected: with a release tag the official plugins stay external, so Codex is not staged into the app.

**Additional information**

OpenClaw doesn't need this helper. In Codex 0.169.0 only the TUI's realtime voice uses it (`codex-rs/tui` -> `codex-realtime-webrtc` -> `VoiceHost`). The app-server and exec-server don't depend on it, and those are the only Codex commands the Codex plugin starts. The "codex resume" terminal runs the user's own `codex` from PATH, not the bundled copy.

Proposed fix: leave `codex-resources/voice` out of the staged Mac Codex packages instead of rewriting the binary with `install_name_tool`. That removes the rpath strip and about 20 MB of unused GStreamer libraries from the app. I have a branch with this and a regression test that fails on main. The packaging run passes with it.

The leftover rpaths come from Codex's own packaging, so I'm reporting that to openai/codex separately.

issues.body:
## Summary

The fix from #172173 (merged 2026-10-15, "skip same-model retries for Chinese quota exhaustion") does not appear to be present in the released **v2026.10.5** bundle. Chinese usage-window exhaustion messages are still misclassified as short-window rate limits, so the runner burns the full same-model retry spiral before failing over.

Related: #172165 (closed), #173436 (closed), #172173 (merged).

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.10.5** (1b58cb9), installed via npm global on macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)
- Provider: `minimax-portal`, model `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview`, api `anthropic-messages`
- Gateway log: `~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log`

## Actual provider response

```
status=429  elapsedMs=862  contentType=application/json
{"error":{"message":"已达到 Token Plan 用量上限：请升级 Token Plan 套餐或购买积分补充用量。 (2056)","type":"rate_limit_error"}}
```

This is a periodic/subscription quota exhaustion, not a short-window throttle.

## What the release bundle still contains

`dist/retry-evidence-*.mjs`:

```js
const LONG_WINDOW_RATE_LIMIT_RE = /\b(?:daily|weekly|monthly|tokens per day|requests per day|per[- ](?:day|week|month)|usage limit|subscription|insufficient[_ -]?quota|current quota|quota[_ -]?exceeded|(?:go|free)usagelimiterror|available balance|out of budget)\b/i;
```

No Chinese usage/quota wording. Searching the whole `dist/` for `用量上限` (and its `\u7528` escape form) returns zero hits on this build.

## Observed behavior

```
transient same-model retry 1/9 … 9/9 for minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview reason=rate_limit
  delayMs=1608 … 30000
model-fallback/decision: decision=candidate_succeeded candidate=deepseek/deepseek-flash
```

Cumulative backoff is roughly 150 s **per turn**, repeated on every turn while the plan stays exhausted. Over one day the provider's `(2056)` quota code appeared **4106 times** in the log.

With a per-agent `retry.provider.maxRetries = 1` override the same probe (a trivial prompt) completes in ~9 s instead of >150 s, which confirms the retry budget is the dominant cost.

## Expected

Per the documented behavior ("Exhausted subscription, daily, weekly, or monthly usage windows go directly to eligible auth-profile or model fallback"), a Chinese periodic/quota-exhaustion message should fail over immediately, without same-model retries.

## Question

Is the release branch missing the merge from #172173, or was the fix later reverted/refactored out? Comparing `v2026.10.5...e0e08a60` reports `diverged` (ahead 3955 / behind 475), which suggests the fix commit is not an ancestor of the release tag.

A backport of the Chinese periodic-usage predicate to the 10.5 line would fix this for MiniMax (and likely other Chinese-hosted providers using 用量上限 / 额度上限 phrasing).

issues.body:
**Version:** 2026.11.5 (e13cf15), npm install, `openclaw update --tag 2026.11.5 --admission installed --no-restart --yes`, Gateway stopped for the run, Linux (WSL2), Node 26.12.1.
**State:** SQLite 6 DBs, 603.8 MiB (state 189 MiB, main agent 328 MiB, title-gen 73 MiB, 3 small agents), `~/.openclaw/credentials` 13 MiB in **3012 files** (3008 of them WhatsApp Baileys signal-store JSON under `credentials/whatsapp/default/`, 14 B to 140 KiB each), `telegram/` 2 files.
**Result:** the update succeeded, but `openclaw update` ran 5409 s (90 min) with the Gateway down; the Gateway was down 97.75 min in total (stop 07:48:02, health 09:25:47). The 2026.11.3 update on the same host took 4887 s.

## What the updater printed, and what it does and does not mean

### 1. "SQLite state schema inspection for credentials/whatsapp/default/<file>.json: 158 B, budget 301 seconds" (×3008, twice)

- **Verified in our run log** (`20261118T074732-run-2026.11.5.log`): before `Phase: requested` there is one such line per file, 3017 distinct paths (3008 WhatsApp files, `browser-extension-relay.secret`, 2 `telegram/` files, 6 `.sqlite`); the same 3008 lines appear again inside `openclaw doctor --fix` ("Preserve original state").
- **Where they come from** (2026.11.5 dist): `update-recovery-baseline-capture-DmtlIUpU.mjs:195-238` walks every protected root recursively (`readdir`, `visit()`), collects every regular file (`S`), SQLite files by header (`T`), and passes `additionalFiles: [...S.keys()]` to `createUpdateDatabaseBackup`; `update-database-backup-Rhmovy56.mjs:336,358,372-385` appends them to the database list (`T = [...discovered, ...additionalPaths, ...additionalFiles]`, sizes read in `readUpdateStateDatabaseSizes(T)`) and hands the list to `runUpdateStateInspectionWorker` as `databases`; `update-candidate-state.inspection-Buya4MQI.mjs:92` calls `resolveAggregateSqliteInspectionTimeoutMs("state schema inspection", e.databases)`.
- **Correction to how it reads:** "budget N seconds" is a **timeout allowance**, not elapsed time. `sqlite-readonly-worker-DLU0Tq7U.mjs:218-239`: `allowance = 300 s + ceil(40 × size / 32 MiB) s`, the debug line is printed whenever the allowance exceeds 300 s (so for any non-empty file), and `resolveAggregateSqliteInspectionTimeoutMs` **sums the allowances of all listed files**. For this tree that is ≈ 3017 × 301 s ≈ 910 000 s (10.5 days) as the timeout of one worker (arithmetic; the clamp `MAX_TIMER_TIMEOUT_MS = 2147e6` ms = 24.8 days, `number-coercion-D6u-4YD8.mjs:67,125-130`, is not reached). The lines are arithmetic in the parent, not work: the 3008 lines inside Doctor sit between two 10-second progress ticks (`Doctor: Preserve original state (54s elapsed)` at log line 4806 and `(64s elapsed)` at 7839), i.e. they took < 10 s.
- **So "3009 files × 301 s" is not a cost.** What it shows is that non-database files are put through the database path and that the worker's timeout stops meaning anything.

### 2. The actual time of `openclaw update` (5409 s), reconstructed from the report and file mtimes

The updater's own report (`update-reports/fb73e632-….md`): `Phases: requested (17.86s) → staging (1.59s) → validating (2212.23s) → activating (1894.33s)` = 4126 s. The log carries no timestamps, so the rest is from our wrapper's clock and file mtimes:

| Span | Duration | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| start → `Phase: requested` ("pre-phase") | ≈ 1173 s (19.6 min) | 07:48:49 start; report time 09:17:08 − 4126 s = 08:08:22 |
| – baseline capture `fb73e632…` (manifest `createdAt` 07:49:27 → manifest written 08:08:15) | 1128 s | `manifest.json` mtime; `database.databases` last write 08:07:15; `payload/` 3018 files written 08:06:09 → 08:07:44 (95 s) |
| validating | 2212 s | of which the 10 timed steps add up to 455 s (`updater-runtime-retention` 45.9, `package-install` 29.3, `candidate-state-snapshot` 48.8, `candidate-doctor` 188.4, `candidate-doctor-lint` 59.2, `candidate-gateway-startup` 76.3, small ones 7): **1757 s of the phase are in no timed step** (INFERENCE: between `candidate-state-cleanup` and `Phase: activating` the log only shows 2 × `[update/package-integrity] reader-started/settled`, `Package publication recovery`, and a 414.7 MiB `update state inspection`; where the time goes cannot be told without timestamps) |
| activating | 1894 s | `database snapshot` 884.4 s + `openclaw doctor` 524.3 s = 1409 s; 485 s untimed |
| after activating (plugin convergence, exit) | ≈ 101 s | 09:17:08 → 09:18:49 |

The same pre-phase appears in our 01:00 attempt (rolled back by us, an unrelated `managed-service-preflight` failure): `openclaw update` started 01:01:56 and failed at admission 01:23:49 = **1313 s** before any phase work.

### 3. The same DB set is copied/inspected 5 times (Verified) and two copies are very slow (Verified), the cause is unknown

Distinct full copies of the ~600 MiB DB set, from the log (sizes as printed):

1. baseline capture `~/.openclaw.update-captures/fb73e632…/database.databases`: 976.0 MiB basis, 33 progress lines, 07:49:53 → 08:07:15 (**≈ 1000 s**, DB part of the 1128 s capture; `du` of the capture dir is 615 MiB).
2. candidate canary `/tmp/openclaw-update-canary-SY1Csy`: 601.7 MiB; `candidate-state-snapshot` 48.82 s, of which the SQLite backup-API copies add up to 13.7 s (main 7.669 s, state 4.006 s, title-gen 1.678 s, 3 small 0.39 s; log lines 3212-3231).
3. `~/.cache/openclaw/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-9i2WE1`: 601.8 MiB, 13 progress lines (log line 3140).
4. activation `database snapshot` = `.openclaw.package-backup-…databases`: 603.8 MiB, **884.38 s** (`update-command-post-update-CxP92Cxl.mjs:1994`, "snapshot databases before migrations").
5. Doctor's own "Preserve original state" capture `doctor-3360b07b…`: same 615 MiB and 3020 payload files, but **103 s** (manifest 09:19:20 → 09:21:03).

Plus partial reads of 414.7 MiB (`/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-wtEgMr`), 423.5 MiB and 610.4 MiB, and ~20 `read-only snapshot for state/openclaw.sqlite: 186.9 MiB` lines.

Two numbers stand out:
- **The same 615 MiB / ~3020-file capture takes 1128 s as the updater's baseline capture and 103 s as Doctor's capture** (same host, same state, 1.5 h apart; also 95 s vs 14 s for the 3018 payload files alone).
- **`database snapshot` 884 s vs `candidate-state-snapshot` 13.7 s** for the same databases: the candidate snapshot uses the SQLite backup API (`update-candidate-state-DZ6C1C7H.mjs:386`, "copying, attempt 1, 83984/83984 pages, 5.700 seconds"); the other two go through `createUpdateDatabaseBackup`.
- Cause unknown. INFERENCE only: load on the host (other processes were running; the Gateway was stopped) or the capture's integrity/verification passes (`integrityCheck: quick`) rather than the copy itself; the log has no per-step timestamps to separate them.

### 4. Our rehearsals did not reproduce it (Verified from the rehearsal logs, capture dirs and manifests; the cause is NOT found)

Two rehearsals of the same update on a full copy of this state (cold page cache, no network, dummy `credentials/whatsapp` of 3008 files and `telegram/` placed in the tree) ran `openclaw update` in 2011 s (channels `{}`) and 1732 s (the four channels enabled with dummy tokens), against 5409 s live. The updater's phases: `19.7 / 1.6 / 508 / 1138 s` and `19.4 / 1.6 / 435 / 982 s` (requested / staging / validating / activating) vs `17.9 / 1.6 / 2212 / 1894 s` live. Both rehearsal baseline captures (`createdAt` → manifest) took **171 s and 142 s with 7 payload files**; the window's took 1128 s with 3018. Neither rehearsal log has a single `state schema inspection for credentials/...` line, although the 3008 files were in the tree.
- **What differs for sure** (capture `manifest.json`): the live capture's `roots` / `protectedPaths` include `~/.openclaw/credentials` and `~/.openclaw/telegram`; the rehearsals' do not. Those paths come from `preparePluginDoctorMigrationBackupResources({ config: sourceConfig, ... })` (`update-recovery-baseline-capture-DmtlIUpU.mjs:121-135`; `doctor-contract-registry-DV0Hx1E3.mjs:643-656`), i.e. from the plugins' doctor **state migrations**.
- **Refuted:** that enabling the channels in the config is enough (rehearsal B: channels enabled, still 7 files).
- **INFERENCE, untested:** the WhatsApp/Telegram migrations declare their paths only for state in the format they migrate; our dummy files are not recognised. If so, the 3008-file walk is a consequence of an actual pending legacy-state migration, not of the tree's size.
- Not explained by file count alone: Doctor's own capture of the same 3020 files took 103 s.
- Not explained at all: validating +1700 s and activating +756 s over the rehearsals. The named steps add up to ≈ 450 s in both; the filesystem is the same; the data volume the snapshot lines print is the same. We cannot say more without timestamps in the updater's output (ask 3).

## Ask

1. **Treat non-SQLite files as files, not as databases**: pass only files that the header probe classified as SQLite (`T`) to the database inspection list and its timeout calculation, copy the rest as plain payload. The aggregate timeout over files is meaningless (≈ 10 days here).
2. **Reuse the baseline capture / one snapshot** instead of 5 copies of the same DB set: the capture taken at the start, the `database snapshot` before migrations and Doctor's own "Preserve original state" capture describe the same generation (`sourceGenerations`); reuse it when the generations are unchanged (the code already has `doctor-capture-reuse`).
3. **Put timestamps in the update progress lines** and a per-step duration for every step of `validating`/`activating`: 1757 s of `validating` and 485 s of `activating` are in no timed step.
4. **Say what the budget lines are**: "allowance", not "budget … seconds", or log elapsed time.

Related: #151546 (state schema inspection budgets on 2026.9.x).

issues.body:
### Summary

Make the length at which Tool Search cuts a network-content result configurable, with three choices: the current 20,000 characters, a length that scales with the model's context window, or a fixed number.

### Problem to solve

`renderToolSearchControlText` in `src/agents/tool-search-control-result.ts` cuts any Tool Search result marked as network content at 20,000 characters (19,988 plus `\n[truncated]`). That covers every MCP tool and OpenClaw's own `web_fetch` when they're called through `dispatch_action`. The count covers the whole `{ tool, result }` envelope written as indented JSON, before the external-content wrapper is added. No config key changes it, on 2026.11.1 or on main.

OpenClaw's live tool-result cap already scales with the model: 16,000 characters below 100K tokens, 32,000 at 100K+, 64,000 at 200K+, and never more than 30% of the window. On a 200K+ model, a tool the model calls directly can return 64,000 characters, and the same tool behind Tool Search stops at 20,000. Tool Search is on by default when `tools.toolSearch` is unset, so most MCP and `web_fetch` calls get the lower limit.

Two cases where the model loses text:

- `web_fetch` returns up to 20,000 characters of page text by default (`maxChars` and `maxCharsCap`). With its other fields and the envelope, a long page always runs past the cut, and the end of the text is dropped.
- A paged read reports where its window ended (`next_start_line`, an offset or a cursor). When the cut falls inside the window, the model continues from that point and never sees the lines between the cut and the cursor.

### Proposed solution

One setting under `tools.toolSearch` that takes:

1. Unset: 20,000, as now.
2. Scale with context: the live tool-result cap for the active model, less room for the wrapper, so a result through `dispatch_action` can be as long as the same tool's result called directly.
3. A number: a fixed limit, at or under the live tool-result cap so that cap never has to cut a wrapped result.

### Alternatives considered

- Keeping tool output under the limit. Our own MCP server's default read size for this agent is 15,000, and its replies put paging fields before long text so they survive a cut. The model still asks for more when it wants a whole document (`max_chars` of 20,000 and 40,000 in the recent cuts), and `web_fetch`'s own default is 20,000.
- `tools.toolSearch: false`. It removes the cut, but every MCP schema goes back into every request.
- Patching the two numbers in `dist`. It works (we run 60,000 now) but has to be redone after every update.

### Impact

- Affected: agents on large-context models that call MCP tools or `web_fetch` through Tool Search, which is the default.
- Severity: medium. The model gets part of a result and can't get the rest from the same call, and a paged read can skip text without any sign.
- Frequency: one agent (local model, 320,000-token window) had 78 of 3,062 `tool_call`/`dispatch_action` results cut between 2026-10-14 and 2026-11-07, and 9 of 757 since 2026-11-03 (7 `web_fetch`, 2 from a paged read tool).
- Consequence: answers from partial pages, extra calls to re-read in smaller pieces, and skipped lines.

### Evidence/examples

Every cut result in that agent's transcripts was 19,615 to 20,307 characters long and ended in `\n[truncated]` inside the wrapper.

A skipped range: a paged read tool returned lines 1 to 49 of a 78-line file with `next_start_line: 50`. The cut left about 46 lines. The model's next call started at line 50, so lines 47 to 49 never reached it.

The code, on 2026.11.1 and main:

```ts
const bounded =
  text.length <= 20_000 ? truncateSanitizedExternalContent(text, 20_000) : undefined;
const truncated = bounded?.truncated ?? true;
const modelText =
  !bounded || bounded.truncated
    ? `${truncateSanitizedExternalContent(text, 19_988).text}\n[truncated]`
    : bounded.text;
```

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Nothing changes for anyone who leaves the setting unset.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
Upgrading a stable install that has heartbeats explicitly disabled to a 2026.11.5 beta cannot succeed without either side effects or a failure:

1. With the disabled heartbeat still configured (`agents.defaults.heartbeat: { agentId: "<agent>", every: "" }`), the candidate updater's admission check refuses the update: `Update refused: configuration is invalid ... agents.defaults: unrecognized key "heartbeat"`. The candidate's own Doctor knows how to retire this key (its docs say Doctor removes `agents.defaults.heartbeat` and `agents.entries.*.heartbeat`), but admission rejects the config before Doctor gets the chance.
2. If the operator follows the hint and unsets the key on the installed stable release, that release falls back to its default heartbeat interval. In our case 2026.11.3 immediately enabled a 30-minute heartbeat automation for the default agent, and on a second machine it created 26 system-owned heartbeat jobs within two seconds of the unset. So removing the key to satisfy the beta re-enables the very thing it was disabling.
3. With the key unset, a later attempt (2026.11.3 to 2026.11.5-beta.2) passed admission but failed in the candidate Doctor's final config validation, reporting `Unrecognized key: "heartbeat"` at `agents.defaults` and at three `agents.entries.<id>` paths, none of which existed in the authored config (`openclaw config get` reported all of them unset). The stable release synthesizes default heartbeat config at runtime while the beta does not, so the candidate may be validating runtime-materialized defaults. That part is not proven, because the updater removes the failed candidate directory.

### Steps to reproduce
- macOS 27.2.1 arm64, Node 26, npm global install, explicit multi-agent roster, SQLite state.
- Installed stable: 2026.11.4 (d843d6a), also reproduced from 2026.11.3 (847611d).
- Config: `agents.defaults.heartbeat = { "agentId": "<agent>", "every": "" }`; `openclaw health` reports `Heartbeat interval: disabled`.
- Run `openclaw update --tag 2026.11.5-beta.4 --accept-capabilities`.
- Result: `Admission checks: config: refuse, node-runtime: ok` / `Failed: candidate-admission (invalid-config)` / `agents.defaults: unrecognized key <key>`. The installed version stays on 2026.11.4 and remains healthy.
- Same result with 2026.11.5-beta.2.
- Then `openclaw config unset agents.defaults.heartbeat` on 2026.11.3: `openclaw health` changes to `Heartbeat interval: 30m (<agent>)` and an enabled `heartbeat-<agent>` automation appears.

### Expected behavior
Admission should accept the retired heartbeat keys (or defer them to Doctor) when the candidate's Doctor migrates them, so a disabled heartbeat stays disabled through the upgrade. If there is a reason admission must refuse, the hint should not tell operators to unset a key whose removal changes behavior on the installed version.

### Actual behavior
- 2026.11.5-beta.4 from 2026.11.4: `Admission checks: config: refuse, node-runtime: ok`, `Failed: candidate-admission (invalid-config)`, `agents.defaults: unrecognized key <key>`. Installed stable stays healthy.
- Unsetting the key on stable (2026.11.3) enables a 30-minute default heartbeat automation.
- With the key unset, 2026.11.3 to 2026.11.5-beta.2 passed admission but candidate Doctor's final validation rejected `heartbeat` at `agents.defaults` and three `agents.entries.<id>` paths that were not in the authored config.

### OpenClaw version
Installed 2026.11.4 (d843d6a), also 2026.11.3 (847611d); targets 2026.11.5-beta.4 and 2026.11.5-beta.2

### Operating system
macOS 27.2.1 (arm64)

### Install method
npm global, Node 26, LaunchAgent Gateway service, SQLite state

### Model
anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (Claude CLI runtime); not model-specific

### Provider / routing chain
Anthropic via Claude CLI, OpenAI Codex fallback; not provider-specific

### Additional provider/model setup details
Stable 2026.11.3 synthesizes a default heartbeat from Anthropic config defaults when none is authored; the beta's config defaults no longer do. That may be how the beta.2 rehearsal saw heartbeat keys absent from the authored file (unproven: the updater deletes the failed candidate directory).

### Logs
Redacted excerpts only; raw configs, update captures and support JSON contain credentials and are not attached.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
- Restoring the disabled heartbeat object on the stable release returns health to `disabled` and removes the extra jobs.
- In an isolated scratch state, the beta's `doctor --fix` correctly retires the disabled heartbeat object and the config then validates, so the migration itself works; the problem is ordering between admission and Doctor (and possibly runtime-materialized defaults in the rehearsal config).
- Related: #181130 (legacy heartbeat migration without blocking startup), merged before these betas; #200083 (failed HEARTBEAT.md archive write blocks the Doctor heartbeat migration), a different failure in the same migration.
- Raw configs, captures, and support JSON are not attached because they contain credentials; redacted excerpts available on request.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
With the documented env-template form `gateway.auth.token: "${OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN}"` and that variable not set in the current shell, `openclaw status` (also `status --all` and `status --deep`) exits 1 with a raw stack trace (`gateway.auth.token resolved to an empty or non-string value.`) instead of printing the degraded report that `status --json`, the object SecretRef form and `openclaw gateway status` already give.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Use this config (the pattern from `docs/gateway/configuration/environment-variables.md`):
   ```json5
   { gateway: { mode: "local", auth: { mode: "token", token: "${OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN}" } } }
   ```
2. Run `env -u OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN openclaw status`.

This is the usual situation when the token lives only in the gateway service environment (LaunchAgent / systemd unit) and the user runs `openclaw status` from an interactive shell. Password mode with `auth.password: "${VAR}"` behaves the same.

### Expected behavior
The normal status report with the gateway marked unreachable or unauthenticated and a warning that `gateway.auth.token` is unresolved, exit code 0. The environment-variables page says missing variables "stay visibly unresolved, emit a warning, and are unavailable to consumers", and `docs/cli/security.md` describes continuing with `secretDiagnostics` instead of crashing.

### Actual behavior
```
error: gateway.auth.token resolved to an empty or non-string value.
      at resolveConfiguredGatewaySecretInput (dist/credentials-secret-inputs-*.mjs:28:20)
      at async resolveGatewayCredentialsWithSecretInputs (...)
      at async resolveGatewayProbeAuthResolutionWithSecretInputs (dist/probe-auth-*.mjs:64:17)
      at async resolveGatewayProbeAuthSafeWithSecretInputs (...)
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
exit code: 1
```
`status --all` prints its `[secrets] ... continuing with degraded read-only config` lines and then crashes the same way.

### OpenClaw version
main @ 151db8d09 (package.json 2026.11.2), first reproduced at 4b077d31b; run from source

### Operating system
macOS (Apple Silicon); the code path is platform-independent

### Install method
Source checkout (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`)

### Model
Not model-specific

### Provider / routing chain
Not applicable (local CLI status command)

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
- Command config scrubbing removes the unset template value but keeps the load fact, so the credential planner reports the path as an unresolved ref. The lazy backstop in `resolveGatewayCredentialsWithSecretInputs` then calls `resolveConfiguredGatewaySecretInput`, which finds neither a ref object nor a value and throws a plain `Error` (`src/gateway/credentials-secret-inputs.ts`). `resolveGatewayProbeWarning` (`src/gateway/probe-auth.ts`) rethrows anything that is not `GatewaySecretRefUnavailableError`, and `status` does not catch it.
- Object SecretRefs (`{ source: "env", provider: "default", id: "..." }`) fail inside `onResolveRefError`, which converts the failure into `GatewaySecretRefUnavailableError`, so they degrade correctly.

### Impact and severity
- Affected: anyone using the `${VAR}` form for the gateway token or password whose current shell lacks the variable.
- Severity: the first diagnostic command users reach for crashes with a stack trace.
- Frequency: always, for that configuration.

### Additional information
Related: #68280 (preserve degraded probes for unresolved SecretRefs).

issues.body:
### Summary

Keep Claude Code's own memory (`CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/rules/`, and auto memory) out of ordinary `claude-cli` agent turns by default, with an Anthropic plugin setting to opt back in and a Doctor-guided path to import existing Claude auto memory into OpenClaw memory.

_Updated 2026-10-07: this originally proposed an opt-in setting. Reworked to a default with an opt-out after confirming the privacy-boundary problem below and the Codex harness precedent._

### Problem to solve

On the `claude-cli` backend, OpenClaw launches Claude Code with `--setting-sources user`. That keeps project-level `CLAUDE.md` files out, but Claude Code still loads its user-level memory into every ordinary turn: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude/rules/`, and its auto memory for the workspace (the `MEMORY.md` index under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/` plus instructions to keep saving there). Verified on Claude Code 2.1.282 through an OpenClaw Gateway built from current `main`.

These sit next to OpenClaw's system prompt and workspace bootstrap files, so:

- memory and rules exist twice: OpenClaw's workspace instructions and memory, plus Claude Code's own;
- OpenClaw's session privacy rule is bypassed: `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` withholds the workspace `MEMORY.md` from group, channel, cron, and subagent sessions, but Claude auto memory is keyed by working directory and reaches every session of the agent;
- the agent saves durable memory under `~/.claude/projects/` instead of the workspace `MEMORY.md` / `memory/`, where `memory_search` does not index it, OpenClaw backups do not include it, and other runtimes cannot see it;
- host-global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` rules apply to every `claude-cli` agent on the Gateway, alongside each agent's own workspace instructions.

Restricted runs already exclude exactly these surfaces through `CLAUDE_RESTRICTED_SETTINGS` in `extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.ts` (`autoMemoryEnabled: false` plus `claudeMdExcludes`). The Codex harness isolates the same way by default: `appServer.homeScope: "agent"` gives each agent its own Codex home, and sharing `~/.codex` is an explicit opt-in. Ordinary claude-cli runs have no switch at all:

- the backend-args override is gone (`agents.defaults.cliBackends` is retired), so an operator cannot add `--settings` themselves;
- a separate `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` breaks session continuity (#145309);
- process-wide Claude Code environment variables in a service drop-in work as a stopgap, but they are not an OpenClaw setting.

### Proposed solution

- Ordinary fresh and resumed `claude-cli` turns pass Claude Code `--settings` with the memory fields of the restricted profile (`autoMemoryEnabled: false` and the same `claudeMdExcludes` patterns), built from one shared field set so the two cannot drift. Restricted runs keep their stricter profile with no duplicate `--settings`; side questions already use `--safe-mode`.
- One Anthropic-owned opt-out restores the previous behavior:

  ```json5
  {
    plugins: {
      entries: {
        anthropic: {
          config: {
            claudeCli: { excludeNativeMemory: false },
          },
        },
      },
    },
  }
  ```

- Reverse migration stays operator-initiated, like Codex memory import. `openclaw doctor` lists each claude-cli agent whose Claude auto memory is no longer loaded and prints a scoped `openclaw migrate claude --agent <id> --from <that workspace's memory dir>` command, which imports only that workspace's memory into `memory/imports/claude-code/`. `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is host-wide, so it is not copied automatically; the docs say to move needed rules into the agent's `AGENTS.md` or `USER.md`.
- Paired-node runs, whose node host rejects Gateway `--settings`, keep the node's own Claude Code configuration instead of failing.

### Alternatives considered

- Opt-in only (the first version of this proposal). It leaves every existing installation with duplicated memory and the privacy bypass unless the operator knows to turn it on.
- Default-on without a reachable override (#140487 as reviewed). Its review blocked on the unreachable backend-args escape hatch; the typed plugin setting fixes that.
- Automatic migration on update. `openclaw migrate claude` without `--from` imports every Claude project's auto memory and appends `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` to `USER.md`, which would mix other projects into each agent and spread host-wide rules again.
- `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: breaks continuity today (#145309) and also separates credentials and transcripts, which is far more than this needs.
- Environment variables on the Gateway service: process-wide, outside OpenClaw config, and invisible to OpenClaw docs and validation.

### Impact

- Affected: operators running `claude-cli` agents on a host where Claude Code is also used directly, so a user `CLAUDE.md` and auto memory exist.
- Severity: Claude auto memory reaches group and channel sessions that OpenClaw keeps `MEMORY.md` out of; agent memory silently diverges from OpenClaw's memory; host-global rules leak into every agent.
- Frequency: every ordinary `claude-cli` turn.
- Consequence: knowledge stranded under `~/.claude/projects/`, manual migration when an agent moves to another runtime, and instructions the operator did not configure for that agent.

### Evidence/examples

- Real-world report on OpenClaw 2026.9.8: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140487#issuecomment-6012070440
- ClawSweeper review of #140487 (Revision 12), whose merge-risk options include approving a new default once a reachable override and installed-Claude upgrade proof exist.
- Claude Code documents both settings (`autoMemoryEnabled`, `claudeMdExcludes`): https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Additional information

Implemented in #166073, which builds on the approach in #140487 by @zijunl.

### Summary

On a PostgreSQL-backed git install at 2026.11.2 (0a9d8c71), `openclaw update --channel dev` to any main commit from caa978ca (#196392) onward is refused at `database-engine-preflight` with "PostgreSQL schema drift detected against generated DDL"; its parent 2702a966 updates cleanly from the same base.

### Steps to reproduce

Isolated install, no Gateway, disposable PostgreSQL 17.11 with `vector` + `unaccent`; local bare mirror of openclaw as the `origin` (via `url.<mirror>.insteadOf=https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git`), so the update target can be pinned.

1. Git checkout at `0a9d8c71cde1` (2026.11.2), `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build`.
2. Fresh `HOME` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` with config:
   ```json
   { "database": {
       "families": { "state": { "engine": "postgres" }, "agent": { "engine": "postgres" }, "workboard": { "engine": "postgres" } },
       "postgres": { "connection": { "source": "env", "provider": "default", "id": "OPENCLAW_TEST_CLI_DSN" } } },
     "gateway": { "mode": "local", "port": 18994, "auth": { "mode": "token", "token": "synthetic" } } }
   ```
   with `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1 OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external CI=1`.
3. `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --auth-choice apiKey --token-provider anthropic --anthropic-api-key sk-ant-synthetic --skip-daemon --skip-channels --skip-skills --skip-search --skip-health --skip-ui --skip-hooks`, then `openclaw agents add probe --non-interactive`, then `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`.
4. Point the mirror's `main` at the target commit and run `openclaw update --yes --no-restart --channel dev`.

Results with the same base and a fresh database per run:

| Mirror `main` | Result |
|---|---|
| `2702a966c3e` (parent of caa978ca) | `✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.11.3 (2702a966) (from 2026.11.2 (0a9d8c71))`, exit 0 |
| `caa978caae7` (#196392) | refused at `database-engine-preflight`, exit 1 |
| `041c3b71646` (main at 2026-11-11 01:00 UTC) | refused at `database-engine-preflight`, exit 1 |

### Expected behavior

The update to caa978ca and later activates, as the update to its parent 2702a966 does from the same base and the same PostgreSQL setup.

### Actual behavior

The update stops in `validating` at `database-engine-preflight`; the checkout and build stay on 0a9d8c71:

```
Update refused: the candidate did not prove support for database.families and the selected PostgreSQL families. Stay on the current version or choose a family-aware candidate. Candidate admission did not return a valid verdict (exit-2); the installed updater will check admission. PostgreSQL schema drift detected against generated DDL. Use a compatible OpenClaw binary or restore the matching PostgreSQL schema and anchor; do not edit schema metadata.
```

The only schema change between 2702a966 and caa978ca is the new lazy column `workspace_setup_state.bootstrap_deferred`. It was added to `src/state/openclaw-state-db-additive-columns.ts` (`["workspace_setup_state", "bootstrap_deferred", "INTEGER", true]`) and to `src/state/postgres-schema.generated/state.postgres.sql` (`"bootstrap_deferred" bigint`). Before the update, the column is absent from the PostgreSQL state schema, which is expected for a first-use column (`information_schema.columns` count 0 in all three runs).

The same refusal happened on a production install: 13 PostgreSQL stores, git checkout of main at 0a9d8c71, update target 041c3b71. The Gateway was stopped for the update; the updater refused and the Gateway was restarted on the old build. No data was changed.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.2 (0a9d8c71) installed; 2026.11.3 at caa978ca / 041c3b71 targeted

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1 (26B131), arm64

### Install method

git checkout (dev channel), `openclaw update --channel dev`; Node 24.22.2; PostgreSQL 17.11 (Homebrew)

### Model

N/A: update path only, no model turns

### Provider / routing chain

N/A: update path only

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
# mirror main = caa978caae7 (first bad)
17:38:29 PG before: workspace_setup_state.bootstrap_deferred cols=0
17:38:29 === openclaw update --yes --no-restart --channel dev ===
Update refused: the candidate did not prove support for database.families and the selected PostgreSQL families. Stay on the current version or choose a family-aware candidate. Candidate admission did not return a valid verdict (exit-2); the installed updater will check admission. PostgreSQL schema drift detected against generated DDL. Use a compatible OpenClaw binary or restore the matching PostgreSQL schema and anchor; do not edit schema metadata.
Update target: 2026.11.3 (caa978ca)
Failed: validating
Failed: database-engine-preflight — Exit code: 1; ...
17:41:52 update exit=1
17:41:52 after: 0a9d8c71cde (build-info commit 0a9d8c71cde1)

# mirror main = 2702a966c3e (parent, last good)
17:28:57 PG before: workspace_setup_state.bootstrap_deferred cols=0
17:28:57 === openclaw update --yes --no-restart --channel dev ===
✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.11.3 (2702a966) (from 2026.11.2 (0a9d8c71)); 21 warnings need attention.
17:37:36 update exit=0
17:37:36 after: 2702a966c3e (build-info commit 2702a966c3e2)

# mirror main = 041c3b71646 (current main at time of test)
Update refused: ... PostgreSQL schema drift detected against generated DDL. ...
Update target: 2026.11.3 (041c3b71)
Failed: database-engine-preflight — Exit code: 1; ...
17:24:56 update exit=1
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The message comes from `verifyPostgresSchemaDefinition` in `src/infra/database-engine/postgres-schema.ts`. That path runs when the stored fingerprint matches the live catalog but `ddl_hash` does not match. It then fails on the comparison of the live catalog against freshly generated DDL.

The bisect above holds everything else fixed: same base build, fresh database each run, and only the mirror's `main` changes.

### Impact and severity

Affected: PostgreSQL-backed installs (`database.families.*.engine=postgres`) updating to main at or after caa978ca, observed on the dev channel.
Severity: blocks the update. The install stays on the old build; no data loss was observed.
Frequency: 3/3 attempts against caa978ca or later (1 production, 2 isolated); 0/1 against its parent.
Consequence: PostgreSQL installs cannot move past 2026.11.2 on main. Each attempt also stops the Gateway for its duration (about 6 minutes in production, after the pre-update archive).

### Additional information

Last known good: 2702a966c3e. First known bad: caa978caae7 (#196392, `feat(templates): open durable chat before verified setup`). Still bad at 041c3b71646. No later commit on main touches `src/state`, `src/infra/database-engine` or `src/agents/workspace-state-store.worker.ts` as of 65367f9b74f.

The candidate-side admission failure is reported only as `exit-2`; its own stderr was not visible in the update output.

## Summary
Android can remain stuck on **Approve node access** after the host successfully approves its node capability request. The request ID flashes during polling, then becomes the literal `openclaw nodes approve REQUEST_ID`. Tapping **I have approved** briefly shows **Checking approval…** and returns to the button without finishing setup.

## Reproduction
1. Pair the official Android app with a Gateway using a fresh setup QR.
2. Enable Camera during the phone-permissions step and continue.
3. Approve the exact pending node request on the Gateway host.
4. Tap **I have approved**.

Expected: finish onboarding once this phone is approved and connected.
Actual: remain on the approval screen despite no pending request. Closing/reopening the unfinished app can return to Connect Gateway rather than resolve the approval step.

## Environment and observed evidence
- Android app version: 2026.11.40; Pixel 8a (Android OS version not captured).
- Gateway: 2026.11.4, Linux; secure remote connection.
- Gateway `node.list`: this phone is paired, connected, and `approvalState: approved`; camera capability and camera permission are present, with `camera.list` but no `camera.snap`/`camera.clip`.
- Gateway `node.pair.list`: no pending request; paired surface has the same policy-admitted command set.
- No model/provider call is needed to trigger this bug.

## Source trace
Confirmed in main at c5ef395ba7204c83240074b584e97f550a3aab7d:
- `GatewayNodeApprovalSurface.onboardingSurface()` requires every locally advertised camera command. Gateway `reconcileNodePairingOnConnect` filters commands through policy before creating the consent request. Camera capture can be withheld by default; another approval cannot make those commands appear.
- `refreshNodesDevicesFromGateway()` removes exact IDs at the start of every refresh, then restores the same ID from the response, producing flicker.
- The screen offers a copyable approve command containing `REQUEST_ID` even without a concrete request.
- The manual check also requires Compose to observe the transient refreshing=true state, which a fast refresh can conflate away.

This differs from the previously closed navigation-loop issue #100949: the current access-stage routing is already present, but approval verification does not complete.

## Impact
First-run setup can block users who enable Camera, even though the Gateway already accepted their phone. A fix should preserve Gateway approval/policy and Android permissions, not enable camera capture globally as a workaround.

issues.body:
## Summary

A newly opened empty chat can show placeholder message bubbles even though it has no saved messages. This affects ordinary empty chats as well as chats opened during Template setup.

## Reproduction

1. Open a new empty chat, or add an agent from a Template.
2. Delay the initial history response while session metadata and the composer become available.
3. Observe message-loading placeholders in the empty conversation.

Reproduced locally in the real Control UI with synthetic Gateway responses.

## Expected behavior

- Empty chats do not show message-loading placeholders.
- Existing chats with saved messages keep the skeleton while their history loads.
- When history presence is still unknown, the conversation area stays neutral until that information arrives.
- Drafts, composer controls, and history requests keep their existing behavior.

## Cause

The placeholder decision used a loading flag plus the absence of rendered messages. That cannot distinguish an empty conversation from saved messages that have not arrived yet. Boot, route-loading, and early transcript-construction paths also inserted placeholders independently.

## Proposed fix

Expose a generic `hasMessages` fact from the existing transcript metadata owner. Show message placeholders only when saved messages are confirmed to exist. Apply the same condition to transcript-construction placeholders, and keep data-free chat boot and route-loading shells neutral. Do not use Template setup state, token counts, missing previews, or session-list absence as evidence.

## Local verification

The plain empty-chat case and Template cases at 400, 820, and 1280 px fail before the fix and pass afterward. The existing-chat control retains its loading skeleton and then displays the saved message. A transcript-owner regression also verifies empty history becoming nonempty after a saved message.

issues.body:
## Summary

In the observed case OpenClaw.app 2026.11.5 was newer than the npm-installed Gateway service on the same Mac (2026.11.4), and the app's launch-time credential preparation failed because its bundled CLI refused a forward schema migration. The CLI stated the cause and the remedy: both versions, the service's install root, and `openclaw update`. The app wrote that text only to the unified log. It showed a fixed alert that names a different remedy (`openclaw doctor --fix` with the matching CLI, and restoring backup credentials) and quit when the alert was dismissed. The person at the Mac saw neither the version mismatch nor the remedy that applies. From source, the app shows the same fixed alert for every credential-preparation failure, so the same result follows whenever the bundled CLI raises this refusal. It was observed once, on one Mac.

## Runtime or environment

- OpenClaw.app 2026.11.5 (build 2611000590), the latest stable release when observed, installed in place through the app's **Check for Updates…**. The app version before that update was not recorded.
- Gateway service and the `openclaw` CLI on `PATH`: 2026.11.4 (d843d6a), a global npm install at `~/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw`, run by launchd, with `update.channel` `stable` and automatic updates enabled. Its update report from the same hour lists the shared-state database at schema 22; the 2026.11.5 source supports schema 36.
- macOS 27.2 (26B123), arm64; Node 26.13.1 on `PATH`.
- Source was read at tag `v2026.11.5` (e13cf15) and on `main` at da8fd16 (2026-11-18 UTC). The cited app code is identical in both, and the cited CLI code differs only in how the service command is read, not in the checks described below. Permalinks point at the `main` build. The documentation quoted under Expected behavior is from `main`; where the tag differs, its wording is given there.

## Steps to reproduce

This is the observed sequence. It was not minimized and not rerun.

1. On macOS, run an OpenClaw Gateway from a global npm install as a launchd service, at the Gateway baseline above, with OpenClaw.app installed for the same account and using the same state directory (`~/.openclaw`).
2. Leave the Gateway service at that version. In the observed case its own update to the app's version was failing for a separate reason, so it could not move.
3. In the app, choose **Check for Updates…** and install the app baseline above. The app relaunches.
4. A few seconds after relaunch the alert under Actual behavior appears. Choose **OK**. The app quits.
5. Read the app's unified log for subsystem `ai.openclaw`, category `credentials`, for example with `log show --last 1h --style compact --predicate 'subsystem == "ai.openclaw" AND category == "credentials"'`. The exact command used for the capture below was not recorded, and I did not run this one.

## Expected behavior

`docs/platforms/mac/bundled-gateway.md`, section "Credential recovery", says: "Credential and local runtime-pin migrations run before the app selects its Gateway runtime. Existing private keys and explicit pins are preserved; a migration conflict stops startup and shows recovery guidance." At the release tag the same file words it as "a migration conflict prevents startup and retains recovery guidance". Stopping startup is therefore documented. The guidance it shows is expected to be the recovery for the conflict that occurred.

For this conflict the project documents the recovery. The 2026.11.4 release notes, `docs/releases/2026.11.4.md` on `main`, say: "Prevents a newer CLI from migrating a database still used by an identified older Gateway service. If migration is refused, run openclaw update or use the service installation’s CLI." The bundled CLI's refusal carries that recovery, with both versions and the service root. So when credential preparation fails with this refusal, what the app shows should convey that the Gateway service is older than the app and that the Gateway must be updated through its own installation.

The same documentation section also says: "Normal migrations complete automatically; unsupported or inconsistent state requires Doctor recovery." The release tag words it as "Doctor remains the recovery path for unsupported or inconsistent source state." The fixed alert reads like that Doctor recovery. For this refusal Doctor is not the recovery: the CLI names `openclaw update`, and from source a `doctor` run from the app's matching CLI meets the same guard while the older service is installed (see Evidence; read, not executed).

## Actual behavior

The following was captured on the affected Mac; I did not run the app myself.

The alert, shown as a critical alert with one **OK** button:

- Title: "OpenClaw client credentials need recovery"
- Text: "Quit OpenClaw, run openclaw doctor --fix with the matching CLI, then reopen OpenClaw. If you restored a backup, restore its matching client credentials too."

![Alert titled "OpenClaw client credentials need recovery" with the fixed recovery text and an OK button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a464fd20-f0fc-4f87-8ebe-784d3c807321)

After **OK** the app quit. No backup had been restored on that Mac. The CLI on `PATH` was the older Gateway's CLI, not the one matching the app.

The app's unified log, with the home directory replaced by `~` and the thread ID removed:

```text
2026-11-18 13:54:38.012 E OpenClaw[57471] [ai.openclaw:credentials] Credential startup failed: Could not prepare local client credentials. [openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: Refusing a forward database schema migration: this CLI is 2026.11.5 but the Gateway service runs 2026.11.4 from ~/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw; run openclaw update (or the CLI from ~/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw).
2026-11-18 13:54:38.012 E OpenClaw[57471] [ai.openclaw:credentials] Client credentials unavailable. Run openclaw doctor --fix before reopening the app.
```

Nothing in the alert mentions the two versions, the Gateway service, or `openclaw update`.

## Evidence

- Expected source: `docs/platforms/mac/bundled-gateway.md`, "Credential recovery", on `main` ([docs/platforms/mac/bundled-gateway.md#L483-L492](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/da8fd166f5bca52a464470cf9172bdd7a58106cf/docs/platforms/mac/bundled-gateway.md?plain=1#L483-L492)), and the documented recovery for this refusal, also on `main` and absent from the release tag's tree ([docs/releases/2026.11.4.md#L207](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/da8fd166f5bca52a464470cf9172bdd7a58106cf/docs/releases/2026.11.4.md?plain=1#L207)).
- Failure source: the unified log lines and the screenshot above, captured on the affected Mac, and the app's failure handler ([apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/MenuBar.swift#L391-L418](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/da8fd166f5bca52a464470cf9172bdd7a58106cf/apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/MenuBar.swift#L391-L418)).
- Evidence provenance: supplied
- Local verification: static-proof
- Reproduction completeness: incomplete
- Missing fact: The app version installed before the update and the app's connection mode were not recorded, and the steps were not rerun from a clean setup, so it is not established whether either input changes the result. In source, connection mode selects between two routes that both call `prepare` and share one failure handler, and I found no read of the previous app version on this path.

Runtime reproduction was not run: this investigation had no disposable macOS environment with an older Gateway service, and the affected Mac was not used for experiments. The log and screenshot are the primary evidence; the source reading below shows that the app-side result follows for every such refusal.

- The launch task runs `ClientCredentialStartup.prepare` for a bundled app, directly or inside the stale-service replacement, and both routes rethrow a preparation failure to one `catch`. That handler logs `error.localizedDescription` and calls `showCredentialStartupFailure()`, which builds the alert from two string literals, takes no argument, and then calls `NSApplication.shared.terminate(nil)`. No branch inspects the error.
- `prepare` runs the bundled CLI as `doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive` and puts the CLI's error output into the thrown error ([apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ClientCredentialStartup.swift#L30-L39](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/da8fd166f5bca52a464470cf9172bdd7a58106cf/apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ClientCredentialStartup.swift#L30-L39)). That is how the refusal text reached the log line above.
- The refusal text comes from `assertGatewayServiceSchemaMigrationAllowed` ([src/state/openclaw-state-service-installation.ts#L6-L23](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/da8fd166f5bca52a464470cf9172bdd7a58106cf/src/state/openclaw-state-service-installation.ts#L6-L23)). It throws when the CLI's startup inspection has recorded an installed Gateway service, that service resolves to the same database, and the database is below the CLI's schema version. The inspection is best effort and records a service only when its version is older than the CLI's ([src/cli/run-main-service-installation.ts#L113-L129](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/da8fd166f5bca52a464470cf9172bdd7a58106cf/src/cli/run-main-service-installation.ts#L113-L129)).
- The same guard runs during CLI startup for a `doctor` invocation outside a managed update ([src/commands/doctor-update-schema-guard.ts#L456-L473](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/da8fd166f5bca52a464470cf9172bdd7a58106cf/src/commands/doctor-update-schema-guard.ts#L456-L473)). Read from source and not executed: the alert's own remedy, `openclaw doctor --fix` run with the app's matching CLI, would meet the same refusal while the older service is installed.

## Restoration check

Failing today: with the app newer than the installed Gateway service across a shared-state schema change, launching the app shows the "OpenClaw client credentials need recovery" alert with the fixed `doctor --fix` and backup text, and the cause appears only in the unified log.

Passing: in that same state, what the running app shows at launch names the cause (the app or CLI version and the older Gateway service version) and the recovery that applies (update the Gateway through its own installation, as the CLI states). It does not send the user to `doctor --fix` or to backups for this refusal. Observe this in the app itself, not only in a unit test.

Controls: the CLI still refuses the forward migration, and the app still does not migrate, stop, or replace a Gateway service it does not manage. A credential-preparation failure with a different cause, such as an invalid config file, does not show the older-Gateway guidance.

## Additional context

The Gateway stayed at the older version because its own update to the app's version was failing for a separate reason. That failure is not part of this report. It matters here only because `openclaw update` could not complete on that Mac, so the app stayed unusable.

Not asserted as a defect: I found no documented contract that the app's updater holds back or warns about an app update while the local Gateway service is older. The updater filters releases by the Gateway's update channel only ([apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/AppLifecycleSupport.swift#L212-L246](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/da8fd166f5bca52a464470cf9172bdd7a58106cf/apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/AppLifecycleSupport.swift#L212-L246)). `docs/platforms/macos.md` says Sparkle follows the Gateway's `update.channel`, and that for a manually managed local Gateway the update card updates only the Gateway. `docs/nodes/pairing-and-status.md` says to upgrade the Gateway first in a staged upgrade. In the observed case the app offered and installed its update while the Gateway service was one release behind, and the next launch was the alert above.

## References

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191503 — explains only the `client_credentials_gateway_held` case, where a running Gateway holds state during maintenance admission, and says every other credential-preparation failure keeps the generic alert. The refusal reported here is raised by the forward-migration guard without that code, so as written it would still reach the generic alert. That is read from the diff and was not run.
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186971 — introduced the forward-migration refusal and its message. This report does not question the refusal, only what the app shows for it.
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187000 — fixed the same quit for app-managed services by replacing the stale service before credential preparation. Its description keeps operator-selected Gateway versions on the failing path as an accepted edge case.
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192737 — its harness notes record this alert appearing until the Gateway on the same state directory was upgraded, say it was resolved there by `openclaw doctor --fix` with the matching CLI, and call that the documented upgrade order. In the case reported here the forward-migration guard would refuse that `doctor` run too, which is read from source and was not run.
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/190149 — the remote-primary companion variant, fixed by service replacement. Its scope is app-managed services.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: provisional
- Impact basis: On the affected Mac the app could not be opened after its own update, the alert named a remedy other than the one the CLI gave, and the cause was visible only in the unified log. Reach is limited to Macs where the app is newer than an installed Gateway service that shares its state across a schema change; it was observed once on one Mac. No data loss was observed, and the refusal itself protects state. The level is provisional because stopping startup is documented and the recovery below was not observed to succeed.
- Workaround status: unverified
- Workaround basis: The CLI's refusal says to update the Gateway with `openclaw update`, and in source the refusal no longer applies once the installed service is not older than the CLI. This was not verified: on the affected Mac the Gateway's update was failing for a separate reason, so the app stayed unusable.

issues.body:
### Summary

`openclaw config set <array>.<index>.<field> <value>` silently writes `null` holes into the config file when `<index>` is past the end of the array. For schema-less paths (for example plugin `config` objects, which are free-form), the strict schema validation that guards the `models.*` path never runs, so the corrupted file is written to disk and the command reports success.

Example with a plugin config array of length 2:

```
openclaw config set plugins.entries.demo.config.tags.5 z
```

Result: the file now contains `["a","b",null,null,null,"z"]` — three `null` entries that were never requested. Plugin code reading this array sees phantom `null` elements; any later strict schema validation on the path also fails.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a config with a schema-less array, e.g. `{"plugins":{"entries":{"demo":{"config":{"tags":["a","b"]}}}}}`
2. Run `openclaw config set plugins.entries.demo.config.tags.5 z`
3. Inspect the config file — it now contains `null` holes

### Root cause

`setAtPath` in `src/cli/config-cli-path.ts` is the only config-path mutation helper that does not check the array index against the current length. Every sibling (`getAtPath`, `unsetAtPath`, `setPathValue` in `io.write-prepare.ts`, `unsetPathForWriteAt` in `config-path-mutation.ts`) guards `index >= length`, but `setAtPath` writes `current[index] = value` directly, producing a sparse array that `JSON.stringify` serializes as `null` entries.

### Expected behavior

The command should reject an out-of-range array index with a clear error and leave the file unchanged (the same way an index that is not numeric is rejected), while still allowing append at `index === length` and the existing empty-container behavior.

### Environment

- OS: Windows
- Runtime: Node 24
- OpenClaw main (recent)

### Impact

Silent config corruption on a user-visible, documented CLI command. The `null` holes are written even though the user never asked for them, and can break plugin config parsing or later validation.

issues.body:
## Summary

When `messages.groupChat.visibleReplies: "message_tool"` is set, a group/channel turn whose model produces its answer as plain final text (without calling the message tool) is **silently dropped**. The user who directly addressed the agent gets nothing except (on recent builds) a generic "I generated a reply but could not deliver it to this chat. Please try again." notice. The work the model did — sometimes a long multi-tool-call business task — is discarded from the user's perspective and must be manually retried with an @-mention.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.1 (ad6fe23), Windows 11, Slack channel sources
- `messages.groupChat.visibleReplies: "message_tool"` (set intentionally so always-on lurking agents stay quiet in shared channels)

## Observed rate

This is not an edge case. Across ~2 days of normal business use (multiple agents, several Slack channels), gateway logs show a steady stream of:

```
dispatch-from-config: final reply suppressed by sourceReplyDeliveryMode: message_tool_only (session=agent:<agent>:slack:channel:<id> ...)
agent produced a long private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool (message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered
```

~197 events between 2026-09-04 08:02 and 2026-09-05 14:37; 13 more in the ~6h after a restart, spread across three different agents running three different models (claude-opus-4-8, claude-sonnet-5, claude-fable-5). Even strong models intermittently skip the delivery tool on long work turns, so any deployment using `message_tool` mode eats a constant low-rate reply loss. One concrete hit: an owner reviewing payroll asked a directed question, the agent completed the analysis, and the reply was dropped mid-review.

## Where it happens

`src/auto-reply/reply/source-reply-delivery-mode.ts` (`resolveSourceReplyDeliveryMode` / `resolveSourceReplyVisibilityPolicy` in `dist/source-reply-delivery-mode-*.js`): once mode resolves to `message_tool_only`, `suppressAutomaticSourceDelivery` unconditionally discards the final text. The resolver already computes `isDirectedSourceReplyTurn(...)` (mention / direct chat / explicit command) but that signal is not consulted at suppression time.

## Request

For a **directed** turn (`isDirectedSourceReplyTurn` true — the user explicitly addressed the agent) where the model produced substantive final text but made **zero message-tool sends**, fall back to delivering the final text to the source instead of dropping it. Ambient/lurk turns (not mentioned, room events, NO_REPLY sentinels) should stay suppressed exactly as today — that's the whole point of the mode.

Alternatively (or additionally): allow a per-channel override of `visibleReplies` in channel bindings, so owner-only working channels can run `automatic` while shared team channels keep `message_tool`. Currently Slack channel bindings only carry `enabled`/`requireMention`, so the policy is all-or-nothing.

Either shape turns "model forgot the tool call" from silent data loss into a delivered (or at least deliverable) reply, while preserving quiet-lurker behavior in shared rooms.
