prs.title: fix: keep the Template category when you go back from a Template
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the Templates page, someone browsing one category opens a Template to read about it and then goes back. The page returns to **All**, so they have to find and select the category again, and any search text is gone.

## User Impact

User impact: going back from a Template detail reopens the same category and search the visitor was browsing, whether they use the Back link or the browser's Back button. Leaving Templates for another page still starts over at **All**.

## Why This Change Was Made

The category and search lived only inside the Explore view, which is removed while a Template detail is shown. The Templates page now keeps that selection for as long as the visitor stays on the Templates route and hands it back to Explore when it reappears. Nothing is added to the URL or stored beyond the visit.

## Evidence

Checked in a real browser on an isolated Gateway with the Control UI from this branch, reading the production ClawHub catalog. Flow: **View all** on Research, open the first Template, then the Back link. Before is `main` at `29f2687`; after is this branch. Same 1440×1000 viewport, light theme and catalog data. The browser's Back button gives the same result in both revisions.

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Before: after going back from a Research Template, the page shows All with every category shelf](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a12dfdc5-ca23-48cb-88b2-fcdd84622285)

**After**

![After: after going back from a Research Template, Research is still selected and its Templates are listed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f6b762d-b52d-4520-8e71-6852fc4247e0)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![Before: the All chip is selected after going back](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c2e8b54-45d6-46ce-a70f-d8a82e1468ad)

**After**

![After: the Research chip is still selected after going back](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b7b2c740-b93d-4b71-8be1-9dbcd8655a26)

Tests:

- A new page test selects a category, types a search, opens a Template and returns. It fails on `main` (the page shows the overview) and passes here, where the page asks the Gateway for the same category and search without reloading the overview.
- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/agents-home/templates-home.test.ts`: 28 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep the prompt series when the bounded window drops an old compaction
prs.body:
## Problem

The prompt owner keys each system prompt series on its history: the newest compaction or reset. Each run hydrates a bounded transcript window. When the history after a compaction outgrows that window (large prompt checkpoints count toward it), the window can start after the compaction. The history id then read as `null`, the series restarted as `restarted:history`, and the system prompt, prompt suffix and tool descriptions were re-rendered. The next run could see the compaction again and flip back. Each flip misses the whole provider prefix.

## Solution

- Port of a local fix (first commit, kept with its author): when the window starts after the boundary, the newest `openclaw.system-prompt` checkpoint in the window names the history.
- Close the stale-checkpoint edge: a checkpoint written before a later compaction still names the earlier history. Each checkpoint now records the transcript boundary count (`sessionManager.getBoundaryCount()`). A checkpoint is evidence of the current history only when its count matches the current count. Otherwise the history is unknown, and the series restarts once with an id that never matches a saved series. `null` stays valid only for a session that never compacted or reset.
- The session fork pin resolves its history through the same resolver.

## Impact

- Sessions that outgrow their bounded window after a compaction keep their system prompt series and provider cache across runs.
- Existing checkpoints do not record a boundary count. In a session that has compacted, the first run after deploy whose window does not contain the compaction restarts the series once. Never-compacted sessions are not affected.

## Evidence

Tests (red on merge base `74e5127c0c3d`, green on head):
- `attempt-session-runtime-prepare.history-boundary.test.ts`: real SQLite hydration; three runs whose byte window includes, then drops, then includes an old compaction keep one series. Base: `restarted:history` on run 2.
- `session-prompt-state.test.ts`:
  - a checkpoint that predates a compaction outside the window restarts the series, and the request carries the re-rendered prompt (base: pinned);
  - a compacted session where neither window names the history does not pin (base: pinned);
  - a never-compacted session stays pinned (passes on both);
  - the ported unit test for a window that starts after the compaction (base: restart).
- Prefix-stability journey (`test/prompt-cache-prefix-stability.test-support.ts`): new step with many runs on a growing session plus a second chat compacting during a run; no unexpected prefix break. Note: this step passes on base too. The fake route did not push the compaction out of the byte window, so it guards the concurrent-compaction case, not this defect.

Real route, isolated scratch Gateway, OpenAI Responses (`gpt-6.2-astra`, embedded OpenClaw harness, `contextTokens: 24000`), same script on base and head: 3 story turns, `/compact` with a long summary, then 7 workspace edits each followed by a follow-up turn. Each edit writes a 31-37 KB prompt checkpoint, so the history after the compaction outgrows the 192 KB window.

| Request | Base cacheRead / cacheWrite | Head cacheRead / cacheWrite |
|---|---|---|
| 14 (edit 5) | 9381 / 484 | 8642 / 484 |
| 15 (follow-up 5) | **2699 / 4361** (`restarted:history`, historyId -> null) | 9126 / 2075 (pinned) |
| 16 (edit 6) | 7060 / 484 | 11201 / 484 |
| 18 (edit 7) | 7544 / 969 (second restart, historyId flips back) | after a real automatic compaction (allowed rebuild) |

Base wrote two restart checkpoints without a compaction (historyId `<compaction>` -> `null` -> `<compaction>`). Head wrote none; its only restarts follow real compactions.

Gates: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types`, focused tests above plus the touched prompt-state, runtime-prepare and foreground suites, prefix-stability journey (openai-responses) on head and base.

prs.title: fix: check a recorded data-at-risk mark before repair or the next update acts on it
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an update step fails after it may have touched state, the updater records a "data at risk" mark on that run, for example `rollback-state-unverified`. Most of these marks come from a failed read or a timeout, not from real damage, and the published 2026.10.33 and 2026.11.5 updaters keep writing them. Nothing ever checked a mark. The update report said "Keep the Gateway stopped" even when the Gateway was running. `openclaw update repair` then refused to start the Gateway for that run every time. The next `openclaw update` ignored the mark completely, and when the installation was already current it exited 0 without a word.

On a Git checkout in release mode, repair could not even get that far: Doctor refused with "the service belongs to a different OpenClaw installation", because the service starts the release launcher and the release is a separate worktree of the checkout.

## User Impact

User impact: a recorded data-at-risk mark is now checked against the state on disk. If the state is consistent, the next `openclaw update` (including an automatic or already-current one) or `openclaw update repair` prints one line, resolves the mark and carries on. Repair starts a Gateway the marked update stopped. A real inconsistency still refuses, says what is wrong and what the Gateway is doing, records the finding on the run, and names `openclaw triage` first, then the manual command. Git release-mode repair now recognizes its own service. The killed-update refusals from #201361 also name `openclaw triage` before the manual command.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One verification owner** (`src/infra/update-data-at-risk.ts`). It answers "is the state on disk consistent with the installed version?". It reuses the runtime schema preflight in a child process with one native read transaction (no database copy, safe beside a live writer), plus the existing recovery-admission readers. Findings: database newer than the installed build, database behind it (unfinished migration), unfinished update recovery, interrupted restore directory, or unreadable (unverifiable).
- **History is not rewritten.** A consistent verification records the step `finalize:data-at-risk-verified:<marked run>` on the run that did the check. Readers in `src/infra/update-run-data-at-risk.ts` treat "marked, later verified" as resolved. The marked run keeps its mark. No new field, schema or protocol. Published updaters store the mark as the `finalize:data-at-risk` step, which the current reader already decodes, so their marks are handled the same way.
- **Repair** verifies the stopping run's mark before it touches the Gateway, and also the newest unverified mark on any other recent run (Git release updates and refusals before mutation never stopped the Gateway). The managed-handoff interrupted-update path reads the same receipt before it restarts.
- **Next update**: admission runs the same check before it creates its run, so it also covers an already-current update. Consistent: one line plus the receipt on the new run. Newer state or an unreadable database: a warning, and the update continues, because its own schema checks still guard activation and updating is the fix for newer state. Any other finding refuses. The refused run records the finding for the agent that `openclaw triage` opens.
- **Messages**: update failure guidance states whether the Gateway was observed running or stopped, which version is installed and whether the update was rolled back. It says the mark is unverified and names the next step that works. It no longer says "Keep the Gateway stopped" or "keep the update installed" after a rollback. Update-path guidance that asks you to stop the managed Gateway now names `openclaw gateway stop --force`, which a non-interactive shell needs.
- **Killed-update refusals** (`update-plugin-cohort-settlement.ts`, the `refuse()` helper from #201361): every refusal now reads `... Run openclaw triage for an agent that reads this update history and settles it. By hand: <the existing command>`.
- **Git release-mode ownership** (`src/daemon/service-layout.ts`). A service that starts `openclaw-launcher.mjs` belongs to a checkout when its release is a linked worktree of that checkout's repository. This is read from `.git` files without running Git. A release that is a worktree of another repository, a copied release, and a direct (non-launcher) command for the same files all stay foreign.

<details><summary>Genuine refusals kept, and their negative controls</summary>

- Database newer than the installed version: repair refuses and leaves the Gateway stopped (owner test with real SQLite, Docker cell `inconsistent-repair`). The next update warns and continues; its target schema check still refuses a target that cannot open it.
- Unfinished migration (database behind the installed version): owner test with real SQLite; the next update refuses (`update-command-run.test.ts`).
- Unfinished update recovery / interrupted restore directory: owner tests with real fixtures; repair and update admission already refuse these first.
- Unreadable state or an unlistable state directory: reported as unverifiable, never as consistent and never as an interrupted restore.
- A service of a different checkout, a copied release, or a direct command: still foreign (`service-layout.test.ts`).
</details>

## Update behavior for published updaters

The installed updater runs first and cannot be patched. Marks written by 2026.10.33, 2026.11.5 and main are read through the same `finalize:data-at-risk` step, and the candidate's repair and next update verify them. A published updater still writes false marks (P0-0 and the catch-alls in the audit are other workers' fixes). After that, the first update or repair run by a CLI containing this change resolves the mark without user action when the state is consistent. A published Gateway's managed-update helper still logs its old text on exit 79; the helper this change ships logs "gateway left stopped: data at risk (...) recorded and not yet verified; run openclaw update repair to verify the state and restart the gateway".

## Steps still left to a person

- **Gateway left stopped by a marked update when no further update or repair runs.** The Gateway is down, so no Gateway-driven automatic path can run. `openclaw update repair` or the next `openclaw update` verifies and resolves the mark. Agent route: `openclaw triage`. Follow-up: verify the mark inside the failing update's own recovery before it decides the restart.
- **Managed handoff exit 79 (P1-4).** Not changed. Exit 79 is a contract with shipped helpers, and the helper is written by the serving (old) Gateway. Design below.
- **A real inconsistency.** By definition it needs a decision: finish a migration, restore a backup, or install a newer build. The message leads with `openclaw triage`, and the finding is recorded on the run.
- **Interrupted state restore directory.** No supported command can finish it safely; the existing docs procedure applies.

## P1-4 design (managed handoff exit 79)

The direct CLI restarts a stopped Gateway after a failure with no data risk (`update-command-failure-recovery.ts`). Under the handoff it does not, because the helper stopped the service rather than the updater (`preManagedServiceStop.stopped` is false in the child). The updater then reports `serviceRestartSafe:false`, and the helper exits 79 and leaves the Gateway down. The contract can stay: the candidate updater, running under `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_RUN_HANDOFF=1`, could take the helper's recorded `service-stop` as its own stop evidence, run the same restart and verification, and report `service: "healthy"` with `serviceRestartSafe: true`. The helper already restores nothing in that case and exits non-79. That fix lives in `update-command-failure-recovery.ts` and the handoff stop receipt, and it only helps once the installed updater contains it. It is left for the second PR so it gets its own red and green handoff proof.

## Evidence

Behavior checked, all on the exact head unless noted:

- **Owner (real SQLite).** `src/infra/update-data-at-risk.test.ts`:
  - current state is consistent beside an open `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` writer, and `prepareSqliteReadOnlyLocation` (the copy path) is never called
  - newer schema, behind schema, unfinished recovery and interrupted restore are inconsistent
  - unreadable state and an unlistable directory are unverifiable
  - Red first: the no-copy and unlistable-directory cases failed on the first implementation (it defaulted to the maintenance copy path and labeled listing errors as an interrupted restore), then passed after the fix.
- **Repair** (`update-repair-service.test.ts`, real ledger and finalization):
  - a false mark with the Gateway stopped: verified, receipt recorded, Gateway started
  - the same with the Gateway running: verified, not restarted
  - a mark on a run that never stopped the Gateway: verified once, and a second repair does not verify it again
  - inconsistent and unverifiable verdicts keep the Gateway as it was and print the exact refusal, including a running Gateway's version
- **Next update** (`update-command-run.test.ts`):
  - a consistent mark prints one line and records the receipt on the new run
  - a later update does not check it again
  - an unfinished migration refuses and records the finding on the refused run
  - newer state warns and continues
- **Guidance** (`update-recovery-guidance.test.ts`): exact text for running, stopped, rolled-back, failed-rollback and unobserved Gateways. Red on base `f5b717d232f`: 11 cases fail; green on head.
- **Git release ownership** (`src/daemon/service-layout.test.ts`, real `git worktree add`): own checkout's release owned; other repository's worktree, copied release and direct command foreign. Red on base `f5b717d232f` for "own checkout"; green on head.
- **End to end**: see the recordings section (filled in below).

Not proven: see "Not proven" below.

`autoreview` does not run on this machine; an independent read-only reviewer reviewed the diff and tests instead (findings and what changed are listed below).

prs.title: fix(gateway): prevent reply-context retention when completion is missing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long-lived Gateway may keep abandoned reply contexts alive when a reply producer never calls `markComplete()`. The process-wide registry previously held a pending-count callback that strongly retained the dispatcher closure and turn data.

## User Impact

Gateway reply-context memory can be reclaimed even when an unfinished dispatcher leaves its pending reservation behind. Shutdown/restart pending counts remain reserved until the owning completion path runs; this is a partial memory mitigation, **not** a fix for the underlying missing-completion producer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Store dispatcher-owned mutable numeric pending state in the registry instead of registering a callback that captures the reply context. Preserve enqueue, in-flight delivery, completion, settlement, and restart reservation semantics.

## Evidence

An isolated, built CLI Gateway experiment on Node 24.22.1 measured the original parent commit and corrected code with the same synthetic missing-completion workload. After GC, **16/16** synthetic contexts remained on baseline and **0/16** remained on the candidate; all **16** abandoned pending reservations remained, and an additional final reply was delivered successfully. Heap snapshots independently showed 16 synthetic marker objects on baseline versus 0 on candidate. The exact commands, caveats, and hash identities follow below. **These do not constitute a clean local full test-suite pass**: affected Gateway Vitest and local lint/typecheck attempts had unresolved failures or blockers. The current-head GitHub CI gate, dependency review, and security-sensitive review checks have succeeded; maintainer review is still required.

Related: #184140

## Problem and change

An unfinished reply dispatcher leaves a pending-count callback in the global registry. That callback can retain the dispatcher's V8 closure context, including delivery options and turn data. Replace that callback with dispatcher-owned mutable numeric state, preserving enqueue, completion, settlement, and restart reservations.

This is a **partial memory mitigation**. It does not identify or repair a producer that misses `markComplete()`; abandoned reservations deliberately remain pending. No TTL, configuration, permissions, persistence, or public SDK change.

The two redundant helper/count tests requested for removal have been removed. Existing restart coverage remains. The latest commit adds rerunnable measurement tools and formats the migrated close-test call; production logic is unchanged from tested head `91fcb5bb65a2029afa5c12a1a77dd7f95c98f139`.

## Actual built-Gateway proof — 2026-10-27

Node **24.22.1** (supported by this revision), Linux x86_64. Installed the frozen lockfile with the available pnpm 11.25.0; the repository pins 12.15.0, so this is not pinned-package-manager qualification.

Baseline: `db92acff277255f64e14866d29ebcb00592822b1` (parent of the production fix). Candidate production: `91fcb5bb65a2029afa5c12a1a77dd7f95c98f139`. Proof tools are committed at `6e21e8cc942bca17f779c8ff043cc83d256c1584`.

Both real compiled CLI Gateways reached **`/readyz` with `ready: true`**, using separate empty state/config directories, fresh loopback ports, disabled plugins/channels, and a scrubbed child environment. No model calls or real messages. The parent verified the measured PID equals the launched Gateway PID, main thread is 0, CLI entry is `dist/entry.js`, and the factory is imported through `dist/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime.js`. Worker preloads are explicitly excluded.

Workload: abandon 16 real dispatchers without completion, each capturing a synthetic 65,536-element array; yield and force GC 12 times; then enqueue a real final reply behind a delivery barrier, mark completion, release delivery, and inspect settlement.

| Observable | Callback baseline | Numeric-state candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Abandoned contexts still alive after GC | 16/16 | **0/16** |
| Abandoned dispatcher objects still alive | 16/16 | **0/16** |
| Synthetic context instances in V8 snapshot | 16 | **0** |
| Synthetic payload backing-store self bytes | 8,388,864 | **0** |
| Pending reservations after GC | 16 | **16** |
| Pending with extra delivery blocked | 18 | **18** |
| Pending after markComplete, delivery still blocked | 18 | **18** |
| Pending after extra delivery settles | 16 | **16** |
| Additional final replies actually delivered | 1 | **1** |

The **identical default regression expectation** (`alive == 0`) failed on the baseline with `AssertionError: (16, 0)` (exit 1) and passed on the candidate (exit 0). Both Gateways' actual shutdown consumer subsequently logged `pendingReplies=16`, confirming orphaned reservations were not silently discarded. The harness terminates its own Gateway after measurement; clean shutdown is not claimed.

The baseline snapshot contains this representative **strong path**, excluding weak edges:

```text
global activeReplyDispatchers Set -> table -> tracked object
  -> pending closure -> V8 Context.options -> options.deliver
  -> delivery closure context -> DispatcherRetentionProbeContext
```

The candidate snapshot has zero such marker objects. Backing-store bytes above are the synthetic arrays' self sizes, **not** whole-heap savings or dominator retained sizes. This is synthetic missing-completion fault injection through the real production bundle, not a reproduction of the incident's unknown natural producer.

### Reproduce

Install dependencies and build separate baseline/candidate checkouts. Use the same committed proof scripts for both:

```bash
python3 scripts/perf/dispatcher-retention-gateway.py /path/to/base baseline /path/to/proof
# Expected: exit 1, alive=16 against the default zero expectation.
python3 scripts/perf/dispatcher-retention-gateway.py /path/to/candidate candidate /path/to/proof
# Expected: exit 0, alive=0.
python3 scripts/perf/dispatcher-retention-snapshot.py /path/to/proof/baseline-gateway.heapsnapshot 16
python3 scripts/perf/dispatcher-retention-snapshot.py /path/to/proof/candidate-gateway.heapsnapshot 0
```

Raw snapshots/logs remain private because they can contain process data. The table and graph above contain only inspected synthetic evidence; credentials, actual endpoint addresses, and private paths are omitted.

Compiled factory identities verified from the SDK imports:
- Baseline `reply-dispatcher-loglChz_.mjs`, SHA256 `ea7a2d34a2357d2063f500b108abd1a243a7a4356f21312296223c6cfdc59bff`: callback registration.
- Candidate `reply-dispatcher-ClcrVgn2.mjs`, SHA256 `84683942aa0675de57cd951107f0031dfc32653cc416cfc8c2f00d52434dfc3e`: numeric-state registration.

## Checks and remaining gates

- Candidate `pnpm build:runtime`: **exit 0**, all build phases completed. It retained an artifact lock after an unverified child-cleanup warning; no lock was bypassed.
- Baseline runtime rebuild emitted the callback bundle and the actual Gateway reached ready. **Overall build exit 1** at runtime-postbuild: ambiguous `findSystemGatewayServices` bridge exports after seeding unchanged built artifacts. This is **not clean baseline packaging qualification**; the selected factory chunk was independently checked as above.
- Repository Gateway Vitest run: **20 passed, 36 failed, 13 unhandled errors** across 56 cases. All three existing restart-reservation cases passed. The close suite's first failure was a supervised-process cleanup deadline, followed by supervisor-shutdown/global-singleton-reset errors. Baseline inheritance of those failures is **not established**. A narrower rerun was interrupted during resource contention and is not a pass.
- Changed TypeScript/JS files: oxfmt **passes**, including correcting the migrated close-test formatting. Python tools: Ruff **passes**; Python compilation and Node syntax checks **pass**. Independent source review found and corrected preload callback, worker attribution, and missing zero-count assertion issues.
- Repository oxlint and core tsgo attempts: **blocked before checking** by retained `file_lock_stale` artifact ownership. Typecheck/lint are **not claimed passing**.
- One earlier concurrent build was OOM-killed; the serial candidate build above succeeded. No throughput/latency or live-agent claim.
- Broad GitHub CI was skipped on a prior Draft head; current-head `openclaw/ci-gate`, `openclaw/dependency-review`, and `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` checks succeeded. Maintainer review and a decision on the partial-mitigation scope remain required.

The memory mitigation has before/after runtime and heap-retainer evidence; missing-completion lifecycle repair remains separate. **Ready for maintainer review of whether this partial mitigation should land independently of the producer-lifecycle fix.**

prs.title: fix: keep the Gateway path out of skills_read results for a remote Codex app-server
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With a remote Codex app-server (`appServer.remoteWorkspaceRoot`), #201491 stopped the skills list from giving a Skill Library skill its Gateway state path and pointed the model at `skills_read` instead. The `skills_read` result still begins with that path:

```
Skill location: <state>/skill-library/<id>/revisions/<rev>/SKILL.md
Resolve relative resource paths from the directory containing this SKILL.md.
```

and each `skills_search` hit still carries it as `location`. The remote machine has no such path. When the instructions name a supporting file, the model resolves it against that directory and the read fails with ENOENT on the remote machine.

## User Impact

On a remote Codex app-server, `skills_read` for a library skill returns the instructions without the Gateway location or the relative-path instruction. When the revision has supporting files, the result starts with one sentence saying they are stored on the Gateway and cannot be opened from this machine. `skills_search` hits for those skills have no `location`. A local app-server (a child of the Gateway) and every other placement are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The skill tools are built in core, which does not know where the app-server's file tools run. The Codex extension does, so it shapes these two results, next to its existing whole-skill check in the dynamic tool bridge. It uses the same condition as #201491: a library skill whose file is not under `remoteWorkspaceRoot` (a copy already delivered under the remote workspace keeps its location). That selection now lives in one helper, `resolveGatewayOnlySkillDirs`, which the catalog rewrite also uses.

Supporting files are detected by listing the pinned revision directory on the Gateway at read time (revision directories hold only bundle files).

Not in scope: delivering supporting files to a remote app-server. `skills_read` with `relativePath` and the paging notice of an oversized skill are unchanged.

## Evidence

`dynamic-tool-skills.test.ts` gains a case that builds the real installed-skill tools through the production host capabilities and calls them through the dynamic tool bridge, for a remote app-server with a supporting file, a remote one with SKILL.md only, and a local one.

- With the fix: the new cases and the existing skill bridge and remote catalog tests pass.
- With the bridge wiring (`dynamic-tools.ts`, `run-attempt-tool-setup.ts`) reverted to `main` and the test kept: both remote cases fail, the `skills_read` result still starts with `Skill location: <state path>`; the local case passes.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.

Test cost: the three new cases take 0.8 to 0.9 s each with `--maxWorkers=1` (the file's first case pays the shared fixture setup, about 7 s, as before).

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

Run on a remote test VM from a snapshot of `main` (19a42c4323c) plus this change:

```
CI=true pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-skills.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.remote-skills.test.ts --maxWorkers=1   # 6 + 4 passed
git checkout <main> -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-tool-setup.ts
```

prs.title: fix(pr): retain equivalent reviewed workflows for baseline proof
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Initial baseline-proof preparation rejects a retained reviewed workflow whenever main advances, even when its workflow, dependency and policy inputs are unchanged. This change admits that equivalent case without relaxing later publication or merge gates.

## User Impact

Maintainers can retain the reviewed workflow for initial `prepare-baseline-refresh --for-proof` after authenticating current main and verifying complete input equivalence. This affects the internal PR workflow, not bot behavior. The dependency audit limitation below still prevents claiming that actual source-only main advances are unblocked.

## Why This Change Was Made

The wrapper compares both revisions' complete inventories, file types/modes, dependency/install inputs and runtime policy, requires reviewed workflow ancestry, and carries provenance through the existing native context and signed baseline binding. Custody and evidence are validated before active preparation evidence is retired. Each admission boundary remains; equal commit IDs reuse their already-computed facts only within that check.

The selected workflow owns its dependency revision independently of the newer bootstrap revision. The reentry regression injects projection loss at the real creator-owned exec boundary: the parent installs the retained workflow once, and the child reuses/reprojects it while preserving the bootstrap identity. This is explicit fault injection, not a reproduced production or supported legacy-parent failure.

The signed integration retains upstream authenticated tree export, using the named lifetime owner in the consolidated materializer. The preceding test-only cleanup starts baseline-proof fixtures at their incoming state, avoiding a correction/init/approval sequence that was immediately reset and repeated. Other callers retain the corrected/approved default. All subsequent native operations, assertions and the 120s limit remain unchanged; this removes proven redundant setup without claiming to resolve every timing cause. The latest three-line test-helper change retains the newly constructed live tree after its first pristine snapshot, avoiding an immediate delete/copy roundtrip. Later acquisitions still restore the complete private root. No assertion, timeout or production code changed, and no runtime improvement is claimed before exact-head CI.

Against frozen main `0eb75626961ddbad95918e83fe471b6b7510092c`, the 14-file authored delta is production **+738/-327 (net +411)**, tests **+581/-35**, docs **+28/-5**, and inventory **+17**. Production growth implements complete admission, sealed provenance and pre-retirement ownership checks; it is not justified as a performance improvement.

## Evidence

- Current signed head: `10e05a7dc5974721f33f50b8a222c0d840848ac7`; parent `a5706c184cfe80064bfa85b619827bfa25a1c3a6`; tree `5b799b9c1c7fec637fd99d29eaec2938bfc1b74a`. Independent review accepted the **+3/-0 test-helper-only** change; diff checks, formatting and intact signed-commit hooks passed. A dependency-free real-Git check executed the exact edited function with the repository copy/cleanup helpers on Node 26.12.1, Darwin arm64: **PASS**, 2.350s. First acquisition preserved constructor-captured filesystem identities; second acquisition restored registration, binary bytes, executable modes, symlink resolution and Git metadata, and removed newly added files. The constructor ran once, and native tracker cleanup removed the fixture. This bounded preservation check is not the full baseline runtime suite.
- [Current-head CI 44471805133](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44471805133) was dispatched once for exact `10e05a7` with the documented default full tier. Preflight checkout/base verification, Node/Bun baseline-proof and incoming suites, and applicable tooling type/lint/guard results are **pending**. Workflow control and tested checkout will be recorded separately; prior-head results below are not current-head passes.
- Prior signed head: `a5706c184cfe80064bfa85b619827bfa25a1c3a6`; parent `62d789cfc7854a8d39030518a71466a9a3920726`; tree `dee4668966f50cb31d620dac75834dcdd847f55e`. prs.title: fix(cli): hooks enable/disable refusals name the online config command
prs.body:
Fixes #197087.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw hooks enable` / `disable` refuse while the Gateway owns state, but the refusal never named the working online alternative, and `docs/cli/hooks.md` plus the `docs/automation/hooks.md` quick start read as if the toggle itself works while the Gateway runs.

## Fix

- The shared enable/disable action resolves the hook through the report owner before refusing, so the refusal names the hook's resolved config key (`hooks.internal.entries.<hookKey>.enabled ...`) instead of the typed identifier: a metadata key override no longer leaves the hook enabled when the suggested command is copied. When the hook cannot be resolved, the refusal points at key discovery (`openclaw hooks info <name> --json`, its `hookKey` field) instead of presenting the typed identifier as an exact command. An ambiguous identifier is rejected with its candidates, as offline.
- Enable refusals now also name the master switch (`openclaw config set hooks.internal.enabled true`) before the entry write: the entry-only write succeeds but leaves every internal hook disabled while the master switch is false. Both documented online workflows (`docs/cli/hooks.md`, the `docs/automation/hooks.md` quick start) include the same step.
- The hot-reload promise is qualified: the Gateway hot-reloads the change without a restart in the default hybrid reload mode; with `gateway.reload.mode=off`, restart the Gateway for the change to take effect.
- `docs/cli/hooks.md` and the quick start now direct key discovery through `openclaw hooks info <name> --json` (its `hookKey` field). The offline path ("stop the Gateway…") is unchanged, and no local write is attempted.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/hooks-cli.toggle.test.ts src/cli/hooks-cli.test.ts` — 37 passed (25 toggle + 12 hooks-cli). Run here via the direct vitest binary with the same config: the `run-vitest` wrapper's worker compiler breaks the foreign-owner mock on this VM (the toggle resolves instead of refusing), while the direct binary reproduces CI behavior.
- New regressions: both toggle refusals reject with `OWNER_UNAVAILABLE`, name the resolved key (`entries.metadata-key.enabled`, not the typed `display-name`), the enable refusal names the master switch, both qualify the reload promise (`gateway.reload.mode=off`), and an unknown hook gets key-discovery guidance instead of a typed config path. Red on base (the message lacked the online command and named the wrong key), green with the fix.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on the touched files: clean. `pnpm exec oxlint` on the two changed source files: 0 errors. `pnpm docs:check-links`: 16564 internal links, 0 broken. `pnpm lint:docs`: 0 issues. `git diff --check`: clean. `tsgo:core`: clean. Test-lines ratchet: OK (slack 0) with allocation `config/test-lines-allocations/197087-hooks-toggle-refusal.txt` (11 → 41).
- Note on CI `check-lint-core-5`: it fails on 7 pre-existing `max-lines` violations in files this PR does not touch (`src/gateway/server-http-request.ts`, `src/gateway/tools-invoke-shared.ts`, `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/plugins.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-maintenance.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-post-update.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle.ts`, `src/secrets/egress-proxy/proxy-server.test.ts`), byte-identical at the merge-base and at main tip; the PR's own files are clean. Reproduced locally with the same shard command (`node --import tsx scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mts --only=core --split-core --core-stripe="5/5" --threads=1`).

### Live-Gateway proof (isolated Gateway, 2026-11-11)

Started an isolated Gateway (isolated state dir + config, fake provider at `provider.invalid`, fake key, no live provider calls) with a workspace hook `display-name` whose metadata key is `metadata-key`.

- `openclaw hooks disable display-name` → refusal naming `openclaw config set hooks.internal.entries.metadata-key.enabled false` (plus the qualified reload promise), exit 1.
- `openclaw hooks enable display-name` → refusal naming `openclaw config set hooks.internal.enabled true` then `...entries.metadata-key.enabled true` (plus the qualified reload promise), exit 1.
- `openclaw hooks info display-name --json` shows `"hookKey": "metadata-key"`.
- Ran the suggested `openclaw config set hooks.internal.entries.metadata-key.enabled false` → `Updated hooks.internal.entries.metadata-key.enabled. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.`; `hooks info` then reports `enabledByConfig: false, disabled: true` — the disable took effect in the running Gateway with no restart.
- Master-switch check: with `hooks.internal.enabled: false`, the entry-only enable still left zero internal hook handlers loaded at Gateway startup (`startup outcomes: internal-hooks=skipped (hooks-disabled)`; no `loaded N internal hook handlers` line, versus 6 loaded with the master on) — proving the entry-only write is insufficient. Then `openclaw config set hooks.internal.enabled true` hot-reloaded and the hook reported enabled again. (Note: the `hooks info` report is per-entry and does not itself reflect the master switch; the loader state is proven by the restart comparison above.)
- Caveats: the CLI and Gateway were run from source via the repo's tsx loader (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/index.ts ...`) because this VM cannot build dist (tsdown needs ~5 GiB; the process cgroup allows ~806 MiB) and `pnpm openclaw` refuses without dist. Same fixed source, separate real processes. The `gateway.reload.mode=off` restart path was not live-demonstrated (textual qualification only); all live runs used the default hybrid mode. Full transcript kept locally.

### Round 2 (2026-11-18, commit 2066314f6)

Addresses the two remaining P2 findings from the 2026-11-11 Codex re-review: plugin-managed hook refusals now direct the operator to the owning plugin instead of the ineffective `hooks.internal.entries` config path, and a remote report's ambiguity no longer rejects a locally unique offline toggle (candidates surface as refusal guidance; local admission still decides). New regressions red before the fix, green after; `vitest run src/cli/hooks-cli.toggle.test.ts src/cli/hooks-cli.test.ts` — 40 passed. `oxfmt --check` clean, `oxlint` 0 errors, `tsgo:core` clean, test-lines ratchet OK (allocation 41 → 85). Live-Gateway proof for the plugin-managed branch completed 2026-11-18 against an isolated Gateway from source (tsx loader, isolated state dir) with a real plugin `proof-hook-plugin` registering hook `proof-demo-hook` via `api.registerHook("command:new", ..., { name: "proof-demo-hook" })`: `hooks list` shows the hook with Source `plugin:proof-hook-plugin`; `hooks info` shows `Source: openclaw-plugin (proof-hook-plugin)` and "Managed by plugin"; `hooks disable`/`enable proof-demo-hook` while the Gateway runs refuse (exit 1, no mutation) naming the owning plugin and `openclaw plugins disable/enable proof-hook-plugin`.

prs.title: fix(matrix): replies that quote a bot mention no longer start bot turns
prs.body:
Root cause: extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler.ts:145 passes the raw event content, including the legacy rich-reply fallback, to mention detection (handler-ingress-content.ts:248 scans the `<mx-reply>` quote's bot link) and to the agent text (handler-ingress-content.ts:111 reads the quoted `> <@user> ...` lines), although the Matrix spec says clients strip that fallback.

Fixes #197065

## What Problem This Solves

In a Matrix room where the bot only answers when mentioned, replying to someone else's message that mentioned the bot started a bot turn, even though the reply itself never mentioned the bot. The old quoted text was also passed to the agent as if the person had just written it.

## User Impact

Replies that don't mention the bot no longer start turns in mention-required rooms. Replies that do mention the bot still start a turn, and the agent sees only the new text. The replied-to message still reaches the agent as reply context, and blockquotes the person wrote themselves are kept.

## Why This Change Was Made

Matrix rich replies used to carry a copy of the replied-to message: leading `> <@user> ...` lines in `body` and a leading `<mx-reply>` element in `formatted_body`. The spec says clients strip both: v1.12 [Stripping the fallback](https://spec.matrix.org/v1.12/client-server-api/#stripping-the-fallback) ("MUST strip the fallback before rendering the reply"), and v1.13 [Rich replies](https://spec.matrix.org/v1.13/client-server-api/#rich-replies), which removed fallbacks but says "clients SHOULD still remove this fallback". The Matrix monitor now strips them once, where it prepares the current message content for replies, before mention detection, history and agent text. The `body` quote is stripped only when it starts like a fallback (`> <@user>`), so an authored blockquote at the start of a reply stays. Mention and allowlist rules are unchanged.

Thanks @Jo2234 for the report and the fix. On top of it: merged current main, simplified the stripping to the spec's two rules, folded the tests into one regression table, and dropped the test-lines allocation record (the change fits the default allowance).

## Evidence

- Gateway on a real homeserver (Tuwunel in a local container), Gateway from source, bundled Matrix plugin, mention-required room, scripted model: on main, a reply without a bot mention started a turn and the model input began with the quoted fallback; on this head it was skipped with `no-mention` and the model was not called. Control: a reply that mentions the bot started a turn on this head with only the new text. Observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197091#issuecomment-7001368517
- Regression `handler.body-for-agent.test.ts` "uses only the current text of a rich reply" (quote-only reply, fresh mention reply, authored blockquote): the first two fail on main, all pass here.
- Production +24/-1, tests +39 against main.

Merge danger: two-way door. A revert fully undoes it; nothing is stored or migrated. Blast radius: Matrix inbound replies only (`m.in_reply_to`). If the stripping were wrong, a Matrix reply could lose leading quoted text or miss a mention that appears only inside the quote.

prs.title: improve: show plugin names and icons in Template contents without source labels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Template's page lists the skills and plugins it adds. Plugin rows showed the raw package reference (for example `@openclaw/workflow-tools`) with a generic plug icon, and every skill and plugin row carried a "ClawHub · Version 1.2.0" or "Bundled with template" label. The rows were hard to scan and looked unlike the same plugins on the Plugins page. On a phone, the "Installed" status also stacked above the row's chevron instead of sitting beside it.

## User Impact

User impact: Template contents now show each plugin by its display name and its own icon, the skill and plugin rows no longer carry source or version labels, and "Installed" stays on the chevron's line at phone widths. No migration or user action is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Plugin rows take their name and artwork from the installed inventory when the plugin is present, otherwise from the plugin catalog detail for the Template's exact pinned version. Artwork loads through the existing authenticated plugin icon transport, and the plug icon remains the fallback when artwork is missing or fails to load.
- The "Installed" check still compares the exact package and version, so a different installed version is not reported as installed.
- The stacked control layout on narrow screens now applies only to action rows (status over a button). Navigation rows keep the status beside the chevron.
- The Plugins page skill rows already had no source label; a regression assertion now protects that.
- The version remains available inside a plugin row's expanded details, and the sidebar preview's selected-item pane is unchanged.

## Evidence

Before/after screenshots (clean and annotated): [proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201652#issuecomment-7001322141). Before is the merge base `a32fc09b4ce`; after is this PR's tree. Both use the real Control UI with the same synthetic mocked-Gateway fixture.

- Red on the base, green on the head: the browser regressions failed on the old labels (`ClawHub · Version`, two `Bundled with template` labels) and on the phone alignment (status centre 22.8px above the chevron centre).
- `ui/src/pages/agents-home/templates-catalog.e2e.test.ts` and `ui/src/pages/plugins/plugin-overview.e2e.test.ts`: 37 passed on the rebased head. The cases cover installed-inventory branding, catalog branding with the exact-version request, unavailable artwork falling back to the plug icon, a different installed version not showing "Installed", and phone/desktop layout.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, scoped oxlint, stylelint, `oxfmt --check`, and `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers` pass.
- Size: production +154/-38 across five files (one new 65-line icon component), tests +104/-33.
- Review: no local automated review was run; hosted ClawSweeper review is requested through this PR.
- Not covered: a live ClawHub registry and real plugin artwork (fixture-only), and WebKit.

prs.title: improve: show clearer icons for SOUL.md, AGENTS.md and BOOTSTRAP.md on Template pages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Template page lists the workspace files the Template adds to a new agent. Three of those rows used icons that did not match what the file is for: SOUL.md showed a paint palette, which reads as "theme and colors"; AGENTS.md showed a generic scroll; and BOOTSTRAP.md showed a flag. Someone scanning the list could not tell the files apart by their icons.

## User Impact

User impact: on a Template page, SOUL.md, AGENTS.md and BOOTSTRAP.md now have icons that reflect their purpose. There is no behavior change.

- **SOUL.md** (persona, tone and boundaries): theatre masks.
- **AGENTS.md** (operating instructions): an agent head above lines of text.
- **BOOTSTRAP.md** (one-time first-run setup): a rocket.

prs.title: fix: keep a sub-agent's task when a retry reloads oversized history
prs.body:
Root cause: src/config/sessions/session-model-context-window.ts:168 takes a history suffix that starts inside the current turn when that turn's tool results exceed the history byte cap, so a retry that reloads history mid-turn loses the request that opened the turn.

Fixes #201605

## What Problem This Solves

A sub-agent working through a long, tool-heavy task (screenshots, large reads) can hit a provider stream error such as `degenerate_output`. OpenClaw retries on the same model, but the retry's request no longer contains the sub-agent's task. The model only sees the system prompt, a failure note and "continue the current task", so it answers without doing the work and the parent receives a "completed" child that did nothing.

## User Impact

User impact: after a transient provider failure, a sub-agent (or any agent turn) whose tool results have grown past the history byte cap retries with its task still in front of the model and continues the work. Turns under the cap, new turns, and retries whose failed stream produced no output are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first attempt builds its history in memory. A retry reloads the transcript through the bounded history window, which keeps the newest events that fit in eight bytes per context token. Inside one long turn there is no later turn boundary to align to, so the window kept only the newest tool frames and dropped the turn's user request. The internal continuation prompt then became the first user message, which is the `historyRewrite(message 0 (user) differs ...)` line in the report.

The window now keeps the request that opened the current turn and fills the rest of the cap with the newest frames, the same way it already reserves the latest compaction summary. If that request cannot fit beside any frame, the old suffix is kept. Saved history is not changed.

## Evidence

Real Gateway from source with a local OpenAI Responses provider that records every request. The parent calls `sessions_spawn` with a task; the child reads two screenshot-sized images, then its third stream emits text followed by a runaway tool call that trips `degenerate_output`.

- `main` (67aacbb676), twice: the retry request is `[system, failed-turn note, "Continue the current task...", runtime context]`, with no task. The child ends with `stopReason=stop` 1.3 s later.
- This branch, twice: the retry request starts with the same task message as the first attempt, and the child continues the task.
- Controls on both builds: a sub-agent turn that does not fail is identical; an output-free failure and a small-history failure already kept the task.
- Regression test `keeps the current turn's request when its tool frames exceed the byte cap`: fails on `main` (`expected [ 3, 4, 5 ] to deeply equal [ +0, 3, 4, 5 ]`), passes here.

Observed request lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201636#issuecomment-7000817156
Re-run after the review fix (tool ownership kept): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201636#issuecomment-7001542528

Thanks @mike1122real-hub for the detailed report with the four failure timings and the history-rewrite line.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: the change only selects which saved events are loaded for one model request and writes nothing, so a revert fully restores the old selection. Blast radius: embedded agent turns whose loaded history exceeds the byte cap in the middle of a turn; they now send the turn's request plus slightly fewer of the oldest tool frames from that turn.

prs.title: fix(codex): let setup verify the standalone installer runtime
prs.body:
Related: #161720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: verified setup and repair inference stops before Codex startup when the official standalone install contains its `codex -> bin/codex` link, even though ordinary agent turns can use the same runtime.

## User Impact

Users of the reported standalone layout can pass the runtime-artifact capture step without deleting a link that the installer recreates on every update. No configuration change or migration is required.

This is a **draft implementation**, not a merge-ready security approval. Codex/runtime-boundary review and the remaining validation below are still needed. Only the exact installer link is admitted; other package symlinks remain unsupported.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing verifier owns package attestation but rejected every symlink. It now recognizes only the package-root `codex` link with literal target `bin/codex`, requires its canonical target to be that regular file inside the package, and fingerprints the link alongside the already-hashed target bytes. Before/after link metadata checks reject replacement during hashing; existing startup revalidation, cancellation, no-follow file reads, and resource bounds remain in place.

This deliberately does not introduce generic symlink traversal, directory-link support, or a second verifier. It retains the existing before/after filesystem-check model rather than claiming an atomic snapshot against concurrent writers.

## Evidence

- **Base-red / fix-green:** the shared-client capture regression failed on base `0633f256350b5580a5bdbcd8a6a5782750de03d4` with the reported `unsupported entry: .../codex` error before app-server startup. The same caller path passes with this fix using a real temporary package tree and a synthetic transport. This is boundary integration proof, not a real model or desktop setup run.
- **Focused checks:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/runtime-artifact.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/shared-client.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **232 tests passed**. Coverage includes target-byte changes, link removal/replacement, rejected non-installer links, npm/Windows neighbors, and expected-artifact startup checks.
- **Targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.** Lint and formatting were rechecked after the interrupted review/restart; the retained source diff is unchanged.
- Personally inspected the [pinned upstream installer](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/064c6b8c737f5b41d171fdda80bd9ef10ad06eb3/scripts/install/install.sh#L946-L971), which creates this exact relative link. The sibling Codex checkout was not mounted, so the source inspection used that pinned upstream file directly. The macOS report, Linux duplicate #177663, and newer Linux report in #161720 were reviewed; no new user-machine reproduction is claimed. #134727 is a distinct, closed npm-launcher issue.
- **Review gap:** local Auto Review was launched against the complete local delta from the base above, then stalled and was interrupted by the Gateway restart without a report. No clean independent-review verdict or PATCH QUALITY score is claimed. Continuing the authorized draft under the current maintainer workflow’s review-timeout policy.
- **Typecheck gap:** direct `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/codex/tsconfig.json --noEmit` failed on workspace package/declaration resolution and package-boundary `rootDir` errors (including `@openclaw/normalization-core`); it is not a passing typecheck. Canonical extension production/test typechecks and broader CI remain outstanding. No full build, real-model setup/update-repair flow, or native macOS/Windows run was performed.
- **Simplification pass:** kept the existing verifier as the sole owner, with no generic traversal/helper framework. Production delta is +32/-5 lines; test delta is +93/-35 lines (+58 net, including formatting of the existing parameterized client test).

Reported and requested by Donniefi.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/235176eb-04cb-46e9-b356-c63ff16f0f5f)

prs.title: fix: preserve the running installation when an agent updates its Gateway
prs.body:
Related: #200978

## What Problem This Solves

The current agent guidance requires an exact revision before an agent can use Git to update its own Gateway, even when the service already runs directly from that checkout. Selecting a different method can change how the Gateway starts: [the built-in Git updater can redirect a directly served checkout to a release launcher](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/053fb62c614/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-git.ts#L657-L685).

## User Impact

An ordinary update follows the host-authorized procedure for the installation that actually serves the Gateway. Switching installation methods is a separate operator request.

## Why This Change Was Made

> When updating the Gateway hosting this session, identify how it is installed and use the update procedure its host authorizes for that installation. Change installation methods only if the operator requests it.

The shared prompt names neither a default updater nor a Git-specific script. Installation-specific commands belong in the relevant update documentation. This changes guidance, not maintenance permissions.

## Evidence

**Current head `5912029`: live Git and package-managed validation pending.** Earlier results below apply only to their named revisions.


**Earlier script-specific revision `9bc7534`: correct update method, no deployment.** On an isolated Gateway served directly from a Git checkout, the authenticated owner sent only `Update yourself.` The hosted agent inspected the running service and its stop/restart hooks, then ran `cd /srv/openclaw && scripts/update-gateway.sh` without a hint or a second request.

The script fetched the target (`cf1954a`) but stopped with `ENOMEM`. In all 230 observations the serving checkout stayed at `9bc7534` and the PID stayed 134. The agent correctly reported that deployment failed. This proves method selection on this run, not an end-to-end update.

**Inspection-first rule (567388a): no update.** Given only `Update yourself.`, the owner-authorized hosted agent identified the directly served Git checkout and the available commit (`a7a22909`), then chose the built-in updater. The external supervisor policy caused it to skip the update. Across 101 observations the checkout remained on `567388a` and the serving PID did not change. This demonstrates inspection, not a successful self-update.

**Foreground Git checkout: the live update failed.** An authenticated owner sent only `Update yourself.` to a real hosted agent on the PR build. The agent chose the built-in updater, which fetched the available target and installed dependencies. The build refused to start: the resolved heap was 4,200 MB; the full build requires 4,352 MB.

The updater reported `succeeded`, but all 399 checkout observations stayed on `c18d4d0f9b0`, not target `26a61641529`. The Gateway restarted (PID 10774 to 14570) and returned healthy on the old build, with the same start command, checkout and configuration. This is evidence of an attempted update and a false success report, not proof of a successful in-place update or selection of an alternate Git method.

**Owner-authorized live test (externally supervised Git checkout): no update.** A real hosted Codex agent received only “Update yourself.” through authenticated WebChat on PR head `c18d4d0f`. The same connection had passed the owner-only command check. The agent called the built-in updater. It returned `skipped`: the host had assigned updates to its external supervisor. The agent correctly reported that no update or restart had been scheduled.

Independent before/after observations: checkout and build both stayed at `c18d4d0f` despite an available fast-forward to test commit `26a61641`; the serving PID stayed 642. The service definition, startup command and configuration were unchanged. Health, readiness and startup all returned HTTP 200 before and after. This is evidence that the external-supervisor policy was respected, **not** a successful update of an ordinary user-managed checkout.

An earlier request through the local agent RPC lacked owner authority and was denied before it could test update behavior. The 55 focused tests pass, but they test the rendered guidance, not an agent updating itself.

prs.title: fix(ci): keep mixed extension batches off Boat runners
prs.body:
Closes #201663
Related: #201116

## What Problem This Solves

Hourly Extension Tests repeatedly lost a mixed extension batch to Boat memory exhaustion after setup succeeded. The provider reported a process exceeding 7,428 MiB RAM plus 6,143 MiB swap; the test step exited 137.

## User Impact

Mixed extension batches keep their existing Blacksmith runners. Boat remains available for file-bounded extension shards under the same maximum of 20 starts per hourly run. Every test, worker limit, deadline, and hosted manual/retry route is preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider adapter now admits only file-bounded extension shards to Boat. Mixed batches can contain multiple concurrent config groups and are not qualified by the file-shard measurements. Skipped batches do not consume the Boat allowance, leaving it available to later file shards. This restores the established runner placement without speculative memory-size increases or a new configuration option.

## Evidence

- Two observed OOM failures: [04:39 run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44459817245/job/135344291352) and [05:39 run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44466669217/job/135366698620). Both failed during tests with exit 137 and the provider RAM/swap warning. A [recent all-Blacksmith hourly run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44452942906) passed; this is comparison evidence at another head, not exact-head runtime proof.
- Direct execution of the actual workflow admission code: base routed five mixed batches to Boat; the fix routed none. All 25 fixture rows remained present and 20 file shards still used Boat. Zero budget and inactive matrices retained Blacksmith.
- The existing complete-manifest regression now requires mixed batches to stay on Blacksmith and checks that every non-Boat row preserves its original placement and metadata.
- Formatting and diff checks passed. Dependency-backed tests, workflow validation, typecheck and the local line-cap hook are pending exact-head CI: this code-only worktree has no qualified dependency install, and the shared hook tooling has oxlint 1.88.0 instead of required 1.89.0. No shared dependencies were changed.
- Local ClawSweeper review completed for `11b65598aa4d6b56ce786a611efbb172775a165b..2fe47c7d3a725783cecae992cdd0c6374fcc5525`; no actionable correctness or security findings. prs.title: fix: install official plugins from the chat card without leaving the conversation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the agent recommends a plugin in chat, the card shows an **Install** button. Selecting it did not install anything: it opened the plugin page, where you had to find and select **Install** a second time, and you lost your place in the conversation.

## User Impact

User impact: selecting **Install** on an official plugin card now installs the plugin right there. The card shows **Installing**, then **Installed** (or **Connect** when the plugin needs an account), and the chat stays open.

Unchanged on purpose:

- Community plugin cards and skill cards still open their details, as the chat docs describe. A community package is installed from its plugin overview.
- A configured install-policy warning still needs an explicit acknowledgment. When an official plugin has one, the card opens the plugin overview, which is where that review is presented.

## Why This Change Was Made

The card's button was wired to navigate to the plugin page with an install hint that the page deliberately ignores, so the click could never start an install. The card now sends the install itself, through the same install owner and config write queue the plugin page uses, so progress, failures and retries look the same in both places and an install started in chat is visible on the plugin page too.

A second click before the first request is admitted does not queue a second install. A retryable failure retries from the card. Anything the card cannot present (a policy review, or a config write refused before a request was sent, for example during an update) opens the plugin page instead of failing silently. Warnings returned with a successful install, which the plugin page lists beside the plugin's row, are announced in a toast because a card has no row to hold them.

## Evidence

Scenario: an official plugin card in chat, **Install** selected once. Before is `main` at `ff4a6c70d6b`; after is this branch. Both run the real Control UI production bundle in Chromium at 1280×720 against the repository's mocked Gateway fixtures (synthetic plugin data, no real installation).

### Clean comparison

Before: the click leaves the chat and no install request is sent.

![Before: selecting Install opened the plugin page instead of installing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23f16333-d978-4273-80e1-e85cdd671b95)

After: the same click starts the install in the conversation.

![After: the card shows Installing and the chat stays open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ae9d743-adec-4bc1-826f-f5e5f1626fea)

After the Gateway confirms the install:

![After: the card shows Installed with a Manage action, still in chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a834ee4-9699-45ae-bf74-8e8d20d65f16)

### Annotated comparison

![Before, annotated: the plugin page with its own Install button highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b84c553-8aea-41d1-998c-b48c5f0669be)

![After, annotated: the chat card in its Installing state highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8819f428-731c-4b51-8cd0-125d4f182b8c)

Recordings of the same click, before then after:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/83f2e12e-81fd-4f6f-8adc-91d5da1774ee

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd864fc9-b064-4ba8-a2ee-d4733ac2be7b

prs.title: improve: reduce repeated setup when paging session history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated session-history reads ask every discovery worker to close readers even when all selected databases are already retained. The no-op cleanup still allocates message channels and async-context snapshots, and settlement repeatedly resolves paths already qualified by the discovery owner.

## User Impact

History reads use less CPU and allocate less on the warm path. Read results, admission charges, archive navigation, and database retirement behavior stay the same. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Settlement consumes prepared physical paths directly for exact candidates and visits retained resources once. It omits exact candidates that are already retained from cleanup, while family candidates still close unowned siblings. Revoked resources, cleanup failure recovery, and conservative worker rotation keep their existing lifecycle rules.

The inventory preparation and inventory-read requests carry different payloads; their byte charges remain intact. No cross-request cache was added. Production code grows by six lines to make the no-op cleanup decision explicit while preserving shared-path revocation handling.

## Evidence

The existing maintenance lifecycle regression fails on the parent with three cleanup requests instead of two. Candidate focused proof passes 78 tests, including real page reads as targets are added/removed, worker restart, archive/cold-store reads, and physical database replacement.

Synthetic benchmark: 5,000 sessions across four stores, 100 messages in each hot transcript, real discovery/presence/history workers, Node 26.12.1 on macOS. Five serial alternating pairs of 200 warm reads, plus two baseline A/A runs. Cold-worker reads are reported separately. Acceptance was fewer cleanup requests and allocations, equal pages and admission charges, and no 20% median/p95 CPU or latency regression.

| Metric | Parent | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warm page p50, median of runs | 2.888 ms | 2.522 ms |
| Warm page p95, median of runs | 3.525 ms | 3.235 ms |
| Process CPU / 200 reads | 783.567 ms | 689.608 ms |
| Main-thread CPU / 200 reads | 189.563 ms | 159.012 ms |
| Cleanup broadcasts / 200 reads | 200 | 0 |
| Awaited cleanup / 200 reads | 27.545 ms | 0 ms |
| Sampled main-thread allocation / 200 reads | 82,270,080 bytes | 75,341,400 bytes |
| Cold-worker first read, median | 4,610.520 ms | 4,553.466 ms |

Page hashes, including post-rotation reads, and complete warm admission-charge sequences match in every run. A/A warm p50 was 2.530 / 2.995 ms; five-pair p50 ranges were 2.780–2.980 / 2.369–2.816 ms. p95 ranges were 3.221–6.379 / 3.073–3.644 ms. Host load was recorded. Allocation sampling and CPU profiles ran separately from timing acceptance. Allocation A/A controls were 82.27 / 85.55 MB on the parent and 75.34 / 75.05 MB on the candidate. The saved allocation profiles attribute 3.63 MB to cleanup receipt creation on the parent and zero on the candidate; resource-owner path-resolution allocation fell from 7.52 to 1.85 MB. Inventory byte-measurement allocation was unchanged (0.53 / 0.54 MB). This measures host discovery/settlement and actual page reads, not disk-capacity stress or Gateway socket latency.

Rerunnable workload: `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-candidate-settlement-measure.mjs --state /absolute/new-fixture --seed --output /absolute/result.json`. Subsequent arms omit `--seed`; `--owner-file` selects the frozen parent owner. `--allocations` captures collected-object allocation profiles.

The two focused browser tests and three history-reading E2E cases pass in Chromium/WebKit. The initial E2E attempt stopped during setup because the pinned WebKit binary was absent; installing that existing test dependency resolved it. `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` passes both production and full-tree scans with zero findings. Independent Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings; the only later edits are lint-only local renames and loop braces. `pnpm check:changed` completed all stages; it found four own lint errors, fixed with green reruns of both affected lint commands. All typechecks, ratchets, dead-export scans, format and boundary/import-cycle guards passed.

CI follow-up: run 44463610852 exposed two existing tests that scheduled work from the redundant cleanup call. Both failures reproduced locally. The cron test now schedules a real foreground read after maintenance discovery and before pruning; the alias-lifetime fixture includes an unowned candidate so its cleanup wait exercises real work. Both repaired cases pass, preserving foreground results, worker reuse and retained-handle custody. Production code and benchmark inputs are unchanged.

prs.title: chore: keep declaration boundary tests passing on Windows
prs.body:
Related: #201629

## What Problem This Solves

The tests added in #201629 assert TypeScript's TS6053 "file not found" diagnostic against a path built with native separators. The fixtures write those `/// <reference>` paths with forward slashes, and TypeScript reports them as written. On Windows the expected path therefore contains `\` while the actual diagnostic contains `/`, so two cases fail even though the build behaves correctly.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Main's Windows test lane stops reporting a false failure in `test/scripts/tsdown-declaration-resolution.test.ts`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The comparison normalizes the expected path to forward slashes, and only for the TS6053 cases (`ancestor ambient types`, `source reference`). The assertions are not loosened: the error code check, the exact path check, and the separate `Declaration input escapes checkout` checks for checkout links are all unchanged.
- The same normalization applies to the direct TS6053 assertion in `test/scripts/native-declaration-boundary.test.ts`.
- One write is removed from the nested optional-import test: the copy of `synthetic-js` in the ancestor install, along with its later manifest change. The candidate has its own copy, so the ancestor's was never resolved and asserted nothing. The rating review flagged it as low value. The test still proves its point by changing the ancestor's `synthetic-fetch` types, which the old pass did read, and comparing the output.

## Evidence

- Which jobs run these files on Windows: `test/scripts/tsdown-declaration-resolution.test.ts` is in `test:windows:ci:2`, which the `checks-windows` job's `test-2` row runs on main (it is also listed in `scripts/lib/ci-windows-test-plan.mts`). Ordinary PRs skip `checks-windows` (`scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs`, `runWindows = !ordinaryPullRequest && …`), so this PR's CI cannot run it. `native-declaration-boundary.test.ts` is not in a Windows lane.
- How I checked the Windows comparison without a Windows runner: I used `path.win32` to build the same fixture spellings (`<root>-outside` and a forward-slashed `index.d.ts` reference inside it) and a TS6053 message in the format TypeScript emits. The old native-separator comparison returned `false`; the normalized one returned `true`.
- On macOS, both files pass: 30 passed, 4 skipped. `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` also pass.

Not proven: a real Windows run of these cases. The first `checks-windows` run on main after this lands is the proof.
