// Self-checking assertions over the provider requests the BUILT OpenClaw CLI
// actually sent to the local stub model endpoint, one capture per scenario.
// Exits non-zero on any failed invariant.
const fs = require("node:fs");
const path = require("node:path");

const ROOT = "/tmp/cap197114-run";
const MARKER_OPEN = '<dropped_plugin_context hook="before_prompt_build">';
const MARKER_CLOSE = "</dropped_plugin_context>";
const SECRET = "sk-FIXTURE-SECRET-must-not-reach-the-prompt";
const HEALTHY = "HEALTHY-CTX-FROM-cap-healthy";

let failed = 0;
let checks = 0;
function ok(cond, label) {
  checks += 1;
  if (cond) {
    console.log(`  ok  ${label}`);
  } else {
    failed += 1;
    console.log(`  FAIL ${label}`);
  }
}

function userPrompt(scenario) {
  const capDir = path.join(ROOT, scenario, "capture");
  const file = fs
    .readdirSync(capDir)
    .filter((n) => n.startsWith("req-") && n.includes("chat_completions"))
    .sort()[0];
  if (!file) throw new Error(`${scenario}: the stub endpoint recorded no chat-completions request`);
  const body = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(capDir, file), "utf-8"));
  const first = body.messages.find((m) => m.role === "user");
  const content = typeof first.content === "string" ? first.content : JSON.stringify(first.content);
  return { file, content, body };
}

function markerSlice(prompt) {
  const start = prompt.indexOf(MARKER_OPEN);
  if (start < 0) return undefined;
  const end = prompt.indexOf(MARKER_CLOSE, start);
  if (end < 0) throw new Error("marker opened but never closed");
  return prompt.slice(start, end + MARKER_CLOSE.length);
}

console.log("[1] healthy: one installed plugin contributes, nothing is dropped");
{
  const { file, content } = userPrompt("healthy");
  console.log(`      capture: healthy/capture/${file}`);
  ok(content.includes(HEALTHY), "the healthy contribution reached the provider request");
  ok(!content.includes(MARKER_OPEN), "no drop marker is present when nothing was dropped");
  ok(content.includes("latest ask from the operator"), "the operator's own ask is still in the prompt");
}

console.log("[2] failing: a healthy and a throwing plugin, both installed");
{
  const { file, content } = userPrompt("failing");
  console.log(`      capture: failing/capture/${file}`);
  const slice = markerSlice(content);
  ok(content.includes(HEALTHY), "the healthy contribution survived its sibling's failure");
  ok(Boolean(slice), "a drop marker reached the provider request");
  ok(
    (content.match(new RegExp(MARKER_OPEN.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&"), "g")) || []).length === 1,
    "exactly one drop marker block",

  ok(slice.includes("cap-failing"), "the marker names the plugin whose contribution was lost");
  ok(slice.includes("handler-failed"), "the marker carries the handler-failed reason code");
  ok(!content.includes(SECRET), "the thrown exception's secret text never reaches the provider");
  ok(!content.includes("ready-work query failed"), "no exception message text reaches the provider");
  ok(content.includes("MISSING from this prompt"), "the marker tells the model the context is missing, not empty");
  ok(Buffer.byteLength(slice, "utf-8") <= 640, `marker block is bounded (${Buffer.byteLength(slice, "utf-8")} bytes <= 640)`);
}

console.log("[3] overflow: one healthy plugin and eight throwing plugins");
{

  const slice = markerSlice(content);

### Proof limits, stated plainly

- The built-CLI capture above runs a **build of our fork's `integration` branch that contains this PR**, not a build of this branch alone; the one production-file difference and its attribution to two other branches are stated with the command that measures it. A build of this branch in isolation was not affordable in this pass.
- The model endpoint is a local stub, so the captures prove what the runtime **sends**, not how a real model reacts to the marker. No API keys, IPs, phone numbers or non-public endpoints appear: the provider is `http://127.0.0.1:1891x/v1` with a dummy `stub-key`, and the fixture secret is the synthetic literal `sk-FIXTURE-SECRET-must-not-reach-the-prompt` (which the assertions prove never reaches the request).
- A from-source (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`) proof can no longer spawn a provider child on Linux at all: `acquireLinuxChildSubreaper` refuses a process owner with source-loader hooks (`src/process/supervisor/linux-child-subreaper.ts:39`). That is why the entry-point capture uses a built CLI; it is a property of current `main`, not of this PR.
- The in-process proof asserts on the assembled prompt string a production consumer returns, not on bytes leaving the process.
- No API keys, IPs, phone numbers or non-public endpoints appear in the captures: the fixture secret is a synthetic `AUTH_TOKEN=sk-live-9f3c-PROOF` with an `internal.invalid` endpoint, and the runtime's own log redaction prints it as `AUTH_TOKEN=***`.

prs.title: fix(agents): Code Mode ask_user questions are cancelled when the turn ends
prs.body:
Closes #197024

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in Code Mode, an `ask_user` question asked from an ordinary cell (without `awaitResults: true`) is cancelled when the turn ends, so the owner never gets an answerable card and the agent never receives the answer.

## User Impact

User impact: agents using Code Mode can call `ask_user` normally and the question stays open until the owner answers, the question times out, or the run is cancelled. Same outcome as `awaitResults: true` today, without the model having to remember the flag.

## Why This Change Was Made

Code Mode already has a required-completion owner that keeps the exec call open while off-VM tool results are pending. Previously only `exec`/`agents_wait` with `awaitResults: true` entered it. A native `ask_user` call was not covered, so a slow human answer let the cell return `waiting`, and turn teardown then aborted the pending question. This change makes every native core `ask_user` call required work. Client-provided tools named `ask_user` and the existing `awaitResults` rules are unchanged; deadlines, Stop and owner replacement still end the call.

One deliberate consequence: a cell that calls `ask_user` and then `yield_control()` now fails explicitly as unfinished required work, instead of parking a handle whose question would be silently cancelled at turn end.

The new regression test adds 18 net test lines, tracked in `config/test-lines-allocations/197024-code-mode-ask-user-owned.txt`. Without it the ratchet fails, because main has only 3 lines of slack.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway proof (isolated local Gateway, real agent and model)

Setup: `pnpm build:runtime` of each commit, then `openclaw gateway run` on loopback with a fresh state dir. The model is `openai/gpt-6-astra` via ChatGPT OAuth, pinned to the OpenClaw runtime. `tools.codeMode = { enabled: true, timeoutMs: 2000 }`. The question is driven over Gateway RPC:
1. `chat.send` asks the agent to run one ordinary Code Mode cell, `const answer = await ask_user({...}); return answer;`, with no `awaitResults` and no `yield_control`.
2. `question.list` finds the pending question, which is held unanswered for 30s (15x the 2s cell budget). `question.get` is checked every 10s.
3. `question.resolve` submits `Amber`. `chat.history` must then show `PROOF-197024 ANSWER=Amber`.

The "end turn" scenario tells the model to reply `PROOF-197024 HANDED-BACK` and end its turn if `exec` returns `waiting`, instead of polling `wait`. That is the hand-back that loses the question in #197024. Both builds got the identical prompt. Base = this branch with only `src/agents/code-mode-bridge.ts` reverted to 3031a32908b (scratch build `3197a25`). Head = `dc3c9c0` (both from `dist/build-info.json`).

| Scenario | Build | `exec` result | Model `wait` polls | Question after 30s | Answer reached the agent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| End turn on `waiting` | base | `waiting` (`pending_tools`) | 0, replied `HANDED-BACK` | **`cancelled`** within 10s of being asked | **no** |
| End turn on `waiting` | head | `completed`, value `{status:"answered", proceed:["Amber"]}` | 0 | `pending` at 10s, 20s and 30s, then `answered` | yes: `PROOF-197024 ANSWER=Amber` |
| Model keeps polling | base | `waiting` | 9 | `pending`, then `answered` | yes, only because the model polled `wait` 9 times |
| Model keeps polling | head | `completed` with the answer | 0 | `pending`, then `answered` | yes: `PROOF-197024 ANSWER=Amber` |

Base Gateway log at the turn end (end-turn scenario; ids shortened):

```text
08:09:53.519 [plugins] [hooks] running agent_end (1 handlers)
08:09:53.527 [agents/code-mode] Code Mode execution failed sessionKey=agent:main:proof-197024-1794413381 codeModeRunId=cm_009676eb-… failurePhase=bridge failureCode=tool_error bridgeDispatchStarted=true bridgeRequestId=bridge:callValue:1 bridgeMethod=callValue errorCategory=Error failureKind=aborted
```

Driver output from the same run:

```text
[16:09:51.986Z] question pending: {"id":"ask_7abe6f4c…","status":"pending",…}
[16:10:06.207Z] t+10s question.status=cancelled
```

Head, same end-turn prompt:

```text
[16:14:03.212Z] question pending: {"id":"ask_e9181f5a…","status":"pending",…}
[16:14:16.214Z] t+10s question.status=pending
[16:14:29.066Z] t+20s question.status=pending
[16:14:42.043Z] t+30s question.status=pending
[16:14:43.868Z] question.resolve after 40s -> {"status":"answered","answers":{"answers":{"proceed":["Amber"]}}}
[16:14:48.773Z] final assistant reply: PROOF-197024 ANSWER=Amber
```

On head, the Code Mode tool result in `chat.history` is `{"status":"completed",…,"sources":{"openclaw":64,"mcp":0,"client":0},…}`, so the native core `ask_user` was used. The head log has no `Code Mode execution failed` line, and `agent_end` fires only after the answer (08:14:46). Both builds also log the same unrelated `agent_end handler from skill-workshop failed: Plugin invocation scope is closed`.

### Unit regression and checks

- Regression in `src/agents/code-mode.wait.test.ts`: an ordinary cell awaits a core `ask_user` whose answer arrives only after the clock is advanced 60s past a 1s cell budget.
  - Base (`code-mode-bridge.ts` from 3031a32908b): fails. The cell ends as `status: "failed"` before the answer arrives.
  - This branch: passes. The cell completes with the answer, and the question's abort signal was never fired.
- `pnpm test src/agents/code-mode.wait.test.ts`: 40/40 passed (Node runtime).
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed. Run locally with the dead-export scan skipped, because that scan reports only files this PR doesn't touch (e.g. `extensions/knowledge/*`) and fails the same way on main.
- `check-test-lines-ratchet --base 3031a32908b --no-merge-base`: OK (slack 3).
- Independent Codex review (default, then gpt-5.6-sol at max effort): the one finding, the test-line ratchet, is fixed. The final pass had no findings.
- Broader Code Mode lanes (`code-mode.bridge*`, `agent-loop`, `auto-results`, `ask-user-tool`, prefix stability) ran in this PR's CI at `dc3c9c0`: 62 checks passed, 56 skipped, none failed.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve native sessions during worker recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained Codex conversations losing native continuity on worker reconnect or confirmed replacement, with useful exit diagnostics that do not export native stderr.

## User Impact

Retained reconnects require recorded native state. Exact provider-confirmed loss permits a fresh thread seeded from bounded retained history; failed recovery preserves the original binding. A preexisting home from interrupted startup does not prevent the first thread from starting. Refusals explain how to restore retained state or continue separately without deleting the binding. Diagnostics contain bounded enum/numeric facts, not prompts, credentials or raw stderr.

Depends on #201026 at `456819cbddd4`, targeting `galiniliev/main7-codex-worker-credentials`. Both depend on prerequisite `1f67db94064`. Land prerequisites and parent before retargeting to `main`. Recovery uses existing v41 columns without a new migration. Unknown/dormant state, inspection errors and requested teardown do not authorize fresh-thread recovery. If a replacement is lost before its binding commits, an older binding may require operator recovery; exact predecessor checks do not invent transitive lineage.

## Why This Change Was Made

Verified placement facts supply the current owner and retention policy. Unexpected provider-confirmed destruction records the exact attached predecessor before retirement in the existing transaction. Receipts preserve it through reopen and eligible redispatch. The native binding remains the existing-state authority; replacement commits only after history seeding succeeds.

Startup stderr is drained and classified immediately, but diagnostics wait until input-listener registration queues framed readiness. Aborting startup releases the wait without sending premature data or hanging cleanup. The bounded queue, privacy rules, framing and retained-state admission remain unchanged. The private contracts facade avoids loading heavyweight session runtime during registration.

## Evidence

### Compatibility replay and isolated Azure evidence

- Replayed published OpenClaw 2026.11.5 state through Doctor and two fresh Gateway starts at this head. Shared SQLite migrated 36→41 and agent SQLite 38→42. The native binding and all three transcript events remained byte-identical. The placement retained its environment identity and owner epoch. The released-version control and candidate both reclaimed the synthetic offline placement the same way. This used the source-built CLI and a synthetic placement.
- An isolated Gateway running this head enrolled an Azure Sandbox. Two real model turns succeeded, and the second resumed the original native Codex thread. After Azure stopped and restarted the Sandbox, OpenClaw reported the runner offline. A replacement enrolled for the same session and refused to start a new thread because the retained native home was missing. A read-only database check after shutdown verified the original binding. No provider-confirmed loss was recorded. History-seeded recovery after confirmed worker loss and the published updater path remain unverified.
- Eight provider-loss and three native worker-runtime cases passed. Hosted CI remains red on pnpm lockfile portability and the memory descriptor probe. Both failure signatures also appear in an earlier run. [Current CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44287145206) · [Earlier CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44280126105)
- Deployed this exact head as a private runtime package in a fresh Azure Container Apps environment. The installed commit matched, and direct in-container health and readiness probes both returned 200. Unauthenticated model listing returned 401. Authenticated listing returned 200 and advertised the default agent. This deployment smoke did not establish external worker enrollment.

<details>
<summary>Earlier validation and review history</summary>

- **8/8 broker-backed provider-loss cases** passed, including reopen, failed-spare retry, redispatch and ambiguous-loss refusal. Removing only the producer's loss argument caused the intended failure. **22/22** placement projection cases passed; three assertions were red before production wiring. The guidance/docs/provider selection passed **141/141**, including **115** native/lifecycle cases.
- [Hosted startup failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44280126105/job/134721795749) failed before worker authentication reached its pending effect. Two native startup tests reproduced the defect: diagnostic data before listener registration, and diagnostic data despite failed registration. Both failed on the old production code. The fixed native and diagnostics suites passed **6/6** with no private core imports in plugin tests.
- The isolated Gateway/paired-node Codex composition test passed with the same production fix, covering admitted-worker selection, resume, cancellation and cleanup. It used the pinned native binary and synthetic loopback inference, not a live model or account. **5/5** real Gateway worker Goal RPC cases passed separately.
- Parent evidence includes **43/43 real PostgreSQL**, **30/30 frozen-chain SQLite migration**, and **37/37 dispatch** cases. Released npm **2026.11.5** (`e13cf15ece9b`) produced settings, session identity and a three-event transcript that survived Doctor migration and two fresh-process reopens at `4eabcf3b2463` (shared **36→41**, agent **38→42**). This is not npm install-over, previous native-binding, placement-lineage or shipped-updater proof.
- Affected typechecks, lint, format, SDK boundaries and canonical budgets passed. Net child test growth is **856** lines with **456** allocated above the standard allowance, including the two native startup-ordering cases. Earlier build/API evidence is pinned to `a7a7984462ea`; the artifact build at `4eabcf3b2463` passed with UI budget warnings. Fresh scoped P0–P2 review found no actionable defect in the supplied startup repair. Earlier hosted review at `69253f04630a` confirmed both private-doc and refusal-guidance findings addressed.
- **Outstanding:** exact-head hosted CI/review and live worker/model/GitHub and native/updater compatibility. Earlier unrelated memory-probe and lock failures remain recorded. The configured Boat route lacks its API-key binding; approved worker command-auth provisioning is unverified. No credential fallback, live Gateway change, merge or release. Platinum readiness is not claimed.

</details>

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve worker GitHub execution credentials
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes worker-hosted Codex commands losing the session's admitted GitHub identity and automatic Goal continuations losing repository dispatch authority after the originating turn ends.

## User Impact

Dedicated-worker commands receive the selected GitHub identity and current credential. Installation and renewal require exact-generation acknowledgments; cleanup joins pending refresh and revocation. Git's helper is scoped to the admitted HTTPS host. This grants no additional repository permission and does not transfer model authentication.

First in a two-PR stack, extracted from `5eea78634ab` with Goal changes from `23dcc5f19b1`. Base remains `galiniliev/main7-worker-prerequisites` at `1f67db94064`; land those prerequisites before retargeting to `main`. Recovery is in #201032.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the Gateway grant owner, private worker profile, native command carrier and Goal queue. Automatic turns retain a dispatch factory, not a settled request's authority.

Prerequisite repairs preserve the declared v41 migration behavior, exact retained rows and rollback. Publication fixtures keep already-loaded identity modules synthetic by default and restore the actual preparation functions before tests that intentionally exercise native identity. Production credential and repository admission are unchanged by the fixture repair. No schema version, migration, credential store or authority source was added.

## Evidence

### Compatibility replay and isolated Azure evidence

- Exact-head hosted CI passed, including all 11 previously failing native identity cases. [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44287142431)
- Replayed published OpenClaw 2026.11.5 state through Doctor and two fresh Gateway starts at this head. Shared SQLite migrated 36→41 and agent SQLite 38→42. The native binding and all three transcript events remained byte-identical. The placement retained its environment identity and owner epoch. The released-version control and candidate both reclaimed the synthetic offline placement the same way. This used the source-built CLI and a synthetic placement.
- PostgreSQL 17.11 passed 14 selected migration and shared-state cases with the repository CI lock-table setting. Nine credential-transport and five schema-engine cases passed. The transport cases used synthetic grants.
- An isolated Azure Sandbox ran pinned Codex 0.164.0 with real worker-owned command authentication. The model completed a local marker command and returned the expected reply. Authenticated API and Git HTTPS reads succeeded separately on the controller. Live delivery of the GitHub App credential to the worker, genuine renewal, credentialed Goal continuation, and revocation remain pending an approved isolated signing configuration.
- Deployed this exact head as a private runtime package in a fresh Azure Container Apps environment. The installed commit matched, and direct in-container health and readiness probes both returned 200. Unauthenticated model listing returned 401. Authenticated listing returned 200 and advertised the default agent. This deployment smoke did not establish external worker enrollment.

<details>
<summary>Earlier validation and review history</summary>

- **9/9 transport cases** use real transport/client/duplex and a typed grant fixture at the exported private-local SDK boundary. They cover installation/renewal acknowledgments and cleanup, not live credentials. **5/5 real Gateway worker Goal RPC cases** passed; the new continuation assertion was red on prerequisite `1f67db94064`.
- Publication fixture coverage: the cached-module regression failed before the repair. The synthetic sibling batch passed **59/59**, and representative publication/admission suites passed **114/114**. The initial fixture repair regressed **11** intentional native-identity cases; all 11 reproduced locally. After explicit restoration, the mixed native/synthetic selection passed **16/16** and the two complete native/boundary files passed **59/59**. Hosted confirmation is pending.
- **43/43 real PostgreSQL cases** passed against task-owned loopback PostgreSQL 17.11, including migration, rollback, original-source preservation, Doctor and prepare-state; fixture containers and volumes were removed. **30/30 frozen-chain SQLite migration cases** and **37/37 dispatch cases** passed. An additional **29/29** cases use synthetic current-DDL fixtures and are not old-schema proof.
- Affected typechecks, lint, format, SDK guards and canonical test budgets passed. Net test growth is **719** lines, with **320** allocated above the standard allowance for the affected credential, Goal, dispatch, migration and publication fixture boundaries. Earlier build/API evidence is pinned to `a7a7984462ea`; the artifact build at `4eabcf3b2463` passed with UI budget warnings. Fresh scoped P0–P2 review found no actionable defect in the supplied repair source; the filename guard omitted the allocation, which the budget checker verified separately.
- Released npm **2026.11.5** (`e13cf15ece9b`) produced settings, session identity and a three-event transcript that survived Doctor migration and two fresh-process reopens at `4eabcf3b2463` (shared **36→41**, agent **38→42**). This is not npm install-over, previous native-binding or shipped-updater proof. Doctor config changes were recorded.
- **Outstanding:** exact-head hosted CI, including previously observed prerequisite pnpm-lock and memory-probe failures, and live worker/model/GitHub renewal and cleanup. The configured Boat route lacks its API-key binding; approved worker command-auth provisioning remains unverified. No fallback credentials, live Gateway changes, merge or release. Platinum readiness is not claimed.

</details>

Original implementation: @galiniliev. Review and repairs preserve the original contributor's authorship.

prs.title: fix: let Git checkout installs build updates again when the candidate sits inside the installed checkout
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Git source-checkout install cannot update to any build that contains #198661. The installed updater builds the candidate in a worktree nested inside the installed checkout (`<checkout>/.artifacts/.openclaw-update-preflight-*/worktree`). The candidate's `pnpm build` then stops at the AI package's declarations with `Declaration input escapes checkout: <checkout>/node_modules/undici/types/utility.d.ts`, and the update fails with `preflight-no-good-commit`. The running Gateway is not touched, but the instance never reaches the new version.

## User Impact

Git checkout installs can update to main again. The candidate's declaration build only uses files inside the candidate, no matter where the updater puts it. `release/2026.11.10` has already reverted #198661 (`9198da0289c`), so this fix is for main and for any future release that carries #198661.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause: `openai@7.47.0` ships declarations that probe `import('../node_modules/undici/index.d.ts')` and nine deeper `../` variants (the probes are marked `@ts-ignore`). Since #198661, tsdown declarations come from a single `tsgo -p … --listFiles` pass, and that pass reads the real filesystem. From the nested preflight worktree, the ninth probe resolves into the installed checkout's `node_modules/undici`. The boundary check then correctly refuses the build. Before #198661, the API-filesystem compile treated outside paths as absent, so the probe missed quietly. The build only passes when the parent's undici version matches the candidate's, because the compiler then dedupes to the candidate's copy. That is why `v2026.11.5` (undici 8.12.3) can still build `release/2026.11.10` (8.12.3), while `v2026.10.33` through `v2026.11.4` (8.12.2) cannot build it and none of them can build main (8.12.4).

Fix: if the command-line pass lists any file outside the checkout, its result is discarded and the same compile runs through the existing bounded API path (`compileNativeProject`, the pre-#198661 path). That path treats outside paths as absent. The boundary check in `local-check-runtime.mts` is unchanged. A link inside the checkout that leads outside still fails with `Declaration input escapes checkout`. The fast command-line pass still serves every build that reads nothing outside the checkout, which covers normal checkouts and CI.

Competing hypothesis rejected: a bare-module lookup missing inside the candidate and climbing to the parent. The trace shows the bare `undici` lookups resolve inside the candidate. The escape comes from a relative `../`×9 import (`trace: Resolving module '../../../../../../../../../node_modules/undici/index.d.ts' from …/openai/internal/types.d.mts`).

Test changes: #198661 pinned "parent-install shadowing fails loudly" as intentional. That behavior is the update blocker, so the four expectations it changed go back to their pre-#198661 values. The optional-import test now proves that the nested build succeeds, that changing the ancestor's install does not change the output, and that a local change does. A new negative control proves that an in-checkout link to the parent install still throws the escape. Paths that exist only outside the checkout now fail as TS2307/TS6053 (absent) instead of as an escape. "builds through a parent package link that resolves back inside the checkout" still passes unchanged.

Update behavior: the installed updater cannot be patched, but it builds the candidate with the candidate's own build scripts. Any candidate that contains this commit builds in the nested preflight worktree. No config, schema, dependency or lockfile change. Nothing is left for a person to do.

## Evidence

- Nested reproduction, the same commands the `v2026.11.5` updater runs (`pnpm install`, then `pnpm build` with `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS=1`, `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`, `BUILD_ALL_CACHE_ROOT=<checkout>/.artifacts/build-all-cache`), in `<checkout>/.artifacts/.openclaw-update-preflight-*/worktree` inside a `v2026.11.5` checkout with dependencies installed, macOS:
  - main base `799c2eb9129`: RED, exit 1 after 24 s, `tsdown-ai failed`, `Declaration input escapes checkout: <checkout>/node_modules/undici/types/utility.d.ts`.
  - this change on that base (first commit): GREEN, exit 0, full build 4m22s, no escape. The nested build with both commits was run on the release tree below: GREEN.
- `release/2026.11.10` (`f4b2aaf0be1`) nested inside a `v2026.11.4` checkout: RED, exit 1 after 31 s, same escape. Inside a `v2026.11.5` checkout it passes, exit 0, only because the undici versions match.
- Regression tests: `test/scripts/native-declaration-boundary.test.ts` and `test/scripts/tsdown-declaration-resolution.test.ts`. On base, the new nested test fails with the escape error, and the four restored expectations fail too. On head all pass. With `native-declaration-subprocess` and `extension-boundary-cache`, that is 34 passed and 4 skipped (platform skips).
- `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, oxlint on the touched files, oxfmt and `git diff --check` all pass.
- The rebase onto `f5e76417687` touched nothing under `scripts/lib`, `test/scripts`, the manifests, the lockfile or the tsconfigs, so the proof still holds.
- Independent review (fresh reviewer) found two real gaps, both fixed in the second commit with tests that fail on the first commit:
  1. The API fallback skipped the checkout boundary when a caller supplied no input policy. It now always applies the boundary; the negative control runs with and without `assertInput`, and on the first commit it resolved instead of rejecting.
  2. A checkout path containing a line break could glue an outside path onto the previous `--listFiles` line and hide the outside read. Such roots now use the bounded compile directly, and the regex splitter is gone.
  One reported gap is not fixed: a JS-only outer package without types is not listed by `--listFiles`. It existed before this PR, and strict settings still fail with TS7016. Left as a follow-up.
- Cost, one cold build each on this machine: a normal checkout reads nothing outside, so it keeps the single command-line pass. Normal (not nested) `pnpm build` on this head: exit 0 in 4m45s, `write-unified-entry-dts` 1m05s. A nested candidate whose pass reads outside the checkout compiles twice: `write-unified-entry-dts` took 1m38-1m50s, against 1m20s for the API-only path on the reverted release branch. The whole nested build stays near 4 minutes.
- Removed test content: the old "fails closed" half of the optional-import test. Its local-only assertions are now covered by the first compile of the rewritten test, so the removal is safe.

Not proven: the real `openclaw update` Docker end-to-end cell on this head. `autoreview` does not run on this machine.

## Cherry-pick for release/2026.11.10

`release/2026.11.10` has since reverted #198661 (`9198da0289c`, now at `995f9059b6e`). It no longer has the command-line declaration path, so it needs no backport, and `git revert -n 5a7d1718aa5` on the new tip is a no-op. This PR is for main and for any future release that carries #198661.

On the old release tip `f4b2aaf0be1`, which still carried #198661, this fix was tested as follows:
- Both commits cherry-pick cleanly (3 files).
- Both declaration test files pass on the picked tree: 30 passed, 4 skipped.
- Nested build from a `v2026.11.4` checkout, with the picked tree as the candidate: RED before the pick (exit 1 after 31 s, escape), GREEN after it (exit 0, 4m04s, no escape).

prs.title: feat: notify users when they arrive or leave, using device location updates
prs.body: Resolves #163480 ## What Problem This Solves iOS nodes emit `location.update` events on significant location changes, but the gateway drops them as `unsupported_event` — verified by two independent users on current builds (#163480). This PR makes the event consumable and closes the full chain: **fix → significance detection → event-driven APNs notification**, with no heartbeat, no session turn, and no coordinates in logs. - **Gateway:** `location.update` is validated, dispatched to the node-event consumer registry, and instrumented at the dispatch boundary. The response ack path no longer crashes (`logGateway.info` → `warn` — every event ack previously failed with `UNAVAILABLE` after dispatch). - **Plugin surface:** `registerNodeEventConsumer` — a plugin-API subscription hook for gateway-validated node events (currently allowlisted to `location.update`). This is the "plugin hook" requested in #163480. - **memory-core consumer:** armed location intents evaluate each fix against fence geometry. Enter fences fire on the first inside fix when armed from afar (previously required a 0→1 crossing that never happened when the intent was armed while already outside); stale-facts-cache reads no longer mask fires. - **Direction-gated crossings (bug fix):** an exit fence no longer fires on an arrival fix, and an enter fence no longer fires on a departure fix — see below. This was found during live verification, not by the test suite. - **Delivery:** fires push an APNs alert at fire time (new plugin-SDK surface `sendNodeIntentAlert`, category `openclaw.location-intent`) — delivery no longer waits for the target session's next turn. The routed system-event enqueue is retained as an in-session record; push failures are logged and never re-arm the one-shot. ## Direction-gating bug (found and fixed during live verification) `decideLocationFire` gated only *one* side of each transition on direction. The inside branch fired for `previous === 0` regardless of direction, and the outside branch fired for `previous === 1` regardless of direction. Consequences observed on real drives: - **2026-11-13 06:33** — a Göteborg *arrival* fence fired on the user's morning *departure* from inside the fence. - **2026-11-16 15:29** — a home *exit* fence fired while the user was *arriving* home (the fix that also correctly fired the Göteborg arrival fence in the same second). Both branches are now direction-gated: `enter` fires only on 0→1 (including the first inside fix when armed from afar), `exit` fires only on 1→0. Each branch carries the live-fire evidence in a comment, and two regression tests cover both directions — the existing test's comment promised this behavior but never asserted it, which is how the bug survived review. ## Evidence - **2026-11-14, live drive:** Skene fence (1.5 km, enter) fired on a real outside→inside crossing from an unsolicited background fix; the APNs alert appeared on the owner's phone (screenshot-timestamped, matching the log fire and the intent description text). Exactly one fire, no duplicates. - **2026-11-16:** home-exit fence (200 m) fired on a real departure; the ack-crash fix verified live (three fixes traced, zero `UNAVAILABLE`). - **2026-11-17, full drive test (3/3 fences, 0 evaluation errors):** | Time | Fence | Fix distance | Accuracy | Outcome | |---|---|---|---|---| | 10:58:46 | home exit (200 m) | 7 m *inside* | 16 m | baselined, **no fire** ✓ | | 11:21:49 | home exit (200 m) | 512 m outside | 46 m | **fired** — correct direction | | 11:37:28 | store (1000 m) | 427 m from store | 11 m | **fired** | | 11:42:51 | destination (1000 m) | 52 m from center | 34 m | **fired** | All three notifications owner-confirmed on the phone (screenshots matching the log timestamps). The exit fence baseline-then-fire sequence is the live proof of the direction-gate fix; the destination fire (52 m from a decoded Plus code) validates arrival geometry end to end. - Consumer tests assert: single push per fire, fire-on-first-inside-fix, no re-arm on push failure, and both direction gates. - **2026-11-18, latest-stable upgrade proof:** the review asked for upgrade evidence covering the changed `standing_intents` fields. The v2026.11.5 release's shipped agent schema (schema version 38, pre-location `standing_intents`) is frozen as a fixture; a database built from it migrates to the current schema, the four additive location columns and `idx_standing_intents_location` arrive, an existing keyword-intent row survives untouched with absent-feature defaults, and a location intent in the stored kernel format is accepted by the migrated table's constraints. Covered by `openclaw-agent-latest-stable-upgrade.test.ts`; fence evaluation and delivery on the identical post-migration shape are covered by memory-core's suites. The added test lines carry a justified allocation record (`config/test-lines-allocations/200867-location-update-consumer.txt`). - **2026-11-18, PostgreSQL store upgrade (review P1):** opening an existing PostgreSQL agent database previously failed schema admission after this change — the location columns changed the canonical DDL with no version bump or migration, so `verifyPostgresSchemaDefinition` threw a schema-drift error, and the migration derivator made every historical version inherit the new fields. The agent schema now advances 43 → 44 on both engines through the existing versioned-migration owners: a new PostgreSQL migration adds the columns, NOT VALID checks (all-new columns cannot be violated by existing rows), and the index in one transaction; the v43 migration entry now targets the pre-location historical shape so old versions keep their real catalog; SQLite converges through its existing additive machinery on every migration branch. Schema 43 remains a supported witness version. Verified by the same suites as above — 55/55 across migration, latest-stable, and location kernel tests. ## Known limitation: fence radius cannot buy lead time at driving speed Reported by the owner on the 2026-11-17 drive: the store fence fired **after** he had passed the store. Measured along-track against the store→destination leg, the firing fix was **+404 m past** the store (137 m cross-track, 427 m straight-line — i.e. comfortably *inside* the 1 km circle, 573 m from the edge). The cause is fix cadence, not fence logic: - 4.28 km travelled between consecutive fixes → 49 km/h on a ~5-minute significant-change cadence - a 1 km circle is a 2 km-wide band; at 4.28 km spacing the chance any given fix lands inside is only ~47%, i.e. whether it fires before or after the POI is close to a coin flip **Enlarging the radius does not fix this.** To gain one fix-interval of lead you would need R > 4.2 km at 50 km/h and > 6.7 km at 80 km/h. At that size the notification fires while the user is kilometres away, so "you're passing the store" becomes false. Radius trades precision for reliability; there is no setting that delivers both at driving speed. This is a property of the fix-delivery platform, not of the fence evaluator. The mechanism that actually fixes approach timing is **device-side region monitoring** (`CLCircularRegion`, 20-region limit): the OS surfaces a callback *at the boundary crossing*, independent of the significant-change cadence. That is the planned device-fence direction, and this drive is its concrete justification. Until then, a fence that fires shortly *after* a high-speed POI is behaving as designed given the fixes it receives. ## Consent and privacy (answers the labels on #163480) - **Consumption is consent-scoped:** fixes are evaluated only against location intents the user explicitly armed ("notify me when I arrive at X"). No armed intents → no consumption into anything user-visible; fixes are evaluated and discarded. - **No precise-location persistence:** coordinates are never written to gateway logs, prompts, or system events. The dispatch-boundary log line records the event name and node id only. (The prior closed PR #50936 was flagged for passive precise-location delivery; this design evaluates and discards.) - **No autonomous turns:** a location fire pushes a notification and enqueues a passive in-session record. It never starts an agent turn — consistent with the passive device-event direction (#196989). Any follow-up ("lets stop by X") is a user-initiated turn. - **Existing consent basis:** the event only exists when the user has granted iOS Always location to the app; this PR consumes that signal purpose-scoped, per #163480's discussion. ## Scope boundaries - One consumer per event by design (registrar rejects a second subscriber for `location.update`; dispatch uses first-match). Fan-out to multiple consumers is a deliberate follow-up, not included here — it widens the location access surface and deserves its own security review. - No fix history is stored; fixes are evaluated against armed intents and dropped. A bounded presence/fix store is a separate proposal. - The event-driven push is the interim surfacing policy ("fired ⇒ notify"). Whether and how to notify is a policy layer question; the follow-up direction (below) explores a tunable local judge for it. - Device-side region monitoring (the fix for the lead-time limitation above) is out of scope for this PR. - **File structure is ratchet-driven, not stylistic.** `location.update` handling lives in `server-node-events-location.ts` alongside the existing `server-node-events-*.ts` handlers. The chat `subscribe`/`unsubscribe` arm moved to `server-node-events-chat-subscription.ts` for one reason: the dispatcher is grandfathered in `config/max-lines-baseline.txt`, and that ratchet rejects *any* growth, so a two-line case arm plus its import had to be offset. That extraction is behaviour-preserving and covered by the existing chat subscribe/unsubscribe tests, but it is unrelated to this feature — call it out if you would rather it land separately. ## Follow-up direction (not in this PR) Significance is currently declared geometry. The next layer separates geometry (deterministic, in code) from interruption policy (a local decision model, evaluated only on events, with the fence verdict as the fail-open baseline). An 11-case eval (incl. negative controls and a conjunction scenario: "passing a store × open shopping-list need") found local decision models (`clef-flash`, `d3:2b` via Ollama's `/v1/systemone`) that discriminate correctly with ~160-token calls. Full methodology and results: https://gist.github.com/zigit/8c765c33d1edea1435f9b26d6d22c896 This PR intentionally ships only the deterministic layer. ## Why this shape (the box, not the cloud) > "It ain't gonna be some cloud… then I don't know who has my shit. It will be > like a box that knows what I need, and when I pass by Ralph's on my way home > I get a message: 'You know we ain't got no milk.' That's what I expect we > have in the future." > > — will.i.am, on stage at CES 2013, as recalled by this PR's author That quote is the reason this PR is shaped the way it is, and the reason the example notification in the drive-test screenshot reads *"We ain't even got no milk."* Thirteen years later the box is an OpenClaw gateway on a Mac, the milk is a reminder in a local database, and the message arrives within a few hundred metres of the store — verified on a real drive, with the notification landing on the phone as the car passed. Two parts of the quote turned out to be design constraints rather than rhetoric: - **"not some cloud… I don't know who has my shit"** — fixes are evaluated against armed intents and discarded; coordinates never reach a log, a prompt, a system event, or a third-party API. The follow-up judge layer runs on a local decision model precisely so that the one component that reasons about *where you are* does not require sending *where you are* anywhere. - **"knows what I need"** — the trigger is a conjunction the user declared (an armed intent, an open shopping need), not an inference over harvested behaviour. Consent is the mechanism, and it is per-intent and revocable. This PR ships the deterministic half: geometry in code, significance declared by the user. The contextual half — a small local model deciding whether a crossing is worth interrupting you — is the follow-up below. ## Change type - [x] Bug fix (ack-path crash; enter-fence miss when armed from afar; direction-ungated crossings) - [x] Feature (node-event plugin hook; event-driven location-intent push) - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Docs - [ ] Tests (covered by existing consumer tests; new asserts added for both direction gates)

prs.title: fix(feishu): keep CardKit streaming alive past the ten-minute window
prs.body:
Related: #161350 (dispatcher-side settlement/deduplication; intentionally separate from this change)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Feishu streaming card freezes at its last snapshot and a second static card is posted when an agent turn runs longer than ten minutes.

Feishu CardKit closes a card's `streaming_mode` ten minutes after it was switched on. The next element write fails with `code=200850 card streaming timeout` and every later one with `code=300309 streaming mode is closed`. `FeishuStreamingSession` does not handle this, so the final text can never be written into the card, `closeWithResult` throws, and the reply dispatcher recovers with a second delivery.

## User Impact

User impact: long-running Feishu turns now finish in the same card they started in — no frozen preview, no duplicate card. Short turns (< 8 minutes) are unchanged apart from one `Date.now()` comparison per push. No configuration change and no new options.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Renew before expiry** — when a push happens 8 minutes or more after `streaming_mode` was switched on, toggle it `false → true` via `PATCH /cardkit/v1/cards/:id/settings`. This restarts the server-side timer and also re-opens a window the server already closed (same mechanism as larksuite/channel-sdk-node#21).
- **On 200850/300309** — renew once and retry the write; if renewal fails, mark the window closed and stop element writes instead of spamming (one production gateway logged 19,597 × `300309` in September).
- **Finalize without streaming** — at close, when the window is closed, land the final text and note with a full-card update `PUT /cardkit/v1/cards/:id` (`streaming_mode:false`, same header) and skip the streaming close. The returned `content` then equals the final text, so the dispatcher sends no recovery card. If the full-card update also fails, the existing `FeishuStreamingFinalizationError` path with the accepted preview content is unchanged.

Window helpers live in `streaming-card-window.ts` to keep `streaming-card.ts` under the `max-lines` limit.

## Evidence

**Live observation** (production gateway running `@openclaw/feishu@2026.9.3` with the same logic applied to the bundle; a controlled 11m20s turn — four `sleep 170` steps — crossed the server window):

```
16:04:26 [feishu] Started streaming: cardId=7691236156303166665, messageId=om_x100b64f8666…
16:19:04 [feishu] Renewed streaming window (age): cardId=7691236156303166665
16:19:30 [feishu] Closed streaming: cardId=7691236156303166665
16:19:30 [feishu] dispatch complete (queuedFinal=true, replies=1)
```

Zero `200850`/`300309` in the run; the chat shows one card with the four step lines, the final line and the footer. Before the change, the same gateway's journal shows every `200850` landing exactly 10:00 after `Started streaming` in 11 of 60 streaming turns, each followed by a frozen card plus a recovery card.

**Full-card fallback path, real Feishu API probe** (standalone script against CardKit, no gateway; same request shapes as the patch): create streaming card → two element writes OK → `PATCH settings streaming_mode=false` (simulates the server closing the window) → element write rejected with `code=300309` → `PUT /cardkit/v1/cards/:id` full card accepted with `code=0` → the chat shows the card with the final text and note (visual readback by the operator).

**Focused tests** (this branch):

- 4 new cases in `streaming-card.test.ts`: age-based renewal on the same card (two settings PATCHes then the write, sequence strictly increasing); re-opening a server-closed window and retrying the rejected write once; stopping element writes and finalizing via full-card update with header and note preserved and no streaming close afterwards; partial-visibility finalization error when both renewal and the full-card update are rejected.
- `streaming-card.test.ts` 34/34, `streaming-card.error-release.test.ts` 3/3, `reply-dispatcher.test.ts` 79/79.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on the three touched files.

Not changed here: the Feishu per-chat 300-second sequential-queue cap (#70133). It evicts a timed-out task from the queue without aborting it and is unrelated to the card window.

prs.title: fix(automations): let authenticated owners inspect run receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an authenticated configured channel owner can load an existing automation with `get`, but its `runs` request loses management authority and can return “Automation not found” for that same job.

## User Impact

Owners and Control UI administrators can inspect execution receipts for automations they can already manage, without changing job ownership or creating replacement jobs. Ordinary caller restrictions remain unchanged.

**Draft for permission-contract review:** existing admission tests explicitly exclude `cron.runs` from management. This proposes changing that contract; maintainer approval is needed. Transcript access (`cron.history`) remains excluded. No live installation or deployment is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

The management grant allowlist includes `cron.get` but excludes `cron.runs`. The tool therefore sends run-history requests without the method-bound management grant. This adds run-receipt reads to that existing mechanism and aligns management-only schema/help, retaining run/method binding, single-use redemption, live-authority checks, expiry, revocation, and self-job restrictions.

The regression was reproduced on the affected 2026.11.3 source revision `847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f`. The candidate has now been replayed onto upstream main `f817a8b3eb1` to resolve the diverged release-line conflicts, preserving newer automation policy checks and binding behavior. It does not alter the scheduler or claim to repair worker-memory failures.

## Evidence

- New tool-boundary regression calls `get` followed by `runs` for configured-owner and Control UI admin contexts. Both cases failed on the original code: the owner path omitted the grant, and management-only execution rejected the action.
- Candidate: **97 targeted tests passed** on the updated candidate across tool management (14), grant security (29), tool schema (45), and creator-context admission (9). This supersedes the 59-test result on the release-based candidate.
- Existing admission expectations were explicitly updated for the proposed run-receipt permission; transcript history remains a negative control. This policy adjustment is not represented as independent evidence that the prior restriction was accidental.
- Scoped type-aware lint, core TypeScript checking, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Updated-main verification: the initial four-file run identified two stale management action/error-text expectations; those were corrected and the affected file passed (14 tests, 7.98s command wall time). The other three files passed unchanged.
- **Independent local review unavailable:** default reviewer preflight found no standalone Codex CLI; the documented OpenClaw reviewer returned `reviewer_unavailable` (exit 1, no report). The requester explicitly approved submitting this draft with that limitation. This is not a clean review claim or a waiver of upstream review.
### Receipt-disclosure follow-up

Added `cron.management-receipts.integration.test.ts` in response to the review of `b03f3f418b73`. It reuses the admitted-run fixture but calls the production Gateway request router, method-bound grant redemption, CronService, SQLite receipt persistence, and worker-backed receipt hydration. No Gateway call, authorization decision, or receipt payload is mocked.

- Control UI administrator and configured channel-owner: `cron.get` then per-job `cron.runs` returns the persisted synthetic receipt from a different creator conversation.
- Ordinary non-owner: both requests fail with not-found and no response payload.
- Configured owner removed during an awaited receipt read: the test delegates to the real storage reader, pauses only its return, removes the owner from the runtime config, and resumes. The Gateway returns an authority error without disclosing the hydrated receipt.
- Negative control: temporarily removing only `cron.runs` from the management allowlist makes both authorized cases fail (admin receipt request denied; owner grant mint rejected). The ordinary non-owner denial still passes. The production allowlist was restored afterward.
- Focused integration test: 3/3 passed; test time 2.33s, runner duration 9.07s, command wall time 11.23s on the first successful warm run. CI seconds not yet available.
- Final adjacent suite: **33/33 passed** across receipt visibility, requester continuation, and the new management receipt integration (83.54s command wall time, including compilation).
- Gateway-methods test TypeScript shard and scoped type-aware lint passed. The requester-continuation test's existing help-text expectation was updated to match the proposed action list.
- Test-line allocation covers only this branch's net 165 test lines. The new cases close the storage/disclosure gap not reached by the original mocked-Gateway tests; no new production hook or authorization path was added.

**Limits:** this is isolated in-process Gateway integration proof using synthetic admitted-client facts, not a network login, live model/channel session, or installed-release E2E. Full CI and post-install verification remain outstanding. Maintainers still need to approve cross-conversation receipt access. No live authorization controls were patched or bypassed.

AI-assisted implementation; submitted for upstream review, not automatic merge.


## Authenticated shipped-entry-point proof (head 2a6431e1b58)

Built this candidate in an isolated Gateway and used real Control UI browser authentication (trusted-proxy synthetic identities), actual chat composer, and the shipped automations tool. No management grants were manually minted or injected.

| Authenticated caller | get | runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Administrator, new chat session | Exact existing job returned | One persisted successful receipt and its unique summary returned |
| Ordinary member, separate chat session | Not found | Not found; receipt summary absent |

The job was created and executed through real Gateway RPC outside the administrator chat session; it is foreign to that chat session, not owned by another human. The receipt is produced by the isolated scheduler execution, not inserted as a fake row.

Committed reproduction: `ui/src/e2e/cron-management-receipt-proof.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (registered in UI E2E routing).

```text
Authenticated automation receipt tool proof
reads foreign receipts as admin and denies an ordinary non-owner through authenticated chat tools
Test Files 1 passed
Tests 1 passed
Scenario 6.327s
```

Runtime build (including Control UI), scoped type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace and test-line budget checks passed. Independent review inspected both the fixture and saved actual tool outputs. Browser/Gateway cleanup completed.

Limits: deterministic loopback provider, not live external model inference; configured Discord-owner ingress remains unproved. This browser test was not repeated on the original permission implementation; earlier in-process red/green controls remain separate. No installed Gateway or billing watch changed. Maintainer permission-scope approval remains required.
