prs.title: fix(telegram): honor group mention activation for commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram currently treats an authorized bare slash command as an effective mention in groups. That lets `/steer` start an agent turn, or `/stop` / `/new` affect a session, even when the group's effective activation is `mention`.

This patch makes Telegram group and forum-topic commands follow the effective mention policy before native dispatch, text-command admission, media download, pending-text cancellation, or ingress supersede. It uses the existing `requireMention` / `/activation` contract; there is no new config surface.

| Context | Bare command | Command addressed to this bot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group/topic with effective `mention` activation | Ignored | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| Group/topic with effective `always` activation | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| DM, including direct-message topics | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |

prs.title: feat(streaming): allow a separate command progress limit
prs.body:
Closes #157614

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot keep raw shell commands compact while allowing longer human-readable progress lines: both currently share one character limit.

## User Impact

Adds optional `streaming.progress.commandMaxLineChars`, for example:

```json5
progress: {
  toolProgress: true,
  commandText: "raw",
  maxLineChars: 400,
  commandMaxLineChars: 100,
}
```

Omitting the new key preserves existing behavior. It neither enables raw command text nor changes default visibility. Native Telegram/Slack labels and status presentation retain their existing limits; the override bounds command detail there. Platform-wide message limits still apply. This is presentation control, not redaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing command-bearing classification now survives progress-line snapshots so shared text, native Telegram live/adopted cards, and Slack cards/task chunks can use the same optional setting without guessing from displayed prose.

No new SDK exports, model calls, shell parser, migration, or default changes. Pure progress config readers move into the existing config-reader module, Telegram live/adopted rendering share account-option resolution, and Slack title deduplication is isolated as a pure render helper. Canonical UI hints describe the new field as a display-only limit rather than a privacy boundary. Existing oversized-file ratchets stay green without exemptions.

Config surface metric: **one optional setting**, projected into **ten channel schema paths** (channel baseline 3786 → 3796). The generated schema metadata and config documentation baseline are refreshed intentionally for that setting. Core/plugin config counts are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact-head focused validation passes **100/100** across shared streaming, compositor, lifecycle, schema, and UI-hint suites. Direct boundary probes also cover Telegram plain/rich rendering, Slack card/native updates, nested account inheritance, Unicode-safe compaction, invalid schema values, and the extracted Slack title helper.
- Negative coverage: ordinary prose and non-command tool paths containing shell words keep their general budget; raw/status privacy remains unchanged; invalid config values are rejected; omitted override inherits `maxLineChars`.
- Regression provenance: the four shell/wrapper command-limit cases fail on the unpatched `streaming.ts` because the rendered commands exceed the requested limit, then pass with this change.
- Existing fixture extension only; no new sleeps, polling implementation, Gateway boot, or external credentials.
- The deterministic pre-PR wrapper passes on frozen base `ef54f6720460` at exact signed head `27eb8524489a` (merge tree `d9fd44e5aa7a`), including core and extension source/test typechecks, changed-file lint/format, dead-export scan, generated metadata/docs, SDK boundaries, and repository ratchets.
- Fresh independent exact-head review found no P0-P2 issue.

**Remaining evidence:** live Telegram Test Server/userbot and Slack-client before/after proof, plus hosted CI. Local transport-boundary proof is not claimed as live-client proof.

AI-assisted implementation and tests. Release note: progress streaming can independently limit raw command text while preserving longer commentary with `streaming.progress.commandMaxLineChars`.

prs.title: fix(codex): complete explicit final messages without false interrupt markers
prs.body:
Related: #111019

## Merge Brief

- **Problem:** clean explicit Codex finals were persisted as false user interruptions.
- **Value:** native completion stays clean while a fixed 10-second fallback still bounds a genuinely stuck turn.
- **Smallest complete fix:** release successful finals through native completion and reopen steering admission only after the app-server confirms a queued steer was consumed.
- **Scope:** Codex app-server attempt lifecycle only; no protocol, config, provider, or `sessions_yield` contract change.
- **Risk:** session-state ordering; guarded by red-before/green-after regression and real app-server traces.
- **Proof:** focused `74/74`, pinned Codex `0.164.0` real-runtime `5/5`, and canonical pre-PR receipt exit `0`.
- **Non-goals:** changing ordinary new-inbound fallback, timeout ownership, or historical delivery telemetry.
- **Maintainer ask:** review exact head `8d65f46f07f3` and its correction-after-presteer lifecycle proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Codex app-server turns that deliver a confirmed final source reply were released through `turn/interrupt`. That persisted Codex's canonical false "user interrupted" marker into an otherwise clean thread rollout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Successful terminal delivery is not a user abort. The turn should finish through Codex's native `turn/completed` path when it wraps normally, while retaining a bounded escape hatch for runaway generation.

This deliberately does **not** change `sessions_yield`: yield retains OpenClaw's current parent-resumption contract and continues to interrupt/release the child turn immediately.

## Behavior

- A confirmed final source reply lets Codex finish through its native `turn/completed` event, avoiding a false "user interrupted" marker in the rollout.
- After the terminal tool batch settles, one absolute 10-second timer bounds the wait; later output cannot extend it.
- A steer confirmed consumed by the native server opens the next steering-admission epoch, so a correction can reach the still-active answer instead of falling into durable fallback.
- Ordinary new-inbound rejection/queue fallback, sibling settlement, and terminal ownership remain unchanged.
- If Codex does not finish inside the grace period, OpenClaw uses the existing interrupt fallback.
- `sessions_yield` remains exempt from this path and keeps its immediate interrupt/handoff behavior.

## User Impact

Long-lived Codex threads no longer accumulate false interruption context after ordinary explicit final-message delivery. A delivered reply remains successful if OpenClaw later needs the bounded fallback interrupt.

## Evidence

- Exact signed head: `8d65f46f07f311a4683a2bee661f824c4505c29e`; tree `ff71f06c42550a9e2db273f5181c727dff8b1cb9`.
- Frozen main: `13900faa92e1e5e33860ea7a8690d93b444c88d5`; conflict-clean merge tree: `4dcee24f707198c1c0911ca645290aa1e2fedbfe`.
- The canonical pre-PR gate passed with exit `0`: formatting, production and test type graphs, type-aware lint, dead exports, SQLite ratchets, plugin boundaries, import cycles, hosted mirrors, and `git diff --check`.
- Focused lifecycle/steering suites pass `74/74`. The new owning-boundary regression was red before the repair because `acceptsSteering` stayed false after consuming input B, then green after resetting only the current attempt's admission latch.
- A real isolated run against the repository-pinned Codex app-server `0.164.0` passes `5/5`: clean final uses native completion with zero interrupts/abort markers; a genuine runaway receives one interrupt after about 10 seconds; `sessions_yield` interrupts immediately; ordinary post-final inbound persists as a distinct fallback; and correction C produces a second real steer, reaches ordered request 3 while B is active, persists no fallback, and completes naturally.
- The first repaired-head runtime attempt is preserved: product behavior was already correct, but the proof harness incorrectly required B's superseded downstream tool call. Only that proof assertion changed before the final `5/5` run.
- No app-server protocol or configuration surface changes.

prs.title: fix(discord): return delegated finals to realtime voice
prs.body:
## Merge Brief

- **Problem:** a Discord realtime consult can yield for delegated work, but the eventual child final is written to text/session state without reliably returning to the requesting voice turn.
- **Why now:** the live voice agent can report uncertainty even when delegated work completed successfully.
- **Value:** delegated results return to the active Discord voice conversation exactly once.
- **Smallest complete fix:** attach trusted requester finals to the accepted voice turn, preserve them across compaction and overlapping yields, and invoke delayed provider callbacks under their live plugin owner rather than a retired caller scope.
- **Scope:** requester-final bookkeeping, trusted PluginRuntime plumbing, Discord realtime delivery, and realtime callback lifetime ownership.
- **Risk:** late, stale, duplicate, or fallback speech; mitigated by exact agent/session/run matching, provider epochs, lifecycle revocation, untrusted-ingress stripping, and promoted-final suppression.
- **Proof:** 68/68 focused tests, exact base-red/current-green callback-lifetime proof, 39/39 selected repository checks, and a real isolated Discord acoustic replay on signed head `1b7519170824f9ed07dfcca7cece1f8dd79628a2`.
- **Non-goals:** no delegation redesign, restart persistence, new user configuration, or cross-channel behavior change.
- **Owner decision requested:** this adds an optional field to the PluginRuntime command parameter type, exported through the Plugin SDK, and permits overlapping yielded attachments. Please confirm that shared contract direction.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord realtime voice routes forced consults through the agent-proxy ingress. If that agent turn yields while delegated work continues, the later child final must survive session rotation and return to the same active realtime provider. The prior path could lose the final during compaction, settle it under a retired plugin invocation scope, or let an empty tool result trigger fallback speech before the deferred exact final arrived.

Browser Talk already attaches requester finals for this lifecycle. This change applies the same ownership model to the trusted Discord realtime path and closes the delayed provider-callback boundary exposed by live acoustic testing.

## What Changed

- add a host-owned `requesterFinal` sink to trusted agent command options and strip it from public ingress
- register after foreground preparation selects the accepted session, then follow durable session-ID rotations
- preserve overlapping yielded requester turns and revoke every matching attachment when a session ends
- transfer the promoted child final into Discord's existing exact-speech queue only while the same realtime provider epoch remains active
- suppress the empty promoted tool result so it cannot generate fallback speech before the deferred exact final
- dispatch delayed subagent settlement outside retired caller scopes and re-enter the exact live plugin owner
- bind provider-to-host realtime callbacks to their owning plugin instance while explicitly exiting stale invocation contexts

## Evidence

### Deterministic proof

- focused suites: **68/68 passed**
  - talk session-runtime callback ownership: 26
  - requester-final attachment lifecycle: 9
  - PluginRuntime requester-final plumbing: 2
  - Discord realtime consult delivery: 26
  - OpenAI optional-capture bridge: 5
- exact negative control: the added provider-callback regression fails on pre-fix head `dfcb4c8f06eb` with `Plugin invocation scope is closed`; it passes on the repaired head
- reviewer-reported preflight-compaction failure is reproduced on prior PR head `7699d8cade77` and passes after registration follows the accepted successor session
- serial requester-wake continuation regression passes after transfer lookup selects by batch/session identity before replacing the requester turn ID
- canonical pre-PR wrapper: **39/39 selected repository checks passed** on signed head `1b7519170824`
- format, lint, typegraphs, dead-code, schema, import-cycle, sidecar, SQLite, and changed-scope gates passed

### Live acoustic Discord proof

The signed exact head ran in a fresh isolated ClawLab state against a private Discord guild. The existing bot was shared across disjoint guilds; production configuration and the production Gateway were not changed or restarted.

- fixed spoken request injected through the QA user's synthetic microphone
- exactly one new Discord final message: `delegated final proof complete`
- receive-side PCM capture recorded the initial acknowledgement and the later delegated final
- local transcription: `Got it. I'll run that through the agent and then share what it returns. Delegated Final Proof Complete.`
- delegated-final phrase occurs acoustically exactly once
- capture: `129.365333s`, peak `0.807892`, SHA-256 `11e57378fde8a303b623b1ddaf855051d26a54c7e6f0ddbd21805ea914b4da1a`
- zero closed-scope warnings in the live transaction

The raw WAV and account credentials remain private; the public proof is the sanitized transcript, exact counts, hash, and runtime receipts.

## Scope Boundaries

- no change to child-agent execution or yield semantics
- no persistence across restart
- no new user configuration; the optional trusted PluginRuntime parameter type is SDK-visible
- no delivery to a replaced or inactive realtime provider session
- no production Gateway/config mutation was used for proof

## Review History

- ClawSweeper's compaction P2 is covered by exact base-red/current-green regressions.
- The first hosted run's serial continuation regression is fixed and locally re-proven.
- Live proof exposed additional retired-scope and fallback-speech defects; each now has a focused regression and the final exact-head acoustic replay passes.

Three lines in AGENTS.md steer agents toward adding code after a red check instead of removing more or stopping:

Net: three lines changed, 85 characters shorter.

Docs-only: `git diff --check` clean.

prs.title: fix: Git checkout updates across a schema change no longer end as post-update-failed after the new release starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a Git checkout install that uses the release layout, an update that changes a database schema succeeds and then reports failure. The new release starts, migrates state and serves, but `openclaw update` exits 1 with `post-update-failed` ("SQLite database pathname changed while its worker owner is active; close the existing store first") and says "Your Gateway is still serving 2026.11.5; nothing to restore". Plugin convergence, the post-plugin Doctor, deferred inspections and owed-step settlement for that update never run, and run history records the update as failed.

## User Impact

User impact: an update across a schema change on a Git release install now finishes with exit 0 and a `succeeded` run record, and its post-update steps run in the same update.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause: the updater opens the shared state database through its shared-state worker owner early in the run, and that owner keeps the file open for up to 30 minutes of idle time. When the Gateway restarts into the new release, the new release's boot upgrade replaces `state/openclaw.sqlite` by copy and swap and keeps the old file as `openclaw.sqlite.pre-<buildId>`. The updater's owner still pins the old file under the same pathname, so the SQLite broker refuses the first new open after the restart. That refusal is correct: two owners in one process must not address one pathname with different files.

The fix keeps that check and stops holding the file across the restart. Around the Gateway restart and its verification, the updater now suspends its progress reader and closes its shared-state handles. When the restart settles, it closes anything opened meanwhile, revokes the path admissions and resumes progress. The remaining steps then reopen the current file by path. This is the same close, revoke and suspend sequence the update Doctor child already uses around its exclusive custody (`runUpdateDoctorProcess`). The wrapper sits at the caller of `maybeRestartService` in `update-command-post-update.ts` and applies only when the Gateway actually restarts. It covers the Git release successor wait, the service refresh restart that the observed run used, and the restart after plugin convergence.

Run history: rows written before the restart are committed before the successor starts, and the boot upgrade copies them into the new file (`update_runs` is not an ephemeral table in the swap map), so the run is neither lost nor duplicated. The new end-to-end run shows the pre-restart steps in the new file and the run finishing `succeeded`. One window remains outside this change: a one-shot ledger write that lands after the successor's copy and before its swap stays only in the `.pre-` file. The boot upgrade owner is moving to in-place migration on a separate branch, which removes that window in the common case. This change is correct with and without that change, because the copy-and-swap fallback can still happen.

Other paths:
- Package installs: the new package's Doctor migrates the databases while the Gateway is stopped, inside the existing Doctor child custody (close, revoke, reopen), so the boot upgrade finds nothing outdated. They are not affected. The wrapper still applies to their restart and only closes and reopens handles.
- Legacy in-place Git runner: it runs the target Doctor before restarting, the same as package installs. Not affected.
- `--no-restart`: the updater does not restart the Gateway, and the swap happens at a later start after the updater has exited. Not affected. The wrapper is skipped, so the updater keeps its open handles and their admission.
- Managed-service handoff: the helper runs the same `finishUpdate` path, so it is covered by the same wrapper.

### Update behavior for published updaters

The fix runs in the installed updater, so it takes effect for updates run by an updater that contains it. An installed updater that has #201463 but not this change still reports `post-update-failed` after a schema-changing Git release update, even though the new release is serving and nothing needs restoring. Recovery needs no action from a person: the next plain `openclaw update` reports `already-current` and converges plugins. That was observed end to end. Updaters without #201463 fail earlier, before the new release starts, as #201463 describes. No config key, stored field, schema, protocol, dependency, retention or permission changes.

### Steps left to a person

None. The previous failure mode on old updaters heals on the next plain `openclaw update`. If that run cannot happen, the update failure output already names the agent-assisted route (`openclaw triage --run --update-result ...`).

## Evidence

End to end through the shipped entry point on macOS, on an isolated launchd Git checkout install with its own profile, state directory and port. The config is synthetic, with no channels, providers or credentials. The setup includes a 512 MiB agent database at schema 42 and, in the busy cell, a separate process writing it at 8 MiB/s. The installed updater is `6691acae` (the commit before the 42 → 43 agent schema bump, already on the Git release layout) plus #201463's fix, with or without this change. The target is this PR's head pinned as the dev target. Each cell runs a real `openclaw update --channel dev --yes`.

| Cell | Installed updater | Target | `openclaw update` | Run record | Wall time | Gateway downtime |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RED busy | `6691acae` + #201463 | `b220df61` (this branch, before the `--no-restart` refinement) | exit 1, `post-update-failed`: "SQLite database pathname changed while its worker owner is active" right after "Gateway: restarted and verified" | `failed` / `post-update-failed` in the new `openclaw.sqlite`; new release serving, agent schema 43, trial settled | 452 s | not reported |
| RED follow-up: next plain update from a RED state | same | same | exit 0, `already-current`, "No plugin updates needed" | `skipped` | 220 s (rebuilds the candidate once) | 0 ms |
| GREEN busy | `6691acae` + #201463 + this PR | `86cfb019` (this head) | exit 0, "OpenClaw updated to 2026.11.5", plugin convergence ran, second restart verified | `succeeded`, 40 steps, none failed, nothing owed | 498 s | 50.5 s |
| GREEN follow-up: second plain update | same | same | exit 0, `already-current` | `skipped` | 178 s | 0 ms |
| GREEN idle | `6691acae` + #201463 + this PR | `86cfb019` (this head) | exit 0, "OpenClaw updated to 2026.11.5" | `succeeded`, 43 steps, none failed, nothing owed | 617 s | 46.2 s |

Earlier GREEN runs of the same fix, without the `--no-restart` refinement, gave the same outcome. Busy against `63b6bbb6`: exit 0, 567 s, 45.9 s downtime. Busy against `433f59bf`: exit 0, 507 s, 50.1 s downtime, then `already-current` in 173 s. Idle against `433f59bf`: exit 0, 483 s, 49.5 s downtime. Every run ended `succeeded` with no failed step and nothing owed.

In every GREEN cell, the Gateway serves the target build from the launcher, the agent database is at schema 43, `.trial` is settled, and `state/` keeps `openclaw.sqlite.pre-<buildId>` beside the new `openclaw.sqlite`. The updater no longer prints "Update progress history unavailable" during the restart. The busy cells also print the existing `NO ORIGINAL-STATE SNAPSHOT` capture warning. It comes from the 8 MiB/s writer and is unrelated to this change.

Extra disk per update, the same with and without this change: one new release tree (4.2 GiB; the previous release is kept for rollback), the agent database's previous generation (about 555 MiB for the 512 MiB fixture), and the shared state's previous generation (about 3.4 MiB). This change adds no files.

<details><summary>Root cause observation (RED, diagnostic build)</summary>

A diagnostic build logged the broker's actors at the refusal. The only holder was actor 1, the updater's first shared-state worker store (`dist/state/openclaw-state.worker.js`), with key `file:…:1772574836` and references 1, still pinning `state/openclaw.sqlite`. The refused admission was the same path with the new file's key `file:…:1773556963`. After the RED run, the new `openclaw.sqlite` held the run as `failed / post-update-failed`. `openclaw.sqlite.pre-<buildId>` held the same run up to the pre-restart steps.

</details>

Focused tests (in `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-doctor-child.test.ts`, beside the Doctor handoff cases) use a child process that replaces the live file with the boot upgrade's own `applyPlan` and `companionRemovals`:
- The remaining steps after a restart, both worker writes and one-shot ledger writes, land in the new file. The run finishes `succeeded` with its pre-swap steps carried over, and the `.pre-` file never receives the later steps. Red on the base behavior: `Command cleanup could not confirm that owned work stopped` ← `Existing-state database generation changed.`
- A restart that throws propagates its own error unchanged, and the failure outcome is still recorded in the new file.
- Negative control: an owner that still pins the replaced file is still refused, and nothing reaches the new file. The broker's pathname check is unchanged.

Also run: `test/scripts/update-restart-module-outcome.test.ts` (its vm fixture stubs the new wrapper as a pass-through), `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts`, `update-command-post-update.test.ts`, `update-cli.git-service.test.ts`, `update-command-verification.test.ts`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint on touched files, `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets`, `pnpm check:docs` and `git diff --check`.

Review: an independent read-only reviewer assessed the diff and the tests. Its blocker was that verification writes would still go through a pinned owner. That does not hold: verification writes are one-shot ledger transactions that open the current file and check its inode inside the transaction (`update-run-write.ts` `mutateRun` → `runExistingOpenClawStateWriteTransaction`). The RED run shows verification completing while the old owner was pinned; the refusal comes at the first worker-owner open after verification. Its other points were addressed: a failure-path test was added, the unused child message was removed and the fork argument was commented. A ClawSweeper review raised two P3 findings, both fixed: the handoff is skipped when the Gateway does not restart, and the docs limit the rerun advice to updaters whose target is already serving. It also called the negative control redundant with broker coverage. The control is kept: it is the only test of the update ledger's worker write refusing after a real replacement (`Existing-state database generation changed.`), a different refusal from the broker's pathname check. `autoreview` does not run on this machine.

### Recordings

These are raw asciinema terminal recordings of the real `openclaw update` cells, rendered to MP4 with idle time capped at 2 s. The terminal output is sanitized (home directory shown as `~`, no usernames or hostnames). Full raw logs are not attached because the Crabbox artifact store rejected the upload from this machine (`http 401`).

## Not proven

- An upgrade that starts from the stable `v2026.11.5` release. No published release includes the Git release layout yet, so no release can produce this state; the installed updater in every cell is `6691acae` from main, the last commit before the 42 → 43 agent schema bump.
- Package installs, the legacy in-place Git runner and the managed-service handoff were checked by code, not end to end (see Other paths).

- Linux and Windows hosts. The end-to-end cells ran on macOS launchd only. The code path has no platform branch.
- A release trial that backs out to the previous build. The wrapper releases and revokes the state handles whenever the restart settles, success or failure, so later writes open whatever file the path names; only a failed restart after a swap is tested (`reopens the current file when the restart fails`), not a back-out end to end.

prs.title: fix: make release validation failures diagnosable
prs.body:
Related: #197510

## What Problem This Solves

Release validation can fail before reaching the scenario, discard useful memory observations when one endpoint is unavailable, or omit which Telegram startup phase failed. Two admission fixtures also simulate a foreign schema mutation after ownership has already been admitted rather than testing rejection of an incompatible replacement.

## User Impact

This improves developer and release-operator diagnostics and makes nested-checkout worker builds select their own dependency files. It does not relax release acceptance, change database admission policy, or alter Telegram authorization, retry, or timeout behavior. No configuration or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Resolve worker dependency entries against the owning checkout instead of treating bare `node_modules` paths as package specifiers.
- Preserve independent RSS endpoints and samples while keeping derived comparisons and release validation strict. Report bounded, payload-free sampling failures.
- Exercise incompatible database replacements before admission in both synchronous and asynchronous fixtures.
- Retain Telegram startup phase, fixed primary/participant role, request outcome, and connection-state diagnostics without targets, messages, or credentials.

## Evidence

Combined-head verification passed: 188 tests across eight focused TypeScript files, the worker-dependency build regression (1 passed, 68 filtered), 48 Python tests, typed lint for all touched TypeScript, state/logging and QA test typechecks, the tooling test typecheck, formatting, and whitespace checks. Original red/green evidence is retained for worker entry resolution, RSS endpoint preservation, database replacement admission on the release baseline, and missing Telegram phase/role diagnostics. An isolated patched-candidate mock Gateway scenario passed with all four RSS samples; the unchanged collaborator scenario passed all 15 inference turns after local browser/proxy setup corrections. These are not claims that the original CI timeout or OS sampling cause is fixed.

No live Telegram operation was performed. An unchanged relocated fs-safe worker fixture fails on this host because its writable temporary ancestor selects the secure fallback; the same signature was reproduced on the unmodified main owner. No assertion or security safeguard was weakened.

Autoreview and ClawSweeper were explicitly excluded by the release owner. Fresh independent source inspection and targeted verification are used; enforced repository checks remain required.

Full `pnpm build` stopped in the unchanged AI declaration phase: OpenAI 7.47.0 explicitly imports parent `node_modules` paths and finds the enclosing checkout’s Undici 8.12.3 despite the owned frozen install containing Undici 8.12.4. The declaration boundary correctly rejects that external input. This is a local nested-checkout build limitation, not a successful full-build result; no dependency/compiler-boundary changes are included. A diagnostic broad package type trace also reported unrelated package-fixture/config errors; the scoped required typechecks above passed.

prs.title: fix(browser): keep shared tabs visible when Chrome blocks automation
prs.body:
## Merge Brief

Shared tabs can disappear when Chrome correctly refuses debugger access to a protected extension frame. This keeps the tab visible with the native refusal and prevents the agent from diagnosing it as disconnected. The existing CDP exclusion contract is unchanged; there is no permission, extension-package, or persistent-state change. The fix is backed by red/green regressions and a real unpacked-extension recovery run. Please review the separation between user inventory and attachable CDP targets. Temporary 1Password suppression is deliberately separate (#198004).

Closes #198002.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a still-shared browser tab disappears from the agent's inventory when Chrome blocks debugger attachment, so using it reports a missing tab rather than the actual restriction.

## User Impact

User impact: the tab remains listed with `automationBlockedReason`; control reports Chrome's refusal and asks for a fresh snapshot after the restriction clears. Healthy tabs remain usable. This does not read protected extension content, disable another extension, dismiss website forms, or replay interrupted actions. No new extension release is required; the change is Gateway-side.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bridge already omits exact Chrome refusals from attachable CDP discovery. That is appropriate for Playwright, but it is not a complete inventory of the user's shared tabs. Record the refusal on the existing tab state, expose it through the existing descriptor endpoint, and retain those records in the user-facing list. The attachment owner records the observation for every failed acquisition, not just enumeration. Successful reattachment, URL change, or extension replacement clears it.

A retired Playwright Page can remain unresolved after its native target disappears from discovery. When the authoritative native inventory is already completely accounted for, that stale Page must not make the whole listing fail. Missing native targets and unrelated transient failures still fail instead of being reported as a complete partial list.

The patch follows the existing refusal classifier from #191578. It does not implement #193589's discovery timeouts or #186674's pending-navigation transport changes. No new manager, config setting, browser permission, or recovery loop is introduced. The additional files carry one output field through its type/schema/formatter/selection consumers.

## Evidence

- Identical focused regressions on base `565b3f99c21b`: **7 expected failures, 68 passes**. With the fix: **75/75 pass** across bridge refusal/recovery, profile inventory/selection, page enumeration, and model-facing output.
- Real Chrome for Testing **153.0.8010.12**, real unpacked OpenClaw extension, disposable profile, synthetic foreign-extension iframe: native `target_closed` detach and protected-origin refusal; blocked tab retained with reason; after removing the fixture frame, fresh snapshot, typing/readback, and Cancel all succeeded **through the repaired OpenClaw relay**, not a substitute browser connection. The protected fixture sentinel was absent from inventory output.
- Canonical production extension typecheck and `pnpm build:runtime` pass. Focused formatting, type-aware lint, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent local autoreview with owning source context identified a P2: focus/close could still dispatch a placeholder and report target-not-found. Both now use the same blocked-tab check, with regressions passing. No claim of whole-repository review.
- Author simplification: reuse the existing tab state and descriptor request; no additional polling, identity registry, or action-replay path. Negative coverage retains near-match refusals/transient failure behavior and unresolved native-target completeness.

Native proof is limited to the tested Chromium build and synthetic protected frame. Separate live Chrome 156/1Password experiments are documented in #198004; no claim is made that this branch was installed into that daily-use browser or production Gateway. The final native run observed one transient inventory error during detach propagation, followed by a successful separate settled-state read and complete recovery. Immediate transition reads are not claimed to be atomic; transient failures still fail the complete request. Earlier failed attempts are not counted as passes. Broad cross-platform checks are delegated to PR CI.

Release note: browser extension profiles now report shared tabs blocked by Chrome debugger restrictions instead of presenting them as missing/disconnected; restore control only after normal attachment succeeds.

prs.title: fix(codex): let saved conversations recover after a remote failure
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a failed turn on a remote Codex app-server, a saved conversation can get stuck when OpenClaw needs to apply a different configuration. The server can keep the failed runtime loaded across WebSocket reconnects.

## User Impact

When Codex confirms the failed runtime unloaded, OpenClaw asks the user to retry their message in the same saved conversation. If another client keeps the thread loaded, OpenClaw explains what the user needs to close. Other conversations on the connection can continue.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw unsubscribes from the affected thread and checks that Codex unloaded it. Codex's default idle retention can take up to a minute after the last subscriber leaves. The next message uses the existing cold-resume flow and runs current policy checks. Ending the first attempt after unload confirmation avoids relying on a resume response that can acknowledge ignored settings on a competing loaded runtime. The native protocol still has separate read and resume operations, so an external client can reload the thread between them on retry.

## Evidence

- The focused adoption suite passed all 11 tests, including four WebSocket recovery cases. A synthetic app-server peer exercised the real WebSocket transport and verified same-thread retry, preserved bindings and sibling work, competing activity rejection, and current-policy denial. Node 24.22.1, one worker, 208 seconds wall time with cold worker preparation. A live app-server was outside this validation.
- Scoped Codex typecheck and lint, format, the repository commit hook, and `git diff --check` passed. A direct check of the production channel failure renderer verified that it shows the retry guidance.
- Independent source review of the exact seven-file patch at base `0321f852d91a` found no actionable issues. The automated command-line review failed at model startup and produced no verdict. Native unsubscribe and shutdown behavior was checked against Codex source.

prs.title: fix: show the sign-in explanation when a proxy sign-in expires
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Control UI sits behind a sign-in proxy such as Cloudflare Access and that sign-in expires, the "Sign in to continue loading content" dialog appeared with only "Couldn't load this panel." and a Retry button. Retry could never succeed. The dialog's own code was downloaded on demand, and once the proxy sign-in has expired, every new download is redirected to the sign-in page. So the dialog could not load in exactly the situation it exists for. OCE Fleet users reported this.

## User Impact

User impact: when a proxy sign-in expires, people now see the intended explanation ("Your website sign-in has expired. Images and files cannot load until you sign in again…") with Not now and Sign in, instead of a panel-load error. Sign-in, Check again, the native Mac app reconnect, and the access probe work as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The recovery dialog is now imported statically, so it ships in the boot bundle the page has already loaded. The unreachable lazy-load error fallback, with its Retry button, and its unit test are removed.
- The dialog renders inside the shared `openclaw-modal-dialog` element. That element is downloaded on demand from the New Session boot group, so on Chat it is not always loaded already. Recovery now preloads it at idle time when it starts, while access is still valid. If the preload fails, opening the dialog tries the download again, as it did before.
- Statically importing the modal element was rejected: it added about 11.5 KB gzip and one request to Chat boot, which goes over the Chat boot budgets.
- Accepted edge case: if the proxy sign-in expires before the idle preload finishes, for example a tab opened in the background and never shown, the modal element can still fail to load. That gap already exists on main.

Bundle cost, from `scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts` against the main build: Chat boot JS +437 B gzip (1,331,339 B, under the 1,332,290 B limit), New Session boot JS +685 B, startup JS +1 B, and request counts unchanged. The local build of main already fails the CSS and Chat-boot-request checks by the same amounts as this branch, so those failures come from main.

## Evidence

The browser E2E now redirects every `/assets/**` request to the sign-in page once access expires, the same way a real proxy behaves. It then checks that the dialog shows the sign-in explanation and never shows "Couldn't load this panel."

- Main (053fb62c6141), before the preload wait was added to the test: the service-worker-allowed interactive case shows the reported symptom, and the copy assertion fails. The service-worker-blocked case never opens the modal, because the modal element cannot be downloaded either. With the committed preload wait, main fails all 4 cases at that wait.
- This branch: `ui/src/e2e/browser-auth-recovery.e2e.test.ts` passes 4/4, and `ui/src/app/browser-auth-recovery.test.ts` passes 13/13. `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt and `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers` pass. `ui/src/e2e/boot-module-boundaries.e2e.test.ts` passes 18/18.
- An independent review of the diff found no P0–P2 issues.

### Clean comparison

Interactive renewal with the service worker allowed, 1280×900, synthetic conversation fixture. Before: main 053fb62c6141. After: this branch.

prs.title: fix: let admins suspend OpenClaw ID members and use one role for everyone
prs.body:
Closes #201526 (parts A–C; part D is in a separate PR)

## What Problem This Solves

People who reach a claw through OpenClaw ID were governed by a second role system. Their membership role decided what they could do, separately from the Gateway profile role that every other sign-in route uses. Because of this, admins couldn't suspend a member, @mention invitations judged members by the wrong role, and the same person could have different permissions depending on how they connected.

## User Impact

User impact: an OpenClaw ID member's permissions now come from their Gateway profile role, the same as everyone else's.

- **Admins and the owner can change or clear a member's role** with **People** or `users.setRole`. The member's connections and running, queued, child, scheduled and recovered work stop immediately.
- **@mention invitations** of members now work and use the member's real role.
- **No role means no access.** A member, or any identified non-owner, left with no role or no scopes is refused at connect instead of connecting with nothing. A configured role catalog is enforced for OpenClaw ID members even without `gateway.roles.default`.
- **Upgrade:** each existing member's current membership role is copied to their profile once, only when the profile has no explicit assignment, so nobody's access changes on upgrade.
- **Unchanged:** owner devices keep full owner authority, and nodes keep no operator scopes. The membership role remains as the label shown on Access and in the loader.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw ID is meant to provide connectivity, with the Gateway as the source of truth for authorization. Members now resolve through their linked profile on the same path as every other identified person. Invite approval and Access role changes write the profile role, and the Gateway publishes the effective role name to Discovery as a label. This removes the member-specific special cases that each profile-based check previously had to remember.

## Evidence

Real-Gateway tests with members connecting through OpenClaw ID:

- **@mention invitations** of `sessions.others: "invited"` members succeed in all three enforcement modes (enforcement off, permissive default, denying default), and the invited member sees only the invited session.
- **Demotion or clearing** by an admin and by the owner closes tunnel connections and stops in-flight, queued and steered, subagent, automation and recovered work. Owner devices stay connected.
- **Reconnecting with no role** is refused.
- **Upgrade:** the role is imported once, survives a restart, and isn't re-imported after a role is cleared. Concurrent assignments are never overwritten, and repeat invitations assign their role.
- **Discovery labels** stay current across an OpenClaw ID off/on toggle and same-second snapshots.

An independent review found six issues, all fixed with regression tests: a missing catalog granting uncapped access, repeat invitations not assigning a role, migration overwriting a concurrent assignment, local iOS devices losing approval pushes, the publication listener lost on toggle, and delayed label publication.

After rebasing on main: the 5-file end-to-end set passes (45 tests), and `pnpm check:changed`, `pnpm config:docs:check`, format and lint pass for the changed files.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/gateway/server.openclaw-id-session-invite.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server.openclaw-id-member-suspension.test.ts \
  src/gateway/openclaw-id/member-profile-role-recovery.test.ts \
  src/gateway/openclaw-id/member-profiles.persistence.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server.auth.openclaw-id-tunnel.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

Also run: openclaw-id service, publisher, role-policy, run-recovery, users, doctor member-roles and Access plugin People suites.

</details>

prs.title: fix(android): keep inline code in markdown plain-text extraction
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android chat renders remote Markdown images as plain alt text (no image fetching on this path). `buildPlainText` in `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/chat/ChatMarkdown.kt` handled `Text` and line-break nodes but fell through to the generic `else` branch for the leaf `Code` node, which recurses into `firstChild` — always `null` for a commonmark `Code` node — so inline-code literals were silently dropped.

Concretely, an alt like `![Open **`setup.json`** now](https://example.com/diagram.png)` rendered as "Open  now", and a code-only alt produced an empty string, falling back to the generic `image` label.

Fixes #196086

## Solution

Append the `Code` node's `literal` directly in `buildPlainText`, matching how the rendering path (`appendInlineNode`'s `is Code` branch) already handles inline code. The `org.commonmark.node.Code` import was already present.

## Impact

Inline-code literals in remote-image alt text now appear in the rendered placeholder text, including code-only alts which previously degraded to the generic `image` fallback. No other plain-text consumers change behavior: every non-leaf node still recurses as before.

## Evidence

### Before / after (Android chat, production markdown pipeline)

Captured on a local Android 16 (API 36) emulator from the app's built-in screenshot fixture mode (`openclaw.screenshotScene chat`, no Gateway or credentials involved). The fixture chat was temporarily extended with the two labels from the linked issue on both builds; that local scaffolding is not part of this PR. Both screenshots show the same seeded message rendered through the real `ChatMarkdown` pipeline:

![Before (main): label reads "Open  now" and the code-only alt falls back to "image"](https://github.com/Heetisk/openclaw/raw/proof/196086-screenshots/proof-before.png)

![After (this PR): label reads "Open setup.json now" and the code-only alt shows "config.yml"](https://github.com/Heetisk/openclaw/raw/proof/196086-screenshots/proof-after.png)

- Before: mixed label reads "Open  now" (inline code dropped); code-only alt falls back to the generic "image".
- After: mixed label reads "Open setup.json now"; code-only alt shows "config.yml".
- Both builds otherwise identical (`origin/main` + the same local fixture vs. this branch + the same fixture).

### Tests and CI

- Two focused regressions in `ChatMarkdownTest` exercise the user-visible path from the issue (`buildChatInlineMarkdown` → `appendInlineNode` → `MarkdownImage` → `buildPlainText`):
  - `imageAltTextKeepsInlineCodeLiteral`: mixed bold + inline-code alt extracts `Open setup.json now`.
  - `imageAltTextKeepsCodeOnlyFallback`: code-only alt extracts `setup.json` instead of falling back to `image`.
- CI green on head `1e79292b4`: `android-test-play` (runs these regressions), `android-ktlint`, `android-test-third-party`, both `android-access-native` lanes, `native-i18n`, `security-fast`, and `PR context and evidence`.

prs.title: fix: keep shared collaborators from loosening your session's guardrails or approving your commands
prs.body:
Related: #201526 (part D)

## What Problem This Solves

When you share a session with someone, they could change its permission mode to something looser than you set, for example from **Ask me** to **Auto-review**. They could also approve shell commands that your own turns were waiting on. Inviting a collaborator could quietly remove the guardrails you chose for your session.

## User Impact

User impact: in a session you created, people who aren't you or an admin can tighten its permission mode but not loosen or clear it. They can only see and resolve approvals raised by their own turns.

- **The creator and admins keep full control** of both.
- **Changed for teams:** teammates with `sessions.others` set to `view`, `suggest` or `write` no longer receive or resolve approvals raised by other people's turns.
- **Changed for unprofiled devices:** non-admin devices without a profile no longer get device-only approval access.
- **Docs:** the earlier statement that apps could decide any chat's approval has been corrected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Permission-mode changes are checked once, by the shared session patch owner, so the single and bulk RPC, tool, create and reset paths all follow the same rule. Approvals now record which profile's turn raised them, and listing, resolving, events and push notifications check that record. An approval with no recorded raiser is creator- or admin-only. A schema 41 migration (SQLite and PostgreSQL) adds the requester column.

## Evidence

Real-Gateway tests with an invited member, a `write` teammate, a non-admin creator and an unrelated admin:

- **Permission mode:** tightening succeeds. Loosening and clearing are refused, including through the bulk, create and reset paths.
- **Approvals:** provider-driven turns raise real exec approvals. Each person sees and resolves only their own, and the creator and admin see all.
- **Events and notifications:** requested and resolved events, web push and iOS push reach only people allowed to act on the approval.
- **Migration:** SQLite and real PostgreSQL v40→v41 migrations pass.

361 tests across 15 files pass. An independent review found two issues, both fixed with regression tests: PostgreSQL column-position drift, and owner-scoped approval events matching the wrong identity. After rebasing on main, the permission, approval, workspace-policy and migration suites pass again (122 tests).

**Inherited failures from main.** The state schema bump in `package.json` makes `check:changed` run the whole-repo gates. Typecheck and every other gate pass, but these three fail on main itself:
- **Plugin SDK surface budget:** 3,900 public exports against a limit of 3,894. It fails identically on a clean `origin/main` (`7058196e`), and this PR changes no SDK exports.
- **Lint `max-lines`:** `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts` (1,099 lines on main) and `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/index.test.ts` (1,103 lines on main). This PR doesn't touch either file.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/gateway/server.session-member-authority.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server.sessions.create.workspace-policy.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

Plus the approval, push, persistence, migration and generated-schema suites.

prs.title: fix(gateway): session observer digests authenticate with the session owner's linked account
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #201585

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where, on a multi-user Gateway, every Control UI session observer digest for a session was sent through the agent-level auth order instead of the session owner's linked model account. When that agent-level profile is an unusable placeholder, every observer utility call returns 401 and the observer disables itself for the run, even though the session's own turns run fine on the user's linked account.
- Affected surface: Control UI session observer digests (`gateway.controlUi.sessionObserver`) on multi-user Gateways where sessions run on per-user linked model accounts.

- **Related:** #195172 (who pays for unattended utility-model calls); ClawSweeper confirmed current main drops the session's selected account on the observer path and no PR owns this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** The observer's utility model resolution and route-currentness checks now consume the session's established route — effective provider/model plus the session-sticky auth selection (linked account first, then the configured primary's profile on the same provider) — exactly like dashboard session titles already do per docs/gateway/config-agents/models.md (`utilityModel`). The derived utility modelRef carries the session's `@profile`, so preparation authenticates with the session owner's account.
- **Out of scope:** Explicitly configured `utilityModel` routes are preserved unchanged (the resolver returns them as configured); no changes to regular chat routing, auth order, or persistence.
- **Highest-risk area:** Route-currentness comparison (`modelStateIsCurrent`) must use the same session-scoped resolution as the claim that produced the state's ref, otherwise digests get demoted mid-run.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** Both the model-slot claim and the currentness check share one `resolveUtilityModelRef(agentId, state)` helper; the route snapshot is captured once at admission from the session entry and refreshed on re-admission, so the comparison inputs cannot diverge.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** Two interleaved sessions on one agent, each with a different linked account and an unusable agent-level auth profile, now get observer digests authenticated to their own accounts (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5@<session-profile>` per session) instead of a shared 401 loop.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/gateway/session-observer.ts` (shared resolver), `src/gateway/session-observer-lifecycle.ts` (route capture at admission), `src/gateway/session-observer-model-slots.ts` + `src/gateway/session-observer-audience.ts` (session-scoped claim/currentness), `src/agents/session-model-ref.ts` (`resolveSessionAuthProfile`, extracted from the dashboard-title contract and now shared by both callers). Regression: `src/gateway/session-observer.test.ts` "routes observer utility digests through each session's linked model account".

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Isolated worktree at `aispace/worktrees/issue-201585` (openclaw main @ 02078202f31), Node 26.12.1, project vitest runner with a fixture plugin metadata snapshot declaring `anthropic`'s default utility model (auto-derivation path, no explicit `utilityModel`).
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/session-observer.test.ts src/gateway/session-observer-model-slots.test.ts src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.test.ts
  # GREEN (with this patch): 3 files, 56 tests passed (exit 0)
  # RED (same test files with implementation reverted to origin/main, tests kept):
  #   AssertionError: expected [ 'anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5', …(1) ] to deeply equal [ …(2) ]
  #   - "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5@anthropic-alice"  + "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"
  #   - "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5@anthropic-bob"     + "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"
  # Regression scope: full src/gateway observer suite via validate.sh (2 vitest shards, all passed)
  # Type check: node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json (exit 0)
  # Format/lint: oxfmt --check + oxlint on all changed files (clean)
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  Test Files  3 passed (3)
       Tests  56 passed (56)
  prepareModel.modelRef (per session, sorted) = [
    "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5@anthropic-alice",
    "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5@anthropic-bob",
  ]
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Each of the two interleaved sessions on agent `main` (auto-derived utility model, unusable agent-level auth order) prepares its observer digest with its own session's `@profile`, so the digest call authenticates with the session owner's linked account; the agent-level placeholder is no longer used for those digests.

prs.title: fix(openai): cache system prompts on GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
prs.body:
## Problem

`gpt-6.2-astra` never caches the Responses `instructions` field. Input items and tools cache normally, and `gpt-6-astra` / `gpt-6.1-sol` cache `instructions`. On native OpenAI Responses, OpenClaw sends the system prompt in `instructions` (`usesInstructionsField` in `openai-responses-payload-policy.ts`). So on `gpt-6.2-astra` the full system prompt is billed as plain input on every request. On a real Gateway turn that is about 9.5k plain tokens per request (measured below).

Controlled API replays with the same body:

- System text in `instructions`: 0 written, 0 read on every try.
- The same text as an input message: written once, then fully read.

## Solution

- New model capability `compat.cachesInstructions` (default `true`). The OpenAI catalog sets it to `false` on `gpt-6.2-astra`. `supportsInstructions` still means "the route accepts the field". The new capability means "the model caches it". The payload policy uses `instructions` only when both are true. In all other cases the prompt goes into `input`, which is the path that already exists for routes without `instructions`.
- Placement (`openai-responses-replay-messages-internal.ts`): the system item now goes directly after the compaction item (or compacted window), not before it. OpenAI drops input that comes before a compaction item, and server compaction absorbs a developer item placed before it. Layout: `[compaction, developer(system), tail…]`. Without compaction: `[developer(system), …]`. Provider-style and Azure routes, which always embed the prompt, use the same rule.
- Continuation needs no new code. The item belongs to the stored input prefix:
  - The same prompt continues the chain. The delta does not resend the item, because `previous_response_id` carries it.
  - A changed, added or removed prompt changes the prefix. Continuation then returns `history_changed`, and the request is a full replay with no `previous_response_id`. It carries only the new item, so the model never sees two system prompts.
  - Prompt updates that arrive as appended instruction messages keep the chain. The pinned system prompt stays the same.
- `/responses/compact` on native OpenAI still receives the prompt as `instructions`, which keeps the prompt out of the retained window. Without this, the next replay would send the old prompt from the window and the current one. The item carries a symbol marker (`RESPONSES_SYSTEM_PROMPT`). The marker never reaches the wire.
- Context-usage accounting found the embedded prompt by checking `input[0]`. After compaction, `input[0]` is the compaction item, so accounting now uses the marker.
- The Responses image sanitizer rebuilt each mutable input item from its string keys, which dropped symbol markers before the compact call and accounting read them. The new compact test found this. The sanitizer now copies with a spread, so the markers stay on the copy. The V2 compaction step that restored only `RESPONSES_RETAINED_USER` after sanitation is removed.
- Docs: the `cachesInstructions` row in custom-providers, plus one paragraph in prompt-caching (OpenAI section).

## Evidence

### Red/green (`ocx test`)
- `openai-responses-uncached-instructions.integration.test.ts` (real HTTP/SSE loopback, unmocked SDK, native route):
  - capability missing → `instructions` (green on base and head, default unchanged)
  - capability `false` → no `instructions`, developer item first, delta has no developer item, changed prompt → full replay with only the new item (**red on base, green on head**)
  - after a compaction item the developer item comes next (**red on base, green on head**)
  - continuation decision: same prompt continues; changed / removed / added prompt → `history_changed` (a missing prompt never matches a present one)
- `openai-responses-compaction-replay.test.ts`: provider-style replay puts the prompt after the compaction item (**red on base, green on head**)
- `openai-responses-client.compact.test.ts`: compact body keeps the prompt in `instructions` for both models

### Real route, isolated scratch Gateway (`env -i`, random port, real `openai/gpt-6.2-astra`, `responsesCompactThreshold: 28000`)
The same 6-turn chat ran on the merge base (`6a8eb5a93234`) and on this head (`3a600ca`; rerun on `18cb195` matched: plain 119–220, cacheRead 17,949 / 40,421 on turns 5/6, rules held). Turn 4 pastes about 15k tokens, which crosses server compaction. The workspace rules are: end every reply with `ZEBRA-17`, and answer `REFUSED` when asked for the secret word. Provider usage per request:

| Turn | base plain input | base cacheRead | head plain input | head cacheRead |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (cold) | 9,475 | 0 | 119 | 0 (write 17,943) |
| 2 | 9,475 | 8,583 | 119 | 17,943 |
| 3 | 9,475 | 8,796 | 119 | 18,158 |
| 4 (+15k paste, compacts) | 9,475 | 8,992 | 119 | 18,354 |
| 5 (first after compaction) | 9,569 | 8,583 | 208 | 17,943 |
| 6 | 9,576 | 31,045 | 211 | 40,409 |

- Plain (neither read nor written) input per request: **~9.5k → ~120–210**. The system prompt moves from plain to cached.
- Wire shapes (from `OPENCLAW_DEBUG_MODEL_PAYLOAD=summary`). Base: `instructions` present on every request. Head: no `instructions` field, and the input begins with `message:developer`. After compaction, base sends `compaction,message:user,…` and head sends `compaction,message:developer,message:user,…`.
- Rules held on both sides before and after compaction (turns 2 and 5: `REFUSED` + `ZEBRA-17`, all turns end with `ZEBRA-17`).

### Real `previous_response_id` chain with a prompt change (`openai-responses-uncached-instructions.live.test.ts`, real `gpt-6.2-astra`)
| Request | previous_response_id | developer items | cacheRead | reply |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prompt A | no | [A] | 0 | `Hi! ALPHA-1` |
| prompt A | yes | [] (delta) | 2,128 | `7. ALPHA-1` |
| prompt B (A rule removed) | no (full replay) | [B] | 0 | `4. BRAVO-2` |

The rule that exists only in B is followed. The rule from A, which B removed, is no longer applied.

### Gates
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types`
- `ocx test` on `packages/ai/src/transports`, `packages/ai/src/providers`, `packages/model-catalog-core`, `extensions/openai`, config/model-registry schema tests
- oxlint + oxfmt on changed files, `git diff --check`
- Local ClawSweeper review (gpt-6.1-sol, normal speed) on `18cb195`: complete, "patch is correct", zero findings
- `pnpm static:validators:gen`, `pnpm config:schema:gen`, `pnpm config:docs:gen` (regenerated outputs committed)

## Impact / risks
- Only models whose catalog sets `cachesInstructions: false` change wire shape (today only `gpt-6.2-astra`).
- Placement after compaction also applies to routes that always embed the prompt (Azure, provider-style replay). Before this change those routes put the prompt before the compaction item, where OpenAI drops it.
- Accepted edge case: a payload hook that rebuilds input items from JSON loses the marker. The compact call then sends the prompt in `input`, and context-usage falls back to the conservative local estimate. Both are visible and recoverable.
- Authority of a developer item vs `instructions` was equal on a small probe (12/12 vs 12/12). This is not a proof for every prompt.

prs.title: fix(sessions): preserve the initial followup policy denial reason
prs.body:
Closes #200072

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `sessions_send(mode: "followup")` replaces every policy denial with `Followup session access was revoked.`, even when the denial happens on the initial admission and nothing was revoked. Operators cannot tell a real authorization restriction from a defect, and the endpoint and reason are discarded.

## User Impact

The initial refusal now names the endpoint (requester or target), the policy code, and the real message. Only a denial detected after admission keeps the "revoked" wording, so a restriction is no longer misreported as a lost grant.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Track whether the initial admission already succeeded. A first denial reports "denied"; a later one reports "revoked".
- Surface the endpoint role plus the denial `code` and `message` from the policy owner instead of a fixed string.
- Keep the access watcher, revocation latch, and custody behavior unchanged.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/sessions-send-followup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 6/6 passed, including the new initial-denial case and the existing revocation latch cases.
- Red-on-base: reverting only the custody source produces `Followup session access was revoked.` instead of the denial details.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint clean on both changed files.

prs.title: fix(ui): load saved accounts before the account menu opens
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The model picker used to wait until you opened **Account** to fetch saved accounts. On a slow response, the open menu showed a separate “Loading…” row instead of the choices.

## User Impact

Opening the model picker now starts the first page of saved accounts without waiting for the model catalog. The picker keeps the current account label visible and temporarily swaps the dropdown chevron for a spinner. It enables the dropdown when the first page arrives; if the request fails, **Retry** is available in the menu. Scrolling to the end automatically fetches the next page, with one static skeleton row while existing choices stay available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model catalog and the signed-in viewer’s saved-account list have separate scopes and can load independently. The account list is not added to `models.list`, and a slow or failed account read does not hold up the model list.

prs.title: feat(gateway): admit sessions_send wake starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_send` can fan out wake-starting work through the gateway `agent` RPC. Before this change, concurrent senders could bypass sender-local batching and rate limits. This adds an optional gateway-owned admission boundary for typed `sessions_send` wake traffic. It intentionally does not affect `mode:notify`, which does not create recipient work.

## Summary

- add a disabled-by-default `gateway.sessionsSendWakeAdmission` policy (six starts per 15 minutes by default)
- enforce it at the common gateway `agent` admission boundary only for typed `inputProvenance.kind=inter_session` / `sourceTool=sessions_send`
- persist one idempotent per-recipient decision in a separate SQLite database, atomically, and fail closed if state is unavailable

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/sessions-send-wake-admission.test.ts`: 4/4 passed (default-disabled, seven-recipient load, restart/idempotency, fail-closed state error)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm format:check`, and `git diff --check` passed locally
- implementation is based on released OpenClaw `v2026.10.9` / `8b18b557`, matching the runtime that exposed the issue

## Rollout

Feature remains off by default. This PR contains no config enablement, runtime rollout, or gateway restart. Rollback is retaining the disabled flag or reverting this commit; the receipt database remains as audit evidence.
