The revised capture warning comes from the backup owner. `update-database-backup.test.ts` asserts its exact rendered text, and three engine tests assert it for the write case and the unavailable-generation case. The cells cannot show it, because the installed `2026.11.5` updater prints its own copy of the warning.

CI on head f443ea86e29: two failing shards, both inherited and unrelated to this diff. `checks-node-changed` fails on `test/gateway-restart-handoff.e2e.test.ts` (a session `resumeAfterRestart` entry shape, from restart-resume code this diff does not touch; the test is Linux-only and could not be run locally). `checks-node-changed-compact-large-30-1` hangs on `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-reclamation-wal.test.ts` (reclaim); it also hangs locally for 300 s with this PR's production files reverted to main.

Checks run on head:
- Focused Vitest for the preflight, admission, schema-inspection worker, node-sqlite, SQLite read-only location, update candidate state, backup and status suites. All pass except two `update-candidate-state.result.test.ts` cases that fail with `ENAMETOOLONG` on this macOS host; they fail the same way on the base.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint on the touched files, `check:baseline-ratchets`, and `git diff --check`.
- An independent read-only reviewer (Opus); findings and resolutions are below. `autoreview` does not run on this machine.

Not proven:
- Windows: not run. If SQLite there cannot use a read-only index, the read falls back to the existing private snapshot.
- The automatic update campaign, which the harness cannot drive: the `2026.11.5` update check asks public npm, and the stable channel waits 6 hours plus jitter.

<details><summary>Independent review findings and resolutions</summary>

1. The warning claimed a write when the generation was only unreadable. Fixed: one sentence now covers "changed or could not be confirmed".
2. No test proved byte preservation or WAL-only detection on the new path. Fixed: added an idle-owner test (unmasked, all sidecars). The live-owner test now asserts that no private copy was made and that the owner kept committing.
3. Close race: when the last connection closes while admission opens the store, the read-only index cannot be opened and SQLite throws `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` (found by the landing review: 60 to 65 of 400 reads in a close-race probe, plus 2 in a long stress run; never a wrong, torn or stale version). Before the fix, that throw escaped the read's handler, so the preflight refused with "could not inspect agent database". Fixed: under artifact preservation, `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` now returns no result, and the store goes to the private snapshot path. That path rereads the closed store, which has no live writer, and reports any lasting open failure itself, so a fallback can never admit on its own. No other open error is converted. Regression: `falls back to the private snapshot when the last owner closes during a preserving read` runs 300 reads against an owner that opens, commits and closes as the last connection. It failed 3 of 3 runs before the fix (`unable to open database file`) and passed 3 of 3 after; the probe went from 60 errors in 400 reads to 0 (233 in-place reads, 167 snapshot fallbacks), with no sidecar left behind.
4. No test for the `SQLITE_READONLY` fallback. Not added: SQLite returns that code only when it cannot use a read-only index, and that cannot be forced on SQLite 3.54 without mocking the native layer. The fallback is the existing snapshot path, which is covered.
5. Test cleanup could mask a writer crash. Fixed: stop is sent only while the IPC channel is connected.
6. Doctor and startup checks that preserve artifacts and verify integrity now run on the live store inside one read transaction, not on a full copy. While they run, the checkpointer cannot restart the WAL. Accepted: no bytes change, the alternative is a full copy, and the WAL is checkpointed after the read.

ClawSweeper (one local round): overall D, proof D, patch C, "patch is correct".
- It noted #201327 on the base. That is now addressed above with the base-versus-head cost table.
- Its P3 asked to reuse `sqlite-checkpoint-writer.test-support.ts`. Rejected: that helper arrived with #201327 and does not exist at `v2026.11.5`, so the test would not cherry-pick. As it also asked, the owner fixture now checks that the owner kept committing across the check, and the idle case uses a small fixture.

</details>

## Cherry-pick for the release line

- Commits to pick: the squash merge of this PR. On the branch, that is `fix(update): read live agent schemas without a stable copy`, `test(update): check live-owner progress across admission and shrink the idle fixture` and `fix(update): fall back to the snapshot when the last owner closes during a preserving read`.
- Tested on a detached `v2026.11.5` (e13cf15ece9). `git cherry-pick -n` of the fix commit gives three mechanical textual conflicts:
  - `src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.ts`: the tag also reads cleanly closed runtime stores natively. Take the PR's block, and keep that path non-preserving by adding `&& !(purpose === "runtime" && readSqliteDatabaseCleanClose(realAgentPath))` to the `preserveSourceArtifacts` expression.
  - `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-inspection.ts`: comment wording only. Take the PR's `preserve`/`closedWal`/early-return block, and keep the PR's `try`/`catch` around the final `withSqliteSourceReadDatabase` call, together with the `isSqliteCantOpenError` helper (the close-race fallback).
  - `src/infra/update-database-backup.test.ts`: the PR's surrounding test does not exist at the tag. Keep the tag's side, and update the tag's one existing assertion of the old warning text to the new sentence.
- The test commit applies unchanged to the artifacts test file, which is identical at the tag and the base.
- The close-race fix commit (`fix(update): fall back to the snapshot when the last owner closes during a preserving read`) cherry-picks cleanly on top of the resolved pick at the tag. I did not rerun the tests at the tag for it: the machine is being kept quiet.
- After that, `tsgo:core` passes, and 292 focused tests pass at the tag: the preflight artifacts and main suites, schema-inspection worker, node-sqlite, backup, backup engine, status, candidate admission and schema preflight. The package built from the tag plus the pick is the GREEN cell above.
- No other commit is needed: it does not depend on #199706 (Git release mode), #201463 or #201327.
- Alternative or companion for the release line: #201327 (`07baab52b41`) by itself also removes the refusal. Its cherry-pick onto `v2026.11.5` has one conflict in `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.ts`: take the incoming side, which adds the `LIVE_WRITER_CHANGES` set and the async online-backup fallback. After that, `tsgo:core` passes and its own `sqlite-readonly-location.test.ts` passes there (26 passed, 1 skipped). Its Docker cell (installed published `2026.11.5`, candidate `v2026.11.5` + #201327, same load) exits 0 and the Gateway serves `2026.11.6`: 224 s wall, one 93 s outage, peak extra disk 3.7 GiB. It still copies the live store during admission, which is the cost in the table above. The two commits compose: this PR reads live WAL stores in place, and #201327's fallback covers whatever still takes the copy path.


## Landing follow-up

`aaf5c777a45` reads the open failure code through `sqlitePrimaryResultCode` (`src/infra/sqlite-error-diagnostics.ts`) instead of a type assertion, which the `assertion-safety` ratchet rejected on `712b9684bf7`. Behavior is unchanged: on that head the assertion-safety ratchet passes, `openclaw-database-preflight.artifacts.test.ts` passes (9/9, including the close-race fallback test), and a 400-read open/commit/close probe returns no errors (180 in place, 220 via the snapshot).

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.



## Round 3 (ClawSweeper re-review findings + live-Gateway proof)

Head `1e502cd5e72` (synced with upstream/main, 0 behind). All review findings addressed:

- **[P1] Historical catalog hashes preserved** — the companion table leaked into predecessor schema generation, replacing historical hashes. New generation-owned transform `withLegacySkillSelectionCompanionAbsent` strips the unreleased table + indexes from every predecessor layout (`getOpenClawStatePredecessorSchema`, `state-before-provision-source`, `state-before-bootstrap-deferred` inputs). Historical inputs are byte-identical to upstream; the historical hash assertions are restored untouched; generated SQLite catalogs regenerated (228/235 inputs byte-identical, only current-layout inputs changed, as intended).
- **[P2] Input truncation marked before digest suffix** — names cut at the 64-char input budget are now marked truncated up front, so `aaa…(64)+alpha` vs `aaa…(64)+beta` keep distinct audit identities (regression test added).
- **[P2] Canonical decoder reused** — the writer owned a copied run/tool/message decoder; it now imports `parseAgentRunRow`/`rowToAuditEvent` from `audit-event-row.ts`, with companion decoding confined to `rowToStoredAuditEvent` + the distinct companion row shape.
- **[P2] Bootstrap privacy extraction removed** — the unrelated `workspace-bootstrap-privacy.ts` extraction is reverted; `src/agents/workspace.ts` is byte-identical to upstream again.
- **[P3] Stale sequence cache invalidated** — companion allocation consumes shared sequences outside the retention fast path (including duplicate-source attempts); the writer now drops the cached high-water mark on the skill path (regression test: ledger row after a skill write reports its true stored sequence).
- **Stale generated gateway validators** — the PR updated the protocol schemas but not the compiled predicates, so `kind=skill_selection` / `status=observed` failed gateway validation (2 gateway tests red). Regenerated via `scripts/generate-gateway-validators.mts`; 21/21 gateway tests green.
- **Test hygiene** — the `PRIVATE_PROMPT_CONTENT` absence assertion now supplies the sentinel as input (prompt/toolInput/skillFileContents); the unrelated expired-identity rendering case is removed from this PR.
- **Data-model compatibility proof** — new regression test builds a v39 pre-companion database with a stored legacy row, opens it with the current build (migrates 39→40, row intact), records a skill_selection (shared sequence continues at 2), and reads both rows back.

### Live-Gateway behavior proof (new, real Gateway + shipped CLI)

Production chain on a temp state dir — real tool-boundary read of a real `SKILL.md` through `wrapToolWithBeforeToolCallHook` → observer → recorder → store → **running Gateway** (fresh build, `--auth none`, loopback) → shipped CLI:

```
$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection
TIME                          KIND             STATUS    AGENT  RUN           ACTION                     SELECTED
```

prs.title: feat(talk): report which speech-to-text path talk.catalog uses
prs.body:
Closes #197958

## What Problem This Solves

When Talk dictation and voice notes use different providers, Settings → Talk mixes their readiness and does not explain how Talk selected its provider.

## User Impact

Settings → Talk separates speech to text into **Talk** and **Voice notes** rows so each shows its own readiness.

- **Talk** names the provider and how it was selected: the provider named in Voice Call streaming settings, the agent's voice model, automatic streaming selection from available keys, or the voice notes model. When another audio model is serving as fallback for the picked voice notes model, the row names the provider in use. **Change** and **Set up** open the settings that control that path.
- **Voice notes** keeps the audio model picker and checks that model's media-transcription credentials. **Open Models** appears only for providers Models can connect; media-only providers such as Deepgram get a Gateway environment key hint instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway records the selected path in the optional `talk.catalog.transcription.source` field and supplies separate `mediaProviders` readiness when Talk uses another path. `streaming` means the Voice Call config names a provider; provider options without a named provider report `streaming-auto`, because the runtime still picks by order and readiness. These fields are omitted for callers without `operator.read`; the protocol version stays unchanged.

The Talk page publishes the catalog as soon as it arrives. The Models lookup that decides whether **Open Models** applies is read on its own and never delays Talk facts.

## Evidence

**Before:** a generic status and separate preferred-model warning mix Talk's streaming provider with voice-note readiness.

![Before: generic Talk transcription status and a separate preferred-model warning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/43c32bfc4b4396590cba933c140f07fdb10340e5/images/2026/11/caded058-6aab-4989-9ed2-d33ebb7584ed.png)

**After:** Talk shows OpenAI live transcription with its Change button. Voice notes shows Deepgram nova-3 as Not ready and explains where its key belongs.

![After: separate Talk and Voice notes rows with independent readiness and setup guidance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/43c32bfc4b4396590cba933c140f07fdb10340e5/images/2026/11/28bdfda0-f129-4770-b37b-3979c40f0690.png)

The pair uses the real Control UI and isolated Gateways with made-up settings: OpenAI streaming enabled with a synthetic key, Deepgram nova-3 selected for voice notes without a key. The before capture is from the existing pre-change Gateway proof; the after capture exercises this PR head. No real provider transcription was requested.

Validation: 4 focused Talk test files pass (90 tests): `talk-transcription.test.ts`, `talk.test.ts`, `catalog.test.ts` and `file-transcription.test.ts`. Three of those tests fail without their fix and pass with it: the catalog renders while Models never answers, provider options without a named provider report `streaming-auto`, and the Talk row names the fallback provider. UI and core typechecks, lint on the changed files and `git diff --check` pass. The real UI capture checks the Gateway catalog, independent readiness, and the Deepgram key hint; the fallback wording and the `streaming-auto` case were not run in a live Gateway. Broad CI results are reported by the PR checks. Real-provider transcription, native clients, and the voice-model path in a live Gateway were not tested.

Known main CI failure: the latest completed full-main run has four post-cancel failures in `client-native-control.test.ts` ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43659747920/job/132646591715)).

prs.title: fix: show the Access page when you turn on OpenClaw ID with a plugin allowlist
prs.body:
Closes #198468
Related: #198470

## What Problem This Solves

If a Gateway already has a plugin allowlist (`plugins.allow`) that does not list `openclaw-id-access`, turning on OpenClaw ID leaves the Access page blocked. Remote access works, but the owner has no page to see members, approve invites or remove anyone, and restarting does not help.

## User Impact

User impact: turning on OpenClaw ID from the Labs page, the CLI or setup now also allows its Access page when a plugin allowlist is in use, so the page appears right away.

- If you explicitly blocked the plugin (`plugins.deny`, `plugins.entries["openclaw-id-access"].enabled: false`, or plugins turned off entirely), nothing is changed. You see a plain warning that the Access page stays off and why, in the Labs page, the CLI and the config RPC reply.
- If you turn OpenClaw ID on by editing the config file by hand, the Gateway does not rewrite your file. It logs one warning, and `openclaw doctor` offers to add the plugin to the allowlist, only if you agree. Declining leaves the file byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Turning OpenClaw ID off leaves the allowlist as it is.
- Like other activation writes, this rewrites the config as JSON, so comments in a JSON5 config are lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Turning on OpenClaw ID is consent to use its bundled management page; leaving it blocked gives a claw with remote access but no way to manage who has it. The change only happens on an explicit off-to-on write, in the same config write that already installs missing member-role presets, and it adds exactly one plugin id. Whether the page is blocked is decided by the plugin loader's own policy, so the warnings and the repair follow the same precedence (plugins off, deny, explicit disable, then allowlist). Docs for experimental features and plugin management describe the behavior.

## Evidence

- Tests written first, failing on the base (9 behavioral failures, plus the Labs warning), then passing: real config writers for RPC, CLI and setup; deny, disable and plugins-off kept with warnings; empty or already-listed allowlists untouched; hand-edited and read-only configs not rewritten; Doctor consent and byte-identical decline; turning off leaves plugin policy unchanged. 300 distinct tests pass across the activation, config write, role activation, RPC, Doctor, reload-plan, plugin-policy, CLI and Labs suites.
- Typecheck, test types, source-contract checks, ratchets, format, typed lint and docs checks pass. Test lines +247 of the 400 allowance.
- Independent review found one issue (a blocked page consumed the role-preset activation step), which was reproduced, fixed and re-reviewed with no remaining findings.
- Live check on an isolated Gateway with `plugins.allow: ["browser"]`, no restart: turning OpenClaw ID on changed the allowlist to `["browser", "openclaw-id-access"]` and the Access page appeared with the same Gateway process. With the plugin denied, the CLI and the Labs page left config unchanged and showed the warning. A hand edit left the file byte-identical with one warning; Doctor without consent changed nothing, and with consent added only the Access plugin plus its usual run timestamp.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix(install): honor --beta and warn when a git install cannot resolve a release tag
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #201335 (reported by anmol0b). `install.sh --install-method git` ignores `--beta` and silently falls back to `main` when the latest release tag cannot be resolved.

Two defects in `resolve_git_openclaw_ref` (`scripts/install-policy.sh`):

1. **`--beta` is ignored for git installs.** `--beta` only sets `USE_BETA=1`; the resolver reads only `OPENCLAW_VERSION`, and `USE_BETA` was used only by the npm/Bun engine resolution that runs after the ref is already picked. So a git install with `--beta` checks out the stable release (or `main`), never the beta tag the install plan already advertises ("Beta channel: enabled").
2. **A fresh host without npm silently gets `main`.** `installer_npm view openclaw dist-tags.latest` runs before `ensure_node`, fails on a host that has not installed Node yet, the error is swallowed (`2>/dev/null || true`), and the resolver returns `main` — building unreleased `main` with no visible warning beyond a plain `Using git ref: main` line.

## Solution

Fix both in the shared release-resolution boundary (`resolve_git_openclaw_ref`):

- When `USE_BETA=1` and no explicit version is given, resolve the `beta` dist-tag instead of `latest`, matching how the npm and Bun engine channels already honor `--beta`. An explicit `OPENCLAW_VERSION` is never overridden.
- When the `latest` dist-tag lookup fails, keep returning `main` (the current behavior) but print a warning to stderr instead of doing so silently.

Review follow-up (commits `8a29688dda3` and `524a56ed00d`, ClawSweeper P1): routing `--beta` into the beta lookup without a fallback returned the literal string `beta` when that lookup failed (npm missing on a cold host, or no published beta tag). No `beta` git ref exists, so `checkout_git_openclaw_ref` aborted the install with `Requested git version not found: beta` — turning a working install into a hard failure. The resolver now honors the documented channel contract (`--beta`: use beta dist-tag if available, else fall back to `latest`, per the installer flags reference): a failed beta lookup retries `latest` with a stderr warning; only when both lookups fail does it fall back to `main` with the existing warning. This matches the npm engine path (`Could not resolve beta tag; using latest`) and the Bun engine path (beta → latest fallback) that already implement the same contract. The follow-up commit also normalizes npm variants that print `undefined`/`null` for a missing dist-tag (guarded the same way in install.sh's `resolve_beta_version`) so they resolve as unresolved instead of producing a literal `vundefined` ref.

The `main` fallback remains a visibility-only repair, not a behavior change: the offline/bootstrap fallback still installs `main`, exactly as today — but the user is now told. Resolving tags without npm (e.g. raw registry HTTP) would bypass the npm registry config (mirrors/`.npmrc`) that `npm view` honors — the same constraint the pre-existing `latest` lookup has on main — so this PR keeps npm-based resolution and makes every failure visible instead. The issue's expected behavior explicitly asks for this ("It does not quietly build `main`"); resolving the tag after Node is installed or failing outright would change bootstrap behavior and is a maintainer call, which this PR deliberately does not make. No new options, config, or persistence.

Explicit versions (`v1.2.3`, `beta`, `main`) behave exactly as before.

## Impact

Real user fault on first-run setup: a git install with `--beta` now checks out the beta tag, a host without npm is told that `main` is being used instead of silently building unreleased code, and the beta path can no longer abort on a nonexistent `beta` ref. ~20 production lines in one function.

## Evidence

- Regression (red/green): new tests in `test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts` —
  - `falls back to the latest release when the beta tag cannot be resolved` fails on base (`beta-missing=beta`) and passes with the fix (`beta-missing=v2026.5.12` + stderr warning); this is the P1 hard-failure regression.
  - `falls back to main with a warning when beta and latest both fail on a cold host` fails on base and passes with the fix.
  - `applies --beta to the git install ref when no explicit version is given` now actually clears `OPENCLAW_VERSION` for the empty case (review finding: it previously repeated the `latest` input).
- Installer-entry chain proof (new `installer entry` tests): the shipped resolver and checkout owner run against a real clone of a real local remote (offline fixture; npm presence controlled via PATH):
  - warm host `--beta` → selects `v2026.5.12-beta.3`, checks out the real tag (`kind=immutable`).
  - cold host without npm on PATH → selects `main` with `Warning: could not resolve the beta release tag (npm registry lookup failed); falling back to the main branch.`, checks out the real `main` branch (`kind=moving`) — previously a hard `Requested git version not found: beta` abort.
  - existing-install rerun with an explicit pin and `--beta` → `OPENCLAW_VERSION=v2026.5.12` wins, checkout moves off the beta tag to the pinned stable tag.
- Real-registry entry proof (local run against registry.npmjs.org, redacted): `npm view openclaw dist-tags.beta` → `2026.11.5`, `dist-tags.latest` → `2026.11.5`; shipped `scripts/install.sh` (sourced with `OPENCLAW_INSTALL_SH_NO_RUN=1`, the repo's `test-install-git-ref.sh` pattern) resolved `v2026.11.5` and checked out the real tag; rerun with `OPENCLAW_VERSION=v2026.11.4` moved the checkout to the pinned tag; cold-host rerun (Node toolchain dropped from PATH) selected `main` with the warning above and checked out `main`. All three scenarios PASS.
- **Normal-invocation proof (new — addresses the re-review blocker).** The shipped installer was executed end to end as a plain process (`bash scripts/install.sh --git …`, no `OPENCLAW_INSTALL_SH_NO_RUN`, no sourcing), covering all four required behaviors. GitHub was mirrored to a local bare remote through a per-run `git insteadOf` rewrite (installer code unmodified); dist-tag lookups hit a local registry stub via real `npm view` (the machine sits behind a proxy, so registry.npmjs.org is unreachable from the test host); every scenario ran with a fresh `HOME`. All four scenarios PASS:
  ### Setup
  - GitHub is mirrored to a local bare remote via per-run `git config url."file://…".insteadOf`; the installer still clones `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git` and runs unmodified (`bash scripts/install.sh`, no `OPENCLAW_INSTALL_SH_NO_RUN`).
  - npm dist-tag lookups go to a local registry stub (real `npm view` against a real HTTP registry); `dist-tags` are switched per scenario.
  - Fresh `HOME` per scenario; cold host = `PATH` limited to a tool symlink dir (git + coreutils; no node/npm/corepack/pnpm/curl/wget).
  - Fixture remote refs: `main` (1 commit past `v2026.11.6`), tags `v2026.11.4`, `v2026.11.5-beta.1`, `v2026.11.6`.
  
  ### S1 — warm host, `--beta`, beta tag available (dist-tags: latest=2026.11.4, beta=2026.11.5-beta.1)
  ```console
  · Installing OpenClaw from GitHub (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git)
  · Using git ref: v2026.11.5-beta.1
  ✓ Node.js v24.22.1 found
  🦞 OpenClaw installed successfully (0.0.0-fixture)!
  HEAD: d263ff48168c950087bb478c42671f1c3e9a0e83   # == tag v2026.11.5-beta.1 (remote)
  PASS — beta channel selected and installed.
  ```
  
  ### S2 — warm host, `--beta`, registry has no beta tag (dist-tags: latest=2026.11.4 only)
  ```console
  Warning: could not resolve the beta release tag; falling back to the latest stable release.
  · Using git ref: v2026.11.4
  🦞 OpenClaw installed successfully (0.0.0-fixture)!
  HEAD: 791b07e91a52edb736dae3329a42845fa1e52e12   # == tag v2026.11.4 (remote)
  PASS — warned, fell back to the latest stable tag.
  ```
  
  ### S3 — cold host (no npm on PATH), `--beta`
  ```console
  Warning: could not resolve the beta release tag (npm registry lookup failed); falling back to the main branch.
  · Using git ref: main
  · Checking out main
  · Node.js not found, installing it now
  ✗ sudo is required for system installs on Linux
  HEAD: 678a43df36b1f14ecae8ceff833a43fc0e8a2649   # == remote main (describe: v2026.11.6-1-g678a43d)
  PASS — warned and checked out main instead of hard-failing on the literal "beta".
  The run then stops at Node.js system provisioning ("sudo is required…"), which is outside this change and matches main-line behavior on hosts without a usable runtime.
  ```
  
  ### S4 — existing latest-stable install, rerun after `latest` moves; settings intact
  Pre-seeded user settings at `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (custom gateway port + marker field). Run 1 with dist-tags latest=2026.11.4:
  ```console
  · Installing OpenClaw from GitHub (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git)
  · Using git ref: v2026.11.4
  ✓ Doctor complete
  🦞 OpenClaw installed successfully (0.0.0-fixture)!
  HEAD: 791b07e91a52edb736dae3329a42845fa1e52e12   # == tag v2026.11.4 (remote)
  ```
  Registry `latest` bumped to 2026.11.6, installer rerun (no flags):
  ```console
  · Installing OpenClaw from git checkout: /tmp/<sandbox>/s4-rerun/home/openclaw
  · Using git ref: v2026.11.6
  ✓ Doctor complete
  🦞 OpenClaw installed successfully (0.0.0-fixture)!
  HEAD: 409fe81f540af1d78294202f0ae703016bbecd23   # == tag v2026.11.6 (remote)
  settings sha256 identical across runs: 5f82362402a7ecef8dc913604a76b3633fc0c31198f9cb8c0fa58673bfcc13b6
  PASS — checkout moved v2026.11.4 → v2026.11.6; user settings untouched.
  ```

- Commands (all green locally):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts test/scripts/install-sh-beta.test.ts test/scripts/install-sh.provisioning.test.ts test/scripts/install-git-ref.test.ts test/scripts/standalone-installers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 239 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing), no regressions in the touched suite.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/install-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (the other consumer of `install-policy.sh`) — passed.
  - `/bin/bash -n scripts/install-policy.sh scripts/install.sh scripts/install-cli.sh`; `git diff --check`.
- Local review: shared autoreview helper attempted (codex engine) — unavailable in this environment (`api.openai.com` 403 on the model websocket), no report produced; gap disclosed rather than claimed. Independent local review of `origin/main...HEAD` (both commits) by a fresh reviewer agent instead: **no P1/P2 findings**; three P3s — two fixed in `524a56ed00d` (undefined-dist-tag guard; beta-missing test mock now mimics real npm exit-0-empty behavior), one recorded here as a pre-existing follow-up: `--version next` with an unresolvable `next` dist-tag echoes the literal `next` and fails checkout identically on current main (no documented fallback contract for `next`, so behavior intentionally unchanged).

## Collision note

#201350 was opened 94 seconds after this PR for the same issue. It fixes only the `--beta` half and defers the silent-main fallback to a maintainer call; this PR covers both reported defects, the review-found beta fallback hard failure, and now includes installer-entry proof.

## Related precedent

#188005 fixed the npm-only `--beta` path on a fresh host; this closes the git-install gap in the same shape, and the beta→latest fallback mirrors the Bun engine channel's existing behavior.

prs.title: fix: run scripts from symlinked checkouts
prs.body:
Related: #201528 and #201539 (the macOS packaging case).

## What Problem This Solves

Running a repository script by absolute path through a symlinked checkout can exit successfully without doing any work. For example, CI scope detection writes no outputs, and the Docker release policy command returns no JSON for its caller to read.

## User Impact

Developers can run the same repository script through a symlink or its physical path and get the expected output and exit status.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node normally resolves the main module's symlinks for `import.meta.url` while leaving the invocation path in `process.argv[1]`. The shared entrypoint check now resolves that path when its direct comparison misses. The direct comparison still handles Node's preserve-symlinks mode and Windows case matching. Four callers now reuse the shared check for behavior they previously implemented themselves.

## Evidence

- On Linux with Node 24.18.0 and main `02078202f31`, running `node "$linkedCheckout/scripts/ci-changed-scope.mjs" --base HEAD^ --head HEAD` with an isolated `GITHUB_OUTPUT` exited 0 without creating the output or changed-paths manifest. The same invocation with this patch writes all 20 output lines and a manifest identical to the physical-path control, except for the output path recorded in the workflow output.
- `node "$linkedCheckout/scripts/lib/docker-release-policy.mjs" 2026.11.5` went from empty stdout to the same stable-channel JSON as the physical-path invocation. Checked the repaired attestation help and Docker policy commands on Node 24.22.1 too, including Node's preserve-symlinks mode.
- The real attestation CLI regression failed on the base because the symlinked invocation produced no usage text. Physical-path and preserve-symlinks controls passed. The fixed entrypoint, watchdog, ClawHub recovery, and Docker release policy suites passed all 62 tests via the repository Vitest wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`.
- Local Codex autoreview of the full patch against `02078202f31` returned `scoped-clean` at P0. The Windows junction case is covered in the regression and awaits native Windows CI.
- Targeted scripts and tooling-test typechecks, file-scoped lint and formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Production scripts are net −12 lines. Tests are net +18 lines.

<details>
<summary>Captured output from the symlinked checkout on Linux (Node 24.18.0)</summary>

The paths below use placeholders for the local checkout and output directories. Output lines are excerpts from the original run.

```text
Before (02078202f31)
$ node "$linkedCheckout/scripts/ci-changed-scope.mjs" --base HEAD^ --head HEAD
[exit 0, output and changed-path manifest absent]
$ node "$linkedCheckout/scripts/lib/docker-release-policy.mjs" 2026.11.5
[exit 0, stdout empty]

After (ed4e9eedf)
$ node "$linkedCheckout/scripts/ci-changed-scope.mjs" --base HEAD^ --head HEAD
$ wc -l < "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
20
$ cat "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"  # excerpt
run_node=true
run_macos=false
run_windows=false
$ node "$linkedCheckout/scripts/lib/docker-release-policy.mjs" 2026.11.5
{"version":"2026.11.5","channel":"stable","movingAliases":{"default":["latest","main"],"slim":["slim","main-slim"],"browser":["latest-browser","main-browser"]}}
```

</details>

prs.title: improve: keep subagent spawns fast in large registries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Spawning a child in a large retained registry copies every run and rebuilds the complete read topology just to check one parent's child limit.

## User Impact

Subagent spawn admission scales with the selected parent's children and their relevant descendants. Child limits and pending-delivery behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registry already owns indexed memberships. Admission now consumes those memberships, overlays raw live rows, and follows only selected child edges. Controller and swarm admission membership share the existing bucket; no new persistent cache or database schema is introduced.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, recorded before measurement: use 20,000 synthetic persisted runs and 4,800 live rows (3,200 overlaps), with about 20 direct children for the measured session. Compare the frozen previous algorithm and the registry owner in serial A/A and A/B pairs (five each), separating first indexed-read cost from warm measurements. Record per-call wall time, CPU and sampled allocation including collected objects. Require identical counts, zero warm full-registry iteration, and at least 80% lower warm CPU and allocation; investigate any measured regression of 20% or more. Capture CPU profiles. This is an owner microbenchmark, not a full Gateway or btrfs workload claim; the owner does not scan workspaces or query an agent database during admission.

| Warm per-admission metric (median / p95, five pairs) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Wall time | 27.435 / 27.649 ms | 0.01475 / 0.01995 ms |
| CPU | 38.735 / 38.965 ms | 0.02821 / 0.06078 ms |
| Sampled allocation | 82,286,112 / 82,473,655 B | 26,682 / 30,110 B |

A/A median wall times were 27.401/27.293 ms; CPU 38.070/38.105 ms; allocation 82,342,314/82,371,172 B. Timing samples use 100 calls, allocation samples 20 calls at 4 KiB sampling, including collected objects. Node 26.12.1 on macOS; shared-host one-minute load 5.38–6.63. First indexed read was 20.022 ms versus 47.936 ms for the baseline; this single cold observation is not a repeated cold benchmark. The existing lookup initializes once, then publications update it. The baseline CPU profile has 512 self samples in topology construction/patching (1,858 total); the candidate profile has no such frames (575 total). Profiling uses 100 baseline calls and 100,000 candidate calls, separate from comparable timing/allocation measurements.

All 122 focused tests pass (7 files, 48.0 s wrapper wall time; new differential regression 0.210 s). The new regression compares every session and filter across persisted/live overlap and ownership/generation changes. With full-registry iteration disabled after preparation, the original owner fails at its Map copy and the candidate passes. Existing scoped-read tests cover controller/swarm membership replacement and deletion. No changed production module is imported by ui/src.

Author simplification deletes the superseded counting function and its stale comment, preserving one admission owner. Production delta is +37 lines: bounded descendant traversal and swarm membership maintenance replace the full topology rebuild without adding a second index. Tests +227 lines; benchmark 118 lines. No schema, config, public API, or permission change.

Independent Codex autoreview of the complete local change against 02078202f318329663680c2bcc0a4738f8b883ec is scoped-clean at P0–P2, with no actionable findings. `pnpm check:changed --staged` passed. After preserving the old direct-child clock behavior, all 33 affected tests passed again; final Codex autoreview is also scoped-clean. Hosted review and exact-head CI remain required before merge.

Reproduce: `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/subagent-spawn-admission.ts [profile-prefix]`. The baseline is the frozen previous merge/count algorithm; synthetic durable rows are written to isolated SQLite through the fixture owner. Admission measurements run on resident facts and exclude fixture creation. No production data was copied.

prs.title: fix(worktrees): reuse templates when sessions alternate base commits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Starting sessions on alternating base commits repeatedly refreshes the same managed worktree template, including when returning to a commit prepared earlier. Managed templates were excluded from the retained-generation mechanism already used by sandbox templates.

## User Impact

Returning to a retained base commit reuses its existing source generation without another template refresh. The existing collector keeps four recent idle generations per managed template identity; active readers remain protected. No configuration or SQLite schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Refresh-capable producers share retained publication and lookup. Managed retention is grouped by repository/destination/checkout identity; sandbox runtime grouping stays unchanged. Prepared checkouts keep one stable slot across retained source generations. Invalid managed generations still retire through ordinary maintenance, preserving the earlier request-path cleanup fix.

This is the narrow managed-retention slice overlapping parked #197301; it does not add its scheduler or build/publication concurrency changes. Related: #195883, #201364.

## Evidence

The real-Git `ManagedWorktreeService.create` A→B→A regression fails on parent `c5f6eed45299476fe06611784328c9395fa43201`: returning to A performs two clones. With the fix it reuses A's original generation, calls no `createTemplate`, and clones only the private checkout. Separate coverage verifies four-generation eviction with live readers and one refill slot across retained generations.

- 92 focused tests pass across managed acceleration, reader custody, retained slots, registry, prepared checkouts, and sandbox template consumers. Infra shard: 75.54 s; agents-support shard: 27.61 s; sandbox-consumer file: 26.60 s. CI seconds pending.
- `pnpm check:changed` and `git diff --check` pass. No Control UI imports of the touched owner modules were found.
- Codex autoreview, complete owner source plus final local diff against the parent, scoped clean through P2; no actionable findings.
- Production delta: **+5 lines** (27 added / 22 removed). The growth separates retention identities and preserves deferred invalid-generation cleanup; no new cache or scheduler.

Native Btrfs storage proof uses a synthetic 62,000-file workspace (50,001 tracked source files; ignored dependency files do not enter source templates), a 22-file commit change, and a 37,621,817,344-byte synthetic SQLite occupancy file with 5,000 rows. Two source generations share 1,023,549,440 extent bytes and each has 450,560 exclusive data bytes. Deleting the older generation and its Git registration reduces overall used filesystem space by **37,670,912 bytes (35.93 MiB)**, including index and metadata with Btrfs DUP metadata. Shared subtree sizes must not be summed. This is native storage accounting, not Gateway load.

The APFS series completed two baseline controls and five counterbalanced baseline/candidate pairs. Each arm seeds A outside timing, then measures B→A→B. All ten candidate return requests keep the same two IDs and perform **zero template refreshes**; baseline refreshes on all ten. Both variants produce the selected clean commit. Acceptance was recorded before measurement; no samples were discarded.

| Return request metric (10 samples/variant) | Baseline median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Template preparation | 3.235 / 4.861 s | 0.821 / 0.983 s |
| Whole service creation | 11.536 / 23.217 s | 9.059 / 10.062 s |
| Process CPU | 7.643 / 14.688 s | 6.308 / 6.774 s |
| Main-thread CPU | 402 / 606 ms | 226 / 271 ms |
| Main-isolate allocation | 305.5 / 310.2 MB | 164.0 / 177.9 MB |
| Native clones per request | 2 | 1 |

The initial B advance still refreshes once: median owner time 3.453→2.867 s; whole creation 5.913→5.583 s; process CPU 2.649→2.705 s (+2.1%, inside A/A control spread); allocation 310.2→308.5 MB. A/A return controls span 2.416–3.060 s owner time and 298.6–308.6 MB allocation. Baseline pair 4 has a retained 23.217 s tail with load average 18.4 and a 10.036 s allocation/mutation wait; that explains part of the whole-service tail difference, not a universal latency guarantee. Median improvement and zero-refresh work counts hold separately.

Process CPU includes workers, excludes Git subprocesses; allocation covers the main isolate, not workers/native allocation. Owner timings are APFS, not Btrfs or a live Gateway/35-GiB agent-store workload. The Btrfs probe separately qualifies native storage sharing with synthetic occupancy. No production data or live deployment is used.

Rerunnable workloads: `scripts/perf/worktree-creation-measure.ts --repo <synthetic-repo> --output <new-output> --samples 3 --expected-commit <A> --alternate-commit <B>` (parent-owner overlay through `OPENCLAW_BENCH_BASELINE_DIR` for baseline); `scripts/perf/worktree-template-retention-disk.py --fixture <synthetic-repo> --root <empty-scratch>` in a disposable, network-disabled privileged Linux container.

### Persisted-state compatibility follow-up

A separate new-process probe opened the existing synthetic registry and APFS template produced by exact-parent owner code, without rebuilding, migrating, or editing rows. Candidate B→A→B preserved the original B generation ID throughout; ready generation counts were 1→2→2, native clone counts 1→2→1, template owner times 891→2851→756 ms. Every checkout had the correct commit and clean Git status. Only first-time A preparation refreshed. This proves existing stored templates remain usable across the code upgrade; schema and record shape are unchanged. This is native service/SQLite/Git proof, not full Gateway/model coverage.

prs.title: feat(plugins): guard effects against stale conversation assignments
prs.body:
Related: #196909

> **On hold — draft conversion requested.** No detached-binding incident has been reproduced in Campaign Keeper, and the need for a new public SDK authority surface has not been established. Evaluate the Codex-style plugin-owned lifecycle approach using supported APIs before advancing this proposal. Codex’s owner/admin admission is not a multiplayer authorization policy, and its private harness helpers are not proposed for import into Campaign Keeper. The implementation and test evidence below are retained; they establish mechanics, not the necessity of SDK expansion.

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins cannot safely tie an authorized non-owner participant's later effects to the exact current plugin conversation assignment using an awaited binding snapshot or the existing owner-only command guard.

## User Impact

Adds an opt-in `withCurrentConversationBinding` capability to supporting command and V2 tool contexts, without granting owner privileges or application membership. A callback receives host-bound requester/conversation/session facts, a live assertion, and an opaque restriction that V2 state writers enforce against the native binding row inside their transaction.

**On hold: the need for SDK expansion is being reassessed.** This is a working implementation proposal, not an accepted or released SDK contract. Custom/legacy binding owners, different physical state stores, missing identities, and Control UI/guest principals without an authenticated native channel requester fail closed. Command adapters must provide live host authorization; the text-command path and native Discord dispatch forward it here. No configuration migration, owner-only gate relaxation, Gateway change, deployment, or multiplayer claim is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing plugin lifecycle, session-incarnation, prepared binding-selection, and V2 state owners rather than asking plugins to reconstruct host authority. Preserve the opaque restriction when composing application checks; registered worker operations retain their stores' restrictions too. The native writer compares the exact binding and expiry after the final host commit grant while holding the mutation transaction.

V2's existing host commit-grant ordering remains: later revocation does not retroactively undo an accepted write. Application membership and actor ownership still belong at the application's conditional mutation owner. The reused prepared-selection owner is conservative: binding publications, including benign refreshes, can retire a callback and require a new request. There is no custom-adapter snapshot fallback or new persistent authority store.

The Campaign Keeper consumer remains unchanged and owner-only. Its [handoff](https://github.com/ekinnee/openclaw-agent-templates/blob/feat/campaign-keeper/docs/campaign-keeper-multiplayer-authority-handoff.md) supplies the concrete need, not multiplayer proof. This PR addresses the host-owned seam; it does not expose private capability scope to separate trusted-policy hooks.

## Evidence

CI follow-up head: `3c829853bca9e8f6243eadd32176c5363107212b`; local source: `8dd6758339068db244a6e17dc0861174fb47caaf`.

### P1 repair: preserve the original requester across command preparation

Published head: `6d074fc477cc332fc0cbf84a26053500c0150c6b`; local source: `2533f20a64e3d5d425fde6a72d79ccf52dbf8fcc`.

**The reported preparation-time gap is reproduced and repaired.** Previously, `getRequesterProfile` ran after `await prepareCommandAuthorization`; revoking the original linked requester during that wait made it return `undefined` and omit the rejecting requester assertion. Native Discord could then pass its unchanged sender allowlist. `resolveCommandAuthorizationAsync` now captures the original host requester **before** preparation and passes it explicitly to the authorization retainer. Revocation preserves a rejected original principal; it never turns that request into an unlinked-principal invocation or borrows the replacement profile. Native Discord retains its own policy and owner-first refusal ordering; neither binding nor session checks substitute for the requester restriction.

The [new regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6d074fc477cc332fc0cbf84a26053500c0150c6b/src/channels/message-access/discord-native-owner.test.ts) pauses the channel-owned allowlist hook inside real command preparation, then unlinks or reassigns the linked member before resuming. It runs the bundled native Discord command handler, real host-profile admission, actual registered plugin dispatch, `withCurrentConversationBinding`, and V2 state-worker persistence. The fixture delays the allowlist resolver but preserves its real result; sender allowlist and channel policy stay unchanged. Persistence uses the existing **core/native account binding owner**, not a stock Discord platform-adapter snapshot. Top-level thread routing and interaction I/O are fixed fixtures. This qualifies the native admission/preparation boundary, not live platform authentication or stock Discord binding-manager support.

**Red/green:** on the preceding source revision, the allowed control passes and both revocation regressions fail because each persists one move. With the repair, the control still persists one move; unlink and reassignment are rejected before handler entry and persist zero effects.

prs.title: fix(agents): node tools with an unverified plugin owner can pass plugin-ID tool policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a node tool that claims a plugin owner it is not registered under can pass a tool policy that allows tools by plugin ID, when the tool was first admitted through a broad plugin grant.

## User Impact

User impact: a plugin-ID entry in a tool allowlist now admits only tools whose ownership was verified when the node tool was materialized. The same holds for the tools a cron job captures from its creator, and for descriptors that use a case or whitespace variant of the reserved owner name without being genuine node-MCP descriptors. Exact tool-name grants, broad plugin grants, registered owners and genuine node-MCP descriptors behave as before. Deny rules still match on the claimed owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node-tool materialization already distinguishes verified from claimed ownership, but that distinction was lost in policy metadata, in caller snapshots and in cron creator-tool capture. The reserved-owner exception also normalized the ID without checking that the descriptor really has the node-MCP shape. The ownership decision is now made once, during materialization: the reserved exception requires the core MCP command and non-empty server and tool metadata, and unverified ownership is carried through the policy and cron projections. Plugin-ID allows and intersections expand using verified owners only.

## Evidence

Run with Node 24.22.2 and pnpm 12.15.0. Transport is mocked; no remote tool is invoked.

- The regression in `src/agents/node-plugin-tools.test.ts` uses real node publication, materialization, policy filtering and cron creator selection. Replayed unchanged against `main` it fails 7 of 25 cases; on this branch all 25 pass.
- A second, separately written test set covering the policy pipeline, caller snapshot, cron creator selection and reserved-owner variants: 19 failed / 6 passed on `main`, 25 passed on this branch.
- Changed-scope suites (policy, cron, caller and delegated authority, node snapshots, effective-tool reporting, embedded construction, prompt-prefix stability): 20 suites, 359 tests passed.
- Full build and all test typechecks passed. Scoped lint reported no warnings or errors across the ten changed TypeScript files; formatting, policy guards, import cycles and the test-line budget check passed. The per-change test allocation is 140 lines.

Gap: the broad `pnpm check` passed production, UI, extension, script and root-test types and script lint, then extension lint reported two line-limit errors in unchanged Tlon and Crabbox tests that also occur on an untouched `main`; the remaining core lint scan was stopped there, so the full check is not claimed green locally.

### Running Gateway with a connected node

A real built Gateway and a real built node host were started from each revision, with device and node pairing approved through Gateway RPC. Synthetic external plugins supplied harmless marker tools. A loopback MCP HTTP server stood in for the node-MCP far end, and a loopback Responses endpoint stood in for the model, recording the tool names it was offered. Neither is a hosted service or a real model. No product source was changed and the same driver ran on both builds.

- Base: `b382a29a688a`. Head: `3d064663c293`. Node 24.22.2, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, private-QA build.
- Policy: `tools.allow = ["policy-owner", "node-mcp", "policy_exact", "automations"]`, full profile, Code Mode and Tool Search off. `node.list` confirmed the published descriptors. Offered tools were read from `tools.effective` and from the requests of a completed turn, which agreed.
- In that turn the model stand-in created a cron job through the product's `automations` tool; `cron.get` returned the persisted tool cap. The policy was then replaced through `config.patch` with `["policy_exact", "automations"]` and the job was run with `cron.run`.

| Synthetic tool | Base: offered | Base: in cron cap | Head: offered | Head: in cron cap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `policy_verified` (registered, verified owner) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| `control_probe` (genuine node MCP) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| `policy_claimed` (claims `policy-owner`, not registered under it) | **yes** | **yes** | no | no |
| `policy_exact` (exact-name grant) | yes | yes | yes | yes |

After the plugin-ID entries were withdrawn, the cron run was offered only `policy_exact` on both builds.

Not observed: a non-MCP descriptor using a case variant of the reserved owner could not be published through the normal node-plugin loader on either build (the manifest loader rejects the reserved ID case-insensitively), so that case is covered by the unit regression only.

Limits: local stand-ins for the MCP far end and the model; offerings and the cron cap were observed, not execution of an excluded tool; restart and crash recovery were not exercised.

## What Problem This Solves

When you sign in with OpenClaw ID from the macOS app, the sign-in dialog shows a code and an "Open OpenClaw ID" button. Clicking the button opened the OpenClaw ID page in the app's built-in browser panel, not in your usual browser. So you couldn't use the browser where you're already signed in or where your password manager works.

## User Impact

User impact: "Open OpenClaw ID" in the device sign-in dialog now opens your default browser. In a regular web browser it still opens a new tab, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The button is an ordinary link, and the macOS app sends ordinary links to its built-in browser panel. The button now has the existing "always open externally" link marker, the same one the model-provider sign-in button already uses, so link routing hands it to the system browser.

## Evidence

- New `device-sign-in-dialog.test.tsx` runs the real dialog with the native link router and a stubbed macOS WebKit bridge, then clicks "Open OpenClaw ID". It checks that the click becomes an external `open-link` request and that no browser-panel request is made. The test fails on the base commit and passes with the fix.

prs.title: feat(update): run every Git install from releases and delete the in-place Git runner
prs.body:
Slice 4b of the update foundation. Follows #199706 (slice 4) and #198835 (release link).

## Problem

Slice 4 moved POSIX Git checkouts that have a Gateway service onto `git worktree` releases behind the release link. Three cases still used the in-place Git runner: Windows checkouts, package-to-Git switches, and checkouts with no Gateway service. Also, the installer's `openclaw` wrapper still ran `<checkout>/dist/entry.js`. A release update does not rebuild that file, so after conversion `openclaw` on PATH stayed on the old build. On Windows, conversion also warned "Gateway service still points outside the updated install", because the check compared the running process root instead of the service definition.

## Change

- Every Git install now updates through releases. The in-place Git runner and its command-side rollback are deleted on every platform in one cutover. `openclaw update` no longer moves the checkout HEAD or rebuilds its `dist`.
- Windows: the release link is an NTFS junction (no admin rights), owned by the existing `package-release-slot*` code. The Windows task supervisor starts its Gateway child through the release launcher.
- Package-to-Git: the checkout is cloned and the target is built as the first release (a fresh worktree). This is so even when the checkout is already at the target. The global npm package's `openclaw.mjs` now starts the release launcher, so the existing bin shims follow releases. The rest of the package stays in place, because this updater and a running Gateway still load from it.
- CLI entry (decision A, 2026-11-17): after a Git release update, the installer's `openclaw` wrapper (POSIX and Windows) is rewritten one time to run `<git-install>/openclaw-launcher.mjs`. `scripts/install.sh` and `scripts/install.ps1` recognize that wrapper as theirs.
- Launcher: a pending (`--no-restart`) release is selected, and a trial start is counted, only for real Gateway starts: the service's `gateway --port …`, or a foreground `gateway` / `gateway run`. Root options can be anywhere in the command. `gateway status`, `--help`, `--version` and `--task-supervisor` parents do not count.
- `serviceUsesUpdatedRoot` now reads the service definition. A `--no-restart` Git release update whose service still starts the checkout records an owed `service-definition` step that tells the operator to run `openclaw gateway install --force`.

## Impact

- One update path for Git installs on macOS, Linux and Windows.
- `openclaw` on PATH runs the current release after an update, with pending-release and switch-back handling.
- Accepted edge case: two checkouts that share one state directory share its single release install. An update run from checkout B updates the install that the state directory owns (first made from checkout A). Previously B updated itself in place. A revision that only B has fails to resolve, with a visible error. It is not handled in code.
- Accepted: after a package-to-Git switch, the old npm package keeps its disk space until `npm uninstall -g openclaw`.

## Size

Measured against `origin/main` at head `ec70cb33c859`:

| | added | removed | net |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| production | 337 | 1,780 | −1,443 |
| tests | 217 | 6,528 | −6,311 |

With slice 4's +980, the production net for slices 4 and 4b is −463.

## Evidence

Real installs: a source checkout with a Gateway service, the installer wrapper on PATH, and a local upstream that gets a new commit before each update. Probes hit `/readyz` every few hundred ms.

| Platform | Case | Head | Result | Longest outage | CLI on PATH after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| macOS (launchd) | conversion | `ec70cb3` | ok, 322 s | 6.6 s | launcher, new commit `ecf2616` |
| macOS | release → release | `ec70cb3` | ok, 153 s | 7.6 s | launcher, `5a62315` |
| macOS | crash release | `ec70cb3` | failed twice, launcher switched back to the previous release | 28.6 s | — |
| macOS | no service | `ec70cb3` | ok, 217 s; checkout HEAD unchanged | — | launcher, `09d9571` |
| Windows (Scheduled Task) | conversion | `ec70cb3` | ok, 607 s; slot junction → `releases\git-…` | 78.6 s | launcher, `ec70cb3` |
| Windows | release → release | `ec70cb3` | ok, 562 s | 93.9 s | launcher, `248166f` |
| Windows | release → release | `ec70cb3` | ok, 552 s | 112.6 s | launcher, `46db59a` |

- Windows: the service-definition warning is gone. The task runs `openclaw-launcher.mjs gateway --port … --task-supervisor`, and the child runs through the launcher. Windows outages are long because the Gateway on the test VM (m7i.large, Defender off) takes about 80–110 s to become ready again after a restart. The outage is restart time, not update time.
- Red on base: these tests fail on `6747b1ec5a` and pass on this branch: wrapper retirement, "moves something other than a release link aside", and "publishes the first release of a package-to-Git switch from a current checkout" (fails before the last fix).
- Focused tests: `src/infra/git-release.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-runner-git-release.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-wrapper-retirement.test.ts`, the update CLI suites touched here; `tsgo:core`, `check:test-types`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Not run end to end: package-to-Git (npm install, then `openclaw update --channel dev`). The unit test covers the first release, and the npm entry rewrite is one atomic file replace.

## Review

Local ClawSweeper (gpt-6.1-sol), five rounds. Fixed: wrapper bypassing the launcher, npm bin shims, root-option and help invocations in the launcher, package runtime kept in place, first release always built, and the `--no-restart` owed step. The last open finding (checkout B reusing checkout A's release slot) is the accepted edge case above.

prs.title: fix(database-port): prepare runtime config before the offline memory rebuild
prs.body:
Closes #201575

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw database port --to postgres` completes, but its built-in post-port memory rebuild fails for agents with real indexes because the embedding provider reads the prepared runtime config before the port command captured it, logging `Runtime config is not prepared. Await captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader()() first.`

## User Impact

The port's offline memory rebuild now prepares the runtime config reader first, matching the standalone `memory index` command. Agents with real content rebuild during the port instead of being left dirty with a manual follow-up command.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Capture the runtime config with `captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader({ skipPluginValidation: true })()` at the start of the offline rebuild, before the memory plugin opens.
- Keep the existing offline state ownership, secret resolution, and per-agent isolation unchanged.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-database-port-memory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 7/7 passed, including a new case that starts without a prepared reader and asserts `readRuntimeConfig()` succeeds inside the real rebuild path.
- Red-on-base: reverting only `doctor-database-port-memory.ts` makes the new case fail with `expected undefined to be defined`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint clean on both changed files.

- Rebuild-path probe: the new regression starts from `resetConfigRuntimeState()`, then runs the real `rebuildPortedAgentMemory` custody with the real config loader; the memory-plugin seam calls `readRuntimeConfig()`. Before the fix that call throws `Runtime config is not prepared. Await captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader()() first.` and the agent ends `failed`; with the fix it returns the captured config and the agent ends `rebuilt` (7/7 tests pass).
- Environment note: a full `database port --to postgres` CLI run needs a PostgreSQL-backed port of an isolated store; the preflight in a fresh isolated state additionally enumerates an unrelated `plugins/team-reports` store and refuses before reaching the memory rebuild. The regression exercises the changed rebuild owner directly, which is where the reported failure occurs.

prs.title: fix(database-port): treat SQLite zero sequence high-water as uncalled
prs.body:
Closes #201573

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw database port --to postgres` aborts when an `AUTOINCREMENT` table has a `sqlite_sequence` row with `seq = 0` (an empty `audit_events`, for example). The port derived `{ value: "0", called: true }` and emitted `SELECT setval(seq, 0, true)`, which PostgreSQL rejects with `value 0 is out of bounds for sequence (1..9223372036854775807)`.

## User Impact

An empty AUTOINCREMENT table no longer aborts the port. SQLite treats `seq = 0` like an absent row, so the destination now keeps the uncalled shape (`setval(seq, 1, false)`) instead of jumping to an out-of-range value.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Treat a zero high-water (and a zero row maximum) as "never called" when reading a SQLite identity.
- Extract the per-identity SQLite allocation read and fact shaping into `port-allocation-fact.ts` so the worker stays within its line cap.
- Legacy values above zero and genuine row maximums keep the existing `called: true` behavior.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.allocations.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 2/2 passed: zero-sequence case yields `{ value: "1", called: false }`; a real high-water of 7 yields `{ value: "7", called: true }`.
- Red-on-base: reverting `port.worker.ts` makes the zero-sequence case fail with `expected { value: '0', called: true }`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint clean; line-cap ratchet reports no violation for the changed files.

- Real PostgreSQL probe against the real agent port descriptor and a real SQLite source (`session_pending_inputs` with `sqlite_sequence.seq = 0`, zero rows):
  - Before this head: reader returns `{ "value": "0", "called": true }`; `setval(seq, 0, true)` fails with `setval: value 0 is out of bounds for sequence "zero_watermark_probe" (1..9223372036854775807)`.
  - After this head: reader returns `{ "value": "1", "called": false }`; `setval(seq, 1, false)` succeeds and the first `nextval` returns `1`.
  - Control: `setval(seq, 0, true)` still raises the same out-of-bounds error, confirming the probe exercises real server bounds.
