prs.title: fix(update): keep updating when a pre-migration database image does not fit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update` refused to start whenever the disk could not hold about five times the size of the shared database. That covered a backup copy, a second copy, three more for restore scratch, and room on every other volume. For a 20 GiB database it wanted 100 GiB free, even when the migration itself needed far less. Git release updates take no database backup at all, yet ran the same check and refused for it.

## User Impact

An update no longer refuses because a pre-migration database image does not fit. When the backup measures that the image will not fit, the update skips it before copying anything, records a warning that names the space needed and free and what is given up, and continues. What is given up: once the new version's migration commits, the previous version cannot be restored and a failed update is fixed forward. The update still refuses, before changing anything, when the disk cannot hold the migration itself, and the message says how much to free. Git release updates run no snapshot check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The owner approved "skip the snapshot and continue instead of refusing the update" after the proof in the copy inventory. Every schema step commits in one SQLite transaction with its version bump. 94 SIGKILLs across `doctor --fix` and `gateway run`, plus a disk-full run, lost nothing. A pre-migration image matters only for running the previous build after a migration commits. This change keeps that image whenever it fits and stops refusing when it does not.

- **One owner of the space calculation** (`src/infra/update-database-backup-space.ts`). It demands only what the image writes: the families once, plus the larger of two needs that never overlap:
  - one family of private staging during capture;
  - on a shared volume, the migration's room afterwards.

  Restore already checks its own space before it moves any live database (`update-database-restore.ts`), so capture no longer reserves restore output.
- **The migration's room** is the largest database plus 64 MiB. A schema migration's write-ahead log holds about one copy of each rewritten page; the report measured 685 MB of log for a shared database of about 0.7 GB. This is the only refusal left. It is always smaller than the old bound, so no update that passed before refuses now. The message gives the shortfall in MiB/GiB and in bytes.
- **The preflight** reports a skipped image as a warning and refuses only for migration room. It returns `{ step, shortfall }`, so the interactive offer to remove retirable recovery copies still appears when the image would be skipped. Without a terminal, it adds the removal advice as a warning instead of "then retry".
- **The activation capture**, `captureUpdateDatabases`, skips only the backup owner's own measured shortfall (`UpdateCaptureSpaceError`, which crosses the worker boundary). That check runs before any family is checkpointed or copied, so no partial image or server capture exists. In that case the capture:
  - removes the empty directory it created exclusively;
  - returns no backup, which is the existing "automatic restoration unavailable" path;
  - records a `database snapshot` step with exit code 0 and the warning.

  With no backup, the existing rollback owner already refuses to put the previous code on migrated state (`state-migrated-no-rollback`). Any other failure still fails the update before migration. That includes a disk that fills during a copy, and a shortfall joined by a cleanup failure.
- **Git release** (`gitReleases`) no longer runs `snapshot-space-preflight` before staging or before a package-to-Git clone. Release boots migrate at Gateway start, under that path's own space rules.
- **The interactive cleanup offer** is skipped for an install already serving from a Git release.

Not changed here, by scope:
- The image still covers every database family, not only the ones whose schema the target changes. Restore puts the families back as one generation set; narrowing that is fix-plan item 5.
- The activation capture reads through SQLite into private staging even under custody, so it is a byte copy, not a clone. Its demand is therefore the bytes it really writes; the "about zero on copy-on-write" case needs item 5.
- The migration-room refusal is computed before the target's schemas are known, so it also counts databases the target will not migrate. It is still far below the old bound. Narrowing it needs target schema admission earlier.
- After activation, the migration's room is not checked again. If staging has used the space by the time of capture, the image is skipped. A migration that then runs out of room fails inside its SQLite transaction and loses nothing.
- **Cleanup offer from a checkout:** release mode is selected after this preflight, from service ownership. An update started from the original checkout of an install that already serves from a release (or a first conversion) can still be offered removal of retirable copies. It removes them only with an interactive yes.
- **Other backup owners still refuse:** `openclaw update migrate` (the supervisor capture), database migration capture, standalone Doctor's capture comparison and the original-state capture still refuse when their image does not fit. They now refuse at the smaller "what it writes" bound, keeping the "Free disk space before retrying; the databases have not been migrated" guidance. Their callers need the image as a receipt.
- The legacy-driver rehearsal snapshot (`requiredSnapshotBytes`, used only when an older published updater drives) keeps its current check. Its refusal belongs to a contract with shipped updaters.

Update behavior for published updaters: this changes the updater's own preflight and capture. An installed updater older than this change keeps its refusal until the first update after this lands has replaced it. The candidate side needs nothing. All install kinds share this code. Package and Git checkout updates get the skip-and-continue rule. Git release takes no image and runs no check.

Steps left to a person: none. Freeing space is optional: it only lets a later update keep its image. When the migration itself has no room, the refusal says how much to free; that is a migration that would fail, not a snapshot. The agent route `openclaw triage` covers it.

## Evidence

**End-to-end, real disk, nothing mocked:** a real 70 GiB APFS disk image (`hdiutil` sparse image) holds a state directory whose shared database reports 40 GiB, as a valid sparse SQLite file whose header page count wins, plus an agent database. The real `assessInitialUpdateSnapshotCapacity` ran from each checkout against it:
- **RED, base `999e873a916`:** `exitCode: 1 (update refused)`, "Update database backup needs 200 GiB … only 70 GiB is available".
- **GREEN, head `a23f19641d1`:** `exitCode: 0 (update continues)`. Warning: "No pre-migration database image: it needs 80 GiB … and 70 GiB is free. Without it, the previous version cannot be restored once the new version's database migration commits; a failed update then stays on the new version and is fixed forward." Migration room: 40 GiB needed, 70 GiB free.
- Free disk demanded: 200 GiB before. After: 40 GiB to proceed, 80 GiB to also keep the image. Preflight time: 3 ms vs 4 ms.

Recordings (playable MP4):
- RED: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61ec1190-a822-4730-acd2-fb00ae54cf44
- GREEN: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a9b7d0da-9188-4433-8b04-92bdeaaa03b9

Earlier recordings on superseded heads are in the PR comments. Full raw logs are not attached because the artifact store rejected uploads from this machine.

<details><summary>Raw terminal output (paths redacted)</summary>

```text
== RED: openclaw 999e873a916
free near backup dir: 70 GiB
exitCode: 1 (update refused) in 3 ms
stderr: Update refused: Update database backup needs 200 GiB (214815490048 bytes) near /volume/install, but only 70 GiB (74830626816 bytes) is available. Free disk space before retrying; the databases have not been migrated.

== GREEN: openclaw a23f19641d1
free near backup dir: 70 GiB
exitCode: 0 (update continues) in 4 ms
warning: No pre-migration database image: it needs 80 GiB near /volume/install and 70 GiB is free. Without it, the previous version cannot be restored once the new version's database migration commits; a failed update then stays on the new version and is fixed forward. The update continues and measures the image again before the migration.
diagnostic: Database migration room near /volume/state/state: 40 GiB (43016781824 bytes) needed; 70 GiB (74830626816 bytes) free.
diagnostic: Pre-migration database image near /volume/install: 80 GiB (85966462976 bytes) needed; 70 GiB (74830626816 bytes) free.
```

</details>

**Through `updateCommand`** (`update-command-package-space.test.ts`, the real command with the fixture's staging stub). Free space is faked only at the owner's seam, `tryReadDiskSpace`.
- A 16 MiB agent with 90 MiB free near the package:
  - **RED on base:** the update refused with `snapshot-capacity-insufficient` before staging (this was the file's previous test).
  - **GREEN:** the update reaches staging, and the exact skip warning is printed.
- With 50 MiB on the state volume, it still refuses before staging, with the exact message including "Free at least 30 MiB (… bytes)".
- Retirable recovery copies are named as advice and nothing is removed.

**Capture** (`update-command-database-retention.test.ts`): the owner's measured shortfall skips the image, removes its empty directory, and records exit code 0 with the exact warning. The update still fails for an integrity failure, for a disk that filled mid-copy, and for a shortfall joined by a cleanup failure. RED on the previous head `c82e86eeba9`: the last two were skipped. GREEN now.

**Git release** (`update-command-git-snapshot.test.ts`): `updateGitInstall` hands the runner a staging space check only outside release mode, and running that check reads the snapshot source. RED with base `update-command-git.ts`: a check was handed in release mode. GREEN now.

**Space owner** (`update-database-backup-space.test.ts`), with a sparse 20 GiB shared database:
- 35 GiB free → continue with the warning (the old formula wanted 100 GiB).
- 10 GiB free → refusal naming how much to free, in bytes too.
- 41 GiB free → the image is kept.
- A real capture with 70 MiB free is refused before any checkpoint or copy, with the sources unchanged; at 80 MiB it captures both families intact.
- The sparse cases are skipped on Windows, where truncation writes zeros.

<details><summary>Checks run on the exact head</summary>

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on the eight touched test files: 106 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`: passed.
- oxlint on the touched files: passed.
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets`: all ok.
- `pnpm check:docs`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `origin/main` was merged in; the core typecheck was rerun after the merge.

</details>

<details><summary>Review rounds and what changed</summary>

**Independent reviewer** (fresh read-only subagent):
- Migration room is not rechecked at activation: kept as a stated limit, with the warning wording corrected.
- Git release cleanup offer: fixed for installs already serving from a release.
- Deleting a directory this run did not create: no longer reachable. The capture creates `<root>.databases` exclusively (`mkdir` without `recursive`), and only the owner's measured shortfall, raised before any copy, is skipped.
- Other backup owners still refuse: scoped above.
- Test quality: Windows sparse skip, a baseline assertion in `unchanged`, and a Git release test added.

**ClawSweeper round 1** (head `c82e86eeba9`): overall F, proof F, patch D. Findings:
1. Skipping on a text match for ENOSPC could turn unrelated or cleanup failures into a skip. **Real; fixed:** only the typed owner shortfall, with no aggregate in the chain.
2. A mid-copy ENOSPC could delete manifests of completed PostgreSQL captures. **Real; fixed** by (1): a mid-copy failure now fails the update and keeps everything.
3. The budget summed staging and migration room. **Real; fixed:** it uses the peak.
4. The migration estimate counts databases the target will not migrate. **Kept and documented:** it is strictly smaller than the old refusal, the owner asked for a truthful migration-room refusal, and target schemas are not known at this point.
5. The cleanup offer is inferred from the path. Partly fixed (an install serving from a release); the remaining case is documented.
6. "Free at least 0 MiB": fixed, with bytes added.
7. Docs: corrected for the peak and for the narrower skip.
- **Product decision:** the owner approved skip-and-continue (option D, items 4, 8 and 9) in this task.
- **Real-proof gap:** a full installed-package update on a full disk was not run; stated below.

</details>

Test files audited in full:
- `update-database-backup-space.test.ts` (rewritten).
- `update-command-package-space.test.ts`: the two refusal tests were replaced, because refusing for image space is the removed behavior; the migration-room refusal is kept.
- `update-snapshot-space-cleanup.test.ts`: the assess shape changed, and a skip case was added.
- `update-command-git-snapshot.test.ts`: refusal wording, and a release test added.
- `update-command-database-retention.test.ts`: skip and still-fails cases added.
- `update-candidate-rehearsal.resources.test.ts`: the preflight case now asserts skip, not refuse.
- `update-command-git-timeout.test.ts`: the mock shape.
- `update-database-backup.test.ts`: the case "preflights a separate source volume" asserted that capture reserved restore output, which is removed on purpose. It now asserts that capture succeeds on a tight or unknown source volume without a warning, and that the snapshots are intact.

Why the removals are safe: each removed assertion checked the refusal this change removes, and its replacement checks the new outcome at the same seam.

Not proven:
- A full `openclaw update` of an installed package across a schema change on a full disk, end to end. The capture skip is proven at `captureUpdateDatabases`, with the backup owner stubbed at its boundary; the real owner's shortfall before any copy is proven in `update-database-backup-space.test.ts`.
- PostgreSQL families.
- `autoreview` does not run on this machine; an independent reviewer subagent was used instead.

prs.title: fix(read): accept optional false without schema rejection
prs.body:
Closes #189440

## What Problem This Solves

The read input schema accepts only literal true for optional. A model that sends optional false gets a validation error before reading an existing file, adding a retry and model round trip.

## User Impact

Explicitly required reads work on existing files. Missing required files still produce errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

Widen the existing optional field to boolean. Execution already suppresses missing-file errors only for true. Update the Code Mode and Gemini advertised-schema expectations with the same contract.

## Evidence

The existing contributor capture at head `9b7d6de6a0ee4b65ec838d1c08f8e0e8b4b1ed37` runs a native Linux Gateway with Node 24.22.1 and a loopback OpenAI-compatible SSE provider fixture.

The public `chat.send` entry point receives a model-generated `read` call with `optional: false`. The shipped read tool returns the existing file contents, then the agent completes. A second turn accepts the same flag and returns a file-not-found tool error for a missing required path.

```text
present.txt + optional false
  toolResult.isError = false
  toolResult.content = hello-from-proof
  final answer = FILE_CONTENTS_OK

missing-required.txt + optional false
  toolResult.isError = true
  toolResult.error = File not found
  final answer = MISSING_HANDLED

same input through TypeBox Value.Check
  base Literal(true) accepts optional false = false
  head Boolean accepts optional false = true
```

The full redacted Gateway transcript and focused regression output are inspectable in the existing evidence comment. This description consolidates that capture and does not represent a new run.

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192113#issuecomment-6620334332

The latest ClawSweeper review of this head accepts the shipped-entry-point proof and reports no findings. The head's `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency review, and security-sensitive review statuses are successful as checked on November 5.

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192113#issuecomment-6610761086

### Evidence boundary

The provider and credentials were synthetic. The Gateway, argument validation, read implementation, tool result, and agent turn used the production path.

prs.title: fix: let read accept optional: false as a required read
prs.body:
Root cause: `src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-schemas.ts:95` publishes `read.optional` as literal `true`, and the OpenClaw read wrapper (`src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts:712`, `createOpenClawReadTool`, which owns how `optional` is interpreted) prepares no arguments, so agent-core validates the model's `optional: false` unchanged and `packages/llm-core/src/validation.ts:416` rejects the call with `optional: must be equal to constant` before the read runs.

Fixes #189440.

Thanks @Pkieffaber-dotcom for the report with session counts and the exact received arguments, @wr-web for this PR, and @moonbow0407 for #192113, which fixed the same bug. @wr-web's commits are kept as they are; the fix commit on top replaces the schema change.

## What Problem This Solves

Some models send `"optional": false` on `read` to mean "this file is required". OpenClaw rejected that call with `optional: must be equal to constant` before reading anything, so the model had to spend another turn retrying without the flag. The reporter saw it on 13 of 38 cron runs with `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`.

## User Impact

`read` with `optional: false` now reads the file on the first try. A missing file with `optional: false` is still an error, and `optional: true` on a missing file still returns the structured "Optional file not found" result.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `createOpenClawReadTool` now sets `prepareArguments` to `prepareReadToolParams` (in `agent-tools.params.ts`), which drops `optional: false` before validation, so it means the same as leaving the flag out. It is typed `unknown -> unknown` like the cron and computer preparers; no type assertions. Agent-core runs it before argument validation.
- The canonical daily-memory path check moves next to it in `agent-tools.params.ts` unchanged, so both rules about `optional` live together and `agent-tools.read.ts` does not grow past its line cap.
- The input schema stays `optional: true` only. The tool definition the model sees is byte-identical to `main`, so prompt caches are not invalidated. @wr-web's first commit widened the schema to `boolean`; that changed the published definition, so it is reverted here.
- Accepted edge: a canonical daily-memory journal path (`memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`) is already read as optional when the flag is absent. With `optional: false` on a missing journal the model now gets the same "Optional file not found" result as with no flag, not an error.
- Merged current `main` (`src/agents/code-mode.test.ts` was deleted on `main`, so this PR's change to it is gone).

Line deltas against the merge base: production +21/-4 (`agent-tools.params.ts` +17, `agent-tools.read.ts` +4/-4), tests +25/-1 (one regression in `agent-tools.schema.test.ts`).

## Evidence

Real Gateway from source (`ocx src`: `gateway run`, then `openclaw agent` through the Gateway), isolated profile and state, and a scripted OpenAI-compatible model with a fixture key. In each turn the model calls `read` once; the result is the tool output the model got back in the next request.

| `read` call from the model | main `96189709bc50` | this branch `ada2a82357f1` |
|---|---|---|
| existing `SKILL.md`, `optional: false` (reporter's argument shape) | `Validation failed for tool "read": - optional: must be equal to constant` | the file content |
| missing file, `optional: true` | `Optional file not found: missing.md.` | same |
| missing file, `optional: false` | validation error | `File not found: .../missing.md.` (required read fails) |
| `read.optional` schema sent to the model | `{"type":"boolean","const":true,...}` | same |

Observed proof lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189494#issuecomment-6998463471 (reruns on later heads below it)

Tests: `agent-tools.schema.test.ts` "runs read optional: false through the agent loop as a required read" runs the wrapped read tool through `runAgentLoop`: an existing file reads, a missing one fails as required. It fails on `main` with `optional: must be equal to constant` and passes here. `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`, `agent-tools.workspace-outside.test.ts` (daily-memory rule) and `sessions/tools/read.test.ts` pass.

Not covered: no run against `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` on OpenRouter; why that model started sending the flag after 2026.10.7 is not investigated.

Merge danger: two-way door. The change only rewrites one tool argument before validation and writes no state, so a revert fully undoes it. Blast radius: `read` calls that send `optional: false`, which failed before and now run as required reads.

prs.title: fix(google): Gemini 4 Hydrogen refuses xhigh thinking or sends it as HIGH
prs.body:
Closes #198001

## What Problem This Solves

Gemini 4 Hydrogen can't use Google's deepest thinking level: `--thinking xhigh` is refused, and `xhigh` set in config is sent as `HIGH`, although Google accepts `XHIGH` for this model.

## User Impact

A Gemini model row that maps `thinkingLevelMap: { xhigh: "xhigh" }` now offers `xhigh` and sends `thinkingLevel: XHIGH` (Interactions: `thinking_level: "xhigh"`). Rows without that entry are unchanged, so Gemini 4 Carbon, which rejects `XHIGH` with HTTP 400, keeps sending `HIGH`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generic thinking layer already reads a row's `thinkingLevelMap.xhigh` as support, but the Google profile never offered `xhigh`, the transport had no `XHIGH` value, and both Google payload wrappers rewrote `xhigh` to `HIGH`. Each now honors the row's opt-in, so the level menu, validation and the request agree.

The bundled Hydrogen catalog row is left as is: released installs read that row from the hosted catalog and would offer `xhigh` while still sending `HIGH`. Its `xhigh: "xhigh"` entry can follow once a release sends `XHIGH`.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5: change details</summary>

- `googleSupportsXHighThinking(model)` (`packages/ai/src/transports/google-thinking-level.ts`): true when `thinkingLevelMap.xhigh === "xhigh"`.
- Transport (`google-shared.ts`): `getGoogleThinkingLevel` returns `XHIGH` for `xhigh` (and `max`, which clamps to it) on an opted-in Gemini 3/4 thinking-level row. Gemma 4 and Gemini 2.5 rows that carry the entry keep `HIGH` and the high budget.
- Payload wrappers: `sanitizeGoogleThinkingPayload` takes the row's map; the Google provider `wrapStreamFn` and the embedded runner's `createGoogleThinkingPayloadWrapper` both pass it. The deprecated `resolveGoogleGemini3ThinkingLevel` keeps its signature (Gemini Live indexes the SDK enum with it).
- Profile: `resolveGoogleThinkingProfile` appends `xhigh` for an opted-in Gemini 3/4 row.
- Tests (red on the base, green here): `extensions/google/thinking.test.ts`, `provider-hooks.test.ts`, `provider-policy-api.test.ts`, and `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner-extraparams-google.test.ts`.

</details>

## Evidence

**Live, before and after:** throwaway Gateways on 2026.11.3 and on this branch, with a real Vertex key and a `google-vertex` row as a Vertex user writes it (`gemini-4-hydrogen` with `thinkingLevelMap: { minimal: null, xhigh: "xhigh" }`, `gemini-4-carbon` with `{ minimal: null }` as the control). Each turn sends the same short reasoning question with `openclaw agent --model <ref>`. Google bills thinking as output, so output tokens show how hard the model thought; every completed turn gave the same correct answer.

| Vertex row, output tokens | `--thinking high` | `--thinking xhigh` | `params.thinking: "xhigh"` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hydrogen, 2026.11.3 | 1,540 | refused: `"xhigh" is not supported` | 999 |
| Hydrogen, this PR | 608 | 5,250 | 4,900 |
| Carbon, 2026.11.3 | 4,302 | refused | 4,268 |
| Carbon, this PR | 3,793 | refused | 4,009 |

Tested on 90cfb370a0c, then rebased onto main for #198763, which edits the same Gemini 3.1 Pro lines; the merge keeps both changes, and the Hydrogen and Carbon paths above don't touch them. Rebased head 89f0afb2ebd: the checks below pass again.

- Request bodies, against a local stub that records them: 2026.11.1 sends `"HIGH"` for `xhigh` from config; this branch sends `"XHIGH"` on `google-vertex` and `google-generative-ai`, `"xhigh"` on `google-interactions`, and `"HIGH"` for Carbon. Google's side: a direct Vertex call with `XHIGH` returns 200 for Hydrogen and 400 for Carbon (#198001).
- Checks: the focused tests above plus `extensions/google/index.test.ts` and `transport-stream.test.ts` pass on 89f0afb2ebd (251), lint is clean, `pnpm tsgo:core` and the Google plugin typecheck pass; `pnpm check:changed` passed on the previous head (this commit only edits tests, docs and the manifest) except two lanes that fail the same way on the base (Plugin SDK surface budget, dead export scan).
- Gap: the real-model turns show the effect, not the request bytes; those come from the stub run and the unit tests.

prs.title: fix(onboard): reject token auth under Tailscale Funnel with accurate guidance
prs.body:
Closes #201385

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --tailscale funnel` tells users to "use --gateway-auth token", but Funnel always forces password auth, so following that advice reproduces the same failure. An explicit `--gateway-auth token` is silently replaced by password auth.

## User Impact

The error now names the real requirement: Funnel needs a password. It points at `--gateway-password` or `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD`, never at token auth. An explicit `--gateway-auth token` with `--tailscale funnel` is rejected with that reason instead of being silently overridden.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reject `--gateway-auth token` under Funnel the same way `trusted-proxy` is already rejected, instead of overwriting it.
- Make the missing-password error Funnel-aware so it stops recommending the path Funnel has already disabled.
- Keep the existing normalization for a token-only rerun that targets an already-password Funnel.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/gateway-config.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 30/30 passed.
- Red-on-base: reverting only `gateway-config.ts` makes both new cases fail; the existing token-only rerun case still passes.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint clean on both changed files.

- Shipped CLI proof (real `openclaw onboard --non-interactive`, isolated profile, no daemon):
  - **Before** (upstream source): `--tailscale funnel` exits 1 with `Missing --gateway-password for password auth. Pass --gateway-password or use --gateway-auth token.`; adding `--gateway-auth token` exits 1 with the same message.
  - **After** (this head): `--tailscale funnel` exits 1 with `Tailscale Funnel requires password auth. Pass --gateway-password or set OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD.`; `--tailscale funnel --gateway-auth token` exits 1 with `Tailscale Funnel requires password auth and cannot use "--gateway-auth token". …`.
  - **After**, `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD` set: onboarding succeeds and writes `{"mode":"password"}` with `tailscale.mode=funnel`.

- Latest-stable upgrade proof (state and config created by `openclaw@2026.11.5`):
  - `2026.11.5` wrote `gateway.auth={"mode":"password"}` with `gateway.tailscale={"mode":"funnel"}`.
  - This head, run as an ordinary Funnel rerun over that config with `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD` set, exited 0 and kept `{"mode":"password"}` + `funnel`.
  - The same rerun with `--gateway-auth token --gateway-token …` exited 1 with the actionable `cannot use "--gateway-auth token"` rejection.

prs.title: fix(browser): avoid background screenshot stalls after Playwright connects
prs.body:
Related: #165312 (P1), specifically the [headless background-tab reproduction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165312#issuecomment-6014153598).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a missing activation step that can stall background-tab screenshots after a headless browser switches from raw CDP capture to Playwright.

## User Impact

User impact: headless background tabs receive the same pre-capture activation in both screenshot backends, including element and labeled captures. Known headed browsers keep their existing focus behavior. This draft does not establish a fix for the original intermittent headed/Xvfb hang or recover a capture that is already stuck.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Playwright capture path now follows the existing raw-CDP rule using the running browser's observed launch mode. Screenshot media helpers move intact into a sibling module to keep the route within its line budget. Existing capture deadlines, emulation restoration, and queue ownership remain in place.

The focus-sensitive risk is activating a headed browser by mistake; added mode coverage checks that an observed headed launch overrides a conflicting profile configuration for both backends.

## Evidence

### Local Gateway and Chromium

Built main `02078202f31` and the same base with this PR's full patch applied. Both runs used the real Gateway, Browser CLI, and managed Chrome for Testing 154.0.8037.92 on Linux with Node 24.22.1. The Browser plugin files in the candidate match those in GitHub's merge ref `29675fb80a6a`.

1. Open two local HTML pages with distinct background colors. Take a normal screenshot of A, open B, run `openclaw browser snapshot --target-id "$a"` to establish the Playwright connection, then run `openclaw browser focus "$b"`.
2. On main, `openclaw browser screenshot "$a"` exited 1 with `Screenshot via Playwright timed out after 20000ms`. Repeating it reported that the cancelled capture was still running.
3. With the patch, the same screenshot and retry each exited 0 in about three seconds and saved 780×437 PNGs. With B brought forward before each request, element capture, `screenshot --labels`, and `snapshot --labels` also saved PNGs. FFmpeg pixel readback confirmed A's background color, and both labeled outputs reported two annotations.
4. With the patch and a visible Chrome window under Xvfb, taking a background screenshot kept B selected, as shown by the X11 window title. The headed capture still timed out and its retry reported a pending capture. The PR remains a draft while that behavior is open.

The standalone Chromium route fixture also passed against the unmodified production source. The real Gateway sequence above supplied the failing/passing headless reproduction. Local Codex autoreview of the current-main patch returned `scoped-clean` at P0.

### Earlier validation

Source inspection against `bfcaa1b2cd1cf2f0e7d617b773e4743218eb219c` found activation in `captureScreenshot` but none in the shared Playwright screenshot owner. Both screenshot routes and snapshot-label capture now carry the same launch-mode fact. The pinned [Playwright Chromium implementation](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/v1.64.1/packages/playwright-core/src/server/chromium/crPage.ts) implements `bringToFront` with `Page.bringToFront`; its screenshot path does not perform that activation.

Added regression coverage for true/false/unknown launch modes, launch-mode propagation to both backends, and a real Chromium route sequence that backgrounds an already captured tab and requests ordinary, labeled, and snapshot-label images. Existing interruption tests continue to target capture/restoration ownership.

Validation actually completed: `git diff --cached --check` passed; an independent read-only source review found and corrected the new regression's `path` versus `imagePath` handling. No additional concrete P0–P2 finding remained in that review. Production delta is +18 lines after accounting for the helper move; tests/test support are +51 lines.

[Remote Chromium regression](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/actions/runs/40626440967) passed the background-tab route test on a temporary child of head `160ab685fbad35d3e60612d469d85a98c65f4619` (1 passed, 15 skipped; test body 1.085 s). This uses real headless Chromium and production route handlers with a test route context.

[Remote base comparison](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/actions/runs/40627216743) ran the same candidate test with the two production screenshot paths restored to the PR parent. The test passed both before and after, so it did not reproduce the reported stall or establish a behavioral before/after fix.

Hosted CI for the ready-for-review PR remains pending.

prs.title: fix(feishu): unset groupPolicy admits unlisted groups
prs.body:
Closes #152605

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a configured Feishu bot answers every group it has been added to, and allows group reads outside `groupAllowFrom`, when `groupPolicy` is left unset.

## User Impact

User impact: unset Feishu `groupPolicy` now matches the documented allowlist default. Unlisted groups are dropped; allowlisted groups require an @-mention unless `requireMention` is set. Group reads of a non-current, unlisted chat are denied.

Operators who relied on the undocumented open fallback need `channels.feishu.groupPolicy: "open"` explicitly. `channels.defaults.groupPolicy` and explicit Feishu policies are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu declares `groupPolicy` default `allowlist`, but the exported input-mode schema never materializes that value. The inbound handler and read-action gate then used the open-provider resolver, which maps configured-provider plus unset key to `open`.

Both call sites now use `resolveAllowlistProviderRuntimeGroupPolicy`, the resolver the Feishu security-audit collector already uses. Explicit policies and the missing-provider fail-closed path are unchanged.

## Evidence

Old red (unfixed resolvers, same commands):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/read-policy.test.ts -t "fails closed to allowlist for group reads when groupPolicy is unset"
```

Failed: `expected [Function] to throw an error` — `oc_unlisted` was allowed.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts -t "drops unlisted group messages when groupPolicy is unset"
```

Failed: inbound log was `received message ... in oc-group` instead of `not in groupAllowFrom (groupPolicy=allowlist)`.

New green (this head): the same two commands passed. Mention-gated allowlisted groups also pass.

Owner files:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/read-policy.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts
```

125 passed. `oxfmt --check` on the four changed files was clean. `git diff --check` was clean.

What was not tested: no live Feishu tenant or WebSocket stream; no agent turn.

prs.title: fix(browser): stop page text reads from returning another page's text after a navigation
prs.body:
Root cause: `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.activity.ts:46` (main c5f6eed452) returns `locator.innerText(...)` without checking that the tab still shows the document the read started on; Playwright locators wait for their selector and re-resolve after a navigation, so a read that overlaps a navigation or reload finishes on the next page.

Fixes #196658

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent reads page text and the tab navigates or reloads while the read is waiting (a meta refresh, a redirect, a script calling `location.assign`), the browser tool returns the new page's text as the answer for the page the agent asked about. The model only sees the text, so it acts on content from a different page.

## User Impact

User impact: a page text read that overlaps a navigation now fails with the existing browser error `Frame changed while its browser snapshot was being captured; retry.` instead of returning another page's text. Reading again returns the current page with its real URL. Reads on pages that stay put, including pages that fill in their content in place, are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The text reader now runs inside the frame guard that snapshots already use: it watches the main frame for a navigation or detach while the read runs and rejects the result if one happened. This replaces the earlier version of this PR, which read the CDP frame tree twice per read, added a new error message and bound the read to the route's tab URL; the guard needs no extra CDP sessions and no route change.

Accepted limits: same-document URL changes during a read (`pushState`, hash changes) also reject, as they do for snapshots; child-frame navigations are not watched; a navigation that commits after the text is read but before the route looks up the tab URL can still pair the text with the newer URL in the response details.

Thanks @martins-oss for the report, the diagnosis and the original fix.

## Evidence

Real Gateway (built `dist/`), managed headless Chromium, a local page that meta-refreshes from `/a` to `/b` 1.5 s after loading; each read is `browser.request GET /text` with `selector: "#total"` on the `/a` tab. On `main` the read returns page B's text; on this head it returns the existing retry error, the next read on the same tab returns page B with URL `/b`, and stable and in-place-update pages read unchanged. prs.title: fix: keep ChatGPT model discovery independent of npm
prs.body:
Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/201480

## What Problem This Solves

ChatGPT model discovery depends on npm to choose the client version it reports. When that lookup fails, discovery reports the bundled Codex version, which can hide models requiring a newer client; cache misses also add an unnecessary registry request.

## User Impact

User impact: ChatGPT model discovery no longer depends on npm availability or the installed Codex version. No configuration changes are needed.

Discovery can list a model that an older native Codex binary cannot run. The existing update instructions remain unchanged; this does not update Codex or change its binary selection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the same OpenClaw version source as Responses requests. Accept calendar versions with a four-digit year from 2026 onward, preserving versioned prereleases and build metadata; use 99.0.0 when unavailable or invalid. Responses headers themselves are unchanged.

Remove the npm fetch, six-hour version cache, bundled-version floor, obsolete mocks and fixture routes, and superseded pin-equality test. Update the affected docs and test registration together.

## Evidence

- Before/after: the final discovery regression fails on unchanged main and passes with the fix. The 2027 case also failed with the earlier year-locked patch and passes now. Cases cover stable/prerelease/build versions, placeholders, Codex-style versions, the lower year bound, and the four-digit upper bound.
- Fresh focused run: **149 tests passed across 9 files**, covering subscription and API-key catalogs, account isolation/access programs, endpoint routing, Responses attribution, and prompt stability. Wall time: 35.2 seconds; hosted CI time is not yet available.

prs.title: feat(mcp-events): accept a callback base URL with a path prefix
prs.body:
Closes #184684

## What Problem This Solves

MCP Events can't receive callbacks through a reverse proxy or webhook relay that gives the Gateway a path instead of its own hostname, because `callbackOrigin` rejects any URL with a path.

## User Impact

User impact: operators set `callbackBaseUrl` to an HTTPS URL that can include a path prefix, such as `https://proxy.example.com/openclaw`, and callbacks go to `<callbackBaseUrl>/plugins/mcp-events/callback/<binding>`.

`callbackBaseUrl` replaces `callbackOrigin`. A config that still has `callbackOrigin` fails validation with the next step, `openclaw doctor --fix`, which also runs during `openclaw update`. Doctor moves the value as it is, so the callback URL doesn't change and existing subscriptions are kept.

## Why This Change Was Made

The proxy removes the prefix and forwards `/plugins/mcp-events/callback/<binding>`, which the existing route already serves, so only the URL OpenClaw gives the MCP server changes. Voice Call's `publicUrl` already works this way: a full public URL with a path that a reverse proxy maps to a local route.

I also considered carrying callbacks over MCP Relay, so a local Gateway would need no proxy at all. I left it out: the relay's ingress currently refuses webhooks, and MCP Events would then depend on a second plugin.

`callbackOrigin` shipped in stable releases (2026.10.10, 2026.11.2 and 2026.11.3), so the rename ships a Doctor migration, following the existing plugin config renames. Doctor only moves values the old setting accepted. A `callbackOrigin` with a path fails at startup today; moved as a base URL it would start and send callbacks to the wrong path. Doctor removes such a value instead, without echoing it (it can hold credentials; the config backup keeps it), and asks for `callbackBaseUrl`. A disabled entry is then valid, and Doctor's existing quarantine for invalid plugin configs disables an enabled one, so `openclaw update` still proceeds.

The tests add 141 lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/mcp-events-callback-base-url.txt`. The config surface doesn't grow.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `pnpm test:extension mcp-events` (17 passed) and the new config and Doctor tests (17 passed in 0.8 s). The Doctor contract closure guard passes. Cases are listed below.
- Red/green: with the resolver from `main`, all 13 new config tests fail; with this change they pass.
- Docs: `pnpm docs:check-config-examples`, `docs:check-mdx` and `docs:check-links` pass (0 broken links), and `git diff --check` is clean.
- `pnpm check:changed`: everything this change touches passes, including type checks, lint, format, the config baseline, the Doctor contract guards and the test-line ratchet. Three checks fail locally for reasons outside this change; details below.
- Live run on macOS with an isolated Gateway (own home, state and profile, loopback port 18871):
  - `callbackBaseUrl` set to a hosted webhook relay URL that addresses receivers by path and forwards to localhost. The Gateway subscribed to a real MCP Events server, a signed test event reached its callback, and the automation started.
  - A config with only `callbackOrigin` stopped the Gateway with the Doctor hint. `openclaw doctor --fix` moved it to `callbackBaseUrl` with a backup, and `openclaw config validate` then passed.
  - An invalid `callbackOrigin` containing credentials, with the entry disabled and then enabled: `openclaw doctor --fix` removed it without printing it, quarantined the enabled entry, and `openclaw config validate` passed both times.
- Upgrade from 2026.11.3, installed from npm, with a live subscription, on macOS with an isolated Gateway. 2026.11.3 accepts only a bare origin and Hookdeck relay URLs carry a path, so this run used a public HTTPS tunnel as `callbackOrigin`. On 2026.11.3 the Gateway subscribed, the MCP server's verification challenge and a signed test event reached the callback (200), and the automation started. On this branch's build, with the same state, the Gateway didn't start until `openclaw doctor --fix` ran. Doctor moved `callbackOrigin` to `callbackBaseUrl` and migrated the state databases, with backups. The Gateway then loaded the subscription 2026.11.3 had saved in plugin state, with the same binding, callback URL, signing secret and remote subscription, sent nothing to the MCP server, and a new signed event reached the callback (200) and started the automation.
- Verification challenge through a path prefix, on this branch's build: `callbackBaseUrl` set to a public HTTPS tunnel URL with an `/openclaw` prefix, in front of a reverse proxy that removes the prefix. The MCP server received the prefixed callback URL, sent its verification challenge to it, and the Gateway answered (200). A signed test event then reached the callback (200) and started the automation, and removing the automation unsubscribed with the same URL.
- Refresh after the upgrade: the same upgrade from 2026.11.3, with the MCP server granting 7-minute subscriptions so a refresh fell due after Doctor. This branch's Gateway refreshed the subscription with the same callback URL, and the MCP server kept the same subscription and moved its expiry forward. The saved binding changed only in its refresh fields and a rotated signing secret. A signed test event after the refresh reached the callback (200) and started the automation.
- TTL expiry after a restart: with the same short grant, removing the automation after a Gateway restart left the subscription on the MCP server (`cleanup_failed`). When the grant ran out, the MCP server expired it and removed its delivery resources, with no manual cleanup. SEP-3415 makes unsubscribe optional for this reason: subscriptions expire when the client stops refreshing.
- Gaps:
  - The isolated profiles had no model, so each automation run was admitted and then failed at the model step.
  - Removing the automation after a Gateway restart doesn't send `events/unsubscribe` (`cleanup_failed`), so the subscription stays on the MCP server until its grant expires, as the TTL run shows. 2026.11.3 alone does the same, so this change doesn't cause it.
  - Local review: the `autoreview` helper isn't installed here, so I ran independent agent reviews and the repo's `pr-simplify` pass instead. They led to the Doctor handling of invalid origins described above and the test-line allocation.

How I tested it, and why: I work at Hookdeck, and I hit this connecting OpenClaw to the [MCP Events bridge](https://github.com/hookdeck/mcp-events-bridge), an open-source MCP server I work on that turns webhooks into MCP events. For a Gateway on a laptop, the bridge gives the client a public relay URL on Hookdeck's Event Gateway (`https://hkdk.events/<id>`) that forwards to a local port. The live run used that setup: the bridge as the MCP server, the relay URL as `callbackBaseUrl`, and the relay forwarding to the Gateway on localhost.

- `pnpm test:extension mcp-events`: 17 passed, including a new case for a path-prefixed base URL across restart and a base URL change.
- `pnpm test extensions/mcp-events/src/config.test.ts extensions/mcp-events/doctor-contract-api.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 17 passed in 0.8 s, covering path prefixes with and without trailing slashes, origin-only URLs, invalid values, and the Doctor migration, including an invalid origin and `callbackBaseUrl` already set.
- `pnpm check:changed` failures outside this change: the SQLite worker ratchet needs `rg`, which this machine doesn't have; changelog attributions flags existing `CHANGELOG/**` entries; and the dead-export scan flags files this PR doesn't touch (`src/daemon/launchd.ts`, `src/plugins/provider-runtime.ts`, `src/plugins/provider-external-auth.ts`, `ui/src/pages/dashboards/dashboard-tools.tsx`).

</details>

prs.title: perf: defer transcript search snippets and retain reader scope
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent `sessions_search` calls spent tens of seconds queued behind slow transcript searches. SQLite eagerly generated snippets for every matching row before sorting, although the visibility cursor consumes only enough candidates to fill the result. Sort candidate metadata first and generate snippets as the cursor advances. Also retain filtered reads in the existing matching worker read scope: bypassing that scope let cleanup discard the connection's ownership and caused worker churn.

The search lane keeps its original two-worker policy, comments, and sizing tests. Making each search cheaper removes the observed fan-out backlog without adding isolates. Search visibility, ordering, results, and timeouts keep their existing contracts; recall filtering is unchanged.

The supplied Team evidence (release a0b14727, November 18–19 UTC) shows six RPCs issued within one second completing in 9.7, 29.7, 31.7, 38.6, 39.4, and 41.3 s; solo calls took 6.7–10.1 s. The host had 128 cores but the search lane had two workers. On every slow line, search time equaled total elapsed time inside `sessions.search`; approximately 90 s maxima were the tool's Gateway timeout. The same runs logged 26 bridge tool errors. Slow-only hourly count / median / maximum were 36 / 46.3 / 90.7 s at 20Z; 72 / 15.5 / 90.0 s at 21Z; 43 / 13.2 / 90.1 s at 22Z; 20 / 8.3 / 21.2 s at 23Z; 25 / 9.4 / 44.0 s at 00Z; and 16 / 31.7 / 50.5 s at partial 01Z.

## Evidence

Synthetic SQLite fixture: 2,000 sessions × 50 messages × approximately 1,000 words, populated FTS, five solo samples and five six-call batches per version on a host with 32 available cores. All versions returned the same result hash. These measurements exercise the real search facade, worker lanes, and native cursor with a synthetic allow-all visibility callback; they do not measure the unchanged recall visibility policy or a live Gateway round trip.

| Measurement | Base, two workers | Fix, two workers |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median solo | 5.269 s | 0.561 s |
| Sorted six-call completion medians | 5.744 / 5.744 / 5.744 / 13.999 / 13.999 / 13.999 s | 0.914 / 0.914 / 1.847 / 1.849 / 2.767 / 2.769 s |
| Full-batch completion range | 13.609–14.595 s | 2.751–3.023 s |
| Maximum lane queue wait | 12.073 s | 2.123 s |
| Peak process RSS, including fixture creation | 1.38 GiB | 1.37 GiB |

The slowest-call median falls from about 14.0 s to 2.8 s. The six-worker ablation with the same SQL and scope fixes had a 0.585 s solo median, six-call completion medians of 6.738 / 6.738 / 6.751 / 6.758 / 6.758 / 6.765 s, a 6.067–7.321 s batch range, and 2.09 GiB peak RSS. Keep two workers: six cost more memory and completed the batch later. These are shared-host observations, not a matched-load throughput guarantee: base host load was 14.7–16.8, fixed two-worker load 6.8–7.2, and six-worker load 12.9–13.5. No compiler checks overlapped the samples. The manual benchmark is removed from the PR; its evidence is retained here.

Phase attribution on the base: native ordered search 2,708 ms; MATCH-only count 2.57 ms; the same ordered query without snippets 646 ms, attributing approximately 2,062 ms of 2.7 s to eager snippets. These counterfactual SQL measurements overlap rather than forming disjoint engine clocks. Synthetic visibility over 26 candidates took 0.004 ms; result serialization 0.041 ms; execution capture 10.9 ms; cold readiness including startup 4,535 ms, versus 0.076 ms warm. The fixed six-worker native query took 744 ms, or 731 ms without snippets.

Writer admission stays unchanged. The execution capture keeps the database execution owner alive; it does not reserve the writer queue. A real synthetic transcript append persisted while a search remained held at its visibility exchange, before releasing the search (9.65 ms in the two-worker run).

Two deterministic regressions are red on base and green with the fix: consuming four filtered candidates evaluates 160 snippets on base and four after the fix; alias cleanup fails to revoke the escaped filtered reader on base and revokes it after the fix. Neither uses wall-clock thresholds. Test consolidation preserves cold projection-writer reentry and independence from both foreground reader lanes; duplicate assertions and a self-derived result oracle were removed. Net test growth is negative.

Node and Bun each passed all 80 relevant search, worker-lane, and read-scope tests. Targeted format, lint, core/test/script typechecks, the complete `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 895091c987878103a8d76b5de3db004e691fe831`, all 11 baseline ratchets, and `git diff --check` passed. Local Codex autoreview at maximum priority P1 completed scoped-clean with no accepted/actionable findings. Against merge base `895091c987878103a8d76b5de3db004e691fe831`: runtime +21/−5 lines (net +16), tests +76/−77 (net −1), documentation +1; no benchmark or worker-sizing changes. All fixtures are synthetic. No Team server, Gateway, or production state was contacted.

prs.title: fix(agents): agent --local exits silently when the session key has uppercase letters
prs.body:
## Problem

On main, `openclaw agent --local --session-key <key>` exits with code 13 and no output whenever the key contains an uppercase letter (for example a Slack channel id, `agent:main:channel:C3TT2OEIAJ7`). stderr shows only Node's `Warning: Detected unsettled top-level await at openclaw.mjs`. Lowercase keys work. 2026.11.2 and 2026.11.3 are not affected.

Repro on c581fe06 (any provider; fails before the first model request):

```
openclaw agent --local --session-key agent:main:X --message hi --json   # exit 13, empty stdout
openclaw agent --local --session-key agent:main:x --message hi --json   # ok
```

The Gateway is affected too: `POST /v1/responses` with an uppercase `x-openclaw-session-key` (for example `agent:main:channel:C3TT2OEIAJ7`) never returns on c581fe06; the Gateway log shows `reply watchdog: ... action=warn reason=no_semantic_progress`. The `openclaw agent` client through the Gateway is not affected.

## Cause

`agentCommandInternal` claims the session turn with `withSessionTurn` under `prepared.sessionKey`, the key as given. The embedded runner then admits its own turn under the stored key (`prepareEmbeddedRunSession` replaces `sessionKey` with `runSessionTarget.sessionKey`, which is case-folded). `withSessionTurn` inherits the ambient owner only when `owner.aliases.has(sessionKey)`, an exact match, so the runner does not inherit the command's claim. Its target still resolves to the same mailbox through the session-id alias, so it submits a second task behind the claim its own caller holds. Session-controller diagnostics show it:

```
source-claim selected  pendingInputs=1 reason=claim-owned      (command)
lifecycle-admission settled reason=acquired
source-claim waiting   pendingInputs=2 reason=claim-owned      (runner, never selected)
```

Nothing else keeps the event loop alive, so the process exits.

Loosening the alias match is not enough: with that change alone the run fails later with "Native registration does not match the exact admitted session turn", so exact-key identity is relied on downstream.

## Fix

Claim the command's turn under the stored key (`normalizeStoreSessionKey`), the same key the runner uses, so both layers name the same owner.

## Verification

- New test in `agent-command.cancellation.test.ts`: times out without the change, passes with it.
- `agent-command.cancellation`, `agent-command.admission-failure`, `agent-command-local` suites: 36 passed.
- End to end on a build of c581fe06 with the equivalent change applied to the bundle: 40 multi-turn trials launched with `agent --local` and mixed-case keys, 0 failed turns of 110 (56 of 110 failed before), and a second turn on the same key sees the first turn's history.

prs.title: fix(discord): removed DM senders can still message and run commands through an existing session binding
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Discord direct-message sender who has been removed from the allowlist, or who is no longer paired, can still message the agent and run commands when an earlier session binding exists for that conversation.

## User Impact

User impact: removing a sender from the DM allowlist or pairing takes effect for bound conversations too. Rejected senders reach the normal denial or pairing path, and command authorization follows the current access decision. Admitted senders keep their existing binding and routing. No configuration or storage migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

DM preflight treated the existence of a routing binding as an alternative access decision, and also ORed the binding into command authorization. The binding lookup and both overrides are removed from preflight, so admission and command authorization come only from the current ingress result. The existing routing owner still restores bindings for admitted senders. Production code removes 25 lines and adds two.

## Evidence

Run with Node 24.22.2 and pnpm 12.15.0. No live Discord connection was used; ingress decisions and transport are mocked.

- The new regression (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.bound-dm.test.ts`) calls the production `preflightDiscordMessage` entry point with an in-memory binding adapter. On `main` 3 of 4 cases fail (allowlist rejection, pairing rejection, and command authorization for an admitted sender); on this branch all 4 pass.
- A second, separately written test set against the DM preflight access resolver: 11 failed / 14 passed on `main`, 25 passed on this branch.
- DM authorization, pairing-decision, message-preflight and routing-preflight suites: 77 passed.
- Full build and full test typecheck passed. Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap, test-line and mock-export checks passed.

To run the regression:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.bound-dm.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'bound direct messages'
```

Gap: the broad `pnpm check` is not green locally. Extension lint reports line-limit errors in the Tlon and Crabbox tests that reproduce on an untouched `main` with identical counts, and the run was stopped while core lint was still pending, so its later formatting and policy stages did not complete.

### Running Gateway (loopback Discord provider)

The real Discord plugin and Gateway were started from each built checkout through the repository's QA-lab suite runner with the Crabline loopback Discord provider and the mock model provider. No product module is patched or replaced. This is a local provider stand-in, not the Discord service, and the senders are synthetic IDs, not human accounts.

- Base: `b382a29a688a`. Head: `1ff91cc0ded1`. Node 24.22.2, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm build` with private QA enabled.
- Two synthetic DM senders, A and B, each with an existing session binding. Provider-native `MESSAGE_CREATE` DM events are injected through the provider's authenticated local ingress. Policy changes go through the Gateway's `config.patch` RPC with `replacePaths: ["channels.discord.allowFrom"]`. Bindings are left in place throughout and re-read after every step.
- Each step sends one message and one command per sender and records whether it reached agent execution, whether the agent's marker reply came back, and whether the command took effect.

| Phase | Sender | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Both on the allowlist | A | message and command executed | message and command executed |
| 1. Both on the allowlist | B | message and command executed | message and command executed |
| 2. A removed from `allowFrom`, binding retained | A | **message reached the agent and was answered; command executed** | denied: no agent execution, no reply, command not executed |
| 2. A removed from `allowFrom`, binding retained | B | message and command executed | message and command executed |
| 3. `dmPolicy: pairing`, A unpaired, binding retained | A | **message reached the agent and was answered; no pairing request was created** | not delivered to the agent; pairing request issued; command not executed |
| 3. `dmPolicy: pairing`, A unpaired, binding retained | B | not reached (run stopped at A's step) | message and command executed |

On head the scenario completed with all three phases passing. On base it recorded the violations above in phase 2 and stopped in phase 3 because the expected pairing request never appeared.

Limits: provider-native events from a loopback stand-in are not genuine human-to-bot DMs, and native slash interactions were not exercised; commands were sent as message text. No production Discord behaviour is claimed.

prs.title: Keep the selected model when faster service tiers are unavailable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A premium speed limit currently sends Codex directly into model fallback, even when the selected model could serve the request at a lower speed. Keep the selected model and thread while trying Ultrafast, Fast, then regular speed before allowing existing model fallback. Each retry applies only to that turn and preserves the saved preference.

Retry only definite usage-limit or overload rejections and safely settled failures. Do not repeat ambiguous work, visible partial output, tool actions, approvals, or authentication failures. Keep usage accounting across retries, leave older app-servers on the existing behavior, and defer account cooldown until the speed options are exhausted.

## Evidence

Codex already exposes a [turn-only service-tier override](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs#L262), while OpenClaw currently sends tier failures directly to its model fallback machinery. The change uses that existing protocol without altering the persistent thread setting. The release branch also inherits an unrelated CI preflight failure: its workflow does not recognize the repository's current runner backend, so it stops before any tests run.

prs.title: fix(meme-maker): retain long captions in local images
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: locally rendered memes silently omit the end of a caption when it wraps beyond five lines.

## User Impact

SVG and PNG drafts retain the complete caption. Long captions shrink to fit the text box height, with a proportionate outline; very small boxes still mean small text.

## Why This Change Was Made

Let the existing per-box sizing account for every wrapped line, and size the outline with the caption so it cannot overwhelm small letters. No new renderer, dependency, or option is needed.

## Evidence

- Real CLI before/after on Linux with downloaded public template images and an isolated cache: the original exits 0 but drops the final punchline; the fix retains it. Inspected both actual PNG CLI outputs in Chromium 145.0.7632.6 (Playwright 1.58.2).
- Actual SVG CLI + Chromium readback covered Drake, Two Buttons, Change My Mind, and This Is Fine: long captions, short captions, multiple captions and XML characters. Complete text is retained after the fix, with glyph height within the tested boxes. Existing wrapping and width estimation are unchanged.
- `test/scripts/meme-maker.test.ts`: the new regression fails on the base because the caption is incomplete; the fixed focused suite passes (3 tests, 1 opt-in PNG test skipped; 100 ms test time, 396 ms runner time). The opt-in PNG test was then run separately and passed (659 ms test time, 885 ms runner time). Local proof used Vitest 4.1.10 with a focused config; see the exact-head CI result below for repository checks.
- Targeted TypeScript 6.0.3 check, repository-rule Oxlint (258 rules, one test file, zero diagnostics), formatting, `node --check`, and `git diff --check` pass. Tool dependencies were resolved from existing or isolated local installations; no project dependency files changed.

Base: `cdd7ee54ee8df226291bb97a1077731f40fbd273`. ![Before: the final punchline is missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd5621be-6b94-4185-abe8-4a61d4c973d2)

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): store every reply in chat history, not just the final one
prs.body: Closes #195856 Related: #164293, #166511 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: with the `claude-cli` backend, replies sent before the final message vanish after a CLI session rotation, or after a run is killed or fails. ## User Impact User impact: completed user-addressed replies remain in the conversation after a session reset. Text from an interrupted run remains visible, marked "Interrupted". Yielded progress remains progress; scheduled execution prose retains its audit-only policy. ## Why This Change Was Made Previously, only the final reply was durable; earlier replies depended on the currently bound Claude log. This change buffers the latest revision per native UUID and persists it when the next assistant record arrives or the process ends. Writes retain normal preparation hooks and ownership checks. Final settlement deduplicates by native identity and awaits queued writes, including on failure. The change works with commentary streaming enabled or disabled. #164293 covers commentary-enabled persistence; #166511 covers a watchdog interruption slice. Settlement uses a closed assistant-metadata operation: content, identity, timestamps, topology and replay inputs cannot change. It preserves the account-bound history generation and returns the current anchor without relaxing generic rewrite invalidation. Current native login is attested before a snapshot append; foreign or unattested credentials still cannot authorize history coverage. ## Evidence ### Upgrade from latest stable v2026.11.5 to head `7b3e9d23b50` Both builds were made from clean checkouts (buildstamps `e13cf15ece9` = v2026.11.5, and `7b3e9d23b50`). One throwaway Gateway state directory was used, with the `claude-cli` backend, driven through the real Control UI. - **Seeded on v2026.11.5:** a settled six-step narrate-then-tool run (`DONE-A`), then a ~120-word story streamed as visible text with Stop pressed while its `sleep 60` tool was running (tool start observed at 6.70 s, Stop clicked at 6.84 s). The story stayed visible, marked "Interrupted", live and after reload. - **Upgrade:** stopped the Gateway, switched to the candidate build, and ran offline doctor. SQLite `user_version` went from 38 to 42. `quick_check` returned `ok` before and after. A pre-migration backup was written, and its integrity check passes. - **Existing data:** the selected model and settings are the same. All 11 canonical transcript events match before and after the upgrade (field-by-field projection). The same session reopened **before** any new turn showed the old history: `DONE-A` once and the interrupted story once. - **First candidate turn (native replacement):** `REPLACEMENT-OK-196092` settled as a new message. The local session ID is unchanged, and the Claude CLI binding moved to a new native session. The imported reply matches the new binding. After reload, `DONE-A`, both interrupted stories and the new reply each appear exactly once, and two events are appended after the unchanged 11. - **Scope note:** v2026.11.5 never wrote non-final text to canonical storage; it showed it only from the bound Claude log. That covers the narration lines and the pre-tool text of completed runs. Once the first post-upgrade turn replaces the Claude session, that pre-upgrade text is no longer shown. This PR persists such text for runs from this version on; it cannot recover text the old version never stored. This upgrade's replacement came from `cli session reset … reason=mcp`. The resume-hash canonicalization in `bundle-mcp.ts`, which this PR does not change, now normalizes the openclaw server's `alwaysLoad`. As a result, bindings stored while tools were deferred do not match once after upgrading. v2026.11.5, story interrupted by Stop, after reload · after upgrading, same session before a new turn · after the replacement turn, after reload: ### November 18 conflict-repair update — `51bc1056a612` Updated against main `b609d22c129f2944c1abaec1d2895eb659493a36`, preserving the newer transcript-lease and stopped-first-session recovery behavior. - Held replies arriving without snapshot callbacks now use the same native-keyed settlement writer as streamed snapshots. Both paths retain each answer once, including transformed output and a final interim result. The separate recursive interim writer and its identity helper were removed. - Three held-history cases failed after a mechanical merge (one saved answer instead of two), then passed after reconciliation. The existing history matrix now also exercises streamed snapshot deduplication. - Independent review identified three P2 cases: saved commentary trimming an unrelated answer, an unterminated final revision losing to an earlier snapshot, and delivered-failure recovery skipping settlement. Seven regression cases failed before their repairs, including confirmed progress (`final: false`) delivery; matching mirrors are hidden without promoting progress into completed-answer evidence. - Repaired runner/parser/chat-consumer checks: **217 passed, 3 skipped** across 10 files (86.64 s). Final parser/framing/budget/reasoning/persistence checks: **229 passed, 3 skipped** across 8 files (54.67 s). The final progress/final delivery correction passed 90 tests (3 skipped) across history, transcript, and settlement suites (66.49 s). These selections overlap and are not additive totals. - Core and UI typechecks, targeted format/lint, `git diff --check`, and exact-base max-lines/test-lines ratchets passed. The test allocation is 860 lines beyond the ordinary 400-line allowance, covering native identity/settlement and the held-reply/commentary/terminal-revision/delivered-failure regressions. Whole-change net delta against this base: +831 production lines and +1,260 test lines. Stream framing and budget accounting now live together in the existing stream-limits owner, with unchanged limits, keeping the parser within its file-size cap. - **Independent review:** User-authorized, separate read-only source review covered the candidate against the stated base and the subsequent repair deltas. Three P2 findings were reproduced and corrected; the same reviewer confirmed all findings resolved. This was source inspection, not an independent test rerun. Native autoreview was unavailable: its bounded attempt timed out after 180 seconds without a report; no clean autoreview result is claimed. - **Proof limits:** the v2026.11.5 upgrade run above is a live run at head `7b3e9d23b50`. The other live Claude/Control UI evidence below is retained from the stated earlier revisions. Current-head hosted CI must be read separately; no prior-head result is represented as a current-head pass. ### Earlier implementation evidence - Native Claude CLI steering: three accepted steers (A/B/C), with one `DONE: STEER-A, STEER-B, STEER-C` live and after reload. Narration stays between the steers. - Stable upgrade from v2026.11.3: Doctor migrated schema 27 → 42. Old history loaded before the next turn; Claude recalled the seed and produced one settled reply, preserved once after reload. The durable reply has `stopReason: "stop"` and nonzero usage. - Hook visibility: two snapshot-persistence/stranding regressions failed before the fix and passed afterward, covering explicit `display: false` and `display: true`. - Steering and history/stream consumers: 79 tests passed. Saved-prefix replay, whitespace, foreign-run isolation, and idempotent reconciliation are covered. - Chat-entry gzip diagnostic: 132,226 B before and after the state-owner projection change (+0 B). - Pruned redundant saved-stream adapters and unused cached prefix state without changing reconciliation behavior; exact-head [control-ui-performance passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43852886496/job/133250595655). Final live settlement and after reload: ### Prior live-proof head `9bc5ccf5489`: Stop retention, native replacement, single narration Throwaway proof Gateway built at the exact head (buildstamp `9bc5ccf5489`, clean inputs), driven through the real Control UI with the `claude-cli` backend: - **Stop before flush:** a ~120-word story was streamed as visible text, then Stop was pressed while a `sleep 60` tool was pending. The story remains visible exactly once, marked "Interrupted", both live and after a full page reload; no tool card or error banner is left behind. - **Native replacement:** the next turn (`REPLACEMENT-OK-196092`) settles as a new assistant message; the interrupted story is retained exactly once, live and after reload. - **Single narration:** a 6-step narrate-then-tool run showed each `Narration N` line exactly once while streaming; the final accumulated assistant message contains each of the six lines exactly once (192 chars), with no duplicated narration live or after reload. - **Budget:** paired chat boot +222 B vs the merge base, 187 B under the CI cap; `control-ui-performance` and the max-lines ratchet are green at this head. - **CI:** the only red check is `checks-node-changed-compact-large-11-1` — 7 tests in `run.prepared-harness-source-delivery.integration.test.ts` failing with the `run-loop.ts:501 .providerOutcomes` TypeError introduced by main #200073. The identical 7 failures reproduce on the pure merge base `30e9d3ee295` (local attribution run); this PR touches no `embedded-agent-runner` files. Inherited from main, not caused by this change. Stop retention (live, then after reload): Native replacement (live, then after reload): AI-assisted: implementation and validation with Claude and GPT agents. Original PR author: @Marvinthebored. The work-session link below records the November 18 PR update. ## Work sessions Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public. - [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/67a23b12-5823-42b8-9aff-a9c829b2b8d8) ### Round 5 (head `267a360d9d7`): source-reply delivery no longer hides distinct snapshots Addresses the 16 Nov ClawSweeper P2 (`cli-assistant-settlement.ts:146`). When a message tool delivers the source reply, settlement now marks `display:false` only on saved snapshots whose text matches a delivered source-reply body (the dispatch-owned mirror). Distinct earlier snapshots such as `Findings: BLUE-HERON-42` followed by a tool-delivered `Done` keep their prepared visibility. - New regression `keeps distinct snapshots visible when the message tool delivers a different reply`, plus the settlement matrix now asserts per-row visibility (mirrored `Answer` hidden, distinct `Progress` visible). Both fail on `9bc5ccf5489` (2 failed) and pass after the fix. - Acceptance: `cli-run-transcript.test.ts`, `cli-runner.history-ownership.test.ts`, `cli-session-history.segments.test.ts` pass; `tsgo:core`, oxlint/oxfmt, max-lines and test-lines ratchets clean. - Stop, native-replacement and narration paths are unchanged by this commit; the live proof above (exact-head `9bc5ccf5489`) still covers them.

prs.title: feat(agents): hide picker-hidden agents from user-facing pickers
prs.body:
Related: #166678

## What Problem This Solves

Internal worker agents must be configured as full `agents.entries` entries to stay spawnable as `sessions_spawn` targets, so every user-facing agent picker (sidebar roster, agent switcher, New Session target picker) lists agents that are never meant to be chatted with directly. The only way to remove one from the picker today is to delete its entry, which breaks spawning.

## User Impact

Operators can set `agents.entries.<id>.picker.hidden: true` to keep those agents out of chat-facing agent pickers and switchers. Hidden agents remain valid `sessions_spawn` targets and stay listed by `openclaw agents list`, marked `(hidden)`. Administrative and automation surfaces keep them selectable.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the config flag proposed in #166678. The UI distinguishes the two roster predicates: `listSelectableAgents` and `findSelectableAgent` remain the administrative/automation projection (system rows only), while chat-facing surfaces use the new `listChatAgents`/`chatAgentsList` helpers (`kind === "system"` and `hidden` excluded). That fixes the first review's Settings finding: `SettingsAgentSelector` still offers picker-hidden agents for management. Docs state the scope as the Control UI and the TUI `/agents` picker; native apps (macOS, iOS) do not yet consume this flag. The follow-up round (head `e736f2bda`) added TUI picker filtering, dock-Home resolution for hidden selections, and the roster-mode/default-agent doc notes.
