prs.title: fix(pr): reuse dependency caches after device renumbering
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: PR tooling refuses an otherwise unchanged dependency cache after filesystem device numbers change across a remount or restart.

## User Impact

Maintainers can reuse the existing dependency cache without rewriting its ledger or manually adopting new device numbers. There is no user runtime change, schema migration, or required user action. This PR does not activate the tooling, modify the real shared cache, or change the Gateway.

The accepted tradeoff is that a replacement volume mounted at the same physical paths with identical inode, owner, and mode metadata is treated as the same disposable cache. Ambiguous operation leases remain protected rather than collected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Persisted identity comparisons ignore only `st_dev`; current-operation path and descriptor comparisons remain strict. Holds, operation leases, transitions, and explicit release are grouped by physical anchor so mixed historical device rows cannot bypass a live lease or leave settlement incomplete. Existing sealed adoption remains available for older frozen wrappers; ordinary reuse needs no ledger rewrite.

The existing lifetime owner retains responsibility for collection and settlement. No new cache, schema, or recovery owner is introduced. The necessary growth covers persisted-versus-live identity semantics and regression protection for mixed-device rows and live leases. Explicit release also matches current hold membership by path and inode before checking for live consumers, so historical device variants cannot skip that evidence check.

## Evidence

### Initial fix

Validated on base `4092d358a35afd2a8e2f28326175c8b631dd8855` plus initial patch SHA-256 `8cbc8c141a9570613e7483ab94a9a6378d570966f12df6cf2843b5fbb6942564`:

- Production wrapper entry-point regression failed on the base and passed with the fix; the downstream GitHub review body is stubbed, while wrapper admission and dependency materialization remain real.
- Final owner suites: 86 tests passed; targeted wrapper regression: 1 passed; Python retirement suite: 13 passed. Earlier broader validation: 267 tests passed.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, MDX, and test-line budget checks passed on that initial snapshot.
- Fresh managed checkout: verified the base, applied the exact patch, matched the resulting patch hash, and passed `git diff --check`. Existing proof was reused without rerunning broad suites.
- Independent local model review found two mixed-row bugs, which were fixed; the final review, including unique-entry settlement, had no remaining findings. Local ClawSweeper and the prescribed autoreview helper were unavailable: this is **not** a completed official local review, and that review-tool gap remains disclosed.

### Follow-up: live-consumer protection and test-line accounting

Applied exact reviewed repair SHA-256 `1ab5be7f0dab4b404fe4b74267d5d65786d03a7441d837ae0211913854d8f489` to initial published head `7d60567b1edaa7e0b83c15cfb3f6d5a0d8e791bd`; published follow-up head is `14a3b81346eb02ff17dc01b6c424aa0c7d420dd9`.

- Mixed-device cwd and argv live-consumer regressions failed on the original published head and passed with the repair. All 14 release tests passed; an independent rerun of all 6 live-consumer cases passed in 17.82 seconds, including byte-for-byte ledger preservation on blocked release.
- JavaScript syntax, oxfmt, and diff checks passed. Publication checkout independently matched the repair hash and passed JavaScript syntax and diff checks.
- Test-line allocation is now 120: the original 94 plus 26 actual regression lines; 5 obsolete inherited-debt lines were removed. Replaying the identical repair on CI merge tree `ccf5e94d2c4ef50f672354779a5ffa988acc59ea` against `b02e65704473de71d06b4d7ca46ee08f211ff9d7` passed the ratchet: 6,669,120 lines against a 6,669,122 ceiling. The historical unmerged tree still contains 5 inherited over-budget lines; it is not reported as a passing CI-merge-tree check.
- Fresh independent review found no actionable findings; this was not official ClawSweeper/autoreview. Follow-up typecheck was blocked by the physical-checkout/shared-symlink rule. Pinned oxlint 1.89 was unavailable (installed: 1.88); no upgrade or substitute lint run was used. These remain validation gaps, not passing checks.

Testing used isolated fixtures; neither the real cache nor the running Gateway was touched. No real ledger, HOME, or shared dependency installation was modified. Publication only; no merge or activation is requested.

prs.title: improve: reduce CPU work when refreshing session lists
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large session rosters spend avoidable CPU comparing accepted metadata twice and walking already-frozen row fields again during publication.

## User Impact

Session list and event refreshes do less main-thread work. Row contents, sharing, lineage, archive behavior, and change notifications stay the same. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lineage owner already compares fresh snapshots and retains the accepted entry identity. Its projection changes only `parentSessionKey` and `spawnedBy`, so acquisition can consume that identity and compare the two original keys instead of comparing the entire stored entry again. The fresh-snapshot comparison remains necessary for same-timestamp metadata changes and deferred archives.

The existing nested-field reuse pass now freezes new fields and the row shell together. Fields retained from the previous immutable publication need no further freeze traversal. Fact replacement freezes only newly supplied child links. There is no new cache; production code shrinks by one line.

## Evidence

The acquisition regression fails on the base with two full comparisons of one fresh snapshot and passes with one. Differential replay over 700 rows in both per-sender and global scopes produced identical rows, change decisions, and dependent-row invalidations for 14,000 transitions: equal rereads, same-timestamp edits, re-parenting, archive/unarchive, deferred archive acquisition, and compaction successors. Existing focused tests cover the real database/publication owners as well as nested identities, immutable fields, and JSON property order.

61 focused tests passed (9 files; 93.75 s Vitest wall time), plus 4 browser tests and 7 UI E2E tests against a fresh production UI build. The updated mutation assertion passed its final 4-test file rerun. Codex autoreview of the local change against base `0321f852d91a0bd9c6448ecab353f3a96227933e` found no actionable P0–P2 findings. `pnpm check:changed` passes on the final candidate; the first run caught test typing and benchmark lint issues, which were repaired. Exact-head CI is pending.

<details>
<summary>Performance workload and acceptance</summary>

Before measurement: require identical row bytes and change decisions, lower CPU/allocation in the affected work, and no 20% median/p95 regression. Run serially, two warmup passes, A/A controls, five alternating A/B pairs, with collected-object-inclusive allocation and CPU profiles in separate processes. Node 26.12.1; synthetic data only.

Reproduce with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-row-lineage-measure.ts --sessions 700 --passes 30 --reads 20 --materialize`. Save the four measured `src/gateway` owners from the base under a separate directory and use `--base-dir <directory>`. Add `--allocation --passes 10` for allocation, `--corpus <file>` for differential output, or `--cpu-profile <prefix>` for profiles.

Each cycle acquires a resident row 20 times, materializes it once, and publishes transcript fields once. Values below are medians of five process samples per arm; timings exclude setup, warmup and differential checks.

| Metric, per row cycle | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Per-sender main-thread CPU | 96.58 µs | 92.13 µs |
| Global main-thread CPU | 138.46 µs | 135.77 µs |
| Per-sender sampled allocation | 198,298 B | 197,231 B |
| Global sampled allocation | 333,530 B | 332,888 B |
| Per-sender p95, 700-row pass | 75.29 ms | 72.55 ms |
| Global p95, 700-row pass | 105.05 ms | 99.98 ms |

A/A CPU variation was 3.44% per-sender and 2.59% global. The global resident-read difference is within that variation; no significant global CPU improvement is claimed. Allocation reductions are small: 0.54% and 0.19%. Cold owner initialization medians were 252.20→242.51 ms and 65.02→65.06 ms. The shared host had outliers: per-sender CPU ranges were 92.09–105.76 µs before and 91.24–110.89 µs after; global ranges were 136.08–152.93 and 132.85–158.62 µs. These limits are why the resident result is not presented as a general production speedup.

A second arm isolates fresh-snapshot acquisition plus materialization/publication (`--snapshots --reads 1`), retaining the same 700 rows, passes, interleaved samples and separate allocation runs. It exercises the required value comparison rather than only resident identity reads.

| Fresh-snapshot cycle | Before median [min–max] | After median [min–max] |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Per-sender CPU, µs | 54.08 [53.78–55.26] | 49.54 [49.47–50.09] |
| Global CPU, µs | 54.24 [53.81–55.06] | 49.37 [48.77–50.20] |
| Per-sender allocation, B | 70,258 [70,064–70,396] | 67,615 [67,044–67,706] |
| Global allocation, B | 75,405 [75,066–75,515] | 73,006 [72,893–73,312] |
| Per-sender p95 pass, ms | 44.61 [42.07–45.12] | 38.92 [38.32–39.14] |
| Global p95 pass, ms | 46.39 [42.05–47.61] | 38.65 [37.87–39.40] |

Fresh-snapshot CPU falls 8.4%/9.0%, versus A/A CPU variation of 1.07%/1.69%. Allocation falls 3.76%/3.18%. Cold owner initialization remains comparable: 216.56→215.81 ms per-sender, 56.79→57.52 ms global (+1.28%). Separate CPU profiles show the expected reduction in deep comparison and repeated freeze work; they are attribution evidence, not the timing samples. Timing runs had no other lane-owned checks running; allocation/profile runs overlapped static validation. The resident arm used the same runtime logic before formatting, and the fresh arm pins the final formatted sources.

This is an in-memory owner microbenchmark, not whole-Gateway throughput or a large SQLite/filesystem benchmark. It does not claim that the remaining parent/key resolution, input preparation, or roster work disappears.

</details>

prs.title: fix(agents): long conversations get stuck when the primary model's explicit auth order has no usable profile
prs.body:
Related #194689

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long conversation gets stuck with "This conversation is too long, and OpenClaw couldn't shorten it" on every message when the session model's explicit `auth.order` has no usable profile, even though ordinary turns already answer from the configured fallback model.

## User Impact

User impact: when the primary model's ordered credentials are all unusable, compaction now summarizes with the next model in `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`, the same chain ordinary turns already use, so long sessions keep working until the operator signs in again. Ordinary turns behave as before (the primary is tried, fails, and the "Model switched from … to …" notice is posted, now with `(auth)` instead of `(unknown)`). With no fallback configured, the reply names the cause, "This saved login isn't available. Choose another login…", instead of "Your request couldn't be completed." A user-pinned login with no stored credential, which the rate-limit pre-check used to move behind the fallbacks silently, is now tried first, then the turn switches with the notice.

Accepted edge case: the message is the same whatever made every ordered login unusable (missing, expired, permanently disabled); it names the login rather than the underlying reason, which the operator's auth status already shows.

Accepted edge case: a refused route stays in the reordered chain, so the candidate before it still sees a later fallback. With a chain like `primary/main → backup/fast → primary/other`, a missing login for `primary` and a replay-safe 429 on `backup/fast` whose retry floor exceeds the 15-second fallback window, `backup/fast` moves on instead of waiting, and the turn fails when `primary/other` is refused too; `main` marked the route unavailable and kept the longer wait. It needs all three conditions; separating notice ordering from fallback eligibility is a follow-up if a maintainer wants it.

Not changed, on purpose: the reporter's second case, an explicit `agents.defaults.compaction.model` that cannot authenticate on the embedded path. That override stays exact and has no fallback chain, as `docs/concepts/compaction.md` documents; checking at config time whether a compaction model can work is not part of this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Auth preparation refused the explicit-order case with a plain `Error`. Turns fall back on any candidate error, but compaction moves to the next model only for a classified failover error, so it stopped after one attempt (`attempt=1 maxAttempts=1 outcome=failed reason=unknown`). The refusal is now a `FailoverError` with the existing `selected_auth_profile_unavailable` code (reason `auth`, no HTTP status): it is a local refusal, not a provider response, so it gets that code's "saved login isn't available" copy and no re-authenticate hint. Compaction already forwards the failure code to its fallback classification, which maps this code to `auth`.

The rate-limit pre-check that reorders fallback models before each turn treats an auth-preparation `FailoverError` as "skip this candidate" and records nothing for it. It now leaves `selected_auth_profile_unavailable` to the fallback runner, which attempts the primary, logs `candidate_failed`, and posts the notice, as on `main`. This keeps the shared token-rate-limit pre-check's purpose (bound same-model recovery when a usable fallback exists) for every other refusal; only this local saved-login refusal is left in place, because demoting it silently skipped the failure record and the switch notice.

Docs: `docs/concepts/compaction.md` lists this case beside the cooldown case, and `docs/auth-credential-semantics.md` (Explicit auth order filtering) says what happens when no ordered profile is usable.

Not changed: the turn fallback order and policy, compaction's failover classification, `compaction.model` exactness, the other route refusals (`configured-auth`, `required-profile`).

## Evidence

### Live run: full-product repro on `main` and the same runs on this change

Built Gateway (`openclaw.mjs gateway run`, bench tree at `main` `3d172a63470`; this change = `89d82d887f1`, whose later amendments added only doc lines) in a no-network container. Config: `primary/main-model` with `auth.order.primary: ["primary:revoked"]` (declared, no stored credential), fallback `backup/backup-model`, both 16k-token windows, served by a local Responses model that reports request size as usage. The shipped CLI sends long messages with `gateway call chat.send` and reads `gateway call chat.history`.

With the fallback configured, `main`:

```
turn 1-3: Model switched from primary/main-model to backup/backup-model (unknown).
          log: lane task error "Explicit auth order for primary has no usable profiles." / candidate_failed primary / candidate_succeeded backup
turn 4:   [compaction-diag] end ... trigger=budget provider=primary/main-model attempt=1 maxAttempts=1 outcome=failed reason=unknown
          preflight compaction failed: Explicit auth order for primary has no usable profiles.
          ⚠️ This conversation is too long, and OpenClaw couldn't shorten it. ...
summary requests to backup-model: 0
```

This change:

```
turn 1-4: Model switched from primary/main-model to backup/backup-model (auth).
          log: candidate_failed primary / candidate_succeeded backup
          compaction summary requests to backup-model: 4; history ends with a Compaction entry; every turn answered
```

(Repeated `candidate_failed` lines for the same auth refusal are coalesced by the existing decision-log rule, so fewer lines appear than on `main`.)

With no fallback configured, one message: `main` replies "Your request couldn't be completed."; this change replies "This saved login isn't available. Choose another login under Models in the OpenClaw app or run `openclaw configure`."

Proof artifice: both models are one scripted local Responses server, and the dead login is a profile declared in config with no stored credential.

What the substitute proves and what it does not: the reporter ran `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` with a Codex OAuth profile; this run uses a local provider on the OpenClaw runtime. Compaction hits the same refusal through the same `rejectionError` (the reporter's `[compaction-diag] end … attempt=1 maxAttempts=1` line comes only from the embedded compaction path this change covers), so the compaction fix applies to their route; the OpenAI/Codex route itself was not run. The Gateway, auth preparation, fallback runner, compaction and CLI are the shipped ones. Upgrade run: not applicable (no update, Doctor, config or state change).

### Tests

- `compact.auth-preparation.test.ts`: "compacts through the configured fallback" gains an explicit-order row next to the cooldown row. Fails on `main` (compaction stops on the primary), passes here.
- `model-fallback.sticky-rate-limit.test.ts` ("shared model saturation guards", where `main` moved the pre-check cases in #198916): the rate-limit pre-check keeps a primary refused by its explicit auth order in first place with no recorded skip, so the runner attempts and reports it. A guard for the pre-check exemption (it passes on `main`, where the refusal was a plain `Error`).
- On the proof machine, the touched files plus neighbours (`prepare-auth*`, `compact.summary-fallback`, `model-fallback.test`, `model-fallback.{probe,personal-cooldown,sticky-rate-limit,shared-rate-limit.integration,reply-entry.e2e}`, `model-fallback-observation`): all pass on this change (5 shards).
- `pnpm check:changed` on `89d82d887f1`: passes (typecheck core and tests, lint, format, docs, guards) except the dead-export scan, which already fails on `main` (`src/gateway/openclaw-id/member-role-change.ts`, from #197770), outside this change.
- `model-fallback.sticky-rate-limit.test.ts` › "rechecks a fallback refused for an unusable saved login on the next turn": with `OPENCLAW_FALLBACK_SKIP_TTL_MS` set, a fallback refused for this saved-login reason is attempted again on the next turn instead of being skipped until the window expires, so fixing the order takes effect at once. The skip cache now owns that rule (`cachesAuthFailureSkip`). Fails on `main` (the backup is tried once in two turns), passes here.
- After merging current `main` on 18 Nov (`52b87b23676`; `main` had deleted `model-fallback.shared-rate-limit.test.ts`, so the guard case moved with the rest of that file's cases), on the proof machine: both touched test files and the `prepare-auth`, `model-fallback` and `model-fallback.personal-cooldown` neighbours pass, and `pnpm check:changed` passes in full.
- Test lines are net +77 against `main`: one row in the existing compaction fallback table, one guard case beside the existing pre-check cases and one skip-cache case; no existing test drives this refusal.

prs.title: chore: keep the Gateway restart handoff test in step with restart markers
prs.body:
Related: #200533, #200394

## What Problem This Solves

The Linux-only Gateway restart handoff test fails on every pull request whose changed-file CI lane selects it (`checks-node-changed`), so `openclaw/ci-gate` is red for changes that have nothing to do with sessions. The test still expects each interrupted session's restart marker to carry an empty queued-input list. Production stopped writing that list on purpose in #200533.

## User Impact

User impact: no user-visible change. Pull requests that select this test get a green CI gate again, and the test once more checks what a planned restart actually records.

## Why This Change Was Made

#200533 (`703c82d20c5`) moved accepted queued input onto its own pending rows, which startup replays in order. Since then the restart-resume marker (`resumeAfterRestart`) is documented as "running root-session resume only; accepted queued input owns its own durable row". Its type has only `operatorSource` and `scope`, and #200533's own tests stopped seeding `queuedInputIds`. #200394 added `operatorSource`, the interrupted requester. Restart resume (`src/gateway/session-restart-resume.ts`) revalidates that source before it admits the replacement turn. Restart discovery only checks that a marker exists.

The test kept asserting `resumeAfterRestart: { queuedInputIds: [] }`. Here a real Gateway interrupts six pending turns for an authenticated local backend operator, and the marker it now writes is `{ operatorSource: { kind: "gateway", snapshot: { profileId: "gateway-owner", localOperator: true, … } } }`. The test now asserts that marker, the part of the contract restart resume depends on, instead of the removed list. `gateway-owner` is the protocol constant `GATEWAY_OWNER_PROFILE_ID`.

Test file audit (whole file): one Linux-only test. Every import and constant is used, the fixture owns its temp plugin directory, provider, instance and client, and the cleanup callbacks close each of them. The `journal` helper copied a `check` field into each row that nothing read; it is removed. Nothing else is removed, skipped or loosened.

## Evidence

The test runs only on Linux (`it.skipIf(process.platform !== "linux")`), so CI is the red/green proof:

- Red, without this change: `checks-node-changed` fails this test with `expected { …(31) } to match object { resumeAfterRestart: { …(1) } }`. In the received entry, `queuedInputIds` is missing and `operatorSource` is present (for example #201545, CI run 44445370253).
- Green, with this change: `checks-node-changed` on this PR must pass this test.

Locally on macOS the file loads and its one test is skipped, as designed. `oxfmt`, `oxlint` and `git diff --check` are clean.

prs.title: fix(ci): bound full-dispatch compact test groups
prs.body:
# Fix hosted full-dispatch compact envelopes

## Problem and solution
Full dual-runtime dispatch intentionally uses the capped compact plan. Its full-inventory path missed incident-backed main file limits, permitting underpriced large chat, support and config groups. Reuse the existing compact file-limit map for GitHub-hosted full inventory, separately from main-only updater isolation. The timing refit source selector also excluded current compact dispatch spans; admit them to its existing compact parser. No new splitter, parser, public option, limit or generated timing data.

## Preserved boundaries
- Same file/config/runtime/engine and required prerequisites; Node/Bun rows and exceptions remain independent. Declared execution settings, effective workers, caps and budgets are retained.
- Main-only updater isolation remains unchanged; full dispatch keeps its existing runtime prerequisite group.
- Successful-job gate, attempt identity, frozen cutoff, partial-inventory protection, minimum two independent runs and runtime-specific timing identities remain unchanged.
- No packing implementation from #160254 or generated timing JSON owned by #198212.

## November 19 integration and current proof
Head `068c162e699c19733b0d4cfc0b6359b2919ccd01` merges main `96189709bc5042cac232926c541f27fe2efd1dfc` to repair an actual conflict with #201270 (`7eb33ccb25f76747be9a60ef74b69b83b76fd471`). That landed change deliberately bounds Gateway methods in ordinary compact PR layouts and dedicates rows to chunks above 32 files. Preserve it, including hourly-main's 77-row packing. The conflict resolution is the union of the existing applicability predicates, not a second planner. No added permanent tests or new machinery in this repair.

- All three touched suites pass: **287/287 tests**, 172.47s. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan-hosted-tail.test.ts test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts test/scripts/ci-test-timings.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Includes main's Gateway isolation regressions and this PR's full-inventory and sampler regressions.
- Production and root-tooling typechecks, scoped production/test lint, six-file formatting, changed-doc MDX and diff checks pass.
- Replayed actual full dual-runtime GitHub manifest against current main and the integrated candidate. **53 configs; 31,785 runtime-specific file tuples per side; zero required-execution additions/removals; 192 rows on both sides (96 Node/96 Bun); four direct worker rows byte-identical.** The increase from the historical 180-row evidence below is already on main, not introduced by this repair.
- All 500 main and 540 candidate group occurrences receive at least their canonical prerequisite. Compared config/file/runtime/engine, non-exclusion arguments, effective declared environment, required preparation, dist requirement, runner/cpu/concurrency and fallback worker/memory fields. Reconstructed all six affected families' timing generations with the existing owner; Gateway's eight keys are unchanged.
- Current maximum group sizes: chat **120→30**, support **245→62**, config **309→62**, status **131→47**, Doctor **117→61**. Gateway **88→88**: its earlier improvement is already landed in #201270 and is not counted again. Forty additional group occurrences may add startup overhead; no additional rows or requested worker capacity.
- Repacking changes incidental sibling preparation and derived cache/prebuilt flags. It also moves **8,129** file/runtime tuples between existing job watchdog envelopes. No literal raw-job-environment or per-file-watchdog equality is claimed. The scoped effective-execution comparison passes; failed historical literal-parity evidence is retained, not hidden.

## Earlier regression and real-workload evidence
These are prior-head results, not new-head CI:
- Both original regressions fail on the original base and pass with the fix: full inventory exceeds 30 chat files; compact dispatch ingress omits its 30-second Node sample. Original focused suites: 113 passed.
- Earlier consumer run: 53 unit-fast and 450 tooling tests passed; an obsolete two-group pricing assertion was corrected to four bounded stripes, preserving its 1,000-second total, then passed. Not represented as a clean initial broad run.
- Original manifest replay: 31,735 tuples/53 configs; 180 rows (90 per runtime), 490→540 group occurrences. All 697 preparation transitions accounted for: 419 lose incidental sibling preparation, 268 gain it, 10 move private-QA to their required ordinary runtime build. Historical watchdog membership changes: 6,988, with 150/30 row counts retained.
- Original actual runs-on evaluation: Ubuntu 24.04 across 360 before/after rows; actual resource shell retains 2/3/4/6 workers on physical 2/4/8/16 CPUs and serial plans.
- Five representative none-condition shards passed 75 original tests without private-QA/prebuilt flags. Two selected runtime consumers passed (2 files/2 tests, wrapper 180.03s) after the normal runtime qaRuntime owner completed in 115.4s with `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=0` and prebuilt flag absent. It verified 56 plugin control-plane modules and all 14 postbuild phases; worker compilation verified its generation. Existing artifacts were not destructively cleaned: this is not pristine runtime-only filesystem proof.

## Critical path, history and limitations
Observed CI runs https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44268159668 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44264437379 had compact spans 65m03s/71m07s, peak running counts 95/94, max queue delays 800s/766s. Job https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44268159668/job/134678365855 spent 2,601s in its large stripe, including 2,214s for 277 Gateway files. These pre-#201270 measurements motivate bounded groups, but do not establish this PR's remaining end-to-end benefit after that fix.

Preserves deliberate runtime-consumer separation from #138839 (`d1a69c0b2095`) and removal of unnecessary update preparation in #195288 (`f1c5af0f6bc3`). Reuses incident-backed main limits from #157302/#198992 and Gateway isolation from #201270.

**No measured FRV speedup or 12-minute guarantee.** Smaller groups permit redistribution by the existing packer; setup, queue/capacity, combined-policy prices and downstream barriers can hide component savings. The more recent fully drained stable-2026.11.6 audit found the package-survivor branch dominant, not ordinary CI; this PR is not credited with reducing those parents' completion time. The separate survivor-cap proposal #201265 targets that bottleneck.

Local dist existed. Clean snapshot execution was blocked by an escaping dependency symlink after native-pnpm preflight, not a product-test failure; no install/isolation bypass. No full-dispatch Node/Bun candidate execution or peak-RSS/wall comparison. Ordinary PR CI is not a hosted full-dispatch performance experiment. No catalog or baseline weakened.

## Hosted finding repair
ClawSweeper's valid P3 concerned dispatch provenance being inferred from packed job names. Commit `886b3d0251725ca05a7fd72add266bdd7b11e145` instead records run IDs at admission; the earlier two-main-run eligibility gate is unchanged. Existing CLI fixtures reproduce four main contributors before and correctly report two main/two dispatch afterward. Earlier timing suite: 110 passed/29.58s; current 287-test run includes it. No extra fixture was added for that repair.

## Size and review state
Current merge-base delta: production **+17/-13**, tests **+87/-21**, docs **+1/-1**; six files **+105/-35**. Prior revision: +103/-32 total; the integrated delta retains main's isolation instead of replacing it. Author simplification applied: one existing predicate/map/parser, no duplicate owner or additional tests. Separate local independent review explicitly waived.

**Ready for review as of November 19, 2026, 03:19 UTC.** Current head `068c162e699c19733b0d4cfc0b6359b2919ccd01` is conflict-free. Exact-head CI https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44448944731 completed successfully; the observed rollup has 57 successful checks/statuses, 61 skipped checks and one neutral check, with no pending or failing checks. Required commit statuses are green at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44450267755. ClawSweeper completed its exact-head review at 03:12:47 UTC with no findings or before-merge items: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201181#issuecomment-6979063118. The explicit request acknowledgment confirms completion: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201181#issuecomment-6998450553. Review readiness does not establish a measured full-FRV performance improvement; the limitations above remain.

prs.title: fix(signal): view-once attachments are downloaded and passed to the agent
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Signal view-once photos and videos are downloaded and handed to the agent like ordinary attachments when a view-once message is received.

## User Impact

User impact: media a sender marked view-once is no longer fetched, saved to the inbound media store, or passed into the agent's context. The agent sees `[signal view-once media not shown]` instead. Ordinary attachments behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Signal receive handler did not look at `dataMessage.viewOnce` before calling the attachment fetcher, and the fetcher saves the downloaded bytes for downstream use. The handler now skips the fetch when the flag is strictly `true` and emits the notice. A missing, `false` or `null` flag keeps the existing attachment path.

The unavailable-media text moved into the existing Signal media-text module so the already oversized event handler does not grow.

This covers OpenClaw's fetch decision and the context sent to the model. signal-cli's own attachment storage is outside the change.

## Evidence

Run with Node 24.22.2 and pnpm 12.15.0. No live Signal account or model provider was used; attachment transport is mocked and identifiers are synthetic.

- The new regression (`extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.view-once.test.ts`) drives the real `createSignalEventHandler` and inbound runner. On `main` it fails 2 of 5 cases (the view-once attachment is fetched); on this branch all 5 pass, including three ordinary-media controls.
- A second, separately written test through the same entry point covers direct, edited, group and captioned view-once messages plus `ignoreAttachments`: 5 failed / 4 passed on `main`, 9 passed on this branch.
- Existing handler and media-text suites together with the new test: 36 passed across three files.
- `pnpm build` and `pnpm check:test-types` passed. Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, line-growth and test-budget checks passed. The per-change test allocation is 78 lines.

Gap: `pnpm check --base origin/main` passed its preflights and typechecks, then hit Tlon and Crabbox test line-limit errors that reproduce on an untouched `main` checkout. The remaining core lint shard was stopped after eleven minutes without diagnostics, so the full repository check is not claimed green locally.

### Running Gateway (local signal-cli stand-in)

The real Gateway was built from each revision and started with the Signal plugin enabled in its documented external daemon mode. The far end was a local stand-in for the signal-cli daemon, not signal-cli or the Signal service: JSON-RPC over HTTP plus the SSE receive stream, on loopback. A second local stand-in answered the model request with a fixed reply. Gateway transport, ingress, media storage, agent dispatch, transcript persistence and reply delivery ran unmodified. No real account or provider credential was used.

- Base: `b382a29a688a`. Head: `730cfcd13971`. Node 24.22.2, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm build`, then `pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --verbose`.
- The same scenario ran on both: a captionless view-once image, wait for the reply, then an ordinary image. Both attachments are the same synthetic 16x16 PNG (79 bytes).
- Observations come from the stand-in's request log, file events and snapshots of the inbound media store, the captured model request, and the Gateway's persisted transcript.

| Revision | Received | Attachment fetches | New inbound files | Persisted media paths | Images in the model request | Reply delivered |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Base | view-once | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Head | view-once | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| Base | ordinary | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Head | ordinary | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |

On head the persisted user content for the view-once message is exactly `[signal view-once media not shown]`; the retained media fact carries only the content type and kind, with no path or URL. The Gateway's own pre-prompt diagnostics report `promptImages=1` for the base view-once message, `promptImages=0` for head, and `promptImages=1` for the ordinary control on both.

Limits: this is the running product against local stand-ins. It does not establish the live Signal service's wire contract, account or device behaviour, or real-model behaviour. The no-write observation covers the inbound media store from injection through reply delivery plus one second; it is not a syscall audit.

prs.title: feat: reset OpenClaw ID owner access from the claw's own computer
prs.body:
Related: OCF-319, OCF-323. Stacked on #201586 (base branch); retarget to `main` once that lands. Supersedes draft #198576.

## What Problem This Solves

If a claw's OpenClaw ID recovery kit is lost or leaked, there is no way to take back owner access: every owner browser and the old kit keep working, and the only fallback is relinking the claw as a new one.

## User Impact

On the computer that runs the claw, the owner can reset owner access from **Settings → OpenClaw ID** or with `openclaw id reset`. A reset makes a new recovery kit, removes every owner device, person, node and invite, closes their remote sessions, and gives the claw a new Gateway key. The claw's address, connection key and data stay. It needs both:

- **A direct connection to this computer's running Gateway.** The tunnel, reverse proxies and Tailscale Serve are refused (`not_local_operator`); the page explains why and keeps the button off.
- **A link code from the OpenClaw ID account that owns the claw.** The Control UI takes it from the signed-in account; the CLI prompts for it or takes `--code`. The Gateway checks it with Discovery before anything changes.

Until Discovery adopts code-gated root changes, a reset commits locally but its publication is refused, so **do not use this outside tests yet**. The PR stays in draft until Discovery is ready.

## Why This Change Was Made

This builds on the earlier owner-reset work (#198576) and adapts it to #201586: a reset stages a new Gateway key and publishes under it with the snapshot and the owner's code, the same path as a move to new keys. A copied Gateway key file therefore can't reset the claw.

Changes after review:
- Re-binds and resets share one lane, so cancelling a move can't delete the key a reset is committing to.
- Before resetting, Discovery must still publish this computer's root and binding. A restored backup is refused with `binding_superseded` instead of stranding the claw.
- Failures after the reset is stored come back as `followUpError` on a committed result, never as a refusal.
- The CLI shows the new kit and asks for it to be saved **before** committing.

The stopped-Gateway `openclaw id reset` path from #198576 is removed: reset is offered only through a direct connection to the running Gateway.

## Evidence

- **Real Gateway, loopback, recording Discovery stand-in:**
  - Without a code: `needs_link_code`; with a wrong code: `code_invalid`.
  - With the owner's code: one descriptor write signed by the **new** Gateway key, carrying the code, the snapshot and a `RootReset` that `verifyRootReset` accepts.
  - A tunnel client is refused before the service is asked.
- **Service tests (`owner-reset.test.ts`, 12):**
  - Removals happen; K_srv is kept and the Gateway signs with K_gw' afterwards.
  - Refused with no code, a wrong code, an unpublished claw, Discovery unavailable, or a superseded binding, and none of these change anything.
  - A queued re-bind cancel doesn't destroy the staged key. This test fails without the shared lane.
  - Follow-up failure reporting.
- **CLI tests (5):** the kit is shown once before commit; nothing is committed until "saved"; refusals are told apart from unknown outcomes; follow-up failures exit with code 2.
- **Control UI:**
  - Page tests: both requirements are shown, and the button is off over the tunnel or without a sign-in.
  - Browser e2e against a mocked Gateway: the full reset runs locally, both steps carry a link code, and the confirmation alert says "This can't be undone".
  - Screenshots were captured locally but not attached here.
- **Checks:** `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- **Inherited failure:** `src/gateway/openclaw-id/member-role-recovery.test.ts` (2 tests) fails identically on `main` + #201586 without these changes.
- **Not run:**
  - Staging end to end: blocked on Discovery adoption.
  - The human-presence check (OCF-334) is still open.

prs.title: fix(cli): restore PowerShell completion for quoted option assignments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PowerShell offers no value completion when the current option and its value are quoted together, such as `openclaw completion '--shell=f'` or `openclaw completion '-sf'`.

## User Impact

Tab completion now offers `--shell=fish` and `-sfish` for those inputs, including an unfinished quote. Regenerate cached PowerShell completions after updating with `openclaw completion --shell powershell --write-state`, then reload the shell.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing literal AST decoder before recognizing attached long and short options. Previously, only the choice prefix was decoded, while option recognition still read the quoted token. Cursor truncation continues to run first. This reuses the existing parsing path without adding production lines or helpers.

## Evidence

- Built both base `afaaa8d287` and head `71459264cc` with `pnpm build qaRuntime`. Generated each script through `pnpm --silent openclaw completion --shell powershell` using isolated configuration, then loaded it into PowerShell's native `CommandCompletion.CompleteInput` engine on Windows.
- Four cases fail on the base and pass on the fix: single-quoted and double-quoted `--shell=f`, single-quoted `-sf`, and an unfinished single-quoted assignment. Four controls pass on both, including completion with the cursor immediately after `f` in `'--shell=fjunk'`.
- The four added native PowerShell regression cases also fail on the original implementation. The completion, alias, visibility, and command-tree suites pass **45 tests**, with **29 other-shell/platform skips**. Ran the CLI-process and command-tree groups separately after the combined invocation passed both shards but failed while publishing its aggregate report.
- Targeted production/test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, staged test-line budget, and `git diff --check` pass. The four test rows reuse the existing PowerShell process and have an exact four-line allocation.
- Independent local review of the complete candidate through P3 found no actionable issue. A cursor-boundary concern from an earlier incomplete-context review was checked in the native shell and resolved by supplying the existing prefix-AST handling. No extra production change was needed.

Other operating systems and the full repository test suite were not run locally; upstream CI covers the broader lanes.

prs.body:
Related to [#198737](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198737). Removes repeated test instrumentation, stress multiplicity and generic presentation/metadata inventories while retaining the existing behavioral harnesses. No production changes.

Preserves all prior approval, Guardian, warning, model/auth, inventory, Code Mode and cleanup repairs. Multi-pool critical-memory cleanup and manifest-only profile grants are also retained through actual assembly. Fresh review guards are restored: actual lazy-process declaration/execution composition, bounded burst cooldown, and successful concurrent/sequential skill-read receipts. Existing helpers retain the original fixtures and describe hooks; no new support module. The latest guard restorations retain real sandbox AVIF detection from the read buffer, exact three-line past-EOF recovery, and all five exec parameter normalizations through preparation/conflict/success. The catalog case retains collision-suffixed operator exclusions across synthetic resource-tool materialization. Expired-approval delivery suppression is retained separately from ordinary error warnings; the completion-only optional-runtime case is removed. The streamed-HTML regression retains all four original96-line fixtures, scan-work budgets and late-marker activation. All four Revision10 work guards are restored: inbound-metadata append/replacement bounds, shared catalog initialization bytes and live limits, actual automatic-CLI-fallback lookup reuse, and configured/visibility provider-policy reuse with physical-route refresh. The latter original introduction remains UNKNOWN; the actual current cache owner is openai-model-routes.ts. The read cases preserve the original intent of [#121508](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/121508).

**Candidate:** `811a175cdfb9d5a1e8e6ddaa8e9cc2fade663f8b` against `a90c5419b779df517ea3c3ea0bee0b37e87f85ac`. 23 test/support paths plus one test baseline, +675/-1129 = **454 net lines removed** (452 test/support, 2 metadata); production +0/-0.

**Local validation:** 36 scoped files: 614 passed, one intentional Bun-only cancellation-tail skip; separate Node resources 3/3 reused from74ee on the identical test blob and runtime inputs. The four restored suites passed72/72 at signed6575, whose complete source tree equals native811a. The separate streaming-work sibling120/120 result is reused from45dd on its identical test and runtime inputs. All29 original type graphs plus subsequent affected graphs passed, with current formatting, oxlint and line/mock ratchets green. All20,314 compiler inputs and25,389 outputs rehashed without mismatch; canonical build6575 is truthfully reused on the identical complete tree. Fresh nine-pass exact-range review completed with zero findings/gaps,232 full context bodies and24 changed units. All four affected suites passed72/72 and the current compiler inputs/outputs rehash without mismatch. Exact-head hosted [CI attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44446337947) passed (38 successful jobs, 30 intentional skips), and Workflow Sanity passed. Fresh [Claw Revision 11](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198918#issuecomment-6879322158) reviews this exact head with no findings, no before-merge items, and no remaining rank-up moves. Native completed-hosted gates and required-check merge verification passed.

prs.title: fix: stop a copied OpenClaw ID Gateway key from resetting a claw's owner
prs.body:
Related: OCF-319

## What Problem This Solves

Under the OpenClaw ID owner-reset spec, the claw's Gateway key alone authorizes replacing its owner key at Discovery. That key is a plain `0600` file on the Gateway host, readable by anything running as the Gateway user, including an unsandboxed agent session. Someone who copies it could reset the claw from anywhere, lock existing browsers out behind an "owner reset, set up again" prompt that points at their own kit, and repeat that after any legitimate reset, because a reset kept the same key.

## User Impact

No user-visible change yet: the Gateway doesn't implement owner reset and Discovery still refuses every root change. This changes the protocol contract so that, once reset ships, it needs the machine **and** a one-time link code from the account that owns the claw, and a leaked Gateway key stops working at the reset.

## Why This Change Was Made

A reset now has to name a **new** Gateway key (the connection key stays). Discovery already requires a new Gateway key's publication to be signed by the new key, carry its snapshot, and spend a one-time code from the owner account. That rule therefore gates every reset without a new endpoint. The old key still signs the `RootReset`, so pinned browsers can still tell a reset from a substitution, but that signature alone authorizes nothing.

- `verifyRootReset` requires the same K_srv and a different K_gw.
- `enrollment.md`, `discovery.md` and `statements.md` describe both requirements (the machine and the owner account) and the new key.
- Test vectors gain a second Gateway key; the fixture is regenerated from the builder.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test packages/openclaw-id-protocol`: 265/265 after the fix to the leaked-kit test. `reset.test.ts` covers acceptance with a new K_gw, a reset that keeps K_gw (`reset_mismatch`), and the earlier forgeries.
- Portable typecheck (`tsconfig.portable.json`), oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the package.
- The fixture test confirms `statements.json` is exactly the builder's output.
- Discovery `main` (`401734d`) still refuses every root change (`test/claws.test.ts`, "refuses a root change even with valid owner reset evidence"), so nothing deployed changes. Adopting this check there is a follow-up.

The Gateway, CLI and Control UI implementation is stacked on this in a separate draft PR.

prs.title: fix: show app update guidance instead of a failing Update button on app-managed Macs
prs.body:
Closes #198506

Prior work: #198562 tried this and was closed without merging because the update handlers it edited have since moved. This PR is written against current main.

## What Problem This Solves

On a Mac where OpenClaw.app owns the Gateway, Settings > Updates still shows an enabled "Update Gateway..." button and an "Update status unavailable" row. Clicking the button gets a refusal from the Gateway ("Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway."). The page then keeps that refusal as an update error with a "Retry update" button, and the error stays until the page is reloaded. A healthy install looks like it failed an update, and Retry cannot succeed because the Gateway marks the refusal as not retryable.

## User Impact

User impact: on an app-managed install, Settings > Updates now says "Managed by OpenClaw.app" in the status row and shows the app's own guidance ("Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway.") where the update button used to be. There is no button to click, so no error appears and nothing is left to retry. Other installs (package, Git checkout, separately managed Gateways) look and behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already knew the install was app-owned, but `update.status` dropped that fact, so the page had no way to tell this install from any other and offered the normal action. The Gateway now sends the owner under `schedule.install.host`, and the Settings page uses it. Ownership comes from the same install marker the Gateway's refusal already uses, so a Mac connected to a separately managed Gateway still gets the normal update flow.

The protocol schema gains an optional `install.host` object and a `host` install kind, and the generated validators were regenerated from it. The Control UI adds four English strings. The updating doc notes where the owner is reported.

## Evidence

Before the change, the new Settings test fails the way the issue describes: the status row reads "Update status unavailable" and there is no ownership guidance. After the change it passes.

Tests run locally (Node 26, macOS arm64):

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/config.test.ts`: 12 passed, including a new case that accepts the host owner and rejects unknown owners or an empty hint.
- `src/infra/update-install-status.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-startup-host-owned.test.ts`: 10 passed, with expectations updated to include the owner.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/update-status-schedule.test.ts`, `update-status.test.ts`: 49 passed, with the app-owned case now expecting `install.host`.
- `ui/src/pages/config/updates.test.ts` plus the neighboring updates, overlay and i18n suites: 241 passed. The new Settings test takes about 5 ms.
- `generate-gateway-validators` and `generate-control-ui-validators` in `--check` mode report no drift, and `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` are clean.

Not verified:

- No native macOS run and no screenshots. I could not launch Chromium in my environment, and I did not run the app against a real app-managed Gateway. The issue's reporter offered to check a fix on their Mac.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/update-host-owned.test.ts` had one failure ("refuses an immutable surface discovered after initial admission"), a SQLite state lock error in the test's temp directory. It runs code this change does not touch, and I did not check it against main.
- The full `pnpm check:changed` and `pnpm install` were not run. Dependencies were installed with npm in a scratch folder and the checks above were run against those.

prs.title: fix: reduce memory during SQLite usage refresh
prs.body:
Related: #197430

## What Problem This Solves

The background usage refresh can run out of memory on long SQLite chat histories, leaving token and cost totals stale. The paged reader limits decoded payloads, but the worker retains the navigation projection and every parsed billing entry while building the exact-timestamp rollup.

## User Impact

Lower peak heap during SQLite usage refresh without widening time buckets, dropping entries, or changing the cache format. No configuration change or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve billing, latency ancestry and the checkpoint first. Release the navigation projection, then drain the owned billing list in the same order into the existing pricing batches. The latency lookup uses weak keys so it does not keep processed entries alive. Exact buckets still scale with the number of distinct timestamps; this reduces overlapping memory, not the size of the final rollup.

## Evidence

- On current main (6ec27bd739c), the production SQLite scan with an in-memory SQLite fixture of 270,391 billed rows at unique millisecond timestamps reached **473 MiB** maximum sampled post-GC JS heap. The candidate reached **297 MiB** (37% lower), with identical exact-timestamp bucket output (SHA-256 d86644baa3562655253cf070d3254feee0fa59bdeb7cbb3e7108c429bad5cb53). This measures the scan and aggregation, not a production worker restart or an end-to-end cache publication.
- 60 targeted tests passed across refresh, snapshots, scan, codec and SQLite cache, including append, inherited history, rewinds, and branch-local latency. Targeted type-aware lint, format and diff checks passed.
- Reviewed the final diff locally against the billing and checkpoint contracts; the standalone autoreview helper was not installed.


### End-to-end Gateway proof

Tested the unchanged PR head `91e8b402593a1fbd9ef07a32963d481ca7a3f67d` (macOS arm64, Node 24.22.3). Seeded a fresh, isolated agent SQLite store through the existing transcript batch writer with 270,391 synthetic billed messages, each at a distinct millisecond. Started the real loopback Gateway with its usage sidecar enabled, without a heap override or mocks for the worker, SQLite, or cache. Polled `sessions.usage` from an empty cache until fresh, asserted exact expected totals, and checked the persisted SQLite cache after clean shutdown.

Redacted terminal evidence (selected fields; the worker measurement uses sampling, not forced GC):

```text
SQLite input: 270391 rows, 270391 unique generated timestamps
sessions.usage: cacheStatus=fresh input=540782 output=270391 totalTokens=811173 totalCost=33798.875
usage-cost refresh worker: old-generation limit=512 MiB, sampled peak JS heap=440 MiB (3526 samples)
Persisted cache: session-cost-usage-rollup-v3=1, session-cost-usage-projection-v2=1, session-cost-usage-quarters-v1=1
Gateway shutdown: completed cleanly; harness exit=0
```

The worker was sampled externally with Node's `Worker.getHeapStatistics()` while the Gateway owned the real refresh. This is a candidate-only end-to-end pass; the separate post-GC benchmark above is the before/after comparison. No production logs, personal chat data, or credentials were used.

prs.title: fix(agents): requester tools lose authority after child resume
prs.body:
Related: #167022

## What Problem This Solves

An already-admitted requester can lose tool authority when continuing a paused child replaces the child's delivery cohort. This candidate separates the consumed requester's execution lifetime from that mutable delivery progress.

The one-use handoff must still be current at registration and consumption. After consumption, a supplied requester receipt retains requester/store identity for later caller checks and exact-model binding. Delivery keeps its cohort checks. Existing admitted-run liveness, cancellation, operator authority and delegated restrictions remain composed; handoffs without a requester receipt retain the strict predicate. No new grant, registry, configuration, schema or dependency is introduced.

Candidate: `9800ab830b4c08a7bc73d19c2a7056c3299cc528`.
Inspected base: `b81742c8bfb591847601678178ff824336fc73eb`.

## Previously recorded focused validation

- The consumed-handoff/model-binding regression fails on the original implementation; 11 existing cases pass.
- The sessions_send final-enqueue regression fails after **simulated** cohort replacement on the original implementation; 14 other cases pass, including requester/store replacement refusals.
- With the candidate, all **67 focused tests** pass across handoff, model binding, requester-policy and final-enqueue suites. Recorded wrapper wall time: **45.82 seconds**. The two changed test files report approximately 2 and 17 seconds including per-file setup; CI timing remains pending.
- Core production types, both changed-test type graphs, targeted type-aware lint, formatting and git diff --check passed.
- Separate shipped qaRuntime builds passed for exact candidate and base, in 44.7 and 43.2 seconds. Build/source stamps agree. These are runtime-build results, not full package/release validation.

Those focused regressions explicitly supply handoff-bearing caller options. Their simulated evidence is separate from the real-model experiments below. No tests or builds were rerun for this final body assembly.

## Live experiment — shipped Codex runner

One real-model trial per exact source used the shipped Gateway and Codex runner in isolated fixtures. Children remained OpenClaw-managed; native rollout metadata records multi-agent version disabled.

Both trials recorded the child's explicit message wait and registry successor/generation/cohort replacement. Their actual tool receipts differ:

| Tool receipt | Candidate | Exact base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resume | accepted, mode=resume; isError=false | agent tool caller authority is no longer active; isError=true |
| Independent subsequent notify | queued; isError=false | same caller-authority error; isError=true |

**The base produced a successor even though its resume receipt reported an error.** Both independent sends were captured in the final outcome history. Within each trial they belong to the same requester-settle run, use distinct native outer calls, and place the first outer output before the second call. Committed successor replacement was observed before the second call. This is scenario-level live red/green evidence for the Codex-mediated caller flow.

### Authority-path inference and limits

Codex explicitly forwards trustedInternalHandoff into coding-tool options at `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.ts:223`; both built artifacts retain that field. `src/agents/agent-tools.caller.ts:57` reads the settle batch and line 78 selects its receipt predicate. `src/gateway/subagent-completion-tool-handoff.ts:135` constructs the candidate's consumed-execution predicate. Caller authority is captured/composed at `src/agents/tools/gateway-caller-context.ts:440` and line 670. Notify checks communication authority immediately before enqueue at `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.delivery.ts:93`.

This pinned source/build mapping, selected-runtime diagnostics and real receipt difference support the assembly-path explanation. Callback identities, Boolean predicate values, the precise handoff-consumption return and selected requesterPolicySource were not directly recorded. No source, model-I/O or callback instrumentation was added.

Notify success establishes **process-owned queue admission**, not receiver model execution, restart durability or external/channel delivery. The driver captured final history after a final-marker or authority-error observation plus a three-second grace. Later teardown restart/abort diagnostics are not the tested authority failures.

## Separate embedded experiment and remaining gap

The earlier embedded experiment completed the functional sequence on both sources, so it did not establish live base failure or patched-branch coverage. Inspection found that `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-tool-prepare.ts:246` passes handoff to profile resolution, but codingToolOptions starting at line 319 omits it; the shared context builder at `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-tool-run-context.ts:91` does not supply it either.

**That shared embedded omission remains unfixed in this candidate.** The separate Codex red/green result does not repair or retroactively upgrade the embedded experiment. Coverage across other runtimes, revocation cases and every report on the related issue is not claimed, and upstream acceptance is not presumed.

## Evidence and isolation

[Reviewed six-file evidence snapshot](https://gist.github.com/wzysmarthome-dot/dfbf75e8acb274a3d305071e808b16b8) — 27 projected redacted records, integrity hashes and the pre-publication body draft.

The linked six-file evidence snapshot includes projected redacted primary-record excerpts with stable synthetic labels, relative timestamps, source hashes and JSON pointers. They are not complete raw logs or raw terminal output. Actual receipts and source/build inference are labeled separately.

Both Codex fixtures staged only the same designated subscription profile, with no alternative profile or API-key billing fallback. No real conversations, memories or business data were copied. Task ports/processes and temporary credential state were cleaned; production configuration content was unchanged. Both source trees remain at the exact SHAs above and clean. The linked bundle preserves the reviewed pre-publication snapshot. Its local-only status notes describe the assembly stage, not the current publication state.

prs.title: fix: keep one child completion failure from dropping sibling results
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A yielded requester could lose several finished child results when one member of its completion batch had no live Gateway binding. This can happen after restoration, but also during ordinary visible spawning or binding cleanup. The whole batch failed together, and a later requester turn could prevent the failure notice from appearing before the child rows were retired.

## User Impact

Bound children now deliver their results independently of incompatible siblings. Unbound children settle separately, and retired children leave a visible failure that tells the user to inspect their saved results. No configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Visible spawning and watched follow-ups now preserve the caller's captured Gateway binding at registration. The registry partitions frozen batches by Gateway owner and retirement state before dispatch or failure settlement. Native settlement commits the admitted partition while leaving other members pending; the existing sibling wake mechanism advances them.

Failure reporting uses the existing required-completion owner for yielded batches, including when the original requester turn has ended. It verifies that the notice was appended and preserves the existing recovery receipt if publication fails. Failure notices preserve the existing chat-addressed contract across transcript replacement; live writer and completion-delivery lifecycle protections remain intact. Missing or stopped chats receive no notice. This removes the duplicate stable-batch notice path and redundant whole-wave validation; production code is net −12 lines.

Talk final attachments now follow admitted partitions while retaining pending siblings, exact full-cohort revocation, and consume-before-append replay protection. A retired row can resume its settle wake to record a visible failure, while ordinary delivery remains blocked.

Related: #195275. This fixes the separate mixed-binding failure before completion dispatch.

## Evidence

Five regression cases fail on base `0b18f610` and pass with this change: restored unbound membership, live never-bound membership, live binding retirement, visible-spawn registration, and a failed settle after a newer requester yield. The native registry harness asserts actual bound-result delivery and a visible transcript failure for a retired row. Focused persistence, requester-wake and affected tool suites pass (96 tests). All four real-Gateway turnover controls also pass, including model error, reset and Stop. Final `pnpm check:changed`, the session-identity ratchet and isolated Codex autoreview through P2 pass. CI exposed a regression in the consolidated failure-notice path: it must follow the current chat after reset or compaction and preserve the original error detail. The unchanged retry-lifetime suite now passes (17 tests), along with five affected requester-wake regressions rerun after that repair.

Hosted Codex and ClawSweeper identified the Talk attachment contract. The repair adds success-first/failure-first replay controls and extends all three native mixed-binding cases to assert the Talk callback. Those cases fail on the earlier PR head and pass after the repair, including restoration processed first. The complete requester-wake suite passes 41 tests, attachment/dispatch/yield/Talk controls pass 92 tests, and restore/resume controls pass 4 tests. The existing serial-delegation Talk regression from #142830 remains green. Persisted row types, codec and schema are unchanged; the restored case writes, removes the in-memory owner, reloads through the native store, and verifies both delivered siblings and a visible retirement failure.

The 30-minute ordinary completion expiry can defer settle wakes while another delivery owner holds the row. This repair isolates the eventual batch failure; it does not change that timeout or claim to establish the cause of every delayed completion.

Final-head synthetic measurement used a 35.2 GiB agent database, 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs and 62,000 workspace files (1.116 GB), with no production data. Five fresh-process A1/A2/B cycles each used six warmups and 30 measured four-child waves through the real settle owner and native SQLite mutations, with scripted delivery.

| Per four-child wave | Baseline A1 | Baseline A2 | Fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Wall time | 6.662 ms | 6.532 ms | 7.196 ms |
| Process CPU | 31.994 ms | 32.205 ms | 33.985 ms |
| Sampled allocation | 2.040 MB | 2.033 MB | 2.037 MB |

Values are medians of five process medians. Allocation was measured separately with V8 sampling; CPU includes worker threads. The fixture ran on APFS, not btrfs, and host load varied. The fixed wall median is 0.53–0.66 ms higher than A/A, while allocation falls between the controls. Timing was noisy: baseline A2 process medians ranged from 5.66 to 22.91 ms and fixed medians from 5.84 to 27.81 ms; all runs, including contention during local checks, are retained. This does not support a speedup claim or a precise causal estimate of the small median difference. These are owner measurements, not model/network latency.

prs.title: improve(ci): admit more hosted package survivor checks in parallel
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Expanded package-survivor validation leaves independent upgrade scenarios waiting behind a 32-job admission cap. In the completed 2026.11.6 campaign, the 90 targeted jobs occupied 67m38s and were the parent tail. This makes a narrowly scoped 48-job cap reviewable without changing the work being validated.

Related: #132271 (original bounded fanout), #165007 (single-scenario isolation, retained).

## User Impact

No installed-product change. Release operators can admit 48 targeted jobs for the GitHub-hosted expanded package-survivor path, instead of 32. **Peak demand can rise by 16 jobs (+50%) per matching matrix. Actual wall-time improvement and downstream capacity are not yet measured at 48.** No repository variables, runner reservations, higher-concurrency campaign, or release are changed/launched here.

Self-hosted/custom runner groups, source-only/general live work, empty scenario selections, and any matrix selecting update-migration retain 32. Exact rows/order, one scenario per container, timeouts, fail-fast:false, npm worker limits, cache behavior, and artifact/retry identities are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

One inline strategy expression uses existing inputs and the existing validated package-presence output: hosted enabled, empty runner_group, package artifact present, published-upgrade-survivor selected with nonempty scenarios, and update-migration absent. No new option, planner, state, helper, or test scaffolding. Explicit artifact-backed calls satisfying the same workload/routing contract also qualify; this is not a caller-name check.

Package Acceptance inherits workflow_call's hosted=true default and does **not** forward release_test_profile, so that field is deliberately not used to guess beta/stable coverage. Nonempty scenarios matches the existing planner's expanded-selection contract. The owning docs and CI index describe the scope.

The cap introduced in #132271 is an operating choice, not a demonstrated 32-runner platform limit. Preserve the scenario isolation fixed in #165007 rather than regrouping scenarios.

## Evidence

- Existing owning guard evaluates the actual YAML expression with eight scope/fallback cases. Red on the base: expected 48, received 32. Green after the change: 140ms test / 1.24s wrapper.
- Targeted root-scripts typecheck (including this guard), one-file lint, five-file formatting, three-doc MDX, internal link audit (16,755 links; zero broken), and git diff --check pass.
- Full workflow validation passes: pinned actionlint, zizmor, generated CI owner, composite inputs, conflict markers. First attempt hit an empty ambient GITHUB_TOKEN; reran the same gate with empty token variables unset, no skips or config changes.
- Full existing package-acceptance (587 tests) and targeted Docker planner (13 tests) suites pass: 600/600, 125.51s Vitest / 126.33s wrapper. The large existing integration suite exercises workflow admission, artifact identity and planner boundaries; this change adds no test cases outside its existing owning guard. Final follow-up changes only erased TypeScript contracts; runtime proof is reused.
- Author pr-simplify pass complete: one owner/one expression; YAML +2/-1, existing test +37/-5, docs +12/-5. All additions protect the scoped cap or explain it. Local independent review explicitly waived for this task. Runtime/package build is not applicable to this strategy/docs/guard-only change.
- Verified November 19, 2026: exact head `a46932bb53657107ca1875f29f56e286151c8a03` has successful [CI 44325689857](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44325689857) and [Workflow Sanity 44325662738](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44325662738), with successful CI, dependency-review and security-sensitive commit statuses. No pending or failed checks remain; three superseded dispatch/security-review cancellations are retained, not represented as successful executions. GitHub reports mergeable. [ClawSweeper completed this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201265#issuecomment-6982163587) with no findings and no before-merge items. Ready for maintainer review with the performance limitations below.

### Conditional scheduling model — not a measured gain

Same observed complete-job durations and admission order, earliest-free-slot replay; no shorter jobs, skipped rows, reordering credit, or merged containers. Retain observed sibling floor and parent overhead.

| Completed campaign | Observed targeted work | Modeled cap32 → cap48 | Conditional parent saving |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [2026.11.6 parent 44290981153](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44290981153), [candidate child 44294810205](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44294810205) | 90 jobs; 67m38s span | 4053s → 2952s | **18m21s**; parent 106m55s → 88m34s |
| [Earlier stable parent 44267376322](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44267376322), [child 44270968526](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44270968526) | 90 jobs; 68m47s span | 4123s → 2927s | **19m56s** |

These parents failed elsewhere: shortening their diagnostic tail would not turn them green. Add 5 or 10 minutes of new critical-path contention to the recent model and projected savings fall to 13m21s or 8m21s. Same nominal total work does not guarantee unchanged runner-minutes or billing if contention/retries increase.

The latest two sampled targeted matrices reached 64 combined active jobs; earlier sampled children reached 84 hosted jobs across their work. That refutes a global 32-job ceiling but does not establish spare organization capacity. Runner inventory returned 403; hosted entitlement, registry/cache/network headroom, and 48-cap failure rate remain unproven. No claim of measured speedup or cost reduction. A later authorized qualification should compare identical rows/bytes/cache policy and record admission delay, parent tail, 429/5xx, retries, and runner work without relaxing any gate.

prs.body:
Closes #201390

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on macOS, `openclaw doctor` always advises `openclaw doctor --fix` for stray `ai.openclaw.*` launchd jobs, even when `--fix` is designed to refuse that repair (non-default install identity, external service policy, active update, or another supervisor). Users follow advice that cannot help, see it on every run, and never learn the real reason.

## User Impact

Doctor now checks the same identity, policy, and supervisor gates before printing any removal hint. When it cannot repair, the per-job line and the summary name the specific reason and give a next step that works: run Doctor from the owning install/profile, remove the job through the supervisor, retry after the update, or remove the launchd job manually.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Resolve repair eligibility once, before building the report, and reuse it for both the advice and the actual repair.
- Reject the `--fix` hint when the invocation cannot repair, replacing it with a reason-specific explanation.
- Add an opt-in `repairAvailable` control to `formatForeignLaunchdJobs` so the per-job `Removable with openclaw doctor --fix.` line is accurate too. The default keeps `gateway status` output unchanged.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-foreign-launchd-jobs.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 13/13 passed, including the default-identity advice case and the four refusal cases.
- Red-on-base: reverting both source files makes all four refusal cases fail.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint clean on all three changed files.

prs.title: fix(templates): Template Add creates an agent with a reserved system ID that cannot be deleted
prs.body:
Closes #196713

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Template Add creates an agent with a reserved system agent ID (`openclaw`, `crestodian`) when the Template declares one, and that agent cannot be deleted afterwards.

## User Impact

User impact: Template Add now refuses a reserved agent ID before creating anything, the same way `openclaw agents add` does, and the error says to choose another agent ID.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Add planner only checked for collisions with configured agents, and system agents are not configured entries. It now checks the same reserved list `agents add` uses and blocks the plan with `reserved_agent_id`. That covers the CLI and the Gateway, and both an ID from the Template and one passed with `--agent-id` / `agentId`.

An earlier revision renamed the agent to `openclaw-2`; following maintainer feedback it now rejects the ID instead.

## Evidence

Real CLI built from this branch (`a7ffff098de`, includes main `0f0c5f0f6e5`), isolated state and home directory, Templates turned on in Labs:

- `templates create ./openclaw`, then `templates add ./openclaw`: exit 1 with `reserved_agent_id`; `agents list` still shows only `main`.
- `templates add ./openclaw --agent-id crestodian --dry-run`: exit 1 with `reserved_agent_id`.
- Control: `agents add openclaw` exits 1 with `"openclaw" is reserved`.
- `templates add ./openclaw --agent-id openclaw-helper`: the agent is created. (`status: partial` only because this isolated host has no model credentials for the agent's first reply.)
