prs.title: fix(state): repair private state stores after K8s fsGroup remount
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Kubernetes PVC remount with `fsGroup`, `openclaw gateway run` repairs the SQLite credential store but managed GitHub identities still fail `git push` ("Reconnect or change GitHub Identity") and Codex workers report `Worker Codex configuration directory is unsafe` — their private stores stay group-writable (`2770` dirs / `0660` files) because the startup repair only enumerated `.update-captures`, `client/credentials.sqlite`, and `control/services.sqlite`, missing `credentials/github/<scope>/<profileId>` and `codex-runtime`.

## User Impact

Users running openclaw on Kubernetes or Podman who have enrolled managed GitHub identities or Codex workers keep them after a PVC remount — no reconnect, no re-enroll. Unaffected installations see no change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend `restorePrivateStateStoreModes` to enumerate two minted-store families through their owners' naming contracts:

- **GitHub**: `credentials/github/system`, `credentials/github/personal`, and every 64-hex hashed agent key under `credentials/github/agents/<key>`, then every child matching `isManagedGitHubProfileId` (`ghp_[a-f0-9]{32}`)
- **Codex**: `<stateDir>/codex-runtime` (direct child of state root)

Each minted store is restored as a whole: directory first (descriptor-bound, `O_NOFOLLOW`, uid-match), then every regular file directly inside. `namesPlainDirectoryChainSync` refuses symlinked ancestors above the store so an alias at `credentials` or `credentials/github` cannot lend the repair to another tree.

## Review follow-up: repair owned stores without requiring unrelated ones

The previous revision bailed out entirely when the state directory contained neither `<stateDir>/.update-captures` nor an existing SQLite store, as a workaround for test fixtures that stub `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` at synthetic roots. That pre-check was wrong twice over:

- it probed `<stateDir>/.update-captures`, while the capture root is the sibling `<stateDir>.update-captures`;
- it skipped real stores whenever an unrelated one was absent, including the capture-only layout `main` already repaired.

The pre-check is gone. Every store admits itself through its own descriptor, so a state directory that holds only some stores is repaired for what it holds, and the repair makes no decision about stores it cannot see. Two regressions pin that, both with no SQLite store present: a capture root mounted alone, and minted GitHub/Codex stores mounted alone.

## Evidence

All repair paths run through `openclaw doctor --non-interactive --repair`, which invokes `ensureOpenClawStatePermissions` via `doctor-config-preflight.ts:100` and `gateway-lock.ts:531` (gateway startup path).

### Red/green on the reviewed defect

Same filesystem layouts, same code path, only `src/state/openclaw-state-db-permissions.ts` differs:

| Layout | Before (reviewed head `5cebd16`) | After (this head) |
|---|---|---|
| capture root only (no SQLite) | `2770`, not repaired | `0700`, repaired |
| GitHub profile + `codex-runtime` only (no SQLite) | `2770` / `0660`, not repaired | `0700` / `0600`, repaired |

### Driver-lane GHA upgrade proof (external repo)

Public repo `github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-privatestore-upgrade-proof`, run [42953923900](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-privatestore-upgrade-proof/actions/runs/42953923900), checked out at `42653076a7b7b3ad36e1fcc64ce1a1b138288785`. Recipe: install **latest stable** `openclaw@2026.11.3` → fixtures widened to `2770`/`0660` → driver `doctor` confirms what it can and cannot repair → tarball built from this PR head (stamped `2026.11.4`, see note) → `openclaw update` installs it over the stable driver → candidate `doctor --repair` repairs every private store → data retained.

The candidate carries the version stamp `2026.11.4` because this branch still declares `2026.11.2` in `package.json`; without a stamp above the driver's `2026.11.3`, `openclaw update` would treat the candidate as a downgrade. The stamp is the only change CI makes to the packaged tree — `dist/` and every source file come from this head.

| Fixture | Driver widens | Driver repairs | Candidate repairs | Data retained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SQLite `.update-captures/` | 2770 dir | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `client/credentials.sqlite` | 0660 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| GitHub `credentials/github/system/ghp_*` | 2770 / 0660 | ❌ (not enumerated) | ✅ | ✅ |
| GitHub `credentials/github/personal/ghp_*` | 2770 / 0660 | ❌ (not enumerated) | ✅ | ✅ |
| GitHub `credentials/github/agents/<64hex>/ghp_*` | 2770 / 0660 | ❌ (not enumerated) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Codex `codex-runtime/` | 2770 / 0660 | ❌ (not enumerated) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Capture root only, no SQLite (new) | 2770 dir | —¹ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Minted stores only, no SQLite (new) | 2770 / 0660 | —¹ | ✅ | ✅ |

¹ The two minimal layouts run against the candidate binary, after the upgrade step has replaced the driver. Both contain only the capture root / the minted stores when doctor starts; doctor then creates its own state database inside them, which is why the log later lists `client/credentials.sqlite` beside the repaired stores. The reviewed-head red check for both layouts is in the table above.

<details>
<summary>Raw proof log (trimmed to the permission checks)</summary>

```

driver: OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d)   candidate tarball: 2026.11.4

  MINTED-STILL-WIDENED (expected): codex-runtime → 2770

=== step 7: upgrade driver → candidate tarball ===
✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.11.4 (from 2026.11.3); 22 warnings need attention.
Update target: 2026.11.4

=== step 8b: permissions after candidate doctor --repair ===

600 .../proof-state/credentials/github/agents/aaaaaaaa...aaaa/ghp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef/hosts.yml
700 .../proof-state/codex-runtime
600 .../proof-state/codex-runtime/config.json
  MINTED REPAIRED (expected): codex-runtime → 700
    FILE REPAIRED (expected): config.json → 600

=== step 10: candidate repairs a capture-only state directory (no SQLite store) ===
before: 2770 .../proof-capture-only.update-captures
capture-only doctor exit=0
  [capture-only] capture root → 700 (want 700), repaired=true
  [capture-only] captured bytes retained=YES

=== step 11: candidate repairs minted stores without an installation database ===
minted-only doctor exit=0
  [minted-only] ghp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef dir → 700 (want 700)
  [minted-only] hosts.yml → 600 (want 600)
  [minted-only] codex-runtime dir → 700 (want 700)
  [minted-only] config.json → 600 (want 600)
  [minted-only] repaired=true

=== FINAL VERDICT ===
  VERDICT=PASS

Checklist:
  [driver] controls_repaired       = YES
  [driver] minted_still_broken      = YES
  [candidate] all_stores_repaired   = YES
  [candidate] data_retention        = YES
  [candidate] capture_only_repaired = YES
  [candidate] minted_only_repaired  = YES
  [upgrade]  exit_code              = 0
```

</details>

### Regression tests

15 test declarations (16 cases) in `src/state/openclaw-state-db-permissions.test.ts` covering minted-store enumeration, descriptor admission (`O_NOFOLLOW` + uid-match), ancestor alias refusal, Codex bundle repair, and the two minimal layouts above. No new test file; the added lines are covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/fsgroup-remount-minted-stores.txt` (181 lines, the ceiling growth the ratchet grants this diff).

### CI note

After rebasing onto current `main`, the previously-red `sessions-rewind.storage.test.ts` and `telegram-model-picker-prepared-gateway.e2e.test.ts` shards are green: `main` fixed the former in #196702, and the latter was an intermittent e2e flake. This head still fails four shards on tests this diff does not touch:

- `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.direct-stop-active-work.process.test.ts` — timing assertion on the shared runner's systemd shutdown budget;
- `test/loopback-ask-user-telegram-channel.test.ts` — Telegram loopback flake;
- `src/gateway/server-close.session-rewind.test.ts` — session-rewind race;
- `ui/src/e2e/screen-requester-routing.e2e.test.ts` — UI e2e flake (this file differs from `main` only because `main` advanced past the rebase point via #197001; the PR does not touch it).

All four are byte-identical to the rebase base (or, for the UI file, untouched by this diff), none appear in `git diff --name-only`, and the changed code only narrows modes on paths the process already owns. The prior `sessions-rewind.storage` failure was independently reproducible on #192552 (`agentic-gateway-methods-hosted-4`, [job 129605811557](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42748112814/job/129605811557)).

prs.title: fix: make early chat metadata reads retryable during startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Clients that reconnect during Gateway startup can read chat metadata before the first model owner publishes. Those reads currently return an unclassified snapshot-unavailable error, even though startup is progressing normally.

## User Impact

`chat.metadata` and passive `models.list` reads return a retryable `UNAVAILABLE` response with a starting message until the first usable metadata publication. Subsequent reads serve the published models. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The metadata owner records whether it has ever published prepared agent facts; an empty catch-up generation does not count. Before that first publication, it uses a startup-specific subtype of the existing model-owner-not-published contract. The chat RPC converts only that subtype; models.list already handles it. Retired owners, superseded access, shutdown, and recorded publication failures retain their existing failure behavior. `chat.startup` continues omitting unavailable optional metadata.

This chooses the established retryable outcome instead of adding timers or a wait queue. Runtime code grows by 19 lines to represent the missing lifecycle distinction and translate it at the RPC boundary. The separate measurement script is opt-in tooling. The catch-up settlement race in #195051 is separate and its lifecycle changes are untouched.

## Evidence

The real-Gateway regression holds first model publication, verifies `/readyz` is 503, and sends raw WebSocket requests. On parent `053fb62c6141c`, `chat.metadata` returned `ChatMetadataSnapshotUnavailableError` without `retryable`. With the fix, both RPCs return retryable startup responses, then return the configured model after publication. Raw transport is necessary because the ordinary test RPC helper prepares an owner itself and hides the defect.

All 99 focused runtime, lifecycle, shutdown, retired-owner, handler-authority, and WebSocket tests passed across six files (Vitest 101.49 seconds; wrapper 110.49 seconds). `pnpm check:changed` passed, including typechecking, lint, format, both export scans, and the database guards. Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. No Control UI module imports the changed server modules.

Synthetic measurement acceptance: five serial interleaved A/A/B groups on 5,000 sessions, approximately 35 GiB of agent state, and 62,000 files / 1.116 GB of workspace contents. Each group measures 5,000 pre-publication owner reads after 500 warmups, then a separate 5,000-read allocation pass. Required result: every candidate read produces retryable startup, with zero snapshot-unavailable errors. Report median/p95 elapsed time, main-thread CPU, sampled allocation, and A/A variation; investigate any >20% regression. The fixture and all five groups completed. Results follow; the owner accepted the measured startup CPU tradeoff.

These are startup owner read costs, not whole-Gateway throughput or restart-duration measurements. This path does not scan the session database or workspace. The synthetic host uses macOS/APFS, not Linux/btrfs. No live Gateway state is accessed.


## Synthetic results and tradeoff

All 25,000 candidate timing-pass reads returned the retryable starting outcome; all 50,000 A/A reads returned snapshot-unavailable. The fixture contains 5,000 sessions, a 37,790,253,056-byte agent database (35.20 GiB), and 62,000 workspace files totaling 1,116,000,000 bytes. Model-catalog load count is zero in every arm (the callback throws if invoked).

Each cell below is median / nearest-rank p95 per 5,000 reads. Five samples per arm; pooled baseline has ten. Elapsed and CPU are milliseconds; allocation is sampled bytes.

| Metric | A1 baseline | A2 baseline | B candidate | B vs pooled A median |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Owner elapsed ms | 14.450 / 15.368 | 13.782 / 14.494 | 18.223 / 19.527 | +30.7% |
| Main-thread CPU ms | 14.453 / 15.433 | 13.849 / 14.561 | 18.298 / 19.569 | +30.8% |
| Sampled allocation bytes | 17,953,816 / 18,129,792 | 17,785,152 / 17,864,808 | 12,712,024 / 13,229,104 | -28.8% |

A/A median differences are 4.8% elapsed, 4.4% CPU, and 0.95% allocation. Baseline elapsed range is 13.342–15.368 ms; candidate is 17.310–19.527 ms. Host one-minute load ranged 5.39–11.12. This is a consistent CPU tradeoff, not noise: **+0.861 microseconds CPU per early read**, or approximately 8.6 microseconds across ten startup reads. It is not a measurement of RPC latency or whole-Gateway restart time.

Investigation: separate 100,000-read CPU profiles identify error construction as the startup hot spot. An explicit subclass constructor did not improve it (18.315 ms CPU/5,000). A diagnostic-only asynchronous yield before constructing the error reduced CPU to 12.647 ms, supporting the stack-capture cost of throwing before the first await. That variant is not included: adding a scheduling step solely to flatten an error stack would complicate this bounded, immediate startup response. The proposed code remains the reviewed +19-line correction. Owner acceptance: +0.861 µs per startup read accepted by the perf lead in exchange for removing 6–10 user-visible startup errors per restart

Rerun the committed workload with:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/chat-metadata-startup-measure.ts --state-dir "$fixture"
# Baseline: same command with --owner pointing to chat-metadata-runtime.ts from
# 053fb62c6141c801fdd0f9bb2dfc3060a6fed912, retaining resolving sibling imports.
```

Final-head CI [44443188297](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44443188297) passed. ClawSweeper reviewed `0b9961ad68d1e1ebce5c5ec1c32b6b15da139e86` with no findings or open checklist items. Its runtime-proof note is covered by the running isolated Gateway regression, which uses the real startup lifecycle and raw WebSocket transport. The final test output was:

```text
PASS src/gateway/server.chat-metadata-boundary.test.ts
metadata RPCs recover from retryable startup and preserve owner isolation and publication failures (5610 ms)
Test Files  6 passed (6)
Tests       99 passed (99)
```

The test explicitly observes readyz 503 before both startup RPCs, releases first publication, waits for readiness, and verifies both RPCs return the configured model. No model inference or live deployment is involved in this metadata-only contract.

prs.title: fix: align Goal authority proof with admitted-run policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Goal authority E2E test timed out for 120 seconds after #201377 because its provider fixture waited for revocation to cancel an already-admitted turn before releasing that turn's response. That cancellation expectation contradicts the admission-time authority contract from #197557.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. The test now proves that admitted Goal work finishes, a revoked requester gets no subsequent automatic Goal turn, and explicit Stop still cancels promptly with a visible paused/interruption outcome. Existing sibling-agent restrictions and revoked-client disclosure checks remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing real Gateway, identified clients, provider transport, child settlement, and persisted history fixture. Release the admitted response after role revocation; separately require Stop to close the real provider socket before the Gateway drain settles and before the fixture releases its response. Policy refusal leaves the stored Goal active; Stop pauses it. Production LOC delta: **0**; test delta: **+51 / −30**.

Thanks @obviyus for #201377, which correctly fixed occurrence authority after admission. This updates the stale downstream test rather than restoring mid-run policy checks.

## Evidence

The unchanged test on `053fb62c6141c801fdd0f9bb2dfc3060a6fed912` times out at 120 seconds. The updated product test passes against the identical production tree. It checks persisted admitted completion, zero successor turns after revocation, prompt provider cancellation on Stop, and the persisted interruption note. Identical final-source A/A runs took 17.767 and 12.857 seconds of test time; it reuses one Gateway for three lifecycle scenarios. This is test timing, not a production performance claim.

All 174 focused tests passed across Goal continuation, scheduled operator recovery, and cron active-job suites, including current-policy rejection at the next admission. Codex autoreview of the complete local patch against the commit above is scoped-clean through P2, with no actionable findings. No schema, configuration, cache, or UI-imported module changes.

prs.title: fix: Git checkout updates no longer fail before the new release starts on a schema change or a busy database
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update` on a Git checkout install can fail right after it switches the release link and before the new release ever runs. The Gateway is still serving the old version on untouched state, but the update reports a failure anyway, in one of two ways:

- **"Agent database migration did not finish"** (`openclaw doctor`): this happens on every update to a target that bumps a database schema.
- **"data at risk (rollback-state-unverified)"** together with "Keep the Gateway stopped": this happens when the serving Gateway kept a large database busy.

Either way the link is left half-switched.

## User Impact

User impact: a Git checkout update now gets through a schema change and a busy database. The Gateway restarts into the new release, which migrates state when it starts, and the release trial settles as designed.

This needs an installed updater that contains the fix. Installs whose installed updater is `8f80fe08`, or any main build between #199706 and this fix, still fail in that updater's own process on every Git update that changes a schema. Their checkout must be rebuilt once (`git pull` and `pnpm build` in the checkout) to get a fixed updater. The candidate cannot repair this, because the installed updater runs first. The failed update's own output already offers `openclaw triage`, which hands this step to a repair agent on that machine.

Package installs (stable, beta) get the same evidence rule: they are reported as data at risk only after the new version's Doctor or boot check may have written state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause: after the switch, `inspectActivatedUpdateState` (`src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrated.ts`) applied package-install assumptions to Git releases.

- **It required the new schema before the new release had run.** A Git release runs no Doctor, and the Gateway that starts from the release migrates state at boot. So for any target that bumps a schema, the "migration did not finish" check failed every time.
- **It copied every live store** (`preserveSourceArtifacts: true`). That flag protects the database generation a package update's final Doctor captured, and a Git release captures none. Its `catch` also marked any read failure as data at risk (`rollback-state-unverified`), even though no new-version process had opened state.

Changes:

- **Git release mode** reads agent and local store versions directly, the same way the pre-activation baseline does. It skips the "migration did not finish" check before the new release starts, and it still blocks a schema that actually moved (`state-migrated-no-rollback`).
- **Positive evidence on every path.** `executeMutableUpdate` reports `candidateOpenedState`. It is false only for a Git release before its restart, and for a package install before its candidate Doctor ran (and not under `--no-restart`). The in-place Git runner stays conservative. A result that already records data at risk keeps its route. Otherwise, a store the updater cannot read becomes a one-line `state-schema-verification` warning that says what is true: no data was changed, and whether the update continues.

#201327 (merged on main today) changed the copy path itself. When every copy attempt loses to a writer on a complete WAL family, it now takes one online-backup read transaction instead of failing with `wal-copy-unstable`, so artifact-preserving reads no longer fail under load. This PR does not conflict with it: package installs keep that copy path. Git releases still need the direct read, for time and disk: on a 555 MiB agent database with a writer committing about 8 MiB/s, current main's copy read took 568–667 ms and used 555–566 MiB of extra disk per read. The direct read took 6–7 ms and used no extra disk (3 runs each). Both costs grow with the database, so a 20 GiB store means a 20 GiB copy on every update. #201327 also explains why the candidate-side recovery that an earlier revision of this PR carried is gone. With current candidates the shipped updater's copy succeeds, so the failure that recovery recognized no longer occurs; the shipped updater fails earlier, on "migration did not finish", which only an installed-updater fix can address.

## Evidence

Real `openclaw update` on an isolated macOS launchd Git checkout install (its own profile, state and port; no channels, providers or credentials), pinned to the PR head `db9a13ce` as the dev target. The installed updater is `6691acae`, the last main commit before the agent schema 42 → 43 bump; it already has the Git release layout. The agent database is 512 MiB at schema 42.

| Cell | Installed updater | Writer | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RED | `6691acae` | 8 MiB/s | `⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: openclaw doctor` with "Agent database migration did not finish … expected 43, found 42", after 425 s. Left half-switched: link on the new release, `.trial` armed, service still on the checkout, schema 42, Gateway serving the old build. |
| GREEN busy | `6691acae` + this fix | 8 MiB/s | The core behavior works: activating 6.3 s, restart, Gateway serving 2026.11.5, "version verified; channels ready; HTTP ready; core ready", agent schema 43, trial settled, service on the launcher, writer alive, nothing marked data at risk. **But the run still exits 1**, as `post-update-failed`: "SQLite database pathname changed while its worker owner is active". See Not covered. 403 s wall. |
| GREEN idle | `6691acae` + this fix | none | Same as GREEN busy, including the `post-update-failed` exit after verification. 383 s wall. |

Gateway downtime in the GREEN cells is the restart window of about 4 s; the run's verifying phase then took about 30 s. Extra disk in the GREEN busy cell: about 2.8 GiB for the release build and the state upgrade's `.pre-<build>` copies; the inspection itself adds none.

Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrated-schema.test.ts src/cli/update-cli.preactivation-inspection.test.ts src/infra/update-migrated-finalize.worker.test.ts`: 64 tests pass. The new cases fail on base for the stated reasons:
- **Git release and package-before-Doctor**, unreadable store: `rollback-state-unverified` instead of a warning.
- **Git release, unmoved schema** with a candidate schema bump: status `error`, `openclaw doctor`.

The controls pass on both base and the fix:
- package after Doctor, or a caller without the fact, still reports data at risk;
- a Git release whose schema moved still blocks;
- the in-place runner and an already-recorded risk keep their routes (`update-cli.preactivation-inspection.test.ts`).

The rendered next-action text is asserted for each outcome.

<details><summary>Checks</summary>

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, the CLI-update test type lane and oxlint on the touched files: pass.
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base <main>`: all ok.
- `pnpm check:docs`; `git diff --check`: clean.
</details>

Independent review by an Opus reviewer and a ClawSweeper rating (round 1: D/D/D) were done on the earlier, wider revision. Their findings on the remaining code are fixed: POSIX-only fixtures, truthful warning text, and the in-place and recorded-risk routes. `autoreview` does not run on this machine.

## Not covered

- **A second defect after verification, newly reachable (blocks a clean exit):** once the update gets past the false failure, the new release's boot state upgrade replaces `state/openclaw.sqlite`, and keeps the old file as `.pre-<build>`. The installed updater still holds a SQLite worker on the old file. Its post-update work then refuses with "SQLite database pathname changed while its worker owner is active; close the existing store first". It also logs "Update progress history unavailable: SQLite database file identity changed". The Gateway is already serving the new version and the result text says so, but the run exits 1 as `post-update-failed`. This PR does not change that store-lifecycle path; it needs its own fix (close or reopen the updater's state store across a Git release restart). A follow-up PR fixes it next.

- **Installed updaters without this fix** (`8f80fe08` and main builds from #199706 up to this fix): they fail every Git update that changes a schema in their own process, before the new release runs. They need their checkout rebuilt once.
- **"Update finalization left the update run nonterminal":** seen in an in-place control run. This PR no longer touches that path; it is a separate known defect.
- **Original-state capture:** it still copies the live databases; this is a separate follow-up. #201327's fallback applies there too.
- **Platforms:** macOS launchd only. The busy writer is a stand-in process, not the real Gateway's load.

prs.title: docs(voice-call): inboundPolicy "pairing" rejects unknown callers without saying why
prs.body:
Related: #164966

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `inboundPolicy: "pairing"` is a valid voice-call setting that reads like the pairing flow chat channels have, but the docs and config help never say that it only screens callers against `allowFrom`, so an operator who selects it expecting pairing requests gets every unknown caller rejected with no explanation.

## User Impact

User impact: the inbound-calls page and the config help now state what each `inboundPolicy` value accepts and that `pairing` currently applies the same caller-ID check as `allowlist` (no pairing code, no approval request; an empty `allowFrom` rejects everyone), without the realtime callback exception, which only `allowlist` has. No behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the narrow clarification recommended in the review of #164966: document the limitation and leave caller admission as it is. Whether `pairing` should later be implemented, warned about at startup, or retired through a migration stays open on the issue; this PR does not decide it, which is why it links the issue instead of closing it.

- `docs/plugins/voice-call/tts-and-inbound-calls.md`: a four-row table of the policies and a note on `pairing`, including that callbacks require `allowlist`.
- `docs/plugins/voice-call/configuration.md`: the `allowFrom` row names both policies that read it.
- `extensions/voice-call/openclaw.plugin.json`: `help` text for `inboundPolicy` and `allowFrom` (labels unchanged, schema unchanged).
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`: regenerated for the new help text.

## Evidence

The documented behavior, on main `f4b43b4714`:

- Classic calls: `shouldAcceptInbound` in `extensions/voice-call/src/manager/events.ts` handles `case "allowlist":` and `case "pairing":` in one branch that returns `isAllowlistedCaller(normalized, allowFrom)`.
- Realtime calls: `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-inbound-admission.ts` accepts when `inboundPolicy === "allowlist" || inboundPolicy === "pairing"` and the caller is in `allowFrom`; otherwise a call is admitted only if the manager records it as a callback. That cannot happen under `pairing`: `findRecentOutboundCallback` in `extensions/voice-call/src/manager/callbacks.ts` returns nothing unless `inboundPolicy` is `"allowlist"`, and the classic `allowlist`/`pairing` check then rejects the caller. So callbacks are the one place where `pairing` differs from `allowlist`, and the docs now say so (corrected after review; the first version of this PR claimed callbacks applied under `pairing` too).
- Nothing in the plugin creates a pairing or approval request for a caller.

**Running settings form.** Branch build `7ed9258cad` (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build`), `openclaw gateway run` with `plugins.entries.voice-call` enabled (`provider: "mock"`, `inboundPolicy: "pairing"`, `allowFrom: []`), Control UI at `/settings/plugins/voice-call?view=settings`, Inbound calls section.

After (this branch, footer `docs/voice-cal…@7ed9258`): both help strings render under their fields, including the corrected `pairing` wording ("the same caller check as allowlist, without callbacks").

![Inbound calls settings on this branch: help text under Inbound policy and Inbound allowlist](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64cba84e-4631-4c76-815c-27a72df3172c)

Before (same Gateway config; a build of main `f4b43b4714` plus an unrelated change outside voice-call, so the footer shows another branch name; `extensions/voice-call` and `docs/plugins/voice-call` are identical to main): neither field has help text.

![Inbound calls settings before: no help text under Inbound policy or Inbound allowlist](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be823597-947d-4e4a-9186-9d7a24b19d61)

**Checks**, in a Node 24.22.1 container on this branch:

```text
$ oxfmt --check docs/plugins/voice-call/configuration.md docs/plugins/voice-call/tts-and-inbound-calls.md
All matched files use the correct format.
$ pnpm format:docs:check
Docs formatting clean (1422 files).
$ pnpm config:docs:check
OK docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256 and docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json
$ pnpm test extensions/voice-call/src/config.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  61 passed (61)
```

The help text changes the generated config baseline hash (`config-baseline.json` and `config-baseline.plugin.json` lines in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`, regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`); the counts file is unchanged.

Not covered: no live inbound call was placed; the behavior described is read from the source above.


**Rebased onto main `443e973069` (2026-11-16)** to clear a conflict in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`. The docs and help-text commit was unchanged by the rebase (same `git patch-id`), and the hash commit was regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`.

**Review fix (`7ed9258cad`).** The first version said realtime callbacks still apply under `pairing`. They do not: `findRecentOutboundCallback` (`extensions/voice-call/src/manager/callbacks.ts:12-23`) returns nothing unless `inboundPolicy` is `"allowlist"`, and `extensions/voice-call/src/manager/events.ts:234-241` then falls back to the `allowlist`/`pairing` caller check, which rejects a recent outbound recipient who is not in `allowFrom`. The table row, the note and the `inboundPolicy` help text now say that `pairing` applies the same caller-ID check as `allowlist` without callbacks, matching `docs/plugins/voice-call/realtime-and-streaming.md` ("Under `inboundPolicy: "allowlist"`, enabled callbacks accept…"). The help text change regenerates the baseline hash again (`config-baseline.json` and `config-baseline.plugin.json` lines only; counts unchanged). The screenshot above is from this head.

Re-run on `7ed9258cad`:

```text
$ pnpm config:docs:check
OK docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256 and docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json
$ pnpm format:docs:check
Docs formatting clean (1431 files).
$ pnpm exec vitest run extensions/voice-call/src/config.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/manager/events.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  119 passed (119)
```

On the rebased head `2cd2c1078d` the wider voice-call set also passed (config, manager.async-store, manager.notify, manager/events, runtime.realtime-routing, runtime: 6 files, 169 tests). The cited source is the same on `443e973069`: `extensions/voice-call/src/manager/events.ts:51-58` (`case "allowlist":` and `case "pairing":` share the `isAllowlistedCaller` branch) and `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-inbound-admission.ts:19`.

**Rebased again onto main `059db8a7c5` (2026-11-16)** for the same generated-hash conflict (main changes `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` often). Both content commits are unchanged (same `git patch-id` for `docs/plugins` and `extensions`), and the hash was regenerated against the integrated tree. On the new head `f5454d68b`:

```text
$ pnpm config:docs:check
OK docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256 and docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json
$ pnpm format:docs:check
Docs formatting clean (1432 files).
```

The screenshot above is from `7ed9258cad`, whose docs and help text are identical to this head.

prs.title: fix(status): keep the gateway token conflict hint readable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw status` renders the `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` / `gateway.auth.token` conflict warning as unusable text (reported in #200937):

```
- OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN conflicts with gateway.auth.token: *** OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN from the shell, ~/.openclaw/.env, or launchctl env if gateway.auth.token is
```

Two separate defects stack up:

1. The producer joined the title and the remediation with `": "`, so `gateway.auth.token: Remove OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN …` reads as one `key: value` pair. `redactStatusSecrets` matches that shape and replaces the remediation's leading word ("Remove") with `***`.
2. Status applied the 160-character owner-identity bound to command-local diagnostics too, cutting the sentence mid-word. The full diagnostic is ~290 characters, so fixing the masking alone still leaves a truncated hint.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `src/gateway/auth-token-source-conflict.ts`: join title and remediation as prose (`. `) instead of `key: value`, so the redactor stops treating "Remove" as a secret value. The fix is at the producer on purpose — loosening `redactStatusSecrets` would weaken a security control that `status`, `status --all`, and the audit formatters all share.
- `src/commands/status-overview-values.ts`: split redaction from bounding. Owner ids and paths are arbitrary user data and keep the 160-character bound; command-local diagnostics are in-repo prose whose remediation is the point, so they are redacted but no longer cut.

## User Impact

Operators who hit the env-vs-config token conflict now see the actual remediation: remove the shell variable, or point `gateway.auth.token` at the environment variable. Before, the actionable verb was masked and the sentence was cut before the second option.

## Evidence

Reproduction at the production boundary (both functions are the ones `openclaw status` uses):

```
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ./probe.mts   # calls resolveGatewayAuthTokenSourceConflict + buildStatusSecretDiagnostics
RAW      : "OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN conflicts with gateway.auth.token. Remove OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN from the shell, …"
BEFORE   : "OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN conflicts with gateway.auth.token: *** OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN from the shell, ~/.openclaw/.env, or launchctl env if gateway.auth.token is"   (len 160)
AFTER    : full sentence, no `***`, ends "… if the environment variable should supply the token."
```

Regression (`src/commands/status-overview-values.test.ts`, new):

```
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/test-projects.mts src/commands/status-overview-values.test.ts
base (both src files reverted): FAIL — expected '…' not to contain '***'
with this change:              2 passed
```

Consumers re-run: `src/commands/status.usage-routing.test.ts`, `src/commands/doctor-security.test.ts`, `src/commands/status-all/format.test.ts` — 3 shards passed.

Gap, stated plainly: I could not run the end-to-end `openclaw status` reproduction on this machine. A locally installed Gateway service (different version, different token) makes `status` abort with a version-drift line and a token-mismatch error before it prints the report, so the before/after above comes from calling the same production functions directly rather than from a full CLI transcript. Anyone can reproduce end to end on a host without that service:

```
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/probe OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/probe/openclaw.json \
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=shell-side-token pnpm -s openclaw status
# config: {"gateway":{"mode":"local","auth":{"mode":"token","token":"config-side-token"}}}
```

Redaction itself is unchanged: `src/commands/status-redaction.ts` is not touched, and the existing masking test (`src/commands/status-all/format.test.ts`) still passes.

## AI Assistance

Drafted with an AI coding agent; the reproduction above was run locally and the diff was reviewed line by line.

---

```
机制对位: 症状在 src/commands/status-overview-values.ts:29-30（160 截断）与 src/gateway/auth-token-source-conflict.ts:74（": " 用 key 形式拼接被脱敏器当成凭据值），我改这两处，因为脱敏器不该被放松（它同时服务 status/status --all/audit）
复现: OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/test-projects.mts src/commands/status-overview-values.test.ts 在 base 上是 1 failed（not.toContain('***') 失败），修复后是 2 passed；另有生产函数直调的前后对照行
证据类别: 渲染层 + 生产函数直调，本机可得: 是（node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs 调 resolveGatewayAuthTokenSourceConflict 与 buildStatusSecretDiagnostics）；端到端 openclaw status 本机不可得（已装 Gateway 服务版本漂移 + token 不匹配会先中止），PR 里写明
契约核对: diagnostic 字段仅由 src/commands/status.scan-overview.ts:153 消费；脱敏规则由 src/commands/status-redaction.ts 拥有（未改）；160 上限由 src/commands/status-overview-values.ts 的 buildStatusSecretDiagnostics 拥有（改为仅约束 owner 标识与路径）
风险: 2 个生产文件 + 1 个测试文件，不跨层、不涉及状态机；未放松任何脱敏规则
```

prs.title: fix: keep queued channel recovery replies alive
prs.body:
Related: #191476

## What Problem This Solves
Matrix recovery can lose a reply when the original turn releases its channel consumer before a queued follow-up invokes retained callbacks. A real Matrix/live-model reproduction failed with `Plugin matrix consumer is closed` during recovery.

## User Impact
Queued recovery replies remain deliverable after the original turn ends. Closed-consumer and operator-authority checks remain strict. No configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made
Give queued callbacks their own consumer lifetime, independent of one-shot ingress adoption. Release that lifetime through queue-source settlement, retain all contributing consumers when collecting follow-ups, and preserve custody through overflow compaction. Recovery acquires fresh custody rather than reusing the original ingress cancellation identity. Restore same-owner values before copying prewrapped reply options so native cancellation signals retain their identity.

## Evidence
- Real baseline Matrix/live-model recovery reproduced the closed-consumer error; the first failing callback was `onModelSelected`.
- The fixed real-model scenario triggered private-final recovery, delivered the visible marker exactly once, and produced no repeat during the following eight seconds.
- Initial proof: 134 focused tests and 28 sibling tests passed; after test-file extraction, 90 affected tests passed. Core typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, build, docs checks, line-cap ratchet, and diff checks passed.
- Independent and canonical local review found no remaining actionable P0–P2 issues after collection/overflow propagation fixes.
- CI exposed a type-import cycle. Moving the callback contract into a dependency-free leaf produced zero Madge cycles and 47 passing focused tests. The subsequent CI architecture gate passed at `09e9c9d5c5ba1b2456c54a0811abb55c91f9a259`.
- CI also caught three import-order formatting errors; repository formatting fixed them. Both docs and lint failures in that run originated from these same import blocks; all docs content checks passed.
- CI job `135274685539` exposed an introduced prewrapped-options regression: `AbortSignal.any` rejected a proxied signal. The existing delivery-custody suite passed 14/14 on frozen base, failed 1/14 on the candidate, and passed after restoring native option values before copying. Expanded the focused identity test to include prewrapped options; both files now pass 31/31 tests (59.36s wrapper wall time including compiler preparation; 57.37s Vitest duration). Targeted lint and formatting pass. Fresh independent review found no P0–P2 findings and confirmed callback fencing remains intact.
- At head `333f2682172dd9ee3f2fa1a461cfa854d7287448`, CI passes architecture, docs, lint, production/test types, and the delivery-custody test shard. ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head and reported no actionable findings.

### Retained real Matrix proof — sanitized excerpts
The isolated official Matrix plugin/live-model run used frozen base `d6f628897ad7830e7cd54063c18de41c9c4cc73e`. Baseline occurrence `70079534-2004-4f61-a67f-37c0d9ec1314` timed out after recovery hit the released consumer. IDs, local paths and model/provider details are omitted below; no message content or credentials are included.

```text
2026-11-19T00:55:19.460+00:00 [source-reply/private-final]
agent produced a private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool
(message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered to the source channel
channel=matrix chars=2924
2026-11-19T00:55:19.621+00:00 [turn/execution]
visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads: channel=matrix cause=completed
2026-11-19T00:55:19.900+00:00 Error: Plugin matrix consumer is closed
```

Fixed occurrence `40d72565-7593-4cce-b9bf-823e4be426c1`, from the reviewed original production repair before subsequent CI-driven corrections:

```text
2026-11-19T01:17:33.913+00:00 [source-reply/private-final]
agent produced a private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool
(message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered to the source channel
channel=matrix chars=2671
scenario: Matrix custody real-model diagnostic — pass
Prepare Matrix live — pass
recovers a substantive private final through one message tool retry — pass
recovered=1; WARN logged=true
scenario counts: passed=1 failed=0 skipped=0 total=1
QA scenarios passed, but cleanup failed
```

The scenario requires the private-final warning, asserts exactly one matching outbound marker, waits 8000ms, and asserts the count remains one. A direct first-answer send cannot satisfy this proof. Live provider-request counters were unavailable and are not evidence of request counts. The cleanup limitation is detailed below; the live scenario was not rerun on the later CI-correction head.

## CI Failure Classification
CI run `44440362497` completed with four failed jobs. These three signatures reproduce on frozen base `d6f628897ad7830e7cd54063c18de41c9c4cc73e`; none of their test files was changed:
- `src/gateway/operator-run-cancellation.test.ts:265`: two accepted-turn cases expect device revocation to throw, but it does not. Base and candidate each report 2 failed / 16 passed; repeated in current-run job `135280128892`.
- `src/gateway/server-plugins.user-profile.test.ts:143`: role-lifetime case expects rejection, but resolves `undefined`. Base reproduces 1 failed / 3 passed; repeated in current-run job `135280128930`.
- `test/cron-message-read.integration.test.ts:727`: the `claude-cli/channel-edit/native, disabled before undefined` case lacks `toolsAllowProvenance.channelRequester`. Frozen-base targeted run reproduces the exact missing-field assertion: 1 failed / 8 skipped, 33.07s Vitest duration (37.79s wrapper). Current-run job `135280128752` has the same signature. This is not introduced by the Matrix patch.

Current-run job `135280128915` fails `test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts` because the yielded parent receives a child shutdown-completion input instead of `RESUMED_0_parent`. Important source distinction: CI tested merge `eb1e725093ef48832a1a6e36f0b771b16c4fbadb`, merging this head into `053fb62c6141c801fdd0f9bb2dfc3060a6fed912`, not the frozen branch tree alone. That base contains upstream #201544 (`82e52b648cf0`), which intentionally replaces quiet child shutdown with retained error completion. The unchanged restart fixture still expects quiet child settlement. This matches the observed failure path; exact matched-runtime baseline reproduction remains unproven. The earlier local frozen-base run failed before restart and is not evidence that this signature is inherited. No safe Matrix-scope correction is established, so the failure remains explicitly unresolved rather than reverting upstream behavior or weakening the test.

No assertions, baselines, or authority checks were weakened. CI remains red; passing gates are not a claim that all checks passed.

## Limits and Cleanup
The real scenario passed, but its QA process exited 1 during rootless Podman cleanup. Task-owned containers and networks were subsequently removed and the private service stopped; this is not reported as a wholly green QA command.

The original image/completion-plus-inbound overlap and encrypted Matrix transport were not separately exercised. This PR addresses the reproduced shared callback-lifetime failure, rather than claiming every report in #191476 is resolved.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): let nested page reclamation finish
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Nested SQLite page reclamation can wait for the foreground writer that is awaiting that same reclamation, leaving the operation and cleanup stuck. The existing WAL regression timed out on main.

## User Impact

Background reclamation requested by an active foreground writer can proceed through the existing reentrant admission path. Normal background work still waits for queued foreground work. No schema, retention, or authority policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Skip the preliminary background drain only when the current async context already owns the same physical database queue and its holder is a foreground writer. The existing reservation still checks reentrancy, identity, cancellation, and permitted keys; worker callbacks cannot borrow a worker holder.

## Evidence

- Original regression: [main CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44431353575/job/135249910992), `reclaims pages off-thread and applies current checkpoint receipts (reclaim)`, with a 120-second test timeout and 180-second cleanup timeout.
- The four causal source/test files and dependency manifests are unchanged between the failed revision and this fix's base. Configuration inventory changes only add unrelated test files.
- Formatting and normal signed-commit hooks passed. Local ClawSweeper review of `c027899907abc325f11a7ce5b47e316a166b4899..4b4afe3c735befdac35efcdb185bf9a9c2c42dfd` found no correctness or security findings (confidence 0.90).
- The unchanged WAL file passed all 4 cases: reclaim (635 ms), resource close (470 ms), shared-state close (470 ms), and periodic vacuum (857 ms). The full admission file passed all 34 cases, including foreground ordering, background cancellation, and worker-lock exclusion.
- Targeted formatting, type-aware lint, core types, and the state/logging and agent/session test-type leaves passed.
- Local proof used the checksum-pinned OpenClaw Bun 1.4.4 fork with Node 24.22.1 on macOS arm64 and a private frozen dependency install. The original failure was Linux CI; no production incident is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Exact local proof commands</summary>

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-reclamation-wal.test.ts -- --maxWorkers=1
```

The tests retain their original assertions and deadlines. The existing failing regression was reused; no duplicate test or test-only production seam was added.

prs.title: feat(ui): open the next chat after archiving the open one
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Archiving the chat you have open, from the sidebar, the chat header, or **⌘⇧A**, hides its row but leaves you on the archived conversation, with the composer replaced by "This session is archived. Unarchive it to continue the conversation." To keep working through your chats you have to click the next one every time.

## User Impact

- **Before:** archive the open chat, and you stay on it behind the archived banner. Click another chat to continue.
- **After:** archive the open chat, and the chat below it in the sidebar opens, or the one above when it was the last. Pressing ⌘⇧A again archives that one and moves on, the way archiving works in Apple Mail.

**Undo** still brings the row back instantly, without switching chats. When no other chat is listed, the archived chat stays open with its banner, as before. Archiving a chat you don't have open, or archiving from the Sessions page, never navigates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every archive entry point (sidebar row button and menu, chat header menu, ⌘⇧A, multi-select and tree archives) already goes through `archiveConfirmedSessionsWithUndo` and `holdArchive`. `session-archive-hold.ts` gains `subscribeArchiveStarts`, which runs once per archive as its Undo window opens.

The sidebar owns the visible order and session selection, so it is the subscriber (`app-sidebar-archive-advance.ts`, wired with three lines in `app-sidebar-session-navigation.ts`):

- **Order:** it keeps the order from its last render. An archive hides its rows before it starts, so a fresh read could no longer place the archived chat between its neighbors.
- **Choice:** it picks the next openable row below, then above, and skips every chat in the same archive (batch or tree).
- **Navigation:** it opens that chat through the sidebar's own `selectSession`, in a microtask after the Undo notice is shown, and only if the archived chat is still the open one.

`visibleSessionTreeInOrder` becomes public so the helper can read it; it has no side effects. There is no new Gateway call, setting, or string.

Undo deliberately does not navigate back. The existing e2e *held archive survives navigation, Undo restores it without a write* expects Undo to leave the route alone, and by then the reader may already be working in the next chat.

## Default behavior change

This replaces the current rule that archiving "keeps its conversation open" (docs, and the held-archive work in #194694). The open archived chat was a dead end: its composer is disabled, so the only next step was clicking somewhere else. Apple Mail moves to the next message instead.

The archived-chat presentation still exists and is still covered: it shows when no other chat is listed and when you go back to the archived chat. If maintainers prefer to keep staying on the archived chat as the default, this can sit behind a sidebar display option instead.

Four existing tests asserted "archiving the open chat does not navigate". They now assert the new behavior and keep their other checks:

- `app-sidebar-cases/interactions.ts` *hides an archiving current thread immediately and opens the next thread*: the thread opens once, and nothing else changes.
- `app-sidebar-cases/session-mutations.ts` *holds archive behind Undo without altering the active session's personal pin*: the pin and write assertions are unchanged; each archive of the open chat opens the next chat.
- `session-management.archive.e2e.test.ts` *keeps archive state after navigating away and back*: archiving now moves to the neighbor itself, and Back still shows the archived notice.
- `session-management.archive.e2e.test.ts` *keeps the selected session through archive refreshes and restores an empty composer*: after archiving, Back returns to the archived chat before the refreshes arrive, and every later assertion is unchanged. Its pane-title history now records the visit to the next chat.

## Evidence

Scenario: five synthetic chats, starting on "Deploy check: api-gateway". Playwright WebKit on Linux at 1280×800 with the mock Gateway fixture; the corner badge shows each key press (recording only, not part of the change). Before is `main` at 895091c9878, after is this branch.

| Before: ⌘⇧A leaves the archived chat open | After: ⌘⇧A opens the next chat |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: after Command-Shift-A, Deploy check stays open with the archived banner and a disabled composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76b1fbff-fb2d-4168-88aa-db0527944642) | ![After: after Command-Shift-A, Design review notes, the next chat in the sidebar, is open with the Undo notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7b5cec5-3b6d-496a-8101-9c4d81d9a922) |

After Undo, the archived row is back in the sidebar and the current chat stays open:

![After Undo: Design review notes is back in the sidebar while Customer import stays open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3eb1da9-1f3c-4aac-9a39-ce2abe098492)

### Recordings

After: ⌘⇧A opens the next chat; ⌘⇧A again archives that one and opens the next; Undo restores the row without switching chats.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08977ca9-77f2-4e60-ab26-3cd4c8f7f7e0

Before (`main`): ⌘⇧A leaves the archived chat open behind its banner.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0745f66-ef4f-453f-b690-811e4cec8ce9

### Tests

- **E2E** `ui/src/e2e/session-management.archive-advance.e2e.test.ts`, through the real sidebar and chat header with the mock Gateway:
  - Archiving the open chat from the header or the sidebar opens the chat below it, and Undo restores the row with no `sessions.patch` and no route change.
  - Archiving the last chat opens the one above.
  - Archiving another chat keeps the open chat.
  - With this branch's tests on `main`'s source, the first three fail and the last passes.
- **Unit** `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-archive-advance.test.ts`: below first, above for the last chat, skipping chats that can't be opened, batch archives skipping every archived chat, no navigation for other chats, outside chat routes, after disconnect or with no other chat, and no override when the reader already moved before the archive settled.
- **Checks** (Boat sandbox, head 5a949ef4082 on 895091c9878):
  - `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint on the changed files (0 findings) and oxfmt pass.
  - Unit tests pass: the new file, `session-organizer-archive`, `app-sidebar.sessions` and `app-sidebar.interactions` (219 tests).
  - Every archive e2e file passes, 7 files and 37 tests: archive, archive-undo, archive-batch, archive-automation, archived-actions, nested-archive and the new file.
- **Docs:** `docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md` (archive paragraph).

prs.title: fix(ai): round-trip LiteLLM thought signatures on openai-completions routes
prs.body:
Root cause: `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-completions-stream.ts:69` (`extractToolCallThoughtSignature`) never reads LiteLLM's `tool_calls[].provider_specific_fields.thought_signature`, and `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-completions-replay.ts:37` returns early for every non-Google endpoint, so a LiteLLM `openai-completions` route never sends Gemini's thought signature back. Strict tool-call id sanitization also cuts LiteLLM's id copy, so LiteLLM falls back to `skip_thought_signature_validator` and Gemini stops reasoning after the first tool result.

Fixes #186842.

Thanks @bluet for the detailed report and the re-test on 2026.11.5, and @wr-web for the fix. Their commits are kept as they are.

## What Problem This Solves

A custom `openai-completions` provider pointed at LiteLLM in front of Gemini 3 loses the thought signature on every tool call:

- LiteLLM returns the signature in `tool_calls[].provider_specific_fields.thought_signature` ([LiteLLM Gemini 3 guide, "Thought Signatures"](https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/gemini_3)). It may also add it to the tool-call id as `__thought__<sig>`, but only when `thought_signature_in_tool_call_id` is on.
- On the next request LiteLLM reads the signature back from `provider_specific_fields` on the tool call (or its function), then from the id suffix ([`get_thought_signature_from_tool`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/795baa77e5a26828f205c9d6f8389e60cbe36847/litellm/litellm_core_utils/prompt_templates/factory.py#L1307)). If neither has it, LiteLLM sends a dummy `skip_thought_signature_validator` signature.
- Gemini 3 needs the signatures from earlier responses sent back: a missing one means HTTP 400, and the skip value "should be a last resort as it will negatively impact model performance" ([Vertex AI, Thought signatures](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/thought-signatures)).

OpenClaw never captured that field and never sent it back, and strict id sanitization cut the id copy down to 40 alphanumeric characters. The reporter saw 0 reasoning tokens on every request after a tool result.

## User Impact

On LiteLLM-fronted Gemini routes, the signature now goes back with each tool call, so Gemini keeps reasoning after tool results. Requests to plain OpenAI-compatible providers, Google endpoints and Venice do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Capture (contributor): `extractToolCallThoughtSignature` also reads `provider_specific_fields.thought_signature` into the existing `toolCall.thoughtSignature`.
- Replay (contributor): on non-Google endpoints, `injectToolCallThoughtSignatures` sends back only signatures issued on the same route (same api, provider and model), in `provider_specific_fields.thought_signature`. Cross-route signatures, the skip-validator fallback, truncated signatures and JSON reasoning details (OpenRouter) are never sent there. Google endpoints keep `extra_content.google` as before, and id sanitization is unchanged.
- Venice (added on top): Venice already replays its own Gemini signatures in its top-level `thought_signature` field, matched per assistant turn because Venice reuses tool-call ids (#119783). Without this change Venice requests would also get the generic `provider_specific_fields` copy, which is keyed by id. The Venice adapter now drops that copy, so Venice requests stay byte-identical to main.
- Merged current `main`.

Line deltas against the merge base: production +24/-9 (stream +5/-0, replay +15/-8, Venice +3), tests +65/-56.

## Evidence

Real Gateway from source (`gateway run` + `agent --message` through the Gateway, isolated profile and state). It runs against a local LiteLLM-shaped fixture: the tool-call turn carries `provider_specific_fields.thought_signature` and the `__thought__` id suffix, and the fixture reads the continuation request the way LiteLLM does. Fixture key only. Base and candidate run from the same checkout path so request bodies can be compared.

| continuation request after the `read` tool result | main `c027899907ab` | this branch `e113e72c6bc7` |
|---|---|---|
| replayed tool-call id | `call6055144thoughtQ2lZQjRIMUZ4ZmlYdHVyZT` (signature cut off) | same |
| `provider_specific_fields.thought_signature` | absent | the issued signature |
| what LiteLLM would send Gemini | `skip_thought_signature_validator` | the real signature |
| plain OpenAI-compatible provider, both requests | | byte-identical to main |
| Venice Gemini, both requests | | byte-identical to main |

Tests: the signature table in `openai-completions-replay.google-signatures.test.ts` fails 2 rows on main (LiteLLM capture, LiteLLM same-route replay). The Venice reused-id case fails on main once the transport field is in its input. All of these pass on this branch, and so do `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` and all `openai-completions*.test.ts` files.

Observed proof lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186942#issuecomment-6997227857

Not covered: no run against a real LiteLLM and Vertex deployment (no Vertex credentials). The reporter's direct LiteLLM check shows that sending the signature back brings reasoning back (64/188/160 vs 0/0/0 reasoning tokens).

Merge danger: two-way door. The change only shapes outgoing requests and writes no state, so a revert fully undoes it. Blast radius: `openai-completions` routes to non-Google endpoints that issue thought signatures (LiteLLM, plus any other proxy that returns one) now get `provider_specific_fields.thought_signature` back on same-route tool calls.

prs.title: fix: reject message tables without a caption instead of silently dropping them
prs.body:
Root cause: `src/interactive/payload.ts:738` (`normalizeTableBlock`) drops a table without a caption by design (the presentation docs make table normalization atomic and the caption required, and Slack's `data_table` requires `caption`), but nothing in the message action path checked the caption before that drop, so the rest of the message was sent and the tool reported `deliveryStatus: "sent"` without the table.

Fixes #196312

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent sends a Slack message through the `message` tool with a table block that has no `caption`, the table vanishes. The text around it is posted, and the tool tells the agent the message was sent, so the agent reports success while the data it meant to share is missing.

## User Impact

A table without a caption is now rejected before anything is posted, with the same "`<field> required`" tool error the message tool already uses for missing inputs (`presentation.blocks[].caption required`). The agent sees the error and can retry with a caption instead of reporting a send that lost its table. Tables with a caption are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The caption is part of the documented table contract, and Slack's native data table block requires it ([Slack data table block](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/blocks/data-table-block): `caption` is Required), so rendering a captionless table would mean inventing a heading, which the docs rule out ("drops the table block instead of truncating or repairing its data"). The check now lives with the other message-action parameter parsing, right after the `presentation` JSON is parsed, so every message action rejects the table before any part is sent. It reuses the existing required-parameter error instead of adding new wording.

This adopts @indra622's PR: their commit added the check inside the send payload builder with a new error message. On top of it, the check moved to the parameter owner, uses the existing error, and the regression is folded into one test; the test-lines allocation file is dropped.

## Evidence

- Real Gateway from source (`ocx src`) with the bundled Slack plugin in Socket Mode against a local Slack Web API and Socket Mode fixture; a deterministic model calls the `message` tool with "Contract summary", a text block and a two-row table, first without a caption, then with one.
  - main `0b18f610d325`, no caption: Slack receives `chat.postMessage` with only two `section` blocks and no table, and the tool returns `deliveryStatus="sent"`, `payloadOutcomes[0].status="sent"`.
  - this PR `a8aa768ead2b`, no caption: no Slack call; the tool returns `error="presentation.blocks[].caption required"`.
  - control, with caption, both refs: Slack receives `section`, `section`, `data_table` (caption "Expiring contracts", 3 rows), `deliveryStatus="sent"`.
  - Observed proof lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196367#issuecomment-6996541780
- `src/infra/outbound/message-action-send.validation.test.ts`: the new case fails on main (the send resolves instead of rejecting) and passes here (18/18). Neighbouring send, params and runner suites pass (102 tests).

Thanks @judeKim for the clear report with both receipts, and @indra622 for the original fix.

Merge danger: two-way door. Only adds input validation; a revert restores the old silent drop. Blast radius: message tool and `openclaw message` calls that include a table block without a caption now get an error instead of a partial send; tables with captions and all other blocks are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(cli): connect through gateway.remote.edgeAuth without a Gateway token
prs.body:
Closes #199691

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw tui`, `openclaw tui --url` and `openclaw gateway call` refuse to dial a Gateway behind Cloudflare Access (or another identity-aware proxy) when the client has `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` but no Gateway token or password. A guest's device therefore never files its first pairing request.

## User Impact

User impact: a CLI configured with `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` connects to a trusted-proxy Gateway without a shared Gateway secret. On first contact `openclaw tui` gets `device pairing required` and leaves a request for the admin, as the [Cloudflare Access guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/cloudflare-access#verify) already describes. Configurations without edgeAuth, and targets on other origins, still require credentials as before. A Gateway on token or password auth still needs its credential: edgeAuth only gets the connection through the proxy, and the Gateway then refuses the missing token. A device that has never connected pairs through `openclaw tui`; its `openclaw gateway call` now says so instead of answering with a bare `missing scope: operator.read`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three local prechecks reject a connection that has no token, password or stored device token: one in `callGatewayWithScopes`, `ensureExplicitGatewayAuth` for `--url` targets, and the TUI's connection resolver. None of them knew that the proxy authenticates the upgrade. Each now skips the shared-credential requirement when edge-auth headers are configured for the target's origin, using the existing `gatewayEdgeAuthValueForTarget` origin match. The Gateway's device pairing then decides access, so nothing new is trusted on the client.

First pairing stays in `openclaw tui`. `openclaw gateway call` is read-only, so on a device that has never connected it has no device identity to pair; the Gateway accepts the connection and refuses the method with `MISSING_SCOPE`. When edge-auth headers are set, the call has no device identity and the Gateway answers `MISSING_SCOPE`, the error now adds `Fix: this device is not paired with this Gateway yet. Run \`openclaw tui\` once to pair this device, ...` (`withEdgeAuthPairingHint` in `src/gateway/call-device-auth.ts`). When the call was given `--url`, the command in the hint keeps it (`openclaw tui --url <url>`), as the existing stored-device-auth recovery message does, because a bare `openclaw tui` can select another Gateway, such as a local one. `call.ts` is over its line cap, so its edge-auth header lookup is inlined, as the TUI's already is, to keep the file from growing.

`docs/cli/tui.md` and `docs/gateway/remote.md` say that, when the Gateway uses trusted-proxy auth, the first connection through edgeAuth needs no token and sends a pairing request, and that a Gateway on token or password auth still needs its credential.

## Security

Based on a source comparison against `main`, the CLI connects through Cloudflare Access as another interface to the same Gateway, using Access headers instead of the web UI's browser cookie. Both paths use the same server authentication, scope caps and role limits. This change grants no new scopes. Access headers do not replace Gateway token or password authentication.

New TUI devices still need pairing approval under the Gateway's existing policy. A fresh `openclaw gateway call` can connect without a device identity, but the server clears its claimed scopes. That device-less session receives scoped access only through explicitly configured identity grants, capped by role limits, as with the existing device-less web UI path. Without those grants, pair through `openclaw tui` before making scoped calls.

## Evidence

- **Tests:**
  - New `src/gateway/call.edge-auth.test.ts` (6 cases) and one new case in `src/tui/gateway-chat.connection.test.ts`.
  - Pairing hint: an edgeAuth device with no identity that gets `MISSING_SCOPE` now sees the `openclaw tui` hint; without this change that case fails with the bare `missing scope: operator.read`. With `gateway.mode: "local"` and an explicit `--url`, the hint names `openclaw tui --url <url>`; that case fails on `d2fade98ea1` with the bare `openclaw tui` hint. A device with an identity keeps the bare message on both. `call.test.ts` 91/91.

prs.title: fix: update the checkout a macOS Gateway actually runs
prs.body:
Related: #200833

## What Problem This Solves

When a macOS LaunchAgent still starts a Git checkout, clicking **Update** in the Web UI or typing `/update` can select a new release on disk while the Gateway keeps serving the old checkout. A later update can then mistake a release that never served for the build it should roll back to.

## User Impact

With the corrected updater installed, both Web UI entrypoints update the checkout the service actually starts. Services already using the stable launcher keep their existing release-switch behavior. This is preventive: it does **not** bootstrap the already-affected `5484e18dab2b` or `caa595355fe6` updaters. Those builds choose the update path before invoking the target.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both entrypoints submit `update.run`, so the decision belongs in the shared updater, not in the UI. On macOS, a Gateway-initiated update uses the existing in-place transaction if the service does not own the selected release. A later independently started update also stays in place if an unused selection already exists. Neither path adopts, deletes, or repoints that selection. Service ownership and self-install safeguards are unchanged.

## Evidence

**408 focused tests passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed** on the independently reviewed diff against `8f2cfd47eac1d600a779780a5462def8b8b997ce`. Both Web UI entrypoints submitted exactly one `update.run`. These are Linux fixture and repository tests, not native macOS end-to-end proof.

- In one persistent fixture, checkout A updated to C while the unused slot still selected B. An ordinary restart served C. When the next Dashboard target D refused to start, rollback and another restart both served C's full build ID (`f1739a6fad2c60fee75a498aadd124192d22a513`), not B. The original A/B release trial stayed at zero attempts.
- An already converted service retained launcher rollback; a fresh Linux checkout still converted and restarted on the target. Core typecheck, targeted lint, formatting and docs-link checks passed. The release regression suite also passed on a separate Node replay (12/12; not added to the 408).

No native macOS Dashboard click, launchd restart, reconnect, or live target RPC build ID was verified. Independent focused review found no actionable findings.

## Worked on by

- @hannesrudolph

<!-- openclaw-publication:d77a55d0-9954-46b2-97fb-1494ff502806 -->

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8f492acc-7abb-4437-96b2-16b2963ccc60)

prs.title: fix(gateway): recover completed waits after restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A caller can disconnect after a successful chat turn and miss the reply. Replacing the Gateway used to make `agent.wait` time out for the original run ID even when an identical retry did not execute the tool again.

## User Impact

An authorized caller can recover the successful result and its original timestamps after a restart when the Gateway opens a single saved session with one identifiable initiating input. Steering inputs do not own that result. Multiple saved sessions, incomplete or oversized history, and ambiguous input ownership fall back to the ordinary wait timeout. Live observations take precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway keeps at most one candidate from its startup session projection. After a live-cache miss, it checks the stored run ID and the initiating input's byte-exact idempotency key in a single bounded read. A later change of run ownership invalidates the candidate. The wait checks for a current reservation again when the read completes. A recovered result must pass the target session’s read policy. An unreadable draft follows the same wait path as a missing run. A positive wait deadline includes the recovery read, and a late read cannot replace a timeout. The fix uses existing session data.

## Evidence

- The public wait handler and SQLite regression tests exercise a steering key that differs only in whitespace, a concurrent reservation in another session, and a reused ID hidden by a later run across restarts. The public RPC test checks an owner and a nonmember with the view role against the same draft. A separate timing test delays a successful recovery read beyond the caller’s deadline. The plugin test also covers a nonmember caller.
- In an isolated upgrade test, the caller disconnected after the turn started. The original run ID returned `ok` before retry and on six subsequent waits. An identical retry preserved the tool call ID and random output, with exactly one execution. A fresh request produced a second execution and a different output.
- The session identity ratchet passed with its existing baseline.

prs.title: fix(agents): continuation-skip turns tell the model its workspace instructions were removed
prs.body:
Related: #196122

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `contextInjection: "continuation-skip"`, every continuation turn on routes that pin the system prompt (direct Anthropic, official OpenAI Responses) tells the model that AGENTS.md, USER.md, MEMORY.md and every heading inside them were "(removed)".

## User Impact

On those routes, skipped turns keep the workspace instructions the model already has, without a system update revoking them. Skipped turns still send no workspace files, and an explicit `contextInjection: "never"` still announces the removal. Sessions that already received a false removal from an earlier skipped turn get their files redelivered once on the next skipped turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

A skipped continuation withholds files that the pinned prompt prefix still carries, but the prompt series diffed the file-less prompt against that prefix and reported each Project Context section as removed. The bootstrap stage now reports that it withheld already-delivered context, and the pinned series reuses its own Project Context block for that comparison, placed inside the framed stable region (before `<!-- /openclaw:attempt:STABLE -->`, or the cache boundary when unframed). If the saved comparison state already lost the block, the block comes from the admitted prefix, which still has it.

Scope: this does not change what unpinned routes (OpenRouter, most OpenAI-compatible providers) receive on skipped turns. Whether those routes should keep workspace files under `continuation-skip` is the separate product question in #196122; this PR leaves the #154923 behavior as is.

## Evidence

- Regression in `session-prompt-state.test.ts` built from real `buildAttemptSystemPrompt` output (with STABLE/DYNAMIC framing): on a pinned series, a withheld turn emits no update; redelivering unchanged files emits nothing; a removal without the withheld flag reports `(removed)` for the file and its inner headings; a comparison state that already lost the files redelivers them (`Be brief.`) once.
- Mutation checks: ignoring the STABLE terminator makes the "no update" assertion fail; dropping the admitted-prefix fallback makes the redelivery assertion fail.
- `session-prompt-state.test.ts`: 36 passed. `tsc` for `tsconfig.core.json`, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json`, `tsconfig.scripts.json`: no errors in changed files or for `workspaceContextWithheld`. `check:test-lines-ratchet` passes with the allocation. `oxfmt --check` / `oxlint` clean.
- Evidence gap: I have not captured a live provider request on a pinned route. Pinned routes require a direct Anthropic or official OpenAI endpoint with a real key, so the existing loopback Gateway fixture (`gateway.continuation-skip-bootstrap.integration.test.ts`) resolves as unpinned and cannot show this path. `attempt-bootstrap-prepare.test.ts` hits `EMFILE` on Windows for 14 cases, identically on unmodified `main`.
