prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search
prs.body:
Related: #101422 Supersedes #177868 by @CheekyHobson (closed for inactivity on 2026-11-18): their reviewed head `a2008ab09`, ported onto current main with co-author credit on the commit, plus the proof ClawSweeper asked for. ## What Problem This Solves Generated dreaming reports under `memory/dreaming/` are indexed like curated notes and crowd them out of memory search, and there is no setting to exclude paths inside the default memory folders. ## User Impact User impact: operators can set `memory.search.excludePaths` (globally or per agent), for example `["memory/dreaming/**"]`, to keep matching workspace files out of memory search and file watching. - Unset or empty changes nothing. The index scope hash is identical to the one 2026.11.5 writes, so this setting adds no rebuild on upgrade. - Setting or changing the list is a scope change, like changing `extraPaths`: `openclaw memory status` reports it, vector search pauses, and `openclaw memory index` rebuilds and drops the excluded rows. - Search only: excluded files are not deleted, `memory_get` can still read them, `memory forget` still scrubs them, and short-term recall/promotion eligibility is unchanged. - Patterns are workspace-relative globs. A leading `./` or `/` and a trailing `/` are accepted (`memory/dreaming/` is the same as `memory/dreaming/**`), and per-agent lists add to the global list. ## Why This Change Was Made One workspace-relative glob check, using the same minimatch options as the `extraPaths` matcher beside it in the memory host SDK (so patterns behave the same on Node and Bun), is applied where search scope is decided: file discovery (local and remote workspace providers), watcher eligibility, and the index scope hash. Shared watchers include the exclusions in their selection keys, so agents with different exclusions on one workspace rebaseline when one joins or leaves (the P2 ClawSweeper found on #177868). **Portable glob matching (ClawSweeper's 2026-11-09 review on `05585b7`):** the exclusion matcher called `path.posix.matchesGlob`, which Bun implements with `Bun.Glob`: extglobs never match and wildcards match dotfiles, so `["memory/dreaming/**/!(*.keep).md"]` excluded a report on Node but not on Bun. Main's #194912 had just moved the `extraPaths` matcher to minimatch for the same reason. `1463f6e` moves those minimatch options into one shared constant and uses it for `excludePaths` too, with compiled matchers cached per configured list. Results on Node are unchanged; on Bun they now match Node. **Pattern spellings (`2b7dc7f`):** gitignore-style spellings such as `memory/dreaming/`, `./memory/dreaming/**` or `/memory/dreaming/**` excluded nothing. `resolveMemorySearchIndexConfig`, which every reader (scan, watcher, scope hash, remote file worker) gets its settings from, now normalizes each entry once: trim, drop empty entries, use `/` separators, strip one leading `./` or `/`, turn a trailing `/` into `/**`, and dedupe in order. The matcher is unchanged. The docs and help example drop `memory/.dreams/**`: that folder only holds `.txt` and `.json` dreaming state, which memory search never indexes. Changes compared with #177868 at `a2008ab09`: - Rebased onto main: the scope hash goes through the single `resolveConfiguredMemoryScopeHash()` owner, and the matcher is exported from `plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-fs`, the subpath #181891 narrowed the file worker to, instead of `engine-storage`. Both are private local-only subpaths, so this adds no third-party SDK contract. - The matcher lives in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts` beside `matchesExtraMemoryPathEntry` instead of core `src/memory/root-memory-files.ts`. - Added the config field label, corrected the docs about the rebuild step, and linked the setting from the dreaming docs. - Tests: replaced the 13 s CLI e2e case with a manager test of about 4 s that mirrors two unforced `openclaw memory index` runs (the real CLI run is below). Dropped a test that indexed an excluded file through a private method, a `selectionKeys` shape test covered by the join/leave behavior test, a worker integration test that still passed with the P2 fix reverted, and (after ClawSweeper's review) a test that only checked the worker request shape. Size against main `4484f83`: production +102/-21 in 15 files (including moving main's glob options into the shared constant); tests +159/-3; docs +18/-4; generated baselines +3/-3. (#177868 was +439/-18 in 33 files.) ### Maintainer decision needed #101422 asks for both search exclusion and recall/promotion eligibility control. This PR is the narrow first stage: search discovery, watching, and index scope only, with defaults and promotion safeguards unchanged. ClawSweeper's review of #177868 recommended approving that narrow search stage and leaving recall inclusion and diagnostics to follow-up work; the alternative is one combined search+recall include/exclude design. An operator on #101422 said the search-only step covers their need. Config surface: `pnpm config:docs:gen` raises the core count by 4 (2656 -> 2660 on main `4484f83`) for `memory.search.excludePaths` and `agents.entries.*.memory.search.excludePaths`, each with its `.*` item path. That is the new setting itself. ## Evidence Real runs on `59298b8` (on main `176f2ff`), starting from the latest stable release, `openclaw@2026.11.5` from npm (installed with `--ignore-scripts`; the CLI runs without the package's install scripts). The current head `19a3563` adds only a merge of main `4484f83`. Earlier runs from 2026.11.4 on `ddb2348`, from 2026.11.3 on `c210875`, from 2026.11.2 on `1463f6e` and on `05585b7` (before the portable-matcher change), from 2026.11.1 on `6d9ace7` and from 2026.10.10 on `b607675` showed the same behavior. Synthetic workspace: 3 curated files (`MEMORY.md`, `memory/backups.md`, `memory/garden.md`) and 7 generated reports (5 light, 2 REM, one REM report containing only "No strong patterns surfaced."). Isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` under `env -i`, Node 26.12.1, and a local OpenAI-compatible embeddings stub on 127.0.0.1 (deterministic vectors, no provider calls). **Upgrade from 2026.11.5 and existing data:** 2026.11.5 builds the index (10 files, 10 chunks). After this branch's `doctor --fix` (main's agent-database migrations since 2026.11.5, v38 -> v42), the existing index loads clean (`Dirty: no`) and returns the same results and scores as 2026.11.5, before any re-index. With `excludePaths` unset, `memory index` keeps the stored scope hash, the chunking version and every stored chunk row (same count and same fingerprint over `id`, `path`, `hash`). This PR adds no database schema or stored fields; the scope hash changes only when `excludePaths` is set. The branch build prints main's version string, 2026.11.4, because 2026.11.5 shipped from a release branch. **Opting in:** setting `excludePaths` marks the index dirty with a scope change and pauses vector search until a rebuild, both shown in `memory status`. `memory index` then drops the 7 reports and keeps the 3 curated files; the curated note ranks first, and an edit refreshes it.
Terminal output (paths redacted to $OPENCLAW_HOME) ```text $ openclaw --version # npm openclaw@2026.11.5 OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.240 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.235 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.229 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.224 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.219 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 # stored index identity (2026.11.5): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (2026.11.5): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw --version # this branch OpenClaw 2026.11.4 (59298b8) $ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive # main's state migrations since 2026.11.5 Upgraded agent database schema in $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: v38 -> v42 $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/10 files · 10 chunks Dirty: no $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main # existing 2026.11.5 index, before any re-index 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.240 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.235 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.229 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.224 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.219 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. # stored index identity (this branch, no excludePaths): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (this branch, no excludePaths): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw config set memory.search.excludePaths '["memory/dreaming/**"]' --strict-json Updated memory.search.excludePaths. Restart the gateway to apply. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/3 files · 10 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index scope changed (owner: configuration, code: scope) Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 3/3 files · 3 chunks Dirty: no # indexed rows by path: {"path":"MEMORY.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/backups.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/garden.md","chunks":1} $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. # edit memory/backups.md: 02:30 -> 03:15 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 03:15 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. ```
**Pattern spelling on `2b7dc7f`:** the same synthetic workspace with a trailing-slash pattern, `["memory/dreaming/"]`, which matched nothing before `2b7dc7f`.
Terminal output ```text $ openclaw --version OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (2b7dc7f) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.249 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.243 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.238 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.232 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.227 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 $ openclaw config set memory.search.excludePaths '["memory/dreaming/"]' --strict-json Updated memory.search.excludePaths. Restart the gateway to apply. $ openclaw config get memory.search.excludePaths [ "memory/dreaming/" ] $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/3 files · 10 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index scope changed (owner: configuration, code: scope) Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 3/3 files · 3 chunks Dirty: no $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. ```
**Gateway watcher:** a throwaway loopback Gateway with `excludePaths` set. One agent turn opens the Gateway's default memory manager and its watcher: a local chat-completions stub calls `memory_search` once, through `dispatch_action`, because current main keeps `memory_search` behind Tool Search for this model. Then, with no further CLI calls, a new dreaming report is written and the curated note edited: the watcher refreshes the note within about 2 s and never indexes the report.
Terminal output ```text $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw gateway run --bind loopback ... # throwaway Gateway [gateway] ready $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "When does the nightly backup run?" # stub model calls memory_search once via dispatch_action Done. tool call: dispatch_action {"id":"memory_search","args":{"query":"nightly backup"}} # memory_search result paths (from the stub log): memory/backups.md # indexed memory/ rows before edits: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # wrote memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-29.md and edited memory/backups.md (02:30 -> 04:45); no CLI calls from here # after the Gateway watcher sync (~2s), plus 5s more: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 04:45 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # dreaming rows: {"dreamingRows":0} ```
**Regressions fail without the fix:** - `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` "rebaselines shared exclusions when a differently scoped agent joins and leaves" fails with `excludePaths` removed from `selectionKeys` ("expected setScopes to be called once, but got 0 times"). - `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` "drops generated Dream reports once excluded and keeps curated edits fresh" fails when the config resolver drops `excludePaths` (the report is still found). - `internal.test.ts` "keeps generated dreaming reports out of default and overlapping extra paths" also lists files with `memory/dreaming/**/!(*.keep).md`. With the old `path.posix.matchesGlob` matcher, `listMemoryFiles` under Bun still returns the report: on stock Bun 1.3.14 it lists `memory/current.md, memory/dreaming/light/pinned.keep.md, memory/dreaming/light/report.md`, and with `1463f6e` only `memory/current.md, memory/dreaming/light/pinned.keep.md`. On Node both matchers agree, so the Node run passes either way; the CI shard that runs this test (`checks-node-changed-compact-large-6`) sets up the pinned Bun 1.4.4 test runtime. **Changed test files** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on `685db0c`, same test code as `8eb4b7b`): | File | Result | Wall | Vitest duration | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` | 29 passed | 48s | 41.65s | | `manager-reindex-state.test.ts` | 49 passed | 40s | 36.19s | | `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` | 11 passed | 71s | 64.91s | | `watch-policy.test.ts` | 6 passed | 47s | 41.51s | | `internal.test.ts` | 43 passed | 4s | 749ms | | `memory-search.test.ts` | 39 passed | 46s | 42.06s | Vitest time is mostly cold transform; the new manager case takes about 4 s and the other new cases take 1-24 ms. **Checks:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` on `83eb31b` (main `200afde`, same code) passes typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), lint, format, config docs baseline, Plugin SDK package exports, plugin boundaries and the other changed-file guards. Three lanes fail outside this PR: wrapper shadowing (`buildSkillWorkshopPromptSection`) and the public Plugin SDK surface budget (`agent-harness-runtime`) fail identically on clean main `200afde`, and the dead-export scan lists only auto-reply, gateway and UI exports this PR does not touch. The `pnpm check:docs` content checks pass. Test lines grow by a net +154, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/memory-search-exclude-paths-188294.txt`: default scope-hash compatibility, the shared-watcher rebaseline, discovery and portable (Node/Bun) glob matching, and the exclusion rebuild. **PR CI:** CI has not run on the current head `19a3563` (merging main `4484f83`) or on the five heads before it: GitHub holds this fork PR's workflows until a maintainer clicks "Approve and run" (`action_required`), so `openclaw/ci-gate` shows failure until CI completes. The last completed run, on `fc2ef72`, passed 72 checks; its three failing memory-core tests are in files this PR does not touch, failed the same way on main without this PR, and main fixed them in #197543. Earlier red runs also came from main and were fixed there. Merges of main conflicted only on the generated config baseline, which was regenerated each time. The full CI history is in this description's edit history. **Local review:** autoreview, Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode against `upstream/main`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, "patch is correct" (0.87). It ran on `685db0c`, before the rebases onto `200afde` and `f980e01`, which changed only the base and the generated baseline files. For `2b7dc7f`: autoreview with the Claude engine, local mode, P0–P2: scoped-clean, "patch is correct" (0.8). On `2b7dc7f`, `memory-search.test.ts` (39/39; the updated case fails on `e768746`), `schema.help.quality.test.ts`, `internal.test.ts` and `workspace-memory-client.test.ts` pass, as do `tsgo:core`, oxlint, oxfmt, `check:docs`, `config:docs:check` and the test-line ratchet. On `19a3563` (main `4484f83`), `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `config:docs:check`, `prompt:snapshots:check`, oxfmt on this PR's files, `check:docs` and the test-line ratchet (net +154, covered by the allocation) pass, and so do the touched tests plus neighboring memory tests (16 files). Locally, one `cli.test.ts` test from main's #197543 (`fails index --force after full verification records orphaned provenance`) fails; it fails the same way on main `176f2ff` without this PR. Not covered: Windows paths (the matcher normalizes `path.sep`) and a live remote node workspace (the harness test checks that list and watch requests carry `excludePaths`).

prs.title: fix: explain why Doctor cannot restore a scheduled job’s account
prs.body:
Follow-up to #200653. Related: #200600.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor --fix` silently skipped a scheduled job with a stale account binding when no usable upgrade receipt remained. The operator saw neither the affected job nor how to get it running again.

## User Impact

Doctor names the job, says it was left unchanged, and shows commands to list the agent’s accounts and explicitly select the intended one. A healthy job does not get a warning just because there is no receipt.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor now asks the existing credential owner to verify the saved binding even when there are no receipt paths to try. A matching current account stays quiet; a verified old path can still be repaired. A missing or nonmatching receipt never grants authority to switch accounts. Schedules, enabled state, and run history are not changed by the new diagnostic.

## Evidence

On an isolated Gateway, a job created on the latest stable release (2026.11.5) ran successfully, then failed after an affected upgrade because its saved account no longer matched. A second, healthy job ran against the same local test provider. With the genuine upgrade receipt moved aside, `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` built from this PR’s exact tree exited 0. It warned only about the stale job. No production jobs or credentials were used.

<details><summary>Redacted Doctor output and before/after checks</summary>

Job ID redacted; terminal wrapping removed:

```text
Automation StaleFixture (<job-id>): inference account was not migrated: The saved account no longer matches and no usable upgrade receipt proves it is the same account. The job was left unchanged. Inspect available accounts with openclaw models auth list --agent main, then explicitly adopt the intended stored account with openclaw automations edit <job-id> --model 'standin/fixture@<profileId>'.
```

There was no warning for `HealthyFixture`. After restarting the disposable Gateway on the candidate, `cron.get` confirmed unchanged IDs, names, creation times, schedules, enabled flags, payloads, delivery, session targets, account bindings and runtime state for both jobs. `cron.runs` returned exactly the same entries before and after Doctor: two for the stale job (one successful release run, then the upgrade refusal), one successful run for the healthy job. Doctor neither rebound nor replayed either job.

</details>

The regression failed on unchanged `main`: Doctor returned no warnings for either stale job. Both Doctor account migration suites passed (23 tests), including the case where a receipt exists but cannot prove this job’s account. Scoped lint and formatting passed.

## Worked on by

- @VACInc

prs.title: fix: keep Code Mode usable after read-only workers retire
prs.body:
Related: #198187

## What Problem This Solves

Fresh Code Mode workers can run out of their default 64 MiB heap before executing even a no-tool script after enough read-only database workers retire. Departed workers leave database references behind, keeping closed databases' metadata in the startup data inherited by every new worker.

## User Impact

Code Mode, including automation trigger scripts, can keep starting after read-only database workers retire without increasing the heap allowance or restarting the Gateway. No migration, configuration change, or operator action is required.

This repairs a reproduced path to the failure in #198187. The reporter's specific 28–37-hour traffic pattern has not been captured, so this PR does not claim to exclude every other possible source of startup-data growth.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read-only task workers now use the same native-exit admission cleanup as other workers. That owner settles interrupted work, removes departed references, and lets the final closed database release its metadata while preserving live siblings.

The change removes an exception rather than adding a cache or another lifecycle owner. Production is net -1 line; regression coverage is +39 lines. Permissions, read-only admission, model eligibility, native harnesses, executor isolation, and the default heap allowance are unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Reproduced the reported startup heap failure on current main:** after 800 real agent databases were opened, read by real read-only workers, and closed after those workers exited, all 800 closed admissions remained inherited. A fresh no-tool Code Mode worker failed with the exact 64 MiB runtime_unavailable heap-exhaustion message before bridge dispatch. Its heap rose from 14.2 MiB initially to 53.2 MiB after 700 closes.
- **The same 800-database workload passes with this fix:** zero closed admissions remain, and the fresh worker completes with approximately 14.8 MiB of heap under the unchanged allowance. Every intermediate fresh-worker checkpoint also passed. The scaled reproduction is kept out of routine CI; the committed regression protects the owning lifecycle directly.
- **Regression red/green:** both retained-native-handle and explicitly-closed-handle cases fail on the base because the exited worker remains referenced. Both pass after the repair, while the host connection remains usable and final database retirement succeeds. The three-test file takes about 3.3 seconds of local test execution, including about 1.5 seconds for the new cases; compiler preparation is separate. Per-file CI timing has not been extracted.
- **Sibling proof:** 88 tests across five files pass, including direct/retained native custody, stale admission snapshots and live siblings, shared-state readers, plugin model-catalog readers, and snapshot staging. Production and focused test typechecks, targeted lint/format, and git diff --check pass.
- **Sustained real Gateway acceptance passed:** a 60-minute run completed 888 real tool-bearing agent turns, 2,341 persisted automation-gate evaluations, and indexing of 444 session transcripts, with no workload, gate, or provider-fixture errors. At the same 888-turn work count and approximately 60 minutes, agent-database positive references were 131 on the base versus 16 with the fix; quarantine zero-reference cells were 133 versus 17. The fixed run peaked at 18 in each category instead of accumulating departed workers. The workload includes four concurrent sessions, nested shell/memory calls, 20 gates, reset/delete churn, and keyword-only indexing. This complements the causal OOM replay; a healthy hour alone is not treated as proof against the original uptime report.
- **Review:** independent P0–P2 source/lifecycle review found no issues. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; local autoreview (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, P0–P2) of c5ef395ba720…a82250946c31 with the surrounding lifecycle source supplied completed scoped-clean. Published head f7d99c17f534 is tree-identical to the reviewed candidate. The automatic hosted ClawSweeper review has started on that published head; no duplicate review request was posted.
- **Exact-head CI remains blocked:** [run 44432331724](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44432331724) passed the changed Node, type, lint, and security checks but failed [checks-ui-e2e (1/4)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44432331724/job/135253321355). The failing case is the cached-reader, two-round history-refresh scenario in chat-snapshot-text-fidelity.e2e.test.ts: the mocked browser reader anchor moved about 21 pixels. The repository classifier reports unknown attribution because no matching main job was available. One focused untouched-base attempt and one published-head replay passed (one selected test, five skipped each); passing replays do not resolve or establish inheritance of the CI failure. The published-head replay used the CI Node 24.22.1 runtime. Source inspection found the scenario uses a mocked WebSocket/Vite preview, not the changed server worker-start callback. CI ordering/environment effects remain unresolved. No hosted rerun, re-push-for-green, weakened assertion, or bypass was used.

The workload uses synthetic isolated state and a loopback model-response fixture, not a paid/live inference provider. No live Gateway was changed or restarted.

## Contributor credit

Thanks to @alexph-dev for the issue report and Vincent Koc (@vincentkoc) for requesting and directing this repair.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/43ff77dc-01d9-443c-87ee-fa92f18788da)

prs.title: fix: avoid duplicate replies while delivery checks are retrying
prs.body:
Related: #200553

## What Problem This Solves

A final reply can reach its destination even when the send response is lost. If the channel's follow-up delivery check then times out, OpenClaw currently treats that retryable lookup failure as permission to send the reply again, instead of retrying the check. That can duplicate replies when a channel does not deduplicate repeated sends.

## User Impact

Final replies stay queued for another delivery check when the channel reports a retryable reconciliation failure. A later receipt completes the original delivery without sending another copy. Proven-unsent retries and the existing bounded fallback for channels without reconciliation remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing replay-policy owner now honors the adapter's retryable unresolved verdict. Live recovery also leaves deferred lookup custody with the queue instead of retiring it when that lookup consumes the remaining retry budget; the next recovery pass can still confirm an already-sent message. No new configuration, schema, storage fields, retry budget, or adapter API is introduced.

This deliberately preserves the loss-versus-duplicate policy introduced in #200553 for channels that cannot reconcile. It fixes a narrower case where reconciliation can recover but its temporary failure was being bypassed. Related open #197000 concerns message-tool outcome reporting and Matrix SDK behavior, not this queue-recovery repair.

## Evidence

- Two production-path regressions cover returned and thrown reconciliation failures. On base a90c5419b779df517ea3c3ea0bee0b37e87f85ac, each records two visible effects in a synthetic non-idempotent recipient sink after a lost acknowledgment. With the fix, each records one send, retains the unresolved queue entry, accepts the later original receipt, and suppresses another request for the completed intent.
- 88 focused delivery/recovery tests pass, including proven-not-sent retry, pending queue completion, reconciled-as-sent, no-reconciliation fallback, and late receipt/cancellation controls. Runner wall time: 194.53s.
- 77 outbound payload and message-action consumer checks pass. Runner wall time: 75.59s.
- Targeted messaging TypeScript check, lint for all three changed TypeScript files, formatting for all four files, and git diff --check pass.
- Refreshed-base validation: on b96a3f2dacfaef47fa7abb004bbe3222ba147cb4, 21 focused queue-integration and final-text recovery tests pass (89.85s runner wall), along with the messaging TypeScript shard, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks. The four-file patch is byte-identical to the independently reviewed candidate; the earlier 165-test evidence above remains bound to a90c5419b779df517ea3c3ea0bee0b37e87f85ac.
- The unit/integration proof above uses local isolated state and synthetic channel destinations; the separate real-client/local-service proof below extends that evidence. No live external service or model was used. No packaging/runtime-import boundary changed, so no package build was required.
- Independent native-agent source review at P0–P2 found no actionable findings in the complete transferred semantic change against base a90c5419b779df517ea3c3ea0bee0b37e87f85ac. The source owner/caller review was separate from implementation; tests were not independently rerun. Managed Auto Review failed with a missing handoff response file and produced no report; no Auto Review pass is claimed.

### Real Matrix client and local Synapse behavior proof

Executed published head 14e94f774a0ef4cf7845cfe1f241e2c1d9d32f31 against a separately launched Synapse 1.165.0, with the production Matrix adapter and matrix-js-sdk 44.0.0, synthetic accounts/rooms, and a loopback fault proxy. Send, reconciliation and queue owners were not stubbed. Baseline comparison used b96a3f2dacfaef47fa7abb004bbe3222ba147cb4. No production service, real-user credentials or external model was used.

The proxy withheld the acknowledgment only after Synapse had accepted the event; an independent recipient observed that event. The sender was deliberately SIGKILLed, and a fresh sender process recovered the actual durable state after lease expiry. HTTP 503 responses caused the retryable lookup failures.

Sanitized observations:

| Observation | Accepted transaction PUTs | Recipient events | Durable state |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Candidate: accepted send, acknowledgment withheld | 1 | 1 | pending; attempt 1, retry 0, max 2 |
| First retryable HTTP 503 lookup failure | 1 | 1 | pending; attempt 1, retry 1 |
| Second lookup failure, at retry ceiling | 1 | 1 | pending; attempt 1, retry 2, max 2 |
| Lookup recovery / original receipt completion | 2 | 1 | completed |
| Repeat completed delivery intent | 2 | 1 | completed; no further request |
| Baseline after first lookup failure | 2 | 1 | completed immediately through fallback |

Both accepted PUTs reused the same transaction ID and returned the same original event ID. Matrix reconciliation itself performs an idempotent transaction PUT: this demonstrates no fresh transaction and no duplicate recipient message, not zero additional HTTP requests. Matrix's native idempotency also protected the baseline from a second visible message. The real-service experiment therefore proves the corrected reconciliation precedence and custody retention; visible duplicate effects are established by the separate non-idempotent synthetic-sink regressions above, not by claiming duplicates in this Matrix run.

A normal authorized control delivered once. Separate post-run recipient reads and read-only durable-state verification exited 0 and confirmed one original event, one control event, completed custody and the original event identities. All owned services terminated; their listener ports were independently checked closed.

**Remaining runtime-proof failure:** the candidate passed its delivery assertions but the complete runner exited 1 due to an unsuppressed Matrix SDK ConnectionError from an aborted initial GET /sync. This is not a clean overall run. An origin-tracing probe captured the exact initial HTTP promise during a fully awaited production send, before fixture disposal while both services remained running. That probe explicitly required zero unhandled rejections and failed (42.403s), rather than suppressing the error.

<details>
<summary>Failure qualification and retained evidence</summary>

The SDK creates its initial sync request before entering its running loop. Transient-client retirement can stop sync in that startup window; stop aborts the request, the running loop can be skipped, and STOPPED is emitted without joining the original rejected request. The observed paths were client-bootstrap.ts, client/shared.ts and client-sync-quiesce.ts in the Matrix implementation, plus matrix-js-sdk/lib/sync.js. These are outside this PR's four changed files. No separate production lifecycle fix is included here, and no wider runtime/platform qualification is claimed.

A diagnostic-listener rerun also recorded the abort but disabled the generic rejection reporter; its exit 0 is explicitly rejected as clean evidence. The original unsuppressed exit-1 log, failing explicit zero-rejection probe, baseline recovery exit 0 and independent final verification exit 0 remain separate records. Deliberate crash stages exited nonzero as expected. The baseline comparison's protocol/source semantics are unchanged.

Private retained evidence includes the wire acceptance/failure trace, actual queue observations and closed-state snapshots, exact source bindings, candidate recovery and lifecycle-provenance logs, baseline observations, independent final verification and cleanup receipts. Only this inspected sanitized excerpt is published; credentials, account identifiers, transaction paths and raw logs remain private. Production source and the reviewed four-file patch are unchanged.

</details>

Contributor credit: Mitchell Etzel.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78368fe5-6c3a-4170-accd-485f2861ef5d)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/6c8b528a-0a66-4dad-b215-924f4c43575d)

## Worked on by

- @etzelm

prs.title: fix(state-migrations): allow OAuth dirs reached through a state-dir alias
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR` is spelled through a symlink alias of the copied state directory, the legacy state migration plan refuses it as `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot` even though its real path is inside the snapshot. The containment check compares two lexical spellings, so a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through an alias fails closed.

Precedent: #195061 (path containment through a canonical spelling owner). That PR audited 53 files combining path resolution with containment comparison and explicitly deferred this exact wrong deny: "**`infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts` OAuth-dir check.** It compares two lexical spellings, so `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR` spelled through a state-dir alias is refused as `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot`. This is a minor wrong deny that fails closed."

Related: #195061

## Why This Change Was Made

The plan's `oauthDirOutsideSnapshot` predicate compares `callerOAuthDir` against `requestedSnapshot.stateDir` with `isPathInside`, which is purely lexical (`@openclaw/fs-safe/path`). `resolveOAuthDir` expands `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR` with `resolveUserPath` (tilde + absolute, no realpath), so an alias that resolves inside the snapshot is judged outside.

The fix resolves both sides through `resolveIdentityPathViaExistingAncestorSync` (the same helper the sibling endpoint check at `listMigrationEndpointsOutsideRoot` uses) before the containment comparison. The admission lives in `resolveSnapshotOAuthDirAdmission` in `src/infra/state-migrations.plan.ts`, next to the plan-env owner (`createLegacyStateMigrationPlanEnv`); `planLegacyStateMigrationsReadOnly` consumes the admission. This re-spells the OAuth dir to its real location, so an alias inside the snapshot is admitted while a genuinely external directory stays refused.

No new validator, option, config, or persistence policy. The refusal path is otherwise unchanged.

The assignment that feeds later discovery also changes: it now stores the already-resolved canonical identity rather than the raw alias spelling. Admitting a path and then handing the unverified spelling to later directory I/O would leave a window where retargeting the alias redirects reads outside the admitted snapshot. Resolving once and reusing the checked result closes that window without adding a second resolution site.

Production LOC vs base: `state-migrations.plan.ts` `+32` (new admission owner), `state-migrations.doctor.ts` `+22/-3` (net +3 physical lines; counted lines stay under the base 2805 — the file is grandfathered over its line cap and the ratchet rejects any growth, which is why the admission lives in `plan.ts`).

Classification: `behavior-completing` (completes the path-containment canonicalization that #195061 landed).

## User Impact

Operators who keep their OAuth credentials inside a symlinked state-dir alias no longer get a spurious `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot` refusal from the migration plan; the read-only doctor/startup plan now recognizes the directory as snapshot-bound. Truly external OAuth directories are still refused, and the security boundary that rejects symlinked state snapshots (`captureLegacyStateSnapshotIdentity`) is untouched.

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI proof (source entry, same argv as the packaged CLI)

Proven through the shipped CLI entry `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts update migration-plan --snapshot-home <h> --snapshot-config <c> --snapshot-state <s> --json` (argv tree is identical to the packaged `openclaw` binary), with a real filesystem fixture: `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=/ws/proof/alias/operator-credentials` where `alias` is a symlink to the copied state dir, and `operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json` inside it. No credentials involved.

```text
# BASE (production without the fix): the shipped CLI refuses the alias-spelled OAuth dir
$ OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=/ws/proof/alias/operator-credentials node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts update migration-plan --snapshot-* --json
{
  "outcome": "refused",
  "refusal": {
    "code": "oauth-dir-outside-snapshot",
    "message": "Configured OAuth migration directory is outside the copied state snapshot: /ws/proof/alias/operator-credentials"
  }
}

# HEAD (this fix): the shipped CLI no longer refuses it (planner proceeds to its normal
# staged-candidate identity refusal; no oauth-dir-outside-snapshot anywhere)
$ OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=/ws/proof/alias/operator-credentials node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts update migration-plan --snapshot-* --json
{
  "outcome": "refused",
  "refusal": { "code": "candidate-artifact-digest-required", ... }   // planner's fixed artifact guard, unrelated to OAuth
}
```

No wrong allow — the same shipped CLI still refuses both a genuinely external OAuth dir and a **reassigned** alias (alias retargeted to an outside dir). Re-verified on the current head after the refactor:

```text
# HEAD, OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=/ws/proof-external/operator-credentials (outside the snapshot)
{ "refusal": { "code": "oauth-dir-outside-snapshot", "message": "...outside the copied state snapshot: /ws/proof-external/operator-credentials" } }

# HEAD, alias reassigned to point outside (/ws/proof/alias -> /ws/proof-external)
{ "refusal": { "code": "oauth-dir-outside-snapshot", "message": "...outside the copied state snapshot: /ws/proof/alias/operator-credentials" } }
```

### Directory I/O confinement after admission (alias retargeted)

The admitted plan must not leave later discovery reading through the alias spelling: retargeting the alias afterwards would redirect directory I/O outside the snapshot. The plan records the OAuth source in the `channel-pairing` step, so that step is the readback boundary.

Same fixture (alias `.../alias` -> `.../state`, `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=.../alias/operator-credentials`), same shipped CLI, only the assignment under test differs:

```text
# BASE (assignment keeps the raw alias spelling)
channel-pairing source: /ws/proof2/alias/operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json

# HEAD (assignment stores the resolved canonical identity)
channel-pairing source: /ws/proof2/state/operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json
```

Re-verified on the current head: `channel-pairing` source is the canonical `/ws/proof2/state/operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json`. BASE resolves through the alias for the containment check but then re-spells the env var with the alias, so a retarget after admission moves the recorded source outside the snapshot. HEAD records the checked canonical location, so the same retarget cannot change where the admitted plan reads.

### Retarget between admission and directory I/O (same run)

The two runs above retarget the alias between invocations. The stricter case retargets *inside one plan run*, after the containment check admits the directory and before `detectLegacyChannelPairingState` enumerates it.

Instrumentation is a `--import` preload on the shipped entry, hooking `fs.readdirSync`: when the OAuth directory is first enumerated, it repoints the alias to an outside directory and then performs the read, tracing the actual path. The outside directory holds `discord-pairing.json`, which the snapshot copy does not, so any external read shows up in the plan itself.

```text
# BASE trace
RETARGET before readdir of /ws/rt/alias/operator-credentials
RETARGETED /ws/rt/alias -> /ws/rt/outside
READDIR /ws/rt/alias/operator-credentials          <- reads outside the snapshot
plan refs: /ws/rt/alias/operator-credentials/{telegram,discord}-pairing.json

# HEAD trace
READDIR /ws/rt/state/operator-credentials          <- reads the admitted snapshot dir
plan refs: /ws/rt/state/operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json
external-only "discord-pairing" occurrences in plan: 0
```

On BASE the retarget lands, the plan enumerates through the alias and picks up the external-only `discord-pairing.json`. On HEAD the alias spelling never reaches the directory read: the admitted plan reads the canonical snapshot directory and the external-only file never appears.

Reproduce: `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=<alias>/operator-credentials node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs --import <preload> src/entry.ts update migration-plan --snapshot-home <h> --snapshot-config <c> --snapshot-state <s> --json`, with `alias` a symlink to the copied state dir and the preload retargeting it on the first `readdirSync` of the OAuth directory.

The regression test `preserves a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through a state-dir alias` asserts exactly this: on the base it fails on the canonical path mismatch (it previously asserted the alias spelling), on this head it passes.

Red (base) / green (head) / external-rejection (head) all captured on the same fixture and CLI. Current head: `37dec884e1cb` — `state-migrations.plan.ts` sha256 `b99eae1f52f0e978fe42fc5cab12fe0ef4fc357523547d701dc7d2ba9979a697`, `state-migrations.doctor.ts` sha256 `3c5c11494159520e8b3cd04c083c0e433a20d265324aa4ea530d5b34a571cac1`.

### RED -> GREEN

The alias case is covered by a new regression test `preserves a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through a state-dir alias` in `src/infra/state-migrations.caller-mode.refusal.test.ts`. On the base with production WITHOUT the fix and the test WITH the alias case, the test fails with `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot`; on this head it passes.

- Baseline (RED) SHA: `cdcef6c25f75fd7e2e2ddea93636a0ff629ce45a` (the branch's original base) + alias regression test → test FAILs. `src/infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts` and `src/infra/state-migrations.plan.ts` are unchanged between that base and current `main` (`3e9d22d51026`), so the RED verdict still holds on current main.
- Head (GREEN) SHA: `37dec884e1cb` (this branch) + alias regression test → test PASSes
- Production entry: `planLegacyStateMigrationsReadOnly` in `src/infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts`; admission owner: `resolveSnapshotOAuthDirAdmission` in `src/infra/state-migrations.plan.ts`
- Decision surface: `oauthDirOutsideSnapshot` / `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR`
- Recorder/readback boundary: plan `refusal.code` and `channel-pairing` step `source`

```text
# RED (base cdcef6c25f + alias test): plan refuses the alias-spelled OAuth dir
FAIL: preserves a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through a state-dir alias
  AssertionError: oauth-dir-outside-snapshot refusal present

# GREEN (head 37dec884e1cb + alias test): plan admits the alias-spelled OAuth dir
PASS: preserves a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through a state-dir alias
```

### Legal control (no over-broadening)

- `refuses an OAuth migration directory outside the copied state without inspecting it` — still PASSes (external dir kept refused)
- Retargeted-alias control: after the alias is repointed outside, the shipped CLI still refuses with `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot` (see above)
- `preserves a snapshot-bound OAuth directory in the read-only plan` — still PASSes (direct inside path unchanged)
- Security boundary `rejects a symlinked state snapshot before migration detection` — unchanged, untouched code

### Latest-stable upgrade run (published-driver × candidate)

The upgrade cell uses the published `openclaw@2026.11.3` npm package (`OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d)`, dist-tag `latest`) installed in an isolated prefix against a **real state it produced itself** (`openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` in a clean `HOME`): config `openclaw.json`, state `openclaw.sqlite` (+wal/shm/seal), plus a synthetic `operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json` (stub `{"version":1,"requests":[]}` — no real credentials anywhere). The state is copied to a snapshot (`--snapshot-home/--snapshot-config/--snapshot-state`), `alias -> snap/state`, and `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=<alias>/operator-credentials`. Same snapshot for both cells.

```text
# PUBLISHED DRIVER (openclaw@2026.11.3, the real latest-stable CLI) — reproduces the bug
$ HOME=<snap-home> OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=<alias>/operator-credentials openclaw update migration-plan --snapshot-* --json
{ "outcome": "refused",
  "refusal": { "code": "oauth-dir-outside-snapshot",
               "message": "Configured OAuth migration directory is outside the copied state snapshot: /tmp/oc-upgrade/alias/operator-credentials" } }

# CANDIDATE (head 37dec884e1cb, source entry, identical argv) — OAuth admission passes
$ HOME=<snap-home> OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=<alias>/operator-credentials node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts update migration-plan --snapshot-* --json
{ "outcome": "refused",
  "refusal": { "code": "candidate-artifact-digest-required",
               "message": "Candidate artifact content identity must be supplied by the staged-candidate owner." } }
  oauth-dir-outside occurrences: 0
  channel-pairing source: /tmp/oc-upgrade/snap/state/operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json   <- canonical, not the alias
  snapshot digests: configDigest sha256:df51e382…, stateDigest sha256:06817eca…
```

`candidate-artifact-digest-required` is this diagnostic command's by-design terminal refusal (see `update-command-migration-plan.ts`: "This diagnostic command cannot bind candidate bytes, so the planner returns a closed artifact-identity refusal"); it fires **after** the OAuth admission, so the cell shows exactly the boundary under change: the published driver refuses at `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot`, the candidate passes it and records the canonical discovery path.

Equivalence check — the same snapshot run with a directly spelled `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=<snap>/state/operator-credentials` produces a **byte-identical plan JSON** to the alias-spelled run (steps, digests, refusal, warnings all equal), so the alias spelling is admitted on equal footing with the direct spelling.

**Settings and data remain intact:**

- 6-file sha256 manifest of the snapshot is identical before and after all four runs (1 published-driver + 3 candidate) — the plan never writes.
- Original config bytes unchanged: `sha256 a91d2ac9b4b6…` for both the original `HOME/.openclaw/openclaw.json` and the snapshot copy taken before any plan run.
- Published stable re-opens the original state after the runs: `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite validate --json` → exit 0, `issues: 0`; `openclaw doctor --lint --json` findings are only environmental fixture facts (gateway never started in this fixture: auth off, `gateway.mode` unset; host `proc-safe` native check), no config/state corruption.
- Sensitive values: the fixture is fully synthetic; evidence carries only paths and digests, no credentials.

**Gap named:** this cell runs the upgrade's copied-state planning stage (the surface ClawSweeper's item cites: `update-command-migration-plan.ts:29`) from source entries; a full `openclaw update` install-switch was not run because the candidate is an unpublished branch (no published artifact to switch to), and the fixture gateway was never started (integrity proven by manifest + stable validation instead).

### Verification

Current head `37dec884e1cb` (rebased onto current `main` `3e9d22d51026`), all re-run after the line-cap refactor:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/state-migrations.caller-mode.refusal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 23/23 pass.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check src/infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts src/infra/state-migrations.plan.ts` — passes.
- `node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mts --base origin/main` — OK (`no new violations or over-cap growth`; doctor.ts no longer grows).
- `node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main` — OK (`Net test lines: +28; allowance: 400`).
- `npx oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` on both changed production files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Not tested locally: `tsgo:core` (the pinned `tsrs` native binary needs GLIBC 2.34; this host's libc is older — environment limitation, not a code verdict) and the full repository suite. PR CI covers both.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC vs base: `state-migrations.plan.ts` `+32`; `state-migrations.doctor.ts` `+22/-3`; Test LOC: `+28`.
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `resolveIdentityPathViaExistingAncestorSync` (same helper as the sibling endpoint check) and `isPathInside`; no new validator or resolution primitive.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none beyond admitting alias-spelled snapshot-bound OAuth dirs (the intended fix); external dirs and symlinked-snapshot defenses unchanged.

### Line-cap: admission owned by the plan module

`src/infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts` is grandfathered over its line cap (2805 counted lines, cap 700), and the checks-fast-baseline-ratchets line-cap job rejects **any** growth on such files (`allowed = max(cap, base count)`). The containment + canonical-assignment logic therefore cannot stay inline without shrinking `doctor.ts`. Commit `37dec884e1cb` moves the admission into `resolveSnapshotOAuthDirAdmission` in `state-migrations.plan.ts`, which already owns the plan env's snapshot-bound directory decisions; `doctor.ts` ends below its base counted lines and the line-cap ratchet passes (`no new violations or over-cap growth`). Behavior is unchanged.

### Test-line budget: +28 lines, inside the standard allowance

The branch originally carried a `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` scalar raise (+127) because the then-current ratchet rejected on inherited base debt (99 lines over ceiling before this change added anything). Current `main` has since replaced that shared-scalar mechanism with a per-change delta allowance (`ALLOWANCE = 400`, `scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts`) and deleted `config/test-lines-baseline.txt`; this branch was rebased onto that main and **drops the scalar commit entirely**.

```text

Line-cap ratchet OK: 3 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth.
```

+28 test lines is well inside the standard allowance, so **no maintainer scalar approval is needed anymore**. The line-cap constraint is resolved by the admission moving to `state-migrations.plan.ts`.

prs.title: feat(cron): add up to eight runs past the default when memory is free
prs.body:
Related: #196859

## What Problem This Solves

Due automations wait behind a fixed cap of eight runs, even on a host with plenty of memory to run more.

## User Impact

- Up to eight automation jobs run at once, as before.
- While all eight are busy and more jobs are due, each drain of the run queue starts one more job if at least 1 GiB of memory is free, up to 16 at once. The queue drains when a run ends and when jobs come due, so on a host with room the count grows by one job per drain.
- The reading is Node's `process.availableMemory()`, which counts the process's cgroup memory limit: in a 512 MiB container it reads about 500 MiB, while `os.freemem()` reads the VM's 5.4 GB.
- Running jobs are never stopped, condition checks do not use run slots, and there is no new setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The run queue owns admission. The host adds one fact to each drain, whether one memory reading shows 1 GiB free, and the queue uses it to start at most one run past its eight default slots per drain. Each later drain reads memory again with that run counted, so the extra runs stop once memory gets short. No timer, threshold ladder or per-run memory estimate is involved.

Automation agent turns run in the cron lane, which shares one capacity budget with hook dispatch. That budget is 16 wide, since with it at eight an extra run would only wait in the lane for a slot. Hook dispatch keeps its own width of eight, so hooks alone never use more than they could before. Together, hooks and automation can hold up to 16 slots where they shared eight. Keeping them at eight combined would mean republishing the lane budget from the run queue on every drain, which this change leaves out. With hooks enabled, one of the 16 stays reserved for hooks, as one of the eight was.

Accepted edge cases:

- The eight default runs do not read memory. A small container with a heavy neighbour can still be OOM-killed with eight runs, as on main.
- One reading admits one run, and that run's memory may not show yet at the next drain. A run that later needs more than the memory left can still run short; each drain adds at most one run.

## Evidence

Targeted tests pass: `service.cross-tick-admission` (10), `service.run-queue` (16), `service.one-shot-schedule-ownership` (17), `service/ops.native-attempt` (7), `service/ops.gateway-mutations` (11), `service/ops.run-admission` (8), `service/manual-ack-durability` (3), `service/timer.regression` (16), `store/scheduler-actor.worker` (24), `server-lanes.hook-group` (2), `server/hooks.early-failure` (27).

- Twelve due jobs with 1 GiB free: the first drain starts nine, the next starts a tenth, and with one byte under 1 GiB a further drain starts none. With extra runs disabled it fails: eight start, not nine.

Tests that fill exactly the eight default slots mock the memory reading to report no spare memory, so they do not depend on the machine running them. With the memory reading set to 16 GiB, as on CI, `timer.regression`'s slot fixture without the mock fails its two queueing cases (a queued run starts instead, and a wait times out); with the mock all 16 cases pass.

Cron suite, run once on this change with the memory mock applied to every cron test: 292 of 299 files passed. The mock then moved into the tests that fill the eight slots, and those tests were rerun (above). The seven failing files were rerun on this branch and on its merge base `4b0d586f272`. `maintenance-lifecycle` (18), `maintenance-snapshot` (5), `maintenance` (1) and `trigger-script.mcp` (3) fail the same on both. `service.pr-automation-feedback` and `service/command-timeout` pass on rerun. `service/manual-ack-durability` filled the eight slots with memory to spare and so started its queued request; it passes with the memory mock. Core, cron-test and gateway-server typechecks, lint and format pass; net test lines +63.

Gateway run of this change and its merge base in a private macOS VM, with 12 cron agent jobs due together and a synthetic model that holds every request open ([full table and script](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197394#issuecomment-6940499855)):

- Memory free: 9 runs start where the merge base starts 8; a drain without a run ending adds a tenth; a drain after a run ends refills that slot.
- Gateway memory reading at 512 MiB: no extra run starts, and the count falls back to 8 as runs end and holds there.
- Hooks: beside 8 automation runs, 10 hook requests get 8 hook turns running (the merge base runs 1 and answers the other 9 with 503).
- Restart on the same state keeps all 14 jobs and the config unchanged; all 14 runs end `ok`.
- Up to the cap ([table and script](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197394#issuecomment-6941726543)): with 21 jobs, each request with memory free adds one run, 9 to 16; a request at 16 leaves the run waiting; a request with the reading at 512 MiB starts nothing; all 21 runs end `ok`.

## Validation Limits

The model was synthetic. In the VM a macOS guest swaps instead of staying under 1 GiB, so for the low-memory steps the Gateway's `process.availableMemory()` was pinned at 512 MiB through a preload; the rest of the run was the shipped build. An upgrade from the latest stable was not shown, because main fails it on its own: starting main `b9a72b5bef8` on state written by 2026.11.4, in the same VM and without any scenario preload, fails after the state migration with `Startup failed: required secrets are unavailable. Error: disk I/O error | ERR_SQLITE_ERROR`. This head fails the same way there, also with no stable process left running and with no plaintext secrets in the config; that startup failure is separate from this change. Windows, Bun, x86 Linux, real channels and the full suite were not exercised.

prs.body:
Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

## Evidence

Current tested head: `c326ed5fc8fc63d243f337ff928a9cca42304f5b` (tree `f7d308969f6204e5309accb9137dfac74b82069c`). This is a normal two-parent merge preserving the original PR head `d7bdb5a3c123b1db96eeb9322a42efeb0075df71` and upstream `5584b16af9109db5235f776cb1302093f6bf2f59`.

- The real Notifications route, ConfigPage, capability adapters, and rendered DOM are exercised together. The migrated test fails eight native cases against untouched upstream production; the Safari/PWA/Mac controls pass.
- Final focused run: **140 tests passed in six files, 8.12 seconds wall time**, covering iPhone/iPad, base paths, delayed and changed native snapshots, missing fields, ordinary/modified clicks, absent callbacks, and browser/Mac controls.
- Production Control UI build completed successfully in **18.94 seconds**.
- i18n verification, focused style checks, documentation MDX/link checks, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety guards, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review identified missing route-loader result narrowing in the migrated test fixture. Explicit route and result guards address it; the final focused rerun and fresh canonical P0–P2 autoreview passed without remaining actionable findings.

**Outstanding verification:** Physical iPhone QA and inspected before/after screenshots remain unavailable. The DOM tests provide synthetic bridge-contract evidence and do not establish native-device or visual behavior. Production UI typechecking, a reduced focused typecheck, and typed lint were terminated with exit 137/SIGKILL without source diagnostics; those gates are not claimed green. Full repository tests have not run, and current-head hosted CI is not yet verified. This remains a draft pending those checks and the required native/visual evidence.

Checks ran on Node 24.19.0 through the repository wrappers. Dependencies were installed with the frozen lockfile using the environment's pnpm 11.25.0. The pinned pnpm 12.9.0 install was attempted but could not open its store operation lock on this host's read-only filesystem; this tooling limitation remains explicit.

Codex generated the change and performed the code review and automated checks described above; no human review is claimed.

prs.title: fix: remove updater-only restrictions from agent maintenance guidance
prs.body:
Related: #200779, #200809, #198396, #136588

## What Problem This Solves

An operator can explicitly request a Git-based source update and forbid the updater, yet the agent's prompt requires the updater and forbids exec for its own installation. The agent then refuses a valid maintenance method or substitutes a different update path. The config-recovery change in #200809 left this separate restriction intact.

## User Impact

User impact: a source-checkout maintenance request no longer conflicts with an updater-only prompt rule. This removes that rule, rather than adding a new exception or permission setting.

Existing execution permissions, owner admission, approval decisions and live-output build protection are unchanged. This does not make rebuilding files used by a running Gateway safe or deploy an update.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Delete the no-exec maintenance mandate, forced updater/helper routes, duplicate tool-description directives and the redundant component-build exception.
- Keep capability descriptions and existing restart/cleanup safeguards; reconcile the corresponding docs and regenerate the canonical prompt artifacts.
- Remove the Gateway-specific cross-tool description rewrite. Production delta: **7 added / 20 removed lines**. Existing test delta: **13 added / 26 removed lines**; no new test suite, configuration, runtime policy or fallback.

## Evidence

- Canonical `pnpm build:runtime` passed at exact head `f6bf7dc8c7cf981766ae7b762c852c7ec93529eb` in 287.7 s, including core, bundled plugins, Codex and Control UI. Independent verification matched current source signatures and every recorded Codex output hash; this is runtime-build proof, not a full SDK declaration build.

- The original prompt fails the four tool-availability regression cases. The changed ordinary and native-harness prompts remove the exclusive routing while retaining restart-custody and authorization-denial guidance.
- Canonical snapshot generation/check passes all six outputs. After the main refresh, the Telegram Codex fixture, including dynamic tools, shrinks from 118,516 to 117,822 characters: **694 fewer characters, 173 fewer rough tokens** (the repository's text estimate, not provider token accounting).
- Focused coverage passes: 174 prompt/harness/catalog cases, 14 Gateway-tool cases, 17 owner-admission cases and 7 snapshot cases. Unaffected successful cases were reused; corrected assertions were rerun. The snapshot/catalog/Gateway-tool follow-up took 112.76 s, and the two affected owner-prompt cases took 149.06 s (cold compilation dominates). Upstream CI timing is pending.
- Targeted TypeScript graphs pass: agents-root (44.0 s), agents-tools (29.4 s), gateway-methods (36.4 s). Scoped lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. The automatic typecheck selector expanded to all graphs and was stopped; these explicit affected graphs are the claimed typecheck scope.
- A bounded independent native source audit found no remaining direct updater-only/no-exec maintenance mandate in the inspected surfaces. Local Codex autoreview against base `bd1c54cfde534824d31a4cc3c01ce3a116234549`, through P2, returned `reviewer_unavailable` without a report. The subsequent [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200978#issuecomment-6968967010) covered head `f6bf7dc8c7cf981766ae7b762c852c7ec93529eb`, identified no actionable code findings, and required real-behavior proof and an area-owner decision. The unavailable local review is not represented as clean.

### Real-model source maintenance (November 18)

An isolated Gateway ran the exact reviewed runtime with OpenAI Codex `gpt-6-astra`, reasoning `xhigh`. One user request asked it to inspect its deployment and update a designated Git revision without an updater. Deployment/ref/service facts and the canonical build entry point were supplied, not a step-by-step recipe. The model chose a local `git fetch` plus `merge --ff-only`, authored an independently supervised systemd worker and recovery command, built with `pnpm build:runtime`, restarted the Gateway, and verified the result.

The first worker failed because its PATH lacked `corepack` (exit 127). Its recovery command restored the previous source/runtime and a healthy Gateway. Native restart recovery resumed the model without another user message; it diagnosed the PATH error, launched a corrected worker, and completed the update. The final model response accurately reported both completion and the recovered failure.

Independent observations establish:
- Both actual Gateway shutdowns had a running worker in a separate systemd cgroup, with no `PartOf`/`BindsTo` dependency on the Gateway. Native monotonic worker-start/stop pairs were `258159467141 < 258168804254` and `258239308076 < 258247297301` microseconds.
- The final worker exited 0; the original failed worker remains recorded as exit 127. The new Gateway invocation started at `258450560472` microseconds, after the final stop.
- Git HEAD and build identity match `6fe8e4ac013e5b36b24fd8007e011bac9a77203b`, a local marker-only child of reviewed head `f6bf7dc8c7cf981766ae7b762c852c7ec93529eb`. The checkout is clean. Independent source/build/runtime signatures and every recorded Codex output hash match.
- `/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/startupz` returned HTTP 200; readiness reported `ready=true`, `coreReady=true`. A read-only Gateway history query found exactly one user request and the final OpenAI/Astra response with positive usage (499 input, 47,232 cached input, 112 output tokens).

Redacted actual worker log excerpt (UTC):
```text
05:12:20 ERROR line=109 exit=127
05:12:42 Original revision and service health restored; requested update FAILED
05:13:38 building
05:16:57 starting
05:17:35 SUCCESS: exact target built, restarted and healthy
```

**Instrumentation failures are not green tests.** Earlier attempts exposed a unit-file quoting error, ambiguous fixture paths, contradictory worker scope, and incomplete Luna/low follow-through. An Astra attempt reached the target but the harness incorrectly read a discarded stop timestamp; cleanup triggered a verified rollback. The final run completed in reality, but its harness incorrectly required the *first* worker to finish successfully even after the model recovered and used a second worker. A separate read-only recorder captured the completed result before cleanup; an independent validator checked both shutdown boundaries, the successful final custodian, health, build provenance and final model response. No claim is made that the original Vitest harness passed; the failures and exact inputs remain retained.

**Limits:** This proves the exercised Linux/systemd source-maintenance and recovery flow, not universal model behavior or automatic method selection for an unspecified update request. The synthetic target changes no product/dependency files; dependency installation, a release/schema migration, and Discord delivery were not exercised. No production deployment was performed. Full CI remains unverified; the published CI run requires maintainer action.

## Owner decision

Merge-conflict follow-up: merged main `5e677bad858c331ec7db0a547bebf0b15e4786d4` in `2e69e54bf57f0b97309927378e55fadae3776140` without rewriting history. Only two generated prompt snapshots conflicted; canonical regeneration resolved them and all six outputs pass `prompt:snapshots:check`. `git diff --check` passes. The non-generated PR patch is identical (stable patch ID `e30b142e7757c4bcb49218a177b0cbace0071168`), and all three maintenance-guidance/tool owners are byte-identical to reviewed/live-tested `f6bf7dc8c7cf981766ae7b762c852c7ec93529eb`. The prior review and runtime proof are reused for that unchanged patch, not claimed as a new full live run on the merge commit. No additional hosted review was requested for this mechanical refresh, consistent with the repository's review-reuse policy.

This intentionally changes the updater-only routing policy retained by #198396 following the self-stop incidents described in #136588; it is not restoration of an established product contract. Requested decision: accept owner-selected source-maintenance methods under existing execution authority and mandatory restart custody. This PR does not claim that tests or a bot review supply that product approval.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A one-shot reminder scheduled in the same turn through the MCP tool (`mcp__openclaw__automations`, action `add`) is created and enabled, but OpenClaw still appends "Note: I did not schedule a reminder in this turn, so this will not trigger automatically." The reminder fires on time, so the note is false. Reported in #193958 for the claude-cli / MCP tool path.

## User Impact

The agent delivers a tool confirmation plus a note saying nothing was scheduled. The reminder works, so the note only erodes trust.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runResult.successfulCronAdds` suppresses the note. The embedded runtime counts successful adds (`isAutomationsToolName` + `isCronAddAction`), but the CLI runtime never did: `createCliToolTracking` captured messaging delivery, session spawns and media, and no scheduler facts. An `add` over MCP was never counted, so the guard fired. Prior PRs (#193965, #193983, #194021) patched the harness telemetry helper, which serves the codex extension, not this path. The counter now lives where the CLI runtime owns its evidence: `recordMcpLoopbackToolCallResult` → `onToolCallResult` → `CliOutput` → settled `AgentRunResult`.

## Changes

`createCliToolTracking` now keeps `let successfulCronAdds = 0`, increments it in its own `onToolCallResult` via a pure `isSuccessfulCliSchedulerAdd()` (reusing `isAutomationsToolName`, which handles the `cron` alias, and `isCronAddAction`), and projects it through `CliOutput` → settled `AgentRunResult` (omitted when no add was recorded). A pure `matchesCliLoopbackCall` helper correlates the result to its call. Tests cover the add cases, the `cron` alias, non-add ignored, and the fact reaching the run result; a test-lines allocation replaces raising the shared baseline.

## Evidence

**Before / after — the reply payload a channel delivers (real Claude CLI + real model turn, isolated automations add):**

![Before (counter neutralized): the false "I did not schedule a reminder" note is appended even though the job exists. After (this head): the reminder is scheduled and no false note is appended.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96170953-402b-487a-8ac5-8ead455879ad)

**Mechanism (guard-diag, same real turn): `matched=false` in both arms (isolated session), so only `successfulCronAdds` suppresses the note; removing just the increment brings it back:**

![Annotated guard-diag: reverse arm shows matched=false jobs=1 then append-called with the false note; this head shows commitment=true with no append-called, reply delivered clean.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d43bb77-3aa0-4b29-af60-7255cf9fb912)

Before/after on the same head bundle — "Before" neutralizes ONLY the counter increment (`k += isSuccessfulCliSchedulerAdd(t) ? 1 : 0` → `k += 0`); "After" is this head. Each cell is one real turn (real `claude` native executable + real model). Observable is the guard's reply payload (`OPENCLAW_193958_DIAG` guard-diag), the artifact a channel transport delivers (see Observation point):

| Case | Before (counter neutralized) | After (this head) |
|---|---|---|
| successful isolated `automations` add | 1 job (`sessionKey` null); `matched=false jobs=1`; `append-called payloads=1` → **false note present** | 1 enabled job (`sessionKey` null); `commitment=true`, no `append-called` → **note absent** |
| no tool call (control) | 0 jobs; `matched=false jobs=0`; `append-called payloads=1` → note present | 0 jobs; `matched=false jobs=0`; `append-called payloads=1` → note present (unchanged) |

### Live CLI turn — commands and verbatim guard-diag

Real Gateway (built `dist/entry.js`) + bundled `anthropic` plugin + the real `claude` native executable (Claude Code v2.1.193) + a real model turn + real HTTP MCP loopback + real cron store, on Linux. The reminder targets an isolated session (`sessionTarget: "isolated"`), so the job's `sessionKey` differs from the chat turn's — `coveredByExistingCron` does not cover it, and only `successfulCronAdds` can suppress the note.

```
$ node dist/entry.js gateway --port <port>   # shipped entry; bundled anthropic plugin, agentRuntime claude-cli, real HTTP MCP loopback + cron store
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs proof-driver.mts <port> <token> scheduled   # real claude native executable + real model turn; control arm passes "control"
```

Verbatim guard-diag — After (scheduled), Before (reverse), then control:

```
[guard-diag] commitment=true text="I'll schedule that reminder now.\n\nI'll remind you tomorrow at 9am to call the dentist."
```
```
[guard-diag] commitment=true text="I'll fetch the automations tool schema first.\n\nI'll remind you tomorrow at 9am to call the dentist."
[guard-diag] session-cron-check matched=false jobs=1
[guard-diag] append-called payloads=1
[guard-diag] appended-text="I'll fetch the automations tool schema first.\n\nI'll remind you tomorrow at 9am to call the dentist.\n\nNote: I did not schedule a reminder in this turn, so this will not trigger automatically."
```
```
[guard-diag] commitment=true text="Sure - I'll remind you tomorrow at 9am to call the dentist."
[guard-diag] session-cron-check matched=false jobs=0
[guard-diag] append-called payloads=1
[guard-diag] appended-text="Sure - I'll remind you tomorrow at 9am to call the dentist.\n\nNote: I did not schedule a reminder in this turn, so this will not trigger automatically."
```

The scheduled turn creates a real enabled job and the guard stays silent; removing only the counter brings the false note back even though the job exists. `matched=false jobs=1` rules out `coveredByExistingCron`, and the control still appends on both sides, so this is not "the guard stopped running" — the counter alone flips the scheduled case.

### Red on base, green on head (owning boundary)

```
$ vitest run src/agents/cli-runner/execute-tool-tracking.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-settlement.test.ts   # on origin/main e9fcf00afa3, both test files unchanged
 Test Files  2 failed (2)
      Tests  3 failed | 53 passed (56)
   × projects successfulCronAdds from CliOutput into the settled run result
   × counts a successful mcp__openclaw__automations add toward successfulCronAdds
   × counts a successful mcp__openclaw__cron add toward successfulCronAdds
AssertionError: expected undefined to be 1 // Object.is equality
```

Only the three positive cases fail; the non-add controls pass on both sides. They pass on this head in PR CI.

### What is real, what is environment compensation

Real: the Gateway, the bundled `anthropic` plugin, `agentRuntime: claude-cli`, the real `claude` native executable, a real model conversation, the CLI runner's `--mcp-config` injection, the HTTP MCP loopback, tool-authority capture, `cron.add` validation and store, and the guard's inputs and outputs. No fixture executable and no mocked model response.

Environment: the host glibc (2.28) cannot load the proc-safe native binding (needs ≥2.33), so the Gateway runs in a local Ubuntu 22.04 container (glibc 2.35) with the host Node mounted; the model is served through a local Anthropic-protocol endpoint (provider and model identity redacted). In that slow container the CLI's `init` snapshot can capture the OpenClaw MCP server as `pending` before the loopback handshake finishes; a DIAG-gated tolerance lets the turn proceed (MCP connects mid-turn) instead of retiring the process. With DIAG off the shipped `init` check is unchanged. This compensation is orthogonal to the counter under test and is not part of the PR; diagnostics are log-only, gated behind `OPENCLAW_193958_DIAG`.

## Scope

Scoped to the CLI / MCP tool path evidence pipeline. The embedded runtime, guard logic, cron store and config are unchanged.

Observation point: the note is appended to the reply payloads, which is what a channel transport delivers. On the webchat `chat.send` stream the CLI runtime owns the assistant message, so the note is not injected into that stream — the guard's payload is the delivered artifact. Making the note visible on webchat would be a separate change.

`check:test-lines-ratchet` is green on this head against its base `e9fcf00afa3` (slack 8 with the +80 allocation), and `check:line-cap-ratchet` passes. The recorded `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` red is `test-lines` only: that merge tree sat 5 over the ceiling while this PR's +80 net test-line delta was fully allocated, so the residual 5 is inherited main-baseline debt, not test lines this PR adds (the `line-cap` 700→701 note is advisory).

Fixes #193958
