prs.title: fix: keep Gateway updates moving when the token is in the secret store
prs.body:
Related: #200289

## What Problem This Solves

When a supervised Gateway uses a token from OpenClaw's secret store, an update can stop the Gateway and then fail with `database is locked` while recording that stop. The service probe itself can leave a SQLite reader open in the update process.

## User Impact

Updates using a store-backed Gateway token can record the handoff and continue past this point. This covers the [reproduced lock](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/200289#issuecomment-6994870481) in the broader update report.

## Why This Change Was Made

After Doctor obtains maintenance ownership and admits the receipt, it closes the process's state workers for that database before requesting SQLite's exclusive lock. If capture fails, the fallback records the stop against the original database source. SQLite still enforces exclusion against other processes.

## Evidence

- On the parent commit, the real maintenance drain resolved a synthetic store-backed token, then the predecessor-stop receipt failed with SQLite error 5. The same exercise on this branch recorded one stop and verified the captured database generation and rollback attribution.
- With a separate process holding a WAL reader, the patched receipt still failed with SQLite error 5.
- All five receipt and rollback cases passed, including a database change while Doctor held custody. The regression uses real token resolution, SQLite and receipt capture with simulated service and RPC boundaries.
- Replayed the committed test on a detached parent checkout (`9dc69b2`). Only the store-token case failed with SQLite error 5. On `d64084f` all five passed. The local build, core type check, changed-file lint and formatting passed.
- In a disposable ARM64 Linux VM, updated a running systemd Gateway from the published 2026.11.5 build (`e13cf15`) to the PR tarball (`d64084f`) using `openclaw update --yes --tag <tarball>`. The run succeeded, Doctor exited 0, readiness returned true, and a fresh `gateway status --deep --require-rpc` authenticated using the same store-backed token reference. The released driver performed its own service stop. The focused regression above exercises the candidate Doctor receipt directly.
- The VM updater reported database activity during its initial snapshot and warned that this snapshot would require manual recovery. The live run verified successful activation and restart. Rollback attribution is covered by the focused tests.

### Live candidate-owned stop on ARM64 macOS

At reviewed head `6aa4ebb`, I ran the candidate Doctor’s production `stopSupervisedPredecessorGateway` against an isolated launchd Gateway. The harness created an update run, admitted a real SQLite database-write capture, and called the same stop function the delegated Doctor calls in update mode. The service adapter, Gateway RPC, token store, and receipt writer all ran against the live profile.

1. Before the stop, `gateway status --deep --require-rpc` authenticated to the running Gateway on port `41935` (PID `85015`). The profile used the store reference `default/PROBE_TOKEN`.
2. The candidate returned `didStop: true`. The persisted ledger for run `d2bf1623-66d5-41e8-83cd-390002adbd36` contained exactly one completed stop receipt, `finalize:predecessor-stop:1795048906906:-:85015:4bd8588b3af20214ea4ca1d92e9a749c3a5e3c4ce0f7cce4cc48e0c66c8af078`. Its PID matches the pre-stop service. An independent `launchctl print` confirmed the job was gone.
3. After explicitly starting the isolated service again, the same RPC check succeeded with the retained store reference and a new PID, `85424`.

This exercise covers the candidate-owned stop and durable receipt directly. The run warned about config health-state and stale-process cleanup writes during maintenance. It also detected database changes before Doctor obtained custody and reported that automatic database restoration was unavailable. The stop receipt still completed. The full CLI upgrade and rollback-test evidence is recorded above.

**Same-process SecretRef probe and stop.** I repeated the exercise with the SQLite reader warmed in the candidate process itself. On macOS the harness explicitly called the production probe-context, read-only auth-resolution, and Gateway RPC functions used by the Linux drain. After admitting the capture, that process resolved the configured store token and issued an authenticated `status` RPC, which returned the live predecessor PID `85424`. It then invoked the candidate stop owner with no intervening worker cleanup. Run `c97b5809-bf14-42dd-b928-592db1f02314` returned true and persisted exactly one completed receipt:

```text
finalize:predecessor-stop:1795048980957:-:85424:4bd8588b3af20214ea4ca1d92e9a749c3a5e3c4ce0f7cce4cc48e0c66c8af078
```

The launchd job was absent and the port refused connections after the stop. An explicit restart brought up PID `86007`, readiness passed, and deep RPC authenticated again. The same maintenance and restoration warnings occurred as in the first run.

prs.title: fix(cron): scope cron inner work to the owning agent
prs.body:
## Problem

Cron inner work shared a single `cron-nested` command-queue lane across every agent. One agent's cron turn could therefore occupy the lane another agent's heartbeat had to observe, so a slow or wedged run in one agent could stall unrelated agents' cron slots.

## Change

Scope the cron inner lane to the owning agent.

- `src/process/lanes.ts` — add `CRON_NESTED_LANE_PREFIX`, `isCronNestedAgentLane`, and `resolveCronNestedAgentLane`.
- `src/agents/lanes.ts` — `resolveCronAgentLane(lane, agentId?)` resolves `cron-nested:<agentId>` when the owner is known, and keeps the shared `cron-nested` lane when it is not (unscoped work cannot be attributed to an agent).
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/lanes.ts` — `resolveGlobalLane` reads `context.agentId` for cron lanes.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts` — pass `params.agentId` into `resolveCronAgentLane`.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts` — timeout matching accepts both the per-agent lane and the legacy shared lane.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-fallback-candidate.ts` — resolve the per-agent cron lane instead of using `CommandLane.CronNested` directly.
- `src/process/command-queue.state.ts` — per-agent cron lanes inherit the cron lane width.
- `src/process/command-queue.capacity-groups.ts` — capacity groups can claim dynamically named lanes by prefix, so per-agent cron lanes stay inside the shared cron/hook budget while each agent keeps its own lane queue.
- `src/process/command-queue.ts` — group clear removes prefix index entries.
- `src/gateway/server-lanes.ts` — the `cron-hooks` group declares `memberPrefixes: [CRON_NESTED_LANE_PREFIX]`.

## Why prefix membership

Per-agent cron lanes are named at run time, so an exact member list cannot enumerate them. A prefix keeps every agent's lane inside the same shared budget without publishing agent ids up front. Longest-prefix matching wins so a narrower prefix can shadow a broader one, and prefix-scoped lanes are validated against the same group-ineligibility rules as exact members.

## Tests

- `src/agents/lanes.test.ts` — cron inner work scopes to the owning agent; the shared lane is retained when no agent owns the work.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/lanes.test.ts` — `resolveGlobalLane` scopes cron lanes by `agentId`.
- `src/process/command-queue.capacity-groups.test.ts` — prefix-scoped lanes count against the shared budget and block siblings.

All three files pass; `oxlint` reports no problems on the changed files.

## Note on local verification limits

The `src/cron/**` Vitest shard exceeds this host's 1280 MiB memory bound and could not be executed here — the same failure occurs on untouched files, so it is a pre-existing host constraint rather than a regression from this change. `tsc --noEmit` was likewise killed by the same bound (the host has no `tsgo`/`@typescript/native-preview` available).

prs.title: fix(discord): honor provider interruption policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord realtime playback currently admits a fresh receive stream only when local `bargeIn` is enabled (or output is continuous). With `bargeIn: false`, that prevents provider-side VAD from hearing a new speaker turn even when `interruptResponseOnInputAudio` is enabled. The provider therefore cannot perform the interruption policy it was configured to own.

## Merge brief

- **Root cause:** receive admission during playback was coupled only to local raw-audio barge-in policy.
- **Fix:** retain the resolved provider interruption flag on the realtime speaker session and include it in `canReceiveDuringPlayback()`.
- **Preserved boundary:** raw local audio still does not stop playback when `bargeIn` is disabled; provider input must qualify speech and own the interruption.
- **Protected mode:** when both local and provider interruption are disabled, capture during playback remains blocked.
- **Scope:** one Discord voice source file and two test files; no new config or public API.

## Evidence

### Deterministic proof

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/voice/transcripts-readiness.test.ts extensions/discord/src/voice/voice-session.lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **51/51 passed** on head `4dbdf05f2f53a6ee5864366761aa50d2c2b89fe9`.
- Positive regression: provider interruption enabled + local barge-in disabled admits capture without stopping the player locally.
- Closest negative regression: both interruption paths disabled rejects capture during playback.
- Adjacent readiness regression: provider-owned bidi capture during playback reaches the provider while STT/TTS and protected paths retain their prior expectations.
- `pnpm check:changed` — passed, including formatting, Discord extension tests/typechecks, lint, dead-export, boundary, and import-cycle checks.
- `git diff HEAD^ --check` — passed.
- Independent P0/P1 review found no actionable issues.
- Baseline comparison: the new provider-only lifecycle regression fails on base `231fae1903a04b51df073b25b20906fb4d58799e` because `receiver.subscribe` is called zero times during playback. On candidate `4dbdf05f2f53a6ee5864366761aa50d2c2b89fe9`, that positive case and the both-off negative case both pass (2/2 selected tests).

### Live acoustic Discord proof

The exact public head ran in a fresh isolated ClawLab state against a private Discord guild. The existing bot was shared across disjoint guilds; production configuration and the production Gateway were not changed or restarted.

- **Provider-owned interruption:** with local `bargeIn=false` and provider interruption enabled, a long spoken count was interrupted after eighteen by a fixed QA utterance; the next spoken output was exactly `provider interruption complete`.
- **Both-off protection:** with both controls disabled, the same injected phrase was ignored and the acoustic trace completed the count from one through fifty without the phrase.
- Provider-owned capture: `58.026667s`, SHA-256 `2b7a1f9cbb20ba0e616fc523cd95ff3b4d9595b923b14ae2e96ea1153e4e6acc`.
- Both-off capture: `89.685333s`, SHA-256 `c13a17df15d94dc76d1bce8262513a8e146bbc3671825e72ef19f493a205abe4`.

The raw WAV files and account credentials remain private. The public evidence is the sanitized transcript/result, exact controls, durations, hashes, and exact-head runtime receipts.

## Non-goals

- Changing speech qualification thresholds or VAD behavior.
- Enabling local raw-audio cancellation when `bargeIn` is false.
- Changing non-realtime Discord voice handling.

prs.title: fix(openai): send session affinity on Sign in with ChatGPT requests
prs.body:
Closes #197532

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Sign in with ChatGPT requests on the OpenClaw runtime carry no `session_id` affinity header, so the subscription backend derives a new prompt-cache key for every request and a growing conversation never reads the cache (0% cached input in the reporter's matched runs, against 99% with a stable header).

## User Impact

User impact: conversations under a ChatGPT subscription login reuse the provider's prompt cache from the second request on, the same as Codex logins already do. Nothing changes for API-key users, for proxies, or for turns with caching disabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transport's session-header generator (`buildOpenAIClientHeaders`) sends `session_id` by default only on the native ChatGPT Codex backend; otherwise it needs `compat.sendSessionIdHeader`. Sign in with ChatGPT runs as `openai-responses` on `https://api.openai.com/v1`, so the default is off, and a configured `sendSessionIdHeader: true` is dropped by the catalog-owned compat guard because the route matches the catalog's. The only code that knows the auth flow at request time is the SIWC stream wrapper in the OpenAI plugin; it now hands the transport a model with `sendSessionIdHeader: true` unless the model already states the flag. The generator keeps its existing rules: no header when caching is disabled, a caller-supplied `session_id` wins, and the value is the run's own session id, clamped.

Not changed: the catalog guard, Platform API-key routes, managed proxies, the Codex route, and the body's `prompt_cache_key`.

## Evidence

### Full-product repro on main

Built Gateway from `main` (`4c04a9e9526`) started with `openclaw.mjs gateway run` in a no-network container. Sign in with ChatGPT is pinned to `https://api.openai.com/v1`, so a local HTTPS stand-in for that host (throwaway CA via `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`) sits behind a local CONNECT proxy that the Gateway picks up from `HTTPS_PROXY`. A token-sharing OAuth credential was imported with `openclaw doctor --fix` from the retired `auth-profiles.json` path (exit 0); `agents.defaults.model.primary` is `openai/gpt-6-astra` on the `openclaw` runtime. Two `chat.send` turns in one conversation. What the stand-in recorded per request on `main`:

```
POST /v1/responses  session_id=<absent>  x-client-request-id=c80b0187-…  x-openai-chatpass-test=codex-direct  prompt_cache_key=c80b0187-…:0
POST /v1/responses  session_id=<absent>  x-client-request-id=c80b0187-…  x-openai-chatpass-test=codex-direct  prompt_cache_key=c80b0187-…:0
```

The SIWC marker header and the body's `prompt_cache_key` are there; the `session_id` header the backend keys its cache on is not.

### Live run: the same built Gateway on this change

```
POST /v1/responses  session_id=0bea6f12-8be3-4512-b375-b2f4fc9e61ad  x-client-request-id=0bea6f12-…  x-openai-chatpass-test=codex-direct  prompt_cache_key=0bea6f12-…:0
POST /v1/responses  session_id=0bea6f12-8be3-4512-b375-b2f4fc9e61ad  x-client-request-id=0bea6f12-…  x-openai-chatpass-test=codex-direct  prompt_cache_key=0bea6f12-…:0
```

Both requests carry the same `session_id`, the run's session id, matching the `prompt_cache_key` prefix. Both turns completed (4.7 s, 0.7 s).

Upgrade run: not applicable. This change touches no update, Doctor, config, state or plugin-loading code (one request-time option in the OpenAI plugin's SIWC wrapper and its test), so the latest-stable upgrade rehearsal the repo asks for on those changes does not apply. The `doctor --fix` step in the proof above only seeds a credential into a fresh state directory; it is not an upgrade of an existing installation, and this change does not alter what Doctor imports or retains.

Proof artifice: api.openai.com is a local stand-in reached through a local proxy, the credential is a fake token-sharing profile (never refreshed; expiry a week out), and the model replies are scripted; the Gateway, the OpenAI plugin's SIWC wrapper, the transport, the proxy handling, the credential import and the CLI are the shipped ones. The backend's cache behaviour behind the header is the reporter's measurement (0% vs 99% cached input with the header supplied by hand), not re-measured here.

### Tests

- `extensions/openai/token-sharing-stream.test.ts`: a request through the shipped SIWC wrapper, with its headers built by the real transport builder (`buildOpenAIClientHeaders`), carries `session_id` for the run's session; a model that states `sendSessionIdHeader: false` sends none. The first case fails on `main` (no header), passes here.
- On the proof machine, `pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on that file plus `openai-transport-params.session-header.test.ts` and `provider-transport-session-headers.test.ts`: 8 of 8 in the wrapper file on this change; on `main` with the new cases added, 7 pass and the opt-in case fails (no `session_id`).
- Test lines are net +25 against `main`, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/197532-siwc-session-affinity.txt`: two rows in the existing SIWC wrapper suite; no existing test drives the SIWC wrapper and the session header together.

prs.title: fix(test): UI test browser preflight fails without saying Chromium is missing system libraries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a Linux host where Playwright's Chromium is installed but its system libraries are missing, the UI test browser preflight reinstalls Chromium and then fails with only "Chromium is still not runnable", so the developer cannot tell what to fix.

## User Impact

User impact: developers running `pnpm test:ui` or `pnpm test:ui:e2e` on such a host now see the actual launch error (for example the missing `libnspr4.so`) and the command that installs the libraries. There is no product or runtime change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The preflight probes Chromium with its output discarded. When the browser exists but still cannot start, it now reruns that probe once, prints the first error line, and for a missing shared library names `pnpm --dir ui exec playwright install-deps chromium` as the root-level fix. It does not launch a browser that is missing, and it does not change which browser is selected or installed.

Not included: installing libraries without root. A host without root needs its own user-level library setup; the preflight only reports the cause.

## Evidence

Real entry point on an Ubuntu 26.04 host without root and without Chromium's system libraries (cache paths shortened):

Before:

```text
[ui-e2e] Playwright Chromium is not runnable at <cache>/chromium-1248/chrome-linux64/chrome; installing chromium.
[ui-e2e] Playwright install completed but Chromium is still not runnable at <cache>/chromium-1248/chrome-linux64/chrome.
```

After (exit status stays 1):

```text
[ui-e2e] Playwright Chromium is not runnable at <cache>/chromium-1248/chrome-linux64/chrome; installing chromium.
[ui-e2e] Playwright install completed but Chromium is still not runnable at <cache>/chromium-1248/chrome-linux64/chrome.
[ui-e2e] Chromium launch failed: <cache>/chromium-1248/chrome-linux64/chrome: error while loading shared libraries: libnspr4.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
[ui-e2e] Install Chromium's system libraries as root: pnpm --dir ui exec playwright install-deps chromium
```

With the libraries made visible to the same command, the preflight exits 0 and prints nothing.

### Verification

- `test/scripts/ensure-playwright-chromium.test.ts`: 18 passed, including a new case for the missing-library report. The existing "does not launch missing browsers" case still passes.
- Format, docs format, script lint, and `pnpm tsgo:scripts` passed. `pnpm tsgo:test:root` reports no errors in the changed test; its only errors are in an Android release test whose source the local sparse checkout omits.
- `pnpm check:changed` did not complete locally: its SQLite worker ratchet stage exceeded the host's memory limit twice. CI is the authority for the full gate.
- CI on the first head failed only the test-lines baseline ratchet (net +20 test lines). A 20-line allocation for the regression is added; the ratchet passes locally against current `main`.
- Size: production +25/-1, tests +21/-1, docs +1.

### Limitations

`playwright install-deps chromium` itself was not run (no root on the test host). macOS and Windows paths are unchanged and were not exercised beyond the unit tests.

prs.title: fix(browser): prefer CDP for managed role snapshots
prs.body:
## Summary

- run unscoped managed role snapshots through CDP before Playwright when the request actually asks for role-snapshot features
- publish finalized CDP refs into the Playwright target cache after document revalidation and backend DOM marking
- preserve duplicate `nth` metadata, resolve `domMarker` for both `eN` and `axN`, and disable iframe recursion only on the new fast path

Fixes #133514

## Root cause

The managed snapshot route selected Playwright before CDP. A stalled Playwright role snapshot could therefore consume the request deadline before the existing CDP fallback ran. CDP refs also were not published through the Playwright action cache, so switching the order alone would have returned refs that later actions could not reliably resolve.

The exact-head review also found that the CDP producer omitted `nth` from the first member of a duplicate role/name group. When backend marker publication failed, that first ref fell back to an unqualified `getByRole` locator and strictness-failed.

The route is the ordering owner, CDP snapshot construction is the duplicate-index owner, and Playwright snapshot storage is the ref-publication owner.

## Behavior

CDP-first is limited to requests where all of these are true:

- `plan.wantsRoleSnapshot`
- `refsMode !== "aria"`
- Playwright is available
- the tab has a CDP WebSocket URL
- there is no selector or frame scope

`refs=role` alone is not a trigger. On an early CDP error, the route checks cancellation and falls back to Playwright once. Fallback is not guaranteed after CDP consumes the full request deadline; this change does not partition or extend the budget.

ARIA, selector-scoped, and frame-scoped requests remain Playwright-first. Recursive actionable CDP iframe refs remain out of scope.

Duplicate CDP role/name groups now publish `nth: 0` for the first ref and the later zero-based indexes for siblings. Singleton refs still omit `nth`.

## Validation

- pre-fix original focused reproduction: 6 expected failures across ordering, marker resolution, publication, and iframe recursion
- pre-fix duplicate regression: real Chromium failed because `e1` matched both same-name buttons after its backend marker write was rejected
- focused browser tests: 159 passed
- full Browser plugin suite: 3,495 passed, 26 skipped
- real Chromium snapshot-to-action suite: 3 passed; both duplicate native refs act after marker publication failure, and the cursor-only control remains actionable through its marker
- changed-file guards: formatting, boundaries, dead exports, dependency pins, assertions, and related guards passed; local aggregate extension typecheck reached an unrelated stale shared grammY install mismatch
- exact lint regression from the first review-fix head was reproduced locally and repaired in test code
- autoreview: no actionable findings, confidence 0.99
- test-audit: producer metadata is covered by a normal unit test and marker-failure actionability by the real Chromium boundary without a test-only production seam
- exact-head CI: 57 successful, 43 skipped, 0 failed or pending on `34ad2663ddce62b07aff12066f56b7e4256482c8` ([run 33342515329](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33342515329))

## Scope

- production: +82 / -42, net +40
- tests and test support: +452 / -135, net +317
- removed the oversized snapshot omnibus from the general server contract test and moved its focused route coverage to `agent.snapshot.local-managed.test.ts`
- no config, schema, protocol, dependency, planning-contract, or changelog changes

prs.title: fix(ai): name the output cap when max_tokens cuts an Anthropic tool call
prs.body:
Fixes #196544

## What Problem This Solves

An Anthropic turn that hits `max_tokens` inside a `tool_use` block shows up only as `Provider completed stream with an incomplete tool call`. The real cause is that the request's output cap was reached. For a configured model row without `maxTokens`, that cap is a silent default the user never set. Users therefore read a configuration limit as a provider defect. The report shows 12 such failures in one day, each at exactly `usage.output = 8192`.

## User Impact

The failure now reads `Provider completed stream with an incomplete tool call: output token limit reached (max_tokens N); raise the model's maxTokens`, with the actual request cap filled in. The user can see the cause and the fix (the `maxTokens` workaround from the issue) without opening a transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper asked for a focused diagnostic repair that keeps the strict rejection of incomplete tool calls. Guessing the catalog family, raising budgets or adding continuation policy are out of scope.

- **Lifecycle:** `packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-stream-lifecycle.ts`, used by both the Anthropic SDK path and the transport path.
  - It records the terminal `stop_reason` from `message_delta`.
  - When the stream still has an unsealed tool call and that reason is `max_tokens`, the rejection names the `max_tokens` value the request sent.
  - Every other incomplete-tool-call case keeps the exact existing message.
- **Classifier:** `isPreDispatchToolCallRejectionMessage` (`src/agents/failover/message-patterns.ts`) also accepts the new message as a prefix. Retry and recovery treat it exactly as before: a pre-dispatch rejection, nothing executed.

## Evidence

![live run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/196544/proof.png)

**Live run:**

- An isolated source Gateway ran on loopback. Provider `stubanth` used `api: "anthropic-messages"` and pointed at a local Anthropic SSE stub.
- The model row had `contextTokens` and no `maxTokens`, as in the report.
- The stub answered each request with a `tool_use` block cut off by `stop_reason: "max_tokens"`.
- Both runs used the same tree, with the two changed files from main `0b9114291429` (left) or from this branch `8452188f5893` (right).
- Command: `openclaw infer model run --gateway --model stubanth/claude-fable-5-2 --prompt "write a long note"`.

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| error shown | `Provider completed stream with an incomplete tool call` | `Provider completed stream with an incomplete tool call: output token limit reached (max_tokens 32000); raise the model's maxTokens` |
| request cap the stub saw | `max_tokens=32000` | `max_tokens=32000` (unchanged) |

**Tests:**

- **New lifecycle test:** `packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-max-tokens-tool-call.test.ts` covers both the Anthropic SDK and the transport implementations. Both cases fail on main and pass here.
- **New classifier test:** `src/agents/failover/pre-dispatch-tool-call-rejection.test.ts` checks that the new message and the old one both stay pre-dispatch rejections.
- **Existing suites:** `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` and `transport-failure.test.ts` pass, 91 tests in total.
- **Checks:** `oxfmt`, `oxlint` and `check:line-cap-ratchet` pass. `check:test-lines-ratchet` passes with a 67-line allocation, `config/test-lines-allocations/196544-anthropic-max-tokens-tool-call.txt`.

prs.title: fix: let Mac packaging run from a symlinked checkout path
prs.body:
Fixes #201528

## What Problem This Solves

Packaging the macOS app from source fails with `plugins.json: Unexpected end of JSON input` when the checkout is reached through a symlink, for example any checkout under `/tmp` on macOS (`/tmp` links to `/private/tmp`). The error points at a JSON file, so nothing tells the developer that the path is the trigger.

## User Impact

Developers can package the Mac app from a checkout reached through a symlinked path. There is no change for packaging from a real path, and no user-visible change in OpenClaw itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

`scripts/lib/desktop-runtime-plugins.mjs` runs its `plan` or `stamp` command only when it was started directly, which it checks by comparing `argv[1]` with its own module path. Node resolves the module path through symlinks while `argv[1]` keeps the path as typed, so through a symlink the check fails, the script prints nothing and exits 0, and staging reads an empty plan. This change compares the real path of `argv[1]`, and only when that path exists: importers such as the Linux staging tests pass a non-path `argv[1]`.

Other scripts use the same kind of check, including the shared `isDirectRunUrl` helper. This PR keeps to the Mac packaging path; the issue lists the wider follow-up.

## Evidence

- **Mac runtime staging through a symlinked checkout:** on macOS arm64, `scripts/stage-mac-runtime.sh <tmp>/runtime arm64` was started from a symlink under `/tmp` that points to a checkout built at `a0def92`. With main's `desktop-runtime-plugins.mjs` it fails with `plugins.json: Unexpected end of JSON input`. With this branch it exits 0, stages the Codex plugin and records `stagedOfficialPlugins` in the staged `build-info.json`, so both `plan` and `stamp` ran. Terminal output, filtered to the staging, error and exit lines (temp paths shortened to `$TMPDIR`):

  ```text
  # HEAD a0def92f1f8 on main 949e51dff17, 2026-11-19T00:06:21Z
  ## main's desktop-runtime-plugins.mjs
  SyntaxError: $TMPDIR/openclaw-mac-runtime.oNK47k/plugins.json: Unexpected end of JSON input
  SyntaxError: $TMPDIR/openclaw-mac-runtime.oNK47k/plugins.json: Unexpected end of JSON input
  exit=1
  ## this branch
  Staging official plugins codex (all-plugin estimate: 1641899842 bytes)
  exit=0
  stagedOfficialPlugins: {"commit":"a0def92f1f87a8cfb1798dfa338eac3a62a85a12","pluginIds":["codex"]}
  ```

- **Regression test** `test/scripts/desktop-runtime-plugins.test.ts` "plans when the script is run through a symlinked checkout path": fails on main (empty output, JSON parse error) and passes here; the file passes 23/23.
- **Linux staging**, which imports this module: `node --test ../scripts/test-stage-runtime.mjs ../scripts/test-stage-package.mjs` from `apps/linux/src-tauri`, 25/25 pass.
- oxlint, oxfmt, the scripts typecheck (`test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json`) and `git diff --check` are clean.

Not run: a full `scripts/package-mac-app.sh` app build; the staging step above is the part this change affects.

prs.title: fix: reject out-of-range config array indexes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw config set` accepted array indexes beyond the current length and wrote null holes into the saved configuration.

Fixes #196098

## Why This Change Was Made

Array writes reject skipped indexes before modifying the array. The error points to an existing index for updates or the next index for appending; on an empty array it directs users to index 0. An index equal to the current length still appends, including when creating a nested value.

## User Impact

Invalid array paths fail without corrupting existing values, while append-by-index continues to work.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli-path.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 19 tests passed in 2.30s on the source tree committed as `664480c2c7598eb804ca464d48029a88e853c671`.
- The same test file failed on pinned base `999e873a916552e652239e47e9ad26dea4228517`: all 3 new out-of-range cases failed because the base did not throw; the other 16 tests passed.
- Existing live CLI proof at prior repair head `73db5be0b2b3b092baf2fe2f9993c697af3d7d30` demonstrated sparse persistence before the repair, rejection after it, and append-at-length. This update changes only the rejection guidance.
- A fresh CLI replay on the pinned base stopped before mutation because `run-node` could not verify that the affected Gateway was offline; the isolated config remained unchanged. This attempt is not counted as product proof.
- `openclaw-preflight.sh --profile auto` passed at head `664480c2c7598eb804ca464d48029a88e853c671` against pinned base `999e873a916552e652239e47e9ad26dea4228517`; format, lint, core TypeScript, core test typecheck, and focused tests passed (19 tests). Merge compatibility was clean against observed main `d6f628897ad7830e7cd54063c18de41c9c4cc73e`.
- Established contract: an array index equal to the current length still appends.

```text
$ pnpm openclaw config set 'plugins.entries.demo.config.tags.5' z
before: base 0eabe3398c9e0334e8c3b9b03f6a12040c7a1c12 => exit 0; saved tags=["a","b",null,null,null,"z"]
tested head SHA: 73db5be0b2b3b092baf2fe2f9993c697af3d7d30 => exit 1; Array index 5 is out of range for an array of length 2; saved tags=["a","b"]

negative-control: `pnpm openclaw config set 'plugins.entries.demo.config.tags.2' z` => exit 0; saved tags=["a","b","z"]
```

<details>
<summary>proof-live.sh</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

expect_out_of_range="${EXPECT_OUT_OF_RANGE:-reject}"
pnpm_home="${PNPM_HOME:-}"
if [ -z "$pnpm_home" ]; then
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin*) pnpm_home="$HOME/Library/pnpm" ;;
    MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) pnpm_home="${LOCALAPPDATA:-$HOME/AppData/Local}/pnpm" ;;
    *) pnpm_home="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/pnpm" ;;
  esac
fi
scratch="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$scratch"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$scratch/home" "$scratch/state" "$scratch/xdg"
export PNPM_HOME="$pnpm_home"
export HOME="$scratch/home"
export XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$scratch/xdg"
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$scratch/state"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$scratch/state/openclaw.json"

reset_config() {
  printf '%s\n' '{"plugins":{"entries":{"demo":{"config":{"tags":["a","b"]}}}}}' > "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"
}

saved_tags() {
  node - <<'NODE'
const fs = require("node:fs");
const config = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.env.OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH, "utf8"));
console.log(JSON.stringify(config.plugins.entries.demo.config.tags));
NODE
}

case "$expect_out_of_range" in
  reject) expected_status=1; expected_tags='["a","b"]' ;;
  allow) expected_status=0; expected_tags='["a","b",null,null,null,"z"]' ;;
  *) printf 'EXPECT_OUT_OF_RANGE must be reject or allow\n' >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

reset_config
if pnpm openclaw config set 'plugins.entries.demo.config.tags.5' z > "$scratch/out-of-range.log" 2>&1; then
  out_of_range_status=0
else
  out_of_range_status=$?
fi
printf 'out-of-range exit=%s\n' "$out_of_range_status"
if grep -Fq 'Array index 5 is out of range for an array of length 2' "$scratch/out-of-range.log"; then
  grep -F 'Array index 5 is out of range for an array of length 2' "$scratch/out-of-range.log"
else
  sed "s|$scratch|<temp>|g" "$scratch/out-of-range.log" | tail -n 20
fi
actual_tags="$(saved_tags)"
printf 'saved tags=%s\n' "$actual_tags"
if [ "$out_of_range_status" -ne "$expected_status" ] || [ "$actual_tags" != "$expected_tags" ]; then
  exit 1
fi

reset_config
pnpm openclaw config set 'plugins.entries.demo.config.tags.2' z > "$scratch/append.log" 2>&1
printf 'append exit=0\n'
grep -F 'Updated plugins.entries.demo.config.tags[2].' "$scratch/append.log"
actual_tags="$(saved_tags)"
printf 'saved tags=%s\n' "$actual_tags"
[ "$actual_tags" = '["a","b","z"]' ]
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(knowledge): scribes stop after one item when a run can do more
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Knowledge scribes stop after one item when a run is allowed to do more. On Nov 13, a scheduled Knowledge Consolidation run retired 1 of its "up to 10" written Timelines and reviewed 1 of its "up to 5" pages. With 200+ Timelines waiting, a weekly scribe at that pace would take years. Learn from Granola did the same thing, ingesting one meeting per run while others stayed pending.

## User Impact

User impact: scheduled scribes now work toward a stated amount each run instead of stopping after the first item.
- **Knowledge Consolidation:** a weekly run retires 15 written Timelines and reviews 6 pages; a nightly run does 10 and 5.
- **Learn from Granola:** a scheduled run ingests 4 meetings. A one-time run ingests everything pending.
- **Saved instructions:** unedited saved run messages upgrade automatically when the Scribes page opens. A message you edited is offered the new text instead, including one edited from the version just before the amounts. A message that names its own amount keeps it. A consolidation scribe on a custom, interval or one-time schedule gets no amount, so the skill's defaults apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The skills described the counts as ceilings ("up to 10"), and models read that as permission to stop early. The skill text now calls them targets, and cites this PR as the incident behind them. A run stops short only when nothing is left, or when what's left is held up for a reason outside the run. Compaction is no reason to stop. The generated run message states the amount for the schedule, so a weekly run does more than a nightly one.

Each target is sized to fit the scheduler's 60-minute limit for an agent turn with no timeout of its own. A new run-wording version lets earlier generated messages be recognized and upgraded. When a message that differs from every generated version is matched, only its source settings are compared, so an edited message from before the amounts still keeps its meeting settings. An edited message that keeps the current work step but names no amount, where the current wording adds one, is offered the new instructions.

## Evidence

- **Upgrade from the latest release, real Control UI** (fresh Gateway state, 2026.11.5 → this PR's head `0ec6b35`):
  - On 2026.11.5, set up Knowledge Consolidation (nightly) and Learn from conversations from the Scribes page, then edited the conversations automation's message by appending a line.
  - Restarted the same state on this PR's build and opened the Scribes page.
  - **Consolidation (unedited):** upgraded on its own. Its message now carries `Each run: retire 10 written Timelines and review 5 pages.` and the current steps. Schedule (`45 3 * * *`, America/Los_Angeles), delivery (none), failure alert (after 2) and enabled state are unchanged.
  - **Learn from conversations (edited):** keeps the appended line and its earlier wording. The page shows **New run instructions** instead of overwriting it. Schedule, delivery and failure alert are unchanged.
- **Live consolidation runs on a Gateway** (a vault with about 440 pages):
  - **Nov 13, old wording:** retired 1 Timeline and reviewed 1 page.
  - **Nov 15, skill-default targets:** retired 11 Timelines and reviewed 5 pages in 36 minutes.
  - **Nov 15, weekly 15/6 run message:** retired 14 Timelines and reviewed 4 pages in 44 minutes, at about 3 minutes per Timeline. An unrelated Gateway shutdown then interrupted the run. Each retirement and review was verified.
- **Tests:** `pnpm test extensions/knowledge/src/scribes-state.test.ts extensions/knowledge/src/scribes-view.test.ts extensions/knowledge/src/skill-packaging.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 49 tests. They cover:
  - per-schedule amounts
  - the Granola amount, which one-time runs don't get
  - unedited upgrades from every earlier wording
  - edited messages from the version just before the amounts, for Consolidation and Granola, being offered them
  - an edited message keeping its settings, and a message naming its own amount keeping it
  - custom cron, interval and one-time schedules staying on the skill defaults
  - the update dialog's changed-lines diff
- **Other checks:** `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint and oxfmt pass.
- **Gap:** a live Granola run with the 4-meeting target is pending a Granola sign-in on the proof Gateway.

prs.title: fix: keep session assessments working with ChatGPT token sharing
prs.body:
Related: #175646

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: session assessments fail before inference on ChatGPT token-sharing routes because the observer's internal token and temperature defaults are treated as mandatory limits.

## User Impact

The observer can use the selected ChatGPT token-sharing credential without switching runtimes, accounts, endpoints, or billing routes. API-key calls keep the existing sampling limits. Explicit caller-required limits remain strict and are still rejected before inference when unsupported.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the distinction between preferred internal defaults and required sampling limits through the existing isolated-completion contract. The observer marks its hardcoded defaults as preferred; Codex omits them only after resolving an actual token-sharing credential. Other calls keep strict behavior unless they opt into that intent. This adds no configuration option, new authentication path, or permission bypass.

The dependency contract was re-inspected at Codex `633ab199cfd724aa78013c006b27a2b3d049fc3b` (the retained execution proof used the earlier pinned source): the native Responses request does not carry these sampling fields. The existing token-sharing rejection remains in place for strict requests.

## Evidence

- **November 11 candidate:** `191a6937efd18ff868472e412fcd725ca18b6456`, tree `f70e02fa56e3308eec681a35aa43a72d991c2863`. Independent native review found no actionable mechanical-conflict or clock-fixture defect. Both new performance-clock spies use scoped `using` resources; dedicated deadline tests retain advancing clocks and verify expiry, cancellation, cleanup and retry budgets. Production deadlines are unchanged. New-head hosted CI remains pending.

- **Current-main integration:** merged `ae651f116c7713295d6969b36bb1762ee0196edc`, retaining opt-in preferred sampling beside upstream invalid-output classification, fallback deadlines and physical work settlement. Independent review found no conflict-resolution defect. Core and extension types, focused production/test lint, formatting, the test-line allocation check and observer preparation (8 checks) passed. The repaired native API-boundary suite passed 13 checks; the budget/deadline suites passed 31 checks. This is integration verification, not a repeat of the retained real-grant execution.
- **Test-fixture correction:** the harness-v2 budget case hit its inherited one-second deadline during cold module loading. The token-budget suite and API-boundary sampling table now use the existing monotonic-clock spy pattern (the API-key fixture likewise hit its inherited five-second deadline during cold loading); the request timeout and production deadline implementation are unchanged. The budget/deadline run passed all 31 checks; deadline behavior remains checked with an advancing clock.

- Retained execution proof on original candidate `16d08c5bc9b39a67aa539e2da12a646e98421fec`. [Real-grant Gateway execution, upgrade receipts, controls and limitations](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/tree/bf880940fe9afa8b605ef89064e60f79625851a0).
- **Actual Gateway + real SIWC grant:** four model-written observer assessments during a successful 61.8-second session, then persisted `done` state. OpenClaw/Sol drives ordinary activity; Codex/Luna performs the observer assessments. The real grant was obtained through supported stable sign-in; no production credential was copied and no provider response was mocked in this scenario.
- **Latest-stable upgrade:** official npm 2026.11.2 → exact candidate through canonical Doctor migration, same isolated state. Account/profile identity and utility model preserved; retained session ID/provider/model/runtime and transcript payloads match. Ordinary Codex-primary turns hit the same separate prepared-API-key support rejection on both builds; the successful observer scenario uses a new OpenClaw-primary session. This is not an identical primary-workload red/green comparison.
- **Controls:** same real grant + explicit 37-token/temperature-0 limits rejects before native launch. Actual managed Codex 0.164.0 preserves 300/0.2 and 37/0 in two physical TLS WebSocket API-key requests. These controls use the built harness API; API-key credentials/receiver output are synthetic. The artifact discloses the PID-observation limit and all failed setup attempts.
- Prior [native synthetic proof](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/tree/5eff9dc8b0576a1b025a69706f22326034c88f58) remains historical evidence. Boundary tests: 13 passed; removing the repair fails only the preferred token-sharing case. Budget propagation: 7 passed; prefix stability: 14 passed. Core typecheck, focused lint/formatting, import inventory and package-boundary compilation passed; exact-head CI was green for the original candidate, not this new integration head.
- The original candidate's independent read-only code review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. CLI autoreview was unavailable due to authentication failure; no successful CLI review is claimed.

**Owner decision remains open:** accept the narrow opt-in advisory contract while keeping omitted-mode callers strict. The evidence does not claim that this decision has been approved.

Real provider inference and Gateway runs above were confined to the isolated proof profile. No production Gateway/configuration change, merge or deployment was performed. Runtime deadline, malformed-output recovery and the separate ordinary Codex support gate are outside this PR.

prs.title: fix: keep carried-over scheduled jobs running after updates
prs.body:
Fixes #200600

## What problem this solves

An upgrade could make a carried-over scheduled job report that its account had been replaced, even though nobody changed the account. Newly created jobs still worked.

## What changes

Upgrade Doctor operates on a private state copy. It now identifies copied credential databases by their eventual live paths. For jobs an earlier upgrade already broke, `openclaw doctor --fix` checks the retained upgrade receipt and verifies that the credential is still the same before repairing the saved job. It leaves unverifiable, replaced or revoked accounts alone. It does not enable disabled jobs, edit schedules, or replay missed runs.

The existing account owner still computes the same hash over the same namespace and credential lifetimes. The PR adds no environment override, schema, permission, scanner exception, or budget increase. The receipt reader treats `appVersion` as an application build stamp while retaining its filename and work-directory equality checks.

## Evidence

**[Four end-to-end cases on `95e0215cfaf5`, with redacted terminal results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200653#issuecomment-6991396273)**

- **Upgrade prevention:** Real `2026.9.7`, `2026.10.10` and `2026.11.5` releases each created a scheduled job. On first start of the final candidate, all three jobs retained their IDs and settings and ran successfully through the real scheduler.
- **Already-broken job:** An unpatched upgrade produced a real receipt, and the carried-over `2026.11.4` job failed as though its account had been replaced. The final Doctor CLI restored the same account; the same job then ran successfully. Its schedule, settings, prior run history and scheduler state were unchanged by Doctor.
- All four used isolated state and a local model stand-in; no production job, credential or live hosted model was used. The old branch reproduced an unrelated post-swap SQLite startup failure on all three baselines; a normal merge of `main` brought in [the upstream startup fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200596). No force push or schema-check override.
- **94 tests across six files passed** on the final commit: state upgrade (12), credential authorization (14), cron inference binding (5), CLI registration (43), and Doctor migration (20). Runtime build, the previously failing session-identity check, and `git diff --check` passed. Tests cover actual replacement, revoked or unverifiable accounts and repeat repair. Local results do not substitute for required hosted CI.

**CodeQL alert 1216:** The SHA-256 input here consists of a fixed namespace, profile ID, database paths and owner-issued random credential-lifetime UUIDs. It is not a password hash: neither passwords nor bearer credentials enter this digest. The hash algorithm and bindings are unchanged; no alert dismissal or scanner suppression was made.

**Earlier evidence:** [Daniel’s macOS VM upgrade](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200653#issuecomment-6954076318) and [the earlier isolated recovery transcript](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200653#issuecomment-6991107127) are prior-revision proof. At `c3dfd14327c7`, 93 tests, scoped lint, formatting, core types, the max-lines and session-identity checks passed; environment names stayed at 461/461. Earlier recovery work at `f16eacaaf16e` passed 50 focused tests and local review. The final-head results above supersede the earlier live-proof gap.

Co-authored-by: daniel-lxs <57051444+daniel-lxs@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: VACInc <3279061+VACInc@users.noreply.github.com>

## Work sessions

prs.title: fix: warn callers before retrying a tool action that lost its reply
prs.body:
Related: #145117 (durable receipts after restart; this fixes an already-settled run).

## What Problem This Solves

A tool can finish its work even if the agent never sends a final reply. In that case, a caller waiting on the run could get just `failed`, losing OpenClaw’s warning to check what already happened before retrying.

## User Impact

`agent.wait` now returns the existing warning, so a caller knows to verify the result before repeating an action. The run still reports an error. This does not automatically retry the action or turn a missing reply into a success.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway had already recorded the right message but left it out of the settled response read by waiters. Carry only the two existing host-authored missing-reply notices across that boundary. Other diagnostics on this path remain generic; timeouts are unchanged.

## Evidence

Two isolated real Gateways, one harmless workspace file write each, then no final reply. On the original package, waiting on that same run returned `status: error` and `failed`. On the fixed build, it returned `status: error` with the verify-before-retry warning. Both histories showed one successful write, and the expected file was present. No live provider or operator Gateway was used.

```text
Real CLI → gateway call agent.wait, same run as the completed tool action:
Before (3da0bc802e10): status=error; error="failed"; writes=1; file present
After  (d1276e15794d + production patch in c3c538c227dc): status=error; error ends "please verify before retrying."; writes=1; file present
```

The focused regression on unpatched source failed with `failed` where the warning was expected (1 failed, 3 passed); all four cases passed with the fix. All **382 tests** in the affected Gateway suite passed on the final change, including controls for generic producer errors and timeouts. Runtime build, core typecheck, targeted type-aware lint and formatting passed.

Local ClawSweeper found no correctness or security findings on the committed range. It asked for shipped-entry-point proof; the redacted `agent.wait` comparison above supplies it. This verifies an already-settled run, not receipt recovery across a restart or a guarantee that a caller will act on the warning.

Contributor: @VACInc requested and directed the investigation and fix.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix: stop one dropped connection from locking plugins out of a model
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a plugin asks OpenClaw for a one-shot model call (for example lossless-claw summarizing a conversation) and the network connection drops before the provider answers, OpenClaw puts the whole login on a cooldown for that model. The plugin's retry a moment later is refused with "Auth profile … is temporarily unavailable", so one brief network blip turns into a failed job. For lossless-claw this means compaction falls back to plain truncation and the conversation loses detail.

## User Impact

A connection that drops before the provider sends anything no longer locks plugins out of that model for 30 seconds. The plugin's own retry, or the next configured profile, goes through on a fresh connection. Real provider failures (rate limits, auth, billing, timeouts after the response started) still put the profile on cooldown exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The one-shot completion path always told the auth-health policy that the provider had started, so a pre-response socket close was recorded as a provider timeout. The policy in `auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` already intends transport-only failures to stay out of shared profile health ("so one bad … connection does not cool down an otherwise healthy provider profile"); this path just never told it the truth.

Key points:
- **What changes:** `providerStarted` is now derived from the terminal `provider_transport_failure` diagnostic. It is false only when no provider events were emitted, there is no content, there is no response id, and the diagnostic is not a WebSocket leg that fell back to SSE.
- **What does not change:** profile rotation keeps its existing trigger, so a pre-response drop on one profile still moves on to the next. Rate-limit, auth and billing classifications are unaffected because only `timeout` depends on `providerStarted`.
- **Not in this PR:** the embedded agent-turn path (`assistant-failure.ts`) derives `providerStarted` separately and may have the same gap. It is left alone to keep this change to one concern.

## Evidence

Live failure on a gateway running current main plus local patches (email redacted). One socket close, then the retry refused 14 ms after the first attempt returned:

```
07:49:05.070 [model-fetch] error provider=openai model=gpt-5.6-luna elapsedMs=507 name=TypeError causeName=SocketError causeCode=UND_ERR_SOCKET
07:49:05.092 [lcm] empty normalized summary on first attempt; provider=openai; model=gpt-5.6-luna … retrying with conservative settings
07:49:05.106 [lcm] runtime.llm.complete error: Plugin LLM completion failed: Auth lookup failed for provider "openai": Auth profile "openai:<email>" is temporarily unavailable for openai/gpt-5.6-luna.
07:49:05.108 [lcm] ALL PROVIDERS EXHAUSTED: 1 candidate(s) tried, none succeeded. Compaction falling back to deterministic truncation.
```

Tests in `src/agents/simple-completion-runtime.test.ts`:
- **Regression test** (builds the failure through the real `assignTransportErrorDetails` from `TypeError("fetch failed")` over an `UND_ERR_SOCKET` cause, with the real classifier). It checks that p1 is not cooled, the call rotates to p2, and p2 succeeds. **Fails on current main** (`markAuthProfileFailure` called with `reason: "timeout"`) and passes with this change.
- **Boundary tests:** a timeout is still recorded after provider events, after a response id, after a WebSocket leg fell back to SSE, and after partial output. Each one was shown failing by removing the matching guard from the predicate.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/agents/simple-completion-runtime.test.ts
  stock source:  Tests 1 failed | 23 passed (24)
  patched:       Tests 24 passed (24)
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/agents/simple-completion-runtime.plugin-scope.test.ts src/agents/simple-completion src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy
  Test Files 7 passed (7), Tests 114 passed (114)
pnpm tsgo:core   rc=0
oxlint / oxfmt --check on touched files: clean
```
</details>

AI-assisted (Claude Code); reviewed adversarially by Codex and a separate Claude pass before filing. The rotation and stale-WebSocket-diagnostic points above came from those reviews.

prs.title: fix: release PR lookup state when sessions retire
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long-running Gateways retain PR lookup identities for sessions that have already been removed. A session that was both prepared for the sidebar and watched by a client can also leave its PR cell alive after invalidation and the last unsubscribe.

## User Impact

Retired sessions release their PR lookup state instead of increasing the Gateway's memory floor. Active watchers keep their existing lifetime. No configuration, schema, migration, or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prepared reader removed cells without removing their reverse-index entries, and invalidation left watched cells marked as prepared. Clear both forms of prepared ownership during invalidation, retire unused cells through the existing helper, and clear the reverse index when the owner stops. This adds six production lines for the missing cleanup and removes duplicated retirement logic.

Related: #192350 renames this owner as part of the GitHub-plugin migration; preserve this cleanup when carrying it across.

## Evidence

Both new regressions fail on the exact parent and pass with the fix. The first retains 21.5 MB for 5,000 retired synthetic identities on the parent; the second proves an invalidated source is collectible after its last watcher leaves. All 56 focused tests pass. The new regression file takes 642 ms of test execution (23.10 s isolated wall with compiler reuse); Exact-head CI completed in 12m30s; its Node jobs took 159–281s including setup, not separate per-file measurements. The affected Chromium/real-Gateway scenario passes in 27.26 s of test execution (151.90 s Vitest wall after fixture builds), preserving PR/CI presentation across workspace and reader changes.

The committed `scripts/perf/session-pr-prepared-retention.ts` drives the public subscription owner with 24,000 distinct retired session keys per run. Five alternating pairs reduce the median post-GC slope from **4,205.93 to 3.40 bytes/key**: **84.12 MB to 0.068 MB** over 20,000 additional keys. Identities are deliberately flattened 4 KiB synthetic strings, not an estimate of typical session size. Two A/A controls reproduce the baseline slope. CPU is unchanged within A/A variation; sampled allocation decreases about 2.3%. This is owner-lifecycle proof, not a production memory forecast.

Independent Codex review through P2 found no actionable issues. No projection or prepared-row internals are changed.

`pnpm check:changed --staged` passes every selected stage except the existing unused-export scans. The clean exact parent `2ea3a1760e21ce8e7ceafb9a078c0b2c8547d590` reproduces the identical 36 production / 29 full-tree findings, with zero additions or removals. The compaction exports originate in #201304 (`777fc99a8993b`); the orphaned UI test helper originates in #198967 (`a90c5419b779d`). Those main validation regressions were subsequently repaired by #201497 (`bf7681df7893a`), which landed while this lane was validating; no duplicate cleanup is included here. Format, lint, all selected type graphs, database guards, and zero runtime import cycles pass.

[Exact-head CI 44426602125](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44426602125) passed on `e8be77b5c984e60241e1aaae5dcd58d6ded97c9b`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, without a rerun or admin exception. [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201533#issuecomment-6995628095) has no findings or before-merge items on that same head. Its proof-boundary note is accurate: the GC rig measures the subscription owner directly, while the separate Chromium/real-Gateway test validates the user flow.

prs.title: fix(secrets): yield during multi-agent auth-store preparation
prs.body:
Fixes #149933.

## What Problem This Solves

`prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot` (`src/secrets/runtime.ts`) loads and
`structuredClone`s every candidate agent's auth store in one synchronous
`for` loop before it ever yields to the event loop. Both call sites in the
function (the fast-path branch and the resolver-path branch) share this
loop via `loadAuthStoresWithMigrationIsolation`, and it runs on **every**
config hot reload via `activateRuntimeSecrets` in
`src/gateway/server-reload-managed-secrets.ts` — even a reload that only
flips which agent is `default`.

On a multi-agent deployment (the report cites 237 agents on a slow disk)
this synchronous scan blocks the Node event loop for the entire duration of
the reload, so the Gateway cannot service any other request (chat replies,
health checks, etc.) until every agent's auth store has been read and
cloned. The reporter measured ~47s of blocked time on their deployment.

The issue's own suggested fix — skipping the secrets rebuild entirely when
only `agents.list` default flags changed — was reviewed by the repo's
automated triage and rejected as imprecise: unchanged agent IDs don't
guarantee unchanged credential dependencies, so skipping the rebuild could
serve stale runtime state. The triage instead recommended a scheduling fix
that keeps full-refresh semantics but makes the multi-agent preparation
cooperatively yield, which is what this PR does.

## The Fix

`loadAuthStoresWithMigrationIsolation` now yields to the event loop every
25 agent directories (`setImmediate`-based, matching the existing
`SWEEP_YIELD_BATCH_SIZE` batching pattern already used by the task-registry
maintenance sweep in `src/tasks/task-registry.maintenance.ts`), and both
call sites now `await` it. Publication/activation semantics, atomic
snapshot commit, and the credentials-revision watermark are untouched —
only the read loop's scheduling changes.

## Evidence

New regression test
(`src/secrets/runtime.fast-path.test.ts`, "returns control to the event
loop before finishing a large multi-agent auth-store load") drives
`prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot` with 30 synthetic agent dirs and asserts
that control returns to the caller (a still-pending promise) before all 30
auth stores have been loaded — i.e. the event loop gets a chance to run
other queued work partway through the scan.

Confirmed this test fails on the pre-fix code by reverting only the
source file and rerunning:

```
$ git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/secrets/runtime.ts   # (pre-fix state in this session)
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/secrets/runtime.fast-path.test.ts -t "returns control to the event loop"
 × secrets runtime fast path > returns control to the event loop before finishing a large multi-agent auth-store load
   → expected 30 to be less than 30
 Tests  1 failed | 13 skipped (14)
```

Restored the fix and reran — passes, along with the full related suites:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/secrets/runtime.fast-path.test.ts src/secrets/runtime.auth-migration-isolation.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-managed-secrets.test.ts
 ✓ |gateway-server| src/gateway/server-reload-managed-secrets.test.ts (8 tests)
 ✓ |secrets| src/secrets/runtime.fast-path.test.ts (7 tests, incl. the new one)
 ✓ |secrets| src/secrets/runtime.auth-migration-isolation.test.ts (1 test)
 Test Files  2 passed (2) / 1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15) / 8 passed (8)
```

Also ran, both clean:

```
$ pnpm tsgo:core
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/secrets/runtime.ts src/secrets/runtime.fast-path.test.ts
[exited with code 0]
```

`git diff --check`: clean (no whitespace errors).

## Real-behavior reload responsiveness proof

Addressing the "needs real behavior proof" review: ran a standalone script
(not committed — scratch-only, deleted after use) that drives the actual
`prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot` production path against 250 real,
SQLite-backed agent auth-profile stores on disk (via `saveAuthProfileStore`,
the same persistence the Gateway uses), while a real `http` server stands in
for a concurrent Gateway request. It logs when the `prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot`
call itself returns control (i.e. how long the caller is blocked before the
function can yield at all), when the concurrent HTTP request completes, and
when the reload finishes.

Pre-fix (`git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/secrets/runtime.ts`), calling
`prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot` blocks the event loop for the *entire*
synchronous scan before returning any promise at all, so nothing —
including accepting the concurrent request's connection — can run until
then:

```
[proof] agents=250
[proof] prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot() call returned control after 468.8ms (synchronous portion before first real yield)
[proof] concurrent HTTP request completed at +495.1ms
[proof] reload finished at +495.2ms, auth_stores_loaded=250
```

Post-fix (restored, `git checkout HEAD -- src/secrets/runtime.ts`), the call
returns almost immediately and the concurrent request completes well before
the reload itself finishes:

```
[proof] agents=250
[proof] prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot() call returned control after 52.4ms (synchronous portion before first real yield)
[proof] concurrent HTTP request completed at +168.9ms
[proof] reload finished at +515.2ms, auth_stores_loaded=250
[proof] concurrent request completed before reload finished: true
```

So pre-fix, the caller (and by extension any other queued Gateway work) is
blocked for ~469ms out of the ~495ms total reload before the function can
even yield once; post-fix it's blocked for only ~52ms before yielding, and a
concurrent request completes in ~169ms while the reload is still running
(~515ms total) — i.e. the Gateway can service other requests during the
scan instead of only after it. This sandbox's tmpfs-backed SQLite reads are
far faster than the reporter's "slow disk", so absolute numbers here are much
smaller than the reported ~47s, but the relative before/after behavior
(fully blocking vs. yielding-and-interleaving) is the same mechanism the fix
targets.

## AI assistance disclosure

This change was written by an autonomous Claude Code agent (Sonnet 5).


## November 18 update

Updated against current main while preserving its newer lifecycle/admission behavior. 10 secrets runtime fast-path tests and formatting checks passed; the updated regression observes actual next-macrotask progress rather than assuming synchronous admission. Independent source review found no remaining introduced regression. Earlier live measurements above retain their original source and scope; no new provider call is claimed.

Validated revision: `eb81c7140a2090b75167c7055cf1c3510e60b7ad`.
Validation: https://github.com/chelsealong/oss-pipeline/actions/runs/44297210447

The November 18 refresh and regression adaptation used Codex assistance.


Final regression cleanup reuses the current runtime import. Changed source and regression types, lint and formatting pass: https://github.com/chelsealong/oss-pipeline/actions/runs/44302029360

## What Problem This Solves

Targets #198084's branch. `RootSidebarLifecycleTests` did not compile (`private` `@Observable` classes used outside their scope), and once compiled, `foregroundAdmissionSurvivesInactivityButEndsInBackground` failed on every run with `Background must cancel the event consumer`.

The test counted every `sessions.list` with `limit=200` as root sidebar work. The chat view model also reads 200 sessions when a `seqGap` arrives, and it is not paused in the background, so its read landed after the background snapshot. The test also took that snapshot as soon as the first 200-row read appeared, which was often chat's read rather than the roster's repair.

Request logging during the failing test showed that after backgrounding, the root roster sent nothing until the app returned to the foreground. Only chat's read arrived. #198084's production change is correct; the test was miscounting.

The fix counts only the roster's paged reads (they carry `offset`). This also makes the existing wait observe the roster's own repair before the snapshot. `Scene` and `Requests` become `fileprivate` so the file compiles. Test-only; no production change.

None. Lets #198084's lifecycle regression run and pass.

prs.title: fix(talk): let admitted consultations finish after revocation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Talk consultation that already passed admission can incorrectly refuse a native action if its device is revoked while it is running. Main CI also still expects revocation to cancel a pending Talk approval, so both public-callback variants wait forever for a cancellation that the current contract no longer promises.

## User Impact

Admitted Talk work can finish after device revocation. The next consultation must pass authorization again, and explicit Stop still cancels pending approvals without executing their native action. No configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the retained Talk source check to consultation entry and remove its repeated raw device/policy check from native effects. The admission owner already reauthorizes before execution; retained lifetime and cancellation checks remain in place. Production code shrinks by three lines.

Update the Talk approval fixture to resolve an admitted approval after device revocation, explicitly exercise Stop, and settle failed fixtures through cancellation.
