prs.title: fix: wait the full hour and keep Hold for automatic owed-plugin retries on a schedule
prs.body:
Related: #201178

## What Problem This Solves

With automatic updates on, the Gateway retries plugin work that an earlier update left owed (#201178). Two timing bugs show up only when an automatic-update schedule (`update.auto.schedule`) is set:

- On a closely spaced schedule, for example every five minutes, the retry could restart the Gateway a few minutes after the automatic update that installed the version, although the docs promise at least an hour.
- When an admin pressed **Hold 1 h** on the retry, the next hourly check outside the schedule window cancelled the campaign. The retry never resumed when the hold ended.

## User Impact

User impact: on installs with automatic updates and a schedule, the owed-plugin retry now waits a full hour after the installing update, and a held retry resumes when its hold ends and runs once. Installs without a schedule, and every install with automatic updates off, behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause, both in the already-current branch of the Gateway update check (`src/infra/update-startup.ts`):

1. The retry reused the shared "recent automatic attempt" check. With a schedule, that check compares the attempt with the start of the current cron window, not elapsed time. An attempt made at the previous window five minutes ago counts as old, so the retry starts. Competing hypothesis: the campaign's own `canStart` window gate let it through. Ruled out: `canStart` only checks that the clock is inside a window, which it legitimately was.
2. Outside a cron window the same check always reports a recent attempt whenever the stored attempt is for the current version, however old. The retry branch then fell through to `retireUpdateTarget`, which clears the campaign, including a held one. The newer-release branch does not have this problem because it never clears a campaign it declines to announce.

Fix, at the same owner:

- The retry computes its cooldown from elapsed time since `autoLastAttemptAt` for this version and passes it to the campaign as a start gate. The campaign controller applies start gates only when it creates a campaign, so the cron window and the cooldown both limit when a retry starts, and neither cancels one that is already announced.
- While the row is still owed, every check re-announces the same-version target. The controller keeps an existing campaign for the same target with its hold and deadline. When the row is settled or no longer owed, the check retires the campaign as before. A newer release replaces it through the existing target reconciliation.
- The one-retry-per-row-per-version bound is unchanged. It comes from the update-run ledger (`owesAutomaticPluginRetry`), not from the cooldown: once the handed-off same-version run exists, no later check announces again.
- The "will retry owed plugin steps" log now prints only when a campaign actually starts.

No new config key, stored field, protocol change, or permission. Ordinary release campaigns and dev campaigns do not pass the new start gate, so they behave as before.

Docs (`docs/install/updating/automatic-updates.md`): the cooldown is elapsed time, a held retry resumes outside the schedule window, and a newer release replaces a pending or held retry. I also corrected the example in that section. An npm registry outage does not record an owed plugin-convergence step: per-plugin failures are retained as plugin warnings (`src/plugins/update-installed.ts:224-233`). The step is owed only when plugin sync, update, or repair throws before anything is published, as `docs/cli/update/how-updates-run.md#owed-steps` already says.

Update behavior: only the Gateway's own scheduling changes. A published updater is not involved, and existing update history and check state are read as before.

## Evidence

Behavior checked: on a five-minute schedule, an owed row whose installing automatic attempt ran five minutes earlier does not start a retry at the next window, or at an off-window check after the hour. It starts at the first window an hour or more after that attempt. On a daily schedule, a retry held 30 seconds into its window survives a check an hour later outside the window, counts down when the hold ends, and hands off exactly once. Neither later checks nor the next day's window start another campaign. Guards: a held retry ends without an update run when a newer release appears, and when a manual update settles the row.

RED. The PR's tests against the base production file (`9fbb4b6f39f`): the five-minute schedule test fails because the retry ran (`runAuto` called once), and the hold test fails because the campaign was gone after the off-window check.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9571eee-3329-419c-8fc4-15e6f3f9baf4

GREEN. The same command at the PR head: all four selected tests pass.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/075cb277-a562-4532-b0eb-dfa4b81187d1

<details>
<summary>Commands and results</summary>

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-startup-owed-retry.test.ts`: red on base, with 2 failures for the reasons above (first reproduced on `6d815d786f4`, then recorded on `9fbb4b6f39f`; the commits between them do not touch the update scheduler). Green on head: 24/24.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-startup*.test.ts src/infra/update-campaign*.test.ts` on the final head: all passed, including the opt-out matrix (automatic updates off, `checkOnStart: false`, `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE`, no or external supervisor, dev, extended-stable).
- `pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test`: passed.
- `oxfmt --check` and oxlint on touched files: clean.
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base 9fbb4b6f39f --no-merge-base`: passed.
- `pnpm check:docs`, `pnpm format:docs:check`, `git diff --check`: passed.

```
RED (base production code, PR tests)
 × waits an hour after the installing automatic update on a five-minute cron schedule
   → expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times
 × resumes a held retry when the hold ends outside its cron window, once
   → expected undefined to match object { holdUntilMs: … }
 ✓ drops a held retry for a new release
 ✓ drops a held retry after a manual update settles the row
GREEN (PR head)
 ✓ all four
```

Full raw logs are not attached because the artifact store rejected uploads from this machine. The recordings are the raw terminal output, with only the recording header's local paths dropped.

</details>

Test file audit (`src/infra/update-startup-owed-retry.test.ts`, whole file): every case, helper, and import is used, and there are no skips. Each test owns its state directory, fake clock, scheduler, and ledger database, and `afterEach` clears the campaign, stops the lifecycle and scheduler, closes databases, and restores mocks. The existing one-hour cooldown test now uses the shared `recordInstallingAttempt` helper with the same meaning. Review follow-ups: the five-minute test now checks the window five minutes short of the hour (no retry) and the window exactly at the hour (retry), and the settled-row test settles the row directly without an unused CLI run. Nothing else was removed. The two "drops a held retry" tests and the tail of the hold test also pass on base. They are kept as guards for the end-of-retry and once-only rules.

Independent review: a fresh read-only reviewer got the diff and the behavior contract. It found nothing blocking and raised three P3s. Two are applied: an off-window check after the cooldown, and the docs sentence about newer releases. The third is kept: the manual-update test's CLI run is realistic context, and the explicit settle decides the outcome. `autoreview` does not run on this machine.

## End-to-end run on a real managed Gateway

One installed-package Docker run (harness and candidate package built from `3a14af17ef8`, whose `src/infra/update-startup.ts` matches the final head) exercised the cooldown through a real Gateway under the fixture systemd service, with `update.auto = { enabled: true, schedule: "* * * * *" }`:

- A real `openclaw update --tag file:<fixture>` installed the version. The owed `finalize:owed:plugin-convergence` row was then **seeded** in SQLite on that update's run, as in the #201178 cell. A real update did not produce it (see Not Proven). The installing automatic attempt time was also set as fixture state.
- Phase 1, with the attempt recorded 5 minutes earlier: the Gateway checked in four consecutive one-minute windows plus a 75-second grace period. It created no update run and logged no retry campaign: `{"newRuns":[],"announcements":0}`.
- Phase 2, with the same attempt 2 hours old: the next window announced one campaign, which went through waiting-for-idle, countdown, applying, and handoff. The handed-off run was `trigger: campaign`, `before = target = 2026.11.6-first-hop.5`, status `skipped` (already current). The owner row became `completed`. Two further windows started nothing: `campaignRuns: 1`, `announcements: 1`.

<details><summary>Gateway log excerpt (phase 2)</summary>

```
22:16:22.930 [gateway] update campaign waiting-for-idle
22:16:22.931 [gateway] automatic update will retry owed plugin steps
22:16:27.938 [gateway] update campaign countdown
22:17:27.940 [gateway] update campaign applying
22:17:29.063 [gateway] auto-update handoff started
22:17:38.303 [gateway] update campaign ended
```
</details>

That run's driver then failed on its own bug: it compared the retry's version objects with strings, while the printed values matched. Machine load stopped work before a corrected rerun or the base-package RED run, so the cell is **not** part of this PR. Its exact harness was ad hoc and is not committed.

## Rating

The local ClawSweeper review (GPT 6.2 Sol), round 1 on `605014063228`: overall D, proof D, patch C, verdict "patch is correct". Its P3s are fixed: the first eligible window is tested exactly, the docs say "first eligible" and "hour from the recorded start", and the redundant CLI run is removed. What still holds the rating down is proof: it wants an installed Gateway showing the blocked early window, a hold that survives an off-window check, and exactly one handoff after it resumes. The run above covers the first and last of these on a real Gateway, but it is not committed as a lane. No later round was run.

## Steps Left to a Person

None added by this change. The retry, its cooldown, and its resume after Hold are automatic. Hold 1 h is an optional admin choice, not a required step. An owed step whose single automatic retry fails stays visible in `openclaw update status`, unchanged from #201178. The next release or `openclaw update` settles it, and the instance's agent can run `openclaw update repair` through the Gateway.

## Not Proven

- A held retry resuming after an off-window check on a real Gateway. That needs an hour of wall-clock time or a clock the Gateway does not expose. The fake-clock suite drives the real update check, campaign controller, and ledger.
- A real update producing the owed row. A real `openclaw update` records `finalize:owed:plugin-convergence` only when plugin convergence throws before publishing. An npm outage, a missing package, and a broken plugin tarball all become per-plugin warnings instead (`src/plugins/update-installed.ts:224-233`). The only fault found that can be induced from outside the process corrupts plugin ownership state: two install records resolving to one package path. It was not tried.
- RED for the end-to-end run on a base-scheduler package. The package was built, but the run was stopped by machine load.

Closes #196224

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: setting up or repairing a Knowledge scribe can remove another agent’s scheduled scribe when the operator can manage both agents.

## User Impact

Each agent can retain its own scheduled scribes when another agent starts or repairs the same scribe. Existing pauses remain preserved during setup; repair still enables its own automation. Previously removed schedules need to be recreated through the normal owner-authorized setup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generated instructions now explicitly list and create automations for the Runtime agent, inspect recorded `owner.agentId`, and leave other or missing owners untouched. The documentation example uses the same scope. Existing cron authorization and declaration matching are unchanged.

## Evidence

Current-head runtime proof at `c2042d62fb5e55dba9c255731fb950a8b3565024` exercised the unmodified generated setup, setup-repeat, repair and repair-repeat prompts through a running isolated Gateway and production agent tools, using native Codex app-server with the existing ChatGPT subscription (`gpt-6.1-sol`, medium). Independent persisted readbacks show four schedules across three agents: setup preserves the owned pause, repair enables only its own schedule, repeats create no duplicates, and all three foreign records remain entirely unchanged. All four real inference turns reached terminal `ok`. No synthetic inference was used in those measured turns, no production source changed, and no credentials/auth order/model defaults were changed. This is headless Control UI protocol proof, not browser-button interaction or overnight execution; prompt-image delivery below remains open.

- The added setup/repair scope contracts fail on the original generated instructions and pass with this fix; final Knowledge state/view suite: **36 passed**.
- Real Gateway-handler/SQLite ownership suite: **5 passed**, covering three agents with two shared declaration keys, agent-filtered administrator lists, idempotent retries, preserved pauses/foreign definitions, and retained explicit administrator get/update/remove. These protect already-correct backend behavior and are not a reproduction of the prompt defect.
- The primary ownership/validation/Knowledge run passed **192 tests** before final wording/fixture refinements; the affected suites were rerun afterward. Formatting, whitespace and scoped documentation checks passed.
- Earlier installation report (separate from the current-head run above): the browser-source patch was built and adopted through the supported plugin asset/metadata pipeline, followed by native Control UI plugin reload. The report described the corrected setup guard and six schedules across three agents. That earlier report lacks inspectable attached runtime media and is not presented as the new four-schedule proof or as completed proof delivery.

- Focused Knowledge typecheck passed through the native wrapper using the canonical extension-test configuration and ambient declarations. Typed lint passed for the changed Knowledge source/test and Gateway regression (zero warnings/errors). The dependency-ownership refusal was resolved with a task-owned offline frozen install: 1,482 packages reused, zero downloads, no guard bypass. The broader browser package-project declaration failure is retained separately; this is a scoped validation claim.

### Synthetic rendered before / after

The real Knowledge view, dialog and styles were rendered with a synthetic host at base `2e73417ca8a52bfe2e8de64c5263f8b03a4dc6f3` and head `b15b817cbc7b8fb7884b70e7769b216c83b04e2e`. This is synthetic rendering evidence, separate from live schedule readback.

The required inline-image delivery gate remains incomplete; no generated media was committed and no alternative upload destination was substituted. Private runtime screens are excluded. prs.title: fix(memory): keep Dreaming promotions trusted through later edits
prs.body:
Refs https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164866
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/180796 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/153426

## What Problem This Solves

A successful Dreaming promotion can change MEMORY.md without refreshing its artifact-provenance hash. The next clean tracked edit then marks the file untrusted and excludes it from automatic bootstrap context. This fixes that writer path, not the other writer or recovery work in the related issues.

## User Impact

Acknowledged promotion refreshes the hash so the next clean tracked edit preserves trusted memory eligibility. Previously untrusted files stay untrusted; hash continuity and quarantine are unchanged. There is no schema, configuration, retention, or migration change.

**Still draft:** the live proof below covers the previous head, not this core-ownership revision. A rerun on the new head, including upgrade from the latest stable with existing provenance rows, remains pending. Landing is left to a maintainer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Addresses [ClawSweeper's P2 finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201507#issuecomment-6994509032) and restores the ownership intent of [#126489](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/126489): the packaged Memory Core provenance facade is read-only. Neither that facade nor the file-operation facade exposes the raw provenance recorder or clearer.

The existing local/IPC file publication implementation now lives in core at src/memory/memory-file-publication.ts. Core reads and checks the pre-image, performs the actual publication, and refreshes provenance through its private recorder. This is a file-publication operation, not a renamed recorder or a caller-supplied publication callback. All bundled callers use it; promotion markers remain plugin-owned. The old plugin publisher is removed, and shared mode/remote-maintenance helpers move with their owner rather than being duplicated.

The Gateway still owns provenance when files live remotely. Rejected or uncertain publication leaves the artifact row untouched. Known-committed failures retain committed semantics, including when recording fails after publication, so callers cannot roll back entry origins or replay a committed replacement. A crash or store failure between file publication and recording can still leave a conservative hash gap; no cross-filesystem/database transaction is introduced.

## Evidence

- The existing facade guard failed on the previous head `c5da6d82ea4d` because it exposed `recordMemoryArtifactWriteProvenance`. Both complete facade contract suites now pass. The regression additionally rejects raw recorder/clearer exports from the file-operation facade, while retaining the high-level publisher.
- Real-store promotion → clean tracked edit → bootstrap regression and all controls pass after the core move. Serialized file-client/worker tests cover remote success, known-committed errors, and lost replies; these are in-process IPC-contract tests, not live remote-Gateway proof.
- Broader focused run: **294 passed; one existing ACL case could not execute** across 18 files. The only failure was the setfacl-dependent case in workspace-file-mode.test.ts because setfacl is unavailable here. No skip or weakened assertion was added.
- Final publisher/error-path rerun: **19/19 passed** across the two promotion publication/provenance suites. Tests used `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks`. The final new regression file's seven test bodies took about 4.41s; the two-file run took 45.02s including cold worker preparation. Hosted CI timing is not yet available.
- Core production, extension production, extension-test, and plugin-platform test typechecks passed. Targeted lint, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. The assertion-safety check and pnpm build passed; a direct import of both built package facades also confirmed that raw provenance mutation is absent and the core publisher is available.
- The previous independent autoreview **did not complete** and was stopped at the requester's instruction; it has not been restarted. This revision does not claim a completed independent review. The hosted review linked above is the prior-head review whose P2 this revision addresses.
- Simplification: remove the raw SDK mutation export and the plugin-owned publisher, retaining one core publication owner and the existing trust algorithm. Against the base, production TypeScript is +143/-83 and tests are +277/-12, including the initial regression; most of the ownership repair is relocation and caller-import changes. The retired unsafe cast is replaced by the existing error-code extractor, and its old assertion-baseline allowance is removed rather than moved or expanded.

### Live proof — previous head

Revised head for the requested rerun: `f32f28475b4fb51601956429798bd02aa7935a32`.

[Holger's real-Gateway before/after CLI proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201507#issuecomment-6995176989) covers c5da6d82ea4d53b3f0ec5dd99e9ece511c7b937c on an isolated Linux Gateway with Dreaming enabled, Node 24.22.3, FTS-only search, default promotion thresholds, and real tracked write/edit tools driven by a deterministic mock model.

It reports a matching agent hash after CLI promotion, no duplicate on repeated apply, agent classification after the next clean tracked edit, and MEMORY.md in a fresh session's context. The previously-untrusted control remains untrusted and excluded. This does not establish the cause of the earlier production incident.

**Live gaps:**
- No scheduled/nightly Dreaming run.
- No live remote-workspace/IPC publication path (automated serialized coverage is separate).
- No upgrade-from-latest-stable check with existing provenance rows yet.
- No live publication-failure scenario.
- The proof must be rerun against the new head after this core-owned publication change. The requester will supply that rerun, including the upgrade check, as a PR comment.

Related: #161885

## What Problem This Solves

Browser Talk consults routed through `claude-cli` request a direct Anthropic API key and fail before trying the configured fallback.

## User Impact

Browser/native GPT-Live consultations use the selected model's runtime and configured fallback chain while retaining the caller's existing authority, cancellation, session continuity and terminal ownership. No configuration or public SDK changes are required. Meeting, voice-call and FaceTime consultation paths are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Refreshed against `main` at `dab3fcdf8edd36df38144a961f8330fcbede872e` to resolve the stale branch's conflicts. Talk now uses the existing admitted turn and CLI-candidate owners, with one admission and transcript recorder across candidates. Hook-resolved routes are applied before runtime selection. Steering uses the admitted session operation; a live CLI without injection support uses the provider's existing joined replacement flow.

The refresh preserves main's exact source/Gateway binding and terminal-write draining. It removes the browser's direct embedded-only dispatch and the redundant Talk-side steering projection. Existing consumer fixtures move to the dispatcher boundary, preserving their permission, source, final-effect and lifecycle assertions.

## Evidence

Published head: [`e08988c594b`](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/commit/e08988c594b647757d7ce82d508f53eea8e48a5b).

- **Real baseline:** an isolated Chromium call through the genuine native Talk service on `main` `9bf3e79c823` reached a delegated consultation, then recorded `missing-provider-auth` for Anthropic despite the configured `claude-cli` runtime; fallback was not attempted. Audio input was synthetic; the browser, Gateway and service were real.
- **Focused checks:** 88 tests across six routing, steering, admission, source-scope, prompt-prefix and provider-controller files passed in 219.61 seconds. After fixing the review's hook-routing finding, the routing file passed all 16 tests in 74.10 seconds, including compilation; both new hook regressions fail on the preceding candidate.
- **Static checks:** core and plugin production types and Gateway test types passed. Formatting, conflict-marker, line-cap and mock-export guards passed. Plugin typed lint also passed. A further seven consumer files had 90 passing and four failing tests in 278.51 seconds; the four cancel-then-new-request failures reproduce with the same assertion and no speakable answer on unmodified `main` `dab3fcdf` (all four fail in the baseline run, 92.52 seconds). Running those scenarios through the actual Talk adapter produces the same four failures; they are not counted as passing. Exact-head hosted CI and its CI seconds are pending.
- **Independent review:** fresh Codex autoreview of the production adapter and then-current consumer fixtures against `dab3fcdf`, through P2: `scoped-clean`, no accepted/actionable findings. Production source is unchanged since that review; the subsequent native real-runner fixture now invokes the Talk adapter. The earlier hook-routing finding was fixed and covered by the red/green tests above. The model-lock suggestion was declined against the existing Talk owner's explicit rejection contract and tests in `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts:99` and `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts:334`.
- **Size:** production +549/-43 (net +506); tests/support +671/-53 (net +618); other +2/-5. Production growth supplies the previously missing browser-to-CLI adapter using existing runtime, auth, continuity and settlement owners; it adds no fallback loop or configuration. The test-line allocation covers distinct routing/preflight and steering-lifetime boundaries.

### Remaining validation and follow-ups

**Inherited validation failure:** native cancellation followed by a fresh delegated consultation returns the no-answer fallback in four existing tests. This reproduces on unmodified `main` as well as this candidate; underlying product-versus-fixture cause remains unconfirmed. It is recorded as follow-up, without weakening the assertions.

A successful authenticated Claude CLI after-run remains unverified because the local Claude CLI is logged out. No live CLI allowed-read/forbidden-write result is claimed. The ClawSweeper rank-up request for those final effects remains outstanding; retained-callback rejection has focused controller-boundary coverage, not a live Claude tool-call claim. Ready is a review state, not a claim that these proof gaps or required CI are cleared.

The shared CLI catalog concerns [B/C](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164229#issuecomment-6789739547) remain named follow-up work: this refresh forwards the logical `modelProvider` (A), but does not include the separate shared capability/intersection-policy patch or claim those catalog cases fixed.

Earlier [proof artifacts](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/tree/d530ab2f733aaf74a1e4dc1585e546b4c9f7943d/proof/issue-161885-terminal-repair) remain historical evidence for their recorded revisions; they do not validate this refreshed head. The refreshed full build and remaining platform/live checks are pending exact-head CI or follow-up validation.

prs.title: fix: let Doctor restore config after reported truncation
prs.body:
Related: #152565

## What Problem This Solves

After an external edit truncates a configuration that still validates, the Gateway can report the loss and protect its backup, but `openclaw doctor --fix` can exit successfully without restoring the missing settings. Later accepted edits can also rotate an incomplete predecessor into `.bak`, where added metadata disguises the loss.

## User Impact

Explicit Doctor repair can restore the intact configuration even after the anomaly has already been reported. It preserves the exact rejected bytes and leaves unverified backups available for manual recovery rather than mistaking them for repaired settings.

Startup and passive-read recovery policy is unchanged. There are no new settings, schema changes, or migration actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing prepared-recovery owner now receives an explicit Doctor repair intent. It rechecks the anomaly, prefers an eligible healthy rotating backup, and can fall back to the hash-verified promoted copy. When a healthy baseline is recorded, rotating bytes must match an existing healthy fingerprint; byte size or a particular observation-marker spelling is not enough.

Candidate validation, migration, source-change guards, read-only/include/future-writer checks, and archive-before-replace behavior remain in place.

## Evidence

- Regression cases were red before their corresponding repairs. The final focused/sibling run passes **90 tests across five files**, including repeated accepted edits, intervening observations, newer healthy backups, and non-repair/reseed/tampered-backup controls.
- Actual built Gateway → external valid truncation → real reload observation → SIGTERM → standalone public Doctor CLI: both published **2026.10.10** and main failed to restore despite Doctor exiting 0. Tested commit **c706391fb638** restores all 80 synthetic proxy settings, archives the exact rejected stub, preserves last-good, and exits 0.
- Runtime build at the tested production commit, targeted typecheck/lint/format, and committed-range whitespace checks pass. Fresh independent native review of the complete six-file final change found no actionable P0/P1/P2 or meaningful lower-priority findings. This is not an autoreview/ClawSweeper certification claim.
- The original npm-installed **2026.10.10 → fixed candidate** upgrade proof remains valid and separate: package swap, database snapshot, pre/post-plugin Doctor and final CLI exit succeed; the database snapshot directory is retired, authored include reference/bytes remain intact, and no restoration-refusal warning appears. Updater time: 125.01 seconds.
- Latest-stable **2026.11.5 → fixed candidate** installed update and subsequent public Gateway-observation-to-Doctor recovery also pass; details below.

### PostgreSQL CI follow-up

[Run 44417143796 / PostgreSQL conformance (1/4)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44417143796/job/135201100112) failed with `ECONNREFUSED` at the intermediate readiness poll, before the held-writer, durable-receipt and restart assertions. Its classifier was “new” with no selected-scope comparison; this report does not silently relabel that original run as inherited.

Follow-up **7cc111fa8631** replaces the fixture’s transient `/readyz` 503 poll with the existing completed HTTP-close trace. After transport retirement it independently requires the same PostgreSQL backend to remain blocked and the original Gateway child to remain OS-alive. Every original unlock, clean-exit, receipt, fresh-process restart, no-replay, anchor and backend-release assertion remains. There are no production shutdown-policy changes, new retries or timeout increases.

A controlled bad interleaving held the real finalizer until the HTTP-close completion before exercising the old readiness predicate: the same backend remained blocked and the original child remained alive, but the local proxy returned 502 for the retired transport and the original predicate failed. The corrected complete file passes both cases on that same local pinned-Bun route. This demonstrates the synchronization defect, not the unseen child/SQL state of the original CI job.

Explicit **Node 24.22.1 + PostgreSQL 17.11** qualification also passes **2/2 tests**. The running Vitest and Gateway executable paths were both verified against the official Node binary. Case times: 28.955s and 23.776s; complete-file wall time: 64.83s; wrapper including compilation: 99.47s. Local pinned-Bun complete-file proof passes in 60.14s. New-head CI timing remains pending. The real PostgreSQL custody, process-death and fresh-process recovery contract requires the existing process boots and foreground-close grace; no additional test case or sleep was added.

Targeted Gateway-server test typecheck, one-file lint/format and commit-hook checks pass. Earlier repair-proof attempts were disqualified because the replacement local database lacked required search extensions and stalled before shutdown. After verifying `unaccent`, `pg_trgm` and `vector`, the controlled red/green and explicit Node qualification above completed; those setup failures are not presented as product failures.

### Latest-stable installed update and public Doctor recovery

Installed official npm **2026.11.5**, release build **e13cf15ece9b**, then ran the supported installed `openclaw update --tag <canonical-candidate.tgz> --yes --json --no-restart` to fixed build **c706391fb638**. The successful installation/update/recovery run took **163.355 seconds**.

```text
baseline: 2026.11.5-release-e13cf15ece9b
candidate: 2026.11.5-c706391fb638
package SHA-256: 20e395236a5912558d0f92c34ba0b5b54a1687977a35c4b6279e4ec5f703900d
installed package swap: passed; both update Doctor phases exited 0
preserved: 80 trusted proxies; idle timeout 46; authored include reference and exact include bytes
healthy .bak and .last-good bytes: exact; config-health hashes: bound to the correct generations
database update snapshot: removed after success
post-upgrade real Gateway: parseable truncation observed; suspicious signature persisted
public doctor --fix: exit 0; settings/include reference restored; rejected stub archived; suspicion cleared
```

Package/source binding verified 18,485 packaged dist files against the retained canonical build; the generated worker archive matches its canonical package inventory. c706 and d304 have identical Git trees. Follow-up 7cc changes only the cron test; managed publication appended attribution-only **88ec93d571f9**, whose Git tree is identical to tested 7cc. Runtime/package proof is reused because those production inputs are unchanged. CI must bind the new published head.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation and limits</summary>

The Doctor focused command was:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=$PWD/.openclaw/tmp/deeper-config-fix-cache node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.recovery.test.ts src/config/io.snapshot.recovery.test.ts src/config/io.snapshot.promotion.test.ts src/config/io.observe-recovery.test.ts src/config/recovery-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

It covers Doctor preflight recovery, snapshot recovery/promotion, suspicious-read recovery and recovery-policy siblings: 132.31 seconds including compilation; changed Doctor file 41.13 seconds. The cases use real native SQLite health persistence and Doctor/config IO owners rather than mocked recovery decisions. The implementation reuses the existing planner/publication effects; the cron follow-up is test-only (+7/−15 lines).

Public-flow and installed-update proof use isolated Linux foreground Gateways and `--no-restart`, not managed system-service restart, channel/provider traffic, or native Windows/macOS qualification. Doctor’s existing roster/migration/wizard normalization was checked separately from authored settings.

The damaged root in the successful latest-stable recovery probe no longer contains an include directive; recovery restores that reference from a verified healthy backup. Retaining an include directive in a damaged root intentionally blocks whole-root replacement under pre-existing policy. That initial out-of-scope probe and its non-restoration are retained, not suppressed. Loss without trusted baseline facts or an eligible intact backup remains outside automatic-repair guarantees.

The release promotion guard was reapplied before published 2026.10.10. This repairs a shared inherited Doctor recovery gap, not a working release repair absent from main.

</details>

## Contributor credit

Thanks @vincentkoc for requesting and authorizing the release-divergence investigation and repair.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep resumed conversations on the same native writer
prs.body:
Related: #167443

## What Problem This Solves

A Codex conversation can fail to resume with “already has an active writer” after a catalog or conversation-binding request and a model turn prepare Git settings differently. Matching connections then start separate native processes, and the second process cannot resume the thread still loaded by the first.

## User Impact

Matching local Codex connections reuse the same native writer regardless of which request prepared Git defaults first. Authentication, explicit environment differences, isolated clients, and external app-server connections keep their existing separation. No configuration migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the existing host Git maintenance policy in the client acquisition owner, after authentication/environment filtering and before cache-key selection and spawn. Remove the duplicate turn and MCP process transforms while retaining their shell-environment policy. The cache still distinguishes process configuration; this does not weaken writer locks or exempt environment values from identity.

The existing startup-policy module owns this preparation, keeping the shared-client lifetime owner within its line-growth limit. Related endpoint-selection tests move intact into a sibling registration module; no coverage is removed. The complete repair adds five net production lines, plus focused regressions. The SDK change is one additive export on the existing process-runtime subpath.

## Evidence

- **Red on main `71ee55620d0786d4078dfa41c3527488c4a7cad4`:** two acquisition-order regressions returned different physical clients. A real pinned Codex **0.169.0** process, using disposable state and a credential-free loopback provider, rejected the second client’s `thread/resume` with RPC **-32600**, “already has an active writer”.
- **Green with the final fix:** the native scenario creates a thread, completes a turn, and resumes on the original writer. **165 tests across three owner files passed after the line-cap extraction** (63.06 seconds wrapper wall time; native regression 1.06 seconds), including both acquisition orders. An earlier broader run passed **291 tests across 10 files** in 115.76 seconds, including unchanged Stop/handoff controls, configured MCP ownership, environment placement, and four native shell-policy scenarios.
- Focused production/test typecheck, ten-file lint, formatting, diff, and mandatory line-cap checks passed. **Full final `pnpm build` passed** in 1m 47.1s, including SDK declarations and validation of all 163 public SDK subpaths. The committed-base SDK API comparison reports no public API changes. An earlier uncached UI build reported CSS-size and boot-request budget warnings; no UI files changed and those warnings were not attributed in this task.
- **Independent final review:** local autoreview assessed the complete final 12-file staged candidate against the base above through **P2**, including supplied worker/fallback source context, and returned `scoped-clean`, with no actionable findings. A separate independent source/design review also found no P0–P2 design objections. The reviewer did not independently rerun the reported checks. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable in the task checkout.
- **Hosted exact-head proof:** after marking ready under the maintainer’s landing instruction, [CI run 44407424939](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44407424939) completed with `openclaw/ci-gate` successful for `a01d50a286f558a03ace6fe5c1b212074f550069`. The exact-head security review also succeeded. ClawSweeper’s advisory hosted review was started; no outstanding actionable findings were present at landing inspection.

**Remaining proof:** an authenticated isolated Gateway or UI-driven `/codex resume` flow was not run. The regression exercises the actual pinned native process and writer locks with a loopback model fixture, not a paid provider. The contributor-guide SDK import-inventory script is absent in this checkout, so that specific inventory was not run; SDK export validation and boundary declaration checks passed.

prs.title: fix(ios): avoid sidebar reloads on chat switches and brief interruptions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: switching same-agent chats or briefly opening Control Center needlessly restarts the iOS sidebar's roster, dashboard reads, and session subscription.

## User Impact

User impact: switching conversations and returning from a temporary inactive overlay no longer invalidate unrelated sidebar data. The current UI, selected-row presentation, sidebar animation, grouped replies, and word fade are unchanged. Mike reported native regression and real-device request-count proof on a local main integration, detailed below. The test-only repair in #201532 is still required on this published branch. The measured benefit is fewer redundant requests; tap-to-history latency, frame-time, CPU and memory improvements are not claimed. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selected chat is a presentation input, not an input to these shared reads. Remove it from the refresh identity and retain an already-admitted foreground task lifetime through `.inactive`. One scene-local Boolean starts false, admits work on `.active`, and closes it on `.background`; cold or background-to-inactive transitions cannot start work. Gateway, agent, connectivity, and authority changes still invalidate the tasks.

Observer visibility remains **active-only**. Permission refreshes, microphone/capture gates, discovery, reconnect checks, and storage recovery are unchanged. RootTabs' separate branding/agent overview refresh still runs on activation: this does not eliminate all activation traffic. Event-driven updates and the ten-minute refresh remain; if an overlay stays inactive that long, the periodic read can still run until actual background. No new timer, debounce, cooldown, cache, or manager.

Contributor credit: @vyctorbrzezowski and @mikengyn.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6b98dedd-1923-4f79-837e-5d48ac84b6c4)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b12bdfba-cb0b-43f7-a2f5-ca17649c42bc)

## Evidence

### Source and tested revisions

- Original implementation base: `0633f256350b5580a5bdbcd8a6a5782750de03d4`.
- Published source head at this evidence update: `f29473645453cfb4f563a296b71dd7998794902f`.
- [Mike's native and physical-device report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198084#issuecomment-6995398901) tested this change rebased locally, without conflicts, onto main `0eabe3398c9`, plus [test repair #201532](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201532). These are attributed results from that local integration, not a fresh execution of the currently published tree by Roboclaw.
- **Integration still required:** #201532 fixes test compilation (nested observable helper visibility) and distinguishes the root roster's paged `sessions.list(limit:200, offset:...)` calls from chat's own 200-row metadata read on `seqGap`. The published branch has not yet incorporated that repair. The repaired test waits for the roster's own sequence-gap recovery before checking background cancellation; it does not relax the production invariant.

### Native regressions reported by Mike

- `RootSidebarLifecycleTests`: 3 of 3 runs passed with the repair. Restoring main's `RootTabs.swift` fails at transient inactivity: one inactive/active cycle doubles each of the four shared reads.
- `RootSidebarLifecycleTests RootTabsPresentationTests RootSidebarModelSessionEventsTests RootEventSubscriptionTests`: **73 passed, 0 failed**.
- `SidebarRefreshUITests`, using the loopback Gateway fixture: passed. With main's `RootTabs.swift`, five same-agent switches produce five root roster reloads.
- SwiftFormat and SwiftLint: reported clean on the local integration.
- The lifecycle test mounts real RootTabs and covers foreground admission, inactive lifetime, active-only observer visibility, sequence-gap consumption, background cancellation and foreground restart. It is distinct from physical scene-transition proof.

### Physical device: measured outgoing work

Mike used an **iPhone 16 Pro, iOS 27.2.1, Debug build and a real Gateway**. A temporary local app logger counted every outgoing Gateway request and scene phase; that logger was not committed. Gateway file logs omit successful responses under 50 ms and are not an adequate source for these request counts.

| Device action | Extra root sidebar shared work observed |
| --- | --- |
| Eight same-agent chat switches | Zero shared roster/dashboard/subscription requests |
| Control Center open/close, inactive/active only | Zero shared requests |
| Notification Center, five pulls | One full reload on return to active; observed transitions included background |
| Initial launch | One full load |

The shared work is the root roster `sessions.list` with limit 200 and paging offset, `usage.cost`, `cron.list`, and `sessions.subscribe`. Requests belonging to the chat owner must be counted separately.

Notification Center entering `.background` correctly ends foreground admission under this PR's policy. Retaining work across actual background is a separate lifecycle decision, not part of this fix. Initial activation still loads; the separate branding/agent refresh, permission checks, event-triggered updates and periodic refresh retain their existing owners.

### Remaining limits and final validation

- Integrate #201532, review the complete combined change, and verify checks on the resulting published head. Native results above establish the tested local integration, not automatic exact-tree coverage of a later published head.
- Earlier local P0–P2 review of the original complete three-file change found no findings; the hosted review currently shown covers earlier head `6d8fcadbd7eac451cf4d042f10ce4d2edd4a6b85`. Neither is presented as a fresh review of the not-yet-integrated test fix.
- Current draft CI largely skips native jobs; a green lightweight summary is not an iOS build/test result. #201532 currently has workflows awaiting approval.
- Device checks for permission prompts, Face ID, agent/Gateway changes and reconnect were **not performed** in Mike's report. The reported Control Center sequence should not be relabeled as five measured device cycles.
- Tap-to-history timing, hitches, CPU/memory comparison and before/after video remain unmeasured/unprovided. No global speedup is claimed from the request counts alone.
- Mike also observed approximately 15 separate chat-bootstrap requests per switch, including a `sessions.list(limit:10000)` sub-session lookup, `config.get`, `skills.status`, `tools.effective`, `models.list` and `health`. Investigating that work is a separate follow-up, not scope for this sidebar fix.

### Acceptance and reproduction

The work-count invariant remains: after warm-up, switching same-agent chats or a genuine inactive/active-only interruption must not restart the root's shared roster/dashboard/subscription work. Actual background closes admission; foreground restarts it. Selected history and row presentation remain correct, active-only observer visibility is retained, and real Gateway/agent/authority changes still invalidate their scopes.

Native commands used for the focused suite group:

```sh
IOS_SIM="$OWNED_SIMULATOR_UDID" pnpm ios:test \
  RootSidebarLifecycleTests RootTabsPresentationTests \
  RootSidebarModelSessionEventsTests RootEventSubscriptionTests

IOS_SIM="$OWNED_SIMULATOR_UDID" pnpm ios:test OpenClawUITests/SidebarRefreshUITests
```

The UI suite requires the isolated `test-ios-shell-gateway.mjs --session-mutations` fixture and setup/environment described in the implementation handoff. Zero matching or skipped tests do not count as proof. For any later latency claim, use at least five interleaved baseline/candidate runs, distinguish cold/warm paths, record raw samples/spread and assess hitches, CPU and memory separately.

## Worked on by

- @mikengyn
- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: feat(codex): verify the admitted app server before sending credentials
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Kubernetes Service can point to a different Pod after its original app server exits. A Gateway that knows only the service address cannot tell whether the new listener belongs to the execution that was granted the app-server bearer.

## User Impact

Operators can supply the admitted server's PEM certificate in `appServer.tlsPeerCertificate`. OpenClaw rejects a different listener before sending credentials. Admitting another execution requires updating the pin.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing WSS transport verifies the hostname and exact leaf certificate on each new connection. The runtime connection identity includes the pin so a configuration change cannot reuse an old connection.

The plugin configuration budget grows by one for the optional admitted certificate. The service URL and bearer identify where to connect and which credential to send. Neither identifies the execution allowed to receive that credential.

## Evidence

- A real TLS listener changed certificates while keeping its address, hostname and key. The replacement received no WebSocket upgrade or frames.
- The focused Codex suites passed (68 tests), as did extension typechecking, formatting and lint.
- On ARM64 Kubernetes, the Gateway completed a real model turn against the admitted Pod. After Kubernetes replaced it at the same Service address, all six Gateway handshakes were rejected and the replacement received zero HTTP requests. After a cold boot and fresh admission, the Gateway completed another real model turn.

prs.title: fix(voice-call): realtime phone consults fail on Claude CLI agents with no API key
prs.body:
Related: #188440 (this fixes the realtime consult path; the classic responder that #188440 reports is unchanged, see Gaps)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: realtime phone consults fail with `No API key found for provider "anthropic"` when the called agent runs on a CLI runtime such as `agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" }`.

## User Impact

User impact: a realtime Voice Call consult now runs on the agent's configured runtime, including a subscription-backed Claude CLI agent with no provider API key. Each consult is an ordinary turn of the call session, so later consults in the same call keep earlier ones, and the agent's normal tools (for example `sessions_send` to another agent) work under `toolPolicy: "owner"`. The caller stays a guest: owner-only tools stay refused, and `voice_call` stays bound to ending the current call.

The classic (non-realtime) phone responder is unchanged and still runs `runEmbeddedAgent`; see Gaps.

## Why This Change Was Made

Realtime consults called `runEmbeddedAgent`, which never selects a CLI runtime. Discord voice does not have this problem because it runs a normal agent turn (`runCommandFromIngress`). Consults now take that same path:

- `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` accepts `runner: "agent-turn"`: session preparation (fork, lineage, delivery) is unchanged, and the turn runs through `agentRuntime.runCommandFromIngress` as a guest. Voice Call opts in; other consult callers keep `embedded`.
- Plugin ingress: a plugin that owns no channel may admit a turn without `messageChannel`, and only as a guest. Owner elevation still requires the exact trusted plugin of the named channel. `toolBindings` are accepted only for tools the calling plugin declares in `contracts.tools`. Public `agentCommandFromIngress` still strips both.
- The CLI runner carries `toolBindings` into the MCP loopback grant (they already reached embedded tools), so `voice_call` keeps its active-call binding on the CLI route.
- Voice Call runs consults in its service context. Webhook handlers run outside the Gateway, and without the service's Gateway context `sessions_send` failed with "Requester provenance requires trusted in-process Gateway dispatch."

A CLI-dispatch alternative (`cliBackendDispatch` on the embedded runner) was considered and rejected: it is a one-shot helper path without session history or the requester's normal tool policy.

## Evidence

Focused tests (all new tests fail on `origin/main` and pass here):

- `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts` 18/18: agent-turn consult shape (guest, `deliver: false`, one-shot thinking, bindings), and refusal of embedded tool-context adaptation.
- `src/plugins/registry-runtime.channel-ingress.test.ts` 32/32: channel-less guest turn admitted; owner claim and foreign channel refused; foreign tool binding refused; bindings snapshotted.
- `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.cli-mcp.test.ts` 5/5: `toolBindings` reach the prepared CLI run.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/{mcp-grant-context,tool-authority}.test.ts`: bindings snapshotted into the loopback grant.
- `extensions/voice-call/src/runtime.test.ts` 23/23: consults run as agent turns (an embedded call throws) inside the service context; a host-forced consult (`consultPolicy: "always"`, called the way `scheduleForcedAgentConsult` calls it) runs as a guest agent turn and its owner's abort cancels the turn.

Gateway e2e (real Gateway, real Voice Call plugin with the mock carrier, fixture realtime provider issuing two consults, agent on `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` with `agentRuntime: claude-cli`, stub `claude` that speaks stream-json and uses the real MCP loopback, second agent on the mock model):

| Check | `owner` | `safe-read-only` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Consult 1 / 2 answered by the CLI runtime | yes / yes | yes / yes |
| Consult 2 in the same Claude process and session | yes (`turnInProcess=2`) | yes |
| `No API key found` in Gateway log | 0 | 0 |
| Native Claude tools | `ToolSearch` only | `ToolSearch` only |
| MCP tools | normal agent surface | `read, web_fetch, memory_search, memory_get, voice_call` |
| `voice_call initiate_call` | refused: may only `end_call` | refused: may only `end_call` |
| `gateway`, `automations` | refused: needs owner authority | not available |
| `sessions_send` to another agent | `accepted`; target model received the message | not available |

Host-forced consults (`realtime.consultPolicy: "always"`; the fixture provider never calls the consult tool and emits two final caller transcripts, so `scheduleForcedAgentConsult` issues both consults):

| Check | `owner` | `safe-read-only` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Forced consult 1 / 2 answered by the CLI runtime and spoken via `sendUserMessage` | yes / yes | yes / yes |
| Consult 2 in the same Claude process and session | yes (`turnInProcess=2`) | yes (`turnInProcess=2`) |
| `No API key found` in Gateway log | 0 | 0 |
| MCP tools | normal agent surface | `read, web_fetch, memory_search, memory_get, voice_call` |
| `voice_call initiate_call` | refused: may only `end_call` | refused: may only `end_call` |
| `gateway`, `automations` | refused: needs owner authority | not available |
| `sessions_send` to another agent | `accepted`; target model received the message | not available |

Before the service-context commit, the same e2e returned `Requester provenance requires trusted in-process Gateway dispatch.` for `sessions_send`.

Regression: `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/voice-call-gateway.ts` (`voice-call-cli-rpc-agent-tool`) passes.

After rebasing onto `origin/main` 2e24ab71b1, the six focused suites above and the four `tsgo` checks were rerun and pass.

Other checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint on touched files, format check, docs markdown lint, `git diff --check`.

Size against `origin/main`: production +240/−105, tests +256/−22. The ingress admission check moved out of `registry-runtime.ts` into its own module unchanged, with the guest and binding rules added there.

## Gaps

- A failed host-forced consult is still only logged (`realtime forced agent consult failed`), so the caller hears nothing. Unchanged here.
- Classic phone responder (`generateVoiceResponse`) still uses `runEmbeddedAgent`; it relies on pre-compaction early-speech block hooks that the agent-turn API does not expose. Moving it needs a separate change.
- `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: `manager.async-store.test.ts` "checks registered steering admission and effects" (3 cases) fails identically on `origin/main` code on this host; all other files pass.
- `check:line-cap-ratchet` / `check:test-lines-ratchet` need `git cat-file --batch -z` (newer than this host's git 2.34); line growth was checked by hand and no grandfathered file grows.

prs.title: fix: let Codex subagents start when an agent folder name uses capital letters
prs.body:
Root cause: src/gateway/session-row-scope.ts:262 (main 852f25b33359) mapped each physical store target to a resident store by exact path string, while resident stores are keyed by canonical filename. When an agent's `agentDir` folder uses capital letters (`agents/Worker/agent`) and the default lower-case locator (`agents/worker/...`) reaches the same database on a case-insensitive volume, the lookup missed the resident row. The Gateway session index then reported a newly spawned child as absent, and the Codex requester-policy re-check, which reads the database directly and finds the row, refused the child.

Fixes #201423

## What Problem This Solves

On macOS, if an agent's folder name contains capital letters, every `sessions_spawn` into a Codex-runtime child fails within a few hundred milliseconds, before the child's first turn, with "Codex requester policy changed; retry the turn to prepare current policy." Retrying doesn't help. Turns in existing sessions still work.

## User Impact

User impact: subagents on the Codex runtime start normally again when agent folders use capital letters on a case-insensitive disk. Folder names whose case already matches, and case-sensitive file systems, behave as before. The requester-policy check is unchanged: a requester that really changed between spawn and child start is still refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session index answers "is this row present?" for policy preparation. Its scope mapped a store path to the loaded store only when the strings were identical. The fix resolves the path through the existing canonical database-path key (`resolveDatabasePathKey`) before falling back, so both spellings select the same loaded store. No new config and no change to the policy check.

Thanks to @thejeys19 for the precise report, the trace to the session-index "known absence" answer, the local patch confirming it, and the follow-up that pointed to capitalized `agentDir` folders.

## Evidence

Proof lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201520#issuecomment-6994732919

- Reproduced through the real product: built Gateway, real bundled Codex app-server, local ChatGPT-backend fixture. A parent session calls `sessions_spawn` into agent `worker` with `agentDir` `agents/Worker/agent` (folder created with that case).
  - base 852f25b33359, twice: child fails with "Codex requester policy changed", no child output.
  - v2026.11.5 (e13cf15ece9b), the reporter's build: same failure (`lane task error ... durationMs=103 error="Codex requester policy changed ..."`).
  - candidate, twice: child runs and replies.
  - control, candidate with a matching-case folder `agents/worker/agent`: child runs and replies.
- Regression test `session-row-projection.topology.test.ts` "reads an agentDir row through another spelling of its database file (#201423)": red twice on base (`expected undefined to be 'child-id'`), green twice on candidate. It uses a directory link on case-sensitive file systems so CI on Linux covers the same mismatch.
- Control: a reassigned requester (`spawnedBy` changed after preparation) is still refused by `prepareCodexNativeExecutionPolicy` (throwaway probe, not committed); an unchanged requester is admitted.
- Focused suites green: session-row-projection.topology, session-row-projection.archived, native-execution-policy, native-execution-policy.authority-chain. oxfmt and oxlint clean on changed files.
- Codex: the refusal happens before `thread/start` (`~/Developer/codex` 7fb4014d52, `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs:609`); no Codex-side behavior is involved.

Line delta vs merge base: production +18 −2, tests +35 −1. The canonical path lookup runs once per physical target during topology preparation; row queries compare strings only.

prs.title: fix: preserve memory trust after Claude CLI file edits
prs.body:
Refs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/180796
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165452, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/153426

## What Problem This Solves

Explicitly selected native Claude `Edit`/`Write` can change saved memory without updating its provenance, causing the next clean edit to quarantine it. CLI loopback and native network results could also lose turn taint, allowing untrusted memory to retain agent trust.

## User Impact

Local Claude CLI memory writes retain their hash continuity and turn origin: clean tracked files remain eligible for automatic memory, while tainted, non-owner, and already-quarantined files remain untrusted. Native tool permissions do not expand; Agent/Workflow-only selections still deny native Edit/Write.

This does not rehabilitate existing quarantine, change the schema or hash-continuity rule, or track shell writes, paired-node writes, or other harnesses' native tools. The session-rooted tool-builder repair is separate in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201509.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share one host-owned admitted-turn taint state across CLI events, transcript recording, native observations, and loopback write/edit/apply_patch. Capture the canonical preimage after an allowed native `PreToolUse` and observe the actual file after successful `PostToolUse` through the existing provenance owner. Native execution and rollback remain native-owned.

The P1 follow-up reuses the backend's existing `projectNativeToolAuthority` capability mapping to classify native network results, including Claude `WebFetch` and `WebSearch` when no projected MCP network-tool metadata exists. It does not guess from native tool spelling or accept client-supplied taint. MCP and display-only events do not acquire native capability metadata. Simplification retained the existing owners; no new capability API, store, schema, or recovery path was added.

## Evidence

### Current repair

- Native WebFetch and WebSearch regressions failed against prior PR head `44fd853a85b0ffeed0ca9ba01d6efeded374f458`: provenance remained `agent` after native mutation and a clean tracked follow-up, and the root files remained in bootstrap. They pass with this repair.
- The regressions use the production Claude backend's metadata, actual stdio transport and parser/event/tracking path, actual PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks, a synthetic native executable, and real filesystem/provenance/bootstrap. They seed `MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, and `memory/nested/note.md`. Native-only cases intentionally have no projected MCP network metadata. Clean, non-owner, stale-hash/quarantine, failed-mutation, retired-callback, and Agent/Workflow-only controls remain covered; separate controls reject name-only, MCP, and display-only classification.
- Focused native, loopback, taint, transcript, permission, and protocol suites: **160 tests across 9 files passed**. The final native fixture also passed all **6 cases** after the small test-table simplification. Commands used `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks`.
- Core and affected agent-test type lanes, scoped lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. An initial lint preparation hit the host's OS-thread limit; the same supported lint path passed with `GOMAXPROCS=2`. No checks were disabled.

### Real Claude proof — prior combined build

[Holger's live proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201478#issuecomment-6995176499) reports 20 real Claude CLI turns on an isolated Gateway. Before: `da8fd166f5bca52a464470cf9172bdd7a58106cf`. After: this PR's **old head `44fd853a85b0` plus PR #201509 head `8cd5bf449788`, merged locally**. All live turns were owner turns via `chat.send` with `operator.admin`.

That proof covers clean and network-tainted **loopback** writes, native Edit/Write hash continuity and bootstrap eligibility, failed native edits, sticky quarantine after shell-induced hash drift, and Agent/Workflow-only denial. It supersedes the previous blanket statement that no real Claude proof had been performed, but **does not cover the native-network P1 flow or this new head**.

Coverage limits:
- The native Edit/Write live runs used **agent-level** `tools.exec.host: "node"` while Claude still ran locally. **Per-session** `execHost: "node"` instead selected paired-node placement and failed without a paired node (`missing execNode`). Paired-node writes remain out of scope.
- A missed PostToolUse and a retired callback/grant could not be forced live; those remain synthetic-boundary controls.
- **Required live rerun on head `5656d83c6340d84137ced409b63fafc0682193ff`:** native WebFetch/WebSearch → native Edit/Write → clean tracked edit → provenance and fresh-session bootstrap checks. This rerun remains reserved to Holger; prior-head combined-build proof is not current-head proof.

### Review status

[ClawSweeper's P1 review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201478#issuecomment-6993425706) covers old head `44fd853a85b0` and identified the native-network defect addressed here. It is prior-head review evidence, not a fresh review of this repair. The earlier Auto Review helper was unavailable; no clean local review or new hosted re-review is claimed. **Remain draft: live rerun and current-head independent/security review are pending. No landing performed.**

Contributor: Holger Gruenhagen (@holgergruenhagen).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @holgergruenhagen](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/692b31b0-d814-47d4-aa85-65f70a3d4c48)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/f5c7778d-2e4d-4562-9405-715610c495a5)

## Worked on by

- @holgergruenhagen

prs.title: fix(ui): point gateway-token errors at the secret source and #token= link
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This replaces advice to run `openclaw doctor --generate-gateway-token` in the Control UI auth-required step, its English string, and the CLI and gateway error messages. The new text points at the configured secret source and the `#token=` fragment link already supported by the Control UI.

The old advice is destructive in practice: it rotates the gateway token, disconnecting other session pages and daemons that still hold the old one. The common cause of 'unauthorized: gateway token missing' is simply that this browser has no token saved in session storage. The supported fix is a `#token=<token>` fragment link, which the UI accepts and strips. No token is printed and no query parameter is used.

## Changes

- `ui/src/components/login-gate-feedback.ts`: remove the `--generate-gateway-token` command from the auth-required step.
- `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-login.ts`: `login.failure.authRequired.stepGenerate` now distinguishes 'this browser has no token saved' from 'no token configured', points at `gateway.auth.token` and the `#token=` link, and warns that generating a new token disconnects other sessions.
- `src/commands/gateway-auth-token.ts`, `src/flows/doctor-gateway-auth.ts`, `src/gateway/auth.ts`, `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/auth-messages.ts`: the same non-destructive guidance in the CLI, doctor, startup and WebSocket close messages.
- Three tests updated to assert the new strings.

Generated translation caches are intentionally excluded: the repo's i18n tooling says to commit only the English source and let the post-merge refresh translate.

## Evidence

- 11 of 11 login-gate UI tests pass; the three updated source tests pass.
- `oxlint` is clean on all nine changed files.
- The WebSocket close message is 107 bytes, under the 120-byte limit.
- Three independent reviews at the wall: spec clean, security clean, bug and lint clean on the diff.

## Scope note

Other copies of the phrase remain in the wizard, security audit, known-weak secret path, macOS probe and docs. They are deliberately outside this patch to keep it small and reviewable; a follow-up can cover them.

prs.title: fix(agents): compact on predicted overflow instead of trimming tool results the provider already cached
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a production gateway over 36 hours, one signature caused 14 warm prompt-cache breaks (about 3.1M cached tokens lost), all on `openai-responses`:

- `[prompt-cache] message N (toolResult) differs from the previous request; history must be append-only; changed fields: content[0].text`, with N an early message (3, 16, 17, 27).
- `cache read dropped ~250k -> ~19-23k` (the system prompt only) on `request=1` of a new run, `systemPromptSeries=pinned`, request gap 0.8-5.6 s.
- Some sessions broke on 3 consecutive runs a few minutes apart.

All 14 breaks follow, within 20 s, a `[context-overflow-midturn-precheck] route=truncate_tool_results_only handled=true truncatedCount=N` line and a `[tool-result-truncation] Truncated N tool result(s) in session (... aggregate=N)` line for the same session. The sessions were near their context window (260k on that route) and had no compaction in between.

## Root cause

- When the pre-request pressure check (`resolveCompactionPressureDecision`, `run/preemptive-compaction.ts`) predicts an overflow, it chooses `truncate_tool_results_only` if trimming tool results could recover 1.5x the overflow. It counts every tool result in history, including results that earlier requests already sent in full.
- `handleEmbeddedAttemptMidTurnPrecheck` (`run/attempt-prompt-preflight.ts`) then calls `truncateOversizedToolResultsInSessionManager`. That rewrites the transcript in recovery mode, which ignores the frozen projection state, and trims the oldest results down to the aggregate tool-result budget.
- These results are already in the provider's cached prefix. Their text changes, so the cache restarts after the system prompt. This rebuild is not one of the allowed points (`/new`, `/reset`, compaction, model or provider switch) in `docs/reference/prompt-caching.md`.
- The trim removes only enough to fit. The next run adds new results, crosses the window again, and trims again. One break follows another.
- Recovery mode was designed for a prompt the provider already rejected. A predicted overflow is not a rejection: the provider accepted every byte so far.
- The prompt-time projection (`truncateOversizedToolResultsInMessages` with its frozen projection state) already keeps sent results byte-stable. It is not part of this break. The difference comes from the session rewrite above.

## Fix

- `buildToolResultReplacementPlan` (`tool-result-truncation.ts`) gets `preserveSentToolResults`. Results before the last assistant message are already sent, and the plan does not touch them. Only the unconsumed tail (results the provider has not received) can still be capped.
- The pressure decision counts only that unsent reduction. When sent history causes the overflow, the route becomes `compact_only` or `compact_then_truncate`. Compaction is an allowed rebuild point, and it frees enough space that the following runs append again.
- The mid-turn handler passes the same option to the session rewrite, so a predicted overflow cannot rewrite sent bytes through that path either.
- Recovery after a real provider rejection is unchanged. It still truncates all results when compaction cannot help, because the rejected prefix cannot be reused anyway. Sessions with compaction disabled therefore keep their previous fallback.

## Proof

**Real route (isolated throwaway Gateway, direct OpenAI Responses, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, `serviceTier: ultrafast` = 260k window, server compaction threshold set to the window).** One session: runs of three `exec` calls (~60k chars each) until the next run starts above the window.

| | main (d9a5437) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| pressure decision at the crossing request | `route=truncate_tool_results_only toolResultReducibleChars=364430` | `route=compact_only toolResultReducibleChars=0` |
| what happened | session rewrite refused (`Pending input relocation does not match its admitted transcript entry`), fallback to compaction | compaction |
| provider cache reads, whole session (41-42 requests) | 4,671,788 | 4,707,588 |
| requests with 0 cached tokens | 4 | 4 |

- On main, the trim was attempted on already-sent results, as in production. In this local harness the transcript rewrite is refused by the pending-input custody check for the turn's user message, so main also ends in compaction, and cache reads are the same. In production the rewrite succeeds in most cases (12 of 15 attempts in the same logs), and that is the break above.
- **Limit:** I could not make main's rewrite succeed on a real route, so this PR does not include a provider-measured before/after cache difference for the break itself. The production numbers above are the evidence for its cost. The PR stays a draft until a real-route before/after exists or a maintainer accepts this evidence.

**Prefix-stability journey** (`test/prompt-cache-prefix-stability.test-support.ts`, both routes): a new step sends 14 large exec results (past the aggregate budget), then 4 parallel results with the provider reporting the session just under the proactive threshold. This puts the next request past the window. The journey now allows breaks only at compactions and requires that this step compacts. A debug probe on main showed that this step reaches `route=truncate_tool_results_only`. On main the journey still passes, because the trim falls back to compaction as above. The journey makes sure the outcome stays a compaction.

**Focused tests:**
- `preemptive-compaction.test.ts`: sent results over the aggregate budget with a small overflow now route to `compact_only` (on main: `truncate_tool_results_only`; the test fails on main).
- `tool-result-truncation.test.ts`: a session rewrite with `preserveSentToolResults` keeps the sent results byte for byte and still caps the unsent oversized tail.
- Existing route tests (unsent tails still use `truncate_tool_results_only` / `compact_then_truncate`) are unchanged and green.

auto_merge.commit_title: fix(agents): compact on predicted overflow instead of trimming tool results the provider already cached (#199530)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* fix(agents): compact on predicted overflow instead of trimming tool results the provider already cached

The pre-request pressure check counted every tool result as reducible and, on the truncate-only route, rewrote the oldest already-sent results down to the aggregate budget. That changed bytes inside the provider's cached prefix and, because it trimmed only enough to fit, recurred on every run near the window.

Predicted pressure now counts and trims only results the provider has not received (after the last assistant message). Overflow from sent history routes to compaction, an allowed rebuild point. Recovery after a real provider rejection is unchanged.
