prs.title: fix(plugins): tell hooks which turn started the command a completion run reports
prs.body:
Related: #200664, #152204

## What Problem This Solves

When an `exec` call goes to the background (`yieldMs`), its completion later runs as its own agent turn, with `trigger: "event"` and `inputProvenance: { kind: "internal_system", sourceTool: "exec" }`. Plugin hooks on that run have no field naming the turn that started the command. `senderId`, `chatId` and `requesterDeviceId` (#200664) are set only for `trigger: "user"`, so they're absent here.

The trace can't be used to recover the starter either. When the session is busy, the completion runs after the turn that was running when the command finished, and its trace is that turn's trace. A plugin that follows the trace gets the wrong turn.

## User Impact

A plugin that applies a rule per requester, such as gating a tool call on who asked for it, has two bad options on a completion run today. It can treat every completion as unknown, which blocks legitimate follow-up work, or it can guess, which can attribute the work to whoever happened to be talking at the time.

With this change, hooks on that run get `ctx.execRequestOwners`, which names the turn that started the command. Nothing changes for plugins that don't read the field.

## Why This Change Was Made

The host already keeps this ownership. The completion run inherits the starting request's exec owners in `src/infra/exec-request-context.ts`. This change exposes a read-only copy of those records on the hook context and adds no new bookkeeping:

- `readInheritedExecRequestOwners(runId)` returns one frozen `{ runId, sessionKey?, sessionId?, ownerDeviceId? }` entry per inherited owner. `runId` is the run that called the tool, not a later continuation. Owners the run created for its own request are left out. The function returns `undefined`, never an empty array, when the run continues no other request or the run id isn't the current run.
- `buildAgentHookContextIdentityFields` takes `runId` and always adds the field, whatever the trigger. So every agent hook context built through it gets the field without per-builder edits. The CLI runner's prepared hook context passes it along.
- The Codex harness needs no change of its own: its prompt, lifecycle and compaction hooks go through the shared `buildAgentHookContext`, which calls the same identity builder, and its dynamic tools go through the shared `before_tool_call` wrapper. No plugin SDK export is added.
- `before_tool_call` gets the same field through `PluginHookToolContext`.
- The field comes only from the host's exec records, and the array and its entries are frozen. It is ancestry metadata only: the type doc says it grants the run none of the starter's authority or approvals.

## Evidence

Head: 30f02842760. The first commit adds the field. The second follows the first review: it removes the Codex projection and the SDK export, and routes the tests through the shared builder.

**Real model, real exec, busy session.** I built this head's package with `node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` (`OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (30f0284)`) and ran a loopback gateway with `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`. A small plugin logs each hook's `ctx`, and a paired-device operator client sends `chat.send`. Device ids are masked to their last 4 characters.

1. Run A: "Use the exec tool to run exactly: sleep 30; echo a-done -- set yieldMs to 1000 so it keeps running in the background…". The model called `exec`, the command yielded, and run A ended.
2. Run B, sent once A had ended: "Use the exec tool to run exactly: sleep 40; echo b-done -- in the foreground…". This kept the session busy while A's command finished.
3. When B ended, the completion ran as its own turn (`trigger: "event"`, `sourceTool: "exec"`):

```
23:50:03 before_agent_run      real-b-…  user   owners=ABSENT
23:50:47 agent_end             real-b-…  user   owners=ABSENT
23:50:48 before_prompt_build   528f2655… event  exec  owners=[{"runId":"real-a-…","sessionKey":"agent:main:real-busy2","sessionId":"70c717a4","ownerDeviceId":"..73f0"}]
23:50:48 before_agent_run      528f2655… event  exec  owners=[same]
23:50:52 before_agent_finalize 528f2655… event        owners=[same]
23:50:52 agent_end             528f2655… event        owners=[same]

trace ids: run A …595ca, run B …bbb48, completion …bbb48
```

The completion's trace is run B's, and `execRequestOwners` names run A, the run that started the command. The field is absent on A's and B's own hooks.

**Mock model, more cases** (first head 318096fb79e; the agent hook path is the same at this head). With an OpenAI-shaped mock that calls `exec` with `yieldMs: 1000`:

- idle: the completion names its starter on before_prompt_build, before_agent_run, before_tool_call, before_agent_finalize and agent_end;
- busy: same result as the real-model run;
- two overlapping execs: two completion runs, each naming its own starter.

**Unit tests** (`src/plugins/hook-agent-context.test.ts`, 5 new). They cover idle, two overlapping execs, the busy-session case, before_tool_call matching the agent hooks, and absence outside a run.

- On base a4be1ae09e3 with the source changes reverted, 5 fail. The idle, overlap and busy tests fail on the missing field through the existing `buildAgentHookContextIdentityFields` (for example `expected {} to deeply equal { execRequestOwners: [ … ] }`). The other two fail because the tool-context helper is missing.
- On this head, 11 pass.

**Checks on this head:**

- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` pass.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on the changed files.
- `check:test-lines-ratchet`, `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check:assertion-safety`, `lint:tmp:export-name-collisions` and `lint:tmp:tsgo-core-boundary` pass.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:diff --base a4be1ae09e3 --head HEAD` exits 0 (digest `efb88881`). The change is one optional context field, with no new function export.
- On the first head, every other `lint:tmp:*` script passed, along with `lint:kysely`, `check:database-worker-ratchet`, `check:test-timeout-race-ratchet`, `check:temp-path-guardrails`, `check:database-first-legacy-stores` and `git diff --check`. The second commit touches only the four files above.

## Accepted edge cases

- `after_tool_call` and hooks outside agent runs (`reply_payload_sending`, `message_sending`, `before_dispatch`) don't carry the field. The real run shows this.
- `ownerDeviceId` is left out when the starting connection had no verified paired device, for example a shared-token client with no device identity.
- One completion run that drains two owners returns two entries. The unit test covers this, but in the real run the two overlapping execs completed as two separate runs.
- The subagent-session heartbeat wake (trigger `heartbeat`, `sourceTool: "exec"`), the CLI runner and the Codex harness reach the same shared builders and are covered by types and unit tests. I didn't run them end to end.

prs.title: fix: show the plugin-update restart countdown next to the update that needs it
prs.body:
Related: #201236, #201178

## What Problem This Solves

With automatic updates on, a Gateway that still owes plugin updates from its last update restarts on its current version to finish them (#201178). That update ran recently and succeeded, so the Gateway reports it as the last run, and the Control UI Inbox showed only that earlier outcome ("✅ OpenClaw updated to …"). The "Restarting in 0:45 to finish plugin updates" countdown and its **Hold 1 h** button stayed hidden, so the Gateway restarted with no warning. Dismissing that outcome row also hid the restart.

## User Impact

User impact: when the Gateway is about to restart to finish plugin updates, the Inbox row says "Finishing update · Restarting in 0:45 to finish plugin updates". Opening it shows the countdown, **Hold 1 h**, and the earlier update's outcome underneath. This covers the waiting-for-idle, held and applying states too. The row cannot be dismissed while that restart is pending. A failed earlier run keeps the row's error color. Release and Git update campaigns look exactly as before, and an update that is still running still comes first.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway sends the UI everything it needs: a campaign with no `schedule.target` (the one #201178 announces to finish owed plugin steps) together with the last finished run. The Inbox card always ranked a recent finished run above any campaign. For a release campaign that is fine. For this campaign the run is the reason for the restart, so hiding the restart behind it was wrong.

- `isFinishingUpdateCampaign` in `update-schedule-projection.ts` is the single test for "campaign with no target". The campaign label formatter, the card title, the card ranking and the Inbox dismissal now all use it.
- `SidebarUpdateCard`: when a finished, not running, run is visible and a finishing campaign is pending, the campaign leads the compact row and its card. The run's outcome is rendered beside it, without a second copy of the status banner. Opening the row no longer starts a status check, because there is no target to refresh, so the countdown stays in view. Pressing the restart button still checks first.
- `resolveSidebarUpdateAttention`: the run's "dismiss this outcome" signature no longer applies while a finishing campaign is pending. The row is not dismissable then, which matches how the same campaign behaves when no run is shown. The entry still carries that signature as `retainedDismissal`, and the Inbox store keeps it during dismissal reconciliation, so an outcome the operator already dismissed stays dismissed if the restart is retired without a new run (for example, automatic updates turned off mid-countdown).

There is no new copy, Gateway protocol, schema, config or stored-state change. Updates settings already showed the countdown and Hold alongside the "Latest update attempt" section, so that page is unchanged.

Update behavior: this is Control UI code served by the Gateway it ships with. It does not touch the updater, Doctor, service lifecycle or migrations. Older Gateways never announce a targetless campaign, so nothing changes for them.

## Evidence

**Fixture provenance:** every screenshot fixture is a real `update.status` reply recorded from a live Gateway (below). The unit-test fixtures use the same shape built from source fixtures.

**Live Gateway payload.** I ran the installed-package Docker cell `OPENCLAW_DOCKER_ALL_LANES=package-installed-recovery-owed-plugin-retry pnpm test:docker:all` on base `6d815d786f4`, and it passed. That cell brings a real managed Gateway to an owed-plugin retry. Next to it, a read-only poller ran `openclaw gateway call update.status` inside the container about every 1.7 s, which goes through the Gateway's own client method. During the retry the live Gateway returned exactly the state from the finding:
- `lastRun`: a `succeeded` CLI update (2026.11.5 → 2026.11.6-first-hop.5) whose last step is `finalize:owed:plugin-convergence: skipped`
- `updateAvailable: null`
- `schedule`: `{ channel: "stable", autoEnabled: true, install: { kind: "package" }, campaign: { state: "countdown", applyAtMs, forceAtMs, … } }`, with no `target`

The sequence was `waiting-for-idle` for about 5 s, then `countdown`, then the retry run. The only edit to the recorded reply was replacing the container hostname. It is the fixture for the screenshots below.

**Screenshots.** Control UI E2E harness in Chromium, 1280x720, light theme. The mock Gateway's hello snapshot and its `update.status` reply both carry that recorded live reply. The browser clock is fixed 45.5 s before the recorded `applyAtMs`, and the Inbox is opened from `/chat` and expanded. Before uses the production files from `origin/main` `1ab0fc86340`; after was recaptured on the final PR head `fc7e6504a34` (its row and card crops are byte-identical to the first capture on `1be95dfba2a`).

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Inbox row shows only the earlier update outcome, no restart notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/836121ac-ae28-4e23-9379-f18b3394a304) | ![After: Inbox row titled Finishing update with the restart countdown, Hold 1 h, and the earlier outcome beneath](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce7107e2-ae90-4198-bdef-7d575aba1acf) |
| ![Before: expanded card with only the earlier outcome](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c75fa046-5688-44cb-9031-63043343ade0) | ![After: expanded card with countdown action, Hold 1 h, and the earlier outcome](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58072253-d7a2-4ed9-bffc-c9474fb26065) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Earlier outcome alone highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5fef6165-d338-4702-b120-1ade2bdd0487) | ![Countdown with Hold and the earlier outcome highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/299dd2b2-b8fb-4476-a710-050cbd53e65a) |

Control: I ran the same capture with the same live reply plus a release target (`target: { kind: "package", version: "2099.1.1" }`). It produced byte-identical row and card crops on base and head; both show the earlier outcome first, as before.

| Release control, before | Release control, after |
| --- | --- |
| ![Release control before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f661618-c776-491a-a738-cb7b472f702e) | ![Release control after, identical](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f12694f6-165b-4e9f-b209-2fafd24a99e5) |

Updates settings with the same reply read "Restarting in 0:46 to finish plugin updates · Hold 1 h" on both base and head. It was not affected.

**Terminal recordings** of the same focused tests. RED uses the production files from `origin/main` `7ce2d10eced` with the PR's tests; GREEN is the exact PR head `fc7e6504a34`:

RED (base):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09f8f68c-7af5-436e-b105-e8ba027d0ba7

GREEN (head):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79c2afdf-2731-402f-9642-06dba8c5187b

Full raw logs are not attached because the Crabbox artifact store rejected the upload (`http 401`). The decisive output is below.

<details>
<summary>RED on base: 7 failures, release control passes</summary>

```
 ✓ … keeps a recorded run ahead of a release campaign
 × … keeps the countdown finishing restart visible beside the update that owes it
 × … keeps the waiting-for-idle finishing restart visible beside the update that owes it
 × … keeps the held finishing restart visible beside the update that owes it
 × … keeps the applying finishing restart visible beside the update that owes it
 × … keeps a finishing countdown in view when opened beside a failed run
Expected: "Finishing update"
Received: "✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.9.2 (from 2026.9.1)."
Expected: "Restarting in 0:45 to finish plugin updates"
Received: "1 of 3 phases complete"
      Tests  5 failed | 1 passed | 27 skipped (33)
 × … renderSidebarUpdateSurface > leads with the restart that finishes the plugin updates its last run owes
+ Received:
  "signature": "[\"run\",\"6631ecee-adbf-41e8-a0e3-1b88b28b0a59\"]",
      Tests  1 failed | 12 skipped (13)
 × … sidebar attention source publication > shows a finishing restart over a dismissed run and keeps that dismissal for later
      Tests  1 failed | 31 skipped (32)
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>GREEN on head</summary>

```
      Tests  6 passed | 27 skipped (33)
      Tests  1 passed | 12 skipped (13)
      Tests  1 passed | 31 skipped (32)
```
</details>

**Tests** (each fails on base for the reason given and passes on head):
- `sidebar-update-card.test.tsx`
  - A table over countdown, waiting-for-idle, held and applying: with a recent successful run and a finishing campaign, the compact row is titled "Finishing update" and shows that state's text; the opened card has the same text as its action, shows Hold only where it is allowed, and keeps the earlier outcome.
  - The same setup opened beside a failed run, with a pending status check: the countdown stays in view, no status check runs, and the row keeps its error color.
  - Control: a release campaign with a recorded run still shows the run first and no timer. This one passes on base too, by design.
- `sidebar-attention-store.test.ts`: with a stored dismissal of the earlier run and a pending finishing restart, the Inbox store shows the restart row, keeps the stored dismissal through reconciliation, and hides the outcome again once the campaign is retired. On the first PR head this failed with the dismissal pruned (`{}`).
- `sidebar-issue-item.test.tsx`: the regression runs through the real chain the Inbox uses. The `update.status` reply (same shape as the live one) goes through the overlays projection and `resolveSidebarUpdateAttention` into `renderSidebarUpdateSurface`. The row is "Finishing update" with the countdown and Hold, the outcome is beside it, and the producer offers no run-outcome dismissal.

**Checks run** on the head (rebased on `1ab0fc86340`):
- Both touched test files in full: 33 + 13 passed. Also `sidebar-attention-update`, `sidebar-attention` and `update-overlay-helpers`: 78 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` passed (no new strings). oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files are clean; the one warning, `style` as a string, is in an existing line.
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base 6d815d786f4 --no-merge-base`: all ok, including `test-lines`.
- `git diff --check` is clean.
- `pnpm ui:build && pnpm ui:check-performance`: no zod in boot; startup, chat boot and new boot JS gzip are within budget. Four budgets still fail as they do on `main`: largest CSS, total CSS gzip and raw, and 21 chat boot requests. This PR changes no CSS and adds no module.

**Review.** I asked for an independent read-only review, including test quality. Changes made from it:
- Opening the row no longer swaps the countdown for "Checking…". It used to start a status check meant for a release target.
- A failed earlier run keeps the row's error color.
- The release control now also asserts the run card's title.

The reviewer also noted that a stored dismissal of the earlier outcome was pruned while the restart was pending; the ClawSweeper round 1 review raised the same point as P2. That is now fixed (see `retainedDismissal` above, with its failing-first store test). `autoreview` does not run on this machine.

ClawSweeper local review, round 1 on `1be95dfba2a`: overall F, proof F, patch C. Its one finding (P2, the pruned dismissal) is fixed in `5bd82335368`. Its proof note was that the browser evidence replays a live payload through a mocked Gateway. No further rounds were run.

<details>
<summary>Test file audit</summary>

- `sidebar-update-card.test.tsx`: I read the whole file. Added the four-state table, the failed-run and status-check case, and the release control. Existing helpers are reused (`finishingSchedule`, `succeededRun`, `packageSchedule`, `createDeferred`). These cases fake only `Date`, so the details `toggle` event still fires on real timers; `afterEach` restores timers and mocks. Nothing removed: no dead helpers, skips or redundant cases found.
- `sidebar-issue-item.test.tsx`: I read the whole file. Added one case that uses the existing `updateFixture` and `renderUpdate` harness, with per-test storage stubs and overlay disposal. Nothing removed.

</details>

## What was not proven

- A browser connected to the live Docker Gateway. The cell's Gateway listens only inside a disposable container that publishes no port, and its harness files belong to another worker. Instead, the UI was driven by the recorded live `update.status` reply in the mocked-Gateway E2E harness.
- The countdown text in the screenshots depends on the fixed browser clock, not on wall time from the run.
- An existing layout issue: in the opened card, a long outcome headline runs past the card's right edge. It looks the same on `main` for any recent run, as in the release control above. It is not changed here, to keep CSS (already over budget on `main`) unchanged.

prs.title: fix: keep parent working while native Codex children run
prs.body:
Related: #39127, #168186. Preserves the paused-child distinction discussed in #186387.

## What Problem This Solves

A parent conversation can appear idle after `sessions_yield` while its native Codex child is still executing.

## User Impact

The existing working indicator remains available through `hasActiveSubagentRun` during observed running or waiting native execution, then clears when execution becomes unknown or ends. This changes server-side activity metadata only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native children are owned by the harness monitor rather than OpenClaw's subagent-run rows. Their host-issued event sink now contributes display-only activity to the existing run-registry snapshot. Independent tokens retain concurrent child observations; requester identity and lifecycle revision keep activity from moving to a replacement conversation. The existing registry revision and row publisher invalidate cached projections. Settlement, custody release, and Gateway closure remove the observation independently of result delivery.

## Evidence

Historical pre-integration head: `60bab48c06b0d7d5141919ba1403fc6da49610e9`. Its only change from the reviewed production commit `2738b9d7aa1223ed3f689bdbac027a97b3d6eef6` is the requested test-line allocation.

- **Real main-targeted Gateway/model proof:** [redacted method and live observations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196256#issuecomment-6770721732). A fresh, isolated Gateway built from this PR's main-targeted source runs a real parent that spawns one native child and yields. While yielded, `sessions.describe` reports `hasActiveRun=false`, `hasActiveSubagentRun=true`, `activeRunIds=[]`. After native execution ends, the parent receives the automatic completion and finishes `PROBE_DONE`; both describe and the sidebar's list projection clear the activity. This replay uses no stable overlay, mocked execution, or injected events. It proves server-side behavior, not browser rendering.
- **Exact source:** The built checkout plus allocation has tree `bb621456c7526a4f16d7f4321dff2cc051b040a7`, exactly matching the published head. Canonical `build:runtime` completed successfully (exit 0, 4m38s). It reported Control UI size-budget warnings; no UI sources or budgets are changed here.
- **Test budget:** A separate `config/test-lines-allocations/196256-native-child-activity.txt` grants exactly **23** net regression lines for native observation and lifecycle cleanup assertions. The shared scalar is unchanged. Ratchet against introduction base `6edcaa28edb7`: **6,602,835 / 6,602,838**, slack **3**.
- **Existing focused validation, production-identical reviewed head:** 11 passing current-main tests across native custody, run projection, and registry invalidation. Runner time 171.09s; native/registry shard 44.43s, including compiler/fixture startup. Core typechecks, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace, and import smoke passed. The lifecycle assertions cover running/waiting/unknown, requester replacement, release, settlement, and Gateway closure without inventing a foreground run.
- **Earlier stable evidence:** Four extended custody regressions fail on the 11.2 base at the missing activity assertion and pass with the compatible backport; 9 focused stable tests and the export smoke pass. The earlier installed-backport trace is supplementary; the new real main-targeted replay addresses ClawSweeper's proof request.
- **Isolation:** Separate HOME, state, workspace, and loopback port. The test Gateway shut down cleanly and temporary model credentials/config were removed; the operator Gateway was untouched.

Broad exact-head CI and maintainer review remain integration gates.

## Current-main integration — November 18, 2026

Published head: `808e4911b6f6d4b7ac4c67ebc6f8868c9bced751`, integrating official main `2f658fce2596a82459efccbe84a471b077600633`. The only manual conflict was in the registry's type/value exports. The resolution keeps the native-child projection owner and upstream's delegated-authority and owner-status exports together; no new behavior, configuration, SDK policy, test allocation or baseline change was introduced.

- All **11 focused tests** pass across native completion custody, run projection and registry invalidation (3 files; Vitest 92.74s; canonical wrapper 231.79s including 128.91s cold worker preparation).
- Core production typecheck, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, scoped whitespace and the canonical test-line ratchet pass. Net regression growth remains 23 lines with the existing 23-line allocation; the shared baseline is unchanged.
- Fresh independent local Autoreview (Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, medium, P0–P2) assessed the complete PR delta against the pinned main plus projection context: one complete pass, scoped-clean. Its scope does not claim a new running-Gateway proof.
- The earlier real native Gateway/model proof above remains attributed to its named revision. Newly published-head hosted CI is separate and must be checked before merging.

I have carried the release-adapted fix since **OpenClaw 2026.11.2**, through **2026.11.3, 2026.11.4 and the currently deployed 2026.11.5**. It remains stable in my use. The combined 2026.11.5 deployment passed package-byte verification, native Doctor/migrations, Gateway health and active-plugin checks; this is operational evidence for the release adaptation, separate from a pristine package build of this PR head.


**New-head hosted CI status (November 18):** [CI run 44260090221](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44260090221) is `action_required` and has no jobs. The new-head CI gate is red because the fork workflow has not been admitted, rather than from an executed failing test. Please review and approve the fork workflow run so CI/CodeQL/OpenGrep can start. Local passing checks above do not replace those hosted gates.

prs.body:
Refs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/180796
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165452, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/153426

## What Problem This Solves

A session rooted in a project or worktree can edit the agent workspace's memory without updating its provenance. The next clean tracked edit then quarantines the file, removing MEMORY.md or USER.md from automatic context.

## User Impact

Host-rooted sessions retain provenance and hash continuity when OpenClaw file tools edit the canonical agent workspace's memory. Session-local memory keeps its existing workspace records, and sandbox writes remain isolated to the sandbox filesystem.

This does not loosen quarantine, change the hash-continuity rule, rehabilitate existing untrusted rows, or track shell writes. CLI turn-taint and native-writer coverage are addressed separately in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201478.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the canonical workspace from the execution agent, then let the existing memory-write observer classify that workspace before the session root. Record each artifact under its owning workspace without changing origin classification, rollback, or quarantine policy. The additional host workspace is never passed to a sandbox observer.

## Evidence

- [Live before/after proof from Holger](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201509#issuecomment-6995176114): an isolated Linux Gateway with deterministic model responses exercised real rooted-session write/edit tools, provenance reads, and fresh-session `/context list`. Before: stale hashes followed by quarantine and missing MEMORY.md/USER.md. After: matching agent-origin hashes and both files injected. Session-local ownership and rooted network-taint controls also passed. The after build combined this head `8cd5bf449788214a2e9a3a46143f848700f61193` with PR #201478 head `44fd853a85b0ffeed0ca9ba01d6efeded374f458`; the rooted path exercises this PR's change.
- On base da8fd166f5bca52a464470cf9172bdd7a58106cf, rooted write/edit regressions left stale provenance hashes; the next clean edit recorded untrusted and excluded MEMORY.md and USER.md from bootstrap.
- All six new cases pass with the fix: rooted write/edit, canonical control, tainted-write quarantine, session-local ownership, and sandbox isolation. Tests use real provenance storage and cover MEMORY.md, USER.md, and nested memory notes, followed by clean tracked edits and bootstrap assertions for the curated files.
- 160 existing tests passed across provenance, bootstrap (including personal and remote), coding tools, sandbox, prefix stability, and the session-memory hook. Commands used pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks.
- Targeted TypeScript checks, changed-file lint, formatting, and git diff --check passed. Simplification pass retained the existing observer and provenance store; no schema or new state owner was added.
- New regression file: approximately 4 seconds test time (43 seconds including cold compilation); existing suite approximately 117 seconds in the test runner. Hosted CI has not been run as part of this local proof.

**Review status:** Local Auto Review did not complete and was stopped at the requester's direction; no clean local autoreview is claimed. The [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201509#issuecomment-6994557545) of this head reported no actionable findings. Maintainer review and applicable security approval remain separate; no merge or landing is requested.

**Live-proof limits:** The linked rooted-session proof used a real Gateway and deterministic OpenAI-compatible mock model, not a real Claude model. Sandbox isolation was not exercised live because the test host has no Docker/Podman; shell writes remain out of scope.

Contributor: Holger Gruenhagen (@holgergruenhagen).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/692b31b0-d814-47d4-aa85-65f70a3d4c48)

## Worked on by

- @holgergruenhagen

prs.title: refactor: retire tar and Arrow dependency patches
prs.body:
Related maintainer request: https://discord.com/channels/1456350064065904867/1456744319972282449/1572744859754692649

## What Problem This Solves

Maintainers carry two dependency patches that can be replaced with the libraries’ existing public APIs: tar’s unbundled archive entry and Arrow’s native table builders. The patch inventory also allows obsolete Baileys versions and contains stale maintenance evidence.

## User Impact

Two fewer dependency patches to maintain (18 → 16), with no package-version, archive-format, memory-schema, security-policy or user-configuration change. Archive operations and memory writes continue to work with host code-generation/built-in protections enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Select `tar/raw` consistently in runtime/tooling callers, type imports, mocks and embedded CommonJS fixtures. Remove the tar manifest patch, registration, lock context and allowance. Keep tar 7.5.22, its override, the minizlib fix and runtime bundling. fs-safe owns its native/WASM archives separately; npm’s private tar remains unchanged.
- Build a native Arrow Table at the existing MemoryDB serialization owner rather than requesting generic row inference. Preserve nullable schema/rows, Float32 bytes, malformed-vector rejection, existing overlong-vector truncation and CJS module identity. Remove only the Arrow patch and its private predicate tests; retain and strengthen the actual memory storage regression. No wrapper, fallback, new dependency or replacement parser.
- Remove retired Baileys rc12/rc13 permissions and correct retained-patch versions, hashes and independent removal criteria.

## Evidence

- Stock tar manifest verified byte-for-byte. Original ESM/CJS fixture fails on read-only `Buffer.concat`; `tar/raw` passes both. Bundled regression passes without external non-builtin imports. Archive/guard suite: 49 tests passed; 15 backup/template/package-consumer files passed with one existing skip (208 seconds).
- Stock Arrow + native LanceDB: original source and native-built MemoryDB fail at the intended code-generation boundary; changed source and native build pass. Store/search/list/delete/reopen/close, agent isolation, persisted nullability and nine malformed-vector comparisons retain behavior. Final combined install: 91 memory tests plus 13 patch-guard tests passed (76 seconds).
- Frozen pnpm 12.15.0 install passed with unchanged supply-chain policy. Lock delta only removes tar/Arrow patch contexts. Full final `pnpm build`, including declarations, passed in 173 seconds. It emitted Control UI CSS/boot-budget diagnostics; those surfaces are not claimed fixed.
- Scoped lint, core/scripts/plugin/tooling typechecks, matched formatting, line-cap ratchet and diff check passed. Twenty retained-patch hashes/runtime-file rows independently verified. Full-range independent local review found no actionable P0–P2 defects; it did not rerun tests.
- Remaining broad and platform-specific proof is exact-head PR CI. No Solid upgrade is included; that work overlaps #200929.

Requested by and co-authored with @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/77ee8733-627c-42bb-acb9-c63d819df796)
- [Tar cutover implementation and initial proof](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/16656175-9369-4342-b095-ce26c530568c)
- [Arrow implementation and native verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/a62e7901-509b-4ab5-8a97-f1dae70b1dd6)

## Worked on by

prs.title: fix: let updates finish when plugins change no config and openclaw.json is read-only
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw.json` is a file the updater may not replace, such as a link to a provisioned read-only file, a core update with official npm plugins installed reports `failed` (`post-update-failed`) and tells you to stop the Gateway and run `openclaw update repair`. That happens even though the update finished: the new core serves, `/readyz` is 200, and both plugins are installed at their new versions (install records, packages on disk, and the local `plugins list` inventory). The next plain `openclaw update` then says `already-current` and leaves the failed record in place. The failure report's instruction, `openclaw gateway stop`, also refuses in a non-interactive shell unless you add `--force`.

## User Impact

An update whose plugin work changes no configuration now succeeds on a config file it cannot write, and leaves that file byte-for-byte unchanged. A plugin update that does need a config change is still refused on such a file, exactly as before. When an update does leave maintenance unfinished, the report now names `openclaw gateway stop --force` (for the managed service), the same command `openclaw update repair` names.

## Why This Change Was Made

After plugin convergence, the updater published the plugin install records together with a config-file write, even when convergence had changed no config path. With nothing to write, that write only restamped the file, and a refused write failed an otherwise complete update. Now, when no config path changed, the updater publishes the install records alone through the existing records-only commit and skips the config write.

<details>
<summary>Root cause, and the hypothesis it replaced</summary>

- **Throw site.** A diagnostic copy of the candidate recorded the stack in the process that ran plugin convergence. The throw is `captureConfigRootWriteTarget` (`src/config/io.write-safety.ts`), reached from the publication's `transformConfigFileWithRetry` in `updatePluginsAfterCoreUpdateWithLease`. The error is a non-retryable `ConfigMutationConflictError`, with `publishing: true`, `cohort: false`, `configChanged: false` and **`changedPaths: []`**. The install records were already at the new versions before publication started, because without a cohort the plugin updater commits them plugin by plugin. So the publication's rollback had nothing to restore, and the state was consistent.
- **Hypothesis replaced.** The first theory was that a first update from a published updater fails because it has no plugin cohort, so a convergence failure is rethrown instead of being owed. Falsifier: with a cohort, this same error still rethrows. `pluginConvergenceFailureBlocksUpdate` treats a refused config write as blocking, and so does `stage.publishing`. Both are deliberate (#200507) and documented as never owed. Owing without a cohort would not change the outcome. This PR leaves both rules alone.
- **Broken invariant.** A plugin publication with nothing to commit to the config file must not be able to fail a converged plugin phase. Its owner is the publication block in `updatePluginsAfterCoreUpdateWithLease`. The new branch lives in `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-plugin-records.ts`, which only that owner imports.
- **Freshness and target.** The decision reads the config with the same pending deferred plugin migration facts the update's other reads use. It also checks the config path proof captured when the update read the config for write (`assertConfigPathForWrite`, the same check the config-write path runs), both before deciding and after the index write. So a config link re-pointed to another file mid-update fails the publication with "config target changed since last load", as a write would, and its records are not kept. It runs the same `beforeCommit` and recovery authority checks before the index write. After the write it re-reads the config: if the config no longer reads as valid, the index write is restored and the phase reports the existing `plugin-config-conflict` deferral. A valid unrelated edit in that window is kept, as the config-write path keeps it.
- **Cohort (main-to-main).** The index writer records the cohort's `records` publication the same way on both branches. No config publication is recorded when no config was written, so a later rollback leaves the file alone; a written config is still restored.
- **Retired path.** A config file holding legacy `plugins.installs` no longer reads as valid on main (it is rejected as a retired field), so a records-only branch for it is unreachable and none is kept.

</details>

### Behavior change for main-to-main updates

When plugin convergence changes no config path, the config file is no longer rewritten. That means no `meta.lastTouchedVersion` restamp, no backup rotation and no config-audit row for that no-op. I checked every reader of `meta.lastTouchedVersion`, and none needs this write:

- future-version warnings and `persistValidatedDowngradeConfig`, which restamps a downgrade on its own;
- Doctor's migration source version;
- the bundled-discovery inference, which is guarded by the canonical SQLite row;
- immutable-protection and cohort-recovery diffs, which both ignore the stamp.

An update that changes no plugins already never reached this write, so a stamp the update did not refresh was already a normal state.

### Update behavior for published drivers

The fix lives in the candidate, so it applies on the first update from published updaters. With migrated state, 2026.11.5 hands finalization to the candidate's `update-migrated-finalize` worker, and the candidate's own plugin publication runs there with no cohort; with this change it no longer writes the config. The published parent accepts the worker's result and keeps the candidate's terminal record. No marker, schema, protocol, config key or stored field changes. `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1` is unaffected: both 2026.11.5 and main refuse `openclaw update` up front in that mode, before any staging (observed: 2026.11.5 exits in 1.3 s with the read-only refusal).

## Evidence

**End-to-end proof, in words.** This is a real install driven by a real published updater, not a seeded fixture. In a disposable Docker container, `npm install -g openclaw@2026.11.5` installs the published release from the npm registry. `openclaw doctor --fix` seeds state, `openclaw plugins install` installs the real official packages `@openclaw/zalo` and `@openclaw/voice-call` from npm, and `openclaw gateway install` runs the Gateway as a managed service. Then `openclaw.json` becomes a link to a read-only file. The installed 2026.11.5 `openclaw update` command then updates to a package cut from the candidate, through its shipped entry point, with no test hooks. The future plugin versions are the published 2026.11.5 packages restamped with a newer version and served from a local npm registry that proxies everything else to npmjs.org.

After the update, the cell checks the shipped surfaces:
- the update's own `--json` result and its run record;
- `openclaw update status --json`;
- the Gateway's `/readyz` and `openclaw gateway probe`, for the serving version;
- `openclaw plugins list --json` (the local plugin inventory, not a query of the running Gateway), and each plugin's install record against its package on disk;
- the config file's bytes.

Then it removes the fault and runs a plain `openclaw update` again. On the base, the published updater's update exits 1 and records `failed`. On the head, it exits 0 and records `succeeded`, the Gateway serves the new version with `/readyz` 200, and the local plugin inventory lists both plugins as loaded at the new version. A negative-control run of the same cell also requests another update channel, which is a real config write. That write is still refused end to end, and the failure report from the shipped CLI names the working `gateway stop --force` command.

### Red, green and negative-control recordings

All three recordings run the same lane as committed: published `openclaw@2026.11.5`, the two official npm plugins, and `openclaw.json` a link to a read-only file. Each first update goes to a future core cut from the candidate. Each recording ends with observations read from the cell's own captures. The cell asserts the update exit code and run record status. It also checks that `openclaw update status --json` is readable and names the update's own run, that no owed step was left, that a fresh `/readyz` probe in that run succeeded, that the serving version matches, that the plugin records match their packages on disk and the local `plugins list` inventory lists them as loaded (this reads the local inventory; it does not query the running Gateway), and that the config bytes are unchanged.

**base/red, `3e0d3687c5d`.** The first update exits 1: `error / post-update-failed`, run `failed`, rollback `not-attempted: state-migrated-no-rollback`, while the Gateway serves the new version with `/readyz` 200 and the local plugin inventory lists both plugins as loaded at the new version. The report says `openclaw gateway stop`, which refuses an unattended shell.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c96c1fc6-57c5-47a0-89e7-1439931b6ff6

**head/green, `a8b99203816`** (candidate packed at `90ac53240b9`; the commits after it change only the e2e harness, a lane script entry and a comment). The first update exits 0 with the run `succeeded`, and the same serving and plugin observations hold. The next plain `openclaw update` exits 0 as `already-current`, with no failed record and nothing owed.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09cdc7b9-3006-416e-b11b-255830459ccf

**head/negative control, `a8b99203816`** (`OPENCLAW_PUBLISHED_DRIVER_PLUGIN_FAULT=refused-channel-change`). The same first update also passes `--channel beta`, which needs a real config write against the read-only config.
- That write is still refused: exit 1, run `failed`, with the same `is a symlink` refusal from the shipped CLI.
- The Gateway serves the new version with `/readyz` 200. The plugins stay at 2026.11.5, because the refusal comes before plugin convergence.
- The report now names `openclaw gateway stop --force` for the managed service, so the new wording is captured from the shipped CLI.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfb670a2-1de4-49f2-b539-ccf2f628cd49

**What changed after the recordings.** `git diff a8b99203816..HEAD` is a merge of `main` (`2840dc974fc`) plus three harness-only commits, `d1da62a9520`, `e612b2363e0` and `91dbd6bfb77`, which touch only `scripts/e2e/published-driver-update-docker.sh`, `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/published-driver-plugin-publication.mjs`, the shared plugin fixture packer `scripts/e2e/lib/update-first-hop-package-fixtures.mjs` (an optional target version), its test, and the lane's `package.json` script entry. The four production files are byte-identical between `90ac53240b9` (the recorded candidate) and the head. The merged `main` commits change no update, config-write, plugin install-record or harness code; the closest is #201220, which adds a plugin manifest field for the Customize sidebar.

The final harness was rerun on head `91dbd6bfb77` with the same candidate, both the green cell and the negative control. See "Recorded lane cells" under Commands and results.

Full raw logs are not attached because the Crabbox artifact store rejected uploads (`crabbox artifacts publish`: `http 401 Unauthorized`). The decisive excerpts below come from the sanitized captures. Container hostnames and the synthetic gateway token are redacted; nothing else is changed.

<details>
<summary>base/red: first update result and run record (3e0d3687c5d)</summary>

```text
$ openclaw update --yes --json --tag <future core cut from the candidate>
exit code 1
status: error   reason: post-update-failed
run: status failed, phase finished, reason post-update-failed, 2026.11.5 -> 2026.11.6-first-hop.0
rollbackOutcome: not-attempted / state-migrated-no-rollback
step "post-update verification": exitCode 1
  stderrTail: Config writes need a regular file, but /home/appuser/.openclaw/openclaw.json is a symlink.
              Point OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH at the real file, or replace the symlink with that file.
next action: ... stop the Gateway first (`openclaw gateway stop`), then run `openclaw update repair` to finish maintenance.
after the update: /readyz 200; serving 2026.11.6-first-hop.0; plugins voice-call and zalo at 2026.11.6-first-hop.0 (record and disk), loaded
cell: AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: The first update succeeds   (cell exit 1)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>head/green: first update and the next update (a8b99203816)</summary>

```text
$ openclaw update --yes --json --tag <future core cut from the candidate>
exit code 0
status: ok
run: status succeeded, 2026.11.5 -> 2026.11.6-first-hop.0; update status lastRun is this run, succeeded, no owed rows
openclaw.json: same bytes as before the update (asserted by the cell)
after the update: /readyz 200 (fresh probe); serving 2026.11.6-first-hop.0; plugins voice-call and zalo at 2026.11.6-first-hop.0, loaded
$ openclaw update --yes --json          (fault removed, no newer release)
exit code 0, skipped / already-current; update status lastRun is this run, skipped; owed steps none
cell: plugin publication cell passed   (cell exit 0)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>head/negative control: a real config write is still refused (a8b99203816)</summary>

```text
$ openclaw update --yes --json --tag <future core cut from the candidate> --channel beta
exit code 1
status: error   reason: post-update-failed
run: status failed; rollbackOutcome not-attempted / state-migrated-no-rollback
step "post-update verification": Config writes need a regular file, but /home/appuser/.openclaw/openclaw.json is a symlink. ...
next action: ... stop the Gateway through its service owner first (`openclaw gateway stop --force` for the managed service), then run `openclaw update repair` to finish maintenance.
after the update: /readyz 200; serving 2026.11.6-first-hop.0; plugins voice-call and zalo still 2026.11.5, loaded; openclaw.json unchanged
cell: refused channel change cell passed   (cell exit 0)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Stack from the process that ran plugin convergence (diagnostic candidate, logging only)</summary>

A diagnostic copy of a base candidate packed at `f8727fdcd3a` logged these facts from the plugin publication catch block. It changes no behavior. The process is the candidate's adopted finalization driver, which a 2026.11.5 updater hands the run to after state migration.

```text
publication {"changedPaths":[],"previousRecords":{"voice-call":"2026.11.5","zalo":"2026.11.5"},
             "convergenceChanges":[],"convergenceConfigChanges":[],
             "nextRecords":{"voice-call":"2026.11.6-first-hop.0","zalo":"2026.11.6-first-hop.0"}}
records-before-publication {"voice-call":"2026.11.6-first-hop.0","zalo":"2026.11.6-first-hop.0"}
caught ConfigMutationConflictError: Config writes need a regular file, but /home/appuser/.openclaw/openclaw.json is a symlink. ...
    at captureConfigRootWriteTarget (dist/write-lock-*.mjs)
    at writeConfigFileFromContext (dist/io.write-*.mjs)
    at dist/io.factory-*.mjs
    at runConfigLockScope (dist/write-lock-*.mjs)
    at async withConfigWriteLock (dist/write-lock-*.mjs)
  retryable false, publishing true, cohort false, configChanged false, restoredChannels false
records-at-catch / records-after-rollback {"voice-call":"2026.11.6-first-hop.0","zalo":"2026.11.6-first-hop.0"}
```

</details>

**Published-driver Docker cell** (new lane `published-driver-plugin-publication`): a first update from published `openclaw@2026.11.5`, with `@openclaw/zalo` and `@openclaw/voice-call` installed, while `openclaw.json` is a link to a read-only file in a read-only directory.

| | base `3e0d3687c5d` | head `a8b99203816` |
|---|---|---|
| first `openclaw update --yes --json` | exit 1, `error` / `post-update-failed`, run `failed`, rollback `not-attempted: state-migrated-no-rollback` | exit 0, run `succeeded` |
| Gateway after the update | serving the new version, `/readyz` 200 | serving the new version, `/readyz` 200 |
| plugins (records, disk, `plugins list`) | both at the new version, loaded | both at the new version, loaded |
| `openclaw.json` | unchanged | unchanged bytes (asserted by the cell) |
| next plain `openclaw update` | exit 0, `already-current`; the failed record stays | exit 0, no failed record, nothing owed |

- The corrupt-plugin mode of the same cell (one plugin's target tarball truncated) is unchanged on head: run `succeeded`, a per-plugin warning for `voice-call`, and the next update converges it.
- Owner tests in `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-plugins.persistence.test.ts` run the real `updatePluginsAfterCoreUpdate` with real config and index stores:
  - symlinked config with no config change, without a cohort, with a cohort (then rolled back), and with a pending deferred plugin migration: publishes the records and leaves the file's bytes and link alone;
  - symlinked config with a real config change: still rejects with the same `is a symlink` error and publishes no records (negative control);
  - writable config with a real change, with and without a cohort: written as before, and a cohort rollback restores it;
  - a config edit after the decision: a valid edit is kept and the records publish; an edit that leaves the config invalid defers with `plugin-config-conflict` and restores the index;
  - update authority revoked before the index write: rejects, with no index write, no registry refresh and no config change;
  - config link re-pointed to another valid file during convergence, with the update's real prepared write options: rejects with "config target changed since last load" and keeps no records; the same link left alone publishes (red on the previous head, green now).
- Red on base: the no-change symlinked rows fail with the `is a symlink` rejection, and the writable no-change row fails because the file gets restamped. Mutation checks: removing the post-write freshness check, or the authority hook before the index write, each fails its test.

<details>
<summary>Commands and results</summary>

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-plugins.persistence.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-config-fence.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-recovery-guidance.test.ts test/scripts/docker-e2e-plan.test.ts`: 35, 15, 27 and 46 passed.
- Neighbor update and plugin suites on the final code: 20 files, 458 tests passed (`update-cli.plugin-convergence`, `update-command-{contention,convergence-authority,doctor-*,finalize-refusal,killed-run.process,lifecycle,plugin-caller,plugins.degradation,post-update}`, `update-command.test`, `update-config-provenance.integration`, `install-record-commit{,.retention}`, `update-cohort-recovery`).
- `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` (23 passed) and `test/scripts/update-restart-module-outcome.test.ts` (1 passed).
- `pnpm tsgo:all`: passed. `oxlint --type-aware` on the touched files: clean. `pnpm check:docs`: passed. `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base 3e0d3687c5d --no-merge-base`: all ratchets ok, including test-lines, max-lines and session-identity.
- Final harness cells on head `91dbd6bfb77`, same candidate, under the Docker lock: the green `symlinked-config` cell passed in 459 s (plugins stamped with the core target `2026.11.6-first-hop.0`, the config still the same link with unchanged managed bytes, the next update clean), and the `refused-channel-change` cell passed in 329 s.
- Harness cell on head `e612b2363e0`, same candidate (packed at `90ac53240b9`): `OPENCLAW_PUBLISHED_DRIVER_PLUGIN_PUBLICATION=1 OPENCLAW_PUBLISHED_DRIVER_PLUGIN_FAULT=refused-channel-change bash scripts/e2e/published-driver-update-docker.sh <candidate.tgz> <artifacts>` with no driver argument. It defaulted to `driver=2026.11.5` and passed in 330 s. The channel write was refused with the symlink error. Both plugins stayed at 2026.11.5 in records, on disk and in the local inventory. `update status` names the run `failed` with nothing owed, and the Gateway serves the new core with `/readyz` 200.

The wrapper envelope is 1125 s.

</details>

### Changes to existing tests

- `test/scripts/update-first-hop-package-fixtures.test.ts`: one new case for the plugin fixture packer's target version; existing cases unchanged.
- `test/scripts/docker-e2e-plan.test.ts`: the new lane's plan test no longer runs the package script against a fake wrapper that only echoed its arguments; that could not detect dispatch to the wrong entry, and the real Docker cell proves dispatch. The planner assertion, including the lane command, stays.
- `src/cli/update-cli.finalizer.test.ts`: "refreshes post-Doctor state with requested channel undefined" checks that plugin publication writes against the post-Doctor config (`baseHash` `post-doctor`). Its sync result changed no config, so it now took the records-only branch, wrote nothing, and failed in CI. It now syncs a real config change and still proves the write uses post-Doctor state. Before the next push, all 25 top-level `src/cli/update-cli.*.test.ts` files were run locally: 342 tests passed.
- `update-command-config-fence.test.ts`: the `plugins` flow fences an executor revocation inside the plugin config write. Its convergence result changed no config, so it now took the records-only branch and never reached that write. It now returns a real config change, so it still proves the config-write fence. The records-only fence has its own new test.
- `update-command-plugins.persistence.test.ts`: "rolls back the tentative index after a config failure" and "preserves reference activation only with explicit intent" each changed no config, so they would have passed without writing anything. Each now carries a real config change and still proves its original behavior. The cases that pin "a refused config write fails" and "no cohort keeps failing" are untouched.

### Nearby fix

`openclaw gateway stop` refuses a non-interactive shell without `--force` (`runDaemonStop`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle.ts`). The red recording shows the old instruction as the shipped CLI prints it. The negative-control recording shows the new instruction printed by the shipped CLI on the head, after a refused channel write. The update report for a healthy Gateway with unfinished maintenance now names `openclaw gateway stop --force` for the managed service, matching repair's own next action. Its test is red on base. The same plain `gateway stop` wording remains in `status.ts`, `update-command-service-plan.ts`, `update-maintenance-error.ts`, `update-command-service-publication.ts`, `update-recovery-guidance.ts` (cleanup guidance) and `update-repair-command.ts`. That is a follow-up.

### Review

A fresh, independent read-only review (separate agent, given the diff and the behavior contract) found no blockers.
- Fixed with failing-first tests:
  - the records-only read missed the update's pending deferred plugin migration facts;
  - two existing tests had become vacuous;
  - there was no records-only fence test;
  - there was no real cohort rollback after a records-only publication.
- Also fixed: docs scope and wording, and the plan test's command assertion.
- Not taken: rejecting other wrapper flags combined with the new mode. The wrapper already ignores unrelated mode flags.

`autoreview` does not run on this machine, so it was not run.

### ClawSweeper rating

The local ClawSweeper review (GPT 6.2 Sol) runs offline against this branch.

- **Round 1** (head `2423fb365fc`): overall D, proof D, patch C. Three P2 findings, all verified as real and fixed:
  - Records-only publication skipped the config path proof. It now runs the same `assertConfigPathForWrite` check the write path uses, with a failing-first test.

  - The low-value fake-wrapper plan assertion was removed.
  - The proof gap for the `gateway stop --force` wording is stated under "Nearby fix".
- **Round 2** (head `90ac53240b9`): overall D, proof D, patch C. Three P2 findings in the new lane, all verified as real and fixed:

  - Readiness could be read from a stale probe file. The cell now deletes the file first and accepts it only after a successful probe in the same run.
  - The baseline `npm pack` and fixture packing had no timeout. Both are now bounded by the cell deadline.
  - Proof notes: the green capture predated the final checks, and the new stop instruction had no shipped-CLI capture. All three recordings were redone on the committed harness, and the negative-control mode now captures the new instruction from the shipped CLI.
- **Round 3** (head `2840dc974fc`): overall C, proof B (sufficient real-behavior proof), patch C. One P2 and two P3 findings in the lane, all verified as real and fixed in `d1da62a9520` after the round limit, so they have not been re-rated:
  - The negative control now also requires the `openclaw.json is a symlink` refusal in post-update verification, so an unrelated failure cannot pass it. On the captured runs this assertion matches the negative control and rejects the green capture.
  - A direct wrapper call in this mode now defaults to its own artifact directory.
  - The plugin observation is named after the local inventory it reads.
  - The patch tier was held at C by the lane findings above. The production change drew no findings in this round.
- **Round 4** (head `d1da62a9520`, landing review): overall C, proof B, patch C. One P2 and two P3 findings, again only in the lane and the proof wording. All were verified, and the two lane findings were real:
  - A direct wrapper call in plugin publication mode with no driver argument used the dist-tag `latest` as the fixture package version. The wrapper now defaults this mode to `2026.11.5`, and the cell rejects anything that is not a concrete release version. Red: `node .../published-driver-plugin-publication.mjs <tgz> <dir> latest` got past argument checks on `d1da62a9520`. Green: it now fails at once with "Expected a concrete driver release version".
  - The refused-channel control did not check that the plugins stayed at the driver release, or that the failed run was recorded. It now asserts both plugins' records, disk packages and local inventory at the driver version, and that `update status` names this run as `failed` with nothing owed. The earlier recorded negative-control capture already satisfied these facts.
  - Proof wording: `plugins list` reads the local plugin inventory, not the running Gateway. The body now says so wherever it reports plugins as loaded.
  - Fixed in `e612b2363e0` (harness only) and rerun as a Docker cell (see Commands and results).
- **Round 5** (head `e612b2363e0`): overall C, proof B, patch C. Two new lane findings, both verified as real and fixed in `91dbd6bfb77`; the production change again drew none:
  - P2: the cell stamps the future plugin tarballs from the driver plugin version (2026.11.5 + 1) but advertises and asserts the core target (candidate version + 1). These match today only because the candidate is also 2026.11.5; the lane will break once `main` moves past the driver release. Fix: the shared `packFuturePluginFixture` takes an optional target version, and the lane stamps each plugin with the core target, then asserts the packed version equals what the registry advertises. Its new test in `test/scripts/update-first-hop-package-fixtures.test.ts` was red before the change (a 2026.11.5 plugin packed for a `2026.11.7-first-hop.0` core came out as `2026.11.6-first-hop.0`) and is green now; without a target the packer behaves as before for its other callers.
  - P3: the green cell compares `openclaw.json` bytes through the link but does not assert the entry is still a symlink to the managed file (the owner unit tests do). Fix: the green cell and the negative control both assert with `lstat`/`readlink` that `openclaw.json` is still the link to the managed file, and compare the managed file's own bytes.
  - A further reviewer-style read of the lane found no other check that relies on two values happening to match, reads through the link instead of on it, or would pass if its step never ran.
- **Round 6** (head `91dbd6bfb77`): overall B, proof B, patch B, "patch is correct". One P3 lane finding, left open:

The cell still fails in that case; it only loses some diagnostics. This is a lane diagnostics follow-up, not a correctness gap in the production change.
- An earlier attempt at round 1 aborted on a dirty checkout before reviewing and produced no rating. A round 2 run started with a stale base was stopped before it finished and rerun with the branch's merge base.

Run 44408383488, tested merge `8caa21cf8ff` (`91dbd6bfb77` into `main` at `c5ef395ba72`). `git diff --name-only c5ef395ba72 8caa21cf8ff` lists exactly this PR's files. Every other job passed or was skipped.

prs.title: fix: let Doctor inspect Codex sign-in on PostgreSQL
prs.body:
Closes #201059

## What Problem This Solves

After porting shared state and agent databases to PostgreSQL, Doctor can warn that it cannot inspect working OpenAI OAuth profiles and suggest a general state repair.

## User Impact

Doctor can inspect stored Codex sign-in profiles on PostgreSQL. Missing profiles still get sign-in instructions, and inspection errors only get a repair hint when the underlying error recommends repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inspection was entering the agent database writer's setup, which tries to take a SQLite file snapshot. It now uses the existing PostgreSQL read-only worker path.

## Evidence

- On upstream main (`dda8da4b566`), focused Doctor lint reported a SQLite snapshot refusal and full lint reported a shared-state ownership conflict for both migrated agents. Both commands reported zero Codex findings with the patch.
- The new PostgreSQL CLI regression failed on main with the snapshot refusal and passed with the fix. PostgreSQL catalog verification, adjacent auth tests, core and extension type checks, lint, and formatting passed.
- Local author review traced the read and error paths through the final diff. No independent autoreview was run.

<details>
<summary>Doctor terminal output on the same two migrated agents</summary>

JSON is filtered to the Codex check. The full command also checks unrelated host configuration.

```console
# upstream base dda8da4b566
$ pnpm openclaw doctor --lint --json --only codex/native-profile-recovery
{
  "checksRun": 1,
  "findings": [
    {
      "checkId": "codex/native-profile-recovery",
      "severity": "warning",
      "message": "Could not inspect OpenAI auth profiles for agent \"main\": PostgreSQL cannot use SQLite file-snapshot; stop the Gateway and back up/restore the PostgreSQL schema with its matching anchor (P3-6 export support pending).",
      "fixHint": "openclaw doctor --fix"
    },
    {
      "checkId": "codex/native-profile-recovery",
      "severity": "warning",
      "message": "Could not inspect OpenAI auth profiles for agent \"worker\": PostgreSQL cannot use SQLite file-snapshot; stop the Gateway and back up/restore the PostgreSQL schema with its matching anchor (P3-6 export support pending).",
      "fixHint": "openclaw doctor --fix"
    }
  ]
}

# upstream base dda8da4b566
$ pnpm openclaw doctor --lint --json
{
  "checksRun": 47,
  "findings": [
    {
      "checkId": "codex/native-profile-recovery",
      "severity": "warning",
      "message": "Could not inspect OpenAI auth profiles for agent \"main\": Agent database execution belongs to another shared-state database; drain its existing resources before changing the state directory.",
      "fixHint": "openclaw doctor --fix"
    },
    {
      "checkId": "codex/native-profile-recovery",
      "severity": "warning",
      "message": "Could not inspect OpenAI auth profiles for agent \"worker\": Agent database execution belongs to another shared-state database; drain its existing resources before changing the state directory.",
      "fixHint": "openclaw doctor --fix"
    }
  ]
}

# PR head 2fbae92ebd6
$ node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json --only codex/native-profile-recovery
{
  "checksRun": 1,
  "findings": []
}

# PR head 2fbae92ebd6
$ node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json
{
  "checksRun": 47,
  "findings": []
}

```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Published stable to pull request head with PostgreSQL state</summary>

The direct PostgreSQL upgrade was refused at schema admission. Store IDs and the synthetic profile fingerprint matched before and after the refusal. I then used the published stable CLI to port the fixture back to SQLite, ran Doctor from the head build on the same state directory, and ported it back to PostgreSQL. The hashes below cover the agent roster and normalized synthetic OAuth record. JSON is filtered to the fields shown.

```console

$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15)
$ openclaw database port --to postgres --json
{"phase":"complete","engine":"postgres","portedStores":3}
$ openclaw models status --agent main --json
{"provider":"openai","oauthProfiles":1}

Upgraded agent database schema in [scratch]/agents/worker/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: v38 -> v43.
Doctor complete.
[exit 0]
```

prs.title: fix(discord): keep independent requests from replacing active tasks
prs.body:
Thanks @vincentkoc for reporting and authorizing this fix.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/5a086588-5bfa-48dc-ac67-1ea6127c26f9)
- [Live Discord verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/9c73f4b2-42d5-4f15-818d-59f1b9fe718d)

## What Problem This Solves

When someone asks OpenClaw a question in a Discord guild channel while it is handling another participant’s request, the new message can be consumed as guidance for the existing run. The model can then answer only the newer question and leave the original request unfinished.

## User Impact

Ordinary messages from different Discord guild participants now wait for separate turns rather than joining the active task. Same-requester guidance and explicit commands keep their existing behavior. This intentionally does not identify unrelated topics from the same requester; use `/followup` for those.

There are no config or data migrations. Already-consumed historical requests are not replayed. Another participant’s ordinary correction will wait for its own turn rather than steer immediately; explicit command behavior remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route ordinary cross-requester Discord guild messages into the existing FIFO followup queue before native steering can consume them. Apply the rule both when collaboration is omitted (the default) and when it is enabled; preserve explicitly disabled collaboration policy, other transports, queue cancellation/deduplication, and the no-replay rule for accepted or uncertain native handoffs.

This reuses the existing queue and requester comparison instead of introducing topic classification or another task ledger. Tool permissions and caller authority are unchanged.

## Evidence

The owning-boundary regression fails on the base with unwanted native injections. With the fix, the original request keeps its execution, the remaining requests drain once in FIFO order, duplicate delivery is ignored, and selective cancellation is respected.

Agent-driven live QA also completed a held Gateway-owner request and an actual Discord driver-bot request on separate real-model runs, exactly once each, original first, with no second reply before release. The isolated fixture was cleaned up; the running service was not changed. This is not a two-human Discord test or a live baseline comparison; the deterministic regression establishes the changed admission path.

- Final owner tests: 12 passed; existing receipt/recovery/queue tests: 44 passed.
- Active-steering consumer: 32 passed (169 unrelated cases excluded); command refusal: 13 passed; prompt-prefix stability: 16 passed.
- Core production/core-test typechecks and final targeted messaging typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Independent final-commit review found no actionable P0–P2 defects after correcting a default-setting finding.
- Full `pnpm check:changed` remains red on untouched compaction/replay and UI unused-export findings; no export is added or removed here. Its initial test-lint findings were fixed and the targeted rerun passed.
- A broader runner invocation timed out after the command/prefix suites completed; the relevant active-steering group was rerun successfully. No full runner-file pass or human manual verification is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Source and live-proof identity</summary>

Base: `0eabe3398c9e0334e8c3b9b03f6a12040c7a1c12`. Reviewed commit: `a5380590bc2dcf8f5088ac32a19fb50fcc28aa8e`.

Live-tested production diff SHA-256: `93984c9b3def56ff3d7ef360e05eee2101fc30c32a85548339d549c8349a0e6c`.

</details>

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc

prs.title: fix: keep unused Code Mode lookups from tainting memory
prs.body:
Closes #196857

## What Problem This Solves

Unused Code Mode tool lookups could mark an entire turn as external content and quarantine session-memory snapshots. At the same time, the host memory-write observer missed Code Mode’s per-result provenance and could leave genuinely consumed external metadata trusted.

## User Impact

Unused discovery no longer makes later owner-requested memory writes untrusted. Consumed or emitted external metadata, MCP declarations, and network tool results retain their existing provenance protections. Previously quarantined files are not reclassified; there is no migration or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Code Mode returns lazy callable handles, so its guest already records when external metadata is read or serialized. Stop eagerly marking unused search hits, and forward the existing per-result provenance to the host’s memory-taint observer instead of looking only at static tool metadata. Ordinary Tool Search, execution, stored-value provenance, and memory classification policy are otherwise unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced unused-search turn taint on base c5ef395ba7204c83240074b584e97f550a3aab7d. Isolated real-model Gateway testing also exposed the host observer’s missing dynamic provenance; the production-wrapper memory regression fails on consumed descriptions, emitted handles, and declarations until that observer is fixed.
- The same memory regression passes with the fix; reading a description (even when discarded), returning a handle, and reading a declaration still produce untrusted memory.
- Focused suites: 78 tests passed across Agent-loop, Code Mode output, Tool Search metadata, and network-error provenance suites. Changed test file: 26 tests, 16.51 seconds wall time (CI timing pending).
- Core and affected test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, changed-page MDX, and `git diff --check` passed. Full `pnpm build` passed (2m 58s), followed by a final `pnpm build:runtime` (1m 8s); it reported non-fatal Control UI asset-budget warnings in unchanged UI code.
- An isolated Gateway with a real agent, provider model, and loopback MCP server verified both paths with zero MCP tool executions: unused discovery produced `agent` memory; consuming the external description produced fenced output and `untrusted` memory. The Gateway, sockets, and temporary state were cleaned up. Live test: 36.65 seconds wall time.
- Local autoreview (P0–P2) of the final pre-commit snapshot against c5ef395ba7204c83240074b584e97f550a3aab7d: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The committed patch at 5be12feb75a3ad2fc65c415e187fc8104eaa6606 is byte-identical to that reviewed snapshot. The reviewer inspected the supplied source context but did not rerun tests.

Simplification: remove the duplicate eager observation and reuse the existing internal result-source fact. No new state, owner, public option, trust exception, or provenance mechanism. Production delta: +8/-3 lines; tests: +91/-2; docs: +7. The small production growth forwards the existing source fact into the memory observer.

## Contributor credit

Reported by @Ricardodpalmeida. Fix requested and directed by @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/f302039d-42df-481f-8864-d448f956f8bd)

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc

prs.title: fix(talk): bind steering to exact run authority
prs.body:
Closes #126733

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where browser or relay Talk steering and cancellation could fail with `tool_authority_mismatch` even when the Talk connection owned the active run.

The original Talk path checked connection and session ownership, then discarded that proof and called mutable session-key control. It therefore could not supply the embedded runner's current-run injection authority. A delayed control callback could also select a replacement run, and one stale relay registration could mask a later live run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded runner now owns one opaque exact-run control target. Resolution requires the session registry and run-id registry to identify the same handle. Queue and abort operations synchronously revalidate that captured handle immediately before their effect. Closure, replacement, missing authority, and another owner all fail closed; raw fingerprints and run IDs remain correlation rather than authority.

Browser direct control, browser Gateway-control, and realtime relay control use this exact target. The asynchronous Talk control queue captures the target at admission and carries it unchanged through readiness waits. Relay capture scans past stale registrations to the first live target. There are no mutable session-key fallbacks from these owner-bound paths.

## User Impact

Browser and relay Talk can steer or cancel the run they own. A delayed callback cannot steer or abort a replacement run, while a stale relay registration no longer prevents control of a later live run.

No config, schema, protocol, migration, or public plugin SDK changes.

## Evidence

Pre-fix production scenario:

- The original maturity run reached `tool_authority_mismatch` after the browser owner had identified the active run.
- Earlier isolated runs stopped first at #126730. Current `main` now includes #133019, which independently repairs that preceding browser ownership handoff, so the same real-Gateway scenario reaches this PR's authority boundary.

Exact-head real production-boundary proof:

- `pnpm openclaw qa run --qa-profile all --scenario active-talk-agent-run-status --provider-mode mock-openai --output-dir .artifacts/qa-126733-exact-head`
- Result: 1 passed, 0 failed on `a05aa490a59`.
- A persistent owning WebChat connection completed status, steer, follow-up, and cancel RPCs against one real active agent run.
- A separately authenticated Gateway connection was rejected before it could abort the browser-owned run.
- The owner remained active after that rejection, both injections were observed with queue depths `1,1`, and the cancelled run finished `idle` with queue depth `0`.

Startup-order proof:

- A control admitted after consult admission but before embedded-run registration waits on that specific consult and receives its exact opaque target only after both active-run indexes register the admitted handle; it never re-resolves a later current run.
- The regression fails on the prior branch because control executes immediately with an absent target, and passes after the exact admitted context carries registration readiness from the runner owner boundary.

Replacement and sibling proof:

- Replacing a captured run makes the retained target reject queue and cancellation; neither the old nor replacement abort callback executes.
- Browser Gateway-control captures authority synchronously before queued execution; changing the current target before the queue runs does not change the admitted target.
- Relay control skips a stale first registration, captures the later live exact target, and cancels only that handle.

Verification:

- Focused Talk/runner suite: 218 passed on the exact head.
- `pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test` — passed.
- Diff-scoped deslop — clean after removing a diagnostic-only wrapper.
- Test audit — the added real-Gateway case protects cross-connection rejection at the final effect and introduces no production-only test seam.
- Exact-head P1 autoreview against current `origin/main` — scoped clean; patch correct (0.91 confidence).
- The all-lane changed check reached only unrelated current-main Telegram/grammY type drift (`RichMessageButton`, `stopped_message_generation`, and body variants); focused core and Talk checks are green.

Exact-head LOC: production +306/-61 (net +245); tests/test support +321/-11 (net +310); scenario metadata +2/-1. Production growth establishes and carries the opaque authority boundary across three ingress paths and the shared asynchronous control queue; the previous mutable fallback paths are removed.
