prs.title: fix: automation failure alerts blame every failure in a streak on the last run's cause
prs.body:
Closes #201183

This covers the cron alert defect, which the ClawSweeper review on the issue names as the remaining one.

## What Problem This Solves

When an automation fails several times in a row, the failure alert says "failed 4 times in a row" followed by "Cause: timeout". The count covers the whole streak, but the cause is only the last run's. If the first three runs failed on provider auth and the fourth timed out, the alert reads as four timeouts. The reporter's agent read it that way and rewrote a job that was fine.

## User Impact

User impact: a streak alert now says "Latest cause: timeout", so the cause is tied to the last run and not to every failure in the count. The notice sent when an automation is auto-disabled after repeated failures is worded the same way. A single failure still says "Cause:".

## Why This Change Was Made

The service records one cause, for the latest run, next to a count that spans the streak. Labeling the cause as the latest keeps the alert short and needs no stored history of causes or new setting. It applies to chat and webhook alerts.

## Evidence

- A streak of five failures with mixed causes, ending in a timeout, now alerts with `Automation "daily report" failed 5 times in a row` and `Latest cause: timeout`. A webhook streak gets the same label, and the auto-disable notice after 10 failures says `Latest cause: ...`.
- These tests fail on main with `Cause: timeout` and pass with the change.
- Ran locally: `src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts`, `src/cron/service/timer.batch-finalization.test.ts`, `src/cron/failure-notification-text.test.ts`, `src/cron/service/timer.timeout-watchdog.test.ts`, `src/cron/service/timer-outcomes.regression.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts`, plus oxfmt and oxlint on the changed files.
- Live Gateway run: isolated Gateway built from this head (`openclaw --version` shows 9889859), a command automation "daily report" with a failure alert webhook to a local receiver, threshold 4. Three runs exited with code 3, the fourth timed out. The receiver got one POST:

```
Automation "daily report" failed 4 times in a row
Latest cause: timeout
Last error: command timed out
```

- Not run locally: `src/cron/cron-delivery-outcomes.e2e.test.ts` (its runtime build does not complete on my machine), typecheck, and the wider suites. Those are left to CI. The Gateway run above delivered over a webhook, not a live chat channel.

prs.title: fix: let updates proceed while a busy agent database keeps writing
prs.body:
Related: #200791

## What Problem This Solves

Updating while the Gateway is busy writing to a large agent database could be refused before anything changed: "SQLite source did not stabilize (reason=wal-copy-unstable, attempts=10)". Retrying a few minutes later, after the agent turn finished, was the only way through.

## User Impact

Update admission and other read-only database inspections no longer give up on a large WAL database that an active writer keeps checkpointing. They take one consistent SQLite read snapshot instead. Idle, crashed, and index-less databases keep the existing byte-for-byte private copy, so nothing changes for them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Artifact-preserving inspection copies the database bytes and compares them until they hold still. Appends to the WAL are already tolerated, but a checkpoint during the main-file copy (or the WAL restart after it) invalidates the attempt. With a multi-GB agent database, one copy takes longer than the writer's checkpoint interval, so all ten attempts lose and backoff cannot help.

When every attempt lost to committed writes (`wal-copy-unstable`, `main-changed-during-copy`, `wal-changed-during-copy`) on a complete WAL family (main file, WAL, and index present, no rollback journal), the copy owner now takes one read transaction through the existing online-backup path. Only a live connection can keep checkpointing, so its WAL index is current: the read cannot recover the index or change the 96-byte commit header that update captures compare, only reader slots after it (the same contract #175774 accepted for verified live owners). Source identity is pinned across the backup. Rollback-journal families still refuse, because a native reader would block their writer.

Accepted edge case: if the writer closes in the instant between the last failed copy and the native open, the read-only open sees a closed family. This is visible as a normal refusal or a later capture warning, not data loss.

Rejected alternatives: longer retry backoff (each attempt outlasts the checkpoint interval, so waiting between attempts does not create a quiet window); requiring a recorded owner (agent databases have no owner record, only the shared state database does).

Production LOC: +44/-4 in `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.ts`. Tests +43/-4, docs +12/-2.

## Evidence

- Regression test `takes one read transaction when a live WAL writer outlasts every raw copy` fails on base with the exact reported error and passes with the fix. `keeps a WAL family without its index byte-neutral when every raw copy changes` passes on both and pins that the source is unchanged and no `-shm` is created.
- Local probe on a 600 MB WAL database with a checkpointing writer: raw copy failed 10/10 (`wal-copy-unstable`, 24 s); online backup succeeded in 3.4 s. With checkpoints disabled the raw copy succeeds, which confirms checkpoints, not appends, are the cause.
- `sqlite-readonly-location*`, `openclaw-database-preflight`, and `update-command-admit` suites pass (215 tests). `pnpm tsgo:core` is clean. Autoreview (P2) is scoped-clean.
- Live update on Crabbox AWS Linux with a running Gateway, a 1.8 GB agent database, and an external writer committing to it throughout:
  - Base, main `7eb33ccb25f`, update 2026.11.30 → 2026.11.31: the update was refused at candidate admission with `SQLite source did not stabilize (reason=wal-copy-unstable, attempts=10)` (exit 1).
  - With this fix, update 2026.11.30 → fix build: candidate admission passed and the update completed (`updated to 2026.11.32`, exit 0). I confirmed the installed dist contains the change.

## What Problem This Solves

A channel plugin could forward an internal-only option that made a required-result turn silently accept `NO_REPLY`. The public SDK boundary copied that option into core reply handling instead of leaving silence permission with the host.

## User Impact

Required replies keep their host-selected completion policy when called through the plugin SDK. Trusted host notifications can still explicitly allow silence, and normal visible replies remain unchanged. No configuration change or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Exclude `replyExpectation` in the existing shared public-reply sanitizer, both in public parameter types and at runtime. This adapts the boundary repair from [68bf43c87e27](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/68bf43c87e271aab1c71b90a81b756e9dd20f8e4) to main's current owner without changing trusted host dispatch or treating provenance as permission.

The existing sanitizer remains the single public boundary: no new wrapper, state, or policy owner. Production delta is +3/-1 lines; regression tests add 123 lines plus one broker-runtime routing entry.

## Evidence

- **Red before the fix:** the public dispatch regression received `replyExpectation: "optional"`; the public generation/CLI-flow regression selected `optional` where `result-required` was expected.
- **Green with the fix:** 33 tests across five focused suites. Real session-event admission, reply preparation, and CLI terminal handling preserve permitted silence, reject required silence, retain visible replies, and strip the forged SDK option. External CLI output is deterministic fixture I/O, not a live provider.
- Focused compiler check for the changed TypeScript files and their imports, scoped Oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Type-aware lint emitted SDK boundary declarations successfully.
- Full `pnpm build` passes at committed source `2d112a0efc5a7929bcf7450758478830dda8fc6c` (172.15 seconds wall), including declaration generation and SDK export validation. The unchanged UI build emits CSS-size and boot-request budget warnings; no UI files changed and those warnings were not attributed in this task.
- Independent local **autoreview**, GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Reviewed base `de5f46d8f63b5c375c5e30e1882b0a4df327d868` through the complete staged snapshot committed as `2d112a0efc5a7929bcf7450758478830dda8fc6c`. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; this is the documented fallback route, not a ClawSweeper result. Exact-head CI and hosted review remain before landing.

No live channel/provider run was performed. The proof covers the real core admission/reply/CLI owners with controlled external output, not authenticated provider behavior.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands and test cost</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime.contract.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-reply-expectation.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/source-reply-expectation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

prs.title: fix: report failed Dreaming workspaces in automation health
prs.body:
Refs https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/143206

## What Problem This Solves

The managed Memory Dreaming Promotion automation can finish with one or every workspace failed while recording a successful run, resetting its error streak, and requesting no failure notification. Operators then need a separate journal watcher to discover failed sweeps.

## User Impact

Synchronous workspace failures and synchronous narrative degradation now make the managed run fail and count toward the existing failure-notification policy. Healthy workspaces still finish their promotions and reports, and pending detached narratives alone remain healthy. Partial failures are logged at warn.

The failed-workspace count and first error remain in the job record and failure webhooks. Chat alerts retain their existing normalized-cause contract and do not expose arbitrary error text. There are no new configuration options or public hook/SDK fields.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sweep returns its known failure through the existing handled `before_agent_reply` reply with `isError: true`; both runner paths preserve that payload and cron already owns error persistence, failure streaks, and notifications. The sweep retains the first workspace/phase error and synchronous narrative error until it has processed the remaining workspaces.

A small cron classification correction consumes the existing `providerStarted: false` fact: a synthetic failure cannot be inferred from its text to be a provider auth failure or a provider-transient retry signal. Existing terminal classifications and restart precedence remain intact.

**Covered:** failures already known when the sweep returns, including whole-workspace exceptions and synchronous degraded narrative outcomes. **Still open for the product decision in #143206:** eventual detached narrative settlement, whether to wait for publication or report later, and retry design. This change adds no retries and does not change narrative detachment or the promotion apply path.

## Evidence

- Before the repair on main `dda8da4b5666f0b7411b528309c16bf150ccef65`, scheduled partial failure, total failure, and synchronous degradation all persisted as `ok` with `consecutiveErrors: 0`. The healthy pending control passed. Those failure cases now persist as `error`, increment the streak, and request the configured alert. The webhook case preserves the failed-workspace count and first error.
- The scheduled regression composes the real registered Dreaming hook, CLI synthetic-reply adapter, isolated cron finalization, CronService persistence, and alert dispatch. Workspace phase failures and synchronous narrative results are controlled fixtures; external notification transport is mocked. This is not live Gateway proof.
- Existing real-file narrative tests verify healthy promotion/report/diary output despite another workspace failing, phase/report error propagation, and unchanged detached publication with `narrativesPending=1`.
- The `providerStarted: false` regression failed before the classification correction and passed afterward; true and omitted values preserve existing classification behavior.
- **378 tests passed across 21 files** using `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks`: all 14 memory-core `dreaming*.test.ts` files; cron timer-outcome, failure-alert outcome, silent-failure alert, meta-error and watchdog-cause tests; CLI before-reply tests; and embedded shared integration tests. Four selected runner shards completed in 286 seconds locally. The final scheduled regression rerun passed all four cases after making later workspace errors distinct, proving the first error is retained. Its final standalone wall time was 50 seconds including compiler preparation, with about 5.4 seconds of test execution. CI timing is not yet available.
- Passed `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, and the cron test typecheck (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --incremental`). prs.title: fix: explain how to call deferred tools after a direct call
prs.body:
Closes #186716

## What Problem This Solves

A model that calls a deferred tool directly in structured Tool Search mode gets only “Tool <name> not found,” even though the tool is available through discovery. That gives it no actionable way to recover in the same turn.

## User Impact

The embedded harness now tells the model to call `dispatch_action` with the tool name in `id` and its parameters in `args`. The rejected direct call does not execute or expose the tool. Unknown, filtered, ambiguous, and exact-ID-only names keep their existing behavior. No configuration, defaults, permissions, executor, or native-harness behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing deferred-tool resolver was installed only for Code Mode and directory mode. It now also handles recovery when the structured dispatcher is actually registered, using the same current catalog lookup and returning guidance before tool adaptation.

The resolver moves intact into one named execution-boundary module so the capped preparation source and test suite do not grow past their limits. Code Mode guidance and directory hydration retain their existing owner and hooks; there is no second execution path or new state. Simplification pass: production +39 net lines (mostly the extracted boundary’s typed input), regression +85 lines, documentation +3 lines.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the production-wired agent-loop regression received `Tool probe_write not found` instead of dispatcher guidance. The final focused regression verifies the guidance, no direct execution or provider exposure, unchanged filtered/unknown rejection, and exactly one real file write through `dispatch_action`.
- Final resolver and preparation suites: 27 tests passed. The new suite took 11.60 seconds including imports/transforms; the two-shard command took 51.79 seconds including cold worker preparation.
- Tool Search selection and prompt-prefix stability suites: 37 tests passed.
- Full `pnpm build` passed again at published head `db16310f5ddf9086622cca30a0a63e5e56357c30` (1m 47.9s; clean build inputs). Core production and agents-other test typecheck leaves passed.
- Targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent autoreview of the complete local candidate against `c5ef395ba7204c83240074b584e97f550a3aab7d`, with the catalog, agent loop, and client-tool assembly supplied as context: GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2, scoped-clean; no actionable findings. The reviewer did not run tests. Hosted ClawSweeper also reported no actionable patch findings at the published head.
- The [exact-head CI gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44411080008/job/135186193541).

### Real isolated Gateway recovery proof

Passed at the published head through the repository's compiled Gateway test lane, using `createOpenClawTestInstance`, its standard authenticated synthetic test client, and a local scripted model provider. This exercises the actual Gateway and embedded agent; it is not a live third-party-model test.

The provider first emitted a direct `sessions_list` call. It received the recovery error, followed that guidance with `dispatch_action`, and received the real session-list result. The target remained absent from all three provider tool declarations, and the turn completed without rerouting:

```text
head: db16310f5ddf9086622cca30a0a63e5e56357c30
provider requests: 3
sessions_list declared directly: [false, false, false]
dispatch_action declared: [true, true, true]
direct result: Tool sessions_list is deferred and not directly callable. Call dispatch_action with id "sessions_list" and its parameters in args.
dispatch result: count=1
terminal status: ok
terminal reply: PROOF_DONE
rerouted: false
```

The Gateway proof took 7.064 seconds; its test lane completed in 14.56 seconds including preparation. Earlier source-only startup and operator-CLI attempts hit worker-ownership and attribution guards. The standard compiled synthetic test fixture supplied the successful proof without disabling either safeguard. The previous end-to-end verification gap is resolved; no source push or CI rerun was needed.

Thanks to @xyrolle for the report and proposed recovery approach in #186718, and @vincentkoc for requesting the repair.

prs.title: fix(ui): continue a lone sidebar session list as it scrolls
prs.body:
Related: #200217, #186714, #197587

## What Problem This Solves

A sidebar session list that stands alone (Group by none, or Other with no other groups) stops at its first page behind Show more. With hundreds of sessions, browsing older ones means clicking Show more again and again.

## User Impact

- **One list on its own:** it still opens at its first page (30 sessions when grouped by none, 15 for a lone Other). Scrolling to its end shows the next 15 loaded sessions, and each later visit to the end shows 15 more. Show more stays for keyboard users and for a list too short to scroll.
- **Several groups:** unchanged. Each group pages with Show more, so a large group never buries the ones below it. This includes #200217's case of Other next to a named group.
- A list whose end is already on screen, or comes into view as the mobile drawer opens, keeps its first page until you scroll or press Show more.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar projection decides which sections render, including when an empty Other heading still shows (more pages to load, owner filters, a non-Active status, or a drag). The renderer draws every section it returns, so the projection knows when one section is the whole list and marks it to continue on scroll. Show more and Collapse load lazily, the first time a section has rows to reveal or hide, which keeps the chat boot JS inside its budget. The new code is in that lazy module: it watches the section's end and shows one more page each time the end scrolls into view in a scrolled list.

This covers loaded sessions only. Fetching older pages from the Gateway, and where that control sits, is #197587's part; the two changes meet only at the list's end.

## Evidence

Group by none, 100 sessions, after scrolling to the end of the list twice:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the list stops at Conversation 30 with Show more](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/cad2e20862be439f5f5755439937cdc8e656430a/images/2026/11/1a2df424-1b27-4cdd-a775-6fdb6450154a.png) | ![After: the list continues past Conversation 30](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/cad2e20862be439f5f5755439937cdc8e656430a/images/2026/11/b3af6ea3-531a-444c-9a0e-d570a87d96c9.png) |

Before is main.

- Regression tests:
  - `sidebar-flat-list` E2E: the flat list opens at 30 and shows 45, then 60, as its end scrolls into view. It fails with the scroll handling removed (stays at 30).
  - Projection test: only a lone section continues on scroll, and a shown empty Other heading counts as a second section.
- E2Es that page a lone list with Show more press it without Playwright's scroll into view, since that scroll would reach the list's end and show a page by itself.
- Passed locally in headless Chromium: 8 sidebar unit/browser files (`app-sidebar*` projection, visibility, freshness, memo, feedback, stress, sessions, people), 18 sidebar, session-management and chat E2E files, UI typecheck and UI test typecheck, lint, and formatting.

Browser proof uses synthetic sessions and a mocked Gateway. The full local suite and a live Gateway run were not run.

prs.title: fix: clean up disposable sessions while automatic archiving waits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

While automatic archiving waits for automations to load, session cleanup can leave disposable subagent sessions behind. Older ordinary chats fill the bounded capacity shortlist even though they cannot be archived yet, hiding newer disposable sessions that are eligible for cleanup.

## User Impact

Disposable sessions can still be cleaned up under capacity pressure while ordinary conversations remain protected during automation loading. Enabled automation bindings and existing active-session, ancestry, root, pin, and retention protections are unchanged. No configuration changes or migration are required; protected conversations may still keep the store above its cap by design.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the existing archiving-deferral predicate when selecting SQLite capacity candidates, before the shortlist is bounded—not only when applying the selected candidates. This restores the same eligibility policy used by the full-store planner without adding a second classifier, scan, or retention rule.

The simplify pass retained three production lines and one 28-line regression; no new helper or state was needed.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the real lifecycle cleanup entry point with native SQLite and a registered pending preservation provider. Two older ordinary chats and one newer disposable subagent reproduce the capacity-selection failure with age and dashboard cleanup disabled.
- On base `de5f46d8f63b5c375c5e30e1882b0a4df327d868`, the regression fails with `capped: 0, afterCount: 3`. With the fix it removes the subagent, reports `capped: 1, afterCount: 2, archived: 0`, and retains both ordinary chats unarchived.
- 88 focused tests passed across the maintenance writer, bounded cap, prepared-read protection, exact-read, and automation-binding maintenance suites (93.58 seconds total wall time including compiler preparation).
- The changed writer suite also passed on committed head: 18 tests, 48.25 seconds wall including compiler preparation; the new regression took 808 ms.
- The session-owner TypeScript test shard, targeted three-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent native manual review of the complete three-file change against the base found no P0–P3 issues. The coordinating review then ran local Codex autoreview through P2 on the complete final three-file range, with full candidate/store/planner/preservation context; it returned `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Both reviewed source snapshots match commit `b8e91356889cefd4c3ddf506451df6121e758d28`. Reviewers assessed recorded test evidence rather than independently rerunning suites. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; hosted review and exact-head CI remain before landing.

The added proof exercises the actual cleanup owner/native storage, not a full Gateway/automation-startup end-to-end flow or a PostgreSQL deployment. No retention-policy expansion is claimed.

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-maintenance-writer.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-maintenance-cap.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-maintenance-read.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-exact-read.test.ts src/gateway/session-automation-index.maintenance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

prs.title: feat: keep allowed MCP tools on the worker when other tools need approval
prs.body:
Related: #78308

## What Problem This Solves

Registering a Gateway policy for MCP tool calls currently routes every tool through the Gateway, even when only a few tools need human approval. Operators cannot keep ordinary calls on the worker while reviewing selected calls.

## User Impact

A Gateway policy can admit individual MCP tools for same-worker execution and keep approval-required tools on the Gateway path. Existing policies keep their behavior unless they opt in.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the optional `allowLocalMcpTool` policy callback for an exact node, server, and upstream tool. Only a literal `true` permits local placement. Execution rechecks authority, and narrowing a policy revokes existing local grants. Revocation currently happens at node scope; unaffected tools regain local grants on the next turn. Rejecting MCP execution if a mandatory policy fails to register is a separate follow-up.

Downstream: [openclaw/openclaw-enterprise#6461](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/6461). Merge this change and qualify an OCE runtime pin containing it before merging that draft.

## Evidence

At `79dd246c`, the real local MCP-server integration observed one upstream call per valid grant and zero for ungranted, revoked, stale-turn, and replaced-connection calls. Selective placement, one-shot approval, and approval-to-node dispatch tests passed; the Gateway and sealed worker bundle build completed. Local scoped autoreview reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. Hosted ClawSweeper review is pending until the draft is ready.

**Blocked E2E:** A dedicated OCE Agent with real Slack OAuth has not been qualified. That test waits for the new credential delivery path. This draft does not claim deployed-Agent or live Slack evidence.

prs.title: fix: resume persisted requests when transcript metadata advances
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A persisted user request can fail during initial replay preparation when another writer appends transcript metadata between selection and admission. The user then has to resend an unchanged request.

## User Impact

A benign transcript advance now gets one fresh preparation and admission attempt. A replaced user, completed turn, lost writer claim, or revoked authority still refuses replay. There are no runtime configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final-consumption path already retried once after #181473, but initial preparation used the same read owner without that recovery. Move the existing bounded retry into the shared owner, retain the original entry ID and generation across refresh, and record consumption before calling the consumer. This avoids a second retry layer and preserves exactly-once user-turn consumption.

Current readers throw `SessionTranscriptReadFenceError` for the reproduced version mismatch before returning context-validation facts. The owner handles that existing form and work-start invalidation without changing source, writer, or authority validation.

## Evidence

The new real-SQLite regression is red on base `71ee55620d0786d4078dfa41c3527488c4a7cad4`: a metadata append between selection and admission rejects initial preparation. The fix refreshes once, admits once, and retains one user message. Newer-user and repeated-advance cases still reject. All 80 focused/session/replay sibling cases pass, plus all 16 required prompt-prefix stability cases (96 total).

The complete initial `pnpm check:changed --staged --timed` run passed, as did `pnpm deadcode:unused-files`. After the CI repair, changed-file checks ran again; the nullable-generation type error was fixed and all three affected type graphs passed on rerun. Every remaining changed-file gate passed; the original failed run and targeted passing reruns are retained as evidence. Independent Codex autoreview at P0–P2 is scoped-clean on the final five-file candidate against base `71ee55620d0786d4078dfa41c3527488c4a7cad4`. No Control UI import boundary changes. The repaired 70-case focused/sibling run took 110.92 seconds, and the 10-case recovery/persistence run took 40.96 seconds. Initial CI run 44407917446 caught a PR-caused session-identity ratchet failure from a duplicated anchor guard. The repair shares the existing final guard with initial preparation and passes the ratchet; no inherited-failure waiver is used. Local typechecking caught a nullable-generation annotation, now corrected with all three affected type graphs passing. The complete [dispatched CI run 44412352144](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44412352144) passed on final head `e7eab8d0c898d0a6c23a8c48d916873d916ab467`. The normal [ready-for-review CI run 44414749132](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44414749132) also passed on that exact head. ClawSweeper re-review on this exact head has zero open items and no findings.

The committed benchmark uses an offline synthetic 5,000-session database and a 62,000-file workspace. Measurement acceptance was set before the comparison: two A/A controls and five interleaved A/B process pairs for steady and raced admission, with timing and sampled-allocation passes separated. Unchanged-path cost must stay within control variation; raced admission must succeed exactly once after one refresh. Recovery necessarily does more work than the baseline's failed request, so it is not presented as a latency speedup. The generated agent database is 37,792,735,232 bytes (35.20 GiB), with 200,640 transcript messages and 1.116 GB of workspace file contents. Timing and allocation passes are complete. Each arm has 100 warm observations across five interleaved process pairs, plus separately reported first-use samples.

| Case | Wall median / p95 (ms), before → after | Process CPU median (ms) | Main-thread CPU median (ms) | Sampled main-thread allocation median (MB) | Admitted turns |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Steady | 11.93 / 13.86 → 11.76 / 14.16 | 28.72 → 27.78 | 4.36 → 4.33 | 1.418 → 1.400 | 100/100 → 100/100 |
| Concurrent append | 14.74 / 18.51 → 24.06 / 31.55 | 31.91 → 43.54 | 5.09 → 7.86 | 1.650 → 2.842 | 0/100 → 100/100 |

Steady A/A wall medians were 14.05 and 11.88 ms; sampled-allocation control medians were 1.397 and 1.406 MB. Steady cost remains within control variation. Race recovery adds 9.32 ms median wall time and 1.192 MB sampled main-thread allocation relative to failure, with exactly one refresh and no duplicate user message. First-use wall medians: steady 351.98 → 350.06 ms; race 349.56 → 366.17 ms. Process CPU includes workers; allocation sampling covers the main thread only. A separate 100-iteration CPU profile was inspected; startup/esbuild and forced GC dominate whole-process samples and are excluded from the timed owner windows. No Linux/btrfs, live Gateway, or external-provider equivalence is claimed.

Production delta: +8 lines for selection identity and callback-consumption ownership, with the old final-only retry deleted. The regression adds 58 lines; the standalone benchmark is supporting proof.

prs.title: improve: reduce repeated work when searching session history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Searching session transcripts repeatedly builds the same session-list selection and recipient presentation for every matching key. On larger rosters, that creates unnecessary main-thread work and allocation during recall.

## User Impact

Session recall uses less CPU and memory while returning the same visibility decisions. Global transcript ownership, sharing, federation, cron and phantom exclusions, Incognito, spawned-session restrictions, and pinned visibility remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose the list owner's existing candidate-key selection through its preparation API, prepare/filter each admitted candidate batch once, and use set membership for individual keys. Global keys retain their separate physical-owner authorization. Nothing is retained across worker yields or requests, and transcript indexing is unchanged.

This preserves the request-scoped runtime reuse from #189322 within the indexed recall path introduced by #200355. Production code is net **−3 lines**. Runtime-resolution composite keys remain unchanged: replacing their complete nine-field encoding would add separate cache machinery without addressing the repeated preparation.

## Evidence

The real search regression fails before the fix: 28 preparations for 14 candidate batches. It passes after the fix. All **54 focused tests** pass, including the list selector, filters, retained partitions, search RPC handler, and agent-tool visibility. A mixed-roster differential compares batched verdict bytes with the original exact-key preparation and independently asserts the expected exclusions. The corrected malformed phantom fixture also passed its focused rerun.

Synthetic benchmark: **600 resident rows, 130 indexed matching keys**, real recall owner and transcript worker. Five samples per process; serial ABBA fresh processes, 200 recalls per timing sample, separate allocation sampling with collected objects included. The worker limits batches to 26 keys; this removes per-key preparation, not the fresh authorization boundary after each worker yield. The fixture intentionally does not reproduce multi-gigabyte transcript storage or workspace traversal, which are outside this owner path.

Sampled allocation fell from **9.43 MB to 1.53 MB per recall (84%)**, with same-code process medians within 1%. Both timing pairs improved: **42–55% lower main-thread CPU** and **15–33% lower elapsed time**. The busy shared host produced substantial A/A timing variation, so these ranges are paired observations, not production latency guarantees. Cold worker initialization is reported separately by the script.

| Per-recall metric | Baseline median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU, untraced | 3.77 / 5.00 ms | 1.89 / 2.82 ms |
| Elapsed, untraced | 6.46 / 13.97 ms | 4.75 / 12.20 ms |
| Sampled allocation | 9.43 / 9.48 MB | 1.53 / 1.59 MB |

Each cell has 10 samples across two fresh processes. Timing sample ranges were CPU 3.00–5.00 → 1.34–2.82 ms and elapsed 5.08–13.97 → 3.36–12.20 ms. Cold first-call ranges were 2.66–10.30 → 2.88–5.65 s, dominated by worker admission and unsuitable for attributing this warm-path improvement. The full five-file test run took 230.64 s including compilation; the changed search-scope tests took about 26 s in the first complete run.

Reproduce with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-recall-measure.ts --state-dir <synthetic-directory> --sessions 600 --keys 130 --iterations 200 --samples 5`. Reuse serially with `--reuse`; use `--owner-ref a4be1ae09e3ebe021f55fb65dd3663aa2a152504` for the exact baseline recall owner and `--allocation` in separate processes.

`pnpm check:changed` completed. Its line-cap and two proof-code typing findings were corrected and their gates rerun successfully. The remaining unused UI export reproduces on exact base `a4be1ae09e3ebe021f55fb65dd3663aa2a152504`: the same full-tree Knip command exits 1 with only `ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.test-support.ts: expectPendingNewSessionPresentation (e2e)`. #198967 (`a90c5419b779d`) introduced this main regression by removing every caller while leaving its export. This PR does not change that UI path. All change-caused local failures are resolved; CI remains pending.

Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2 on the complete change against `a4be1ae09e3ebe021f55fb65dd3663aa2a152504`; no actionable findings. Subsequent edits only corrected proof-code types. No Control UI imports of the changed production modules were found. No schema/configuration change or live Gateway modification.

CI run [44411579287](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44411579287) has one investigated failure so far: `checks-node-changed-1`, `sessions-list-privacy.test.ts`, “rechecks named role enrichment after a role change during chat.history”. The identical focused test fails on exact CI main parent `777fc99a8993b55fab66e3cb17faf4ef520cd40f` and on this head: the admitted request returns two rows instead of rejecting. #201334 (`04cb8179ccd66`) deliberately changed authority to remain fixed for admitted requests and apply role changes at the next request, leaving this test's old mid-request rejection expectation behind. This is a main test regression, not a passing CI claim; the test and authority owners are unchanged here. Remaining jobs and final-head ClawSweeper review are pending.

prs.title: fix: run packed SDK consumer checks behind a proxy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The packed SDK consumer check can fail with HTTP 400 while fetching valid public dependencies behind a proxy. Its synthetic HTTP registry for private workspace packages triggers an npm proxy-agent protocol-cache bug before public HTTPS dependencies can install.

## User Impact

Maintainers can run the packed SDK declaration, export, and transport checks with the normal proxy and TLS configuration. There is no product-runtime, dependency-version, or installed-npm change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the fake registry. In the disposable consumer only, version-qualified npm source overrides select the existing private workspace tarballs for declared compatible dependency edges. The SDK remains the consumer's sole direct dependency, and packed manifests retain their semver declarations. Public third-party packages still resolve normally.

This is a packaging-contract fixture, not a scoped-registry transport test. Missing declarations, unused tarballs, incompatible versions, and special-character source paths are covered explicitly. No dependency patch, vendoring, third-party override, request reordering, cache warming, proxy bypass, or TLS relaxation is introduced. The fixture helper shrinks by 33 net lines.

## Evidence

- The unchanged external-consumer E2E fails on base `71ee55620d0786d4078dfa41c3527488c4a7cad4` under both Node/npm and pinned Bun/npm: local HTTP succeeds, then public HTTPS metadata requests return 400. A differentiated transport probe identifies the malformed `http://registry.npmjs.org:443/...` request path.
- With the final fixture, that same E2E passes on Node 26.12.1/npm 11.20.0 and pinned OpenClaw Bun 1.4.4/bundled npm 12.2.1. Fresh npm caches record HTTP 200 cache misses for public metadata and tarballs; proxy and TLS settings remain unchanged. Consumer typechecking, exported-entrypoint loading, and custom-transport assertions complete.
- All four focused helper tests pass on each runtime. They prove declared transitive installation, missing-declaration failure even when a source mapping exists, absence of unused tarballs, SDK-only direct dependencies, unchanged installed declarations, incompatible-version refusal, and paths containing spaces, `#`, and `%`.
- Focused typecheck, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, normal commit hooks, and diff checks pass. The E2E builds and packs the actual SDK workspace graph.
- Independent complete-diff source review found no P0–P2 findings. Local Codex autoreview of the final two-file candidate against the base above is `scoped-clean` through P2, with complete helper/caller/package context; the candidate was committed unchanged as `e756249db80004746ac1405e4fe8fb27796f93c4`. Reviewers reused recorded test evidence rather than independently rerunning it. Hosted advisory review was requested at readiness and remained pending at landing inspection.
- **Exact-head hosted CI:** [run 44417111200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44417111200) completed with `openclaw/ci-gate` successful for published head `eec3b6524d98f36c8ab857a3295d7e54e9c9596c`.

Native Windows installation is not yet verified. Version-qualified source selection covers the current semver workspace contract, not arbitrary tag/git/file/alias dependency specifications. This does not fix npm's upstream proxy-agent defect.

Requested and co-authored by @vincentkoc.

Recovering a plugin can keep a completed caller’s plugin instance and registry in memory for the lifetime of the recovery capture. Repeated recoveries can retain retired request graphs even after their own work has finished.

## Why This Change Was Made

Construct the intentionally generation-unbound native recovery owner under the existing detached async root, instead of clearing only the instance-invocation token. This detaches its ports and descriptor snapshot; the subsequent copy operation, source checks, custody, and disposal remain unchanged.

The existing recovery lifetime test now captures under a finite `PluginInvocationScope`, so it exercises the caller graph that was retained. The production change replaces the narrower context-clearing call; it adds no owner, cache, lifetime, or fallback. Production line count is unchanged; tests add three net lines.

- **Red/green regression:** the strengthened source-recovery GC case fails against base `71ee55620d07` with `Live recovery retained its retired instance`, then passes with this fix. The complete `runtime.retention.test.ts` suite passes **17/17**, including source, bundled CJS, and bundled MJS recovery with recovered bytes still readable. Local wrapper wall time: **50.09 seconds**.
- **Actual native-owner reproduction:** a 1 MiB caller ALS payload survives while the original recovery is held and collects only after disposal. prs.title: fix(macos): allow reopening after credential startup fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a credential startup error, the Mac app can remain alive with no usable window and refuse subsequent launches because it still holds the profile instance lock. This was reproduced on macOS 26.6.2, with the process stuck from 00:55 until it was force-quit at 14:48.

## User Impact

A failed startup can finish quitting and release its profile lock, allowing the user to repair the reported startup problem and reopen OpenClaw.

## Why This Change Was Made

The failure handler calls `NSApplication.terminate` synchronously inside `credentialStartupTask`. The termination delegate returns `.terminateLater` and starts cleanup that awaits that same task. AppKit's nested termination loop leaves the startup task on the stack and also prevents its MainActor cleanup deadline from completing.

Use the existing `AppDelegate.requestTermination()` path, already used by Quit, signal handling, and app relocation. It schedules termination through the run loop so the credential task can unwind first.

The regression launches the real staged app with malformed configuration, requires it to exit within 15 seconds without forced termination, then restores the configuration and verifies credential admission on the same profile. The composition suite is serialized because its process cleanup identifies the shared fixture executable.

## Evidence

- The live process sample contains 2,537 identical main-thread observations in `applicationDidFinishLaunching → showCredentialStartupFailure → NSApplication.terminate → AppKit _shouldTerminate`. Force-quitting and relaunching restored connections to the running local gateway.
- The faulty call and the shutdown task awaiting `credentialStartupTask.value` were verified on current upstream main.
- `swiftc -frontend -parse` passed for both changed Swift files. `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent code review found a test-concurrency issue. Adding `.serialized` resolved it, and the final review reported no remaining P1/P2 findings.
- Native build and red/green regression execution remain **unverified**. A task-owned Tart copy was prepared from the cached public macOS image, but Tart aborted during macOS application registration inside the execution sandbox. The session policy rejected an unsandboxed VM launch.
- The regression runs in the staged app-host lane through `bash scripts/test-macos-app-host.sh --credential-startup-only`. Ordinary PR native tests skip this app-host-only suite. That lane still needs execution on an eligible disposable macOS runner.

This fix addresses the permanent hang after a startup error. The original credential error that triggered the sampled process was unavailable from the sandboxed unified-log reader.

prs.title: fix: avoid waiting for stopped Gateways during updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Updating or recovering an already-stopped Gateway can exhaust the maintenance-drain deadline when local client credentials are unavailable, then warn about interrupting work even though nothing is listening.

## User Impact

Updates and rollback can proceed through the existing guarded stop without client credentials when service inspection reports stopped and the configured local port is free. Running Gateways, occupied or unverified ports, installation-owned control clients, and explicit drain policy retain their existing handling. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Establish the stopped-service/free-port proof before preparing TLS or authentication, rather than requiring a failed authenticated observation to reach that proof. Keep the native stop and its authority checks in the existing owner; remove the later auth-dependent shortcut. The updater or Doctor performing the stop must contain this change; a newer candidate cannot change an older updater's own drain code.

Simplification: no new helper or policy owner; production delta +3 lines, tests +32 lines against the base.

## Evidence

- The new credential-unavailable regression fails on base `71ee55620d0786d4078dfa41c3527488c4a7cad4` because the no-op stop has not run before the drain wait, then passes with this repair. An additional test preserves explicit-drain refusal for the same stopped state.
- Real production `withGatewayMaintenanceDrain` with isolated state, a verified free loopback port, an unsafe synthetic credential store, and a no-op native-stop callback: base exhausts the 250 ms drain budget and warns; repaired code completes without warnings or deadline exhaustion (173 ms observed). The repaired path still checks authority before the callback and its effect. No live service was stopped.
- Drain owner and native-handoff suites: **75 passed**, 43.49 s suite wall time (45.60 s wrapper; 96% transform). The initial isolated regression run took 37.05 s. CI seconds are not available yet.
- Real socket authentication/restart, service-maintenance, and immutable-activation siblings passed. **Two resident-restart tests remain failing with the identical missing predecessor-stop receipt error on both the base and repaired tree** (84 other sibling tests passed in each run). Those separate receipt failures were not changed or hidden.
- Update-CLI typecheck shard, targeted two-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. No package boundary or build-output changes; broad CI and full cross-version/platform update proof remain pending.
- Independent local autoreview: Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2, complete two-file local snapshot over `71ee55620d0786d4078dfa41c3527488c4a7cad4`; **no actionable findings**. The reviewer had unchanged caller/auth/probe context and could not execute tests in its empty sandbox. Local ClawSweeper was not installed; the selected fallback's hosted review is deferred until the parent marks this draft ready.

Contributor credit: @vincentkoc — repair scope and direction; co-authored commit.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix: report terminal errors in model fallback logs
prs.body:
Related: #201443

## What Problem This Solves

After the primary model fails, a backup model can return a terminal error while the fallback log says `candidate_succeeded`. That makes the log disagree with the error shown in chat.

## User Impact

The fallback log shows when a backup stopped with an error. The original error reply is preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The run entry records a chain stop when the result has a failed terminal status and no retry classification. The existing checks for retry eligibility still apply.

## Evidence

I sent a turn through the built CLI to an isolated Gateway with synthetic providers. The primary returned HTTP 402. The backup ran a workspace write and then returned a terminal error. The CLI preserved the failure reply, and the Gateway stopped the fallback chain.

```text
build-stamp {"head": "927df2e1ff9ebe52a96f046485eb10e48a39d7f8", "inputsClean": true}
model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=proof-primary/proof-primary candidate=proof-primary/proof-primary reason=billing next=proof-backup/proof-backup
model fallback chain stopped: reason=returned_terminal_error candidate=proof-backup/proof-backup
agent {"status": "error", "isError": true, "replyExcerpt": "OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply."}
agent.wait {"status": "error", "terminalReply": "fixture_terminal: Synthetic terminal failure"}
provider requests ["proof-primary", "proof-backup", "proof-backup"]
candidate_succeeded events 0
third-model requests 0
```

The original regression reproduced the false success on `1fae66036cc`. The error-only payload case also failed on `19f84ca7f1e`, where the terminal status was `ok`. On the follow-up, both regressions pass. An error-only reply without terminal metadata now reports `error` and keeps the original payload. The follow-up passed 65 focused tests, core typechecking, targeted lint, formatting, and the runtime build. The original change passed 230 focused tests.

The Gateway fixture covers billing followed by a terminal failure after tool execution. The reporter's live provider rotation and transcript collision remain unverified.

prs.title: fix: stop a refused library skill create from leaving files on disk
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Creating a library skill under a name you already use is refused with "A skill named ... already exists", but the refused skill's files were already written to the Gateway's state directory (`skill-library/<new id>/revisions/<rev>/`). Nothing refers to that directory, and nothing removes it, so every refused create leaves an orphan bundle on disk.

## User Impact

User impact: a refused create no longer leaves files behind. The error and the existing skills are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The staged bundle was moved into place before the database write that checks the name. Now a new skill's name is checked against the caller's library before any files are written, so the common case writes nothing. The write keeps its own check for two creates racing on one name; when that check refuses a new skill, the fresh skill directory is removed. Its id was minted for this request (or is the import's own upload id), so no entry refers to it.

## Evidence

One new library service test runs two concurrent creates with the same name and then a third, and checks that only the winner's directory exists under `skill-library/`.

- With the fix: the library service tests pass (24/24).
- On `main` with the new test: it fails with three directories instead of one.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files and `pnpm tsgo:core`: clean.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

Run on a remote test VM from a snapshot of `main` (c5ef395ba72) plus this change:

```
CI=true pnpm test src/skills/library/service.test.ts --maxWorkers=1   # 24 passed
git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/skills/library/service.ts
CI=true pnpm test src/skills/library/service.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "leaves no skill files"   # failed: 3 directories, expected 1
```

</details>

Not covered: orphan directories already left by earlier refused creates stay until removed by hand; a refused rename of an existing skill can still leave its unused new revision directory.

## What Problem This Solves

On macOS, Doctor tells you to run `--fix` for stray launchd jobs even when that invocation will refuse the repair. A relocated state directory can put you in that loop.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor uses the same eligibility checks for its advice and for the repair. The repair still verifies each job against launchd before unloading it and keeps operator plists.

prs.title: improve(workers): reuse admitted prepared project snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worker dispatch repeats repository admission and content validation that project preparation already completed. Snapshot capture also needs to verify the workspace, toolchains, and runtime it is about to preserve.

## User Impact

A fresh, eligible fork can reuse verified preparation from the same admitted dispatch. Ordinary starts and replays use normal verification, and the shortcut expires before code can change the prepared files. Snapshot inspection does not hydrate the worker or repair its runtime cache.

Depends on #201025 at `a0b184ef5716`, which incorporates `main` at `1fae66036cc0`. The stack's schema/auth prerequisite branch remains at `1f67db94064`. Related older proposals #193776, #193872 and #194279 remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry fresh-fork provenance from the exact selected checkpoint, and verify expanded package code through the native CLI before inspecting and capturing project caches. Validate prepared output in its owning HOME and account for bootstrap and repository Node installations separately. Keep snapshot invalidation with the workspace and bundle owners, including before fallback prewarm executes code.

The worker-local setup initializer has no supported production provider in this stack; it is not a shipped capability. Existing protected-egress setup still works. Initializer scope remains open.

## Evidence

- [Exact-head CI at `5690ff3e9d41`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44412835810) confirmed the [session-identity check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44412835810/job/135186598107), [affected lint stripe](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44412835810/job/135188474250), and [shared-publication shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44412835810/job/135186602579) repairs. The affected shard passed **130/130**, including all four previously failing cases. The only blocking failure in this run is the environment-variable ratchet: **464 names versus a cap of 462**. The cap is unchanged and repository policy requires owner approval to raise it.
- Core typechecking, focused prepared-project tests, and the test-line ratchet passed locally after the stack absorbed `main`. The test allocation remains 1,251 above the default 400 (1,651 net test lines).
- Earlier evidence: **226 focused tests across eight files** plus full build and declarations passed at `136587e39e95`. **112 affected tests** passed for the fixture repairs at `7e777df1a9d2`. Independent reviews covered cache/freshness, provider capture, inspection transport, and receipt-reader repairs. Native CLI fixture evidence is not live-provider proof.

**Remaining proof:** a green hosted gate, live PostgreSQL and live-provider/real-model integration, and a forward upgrade from latest stable. The previous [package acceptance run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44262689778) did not reach state-survival assertions. No operator Gateway was changed and no cloud worker lease was allocated.

Original PR by @galiniliev.

prs.title: improve(workers): start nodes with prepared runtimes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worker nodes repeat runtime expansion and prewarm, disposable nodes wait for private-computer preparation before connecting, and retained managed nodes can reconnect with an older runtime after a Gateway upgrade.

## User Impact

Nodes reuse verified package-owned worker code and overlap connection with private-computer preparation. Bundle admission and computer use still join readiness and failures. Dedicated Linux nodes, including supported XFCE desktop workers, can install the current runtime and recover the same enrolled device without replacing its workspace. Pending result cleanup retains its saved runtime.

This is the first worker PR in a two-PR stack extracted from `23dcc5f19b1`. The head incorporates `main` at `1fae66036cc0`, but the PR still targets `galiniliev/main7-worker-prerequisites` at `1f67db94064`. Fresh-snapshot admission shortcuts belong to dependent #201029. Related older proposals #193776, #193872 and #194279 remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep bundle integrity, package preparation, plugin readiness and runtime recovery with their existing owners. The provider invokes the installed native preparation command before recording runtime completion; read-only inspection uses the same owner without repair, download, enrollment, prewarming or bytecode-cache writes.

Deferred preparation retains its resource disposers through early shutdown. Same-node upgrades verify fresh artifacts before retiring the matching process, preserve canonical saved-runtime selection and rediscover the authoritative XFCE environment. Late preparation is released after provider timeouts. Ordinary bundle reuse still performs integrity validation; no snapshot fast path or additional admission state is introduced here.

## Evidence

- After integrating `main`, core typechecking, generated PostgreSQL schema verification, configuration docs, and the import-cycle and export-name guards passed locally. All **108 Gateway tests** in the focused dispatch, disk-custody and shared-publication run passed after the response fix. Runtime timeout regressions passed **16/16**; GitHub exec credential regressions passed **21/21**.
- The later fixture repair reproduced all four hosted shared-publication failures in an isolated environment without GitHub credentials, then passed **36/36**. Dependent #201029's [hosted shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44412835810/job/135186602579) also passed all four cases. The affected lint stripe and the session-identity check passed there; its environment-variable budget check is still red.
- [Exact-head CI at `a0b184ef5716`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44412839969) stopped at preflight. The old prerequisite base makes upstream generated locale files appear alongside source changes; those files are absent in the diff against integrated `main`. Downstream tests were skipped, not passed. The prerequisite ref and the guard were left unchanged.
- Earlier evidence: full build with declarations and all 163 public SDK subpath checks passed at `eeb7ff91c450`; runtime compatibility passed **159 tests across 13 files** at `a79be91bf992`. Those are not exact-head results. Independent reviews covered the runtime changes and repair deltas.

**Remaining proof:** hosted checks after the prerequisite base is updated, live PostgreSQL and live-provider/real-model/native-computer integration, and a forward upgrade from latest stable. The earlier [package acceptance run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44262689778) used a `2026.11.3` candidate against `2026.11.5` and did not reach state-survival assertions. prs.title: fix: open the dashboard in a compatible installed browser
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Onboarding and `openclaw dashboard` can open a browser that cannot run the Control UI even when a compatible browser is already installed. Switching browsers using only the clean dashboard URL loses the one-time pairing handoff and creates avoidable recovery work; this is not a failure of normal pairing.

## User Impact

When the default browser is known to lack required features, OpenClaw can open an identified compatible alternative on macOS, native Windows, or Linux for this session only. Supported and unknown defaults keep their existing opening path. No browser is installed, no OS default is changed, and no automation browser profile is selected.

**Draft: native Windows selection and prepared-profile automatic pairing passed on `6f75e6e45291`, but fresh-profile cold pairing failed. The visible-launch and macOS/Linux HTML-handler repairs below still need native confirmation. Earlier-head macOS dashboard validation remains valid only for its recorded scope; onboarding and broader native coverage are incomplete.** Windows Hub is independently released and is not changed here. WSL keeps its existing Windows desktop opener rather than selecting a Linux browser.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing browser opener now accepts an installed-browser target, while the existing private-file handoff still carries each newly issued one-time pairing URL. Browser-version estimates and actual browser feature probes share the same requirements; browser-side verification remains authoritative.

- macOS resolves the default HTML-document handler through Launch Services and reads application registrations/metadata, including `~/Applications`.
- Native Windows queries the Shell for the effective HTML-file handler and reads installed executable versions without running browsers to identify their versions.
- Linux reads the XDG `text/html` association and normal Chrome/Chromium, Firefox, and Edge executables on `PATH`. Custom wrappers, Flatpak-only installations, and `BROWSER` overrides remain conservative unknown cases.
- Selection order is deterministic. Unknown metadata retains the existing fallback, while missing compatible alternatives retain a terminal/recovery path.
- Explicit remote sessions do not launch on the wrong desktop. Cold GUI processes acknowledge startup without waiting for their lifetime; onboarding separately waits for a newly connected Control UI client.

There is no new pairing mechanism, stored browser preference, configuration option, token handling, or installation step. Changes target main only; no backport or older-Gateway compatibility is proposed. Necessary growth is the three platform discovery adapters and their common selection contract; no registry/cache/manager is introduced.

## Evidence

### Native Windows retest and visible-launch / HTML-association follow-up

Follow-up commit: [`1e5e0cb0a861`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1e5e0cb0a8618ceec47fd2c591bace46e41cc946). Independent source review found no concrete P0/P1/P2 issue in this follow-up; native execution remains unverified.

[@ekinnee’s retest](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200840#issuecomment-6993850519) of `6f75e6e45291` on Windows 11 26H2 confirms **correct selection**, unchanged HTML/HTTPS associations, protected handoff ACLs, credential-free browser arguments, and **60 passing Windows tests, 1 skipped, 0 failed**. Windows assigned HTML to Chrome 124 and HTTPS to Edge 157; the repaired selector correctly chose Chrome 158. With Chrome already visible in a prepared disposable profile, the dashboard opened and established one fresh authenticated Control UI connection.

**Fresh-profile cold launch/pairing still failed:** the selected process remained alive without a visible main window and admitted no Control UI connection, including a repeat launch. A separate harmless-HTML probe showed a window with `windowsHide: false`, but did not show the probe page title. That isolates a visibility problem, not a complete cold-pairing fix.

The follow-up sets `windowsHide: false` only for directly launched user GUI browsers, retaining detached startup acknowledgement and private-file delivery. It does not add first-run bypass flags, change profiles, or equate a process launch with connection/pairing success.

It also addresses ClawSweeper's HTML-handler finding on macOS/Linux: Launch Services resolves `public.html` with the default role, and XDG resolves `text/html`, matching the file actually passed to the opener instead of an unrelated HTTPS association. Unknown HTML handlers retain the existing opening path. Windows already uses the effective HTML association.

- Six visibility/split-association regressions failed before this follow-up and pass afterward. The Mac regression executes the actual JXA discovery program against fixed native-boundary responses; Linux uses real subprocess fixtures with deliberately different HTML/HTTPS defaults. Neither is native GUI proof.
- **102 focused tests across 8 files pass** (17.68 seconds wall time), plus strict affected typechecking, targeted lint/format, and diff checks.
- **Current-head native verification remains pending**, especially fresh-profile Windows visibility and actual handoff redemption. Prepared-profile success on the earlier head must not be reported as a cold-start pass.

### Windows repair after native verification

Repair commit: [`6f75e6e45291`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6f75e6e45291e2769e58df887aabf5fd9cde31c1). Independent source review found no concrete P0/P1/P2 findings in this repair; this was not native Windows execution.

[@ekinnee’s native Windows report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200840#issuecomment-6987294781) exposed a real failure on `cee9b3506c21`: Windows 11 26H2 resolved Chrome 124 as the effective HTTPS/HTML handler, but the legacy `UserChoice` key still named Edge. The PR therefore skipped fallback and opened the unsupported browser, with no admitted Control UI connection. The same run found that the selector suite called POSIX-only `process.getuid()` during shared setup on Windows.

The repair removes legacy default-registration/ProgID command parsing and asks the Windows Shell's `AssocQueryStringW` API for the effective `.html` executable. This is the association used for the private `handoff.html` file; it can differ from HTTPS. Unknown Shell results remain unknown, never fall back to stale default-registration data. Existing application metadata still supplies versions and deterministically ordered alternatives; no browser settings, registrations, installations, or profiles are modified.

Selector fixtures now supply and restore a synthetic macOS UID independently of the native host. Private-file tests run on their real host platform, retaining POSIX permissions versus Windows ACL behavior instead of performing real file operations under a mocked macOS platform.

- Three effective-handler regressions failed before the repair and pass afterward, including unsupported effective Chrome with stale Edge data, a supported effective handler, and an unknown association.
- **100 focused tests across 8 files pass** (16.59 seconds wall time), plus strict affected typechecking, targeted lint/format, and diff checks.
- All **27 selector cases also pass with `process.getuid` removed before the test runner starts** (39.97 seconds wall time, including compilation). This is Linux-hosted portability proof, not native Windows execution.
- **Superseded by the native retest above:** selection, the Windows selector suite, and prepared-profile pairing passed on this repair head; fresh-profile cold launch/pairing did not.

### ClawSweeper repair: inherited SSH variables on macOS

Commit [`cee9b3506c21`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/cee9b3506c218358154da01c7de7bb7ac8afaf75) restores the local-shell behavior protected by [#67088](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/67088) and [#85340](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85340). SSH environment variables alone no longer reject a local Mac GUI terminal. After verifying the console owner, SSH-marked Mac sessions must identify as the current launchd `Aqua` GUI bootstrap; background, unknown, or failed context checks remain blocked, as do Remote Containers/Codespaces. Linux/Windows SSH and WSL handling are unchanged.

Four inherited-SSH regressions failed on the previous PR head and pass with this repair. **70 focused tests across four affected/consumer files pass** (15.44 seconds wall time), along with strict affected typechecking, targeted lint/format, and diff checks. Independent source review found no concrete P0/P1/P2 issue in this narrow repair. This is fixture/source proof, not a new native macOS run: the earlier report's simulated-SSH result applies to `29dae7868b21`, not the new GUI-context distinction.

### Native macOS dashboard validation — passed

[@jjjhenriksen’s native test report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200840#issuecomment-6966181964) validates head `29dae7868b2139b5829806475c52b1f9076d2138` against comparison build `e9561fb93e23aca2a797ed0cf28593cac45edc17` in a disposable Apple Silicon Tart VM running macOS Sequoia 15.7.7, using a foreground loopback Gateway and disposable state.

- **Before:** the dashboard opened the HTTPS default, Safari 18.6, which displayed the unsupported-browser screen; the Gateway recorded no admitted Control UI connection.
- **After:** with Safari still the HTTPS default, the dashboard selected Chrome 158.0.8127.37 installed only in `~/Applications`. Both a cold launch and a repeat launch into the running Chrome process produced fresh, authenticated Control UI connections at the Gateway. The HTTPS default remained Safari.
- **Additional checks:** removing the compatible alternative produced the recovery notice; `--no-open` suppressed launch; `--json` returned the handoff and expiry fields; a simulated SSH session suppressed GUI launch.
- **Onboarding is partial, not passed:** the browser-handoff helper selected Chrome and the Gateway recorded a separate fresh Control UI connection, but the helper did not return before the test cutoff. This was not a full interactive onboarding run or confirmed handoff completion.

The report includes sanitized terminal/Gateway excerpts, not before/after screenshots. It does **not** establish supported-default behavior, unknown/custom metadata, failed browser startup, a forced expired handoff, or a successful chat reply.

### Automated and source validation

- **Prior-head validation:** 89 targeted tests across 8 files passed on `29dae7868b21` (16.96 seconds wall time). The repair reruns the four affected/consumer suites above; unchanged feature-floor, private-handoff, Linux subprocess, and browser feature-admission proof is retained from that run. Focused tests cover browser feature floors, supported/unknown defaults, user-installed macOS alternatives, deterministic selection, native Windows metadata fixtures, Linux XDG subprocess fixtures, headless/SSH/WSL behavior, selected-launch failure, cold long-lived GUI process startup, private-file delivery, and fresh handoffs on repeated dashboard runs. Existing dashboard/onboarding handoff suites and browser feature admission remain green.
- Selected-launch regressions were red on base `e9561fb93e23aca2a797ed0cf28593cac45edc17` (three intended failures) and green with the target-aware opener.
- Strict typechecking of affected production/tests with repository ambient declarations, targeted lint/format, and `git diff --check` pass.
- `pnpm ui:build` succeeds. Existing advisory size budgets also fail on the pinned base: CSS 57.8 KiB vs 56.9 KiB; chat boot requests 21 vs 20; chat JS 1297.2 KiB vs 1296.8 KiB. The candidate reports 1297.3 KiB chat JS; no CSS/request-budget exception is added.
- Independent read-only source review identified cold-GUI lifetime and kernel-only WSL classification defects; both were repaired with regressions. The follow-up review confirms both repairs with no remaining concrete P0/P1/P2 findings in those repairs. Native platform execution is not established by that review. The structured Auto Review attempts were interrupted by Gateway restarts and did not produce a completed receipt.

Linux-specific proof uses real Linux subprocesses for XDG discovery fixtures and a real long-lived process for cold-launch lifetime; those pass locally. This runner has no installed desktop browser or display, so real Linux desktop opening/pairing and screenshots remain unverified, not claimed as passing.

### Remaining native verification

Use disposable state/profile and a foreground Gateway on an unused port, never normal Gateway credentials.

- Finish a full interactive onboarding run and establish why the helper did not confirm completion in the reported test.
- Verify the new macOS distinction between a local GUI shell carrying inherited SSH variables and an actual SSH/background session belonging to the same console user. Also cover the supported-default and unknown/custom browser paths, failed browser startup, forced expired-handoff recovery, and a separately observed chat reply.
- Rerun fresh-profile Windows cold launch with the visible GUI setting, observe any browser first-run UI, and verify the private handoff actually redeems and admits a new Control UI connection. Repeat with a prepared visible profile and preserve the HTML/HTTPS defaults.
- Verify the new macOS/Linux HTML-handler discovery with differing HTML and HTTPS defaults, including an unknown/custom HTML application. Linux subprocess fixtures and the Mac native-boundary fixture do not establish desktop browser behavior.
- Capture sanitized unsupported-default before/after media with actual OS/browser versions. Do not publish pairing URLs, credentials, or private desktop content.

Reported and scoped with @jjjhenriksen. Native test-box verification is still pending.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfef40a9-b1b9-4014-a803-f5a73399e554)

## Worked on by

- @jjjhenriksen

prs.body:

Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Write for someone who uses OpenClaw but has not read the code. The title and
opening problem statement should make sense without the diff or linked issue.

type: <what changes for the person affected>

Use a parenthesized scope only when it helps that reader.
