Good: fix: keep automations running when you open another chat
Bad: fix(cron): guard missing session IDs during authority restoration
Good: fix: let users sign in again after their session expires
Bad: fix(auth): add a null check to the token refresh handler

For internal-only work, name the actual developer or operator workflow affected.

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

Closes #201438

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
In 1–3 short, plain-language sentences, explain what someone is trying to do,
what goes wrong or is missing, and why it matters. For a fix, include the trigger
when known. For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.

Good: "Opening another chat can turn off a reply watcher, so it stops checking
until you notice and re-enable it."
Bad: "Fixes incorrect operator-authority invalidation on session identity mutation."

Describe the experienced problem, not just the code change. Save function names,
missing checks, and the root-cause walkthrough for the explanation below.
-->

Developers investigating native chat startup delays can measure client receipts, but those timestamps alone cannot locate Gateway and provider work. Background model calls also make one-request-per-chat accounting unreliable, so incomplete or unattributed captures need to fail rather than produce plausible timings.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: **there is no user-visible change**. This is opt-in developer tooling for an explicitly owned, isolated synthetic Gateway. It does not launch or reconfigure an installed Gateway, change authentication, or expand operator timing eligibility.

The preload adds unmeasured instrumentation overhead. Its output is diagnostic evidence, not uninstrumented performance or a speedup claim. Self-owned foreground evidence does not establish externally supervised packaged-service behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

Combine an authenticated attach-only synthetic driver, a self-contained process-local preload with build/owner qualification, and an offline reducer with the existing mock provider. Captures contain allowlisted synthetic identities, purposes, timing and counts, not prompts, bodies, credentials or generated content.

The reducer requires complete measured chains and reconciles every Responses request with a measured or purpose-tagged background call. Unexplained requests, retries, loss, HTTP errors and incomplete measured shutdown fail explicitly. Embeddings remain separately counted without invented ownership or latency; background completion after 2xx headers remains unverified.

The author simplification pass retained this as one coherent developer-tooling stage: capture and producer accounting cannot safely land without their strict reducer and rejection controls. No production timing seam, new runtime registration or default instrumentation was added. The full diff adds 2,200 lines and removes two. The explicit 362-line allocation covers 762 net test lines beyond the 400-line default; those cases protect distinct capture, emitted-binding, request-accounting, lifecycle and rejection boundaries.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For visual web/macOS/iOS/Android changes, follow
the PR visual-proof standard and its screenshot delivery gate:
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/.agents/skills/openclaw-pr-maintainer/references/media.md#pr-visual-proof
Keep the clean before/after pair visible first, then the annotated pair.

Start with the behavior checked and the result in plain language. Reviewers will
inspect the code, tests, and CI; do not make them decode command lists to learn
what was verified. Put exact commands, commit hashes, and long output in links
or optional <details>. Keep the useful evidence summary and meaningful gaps visible.
-->

Focused proof passes all 38 tests across three files, including actual opt-in mock HTTP accounting and a real Node preload subprocess. Negative controls reject unknown extra traffic, retry identities, mismatched windows/instances, lost events, incomplete measured chains, HTTP errors, wrong shutdown targets and missing main completion. Emitted-owner regressions exercise renamed bindings, shadowed callback parameters, unchanged results, unsupported declarations and duplicate anchors.

**Current-head behavior proof also passes:** a disposable source-built Gateway processed one authenticated `gateway-client/ui` turn through the mock provider. The unchanged reducer accepted **two Responses requests: one measured and one explicitly attributed session-activity summary**, plus one separately counted embedding. The actual loaded owner hashes match the qualified build.

The exact-target shutdown was scheduled, the main capture exited 0 with all eight anchors and zero dropped events, unclassified identities or write failures, and all six captured Node PIDs were observed stopped before final producer accounting. The orchestrator also observed its CLI wrapper exit 0 but did not retain that wrapper's PID. The main-process claim rests on its authenticated stop target, capture-end, captured chain `40652 -> 15944 -> 56560`, and observed-gone PIDs, not a fully linked launcher tree.

The run retained a boolean `listenerClosed` observation. A separate later socket recheck, recorded at `2026-11-18T22:01:23.062Z`, returned `ECONNREFUSED`; that error code was not recorded by the original run. Helper `native-chat-33760.jsonl` never wrote `capture-end`; it was observed gone and excluded only from the exhaustively accounted main-process Responses scope. This does not certify its clean exit, whole-process-tree completeness or embedding ownership.

Validated head: `6fdf5abb9fef568d12029f90c8ef2ac70ef8b2fa`, based on `b400e8deed133ac0fa084072424fe1285f162952`, on Windows ARM64 / Node 26.13.0 / pinned pnpm 12.15.0. Both final-head Knip unused-file scans pass with **zero entries**; none of the owned paths is reported. The documented scripts have exact Knip entries.

Two independent Copilot subagent code reviews covered the original base-to-candidate change and separately reviewed the emitted-owner correction against actual compiled owners at P0-P2, reporting no significant issues. They also reviewed the real capture evidence; two provenance-accuracy items were corrected as disclosed above. Codex CLI was unavailable; these were narrative reviews, not the shared helper's isolated/frozen-input machine result.

<details>
<summary>Exact local commands and results</summary>

- `pnpm test test/scripts/native-chat-start-capture.test.ts test/scripts/native-chat-start-measure.test.ts test/scripts/diagnostic-preload-ipc.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **passed, 38/38**. Unit-fast shard: 1.16 s for the two new files; tooling shard: 3.32 s for the IPC file (2.000 s test time). CI seconds are unavailable before PR CI.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json --incremental`: **passed**.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.scripts.json scripts/perf/native-chat-start-measure.ts scripts/perf/native-chat-start-preload.mjs scripts/perf/native-chat-start-report.mjs scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs scripts/e2e/lib/mock-inference-facts.ts`: **passed**.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json test/scripts/native-chat-start-capture.test.ts test/scripts/native-chat-start-measure.test.ts test/scripts/diagnostic-preload-ipc.test.ts`: **passed**.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.scripts.json config/knip.config.ts`: **passed**.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check config/knip.config.ts scripts/README.md scripts/perf/native-chat-start-measure.ts scripts/perf/native-chat-start-preload.mjs scripts/perf/native-chat-start-report.mjs scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs scripts/e2e/lib/mock-inference-facts.ts test/scripts/native-chat-start-capture.test.ts test/scripts/native-chat-start-measure.test.ts test/scripts/diagnostic-preload-ipc.test.ts`: **passed**.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`: **passed**, net +762 / default 400 / allocation 362.
- `pnpm deadcode:unused-files`: **passed on final head**, production 0 entries and full-tree 0 entries.
- `node scripts/perf/native-chat-start-preload.mjs --check-owner-root .`: **passed**, eight anchors on candidate source; offline qualification, not execution.
- `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- `pnpm build`: **passed (exit 0)** on final head, 3m 34.5s, with valid equivalent-input cache reuse. The preceding full build took 6m 47.5s.
- `node scripts/perf/native-chat-start-preload.mjs --check-owner-root .artifacts/native-dist-preflight --expected-build 6fdf5abb9fef568d12029f90c8ef2ac70ef8b2fa --expected-owner-hash 36a67e6e9a0b3a24db34d81feb24c9a523b2d413053eb87566ef40e3b3e0b2fb --expected-owner-hash 9d43777cea33233a10a08fb4b9177ca3c0a88a09a85b8f14af61e42508fe1982 --expected-owner-hash c286a29e537a5e89f1967d6c814f1a30ee48302dd3f6d2f978bf12043eef319f`: **passed**, `layout=built-dist`, eight anchors across three actual compiled owners. The staging root contains only a junction to that build's `dist`, not `src`.
- `node --check --input-type=module` with each of the three transformed compiled owners on stdin: **passed, 3/3**, syntax only; imports and Gateway code were not executed.
- The same built-dist preflight with the first expected owner hash replaced by 64 zeros: **expected rejection**, `Unexpected measured owner content`, before execution.

Final preload SHA-256: `5e57885d80f3151a36dc3097fd8ee36039e082e7881c43958ae2ff8a2614d006`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Executed real Gateway capture, accounting and cleanup</summary>

The ordinary source CLI owner was `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --bind <loopback> --port <task-port>` (the implementation of the package's `openclaw` script). Its environment supplied a fresh task-only home, state directory, synthetic config and mock credential; only its own process tree received the preload. The authenticated readiness check matched `status.pid` against the fresh task state-lock PID before any chat. The driver repeated that PID check before requesting the exact `{pid, ownerId, port}` stop.

The locally executed orchestration command was:

```text
node --import <source-root>/scripts/tsx.mjs native-chat-current-head-proof.mjs <source-root> <fresh-proof-root>
```

It launched the committed `scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs` with `MOCK_NATIVE_CHAT_ACCOUNTING=1`, invoked the committed `measureNativeChatStart({samples: 1, url: <task-ws>, mockUrl: <task-http-v1>, timeoutMs: 120000, stopTarget: <verified-task-lock>})`, awaited the spawned wrapper's exit and observed captured PIDs stopped, then retained the mock's final accounting. The wrapper PID was not persisted and is not inferred from `ppid=44000`. It ran the committed reducer:

```text
node scripts/perf/native-chat-start-report.mjs --client <proof-root>/client-receipts.json --capture-dir <proof-root>/capture --mock-final <proof-root>/mock-final.json
```

Both orchestration and reducer completed **exit 0**. All runtime behavior, capture hooks and accounting were the committed code; the local orchestrator only prepared disposable inputs, launched it and recorded observations. It did not patch runtime code or replace transport/admission functions.

Actual reducer accounting (synthetic instance UUID omitted):

```json
{
  "responses": 2,
  "measured": 1,
  "background": 1,
  "embeddings": 1,
  "backgroundByPurpose": {
    "session-activity-summary": 1,
    "session-observer": 0,
    "session-title": 0
  }
}
```

Retained producer-artifact SHA-256 values:

| Artifact | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| Reducer report | `040a76bdeae791db9674e3798069faa65dfc913d631ed775419776fd02fc6f36` |
| Client receipts | `7ca31ca2f1461fd97f5179f7e628e917257f6ebb910779b5e59b9fa4ee965dcd` |
| Final mock accounting/collection receipt | `369bb4c387894f5dc13bc6913255c3a0862e8230457a66655e2ef10b2435d84a` |
| Main capture | `c9298a02c94e77981a4a3937caf5d360d92beb61cdf3702f62fafb44d477396b` |
| Retained synthetic config after the run | `5b34a3ae3b8020ddc8eaa28d63796b63e4d6e3f20d7d4e8801f386b1f60c27b4` |

These are author-run evidence identities, not trusted execution attestations. The config digest identifies the retained post-run generated artifact; its exact prelaunch bytes were not separately hashed, while the driver's live fixture guard checked routing/runtime before chat. Paths, credentials, endpoints and raw host logs are not published. Two earlier local orchestration setup failures were retained and rejected before any chat: an outdated lock-filename selector and an external CIM-listener assertion. The accepted fresh run used the actual state-lock projection and authenticated Gateway PID instead; no reducer guard was relaxed and failed captures were not mixed in.

This is a single instrumented first-turn/cold-session capture/reducer behavior smoke, not a cold/warm benchmark, native application test or performance evidence. Background behavior stayed enabled, and its 2xx headers do not establish later stream/result success.

</details>

Environment limitation: `sqlite-vec` was unavailable on win32-arm64, so the vector index update was skipped, and project memory recall exceeded its 1000 ms budget and continued without project candidates. This does not establish a representative or complete memory-recall path.

The original adapter failed against the actual identifier-minified build (`missing completion-owner`); the correction passes that same emitted-owner boundary without relaxing qualification. Source-only success is not counted as built-dist proof.

The preceding full build reported UI budget warnings: largest CSS gzip 57.3 KiB versus 56.9 KiB; total CSS gzip 331.0 KiB versus 329.4 KiB; total CSS raw 1707.2 KiB versus 1699.4 KiB; chat boot JS requests 21 versus 20. The final build reused the same UI content and refreshed identity. This PR changes no UI files; no base budget comparison or budget improvement is claimed.

The earlier isolated ARM64 experiment against released payload `4ffdd2047d192dd65554de3c8c46c0e0197c6e2a` accounted for six measured and seven background Responses calls, with two embeddings counted separately. That is historical diagnostic-accounting evidence, not current-head live proof or evidence for the separate subagent lock-order fix.

A real source-built Gateway was exercised, not the installed native application or service. Raw network first byte, paint, production providers, externally supervised lifecycle and whole-process-tree completeness remain unverified. No private raw logs, credentials or user state is included.

prs.title: fix: let Mac source builds package with the bundled Codex 0.169
prs.body:
Fixes #201255

## What Problem This Solves

Packaging the macOS app from source (`scripts/package-mac-app.sh`) fails when the Codex plugin is staged into the app. The runtime portability check rejects `codex-voice-host` from `@openai/codex` 0.169.0, which carries an LC_RPATH into Codex's Bazel build tree (`@loader_path/codex-voice-host.runfiles/...`). The existing rpath strip only matched the older `_solib_darwin_*` entry, so every source and dev Mac build stops at the check. 0.170.0 ships the same rpaths (reported upstream as openai/codex#62285).

## User Impact

Developers can package the Mac app from source with the bundled Codex 0.169.0. Release builds are unaffected: with a release tag the official plugins stay external and Codex is not staged into the app. Nothing a user can do in OpenClaw changes, because OpenClaw never starts the voice helper.

## Why This Change Was Made

`codex-voice-host` serves only the Codex TUI's realtime voice (`codex-rs/tui` -> `codex-realtime-webrtc` -> `VoiceHost` in Codex 0.169.0). The app-server and exec-server, the only Codex commands the Codex plugin starts, do not depend on it, and the plugin's "codex resume" terminal runs the user's own `codex` from PATH rather than the bundled copy.

So instead of rewriting the binary with `install_name_tool`, staging leaves `codex-resources/voice` out of the Mac Codex platform packages. That removes the rpath strip and about 20 MB of unused GStreamer libraries from source-built apps, and it keeps working whatever build-tree rpaths later Codex releases carry.

## Evidence

Contributor verification below is for d739e44a, before the Mac-only staging correction:

- **Packaging:** `scripts/package-mac-app.sh` (debug, arm64, ad-hoc signed, MLX TTS skipped) finished with `Verified app native dependencies (27 images)` and `Bundle ready`. The built app contains no `codex-resources` folder and no `codex-voice-host`.
- **Regression test:** `test/scripts/desktop-runtime-plugins.test.ts` builds a stand-in helper with the exact LC_RPATH set of the 0.169.0 binary. 23/23 pass on this branch; on the base commit (74e5127c0c3) the new test fails with the same `Nonportable LC_RPATH ... codex-voice-host.runfiles/...` error (1 failed, 22 passed).
- **Linux staging,** which shares `stampDesktopRuntimePlugins`: `node --test ../scripts/test-stage-runtime.mjs ../scripts/test-stage-package.mjs` from `apps/linux/src-tauri`, 25/25 pass.
- Typecheck `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json` and `git diff --check` are clean.

Not run: an x64 or universal package, and a release-tag package (Codex is not staged there).

### Mac-only staging correction — signed candidate `c72f0990`

The private per-architecture staging step now omits the TUI voice directory only when the source plan bundles Codex. It preserves the release-plan path and the original shared stamp API. The Linux caller and native portability auditor are unchanged from the PR base.

prs.title: fix: keep automatic memory saves out of project repositories
prs.body:
Related: #161253
Related alternative implementation: #162142 by leapdragon.

## What Problem This Solves

When a conversation runs in a selected project or managed worktree, automatic memory saves can create and write daily notes inside that repository instead of the configured agent workspace. This dirties the checkout and risks accidentally committing personal memory alongside project changes.

## User Impact

Automatic file-based memory saves stay in the configured agent workspace while ordinary turns retain their project context. Existing project-local memory is not moved or deleted; users should review any previously misplaced notes themselves. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the configured agent workspace at memory-flush preparation and use it consistently for the maintenance-only working directory, detached transcript, target creation, and execution. Tools-based memory plans retain their existing execution context.

For sandboxed flushes, the detached maintenance session owns the workspace identity while the original session still supplies the sandbox policy. Ordinary worktree containment checks remain in place.

This is our alternative to #162142: rather than carrying a new bootstrap workspace field through queued follow-up runs, it resolves the workspace at the maintenance owner and also handles the current sandbox identity/policy boundary. Credit to leapdragon for the related work; the other implementation was inspected, not executed, so this is not a claim that it fails. The memory documentation now explains placement and treatment of existing project notes.

## Evidence

- **Deterministic reproduction before the fix:** the real flush preparation, runtime/tool assembly, and append writer ran with a synthetic streaming provider. The aligned-workspace control passed; both selected-project cases (main and nondefault agents) wrote into the project instead of agent memory. These regressions pass with the fix.
- **Real UI verification after the fix:** the committed candidate Gateway and Control UI, built-in OpenClaw runtime, and an approved OpenAI subscription completed automatic memory saves for both a direct project and a managed worktree. Nonempty notes appeared only in agent memory; existing project/worktree notes remained byte-identical. Subsequent ordinary turns retained the correct project context. The documented flush threshold was lowered for the test; conversation compaction itself is not claimed. This is deterministic-red/live-green evidence, not a live-model before/after comparison.
- **Focused checks:** final affected-boundary batch: 72 tests across four files passed. An earlier broader batch passed 132 tests across 11 files; it was not wholly rerun after the final sandbox correction, and these overlapping counts must not be added. Targeted typechecks, lint, formatting, documentation sanity, and whitespace checks passed.
- **Container persistence:** two real rootless Podman cases passed with a synthetic provider, verifying agent-root mounts and durable writes, preserved project files, ordinary ownership rejection, and read-only flush skipping. This does not cover Docker or a full ordinary-worktree container lifecycle.
- **Review:** independent read-only agent review inspected every changed hunk in the nine-file local candidate based on `69bc33255cee52904ef42fe27acfdb79d060b740`, subsequently committed as `da0e5cca9d6106ee76aff3eecac28243ba4a2ce8`. No defect findings remained. This was not canonical autoreview, ClawSweeper, or maintainer/security approval; reviewers did not independently rerun the reported tests.
- **Build:** full build exited successfully; the committed-head rebuild also exited successfully and reused the Control UI content cache. The earlier build reported four nonfatal UI-budget findings (largest CSS gzip, total CSS gzip/raw, and chat boot request count). No base comparison attributed these findings to this change; they are not claimed resolved.

**Validation limitations:** the first live attempt selected native Codex implicitly and did not enter this maintenance path; configuring the intended built-in OpenClaw runtime corrected the test setup. Test isolation was imperfect: an initial container attempt created a generated skill mirror outside the task root and was rejected as isolated proof; the corrected run's mounts were verified. During live setup, Doctor deleted 58 shared legacy archive-cache files outside the isolated profile. Deleted contents were not recovered and downstream impact was not established. Isolated Gateway shutdown also reported plugin cleanup errors; task processes and listener were subsequently verified stopped. These observations are disclosed, not attributed to this patch or claimed fixed.

Hosted CI and applicable sensitive-product-change approval remain pending; no upstream validation is claimed.

## Inspectable behavior evidence

Captured on 2026-11-18; these are excerpts from retained outputs, not a new run. Live Gateway/Control UI proof used committed head `da0e5cca9d6106ee76aff3eecac28243ba4a2ce8`; the candidate build stamp and build-info matched that head. The Podman run preceded the commit on the same retained candidate source snapshot, not a separate committed-head rerun.

Each Podman case had its own temporary root, shown as `<CASE_ROOT>` within that case. Paths are replaced with `<LIVE_ROOT>` / `<CASE_ROOT>` / `<CONTAINER_ROOT>`; private model labels and irrelevant UI chrome are omitted. File contents and SHA-256 values below are unchanged synthetic fixture data. No raw configuration, credentials, endpoints, or private diagnostic logs are attached.

Each scenario used ordinary UI turns, not a direct flush invocation. The agent-memory directory started empty; the captured note appeared after the first ordinary reply, before its follow-up. The automatic maintenance transcript is detached and is not displayed in the ordinary chat. These file captures plus the visible follow-up text are the retained behavioral evidence; this is not a recording of the hidden maintenance turn.

prs.title: fix: keep a run going after a long tool call fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent's tool call stayed open for more than about six minutes and then failed, OpenClaw could stop the whole run as "Reply operation stalled" before the agent saw the result. Examples of failed results: an exec killed by the host exec memory budget, an exec that hit its timeout, or a tool that threw. The run is stopped only if the next model request has not started within about a second of the tool settling. That happens when something runs between the tool result and the next request, such as a context engine that owns compaction (for example lossless-claw) assembling context or compacting. A plain nonzero exit is not affected: exec reports it as `status: "completed"` with the exit code, which already counts as success.

## User Impact

A long tool that fails now hands its result back to the agent, which can react to it, instead of the run being cut off as stalled. Aborted tools still do not count as progress, so stopping a run behaves as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session watchdog keeps a run alive while a tool is open. When the tool closes, it restarts the stall timer only if the tool reports progress. The embedded tool wrapper reported progress only for a successful result. A long tool that failed therefore closed without progress, and the stall timer fell back to the last model progress, which by then was well in the past. Until the next model request registered its own deadline, the next one-second tick could stop the run.

The success-only filter comes from #166997. It decides when to clear the diagnostic "repeated requests without progress" evidence, and it is meant to ignore failed tools there. #175837 reused that same flag for the session watchdog. This change separates the two:

- The watchdog now counts any tool settlement that was not aborted, whether it succeeded or failed.
- Clearing the repeated-request evidence stays success-only, as #166997 intended.

The CLI runner and worker turn paths already count failed tool ends as progress, so the embedded wrapper now matches them. A loop of failing tool calls still cannot run forever on this alone, because each retry requires a model call.

Production change: two files, a net reduction of one line. The watchdog decision code is unchanged.

## Evidence

**End-to-end reproduction, red on base and green with the fix.** This ran on two isolated Mac Studio Gateways side by side: base `b413b8e` and PR head `2a6ce2d`. Each had its own home, state directory and port, and used a real model (`clawrouter/openai/gpt-6.1-sol`) with Code Mode off. Each Gateway also loaded a proof-only context engine that owns compaction and passes history through unchanged, but waits 5 seconds in its tool-loop `assemble()`, like a slow lossless-claw assembly. The agent ran exec once with `sleep 900` and `timeoutSeconds: 400`, which returns `status: "failed", timedOut: true` after 400 s.

| | Tool result | Post-tool `assemble()` delay | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base `b413b8e` | 22:52:03.116Z, `failed`, `timedOut: true` | 22:52:03.134Z → 22:52:08.135Z | `reply watchdog ... action=blocked` at 22:52:04.656Z, then `lane task error ... error="Reply operation stalled" staleReason=no_activity pendingTools=[]`; the CLI got `Reply operation stalled \| OPENCLAW_SESSION_WATCHDOG` and no reply |
| Head `2a6ce2d` | 22:52:03.106Z, `failed`, `timedOut: true` | 22:52:03.129Z → 22:52:08.129Z | Final reply at 22:52:12.400Z: `RESULT=timeout The sleep command was terminated after 400 seconds, as expected.` |

Base stopped about 1.5 s after the tool result, in the middle of the assembly delay, with the same signature as the incident (`staleReason=no_activity`, `pendingTools=[]`). Without the delay engine, base and head both survived, in a pass with a plain `exit 3` and again with the same timeout. The next model request started immediately, and its deadline kept the watchdog from stopping.

- Observed on a maintainer Gateway (2026.11.4) on 2026-11-18. A subagent exec started with `timeoutSeconds=2400` and was killed by the host exec memory budget after about 20 minutes (`isError=true`). Within about one second the run aborted with `SessionWatchdogError: Reply operation stalled` (`staleReason=no_activity`, `pendingTools=[]`, `durationMs=1653365`). The run was in lossless-claw assembly and compaction before its next model request.
- The new regression test drives the real tool wrapper against a real session watchdog. A tool stays open past the six-minute stall horizon and then settles in one of five ways: success, a failed result (`status: "failed"`, exit code 137), an error result, a thrown error, or abort. **On the base, the failed, error-result and thrown cases fail** (the watchdog decides `stop`). With the fix all five cases pass, and the aborted case still decides `stop`.
- Tests of the affected consumers pass (11 files): session watchdog, CLI runner command progress, worker turn run owner, controller recovery integration, the exec-deadline stuck-session test, code-mode bridge lifecycle, stalled-turn runner, tool-search scheduling, before-tool-call diagnostics and approval recovery, and the liveness carrier.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and the agents-root test typecheck shard pass. oxfmt and oxlint report no problems on the changed files.
- An independent local review found no P0–P2 issues.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: improve: reduce streaming session broadcast work for multiple viewers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Broadcasting session updates to viewers with different permissions repeatedly prepares the same subagent display facts. During busy streaming sessions this adds CPU and allocation work to each broadcast, even when its rows are unchanged.

## User Impact

Session updates use less Gateway work when several audiences watch the same activity. Message content, row presentation, ancestor updates, and recipient permissions remain unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

The measurements below cover the in-memory publication owners, not whole-Gateway latency or production savings. Maintainer review accepted this focused proof for landing: this change performs no storage I/O, so database size and filesystem type do not affect the changed operation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Immutable rows already reuse prepared presentation facts. The redundant work is rebuilding the subagent display-time view for every audience within the same synchronous publication. Prepare that existing view once at the publication owner, keep its existing registry-revision witness, and pass it to recipient presentations. Sharing and authority checks remain recipient-local; direct presentation callers retain their existing preparation.

Ancestor rows remain necessary for client parent rollups. Existing message/row serialization sharing remains unchanged. Production code grows by five lines for the prepared-input handoff; there is no new cross-event cache, schema, or configuration. The existing ancestor benchmark gains explicit identity-count and baseline-traversal inputs so it can compare current baselines without weakening its traversal assertion.

## Evidence

The regression exercises real prepared-row and connection-broadcast owners with three nested sessions, eight profiles, and 32 connections. On warm unchanged-row events, the base prepares eight display-time views and the fix prepares one. The candidate performs zero underlying row reconstructions; changed message bodies and full-then-reference ancestor delivery remain intact. The regression fails on the base and passes with the fix. Focused publication, authority, ancestry, parity, and connection tests also pass (25 tests total).

Acceptance is reduced repeated preparation, CPU, and sampled allocation without changed delivery counts or payloads. Five counterbalanced pairs use 10,000 events per arm for untraced thread CPU and 3,000 per arm in separate sampled-allocation runs. Two counterbalanced A/A pairs per metric load identical baseline source. Node v26.12.1 on macOS/APFS; warm owner throughput, fixed display clocks, serial runs within this task, host load recorded.

| Owner workload | Metric per event | Base median | Candidate median | Change | Same-source A/A median shift |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Presentation, 65 viewers / 16 audiences | CPU | 224.80 µs | 200.08 µs | −11.00% | −3.69% |
| Presentation, 65 viewers / 16 audiences | Sampled allocation | 576,394 B | 511,947 B | −11.18% | −1.31% |
| Ancestor publication, 1,600 sessions / 65 viewers / eight identities | CPU | 461.65 µs | 448.06 µs | −2.94% | −1.76% |
| Ancestor publication, 1,600 sessions / 65 viewers / eight identities | Sampled allocation | 1,127,949 B | 1,099,685 B | −2.51% | +0.24% |

The complete publication gain is modest relative to A/A variation. Median per-arm consume p99 is 0.769 → 0.755 ms, with no >100 ms stalls in these runs. Every event retains one ancestor traversal, 32 membership reads, and 65 deliveries. Presentation output is byte-identical; the ancestor workload matches after normalizing only independently generated ancestor revision UUIDs under its existing comparison contract.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and spread</summary>

Use `scripts/perf/session-event-audience-measure.ts` and `scripts/perf/session-event-ancestors-measure.ts`. Save the base presentation beside the current owner; for the lifecycle benchmark, save its base projector and lifecycle module with their relative owner imports redirected to those saved files. All other dependencies remain identical.

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-event-audience-measure.ts --base-owner src/gateway/.base-presentation.ts --events 10000 --pairs 5
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-event-ancestors-measure.ts --base-owner src/gateway/.base-lifecycle.ts --base-traversals 1 --identities 8 --clients 65 --sessions 1600 --events 10000 --pairs 5
```

For separate allocation runs, use `--events 3000 --allocations` and separate `--state-root` directories. For A/A, point `--owner` and `--base-owner` at the same saved source.

Presentation CPU ranges: 219.45–229.22 → 197.43–203.69 µs/event. Presentation allocation ranges: 575,192–588,108 → 509,360–513,918 B/event. Ancestor CPU ranges: 436.62–463.27 → 435.42–450.91 µs/event. Ancestor allocation ranges: 1,125,254–1,131,177 → 1,094,930–1,101,620 B/event. With five samples, nearest-rank p95 is each range's maximum.

prs.title: improve(state): reduce CPU spent admitting shared-state reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shared-state reads spend main-thread CPU recursively measuring request metadata and payload-free commands before entering the worker queue. The generic array reducer also creates substantial temporary allocation when reads carry thousands of session selectors.

## User Impact

Session-list prerequisite reads use less host CPU and allocation for queue accounting. Large selector batches retain their full byte charge. Queue limits, results, authority, configuration, schemas, and stored data are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the actual command shape to skip recursive accounting only when its sole enumerable field is `type`. Extra fields always retain full accounting, even for a normally payload-free command. This avoids a second per-command schema that could silently omit newly added payloads. Count paths and the captured environment directly, and replace the recursive array reducer with a loop.

The byte cap remains necessary: `WorkerTaskAdmission` charges pending input before asynchronous preparation, with a 256 MiB default alongside the independent 128-task cap. A count cap or later worker transfer cannot bound a large queued selector. History through #151929 and #160946 confirms this accounting predates the snapshot-lifecycle refactor. #200979 already handles frozen engine selections and explicitly established that there is no existing serialized command length to reuse.

There is no new cache or freshness polling. Session-row projection files are untouched. Production grows by 9 lines to separate flat metadata from recursive payload accounting and preserve a shape guard; this removes the callback closure and temporary path array without adding a command-kind registry. Tests add 30 lines; benchmark tooling extends the existing workload.

## Evidence

Acceptance: preserve admission charges and results, improve owner CPU/allocation beyond the identical-source A/A spread, and introduce no >20% sibling regression. Five serial A1/A2/B triplets per source-derived command shape; each fresh process verifies exact charges before a warmed timed burst. Small shapes use 100,000 fresh request/context/environment envelopes; shared facts use 2,000 requests selecting 5,000 synthetic sessions. CPU is main-thread CPU and allocation is cumulative V8 allocated bytes on Node 26.12.1. With five samples, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum.

| Shape | A1 CPU median / p95 (µs/request) | A2 CPU median / p95 | B CPU median / p95 | A2 → B allocated B/request |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Payload-free session-list prerequisites | 0.352 / 0.356 | 0.349 / 0.350 | 0.264 / 0.269 | 756.82 → 247.05 |
| Mixed small reads | 0.465 / 0.474 | 0.467 / 0.470 | 0.398 / 0.401 | 864.61 → 251.10 |
| 5,000-row shared-facts batch | 3,064.080 / 3,072.204 | 3,057.322 / 3,127.215 | 2,885.030 / 2,938.905 | 2,681,415.22 → 484.02 |

CPU improves about 24%, 15%, and 5.6% respectively. Every paired CPU result improves; A/A changes range from −2.72% to +1.83%, versus candidate improvements of 3.94–25.82%. All **3,030,000 charge comparisons** match. Shared-host one-minute load averages range from 7.46 to 41.85. In the large-batch rerun, A2 → B wall-time median/p95 was 3,540.455/4,259.506 → 3,006.348/4,544.937 µs/request; CPU is the less noisy owner metric under that load.

A separate real `executeExistingOpenClawStateRead`/worker/SQL comparison uses 10,000 synthetic sessions and cron jobs, alternating 500-selector reads. Both arms complete 300 admissions with identical charge and reply digests. This single composition check is not a latency claim: main CPU was 1.630 → 1.728 ms/read, p95 4.539 → 4.868 ms, and allocation 917,934 → 828,284 B/read. The supported performance claim is the repeated accounting-owner microbenchmark.

These are source-derived fixtures, not measured production command frequencies. `subagents.sessionList`, `sessionGroups.snapshot`, and `userProfiles.catalog` are payload-free; `sessionRows.sharedFacts` and placement/key-list reads carry unbounded selectors. The profile stack alone cannot establish their production mix. No production data or live service was accessed, and this does not claim 35-GiB database or filesystem performance.

The regression exercises the real pool's pre-preparation byte refusal for 4,096 large selectors, including extra payload on a normally type-only command. A negative-control implementation that fast-paths that command by kind undercharges and fails the test. This is a behavior-preserving optimization, so the original estimator is expected to satisfy the memory-bound test. Existing exhaustive UTF-16 and queued-selector capture tests remain intact.

All 26 focused request/transport tests pass (49.13 s wrapper wall time, 43.72 s Vitest duration, primarily compiler preparation; new bound test 29 ms). Independent Codex autoreview of the complete staged diff against `a90c5419b779df517ea3c3ea0bee0b37e87f85ac`, with consumer and admission source context, is scoped-clean through P2. No Control UI import reaches the changed production module. `pnpm check:changed --staged` completed. It caught a numeric lifecycle revision in the new benchmark fixture; that field is now a valid synthetic UUID string, script typechecking passes on replay, and all 15 affected benchmark runs were repeated. The preliminary invalid-fixture runs are excluded from the table. All other aggregate checks passed except an unrelated full-tree UI unused export; the same single finding reproduces with Knip 6.40.0 on an isolated, dependency-resolved checkout of exact parent `a90c5419b779df517ea3c3ea0bee0b37e87f85ac`. No module-resolution errors occurred. The starting commit `a90c5419b779df517ea3c3ea0bee0b37e87f85ac` (#198967) removed the last caller of `expectPendingNewSessionPresentation` in `ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.transition.e2e.test.ts`, leaving its export in `new-session-page.test-support.ts`. This is a main regression requiring follow-up, not a waived passing check. There is no claim of a green aggregate check.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```sh
git show a90c5419b779df517ea3c3ea0bee0b37e87f85ac:src/state/openclaw-state-read-request.ts > /path/to/baseline.ts
# A1 and A2, then B; repeat five times for each shape:
node scripts/perf/state-read-request-bytes.ts --baseline /path/to/baseline.ts --module /path/to/baseline.ts --shape session-list
node scripts/perf/state-read-request-bytes.ts --baseline /path/to/baseline.ts --shape session-list
# Repeat with --shape mixed and --shape shared-facts.
```

For real owner composition, put the baseline module at `<baseline-dir>/src/state/openclaw-state-read-request.ts`, use new equal-length output directory names, and compare result/charge digests:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/state-read-worker-bench.ts --output /path/to/fixture-aa --kind mixed --readonly --iterations 100 --verify-charges --owner-dir /path/to/baseline-dir
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/state-read-worker-bench.ts --output /path/to/fixture-bb --kind mixed --readonly --iterations 100 --verify-charges
```

</details>

prs.title: fix: preserve complete Tool Search network pages
prs.body:
Closes #194857

## What Problem This Solves

Reading a long web page or paged MCP document through Tool Search could stop at 20,000 characters even when the active model could accept more. A continuation cursor could survive while the end of its page was missing, silently skipping document lines.

## User Impact

Network-backed Tool Search calls use the active model's existing tool-result budget, including external-content framing, sanitization expansion, and forwarded image context costs. No new setting or migration is required; tool-selection defaults, policy checks, and native harness behavior are unchanged.

If a complete execution result cannot fit, its payload is omitted instead of exposing a cursor for a partial page. Read-only callers are told to request a smaller page from the same starting position, and not to replay mutations just to recover output. Full programmatic details remain intact. Discovery still retains useful schema excerpts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing model-aware budget rather than add another configuration limit. Shared rendering keeps Code Mode fitting and final delivery aligned; batch discovery rejects omitted trial renders rather than mistaking their short notice for delivered candidates.

The fixed 20,000-character policy is removed. Necessary growth is budget propagation, cursor-safe omission, and preservation of discovery excerpts: +75 net production lines, +152 net test lines, and +9 documentation lines against the task base.

## Evidence

- Both reported failures reproduced through actual `dispatch_action` execution in the Agent loop with its context guard: malformed partial pages on a 320k context and cursors for undelivered page tails on a 32k context. Both regressions failed before the repair.
- **181 focused tests passed across eight files** (59 seconds wall time including compiler preparation): gap-free 78-line retrieval, smaller-page recovery, mixed image/text pages, remote discovery batches, sanitization, retained details, Code Mode budgets, termination, and prefix stability.
- **Real-model end-to-end proof passed** through an isolated admitted OpenClaw runner with `gpt-5.4-mini`: one search, two dispatched network pages, four assistant turns, and exact freshly generated markers from lines 47 and 78. The first page exceeded the old cap. Test time was 14.4 seconds (76 seconds wall); no live Gateway state was changed.
- Full `pnpm build` passed in 180 seconds. Core and agents-tools test typechecks, targeted lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent final review found no remaining substantive P0–P2 findings after the batch-admission and image-reservation repairs.
- [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44411564711/job/135187384405) for `deada7dc25d490ad662a290d2def73cf6d131584`; `openclaw/ci-gate` was verified successful on that head. Hosted ClawSweeper review was still running at the landing check and is advisory under the explicit maintainer land instruction.

Requested by @vincentkoc; reported by @lyrakat.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/32a7bc03-9db5-4de0-bda1-0d3828a0832e)

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc

prs.title: fix(android): finish setup after node access is approved
prs.body:
Closes #201481

## What Problem This Solves

Android setup can remain on “Approve node access” after the phone has already been approved. With Camera enabled, Gateway policy can admit the capability and permission while withholding capture commands; setup incorrectly waits for those commands. Background refreshes also make the exact approval command flicker and fall back to a literal `REQUEST_ID`.

## User Impact

Users should be able to finish setup once their enabled capabilities and permissions are approved, without requiring commands the Gateway deliberately disallows. The recovery screen keeps a known request ID stable during reads and only shows an exact approve command when an ID exists.

**Draft: not yet built, installed, or verified on a phone.** The affected user’s recovery is not confirmed. No Gateway policy, pairing, authentication, or command permission is changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate onboarding capability readiness from policy-owned command admission. Explicit in-app approval still verifies the entire actual pending surface, approved/connected state, authority, and request identity. Preserve the previous approval snapshot during refresh, retire exact IDs on failed reads or connection invalidation, and preserve ID-less pending states so polling can recover after repeated failures. A manual check can continue from verified readiness even if Compose never observes a very short refreshing state.

## Evidence

- Live observation with Android 2026.11.40 / Gateway 2026.11.4: phone connected and approved, no pending request, Camera capability and permission present, but `camera.snap`/`camera.clip` absent from admitted commands. The same filtering occurs before the pairing request is stored. No private device identifiers or setup credentials are included here.
- Added regression coverage for policy-filtered Camera commands, retention of request IDs during reads, consecutive failed reads followed by recovery, and nullable recovery commands/manual-check readiness. Extended the existing WebSocket/Compose onboarding test rather than recreating the screen.
- Independent read-only review found a repeated-failure polling defect in the initial patch; addressed with a runtime-boundary regression. Follow-up found no remaining P0–P2 issues in the reviewed diff. Canonical shared autoreview tooling was unavailable; this was direct independent review, not an autoreview run.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Android compilation and focused tests: **blocked before execution** by missing Android SDK (`SDK location not found`). Gradle/JDK and pinned source dependencies were prepared, but no SDK/emulator or attached adb device is available in this environment. No remote Android build capacity is provisioned.
- `./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck --no-daemon --max-workers=2`: passed after fixing the reported style violations (21 actionable tasks). This is formatting/lint proof, not Android compilation or behavioral test proof.
- Required clean and annotated before/after native UI captures: **missing** for the same device/emulator gap. Red/green runtime proof is also outstanding. Keep draft until the exact head passes the required build/tests and visual-proof gates. Automatic PR CI may skip drafts; a maintainer or qualified Android runner must supply exact-head proof before ready/merge.

Intended focused validation from `apps/android`:

```sh
./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.GatewayNodeApprovalTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.GatewayDevicePairingRuntimeTest.nodeRefreshKeepsIdsDuringReadsAndRecoversAfterRepeatedFailures \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.OnboardingFlowLogicTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.InitialOnboardingLayoutTest.nativeNodeApprovalWaitsForCameraButNotPolicyBlockedCaptureCommands \
  :app:ktlintCheck --no-daemon --max-workers=2
```

prs.title: fix: let PostgreSQL Gateways start with plugin-backed secrets
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

A cold Gateway using PostgreSQL for shared state can fail while preparing valid plugin-backed secrets. Secrets preparation now reads plugin metadata through the worker. Web-provider discovery passes the installed-plugin records and migration readiness it read to the scoped loader. External channel contracts reuse the prepared manifest registry.

Related to #201058.

### Scope

Three small adjustments keep every secrets-preparation path on the worker-read facts:

- Plugin metadata is now also loaded when the only plugin-backed surface is a web tool (`tools.web` search or fetch config, via `hasRuntimeWebToolConfigSurface`), so web-tool-only configs get the prepared manifest registry instead of a later synchronous read.
- Plugin metadata is also loaded when only the `assignmentConfig` needs it, so a projected assignment config does not fall back to a synchronous read.
- The channel secret collector skips the `channels.defaults` key. It is shared channel defaults, not a channel id; without the skip, a config whose only channel key is `defaults` would look up a channel contract for it and fall into the synchronous config-wide manifest resolver.

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway that keeps shared state in PostgreSQL could fail to start from cold when its config uses plugin-backed secrets, for example a web search provider plugin with a SecretRef API key. Secrets preparation runs on the Gateway main thread, and plugin metadata, installed-plugin records and migration readiness were read synchronously there. PostgreSQL connections are only allowed from the database worker, so startup stopped with `PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker` before any credential was resolved. SQLite Gateways were not affected.

## Root Cause

The synchronous manifest resolver on the Gateway thread opened PostgreSQL while loading plugin metadata. The regression fixture reproduced the actual admission error, `PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker`, with both a fresh ledger and a committed migration receipt.

Switching only the metadata read leaves a second path through web-provider discovery and the synchronous loader. The loader checks migration readiness. Its asynchronous reader publishes a reusable readiness result only when the process has a committed migration receipt. A fresh ledger can therefore return an empty result from the worker and still cause a synchronous PostgreSQL read afterward. The loader now consumes that empty result explicitly. No cache policy or admission guard changes.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

The fixture opens a disposable PostgreSQL shared-state store, installs the Gateway process role, and verifies that the real guard refuses synchronous PostgreSQL connections on the test thread. It calls `prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot` and uses a local plugin that registers a web search provider. Success means the named provider was selected and the synthetic SecretRef was materialized.

```sh
# Set POSTGRES_TEST_PRELOAD to the file URL for
# scripts/test-database-conformance-preload.mjs with connection=<encoded test DSN>.
NODE_OPTIONS="--import=$POSTGRES_TEST_PRELOAD" pnpm test src/secrets/runtime-web-provider.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

- Before, PostgreSQL stopped at the admission guard in both cases. SQLite passed.
- After, PostgreSQL with no receipt, PostgreSQL with a receipt, and SQLite all passed (`Tests 3 passed (3)`). Local PostgreSQL was 16.16 with a dedicated database and non-superuser role. The test file ran in 8.89 seconds including test setup and transform on the final run.
- The new test is a `.postgres.test.ts` suite, so the hosted PostgreSQL conformance job runs it on this head.

### Verification

- Final local run passed 39 tests across the PostgreSQL regression, web tools, and core secrets snapshots. Channel-contract, plugin-origin, and plugin-loader sibling tests passed before the final web-tools simplification.
- Targeted formatting, type-aware lint and type checking, and `git diff --check` passed.
- [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201063/checks) provides the broad and fork-head checks. On the previous head, the hosted PostgreSQL conformance job ran `src/secrets/runtime-web-provider.postgres.test.ts` and all three cases passed.
- A follow-up test-only commit marks the three updated install-record and manifest mocks as intentionally isolated (`// mock-isolation:`) and drops their superseded entries from `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt`. This fixes the baseline-ratchets mock-exports check; no runtime code changed.
- Remaining CI red is inherited from `main`: `checks-node-changed-compact-large-3` fails only `src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts` "uses fresh revisions after agent create, update, and delete before reload applies" (`gateway request timeout for agents.delete`). Scheduled `main` [run 44401396829](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44401396829/job/135146008105) fails the same test with the same error in the same shard. Its fixture config has no SecretRefs, plugin entries, channels, or web tools, so secrets preparation takes the fast path and never reaches the code this PR changes.

## What was not tested

Full Gateway socket startup, live provider calls, and production startup latency were outside this focused run. The PostgreSQL baseline stopped before credential materialization, so there is no successful before/after latency comparison for the repaired path. The fixture disables bundled plugins, so the bundled web-provider path and the web-tool-only metadata trigger are covered by the existing unit suites, not by the PostgreSQL regression.

prs.title: feat(doctor): check OpenClaw ID member roles and honor an optional roles default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor does not know that `gateway.roles.default` is optional or that OpenClaw ID member roles come from `gateway.roles.definitions`. With role definitions and no default, it wrongly reports that automations will lose owner access. It also has no check for a member whose role is not defined, for missing preset roles, or for role settings that have no effect.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw doctor` reports member-role problems in plain words and can write missing preset roles after asking.

- Fixed: with role definitions and no default, Doctor no longer reports that an automation "will lose access at the next run" or that owner status is unverified.
- New checks when OpenClaw ID is on:
  - a member whose role has no definition, with the member and role named;
  - a missing preset definition, with a repair that writes it. The repair asks first and says that the config file is rewritten as JSON and loses its comments;
  - a sandbox-required role held by a member, or set as the default, when no sandbox backend is available.
- New check for any Gateway: stored role assignments with no `gateway.roles.default`, which means named-role enforcement is off and the assignments have no effect.
- A Gateway with no `gateway.roles`, and one with a default set and OpenClaw ID off, get the same Doctor output as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The cron ownership checks and the replay script now ask whether named-role enforcement is on, as runtime admission does, and no longer test for the presence of `gateway.roles`.
- The member checks read the local claw record, so they work with the Gateway stopped. A claw that has never linked has no record and gets no warning. A record that exists and cannot be read, or whose member list is malformed, is reported with a fixed message that contains nothing from the record.
- The preset repair uses the same code as turning on OpenClaw ID: it adds only missing presets and never writes `default` or `assignments`. Like every Doctor repair that writes config, it also records Doctor's usual last-run metadata.
- Docs for roles and OpenClaw ID describe the optional default, member presets, which role applies to a connection, and what a sandbox-required role does and does not contain.

## Evidence

- Doctor suites: 31 tests in 3 files pass at the review-fix commit. A reviewer separately ran 94 tests in 6 files, covering Doctor, activation presets, the config schema and Doctor's consent modes, all passing.
- Core and test typechecks, lint, format and ratchets pass.
- Independent review found no P0 or P1 and three P2 in the new member check: a corrupt record could put a fragment of an invite key into Doctor's output, a malformed member list passed silently, and a never-linked install got a false warning. The fourth commit fixes all three, with a test that plants a synthetic secret in a corrupt record and asserts none of it is printed. A second review found nothing.
- Two docs anchor checks fail the same way on `main`, in pages this PR does not touch.

Not run: a whole-Doctor output comparison against the parent, a repair while a live Gateway reloads, and real Docker or Podman probing.

Rebased onto main (`b0b88a8fab94`). This PR changes no Gateway runtime behavior: the claw store is identical to main, so a malformed stored member list loads exactly as before. Doctor detects it on its own: it reads the stored claw record through a read-only parser used only by Doctor, and reports a malformed member list or an unreadable record with the fixed message above. What the Gateway itself should do with such a record is a separate follow-up. After the rebase: 156 focused, state-path and storage tests, 197 Doctor and cron tests (2 PostgreSQL-gated skips) and the Doctor tests under CI's pinned Bun pass, with typechecks, static checks and ratchets.

Known, not changed here: the development replay script (`scripts/dev/cron-context-replay.mts`) fails with "User profile catalog is not ready" when replaying a job under a named `gateway.roles.default`; it reproduces the same way on main, and Doctor's own checks are unaffected.

Live proof on this head: both builds and an unlinked preflight on a second isolated machine passed (never-linked Doctor silent; consented preset repair adds only the missing preset; declining leaves config byte-identical; Doctor alongside a running Gateway). Two attempts to repeat the linked checks against real staging services stopped on test-harness problems before reaching them; no product failure was found. The linked Doctor checks passed live on the previous head. Because the Gateway's stored-data loading is byte-identical to main in this PR, upgrade compatibility rests on that identity, the exact-head review and the tests; the maintainer chose to land on that basis.

prs.title: fix(memory): spawned sessions lose memory after their parent compacts or rewinds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a spawned session permanently loses memory access (`stale-lineage`) after its parent session compacts or rewinds, even though the parent was never reset.

## User Impact

User impact: subagents and other spawned sessions keep their inherited memory audience when the parent session compacts or rewinds. Resetting, replacing or recreating the parent still revokes it, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

A spawn receipt records the parent's `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision`. The lineage walk compared both on every ancestor hop. But the parent's `sessionId` also changes within one incarnation:

- **Compaction**: `acceptCompactionSuccessor` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compaction-successor.ts`) patches only `sessionId` to the successor id and keeps `lifecycleRevision`.
- **Rewind and branch switch**: `planSessionMessageCut` (`src/config/sessions/session-message-cut-plan.ts`) mints a new `sessionId` and keeps `lifecycleRevision` unless the mode is `fork`.

Resets do the opposite. They mint a new revision and may keep the `sessionId` (`session-reset-service.ts`, and automatic resets in `auto-reply/reply/session.ts`, `agent-command.ts` and `agent-session-patch.ts`). So the revision identifies the incarnation, and the session id does not.

In the observed incident, child `773c6854…` had a receipt naming parent `327d1145…` at revision `142ed0a3…`. The parent row moved to `460182f7…` with the same revision `142ed0a3…`, and every child turn after that was denied.

Changes:
- Ancestor hops compare only the receipt's lifecycle revision
- Legacy receipts without a revision still compare `sessionId`
- Depth 0 and scheduled-parent links are unchanged
- A root conversation audience uses the root's current `sessionId`
- A killed-main CLI rollover now mints a new revision

The current-`sessionId` change matters because Knowledge keys `conversations/<sessionId>` partitions by this value. After rotation, the child shares the partition the parent now writes, not the retired one. On every path that granted before this change, the value is the same.

The revision change for a killed-main rollover closes a replacement that kept its revision. When a killed main session's transcript is newer than its registry row, `agent-command` starts a fresh transcript with cleared metadata (`isNewSession` without `automaticReset`). It changed only the `sessionId`, which the old session-id comparison happened to catch. It now mints a revision like every other rollover, as `agent-session-patch.ts` already does for the same case on the Gateway path.

Scheduled-parent links are unchanged on purpose. Cron's own admission (`classifyScheduledParent` in `src/cron/execution-context.ts`) already treats a link `sessionId` change as `reset` and runs the occurrence as an unbound parent. That occurrence never reaches this check with a parent memory source. Relaxing only the memory check would be unreachable and inconsistent with cron, so a compaction-tolerant cron link belongs in a separate change.

Generation leases are not affected. `leaseSessionGeneration` binds each hop's *current* `sessionId` and revision, so a rotation before resolution revokes nothing. A rotation during a turn revokes only that turn's grant, and the next turn resolves again.

Accepted edge case: `agent --session-id <id>` on an existing key retargets `sessionId` without a new revision. That is an explicit resume of the same logical session, so spawned children keep memory across it.

## Evidence

New real-SQLite test `src/plugins/memory-audience.lineage-rotation.test.ts`. It commits real rows, calls the real production mutations and resolves the child through the real read worker:

- Parent rewind (`rewindSessionToMessage`): granted, with the audience on the rotated id
- Parent compaction (`acceptCompactionSuccessor`): granted, with the audience on the rotated id
- Parent reset (`performGatewaySessionReset`): denied `stale-lineage`
- Legacy receipt without a revision, then parent rewind: denied `stale-lineage`, as before

Without the memory-audience fix, the rewind and compaction cases fail with `has stale lineage: ancestor agent:main:root was reset or removed`. The reset and legacy cases pass both with and without it.

New `src/commands/agent.session-rollover.test.ts` runs `agentCommand` on a killed main session whose transcript is newer than its row. Without the `agent-command` change it fails with `expected 'killed-main-revision' not to be 'killed-main-revision'`. With the change it passes.

`memory-audience.test.ts` drops the fake-store case that asserted a `spawnedBySessionId` mismatch at the same revision is stale. That case encoded the bug.

- `vitest run src/plugins/memory-audience.test.ts src/plugins/memory-provider-runtime.audience.test.ts src/plugins/memory-audience.lineage-rotation.test.ts`: 46 passed
- `vitest run src/commands/agent.test.ts src/commands/agent.session.test.ts`: 73 passed, 1 failed. The failure is environmental. The managed-worktree helper's temp ancestor `/tmp/openclaw-agent-*/.openclaw` was world-writable on the test host, and this diff does not touch that path.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck core and core tests, lint and every guard passed. The dead-export scan failed on main-inherited exports in untouched files (`src/daemon/launchd.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.ts`, `src/plugins/provider-external-auth.ts`, `src/plugins/provider-runtime.ts`, `src/plugins/types.ts`, `ui/src/pages/dashboards/dashboard-tools.tsx`). The format failure was fixed before push.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup can reject a read when a schema owner arrives after host admission, and native registry inspection failures can lose their diagnostic causes. This main-first release repair also makes the compaction timeout fixture start its controlled clock at the watchdog boundary rather than racing cold startup.

## User Impact

Startup waits for transient schema ownership without replaying a read, still refuses offline maintenance, and preserves native failure reasons and paths. The compaction change is test-only. No schema, stored-data, retention, permission, or configuration changes are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

These are the three prepared main-first repairs authorized for OpenClaw 2026.11.6 qualification. Worker admission reuses the existing cold-admission owner; preflight associates captured inspection errors with the existing cause map. The fixture keeps startup on real timers and only controls the watchdog timeout case. Direct main publication was refused by the repository pull-request rule, so this PR uses the enforced route.

## Evidence

- Worker handoff: exact baseline regression fails for a foreign schema owner; fixed startup bootstrap 10/10 on Node and pinned Bun, plus 34 sibling cases. Types, lint, formatting and test-line allocation passed.
- Native inspection causes: new main regressions fail on unchanged production (10 pass, 2 fail); fixed startup-integrity 12/12 and four sibling files 42/42 on each runtime. Native SQLite authorizer exercises real startup worker/IPC and Doctor paths. Types, lint and formatting passed.
- Compaction fixture: 6/6 on Node and pinned Bun; targeted typecheck, lint and formatting passed. An injected 1200ms preparation delay is red before and green after; original CI causation is NOT established.
- Existing independent final-patch reviews found no actionable findings. No autoreview, ClawSweeper run, or hosted re-review is requested; the session explicitly opted out. Required repository checks still apply.
- All three prepared patch SHA-256 values verified; they apply unchanged on main c5ef395ba7204c83240074b584e97f550a3aab7d. No intervening commits changed these seven files. Signed commits preserve both requested co-author trailers.

Remaining release proof: real-model Gateway / macOS packaged-fresh validation and full exact-source release qualification remain outstanding and are not claimed here. This PR does not publish a release or change release tooling, waivers, or qualification policy.

prs.title: fix(state): PostgreSQL state created before Template bootstrap deferral is refused as schema drift
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

People who run OpenClaw with PostgreSQL shared state could not upgrade from v2026.11.5: update and Doctor refused the existing database as schema drift. Stores created by main builds from before 2026-11-10 hit the same refusal. This change lets those stores migrate in place while unrelated drift is still refused.

## Summary

### High Level TLDR

PostgreSQL shared-state stores from OpenClaw v2026.11.5 were rejected during upgrade because the new build expected a column the released database never had. The existing migration to state schema 40 now adds that column when needed. Stores that already have it keep their values.

Schema 39 had two main-build layouts. Inspection, migration, and backup use the matching exact layout for either one. The migration checks the full predecessor catalog and seals the full destination catalog in the same transaction.

Fixes #196966.

## Root Cause

The Template bootstrap deferral change added `workspace_setup_state.bootstrap_deferred` to generated PostgreSQL DDL while state schema remained at 39. The migration chain reconstructs earlier catalogs from the current DDL. It consequently expected the column even for the schema-36 catalog shipped by v2026.11.5. On the frozen released catalog, unpatched main returned `PostgreSQL schema drift detected against generated DDL` during predecessor inspection. The writable chain uses the same verifier before the first migration step.

## Real behavior proof

Run against disposable PostgreSQL 16 with `POSTGRES_CONFORMANCE_URL` pointing to the test database.

```sh
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres \
  --connection "$POSTGRES_CONFORMANCE_URL" -- \
  src/state/openclaw-state-db-bootstrap-deferral.postgres.test.ts \
  src/infra/database-engine/schema-admission.postgres.test.ts \
  src/infra/database-engine/doctor-migration.postgres.test.ts \
  src/infra/database-engine/backup-schema-capture.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 -t 'PostgreSQL shared state bootstrap deferral upgrade|PostgreSQL schema admission|backs up and restores the real version 36|captures the predecessor before migration|rolls back partial DDL|retires server captures through supervised migrate and finish'
```

The suite uses the DDL emitted by v2026.11.5 (schema 36) and both historical main-build schema-39 layouts. It checks predecessor inspection and the backup source without changing the seal, migrates through the real shared-state writer, reads the retained setup row and expected flag, and closes and reopens the store with the schema-40 seal. The unrelated-column case refuses migration and leaves the predecessor metadata unchanged.

## Evidence

- After the fix, on disposable PostgreSQL 16.16: the focused selection reported `Test Files 4 passed (4)` and `Tests 23 passed | 31 skipped (54)`, including all four new upgrade cases (released schema 36, both schema-39 layouts, and unrelated drift still refused).
- Before the fix, on unpatched main: the released schema-36 case and the schema-39 case without the column both failed with the reported refusal, `PostgreSQL schema drift detected against generated DDL. Use a compatible OpenClaw binary or restore the matching PostgreSQL schema and anchor; do not edit schema metadata.`, thrown from `verifyPostgresSchemaDefinition` during store admission.

## Verification

- PostgreSQL 16.16 on the exact pushed tree reported `Test Files 4 passed (4)` and `Tests 23 passed | 31 skipped (54)`. All four new regression cases ran. The selection also covered shared-state Doctor backup and restore, rollback after failed DDL, supervised recovery capture, and strict catalog admission.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, changed-file format, and `git diff --check` passed. The PostgreSQL conformance inventory includes the new suite.
- The migration and backup changes passed a source readiness pass. An independent maintainer review of this head found no code defects and confirmed the seeded schema-36 and schema-39 layouts match the DDL generated by those historical builds.
- Hosted CI on the first head ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44396030701)) passed every job except PostgreSQL conformance shard 4/4, where six existing shared-state tests failed with `PostgreSQL catalog differs from its generated contract`. Those tests relabel a freshly bootstrapped store as schema 24 to 28 but kept the new `bootstrap_deferred` column, a layout no real store at those versions has. The follow-up test commit rebuilds the empty `workspace_setup_state` table from the historical DDL, the same way the helper already rebuilds the worker tables. No product code changed.
- [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44408307224) runs on the current head, including all PostgreSQL conformance shards.

## What was not tested

This used disposable stores and the production database owners. It did not deploy a release or start an installed Gateway against operator data. The broken upgrade has no successful baseline duration for a comparison. Hosted CI covers the broader PostgreSQL conformance suite.

prs.title: fix: restore projection tests for admitted operator requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two managed-workspace tests fail on main after #201334 because they still treat a role change as cancellation of already-admitted operator work. This maintainer-requested main repair aligns those expectations with the existing request admission contract.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. Already-admitted checkpoint settlement and guest filesystem writes remain allowed after a role change; the next admission is refused. Explicit source cancellation and Gateway shutdown still refuse privileged writes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The older delegated-authority doctrine was explicitly superseded by #197557 (`123f8787c4767`): root `AGENTS.md` says authority is checked when work starts and revocation applies to the next request; the agent guide distinguishes calls already in progress from calls after lifecycle closure. #201334 (`04cb8179ccd66`) applies that rule to Gateway operator-derived turns, while preserving source assertions, cancellation, exact run/claim, physical-store and credential fences. Restoring role-policy reads at every checkpoint would reverse that intentional contract.

The existing boundary fixture now proves the distinction: an admitted guest filesystem write reaches canonical storage after its role changes, reauthorization refuses, and an explicit source cancellation prevents another filesystem write even after a delayed native involvement receipt arrives. Command settlement similarly survives the role edit but refuses after source cancellation. Gateway-owner closure and the surrounding Stop, disposal, replacement and recovery cases remain covered.

Thanks to @obviyus for #201334 and the request-admission contract. Production LOC delta: **0**. No configuration, schema, cache, or runtime guard changes.

## Evidence

Unmodified main parent `d2db7b2267faf4521b3c3a08acd062edd7cbf910`: the two reported cases fail, and the Gateway closure control passes. The corrected three-case selection passes (22.86 seconds Vitest time; 26.62 seconds wrapper time). The initial reproduction took 61.31/65.13 seconds including a cold worker compilation; these are test costs, not a performance comparison.

Full authority/projection selection: **270 tests passed across 15 files**, with two existing environment-dependent skips, in 288.88 seconds wrapper time. This includes the entire projection suite, operator-authority policy/recovery/reconnect suites, admitted-run lifecycle and delegated-claim tests, and sandbox custody/preparation/retirement tests. The queued-admission consumer suite also passes all 27 cases. `pnpm check:changed` passed, including the affected test typegraph, database guards, dead-export scans and changed-file lint. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

Codex autoreview of the complete local diff against `d2db7b2267faf`, through P2: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The test-audit and simplify pass retained the real boundary fixture and added no production helpers; test delta is +41/−10 lines.

No new production performance claim: this changes only tests. Existing 62,000-file/1.100 GB projection measurements from #201410 remain applicable to the unchanged runtime; they were not rerun. The fixture executes real filesystem operations and real authority/checkpoint owners with a local substitute for the container backend; it is not native-container or live-model proof.
