prs.title: fix(plugins): stop source-receipt warnings during model refresh
prs.body:
Related: #177882 (source-receipt warning only; the separate memory-search failure is outside this fix).

## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing models can succeed while the Gateway logs “Plugin source receipt was not recorded: Shared-state admission requires the host broker” and fails to save the record of captured native companion files. This still reproduces on main after #200320.

## User Impact

Model refresh saves its captured native-file receipts without the host-broker warning. Receipt-write failures stay advisory, and the existing discovery deadline is preserved. No configuration, schema migration, or operator action is required for the fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog worker forwards publications over its existing task channel to the retained host-owned publisher, rather than trying to acquire shared-state authority itself. Retained artifacts use the current task channel, exchanges are serialized, and pending receipt writes settle before that channel closes.

The adaptation preserves #200320's broker-owned source roots and cleanup, as well as main's sleep-aware admission watchdog. The two receipt regressions move into a dedicated broker-backed test file instead of restoring the native suite retired on main. The task admission owner keeps its existing input-size validation; the duplicate caller check was removed.

Original fix and regression tests contributed by @MertBasar0. This continues the same PR and preserves its authorship.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/18472a57-03bf-47c3-90c6-29f26dfbd442)

## Evidence

**Fresh real-Gateway comparison on 2026-11-18:** both eager and retained/lazy model refreshes succeed in both variants. Host-broker warnings fall from **2 to 0**; persisted receipts rise from **0 to 1**, covering both captured artifacts with independently verified SHA-256 hashes after Gateway shutdown. The synthetic plugin is installed through the real CLI. No model inference or native binary execution was used; both isolated Gateways and their owned children were joined.

**Current validation:** three regression cases fail on the pinned base for the intended missing-receipt/deadline reasons; **66 focused tests across eight files pass** on the adaptation. After the final duplicate-validation simplification, **40 pool tests pass** (20 repeat earlier coverage), and the real-Gateway comparison passes again. Core, agent-test and package-test typechecks, targeted production/test lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass.

**Published head:** `bba64ec693034893bd25b2db9440ef44affdbb4c`; its complete tree matches the validated workspace. Independent source-snapshot review found no actionable defects across all nine changed files. A test comment was clarified afterward without changing executable behavior. The reviewer did not run tests or verify a checkout; the local Auto Review launcher was unavailable and is not claimed as completed. [One hosted re-review was requested](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198572#issuecomment-6989886602) after the branch and proof were updated; completion is pending. **Required CI is blocked on maintainer workflow approval:** [CI run 44385446283](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44385446283) targets this exact head, reports `action_required`, and has zero jobs started. Other fork workflows also await approval. A repository maintainer must review the fork workflow changes and use **Approve and run workflows** on the pending run(s). Earlier review/CI do not certify this head. The PR remains draft.

prs.title: feat(voice-call): elevate one realtime call's consult tools with a keypad PIN
prs.body:
Related: #193571

## What Problem This Solves

Realtime phone calls run every consult at one fixed `realtime.toolPolicy`. Operators who keep it at `safe-read-only` (the safe default) cannot do owner-level work from a phone call, and raising the policy globally gives every admitted caller owner tools on every call.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator can turn on `realtime.elevation`, and on a call with a trusted number (an inbound caller, or the callee of an outbound call, in `allowFrom`), the person on the line can press `*`, a PIN, and `#` to give that one call the elevated consult policy (default `owner`) until hangup. Everything else keeps the configured `toolPolicy`. Elevation is off by default, so nothing changes for existing configs.

Risks and limits, kept visible:

- Twilio only. Digits come from Twilio Media Streams `dtmf` messages. Config validation rejects other providers while elevation is on.
- Only calls whose other party is in `allowFrom` can elevate: the caller of an inbound call, or the callee of an outbound call. Whoever answers an outbound call still has to enter the PIN; elevation is never automatic. Elevation requires `inboundPolicy: "allowlist"` or `"pairing"`. Caller ID can be spoofed (see #193571 for STIR/SHAKEN attestation), so the PIN is the credential; the allowlist only narrows who may try.
- Wrong PINs count per hashed number across calls (inbound and outbound share one budget) within `lockoutMs`, so hanging up and redialing does not reset the budget. After `maxAttempts` the caller is locked out for `lockoutMs`. Failure counts and lockouts are in memory; a Gateway restart clears them.
- Elevation ends when the call's media stream ends. A stream reconnect within the same call drops the tool policy back to `toolPolicy` (the caller re-enters the PIN), but the call's later consults stay in its isolated elevated session, because the call's transcript still carries answers from owner tools.
- A consult that is already running keeps the policy it started with.

## Why This Change Was Made

The realtime handler already owns each call's telephony binding, so it now also owns that call's keypad state and passes the call's current consult policy to the consult tool handler, which uses it for `toolsAllow`. A new `DtmfElevationGate` collects digits after the prefix, submits on `#`, after 3 seconds without a key, or at 12 digits (not at the configured PIN length, so the length stays private), and compares with `safeEqualSecret`. On success the realtime model gets a short notice so it can tell the caller; on a wrong PIN it gets a "not accepted" notice; failures are counted per hashed caller number across calls (a window of `lockoutMs`), so redialing cannot reset the attempt budget. After `maxAttempts` the call is hung up and the caller is locked out for `lockoutMs`. During a lockout any entry hangs up the call without checking the PIN, so retries reveal nothing. A correct PIN clears that caller's failure count.

Digits never reach the realtime model, the transcript, or logs. Logs record only the outcome, attempt count, and the hashed caller number on lockout. Caller audio is withheld from the model between the prefix key and submission, in case the carrier leaves tones in the media.

The PIN is a secret input (`realtime.elevation.pin`, registered in `configContracts.secretInputs` and marked sensitive), resolved the same way as `twilio.authToken`. It must resolve to 4 to 12 digits; the startup error never echoes the value.

Config surface: this raises the plugin config budget in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` from 5080 to 5087 (the `realtime.elevation` object and its six fields). The feature is opt-in and needs an operator-set PIN, so it cannot ride on an existing field.

To stay within the line-cap ratchet for `realtime-handler.ts`, the existing caller-transcript buffer helpers and `withFallbackConsultQuestion` moved unchanged into `realtime-transcript-text.ts`.

<details>
<summary>Config</summary>

```json5
realtime: {
  enabled: true,
  toolPolicy: "safe-read-only",
  elevation: {
    enabled: true,
    pin: { source: "env", provider: "default", id: "VOICE_CALL_ELEVATION_PIN" },
    prefix: "*",               // one key: 0-9 or *
    elevatedToolPolicy: "owner", // or "safe-read-only"
    maxAttempts: 3,              // 1-10
    lockoutMs: 3600000,
  },
}
```

</details>

## Evidence

Focused tests, all passing locally:

- `realtime-dtmf-elevation.test.ts`: eligibility (inbound + allowlisted only), prefix gating, `#` submit, `*` restart, inter-digit timeout, 12-digit submit, wrong PIN, failures counted across calls (redial does not reset), failure window expiry, success clears failures, lockout across calls and expiry, close drops pending entry.
- `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation.test.ts` (real WebSocket path): consult before the PIN gets `safe-read-only`, after the PIN gets `owner`; caller audio is withheld while entering the PIN; the PIN never appears in manager events, model notices, or console output; a stream close drops elevation; `maxAttempts` wrong PINs hang up the call, and during the lockout the correct PIN on the next call hangs up without a notice.
- `runtime.test.ts`: a consult with call policy `safe-read-only` runs with the read-only `toolsAllow` list, and with `owner` runs with `toolsAllow` undefined (normal agent tool policy).
- `config.test.ts`: defaults, runtime and manifest schema agreement, validation errors, PIN resolution.
- `stream-frame-adapter.test.ts`: Twilio `dtmf` frame parsing; Telnyx frames stay ignored.

Also updated: two `realtime-handler.test.ts` assertions now expect the consult context to carry `toolPolicy: "safe-read-only"`.

Results:

- `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: 52 files, 633 tests passed; database-workers lane 15 files, 182 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm lint:extensions`: clean.
- `pnpm check:changed`: every lane green except the dead-export scan, which reports only pre-existing entries outside this change (for example `extensions/google/provider-catalog-runtime.ts`, `src/config/sessions/session-history-types.ts`).
- `pnpm config:docs:check`: OK after `pnpm config:docs:gen`.

- `runtime.test.ts` (added in 6f93e38): an elevated consult runs in the session `<caller session key>:elevated:<callId>`; consults before the PIN and on later calls keep the caller's normal session.
- **Reconnect isolation (8a6d57d, the P1 from the last review).** The gate remembers which call ids were elevated (pruned after a day), so `wasElevated` survives a new binding for the same call. `realtime-dtmf-elevation.test.ts`: "keeps a call marked elevated across rebinding while its tool policy resets". `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation.test.ts` (real WebSocket path): elevate, end the stream, reconnect the same call; the next consult gets `toolPolicy: "safe-read-only"` **and** `elevated: true`. Together with the `runtime.test.ts` case above, the reconnected call's consults run in `…:elevated:<callId>`, so its retained transcript never enters the shared per-phone session, and a later call without the PIN can't read it.
- **Outbound (4277a5a).** `realtime-dtmf-elevation.test.ts`: "opens only when the other party is allowlisted, in either direction", and "shares failures and lockout between inbound and outbound calls with one number".

Rebased onto `main` at ae0d37b3c4 (2026-11-17). The only conflict was the generated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`, regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen` (`config:docs:check` OK). On the rebased head:

- The PR's test files (`config`, `runtime`, `realtime-dtmf-elevation`, `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation`, `realtime-handler`, `stream-frame-adapter`): 6/6 files pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.
- `pnpm lint:extensions`: the only errors are `max-lines` in `extensions/crabbox/…/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts` and `extensions/tlon/…/monitor/index.test.ts`, both on `main` and outside this change.
- Full `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: failures only in `index.call-scope.test.ts` and `src/manager.async-store.test.ts` (steering/end_call admission). Neither file is touched here, and the same tests fail or hang on unmodified `main` at ae0d37b3c4 on this host.

### Live Twilio proof (2026-11-16)

Host: OpenClaw 2026.11.4 with this change backported onto `v2026.11.4` and installed as a local `npm-pack` build of `@openclaw/voice-call`. The feature code is the same as this branch; only the base differs. Inbound Twilio calls from one allowlisted number, OpenAI realtime, `toolPolicy: "safe-read-only"`, `elevatedToolPolicy: "owner"`, PIN as a store SecretRef. Log excerpt below: phone numbers, Twilio call SIDs and IPs removed. The PIN never appears in any log line.


What the calls show:

- **Read-only before the PIN.** `bf202c8f` and `7992d6c1`: the first consult asked for current alerts; the agent had only the read-only tool list, couldn't reach Grafana, and said so.
- **Elevation.** After `*<PIN>#`: `Realtime keypad elevation granted … toolPolicy=owner`. The next consult in each call used Grafana MCP tools and reported the firing alerts.
- **Reset on hangup.** `52e9a519` (call-back after `bf202c8f`): the consult ran with the read-only tool list again, and the owner tools (Grafana MCP) were not in its catalog.
- **Wrong PIN.** `f10831ae`: `Realtime keypad elevation rejected … attempt=1/3`, and the model received the "not accepted" notice. I stopped after one attempt to avoid locking out the test number; the 3-attempt hang-up and lockout are covered by `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation.test.ts`.

**Found live and fixed in 6f93e38.** With the default `sessionScope: "per-phone"`, the call-back in `52e9a519` couldn't run owner tools, but its consult answered from results the elevated call had left in the caller's shared session. Elevated consults now run in a session scoped to the call (`…:elevated:<callId>`), so owner-tool results never land in the shared session. Re-checked live: `7992d6c1` elevated and fetched alerts into `…:elevated:7992d6c1…`; on the call-back `4fd2dbc6`, the agent had no record of them. The docs now cover this, plus `sessionScope: "per-call"` for no carry-over at all.

### Live outbound proof (2026-11-16, same host and build)

Outbound call to the allowlisted number (`mode=conversation`). The consult before the PIN had the read-only tool list (7 tools) and couldn't reach Grafana. After `*<PIN>#`, the consult ran in `agent:main:voice:call:49796487-…:elevated:49796487-…`, had the owner tool catalog (133 tools, including Grafana MCP), and reported the firing alerts. Those matched Prometheus `ALERTS` at the same moment.

```text
[voice-call] Call finalized callId=49796487-79b6-44d9-9429-b405a7e2d29a providerCallId=CA… endReason=completed
```

### Upgrade and compatibility

- Upgrading this host from 2026.10.7 to 2026.11.4 kept the existing voice-call config (Twilio store SecretRef auth token, realtime provider settings, allowlist, tool policy). `realtime.elevation` defaults to `enabled: false`, so existing configs load and behave as before.
- Operator note: when a newly installed plugin version adds a secret input path (here `realtime.elevation.pin`), the Gateway reads the secret-input registry only at startup. Until a Gateway restart, voice-call fails to start with `unresolved SecretRef`; `secrets reload` and a plugin reload are not enough. This is core behavior, not something this PR introduces.





### Live reconnect + callback proof, and upgrade from v2026.11.5 (2026-11-18)

Elevate → forced stream reconnect → consult → unauthenticated callback on a real Twilio call: after the reconnect the tool policy resets, but the call's consults stay in its isolated session, and the callback's shared session never sees the elevated answer. Also covers the upgrade and data-model proof from the current stable release (v2026.11.5) in a sandbox. Details and redacted logs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200198#issuecomment-6979119355

prs.title: fix(codex): prevent native subagent continuation loss after sessions_yield
prs.body:
Related: #167410 (not a claim to fix every timeout reported there).

## What Problem This Solves

A Codex parent waiting for a native child can lose its original tool declarations when that child finishes but its result is still being delivered. Separately, ending the parent turn too early can replace a successful yield acknowledgement with cancellation before Codex records it.

## User Impact

The parent can resume with its original native thread and saved tool declarations after child completion, and its successful yield acknowledgement is recorded before interruption. Saved declarations do not revive old tool executors. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

This refresh keeps only two production repairs still absent from the pinned main:

- Retain saved declarations while the existing completion owner holds current delivery custody, independently of execution retention. Recheck that owner after loading metadata.
- Wait for matching native output receipts before terminal interruption, including the outer Code Mode output for nested yields.

Upstream already owns child-result context propagation, end-of-turn user context, detached announcement dispatch, and sibling-completion retention (#190999). This PR does not duplicate those repairs. Regression tests also check compatibility with closed foreground scope and bounded-history finalization rejection; those tests are not claims that this PR newly fixes either mechanism.

## Evidence

Refreshed head: `205d6d97ed2664ac714b827e35bbd824de015d8b`, based on main `da8fd166f5bca52a464470cf9172bdd7a58106cf`.

- **162 distinct tests across 14 focused suites passed.** This includes real native Codex 0.169.0 recording the yield output before interruption; direct/nested receipt ordering; pending-result catalog continuity without stale executor revival; revoked custody; final-effect Gateway authority; bounded-history finalization rejection; upstream sibling retention; and original-child follow-up.
- **Fail-before proof against pinned main:** substituting only main's lifecycle controller makes both direct/nested yield regressions fail at the premature `turn/interrupt` assertion. Restoring this PR's controller passes them. No assertions or ownership guards were weakened.
- Core/plugin production types, scoped core/plugin test types, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap and test-line-budget checks passed.
- Fresh local **Codex autoreview**, full committed range with 13 complete owner-context files, P0–P2: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. This is source review, not runtime qualification.
- All six prior commits rebase without conflicts. Range-diff preserves their changes, apart from test-inventory context. Main subsequently advanced to `1fae66036cc0dbcaae0696975030375ba4d278bc`; inspected drift and merge-tree are clean. Checks/review above remain bound to the pinned base/head, not an untested later rebase.

Tests ran separately in secretless, network-disabled containers using synthetic fixtures. Summed test-command wall time: **948.39 seconds** (including cold worker compilation). Native boundary test command: **53.84 seconds**. Repeated inner/outer tooling summaries counted once. Hosted CI for this rewritten head is pending; CI timing is not yet available.

The retained test allocation covers native-boundary, custody, authority and receipt-ordering regressions; shared baselines remain unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Historical evidence — not certification of this refreshed head</summary>

Earlier PR heads had focused source checks and local reviews. Separate stable backports had packaged and live continuation probes, including five turns on the same child and three automatic resumptions. Those results remain historical: they do not certify the refreshed upstream head or a new 11.5 package. The previous stable 11.4 deployment later encountered a multi-child delivery failure; the matching sibling-retention repair is now upstream and is separate from this PR's two remaining fixes.

</details>

Limits: focused source/native-boundary tests are not a fresh packaged Gateway, production OAuth/model, restart recovery, or full reproduction of the historical multi-child incident. No merge, installation, restart, or stable-backport publication is included.

prs.title: feat: switch sessions with Command-1–9 and Control-Tab in the desktop apps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Switching conversations needs the mouse, or Command-K and typing part of a name. With several sessions running at once, this is the most frequent navigation in the app, and the desktop apps have no direct key for it, unlike Slack, Linear, or browser tabs.

## User Impact

User impact: in the macOS app and the other desktop apps, Command-1 through Command-8 (Ctrl on Windows and Linux) open that session in the sidebar, and Command-9 opens the last one. Control-Tab goes back to the session you were in before; hold Control and press Tab again to go further back, or add Shift to go the other way.

**Changed default:** in the macOS app's Gateway menu and the web identity menu's Gateway picker, Gateway shortcuts move from Command-1–9 to Control-Command-1–9 (Control-Option-Command for a new window), so Command-1–9 can open sessions.

Web browsers keep both chords for their own tabs, so nothing changes in a browser tab.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar owns the visible order (pinned, groups, expanded children, then the rest, minus collapsed sections and catalog sessions), so the sidebar handles the keys and opens sessions through its normal row navigation. The keys are bound only when the page runs in a desktop host (`isNativeWebChromeHost()`), the same split New Session already uses for Command-N. They work from the composer, ignore key repeat and text composition, and leave open dialogs alone.

Control-Tab walks a most-recently-used list of up to 20 sessions opened in this window. Holding Control freezes that order for the walk, as app switchers do; releasing Control makes the session you stopped on the most recent one. Sessions that can no longer be opened are skipped. Before a second session has been opened, Control-Tab moves to the next sidebar row.

In the macOS app the Dashboard web view sees key equivalents before the main menu, so the page claims Command-1–9 and the Gateway menu items move to Control-Command so both keep working. The shortcuts dialog lists the new keys in desktop apps only.

Related: #182559 (jump to the next session waiting for you) is navigation by state; this is navigation by position and recency.

## Evidence

Keyboard shortcuts dialog (Command-/), Sidebar section, in the Control UI with the macOS desktop host emulated by the existing `installNativeWebChrome` fixture, Chromium at 1440×900 and 2×, synthetic sessions. Before is `main` at 39250610246, after is this branch.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the Sidebar section lists only the multi-select click chords](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4477ce9-c0c5-49eb-a12a-1db31d1040ee) | ![After: the Sidebar section also lists Command 1–9 to open a sidebar session and Control-Tab to switch to a recent session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2509f99d-4377-4b30-9c1f-67ce31430537) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Sidebar rows outlined: no session switching keys](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb598459-6395-4cfb-bb27-5b64c6add9ff) | ![New rows outlined: session switching keys, desktop app only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13027694-19eb-4800-b49c-ed7bca1c7b7e) |

- **E2E** `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-session-shortcuts.e2e.test.ts`: with the desktop host emulated and focus in the composer, Command-3, Command-9 and Command-2 open the third, last and second sessions; Control-Tab returns to the previous one and back; holding Control and pressing Tab twice walks two back, and releasing Control keeps that session; Control-Shift-Tab walks the other way. A second case checks that a plain browser page leaves Command-2 unclaimed and ignores Control-Tab. Passes.
- **Unit** `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-shortcuts.test.ts` (13 tests): position targets and Command-9, the held-Control walk and its final promotion, skipped unavailable sessions, the 20-session bound, AZERTY-style digit keys, repeat/modifier/composition/browser/modal guards, the next-row fallback, and listener removal. `app-sidebar-native-gateways.test.ts` now expects the Control-Command hints. Both pass.
- **Checks**: `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` pass.

Not verified: the macOS app itself. The two Swift edits only change the Gateway menu items' modifier masks and the native card's hint text, and were not built locally; macOS CI covers the build. The claim that the Dashboard web view sees Command-digits before the menu comes from WebKit's `WebViewImpl::performKeyEquivalent`, which hands key equivalents to the page first when the web view is first responder and passes them on to the menu only if the page leaves them unhandled. The Dashboard's own Command-W handling relies on the same order.

prs.title: fix(ui): collapsed sidebar keeps polling session catalogs
prs.body:
Related: #125989
Builds on: #152200 (by @rondavis007)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI asks the Gateway for the session catalog every 2 minutes when the sidebar is collapsed or hidden. Nobody can see these rows.

## User Impact

User impact: a collapsed or hidden sidebar does not send background catalog requests. When you open the sidebar again, the list is up to date.

Rows that are already loaded stay. Manual refresh works as before. There is no setting to change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before, the UI checked only one thing: is the browser tab hidden? Now it also checks: does the sidebar show the session rows? A collapsed desktop sidebar still shows a narrow rail, but it does not show the rows, so it counts as hidden.

When the rows are hidden:

- The UI stops the 2-minute timer, the retry timer and page discovery.
- It remembers if it skipped work: a waiting refresh, a retry, a late host update or page discovery. This includes a discovery sweep that was cut short because the sidebar closed while a page was loading.
- A refresh that already started finishes, so expanded groups do not go blank.
- The first load still runs once, so the rows are ready and do not jump in when the sidebar opens.

When the rows show again:

- If a poll was due or work was skipped, the UI refreshes one time.
- If not, it keeps the normal 2-minute schedule. Switching views quickly does not add requests.

#152200 by @rondavis007 had the same idea. That branch is about 30,000 commits behind main and does not apply: main deleted 3 of its files. This PR puts the fix on the current code, adds the collapsed-rail case, and credits Ron as co-author.

## Evidence

**Live Gateway, real browser (head `b24b15905cc`, rebased on main `4fa7e62ab43`).**
Setup: `pnpm build`, then the built Gateway (`node dist/index.js gateway --verbose --ws-log full`) on a random loopback port with a temp HOME and state dir, token auth, no model credentials. It serves the built Control UI. Headless Chrome opens it. The temp HOME has a few fake Claude Code transcripts, so the real Claude session catalog has rows. Counts are `← req sessions.catalog.list` lines in the Gateway log (the browser frame count matched in every step). Real time, no virtual clock. "Before" uses the same Gateway with the Control UI built from main; this PR changes only `ui/src`.

1. Collapsed sidebar, 3 sessions (cumulative Gateway requests):

| Step | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Open `/new`, sidebar shown (20 s) | 2 | 2 |
| Sidebar collapsed, 2 min | 3 | 2 |
| Sidebar collapsed, 4 min | 4 | 2 |
| Sidebar collapsed, 6 min | 5 | 2 |
| Sidebar opened again, 15 s later | 5 | 3 |

The 2 at open are one sidebar read and one read by the New session page. The rows were shown after reopening in both runs.

2. Sidebar closed during a discovery sweep, 100 sessions. A saved "Involving me" owner filter hides the native rows, so the sidebar walks the next pages. The browser holds the Gateway reply to the first next-page read until the sidebar is collapsed, then lets it through (it has another cursor). The sidebar opens again 30 s later, well before the 2-minute poll.

| | main | previous head `b68b73e` | this head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reads while collapsed | 1 (the last page, nobody sees it) | 0 | 0 |
| Reads in 15 s after reopening | 0 | 0 (last page waits for the 2-min poll) | 3: first page, the expanded page, the last page |
| Runs | 3 of 3 | 3 of 3 | 8 of 10 |

In 2 of 10 runs on this head, the reopen read came back with the Claude host still `pending` (its scan was refreshing). Discovery skips pending catalogs, which is how main works too, so the last page came with the next poll. This PR does not change that rule.

**Tests:**

- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.catalog-discovery.test.ts`: the hidden-tab discovery test now also runs with the sidebar hidden. The new case fails on the previous head and on main, and passes here.
- `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-catalog-scope.e2e.test.ts`: browser test with a mock Gateway. It now uses the Collapse sidebar button, because main changed what the rail buttons do. On main it fails: `expected … to have a length of 1 but got 2`.
- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.catalog-events.test.ts`: cases for a hidden sidebar, a collapsed sidebar, another sidebar view, a sidebar that starts collapsed, and a hide while a refresh waits in the startup queue. 2 more cases check that opening the sidebar before the next poll does not add a request.

**Other checks:**

- All 64 `app-sidebar*` and `session-data*` test files in `ui/src/components` (918 tests): pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, format check and lint on touched files: pass.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base upstream/main`: net +128 test lines, under the 400 allowance.

**Not covered:** I did not test on a mobile device or with a remote node host. The live runs use the Claude catalog only. This is not a visual change; the page looks the same.

## Review

I did a local review in two rounds before I opened this PR. The first round found 4 issues and the second found 3. I fixed all of them, and the tests above cover them.

prs.title: fix: update status repeats verified transcript filename mismatch warnings
prs.body:
Closes #201369

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update status` keeps reporting transcript filename/header ID mismatch warnings after a completed session SQLite migration already imported that exact source under its header identity, including replaying the same notice from the saved update report.

## User Impact

Verified mismatches disappear from plain and saved update status, and no longer count toward the saved “warnings need attention” headline. Incomplete, ambiguous, unreadable, or unimported sources still show the warning. Manifests and doctor JSON keep the historical detail.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Revalidate `transcript_filename_mismatch` alongside the other transcript findings.
- Suppress it only after verifying the exact source content exists in the owning store under the header identity, reusing the existing transcript-verification owner. Archived originals are resolved through the manifest move mapping.
- Keep it visible when the store is missing or unreadable, the source content is unimported or conflicting, or the header ID cannot be parsed.
- Require the recorded saved claim itself to verify; a matching store with no recorded claim stays visible.
- Apply the same current-state classification when replaying saved update warnings, while leaving the stored run record untouched.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-warnings.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 3/3 passed, including an archived verified source, a bare saved claim, and an unimported source.
- `pnpm test src/infra/update-run-report.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 59/59 passed, including saved-warning filtering and headline attention count.
- Red-on-base: reverting only the source fix makes the verified-mismatch case fail while the unverified case still passes.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint clean on all changed files.

- Shipped CLI proof with a crafted state (`openclaw update status`):
  - verified archived source: `✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.1.1 (from 2026.1.0).` — no mismatch warning, no attention count;
  - unverified identity: the manifest warning, the replayed saved warning, and `1 warning needs attention` all remain.

- Latest-stable upgrade proof: state was created with `openclaw@2026.11.5` (schema 36) containing a verified archived mismatch, an unverified mismatch, and a saved update-run warning. The stable binary reported both warnings plus `1 warning needs attention`. After `doctor --fix` migrated the state and this branch rendered status, only the unverified warning remained; the verified and saved warnings were gone.

prs.title: fix: stop iOS Talk from answering realtime speech twice after a mode switch
prs.body:
Closes #197406

## What Problem This Solves

On iOS, if `talk.realtime.mode` changes from `stt-tts` to `realtime` while continuous Talk is on, the next turn starts the realtime voice session but the old on-device silence monitor keeps running. Every realtime utterance is then also sent as an ordinary chat turn, so the agent answers twice and the phone speaks the extra answer with the system voice over the realtime voice. Those duplicate turns also keep the agent busy, so realtime consult calls get rejected.

## User Impact

Changing the Talk mode during a call no longer produces two voices or duplicate agent work. Realtime speech is handled only by the realtime session, and stopping and restarting Talk is no longer needed to recover.

## Why This Change Was Made

The silence monitor belongs to the native capture session and was only cancelled by `stop()`, backgrounding, push to talk, and muting. When `start()` switched to a realtime route it never touched the monitor, and realtime callbacks fill the same transcript fields the monitor reads. `start()` now cancels the monitor before it takes a realtime route. If realtime startup fails, `start()` falls through to native startup, which starts its own monitor as before, so the native fallback is unchanged.

## Evidence

No device or simulator run exists for this change yet, so there is no observed proof that the duplicate answer is gone. What exists is a new test and static checks.

The new test in `TalkConfigRefreshTests` covers the handoff through the real turn path, with no test-only lifecycle helper:

- It starts native Talk against a connected Gateway fixture and confirms the silence monitor is running.
- It switches the served `talk.config` to a realtime route and sends a final transcript through the existing transcript entry point. The turn reaches `chat.send` and ends on a terminal error acknowledgement, and the resume then starts realtime.
- When `talk.session.create` arrives, the monitor must already be gone. On the base commit it is still running at that point.
- The test then fails realtime startup and checks that native capture resumes with a recognition request and its own silence monitor.

Checks run here: `swiftc -parse` on the two changed Swift files (`apps/ios/Sources/Voice/TalkModeManager.swift` and `apps/ios/Tests/TalkModeConfigParsingTests.swift`) and `git diff --check` pass.

Not run here: the iOS test suite (`pnpm ios:test`), because this machine has only the Command Line Tools and no Xcode, so the new test has not been compiled, executed or timed. A device check that switches `talk.realtime.mode` during continuous Talk and confirms no native `chat.send` or system-voice playback is also not run.

prs.title: test: pin idle-session background exec completion wakes on current main
prs.body:
Refs #171544

## What Problem This Solves

#171544 reports that a backgrounded exec promises `Completion will wake this conversation automatically` but the wake never arrives. Reports covered idle Telegram/Slack sessions, detached compound commands, completions that exit during an active turn, and a completion rejected after the originating operator authority expires.

This PR adds regression coverage for the current session-event path: real child processes settle, completion events are admitted, and a follow-up turn is observed. It does not claim to fix live channel delivery.

## User Impact

Tests only; no production change. The three added cases cover distinct lifecycle boundaries:

- An idle wake after the starting turn's operator authority ends.
- A second completion queued behind an active turn.
- A detached compound command whose grandchild outlives the wrapper process.

The process and session-event paths are real; model inference is synthetic, consistent with the existing suite.

## Why This Change Is Made

Recent fixes changed each stage of completion delivery, but no test pinned the end-to-end process settlement → session-event admission → follow-up turn path together. These cases preserve that behavior without introducing production machinery or claiming the related live-channel issue is solved.

## Evidence

- `corepack pnpm test src/agents/bash-tools.process.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 11/11 passed on macOS arm64 with Node 24.22.1, including the three completion-wake cases, after the type-safety fix.
- The PR review's P2 type-safety finding is fixed by narrowing `receipts[0]` with the existing `expectDefined` helper before reading `accepted`.
- The newly reported P2 is fixed by removing the queued-test references to `admitEvent` and `silentReply`, which were removed from current main, and wrapping the existing model fixture via `model.getMockImplementation()` so admission/reply behavior stays intact while the first turn is held.
- The subsequent CI failure was the detached-child marker timing out. The wrapper now waits for the child `spawn` event before exiting; a spawn error exits non-zero. This keeps the descendant marker assertion intact while eliminating the unobserved-spawn race. The CI Bun shard launcher on macOS passed this suite 11/11; fresh Linux CI is still pending.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/agents/bash-tools.process.e2e.test.ts"]' --concurrency 2` — passed.
- The ClawSweeper request for a shipped Gateway/channel trace or real-model run remains unfulfilled. The tests exercise real processes and session-event dispatch with synthetic model inference; they do not demonstrate transport delivery to a live Slack or Telegram conversation.



- Follow-up for CI run `41653282218`: the detached-child case ran under the Linux Bun test runtime, so its fixture command used Bun's `process.execPath` rather than the installed Node executable. The shared test helper now prefers CI's `NODE_BIN` directory for child-process fixtures and falls back to `process.execPath` outside CI; the test assertion is unchanged. With `NODE_BIN` set to the installed Node 24 directory, the official Bun shard launcher passed this file 11/11 on macOS. Linux CI remains the decisive environment check.

prs.title: feat(cron): skip scheduled runs when a shell precheck finds no work
prs.body:
Supersedes #171738 and links the closed replay #112375. ## What Problem This Solves Scheduled jobs that poll for work still start a model turn when the inbox, queue, or watch target is empty. This supersedes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171738 and replaces the closed replay of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/112375. Those branches targeted the previous cron store and could not be applied to current main. This branch is based on current `openclaw/openclaw` main (`7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92`). ## User Impact User impact: an operator can attach a host shell precheck to an `at`, `every`, or `cron` job. Exit code 0 continues into the trigger and payload. Exit code 2 records a skipped run with summary `precheck-no-work` and does not start the model turn. Denied, unapproved, timed out, or unexpected results fail closed and skip the payload. Agent turns cannot create or edit the command. Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/schedules#shell-precheck ## Why This Change Was Made Current cron jobs live in SQLite `job_json`, with validation in the cron service and execution in `executeJobCore`. The precheck is an optional field on that job, not a new config key or schema version. The probe runs through `createExecTool` with `nonInteractiveApproval` and no host-approval bypass, then the existing gateway allowlist and approval floors. `cron.triggers.enabled: false` disables it. Forced manual runs still run the probe; they do not skip it the way they skip a condition script. ## Evidence Local validation on `7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5`: - `pnpm test src/cron/job-precheck.test.ts src/cron/job-precheck-run.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.precheck.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.occurrence.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-precheck.test.ts` — passed. Cron shard: 4 files, 86 tests. CLI shard: 1 file, 3 tests. The exec-policy file proves a marker file is not created when security is deny, ask is always, the job pin requires ask always, `toolsAllow` excludes exec, or run authority is rejected. An allowed `full`/`off` policy covers exit 2 (no work) and exit 0 (work). - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed TypeScript files — passed. - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check` on the 29 changed files — all matched files use the correct format. - `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed. - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-services-cron.tsbuildinfo` — passed. ## Security review ### Threat model A precheck is an unattended host command. The realistic attackers are a model turn that tries to persist one, an operator who saved a command and later tightened exec policy, and a forced or restarted run that might otherwise skip the gate. The command can do anything the exec tool would allow, including reading or writing files on the gateway host. The feature must not add a second spawn path with weaker defaults. ### How approvals are enforced - The runner calls `createExecTool` with the resolved `tools.exec` host, mode, security, and ask, plus the live exec-approvals file that the tool already re-reads. It does not pass `bypassHostApprovalFloors`. - `nonInteractiveApproval: true` makes approval-requiring commands return `approval_required` before spawn. `ask: "always"`, an allowlist miss, and `security: "deny"` therefore do not run the command. - A stored `toolsAllowExecTarget` pin is applied with `pinExecToolTarget`, so a creator floor of `ask: "always"` still denies a headless run when global policy is `full`/`off`. - A defined `toolsAllow` that does not include `exec` denies the probe before the tool is built. - `assertRunCurrent` is awaited in `executeJobCore` and again inside the runner immediately before `tool.execute`. A rejected run does not spawn. - If the gateway does not wire `runJobPrecheck`, or `cron.triggers.enabled` is false, the job errors and the payload does not start. - Agent creates and patches that set a non-null `precheck` are rejected in the automations tool and again in `assertCronModelJobAllowed`. Clearing the field is allowed. `cron.run` of an existing job is not treated as authoring. - Invalid persisted prechecks quarantine the row instead of being dropped, so a bad write cannot fall open into an unguarded payload. - Each run re-reads current policy. A command saved under a looser policy is denied after the operator tightens it. ### Residual risks - Command payloads (`runCronCommandJob`) still spawn from their own runner and do not use this exec-tool gate. That path is unchanged. - Operators who can already persist command jobs can persist a precheck through the CLI or Gateway API. The protection is the run-time policy check, not a second save-time approval dialog. Reusing the stream approval dialog would describe the wrong effect. - `mode: "auto"` remains the existing exec auto-review path. With `nonInteractiveApproval`, a reviewer that approves can still allow a spawn. Tests pin `mode: "full"` so they do not depend on a reviewer. This change does not weaken or special-case auto-review. - When config omits security, the exec tool keeps its own non-sandbox default and the approvals file still applies its floors. That is the same default as other exec callers. - Exit codes are the only work signal. A command that prints a success banner and exits 2 is no-work. A command that exits 0 after doing nothing is work. Overlapping codes are rejected. - The probe runs on the exec host selected by `tools.exec` unless a gateway pin forces the gateway host. It cannot target a node or sandbox that the exec tool itself would refuse.
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Introduces unattended host command execution on the gateway before scheduled agent turns, gated by exec policy but still a security-sensitive automation surface. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). Updated by merging current upstream main (merge commit `ce9c3641f4`); the precheck, occurrence and CLI cron tests (89 tests) and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass on the merged head.

prs.title: fix(models): model picker switches chat to models the user cannot sign in to from chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: selecting a listed but unauthenticated model in the chat model picker (for example `meta/muse-spark-1.3` before Meta sign-in) reports success, pins the chat to a model that can only fail authentication, and then answers every message with a generic HTTP 401 that gives no direct way to authorize — forcing the user to switch back to another model and hunt for the sign-in flow.

## User Impact

Tapping a model whose provider has no working sign-in now keeps the current model and immediately shows how to connect that provider: a tappable sign-in button for OAuth/device-code providers, secure API-key entry instructions for API-key-only providers (for example OpenCode Go), and a deep link to Control UI → Settings → Model Providers (carrying `?provider=&agent=`) when the gateway advertises a public origin. Auth failures at run time name the provider and carry the same buttons instead of generic boilerplate.

Not blocked: ready, unconfirmed, and cooling-down models; reset-to-default and default selections; and selections on a gateway whose `cloudWorkers.requiredProfile` is a worker-inference device profile (provider credentials live on the node there, per #170132), unless the selection pins an explicit Gateway account. No secrets are requested or stored in chat, and no credential-bearing links are placed in chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker already computed per-model readiness for display, but selection ignored it, and failure copy dropped the provider before rendering.

- The policy lives in the shared selection owner (`applySessionModelSelectionInternal`). Adapters opt in by passing the exact menu facts they rendered (`authReadinessMenu`); a rejection is a dedicated `reason: "auth"` result with a required `authBlock`. Telegram only renders the result. Typed `/model` and `sessions.patch` keep their current behavior and only gain the better failure guidance.
- Menu readiness describes Gateway credentials, so it cannot judge required worker-local inference. The #170132 exception is now one exported predicate in the runtime-normalization owner (`isProviderAuthOwnedByRequiredWorker`), used both by runtime preparation and by the picker gate. Gateway inference, optional placement, and explicit account pins stay gated.
- Each provider's concrete login route is resolved so recovery can tell API-key entry from OAuth sign-in. The provider is carried through failover facts, including typed auth errors buried in the cause graph. Provider ids are slug-validated before they are embedded in commands or guidance.

**Needs a maintainer decision (ClawSweeper "Decision needed"):** should Telegram reject unauthenticated picker selections through the new optional `authReadinessMenu` SDK parameter and `reason: "auth"` result variant, while other selection surfaces (Discord/Mattermost pickers, typed `/model`, `sessions.patch`) keep their current behavior? The PR is built so other adapters can opt in with the same contract later.

## Evidence

Head `484c1ad61fd` (merged current `main` at `fc64180eda0`).

Merge with `main`: conflicts in `failover-classification.corpus.test.ts` (upstream removed neighbouring tests; only this PR's 401 test is added), `user-copy.ts` (kept upstream `TLS_CERTIFICATE_ERROR_USER_TEXT` plus this PR's provider helpers), `commands-models-catalog.ts` (kept upstream's `loginProviders` placement and replaced its filter with the loop that also builds `providerLogins`), and `agent-runner-error-handler.ts` (`buildExternalRunFailureReply` no longer takes heartbeat options upstream; only `config` is passed). The Telegram loopback test now reads the session via `listSessionEntriesAsync`.

Regression for the worker-local finding (`src/model-picker/apply-session-model-selection.test.ts`, "shared auth gate defers Gateway readiness only to required worker inference"; cases `worker`, `gateway`, `optional`, `account`):

- Without the fix: `worker` fails (`Expected: "applied"`, `Received: "rejected"`); the other three pass.
- With the fix: 4/4 pass.

Focused suites on this head (`node scripts/test-projects.mts <files> --maxWorkers=1`), 10 files, 225 tests, all passing:

- `src/model-picker/apply-session-model-selection.test.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-models-menu.test.ts`
- `src/agents/failover/user-copy.test.ts`, `src/agents/failover/failover-classification.corpus.test.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-provider-failures.test.ts`
- `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-login-flow-runtime.test.ts`
- `src/agents/model-runtime-choice.native.test.ts` (the #170132 worker/gateway/optional/account suite, still green after moving its predicate)
- `extensions/telegram/src/model-callback.loopback.integration.test.ts` (blocked selection keeps the current model and renders the Sign in button)
- `ui/src/pages/model-providers/route.test.ts`

Typecheck: `tsgo` core, extensions, UI, and the `messaging`, `other`, and extensions test projects are clean. `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on touched files.

Removed per review: the `buildModelsMenu` "exposes per-model readiness and login providers" case, which only checked copied input identity.

Before the fix, observed on a real Telegram + gateway install: selecting `meta/muse-spark-1.3` printed "✅ Model changed", then every message returned "⚠️ Authentication failed (provider returned HTTP 401)…", and `/login meta` answered with setup text and no link.

**Live proof pending:** redacted Telegram screenshots of (1) the blocked picker selection with the Sign in button, (2) the Control UI handoff opening Model Providers for the right agent, and (3) a run-time 401 reply carrying provider-specific buttons. These need the author's real accounts and device. The earlier "live-traces package" reference was not reachable by reviewers and is withdrawn. The required-worker case is covered by the regression above, not by a live two-machine run.

prs.title: feat(talk): configure GPT-Live launch acknowledgments
prs.body:
Related: #117898, #184803

## What Problem This Solves

Operators who prefer a consistent, short Talk acknowledgment cannot choose its exact wording without patching the OpenAI plugin. The natural, varied replies added in #175603 are useful defaults, but do not replace that preference.

## User Impact

Set `talk.realtime.providers.openai.acknowledgement` to a custom phrase such as `One moment.` for GPT-Live calls with Gateway-owned delegation. Unset, empty, or whitespace-only values retain upstream's natural, varied acknowledgment. Changes apply to new Talk sessions on both browser WebRTC and Gateway-relay transports.

This does not change GA Realtime, native speech/TTS fallback, cancellation, status, or final answers. A launch acknowledgment is not proof of task admission; choose wording accordingly. Blank does not disable speech.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reopened after real use showed that varied wording and configurable wording solve different needs. The earlier closing comment incorrectly treated them as equivalent. This is an additive option on top of #175603, not a rollback of it or a delayed/suppressed-receipt feature like #185415.

The existing provider normalizer trims one optional string, both transports pass it to their shared controller, and that controller selects the existing exact-speech helper or the unchanged natural default. No new core schema, SDK, client setting, helper, or lifecycle state is needed. Existing configurations require no migration: the provider config already accepts extra fields and an absent value preserves current behavior.

## Evidence

- Updated against upstream main `ced77ff1682d86bd1c7cffdca909750aefbef9d6` on November 18. The five affected production modules are unchanged between the original PR base and that main; the original two configured-phrase regression failures remain applicable baseline evidence.
- Fresh focused run: **89 tests passed across four files**, covering browser offers, relay connection, delegation, and relay lifecycle. The transport regressions cover quoted custom text, trimming, unset/empty/whitespace fallback, and successive sessions. Vitest duration **46.00s**, wrapper **47.89s**; hosted CI timing is not yet available.
- Fresh OpenAI package-boundary typecheck, seven-file type-aware lint, native plugin build, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Simplification: retained the minimal shared production decision; removed a redundant custom-phrase test case from each transport and replaced duplicated README setup instructions with a link to the canonical Talk docs. Relative to the previous revision: **8 fewer lines**. Whole feature: production **+14/-1**, tests **+124**, docs **+26** across nine files.
- Prior independent source review reported no actionable findings on the unchanged production patch. That is historical evidence, not a new review of this updated head; the current full diff was manually inspected. A fresh Codex AutoReview attempt at P0–P2 against base `ced77ff1682d` and head `2d91cd47bb81` returned `reviewer_unavailable` because its Responses WebSocket connection failed; no new independent clean review is claimed.
- The same optional-override logic has been deployed on an operator's 2026.11.5 instance and automated plugin recovery passed. This is not audible-delivery proof for this upstream candidate. **Real provider/audio acceptance on browser and relay, and fresh-install/latest-stable upgrade proof requested in the earlier review, remain outstanding.** No recording or live end-to-end success is claimed.
- Upstream CI and refreshed review are pending. Maintainer product acceptance of the optional setting remains required before merge.

prs.title: fix(exec): dollar amounts in agent messages are corrupted when exec text uses $<digit> in double quotes
prs.body:
Closes #179890

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: dollar amounts in agent-sent messages are silently corrupted ("$900" becomes "00") when an `exec` command passes the text in double quotes.

## User Impact

User impact: exec commands that would deliver a corrupted dollar amount are refused before they run. The refusal shows the text as written next to what the shell would deliver, and how to fix it (single quotes, `\$`, or a quoted heredoc), so the agent retries correctly instead of sending the wrong amount to a customer. It can be disabled with `OPENCLAW_EXEC_DOLLAR_GUARD=off`.

**Open question for maintainers:** this is default-on and uses an environment switch. If you'd prefer it opt-in, or shipped as a plugin on the existing `before_tool_call` hook instead of in core, I'm happy to rework it that way. Tell me which shape you want.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runBeforeToolCallHook` checks `exec` command text for a `$<digit>` that the shell would expand, before any plugin or approval policy runs. Codex-native shell commands reach the same policy through the PreToolUse native hook relay. Relay planning now counts the guard as a before-tool-call policy and keeps `exec` in the PreToolUse matcher, so native commands are covered even with no other policy installed.

The scanner is deliberately conservative. It only flags an expansion it can show would be empty:
- It honours single quotes, `\$`, `$'...'`, quoted heredoc delimiters, `${...}`, `$((...))` and comments.
- It recurses into `$(...)`, including substitutions inside unquoted heredoc bodies, with their own quoting.
- It ignores `$0` (the shell or script name) unless it reads as money (`$0.50`).
- It stays out of commands that define functions or set positional parameters (`set --`, `shift`, `getopts`), where `$1.00` may be intended.
- It fails open on anything it cannot parse.

Code-mode `exec` (JavaScript) is excluded.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/shell-dollar-expansion-guard.test.ts` (35 tests): the hazard shapes, every safe quoting form, `$0`, populated positional parameters, heredoc command substitution, `bash -lc` unwrapping, fail-open, and the `runBeforeToolCallHook` veto, allow and disable cases. The `$0`, positional-parameter and heredoc-substitution cases fail on the previous revision and pass now.
- `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.dollar-guard.test.ts` (6 tests): Codex `Bash` and `exec_command` are denied and single-quoted amounts pass. Relay planning enables PreToolUse for `exec` with no other policy and keeps it in a relay scoped to other tools; these planning cases fail without the relay change.
- The existing `agent-tools.before-tool-call*` and `native-hook-relay*` unit suites pass. `native-hook-relay.participants` and `native-hook-relay.remote-http` fail identically on `main` without this change in my environment.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Replayed against 391 unique `$`-bearing exec commands from a production deployment: 18 were flagged, all genuine expansion bugs, with no false positives.
- Still to add: a gateway trace of a real agent refusing and retrying. I'll attach it before asking for re-review.

prs.title: fix(clickclack): discussion rooms fail with PostgreSQL agents
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Panels → Discussion can open a ClickClack room when the Gateway stores agent sessions in PostgreSQL. File-backed ClickClack credentials continue to work after the async session change.

### Root Cause

The discussion open path used the synchronous latest-session reader to check authority before channel operations and when persisting a binding. On a Gateway with PostgreSQL agent storage, the store rejects synchronous access on the Gateway thread. The original built Gateway reproduction returned `UNAVAILABLE: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker` before the loopback fixture received a channel create request.

The open path now uses the existing async prepared-session helper. It refreshes the session at each effect and at binding commit, and releases the preparation in `finally`. A reset during HTTP can still bind the current session. The recheck uses `isDiscussionAccountCurrent`, which compares the token-file path for file-backed credentials. Comparing the metadata token against a prepared token rejects an otherwise current account because metadata deliberately leaves the token empty. The existing file-backed test failed with `ClickClack discussion authority changed while opening the channel` before this correction.

## Verification

### Real behavior proof

- The earlier built Gateway proof used a PostgreSQL agent store and a loopback ClickClack endpoint. `sessions.create` → `session.discussion.open` → `session.discussion.info` produced one remote channel and an independently verified persisted binding. A reset during the held channel-create response still bound the current session. Archiving during the response refused the attachment and left no binding. This proof predates the branch refresh.
- On the refreshed code, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/discussions/{service-contract,service,service-state-persistence,service-open.agent-storage}.test.ts test/scripts/{postgres-conformance-shards,database-conformance}.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot` passed **128 tests in six files**. The existing file-backed test goes through discussion open before checking grant rotation. The real-storage regression ran locally with SQLite. PostgreSQL CI discovers the same test via the conformance planner.
- The test-line ratchet passed with **+234 lines and 234 lines of allocation credit**. The shared ceiling is unchanged.

### What was not tested

The refreshed branch's local run used SQLite and a synthetic ClickClack transport. It did not run the complete Gateway/PostgreSQL exercise, measure latency, or use a live ClickClack account. Hosted checks are tracked on this PR.

## Contributor credit

Co-authored with @etzelm.

prs.title: fix(ui): dictation shows nothing after Send and drops empty transcripts silently
prs.body:
## Issue #198191 scope boundary — November 14, 2026

This PR improves pending-drain and failure feedback; it is **not a demonstrated fix or recovery mechanism for lost multi-minute recordings**. The report's 5m50s recording closed about 17 seconds after commit without transcript.done, while a 65-second recording succeeded. A fixed eight-second browser-close cutoff is not supported by the pinned source or that report.

Pinned-source assessment at 1cd47bb426878f213888397403c60247c0e78b62:
- composer-dictation-session.ts:329–347 awaits talk.session.close with timeoutMs:null and pauses the late-event grace during file-provider finalization.
- gateway/talk/file-transcription.ts:145–176 consumes the buffered capture, calls the canonical media transcription owner, and unconditionally removes its temporary WAV in finally. This PR does not retain audio for retry.
- The Google media provider treats a missing textual result as an error. The report does not include the original provider response/error and event trace needed to distinguish provider failure from another termination path.
- The existing relay test holds a short synthetic capture's provider completion for six seconds and verifies transcript-before-close ordering. Neither that test nor the contributor's six-second local-whisper browser scenario establishes successful long-recording transcription with the reported Google provider.

A causal repair of the multi-minute loss remains blocked on a sanitized reproduction or original provider outcome plus correlated talk events. Extending a synthetic wait would test ordering, not explain or repair that failure. Retaining/retrying recordings would additionally require an explicit durability/privacy policy; no retention change is included here.

Current observed head remains 1cd47bb42. Current check rollup still includes failed check-test-types (the separately verified inherited benchmark at line373), failed aggregate ci-gate, and PR-context/evidence failures. Do not describe the aggregate as green. All older execution and screenshot claims below retain their stated head and contributor provenance. No merge-readiness claim.

## Head reconciliation

At 14:53 UTC, the GitHub PR API again reports 1cd47bb426878f213888397403c60247c0e78b62 as the hosted head, after briefly advertising merge 655a1bc76ab2886d943d30ebcaa3595e601162be. No assistant source push was performed. The briefly advertised merge changed no dictation files; its verified CI runs were approved, but are not evidence for a different hosted head. Evidence below is pinned to 1cd47bb42 where stated. CI and remote head must be reconciled again before landing. No merge-readiness claim.

## Evidence

The contributor supplied [prior-head real-Gateway evidence for 1cd47bb42](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196063#issuecomment-6878827087). I independently opened and inspected all five screenshots: before/after finishing and disconnect states plus delivered transcript/reply. The images show the expected changed feedback, retain the activity meter, and contain synthetic fixture content with no visible tokens, host addresses, or private conversation data. Execution remains contributor-reported, not an assistant rerun. Reported setup: isolated Gateway and actual browser pairing, Chromium fake microphone carrying a spoken WAV, real whisper.cpp local transcription behind a six-second delay, and a fixture response model. Cloud-provider transcription was not exercised.

| State | Before (current-main source) | After (PR source) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Send during final drain | ![Before: no finishing feedback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/real-1cd47/main-real-send-finishing.png) | ![After: finishing feedback and activity meter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/real-1cd47/pr-real-send-finishing.png) |
| Gateway disconnect during drain | ![Before: reconnecting without transcription error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/real-1cd47/main-real-disconnect-outcome.png) | ![After: visible transcription error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/real-1cd47/pr-real-disconnect-outcome.png) |

![After: transcription delivered once and fixture reply shown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/real-1cd47/pr-real-send-delivered.png)

## Current-head qualification update

The contributor has subsequently merged current main as 1cd47bb426878f213888397403c60247c0e78b62, retaining dc389d7b5925cb7de413dedf7780259fa7c60822 as its first parent and bringing in landed worker fix #198895. The contributor merge has not been overwritten. Exact-current-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43604396669. The selected UI E2E and UI shards 2/3 and 3/3 have passed; remaining checks are running. The test-types gate reports scripts/perf/state-read-worker-bench.ts:373 (possibly undefined tasksCompleted), verified unchanged against this merge’s canonical-main parent. This remains an aggregate-CI failure, separate from the dictation change.

Prior-head evidence only: dc389d7b passed all three UI shards, the selected UI E2E shard, production types, lint, and baseline ratchets. Hosted logs explicitly show the pending-drain, empty-result, exactly-once disconnect, and lazy finishing-status regressions passing. Its aggregate CI failed solely on scripts/perf/state-read-worker-bench.ts:373 (possibly undefined tasksCompleted), an unchanged captured-main file. The real-Gateway lane was not selected, and no corrected-head screenshot artifact was produced. These results do not qualify the newer merge head.

Exact-head secretless CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43602712804 (in progress). Prior-head test-allocation gate passed at +66 lines. Prior-head worker mock/type failures concern unchanged current-main files and remain separate from this feedback correction.
## Current-main correction — pending proof

Published signed correction dc389d7b5925cb7de413dedf7780259fa7c60822, retaining contributor history and merging captured main d98f18ff7c3de4bf46706a71d25705cef346b3ab to resolve observed conflicts. GitHub now reports the PR mergeable.

- Preserves main's lazy ActiveDictationStatus, permission hint and live microphone level. Pending-drain mounting and phase selection use that existing renderer; the regression waits for its lazy load.
- Independent source review found duplicate empty active-disconnect feedback; the correction removes it and extends the existing case to cover empty and retained text. A second independent source review found no substantive introduced defect.
- Current net test growth is 66 lines, with allocation updated. Scoped whitespace validation passed. One pending-session owner and one lazy renderer; no new configuration or parallel policy.
- **Not merge-ready:** exact corrected-head tests, UI checks, and sanitized before/after real-Gateway screenshots remain required. Fork code was not executed locally. Incoming screenshots and tests below remain historical evidence only.
- Exact-head fork [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43601597168), [Workflow Sanity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43601596916), and [macOS Periphery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43601596872) were approved after verifying head, repositories, event, and unchanged workflow source; outcomes are pending.
- Browser proof is blocked here by twelve absent shared libraries, including libatk-1.0.so.0; no connected alternative node. No security policy was weakened.

This is scoped pending/empty-result feedback, not proof that issue #198191's multi-minute transcription loss is resolved. Close uses timeoutMs:null; no eight-second close deadline is claimed.

Related: #195982 (this PR covers the pending-drain status and the silent empty drain; live microphone levels and retrying retained audio stay open there)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after Send on a Control UI hold-to-dictate recording, the composer shows nothing while the final transcript is still being drained, and when that drain ends without a transcript (timeout, rejected finish, or a Gateway disconnect) the recording disappears with no message.

## User Impact

User impact: while the final transcript is on its way, the composer keeps showing "Finishing dictation…" until the text lands or the drain ends, and a recording that ends without text now shows a failure instead of returning to idle: "Couldn’t transcribe your voice." with the existing recovery hint, or "Dictation stopped because the Gateway disconnected." when the composer has already seen the disconnect. On a real Gateway drop mid-drain the transcription request usually fails first, so the generic message appears next to the existing "Reconnecting…" banner (shown in the real-Gateway proof below). Typing stays unlocked during the wait, as before (#135109). The chat composer, the session rail composer and the New Session page all use the same owner and status component, so all three get the fix.

Not in this PR (the ClawSweeper review flags both as needing their own design): a live microphone level meter while recording, and retrying the original audio after a failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ComposerDictationOwner.stop()` deliberately unlocks the composer when Stop is pressed and keeps the stopped session as `pendingCommitSession` until its final drain settles. The status only read `active`/`finalizing`, which are already false by then, and the owner published no change when the pending drain started or ended. The empty-drain branch returned `false` without `onError`, and a rejected `finish()` was already mapped to an empty result.

- The owner exposes `transcribing` and publishes a change whenever the pending drain starts or ends, through one `setPendingCommit` helper that replaces the three hand-written assignments.
- `ComposerDictationSession.finish()`, which already owns dictation failure reporting through `reportFailure()`, reports an otherwise silent empty drain with the existing `dictationFailed` copy, or `dictationDisconnected` when it saw the Gateway disconnect. It skips discarded drains (cancel, supersede, dispose) and drains whose provider error was already reported, so the more specific message is never overwritten. The owner's existing session callback forwards it, so nothing new crosses the owner boundary.
- `ComposerDictationStatus` keeps the existing "Finishing dictation…" state while `transcribing`.

`finalizing` and `locksComposer` keep their meaning, so the voice button, the Send action and composer locking are unchanged. No new strings, so no i18n baseline change.

Corrected during current-main integration: empty active-session disconnects are reported by the session alone; retained-text disconnects retain the owner notice. The regression now asserts exactly one error in both cases.

## Incoming-head evidence (255029681; not corrected-head proof)

Focused tests, red on `main` and green with this change:

```
pnpm --dir ui test src/pages/chat/composer-dictation.test.ts src/pages/chat/composer-direct-dictation.test.tsx
main (new tests only):  4 failed | 38 passed (42)
this PR:                42 passed (42)
```

| Test | catches |
|---|---|
| owner publishes the pending final drain while the composer stays unlocked | pending drain invisible / no change notification |
| owner reports why an empty final drain ended (timeout, disconnect) | silent empty drain; wrong cause on disconnect |
| status keeps "Finishing dictation…" after Stop unlocks the composer | status hidden once `active` is false |

The existing case that expects a provider drain error to be reported exactly once still passes.

Consumer suites (`chat-composer`, `chat-composer-microphone`, `chat-composer-solid`, `chat-composer-status`, `chat-session-rail`, `chat-session-rail-composer-lifetime`, new-session `composer`, `draft-dictation-session`, `new-session-page`) pass.

`pnpm check:changed`: every lane passes except two that fail identically on the merge base and touch no file in this PR (changelog bot attributions in `CHANGELOG/`, and the unused `authorDisplayName` export in `ui/src/pages/dashboards/dashboard-tools.tsx`). oxlint and oxfmt are clean on all changed files; `git diff --check` is clean.

Test cost: the new unit/component tests run in milliseconds. Net test growth is 63 lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/195982-dictation-drain-status.txt`; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` passes with zero slack.

Route boot budget: the session module is loaded lazily, so the empty-drain report and its copy stay out of the chat and New Session boot bundles; the owner change in those bundles is the `transcribing` getter plus `setPendingCommit`, which replaces three hand-written copies. An earlier revision kept the report in the owner and pushed `control-ui-performance` 84 B / 69 B over the route boot JS limits on current `main`; this revision moves it to the session instead of asking for a budget raise.

### Screenshots

Captured from the mock-Gateway browser suite (`ui/src/e2e/browser-dictation-status.e2e.test.ts`, Chromium with a fake microphone) with two extra scenarios that hold to dictate, press "Stop and keep text", and either hold the final drain open or close it without a transcript. With those scenarios applied, the whole file passes on this branch (14/14) and the two new ones fail on `main`. I left them out of the commit per the cost budget, since the unit and component tests above prove the same contracts far more cheaply; happy to add them if you'd like the browser coverage.

| | Before (`main`) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Final drain still pending after Stop | ![before pending](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/before-dictation-pending-final-drain.png) | ![after pending](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/after-dictation-pending-final-drain.png) |
| Final drain returned no transcript | ![before empty](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/before-dictation-empty-final-drain.png) | ![after empty](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/after-dictation-empty-final-drain.png) |

One visible difference worth a maintainer's call: on `main` the partial words stay painted in the textarea during the drain only because nothing re-renders (the next keystroke clears them; the committed draft is identical either way, checked by typing during the drain on both sides). With this PR the composer re-renders when the drain starts, so it shows "Finishing dictation…" over the normal draft until the final text is inserted. If you'd rather keep the partial transcript visible during the wait, I can follow up.

### Real Gateway proof

Isolated real Gateway (`createOpenClawTestInstance`, the same harness as the `*.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` suites) on a throwaway state directory, the built Control UI it serves, real browser pairing, Chromium with a fake microphone playing a spoken WAV, and **real local transcription** through the Talk file-transcription relay using whisper.cpp (`ggml-base.en`) configured in `tools.media.models`. The agent model is a local OpenAI-Responses fixture with a synthetic key, so Send gets a real assistant turn. whisper.cpp runs behind a fixed 6 s `sleep` wrapper to stand in for a slow provider (locally it finishes in under 0.5 s, which leaves no observable drain); transcription itself is real. Run once on `main` (UI rebuilt from `main`) and once on this branch. No credentials, IPs or tokens appear in the media.

| Flow | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Hold to dictate, press **Send** while recording, wait during the drain | ![main send](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/real/before-real-send-finishing.png) composer shows nothing for the whole drain | ![pr send](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/real-v2/after-real-send-finishing.png) "Finishing dictation…" |
| Drain lands | (message is still sent once text arrives) | ![pr delivered](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/real-v2/after-real-send-delivered.png) whisper transcript sent, fixture reply shown |
| Stop, then the Gateway process stops during the drain | ![main disconnect](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/real/before-real-disconnect-outcome.png) recording gone, no message | ![pr disconnect](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/real-v2/after-real-disconnect-outcome.png) failure shown beside "Reconnecting…" |

Recordings: [Send on `main`](https://github.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/blob/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/real/real-gateway-send-before.mp4) · [Send with this PR](https://github.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/blob/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/real-v2/real-gateway-send-after.mp4) · [Disconnect on `main`](https://github.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/blob/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/real/real-gateway-disconnect-before.mp4) · [Disconnect with this PR](https://github.com/Likhith-BlueLotus/openclaw/blob/pr-assets-195982/pr-195982/real-v2/real-gateway-disconnect-after.mp4)

Result: the two real-Gateway scenarios fail on `main` and pass on this branch (2/2), re-captured on head `255029681`. The proof spec is local only (it needs a whisper model), not committed.

Remaining gap: no cloud transcription provider was exercised; the provider-independent relay path above is the same one cloud providers feed.
