prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search
prs.body:
Related: #101422

## What Problem This Solves

Generated Markdown under an agent workspace's `memory/` tree can enter Memory Search and compete with curated notes, with no supported path exclusion for the default roots.

## User Impact

Users can opt in to workspace-relative `memory.search.excludePaths` globs, for example `memory/dreaming/**` and `memory/.dreams/**`. With no setting, indexing behavior is unchanged. Source files remain intact; changing the scope triggers index rebuilding on the next sync. This PR addresses search indexing and watcher eligibility only, not short-term recall/promotion eligibility or inline generated blocks within otherwise eligible notes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discovery and local/remote watchers share the same workspace-relative exclusion predicate. It applies to default roots and overlapping extra paths. The configured scope hash changes only for nonempty exclusions, so existing users retain their index identity. The core config baseline increases by four generated entries as an intentional new optional setting.

This is a draft for the open product-scope decision in #101422; it does not claim to resolve the broader coordinated include/exclude request.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: 139/139 passed across config resolution, file discovery, local/remote watch transport, manager indexing/reindexing, and path matching; the final path-boundary regression passed again (3/3).
- Core and extension production typechecks, changed-file lint/format, config baseline check, config example check, and diff whitespace check passed.
- Independent read-only review found two defects (local watcher propagation and a path-segment boundary), both fixed and reverified.
- Extension test typecheck is blocked by an unchanged `extensions/xai/xai-oauth.test.ts:675` type error on current main. The broad `check:changed` run was stopped after detecting unrelated current-main UI line-cap/test-root-budget failures; it is not claimed green.
- No production Gateway/config/index migration or live reindex was performed. A deployed release and an operator opt-in are required before existing indexed rows can be removed in a real workspace.

## Follow-up review repair (rebased head `a2008ab09`)

- Fixed the reviewer's P2 shared-watcher finding: the effective `excludePaths` now participates in shared selection identity, so joining/leaving agents with different exclusion policies rebaseline the watcher. A focused regression failed on the prior head and passes with the fix; watcher lifecycle tests passed 36/36 on the rebased head.
- A real fs-safe worker join test passed 2/2: after an excluding agent starts, a non-excluding agent joins on the same worker and receives an edit to a formerly excluded report. The mocked lifecycle test also checks rebaseline on both join and leave.
- Built CLI end-to-end test passed 2/2 in isolated state: a normal config-change index removed the generated report without `--force`, retained a curated note, and indexed its subsequent edit. The new CLI case is not Windows-skipped.
- After rebasing onto upstream main `f8dcd1d7f` (and verifying a clean trial merge with later `2e7bc82ad`), 129 targeted tests passed across source/config/watcher paths, plus 36 watcher-lifecycle tests on the final amended head. Core and memory-core extension typechecks, changed-file lint/format, generated config-doc check, and diff whitespace check passed. Independent read-only review of the full rebased 33-file diff found no actionable P0–P2 defect.
- Latest stable `v2026.10.5` indexed two synthetic files in an isolated upgrade fixture. The new head refused to open that older state until Doctor obtains backed-up client-credential migration custody. No backup/Doctor migration was run, so cross-version upgrade proof remains open; this is not claimed as a feature regression or as a passing migration.
- This branch has not been deployed to the operator's Mac; no live config change or reindex occurred. Maintainer approval of the search-only opt-in contract under #101422 remains required before merge.

prs.title: fix(database): Team Reports fails to port to PostgreSQL after a successful dry run
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Backups and database port now accept the PostgreSQL schema name that Team Reports already uses. The schema name and its stored data stay in place.

## What Problem This Solves

A Team Reports SQLite-to-PostgreSQL dry run can succeed, then the actual port fails before staging. Once Team Reports is on PostgreSQL, archive and Git backup also reject its SQLite anchor.

## User Impact

Team Reports can keep its existing PostgreSQL schema when making backups, resuming a port, or porting back to SQLite.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root Cause

The namespace builder includes the store ID `team-reports` in the schema name. PostgreSQL accepts it as a quoted identifier. The anchor and recovery manifest validators excluded its hyphen, and the local-companion backup manifest had the same restriction. PostgreSQL also includes quotes when it deparses these schema references, so the port catalog check removes that quoting when comparing with its reference schema.

The validators retain their original rules for the first character and letter case. The port and backup round trips preserve the name. Original investigation and patch by [etzelm](https://github.com/etzelm).

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

On the base, the Team Reports dry run found the store. The real port then failed at `Database port capture originals`. The local-companion backup case failed with `Backup manifest contains an invalid PostgreSQL anchor`.

On disposable PostgreSQL 16, the focused round-trip test returned `1 passed`. It ran dry run, interrupted publication, resumed against the same quoted schema, and returned to SQLite with the original 64-bit value and unchanged neighboring store.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the PostgreSQL proof</summary>

```sh
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection "$TEST_POSTGRES_URL" -- src/infra/database-engine/port-command.mixed.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'resumes and reverses Team Reports'
```

</details>

## Verification

The focused TypeScript, lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Local recovery, update-capture and backup tests passed, including offline verification and restore of an anchor containing a hyphen.

The five local suites passed all 156 tests on PostgreSQL 16.16 with the same database extensions as CI. The earlier local `OWNER_UNAVAILABLE` failure also reproduced on main. The test database lacked the `unaccent` extension. After provisioning the test database with the CI extensions, all eight mixed-family port cases passed.

The first CI run caught an older backup test that used a hyphen as its invalid character. The follow-up changes that fixture to a dot. All 12 tests in `src/snapshot/database-backup.test.ts` passed locally after that change.

### What was not tested

The Git backup and Gateway lock recovery call paths were traced to the shared anchor reader. They were not exercised end to end for this change.

prs.title: fix(media): read owner WebChat reply media without the toolsBySender overlay
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With a restrictive `tools.toolsBySender["*"]` wildcard — the documented way to give unknown DM senders a small tool set — the owner's own WebChat replies can no longer attach local files. A reply with a `MEDIA:<path>` line for a workspace file becomes an `attachment_error`, while the same turn's tools still run, because owner WebChat turns deliberately skip the sender overlay for tools (`senderPolicyMode: "never"` in `resolveConversationCapabilityPolicy`) but the reply-media read did not.

This lands on the Control UI's default session too: `agent:main:main` has no channel segment, so the first version of this fix (which reconstructed the surface from the session key) still failed there. Both paths are fixed now.

Closes #200661.

## User Impact

An owner using the Control UI (or a `cli`/`chat.send` client with `operator.admin`) gets their attachments back — on the default main session and on channel-scoped sessions alike — while the wildcard keeps protecting every other sender. Non-owner WebChat clients, `operator.read`/`operator.write` clients without `operator.admin`, every channel delivery, the `message` tool, and real external senders keep the sender policy unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveAgentScopedMediaAccess` always folded `resolveSenderToolPolicy` into the read check. `WebchatReplyMediaRequesterContext` already carried the caller facts but dropped `GatewayClientScopes`, so the media read could not tell an `operator.admin` requester from a guest, and `resolveChatSendCallerContext` already resolves that scope set for `chat.send`.

The change carries the scope-derived owner fact from the WebChat requester context through `createReplyMediaPathNormalizer`/`createReplyMediaSourcePreparer` into the resolver, and the resolver skips the sender policy when `isInternalOwnerRequester` holds — the same predicate the tools side uses. Global, agent and group policies still apply; `senderIsOwner` is only ever set by the Gateway requester context (scope check) and the harness attempt, never by reply text.

Session-scoped reply-media staging drops `messageProvider` and the sender-policy resolver treats the session key as authoritative, so the surface the owner check needs cannot be reconstructed for a main-session key: `parseSessionDeliveryRoute("agent:main:main")` is null and its channel segment reads `"main"`. The resolver therefore now takes an explicit `requesterSurface` — set from the authenticated `Surface` on the Gateway call sites and from the inbound `messageChannel`/`messageProvider` on a harness attempt — and only falls back to the delivery route and session key when it is absent. Sender-policy lookups themselves are unchanged: they still prefer the session route over the caller's provider.

## Evidence

Live A/B/C on one machine with one script. Isolated shipped Gateway (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` under an empty temp dir, port 28794, mock OpenAI-compatible provider on 28795), config `session.dmScope: "per-channel-peer"` and `tools.toolsBySender["*"] = { allow: ["web_search"], deny: ["read", "write", "exec", "group:fs"] }`. Each run sends `chat.send "please send me probe.txt"` through a GatewayClient and reads the assistant parts back from `chat.history`. For the "before" leg only the four source files of this PR were reverted to `c46be04` and `dist` rebuilt; the session, config and script are identical.

Main-session path (the `[P2]` finding):

| Run | Session key | Client scopes | PR head source | Last assistant parts | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before | `agent:main:main` | `operator.admin` | `c46be04` (reviewed head) | `[{"type":"text"},{"type":"attachment_error","label":"probe.txt","code":"delivery-failed"}]` | P2 reproduced |
| After | `agent:main:main` | `operator.admin` | `5dbde12` (+ main-session fix) | `[{"type":"text"},{"type":"attachment","label":"probe.txt","size":17}]` | fixed |
| Control | `agent:main:main` | `operator.read`, `operator.write` | `5dbde12` | `[{"type":"text"},{"type":"attachment_error","label":"probe.txt","code":"delivery-failed"}]` | control holds |
| Regression | `agent:main:webchat:afterfix2` | `operator.admin` | `5dbde12` | `[{"type":"text"},{"type":"attachment","label":"probe.txt","size":17}]` | channel-scoped path unchanged |

![Main-session before/after/control on the isolated Gateway](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/201414/main-session-proof.png)

Channel-scoped path (earlier head `c46be04`, same rig):

prs.title: feat(sessions): transcript archive retention config + post-archive vacuum pass
prs.body:
This is the content of [openclaw/openclaw#176078](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176078) (transcript-archive retention) rebuilt with upstream ancestry. The original PR was stuck closed-unmerged and could not be reopened because its head branch (`DarojaAI:fix/issue-137`) had orphan history with no merge-base against `openclaw/openclaw` main; GitHub refuses cross-repo PRs without common history. This branch is recreated from upstream main with a single squashed commit carrying the same change, pushed as `DarojaAI:retention-rebased`.

---

Closes #176077

## Problem
No retention control exists for transcript archives: archive accumulation is unbounded, and SQLite freelist pages are never reclaimed after archive passes — long-lived agents fill disk (fleet incident class, see issue repro).

## Shipped solution
- `session.maintenance.archiveAfter` config (`PositiveDurationSchema | false`), resolved to `archiveAfterMs` in `store-maintenance.ts`; malformed values disable archival rather than destroy history; help copy + labels + docs updated
- `reclaimSqliteFreePagesAfterArchivePass`: WAL checkpoint → freelist check → `incremental_vacuum(N)` on modern stores, full `VACUUM` retrofit on legacy ones — wired into `enforceSessionHistoryMaintenanceSerialized` post-pass, best-effort with next-pass retry
- Tests: 3 new eviction cases (age-driven archival without budget, inspect-as-mutation/warn-immutability, post-archive reclaim + retrofit); `session-history-eviction` 7/7, `store-maintenance` + zod extensions 28/28, `schema.help.quality` 24/24

## User impact
Operators gain a bounded archive footprint; maintenance passes shrink on-disk state instead of only moving it.

## Validation
Touched+adjacent src files typecheck clean (scoped tsgo); touched test files exit 0 individually. Known pre-existing `TS7016` in `src/media/qr-runtime.ts` (missing `@types/qrcode`) reproduces identically on pristine main — unrelated to this branch.

Provenance: fix developed downstream (DarojaAI/openclaw-gateway#137), reference-ported; happy to adapt to maintainer preferences on config naming/placement.

## What Problem This Solves
Operators running long-lived agents have no retention control on transcript archives: archive accumulation is unbounded and SQLite freelist pages are never reclaimed after archive passes, so disk fills on busy deployments (repro in #176077). This PR adds the bounded-retention config surface plus incremental vacuum so archive growth stays within operator-set bounds.

## Evidence
- **Behavioral repro:** with no `session.maintenance` config, transcript archives grow without bound and freelist pages are never reclaimed (#176077 repro; observed unbounded archive accumulation on a 5-minute journal cadence in production).
- **Fix verification:** 34/34 scoped shard tests green on current main (eviction, store-maintenance, schema help/quality suites), rebased across the #175837 sessions refactor.
- **Surface:** `session.maintenance.archiveAfter` (`PositiveDurationSchema | false`) resolved to `archiveAfterMs` in store maintenance; eviction tests cover the reclaim and legacy full-vacuum retrofit paths.

prs.title: feat(sessions): protect selected conversations from automatic maintenance
prs.body:
## Current follow-through (October 30)

This remains an opt-in retention-contract proposal, not a merged or activated feature. The last published head is `5c54571a3aaacdf7bca44844c611d1dd1f831a52`; its test-type job and aggregate gate are still red. The obsolete fixture property identified in that job was repaired and type-checked in a retained local checkout, but that unpublished repair is not current-head CI evidence.

The outstanding behavior gate is isolated shipped-API retention across maintenance, restart, clearing and latest-stable upgrade; the earlier focused source tests do not replace that gate. Fresh GitHub readback on October 31 confirms this head now conflicts with main; integration and revalidation remain outstanding. Maintainer acceptance of the opt-in retention contract is still required. We are resuming this preparation within a shared-memory reserve and will not use a production Gateway as the experiment.

## What Problem This Solves

Long-lived nested project or course conversations can disappear through automatic maintenance, but cannot be pinned while preserving their sidebar hierarchy.

## User Impact

Operators can opt selected sessions out of automatic dashboard archiving, age pruning, entry caps, and disk-budget eviction with `maintenanceProtected: true` through the existing session patch API/tool. Discovery returns the flag. Existing defaults and sidebar placement are unchanged.

Protection includes historical transcript generations, survives reset/restart, and can be cleared with `false`. It requires the current `expectedSessionId`; batch targets carry their own identities. Manual archive/delete still work, and an existing archive is not automatically restored. Ancestors must be protected separately if they also need to remain visible. Protected data can exceed configured cleanup targets. Compaction, cold storage and managed-worktree GC are unchanged. No schema migration is needed; older versions ignore the field, so rollback also removes its protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one optional field in the existing session entry and route it through the existing patch, discovery, lifecycle and maintenance owners. Pinning retains its current presentation constraints. No new retention service, database, global setting or UI state is introduced.

Author simplify pass retained only the existing-owner cutover and distinct regressions; removed a redundant standalone patch test. The feature extends the existing session owners; follow-up generated-validator changes are mechanical wrapper removal and regeneration. The remaining growth wires one persistent setting across all of its writers, readers and automatic cleanup paths. Maintainer review of this new opt-in retention contract is requested; this PR does not change defaults.

## Evidence

- 54 focused tests passed: maintenance writer (18), historical eviction preservation (7), patch expected-identity (15), and reset cleanup (14).
- Regression: a protected nested session survives each dashboard/age/cap phase while its unprotected sibling is archived; clearing protection restores normal maintenance.
- History regression first failed with 3 entries removed instead of 1, then passed after retaining every protected owner generation under physical disk pressure. Explicit reset/delete exclusions remain authoritative.
- Existing reset boundary test verifies retention survives lifecycle reset; patch boundary verifies identity admission, persistence, clearing and unchanged nesting.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm protocol:check` (registry, schema, native generation determinism, since guard), targeted typed lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Measured local wall times with `--maxWorkers=1`: writer file 34.13s; patch file 128.11s (cold compiler); reset + history files 161.32s (cold compiler). History alone was 28.02s warm. Tests extend existing suites/fixtures; no new boot process or timer. CI timing is not yet available.
- Independent source reviews found and prompted fixes for historical-generation retention and PostgreSQL JSON-vs-JSONB handling. The standalone automatic reviewer could not start; no automatic clean-review result is claimed.

Not run locally: full repository suite and PostgreSQL runtime execution. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed upstream CI on 698f3b1bc7a. The predicate uses JSON-preserving extraction to avoid rejecting opaque entry strings during a JSONB conversion. No visual UI changes.



## CI follow-up

CI [39210419913](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39210419913) on `698f3b1bc7a` completed with 71 passed, 22 skipped, and 3 failed jobs. The two root causes were a redundant Boolean conversion in the new JSON test and New Session boot gzip 1,050,029 B against a 1,050,000 B ceiling (the measured base was already 1,050,021 B; candidate +8 B). The third failure was the aggregate gate. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards, database-dialect ratchet, generated-output checks, build, and previously failing node lanes passed on that head. A passing replay does not establish a root-cause fix for earlier chat-fixture failures.

Follow-up `c4113f94812` makes the SQLite assertion explicit about SQL 1 versus 0/NULL, and imports TypeBox's exact existing Unicode helper in the standalone-validator generator instead of its forwarding wrapper. All six owned outputs were regenerated. Validation logic, schemas, budgets, and gate enforcement are unchanged; no dependency version or installed dependency file was changed. The larger generated diff is helper-call renaming, redundant wrapper removal, and formatter/declaration-order effects.

All four JSON-owner tests pass (3.07s wrapper wall, 699ms test-run duration). All 23 canonical validator acceptance/rejection tests pass (6.98s wrapper wall, 4.46s test-run duration), including Unicode boundary coverage. Generator determinism, touched source formatting and diff checks pass. Native independent review found no P0-P2 findings and verified all six generated outputs preserve semantics. The standalone automatic reviewer remained unavailable; no automatic clean-review result is claimed. Isolated minified gzip estimates are not shipped-bundle proof.

[CI 39213084474](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39213084474) on `c4113f94812` completed with 77 passed, 22 skipped and two failures: UI performance plus the dependent gate. Main lint, all five core-lint stripes and PostgreSQL conformance passed. New Session boot was 1,050,294 B against 1,050,000 B (same-run base 1,050,257 B, head +37 B); failure classification was new, not an inherited-main exception. The Unicode wrapper removal alone was insufficient.

## Chat-only validator loading correction

Current follow-up `f3f40728171` separates the three goal-update, goal-clear and voice-event validators from shared `session-input` into generated `chat-input`. Only their two existing Chat consumers import the new group; New Session keeps its restriction and placement checks. There is no shared re-export, asynchronous event-admission change, schema change or validation removal. All owned outputs and the stock cold/warm boot manifest were regenerated. The manifest places the new group only in Chat; six additional reachable existing modules were captured by the canonical generator.

Same-machine, same-toolchain, frozen-build-identity stock UI builds measured:

| Route | Before | After | Delta | JS requests before/after | Fixed budget |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| New Session | 1,048,183 B gzip | 1,047,536 B | -647 B | 20 / 20 | 1,050,000 B |
| Chat | 1,487,825 B gzip | 1,487,955 B | +130 B | 25 / 25 | 1,490,000 B |

Both local product checks pass. These local absolute values differ from CI; actual exact-head upstream measurements remain required, not inferred. No budget, baseline, preload accounting or validation gate was weakened.

61 focused tests across canonical validator parity (23), Chat goals and Talk voice selection passed (9.30s wrapper wall, 6.34s test-run duration). Generator determinism, touched formatting and diff checks pass. Independent native review found no P0-P2 findings; all 11 moved/retained validator bodies and declaration signatures preserve semantics, all production imports are reconciled and the final boot manifest is consistent. The `transcript.js` follow-up is generated counter renaming only. Exact-head main CI had not started on f3f40728171 because the PR merge ref was stale and the generated boot manifest conflicted with current main. Earlier expensive host compiler/declaration checks remain incomplete rather than passing evidence; no live-gateway experiments were performed.


## Current upstream integration

Merged upstream `419653b638d8a53822d0c5ad919a6d05fb8e6c94` in `5c54571a3aa`. The only merge conflict was the generated boot manifest, resolved using the stock manifest generator with upstream loading rules. No budgets, baselines, chunking rules or gates changed. Dependencies were reconciled with the frozen lockfile.

All 65 affected tests pass after integration (four JSON-owner tests plus 61 validator/Chat/Talk tests; 12.38s wrapper wall). Generated-output determinism, touched formatting and diff checks pass. Independent native review of the effective feature diff against the new base found no actionable P0-P2 findings, including preservation, lifecycle, cleanup and generated loading paths.

The repository's strict same-machine comparison against exact upstream `419653b638d` passed with frozen build identity and canonical compression:

| Route | Upstream base | Candidate | Delta | JS requests base/candidate | Fixed budget |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| New Session | 1,050,423 B gzip | 1,049,473 B | -950 B | 20 / 19 | 1,050,000 B |
| Chat | 1,486,626 B gzip | 1,486,488 B | -138 B | 25 / 24 | 1,490,000 B |

The validator split remains necessary: current upstream alone still exceeds the New Session ceiling. Candidate headroom is 527 B. This is shipped-byte/request-count evidence, not a latency claim. Exact-head upstream CI remains required before local installation; no live changes have been made.

prs.title: feat(exec): save command output for post-failure diagnosis
prs.body:
Related: #176116

## What Problem This Solves

Failed or timed-out shell commands can lose their diagnostic output when bounded process results expire or the Gateway restarts.

## User Impact

Gateway-hosted `exec` can opt into `saveOutput: true` and return a workspace log path for later inspection. Saving is off by default. The log retains sanitized stdout/stderr up to the first 2 MiB, survives process-result eviction and Gateway restart, and reports capture failures without preventing command execution.

The path precedes large results so it survives the model-visible persistence cap. Timeout, exit status, approvals and completion routing retain their existing owners. Unsupported sandbox/node saving is rejected before launch. The irreversible-loss warning remains when the retained file does not cover discarded in-memory output.

## Scope and Tradeoffs

This proposes the explicit workspace-artifact stage of #176116. Files require manual cleanup: there is no automatic expiry or aggregate quota. Explicit saving also writes files during incognito sessions. These lifetime/storage/incognito choices still need maintainer product acceptance. Logs do not recover running processes or promise durability across power loss.

## CI Repair

- Integrated main `292ca7a1f`, including the upstream Custodian history-fixture fix [#177988](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177988). The previously failed onboarding locale test had no default `openclaw.chat.history` response. No UI assertion or test timeout is changed here.
- Added two exact-rule-ID `nosemgrep` annotations to the existing trusted-host `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` reads. Caller overrides are normalized and rejected before this block; the reads retain host-owned Git policy. These are explicit false-positive exceptions, not a runtime security fix. The global detector correction remains with [#176328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176328); no rulepack, workflow or ignore list is changed here.
- Added a real exec rejection test for canonical and padded lowercase caller Git-config keys with `saveOutput`, checking that neither the command marker nor an output artifact is created.

## Evidence

Windows / Node 26.10.0, with OpenGrep 1.30.2 running under WSL:

- Actual scanner reproduction: two findings before annotation, zero afterward; `--disable-nosem` still reports the original two. Both dangerous sanitizer-override controls remain detected. The unchanged full rulepack scans all 14 feature production TypeScript files with zero findings/errors.
- Production core and agents-tools test typechecks, focused type-aware lint, formatting, the 19-source line-cap ratchet and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Independent canonical autoreview of the two-file repair, with complete relevant sources supplied, found no actionable P0–P2 findings. This is static review, separate from scanner/test execution.

- The previously failing onboarding locale E2E passes locally (one actual Chromium test, unchanged assertions), using the official matching Headless Shell. Initial setup was interrupted during cold compilation; that attempt is not counted as proof.
- All 11 saved-output cases pass, including the new rejection-before-launch case. The real Git partial-clone/host-policy case also passes: 12 cases across two files, with five unrelated GitHub identity cases filtered by the selected test-name pattern. Both Vitest shards completed successfully.

The previous integration head `128ef4f` passed 62 cases across saved output, notifications, process registry and cancellation. Prior production Gateway proof is pinned to `923ef07ad`: actual agent/tool execution retained 250,042 bytes after a nonzero exit, retained timeout output, and read both files after Gateway restart. That proof used an isolated Gateway and deterministic loopback provider, not a live model; it is not new exact-head Gateway proof.

Before the conflict refresh, head `7647a2446f36e7e4f1979c2b826d33d9be72a032` had the following CI evidence. [Main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39369714233) completed successfully: 58 jobs passed and 28 were scope-skipped, including all three UI E2E shards, production/test types, lint and baseline checks. The [OpenGrep PR-diff scan](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39369714260/job/118454599811) also passed. Required `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review statuses are successful. This is CI clearance, not maintainer approval or a merged PR.

## Earlier Conflict Refresh

Conflict-integration head: `72de4acb50cd8605433a52f52f77663950fe88f4`. Merged main `1c787f912131cd0440db781a74330c538359c7db` to resolve four content conflicts. The resolution preserves main's `resolveExecHost` entrypoint, secret-egress bindings, deadline-bearing structured `followUp`, diagnostics formatting, and updated continuation tests, while retaining the saved-path/capping regression and output-log fields. The capture-file implementation is unchanged.

The four conflict files pass syntax checks under Node 26.12.1; the candidate diff passes whitespace checks. Canonical independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issue in the supplied staged diff. This was static diff review: the metadata-only chunks do not prove runtime behavior, unchanged source was not supplied to the reviewer, and it ran no tests. This source-only worktree has no dependency installation, so refreshed-head type/lint/test proof was delegated to PR CI; subsequent results are recorded below, with each result tied to its own head. Prior-head Gateway evidence remains identified above; no new Gateway run is claimed for this refresh.

The `Evidence` heading now matches the authored-context policy, and [the repaired context check passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39891432847/job/120211869451) before this push. The product decision about lifetime, aggregate storage, and incognito capture remains open.

Follow-up head `3d05b09d1e6df4c996d16a55df85933d1ae1e1cf` repaired those two findings. The first refreshed-head CI run exposed a retained test import from the retired heartbeat completion path and an unused max-lines disable after the runtime file became shorter. The follow-up removes that retired import, checks the current handoff's `source: "exec"` and exact `exec:<process-id>` context directly, and removes the unused lint directive. Saved-path and timeout-guidance assertions remain intact. Both edited files pass syntax checks and the diff passes whitespace checks. The earlier failing run is retained as the reproduction; the follow-up and final results are recorded below.

Earlier verified head: `eade44adbc4f5f8c539f933ff34608a5848d7d4b`. Its only delta from the follow-up above removes `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts` from `config/max-lines-baseline.txt`, matching removal of the now-unused suppression. This is an exact one-entry reduction of the exception list. On `3d05b09d1`, [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39894075097) passed tests, types, lint, and all three UI E2E shards; only the stale exemption remained red. The previously failing agents-tools shard passed 217 cases with 5 scope skips, including the saved-output timeout notification regression. The final head's [full CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39894981519) completed successfully: 53 jobs passed, 28 were scope-skipped, with no failures. Types, lint, baseline ratchets, and scheduled test shards passed. The authored-context check, OpenGrep, dependency review, security-sensitive review, and `openclaw/ci-gate` are successful. GitHub reports clean mergeability. Maintainer acceptance of the lifetime, aggregate-storage, and incognito contract remains pending.

## Current integration refresh

Integrated main `2499f2be3e88e025735268fb622e569d69fcd369` to resolve the three reported conflicts. Current head: `3ae0c2600525502125baf94e443daec8c901ff5b`.

- Preserves upstream Guardian review events, shared runtime/exit outcomes, approval transport, and secret-egress bindings. The extracted process options retain every current upstream option plus `saveOutput`; the outcome type now comes from its upstream owner.
- Local syntax checks for the four resolved/adjusted modules, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Independent static autoreview found no P0–P2 findings in the supplied feature diff. Earlier review batches contained integration file-status metadata, not patch hunks; this is not a claim of runtime or whole-upstream validation.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40294616211) completed. Types, lint, scanner, baseline and the other test jobs pass. One test job fails on four assertions also reproduced in scheduled main; its aggregate gate therefore remains red. Earlier Gateway proof above remains prior-head evidence.
- The lifetime, aggregate-storage, and incognito product decisions remain pending maintainer direction.

<!-- exec-integration-refresh-3ae0c260-20261026 -->

### Current CI failure attribution

The automatic classifier reports `unknown: No matching job on main` because changed-file and scheduled-main job names differ. Manual comparison against [scheduled main run 40288296632](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40288296632), head `106f200f0d8da6a14413941749477b68e1ae839d`, found the same failures:

| Failing case group | PR evidence | Scheduled-main evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Three `abort.target-owner.test.ts` Stop assertions: missing `abortedLastRun`, and `SqliteSessionMutationConflictError` instead of selected-session-change / success outcomes | [PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40294616211/job/121478224900) | [Main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40288296632/job/121457285660) |
| `server.visible-spawn-fallback.product-proof.test.ts` → configured profile preference: expected terminal `ok`, received `error` at line 534 | [PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40294616211/job/121478224900) | [Main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40288296632/job/121457285924) |

The baseline commit is an ancestor of this head. The two test files, `abort.handoff.cases.ts`, and `abort.ts` are byte-identical between that main commit and this candidate. This is manual inherited-failure attribution, not a successful CI run or an approval/bypass request. No expectations, timeouts, workflow rules or gate statuses were changed to conceal these failures.

prs.title: feat: add Cloudflare Clef CLI text and image decisions
prs.body:
Closes #175581

## What Problem This Solves

Operators who already have an authenticated Cloudflare `cf` CLI cannot select hosted Clef Decision models without writing their own adapter. This optional, private plugin registers Clef, Clef Flash, and Clef Omni for Boolean, Choice, and Score decisions, including one embedded PNG, JPEG, or WebP image with text, through the existing `api.runtime.decisions.evaluateV2` contract. It changes no chat model and adds no core tool. Audio, video, multiple images, lists, sort, and tags stay unsupported. Screenshot admission remains #166113 / #166114. Supplied evidence goes to Cloudflare and incurs normal Workers AI usage charges.

## Evidence

Head `1ecd065f9703ddcde1be5ab1a6519cf50fbcd631` rebases the reviewed plugin onto `15ae101a0d8` and corrects the guide. Runtime plugin sources are unchanged from `a4c924769e0`. The registered-host live run loaded the real plugin and a consumer, called the public SDK runtime, and used a real `cf` child with the existing CLI login. Inference and `context.isAdmissible` were not mocked.

Observed terminal output, with the random generation id omitted:

```jsonl
{"case":"allowed-sdk-dispatch","outcome":{"status":"ok","result":{"model":"clef-flash","answers":{"red":{"type":"boolean","probabilityTrue":0.9737}},"usage":{"inputTokens":213,"outputTokens":0}},"provenance":{"providerId":"cloudflare-clef","rubricVersion":"1"}},"cliDispatches":1}
{"case":"revoked-caller-source","rejected":true,"additionalCliDispatches":0}
{"case":"caller-cancellation","rejected":true,"activeRequests":0,"childProcessesAlive":0,"requestFilesRemaining":0}
{"case":"disposed-consumer","rejected":true,"additionalCliDispatches":0}
{"case":"revoked-provider","outcome":{"status":"unavailable","reason":"retiring"},"additionalCliDispatches":0}
```

That run passed 7/7 tests in 31.64 seconds. After this rebase, the focused adapter file passed 18/18 tests in 4.69 seconds. Reproduce the live suite with an existing CLI login:

```bash
OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 OPENCLAW_LIVE_CF_CLEF=1 OPENCLAW_LIVE_USE_REAL_HOME=1 \
  pnpm test:live -- src/decisions/cloudflare-clef.live.test.ts
```

Real-home mode is selected only for the CLI login. The test overrides OpenClaw state, config, and agent paths into its temporary workspace. This is in-process production-runtime proof, not a WebSocket handshake and not a real profile-store revocation.

## Problem and user impact

Operators with an authenticated Cloudflare `cf` CLI cannot select hosted Clef Decision models without writing their own adapter. This optional plugin adds Clef, Clef Flash, and Clef Omni for Boolean, Choice, and Score decisions using the Gateway user's existing CLI OAuth login. It changes no chat model and adds no core tool.

Supported evidence: text/JSON and **one embedded PNG/JPEG/WebP image with text**. `decision_evaluate` accepts that inline image with `contractVersion: 2` and tagged state `{type: "image", dataUri, text?}`, then dispatches it through the selected V2 provider. Plugin code can pass the same state to `api.runtime.decisions.evaluateV2`. Audio/video, multiple images, lists, sort, and tags stay unsupported. A local screenshot file path is separate admission work in #166113 / #166114. Supplied evidence goes to Cloudflare and incurs normal Workers AI usage charges.

## Repairs following review

- **Released-host compatibility:** npm `openclaw@2026.10.4` exports only the V1 Decision SDK. Removed the false `>=2026.10.4` install/compatibility claims. The package is now **private, source-checkout-only, with both npm and ClawHub publication disabled**. No future host release number is invented; a real released V2 host must be verified before enabling publication.
- Added the package-local README and replaced the repository-private test helper import with `openclaw/plugin-sdk/test-env`.
- **Production-path defect found by the new proof:** declared static plugin-owned auth scope and the synthetic/non-secret CLI marker in the manifest, matching the runtime provider. Before this correction, real prepared host dispatch returned `credentials-unavailable`; direct adapter tests missed it.
- Replaced raw temporary-directory creation with the public SDK private-workspace helper and cleanup. Fixed the abort-rejection lint defect and two test type errors.
- Regenerated plugin inventory and config baselines using their owners. Exactly 24 introduced plugin config paths are accounted for (three Clef settings plus the existing generic per-plugin envelope); core/channel config budgets and hashes are unchanged.

## Authority-chain and real CLI proof

The new `src/decisions/cloudflare-clef.live.test.ts` loads the actual plugin through the production loader plus a minimal consumer plugin. The consumer invokes **the public SDK runtime**, then the actual prepared model/catalog/auth owner, provider host, adapter, and CLI. Neither inference nor `context.isAdmissible` is mocked or replaced by an always-true predicate. A real `cf` child uses the existing CLI OAuth login.

OpenClaw state/config/agent paths and synthetic media are isolated from the running Gateway. The observation executable only records child startup and delegates to real `cf`. It does not forward termination: on POSIX the CLI inherits the observer's process group, deliberately testing the transport's negative-PID group kill. Both recorded PIDs must be dead, private files removed, and host active-request count zero before proof completes. This suite is POSIX-only, not a Windows cleanup claim.

The five cases establish: a permitted native image decision; host-issued operator-source revocation before another CLI starts; actual consumer-instance disposal; actual provider reload/retirement; and cancellation settlement of the observer and real CLI. The operator identity is synthetic and bound through the host's authority issuer/caller context. The installed Gateway was not restarted or migrated.

`OPENCLAW_LIVE_CF_BINARY` and `OPENCLAW_LIVE_CF_PROFILE` optionally select the CLI executable/profile.

## Validation

- 18 focused adapter tests passed on the rebased head, including typed wire translation, image limits, malformed results, credential-override rejection, environment isolation, cancellation/deadlines, cleanup, and authority refusal.
- 9 package publication/collection tests passed on the previous head, including the formerly failing plugin-release suite.
- The registered-host live test passed all five scenarios in **4.871 seconds test time**; both live files passed **7/7 tests in 31.64 seconds wall time** (CI seconds unavailable).
- All six live adapter-level cases were rerun successfully on the repair: text and image on each of Clef, Flash, and Omni, with Boolean/Choice/Score questions. They are transport/typed-answer proof, not general accuracy claims; the new host-path evidence closes the previous direct-context gap.
- Targeted core host-proof typecheck and type-aware lint passed on the previous head. The changed-graph preflight hits unrelated gateway/infra root-budget limits; the canonical `other` test graph was checked directly rather than running every core shard.
- Config baseline was regenerated on this rebase. Plugin config paths moved from 4711 to 4735. Core stayed 2565 and channel stayed 4043. Generated plugin inventory, public extension-test import boundary, temporary-directory lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed on the previous head.
- Fresh Codex repair review completed. Its one P2 suggestion to add observer signal forwarding is not applied: the unchanged production transport already kills the entire POSIX group, and a forwarder would conceal a group-termination regression. Actual observer/CLI liveness and cleanup are checked, and Windows is explicitly excluded.

Prior-head CI also reported failures in unrelated Discord/Signal/Telegram ingress, memory reindex, terminal delivery, and Android Wear suites. They were inspected but not reproduced on base, so this PR does **not** claim their inherited status is proven. Updated-head hosted CI remains the broad gate.

## Merge conflict

Resolved again onto `15ae101a0d854480cfb500a5e241055450da39da`. The only conflicts were the generated config baselines. Regenerating them left core 2565, channel 4043, and plugin 4737, which is 24 plugin paths over the new main count of 4713. Core and channel hashes are unchanged.

## Simplify

The optional plugin stays. It is the existing Decision provider owner: one codec, one CLI transport, and the prepared V2 contract. This pass did not add a second image API or cut production code. It removed the guide claim that `decision_evaluate` is text/JSON-only. The tool already accepts `contractVersion: 2` inline image state. A local screenshot path stays a separate admission feature.

Follow-up on head `a4c924769e0`: current main's package-boundary compile selects every extension whose tsconfig extends the packaged boundary base, then requires a bundled or published surface. This package is private, `bundledDist` is false, and both publication flags are false, so that opt-in failed with `No packaged surface for extension boundary: cloudflare-clef`. The opt-in tsconfig is removed. Adapter tests on this head: 18/18 passed.

## Repository adoption

**Answer: yes. Adopt this as a repository-owned optional plugin.**

Keep it in this repository. Leave the package private, source-checkout only, with `publishToClawHub: false` and `publishToNpm: false`, until a released host that exports the V2 Decision runtime is verified. Do not publish it, and do not add a core tool or a chat model. The public SDK contracts stay the implementation boundary, so a later independent package remains possible. This is the contributor's adoption request for the decision on this pull request. It is not a maintainer approval, and it does not approve the workspace lockfile change.

## Beta compatibility and native-tool follow-up

Commit `39e0e9ec65a195980d760c682165068894ee5f94` adds two additions on top of the previously reviewed head (no rebase and no production plugin changes):

- Document verified Decision V1-only exports in both published `2026.10.4` and `2026.10.10-beta.2`. Discovery/picker metadata does not prove provider registration. This V2 candidate remains private and source-checkout-only; publication stays disabled and no released compatibility floor is claimed.
- Extend the existing registered-host live suite to exercise the actual native `decision_evaluate` bridge (`createDecisionTool`) as well as the SDK, including native caller-source revocation with no additional CLI dispatch.

Updated live proof: **1 test passed, six logged scenarios, 50.77 seconds wall / 5.991 seconds test**. SDK and native dispatch each used real Clef Flash with a synthetic red image and returned Boolean `probabilityTrue: 0.9737`. Revoked callers did not dispatch; cancellation settled with zero active requests, live child processes, or remaining private request files. Consumer disposal and provider retirement checks also passed. This is POSIX in-process source-host proof, not a WebSocket handshake, profile-store revocation, whole-Gateway upgrade, or soak certification. The installed Gateway was not changed.

Reproduction on this host uses the existing live command above with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`. Scoped MDX validation (two docs), type-aware lint of the changed test, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. A prior full source build passed in 9m 1.7s before these docs/test-only additions; no fresh full build is claimed. CI time for this follow-up is not yet available.

The branch still requires separate base-conflict resolution and maintainer adoption/dependency approvals. Prior failing extension CI reported `extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-index-recovery.test.ts:138`; its inherited status has not been established. Neither source inference nor this documentation update authorizes a live Gateway switch; isolated upgrade/recovery and soak validation remain pending.

The contributor explicitly requested commit/push and hosted ClawSweeper review after the local AutoReview attempt failed authentication without producing a report. That attempt is not counted as a completed review.


## PR simplify follow-up

Head `a75fb0624a33c7b04626951ad5f65c8e27ee361b` applies the repository's `pr-simplify` pass across the complete 20-file proposal. The smallest coherent stage remains a private, source-only optional Decision provider; publication and any shared media-contract expansion remain deferred.

- Removed the codec's redundant whole-batch validation. `evaluateVersion` owns input admission before prepared dispatch; the adapter retains Clef-specific model, input-shape, question-ID and rubric limits. Response decoding/validation and live authority checks remain intact.
- Consolidated identical codec checks across model names (four duplicate executions removed) and removed the fixture's self-check. Real subprocess dispatch still covers all three model routes; typed translation, image framing/full-size input, malformed responses, credential/routing refusal, failure categories, cancellation and private-file cleanup retain their assertions. The separate opt-in adapter/live-host suites remain unchanged.
- Kept the single provider/codec/transport and entrypoint: no new state, wrappers, core tools, SDK contracts or compatibility fallback. Retained manifest/package discovery, auth and release metadata, generated config/inventory artifacts, navigation and setup/compatibility docs because each serves installation or the provider contract. No unrelated hunks or new dependencies were added.

Delta against merge base `15ae101a0d854480cfb500a5e241055450da39da`: production TypeScript **+415/-0**, tests **+650/-0**, metadata/docs **+627/-5**. Relative to the preceding PR head only: production **-2 lines**, test LOC unchanged, four fewer duplicate test executions. No broader size reduction is claimed.

Fresh proof: **14/14 offline adapter tests passed** (4.24 seconds wall); scoped formatting, commit-hook formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The registered-host live rerun failed its first allowed SDK dispatch with `unavailable/credentials-unavailable` (54.39 seconds wall). The CLI login check succeeded, including with the adapter's filtered environment and isolated working directory; the host failure's cause is not established. Earlier successful live runs above remain prior-input evidence, not a passing result for this head.

The scoped type-aware lint wrapper expanded into SDK declaration preparation; that preparation was interrupted (exit 130), so no fresh lint/typecheck pass is claimed. Local AutoReview again failed authentication without producing a report. After being told the review was unavailable, the contributor explicitly directed commit, push and ClawSweeper review. Hosted review/CI remain outstanding. Nothing here certifies a whole-Gateway upgrade or soak; the installed beta is unchanged.


## Simplify (cf51c14fca6)

The plugin README no longer repeats host compatibility, publication rules, or live-test commands. That policy stays in the Clef setup guide, which the README links to. Codec, CLI transport, manifest, offline tests, and both live suites are unchanged: each still covers a distinct failure (wire translation, process settlement, catalog limits, direct CLI inference, and registered-host authority).

Against `origin/main` at this head: 20 files, +1650/−5. This revision is docs only, −42 README lines, and no production or test delta. The live `credentials-unavailable` discrepancy, maintainer dependency approval, and repository-adoption decision are unchanged.


## Live proof on cf51c14fca6

Registered-host suite rerun on 2026-10-29 against head `cf51c14fca6`. `cf` 1.0.0-beta.12 already had a valid OAuth login. The suite loaded the real plugin in-process, kept OpenClaw state, config, and agent paths in a temporary workspace, and delegated to the real `cf` binary. The running Gateway was not restarted. One test passed in 5.458s; wall time including worker startup was 65.53s.

```jsonl
{"case":"allowed-sdk-dispatch","outcome":{"status":"ok","result":{"model":"clef-flash","answers":{"red":{"type":"boolean","probabilityTrue":0.9737}},"usage":{"inputTokens":213,"outputTokens":0}},"provenance":{"providerId":"cloudflare-clef","rubricVersion":"1"}},"cliDispatches":1}
{"case":"allowed-native-dispatch","outcome":{"status":"ok","result":{"model":"clef-flash","answers":{"red":{"type":"boolean","probabilityTrue":0.9737}},"usage":{"inputTokens":213,"outputTokens":0}},"provenance":{"providerId":"cloudflare-clef","rubricVersion":"decision-v1-5c8ca25498a3175a5d021b3b"}},"cliDispatches":1}
{"case":"revoked-caller-source","rejected":true,"additionalCliDispatches":0}
{"case":"caller-cancellation","rejected":true,"activeRequests":0,"childProcessesAlive":0,"requestFilesRemaining":0}
{"case":"disposed-consumer","rejected":true,"additionalCliDispatches":0}
{"case":"revoked-provider","outcome":{"status":"unavailable","reason":"retiring"},"additionalCliDispatches":0}
```

Prepared SDK dispatch and native `decision_evaluate` both returned ok for the synthetic red square. The earlier `credentials-unavailable` result did not recur. Revoked callers, cancellation, consumer disposal, and provider retirement started no further CLI work.

prs.title: improve: resume cold-history navigation after update readiness
prs.body:
Related: #182616

This addresses only reconstructible cold-history navigation in the stopped update window, not the issue's other copy/hash or repeated-Doctor costs.

## What Problem This Solves

Updates can keep the Gateway stopped while Doctor builds navigation for old cold-history archives. Those archives remain restorable without the navigation, so this work need not delay readiness.

## User Impact

Update Doctor leaves reconstructible SQLite navigation pending for post-readiness maintenance. Required migrations, integrity and recovery checks remain before activation. Standalone Doctor and PostgreSQL retain their existing behavior. No schema, configuration, retention or permission changes.

**Still a draft: foreground-latency acceptance and five interleaved update/downtime samples are incomplete.** Preparation now runs outside the canonical writer and outside the foreground discovery-reader pool, but complete-archive publication remains atomic. A single diagnostic pair at prior head `471ff839a604` exceeded the declared 20% investigation threshold in tail latency; this is not an accepted regression or a no-regression claim. The test host also reproduced long hot-write COMMIT stalls on unchanged baseline code. Controlled comparative measurement is required before this PR can be marked ready.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing pending SQL predicate and post-readiness transcript-facts scheduler. A cancellable, lifecycle-owned reader prepares verified archive navigation in disposable SQLite. A separate lazy maintenance reader lane prevents foreground discovery cleanup from waiting for the whole archive. The canonical writer rechecks the source/archive identity and pending state, then copies the complete projection in one transaction. No incomplete canonical rows or new durable progress store are published; unused preparation is discarded and restart rediscovers pending archives.

Typed archive-read failures leave the affected archive pending while healthy later archives progress. Authority, cancellation, SQL and lifecycle failures are not swallowed. Ordinary foreground reader deadlines remain unchanged.

## Evidence

### Bounded qualification attempt — 2026-11-18 21:28–21:29 UTC

Stopped before expensive work because sustained host qualification failed. Sixty one-second observations spanning 59.11 seconds used the declared quiet-host limits of I/O full-pressure avg10 <=1% and one-minute load/CPU <=0.25. **48 of 60 observations exceeded the I/O limit**: range 0.69–6.89%, ending at 1.56%. Maximum load/CPU was 0.08094 (128 CPUs), so load was within its limit. The earlier low-pressure snapshot did not hold throughout the window. This is host evidence, not a fresh baseline-write stall or a candidate regression measurement.

Source and publication remain `a078fd677795d17d6633a9c2a189e96c024039ea`, with no local delta. The retained qualified candidate package digest was rechecked as `90fbb6b12768052a4af4262cae161745c0bf1e2567366739b60a3bb2b8c9f5e9`. The admitted base `0aafe6691b818c24ac00a2172e57819b21632554` has state40/agent43; retained historical control has agent42 and was not reused. A matching-base package is not retained. Its supported route is a task-owned detached worktree from that exact admitted Git object and the existing canonical `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mts` build/integrity workflow, not rebuilding the candidate or altering the shared checkout.

Because the host capacity gate failed, that missing baseline was not built. A qualifying committed-runner manifest/preflight and unchanged-baseline RPC control therefore remain unrun, as do all five interleaved pairs. No package installs, Gateway launches, source/review changes, retries for green, threshold changes or native-downtime claims were made. Required next condition: a sustained qualified quiet host, followed by the missing matching-base artifact and the unchanged committed sampler.

### Workload-only follow-up (`a078fd677795d17d6633a9c2a189e96c024039ea`)

This follow-up changes only the performance entrypoint/helper, its README, one plan test and the test-line allocation. Product runtime remains identical to `9901fa77f855c0cf2eecaa0b0032a0086d699f77`; the package/update/restore/automatic-rollback proof below stays bound to that runtime artifact, not a newly built package.

The existing update-performance entrypoint now owns the rerunnable installed-Gateway foreground procedure. Read-only plan/preflight checks artifact and Node SHA-256, fixture-producer bytes, schema compatibility, a fresh owned scratch root and at least five serial A/B pairs. It preserves qualified source/build receipt references as declarations, not inferred provenance. A matching schema-43 baseline package is required; the historical schema-42 control is not qualified for this composition.

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/update-doctor-generation-measure.ts \
  cold cold-navigation-runtime plan .openclaw/tmp/cold-runtime-input.json
```

The manifest and controlled-host requirements are documented in `scripts/perf/README.md` under **Installed cold-navigation foreground workload**. Change only `plan` to `run` after artifact and quiet-host qualification. The fixed workload is three 4,096-event archives, an independent hot session, two `chat.inject` loops and one `chat.history` loop for 60 seconds with 50 ms after responses. Receipts retain all RPC IDs/errors, readiness request intervals, pending/atomic-publication observations, archive hashes/FK checks, host/IO pressure and joined cleanup. The command stops on failures or >=20% adverse paired tail movement rather than retrying for green. It leaves TOTAL UPDATE and native-service GATEWAY DOWNTIME **unmeasured/null**; the separate real native handoff remains required.

Validation: two focused tests passed (570 ms tests, 1.73 s wrapper): real-entrypoint plan/schema refusal and the measured-overlap qualification regression, including mismatched package/Node/fixture/schema and pre-existing-root refusal before fixture mutation. Scripts and tooling-test typechecks, targeted lint/format, script erasability (1,949 files), both Knip unused-file scans (zero findings), scoped diff checks and the official test-line ratchet passed. Net test lines are now 577 with a justified 177-line excess allocation; this includes the prior 435-line runtime regressions plus 142 workload-test lines. CI seconds are not yet available. No packages were installed, Gateways started or full timing samples run for this workload-only addition.

A bounded workload-delta narrative review found a real P2: backfill could finish during unrecorded warmup, allowing a false performance pass. The completion-only gate reproduced that failure. Warmup is now recorded/correlated and compared separately; both measured writes and history must complete with pending work at both request boundaries, followed by eventual completion. Missing overlap is explicitly inconclusive. Request/transition/completion clocks share Gateway launch origin. The report distinguishes sampled pending-window overlap from exact writer-lock occupancy. Targeted supplied-source verification resolved the finding with no new actionable P0–P2 findings. The reviewed workload-only patch SHA-256 is `4aa874f63a498042b7d285c2ed3fc222e01a10e96d061a29cd6ec1aa9d967bbe`; review was narrative, without independent checkout/hash custody or test execution. This does not replace helper-validated review or an end-to-end run of the newly committed sampler.

### Current refreshed-base integration

Source: `9901fa77f855c0cf2eecaa0b0032a0086d699f77`, integrating main `0aafe6691b818c24ac00a2172e57819b21632554` through the managed base-refresh workflow because the PR conflicted. This resolved the reported conflict at that runtime head.

- The sole manual conflict resolution preserves upstream agent-creation alias checks, claim capture and cleanup reservation before the caller-owned maintenance deadline. Dispatch/settlement claim assertions and native witness propagation remain intact. Whole-archive atomic publication and off-writer preparation are unchanged.
- **61 tests across four affected suites passed** in 103.13 s: session-transcript worker lanes, active-facts backfill, cold-storage worker and usage-worker environment/recreation coverage. Core and affected agents/sessions test types, targeted runtime lint/format and scoped diff checks passed. A whole cached diff against the old guest base flags an upstream release-note blank EOF; that release-owned file was not changed by this repair and is not in the PR diff.
- A bounded independent narrative review of the resolved runtime and claim/scope owners found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Runtime-file SHA-256: `234e4249a1e951f802bad47558cffc62ff49c9e7070a5bceb81cf0c41bc2fb24`. This is not helper-validated Auto Review or a review of unrelated upstream changes. No unbounded helper retry was launched.
- The refreshed base carries upstream version/schema and cold-body maintenance changes; this PR adds no new schema or partial canonical navigation contract. Installed-package/update/rollback correctness is now requalified for `9901fa77…` below. The performance measurements remain prior-head diagnostics; no new latency or downtime-distribution claim is made.

### Current artifact and latest-stable functional qualification

- A new canonical package was built once from the accepted source for `9901fa77f855c0cf2eecaa0b0032a0086d699f77`; full package integrity passed. SHA-256: `90fbb6b12768052a4af4262cae161745c0bf1e2567366739b60a3bb2b8c9f5e9`. The managed staged-source snapshot stayed unchanged through build and execution (`b3647cf94ea2d16dc701a2ba23f329d17b4631e201fce42feae71e7d6708846f`); the older `471ff839…` package was not reused.
- The live npm latest-stable tag resolved to **2026.11.5**, and that exact released driver installed under the existing age/script policy without an override. Its Doctor imported real synthetic legacy input and produced agent schema **38**. The correctly bound actual package entrypoint performed a successful real update to the source candidate, also version 2026.11.5 but agent schema **43**. All three 4,096-event archives were pending immediately after update. Node 24.22.1 was used throughout.
- Public `chat.history` opened an old archive before its navigation existed. The existing legacy fallback restored that archive; **all 4,096 original event payloads, sequence values and creation timestamps matched the independent pre-update digest**, including after reopening in another process. The two remaining archives stayed byte-identical. Separate installed Gateways reached HTTP readiness with pending counts **2**, then **1**, and resumed background completion to **0**; foreign-key checks were empty.
- The initial fixture expected history to leave zero navigation rows and therefore stopped after observing 4,096 restored rows. Source inspection confirmed the supported missing-navigation restore fallback. The incorrect fixture oracle and its failure were retained; exact restored bytes were verified independently, and execution continued from the existing state without replaying the successful update or history mutation. No production code or acceptance timeout was changed.
- The maintained, exact-state-bound failing-Doctor package caused a real post-activation failure and **automatic rollback succeeded**. Config, installed finalize-worker hash, six agent-table hashes, schema and remaining archive payloads matched the pre-failure oracle exactly. The restored installed Gateway reached readiness with zero pending navigation. Update run: `2609fcae-bfcb-48c6-b4b0-048d3923af79`; rollback run: `31b95910-bb4b-4ad5-94d0-b90a80d56e7b`.
- This is the same isolated foreground-process `--no-restart` workflow with managed stop/relaunch, not native-service automatic-restart or performance acceptance. No five-pair timing runs, architecture changes or Auto Review retry were performed.

### Prior-head implementation proof (`471ff839a604`)

- Focused repair validation: 46 tests across three affected suites passed (65.44 s wall), followed by two exact-restore/resume regression cases after the final test-only assertion (49.42 s wall). Prior unchanged codec/Doctor and reader-adapter evidence is retained. The foreground-pool routing regression was red before the isolation repair and green afterward. Cold restore before/after completion, missing/corrupt archive progress, cancellation/recreated pass, concurrent restoration, atomic rollback and exact archive preservation are covered.
- Core and affected agents/sessions test typechecks, targeted six-file lint, formatting, docs/script formatting and diff checks passed. The test-line gate passed with 435 net lines and a justified 35-line allocation for the distinct update/restore/corruption/preparation/lifetime/cleanup boundaries.
- Canonical package build and full tarball integrity passed. Candidate SHA-256: `ed3935063014a778e765b27fc6c4d111b7369a45b51dfe5c769180013238e390`. The installed preparation dependency was inspected to verify the isolated lane and private schema transaction, rather than relying on an unchanged worker entrypoint hash. Packaging's UI warnings were also present in the pinned baseline build.
- **Actual update and rollback passed for prior head `471ff839a604`**, using Node 24.22.1 and a fresh published 2026.11.2 installation. Released Doctor imported real synthetic legacy input and created schema 27. A dry run verified the actual package entrypoint, isolated installation root and npm-global mode. The real CLI update succeeded to the rebuilt candidate/schema 42 with all three cold archives still pending.
- Two separate installed-candidate Gateway processes reached real HTTP readiness with pending counts 3 and 2. The first stopped after one complete archive; the second completed the remaining two. Three archives × 4,096 events (12,288 events; approximately 150.9 MB raw envelope bytes) retained exact payload hashes and checked archive metadata, with no foreign-key failures.
- The maintained state-scoped failing-Doctor package caused an actual post-activation failure. Automatic rollback reported succeeded. Config, installed finalize-worker hash, six agent-table hashes, schema and archive payloads exactly matched the pre-failure oracle; the restored installed Gateway reached readiness. Update run: `79d9bfed-a7de-422a-941b-bb183e9abdef`; rollback run: `1c59e044-3cbc-4bbf-8acb-5e2a73d87a26`. This is an isolated foreground-process, `--no-restart` fixture with manual supervised relaunch, not native-service automatic-restart or downtime-distribution proof. All owned Gateway processes were stopped, joined and verified absent.

### Performance qualification is not complete

The prior-head 60-second pilot uses two public `chat.inject` loops plus one `chat.history` loop, with 50 ms between responses and the same archive shape. The following is **one diagnostic pair, not five-pair acceptance**:

| Observed metric | Pinned baseline | Prior candidate (`471ff839a604`) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Successful foreground writes | 2,083 | 1,999 |
| Write median / p95 / p99 (ms) | 7.02 / 9.88 / 14.11 | 7.30 / 11.55 / 38.83 |
| Write p99 after first 3 seconds (ms) | 13.37 | 16.95 |
| Successful history reads | 1,100 | 1,095 |
| History p95 / p99 (ms) | 6.22 / 7.27 | 6.26 / 8.80 |
| Canonical cold publication | Completed before startup | 3 atomic commits; 48.0 ms maximum admitted execution, 137 ms total |
| Cold preparation outside writer | Not applicable during runtime | 3,025 ms total |
| Host I/O full pressure, avg60 start → end (%) | 6.90 → 2.12 | 1.73 → 0.88 |

The measured prior candidate reached readiness with all three pending and finished navigation after 47.5 s. Those timings are diagnostic observations, not a gain claim. The largest remaining write delays were not all archive-overlapping, so atomic copying has not been established as their sole cause.

An earlier prior-candidate pilot failed when a hot-session COMMIT took 14.3 s after backfill had completed. A bounded unchanged-baseline diagnostic then reproduced a 17.9 s COMMIT and the same RPC timeout with no cold backfill running; host I/O pressure rose to about 22% full avg10. Both failures are retained. This demonstrates a baseline problem under those conditions, but does not explain away every candidate tail-latency difference. No timeout, safety or acceptance threshold was increased. Comparative runs stopped rather than retrying for green.

Remaining performance gates: a controlled environment without these baseline stalls, matching-base/current runtime artifacts, execution of the committed foreground sampler, and five interleaved baseline/candidate real-update/native-handoff samples separating TOTAL UPDATE, observed GATEWAY DOWNTIME, eventual background work and foreground latency. The new runtime sampler does not provide updater/native-service measurements. Latest-stable functional upgrade/rollback is now qualified for `9901fa77…` using the newly admitted 2026.11.5 driver. Earlier age-policy refusals and the 2026.11.2 run are historical evidence only. Performance acceptance remains open despite functional correctness passing. The reported main conflict is resolved at `9901fa77…` against `0aafe669…`. The historical installed proof used base `b255cc584…`; refreshed-base acceptance must not be inferred from that older artifact.

### Review and prior-head evidence

The previous published head `54795095a26a7f08b064cee7246395ab19d6eec7` decoded/projected archives while holding the canonical writer. Its prior update/rollback proof remains prior-head evidence, and its measured roughly 540–570 ms archive-overlapping RPC waits prompted this repair. Its [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200908#issuecomment-6966703854) does not cover the new implementation.

Independent narrative supplied-source reviews resolved two real P2 findings: corrupt-first-archive starvation and inheritance of the foreground 60-second deadline. The pre-refresh targeted review found no new actionable P0–P2 in lane isolation, scratch transaction, cancellation or cleanup. It reviewed runtime snapshot `111da2db5296df74b7e844b9d064220ddec3c391fbf92dd4dfde99da59497f9e`; the final local snapshot `1177095149ebe6c5794513e7812ee7eb44e6cba8c902deb2432e447424a6f1f0` differs only in test/line-allocation metadata. This was not live-checkout or helper-validated review. A newly available bound Auto Review was attempted on the current complete candidate, then interrupted by Gateway shutdown; no validated report was recovered and it was not rerun. Local structured review and current-head CI remain incomplete.

prs.title: fix: let queued chat writes run before background page cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Transcript appends and session patches can wait behind another archive-pruning free-page pass even when foreground work is already queued.

## User Impact

Queued foreground writes run before the next background free-page reclaim pass. A pass already in progress still finishes first, so slow native commits or checkpoints can still delay a write. No configuration, schema, retention, or durability changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session writer now passes the queue's existing background priority for worker `session.history.free-pages` operations. The queue remains the sole admission owner; other session operations and explicit native maintenance keep their existing priority.

## Evidence

- The new regression fails on the unchanged base with admission order `reclaim, foreground`, and passes with `foreground, reclaim`. It exercises the real reclaimer and queue and confirms the same two pages are reclaimed.
- All 63 focused archive-pruning, source-binding, and writer-admission tests pass. The regression takes about 0.9 seconds; the runtime-config test shard takes 49 seconds, including existing real worker/lifecycle coverage.
- Chromium session-view tests: 3 passed. Production-build session-navigation E2E: 5 passed.
- Codex autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Simplification retained one existing priority argument: production +6 lines, tests +62, docs +3.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed, including production and all core-test typechecks, changed-file lint, database guards, and dead-export scans.

This is an admission fairness fix, not a hard writer-hold bound. Prior synthetic one-page evidence with 500 ms added per sync still measured a 4.093-second hold; changing that maintenance design is outside this PR.

## CI Investigation

Exact-head CI run [44393832611](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44393832611) completed with failure. Six jobs failed before tests because Launchpad returned HTTP 503 while installing Git. A separate Linux Talk cancellation test stopped producing output and hit the runner watchdog.

The Talk test also fails on the exact branch parent, `cf5cf7a8c609d8b26bd81495634eda973a2e4742`: scheduled main run [44390931290](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44390931290/job/135108965802) records a 120-second timeout for `keeps host-authenticated node approval cancellation (public callback: false)`, a 180-second cleanup timeout, and stale lifecycle state in the following case. This is a main CI regression requiring follow-up. Source history identifies #201334 (`04cb8179ccd66`): it removed the operator authority's device-revocation subscription while the Talk parity fixture still invalidates that source and waits for the running approval to abort. No unrelated test or authority-policy change is included here. The lane is not claiming that failed CI is green.
