prs.title: fix(agents): stop sessions_send from blocking turns past its timeout
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A `sessions_send` to a busy child can remain blocked before its reply wait. Without a declared host deadline, a Code Mode call can hold the turn until the 15-minute watchdog aborts it, delaying queued user messages; the next turn can repeat the same hang.

The reproducible unbounded await is active-child steering in `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.delivery.ts:275`: `deliveryTimeoutMs: undefined` leaves transcript acknowledgment unbounded at lines 324–334. The original tool entry point supplied no admission ceiling or execution deadline. The incident arguments are unavailable, so the exact production await and proposed announcement cycle remain unproven.

## Fix

A fixed, named 30-second admission ceiling covers requester-source acquisition, target lookup, preparation, admission, and transcript acknowledgment, including zero-wait sends. After acceptance, `timeoutSeconds` retains its existing reply-only contract (default 30 seconds; zero skips waiting). Direct calls and retained replay share this owner. The declared watchdog deadline is tool start plus the admission ceiling plus the reply wait.

Admission expiry returns a visible timeout advising inspection before retry, fences new sender effects, and releases communication subscriptions without cancelling receiver-owned input. Late materialized results still transfer to the existing reply-delivery owner. No watchdog window, retry policy, or configuration changes.

The follow-up fixes a regression in `8588ea86849b`: the initial combined budget could return false ambiguous timeouts when admission exceeded a short reply timeout. Documentation now states the two independent budgets.

The `github_publish` sibling already has bounded response waits on this base via #200927; its previously verified Node and QuickJS Code Mode regressions pass. Its separate deferred workspace handoff was not reproduced as hanging or changed here.

## Evidence

- The deterministic one-second reply / two-second admission case fails on `8588ea86849b` and passes with this fix. It is folded into the existing fake-timer child-result case.
- The busy-child transcript-ack ceiling and long declared deadline / late child-result regressions remain green. The original two owner regressions were also proven red on base `04cb8179ccd66`.
- The exact requested three-file command with `--maxWorkers=8` passes **83/83**: admission 18, sessions 57, agent-step 8; 178.81 seconds locally. These real owner compositions exercise SQLite-backed admission, caller authority, and completion custody.
- The 11 sibling files cover **163** unique tests. The first batch passed 162; the retention fixture failed because GC was unavailable. A direct CLI GC flag did not reach that worker. The repository runner (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --maxWorkers=8 src/agents/tools/sessions-send-followup.test.ts`) supplies the required flags and passes all five tests in that file. No production changes or test bypass were needed.
- Core and agent-tool test typechecks, touched-file lint/format, documentation lint, and diff checks pass. No production access or external Gateway was used.
- Author simplification and Codex autoreview of the complete staged branch diff are complete; review is scoped-clean at P0–P2 with no actionable findings.

Whole-PR test lines: **+164 / -164, net 0**. Production: **+118** net; documentation: **+5** net. Duplicate notification assertions and redundant test state were removed while preserving the admission, receiver-custody, inline-reply, and late-result contracts.

Auto-merge remains disabled. This follow-up is pushed for coordinator verification; it does not authorize or perform landing.

## What Problem This Solves

Searching for a version such as `5.5` lists one provider’s entire block before another provider’s equally good matches. A starred model can land below a dated snapshot even when the snapshot’s rolling alias is already visible.

## User Impact

In Chat and New Session, exact names and model IDs beat partial matches. Among equally close matches, selectable favorites and catalog recommendations rise across providers. A dated build stays directly searchable; browsing without a query is unchanged.

prs.title: fix: let macOS dashboard updates switch to the release launcher
prs.body:
Closes #200833.

## What Problem This Solves

The first dashboard update of a checkout-backed macOS Gateway could select a new release without ever starting it. The old process still answered `/readyz`, even though live RPC reported its old build and the target trial had zero starts. This also happened when the two builds had different package versions.

## User Impact

A dashboard update can switch the LaunchAgent to the stable release launcher without asking the serving job to replace itself. If the installer confirms the rebind was refused before activation, OpenClaw keeps the old service and restores the previous release selection. An uncertain install result is not treated as proof that rollback is safe.

## Why This Change Was Made

The serving Gateway hands this first conversion to a temporary sibling LaunchAgent. It verifies that the helper is outside the serving job before transferring update ownership; the installer's self-install guard stays in force. A healthy old endpoint is not a successful update: the verifier must observe the target build.

**Overlap:** #200876 addresses rollback after refusal, not successful conversion. This combined fix includes that recovery, tightens the evidence required to restore a never-started trial, and adds the activation path. It does not require #200876 to be applied separately.

## Evidence

- **Linux: 379 passed / 15 skipped across 15 focused files.** In the process fixture, the old PID still served with zero trial attempts after selection. After rebind, a different PID on the same port served the full target build ID, answered health RPC and `/readyz`, and settled its trial after one start. The handoff helper exited successfully.
- Refusal coverage checks that the previous selection and serving-process record survive, the matching unstarted trial is cleared, and the installer issues no mutating `launchctl` command. Incomplete inspection does not authorize rollback.
- **Native macOS launchd was not tested.** Linux used real scratch processes and modeled launchd; this was not an end-to-end dashboard run on a Mac. The native case in `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-launchd.process.test.ts` still needs a disposable macOS GUI account to verify sibling placement and survival through incumbent bootout.
- Core and focused-test typechecks, lint, formatting, the line-cap check, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent local autoreview of the complete combined tree `f14c4358f9f2e0395bd6aef89409daa3f9c6404b` against `e93a426be3297ed947f54b4e15c87827225b6c90` found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The park function was extracted for the line-cap check; expanding it reproduces the previously reviewed helper byte-for-byte.

@hannesrudolph reported the two affected profiles and verified the original patch hash. The included rollback work from #200876 credits @steipete.

## Worked on by

- @hannesrudolph

prs.title: feat: name new automations from their prompt
prs.body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/38c3a6ca-1655-4fdc-8922-a20d282c4a5b)

## What Problem This Solves

Creating an automation in the Control UI required inventing a name even when the prompt already described the task.

## User Impact

User impact: write the prompt, pick the schedule and create the automation. The authenticated Control UI tries to name it with the agent’s session-title models. You can rename it later, and you can change a copy’s suggested name before saving it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the interactive create form needs a model-generated title. Unnamed CLI, agent and other non-UI requests keep their deterministic naming behavior without an extra provider call. Explicit names and declarations also skip model naming.

The utility and primary model share one five-second naming budget, including setup. They use the same title prompt, normalization and operator model policy as session titles. If neither answers in time, or no operator grant is available for naming, the automation keeps its existing prompt-derived name. A late response cannot overwrite it. Clearing a saved name shows the current name as the placeholder and preserves it on save.

## Evidence

Original visual comparison of the title-field removal: mocked Control UI at 1280×820, light theme, synthetic Gateway data. Before: `9d6f4a94adf5`; after: `e3e0e5c9e13f`. Browser verification of the integrated update is described below.

prs.title: fix: keep your place while reading Activity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an older session received a live update, Activity moved it to the top—even if you were reading it. The row could jump completely out of view.

## User Impact

You can scroll through older sessions without losing your place. Titles, status, and recaps still update. When you return to the top and stop scrolling, the latest sessions appear automatically. There is no refresh button.

## Why This Change Was Made

Activity holds the displayed row order and day groups while you read, not the underlying data. Returning briefly to the top and reversing direction does not reshuffle the list. Once scrolling settles at the top, the feed resumes its newest-first order using the existing list animation, which respects reduced motion. Changing filters starts a fresh list.

## Evidence

[Before and after: the same live update at phone width](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201448#issuecomment-6991169321)

In production-bundled Chromium with synthetic Gateway updates, the reading row moved 881 CSS pixels on desktop and 922 on an emulated phone before the fix. On both layouts it now moves less than 1 pixel in the same scenario. The tests also cover recap growth above the reader, new arrivals, reversing at the top, automatic catch-up, and a filter that introduces a previously unseen session. The 28 existing Activity view tests and UI typecheck passed. Independent re-review found no remaining P0–P2 issues after a filter-scope correction. prs.title: fix(voice): Discord controls and phone consults fail with PostgreSQL agent stores
prs.body:
Related: #189036

Contributor credit: Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm) requested and guided this repair.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/65edb98b-73fa-47e9-8242-be1ae73fb4b9)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/91bf5c8e-90b2-4f50-a7b4-fd877499b08b)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord voice active-run controls and realtime phone-call agent consultations fail when agent storage uses PostgreSQL.

## User Impact

The two bundled voice surfaces can use PostgreSQL-backed agent stores while retaining model-selection locks, current speaker/call authority, and the existing synchronous SDK contracts. No configuration, schema, migration, or permission-policy change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both consumers still reached synchronous session-entry reads on the Gateway thread, which PostgreSQL intentionally refuses.

- Expose the existing worker-backed model-lock check as an additive async SDK helper, reuse its existing candidate selection/predicate, and await it in voice-call before fast-context lookup and before returning its result. Recheck the live call after each wait.
- Allow asynchronous caller-policy preparation in the existing run controller and migrate Discord to it. Preparation repeats for each injection admission; a separate live caller assertion remains at enqueue and cancellation effects, including the legacy key-selected path.
- Preserve the synchronous helper/callback and released dependency-adapter contracts; no synchronous fallback is selected after a worker failure.

This is distinct from @ceckert's #189036, which owns the four Gateway Talk surfaces and excludes these bundled SDK consumers. #189036 landed first; main was then merged into this branch to reconcile the shared run controller. Because the public `controlRealtimeVoiceAgentRun` parameters now declare `getToolAuthorityOverlayAsync` and `assertCurrent`, the internal `controlTalkAgentRun` takes that same parameter type instead of redeclaring the async reader. Its per-admission reread, compat check and requester-device propagation are unchanged, and `assertCurrent` is layered on top. Both sets of async-authority regressions in `agent-run-control.stop.test.ts` are kept. The edits to `extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime-turns.test.ts` were dropped because main removed that file.

The private async lock check is consolidated rather than adding another lock owner. Production changes are +58/-22 lines; no new manager, cache, or storage owner is introduced. The 242 net test lines cover the distinct consumer lifetime, worker-failure, model-lock, fingerprint and final-cancellation boundaries and are recorded in their own test-line allocation.

## Evidence

### Actual product and storage boundary

Built the clean baseline `9c22cf86f68b34269e49a25a95827c1c23b52ce0` and the candidate with the canonical `pnpm build`, on Node 24.20.0. All six changed production blobs remain unchanged since the candidate product proof; later adjustments only prepare runtime config in the cancellation-test fixture and migrate the root Discord integration assertion.

The disposable Gateway used real PostgreSQL 17.11 agent storage (`database.engine: sqlite`, `database.families.agent.engine: postgres`). A signed synthetic Twilio webhook issued the one-use stream URL; a carrier WebSocket sent documented start/media frames through the real voice-call server and bundled OpenAI Realtime bridge. Local Realtime WebSocket and model SSE protocol fixtures supplied synthetic transcript/tool output and a deterministic model response. The actual OpenClaw agent turn, session controller, storage, public history RPC and shutdown ran normally. No paid provider traffic or live Team state was used.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Clean baseline, PostgreSQL | Final tool result contains `PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker`; zero agent-model requests. |
| Candidate, PostgreSQL | One agent-model request; final tool result contains `VOICE_PRODUCT_ANSWER`; authenticated `chat.history` returns that assistant answer. |
| Independent PostgreSQL read after clean Gateway shutdown | `assistant_rows=1`, `marker_answers=1`. |
| Candidate, SQLite control | Same signed-carrier flow returns `VOICE_PRODUCT_ANSWER` with one model request; clean shutdown. |

A separate source-bound probe runs the real registered voice-call consult handler and the actual Discord voice consumer/public controller against real PostgreSQL session reads. Both baseline consumers refuse at their synchronous session reader; both migrated consumers pass on PostgreSQL and SQLite. The Discord backend is a synthetic guarded run attached through the real controller, not a real Discord transport. A separate Gateway-role probe confirms the deprecated synchronous PostgreSQL read still throws the original main-thread guard.

Limits: the carrier is a simulator, and Realtime/model responses are protocol fixtures. This does not claim real Twilio/Discord server operation, microphone capture, speech recognition/synthesis quality, or commercial model inference.

### Regressions and checks

- After the main merge (head `bc13f168520`), PR CI run 44393205410 passed the touched suites: `src/talk/agent-run-control.stop.test.ts` (Discord async-policy cases and the Gateway Talk async-authority cases), the Discord voice suites, `extensions/voice-call/src/runtime.test.ts`, `voice-runtime.e2e.test.ts`, the root Discord audio integration test, and the type, lint and guard jobs. Its one failed job is the bun gateway-server shard stalling in `server.talk-consult-history.test.ts` at the unchanged node approval cancellation case, the same stall seen on scheduled main.

- With the original six production files temporarily restored, the three new run-control regressions fail for the intended behavior: allowed async-policy steering does not reach the backend, and cancellation proceeds instead of honoring the revoked caller. The candidate was restored byte-for-byte; the complete stop/control suite passes 12 tests.
- New consumer cases deny use after speaker revocation, session/call replacement or closure, worker failure, and a model lock applied during fast-context preparation. Existing synchronous callback/dependency-adapter cases remain covered. The synchronous model-lock helper and dependency-adapter type are byte-identical to the baseline.

prs.title: fix: retain diagnostics for VM-created errors in logs
prs.body:
Related: #200439

## What Problem This Solves

When a subsystem logs an Error created in a Node VM, the file log and console can show `error: {}` instead of the failure message and stack. That leaves operators without the details needed to investigate the failure.

## User Impact

VM-created errors retain the same diagnostic fields as ordinary errors: name, message, error code when present, and stack. File logs keep the full stack; the console keeps its existing six-line limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each VM has its own Error constructor, so the host's `instanceof Error` check misses these native errors. The existing metadata preparation step now also uses Node's native-error check. The fix reuses the current field selection and sink handling without adding a formatter or changing plain-object metadata.

This is a reproduced remaining error shape, not a confirmed explanation of the original reporter's warnings in #200439. That issue should remain open until its actual caught value is identified.

## Evidence

- The new VM case failed on the original implementation while the same-realm control passed. With the fix, all 84 tests across the subsystem, logger redaction, console capture, and console timestamp suites passed on Node 24.22.1/Linux.
- A separate source-level Node process used normal logging configuration, `createSubsystemLogger`, and `flushLogger`, with no logger mocks or overrides. Both the real JSONL file and JSON console changed from `{"error":{}}` to an error record containing `name: "Error"`, `message: "VM operation failed"`, and the stack. The original process failed its diagnostic assertion; the fixed process passed. This was a logging-boundary check, not a live Gateway reproduction of the reported incident.
- Targeted production/test typechecks, lint, formatting, the test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent scoped review found no actionable issues.
- Simplification kept the fix at the existing owner: one production predicate change and one additional case in an existing integration test, with no new helper or state.

<details>
<summary>Focused test command</summary>

```sh
pnpm test src/logging/subsystem.test.ts src/logging/logger-redaction-behavior.test.ts src/logging/console-capture.test.ts src/logging/console-timestamp.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The pinned Bun download was unavailable locally, so the repository's supported Node fallback ran these tests.

</details>

prs.title: improve: stop floating "Loading…" beside Talk trigger words
prs.body:
Contributed by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/793028d2-8a55-41e5-8052-5e02de8fe302)

Related: #201396

## What Problem This Solves

In Settings → Talk, “Loading…” sat beside the empty Trigger words editor. When the words arrived, “Saved” took up space beside the editor instead. At a 1280 px viewport that status took 46.5 px away from the field.

## User Impact

User impact: the editor stays in the same place and keeps its width as you open Talk, edit trigger words, and wait for them to save. “Saving…” and “Saved” appear next to the field title instead of pushing on the text box.

## Why This Change Was Made

The disabled editor already marks itself busy for assistive technology. Removing the extra loading label and keeping save feedback in a separate status region preserves both signals without changing the editor’s size.

## Evidence

Real Control UI in Chromium with a mocked Gateway, dark theme, 1280×800 viewport. The first comparison holds the initial read pending (main `b413b8e1966780` versus the initial PR revision `189dc55`). The second shows the same field after the words arrive.

**After**

![After: full-width disabled trigger words box with no extra label](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49d965cf-bfd3-42fc-904b-31c001efc3c6)

prs.body:
<!--

below this comment.

can help update the branch when needed.

Closes #201405

## What Problem This Solves

An unattended run can have an allowed MCP tool hidden behind Tool Search controls, so the model overlooks a reachable tool named in its instructions. Prompt plugins currently cannot see the attempt's incoming allowlist or which allowed tools were actually deferred, making a reliable discovery hint difficult.

<!--

when known. For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.

missing checks, and the root-cause walkthrough for the explanation below.

## User Impact

User impact: prompt plugins can name the deferred tools reachable in an embedded attempt without re-reading job configuration. This only exposes information: it adds no hint by default, changes no model-facing tools, and grants no authorization or policy-widening capability. No migration or configuration changes are required.

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

## Why This Change Was Made

Add optional read-only `toolsAllow` and `deferredToolNames` fields to the `before_prompt_build` event. The first preserves the incoming allowlist, including omitted versus empty; the second reads executable, non-direct identifiers from the catalog the attempt registered. Unique callable names remain names; collisions use exact catalog IDs instead, preserving the complete view without emitting ambiguous selectors. Consumers must not blindly intersect qualified IDs with a name-based allowlist. Catalog preparation already precedes prompt assembly, so no execution reordering is needed.

All handlers, including authorized enrichment, receive the same pre-hook scope snapshot; earlier returned restrictions still intersect afterward and do not rewrite it. Supplied arrays are detached/frozen and cannot be replaced. The existing mutable event-envelope convention is otherwise preserved. Generic harness and CLI paths omit unsupported scope fields; the docs explicitly distinguish informational scope from finalized `ctx.toolAuthority`.

<!--

## Evidence

Native Gateway integration proof passed at `13df52115ee2511778a078388fc2d1abfca6821e`: a real isolated cron attempt loaded a prompt plugin, delivered `toolsAllow: ["read", "proof__lookup"]` and `deferredToolNames: ["proof__lookup"]`, and carried the plugin's hint into the actual provider request. The model-facing tools contained only `read` and the three Tool Search controls; a non-allowlisted MCP sibling was excluded. The real controls searched, described, and dispatched exactly one stdio MCP lookup, its result reached the next provider request, and the cron run finished `ok`.

This uses deterministic local model responses, not a live model. It proves Gateway/plugin/MCP integration and prompt delivery, not spontaneous model discovery or production cron reliability. No operator Gateway or real provider credentials were used.

The initial 59 focused tests passed at `65385cdc1e2`, covering absent/empty allowlists, Tool Search off/on, actual MCP deferral, earlier narrowing without widening, authorized snapshot stability, array mutation isolation, and unsupported harness omission. The initial five embedded regressions failed for missing scope fields before implementation.

The collision follow-up reran 21 tests successfully. Two new regressions first failed on deduplicated bare names, then passed with exact IDs for direct/deferred and deferred/deferred collisions. They dispatch every reported ID through the real Tool Search runtime and verify the intended tool executes. The isolation test also confirms caller arrays remain mutable: the existing graph clone already detaches them before freezing. Earlier-handler narrowing was already covered for both ordinary and authorized handlers and remains green.

Independent Copilot code review completed with the operator's approval after canonical autoreview could not start (Codex absent; Claude workspace authentication rejected). One suggestion to prevent adding initially absent event properties was declined: no run-state array is exposed in that case, and sealing/proxying the existing event envelope would broaden compatibility changes beyond this additive view. Supplied scope arrays remain frozen and non-replaceable.

Fresh independent review of the collision follow-up found no actionable P0-P2 issues.

Production and test typechecks, changed-file lint/format, docs, and policy checks passed. The broad `pnpm check` remains red on 20 unrelated max-lines errors; every failing source is byte-identical to the pinned upstream base.

Production catalog-before-hook ordering, generic harness/CLI omission, and Code Mode exclusion were source-traced; only the finite-allowlist/MCP-deferral scenario above was exercised through the native Gateway. Other scope variants retain their focused-test proof. Fork CI has required maintainer workflow approval; no CI success or CI seconds are claimed here.

<details>
<summary>Native Gateway behavior proof: setup and redacted output</summary>

Linux source checkout at the exact head above. A task-owned controller ran with Node 24.21.0 (`node <task-proof>/run.mjs`, exit 0) and launched the supported `pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --port <ephemeral>` entry point. State, agent credentials, workspace, and configuration were isolated through the documented `OPENCLAW_*` paths. It waited for `/readyz`, authenticated with the public `GatewayClient` SDK, then used the native `cron.add`/`cron.run`/`cron.runs` RPCs. The prompt plugin was loaded from an explicitly enabled local path; an SDK-based stdio MCP server advertised `lookup` and an excluded `delete` sibling. The OpenAI-compatible endpoint was local, with a nonsecret fixture key.

The plugin registered an earlier handler, a later ordinary handler that derived a hint from the event, and an authorized handler. All three independently recorded the same allowlist/deferred identifiers and frozen arrays. The provider received the derived hint before any tool call. Canned streaming responses then exercised the real `tool_search` -> `tool_describe` -> `dispatch_action` path; no catalog, hook, or tool execution was substituted.

prs.title: fix: finish updates when another tool reads OpenClaw's databases during the update
prs.body:
Related: #197083 Related: #201085 ## What Problem This Solves An update could fail and leave the Gateway stopped when anything outside OpenClaw briefly opened its SQLite databases read-only during the update. A monitoring script using Python `sqlite3` with `mode=ro` is enough. Doctor then reported `Automatic database restoration cannot attribute migration writes: SQLite migration publication could not be verified`, refused rollback because "the writer is unknown", and kept the Gateway down (`state-migrated-no-rollback`). One reporter was offline for 13 hours. ## User Impact User impact: updates now finish when an outside tool reads OpenClaw's databases during the update. Automatic restoration stays available because nothing was written. Any real write after Doctor admits a database still refuses as before. ## Why This Change Was Made A database's WAL file can keep committed frames after the last writer exits, for example when a status or monitoring reader is still open at the time. The next process that becomes the only connection rebuilds SQLite's WAL index (`-shm`) from those frames. A read-only open is enough. The rebuild resets the index change counter to zero and recomputes the header checksum. The frame count, last-frame checksum and salts stay the same, and so do the committed data. Doctor's write evidence includes that counter, so a no-write rebuild after Doctor's admission looked like a foreign commit. That happened in two places: - in the migration's pre-read ("SQLite migration source changed after update capture"); - inside a single observation when the open raced the read ("SQLite WAL commit publication could not be verified"). The owner of the generation fingerprint (`update-database-generations.ts`) now handles both: - **Inside one read:** it accepts a header change that is exactly a rebuild, meaning only the counter (now 0) and the header checksum differ, and the file family is unchanged. - **Across reads:** every observation of a WAL database with frames also reports the fingerprint that same database would have after an index rebuild. That fingerprint uses the same file identity, the same committed-content digest and the same last-frame checksum, with the counter at 0. Doctor's update capture remembers that alternate from its own admission. It accepts the alternate at the migration pre-read, at companion checks, at every repeated admission and at settlement. **Why the signal stays sound.** The alternate binds the digest of the committed content and the last frame's cumulative checksum. Any commit after admission appends frames and changes that checksum, including a commit that restores identical content. A WAL restart changes the salts. So the alternate cannot match a real write, and those cases still refuse. A regression test covers the same-content commit. The policy for a stale initial capture (#200328) and for predecessor-stop writes (#200569) is unchanged. Rejected alternative: extending #200328's "warn and continue" policy to changes after admission. Maintainers deliberately kept post-admission checks strict, and a rebuild with no write can be proven, so it does not need a policy exception. Production LOC: about +75 / −12 across five files, plus a doc paragraph in `docs/install/updating.md`. Most of the growth is passing the new alternate field through the worker schema and the Doctor capture. ## Evidence **Live reproduction and fix on Crabbox AWS (Ubuntu, c7a.8xlarge).** Each lane is a managed `update.run` with a 400 MB state database and an outside Python `sqlite3` `mode=ro` reader. The reader holds a read transaction while the Gateway stops, which is how frames survive. It releases when the post-install Doctor starts and opens the databases again 10–60 s later, then keeps polling. | Run | Base (main `05d1e6f1f1f`) | With fix | |---|---|---| | 2026.11.5 → target, reader polls every ~1.3 s | 5/5 failed | 4/5 succeeded | | 2026.11.4 → target, reader polls every ~1.3 s | 5/5 failed | 5/5 succeeded | | 2026.11.5 → target, reader polls every 30 s | 1/1 failed | 2/2 succeeded | | 2026.11.4 → target, reader polls every 30 s | 1/1 failed | 2/2 succeeded | The fix runs include alternating base/fix lanes on the same box. The last four fix runs used a package built from this PR's exact head. **Every base failure:** - The update ended `failed`. - The Gateway was left stopped (`state-migrated-no-rollback`). - The error was `SQLite migration source changed after update capture`. - The 11.4 runs also logged `cannot open your existing data`. **Every successful fix run:** the update `succeeded`, the Gateway was active on the target, and none of the watched failure signatures appeared. **The one failed fix run** has a different cause. Under the aggressive 1.3 s polling, Doctor's own schema-admission step hit `database is locked` from the outside reader's lock. No rebuild or publication signature appeared. I'm tracking it as a separate follow-up. **Regression tests:** - `update-database-generations.test.ts`: a rebuild during the read binds the rebuilt generation and equals the earlier observation's alternate. - `update-doctor-migration-wal-rebuild.test.ts`: migration is attributed when the rebuild happens during Doctor's read and after admission, with no warnings and `unchanged: true`. A same-content commit before the rebuild still refuses, and a rebuild between two Doctor admissions stays attributable. On base, the first two migration cases fail with the exact user signatures (`SQLite WAL commit publication could not be verified`, `SQLite migration source changed after update capture`); with the fix they pass. **Checks:** - Touched suites pass. Two `completes retirement …` cases fail locally on base and on the fix alike: Node strip-only cannot load a parameter property in `update-doctor-result.ts`. They are unrelated. - `doctor-maintenance` settlement and worker suites: 54/54. - `tsgo:core`, type-aware `oxlint` (core shard) and `oxfmt` are clean. **Reviews:** autoreview at P2 came back `scoped-clean` on the final head. An independent `codex exec` review found one real issue: two test mocks lacked the new pair field. That is fixed in `eaad4658610`, and it found no other P0–P2 defect. **Head delta since the live proof.** The Crabbox lanes ran a package built from `eaad4658610`. The landing head adds production edits, not a rebase. They fix the `session-identity` baseline ratchet that failed on `eaad4658610`, and they are behavior-equivalent to the proven head: - `readMatchingUpdateDatabaseGeneration` now takes the accepted generations as a list. It accepts the same values as before. The only theoretical widening, an empty-reader alternate equal to the rebuilt alternate, cannot occur: rebuilt alternates exist only when the WAL has frames, and empty-reader alternates only when it has none. - Doctor's capture still accepts the remembered rebuilt alternate at every `admit()` and at settlement, exactly when the observed generation equals it. It is now written as a loop over the remembered alternates. An intermediate commit (`4d705cc6ff5`) briefly dropped the admit/settlement acceptance. The independent review caught that this breaks the production sequence of repeated admissions (finalization, predecessor stop, maintenance). `7c40b6de1be` restores it, with a regression test that fails without the restored acceptance and passes with it. Other changes: - The new tests moved to `src/infra/update-doctor-migration-wal-rebuild.test.ts`, because the original file hit the 1000-line cap. - One test caller was updated for the list signature. - The allowlist entry for `update-database-generations.ts` shrinks from 2 to 1. Follow-up from ClawSweeper, the same-content control now updates and restores one row (`WHERE value = …`) and asserts the committed rows equal the admitted ones before expecting the refusal. That makes the refusal come from the new frames' checksum alone. The change is test-only.
Redacted lane output (exact eaad4658610 build as 2026.11.28; base main as 2026.11.30) ```text RESULT head115 2026.11.5 -> 2026.11.28 last=succeeded readyz=core active=active greps: none RESULT head114 2026.11.4 -> 2026.11.28 last=succeeded readyz=core active=active greps: none RESULT slowbase115 2026.11.5 -> 2026.11.30 last=failed active= greps: state-migrated-no-rollback, SQLite migration source changed after update capture, cannot attribute migration writes RESULT slowbase114 2026.11.4 -> 2026.11.30 last=failed active= greps: state-migrated-no-rollback, SQLite migration source changed after update capture, cannot open your existing data ``` `readyz=core` means the core is ready. The lane uses a fake Telegram token, so the channel readiness probe reports degraded by design. These lane criteria check update status, the Gateway service, version, readiness and failure signatures. They do not count seeded rows separately; config is preserved, because the same `openclaw.json` served the target.

prs.title: fix(update): supervised PostgreSQL updates ignore server recovery captures and orphan them on finish
prs.body:
Closes #198401
Supersedes #198435

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `database.postgres.recoveryCaptures: "server"`, supervised `openclaw update migrate` exported every PostgreSQL store to local files while the Gateway was stopped, extending downtime, and `update finish` would orphan server-side captures if they were made.

## User Impact

User impact: supervised PostgreSQL updates honor the configured server recovery captures (shorter stopped window, no local export copies), and finishing the update retires those server captures instead of leaving `restore_<uuid>` schemas behind. Cleanup stays best effort: if retirement fails, the update still succeeds, the backup is kept, and a warning says to retry `update finish`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Builds on @qingminglong's #198435, which forwards the existing setting to the supervised migrate backup, matching the native updater. That alone would keep rows in server schemas whose only references are the local backup manifests, and `update finish` deletes those manifests without dropping the schemas. Finish now retires them through the existing `discardPostgresSchemaCaptures` owner (the same one the native updater uses) before removing the backup directory; a failure keeps the manifests so a retry can finish, and `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS` keeps retries idempotent. Doctor's capture pruning cannot reclaim these because supervised captures lack its prefix marker.

Rolled-back (restored) receipts keep their captures under the existing rollback retention contract; no retention policy change.

## Evidence

- New finish regression in `update-command-migrate.test.ts` (real finish command, discard owner mocked at its module boundary): **red** on #198435's head (discard never called), **green** with the fix; covers ordering before directory removal, discard failure keeping the directory with a warning, and retry.
- `update-command-migrate.test.ts` 22 passed (including #198435's tests); `update-command-database-retention.test.ts` 15 passed.
- The PostgreSQL migrate→finish lifecycle case **ran and passed against a real PostgreSQL service in CI**, not skipped: [PostgreSQL conformance (1/3), run 43512134482](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43512134482/job/132185832402), `retires server captures through supervised migrate and finish` (13.124 s). The adjacent existing exact-capture→rollback→retirement test also passed (6.696 s), preserving the frozen capture and row verification. This remains in-process boundary proof (Doctor is stubbed), not an installed CLI upgrade.

prs.title: fix: explain Discord mention requirements in channel diagnostics
prs.body:
Related: #200429 (distinct session-status activation reporting)

## What Problem This Solves

Discord's targeted capability check can report that every required permission is present without explaining why an ordinary message still does not start a turn. Operators cannot see whether that channel requires a mention or which guild/channel/account setting is responsible.

## User Impact

User impact: the Discord channel capabilities command now explains the configured mention requirement and channel access separately from Discord permissions, and points to the responsible configuration scope. It recommends mentioning the bot in an allowed channel from an allowed sender for the first test.

No admission defaults, allowlists, permissions, configuration options, or public denial replies change. This is a local-config diagnostic, not a sender authorization decision or a live Gateway connectivity check. Name-based policy bindings and bound-thread route activation are explicitly left unverified rather than guessed; use numeric guild/channel IDs and check channel status separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse Discord's existing mention-policy and channel-access owners. The mention resolver returns its winning configuration scope alongside the unchanged decision. The existing permission lookup already retrieves the channel, parent, guild and bot facts needed by the targeted diagnostic, so no additional Discord requests are added. The explanation loads only when requested.

Simplification: no new subsystem, cache, configuration, or parallel admission implementation. The remaining production growth is the operator explanation and source paths; the regression exercises the real permission lookup with fixed external REST responses.

## Evidence

- Actual CLI reproduction on base bde2e84084bffa49cad046351f7ddd739d26d9ea with isolated synthetic config/state and a loopback Discord API: before, permissions were complete but mention policy was absent; after, the same command reports channel access, requireMention=true, its exact channel config path, and sender/connection limitations. Both runs issued the same six read-only HTTP requests. No live Discord messages were sent.
- Corrected regression was red on the base because messagePolicy was absent, while the permission-success assertion passed; green after the repair. Controls cover account-vs-root inheritance, channel/guild/default precedence, disabled channels, empty account guild overrides, bot-owned thread parent settings, and unresolved names.
- Focused channel, mention-policy and send-permission suites: 105 tests passed. Final focused invocation wall time: 42.8 seconds (40.4 seconds runner duration, mostly cold compilation); individual new regression executes in milliseconds. CI seconds pending.
- Full pnpm build, Discord package typecheck, targeted lint, seven-file formatting check, and git diff --check passed. Build emitted existing UI asset-budget warnings; its exit status was 0. No UI source is changed.
- Local Auto Review (P0–P2, complete local candidate against the pinned base) was cancelled after stalling without a report. It is incomplete, not a clean review. Hosted review remains required.
- Live proof gap: the supported Discord QA readiness command failed during Convex lease acquisition before any Discord checks. No credential was obtained or borrowed, and no transport/reply claim is made. Cold-import screening completed; qualification was unavailable while the source tree was dirty.

### Inspectable CLI evidence

Actual retained stdout excerpts; synthetic config/state and local Discord REST fixture, not a live Discord send. Base: `bde2e84084bffa49cad046351f7ddd739d26d9ea`. After: repaired head `d8a62ed574e58c7ec8b6e5a68ee3f7f8c4499780`.

Command: `pnpm openclaw channels capabilities --channel discord --account default --target channel:222`

Before:
```text
Permissions (222): SendMessages, ViewChannel
Missing required: none
```

After:
```text
Permissions (222): SendMessages, ViewChannel
Missing required: none
Message policy (local config): groupPolicy=allowlist (source: channels.discord.groupPolicy)
Channel access: allowed (source: channels.discord.guilds["123"].channels["222"])
Mentions: requireMention=true (source: channels.discord.guilds["123"].channels["222"].requireMention)
Sender access: not evaluated; no sender context was supplied. Guild/channel users and roles still apply.
First test: mention the bot in this allowed channel from an allowed sender. Check channels status --probe separately for Gateway connectivity.
```

Retained after-run exit and request trace (unchanged from the baseline):
```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "requests": [
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/users/@me"
    },
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/oauth2/applications/@me"
    },
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/channels/222"
    },
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/users/@me"
    },
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/guilds/123"
    },
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/guilds/123/members/999"
    }
  ]
}
```

### CI repair

The first head failed [the permission-response integration check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44376909315/job/135059455016): diagnostic metadata had escaped into ordinary permission-tool responses. The fix makes that context opt-in only for the operator diagnostic and preserves the existing public response; the existing exact-response assertion is unchanged. Reproduced locally red, then all 55 metadata-read authority integration tests plus 100 channel/send tests passed (17.74s total focused run). Targeted typecheck/lint and actual CLI reproduction passed again. The standard failed-CI helper was unavailable (`spawn gh ENOENT`); the exact job log was read through the managed GitHub reader instead.

### Policy/transport distinguishability verification

Seven additional focused cases passed on the repaired head, reusing the earlier 155-test and capabilities-CLI proof:

- **Four admission cases:** the real Discord dispatcher/live-policy/preflight path distinguishes an unmentioned message (`reason=no-mention`), a disallowed channel, and a disallowed sender. All three denied cases made **zero agent-processing calls and zero outbound REST writes**; only the unmentioned allowed message entered pending history. An allowed-sender/channel mention passed the positive admission control, which intentionally stopped before model execution or outbound delivery.
- **Three status-command cases:** a reachable-Gateway RPC fixture rendered `Discord default: enabled, configured, running, disconnected, check failed`; existing controls preserved Gateway protocol rejections and config-only transport-failure fallback. Separately, the actual `channels status --channel discord --probe --timeout 1500` CLI against an isolated closed loopback endpoint reported `Gateway not reachable; showing config-only status.` Its exit 0 denotes the documented fallback, not a successful live probe.

The actual `channels logs --channel all --lines 20 --json` CLI retrieved the produced admission records. Channel/sender denial records require existing **`logging.level=debug`** (or trace) during the event. Use the all-channel/general Gateway log view: these legacy denial records are not tagged with the Discord subsystem, and `discord-auto-reply` is not the narrow `discord` log root. An empty `channels logs --channel discord` result therefore does not prove no denial occurred. Sender-denial logs deliberately omit the sender ID; correlate a controlled input/time rather than infer a per-sender decision.

This is isolated synthetic-boundary proof, **not live Discord transport or reply proof**. Target-only capabilities still have no sender context and correctly report sender access as unassessed. The earlier QA lease failure remains unresolved; no credentials or public messages were used. Temporary proof source was removed/reverted; no additional product changes were made. Current-main verification at `b413b8e1966780121c211abbf3f91adb5c173afa` found the admission/status owners unchanged and only three unrelated threading lines changed in `channel.ts`.

Worked on by:
- @etzelm

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ba8717b3-cf77-4a25-bcd9-79ff4fd42b6b)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/ba4b03bf-e9fe-4063-affb-642a421e722b)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android `device.apps` omits disabled launcher apps and activities even when `includeDisabled=true` is requested.

## User Impact

User impact: callers can explicitly include disabled launcher apps without expanding the default inventory or including background-only apps. Existing Installed Apps sharing controls and Android package-visibility limits remain unchanged. No migration or new permission is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the existing `includeDisabled` option to launcher discovery and add Android's `MATCH_DISABLED_COMPONENTS` query flag only when requested. Retain application-level enabled metadata and downstream filtering.

The production delta is +14/-4 lines; the test delta is +137/-1 lines. Two regression cases cover disabled applications and disabled launcher components; the test-only Robolectric shadow corrects its `MATCH_ALL` behavior at the package-manager boundary.

## Evidence

- **Contributor-reported local validation:** [issue #195938](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/195938) reports Base-RED (both `DeviceAppsPlatformTest` cases failed), then Fix-GREEN for `DeviceAppsPlatformTest` and `DeviceHandlerTest`, `:app:ktlintCheck`, and `:app:assemblePlayDebug`. prs.title: fix(test): identify restart completion notices reliably
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The durable-process recovery test identifies completion notices by the first eight characters of a process ID. Different process IDs can share that display prefix, so an unrelated notice can make the test report a duplicate or inspect the wrong completion.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. The recovery test identifies each process's notice reliably while continuing to require exactly one notice and the expected restart outcome.

## Why This Change Was Made

Match the existing event `contextKey`, which contains the full process ID. Add an unrelated event with a colliding display prefix to the existing real-process scenario so the old matcher fails deterministically. Keep all recovery, message-content, and cleanup assertions.

## Evidence

- Original failure: [main durable-process job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44380396155/job/135071716157), where the notice matcher found two entries instead of one.
- With the collision fixture and original matcher, the real durable-process wrapper fails after selecting the unrelated notice. With the full-ID matcher, the same wrapper passes on macOS with Node 24.22.1 and the pinned Bun runtime (29.50 seconds total).
- Targeted agent test types, type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh committed-range ClawSweeper review found no actionable correctness or security issues (0.94 confidence); runtime proof above was performed separately.
- The fixture uses isolated process and event state; it does not change notification production or process lifetime behavior.

prs.title: fix: report actual dashboard pairing-link delivery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw dashboard` announces that a one-time browser pairing link was included before either clipboard or browser delivery succeeds. When both fail on a token-authenticated Gateway, it then recommends a shared-token URL instead of the one-time browser handoff that was actually attempted.

## User Impact

Users see which delivery actually succeeded, and headless or failed-launch sessions get consistent recovery instructions for the one-time pairing link. The printed dashboard address and SSH tunnel remain credential-free; no authentication, pairing permissions, JSON fields, or exit statuses change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing copied/opened outcomes to report delivery, and direct every neither-delivered case to `openclaw dashboard --json` and its short-lived `browserUrl`. Explicitly warn that this URL is a credential, not support-log material. Remove stale shared-token advice and misleading clean-URL fallback wording without adding state or changing the handoff mechanism.

The docs distinguish network access, browser pairing, and Gateway authentication. This is separate from #200905 (where approval happens) and #200840 (compatible-browser selection); the latter has nearby code changes but retains the failure-copy defect.

## Evidence

- Reproduced before and verified after through the real `pnpm openclaw --profile dashboard-handoff-proof dashboard` command against a task-owned token-mode foreground Gateway and its served Control UI document. Checked headless/no clipboard, advertised display with failed opener, and `--no-open`. OS-boundary fixture executables discard input and exit unsuccessfully.
- Additional real-browser proof on the same published source: Chromium 156.0.8078.4 redeemed a fresh `browserUrl` issued by the real profiled CLI against a separate task-owned token-mode Gateway. The signed browser received an administrator device credential, removed the bootstrap fragment, stored the issued credential, and reconnected after reload and in a new tab using that device credential without bootstrap or shared-secret auth. Negative controls rejected a clean URL with `AUTH_TOKEN_MISSING` and reuse of the spent handoff in another browser context with `AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_INVALID`. WebSocket observations were passive, not mocked; retained evidence contains only auth-presence flags, error codes, and runtime metadata, not credential values. Browser and test Gateway were stopped afterward. This proof used Linux headless Chromium; native desktop launchers and other browsers/platforms were not exercised.
- All three fixed scenarios report failed pairing-link delivery, direct users to `browserUrl`, and avoid claiming it was copied or opened. No credential values were printed or included in this evidence.
- Regression suite was red on base `bde2e84084bffa49cad046351f7ddd739d26d9ea` (12 failures for the changed output contracts), then green. All **79 tests across four files** pass: dashboard owner, JSON control, CLI registration, and real-socket reachability. Opened-only, copied-only, both, neither, no-open, clipboard rejection, and issuance/readiness failures are covered.
- Targeted command typecheck, two-file lint, four-file format check, changed-doc MDX check, and `git diff --check` passed. Supported CLI build passed. One overlapping build hit the sandbox thread limit (`EAGAIN`); it passed when run serially after the tests completed.
- Test cost: dashboard file 3.08 s warm wall time (22 cases); four-file run 66.89 s including compiler preparation. Hosted CI passed; a per-file CI duration is not separately reported.
- Simplification: no new helper or state machine; removed the token-dependent fallback and no-open hint suppression. Production delta +12/-13; test delta +69/-14.
- **Review gap:** local Auto Review was started for the full local delta at P0–P2 but produced no report after more than 40 minutes; the coordinator cancelled that stalled review. It is not a clean review. The [completed hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201381#issuecomment-6988674197) covers head `a2524ae51c0a8cc7ee8b10658f4bb177b9c15511`: Ready for maintainer review, Diamond Lobster 5/6 for overall readiness, proof confidence, and patch quality, with no findings or Before-merge items. The [exact-head CI gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44373781115/job/135052859685). No merge is requested.

### Terminal comparison: browser and clipboard unavailable

Before:

```text
Dashboard URL: http://127.0.0.1:19849/
One-time browser pairing included in browser/clipboard URL.
Copy to clipboard unavailable.
Browser launch failed. Open the Dashboard URL above manually.
Token auto-auth not delivered. Append your gateway token (from OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN or gateway.auth.token) as a URL fragment with key `token` to authenticate.
```

After:

```text
Dashboard URL: http://127.0.0.1:19849/
Copy to clipboard unavailable.
Browser launch failed.
One-time pairing URL not delivered. Run `openclaw dashboard --json` and open its `browserUrl` within ten minutes.
Treat `browserUrl` as a credential; do not share it in logs or support requests.
```

Reported and scoped with @etzelm.

prs.title: fix: keep automations running when someone renames a session group or edits sharing
prs.body:
Root cause: src/config/sessions/session-delivery-generation.ts:192 treats the unkeyed `{ all: true, scope: "sessions" }` session-list notification as a stored-row invalidation, so one sidebar group rename or sharing edit retires the delivery generation of every in-flight run on the Gateway.

Related: #185085, #186361

## What Problem This Solves

A scheduled automation, a restart-resumed reply or another background session turn can fail partway through with `Session delivery generation is unavailable; retry after session storage is ready.` when anyone renames or deletes a session group or edits session sharing, even in an unrelated chat. The run ends as an error and its reply is lost.

## User Impact

User impact: renaming or deleting a session group, or changing who a session is shared with, no longer kills automations and background turns that are running in other sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Group and sharing handlers publish an unkeyed session-list notification after their storage writers have already published the exact per-session facts. The sharing-preparation owner already treats that plain notification as harmless once its facts are retained (d53921ac1424, "shared-session runs lose access after session list updates"). The delivery-generation lease is the other consumer of the same notification and still invalidated on it. It now applies the same rule: a plain `sessions` notification is ignored once the lease has retained facts, and every later check still reads the retained source and current facts. Notifications that carry `factsInvalidated` or a `runtimeSession` still invalidate, as before.

The change is in the lease, not in each publisher, so group rename, group delete and sharing edits are all covered without changing what clients receive.

## Evidence

- Production (Team Gateway, 14 days, read-only journal): 28 lines with this error. All of them come from session-event runs (cron `lane=cron-nested` / `source=cron`: 14, restart-recovery turns: 13, one webchat follow-up). The first attempt had been running for 19 s to 91 min before it failed, and several sessions failed in the same second, which points to one Gateway-wide invalidation rather than a per-session write. No exec-completion, subagent or channel-send callers.
- Isolated Gateway, deterministic local Responses fixture, cron job bound to a session whose turn takes 30 s, `sessions.groups.rename` called mid-run. Observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201434#issuecomment-6990134148
  - main 3bc20e28b022 (source and dist): every run that overlapped a rename failed with `Session target preparation outlived its attempt | admitted run authority is no longer active | Session delivery generation is unavailable` and `session event execution failed source=cron`, the same lines Team logs.
  - this branch ff77fa145849 (source and dist): all cron runs finish `ok` with the same renames.
  - control, main without the rename: the cron run finishes `ok`.
- Regression: `session-delivery-generation.native.test.ts` emits the unkeyed `sessions` notification on a prepared lease; red on main, green here. The same test checks that a `factsInvalidated` notification still retires the lease.
- Adjacent suites pass: delivery-generation diagnostics/incarnation/registry, sessions-sharing, sessions-groups, session-sharing-publication integration, sessions-rewind local-workspace handoff, sessions-mutations catalog-queue.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: one guard in the lease, no stored state, schema or config. If it were wrong, a run could keep a delivery generation across a group or sharing edit, but every effect still re-reads the retained source and the current row facts (membership, category, entry and permission changes are published per session and keep invalidating). Blast radius: in-flight session-event runs (cron, restart resume, exec completions) during session-list edits.

Thanks @jorge-monalee and @hvhoon for the detailed reports of runs dying with this error.

prs.title: fix(talk): steering an active voice agent consult fails with PostgreSQL agent stores
prs.body:
Related: #188965, #189418

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: steering, following up on, or cancelling a running voice agent consult fails when the Gateway uses a PostgreSQL agent store.

```
PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker; only synchronous admission, migrations, and CLI one-shots may run on the main thread
```

## User Impact

On PostgreSQL-backed Gateways, Talk control of an active voice agent run works again: browser `talk.client.steer` and the `openclaw_agent_control` tool, relay `talk.session.steer`, and GPT-Live's spoken control phrases ("actually …"). Before this change, GPT-Live answered those with "OpenClaw could not process that voice control" and the run never saw the steer. SQLite behavior is unchanged. No configuration, schema or plugin SDK change.

GPT-Live's provider steer (a plain second request during a consult) no longer fails with the PostgreSQL worker error. For the owner and `operator.admin` callers it still ends the consult with "OpenClaw could not confirm that input", on every engine; #189418 fixes that separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

#188965 fixed the initial consult and left steering out. Every Talk steering surface (provider steer for GPT-Live delegation, `talk.client.steer`, the browser `openclaw_agent_control` tool, relay `talk.session.steer`) built the caller's tool authority overlay with a synchronous session-entry read on the Gateway thread, inside the synchronous `getToolAuthorityOverlay` callback of `controlRealtimeVoiceAgentRun`, and PostgreSQL refuses that read.

This follows #188965's approach: the released synchronous SDK entry point stays as it is, and the Gateway path gets an internal asynchronous variant (there, `assertRealtimeVoiceAgentConsultModelSelectionUnlocked` stayed public and synchronous while consults moved to a private async check).

- `controlRealtimeVoiceAgentRun`, exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/realtime-voice`, keeps its released parameters and synchronous `getToolAuthorityOverlay` and delegates to the internal `controlTalkAgentRun`. The plugin SDK does not export `controlTalkAgentRun`.
- `controlTalkAgentRun` also accepts `getToolAuthorityOverlayAsync`. It is awaited when the run is selected and again in each injection admission's `prepareCurrent`, so caller policy is reread for every admission, not reused. The synchronous `compatAssertCurrent` cannot repeat an asynchronous read; it checks the overlay prepared for that admission while `assertCurrent` still rechecks live operator authority and run ownership.
- `prepareTalkClientControlAuthority` reads the entry with `getSessionEntryAsync` (same `readConsistency: "latest"`), and the four Talk surfaces call `controlTalkAgentRun` with it as `getToolAuthorityOverlayAsync`.

Not in this change: Discord voice control is a bundled SDK consumer with the same synchronous read inside its own synchronous callback. It stays on the released callback; moving it off the Gateway-thread read would need an SDK change of its own. The `voice-call` extension's synchronous lock helper is untouched.

## Evidence

Current-main applicability checked at `83fd655f3fa`. Native #188965 corrected consult start. Follow-up, cancel and steer still need the worker-backed async authority path here. This PR and #189418 both touch the consult callback; the second landing should preserve async lookup and guarded attempt authority.

- The real-storage regression `src/talk/client-voice-session-entry.postgres.test.ts` (from #188580 and #188965) now also steers the consult it starts. Its model boundary holds a real session turn open with a bound tool-authority snapshot and a guarded embedded handle. The probe steers that run with an exact run target and the overlay from `prepareTalkClientControlAuthority`, then checks that the steer is queued, that authority is read again for the injection, and that other main-thread SQL is still refused. It runs in a main-thread child with the Gateway database role, through `scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs` against disposable PostgreSQL 16 on Node 24.22.1.
  - Unchanged `main` (`510e1687e96`), with the steer wired the way `main` wires it: PostgreSQL fails with `PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker` at `prepareTalkClientControlAuthority` → `getSessionEntry` → `loadSessionEntryReadOnly`. SQLite passes.
  - With this change, PostgreSQL and SQLite both pass.
- New cases in `src/talk/agent-run-control.stop.test.ts` drive the real run controller, session controller and injection admission through `controlTalkAgentRun` with `getToolAuthorityOverlayAsync`. An allowed caller is queued. A wrong caller is rejected with `tool_authority_mismatch`. Revoking the caller, or reassigning the run, during the injection's own authority read never reaches backend enqueue. The existing synchronous-callback cases still call the public `controlRealtimeVoiceAgentRun`.
- Public SDK surface: the `controlRealtimeVoiceAgentRun` declaration (doc comment through return type, 23 lines) is byte-identical to `main` (`510e1687e96`), `src/plugin-sdk/` has no diff, and no SDK entry exports `controlTalkAgentRun`, by name or through a wildcard re-export.
- Talk and voice-consumer suites on this head: `src/talk/` 344 passed; `src/gateway/talk/` 621 passed, 1 failed; `server.talk-*`, requester-final, `src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.test.ts` and the tool-authority, steering-authority and message-injection-order tests 133 passed; `extensions/voice-call/` and `extensions/discord/src/voice/` 1,424 passed. The one failure, `client.test.ts > cancels a public provider that resolves after its browser disconnects without creating a chat`, fails the same way locally on unchanged `main` (`510e1687e96`) and is not touched here.
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxlint and formatting on the changed files, and the `mock-exports` and `line-cap` ratchets pass.

Shipped-Gateway proof (built `510e168` vs `309b5ed`, disposable PostgreSQL, local GPT-Live and Responses fixtures, a second spoken request while the first agent model call is held in flight): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189036#issuecomment-6539391285

The same Gateway proof rebuilt at `5f8d5cd` (PostgreSQL and SQLite), plus the public-declaration comparison: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189036#issuecomment-6545993216

prs.title: fix: let upgraded state stores port to PostgreSQL
prs.body:
Closes #201250

## What Problem This Solves

Porting an upgraded SQLite state store to PostgreSQL fails when its valid content-version marker is older than the current schema version.

## User Impact

Operators can port these stores without manually editing state metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

PostgreSQL admission now applies SQLite’s numeric marker rules. It accepts older valid markers while still rejecting malformed or newer markers. The recovery test preserves a separate contract: a verified staged copy must still pass owner admission on resume. Its SQLite source has a global `schema_meta` row with a non-null `agent_id`; SQLite maintenance accepts that row, while PostgreSQL owner admission refuses the copied row.

## Evidence

Using an isolated PostgreSQL 16 container and synthetic state, I initialized a current-schema SQLite store, set its content marker to 39, and added `test.cliPortSetting`. The shipped `pnpm openclaw database port --family state --to postgres --json` command exited 0. PostgreSQL contained both the marker `39` and the synthetic setting. The shipped reverse port to SQLite also exited 0, and both values were present in the resulting SQLite store.

`node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <task-local DSN> -- src/infra/database-engine/port-command.recovery.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 13 tests. Temporarily removing admission from the verified-resume branch made the revised case fail: the port completed instead of rejecting. The production file was restored afterward.

`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.infra.json --incremental`, targeted oxlint, oxfmt check, and `git diff --check` passed. PR CI on the forthcoming commit remains pending.

AI disclosure: Codex assisted with this change; independent review is pending.

prs.title: fix(gateway): deleting an account stalls and reconnects siblings
prs.body:
Related: #142193

## What Problem This Solves

Deleting one channel account can wait behind unrelated Gateway requests and reconnect healthy sibling accounts.

## User Impact

Removing a proven isolated, non-default named account stops only that account, including an account already stopped for migration. Siblings keep their connections. Shared settings, `accounts.default`, ambiguous or unproven identities, unresolvable surviving accounts, and plugins without the opt-in keep whole-channel handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reload planner matches authored keys to plugin-listed runtime IDs using the previous and candidate snapshots. Removal uses the channel manager's captured teardown, waits for that account's work, and retires its runtime state without starting a replacement. Failed or unfinished teardown retains its cleanup owner and requests recovery.

This proposes extending the published `accountScopedRestart` capability to isolated named-account removal. **Maintainer acceptance of that contract extension and current-head security approval are still required.**

## Evidence — October 23

Candidate **`27193149bc2bfa1438b617035637323a522f1009`** merges conflicting upstream **`c537658285b7906c5de296b7c4b379f57d835157`** into the previously published head `68b9e541b1d5a6a02f2440138d3ffbeb43e23598`. The repair preserves upstream's removal of the planner test hook and its current publication, credential and teardown ownership. The resulting PR has 19 changed files, +743/-173.

- **Regression control:** the eight account-identity cases ran against the current upstream planner: four failed and four passed, exposing removal/canonical-identity and dotted-key classification differences. The candidate passes them.
- **Affected owners:** all **482 tests in ten suites passed**; Vitest 255.87 seconds, maintained-wrapper wall time 265.36 seconds. This includes running/stopped account removal during unrelated work, canonical/raw identities, pending startup/task/stop-hook work, failed cleanup recovery, inactive credentials, secrets reload and model publication.
- **Types:** `core-test-gateway-root` passed in 18.9 seconds; `core-test-gateway-server` passed in 16.5 seconds.
- **Static checks:** targeted lint for all changed TypeScript files, formatting of all 19 changed files, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- **Local review:** the canonical isolated autoreview helper reported no actionable P0–P2 findings in the selected diff. Its assessment was limited to supplied diff/context and did not execute tests.
- **Shipped runtime:** the full maintained `pnpm build` passed in **6m 58.5s**. The clean checkout's built CLI removed running/already-stopped accounts in **255/130 ms** while an independently admitted 45-second Gateway request remained pending. Departing sockets closed and runtime accounts disappeared; the sibling delivered **four actual IRC status replies on its original socket, with zero reconnects through the full observation**. Driver exit 0 and child cleanup were verified.
- **CI (rechecked November 1):** [Exact-head code CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40028756475) for `27193149bc2bfa1438b617035637323a522f1009`; the latest PR context/evidence check also passes. CodeQL's aggregate is neutral with a warning that 16 main-branch configurations were not found, so it does not establish introduced-alert coverage for those missing configurations. GitHub reports no merge conflicts, and maintainer edits are enabled. The enforced `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` and aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` still fail solely with “A maintainer must approve the current PR revision.” No security approval or merge is claimed. The source head is retained to avoid invalidating its existing code proof and pending maintainer decision.

Reproduce the focused checks:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/config-reload-plan.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-channel-restart.test.ts src/gateway/server-aux-handlers.test.ts src/gateway/server-channels.account-lifetime.test.ts src/gateway/server-secrets-reload.model-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-model-runtime-scope.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-channel-restart.inactive-accounts.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-gateway-root","core-test-gateway-server"]'
```

<details>
<summary>Fresh shipped-CLI / real-ngIRCd trace and reproduction</summary>

The [public driver and ngIRCd configuration](https://gist.github.com/ceckert/a62e6702bb3f27671c7395b9dbcd7e22) were reused with one fixture-only update: omit the retired `agents.defaults.heartbeat` key from the fresh configuration. All behavioral assertions are unchanged. Original driver SHA256: `2a964b9fab3e7b9d8a9a08b61bfa16c0ffd5321126381d40fe630cbc96a71213`; updated driver SHA256: `2c9fcab889b4a7d0f1465dbdb0a09ba9b1c727b94664ee008d5a03790bdae600`.

Apply this single-line patch to the public driver before reproducing:

```diff
-  agents: { defaults: { workspace: path.join(out, 'workspace'), heartbeat: { every: '0m' } } },
+  agents: { defaults: { workspace: path.join(out, 'workspace') } },
```

Node **v24.22.1**, pnpm **12.15.0**, macOS arm64 Gateway; real ngIRCd **26.1**, Debian package `26.1-1+deb12u1`, in a task-owned Linux AMD64 container with only a loopback host port. The maintained full build exited 0; tracked checkout was clean before and after the proof. Embedded build commit was `27193149bc2bfa1438b617035637323a522f1009` (OpenClaw `2026.10.6`). Build-info SHA256: `265a44dad614bbf15b5eec0f08a2e24dfcc27dfe6eefbd87b48e2e7eb1f80e2c`. Complete trace SHA256: `8cf27b05b7e5b0d3889b4db1c203f04ed262f3d3dc47c64f04eff3c098cfff0d`.

The driver launches `openclaw.mjs gateway run --allow-unconfigured` with a temporary HOME, state and workspace, a sanitized environment, synthetic accounts and loopback endpoints. A transparent TCP observer records connections to real ngIRCd; an independent IRC client receives actual sibling status replies.

```jsonl
{"event":"provenance","head":"27193149bc2bfa1438b617035637323a522f1009","buildCommit":"27193149bc2bfa1438b617035637323a522f1009","node":"v24.22.1","transport":"bundled IRC client -> transparent TCP observer -> real ngIRCd","state":"isolated temporary directory","endpoints":"loopback only"}
{"event":"sibling_delivery","phase":"before","originalConnectionId":1,"receivedByIndependentClient":true}
{"event":"unrelated_request_active","pending":true,"counts":{"rootRequests":1,"cronRuns":0,"sessionMutations":0,"terminalPersistence":0,"lifecycleWrites":0}}
{"event":"removal_complete","authoredKey":"Root","runtimeAccountId":"root","alreadyStopped":false,"configApplyMs":255,"unrelatedRequestStillPending":true,"departingSocketClosed":true,"removedAccountAbsent":true,"siblingOriginalSocketOpen":true,"siblingConnectionCount":1}
{"event":"sibling_delivery","phase":"after-root-removal","originalConnectionId":1,"receivedByIndependentClient":true}
{"event":"removal_complete","authoredKey":"Stopped","runtimeAccountId":"stopped","alreadyStopped":true,"configApplyMs":130,"unrelatedRequestStillPending":true,"departingSocketClosed":true,"removedAccountAbsent":true,"siblingOriginalSocketOpen":true,"siblingConnectionCount":1}
{"event":"sibling_delivery","phase":"after-stopped-removal","originalConnectionId":1,"receivedByIndependentClient":true}
{"event":"sibling_delivery","phase":"final","originalConnectionId":1,"receivedByIndependentClient":true}
{"event":"unrelated_request_completed","status":"timeout","configuredWaitMs":45000}
{"event":"PASS","cases":2,"siblingTransportReconnects":0,"realTransportDeliveries":4,"head":"27193149bc2bfa1438b617035637323a522f1009"}
```

Driver exited 0 after joining its Gateway child. Process inspection found neither the driver nor Gateway child remaining. The task-owned IRC container and its task-specific image tag were removed.

```sh
git checkout 27193149bc2bfa1438b617035637323a522f1009
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build
# Start real ngIRCd using the public configuration on a loopback-only port.
node /path/to/proof.mjs /path/to/clean-checkout LOOPBACK_IRC_PORT /path/to/new-isolated-output
```

</details>

## Maintainer Decisions Still Required

- Accept the extension of `accountScopedRestart` to isolated non-default named-account removal. The previous public contract excluded removal.
- Supply the enforced security-sensitive approval for this exact head after the guard notice updates. The secrets-reload changes pass existing in-memory snapshots to the planner; they add no I/O, logs or RPC fields and preserve preparation, publication, revision checks and rollback.

## Limits and Previous Evidence

The initial October 23 runtime attempt exited 78 before Gateway startup: the old driver's `agents.defaults.heartbeat` field is now rejected as retired configuration. No removal case ran in that attempt. The single-line fixture update above was made before the successful replay; it changes no production source or behavioral assertion.

The new full build exited 0. Its current Control UI startup JS was 276.1 KiB gzip against an enforced 276.5 KiB limit. This is the new build's result, not a claim that this PR repaired the earlier size advisory.

This proves the two removal paths through a local macOS arm64 Gateway and a real Linux IRC service; it does not establish Linux Gateway execution, all-channel behavior, external model/provider behavior, a full repository `pnpm check`, or maintainer security acceptance.

The [October 20 evidence](https://gist.github.com/ceckert/265774b3d6b7232d0d5fb6c2d2a0e7c1) and [earlier author update](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167431#issuecomment-6115046820) retain prior environment/setup failures, restricted-loopback stalls, build-size advisory, and historical UI/export audit results. Those remain evidence for their recorded revisions, not clearance for this candidate. The previously published head's [ordinary CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39444499622); its missing security approval remains separate and cannot authorize a new head.

Current-main applicability checked at `83fd655f3fa`. The planner still falls back to whole-channel restart on named-account removal. Native deferred reload work addresses when changes apply; this PR addresses which accounts are stopped. The remaining merge gates are the account-removal contract and the enforced security-sensitive approval.
