prs.body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/09dcd9d9-56b4-415e-bca7-424ea1d11bb4)

Related: #200301

## What Problem This Solves

When a Cmd+K search finds nothing, people with older conversations on their Gateway don't get the usual "No results match your search." empty state. They get a small gray line instead: "Archived sessions are not included in message search." The line is also wrong. It appears when some message history was moved to cold storage, not when you have sessions you archived from the sidebar.

## User Impact

User impact: a Cmd+K search with no matches always shows an empty state, and the misleading archived-sessions line is gone. The empty state now uses the same quiet pattern as the app's other empty panels: a small muted search icon, a plain title and a short hint.

## Why This Change Was Made

The palette treated skipped cold-storage transcripts as an incomplete search. That suppressed the empty state and showed the notice in its place. Cold storage is a normal, long-lived condition, so warning about it on every empty search was noise. This removes that state from the palette along with its string and styles. The no-results view itself now uses the shared panel empty state instead of its own oversized compose icon and bold heading. The other search notices (failed message search, indexing, model search failure) still replace the empty state as before. The Sessions page transcript search keeps its own count of skipped transcripts. #200301 says it keeps this notice. Whichever PR lands second needs to drop it there too.

## Evidence

Scenario: a search for "quarterly roadmap" with no matching sessions or messages, while the Gateway reports 146 skipped cold-stored transcripts. Production Control UI build against the mocked Control UI E2E Gateway, 1280×900, light theme. Before is main at 0aafe6691b81; after is this branch at 72047685f694. Dark theme and a 390 px phone viewport were also checked; the phone capture is viewport emulation, so it still shows the desktop Tab hint.

prs.title: fix: stop the recurring cold-storage failure when an agent has no database
prs.body:
Closes #200830

## What Problem This Solves

Gateways that set `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention` and have any configured agent without a database logged `transcript cold storage failed: … SQLite archive pruning requires its existing file owner` every minute, indefinitely. A store with no database now simply has nothing to prune.

- Problem: cold-storage maintenance asks the archive owner to prune retention for **every** configured agent id, including ids with no database yet (a fresh agent, or an `acp.allowedAgents` id that never ran). The page-reclamation guard rejects that path-only identity, so the whole pass fails.
- Solution: return no removals when the store's captured identity is not an existing file.
- What changed: `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-archive-store.ts` (guard in `prunePublishedSessionArchivesByRetention`) and a regression case in `session-cold-storage.inventory.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: stores that have a database prune exactly as before, and the page-reclamation guard still rejects identities it cannot explain, so a replaced or inaccessible database is not silently skipped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The read side of the same retention query already returns "nothing" for a store with no database, and the archive step beside this call returns early for the same case; only the prune call treated it as an error.

- Best fix: keep the guard in the archive owner (`prunePublishedSessionArchivesByRetention`) so every caller of the retention query behaves like its read counterpart. `path:` is produced only when the database path does not exist, so this cannot hide a permission or replacement problem — those fail identity resolution and still throw elsewhere.
- Alternative: skip absent stores in the maintenance loop in `session-cold-storage.ts`. Smaller diff, but leaves the same trap for the next caller of the prune entry point.
- Risk / non-goals: a store created between inventory and prune is skipped for that one pass and pruned on the next; retention is age-based, so no archive is lost.

## User Impact

A Gateway with an unused ACP allowlist id, or with a freshly configured agent, stops logging `transcript cold storage failed` every 60 s, and `sessions.storage.status` stops reporting `lastError` for a normal state.

## Evidence

Shipped Gateway run on a source build of this PR head (`5a31f7f`, Debian 13, Node 24.22.1). Config: one agent (`main`) plus one `acp.allowedAgents` id (`codex`) that never ran; `session.maintenance.mode=enforce`, `resetArchiveRetention=365d`, cold storage enabled. `sessions.create` gave `main` a database, then two maintenance passes ran:

```text
== populated sibling databaseBytes(main) = 700416

== retention pass 1
maintenance: {"lastError": null, "lastCompletedAt": 1794970950128}
agents: main databaseBytes=700416 hotTranscripts=1 | codex databaseBytes=0

== retention pass 2
maintenance: {"lastError": null, "lastCompletedAt": 1794970974544}

== sessions.storage.status
agents: {'main': 700416, 'codex': 0}
maintenance: {'lastError': None, 'archivedTranscripts': 0,
              'externalizedTranscripts': 0, 'lastCompletedAt': 1794971010035}
running: false

== gateway log: 'transcript cold storage failed' occurrences: 0
```

This is the reported scenario: the absent `codex` store no longer fails the pass, the populated `main` store stays in the inventory of every pass, and repeated passes complete with `lastError: null` instead of one error per minute. Neither store had eligible archives to remove, so both counters are legitimately 0; removal itself is covered by the existing retention suite below.

Regression test — before/after on the same checkout:

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts \
    src/config/sessions/session-cold-storage.inventory.test.ts -t "no database"
 # before: × keeps the maintenance pass healthy when a configured agent has no database
 #         Caused by: Error: SQLite archive pruning requires its existing file owner
 # after:  ✓ keeps the maintenance pass healthy when a configured agent has no database
```

Pruning for stores that do have a database is unchanged — the same store set still prunes:

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts \
    src/config/sessions/session-cold-storage.inventory.test.ts \
    src/config/sessions/session-history-archive-retention.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
```

What was not tested: no pre-fix Gateway run was repeated for this revision (the pre-fix failure is covered by the regression test above and by the `lastError` in the linked report); no archives were eligible for removal in the Gateway run, so end-to-end removal is covered by the retention suite rather than that run.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `gh`/`git`/`grep` to trace issue #200830 from `runSessionColdStorageMaintenance` down to the page-reclamation guard, plus a source Gateway run and `vitest` for the before/after. The implementer understands the code: the inventory reports `path:` for a database that does not exist yet, the read side of the same retention query already treats that as "nothing to prune", and the guard belongs at the archive owner so every caller agrees. All evidence above comes from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: feat(ui): show live Swarm progress inside chat turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A live Swarm in Control UI chat shows a running count, but the transcript doesn’t show which workers are queued, running, or finished. You have to leave the turn to inspect them.

## User Impact

The turn that launched the Swarm shows a compact grid of worker states. Select an available worker to open it in Subagents. When the parent hands off and resumes, the grid stays with the turn that launched it. The latest completed group stays visible on reload while the Gateway still retains it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The grid reads the same Gateway summary as the existing child roster. It matches groups by exact parent session and launch run ID, including the earlier runs that a resumed frame explicitly continues. There is no new polling or stored UI state. Explicitly shared group IDs remain inspectable in Subagents rather than being assigned to an arbitrary turn. The grid reuses existing button styles and uses distinct SVG markers for worker states.

## Evidence

All four focused browser tests and all 52 grouping and yield tests passed. Desktop and mobile coverage includes deduplication, keyboard activation, and terminal counts after child-session expiry.
- UI typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, diff checks, and scoped P0–P2 autoreview passed for the handoff repair. It changes no stylesheet or performance budget. The prior revision passed CI, including Control UI performance; exact-head checks for the repair are tracked separately in this PR.

prs.title: fix(gateway): recover guest tasks after concurrent managed-workspace edits (#187911)
prs.body:
Closes #187911

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a managed sandbox conversation stays stuck when an administrator and the guest edit the same file at once. Both versions are preserved, but Files and every later turn of the original task keep returning "Local sandbox edits conflict with the managed workspace" instead of letting the authorized user merge the contributions and continue.

## User Impact

The affected conversation can recover without discarding either side. A normal authorized Files save is the acknowledgement: when the operator's expected hash matches the guest copy they read, the save is recorded against that guest version, the resolved file is copied into the private sandbox checkout, and the original task can continue. Files that are still conflicted stay pending. A guest version written after the capture is still rejected, and a save on a worktree without a pending conflict no longer writes a synthetic checkpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Conflict acknowledgement goes through the projection state's own update operation, so the next synchronization sees the current binding rather than a changed one.
- A Files save binds the selected candidate path through the actual write, so nested `fileRoot` sessions cannot resolve the same relative path twice.
- Acknowledgement is only recorded for a retained conflict or a pending receipt, so ordinary saves leave the checkpoint empty.
- A save whose own file is accepted while other conflicts remain is reported as an accepted save, while real write and authority failures still propagate.
- Reconciliation commits resolved canonical files onto the complete accepted baseline, preserving unconflicted guest additions, edits, and deletions.
- Canonical imports hold the existing guest pause through acceptance for either direction, so a background guest process cannot race verified bytes.
- A guest directory that may contain unreviewed descendants is refused, never recursively deleted; a legacy checkpoint without the new fields still settles.
- Resolved copies keep the existing authority revalidation, realpath/symlink containment, recursive replacement of a conflicting type, and a recorded guest version so a later guest edit of the same path conflicts again instead of being overwritten.

## Evidence

- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 pnpm tsgo:core` — clean, no diagnostics.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.worktree.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-projection.conflict.test.ts --maxWorkers=4` — 2 files, 32/32 tests passed. Key cases:
  - `acknowledges and saves a reconciled version via sessions.files.set during conflict` (then prepares the next guest workspace successfully)
  - `resolves conflict hash correctly when session has a nested fileRoot`
  - `preserves compare-and-swap protection for unseen canonical edits outside retained conflicts`
  - `accepts a newer guest version that the operator actually reviewed in projection`
  - `treats a resolved path as a new conflict after the guest edits it again`
  - `does not synthesize a checkpoint for an ordinary managed save`
  - `resolves canonical workspace-relative path when saving absolute path candidates`
  - `overlays resolved paths onto complete accepted baseline preserving unmutated baseline entries`
  - `preserves newer guest divergence in projection if edited while conflict is pending`
  - `rejects unreviewed newer guest version written after administrator review`
  - `refuses to replace a guest directory that gained unreviewed descendants`
  - `settles a legacy checkpoint that predates the conflict fields`
- Broader focused batch (projection, manifest scan, store, checkout, CAS, fingerprints, diagnostics, reconcile/publication, workspace-local reconciliation): 205 passed, 1 skipped.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 pnpm test:unit:fast --maxWorkers=4` — 13,740 passed, 49 skipped; failures only in untouched suites: `completion-fish` spawnSync result shape, `bench-session-history` node spawnSync ETIMEDOUT under load, and one provider-header test that passes alone and only failed in the full shard.
- The suite runs the production `sessions.files.*` handlers against prepared git worktrees, the projection custody owner, and the SQLite worker boundary; it is not a mocked handler harness.
- Supporting Docker-backed regression (`pnpm test test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/managed-workspace-conflict-recovery.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 1/1 passed) uses a mock provider: `pnpm test test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/managed-workspace-conflict-recovery.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 1/1 passed (28 s). It starts a real Gateway child with a Docker sandbox, creates a managed worktree session, provisions the private projection, preserves a real conflict, recovers it through `sessions.files.set`, and completes the next guest turn with both trees holding the merged bytes.
- Real-model product trace (isolated Gateway, Docker sandbox, Codex CLI ChatGPT login; model and paths redacted): three turns through the running Gateway. Turn 1 replied `READY` and provisioned the managed worktree projection (Docker container started, sandbox backend timings recorded). Diverging guest/admin edits produced the preserved `LocalWorkspaceConflictError` on turn 2. `sessions.files.set` returned the updated `preview.html`; turn 3 replied `CONTINUED`, and canonical and projection both held `merged by administrator and guest`.
- The branch is merged with current `main` (`910f6b9427d`).
- Latest-stable upgrade proof (`openclaw@2026.11.5`): created a real managed-worktree conflict with a pending canonical result through the stable release, then opened the same state with this branch. Before upgrade the checkpoint contained only `baseManifestRaw`, `baseManifestRef`, `currentManifestRaw`, `currentManifestRef`, `fingerprints`, `records`, `removed`, roots, tree roots, and `version` — none of the new fields. The upgraded run migrated the state database, preserved an unrelated settings file byte-for-byte, kept the pending ref and both file contributions, and after acknowledgement settled to `pending_ref: null` with canonical and projection both holding `merged after stable upgrade`. All paths and identifiers are redacted here.
- Accepted limits: guest-version probing is bounded at 8 MiB, so a larger guest file records no reviewed version and the retained conflict capture stays authoritative; automatic file-to-directory conflict resolution is refused instead of partially applied.

prs.title: fix: preserve lower-token guidance for unaffordable requests
prs.body:
Related: #25395, #151377

## What Problem This Solves

A provider can reject one request because its maximum token budget costs more than the available credit or key allowance. OpenClaw currently replaces the provider’s “more credits, or fewer max_tokens” advice with generic billing guidance, hiding the option to lower the output limit.

## User Impact

User impact: request-affordability failures explain that lowering maximum output tokens is an alternative to checking the account balance or key spending limit. Explicit key-limit failures get distinct guidance. Generic billing and genuine rate-limit messages retain their existing behavior; an affordability rejection does not establish an empty account.

No configuration migration, automatic token reduction, new retry, provider switch, or credential change is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing billing-message owner now uses the retained provider detail before selecting safe, fixed recovery text. The distinction survives assistant errors, structured fallback attempts, and final reply normalization without exposing provider response bodies or help URLs. Classification, cooldowns, and retry policy are unchanged.

Simplification: reuse the existing raw-error and fallback-attempt fields rather than add new state or classifier categories. Billing copy has one implementation in a small focused module, extracted to keep the existing user-copy module within its enforced line limit. The existing export remains a forwarding export, not a second implementation.

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI proof requested by review

Executed the actual `pnpm openclaw agent exec` command on the unchanged candidate for head `9e86caad82cc1f29a2b80d43b109cac422a82eb4` (workspace tree `383749c396e0a2bea9cde0fb07758aaba1714311`). The normal package entry point prepared current build artifacts. Isolated HOME/config/state/workspace, one fake credential, one local synthetic HTTP 402 server, and no fallbacks were used. No live Gateway, external provider, or paid request was involved.

**Result:** the expected provider-error exit is **1**, not a failed proof. prs.title: fix(cron): scheduled runs refused for a missing account hide the cause and retry ten times
prs.body:
Closes #195802
Related: #191637, #189953, #188946

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scheduled run refused because its automation has no recorded inference account is reported only as "Session event execution failed", and a recurring job keeps retrying it until it is auto-disabled after ten failures.

## User Impact

User impact: automation history, run diagnostics and the failure alert now name the missing recorded account and how to record it, and a recurring job pauses after its first refused run with one alert instead of failing ten times. Chat alerts leave out the stored account; automation history keeps the exact refusal and command, and a webhook failure route still receives the raw last error as before. Gateway startup now also warns about unbound Codex-runtime jobs. Account authorization is unchanged: the guard still refuses these runs, and optional scheduled runs still post no chat failure text.

## Why This Change Was Made

Optional scheduled replies blank their chat failure text, so session-event settlement fell back to generic wording even though the reply operation still held the refusal as its failure cause. The turn owner now passes that recorded cause with its session-event terminal evidence, and settlement uses it when nothing else presented an error, for the run error and diagnostics (redacted through the existing error formatter and diagnostics normalizer).

The refusal is marked when it is created. Cron turns that mark into a permanent classification with a closed failure detail, for both session-event and isolated runs, so the existing failure-alert and auto-disable owners pause the job on the first refusal with fixed copy that names `openclaw doctor --fix` and the `openclaw automations edit` form without the account. Transient failures keep the existing retry ladder and ten-failure limit.

The startup diagnostic (now account-aware after #195905) no longer excludes the Codex runtime: like Doctor, it plans Codex auth through the harness and warns only when that plan would use a stored account. Native or credentialless Codex login and CLI backends that own their login stay quiet.

Accepted edge cases: the paused job records the existing `state.autoDisabled.reason: consecutive-failures` with `consecutiveErrors: 1` rather than adding a new persisted reason. The existing closed-detail notices for command failures and watchdog stops are preserved.

<details>
<summary>Not included: failure alert "explicit channel required"</summary>

A job whose delivery session has no external last channel (for example a session-target job in a WebChat or internal orchestration session) and no `sourceConversation` resolves its failure alert to `channel: "last"`. `resolveDeliveryTarget` then falls back to `resolveMessageChannelSelection`, which fails with "Channel is required when multiple channels are configured …" when more than one channel is configured. The alert is recorded as not delivered and only reaches the passive in-app fallback queue. The job's own delivery route and session are already the inputs to that resolution, so there is no route to fall back to; choosing a destination (owner DM, Control UI attention, or refusing at creation) is a separate product decision that overlaps #189953 and #188946.

</details>

## Evidence

The regressions verify actionable diagnostics without chat failure text, permanent classification for isolated runs, a first-failure pause with one account-free chat alert, and Codex startup warnings. New lifecycle tests preserve timeout, cancellation, supersession and auth-revoked precedence.

- On the reconciled candidate, 13 unique focused suites passed across cron, session events, watchdogs and failure alerts (290 test executions, including a repeated auth-profile suite).
- The new classifier regression fails against base `457486d4` with `unknown` instead of `permanent`, and passes with the fix. The original feature regressions were also proven red/green in earlier revisions.
- Core and source-test typechecks, changed-file lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and line-cap/max-lines/test-lines ratchets passed. Net test growth is 154 lines, within the current 400-line allowance; the obsolete allocation file was removed.
- The final refresh to `1fc5296c` left the reviewed patch’s stable patch ID unchanged. The updated session-event, watchdog, scheduler-outcome and classifier suites passed again (88 tests), along with core typecheck and diff check.
- An independent read-only subagent reviewed the complete diff and all 21 changed files: **no actionable P0–P3 findings**. It reviewed frozen source evidence because its sandbox lacked the checkout; it did not independently verify Git state or rerun tests. The requester explicitly selected this route after Auto Review timed out.

The main reconciliation retains newer invalid-target, session-conflict and watchdog behavior. Returned and thrown watchdog failures now share their notification-detail projection; the existing cron terminal classifier owns lifecycle precedence. The protected creation-time binding files remain unchanged relative to the refreshed base.

These are production-boundary tests with synthetic model execution, not live Gateway/model proof. CI on the newly published head is separate from prior green runs.

Reported by @Marvinthebored in #195802.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/a78de3ca-a70a-4021-89b3-02e448bfa814)

prs.title: fix: setup says which tool profile the agent has and what it allows
prs.body:
Closes #201042

## What Problem This Solves

Setup keeps an existing tool profile, or picks `full` when none is set, and never says which one the agent ends up with. A config that still has `tools.profile: "messaging"` finishes setup with chat working and no file, command or web tools, and nothing in the output points at the profile.

## User Impact

User impact: at the end of setup, people see which tool profile the agent has, where it is set, what it allows in plain words, which other kept tool settings change it, and how to add one tool.

## Why This Change Was Made

Setup already decides the profile in `applyLocalSetupWorkspaceConfig`. One helper next to it reads the effective profile from the existing tool policy owner (`resolveEffectiveToolPolicy`, which also gives the config path and the narrowest `alsoAllow` path) and builds one line. The three setup flows that end with output print it: guided and app setup (the `Workspace:` / `Gateway:` summary), the wizard (a note before the finish), and non-interactive setup (before the web search tip, not in `--json`).

An agent-level profile (`agents.entries.<id>.tools.profile`) outranks the `full` that setup writes, so the line names that path. Kept `allow`, `alsoAllow`, `deny` and `byProvider` settings are named, not modeled: "These settings also change which tools the agent gets: tools.deny." Which profile setup writes is unchanged. No new config and no profile picker (#36868 was closed).

Related: #200936 (an agent that hits a missing tool names the setting and the fix). It changes `session_status` output only; no file overlap.

## Evidence

- Real `openclaw onboard --non-interactive` runs on main and on this branch, below.
- New tests: two cases in `setup-apply.test.ts` (guided setup summary for a written `full` and a kept `messaging`) fail on main, pass on this branch, and fail again with the production change reverted (`git apply -R`). Three cases in `onboard-config.test.ts` cover an agent-level profile, a kept `alsoAllow`, and kept `deny`/`byProvider`/agent `allow` settings.
- Touched and consumer suites on the head: setup-apply, onboard-config, wizard setup, non-interactive onboarding (gateway, migration, default agent, legacy fleet), system-agent setup operations, guided onboarding, tool catalog, Gateway tools catalog and templates schema. All passed.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 4a44f2031e8` (current main): typecheck, lint, format, import cycles and the guards pass. The dead export scan fails on two exports this change does not touch (`describeSpawnAuth` in `subagent-spawn-billing-route.ts`, `ADVANCED_FIELDS` in `ui/src/pages/cron/view-delivery.tsx`).
- Local ClawSweeper review (local range, Claude runner, 4 rounds): the last round on this head is complete, patch correct, no findings, security cleared. Earlier rounds found that the line ignored kept `allow`/`deny`/`byProvider`, that provider entries can widen tools, and that `alsoAllow` was not named. All are fixed here.

prs.title: fix: keep New session Recent to five places without helper checkouts
prs.body:
Thanks @vyctorbrzezowski for reporting this.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4edc0b28-406d-455e-bd38-3e7b9fea4f4a)

## What Problem This Solves

The **Recent** section of the New session project picker could fill with up to eight rows, and most of them were task checkouts that agents created for their own helper sessions (for example `a1-remove-wake-mode`, `a2-retire-main-session-events`). Those are not places the person chose, and picking one starts a new session inside another task's worktree.

## User Impact

User impact: **Recent** shows at most five rows (the agent workspace plus four recent places), and it only lists places from sessions the person started, not checkouts made for agent-spawned helpers.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The Gateway now skips sessions that another session spawned when it builds project recents. The parent session, which the person started, still contributes its own place.
- The picker caps the section at five rows. When the workspace row is shown it takes one of the five, matching the existing four-folder fallback used without a profile.
- The New session docs describe the limit and the exclusion.

Accepted edge case: a person who deliberately keeps working inside a helper's checkout will not see it in Recent; they can still browse to it.

## Evidence

- New Gateway test: a helper session spawned by a parent is skipped, and only the parent's folder is returned and marked as used.
- New picker tests: eight recent folders reduce to four beside the workspace row and to five without it.
- Focused run: `projects-recents.test.ts` and `project-chip.test.ts` pass (2 Vitest shards).
- Checked against the live Team host: the `a1-remove-wake-mode` recent comes from `agent:roboclaw:subagent:…`, a helper attributed to the requesting person, which is why it reached that person's Recent list.

<!-- maintainer-recent-places-proof -->
### Paired picker proof

Ran the production Control UI in Chromium on base `3bc20e28b02` and this exact PR head, with the same simulated Gateway response containing six recent folders. The before picker shows seven rows including the workspace. The after picker shows five rows, retaining the workspace and the four highest-ranked places.

prs.title: fix(compaction): honor configured summary reserve above 20k
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #201397. Compaction safeguard summary requests were clamped to a 20,000-token reserve before the model output limit was applied. An explicit `compaction.reserveTokens: 65536` was therefore reduced to 20,000, producing a 16,000-token summary budget. Reasoning summaries could exhaust that budget without emitting visible text, and operators had no supported way to tune the policy.

## Change

- `resolveSummaryReserveTokens` now honors the configured reserve and applies only `model.maxTokens` as the hard ceiling.
- Added focused tests for a reserve above the former 20k cap and for model output-limit clamping.

## Evidence

- New unit tests cover `65 536 -> 65 536` and `300 000 -> model.maxTokens`.
- Existing compaction safeguard tests remain unchanged.
- Local live verification with an OpenAI-compatible reasoning model: configured reserve 65,536 produced a 52,428-token summary budget; local `ultra` compaction succeeded, reducing a long session from 86,300 to 11,166 tokens in about 720 seconds. With the old 20k cap the same request failed at 16,000 tokens.

## Why

An explicit compaction setting should not be silently overridden by an internal literal. This is the minimal fix for the immediate failure; a follow-up can expose an explicit `agents.defaults.compaction.maxSummaryReserveTokens` policy knob if maintainers prefer a configurable cap.

prs.body:
Related: #201130

## What Problem This Solves

A caller can cancel while the managed Codex app-server is starting. When startup reports that cancellation as an `AbortError`, including as the cause of a diagnostic error with stderr, the gateway can mark the installed binary as failed and use the bundled binary for subsequent requests until restart.

## User Impact

A cancelled acquisition returns its error to the caller and leaves the installed app-server available to later requests. Genuine spawn, initialization, compatibility, and timeout failures still use the existing fallback path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed fallback decision now checks for cancellation before publishing fallback ownership or rejecting the installed binary. The change uses the existing cleanup and request-currentness checks. It requires no configuration or migration.

## Evidence

- The startup regression failed before the fix. The new cases exercise cancellation during initialization and a spawn error with cancellation in its cause.
- On this PR head, all 192 shared-client and managed-binary tests passed. The Codex package-boundary compile, formatting, and lint passed.

prs.title: fix: show the whole token conflict hint in openclaw status
prs.body:
Related: #200937

## What Problem This Solves

When `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` is set and `gateway.auth.token` uses a different value, `openclaw status` warns about the conflict, but the hint is hard to use. The first word of the fix, "Remove", shows as `***`, and the line stops at 160 characters, in the middle of the instruction. `openclaw doctor` shows the same hint in full.

## User Impact

`openclaw status` now shows the whole conflict hint, readable, the same as doctor. Real secret values in status diagnostics are still masked.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hint was built as `... conflicts with gateway.auth.token: Remove ...`. Both the status redactor and the console output redactor read `token: Remove` as a key and a value, so they masked "Remove". The hint now joins the title and the fix with a period, so no redactor sees an assignment. The redaction rules are unchanged.

Status also cut every command-local secret diagnostic at 160 UTF-16 units (added in #126786). The conflict hint is about 290 units, so it was cut mid-sentence. Command-local diagnostics now use a 400-unit limit instead. That fits the whole hint, and the list stays bounded for readability as #126786 and the status docs intend, so long Gateway-returned diagnostics and wrapped error messages are still cut. This follows the review's recommendation: keep the period separator and use a finite limit of about 400 instead of no limit. Both redaction passes still run before the cut, `openclaw status` still prints at most 10 lines, and owner ids and config paths from runtime secret degradation keep the 160 limit.

## Evidence

- Regression test in `src/commands/status-all/report-data.test.ts`: the real conflict hint passes the console redactor unchanged and appears whole in the status report. Secret masking still holds: the console redactor turns `gateway.auth.token: <real-looking ghp_ value>` into `gateway.auth.token: ghp_R3…8sW1`, and the status report shows a value after `gateway.remote.token:` as `***`. A local diagnostic longer than 400 units is still cut at exactly 400. The test fails on main and passes here.
- Mutation check: reverting with `git apply -R` makes the test fail again in each of 4 cases: the whole fix, the period alone, the limit change alone (back to 160), and the 400 bound alone (back to no limit).
- Touched and consumer suites pass: status report, status command, status overview rows, status format, doctor security, security audit gateway (98 tests).
- `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main` passes (main at `2301af4923c`, which has no changes to the touched files or the redaction code; 0 lint warnings, 0 errors).
- Local review: ClawSweeper (local, `--local-range`), base `f3638439b92`, head `f094ac3eb97`: review complete, patch correct, security cleared, no findings. The proof rating there is low only because a local range review reads commit messages, not this body.

### Runtime output

Setup: built dist, `node openclaw.mjs status` with its own state dir and config, no Gateway running. All token values are synthetic `ghp_` strings, and each full output was checked for them before printing.

- Scenario A: local mode, `gateway.auth.token` set in config, and `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` set in the shell to a different value.
- Scenario B: remote mode, with a fake token in the `gateway.remote.url` query string, to show that status output still masks secrets.

**Before, on main `f3638439b92`**

Command:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs status
```

Output (the matching status lines):

```text
-- scenario A
Secret diagnostics:
- OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN conflicts with gateway.auth.token: *** OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN from the shell, ~/.openclaw/.env, or launchctl env if gateway.auth.token is
leak check: no synthetic token value in the full output
-- scenario B
│ Gateway                 │ remote · ws://127.0.0.1:28799/?token=*** (config gateway.remote.url) · unreachable         │
leak check: no synthetic token value in the full output
```

"Remove" is masked as `***`, and the line ends at 160 characters.

**After, on this branch `f094ac3eb97`**

Command:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs status
```

Output (the matching status lines):

```text
-- scenario A
Secret diagnostics:
- OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN conflicts with gateway.auth.token. Remove OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN from the shell, ~/.openclaw/.env, or launchctl env if gateway.auth.token is intended, or point gateway.auth.token at ${OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN} if the environment variable should supply the token.
leak check: no synthetic token value in the full output
-- scenario B
│ Gateway                 │ remote · ws://127.0.0.1:28799/?token=*** (config gateway.remote.url) · unreachable         │
leak check: no synthetic token value in the full output
```

The whole hint is shown with "Remove" readable, and the fake token in the URL is still `***`. No synthetic token value appears in either output.

Not shown: `openclaw status --all` output. It uses the same diagnostics helper, which the regression test covers through the `status --all` report.

Known limit: other diagnostics shaped `<path>.token: <words>` can still lose their first word to the console output redactor. This change does not touch the shared redaction rules.

prs.title: fix: report OpenRouter spending caps as billing failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenRouter returns HTTP 403 when an organization or workspace spending budget is exhausted. OpenClaw currently labels several documented budget responses as authentication failures and tells the operator to sign in again, which cannot resolve the spending cap.

## User Impact

OpenRouter spending-budget failures are identified as billing problems instead of failed sign-ins. Existing fallback behavior remains intact; ordinary permission refusals, authentication failures, rate limits, and timeouts keep their existing handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenRouter plugin recognizes the documented `limit_source` values and narrowly identified budget messages before the generic HTTP 403 classification. This stays within the existing provider hook: no core classification policy, retry contract, configuration, or new failure reason is introduced. Provider documentation explains the reset/admin remedy, including lifetime budgets.

References: [OpenRouter budget errors](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/errors-and-debugging#budget-errors), [budget limits](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/limits#handling-403-budget-errors), and [workspace budgets](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/workspaces/workspace-budgets).

## Evidence

- The included provider regression fails on the unchanged implementation and passes with this fix. The focused provider suite and two provider-precedence/structured-signal consumer suites pass: **32 tests**. The provider test file took **4.94 seconds wall time** on its final run; hosted CI timing is pending.
- A real local HTTP 403 fixture through the production embedded agent and model-fallback runner changed from `auth` plus sign-in guidance on the base to `billing` on the fix. The raw provider message retained its administrator/reset guidance. Both versions sent exactly one primary request and one fallback request. A second patched case with neutral message text proved that the structured budget metadata reaches the classifier through the real transport.

prs.title: fix: tell agents which setting hides a tool and how to add it back
prs.body:
Closes #200933

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent is on the `messaging` tool profile and needs a tool outside it, its capability check says only `messaging profile: exec, read, ...`. It does not say where that profile is set or how to add one tool back. The agent guesses, and users widen permissions or switch the whole profile to get one tool.

## User Impact

User impact: an agent that is missing a tool because of its profile can name the exact setting and the one-line fix, for example `add it to agents.entries.<agent>.tools.alsoAllow`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway's tool inventory already knows the profile's config path and the narrowest `alsoAllow` list for each excluded tool, and the Control UI shows the path. The `session_status` capability summary dropped both. It now prints them on the profile line. Deny and allowlist lines are unchanged, since their text already names the path. Tools the session never loaded keep the path but get no fix line, because a grant cannot show they would load.

Open #192971 also edits `session-status-capabilities.ts`, but only the branch where the inventory check is refused. This change only touches the reason lines of a successful check. The two do not overlap in behavior and merge cleanly (`git merge-tree`, no conflicts).

## Evidence

- New regression test in `session-status-capabilities.test.ts`: fails on main, passes on the committed head `04f7ee0c9f3`, and fails again with the fix reverted.
- The existing `tools-effective-inventory.policy.test.ts` suite (18 tests) still passes on the committed head.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 7f395779d12` (current main) on `04f7ee0c9f3`: passed.
- Real Gateway run on Linux, before and after, below.
- Local ClawSweeper review (local range, base `f3638439b92`, head `04f7ee0c9f3`, full diff): complete, patch correct, no findings, security cleared. Rating: patch A, proof D, overall D. That run saw only the commit, not the Gateway output below.

### Runtime output

Setup: a real Gateway (`openclaw gateway run`, built from source) with one agent, `agents.entries.assistant.tools.profile = "messaging"`, isolated state and a loopback port. A session is created with `openclaw gateway call sessions.create`, then `session_status` with `capabilities: true` is called through `POST /tools/invoke`. No model call and no channel. Linux arm64, Node 24.22.1.

**Before, on main `f3638439b92`**

```text
Not available in this session:
- messaging profile: agents_list, agents_wait, apply_patch, automations, browser, canvas, code_execution, computer, create_goal, dashboard, dismiss_task, edit, exec, get_goal, github_identity_status, github_publish, image_generate, ls, memory_get, memory_search, mobile_ui, music_generate, nodes, openclaw, pdf, plugins, portal, process, progress_card, read, screen, show_widget, skill_library, skill_workshop, skills_read, skills_search, suggest_task, terminal, transcripts, tts, update_goal, video_generate, view_image, web_fetch, web_search, write, x_search
```

The profile line names no setting and no fix.

**After, on this branch `04f7ee0c9f3`**

```text
Not available in this session:
- messaging profile (agents.entries.assistant.tools.profile): browser, canvas, code_execution, dismiss_task, image_generate, memory_get, memory_search, music_generate, pdf, progress_card, screen, show_widget, skill_library, skill_workshop, skills_read, skills_search, suggest_task, video_generate, view_image, web_search, x_search
- messaging profile (agents.entries.assistant.tools.profile); to allow one, add it to agents.entries.assistant.tools.alsoAllow: agents_list, agents_wait, apply_patch, automations, computer, create_goal, dashboard, edit, exec, get_goal, github_identity_status, github_publish, ls, mobile_ui, nodes, openclaw, plugins, portal, process, read, terminal, transcripts, tts, update_goal, web_fetch, write
```

**After, with the printed fix applied (`alsoAllow: ["exec"]`)**

```text
Available tools: ask_user, conversations_list, conversations_send, conversations_turn, exec, gateway, message, presence, secrets, session_status, sessions, sessions_create, sessions_history, sessions_list, sessions_search, sessions_send, sessions_spawn, sessions_yield, subagents, theme
```

The Gateway log for the same request shows the cause: `tool policy removed 26 tool(s) via tools.profile (messaging): agents_list, ..., exec, ..., write`. Those are the tools that get the `alsoAllow` line. Tools the session never built (the first line) keep only the path.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

Gateway proof, one run per state: start `openclaw gateway run --port 18789 --allow-unconfigured` with the config above, then `openclaw gateway call sessions.create --json --params '{"agentId":"assistant","key":"agent:assistant:main"}'`, then `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18789/tools/invoke` with `{"tool":"session_status","agentId":"assistant","sessionKey":"agent:assistant:main","args":{"capabilities":true}}` and a synthetic bearer token. The base run reverts the source change before the build. `dist` is rebuilt for each run.

Tests on the committed head: `pnpm test src/agents/tools/session-status-capabilities.test.ts src/agents/tools-effective-inventory.policy.test.ts`, 2/2 and 18/18 passed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

A message from another chat only shows a generic update count until you open it. That hides what the sender wanted you to know and makes it hard to scan the receiving conversation.

## User Impact

Cross-thread messages now appear on the left in a native incoming chat bubble with a link back to the source thread. A sender can supply a one-line preview; readers can expand it to see the original message. If the sender omits the summary, the original message is shown directly.

## Why This Change Was Made

The optional `sessions_send.summary` is stored separately from the original message. Each message retains its own timestamp, disclosure, and reply and copy actions. Passive notifications and automation messages keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

A real model sent a message using `sessions_send` on an isolated Gateway. prs.title: refactor(workboard): drop the unused claim and observation records
prs.body:
Closes #198705

## What Problem This Solves

Workboard cards carry optional worker claims passed to `workboard_complete` and session-lifecycle observations from #197471. Proof and run attempts already cover the worker report and run outcome. Verification logic also reads claims for claim-linked checks and self-check attribution; this PR intentionally removes those readers with the claim records. #197471 is on main and not in any tag or release.

## User Impact

`workboard_complete` no longer takes a `claims` parameter, and lifecycle sync no longer writes observations. `workboard_verify` works as before: a checker records what it checked, its outcome, and the proof, artifact, or run attempt it covered. Completion, proof statuses, and dependency scheduling are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Proof already holds the worker's report and run attempts already hold each run's outcome, so the two extra records repeated them while costing a tool parameter every worker run sees, an observation write at the end of every linked run, and per-kind retention inside the card's metadata budget.

- Verifications are stored as `metadata.automation.verifications`, without a `kind` field now that there is one record type. Generic metadata writes still cannot add, edit, or remove them.
- A card keeps its 4 newest verifications, only in room its other records leave, dropping the oldest first; `workboard_verify` returns an error when a new one cannot fit. The separate 6 KiB evidence cap is gone.

### Cards written on main since #197471

Those cards store claims, observations, and verifications together under `metadata.automation.evidence`. The next update to such a card converts it before any trimming runs, with or without a metadata patch (a manual move, lifecycle settlement, a comment, a new verification):

- checker verifications move to `metadata.automation.verifications`, newest 4, without their `kind` and `claimId` fields;
- claims and observations are dropped;
- the `evidence` key is removed, so it never takes room from proof, attempts, comments, or artifacts.

Until a card's next write, reads still return its stored `evidence` list unchanged. No Doctor migration: the old shape only exists on main builds, and nothing shipped with it.

- `store-card-helpers.ts` is also changed: `workboard_verify`'s check that a named run belongs to the card and the existing check that refuses a superseded run's late write now share one `cardHasRunAttempt` helper there. Before, that run-id comparison was written out in both `store-evidence.ts` and `store-card-helpers.ts`. Main's session identity ratchet gives a new file no allowance, so it would fail on the copy in `store-verification.ts`. With one copy, `store-card-helpers.ts` keeps its 7 allowlisted hits and the deleted file's 4 are pruned from `config/session-identity-allowlist.txt`.

About 165 production lines removed net.

## Evidence

Public retained evidence for `62c6373c5b467446938e95ee6a29bcb493420985`: [artifact index](https://github.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/blob/dc47f92f37caeb75dc73439598c0d3549203723c/evidence/2026/11/pr-198706-62c6373-df906ec9-e8b0-44ed-82b2-e0b057d938e5/README.md), [redacted terminal output](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/dc47f92f37caeb75dc73439598c0d3549203723c/evidence/2026/11/pr-198706-62c6373-df906ec9-e8b0-44ed-82b2-e0b057d938e5/terminal-output.txt), and [stored-data comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/dc47f92f37caeb75dc73439598c0d3549203723c/evidence/2026/11/pr-198706-62c6373-df906ec9-e8b0-44ed-82b2-e0b057d938e5/stored-data-comparison.json). The files include complete redacted Gateway logs, install/build output, harness sources, and Gateway-returned card snapshots from the same VM run.

- Completion/lifecycle: [settled card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/dc47f92f37caeb75dc73439598c0d3549203723c/evidence/2026/11/pr-198706-62c6373-df906ec9-e8b0-44ed-82b2-e0b057d938e5/snapshots/fresh-lifecycle.json) → [completed card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/dc47f92f37caeb75dc73439598c0d3549203723c/evidence/2026/11/pr-198706-62c6373-df906ec9-e8b0-44ed-82b2-e0b057d938e5/snapshots/fresh-completed.json).
- Verification persistence: [later write / before restart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/dc47f92f37caeb75dc73439598c0d3549203723c/evidence/2026/11/pr-198706-62c6373-df906ec9-e8b0-44ed-82b2-e0b057d938e5/snapshots/fresh-verified-after-write.json) → [after restart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/dc47f92f37caeb75dc73439598c0d3549203723c/evidence/2026/11/pr-198706-62c6373-df906ec9-e8b0-44ed-82b2-e0b057d938e5/snapshots/fresh-after-restart.json).
- Stable-upgrade stored data: [stable before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/dc47f92f37caeb75dc73439598c0d3549203723c/evidence/2026/11/pr-198706-62c6373-df906ec9-e8b0-44ed-82b2-e0b057d938e5/snapshots/stable-before-upgrade.json) → [PR after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/dc47f92f37caeb75dc73439598c0d3549203723c/evidence/2026/11/pr-198706-62c6373-df906ec9-e8b0-44ed-82b2-e0b057d938e5/snapshots/upgrade-verified-after-write.json) → [after restart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/dc47f92f37caeb75dc73439598c0d3549203723c/evidence/2026/11/pr-198706-62c6373-df906ec9-e8b0-44ed-82b2-e0b057d938e5/snapshots/upgrade-after-restart.json). Existing attempts, proof, and artifacts are identical; the PR snapshot includes a new verdict and comment.
- Main-format stored data: [before first write](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/dc47f92f37caeb75dc73439598c0d3549203723c/evidence/2026/11/pr-198706-62c6373-df906ec9-e8b0-44ed-82b2-e0b057d938e5/snapshots/legacy-read-before-write.json) → [first-write conversion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/dc47f92f37caeb75dc73439598c0d3549203723c/evidence/2026/11/pr-198706-62c6373-df906ec9-e8b0-44ed-82b2-e0b057d938e5/snapshots/legacy-first-write.json) → [after restart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/dc47f92f37caeb75dc73439598c0d3549203723c/evidence/2026/11/pr-198706-62c6373-df906ec9-e8b0-44ed-82b2-e0b057d938e5/snapshots/legacy-after-restart.json). The same attempt is settled, the checker verdict is retained without `kind`/`claimId`, and all twelve artifacts remain unchanged.

- `extensions/workboard/src/store-verification.test.ts`:
  - New regression, starting from a main-format card (claim, observation, and verification under `automation.evidence`) seeded through the SQLite store: a manual move to `done` on a nearly full card keeps the settled attempt and all twelve artifacts, carries the verdict into `verifications`, and removes `evidence`; a `{}` metadata patch carries the verdict too. It fails on e395c89b1d1 (the move evicts an artifact to keep the old evidence) and passes on this head.
  - Existing test: a forged verification in raw metadata is stripped on create; a verification too large for a nearly full card is refused; an accepted one survives a later comment, a lifecycle-settled run, and a manual move to `done`; a checker that is the card's own agent gets `checkedOwnWork: true`.

prs.body:
Related: #200929

> **CI note (14:47 UTC):** the only red check on head `27cdbb76` is `android-access-native (16384, google_apis_ps16k)`, which failed in `:app:connectedPlayDebugAndroidTest` because Gradle could not download `com.android.tools.utp` test-runner artifacts from `dl.google.com` ("Resource missing"). I'm not bypassing it: the branch will pick up `main` once the New Session red-main fix (#201268) lands, and that fresh head gets a clean Android run before merge. cc @vyctorbrzezowski

## What Problem This Solves

Chat and New Session both download the code that turns Markdown into plain text for live sidebar previews. Its link scanner kept three separate maps to decide which markup to remove, and both routes are already over their startup JavaScript budgets.

## User Impact

No visible change. Sidebar preview text, and when it appears, stay the same. Chat and New Session each download 321 fewer gzip bytes of JavaScript, with no added requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared plain-text flattener now records the link markup to skip in one map and applies the edits in source order. It keeps the preview's existing treatment of nested labels, escaped image markers, empty links and unfinished Markdown, without adding a dependency or deferring work. Swapping in micromark was ruled out: it treats empty links, nested links and unfinished fences differently from what the preview intentionally shows.

## Evidence

The paired performance comparison against `fb34e996e8e469035e3238734bba3afb1236eb19` passed: Chat and New Session boot JS each −321 B gzip, startup unchanged, request counts unchanged at 21, 17 and 3. A differential run matched the previous output across 49 owner-fixture calls, 1,310 transcript fixtures and streamed prefixes, and 100,000 generated inputs in flatten, label and omit modes. New committed cases cover composed linked images, escaped bangs, empty labels and nested image omission. 412 focused tests (shared scanner, sidebar roster and narration, Cron, server consumers), lint, formatting and the UI typecheck passed.

prs.title: fix(onboard): stop pointing Funnel runs at token auth
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw onboard --non-interactive --tailscale funnel` fails and tells the operator to rerun with `--gateway-auth token`. Following that advice fails the same way, because Funnel always switches the Gateway to password auth.

## User Impact

User impact: the Funnel rejection now names the password requirement instead of pointing at token auth, so the printed next step actually works.

## Why This Change Was Made

`applyNonInteractiveGatewayConfig` forces `authMode = "password"` whenever `tailscaleMode === "funnel"` (`src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/gateway-config.ts:80-89`), then rejects with `"Missing --gateway-password for password auth. Pass --gateway-password or use --gateway-auth token."` (`:145-148`). For a Funnel run that second sentence is unreachable advice. The rejection is now Funnel-aware and points at `--gateway-password` / `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD`.

Scope note: this changes the rejection text only. Funnel winning over an explicit token request is existing, tested behaviour (`keeps password auth when a token-only rerun targets an existing Funnel`), so this PR does not turn that override into an error. The other half of #201385 — the token being dropped without any notice — is left for a maintainer call, since any notice has to stay compatible with the one-JSON-object-per-run promise of `--json`.

## Evidence

New case in `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/gateway-config.test.ts` drives the real `applyNonInteractiveGatewayConfig` with an existing token-auth config plus `tailscale: "funnel"`, and asserts the rejection names the password requirement and no longer suggests `--gateway-auth token`.

Base (production change stashed, test present) — `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/test-projects.mts src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/gateway-config.test.ts`:

```
× points Funnel runs at the password instead of token auth
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ StringContaining{…} ]
Tests  1 failed | 28 passed (29)
```

With the fix:

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  29 passed (29)
```

Neighbouring suites: `src/commands/onboard.test.ts` 66 passed (the non-Funnel rejection string it asserts is unchanged); oxlint 0 warnings, 0 errors on both changed files.

Gap: no live `onboard --non-interactive --tailscale funnel` run here; this host has an installed Gateway and no isolated Tailscale Funnel, so the CLI path is covered at the config-resolution boundary the rejection lives in.

## AI Assistance

Written with AI assistance (DeepSeek Harness agent); the reproduction, tests, and command output above were run on this machine.

---

机制对位: 症状输出在 `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/gateway-config.ts:145-148`，我在同一处 `:145-155` 改，因为 `:80-89` 已把 funnel 的 authMode 强制成 password，旧文案仍在推荐 `--gateway-auth token`
复现: 新用例在 base 上 1 failed（断言 error 含 "Tailscale Funnel requires password auth"），修复后 29 passed
证据类别: 非交互 onboard 的 auth 解析（纯函数 + 已有测试桩），本机可得: 是
契约核对: `--tailscale funnel` 的密码要求由 `gateway-config.ts:80-89` 拥有；`--json` 单对象承诺由 `src/commands/onboard-options.ts:19-26` 的 `rejectOnboardingOption` 拥有 ⇒ 只改文案、不加 stderr 通知
风险: 2 文件（1 生产 + 1 测试）、不跨层、不涉状态机

prs.title: fix: recognize Portuguese requests to search earlier conversations
prs.body:
Closes #195855

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Active Memory misses explicit Portuguese requests to search or review earlier conversations, and questions using the past-tense spelling `combinámos`.

## User Impact

People using these phrasings can pass the existing recall-intent gate. Future instructions, greetings, generic fix requests, and searches of current documentation retain their negative classification. This does not force deep recall on every message or change contextual follow-up handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend two patterns in the existing Portuguese matcher. Conversation-search commands need an explicit match; `combinámos` distinguishes an unambiguous past agreement from the unaccented future-ambiguous form. The existing test tables gain seven positive controls and seven negative controls, with a separate allocation for their 14 lines.

This follows the Portuguese support in #135137; it does not replace that work or alter memory storage, authority, configuration, or diagnostic-prefix rendering.

## Evidence

[Current-head running-Gateway evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195859#issuecomment-6822774006) now supplements the unit regressions. Exact clean head `bd4b96093bcc70718b186e8f01b4459ba8b57df1` was built through the supported source CLI and exercised via persistent `chat.send`, `agent.wait` and stored history with default escalation. Both `Pesquisa nas nossas conversas o que ficou decidido` and `O que combinámos para amanhã?` produced the actual recall-model HTTP request before the terminal answer. A future reminder, current-documentation search and greeting produced only the answer request with the no-recall-intent outcome. All five reached terminal replies.

External inference was synthetic and returned `NONE` for recall. This proves routing through the running Gateway and production prompt hook, not retrieval quality, a memory-tool result or live-provider reasoning. Empty memory used keyword/FTS fallback because the embedding provider was not loaded. No daily runtime, credentials or production source was changed; task processes stopped and ports closed. No before-fix Gateway run is claimed; the RED evidence below is unit-level.

Tested against public `main` at `7ebc4f3e67137c34b0850dfa8cab2b8d68e6576d`, with the same final regression cases on both sides:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Base matcher with regression cases | Five intended false negatives fail; 175 tests pass |
| Patched escalation, prompt, and query owners | 180 tests pass across three files |

The native `run-vitest.mjs` owner command used `--maxWorkers=1`. The final baseline run took 40.74 seconds wall time; the cached passing run took 9.56 seconds. This is not a performance comparison. The tests make no live provider calls and do not establish model-driven deep-recall behavior.

Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, the test-line allocation ratchet, and the file-line cap passed. Independent review approved the production change; one redundant negative case was removed, retaining the explicit generic-request and greeting controls. The test allocation is exactly the 14 added lines.

Validated commit: `bd4b96093bcc70718b186e8f01b4459ba8b57df1`. No tracked dependencies or generated files changed.

prs.title: fix(android): stop Listen playback when remote deletion retires selected chat
prs.body:
Fixes #195826

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android Listen speech can continue, or start after synthesis finishes, when another client deletes the selected chat and Android falls back to the main conversation.

## User Impact

Pending or active Listen speech stops when its conversation is retired; deleting an unrelated conversation leaves Listen uninterrupted. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Connect the existing chat-selection generation to the existing speech controller’s stop operation. Subscribe during controller initialization so an immediate selection change cannot be mistaken for the initial value.

The supplied patch adds five production lines and two regression cases covering pending synthesis and active playback, including unrelated deletion and starting Listen again afterward.

## Evidence

- Supplied local-coordinator evidence for source commit [8c920dae1d83685b61498170d290f6be7ff43800](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/commit/8c920dae1d83685b61498170d290f6be7ff43800): Base-RED → Fix-GREEN, passing `:app:ktlintCheck` and `:app:assemblePlayDebug`, and physical Google Pixel 10 Pro XL verification. These checks were not rerun on the cloud host.

prs.title: fix: keep shell setup instructions visible after installation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a successful shell install, the terminal that launched it may still lack npm's bin directory on PATH. The installer prints a repair early, then buries it beneath Doctor or verification output and ends with an unconditional success message.

## User Impact

The final summary now says **“Installed; one shell setup step remains”** when the original shell needs PATH setup, followed by the existing shell-specific repair command. Immediate onboarding instructions continue to use the verified, quoted executable path, so users can run the CLI before repairing PATH.

Already-correct PATH keeps the normal success summary. No new settings, profile writes, migration, install-method change, or Gateway lifecycle change is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installer is a child process and cannot change the parent shell's environment. This moves the existing PATH guidance into the final summary after successful Doctor/verification, reusing the original-PATH detector and shell-aware renderer rather than adding another repair mechanism. Fatal checks still return before success.

The quoting issue addressed by #187612 is already represented in this base and is not reimplemented here. #200381 and #201043 concern separate build/onboarding behavior.

## Evidence

- **Red → green:** the real assembled installer installed public stable OpenClaw 2026.11.5 under an isolated HOME/npm prefix containing spaces. On the base, installation exited 0 and declared success while the original shell's bare command exited 127; the final-summary assertion failed. With the change, the same original shell consumed the actual emitted immediate command and PATH repair, then reached both onboarding help and CLI help.
- **Native shell coverage:** Bash 5.2, zsh 5.9, and Fish 3.6 passed that original-shell handoff. An already-correct Bash PATH control retained normal success and a working bare command. No real user state, services, or shell startup files were changed.
- **Focused regression:** a main-entrypoint table covers missing/correct original PATH, fresh setup, and configured Doctor completion, then executes emitted commands with space-containing paths. It fails on the base for the intended missing final handoff and passes on the candidate.
- **Owning suites:** 240 passed, 1 existing Darwin-only availability skip across the installer and standalone-assembly suites; 13.16 seconds runner wall time, approximately 11.9 seconds aggregate test time. After moving readiness calculation beside the summary, all 12 affected lifecycle/handoff cases passed again in 2.09 seconds runner wall time, and the real Bash installer replay passed again in 10.05 seconds. The [exact-head CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44374440877/job/135056389704) passed; aggregate CI seconds are not recorded here.
- **Checks:** standalone installer build, Bash syntax, targeted lint, script-test typecheck, formatting, MDX validation, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- **Review:** simplify pass complete. Local Auto Review was started for the complete local delta, P0–P3, but produced no report and was cancelled after stalling; it is **incomplete**, not a clean review. The [initial hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201383#issuecomment-6988768423) found no actionable code defects and requested inspectable terminal evidence; the retained output is included below. Evidence re-review is pending.

Limitations: no native macOS Bash 3.2 run or real Git-method installation; the unchanged quoting renderer and existing Git lifecycle tests remain the coverage for those paths. ShellCheck is unavailable. The real installation used compatible Node 24.20.0 with SQLite 3.53.4 and retained the existing security-patch recommendation. This is terminal-output behavior, not a web/native visual change.

### Inspectable terminal handoff evidence

These excerpts come from the retained real assembled-installer runs, not the synthetic unit fixture. Paths shown below are task-owned test homes; no user data or credentials are included. Omitted package-manager and long CLI-help lines do not change the recorded order.

**Before — base installer, isolated writable npm prefix absent from the original Bash PATH:**

```text
[3/3] Finalizing setup

! PATH missing npm global bin dir: /workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/baseline home/npm prefix/bin
  This directory was not on PATH when the installer started.
  For this shell, run:
    export PATH='/workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/baseline home/npm prefix/bin':"$PATH"; hash -r
  For future shells, check your shell startup file.

🦞 OpenClaw installed successfully (2026.11.5)!
I'm in. Let's cause some responsible chaos.

· Skipping onboard (requested); run /workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/baseline\ home/npm\ prefix/bin/openclaw onboard later

FAQ: https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/faq
Support: https://community.openclaw.ai/
INSTALLER_EXIT=0
/bin/bash: line 6: openclaw: command not found
ORIGINAL_SHELL_BARE_EXIT=127
```

**After — exact candidate installer bytes, real public OpenClaw 2026.11.5:**

```text
[3/3] Finalizing setup

! Installed; one shell setup step remains (2026.11.5)
  A piped installer cannot change its parent shell environment.

! PATH missing npm global bin dir: /workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/final-bash home/npm prefix/bin
  This directory was not on PATH when the installer started.
  For this shell, run:
    export PATH='/workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/final-bash home/npm prefix/bin':"$PATH"; hash -r
  For future shells, check your shell startup file.
· Skipping onboard (requested); run /workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/final-bash\ home/npm\ prefix/bin/openclaw onboard later

FAQ: https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/faq
Support: https://community.openclaw.ai/
```

The same parent Bash process launched the assembled installer through a pipe, then read these commands directly from its final output. The onboarding command was run **before** PATH repair (with `--help` to avoid configuration writes), followed by the repair, `command -v openclaw`, and `openclaw --help`. Its negative control required bare `openclaw` to remain absent before repair.

Actual extracted command files:
```sh
/workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/final-bash\ home/npm\ prefix/bin/openclaw onboard --help
export PATH='/workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/final-bash home/npm prefix/bin':"$PATH"; hash -r
```

Selected lines from that original parent process, in recorded order:
```text
OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15) — All your chats, one OpenClaw.
Usage: openclaw onboard [options] [command]
/workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/final-bash home/npm prefix/bin/openclaw
OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15) — All your chats, one OpenClaw.
Usage: openclaw [options] [command]
```

The final parent process exited **0**, with empty stderr, in **10.045 seconds**. Bash’s `set -eu` and `pipefail` made failed installation, immediate handoff, repair, or CLI help fail the proof. The initial PATH was `/usr/bin:/bin`; HOME, OPENCLAW_HOME, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, npm prefix, and npm cache were isolated. The real installer invocation was:

```sh
cat "$INSTALLER" | /bin/bash -s -- --install-method npm --version 2026.11.5 --no-prompt --no-onboard
```

The retained sibling receipts show the same output-driven replay succeeded in native zsh 5.9 (**10.674s**) and Fish 3.6 (**8.845s**). The already-correct Bash PATH control passed in **8.588s**, printed ordinary success and a bare onboarding command. No source change or CI rerun was made for this evidence addition.

<details>
<summary>Scope and reproducible checks</summary>

Base: `bde2e84084bffa49cad046351f7ddd739d26d9ea`. The installer and shared policy were byte-identical to live main `7ce2d10eced5f379e31a0b01a96fbcbf9741ccbe` when reproduced.

```sh
node scripts/build-installers.mjs
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts test/scripts/standalone-installers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'keeps the final shell handoff actionable|required installer lifecycle'
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.json test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json --incremental
node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/install/installer.md
bash -n scripts/install.sh dist/installers/install.sh
git diff --check
```

Simplification removed the pre-Doctor warning site and reused the existing renderer; no new helper or persistent state. Net production change: +7 shell lines; regression coverage: +108 lines; documentation: +1 line.

</details>

Reported and scoped with @etzelm (Mitchell Etzel).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ba8717b3-cf77-4a25-bcd9-79ff4fd42b6b)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b1948aba-a69b-404a-8115-67168b642128)

prs.title: fix(discord): show busy notices on session initialization conflicts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord messages could be silently lost after reply-session initialization exhausted its conflict retries. The ingress spool repeatedly retried the message, but the user never received the intended busy notice. A quiet session could also remain stuck in this state after equivalent nested metadata was written with a different object key order.

## User Impact

Discord users now receive one visible busy notice, or an intentional suppression when delivery policy requires it. Equivalent nested session metadata no longer causes deterministic initialization conflicts. Failed notice delivery remains retryable; retry counts, backoff, and ingress crash durability are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core's error constructor in `src/auto-reply/reply/session-init-conflict-retry.ts:12` gained the `; please retry your message.` suffix in #165502. Discord's private matcher, introduced by #103562 at `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.retry.ts:3` on the base, still recognized only the old text. Core now exports its existing classifier through the documented `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime` surface, and Discord uses that owner. No other channel plugin had a production copy of this matcher. Existing ingress settlement already completes a successfully delivered or intentionally suppressed notice, so no spool policy change is needed.

The nested-order hypothesis also reproduced through the real local store and reply initializer. `src/config/sessions/session-actor-receipt.ts:53` omits structurally equivalent nested objects from replica deltas, retaining the resident object's older key order when restoring the receipt at line 100. The row can contain the same object in a new key order. The former per-field `JSON.stringify` comparison in `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-entry-equality.ts:30` then rejected every CAS on a quiet session. Equality now compares differing serialized JSON structurally at that single owner, preserving JSON omission semantics and array ordering.

## Evidence

The Discord handler regression uses a core-constructed conflict error. It fails with the base private matcher and passes with the shared classifier: one busy notice or recorded suppression, no propagated conflict after terminal completion, and failed notice delivery still propagates. The test harness now uses the real core retry helper rather than another private matcher.

A synthetic rich session fixture reproduced repeated conflicts during quiet reply initialization with both nested key-order variants. Ordinary same-order writes passed. The committed real-store snapshot/commit regression extends the existing durable/memory test with reordered model metadata immediately before initialization commit; it is red with base equality and green with the fix. This establishes a reproducible defect, without claiming which production metadata field triggered an individual incident.

Focused Discord handler, draft/final delivery, ingress recovery, session accessor, reply selection, core retry, and SDK contract tests passed. Targeted core/Discord typechecks, lint, format, SDK export checks, API comparison, build, and the test-line ratchet passed. Net test-line delta: **0**. The build emitted unrelated existing UI size-budget warnings but exited successfully. No server or live channel was accessed; all runtime proof used isolated local state. The API comparison reports exactly one additive production export, `isReplySessionInitConflictError` on `reply-runtime` (acknowledgement `48d84944`), with no removals. PR CI supplies broad proof.

The change was simplified: both private matchers (production and test harness) are removed, and the retry helper coverage is consolidated without changing production retry policy. Necessary production growth is confined to the shared export and structural JSON comparison. Codex autoreview through P2 found no actionable findings on the final change snapshot based on `0d2cd559284f55b339021db405f24c1bf3012877`, committed as `fce78ec973c44331ad7f07adc00804e2306b8470`.
