prs.title: fix: recognize image input for GPT-6.2 models routed through ClawRouter
prs.body:
Related: #200766

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw leaves prompt images out of requests to GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra through ClawRouter when the router catalog omits input types for both the model and its selected endpoint. The fallback already recognizes image input for `gpt-6.1-sol`.

## User Impact

User impact: OpenClaw can include prompt images in requests to GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra through ClawRouter when the catalog leaves input types unspecified. Input declarations on the model row or selected endpoint still take precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

#200766 added both GPT-6.2 models to the OpenAI catalog. ClawRouter's exact-ID fallback already included `gpt-6.1-sol` and was missing both new IDs. This change adds them and extends the existing fallback test. The ClawRouter test in #200766 supplies `input` in its mock row and bypasses the fallback.

## Evidence

Checked on macOS 15.7.9 (arm64), Node 24.22.2.

- With only the test change applied to the branch's base commit, the fallback test (`retains known native image inputs without granting unknown OpenAI models`) fails because both GPT-6.2 rows come back as `["text"]`.
- With the fix, that test passes, and `extensions/clawrouter/provider-catalog.test.ts` plus `extensions/clawrouter/gpt-62-compat.test.ts` pass together (10 tests, 47 seconds locally).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passes, and `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on the two touched files. The extension test typecheck (`pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`) did not finish locally.
- The original contributor tests did not run a live ClawRouter turn. The fallback test verifies catalog classification, and the compatibility tests check request construction with mocked network calls. The image-loading guard in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/images.ts` skips prompt images when the model lacks image input.

<details>
<summary>Failing output before the fix</summary>

```
$ pnpm test extensions/clawrouter/provider-catalog.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "retains known native image inputs"

 FAIL  |extensions| extensions/clawrouter/provider-catalog.test.ts > ClawRouter provider catalog > retains known native image inputs without granting unknown OpenAI models

    "openai/gpt-6.2-astra": [
      "text",
-     "image",
    ],
    "openai/gpt-6.2-sol": [
      "text",
-     "image",
    ],

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 7 skipped (8)
```

</details>

### Maintainer verification: real GPT-6.2 image inference

On November 18, 2026, an isolated OpenClaw Gateway ran source `f30a86c40da29cd2b4d0b601414820bc597a0d41` (macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1). To reproduce, supply a local discovery fixture with GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra model rows and selected Responses endpoints that both omit `input`. Disable tools and alternate image understanding. Start a fresh `chat.send` turn with a synthetic PNG containing a code absent from the prompt text. Record the number of `input_image` blocks on the serialized Responses request and forward that request body unchanged to ClawRouter production. For the pre-fix control, substitute only the exact base `provider-catalog.ts` blob.

| Routed model | Pre-fix control | Exact PR head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openai/gpt-6.2-sol` | HTTP 200; 0 `input_image` blocks; did not recover the code | HTTP 200; image included; returned `6CD29BB9` exactly |
| `openai/gpt-6.2-astra` | HTTP 200; 0 `input_image` blocks; returned `NO_IMAGE` | HTTP 200; image included; returned `D4275EA1` exactly |

Each candidate request contained two byte-identical copies of its single uploaded PNG, verified by SHA-256. The Sol control did not use the literal `NO_IMAGE`, so the control harness exited nonzero; its wire capture still established that the image was omitted and the code was not recovered. Only catalog discovery was simulated: image upload, hydration, Responses serialization, and model inference were real. This does not establish rollout of the production discovery catalog.

Focused Vitest: 10 passed across `provider-catalog.test.ts` and `gpt-62-compat.test.ts`; formatting, lint, and `git diff --check` passed. [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44206532316) (20 jobs passed, 32 skipped); [exact-head security review passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44374135341/job/135048793953).

## What Problem This Solves

With no model connected, Chat could show an unconfigured default as selected and let users send a message that ended in a misleading authentication error.

## User Impact

Chat guides users to model setup and preserves their unsent draft instead of sending a request that cannot succeed.

## Why This Change Was Made

A default model name does not mean a model is usable. Setup detection now uses completed catalog and account information. Configured models with authentication errors or cooldowns, and catalogs still loading, retain their existing behavior rather than being mistaken for an unconfigured installation.

prs.title: docs: distinguish setup commands from configuration examples
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Discord guild setup and common model configuration recipes show JSON5 fragments without consistently saying where to put them or what existing settings to retain. Someone following setup can mistake a configuration example for a terminal command or replace more of their config than intended.

## User Impact

User impact: readers can distinguish terminal commands from configuration examples, find the active configuration file, and apply a fragment without discarding unrelated settings. This is documentation-only: no runtime, permission, schema, or default changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Label the relevant examples in three existing setup/configuration pages instead of introducing another setup guide. Distinguish a minimal complete file for a new setup from fragments for an existing config, retain guild users and other settings, and provide existing single-path CLI commands for changing mention gating or the primary model. Explain that a chosen fallback array replaces the existing list.

## Evidence

The two newly documented `config set` commands were executed through the real source CLI against isolated synthetic configuration. Changing Discord `requireMention` retained the guild's users/channel map and another guild; changing the primary model retained configured fallbacks, aliases, timezone, and Gateway settings. The resulting configuration passed `config validate`. No live Gateway, Discord connection, credential, or model request was used as proof.

- All three unmodified source pages were byte-identical to current main `7ce2d10eced5f379e31a0b01a96fbcbf9741ccbe` during investigation. The ambiguity is present in current source, not inferred only from historical reports.
- `pnpm docs:list` completed. The repository-wide configuration-example check validated 1,411 examples with no findings.
- Changed-page MDX and formatting checks passed; the internal-link audit checked 16,755 links with zero broken links. `git diff --check` passed.
- `pnpm openclaw config file` completed the source runtime build, then returned the isolated active path. The two documented mutations and `config validate` passed through the same CLI.
- Author simplification kept the change to three docs pages and existing config operations: no new command, configuration owner, test scaffolding, or support-agent rules.
- **Review gap:** local Auto Review of the complete candidate against `bde2e84084bffa49cad046351f7ddd739d26d9ea` was requested at P0–P2, but produced no terminal report after more than an hour and was cancelled. It is incomplete, not a clean review. The subsequent wording clarification names the exact keys to merge. [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201380#issuecomment-6988633105) of head `60b22aeee16a3d0df2166614ae9f098fc40b58f0` is complete: **Ready for maintainer review**, overall **Platinum Hermit 4/6**, proof **Platinum Hermit 4/6**, and quality **Diamond Lobster 5/6**, with no findings or before-merge actions. The exact-head [`openclaw/ci-gate`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44373489163/job/135049174596) passed, including the selected documentation checks.
- Rendered website screenshots and live channel/model operation were not tested; this patch changes documentation directions, not UI or runtime behavior.

Requested by Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm).

prs.title: fix: deliver scheduled reports to unchanged Discord threads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A scheduled audit can finish its report but refuse to post it to the Discord thread it was set up to use. The failure notification can then send the person who requested the audit to a Control UI administrator unnecessarily.

## User Impact

Scheduled reports can post to the same Discord thread whether or not session history repeats the thread ID. If a retry really needs a fresh owner message, the tool now tells the agent that a configured channel owner can reply in chat. No new permissions, dashboard setup, or replacement job are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord addresses a thread by its own channel ID. The scheduler rechecks the destination just before sending; it previously treated an extra copy of that same ID as a change of destination. It now accepts the two forms only when the transport confirms they address the same place. A different recipient, account, channel, or thread still stops delivery. The separate administrator-only policy is unchanged.

## Evidence

The queued-send test reproduced the original “delivery policy or route changed while queued” error on unpatched code. After the change, both forms of the same Discord destination pass. The tests still reject sibling threads, a parent versus a child, DMs with matching numeric IDs, different accounts or channels, disabled delivery, and transports without an equivalence rule. Verified with the real Discord adapter and a local scheduler fixture, not a live message to a production thread.

The scheduled-turn, delivery-target, Discord adapter, and automation management test suites passed, along with the core type check, changed-file lint and formatting, and generated prompt-snapshot check. Local autoreview reported no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Reported and co-authored by @VACInc.

## What Problem This Solves

The New session button in the sidebar header looks exactly like the filter and collapse buttons next to it. All three are faint ghost icons, so the most common action in the header is easy to miss. It also sits between filter and collapse instead of at the edge.

User impact: New session is now the last button in the Sessions header. It has a hairline outline and full-strength icon color, so it stands out without an accent color. The collapse toggle moves to the start of the button group, in the order collapse, filter, New session.

The People and Automations headers follow the same order: collapse, then the panel's filter. Because the collapse toggle now comes before each panel's actions, its position changes slightly between panels that have different numbers of actions.

The shared sidebar panel header now places each panel's actions after the collapse toggle, so the panel's own actions hold the trailing edge. The header title or owner picker takes the free space, which keeps the collapse toggle next to the actions. Before this change, the filter button's own auto margin created that space. prs.title: fix: tell a client waiting for pairing to approve it on the Gateway host
prs.body:
Related: #200904

## What Problem This Solves

A new client that is not paired yet, such as a CLI or TUI connecting to a Gateway on another machine, gets "device pairing required". The hint then says to run `openclaw devices approve --latest` and to pass the same `--url` and `--token/--password` flags. Run from that client, the command fails with the same "device pairing required" error, so a new user following the hint gets stuck.

## User Impact

The hint now says to approve the request from the Gateway host, or in the Gateway's Control UI (Settings -> Devices). Both work before the client is paired.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approve command reaches the Gateway as the same unpaired device, so the Gateway rejects it the same way. Only the Gateway host CLI or an already trusted Control UI session can approve it. The shared remediation text, shown by the TUI and the session commands, now names those paths. It keeps the note about `--url` and `--token/--password` for a host CLI that needs them. The wording matches the hint the TUI already prints for stored device auth.

## Evidence

Real CLI and TUI run against a fresh Gateway (bind lan, token auth, default pairing policy) and a second fresh state dir acting as a remote client (`gateway.mode: remote`, LAN URL plus the token). On the base, the TUI prints the old hint, and following it on the client fails with "device pairing required". On the head, the TUI names the Gateway host and the Control UI. On both, approving on the Gateway host works and the client connects.

- Regression test: the pairing-required rows in `connect-error-details.test.ts` assert the new wording. 2 failed with the source change reverted (`git apply -R`), 27 passed with it.
- Consumer tests: TUI, gateway chat, session target, session ref, daemon probe, restart health probe, gateway probe all pass.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed (lanes core, coreTests).
- Local ClawSweeper review of the committed range: complete, no defects found, patch rated A.

### Runtime output

Base `f3638439b92`, head `58a69057562`. Same script on both: Gateway in one fresh state dir, client in another, macOS arm64. Request IDs, the LAN address and the token are redacted.

The TUI runs under a pseudo-terminal for 25 seconds. The script keeps only screen lines that match pairing, approve, devices or gateway, so wrapped lines outside that filter show as `[...]`. Line order is restored; no line is reworded.

Base, client:

```
[cl] $ openclaw tui --session main
 gateway disconnected: device pairing required (requestId:
 <id>) | device approval needed: preview latest
 Run `openclaw devices approve --latest` to preview the pending request, then
 rerun the printed `openclaw devices approve <requestId>` command and reconnect
 [...]

[cl] $ openclaw devices approve --latest
gateway connect failed: GatewayClientRequestError: device pairing required (requestId: <id>)
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: device pairing required (requestId: <id>)
(exit 1)
```

Head, client:

```
[cl] $ openclaw tui --session main
 gateway disconnected: device pairing required (requestId:
 <id>) | device approval needed: preview latest
 Approve this request from the Gateway host: run `openclaw devices approve
 [...]
 devices approve <requestId>` command (add --url and --token/--password if that
 CLI needs them to reach the Gateway), or approve it in the Gateway's Control
 UI (Settings -> Devices). Then reconnect.
```

Head, following the hint on the Gateway host, then the client:

```
[gw] $ openclaw devices approve <id>
Approved <deviceId> (<id>)
(exit 0)

[cl] $ openclaw health
Gateway event loop: ok max=1ms p99=0ms util=0.006 cpu=0.009
Gateway check duration: 1ms
Agents: main (default)
Heartbeat interval: disabled (main)
```

prs.title: fix(path): read and edit Markdown with carriage-return line endings
prs.body:
Root cause: `extensions/oc-path/src/oc-path/parse.ts:48` splits Markdown only on LF and CRLF, and the editor's offsets and line counts (`source.ts:4`, `emit.ts:13`) count only LF, so in a file that uses a lone CR as its line break, frontmatter is never found, items cannot be addressed, and edits land on the wrong line.

Fixes #200757

Thanks @LinzeShi for the report, the fix and the regression matrix.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw path resolve` and `openclaw path set` fail on Markdown files whose lines end in a lone carriage return (CR). Frontmatter reads return `resolved: false`, bullet edits return `unresolved`, and inserts write LF lines into a CR file. The same file works with LF or CRLF endings.

## User Impact

Users can read and edit CR-delimited Markdown with `openclaw path`. Line endings and untouched bytes stay as they were, including in files that mix CR, LF and CRLF.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Markdown reader, source offsets, line-ending choice and edit splicing now all treat CR, LF and CRLF as line breaks. JSONL keeps LF record boundaries.

When an edit puts a CR directly before an existing LF (or an LF directly after an existing CR), the two bytes would read as one CRLF break. The edit owner (`replaceMdSource`) now keeps the edited text's edge breaks apart from neighboring source breaks on both sides. Before, only the left side was handled, and only for section inserts. Adding frontmatter to a CR file that starts with a blank LF line dropped that blank line, and a follow-up edit on the returned document wrote into the next section.

## Evidence

Bytes are shown with `<CR>` and `<LF>` for the line-break characters.

Built CLI (`node openclaw.mjs path ... --json --file <f>`, isolated home, state and config, `oc-path` enabled), run twice on each side with identical results. Bytes are JSON-escaped.

Base `1d82bed0a7fe` (merge base):
- `cr.md` `"---<CR>name: old<CR>---<CR>## Settings<CR>- name: before<CR>## Other<CR>- keep: untouched<CR>"`: resolve exits 1 `{"resolved":false}`; set exits 1 `{"ok":false,"reason":"unresolved"}`; file unchanged. LF and CRLF controls pass.
- `"<LF>## Intro<CR>- name: first<CR>## End<CR>- name: second<CR>"`: adding `[frontmatter]/+added` writes LF lines into the CR file (`"---<LF>added: x<LF>---<LF><LF>## Intro<CR>..."`); then `intro/name/name` exits 1 `unresolved`.

Previous PR head `c47277d99632`, same file: adding frontmatter gives `"---<CR>added: x<CR>---<CR><LF>## Intro<CR>..."`. The leading blank line is lost.

This head: the `cr.md` resolve returns `old`, and the set writes `"---<CR>name: old<CR>---<CR>## Settings<CR>- name: after<CR>## Other<CR>- keep: untouched<CR>"`. The second file becomes `"---<CR>added: x<CR>---<CR><LF><LF>## Intro<CR>- name: changed<CR>## End<CR>- name: second<CR>"`. LF and CRLF controls are byte-identical to base.

Tests: on the merge base, 8 of the new edit cases fail (two runs). On this head, `extensions/oc-path` passes 33 files and 510 tests (two runs). The new case `keeps an inserted trailing CR apart from a following LF` fails on `c47277d99632`: the follow-up edit changes `End`'s `second` instead of `Intro`'s `first`.

Merge danger: two-way door. A revert fully undoes it; nothing is stored or migrated. Blast radius: `openclaw path` edits to Markdown files with the optional `oc-path` plugin.

prs.title: fix: keep the Automations sidebar list after returning to a background tab
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

If a tab with the Automations sidebar open sits in the background for a while, coming back to it shows a red "Cron inventory is no longer presented" error with a Retry button and no automations. The list only returns a few seconds later, when the next automation event happens to arrive.

## User Impact

User impact: the Automations sidebar keeps showing its automations when you return to a background tab, and refreshes them on return instead of showing an error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared cron inventory deliberately refuses network reads for a hidden tab and rejects them as an abort. The sidebar kept reading on every cron event or reconnect while hidden, and showed that abort as a failure, replacing its rows with the error. Nothing read again on return, so the error stayed until the next cron event.

The sidebar now follows the tab's visibility: it skips reads while hidden and keeps the rows it showed, treats an abandoned read as "keep what is shown" rather than an error, and reads again as soon as the tab is visible. Real read failures still show the error and Retry.

## Evidence

- New sidebar test: with rows loaded, a read in flight when the tab hides is abandoned the way the inventory does it in production, and a cron event arrives while hidden. On current `main` the test fails (the sidebar reads while hidden and loses its rows); on this branch the rows stay, no error appears, and a fresh read runs when the tab becomes visible.
- The existing sidebar tests still pass, including the one that keeps a real failure reachable with Retry.
- UI typecheck, lint, formatting, and the Control UI controller guard pass for the changed files.

<!-- maintainer-automations-visibility-proof -->
### Returning to a hidden tab

Independent replay in the production Control UI bundle, Chromium, with a simulated Gateway and controlled document-visibility changes. The base (`0aafe6691b8`) replaces the three loaded automations with an error and Retry; the PR keeps them and reads again after return, showing the fourth automation without needing a second event.

| Exact base | Current PR |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the sidebar list is lost and an error offers Retry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f806b9c5-df73-450a-a36c-88af66cf5dcc) | ![After: the sidebar shows the original and newly loaded automations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c17546fd-a11f-49fe-b535-817be2bd3d72) |
| ![Before: the error in the full Automations screen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af72c857-f229-4807-b01a-196188d00b70) | ![After: the populated sidebar in the full Automations screen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef7049fd-80e8-4b50-bd76-69f279008da6) |

The focused three-case suite also passed on this head, including the Retry action for a genuine read failure; its visibility scenario failed on the base because it still attempted hidden reads. Independent review found no actionable issues.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix(setup): show why automatic setup could not activate a model
prs.body:
Related: #200923

## What Problem This Solves

Automatic AI setup can ask you to sign in with ChatGPT when an already-detected local model failed for a different reason. The sign-in screen also hides the failed attempts, so the local server problem is easy to miss.

## User Impact

When an attempted connection fails for a non-credential reason, setup now says it could not connect and shows the recorded reason. ChatGPT sign-in remains available as an alternative. When only credentials are missing or expired, setup still asks you to sign in and now shows any recorded credential errors. Existing configured models and successful fallback selection are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The automatic setup owner already receives categorized activation failures. It now retains whether any failure was not authentication-related instead of treating an absent Codex login as the diagnosis for the whole run. This reuses the existing `unavailable`, `needs-sign-in`, `attempts`, and optional `signIn` fields; there is no schema, configuration, permission, or model-capacity policy change.

This is independent of #200923: no context-window floor from that unmerged PR is included. The current-main reproduction uses the existing local-provider HTTP error path.

## Evidence

- Reproduced before editing on current main `bde2e84084bffa49cad046351f7ddd739d26d9ea`: real isolated Gateway and `openclaw gateway call openclaw.setup.auto`, with a synthetic loopback llama-server. Discovery advertises a 32,768-token local model; the real completion request receives HTTP 503 `insufficient_memory`. Setup returns `needs-sign-in` despite a non-authentication attempt failure. No real account or model inference was used.
- New owner regressions fail on the base for the intended status mismatch (3 failed, 19 existing tests passed), then all 22 pass with the fix. They cover local capacity-shaped rejection, timeout, mixed credentials/capacity, and retain existing missing/expired credential behavior. Base wall time 48.02 s; patched wall time 43.01 s (mostly worker preparation). CI seconds not yet available.
- Browser E2E: **8/8 pass** in Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (25.05 s), covering visible non-auth and credential errors, actual recovery-button requests, successful alternatives, dismissal, and native/web recovery. Matching before/after screenshots render the real Control UI with the recorded real-Gateway RPC results (synthetic local-provider HTTP failure, not live model inference); both comparison assertions pass. Clean and annotated comparisons are shown below.
- Patched real-Gateway replay of the same HTTP 503 scenario returns `unavailable`, preserves the attempt reason, and retains optional ChatGPT sign-in. With the local fixture stopped and no native credentials, the same CLI still returns `needs-sign-in` with no failed attempts. Both CLI calls exit 0.
- Product build and `pnpm ui:build` pass. Focused setup-controller tests: 18/18 pass (5.00 s wall). Core, UI, Gateway-method test, and UI-E2E typechecks, changed-file formatting, scoped core/UI lint, controller/i18n guards, and `git diff --check` pass. The broad changed-check invocation was stopped after it expanded into unrelated test graphs; its earlier conflict-scan thread-resource failure passes on the bounded rerun.
- Independent review: bound Auto Review selected the complete local diff against the base plus controller/schema context (one 26,136-byte pass), but timed out without a report. No clean review is claimed from that timeout.

### Clean comparison

Before

![Before: local provider failure hidden behind ChatGPT sign-in](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d274fe01-8874-4ea8-93a6-d710f8ea5c10)

After

![After: local provider failure reason shown with optional ChatGPT sign-in](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9fa1c464-ced0-4180-b1aa-bf50d717f479)

### Annotated comparison

Before

![Before: sign-in-only diagnosis highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aea6a653-f6b5-4615-8fce-7aa1d071e03f)

After

prs.title: fix: keep the Slack question when someone who may not answer presses its button
prs.body:
Root cause: `extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/interactions.block-actions.ts:76` (`respondEphemeral`) posted `{ text, response_type: "ephemeral" }` to the interaction's `response_url` without `replace_original: false`, so Slack applied the reply to the source message and the denial took the place of the question for everyone in the thread.

Fixes #201348

## What Problem This Solves

In a Slack channel where some members may talk to the agent but are not allowed to press its buttons, one denied press on a question made the question disappear. Everyone in the thread then saw only "You are not authorized to use this control.", the buttons were gone, and the agent run stayed blocked until an operator found and answered the question another way.

## User Impact

A denied button press now shows the existing denial text only to the person who pressed. The question and its buttons stay in the thread, so people who are allowed to answer still can. Other private button feedback ("Answer submitted.", approval results) no longer replaces the message it belongs to either. Who is allowed to press is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Slack's `response_url` replaces the source message unless `replace_original` is literally `false`. Slack's guide for interactive messages says: "Responding immediately with a JSON message body will replace the current message in its entirety by default. If you explicitly indicate that you want to create a new message instead, specify a literal false in the replace_original field", and its error-feedback example is `{"response_type": "ephemeral", "replace_original": false, ...}` ([docs](https://docs.slack.dev/legacy/legacy-messaging/legacy-making-messages-interactive)). The thread section of [Handling user interaction](https://docs.slack.dev/interactivity/handling-user-interaction/#publishing-responses-in-thread) warns the same: "be sure to set `replace_original` to `false` or you'll overwrite the message you're wanting to respond to!".

`respondEphemeral` is the one helper all private block-action feedback goes through; messages that are meant to change are updated separately through `chat.update`. Setting the flag there fixes the denial and every other private reply in one place. The denial check and its text are untouched.

## Evidence

- Built Gateway (`node dist/entry.js gateway run`, isolated profile) with the bundled Slack plugin in Socket Mode against a local Slack API, Socket Mode and `response_url` fixture, with a deterministic model that calls `ask_user`. Config matches the report: `groupPolicy: allowlist`, channel with `requireMention`, `allowFrom` = the operator. The operator mentions the bot in a channel thread, the agent posts "Allow ChatGPT to use Spotlight?" with Allow/Decline buttons, a channel member who is not on `allowFrom` presses Allow, then the operator presses Decline.
  - main `7ce2d10eced5`: the Gateway logs the same drop line as the report (`reason=sender-not-allowlisted`); the denial is posted without `replace_original`; the question message now reads only "You are not authorized to use this control." with no buttons; the question stays pending and the run stays blocked.
  - this PR: the denial is posted with `replace_original: false` and reaches only the member; the question and both buttons stay; the operator's press then answers it, the message shows "Answered: Decline", and the run resumes with that answer.
  - control on main without the denied press: the operator's press resolves the question, but the "Answer submitted." reply then overwrites the finalized question in the same way.
  - Observed proof lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201371#issuecomment-6987522374
- The fixture applies Slack's documented `response_url` rules above; a real Slack click needs a human Slack client, so the overwrite itself comes from Slack's docs and the reporter's API readback, not from a live click here.
- `extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/interactions.test.ts`: the private-reply assertion now requires `replace_original: false`; with this test, main fails 16 cases (including the denied block action and the typed question button) and this branch passes 59 of 59.

Thanks @shannon0430 for the detailed report and for pointing at the exact helper and Slack's guidance.

Merge danger: two-way door. One field added to Slack interaction replies; a revert restores the old payload. Blast radius: Slack block-action feedback only (denials, answer and approval acknowledgements); slash commands and message updates are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(state): Gateway startup defers healthy agents behind two slow schema readers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup can defer almost every agent when two agent databases need a slow schema reader, even when every other store has a valid clean-close seal and could be admitted right away.

## User Impact

On a fleet where one or two agent stores are slow to inspect, only those stores are deferred at startup. The other sealed agents are admitted before the listener binds, instead of waiting for background preparation. The reported Gateway deferred 465 of 470 sealed agents. Startup still never runs more than two schema reader processes, and private fallback snapshots stay inside the same two-copy cap. A store that cannot be deferred still holds the foreground, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

#195291 orders clean-closed stores first, which fixes the case where unsealed stores sit at the head of the list. On a boot where every store is sealed, that order changes nothing. Two slow readers can still fill both inspection slots past the 5 second startup wait, and the timer then defers every index that has not finished. The startup list also holds each agent database more than once (configured, agent, and persistent registered paths), so later copies of agents that were already inspected were deferred again.

Startup inspection was bounded to two concurrent readers so a large agent fleet does not multiply child processes. That same change, commit 63e7363c / #139878, accepted at most two private fallback snapshots, because each one is a temporary disk copy. Releasing a startup slot when a reader is slow lets sealed stores admit from the in-process cache, while snapshot preparation and cleanup stay inside the two-slot cap until each copy is removed. A third snapshot waits.

This change does four things:

- When the startup wait ends, a slot that is busy on a slow reader is released while that reader keeps running in the background. Its store is deferred as before.
- A store whose clean-close cache is valid is read without waiting on the busy reader process. A store that still needs a reader waits for the existing process instead of starting a third one.
- Later copies of a database already claimed by real path and agent id are skipped before dispatch, so the first copy keeps its place and its result.
- Fallback snapshot preparation and cleanup stay inside those two slots. A third store waits until a copy is removed.

Admission checks, `canDefer`, config, and public types are unchanged.

## Evidence

Shipped Gateway entry point (`openclaw gateway run`). Isolated Linux machine with Node 24.22.1. The fleet was 41 agents created with `openclaw agents add`, all with a valid clean-close seal, plus the default duplicate startup list (the baseline agent `main` cannot be deleted, so the fleet is 41 rather than 40). The two first-sorted stores, `aa-slow-1` and `aa-slow-2`, were made to miss the in-process cache by editing their sealed metadata version. Each build was started three times from the same fleet.

Compared SHAs:

- main: `c1cf9390ac356d96815dde3f6e10903602b149bd`
- this head: `6f31ca28fa29229ed2cb6d6d95cca4145d264e63`

On this machine's SSD, even a 2 GiB store finished schema inspection in about one second, so the 5 second startup wait did not expire. For these measured starts, a test-only 6 second delay was added at the start of the built schema-inspection worker's request handler, identically on both builds, to stand in for slow disk reads. That delay is not product code and was not committed.

| Build | Deferred agents (runs 1 / 2 / 3) | Who was deferred | `schemaProcessCount` | Readiness | `GET /healthz` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main | 41 / 41 / 41 | every agent, including a-fast and main | 2 / 2 / 2 | 11477 / 11309 / 11479 ms | 200 `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` |
| this change | 2 / 2 / 2 | only the two slow stores | 2 / 2 / 2 | 11619 / 11561 / 11618 ms | 200 `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` |

Readiness took about 11.5 seconds on every run because the slow readers were still in flight (`schemaInspectionCount=0` at the readiness line). The Gateway became ready, nothing wedged, and it served `/healthz` on loopback after bind.

Main run 1, readiness and a sample of the 41 deferral lines:

```text
[gateway] startup phase: cli.bootstrap.admission.database-readiness 11476.9ms ... agentCount=41 schemaProcessCount=2 schemaInspectionCount=0 schemaSnapshotCount=0 ...
[state/agent-admission] Agent aa-slow-1 has not completed startup inspection and preparation. Inspection and writable admission continue after the Gateway listener binds.
[state/agent-admission] Agent aa-slow-2 has not completed startup inspection and preparation. Inspection and writable admission continue after the Gateway listener binds.
[state/agent-admission] Agent agent-01 has not completed startup inspection and preparation. Inspection and writable admission continue after the Gateway listener binds.
... 38 more identical deferral lines, including a-fast and main (41 total)
```

This head, run 1, readiness and the complete deferral set:

```text
[gateway] startup phase: cli.bootstrap.admission.database-readiness 11618.6ms ... agentCount=41 schemaProcessCount=2 schemaInspectionCount=0 schemaSnapshotCount=0 ...
[state/agent-admission] Agent aa-slow-1 has not completed startup inspection and preparation. Inspection and writable admission continue after the Gateway listener binds.
[state/agent-admission] Agent aa-slow-2 has not completed startup inspection and preparation. Inspection and writable admission continue after the Gateway listener binds.
```

The live fleet produced no fallback snapshots (`schemaSnapshotCount=0` on every official start, and no snapshot staging files during startup). The two-copy snapshot cap is therefore covered by the new lifecycle regression test, `keeps fallback snapshot preparation and cleanup within two slots after startup release`, and not by the live run.

Other regression tests that fail on main:

- `defers only slow stores when later targets repeat an already inspected agent`: targets `[a, slow1, slow2, b, a2, b2]`. Main defers `slow1, slow2, b, a2, b2`; with this change, only `slow1, slow2`.
- `reads a clean-close cache while a schema reader child is still busy`: on main the second read throws `Agent schema inspection worker is busy`. With this change, it returns the cached inspection while the child is still running.

These also passed: the scheduler, schema-inspection worker, preflight, lifecycle, prestart, and startup tests, plus `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint, and oxfmt on the touched files. The new test lines are covered by an allocation under `config/test-lines-allocations/`.

### Startup compatibility (head `2ae086ac`, upstream `main` merged at `6d815d786f4`)

The test-only `pendingAgentDatabaseSnapshotSlots` export is removed. The fallback-snapshot cap test now observes the lifecycle instead: foreground settlement while two copies are open, a third copy starting only after one cleanup, and all four copies cleaning up with a peak of two. `src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.lifecycle.test.ts` and `openclaw-database-preflight-agent-scheduler.test.ts`: 17 passed. Core and test typecheck, oxlint, and oxfmt are clean on touched files.

Fresh install on the branch head (`OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (2ae086a)`), Linux:

```text
$ openclaw setup --baseline --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace --json
configStatus: created
$ openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --port 19041
[gateway] startup phase: cli.bootstrap.admission.database-readiness 329.4ms agentCount=1 schemaSnapshotCount=0 stateSealCount=1
[gateway] http server listening (18 plugins; 3.4s)
[gateway] ready
$ openclaw gateway call health --json
ok: true  defaultAgentId: main  modelRuntime.pendingAgents: []  plugins.errors: []  eventLoop.degraded: false
```

Upgrade from v2026.11.3 with settings and agent data kept. On `OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d)`: baseline setup, agents `scribe` and `reviewer` added, `main` identity set to "Atlas 🗺️", one labeled session with a user message created on each agent, then a clean SIGINT shutdown (three clean-close receipts written). Then the same state directory was started on the branch head:

```text
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (2ae086a)
$ openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --port 19031
[gateway] startup phase: cli.bootstrap.admission.database-readiness 686.9ms agentCount=3 schemaProcessCount=2 schemaInspectionCount=3 schemaSnapshotCount=0 stateIntegrityReason=no-proof
[gateway] http server listening (18 plugins; 2.9s)
[gateway] Agent reviewer resume deferred: agent database unavailable (agent-database-inspection-pending)
[gateway] Agent scribe resume deferred: agent database unavailable (agent-database-inspection-pending)
[gateway] Agent main resume deferred: agent database unavailable (agent-database-inspection-pending)
[state/agent-admission] agent database recovered after background inspection and preparation   (x3, within 3.2s)
$ openclaw gateway call health --json
ok: true  modelRuntime.pendingAgents: none  agents: main, scribe, reviewer
$ openclaw agents list --json
main Atlas 🗺️ · scribe · reviewer Reviewer 🔍 (workspaces unchanged)
$ openclaw sessions --all-agents --json
count: 3  main atlas-log · scribe stable-note · reviewer review-queue (same session ids as on 2026.11.3)
$ openclaw gateway call chat.history
main     "Atlas log from the stable install: three agents are configured."
reviewer "Reviewer queue from the stable install: check the map before publishing."
scribe   "Stable install note: Atlas keeps the map."
```

On the first start after the upgrade, the stores have no clean-close proof from the new version (`stateIntegrityReason=no-proof`), so the three agents are briefly deferred and recovered by background inspection. Config `meta.lastTouchedVersion` moved from 2026.11.3 to 2026.11.5. Identities, workspaces, session ids, labels, and messages were all kept. Model turns were not run because no model credential was configured.

Closes #195269

prs.title: fix(ci): prepare a warm snapshot before checking saved chat width
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The saved chat-width reload test can reload without an admitted warm boot record or a settled Details snapshot. It then tests an intentional cold Details entrance instead of a warm reload, producing changing first-frame composer widths.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. This repairs the browser fixture while keeping every original width assertion, including all 30 first-visible-frame samples. The New Session variant remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing trusted-proxy mock authentication contract, provide a canonical empty cron inventory, and wait for complete Details receipts and the existing finite frame animations before flushing the snapshot store and capturing the reference width. These preconditions all run before reload; the measured reload has no new waits or relaxed bounds.

The setup follows the existing warm-reload fixture from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194142 and preserves the intentional cold entrance from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192435.

## Evidence

- [Original scheduled failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44335514975/job/134911689127) and [latest recurrence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44347096893/job/134952967157): composer width moved from 1000px to 889px after reload.
- The unchanged local case reproduced that failure. Ordered receipt inspection showed its apparent cached docking value was produced by the same cold mount.
- Completed fixture: the exact chat case passed, as did the existing warm-reload and cold first-load cases (3 passed). The unchanged New Session variant passed separately and its proof was reused.
- Intermediate probes isolated two missing preconditions: token-mode authentication without a token prevented warm boot admission; after correcting admission all 30 reload frames were 889px, but the reference was captured mid-animation at 922px. prs.title: fix: show how to read saved update reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After an update, OpenClaw prints the saved report path without explaining how to read it. Pasting that path alone into Bash tries to execute the private Markdown file and fails with `Permission denied`.

## User Impact

Saved update reports now include a copyable **Read report** command beside the existing path: `cat` in a POSIX shell, or explicitly labelled PowerShell `Get-Content` on Windows. Paths containing spaces, quotes, or shell metacharacters are quoted. Report permissions, update behavior, and JSON stdout are unchanged; nothing is opened or uploaded automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

One small CLI formatter reuses the existing shell-quoting helpers across final update output, interactive report fallback, and the legacy post-plugin Doctor diagnostic on stderr. It appears only where a saved report path is already printed. The update reference explains that reports are text files, not commands.

## Evidence

- **Real CLI before/after:** ran `pnpm openclaw update --dry-run --channel stable` with isolated synthetic state, never a real update or the hosting Gateway. On base `bde2e84084bffa49cad046351f7ddd739d26d9ea`, copying the generated report path into Bash exited 126 with `Permission denied`. With the fix, copying the emitted command read exactly the generated Markdown bytes and exited 0; permissions remained `0600`. The final proof used a state path containing spaces, an apostrophe, `$HOME`, backticks, a semicolon, and brackets.
- **Regression:** the Linux and Windows output cases fail on the base for the missing read command and pass with the fix. Existing exact JSON assertions pass; failed artifact writes produce no read instruction. Sibling interactive and resumed-Doctor tests check their output destinations.
- **Focused checks:** 86 tests across progress, progress observation, rollback report, Doctor authority callers, and shell quoting passed. The combined command took 94.32 seconds including cold compiled-worker preparation; the existing Doctor-authority suite took 40.68 seconds and exercises real isolated state/Doctor subprocess boundaries. The new command cases each took 2 ms. CI duration is pending. Production and CLI-update test typechecks, targeted lint, format check, docs listing, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Build:** the normal source CLI build completed (50.4 seconds), then the changed CLI copy/paste proof passed.
- **Simplification:** one reused seven-line formatter, three two-line caller changes; no new state or policy. Net delta: +13 production lines, +37 test lines, +6 docs lines.
- **Independent review gap:** bound Auto Review (`local`, base above, P0–P2, complete 9,934-byte change bundle) prepared one pass but its OpenClaw execution timed out without a report. This is not a clean independent review.
- **Platform limit:** Windows command formatting, including apostrophes, typographic quotes, and literal wildcard characters, is regression-tested. No native Windows/PowerShell executable was available here, so Windows execution and macOS execution remain unverified. The labelled shell instruction avoids implying that PowerShell syntax works in `cmd.exe`.

### Terminal comparison

Before:

```text
Report: /tmp/example-state/update-reports/<run-id>.md
$ /tmp/example-state/update-reports/<run-id>.md
bash: ...: Permission denied
```

After (paths abbreviated for readability; actual copy/paste used the complete generated path):

```text
Report: /tmp/operator's $HOME `echo nope`;[1]/update-reports/<run-id>.md
Read report (shell): cat -- '/tmp/operator'\''s $HOME `echo nope`;[1]/update-reports/<run-id>.md
Copied command: exit 0; bytes match generated report; permissions remain 0600.
```

prs.title: fix: stop the session sidebar jumping while subagents run
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a session in the sidebar is running subagents, a blank placeholder row keeps flashing under it. Every session below it jumps down and back up each time one of its subagents reports progress, which can be several times a minute, so the list is hard to read or click while that session works.

## User Impact

User impact: the session list stays still while sessions run subagents or publish to GitHub; rows no longer move under the pointer.

## Why This Change Was Made

A session can be expanded in the sidebar even when all of its children are hidden there (subagent runs and GitHub publication sessions). Each time one of those children changed, the sidebar re-checked the children and treated that re-check as a fresh load. With no visible child rows to keep on screen, it drew the loading placeholder every time.

Now only the first load of a session's children can show the placeholder. Later re-checks keep what is already displayed, which is how sessions with visible children already behaved.

The first load also showed the placeholder immediately, so a fast read still flashed it for a frame or two before collapsing it. The placeholder now waits 300 ms and only appears when the read is actually slow.

## Evidence

Videos below use the mocked Control UI with synthetic sessions. A running "Audit automations feature" session has one GitHub publication child and three subagent runs. The session is expanded (child read takes 120 ms), then five child updates arrive with child reads taking 800 ms, like the team server, and another session is opened midway. Before is current `main`, after is this branch.

The recording script measured the row below the running session on every animation frame:

- **Before:** the placeholder showed on the expand and on every update (about 48 frames each), and the row below moved 32 px each time.
- **After:** no placeholder frames and 0 px of movement, through the expand, all five updates and the session switch.

**Before** (current `main`):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0eeed8f1-8c40-4f6f-a0b2-a0b550eb7a05

**After** (this branch):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01b0230a-1bbd-43ac-bd73-4f40c0f7ec99

Other checks:

- New sidebar tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix: one for a child re-check under a session with only hidden children, one for a fast first read (no placeholder within 300 ms, placeholder after that while the read is still pending).
- The sidebar unit, isolated and browser suites pass (1,216 tests), the sidebar stability browser E2E passes (7 variants, including the slow first-load placeholder), and the UI typechecks pass.
- Local autoreview found no issues.
- The diagnosis came from a real recording: the affected live session had 15 GitHub publication children and 40 subagent runs, all hidden from the sidebar.

Gap: not yet exercised against a live Gateway in a browser. A first child read slower than 300 ms still shows the placeholder once, which is intended loading feedback.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/db28c1b4-b42f-4c5b-a870-03e5a59d2811)

Fixes #195765

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a macOS node reports `UNAVAILABLE` instead of `INVALID_REQUEST` when `system.notify` or `canvas.navigate` receives missing or malformed parameters.

## User Impact

User impact: callers can correct an invalid request rather than treating the Mac as unavailable. Valid notifications and navigation, permission checks, and empty-notification validation are unchanged. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Catch parameter-decoding failures at the two command handlers and return their command-specific invalid-request responses before native services are used. The new regression suite exercises the production `handleInvoke` entry point for missing/invalid JSON, invalid notification field types and enum values, and existing empty-notification validation.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(gateway): config changes no longer exhaust session discovery with GitHub publication refreshes
prs.body:
Root cause: src/gateway/github-publication-discovery.ts:135-146 (main e08aa74ea39e) `refreshAll` schedules a preparation for every remembered session (up to 256) at `delayMs: 0`, and the scheduler starts them all at once. Each preparation reads the session-store inventory on the one-worker, 128-pending "Session target discovery" lane, so one config change fills that lane, refuses user reads with `worker task capacity reached`, and leaves the refused sessions' publication facts unavailable.

Fixes #195649

Thanks @609NFT for the report and the production numbers, and @ElNeMeR70 for the serialization fix this builds on.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: user turns and session reads fail with `worker task capacity reached`, and GitHub publication becomes unavailable for many sessions, right after an agent add or other config change on a Gateway with more than about 128 recently active GitHub-bound sessions.

## User Impact

A config change (agent add, model switch) or a GitHub identity change no longer refuses user work on busy Gateways. Publication facts refresh in the background one session at a time, as before at the same ids and times, and all of them come back.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discovery now prepares one session at a time, per discovery instance (@ElNeMeR70's commit). On top of that, every write to the discovery cache goes through one `store()` owner. When the session being prepared is replaced by demand, its binding is removed, or it is evicted from the cache, the queue moves on right away. The stale preparation still finishes on its own and its result is never published. In the first commit only some replacement paths released the queue, so a demand replacement (a new session id for the same key) left the next session waiting behind obsolete work. No new limits or config; worker admission is unchanged.

## Evidence

Gateway run from source with local model and GitHub API fixtures, 256 managed-worktree sessions with publication facts, an agent add through `config.patch` while user turns (`chat.send`) and session opens (`chat.history`) arrive every 10 ms. Full observed output: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195679#issuecomment-6986684891

- main e08aa74ea39e: one agent add left 131 of 256 publication facts unavailable (refused by the 128-pending lane); in another run 19 `chat.history` requests failed with `UNAVAILABLE` `WorkerTaskError: worker task capacity reached: code=overloaded`.
- This head: 0 capacity refusals, 150/150 turns and 150/150 session opens succeed, all 256 facts prepared again (39 s).
- Controls on this head: one remembered session refreshes in 0.76 s as before; a second agent add 1.1 s into a wave replaces it cleanly (all 256 prepared at 47.8 s, no second full wave, no refusals).
- Regression test fails on main (200 concurrent preparations) and on the first commit (queue stuck behind the replaced session), passes here; `src/gateway/github-publication-discovery.test.ts` 12/12.

Merge danger: two-way door. Process-local scheduling only; no stored state, config or protocol changes, and a revert restores the concurrent refresh. Blast radius: GitHub publication discovery on the Gateway (when publication facts refresh after config, identity or profile changes).

prs.title: fix(install): honor --beta for git installs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Installing with `install.sh --install-method git --beta` still installs the latest stable release. The flag is accepted, nothing warns, and the ref that gets checked out is `latest` instead of `beta`.

## User Impact

User impact: `--beta` now installs the beta channel for git installs, the same way it already does for npm and Bun installs. Explicit versions and branches are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolve_git_openclaw_ref` (`scripts/install-policy.sh:312`) builds its request from `OPENCLAW_VERSION` alone. `--beta` only sets `USE_BETA=1` (`scripts/install.sh:1370`), and that flag is read by the npm and Bun engine paths at `scripts/install.sh:3673` — after the git ref was already resolved at `scripts/install.sh:2994`. The resolver now prefers the beta channel when `USE_BETA` is set and the request is a channel (`latest`/`next`/unset), keeping an explicit pin or branch authoritative.

Scope note: this PR covers the `--beta` half of #201335. The other half (a host without npm falling back to `main` for a `latest` request, `scripts/install-policy.sh:318-320`) is a policy decision — failing the install, warning on stderr, or pinning a published stable ref all change behaviour for offline/bootstrap installs — so it is left for a maintainer call rather than bundled here.

## Evidence

Five cases in `test/scripts/standalone-installers.test.ts` source the real `scripts/install-policy.sh` in bash with a stubbed `installer_npm`, so they cover the resolver the installer calls rather than a copy of it.

Base (policy change stashed, test present) — `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/test-projects.mts test/scripts/standalone-installers.test.ts`:

```
× resolves the git install ref: --beta selects the beta tag
× resolves the git install ref: --beta without a requested version
AssertionError: expected 'v2026.11.5' to be 'v2026.11.6-beta.2'
Tests  2 failed | 9 passed (11)
```

With the fix:

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  11 passed (11)
```

Direct resolver probe:

```
$ env -i PATH="<fake-npm>:/usr/bin:/bin" bash -c 'installer_npm(){ npm "$@"; }; source scripts/install-policy.sh; USE_BETA=1 OPENCLAW_VERSION=latest resolve_git_openclaw_ref'
v2026.11.5            # base
v2026.11.6-beta.2     # fixed
```

Gap: `install.sh --install-method git --beta` was not run end to end here; this host has no clean throwaway root and the installer would mutate an existing checkout. The regression covers the resolver that runs before any install step, and the `no --beta`/pin/branch cases show other requests are unaffected.

## AI Assistance

Written with AI assistance (DeepSeek Harness agent); the reproduction, tests, and command output above were run on this machine.

---

机制对位: 症状在 `scripts/install-policy.sh:312-326`（只读 `OPENCLAW_VERSION`），我改同一函数 `:315-320`，因为 `USE_BETA` 直到 `scripts/install.sh:3673` 才被消费，而 git ref 早在 `:2994` 就定好了
复现: `USE_BETA=1 OPENCLAW_VERSION=latest resolve_git_openclaw_ref` 在 base 上返回 `v2026.11.5`，修复后返回 `v2026.11.6-beta.2`；测试 base 2 failed → 修复后 11 passed
证据类别: shell 脚本解析行为，本机可得: 是（bash 直接 source 真实脚本 + stub npm）
契约核对: `USE_BETA` 由 `scripts/install.sh:1259/1370` 设置，npm/Bun 引擎在 `:3673` 以 `requested=beta` 消费；`OPENCLAW_VERSION` 由同一函数 `:313` 拥有
风险: 2 文件（1 生产 + 1 测试）、不跨层、不涉状态机

prs.title: fix: keep the chat composer width steady on reload
prs.body:
Related: #201177

## What Problem This Solves

Reloading a desktop chat can briefly show the composer at the saved maximum width, then squeeze it as the cached Details panel opens. In CI, the composer first appeared at 1,000 px and moved through several intermediate widths before settling at 889 px.

## User Impact

The composer uses the restored layout from its first visible frame while the Details panel loads its content.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Details layout owner uses the cached panel snapshot for the entrance decision. Content readiness controls when Details content opens. The regression measures every sampled reload frame in Chat and New Session, then widens the viewport to verify the composer reaches the full saved width when there is room.

## Evidence

- The first-frame assertion failed on [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44335514975/job/134911689127) and on [the merge ref of an unrelated PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44339906776/job/134927843797).
- **9/9 composer-layout browser tests passed** in [final-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44357062807/job/134988997627). The spec took 37.8 seconds. Head `97475f69415a` ran as merge ref `7856ea5e853f` with main parent `b70ce1c2adb6`.
- `git diff --check` passed. Codex autoreview of the final staged diff against `ea8755727fd9` found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- The [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44357062807/job/134994621787) is red because [the Bun UI unit shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44357062807/job/134988998724) failed the Cron lifecycle case “keeps a saved model and reasoning level the catalog does not list” at `ui/src/pages/cron/cron-page.lifecycle.test.ts:145` with `expected null not to be null`. The Cron fixture mounts `CronPageContent` directly with mocked RPCs. Its relative source import graph reaches neither changed file, and the Cron test, fixtures, and editor views have identical blob IDs on the tested main parent and merge ref. The failure is unrelated to this change. The sampled scheduled UI jobs passed, so recurrence on main is unconfirmed. [Tested diff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/b70ce1c2adb6f41ca4bc987eb1258eda8db12dba...7856ea5e853faba648fca7fca3338ff49cdac26f) · [Scheduled main UI check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44358588409/job/134994307240)

### Blockers

The before-and-after screenshot pair is still missing. Hosted `captureUiProof` uploads are available in the real-Gateway lane. This reload case runs in the bundled mock-Gateway lane. The available failure artifacts capture the settled page and cannot show the first-frame layout change.

prs.title: fix: make the "OpenClaw was updated" notice easy to see above the composer
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw is updated while a tab is open, that tab has to reload, but the notice telling you so is easy to miss. On desktop it sits in the sidebar footer (or over the composer controls when the sidebar is collapsed), on phones it covers the first message, and at the same time the chat header says "Reconnecting · Saved conversation" even though the server is reachable.

## User Impact

User impact: after an update, an open tab shows one "OpenClaw was updated" pill with a Reload button just above the composer, on desktop and phone, with the sidebar open or collapsed. Nothing else on the page claims to be reconnecting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing refresh notice stays the only owner of this state; it now anchors to the active composer and falls back to the bottom center of pages that have no composer. While it shows, the shell gives the sidebar and the pane headers an empty connection status, so the duplicate "Reconnecting" / "Refresh required" badges disappear. The pill uses the toast surface tokens with Reload as its only accent, reuses the full-page "OpenClaw was updated / Reload" copy (no new strings), and the transcript and jump-to-latest button get clearance so the pill never covers the last message. Progress, "Couldn't reach the server" and "Finish pending work first" keep working in the same pill.

The sign-in screen's own build-mismatch message still says "Server updated"; it is a separate surface and is left unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Simplification notes</summary>

- Replaces the three placements (sidebar footer, collapsed-sidebar corner, below the phone header) with one anchor placement, and the per-surface suppression of the collapsed connection flag with one shell rule that empties the chrome status while the notice shows.
- Engines without CSS anchor positioning show the pill at the top center of the page.
- Production: +167 / −59 lines (most of it the pill's stylesheet). Tests: the six E2E files only change the button/text name they look for.

</details>

## Evidence

Behavior checked: an open chat whose Gateway reconnects with a newer Control UI build. Real Control UI against the mocked Gateway E2E fixture; automatic reload held at its document probe so the state stays on screen. Before = `3925061024` (main), after = `ed5d5c556c`. Light theme, 1280×800 desktop and 390×844 phone.

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Before: refresh notice in the sidebar footer while the chat header says Reconnecting](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2978573e-d778-44f4-9ab4-cf2a142898c5)

**After**

![After: one OpenClaw was updated pill with Reload above the composer, no header status](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0bc219c0-4b49-49c3-a2e6-ec1ef1f2aa91)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![Before, annotated: notice in the sidebar footer and a Reconnecting header status](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6759073a-8d30-44dc-b1c6-03b0f129a86c)

**After**

![After, annotated: one notice above the composer and no second connection status](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40e89124-1528-4671-b3a4-8dd03f48700f)

### Phone

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Server updated pill over the first message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa4da8be-50ea-4a9b-b29d-5957a4ac4280) | ![After: OpenClaw was updated pill above the composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c98a2ba8-0ed3-4bd0-9ee2-ff2bf007c1d0) |

- The six stale-build and refresh E2E files that use the notice pass (46 tests): queued-correction update recovery, outbox reload, login gate, phone stale-build recovery, embedded terminal, board fixture.
- The refresh card unit tests and the navigation-surface unit and browser tests pass; `pnpm tsgo:ui`, stylelint and oxfmt are clean.
- Also inspected in the same fixture: collapsed sidebar at 1000px, Sessions page, hover, Refreshing, Couldn't reach the server, dark theme and a long transcript scrolled to the end.
- Local autoreview on the committed range reported no findings.
- The initial proof above used Chromium. The latest maintainer checks include WebKit and a simulated no-anchor fallback.

Requested and designed with @vyctorbrzezowski.

<!-- maintainer-refresh-notice-verification -->

### Maintainer verification

The follow-up uses the visible update notice as the single live announcement and keeps the lazy sidebar fallback from presenting a second status. Existing update icons and the transcript clearance rules are reused. Actual before/after crops are pixel-identical for the desktop notice (including Retry), Chromium at 320 px and WebKit at 390 px.

Fifteen focused browser cases cover outbox/queued work, existing and private drafts, and phone automatic recovery. On the repaired build, Chromium and WebKit still place the pill above the composer; the Sessions page uses the intended fallback location. An unreachable server offers Retry. Simulated no-anchor support leaves a reachable top-center pill, which can overlap the first message; no legacy engine was tested.

The paired build for this patch used the [same base as hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44338730450/job/134924038337), `0aafe6691b8`: total CSS grows 2,221 B raw and 514 B gzip, versus a 64 B allowance on each. Startup, Chat and New Session CSS are unchanged. The CSS check remains blocking without an exception.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/a7d2d1de-0d27-4ce4-aae4-40a6e6407e40)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

<!-- openclaw-publication:c5de96e5-f3a2-4fce-b005-15b7b3dcfefc -->

<!-- maintainer-refresh-ci-attribution -->
### Hosted CI follow-up

The [current-head size check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44340835385/job/134931520717) matches the paired local build: the PR adds 2,221 B raw and 514 B compressed; 64 B are allowed. This is the PR's remaining introduced failure.

Three browser assertions also failed on this run for reasons outside the PR:
- The [phone keyboard case](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44340835385/job/134931521519) failed identically on exact CI base `0aafe6691b8` and merge `c26535f14c`: bottom 876.140625 px, expected at most 874 px. The Gateway was connected and the reload notice never appeared.
- The [saved composer width case](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44340835385/job/134931521818) started at 1000 px instead of the saved 889 px on both exact builds, with no reload notice. Intermediate width samples varied with timing.
- The [dictation border case](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44340835385/job/134931521407) expected the removed animated orbit on the CI base. That test was updated on main after this CI snapshot by #200234.

prs.title: feat: show installed plugins in the Customize sidebar
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Customize sidebar only lists its own pages (Plugins, Skills, Skill workshop, Templates). Getting back to a plugin you just installed, or to a feature plugin such as Workboard or Knowledge, means opening the Plugins page and searching for it. Opening a plugin's settings from its detail page also renders the settings form inside the Plugins workspace, so the same settings appear in two places.

## User Impact

User impact: the Customize sidebar shows an **Installed** group on every Customize page: plugins you installed, newest first, followed by the enabled bundled feature plugins that opt in (Workboard, Knowledge, Lobster, Diffs, Memory Wiki). System plugins such as OpenClaw Memory, providers, channels and ClawRouter stay on the Plugins page. Choosing a row opens that plugin's usual detail page, and its Settings button now opens the plugin in Settings (`/settings/plugins/<id>`) instead of showing the form inside Customize.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The Gateway's `plugins.list` now reports `installedAt` (from the install record; bundled plugins have none) and a `sidebar` flag taken from a new manifest presentation hint, `catalog.sidebar`. The Gateway and plugin manifests stay the owners of which plugins appear; the sidebar does not hardcode plugin IDs.
- The sidebar reads `plugins.list` once per connection and plugin generation, so installs, removals and enable/disable changes refresh it. It keeps at most 8 rows; the Plugins page still lists everything.
- On a listed plugin's detail page, that row is selected instead of the Plugins row. The page rows render immediately; plugin rows appear below them when the inventory arrives.
- The detail page's Settings action (and the Configure button on a credential) navigates to `/settings/plugins/<id>?view=settings&from=plugins`. An existing `/plugins/<id>?view=settings` link still renders the old inline form, because those URLs may have been shared. Retiring or redirecting that path can follow separately.
- The bundled opt-in set (Workboard, Knowledge, Lobster, Diffs, Memory Wiki) is a starting point for review. It is one line in each manifest.

## Evidence

The Control UI runs with a synthetic Gateway fixture: three installed plugins (Shopify AI Toolkit, Linear, Lobster Theme) with install times, plus bundled Workboard, Knowledge, disabled Diffs, OpenClaw Memory, ClawRouter and Anthropic. Workboard, Knowledge and Lobster Theme use the packaged `icon.png` artwork from `extensions/*/assets`. Before = `origin/main` at `392506102468`; after = this branch. Chromium, 1440×1000, light theme.

### Clean comparison: Customize sidebar on a plugin detail page

**Before**

![Before: the Customize sidebar lists only Plugins, Skills and Skill workshop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b28d4ac1-67ea-45a3-9ca9-295e5d497ee8)

**After**

![After: an Installed group lists Shopify AI Toolkit, Linear, Lobster Theme, Knowledge and Workboard, with Shopify selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/136e529e-eee5-47bf-9514-e4165029deb0)

### Annotated comparison: Customize sidebar

**Before**

![Before, annotated: only the hub's pages are listed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44e1ffbb-e043-4aa6-9609-1e1e173985cf)

**After**

![After, annotated: installed plugins, newest install first, then Knowledge and Workboard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6970ce2a-582a-4c60-b9ff-e47ad57605da)

### Clean comparison: the detail page's Settings button

**Before**

![Before: Settings opens the plugin form inside the Customize workspace](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8abf9fe0-2f98-40cc-9bbd-6b9b8ee530a0)

**After**

![After: Settings opens the plugin under Settings, Plugins](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/945cecb0-ed3a-4d9f-b9d9-6d2c9b3b6b68)

### Annotated comparison: Settings button

**Before**

![Before, annotated: settings open inside Customize](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae1263e7-21fe-47c2-9e99-be2bd54caa42)

**After**

![After, annotated: opened in Settings, with Plugins selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79f6fee1-96a0-48f1-b4da-d9a6fa748831)

What was checked:

- New browser E2E `plugins-customize-sidebar.e2e.test.ts`: row order (newest install first, then opted-in bundled plugins), disabled and system bundles excluded, the listed plugin's row selected instead of Plugins, clicking Knowledge opens its detail page, the list stays the same on the Skills page, and Settings opens `/settings/plugins/shopify?view=settings&from=plugins` with the form loaded.
- Updated E2E expectations in `plugin-overview` and `plugins-lifecycle` for the Settings navigation. `plugins-hub-navigation`, `plugins.e2e`, `plugins-settings-admin`, `settings-subpage-back` and `sidebar-customization` pass unchanged.
- `management-service.catalog.test.ts`: a bundled manifest's `catalog.sidebar` is projected, and an external install record's `installedAt` becomes epoch milliseconds. The catalog, manifest registry, official bundled catalog and featured tests pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm lint:ui:styles`, oxlint on the changed TS/TSX, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, and `pnpm protocol:gen` with the native Swift/Kotlin protocol check all pass.

Gaps: the screenshots use a mocked Gateway, not a live install. The test does not cover a dark theme or narrow (mobile drawer) layout. Full CI has not run yet.

Requested and designed by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8e1a5ccc-a515-4a53-ad56-430c0be6ad5e)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

<!-- openclaw-publication:dd3ba551-2585-454b-b658-2849a03561a1 -->

<!-- maintainer-customize-plugins-proof -->

### Maintainer verification

External installs without a timestamp sort before bundled plugins. Shortcut artwork refreshes after a plugin inventory change; the focused shortcut remains mounted. Both reported bugs reproduced before the repair and passed afterwards. The existing Settings suites preserve legacy direct links, back navigation and read-only access.

On an isolated real Gateway, Customize listed the enabled Diffs plugin and omitted disabled Workboard. The shortcut opened the Diffs detail; Settings opened the real Diffs form. Disabling Diffs advanced the Gateway plugin generation from 5 to 6 and removed its shortcut without a page reload.

![Diffs shortcut and detail in the isolated Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c140486-1f3a-4237-988a-8917e379d6fe)

![The shortcut disappears after Diffs is disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc791c53-bc18-444c-8850-1a31a266e0e5)

![Customize drawer at 390px, production Chromium with a simulated Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/38eaac06-10cb-4d86-9f18-ab1a8fef63fd)

29 focused browser cases, 39 catalog tests, UI types, lint, i18n, and protocol generation/native verification passed. The optional presentation fields require no migration. No latest-stable upgrade was performed. After reusing the existing group styles, the paired build passes gzip (+54 B), with a remaining raw CSS growth of 412 B (348 B over the allowance); no change in largest CSS or the number of Chat boot requests.

<!-- maintainer-hosted-baseline-attribution -->
The [hosted performance check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44336360962/job/134915350125) confirms the remaining CSS violation: +412 B raw, 348 B beyond the allowed growth. The separately failing [New Session geometry case](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44336360962/job/134915350353) reproduced identically three times on main `7179cc0420b2` and three times on the hosted merge `7fd84e8791ff`. In both builds, releasing `agents.list` settles the composer at 176 px high, while the test expects 214 px; the two sibling cases pass. No New Session fixture or composer source changed in this PR.
