prs.title: refactor(gateway): keep operator authority fixed per request
prs.body:
## Problem

A role edit during an admitted Gateway operator turn aborts the turn through `operator-run-authority`'s policy subscription. The failed source assertion then retires its run claim and downstream runtime effects report `agent runtime authority is no longer active` (T01).

## Rule

Check the original person's authority when a request starts, and keep its captured role, scopes and effective model ceiling until that request ends. Role, device, membership and policy changes govern the next request. Ordinary socket closure is not revocation. Explicit cancellation, release, exact run/turn/claim closure, independent source assertions, data fences and secret boundaries remain effective.

Queued work starts another request: reauthorize once at adoption against the original person's current authority, never socket liveness. Refuse a changed effective model-policy membership, narrowing or widening, rather than mutating the captured ceiling. This includes `sourceAgent` model changes even when the role's configured policy object is unchanged.

## Change

- Limit the policy cut to the Gateway operator authority owner: remove its post-admission role/profile/device/membership subscriptions and repeated policy/source-identity reads; preserve capture-time checks and supplied source/cancellation guards.
- Capture role facts and prepared model policy once. The role-policy reader distinguishes an explicitly captured unrestricted policy from an absent snapshot.
- Carry `reauthorize` through the existing admitted-authority contract and invoke it at canonical queued adoption. Permanent refusals retire only that input through the existing pending-input and abandonment owners; transient unavailability remains retryable.
- A returned child result starts a new requester turn. Reauthorize at its Gateway admission after staging the input; a refusal uses the existing durable run-failure notice owner (`withheld:`), keeps the child's result in the cancelled input record, and never starts parent inference. Only host-bound private-completion or returned-delivery facts select this path.
- Keep the runtime approval owner, run registry and runtime effect guard unchanged. Admit prepared sharing policy facts at accepted chat admission (or when carrying an already-admitted run), while retaining requester, physical-source and profile-identity fences.

Production: +232 / −148 (net +84) across eleven files. Deleting the implicit lifetime revocation checks requires explicit queued, returned-result and injected-input admission, plus a terminal refusal for the affected input. The live T01 failure also requires fixing prepared-sharing policy facts at admission while preserving their identity/source fences. Runtime effect, registry and approval validation are not changed.

## Threat model

A captured grant never widens, switches person or adopts a replacement membership. A revoked identity cannot start another queued request. Finishing already-admitted work after a role/device/policy change is intentional. Caller-supplied assertions and abort signals remain opaque and enforced; this does not remove physical-session, credential, plugin lifecycle or exact claim fences.

Prepared-sharing admission freezes policy facts, not the physical store or person. Consumption still checks requester identity, source settlement and the identity-only profile selection; a merge cannot redirect the admitted authority.

## Deferred: separate subsystem PRs

1. Runtime effect guard: source-policy admission versus in-flight lifecycle settlement.
2. Run registry: explicit source-policy/lifecycle assertion scopes.
3. Runtime approvals: lifecycle-only delegated-authority validation, after the registry contract is settled.

No schema, stored-row, configuration or protocol change. Two-way door: reverting restores the former operator lifetime behavior; no persisted migration is involved. Blast radius is Gateway operator-derived turns and their queued starts, not all authority owners.

## Tests

- On this head, 148 tests across nine suites pass: prepared sharing, worker data/config fences, method authorization, native profile-merge steering, operator owners, and queued admission/lifecycle.
- Queued `sourceAgent` regressions: refused after the source agent's model membership narrows or widens; both fail on the previous head.
- ACP custody 3/3: a returned child result after device revocation does not start parent inference; one visible `withheld:` notice; the child's result stays in the cancelled input record.
- Consumer coverage: direct importers of the changed owners and the 18 files that failed on the earlier broad branch (81 files run locally; CI runs the rest). Obsolete mid-request revocation expectations were rewritten to "finishes; next request refused".
- Inherited, unchanged: the five `subagent-spawn.production-boundary` "consumed-*" Stop cases also fail locally on base `c2ca162a9230` (and in CI on unrelated #201216); the session-notify allowed-path case and native-facade explicit-empty-scopes case also fail on that base.
- Test-line ratchet +390 / 400, no allocation. Tier `full`: `ocx build --dts` and the packed tarball installed into a clean prefix (CLI, doctor).

## Evidence

This is a new cut initially tested against `c2ca162a9230`, then rebased onto main `c4549b7f5596`; the broader branch remains untouched. Live proof on `2cadbe5521e6` showed that the operator owner alone was insufficient: a profile-verification refusal aborted the turn before the resumed adapter's canonical runtime check. Prepared sharing still vetoed its captured policy revision. The repair now admits those policy facts explicitly, but keeps source and identity checks; the runtime guard and run registry retain their existing validators. The same real message handoff succeeds on `a73eded68c45`, and explicit Stop still refuses it.

| Representative old-head failure | Boundary implicated by its stack | Narrow-cut treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI-compatible runs | Operator authority membership/role assertions | Keep admitted work; refuse another start |
| In-process requester continuation | Retained operator device assertion and queue custody | Keep admitted policy; preserve release/receiver closure |
| Method authorization | Prepared session-sharing `readSource` contract | Avoid eager source reads when preparing identity facts; retain physical-source checks on stale-policy consumption |
| Recursive subagent production boundary | Child command/Stop custody after parent cleanup and a foreign Stop | Keep registry, runtime guard and approval validation unchanged; retain the existing negative assertions |
| HTTP tool cancellation | Operator membership assertion after HTTP settlement | Keep admitted membership; preserve disconnect/abort and exact admission closure |

Gateway disposal remains a resource fence: an unavailable captured resolver refuses effects, while replacing a context object alone does not revoke the request's admitted policy. Explicit Stop and child-command lifetime proof use the existing production-boundary tests unchanged.

Source-tier live-provider observations on frozen `a73eded68c45`, using real isolated Gateways (`ocx src`), a real model, synthetic operators, and task-owned adapters/latches; no substituted authority predicate or Gateway handler. All task processes, state, and disposable snapshots were removed. These are not full-build claims.

| Real-Gateway flow | Observed on `a73eded68c45` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Real model → builtin `message` → real `message.action`; `users.setRole(writer → denied)` while channel handoff awaits | `message_action_entered`, `hasHandoff=true`, `hasPlatformDispatch=true`; after role mutation: `local_mailbox_delivered`, receipt `3ed50fb6-a3a2-4a57-8791-849e95509b4b`; tool settles `success`; `agent.wait.status=ok`, terminal reply `S1_TURN_FINISHED`; mailbox contains `S1_LOCAL_DELIVERY`. Next fresh request: `FORBIDDEN: missing scope: operator.write`. | **PASS:** admitted handoff delivers and turn finishes after the role change; fresh admission refuses. |
| Same real `message.action` handoff, explicit `chat.abort` while awaiting | `chat.abort`: `ok=true`, `aborted=true`; resumed handoff: `TypeError: agent runtime authority is no longer active`; tool settles `error`; `agent.wait.status=error`, `stopReason=rpc`; no mailbox artifact/delivery. | **PASS:** explicit Stop still fences the effect. |
| Queued `chat.send` follow-up; lose write while first turn is busy | First turn: `state=final`, `S1_QUEUED_RUNNING_FINISHED`. Queued run: one `state=error`, `seq=1` event per observer, `Your operator role changed; reconnect before continuing.`; `queuedToolStarted=false`; no queued-tool start/retry observed before cleanup. Fresh send: `FORBIDDEN: missing scope: operator.write`. Gateway diagnostic: `user transcript persistence failed: SessionMutationAuthorizationChangedError: Your operator role changed; reconnect before continuing.` | **PARTIAL:** first turn finishes and queued input is visibly refused, but the earlier transcript-persistence guard wins; no `withheld:` notice or queued-adoption refusal was observed. |

## CI consumer repair

- Injection is new input: its admission now reauthorizes both the incumbent and incoming operator grants, without changing the running turn's captured authority or the existing different-profile negatives.
- The failing reconnect assertion was committed-source invalidation, not the earlier profile-switch assertion. Production supplies that predicate in `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/authenticated-request-dispatch.ts:289–315`; `src/gateway/server/ws-policy-close.ts:33–58,110–127` publishes committed invalidation. The socket's `connectionSignal` is a separate argument at dispatcher line 257. Reauthorization reads only classified committed-source authority; the raw transport fallback is never consulted. A socket-close-only control remains accepted.
- In the continuation fixture, ordinary requester cleanup leaves a continuation hold. Already-started child work settles after device revocation; the transferred authority refuses the new parent turn. Its `startTurn` mock stops at dispatch, so real returned-turn refusal remains covered by the ACP custody regression. Gateway disposal still prevents dispatch and settles the flow.
- The maintainer's canonical `agents.entries.source` fixture correction and reduced session-identity allowance are included unchanged.
- Vitest-source: **67 tests pass** across reply-tool authority, in-process continuation and queued authority. Session-identity ratchet passes; all **29 `tsgo:core:test` shards pass**. Test-line ratchet: **+400/400**, no allocation credit.
- CI repair committed as `90ae7f2c6621935930d8d948d215cc2b5af794e7`. The admission check and existing lifecycle assertion share the existing inbound-authority module, keeping the caller-policy module within its line cap without weakening any guard.

prs.title: fix(gateway): surface the provider failure behind unavailable secret refs
prs.body:
Closes #200175 ## What Problem This Solves Inside a read-only sandbox, any `openclaw` command needing Gateway auth fails with "gateway.auth.token is configured as a secret reference but is unavailable in this command path" plus a Fix line that pushes agents toward credential overrides — while the real failure (`SECRET_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, the store's cleanup write) is discarded. The provider failure is now preserved as the error's cause and printed on its own line, so agents and operators see that escalation, not new credentials, is the remedy. - Problem: `resolveConfiguredGatewaySecretInput` converts every non-redacted provider error into `GatewaySecretRefUnavailableError(path)`, losing the provider code and cause. - Solution: construct the unavailable error with the underlying resolution error as `cause` and a config-derived `Provider error: (source , provider

)` line; a provider failure now replaces the credential-override advice with provider-recovery guidance. - What changed: `src/gateway/credentials.ts` (optional `cause`/`providerDiagnostic` on the error class, provider-recovery Fix line) and `src/gateway/credentials-secret-inputs.ts` (the conversion site) plus a regression test. - What did NOT change: the redacted-value rethrow, precedence/scan behavior, the engine-selection conversion (which has no underlying provider error), and every consumer of `isGatewaySecretRefUnavailableError`. ## Why This Change Was Made The generic message assumes the ref was merely unresolved, but when resolution ran and the provider failed, the truth is a provider condition — the same conclusion #196160 reached for this function. - Best fix: yes — the provider detail is composed at the secret-inputs layer, so the core error class stays free of secrets-module dependencies. - Alternative: a dedicated error type was rejected; callers already branch on `isGatewaySecretRefUnavailableError` and the code stays stable. - Risk / non-goals: message matching that assumes the exact three-line shape would see an extra line; the guard helpers match on class and `path`, not the message. ## User Impact An agent working inside a sandbox with a store-backed Gateway token reads `Provider error: SECRET_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE: ...` in the failure and asks for sandbox escalation (as the issue reporter's agent did once told the truth), instead of trying to set tokens the sandbox cannot store. ## Evidence Shipped-CLI runs through `gateway call`'s real terminal rendering (isolated state dir; a file provider whose token file contains the malformed bytes `violet meadow lantern`): ```text $ openclaw gateway call health Gateway call failed: gateway.auth.token is configured as a secret reference but is unavailable in this command path. Fix: set OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN/OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD, pass explicit --token/--password, or run a gateway command path that resolves secret references before credential selection. ``` The payload bytes stay out of the rendered diagnostic (they reach resolution as a raw JSON.parse error whose message quotes the file contents; the failure is preserved on the internal `providerFailure` field, not the standard cause chain the shared formatter walks). A ref-level failure through the same shipped command renders scoped advice instead of provider recovery: ```text $ openclaw gateway call health # env ref with the variable absent Gateway call failed: gateway.auth.token is configured as a secret reference but is unavailable in this command path. Provider error: SECRET_REF_NOT_FOUND (source env, provider default) Fix: repair the configured secret reference (source, provider, or id) or supply the missing value; the secret provider itself is available. ``` Regressions in `credentials-secret-inputs.test.ts`: ```text ✓ preserves the provider failure off the rendered cause chain of an unavailable store-backed token asserts formatErrorMessage(err) excludes both the payload bytes and the provider message text ✓ keeps reference-repair guidance for a ref-level not-found failure with an available provider ✓ keeps reference-repair guidance for a ref-level invalid failure ``` Red check on the prior revision (fix reverted, same tests): the sanitization test fails (the shared formatter's output contains the payload bytes via the attached cause) and both ref-level tests fail (they render the provider-recovery line). ## AI Assistance This PR is AI-assisted. Used `git grep` on `GatewaySecretRefUnavailableError` construction sites and `onResolveRefError` to locate the cause-dropping conversion, implemented the optional diagnostic at the secret-inputs layer, and validated with `vitest`. The implementer understands the code: redacted values rethrow, all other provider failures funneled through one conversion that now preserves the cause. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution. Per review, the preserved failure moved to an internal providerFailure field and recovery advice is scoped by failure kind.

prs.title: fix(gmail): retry failed watch registration before the next renewal
prs.body:
Fixes #195746

## What Problem This Solves

Gmail push notifications can remain unavailable for up to 12 hours when watch registration fails at Gateway startup or during renewal.

## User Impact

Transient registration failures retry within minutes instead of waiting for the next full renewal interval. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retry failed watch starts after one minute, doubling the delay up to the configured renewal interval. Reuse the existing scheduler scope so stopping or replacing the watcher cancels retries. Regular renewal cancels a pending retry, and a renewal that overlaps an active retry joins it rather than starting a second registration.

The three original files retain the unchanged patch from `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/gmail-watch-retry` at `1a33b3515d43473c937f8acf6e24022d9f0ffb03`, applied to fresh main `92798ae0fa97e6fa14d7c414b6decef386c53c6a`. The patch adds 35 net production lines and 54 regression-test lines, with no new scheduling owner or configuration. The approved allocation from `saariuslystoned/openclaw` commit `e6f8c12861d7e8f70df8ca44b68b0271618304c6` adds only `config/test-lines-allocations/gmail-watch-retry.txt`; the shared scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before the production fix, both new regressions fail at the missing one-minute retry; the other 20 watcher tests pass.
- With the fix, all 52 tests across Gmail watcher, Gmail configuration, and Gateway scheduler suites pass through the repository test runner. Watcher file: 22 tests, 3.01 seconds wall time; complete three-suite run: 59.02 seconds including compiler preparation. CI timing is not yet available.
- Core and config/CLI/hooks test TypeScript checks pass. Targeted type-aware lint, formatting of all three changed files, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The contributor reports a completed independent pre-publish review. The transplanted patch is identical (stable patch ID `b7b17417d89a20161002f3c8d0994b507408c528`); no substantive changes were made here.
- Tests exercise the real watcher and scheduler with synthetic command results. No live Gmail account or external Gmail API was used. Tests ran on Node after the pinned Bun download was unavailable.

**Allocation repair verified:** the dedicated 54-line allocation covers the two necessary regressions: retry backoff after a failed start and a single in-flight start during renewal. `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 92798ae0fa97e6fa14d7c414b6decef386c53c6a` passes: 6,593,174 test lines, ceiling 6,593,174, slack 0. Before the allocation, it failed by exactly 54 lines. The original production, test, and documentation files are byte-identical to the previously validated PR head, so their 52-test, typecheck, lint, and formatting evidence above remains applicable. The PR comparison base remains `92798ae0fa97e6fa14d7c414b6decef386c53c6a`; no unrelated main changes were merged or rebased.

Thanks @saariuslystoned for the fix and prior review. ☁️

prs.title: docs: guide small-host setup from saved keys to verified chat
prs.body:
Related: #200110, #200111, #200112

## What Problem This Solves

Someone setting up one Linux agent has to connect installation, a saved API key or existing local model, service startup, and their first working chat across several reference pages. The existing secure credential-import transport does not by itself make that journey discoverable for a beginner.

## User Impact

User impact: a guide linked from Getting Started and onboarding connects saved credentials or an existing Ollama server to first chat, with reusable non-secret configuration and precise resume actions. It now also supplies an assistant-facing workflow and acceptance scenarios aligned with the native macOS and model-management implementations below. Loading the dashboard is no longer described as proof that everything works.

This is a documentation-first contribution, not a new credential importer, profile format, installer, automatic receipt, or completed first-run UI. It should not close the broader workflow requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The guides compose the existing onboarding, credential, config, service, Template, and plugin owners. They distinguish configured from exercised capabilities, explain that config dry-run is validation rather than a before/after diff, preserve separate plugin consent, and avoid replaying completed setup mutations.

Maintainer follow-up requested for #200110: its supported stdin/SecretRef transport is acknowledged. Please keep the basic-user access gap owned under #200112: a person with one API key in 1Password or a similar manager should be able to discover the supported connection path, authorize only the intended field, and reach verified chat without source inspection or assembling several internal workflows. A CLI pipeline is an optional route for people already using that CLI, not proof that password-manager selection is integrated into onboarding. No duplicate credential store/flag or reopening solely for the existing transport is requested.

## Coordination with implementation work

This PR supplies a shared assistant-facing workflow and acceptance scenarios for the work below; it is not a replacement implementation. States below were checked on 2026-11-18; the linked PR is authoritative. Cross-references are coordination context, not a claim that the authors have agreed to a dependency or handoff.

| Implementation work | Relationship to this documentation |
| --- | --- |
| #181011 (open) and #182075 (open, stacked on #181011) — custom endpoint editor and unified provider connection | Reuse Settings → Models, configuration/auth/discovery owners, and their preserved local-admin endpoint-definition boundary. Adding an endpoint or credential does not select or verify the primary model. Broader tracking: #177163 and #193323. |
| #200272 (experimental draft) — native macOS account/local-model onboarding | Apply the same detected → chosen → verified distinctions and first-chat acceptance, without treating the proposed picker as shipped or requiring a parallel CLI setup. |
| #200425 (merged) — native Gateway terminal-command installation | Preserve app/profile ownership and existing terminal defaults. For an app-managed Mac, use the bundled runtime and native setup; do not add a global runtime just because a CLI is not found. |
| #194841 (draft) — macOS existing-Gateway choice | The remote/attach acceptance scenario must not create or retain unwanted local hosting while approval is pending. Its native proof remains separate. |
| #200840 (draft) — compatible installed-browser dashboard handoff | Treat dashboard admission and an actual chat reply as separate evidence. The PR reports macOS dashboard validation but only partial onboarding proof. |
| #200329 (open) — Chat routes an unconfigured user to model setup | Preserve the unsent draft and use the existing setup entry point rather than making the user research model configuration. |
| #200858 and #200859 (open) — onboarding completion and diagnostic output | Keep phase completion and actionable diagnostics accurate; neither message formatting nor a success outro establishes working inference. |
| #200836 (open) — native macOS DMG captions; #200910 (open) — app-owned update guidance | Keep installation/maintenance instructions aligned with the native surfaces and installation owner. Installer presentation and update guidance are not first-chat acceptance. |

### Next implementation slice: let the setup agent use the framework

The documentation now defines **inspect → choose → propose through the existing owner → verify → resume → hand off** and four acceptance scenarios: a saved password-manager key, existing Ollama, native/remote macOS hosting, and interrupted setup. The assistant should do the routine inspection and present one next action, not assign these pages to the user.

**Current integration gap, verified in source:** the initial OpenClaw system agent receives docs/source locations, but its primary loop is restricted to the typed `openclaw` tool and its fallback planner explicitly has no file/network lookup. A pointer is not loaded documentation. Ordinary agents have separate docs-first guidance and may read/search only through their available tools. This PR does not claim to wire automatic documentation consumption into the initial bot.

Implementation should start at the existing `src/system-agent/assistant-prompts.ts` prompt builder and `src/system-agent/overview.ts` reference-discovery boundary, with the tool restriction in `src/system-agent/agent-turn.ts`. Reuse the release-matched canonical guide through bounded, deterministic setup context; do not create another installer, config owner, unrestricted reader, public receipt format, or growing copy of the whole docs tree in the prompt. A runtime implementation must preserve the normal/native app action owners, prompt-prefix stability, capability limits, consent, and source-of-truth rules.

Keep #200112 open for that integration and real entry-point acceptance. Validate through the actual initial setup agent and native/CLI entry points: no human documentation hunt, no raw key in model context, no duplicate installation on resume, and an observed chat result or one precise blocker. A documentation-only check or a prompt-string test cannot establish that outcome.

## Evidence

### Bot-consumption and adversarial review

Three sequential rounds used fresh `openai/gpt-6-astra` instruction-following consumers and independent `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` adversarial reviewers: six child runs and 16 synthetic scenario responses across successive drafts. No unsafe next action was observed in those responses; this is not a 16-case live regression suite or a separate verified “Astra-scale” mode.

The review-driven changes stop failed/partial secret reads before import, preserve the actual agent ID, scope the shortcut to OpenAI keys, separate terminal selection from native automatic trials, require an actual intended-agent Gateway chat result, avoid creating an agent or broadening permissions for an optional tool check, reconcile failed rescue work before retry, and gate service start on successful install. A contradictory incidental planning-tool claim in the existing reference was removed rather than treated as a new capability.

### Executed Bash failure/control tests

Actual documented snippets ran in real Bash with synthetic `op`/`openclaw` functions only. **All six final fixtures passed:** failed read; partial read then failure; importer failure; successful import under inherited tracing/autoexport; failed service installation; successful installation control. The captured key was not traced or exported to the importer environment. No real credential, password manager, or OpenClaw service operation ran.

The original snippets wrongly continued to onboarding after read/import failure and started a service after installation failure. The intermediate pipefail-only revision still started the importer after a partial failed read. The final snippet starts neither importer nor onboarding on a failed read, and starts no service after a failed installation. Success controls still proceed.

### Documentation checks and limits

- MDX syntax and targeted formatting pass for all seven changed/new pages; six Bash-fence syntax/continuation checks and `git diff --check` pass.
- The full configuration-example audit validates 1,408 examples with no findings; both new JSON5 examples are included. Internal route checks report no broken routes.
- The anchor audit still reports three unrelated findings in untouched pages/targets: ACP setup duplicate heading, release 2026.10.1 OpenAI runtime anchor, and Code Mode troubleshooting loop-detection anchor. No changed-link anchor finding was reported. ClawHub fragments remain unverified without their separate source checkout.
- Original source/draft review and this follow-up simplification keep the change documentation-only: no production code, state, new public command, receipt format, or competing config/installer owner.
- **Not verified:** a clean-host install, real password-manager import, actual initial setup-agent documentation loading, real model/provider/tool execution, native first-chat handoff, logout/reboot persistence, or outage failover. The synthetic reviews and shell stubs do not replace those implementation acceptance checks.

Requested by Richard O’Shaughnessy through the linked issues and discussion.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d1f8b252-c950-4999-b9ef-66e08f64c9a6)

## Worked on by

- @oshaughnessy-junior

prs.title: fix(macos): keep local socket services available after transient accept errors
prs.body:
Fixes #195592

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS app's local socket services stop listening when accepting a connection encounters a recoverable error.

## User Impact

Local app-control and execution-approval clients can keep connecting after transient accept failures instead of losing the listener. Resource shortages use a 100 ms retry delay rather than a busy loop. No configuration changes or migration are required; fatal errors still stop the listener.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep recovery in the shared `LocalSocketServer` owner: retry `EINTR` and `ECONNABORTED` immediately, and back off on descriptor/memory shortages or temporarily unavailable connections. The sleep remains cancellation-aware. The existing accept/cleanup lifecycle stays in place, and unused peer-address capture is removed.

The original publication transferred only the contributor's two-file fix onto upstream main. This review repair removes the test-only backoff callback and directly awaits the real cancellation-aware 100 ms sleep. Regression coverage now uses real Unix-socket ping/pong recovery, shutdown and socket-path reuse under sustained resource pressure, and fatal-error cleanup. No unrelated fork commits or main rebase are included.

## Evidence

- **Verified here for the repair:** inspected the listener, socket-test support and cancellation-test siblings; ran `pnpm docs:list`, `git apply --check`, reverse-patch applicability and `git diff --check`. The applied two-file repair is byte-for-byte identical to the independently inspected 8,196-byte patch. No unrelated files changed relative to the original published head.
- **Fresh source review:** the original discussion session independently reviewed the repair. A separate local Auto Review against `f2a2e296e69a4ff45b56b8b84fd641deeffa1876` completed with `scoped-clean`, no P0–P2 findings, and “patch is correct.” This is source review, not native runtime proof.
- **Coverage boundary:** the new tests exercise real-client recovery after each injected recoverable error, stop/path release/replacement-listener startup under sustained `EMFILE`, and fatal-error path cleanup. The shutdown gate opens immediately before returning `EMFILE`; it does not deterministically establish cancellation latency inside the sleep. These new native tests have not been executed here.
- **Platform gap:** this Linux sandbox has no Swift, Xcode, SwiftLint, or SwiftFormat. No fresh native build, test, lint, format, red/green, or timing success is claimed. Current-head native proof remains pending CI or a macOS runner. Prior-head Periphery and precise-scan failures were HTTP 504 download/setup failures, not evidence of a Swift test failure.
- **Historical contributor-reported proof:** Swift regression tests for the original patch ran red before the fix and green afterward on the contributor's macOS runner with Xcode; that branch also passed an independent pre-publication review. prs.title: fix: wait for Git command cleanup before releasing custody
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A cancelled Git command can report its result while process cleanup still owns work, releasing Git custody too early. Related runtime checks also raced real HTTP port binding and command output, making their failure reports unreliable.

## User Impact

Git operations retain their existing ownership until process cleanup settles, including startup cancellation. There are no configuration changes or migrations. The MCP and cron changes only make regression tests reliably exercise the real behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Join the existing process-cleanup promise inside the Git attempt before copying its result or releasing custody. Reuse the existing listener reservation for the MCP fixture, with a real HTTP bind-collision regression. Gate cron deadline/cancellation checks on real child readiness and output receipts, and keep a pre-output deadline case. No new cleanup owner, synthetic HTTP substitute, timeout increase, or weakened assertions.

## Evidence

- All 99 focused tests pass on Node 26.12.1 and pinned Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1 against main base `7eb33ccb25f76747be9a60ef74b69b83b76fd471` (62.79s / 31.92s). Covers Git adapters and worker lifecycle, process settlement, MCP prompt instructions, and cron command timeouts.
- Real-process regressions exercise buffered/text/byte Git cleanup with and without cancellation, genuine HTTP listener contention, and real cron stdout/stderr before cancellation or deadline. Earlier red/green investigation and final fixture-correction evidence are retained.
- Targeted format, lint, and type checks passed for the changed files and the infra, agents-root, and services-cron lanes.
- Independent canonical autoreview, OpenClaw engine, P0–P3: scoped-clean for the complete four-file staged snapshot against `7eb33ccb25f76747be9a60ef74b69b83b76fd471`, including unchanged cleanup, reservation, and receipt owners.
- Focused local evidence is not full CI or installed release qualification; exact-head PR CI remains the landing gate.

## Problem
Full dual-runtime dispatches use the compact PR layout, but that layout did not retain the hosted Gateway-methods file ceiling and dedicated heavy rows. A packed Gateway row exceeded its unchanged deadline in FRV 44290065577.

The PR-exempt retention census now passes the same `mainValidation` discriminator as its production manifest caller; ownership assertions and caps are unchanged. The original four-file frozen patch remains unchanged, with only this one-line fixture correction added after CI.

prs.title: feat(stepfun): add step-5-preview and make it the default model
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

StepFun shipped `step-5-preview`, their current frontier model, but OpenClaw's catalog stopped at `step-3.7-flash` / `step-3.5-flash`, so users could not select it and new setups landed on an older model. This adds `step-5-preview` to both StepFun surfaces (standard + Step Plan, CN + intl) and makes it the model new onboarding selects, while leaving every existing configuration untouched.

**User impact:** new StepFun onboarding runs pick `step-5-preview`. Configurations that already pin a model — by explicit primary *or* by the `StepFun` / `StepFun Plan` alias — keep exactly what they had, including after re-running setup on an upgrade. No catalog rows are removed.

## Summary

Adds StepFun's frontier model `step-5-preview` to the `stepfun` and `stepfun-plan` catalogs and promotes it to the default model for both surfaces.

Docs: [zh](https://platform.stepfun.com/docs/zh/guides/models/step-5-preview) · [en](https://platform.stepfun.ai/docs/en/guides/models/step-5-preview)

## Model metadata

| Field | Value | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Context window | 1,048,576 | docs state 1M context |
| Max output | 65,536 | docs cap output at 64K; `max_tokens` defaults to `INF` upstream but the documented ceiling is 64K |
| `input` | `["text", "image"]` | see note below |
| Reasoning effort | `low` / `medium` / `high` | shares the Step 3.7 `compat` block (`maxTokensField: max_tokens`) |
| `/think off` | → `low` | the model has no non-reasoning mode |

StepFun's API also accepts video input. No OpenClaw model declares `"video"` in `input`, and `docs/providers/stepfun.md` already documents that omission for StepFun, so `input` stays text + image.

## Pricing

The model page carries no rates. Taken from [定价与限速](https://platform.stepfun.com/docs/zh/guides/pricing/details): 7 元 input / 0.35 元 cached input / 20 元 output per 1M tokens. The existing StepFun rows convert at exactly 7.0 CNY per USD (verified against `step-3.5-flash`: 0.7/2.1/0.14 元 → 0.1/0.3/0.02), giving `input: 1`, `output: 2.7`, `cacheRead: 0.1`. The Step Plan surface stays zero-cost like its siblings.

## Compatibility / User impact

Configurations that pin a model keep it — `preserveExistingPrimary` is already set on every StepFun auth method, and the existing regression test covering that across all four methods still passes. New onboarding runs select `step-5-preview`. No catalog rows were removed. (This user-impact/compat context previously lived in `CHANGELOG/Unreleased.md`; that edit was dropped per CONTRIBUTING — `CHANGELOG/**` is release-owned — and is retained here instead.)

**Alias preservation on upgrade:** changing the default surfaced a latent onboarding bug — re-running setup would attach the shared `StepFun` / `StepFun Plan` alias to the new default even when a prior run had bound it to another model, so last-wins resolution silently redirected the alias off the pinned model. `extensions/stepfun/onboard.ts` now binds the shared alias to the new default only when no other ref already owns it; fresh installs still get `step-5-preview`, existing alias ownership is left intact. Covered by new re-onboarding regression tests across both surfaces and regions.

## Changes

- `extensions/stepfun/openclaw.plugin.json` — new model row, first in both providers
- `extensions/stepfun/provider-catalog.ts` — `STEPFUN_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID` → `step-5-preview`, which flows to both `*_DEFAULT_MODEL_REF`, the onboarding alias, and the wizard primary
- `extensions/stepfun/onboard.ts` — bind the shared alias to the new default only when no other ref already owns it (preserve alias ownership on upgrade)
- Tests: `extensions/stepfun/{index,onboard}.test.ts`, `src/agents/models-config.providers.stepfun.test.ts`
- Docs: `docs/providers/stepfun.md` (catalog tables, defaults, both full-config examples, notes), `docs/start/wizard-cli-reference.md`

## Testing

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/stepfun/` — 18 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/models-config.providers.stepfun.test.ts` — 4 passed
- `oxfmt`, oxlint over `extensions/stepfun`, `format:docs`, `docs:check-mdx`, `docs:check-config-examples`, `changelog:check` — all clean

### Cost budget

`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` measured a net `+96` test lines from the new endpoint-eligibility coverage and the onboarding alias tests, putting the tree `95` lines over the shared ceiling. `config/test-lines-allocations/153525-stepfun-step-5-preview.txt` records exactly that `+96`, so the grant adds no extra headroom. The added coverage is the price of the change itself: the eligibility rows pin the new default's provider/region resolution, and the alias assertions prove an upgrade does not silently re-point the shared `StepFun` alias. Verified locally with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base HEAD^2 --no-merge-base` — `ceiling: 6629057; slack: 1`.

## Evidence — real provider behavior

Live requests to all four region × surface endpoints with `model: step-5-preview` (API keys redacted; request IDs truncated). Every one returns `HTTP 200` and echoes `model: step-5-preview`, and each response carries a `reasoning` field, confirming the manifest's `reasoning: true`.

| Region | Surface | Endpoint | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CN | Standard | `https://api.stepfun.com/v1/chat/completions` | ✅ HTTP 200 |
| CN | Step Plan | `https://api.stepfun.com/step_plan/v1/chat/completions` | ✅ HTTP 200 |
| Intl | Standard | `https://api.stepfun.ai/v1/chat/completions` | ✅ HTTP 200 |
| Intl | Step Plan | `https://api.stepfun.ai/step_plan/v1/chat/completions` | ✅ HTTP 200 |

Representative response bodies (one per surface):

**Standard (CN)** — `POST https://api.stepfun.com/v1/chat/completions`
```
{"id":"8be57d93…","object":"chat.completion","model":"step-5-preview",
 "choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"pong",
   "reasoning":"…output exactly \"pong\"…"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],
 "usage":{"prompt_tokens":17,"completion_tokens":51,"total_tokens":68}}
HTTP 200
```

**Step Plan (intl)** — `POST https://api.stepfun.ai/step_plan/v1/chat/completions`
```
{"id":"f159b242…","object":"chat.completion","model":"step-5-preview",
 "choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"pong",
   "reasoning":"…output exactly that string…"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],
 "usage":{"prompt_tokens":17,"completion_tokens":38,"total_tokens":55}}
HTTP 200
```

**Onboarding default + upgrade preservation** — running the real `applyStepFun*ConfigCn` handlers, and resolving the alias through the real model-selection code (throwaway specs, not committed):
```
[fresh]  standard primary = stepfun/step-5-preview
[fresh]  plan primary     = stepfun-plan/step-5-preview
[pinned] standard primary = stepfun/step-3.5-flash (was stepfun/step-3.5-flash)
[pinned] plan primary     = stepfun/step-3.5-flash (was stepfun/step-3.5-flash)

# re-onboarding a config that bound the "StepFun" alias to step-3.5-flash:
[upgraded] models = {stepfun/step-3.5-flash:{alias:"StepFun"}, stepfun/step-5-preview:{}}
[resolve]  "StepFun" -> stepfun/step-3.5-flash   (alias stays put; not redirected)
```

Fresh onboarding selects `step-5-preview` on both surfaces; a config that already pins a model — by primary or by alias — keeps it untouched on upgrade.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)



## Live behavior proof (head `a7c6a3fc058`)

All runs below executed against this branch's build (`OpenClaw 2026.10.4 (a7c6a3f)`, full `qaRuntime` build, all phases green), isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, throwaway gateway ports. API key supplied via `--stepfun-api-key`; every key, token, and session identifier is redacted. The key is China-region (`.com`); `api.stepfun.ai` correctly answers `401` for it.

### 1. Fresh Standard setup (China) — connection + inference

```
$ openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --skip-health \
    --auth-choice stepfun-standard-api-key-cn --stepfun-api-key <redacted>
Updated config: <state>/openclaw.json                       (rc=0)
```
Resulting catalog block:
```json
"agents": { "defaults": { "models": {
  "stepfun/step-5-preview": { "alias": "StepFun" },
  "stepfun/step-3.7-flash": {},
  "stepfun/step-3.5-flash": {} } } },
"models": { "providers": { "stepfun": {
  "baseUrl": "https://api.stepfun.com/v1", "api": "openai-completions" } } }
```
First turn through the gateway:
```
$ openclaw agent -m "Reply with exactly: PROOF-OK-STEP5"
PROOF-OK-STEP5                                               (rc=0)
[gateway] agent model: stepfun/step-5-preview (thinking=off, fast=off)
```

### 2. Fresh Step Plan setup (China) — onboarding correct, inference blocked by account tier

```
$ openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --skip-health \
    --auth-choice stepfun-plan-api-key-cn --stepfun-api-key <redacted>
Updated config: <state>/openclaw.json                       (rc=0)
```
```json
"agents": { "defaults": { "models": {
  "stepfun-plan/step-5-preview": { "alias": "StepFun Plan" },
  "stepfun-plan/step-3.7-flash": {},
  "stepfun-plan/step-3.5-flash": {},
  "stepfun-plan/step-3.5-flash-2603": {} } } },
"models": { "providers": { "stepfun-plan": {
  "baseUrl": "https://api.stepfun.com/step_plan/v1", "api": "openai-completions" } } }
```
Inference on this surface could not be completed with the proof key — the Step Plan credentials are not entitled to `step-5-preview`:

```
$ curl https://api.stepfun.com/step_plan/v1/models           -> 200, ids: step-3.5-flash-2603, step-3.5-flash
$ curl https://api.stepfun.com/step_plan/v1/chat/completions  -> 200
  {"error":{"message":"Identity verification is required to call this API. Complete
   identity verification at https://account.stepfun.com/security?action=realname,
   then retry your request.","type":"real_name_required"}}
```
Because live discovery is strict, the plan endpoint does not advertise `step-5-preview` for this account, so the runtime reports the unknown-model diagnostic rather than routing a call. That is an account-entitlement outcome, not a catalog or onboarding defect: the same `step-5-preview` id resolves normally on the Standard surface with the same key.

### 3. Upgrade from released v2026.10.4 — config preserved and functional

Released build (`383c124`) onboarded the same key, then a fallback was added, then the gateway was swapped to this branch's build on the same state directory.

```
# before upgrade (released build)
agents.defaults.model.fallbacks      = ["stepfun/step-3.7-flash"]
agents.defaults.models               = { "stepfun/step-3.5-flash": {"alias":"StepFun"}, "stepfun/step-3.7-flash": {} }
$ openclaw agent -m "Reply with exactly: PRE-UPGRADE-OK"
PRE-UPGRADE-OK
[gateway] agent model: stepfun/step-3.5-flash (thinking=medium, fast=off)

# this branch's build starts on that state: primary + fallbacks + alias unchanged
# (agent session DB schema 24 required the documented `openclaw doctor --fix` migration,
#  which completed and retained pre-repair state)
$ openclaw agent -m "Reply with exactly: POST-UPGRADE-OK"
POST-UPGRADE-OK
[gateway] agent model: stepfun/step-3.5-flash (thinking=off, fast=off)

# cold restart of the same upgraded state, no priming
$ openclaw agent -m "Reply with exactly: COLD-START-OK"
COLD-START-OK
```
The new default is *not* forced onto the upgraded config: primary stays `step-3.5-flash`, the `StepFun` alias stays bound to it, and the `step-3.7-flash` fallback keeps working.

### Observed, not caused by this PR

- **Probe budget vs. always-reasoning default** (`src/gateway/server-methods/models-probe.ts`, `PROBE_MAX_TOKENS = 8`): `gateway call models.probe` reports `status: "format"` for both surfaces on this key. Reproduced at the provider boundary — a 200 response whose entire 8-token budget is spent on reasoning:
  ```
  {"choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"","reasoning":"The user said \"Hi\". This is"},
   "finish_reason":"length"}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":8}}
  ```
  This matches the mechanism reported in #164327 and affects the Control UI "test connection" / `models status` probe for any always-reasoning default. Onboarding itself is unaffected (non-interactive setup validated the key and wrote config; the probe is not its gate).
- **Catalog warm-up window:** a first agent turn issued within a few seconds of gateway boot can report `Unknown model` until the remote model catalog applies. Reproduced on the fresh-setup state and on the released build's own startup timing, so it is a pre-existing discovery-ordering behavior, not a regression from this change.

### Not covered by this proof

- Standard `api.stepfun.ai` (intl) and intl Plan: the proof key is China-region and returns `401` there. The intl rows are unchanged by this PR; catalog values were verified in unit tests only.

Related: #200263

## What Problem This Solves

The Models page can show a green **Ready** badge even after an API-key access check fails. Successful model discovery does not mean the key can run an inference request, so the badge contradicts the failure shown inside the provider row.

## User Impact

Failed or partly successful access checks now appear in the provider summary, including when the row is collapsed. A later successful check restores the normal status. If checks overlap, a late response cannot overwrite the newer result. Existing account and model-catalog problems keep their priority. No configuration, default, migration, or user action changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider badge and expanded check result use the same status decision. Saving a key and clicking **Test access** now share the existing per-provider ordering guard: an older response cannot replace the newer result or show stale verification feedback. A failed check request no longer leaves an old successful status behind.

This covers the Ready-status portion of #200263. It does not duplicate quota wording in #192165 or change retry attribution in #187720. The fallback-model metadata warning remains open. Earlier proposal #200295 was closed unmerged.

## Evidence

- The original patch was reproduced through the real Control UI, an isolated Gateway, and the built-in OpenAI provider. Discovery succeeds while the loopback provider fixture returns HTTP 429 (`insufficient_quota`) for inference. The badge changes from **Ready** to **Rate limited**, even when collapsed; a working replacement key restores **Ready**. Both real-Gateway browser tests passed on `e993300`.
- The maintainer follow-up in [`0ddb1ae`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0ddb1ae5c8d6e478323db4c142e7909da6881472) adds an out-of-order UI regression. On `e993300`, the older response restores **Ready** after a newer manual check returns **Billing problem**. Local Codex autoreview (P0–P3, maintainer delta on `e993300`) reported no actionable findings; the regression was subsequently moved unchanged to the action suite to meet the test file's line limit.

No live paid API account or macOS run. The original base refresh at `2d52a33` was published without rewriting history. No asset budgets were changed.

prs.title: fix: every tracked process names its chat; stop ended cron runs' processes and survivors' later children
prs.body:
Related: #201157, #199079

## What Problem This Solves

#201157 made a hidden subagent's task end and archive stop the chat's processes. Four gaps of the same class remained, all reproduced on isolated Gateways:

- **Isolated cron runs.** A cron run session (`agent:<id>:cron:<job>:run:<id>`) takes no turn after its run, but its `background: true` services, `yieldMs` hand-offs and `nohup … &` survivors kept running until the session reaper ran. The run session is hidden, so nothing showed them. Reproduced with `openai/gpt-6.2-sol`: after a successful cron run, its HTTP server and `nohup` process were still alive.
- **Children a survivor forks later.** Adopted survivors were stopped per pid. A survivor that starts a child after adoption (a Gateway respawning a worker) left that child running untracked after chat end.
- **macOS without the service marker.** An unmanaged macOS Gateway did not hand survivors off, so they were neither tracked nor stopped.
- **The bad state was representable.** `ProcessSession.scopeKey` was optional, so a process could be tracked without an owning chat (`adoptSurvivor` passed `scopeKey ?? ""`, `stopSessionExecProcesses` filtered `!== undefined`, `resolveProcessToolScopeKey` could return `undefined`), and records were built and registered separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

The chat stays the one owner of its processes, and `stopSessionExecProcesses` stays the one stop.

- **Ratchet.** `ProcessSession.scopeKey` is a required `string`. `registerProcessSession(params)` is the only exported way to track a process; it replaces `createProcessSession` plus `addSession` at the four spawn paths (exec runtime, survivor adoption, durable restore, lost-ordinary report). `resolveProcessToolScopeKey` always returns a scope; an exec tool without a session resolves its agent once through the session-agent owner (`resolveExecToolScopeKey`, used by tool assembly and `createExecTool`). `runExecProcess` and `processGatewayAllowlist` require the scope, so a spawn call without one does not compile.
- **Teardown census.** The shared per-file test teardown fails a file that leaves a live process (not durable, no stop requested) in the scope of a hidden subagent whose rows have all ended, and kills it.
- **Group stop.** A survivor carries the process group it ran in at hand-off. Chat end and Gateway stop signal that group (SIGTERM, 5 s grace, SIGKILL) while the survivor still runs in it and it is not the Gateway's own group. `process kill` on one survivor still stops only that process, so it cannot take siblings with it.
- **Relay on every POSIX host.** Agent exec owns its process tree on macOS too, not only on Linux (where it was added for the memory budget, #193044) or under a service marker. The memory budget stays Linux-only.
- **Cron run sessions.** The isolated run's context disposal (moved from `run.ts` to `session-cleanup.ts`) stops the `:run:` session's processes. A yield on the run's commands resumes inside `executeCronRun`, so it has settled by then. Persistent cron targets are not `:run:` sessions and are unchanged.
- **`canStop: false`** (audit note) is not a defect: `openclaw gateway call` connects with least-privilege scopes (`operator.read` for `sessions.processes.list`), and `canStop` correctly says that client may not stop. A write-scoped client (the Control UI) gets `true`, as `session-processes.test.ts` asserts. No UI change.

## User Impact

- An isolated cron run's services and leftover processes stop when the run ends. To keep one, use `durable: true`.
- At chat end (reset, delete, archive, subagent or cron run end) and Gateway stop, a leftover process's later children stop with it.
- On a macOS Gateway started outside launchd, `cmd &` and `nohup` survivors are tracked, listed by `process list`, and stopped at chat end, as they already were on Linux and under launchd.
- Main chats, visible spawned sessions, yielded subagents and the one-shot `agent --local` hand-off are unchanged.

## Evidence

Tests with real child processes, red on `origin/main` `9d6f4a94adf5`, green here:

- `subagent-task-end-processes.lifecycle.test.ts`: the survivor now forks a child after adoption. Base: all 5 stop rows fail with that child alive; branch: all pass. New row "complete without a service marker": base leaves the survivor and its child alive; the branch stops both.
- `run.session-processes.test.ts` (enters `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn`): base leaves the run session's service alive; the branch stops it.
- `subagent-process-census.test.ts`: the census reports an ended subagent's live process and ignores a running subagent's or one already being stopped. The census ran over the subagent and exec suites with no leak found.
- Ratchet: `tsgo` core, core tests and extensions pass. Removing `scopeKey` from a `registerProcessSession` or `runExecProcess` call fails to compile (`Property 'scopeKey' is missing`).
- Consumers of the process-registry API (95 files) and the cron `run.*` suites (39 files): green. Three failures in that run were checked on base: two are load-timing flakes that also fail on base, and one matches the worktree path (it contains "process").
- Full build with declarations and a packed install smoke (`pnpm pack`, global install, `--version`, `cron add --help`).

Fault matrix on isolated Gateways (`env -i`, scratch state, service marker unless noted, scripted model). R2 `yieldMs` hand-off, R3 `background: true`, R4 `nohup &`, R5 child a survivor forks after adoption, R6 `setsid` double fork. Alive after the cell:

| Cell | Base | Branch |
|---|---|---|
| Isolated cron run completed | R2 R3 R4 R5 R6 | R6 |
| Subagent kill | R5 R6 | R6 |
| Parent delete, child running | R5 R6 | R6 |
| Archive | R5 R6 | R6 |
| Subagent completion / failure, parent delete after completion | R6 | R6 (#201157 cells stay clean) |
| Subagent yielded on its hand-off | R2 kept, resumed | R2 kept, resumed |
| No marker: subagent completion | R4 R5 R6 (untracked) | R6 |
| Main chat completion | all alive, counted | unchanged by design |

Real model (`openai/gpt-6.2-sol`, isolated Gateway): an isolated cron job ran a `background: true` HTTP server, a `nohup` process and a foreground command; the run ended `ok`. Base: server and survivor alive afterwards. Branch: nothing left. `ps` excerpts are in the comment below.

The live Gateway was untouched (launchd pid unchanged, config equal to its backup), and every process the proof started is gone.

## Merge danger and blast radius

- Two-way door: no schema, stored row, protocol or config change. Durable rows written before this keep loading (`scopeKey` falls back to the row's `sessionKey`).
- Cron jobs whose isolated runs started services meant to outlive the run lose them at run end; `durable: true` keeps them.
- Group stop signals only a group created for the command; it is never the Gateway's group, and the survivor must still be in it. Accepted edge: a group that empties in the instant between the survivor's exit and the final SIGKILL could be reused.
- macOS agent exec now runs through the relay anchor: one small Node process per command, as on Linux and launchd-managed macOS.
- Size: production +324/−188. About 60 of those lines are re-indentation; the remaining growth is group stop (~50), the cron stop (+49 in `session-cleanup.ts`, −34 in `run.ts`) and the scope resolver. Tests and fixtures: about +380/−140, mostly mechanical fixture moves.

prs.title: fix: keep setup diagnostics separate from progress output
prs.body:
Fixes #200825

## What Problem This Solves

During Quick start > One agent > Skip for now, a database diagnostic can appear directly inside the setup progress line. The two messages run together even though setup succeeds.

## User Impact

Setup diagnostics remain readable without hiding them. Normal stderr forwarding, JSON stdout, and persisted logs are preserved. No configuration change, migration, or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node forwards worker stderr without passing through the host logger's progress cleanup. The database-worker lifecycle now invokes the existing terminal line-clear owner before that forwarding. It does not replace the stream or add another logging path.

## Evidence

### Isolated real CLI before/after evidence (2026-11-18)

Real command: `pnpm openclaw onboard`. Interactive selections: Quick start > One agent > Skip for now.

Debian 12, Node.js 24.20.0, xterm-256color PTY, 110 columns by 50 rows. Each run used a fresh isolated HOME/state, excluding inherited credentials/config. `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` selected Node through the supported source launcher. No mocked diagnostics, manually seeded config, or background service installation. This was a source-built CLI run, not a new installer run.

Before: pristine production source at `b60b11474606ed85297eceae4a0a001ece69cd90`. After: that base plus only this PR's four-file patch, matching published head `5d5fa6044aceb88788b39d0a95ba9639d3d9d6b4`. No sibling completion-message fix or additional production patch.

#### Before

Exact diagnostic boundary, with terminal line endings shown literally:

~~~text
Setting up your workspace, gateway, and sessions…[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main\r\n
~~~

The diagnostic follows the progress text on the same line.

#### After

Exact diagnostic boundary, with control bytes shown literally:

~~~text
Setting up your workspace, gateway, and sessions…\r\x1b[2K[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main\r\n
~~~

The added `\r\x1b[2K` returns to column 1 and clears the active line before the diagnostic. The visible diagnostic line is:

~~~text
[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main
~~~

#### Successful completion, both runs

Actual output lines, omitting terminal formatting and intervening output:

~~~text
Workspace OK: ~/.openclaw/workspace
Sessions OK: ~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions
~~~

Both reached Next steps, including:

~~~text
Add AI later: re-run `openclaw onboard`
After AI connects, add a channel: `openclaw channels add`
Open the dashboard: `openclaw dashboard`
~~~

Both ended:

~~~text
└  Everything's in place.
~~~

Both processes exited 0. The separate duplicate-completion bug remains in this isolated patch, as expected. Fresh five-file focused test run after the capture: 76 passed in 56.14 seconds. Author simplification found no further changes justified; source was restored byte-identically after the baseline capture and `git diff --check` passed. No new commit or push was made for these captures. The captures are evidence for the explicitly named head above, not later base-refresh commits.

### Earlier verification

The real-worker regression failed on the unchanged production base because the stderr write immediately before the diagnostic was `Setting up workspace`, not the line-clear sequence. With this fix, the preceding write is `\r\x1b[2K` (escapes shown literally), the diagnostic remains present, JSON stdout still parses, and all expected log records persist through close.

- All five focused test files passed: 76 tests in 57.44 seconds of wrapper wall time. The changed logging test took 0.256 seconds; lifecycle tests totaled 0.037 seconds. CI timing is not yet available.
- State-logging typecheck, four-file lint, four-file format check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Author simplification reused `withProgress` instead of manual cleanup and a mutable result, removing 7 lines from the supplied candidate without removing assertions. Final delta: runtime +3/-0; tests and fixtures +16/-2.
- Independent review tooling did not return a completed report. The requester explicitly instructed publication using the passing tests and author simplification; no clean independent-review result is claimed.

The original interactive reproduction used the official 2026.11.5 installer on Debian 12 / Node 24.20.0, with installation and onboarding run separately. Source reproduction used base `b60b11474606ed85297eceae4a0a001ece69cd90`; an earlier combined local fix passed the wizard replay. This isolated PR was verified by the focused real-worker and CLI tests above. No macOS/Windows, live-provider, background-daemon, or full-suite validation is claimed.

<summary>Exact local checks</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-worker-logging.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.capacity.test.ts src/cli/progress.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

```

</details>

prs.title: fix(sessions): keep the running turn when a command is delivered mid-turn
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Using a command picker or typing a command such as `/think` while an agent turn is running can still kill that turn: the command is applied and acknowledged, but the running answer is thrown away with `SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite`. This records any context-bearing command exchange delivered during a running turn *after* that turn settles. The running answer survives, and the exchange still enters later model context, as documented.

Fixes #194451.

### Root Cause

- Every delivered command exchange (native menus, picker and button taps, directive acknowledgements, Slack menus, Mattermost pickers) goes through `recordDeliveredCommandExchange` (`src/config/sessions/command-transcript.ts`). It appended a context-bearing user and assistant pair immediately.
- A started turn prepares its answer against the transcript's context version and checks it again at commit. A context-bearing append inside that window changes the version, so the turn's commit throws `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError`, and the finished answer is discarded.
- `/status` was already exempt because its rows are context-free, and context-free rows do not move the fence. Every other command still took the context-bearing path.
- Live evidence (2026.11.5, Telegram forum topic, embedded runtime, IDs redacted). A turn ran for 28 s with three model calls and tool execution. During it the user opened the native `/think` picker, which recorded the menu exchange, and tapped a level, which recorded the acknowledgement. The turn then ended with:
  `lane task error: … error="SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <session>" errorName=SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError taskKind=turn`
  `Embedded agent failed before reply: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <session>`
  The menu row in the transcript carried no `contextFreeCommand` marker; the `/status` rows in the same session did.

### Why this approach

The open PR #194487 addresses the same issue by marking mid-turn directive acknowledgements context-free. Review there noted that this permanently drops them from later model context, contrary to the documented contract, and recommended coordinating command recording with active-turn transcript ownership instead. It also does not reach picker and menu exchanges, which are recorded directly by channel code rather than through the directive path. This PR takes the recommended approach, at the one function every channel uses:

- If a turn on the same session has started execution, and the exchange is neither context-free nor already coordinated through `expectedWriterRunId`, recording is deferred: it waits for `waitForSessionRunIdle`, re-checks, and records. Re-checks are bounded to 8 waits so a continuously busy session cannot leak a waiter forever.
- Delivery already happened before this function runs, and recording failures were already non-fatal, so callers simply get `{ ok: false, reason: "deferred until the active turn settles" }` and continue.
- The recorded rows are ordinary context-bearing rows, so the next turn sees the command and its reply.
- The busy check targets the physical session the recorder writes to (store path and agent), the same target turn admission captures. Two stores can share one logical key; an unscoped lookup would throw on that and reject a delivered command. If ownership can't be resolved, the check falls back to the non-throwing logical-key busy test, so recording stays non-fatal. The deferred write also waits only on that physical session's turn (`waitForSessionRunIdle` takes an optional `target`), so a busy store elsewhere on the same key does not hold it back.
- Docs: `docs/tools/slash-commands.md` states the mid-turn ordering.

### Scope boundary

- No change to transcript fences, schemas, or the turn's commit validation.
- Mid-turn steering of plain user messages, and other conflict sources listed in the issue thread, are out of scope.
- `recordCommittedCommandExchange` (`/new`, `/reset`) is unchanged.
- Gateway `chat.send` command recording uses a different recorder and is not covered here; it needs its own change.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/config/sessions/command-transcript.active-turn.test.ts`: passes. It uses the real session controller: a turn is admitted with `withSessionTurn` and marked execution-started; a `/think` menu exchange recorded during it returns `deferred` and leaves the transcript empty; after the turn settles, both rows appear without `excludeFromContext`. A second case runs two turns on one logical key in two stores, one executing and one only admitted; recording into the idle store succeeds at once. A third case runs executing turns in two stores on one key; the exchange for the first store is recorded once that store's turn ends, while the other store is still running.
- Mutation checks: disabling the deferral fails the first case (`expected { ok: true … } to match object { ok: false … }`); dropping the store-scoped target fails the second (`expected { ok: false, … } to match object { ok: true }`); an unscoped wait fails the third (times out waiting for the two rows).
- `node scripts/test-projects.mts --changed origin/main` (local): `Test Files 976 passed`; the two local failures (`bash-process-durable`, which needs host services, and `runtime-plugins.ingress-load`, a timing test that passes on rerun) do not touch this code.
- Command transcript, dispatch-from-config, Telegram native command delivery and callback, Discord model picker, Mattermost model picker, and Slack slash suites: `Test Files 46 passed (46)`, `Tests 872 passed (872)`.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` on touched files are clean. `check-test-lines-ratchet`: `Net test lines: +153; allocation credit: 153`.

### Real behavior proof

- Before: the live Gateway log above. A mid-turn `/think` picker and tap killed a running turn on 2026.11.5.
- After: the controller-backed regression test above, through the real `recordDeliveredCommandExchange` and transcript writer.

### What was not tested

- A live Gateway race after the patch: this build is not deployed on the affected Gateway yet.
- A session that stays busy through 8 consecutive turns drops that exchange's transcript copy, logged verbosely. Delivery is unaffected.
- Ordering: a mid-turn exchange now appears after the turn's answer in history, not before it.


### CI failures not caused by this change

- `PostgreSQL conformance (1/4)`: `profile-authority.conformance.test.ts` (native COMMIT fencing). The same shard fails on other open PRs that don't touch sessions in the same window.
- `checks-node-changed` ran `reply.triggers.trigger-handling.e2e.test.ts`, which already failed on the base: its inline `/whoami` case sent `please /whoami now`, and main now leaves slash text inside ordinary prose unexecuted (documented in `docs/tools/slash-commands.md`). The changed-files lane selects that e2e file for this PR, so its body now leads with the shortcut (`/whoami please answer now`), the documented form that still runs and strips it. One line, test only; the suite passes 18/18 locally.

Fixes #200826

## What Problem This Solves

After Quick start > One agent > Skip for now, onboarding prints "Everything's in place." twice, with the first message appearing before the next-step instructions. The repeated success message makes the end of setup unclear.

## User Impact

Onboarding now shows one final completion message after the setup summary and next steps. No configuration changes, migrations, or user action are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stop the setup spinner silently before displaying the Local setup summary. The final outro remains the owner of completion messaging, and setup failure handling remains in place.

## Evidence

### Isolated real CLI before/after evidence

Command: `pnpm openclaw onboard`. Interactive selections: Quick start > One agent > Skip for now.

Environment: Debian 12 container, Node.js 24.20.0, xterm-256color PTY, 110 columns by 50 rows. Each run used a separate initially empty HOME, XDG directories, and OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR. The PTY helper only supplied the real wizard keystrokes and captured output. No mocked setup, manual configuration, provider credentials, or background service installation.

Before: production source at `b60b11474606ed85297eceae4a0a001ece69cd90`. After: that base plus only the patch published as PR #200858 head `a5fad898e67c017fa9eb794e90f85358584a2064`. No sibling PR #200859 patch or other production edits. This is the real source-built CLI, not a new official installer run; the package banner labels this source 2026.11.4.

The excerpts below start at Local setup. ANSI control sequences are removed, CRLF is normalized, and the isolated absolute home path is replaced with [isolated-home]. Omitted startup/build/detection output is not part of these excerpts. The separate progress-line diagnostic issue remains outside this patch.

#### Before

```text
◇  Local setup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                                        │
│  Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace                                                      │
│  Gateway: service installation skipped. Run `openclaw gateway run` to start it in the  │
│  foreground.                                                                           │
│                                                                                        │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

◇  Everything's in place.
│
◇  Next steps ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                                     │
│  Workspace:                                                                         │
│  [isolated-home]/.openclaw/workspace  │
│  Add AI later: re-run `openclaw onboard`                                            │
│  After AI connects, add a channel: `openclaw channels add`                          │
│  Open the dashboard: `openclaw dashboard`                                           │
│                                                                                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
│
└  Everything's in place.
```

Exit status: 0. Full captured transcript contains 2 occurrence(s) of `Everything's in place.`.

#### After

```text
◇  Local setup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                                        │
│  Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace                                                      │
│  Gateway: service installation skipped. Run `openclaw gateway run` to start it in the  │
│  foreground.                                                                           │
│                                                                                        │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
│
◇  Next steps ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                                    │
│  Workspace:                                                                        │
│  [isolated-home]/.openclaw/workspace  │
│  Add AI later: re-run `openclaw onboard`                                           │
│  After AI connects, add a channel: `openclaw channels add`                         │
│  Open the dashboard: `openclaw dashboard`                                          │
│                                                                                    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
│
└  Everything's in place.
```

Exit status: 0. Full captured transcript contains 1 occurrence(s) of `Everything's in place.`.

Result: before, a completion is printed between Local setup and Next steps and then repeated as the final outro. After, the only completion is the final outro after Next steps. Both real wizard runs exited successfully.

Evidence-only follow-up: no source changes, new commit, or push. Existing 46 focused tests, commands typecheck, and two-file lint/format proof remain unchanged. Author simplification retained the minimal silent-stop fix and both distinct output-branch regressions; no additional deletion was justified.

### Earlier verification

The two new renderer regressions fail on the base with two completion messages and pass with this fix with exactly one. They exercise the real Clack progress, note, and outro renderers for skipped AI and fixture-connected foreground setup.

The original investigation also reproduced the duplicate in real interactive onboarding on Debian 12 with Node 24.20.0, then observed one completion and exit code 0 with the proposed fixes. That live replay included a separate terminal-cleanup fix; this PR's isolated automated checks cover only the duplicate-completion change. The official 2026.11.5 installer and onboarding were run separately, not as one continuous recording.

- 46 focused tests passed across quickstart, custodian, and progress suites.
- Commands typecheck, touched-file lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Independent review tooling did not complete. The requester explicitly instructed publication using the passing tests and author simplification pass; no clean independent-review result is claimed.

Fixes #200365

## What Problem This Solves

Opening the default macOS DMG in Finder clips the OpenClaw and Applications captions. Native testing also found that Finder can add a vertical scroll bar over the artwork, while the captions need a clearer backing in light and dark appearance.

## User Impact

Both captions have frosted plates behind them, and the taller installer window gives Finder enough room to display the artwork without the vertical scroll bar. Icon sizes, icon positions, the window-bounds override, and drag-to-Applications behavior are unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Set the default outer window to 680×478 (bounds `400 100 1080 578`), leaving 680×446 below Finder's 32-point title bar. The icons centered at y=305 need about 436 points of content height including their labels. Extend both background images downward by 16 points and bake in the selected frosted caption plates, with a wider plate for localized Applications names.

## Evidence

- Daniel reports that the selected plates were checked in a macOS VM in light and dark appearance; that run identified the scroll bar and the required height adjustment. Native verification was supplied by Daniel, not rerun by this Linux editing session.
- Regenerated both PNGs from `524f1e7` with the supplied script and Pillow 13.0.0. Dimensions are 1360×892 and 680×446. Daniel confirmed that both decoded RGBA pixel hashes exactly match the approved images and authorized these PNGs despite different compression bytes. The generator and temporary Python dependencies were removed and are not committed.
- Re-ran `pnpm test test/scripts/create-dmg.test.ts test/scripts/package-mac-dist.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **17 passed, 26 macOS-only tests skipped** on Linux; both test files passed.
