prs.title: feat(webui): add session-scoped reasoning effort
prs.body:
## Why

Tracking: [NAN-355](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-355).

Choose reasoning effort for the next message in one conversation without opening settings, modifying a shared preset, or changing a task that is already running. A click should not create a conversation or synchronize a separate server-side setting.

## What changed

- Reuse the preset editor's existing model catalog and recommendation helper. Chat offers click-only choices; there is no second capability policy or free-text field.
- Update the browser preference immediately and coalesce browser-storage writes for 250 ms. Sending takes the latest value synchronously, without a reasoning save request, acknowledgement, or first-message save barrier.
- Carry the optional effort in the ordinary message. The existing trusted WebUI admission transaction remembers the last-used value in session metadata; execution derives an independent generation snapshot. Preset changes clear the override. Shell/restart/other non-generating control commands retain their existing behavior.
- Remove the dedicated reasoning service, HTTP read/mutation, WebSocket settings action, scope/config signature, and prototype session-header API. Drop the shared segmented control's now-unused pending-save extension.
- Preserve the accepted compact menu, neutral provider icons, selected-row shading/shadow, aligned control edges, inset corners, and narrow-screen touch targets.

## Scope

A selected-but-unsent preference belongs to this browser. The last-used value is saved only with ordinary message admission, and is restored through the existing session list/attach projection after a Gateway restart. No config/preset write, new lock or settings synchronization subsystem is added. The optional `webui.reasoning-effort.v1` flag advertises message support to the UI; temporary chats do not expose this shortcut.

Omitted message effort preserves the saved session/preset value; explicit null follows the preset; native `none` remains a string. The gateway validates trusted generating input, rather than treating the recommendation list as a new authorization or provider-compatibility policy. Existing authentication and temporary-chat ownership checks remain in place.

## Tradeoffs

Recommendations intentionally match the preset editor, including its fallback recommendations. They are not real-generation capability probes or a guarantee that every upstream API accepts each value or gives it a distinct meaning. Existing provider serialization and request-body precedence are unchanged. Unreleased prototype hash-dict session metadata is not migrated.

## Blast Radius

The existing WebUI message admission and per-execution generation snapshot; existing session metadata/list/attach projection; model-menu local preference, first-message transfer, and send options. Regression checks cover token renewal, session/host isolation, preserving a newer target choice, preset switching, and ordinary shell/restart controls. No execution lifecycle, queue architecture, provider protocol, TUI, or deployment redesign is included.

## Verification

- Backend: 223 targeted mock/temporary-data tests passed; touched Ruff and import boundaries passed. The tested backend patch hash was checked against the final candidate.
- Frontend: final hook/menu/segmented-control/thread-shell set passed (135 tests), plus targeted transport, attachment, composer/model-menu tests and the preset-picker recommendation case. Overlapping test runs are not summed. TypeScript, touched ESLint, independent production build, and diff check passed.
- Isolated real Gateway + Chromium + loopback fake provider: clicking on a blank topic did not mutate session/config or send a settings action; latest effort reached the first model request; assistant responses and explicit turn-end events were persisted; another topic remained unchanged; in-flight effort stayed fixed; queued editing/resending and cancellation used the expected values; actual Gateway process restarts preserved both browser-local unsent choice and session last-used choice in a fresh browser. Desktop/320px, light/dark geometry checks confirmed aligned edges and 44px narrow-screen targets.
- Build assets and HOME/config/workspace/sessions were independent. Config bytes stayed unchanged; no real model, credential, daily instance, or handed-off preview was used or operated.
- Follow-up HEAD: `2fa444817f8232fec1b8bd706aeb5eb90f508b35` (normal commit/push). GitHub currently reports this Draft PR as `CONFLICTING` / `DIRTY`; the new head has no check rollup or workflow run. Exact-head remote CI is therefore not verified. No rebase, force-push, or base-merge was performed without authorization.

issues.title: [Bug]: Live Bot Chat approvals time out without an actionable notification in the initiating Desktop session

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: comp/tools
labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: tool/terminal
labels.description: Terminal execution and process management

labels.name: tool/delegate
labels.description: Subagent delegation

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/profiles
labels.description: Multi-profile isolation, HERMES_HOME scoping

issues.body:
## Summary

On macOS Hermes Desktop, an operator viewing a source Bot Chat delegates work through `message_agent` to a live specialist Bot Chat. A terminal approval requested by the target waits and times out, but the operator does not see an actionable approval in the source surface.

This is a **live-owner, same-process multiplex gateway** case, not the cold CLI fallback in #122764, and not solely the after-parent-turn notifier loss in #133514. Please track source-operator notification/routing for target approvals as its own acceptance case.

## Observed environment and evidence

- Incident checkout: `ed1afb082eb3e46cf2edae9d8f68fb67b09ee4df`; macOS Desktop, local terminal backend.
- One live multiplex gateway serves the source and target profiles. Discovery for all nine profiles resolved to the same gateway instance/listener. The separate `bot_mode_dm.py --run-delivery` process was a reply waiter, not another target gateway.
- Target policy: `approvals.mode: manual`, timeout 60 seconds. Inline interpreter `-c` execution was not allowlisted in the target profile.
- Target terminal returned after approximately 60.04 seconds: `status: blocked`, `exit_code: -1`, `No answer within 1 minute — the command did not run.` / `BLOCKED: Command timed out without user response`.
- The human operator reported that no approval card was visible in the source Desktop conversation. No command ran without consent.
- We did not retain the incident's exact renderer receive ACK or complete subscriber inventory. Therefore this report does **not** claim the target event was never published or that off-screen Desktop notifications universally fail.

The original operation combined local file reads, hashing, and scratch backups in `python3 -c`. Private arguments and paths are omitted. The policy correctly required review; the defect is the missing usable route to the human, not the existence of the gate.

## Reproduction outline

1. Run a local multiplex gateway with two live Bot Chat profiles and Desktop attached to the source conversation.
2. Leave the target conversation unopened; configure the target to require one-operation approval for inline interpreter execution.
3. From the source agent, use `message_agent` to ask the target to invoke a harmless terminal command such as `python3 -c "print('approval-routing-probe')"` once.
4. Remain in the source conversation. Observe whether a prompt/notification identifies the target profile, session and exact request and lets the human navigate to it.
5. Without such a route, the target can time out before the source receives any indication that human action was needed.

This is a minimized outline derived from the retained incident and inspected caller path, not a fresh unpatched reproduction against today's latest upstream.

## Source analysis at the incident revision

- `tools/bot_live_delivery.py::await_delivery` polls delivery receipts until settlement; it does not by itself notify the caller when approval becomes pending.
- `tools/bot_mode_dm.py` queries live target state after the long wait returns pending. A 60-second approval can time out and settle within that wait, so the caller sees only the final blocked reply rather than a live `waiting_approval` handoff.
- `gateway/session_local.py::send_exec_approval` returns a local adapter ACK. This ACK is not proof that a renderer received or displayed the request.
- Canonical pending controls and Desktop approval queues are session-scoped. Existing off-screen native notifications operate on events the client actually receives; their existence alone does not establish source-to-target delivery for this workflow.

Pinned source: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/tree/ed1afb082eb3e46cf2edae9d8f68fb67b09ee4df

## Expected behavior / acceptance criteria

- Target approval pending promptly produces an actionable, exact-request notification on the authenticated initiating operator's surface, while retaining the target's normal approval ownership.
- Following the notification opens the correct target request. Receipt/notification ACK must not itself authorize execution or grant source actors target approval rights.
- Approve Once executes only that operation; Deny does not execute it. Denied/expired/stale/wrong-session requests cannot be reused.
- Multiple simultaneous approvals must not disappear through generic log-watch cooldowns, output truncation, or a global watch breaker. Arbitrary process stdout must not impersonate trusted approval notifications.
- If neither a target approver nor a verified operator-notification route is available, return a truthful delivery-unavailable result, not a false delivery success followed by hidden waiting.
- A target's detached child may request approval after the target foreground receipt settles. Preserve exact dispatch lineage and the repository's existing background cancellation contract.

## Local repair experiment and verification limits

We implemented an unpublished local repair using existing canonical approval ownership plus an exact-delivery notification bridge and Desktop target-session links. After rebuild/restart, the human verified **source notification → target request → Approve Once**, and the harmless marker executed with exit 0. A separate Deny probe returned `blocked`, empty output, and explicit not-run confirmation. Direct background-child approve/deny was also exercised.

Targeted isolated regression: 342 passed, 3 skipped; Desktop selected tests: 9 passed; operator-run Desktop TypeScript check: exit 0. These are **local results, not upstream CI or full-suite certification**. Nested target-child source-only-viewer cases have isolated regression coverage but were not live UI-tested because that specialist profile does not expose delegation. Cross-process bridge behavior and durable restart recovery are not claimed.

No guard disabling, blanket allowlist copy, self-approval, or hook bypass was used. We currently retain the repair on a local maintenance branch rather than assume a future update preserves it. The local commit is not pushed; it is not offered as a publicly accessible patch URL.

## Related work

- #133514 / #136199: background approval transport lifetime after parent completion; related but not sufficient to establish this live Bot Chat source-operator route.
- #122764: cold CLI fallback has no human approval route; different owner/execution mode.
- #91732: Desktop delegated approval authority; potentially relevant integration work.

Happy to provide a sanitized minimal patch or align the implementation with maintainer direction. No debug-share archive is attached because raw logs/config contain private data.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

If you decline the gateway service in the setup wizard during `install.sh`, the installer's next step installs it anyway, and overwrites the recorded `gateway.service_install_choice: decline` with `install`.

The developer docs (`website/docs/developer-guide/gateway-internals.md`) say: "Declining records `decline` without creating, enabling, or removing a service", and that only an explicit `hermes gateway install` should opt in later.

Found by reading the code at `main` 95a1d228 (same code in v0.23.2), then reproduced on v0.23.2 in a sandbox (see the first comment).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `install.sh` interactively on Linux with systemd.
2. In `hermes setup`, answer No to "Install the gateway service so Hermes starts automatically at login…". Full and Quick setup both call `ensure_gateway_service(context="setup", interactive=True)` (`setup.py`, `setup_quick.py`), and `wants_service_install` records `decline`.
3. The installer then runs `stage_gateway`: `hermes gateway install --if-missing`.

### Expected Behavior

`--if-missing` respects the recorded `decline` and installs nothing (perhaps printing how to opt in later).

### Actual Behavior

`_cmd_install` (`hermes_cli/gateway.py`) returns early only if a service is already installed. Nothing on this path reads `service_install_choice`, so with no service installed it goes to `_install_systemd_from_cli`. That asks only "Start the gateway now…?" and "Start the gateway automatically on login/boot…?" (both default Yes), then calls `systemd_install()` whatever the answers. Afterwards `record_service_choice("install")` replaces the user's `decline`.

`systemd_install` writes the unit file and runs `daemon-reload` unconditionally; only `systemctl enable` depends on the login answer. So answering No to both follow-up questions still leaves a unit file installed and the choice recorded as `install`. I've only traced the systemd branch, not launchd or Windows.

### Affected Component

Setup / Installation

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Not run: found by reading the code; nothing specific to one install is involved.
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04 (code path is the same on any systemd host)

### Hermes Version

v0.23.2, and main at 95a1d228

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`install.sh` `stage_gateway` comment: "Setup installs the service when it handles the gateway; ask only if it did not." But `--if-missing` can't tell "setup didn't handle the gateway" from "the user declined", because it never checks `service_install_choice`.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

In `_cmd_install`, when `--if-missing` is set and `load_config()["gateway"]["service_install_choice"] == "decline"`, print "Gateway service declined in setup; run `hermes gateway install` to install it" and return. A plain `hermes gateway install` (no `--if-missing`) stays the explicit opt-in.

issues.title: [Bug]: Sandbox browser never starts after the sandbox is recreated: stale SingletonLock from the old hostname

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: backend/ssh
labels.description: SSH remote execution

labels.name: comp/tools
labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: tool/browser
labels.description: Browser automation (CDP, Playwright)

labels.name: tool/file
labels.description: File tools (read, write, patch, search)

labels.name: backend/docker

issues.body:
### Bug Description

With `bot_desktop.placement: auto` (or `terminal`), the sandbox browser's profile, `<sandbox home>/.hermes/bot-desktop/browser-profile`, is persistent whenever the sandbox home is: a docker volume, an ssh host's home, or a Kubernetes PVC. If the sandbox is recreated while its Chromium is running (container recreate, pod reschedule, host reboot), the profile keeps `SingletonLock -> <old hostname>-<pid>`. When the new sandbox has a different hostname, every `browser_*` / `browser_exec` call after that fails:

```
The local browser could not be started: Chromium in the sandbox did not expose a DevTools endpoint in time
Run `hermes tools` → Browser Automation to (re)install Chromium, or switch backend
```

Chromium sees a lock from another host and treats the profile as in use on another computer. It stays running, writes no `DevToolsActivePort`, and Hermes times out. Each later call launches one more such Chromium. It never recovers; deleting `Singleton*` in the profile by hand fixes it.

### Why

`_start_chromium` (`tools/browser_session_sandbox.py:110`) only removes `DevToolsActivePort` before `setsid chromium ...`:

```python
script = (f"mkdir -p {shlex.quote(udd)} && rm -f {shlex.quote(udd)}/DevToolsActivePort && "
          f"(setsid {shlex.join(argv)} >/dev/null 2>&1 & p=$!; ...")
```

Nothing on the sandbox path looks at `SingletonLock`. The gateway placement does: `browser_launcher._foreign_holder` detects a lock written under another hostname and refuses with a message that names the lock. That path has its own stale-lock bug, #147739. The sandbox path only times out, and the error points at reinstalling Chromium, which doesn't help.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `terminal.backend: docker` (or `ssh`) with a persistent sandbox home, image `nousresearch/hermes-sandbox:desktop`, `bot_desktop.placement: auto`.
2. Use the browser tool once, so the sandbox Chromium starts and writes `SingletonLock -> <hostname>-<pid>`.
3. Recreate the sandbox with a different hostname while that Chromium runs (for docker: remove the container without `--hostname` pinned; the volume keeps the profile).
4. Use the browser tool again: the error above after `_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_S`. `readlink <profile>/SingletonLock` still names the old hostname, and `ps` in the sandbox shows the new Chromium running with no `DevToolsActivePort`.

### Expected Behavior

A launch takes over a lock left by an earlier incarnation of the sandbox, the way Chromium itself takes over a stale lock written under its own hostname. If Hermes can't decide that safely, it should at least fail fast with the gateway path's message naming `SingletonLock` instead of timing out.

### Proposed fix

In `_start_chromium`'s launch script, before `setsid`, remove `Singleton{Lock,Cookie,Socket}` when the lock names another hostname and no process in the sandbox runs with this `--user-data-dir`:

```sh
t=$(readlink "$udd/SingletonLock") && [ "${t%-*}" != "$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/hostname)" ] \
  && ! pgrep -f "user-data-dir=$udd" >/dev/null \
  && rm -f "$udd/SingletonLock" "$udd/SingletonCookie" "$udd/SingletonSocket"
```

`create_sandbox_session` only launches after `_live_devtools` reports `GONE`, and this profile directory belongs to the sandbox. So a lock from another hostname means an earlier incarnation of the sandbox, unless two sandboxes with different hostnames share one home; the `pgrep` check can't see that case.

### Environment

Hermes v0.23.0 gateway (`2bd378ed`), multiplexed profiles, `terminal.backend: ssh` to sidecar sandboxes (`nousresearch/hermes-sandbox:v0.23.2-desktop`) in one Kubernetes pod, sandbox homes on a PVC. The pod name, and with it the hostname, changes on every restart. `tools/browser_session_sandbox.py` on current `main` (`fe8b920cae`) has the same launch script. Related: #147739 (gateway placement).

## Feature description

issues.title: [Bug]: Windows: a `\\?\`-prefixed HERMES_HOME gives a different gateway control-pipe name for the same directory

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: os/windows
labels.description: Native Windows behaviour or breakage: PowerShell install, Windows paths, cmd.exe, WSL-vs-native diff

issues.body:
### Bug Description

On Windows the gateway's control pipe is named from a hash of the resolved home path: `sha256(normcase(Path(home).expanduser().resolve()))`. Python's `ntpath.realpath` keeps a `\\?\` (or `\\?\UNC\`) prefix when the input already had one, and strips it otherwise. So `HERMES_HOME=\\?\C:\hermes-home` and `HERMES_HOME=C:\hermes-home` name the same directory but get different pipe names.

A gateway started with one spelling can't be reached by a CLI command that uses the other (for example `hermes gateway status` from a normal shell). Extended-length paths are common when `HERMES_HOME` is set by another program: Rust's `std::fs::canonicalize` and .NET long-path APIs both return them.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Windows, shell 1: `set HERMES_HOME=\\?\C:\hermes-home` then `hermes gateway run`.
2. Shell 2: `set HERMES_HOME=C:\hermes-home` then `hermes gateway status`.

### Expected Behavior

Shell 2 finds the running gateway: both spellings refer to the same directory, so they map to the same pipe.

### Actual Behavior

Shell 2 reports no running gateway, because the two pipe names differ.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp), CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_ (not platform-specific)

### Debug Report

```shell
Not attached: this is a source-level report and the behaviour does not depend on the environment. Happy to attach `hermes debug share` output if useful.
```

### Operating System

Windows (x64)

### Python Version

3.11 to 3.14 (behaviour of `ntpath.realpath`)

### Hermes Version

v0.23.2 (first seen on a git install at b5f15a6; same code on `main` as of 2026-11-19)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

_No response_

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

At v0.23.2:

- `gateway/control_socket.py:47-53` (`_home_hash`, `windows_pipe_name`) hashes `str(Path(home).expanduser().resolve(strict=False))` as is.
- `hermes_constants.py:224-247` (`hermes_home_key`) has the same normalisation gap, so the two spellings also get different registry keys.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Strip the extended-length prefix before hashing (and in `hermes_home_key`):

```python
def _strip_extended_prefix(p: str) -> str:
    if p.startswith("\\\\?\\UNC\\"):
        return "\\\\" + p[8:]
    if p.startswith("\\\\?\\"):
        return p[4:]
    return p

def _home_hash(home: Path) -> str:
    resolved = str(Path(home).expanduser().resolve(strict=False))
    return hashlib.sha256(
        os.path.normcase(_strip_extended_prefix(resolved)).encode("utf-8")
    ).hexdigest()[:16]
```

Stripping is only exactly equivalent when the stripped path resolves to the same directory (which `ntpath.realpath` itself checks before stripping); for naming the pipe a plain strip is enough.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.title: [Bug]: A2A GetTask regenerates artifactId, status messageId and status.timestamp on every read

labels.name: type/bug

labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
### Bug Description

A stored A2A task is re-rendered on every read by `protocol.build_task`, which mints a new `uuid4` `artifactId`, a new status-message `messageId`, and stamps `status.timestamp` with the current time. So the `SendMessage` response and every later `GetTask`/`ListTasks` for the same finished task carry different IDs and a moving timestamp.

Clients can't use these IDs to de-duplicate results, and `status.timestamp` doesn't say when the task reached its state, which is what A2A means by it.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable the A2A platform (`gateway.platforms.a2a.enabled: true`) and start `hermes gateway run`.
2. `SendMessage` any simple task and wait for it to complete.
3. `GetTask` the same task id twice, a few seconds apart, and diff the two responses.

### Expected Behavior

For a finished task, `artifacts[].artifactId`, `status.message.messageId` and `status.timestamp` are the same on every read, and `status.timestamp` is the time of the last state change.

### Actual Behavior

All three differ between reads, and between the `SendMessage` response and later `GetTask` calls. `status.timestamp` is the time of the read.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp), Other

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_ (A2A platform plugin, `plugins/platforms/a2a`)

### Debug Report

```shell
Not attached: this is a source-level report and the behaviour does not depend on the environment. Happy to attach `hermes debug share` output if useful.
```

### Operating System

macOS 27

### Python Version

3.14

### Hermes Version

v0.23.2 (first seen on a git install at b5f15a6; same code on `main` as of 2026-11-19)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

_No response_

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

At v0.23.2:

- `plugins/platforms/a2a/protocol.py:198-206` (`build_task`): `"timestamp": now_iso()` and `"artifactId": uuid.uuid4().hex`.
- `protocol.py:142-144` (`text_message`): `"messageId": uuid.uuid4().hex`.
- `protocol.py:439-444` (`TaskStore.to_task`): calls `build_task` for every read.
- `protocol.py:385-391` (`TaskStore.complete`) records `state`, `reply` and `completed_at`, but none of the rendered IDs.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Generate the IDs and the timestamp once, when the task changes state, store them on the record, and pass them to `build_task`:

```python
# TaskStore.complete (and set_state for non-terminal transitions)
rec.update(state=state, reply=reply, completed_at=time.time(),
           status_ts=now_iso(),
           artifact_id=uuid.uuid4().hex,
           status_message_id=uuid.uuid4().hex)

# TaskStore.to_task
task = build_task(rec["task_id"], rec["context_id"], rec["state"], rec.get("reply", ""),
                  created_at=rec.get("created_iso", ""),
                  status_ts=rec.get("status_ts"),
                  artifact_id=rec.get("artifact_id"),

# build_task / text_message: use the passed values, and fall back to fresh ones only when

```

issues.title: [Feature]: A2A Agent Card `version` should be the Hermes version, not the constant "1.0.0"

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: tool/file
labels.description: File tools (read, write, patch, search)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

`build_agent_card` hard-codes `"version": "1.0.0"` (`plugins/platforms/a2a/protocol.py:70` at v0.23.2, unchanged on `main`). In A2A the card's `version` is the agent's own version, not the protocol version; the protocol version already has its own field (`supportedInterfaces[].protocolVersion`).

So clients and operators can't tell from the card which Hermes build is answering, for example after `hermes update`, or when several installs run side by side.

### Proposed Solution

Use the running Hermes version for the card's `version`, for example `get_version_info().derived_version` from `hermes_cli/version_info.py` (the same value `hermes --version` prints), plus the short commit for git installs if that is useful. Keep `"1.0.0"` only as a fallback when the version can't be read:

```python
def _agent_version() -> str:
    try:
        from hermes_cli.version_info import get_version_info
        return get_version_info().derived_version or "1.0.0"
    except Exception:
        return "1.0.0"

# build_agent_card
"version": _agent_version(),
```

### Alternatives Considered

- Adding a config key for the card version: more flexible, but operators would have to keep it in sync by hand. The running version is a better default; a config override could be added on top.
- Reading the version from `hermes --version` on the client side: needs shell access to the agent's host, which an A2A client normally doesn't have.

### Feature Type

Gateway / messaging improvement

### Scope

Small (single file, < 50 lines)

### Contribution

- [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

### Debug Report (optional)

_No response_

labels.name: type/bug

labels.name: tool/file

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.description: Electron desktop app (apps/desktop/*)

labels.name: area/i18n
labels.description: Localization, locales, translations

labels.name: desktop/files
labels.description: Files in the desktop app: artifacts panel, attachments, image and file previews, file browser, downl

issues.body:
### Summary

Pasting more than ~3,000 characters into the desktop composer converts the text into an attachment (`LARGE_PASTE_ATTACHMENT_THRESHOLD` in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/large-paste.ts`).

When the desktop app is connected to a **remote** gateway, the staged file lands in `~/.hermes/attachments/` under the **localized UI label** — e.g. `粘贴内容 (23.7 KB)` — instead of the Electron-side name `pasted_content_<stamp>_<hex>.txt` produced by `apps/desktop/electron/composer-paste.ts`.

Because the staged name carries no extension (and contains spaces, parentheses and CJK characters), the preview panel cannot resolve it: clicking Preview shows **"Preview unavailable" / "预览不可用"** with an HTTP 404.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Desktop app connected to a remote Linux gateway.
2. Paste > 3,000 characters of plain text into the composer (it becomes a "Pasted content" attachment).
3. Send the message, open the attachment chip, click Preview.

### Expected

The preview renders the pasted text.

### Actual

The preview panel shows "Preview unavailable" / 404.

The bytes on disk are intact and the model reads the content correctly — only the preview fails. Renaming a copy to `*.txt` makes it readable again.

### Evidence

```
$ ls -l ~/.hermes/attachments/
-rw-rw-r--  ...  "粘贴内容 (23.7 KB)"      # no extension
-rw-rw-r--  ...  "粘贴内容 (18.8 KB)"      # no extension
-rw-rw-r--  ...  "Comments on X.pdf"      # previews fine
-rw-rw-r--  ...  "X.zip"                  # previews fine

$ file "粘贴内容 (23.7 KB)"
Unicode text, UTF-8 text, with very long lines, with CRLF line terminators
```

Attachments that keep a real extension preview normally in the same directory, so the failure tracks the staged name rather than the file content.

### Suspected cause

The staging path appears to be built from the localized attachment label (`pastedContent` + human-readable size) instead of the saved paste filename, which drops both the `.txt` extension and the `pasted_content_` prefix that `isPastedContentPath()` matches on. Paths containing spaces, parentheses and CJK characters additionally need URL-encoding in the preview request.

### Suggested fix

Keep the original `pasted_content_<stamp>_<hex>.txt` basename when staging into `~/.hermes/attachments/` (the display label can stay in the UI), and URL-encode the path in the preview request.

### Environment

- Hermes v0.23.1 (commit 3b4215785882)
- Desktop app on Windows 11
- Remote gateway on Ubuntu 24.04

issues.title: [Bug]: `hermes --version` shows origin/main's commit, not the running one, when the checkout is behind

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
### Bug Description

For git installs on the `main` update channel, the version label shows `· upstream <origin/main short sha>`. It shows the checked-out commit (`· local <sha> (+N carried commits)`) only when HEAD is *ahead* of `origin/main`. When HEAD is behind (an older commit checked out, or after a `git fetch` that moved `origin/main`), the label names a commit that isn't running and never shows the one that is.

The same label is used by `hermes --version`, `/version` and the startup banner.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In a git install on the `main` channel, run `git fetch` so that `origin/main` moves ahead of HEAD (or `git checkout <older commit>`).
2. Run `hermes --version`.

### Expected Behavior

The label names the running commit (HEAD), and says how it relates to `origin/main` (for example "behind upstream <sha>").

### Actual Behavior

`Hermes Agent vX (date) · upstream <origin/main sha>`. HEAD is not shown anywhere in the output.

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Not attached: this is a source-level report and the behaviour does not depend on the environment. Happy to attach `hermes debug share` output if useful.
```

### Operating System

macOS 27

### Python Version

3.14

### Hermes Version

v0.23.2 (first seen on a git install at b5f15a6; same code on `main` as of 2026-11-19)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

_No response_

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

At v0.23.2, `hermes_cli/banner.py:183-188` (`_compute_git_banner_state`) computes `upstream` (`origin/main`), `local` (`HEAD`) and `ahead` (`origin/main..HEAD`, clamped to 0). `format_banner_version_label` (`banner.py:238-242`) then shows `local` only when `ahead > 0`:

```python
if ahead <= 0 or upstream == local:
    return f"{base} · upstream {upstream}"
```

### Proposed Fix (optional)

```python
if upstream == local:
    return f"{base} · {local}"
if ahead <= 0:
    return f"{base} · local {local} (behind upstream {upstream})"
return f"{base} · upstream {upstream} · local {local} (+{ahead} carried {_plural(ahead, 'commit')})"
```

Counting `HEAD..origin/main` as well would allow "N behind". Note that `ahead <= 0` also covers a diverged checkout, so "not at upstream" may be more accurate wording than "behind" unless both counts are computed.

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.title: [Bug]: /model picker hides the active provider's models when a custom provider resells the same ids

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: tool/file
labels.description: File tools (read, write, patch, search)

labels.name: provider/openrouter
labels.description: OpenRouter aggregator

labels.name: area/config
labels.description: Config system, migrations, profiles

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
### Bug Description

The `/model` picker hides models from the row of the provider that is currently active, whenever a user-defined provider also lists the same model id.

Concretely: with `openrouter` as the active provider and the active model `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, plus a configured custom provider that resells an aggregator catalog (e.g. `custom:novita` or `custom:inco`, both of which list `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`), the OpenRouter row no longer contains that model. The picker therefore misreports what the active backend offers, and the model cannot be re-selected from the picker — the row you are running on is the one being stripped.

Agent-side view of the same payload (same code path as the CLI picker, `cli.py` builds its list from `build_models_payload`):

```
current provider: openrouter | model: deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash
openrouter len: 289  is_current: True     # after fix
v41: ['deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash']
```

Before the fix the same call returned 215 models for the OpenRouter row with no `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` in it, while `custom:novita` / `custom:inco` rows did list it.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a user-defined provider that shares model ids with a routing aggregator, e.g. `custom:novita` exposing `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`.
2. Set the aggregator as the active provider and one of the shared ids as the active model: `model.provider: openrouter`, `model.default: deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`.
3. Run `/model` and open the OpenRouter row.

Programmatic reproduction without credentials:

```python
rows = [
  {"slug": "openrouter", "is_current": True,  "is_user_defined": False,
   "models": ["deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash", "anthropic/claude-fable-5"], "total_models": 2},
  {"slug": "custom:novita", "is_current": False, "is_user_defined": True,
   "models": ["deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash"], "total_models": 1},
]
from hermes_cli import inventory
inventory._strip_aggregator_overlaps(rows)
# observed: rows[0]["models"] == ["anthropic/claude-fable-5"]  (the active model is gone)
```

### Expected Behavior

The row of the currently active provider keeps its full model list. An active provider is not a duplicate of anything — the session is already running on it.

### Actual Behavior

`_strip_aggregator_overlaps()` drops the id from the current row too, so the active model disappears from the row it is actually served by.

### Affected Component

- CLI (interactive chat)
- Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Root Cause Analysis

`hermes_cli/inventory.py`, `_strip_aggregator_overlaps()`:

```python
user_models: set[str] = set()
for row in rows:
    if row.get("is_user_defined"):
        user_models.update(m.lower() for m in (row.get("models") or []))
...
for row in rows:
    if row.get("is_user_defined") or not is_routing_aggregator(row.get("slug", "")):
        continue
    original = row.get("models") or []
    filtered = [m for m in original if m.lower() not in user_models]
```

`user_models` is collected from every user-defined row, and every routing aggregator row is filtered against it — including the row whose provider is the active one (`is_current`). The dedup is correct for inactive rows (it prevents picking a model from an aggregator row from silently switching the provider, #45954) but wrong for the row the session runs on.

Note this is a different shape from the earlier fix in PR #47211 ("custom provider's own models survive aggregator dedup"): there, the user-defined row was being emptied; here, the active aggregator row is.

### Proposed Fix

Skip the dedup for the current row:

```python
if row.get("is_current"):
    continue
```

Inactive aggregator rows keep dropping overlaps, user-defined rows stay untouched. PR follows.

### Environment

- OS: macOS 15.6.1
- Hermes Agent: v0.21.1 (`8226c2f6a2`, `main`)
- Python: 3.13.7

Debug report intentionally not attached: `hermes debug share` uploads config and recent logs to a third-party paste service, which I do not want to do from this machine. Happy to provide any specific log output on request.

**Proposal:** When you select text in an assistant message, show a small floating toolbar (similar to Claude's apps):
- **Reply:** puts the selection into the composer as a quote chip ("With reply", dismissible with ×). On send, the quote goes in front of your message as context (e.g. `> quoted text` then your reply), so the agent knows exactly which part you're responding to.

issues.title: [Bug]: Classic CLI misjudges Zellij as a non-reflowing terminal: a width shrink duplicates and truncates transcript lines

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
**Component:** comp/cli (classic prompt_toolkit CLI, resize recovery)
**Checked on:** `main` @ 95a1d228c5, Zellij 0.46.0, kitty 0.50.0 and foot as host terminals, sway 1.12 (headless)

#### Description

`_terminal_reflows()` decides how the classic CLI recovers after a terminal width change. For terminals that re-wrap their rows on resize (tmux, GNU screen, kitty, VTE, …) it leaves the transcript alone. For terminals that keep rows in place (`False`), or when it cannot tell (`None`), it erases the viewport and replays the recorded output (`_clear_prompt_toolkit_screen(..., keep_above=True)` + `_replay_output_history`).

Zellij re-wraps on resize the way tmux does. Its `Grid::change_size` (`zellij-server/src/panes/grid.rs`) rebuilds the canonical lines at the new width and moves the overflow rows into the pane's scrollback. But Zellij does not set `TERM` (the pane inherits the host terminal's `TERM`), and `_MULTIPLEXER_ENV` only knows `TMUX` and `STY`. So inside Zellij the result depends on whatever the host terminal or the environment happens to leak:

| CLI inside a Zellij pane, environment | `_terminal_reflows()` today | correct |
|---|---|---|
| `TERM=xterm-kitty`, or `KITTY_WINDOW_ID`/`VTE_VERSION` leaked from the host | `True` | `True` (by accident) |
| `TERM=foot`/`alacritty*` (default in those hosts) | `True` | `True` (by accident) |
| generic `TERM=xterm-256color` and nothing else (Zellij on a remote host over ssh, foot/alacritty with a forced TERM, …) | `None` | `True` |
| Zellij started from an xterm (`XTERM_VERSION` inherited) | `False` | `True` |
| Zellij on the Linux console (`TERM=linux`) | `False` | `True` |

When the answer is `None` or `False`, a width shrink replays the viewport into a terminal that has already re-wrapped and pushed rows into scrollback. Every line that was pushed out then appears twice in Zellij's scrollback, and the row at the seam is cut short.

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Start Zellij 0.46 in any host terminal with a generic TERM, e.g. `TERM=xterm-256color zellij` (and make sure no `KITTY_WINDOW_ID` / `VTE_VERSION` / `ALACRITTY_WINDOW_ID` leaks into the pane; Zellij run on a remote host over ssh is the natural case).
2. In the pane, start `hermes --cli` and get a reply of about 24 lines, each a bit longer than half the pane width (one row wide, two rows narrow).
3. Narrow the pane (resize the host window, or split the pane).
4. Enter scroll mode (Ctrl+s) and scroll up through the reply.

#### Expected

Each reply line appears once and complete, as it does with the same steps when the CLI thinks the terminal reflows (kitty host with `KITTY_WINDOW_ID` visible, or `TERM=foot`).

#### Actual

One shrink from 174 to 116 columns (pane 45 rows, 24 reply lines of 160 characters each):

| host terminal | env seen by the CLI | `_terminal_reflows()` | reply lines duplicated in Zellij scrollback | lines cut short |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| kitty | `TERM=xterm-256color`, no kitty vars | `None` | 7–8 (Q05/Q06–Q12) | 0–1 |
| kitty | same + `XTERM_VERSION` | `False` | 7 | 0 |
| kitty | `TERM=linux` | `False` | 8 | 1 |
| foot | `TERM=xterm-256color` | `None` | 8 | 1 |
| kitty | `TERM=xterm-256color` + `KITTY_WINDOW_ID` | `True` | 0 | 0 |
| foot | `TERM=foot` | `True` | 0 | 0 |

The byte capture of the CLI (`script -O`) confirms the cause. In the `None`/`False` runs the CLI writes Q05/Q06…Q24 again right after the shrink (viewport refill). In the `True` runs it writes no reply line at all after the shrink. Scrolled up in Zellij, the `None` run shows Q05–Q11 complete, then Q12's first row only, then Q05–Q11 again.

#### Root cause

- `hermes_cli/cli_render.py:557`: `_MULTIPLEXER_ENV = ("TMUX", "STY")` has no Zellij entry, so `_terminal_reflows()` (`cli_render.py:564-584`) falls through to host-terminal hints. Zellij does not set `TERM`, so those hints describe the host terminal, not the terminal the CLI is talking to.
- `hermes_cli/cli_terminal_mixin.py:411-418` (`_recover_after_resize`): `reflows` is not `True`, so on a narrowing it takes `_clear_prompt_toolkit_screen(app, keep_above=True)` + `_replay_output_history`. That path is right for xterm/st/urxvt and wrong for a re-wrapping terminal (`_transcript_room`, `cli_terminal_mixin.py:304`, also counts rows "as painted").

`git log -S _MULTIPLEXER_ENV -- hermes_cli/cli_render.py` shows that the table exists for exactly this class of problem: a95242c15f (tmux with `default-terminal xterm-256color` handed panes a generic TERM and fell to "unknown", so a shrink replayed 5–12 lines) and 9f288ba32a (GNU screen re-wraps like tmux; `STY` added). Zellij was never added.

#### Proposed fix

Add Zellij's pane marker to the multiplexer set, at the same precedence as `TMUX`/`STY`:

```python
_MULTIPLEXER_ENV = ("TMUX", "STY", "ZELLIJ")  # Zellij keeps the host's TERM, so only its env names it
```

and mention Zellij in the comment block above it and in the `_terminal_reflows()` docstring. Zellij sets `ZELLIJ=0` (plus `ZELLIJ_SESSION_NAME`, `ZELLIJ_PANE_ID`) in every pane. Verified with that one-line change: the `None` (kitty and foot) and `XTERM_VERSION` cases above all return `True` and show 0 duplicated / 0 cut lines after the same shrink.

Trade-offs, the same ones a95242c15f accepted for `TMUX`:
- An xterm started from a shell inside Zellij inherits `ZELLIJ` and would count as reflowing (xterm truncates in place). `TMUX` has the same ambiguity, and it was resolved the same way.
- A non-reflowing `TERM` prefix still wins, so Zellij on the Linux console (`TERM=linux`) stays `False` and keeps duplicating. A follow-up could treat `ZELLIJ` + a console TERM (`linux`, `cons*`) as reflowing: a VT cannot be a process launched from inside a Zellij pane, so that combination only means "Zellij on the console". `st`/`rxvt` + `ZELLIJ` stay ambiguous (st launched from a Zellij shell vs. Zellij inside st), so this issue leaves them alone.

#### Tests

Behaviour contracts for `_terminal_reflows()`, in a new test file (e.g. `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_terminal_reflows.py`). Each test first clears every variable the table reads (`TERM`, `TMUX`, `STY`, `ZELLIJ`, `XTERM_VERSION`, the `_REFLOW_ENV` names, `TERM_PROGRAM`, `LC_TERMINAL`) with `monkeypatch`:

1. `TERM=xterm-256color`, `ZELLIJ=0` → `True` (red on main: `None`).
2. Same plus `XTERM_VERSION=XTerm(390)` → `True` (red on main: `False`; Zellij started from an xterm).
3. `TERM=st-256color`, `ZELLIJ=0` → `False` (a non-reflowing TERM still wins; guards the precedence).

Existing `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_force_redraw.py::test_resize_never_loses_or_reprints_a_row` already covers the recovery for `reflows=True`, so it needs no change.

#### Duplicate search

Searched issues/PRs for `zellij resize`, `zellij redraw`, `reflow resize multiplexer`, `_terminal_reflows`, `ZELLIJ reflow`, `resize duplicate lines zellij`: nothing covers this. Related, but different: #95375 (tmux generic-TERM case, closed), #66490 (TUI DEC 2026 under Zellij), #19280 (status-bar duplication on resize).

issues.body:
## Bug

The Hindsight plugin dashboard correctly persists fields that are unique to a single mode, such as `bank_id` and `bank_mission`, but `api_url` and `api_key` are lost or revert after a page refresh.

## Suspected cause

The native Hindsight plugin schema declares `api_url` and `api_key` twice: once for `cloud` mode and again for `local_external` mode, using the same field keys in both definitions.

The dashboard form appears to persist values by field key rather than by a mode-scoped identifier. As a result, the hidden duplicate fields from the inactive mode can overwrite the values entered in the visible mode during save/load.

## Reproduction

1. Open the Hindsight plugin configuration in the dashboard.
2. Select a mode that exposes `api_url` and `api_key` (for example `local_external`).
3. Enter valid values for `api_url`, `api_key`, `bank_id`, and `bank_mission`.
4. Save the configuration.
5. Refresh/reopen the dashboard.

### Actual behavior

- `bank_id` and `bank_mission` remain persisted.
- `api_url` and `api_key` are lost, cleared, or revert.

### Expected behavior

All visible configuration values for the selected mode should persist across refreshes.

## Suggested fix

Either:

- make the schema field keys unique per mode and map them back to the runtime Hindsight configuration, or
- update the dashboard form/state handling so duplicate field keys are scoped by mode and hidden fields cannot overwrite values from the active mode.

The second option would also make the dashboard more robust for other plugins that define mode-dependent fields with identical runtime keys.

issues.title: `gateway/run_notifications.py` completion notification ignores `completion_output_chars` and can truncate the tail to 0 chars (Bot Mode DM replies arrive empty)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
### Summary

When a Bot Mode DM delivery runner finishes, the gateway builds the completion notification in
`gateway/run_notifications.py::_build_process_completion_event`. That function has two defects
that together make the notification's `Output:` section empty:

1. **It hardcodes `_LIMIT = 2000`** and never reads `session.completion_output_chars`, so a
   delivery runner that explicitly asked for a large completion payload
   (`bot_mode_dm.py` sets `REPLY_COMPLETION_CHARS = MESSAGE_MAX_CHARS + 2000` = **18000**) gets
   2000 instead.
2. **Its line-boundary snap can empty the tail entirely.** After taking `_raw[-2000:]` it does
   `_tail = _tail[_nl + 1:]` where `_nl = _tail.find("\n")`. If the only newline in that window
   is the *last* character, `_tail` becomes `""`.

Since `bot_mode_dm.py --run-delivery` prints a **single-line `json.dumps`** payload
(`{"outcome": "@pojia answered.", "reply": "..."}`) whose only real newline is the trailing one,
defect 2 fires on every delivery whose reply exceeds 2000 characters.

Result: the sender's agent receives

```
[IMPORTANT: Background process proc_XXXX completed normally (exit code 0).
Command: ... bot_mode_dm.py --run-delivery ...
Output:
[… output truncated — showing last 0 chars]
]
```

— i.e. it knows the runner finished but cannot see the reply, so it answers with a placeholder
and the actual reply is lost until someone manually digs it out of the recipient's `state.db`.

### Environment

```
Hermes Agent: v0.23.0 (2026.9.24) · stable · local 2bd378ed1b8d
Install method: git
OS: Deepin 25 (Linux 6.6.155-amd64-desktop-hwe), X11 session
Python: 3.14.9
```

### Reproduction

1. Two Hermes profiles on one machine (`default` + a second profile, here `pojia`), Bot Mode on.
2. From `default`'s Bot Chat, `message_agent` the other profile with a task whose answer is
   longer than 2000 characters.
3. Wait for the delivery runner (`bot_mode_dm.py --run-delivery …`) to exit 0.
4. Inspect the completion notification that lands in the sender's session
   (`~/.hermes/state.db`, `messages` table):
   ```
   Output:
   [… output truncated — showing last 0 chars]
   ```
5. The process result itself is fine — `~/.hermes/logs/process-results/proc_XXXX.json` contains
   the whole 7–10 KB `{"outcome": ..., "reply": ...}` payload.

Observed three times on 2026-11-07 (15:53, 16:31, and the same pattern at 17:10); each time the
reply had to be recovered by reading the recipient's `state.db` manually.

### Code location

`gateway/run_notifications.py` — current `main`-era source, inside
`_build_process_completion_event`:

```python
_raw = redact_terminal_output(_raw, _command)
# Keep the last ~2000 chars snapped to a line boundary, with a marker when cut.
_LIMIT = 2000                                        # <-- defect 1: ignores completion_output_chars
if len(_raw) > _LIMIT:
    _tail = _raw[-_LIMIT:]
    _nl = _tail.find("\n")
    _tail = _tail[_nl + 1:] if _nl != -1 else _tail  # <-- defect 2: can empty the tail
    _out = f"[… output truncated — showing last {len(_tail)} chars]\n{_tail}"
else:
    _out = _raw
```

### Contrast: the same repo already has the correct implementation

`tools/process_registry.py::_completion_output` does it right:

```python
def _completion_output(session: "ProcessSession") -> dict:
    """``output`` sized by the session's ``completion_output_chars`` plus ``output_cut`` when trimmed.

    Shared by the completion notification AND the wait/poll/kill snapshots: a bot in an api_server
    or one-shot session cannot receive notifications and polls instead, so the polled result must
    carry the same whole reply and the same cut marker (#115334)."""
    limit = session.completion_output_chars or COMPLETION_OUTPUT_CHARS
    cut = len(session.output_buffer) - limit
    return {"output": _output_tail(session, limit), **({"output_cut": cut} if cut > 0 else {})}
```

So the repo has **two truncation paths for the same notification**, and the one the gateway
actually uses (`_build_process_completion_event`, called at the same file's
`completion_evt = self._build_process_completion_event(...)`) is the one that ignores the per-process
size.

### Why it started biting now

`_build_process_completion_event` already exists in **v0.22.5** (`git show v0.22.5:gateway/run_notifications.py`,
`_LIMIT = 2000` at the same spot), so defect 1 and 2 are not v0.23 regressions by themselves.

What changed is the **shape of the delivery runner's output**: v0.23 reworked `tools/bot_mode_dm.py`
(11 commits in `v0.22.5..v0.23.0`, e.g. `ef52d34bdb feat(bot-mode): message_agent fans out with one
combined reply…`, `160339e0dd feat(bot-mode): typed request envelope…`). The reply is now emitted as
a **single-line JSON object**, so the last-2000-chars window contains exactly one newline — the
trailing one — which is precisely the case defect 2 mishandles.

*(This last paragraph is an inference from the commit list and the output shape; I did not bisect
a v0.22.5 run against the same prompt.)*

### Impact

- **Bot Mode DMs**: every reply longer than 2000 chars arrives at the sender as an empty
  completion. Multi-agent setups (Bot Chat as the coordination channel) silently lose replies.
- **Any background process that sets `_completion_output_chars`** (the terminal tool's internal
  knob, used by `bot_mode_dm._spawn_delivery`) is truncated to 2000 regardless of what it asked for.
- Ordinary `terminal(background=True, notify_on_complete=True)` runs are mostly unaffected in
  practice, but still hit defect 2 whenever the last 2000 chars end with their only newline.

### Suggested fix

In `gateway/run_notifications.py::_build_process_completion_event`:

```python
# Size by the process's own completion_output_chars when it set one (a bot DM's reply is
# the payload: bot_mode_dm.py asks for REPLY_COMPLETION_CHARS), else the historical 2000.
_LIMIT = getattr(session, "completion_output_chars", 0) or 2000
if len(_raw) > _LIMIT:
    _tail = _raw[-_LIMIT:]
    _nl = _tail.find("\n")
    if _nl != -1 and _nl + 1 < len(_tail):   # never let the snap empty the tail
        _tail = _tail[_nl + 1:]
    _out = f"[… output truncated — showing last {len(_tail)} chars]\n{_tail}"
else:
    _out = _raw
```

Alternatively, route this function through the existing correct helper
(`process_registry._completion_output`) so there is only one truncation policy.

### Verification after patching

With the fix applied and the gateway restarted, a >2000-char Bot Mode reply shows up in the
sender's completion notification with the full body (up to the runner's requested
`REPLY_COMPLETION_CHARS` = 18000) instead of `showing last 0 chars`. Local patch verified on
2026-11-07 by diffing against a backup, `py_compile`, and replaying the truncation logic against
six input shapes (the empty-tail case returns 2000 chars after the fix, all other shapes are
byte-identical to before).

issues.title: [Feature]: Enforced origin-scoped model allowlist — keep scheduled/delegated workloads on approved routes

labels.name: type/security
labels.description: Security vulnerability or hardening

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: tool/delegate
labels.description: Subagent delegation

labels.name: area/config
labels.description: Config system, migrations, profiles

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

labels.name: area/billing
labels.description: Account usage, credit usage, billing (cross-cutting)

issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Model selection in Hermes is currently advisory. Model pinning (`-m`,
`model_override` on kanban cards, `delegation.model`) does not survive child
cards, delegated subagents, fallback chains, auxiliary helpers with their own
resolvers, plugins issuing raw HTTP, or spawned subprocesses. In an audit of
scheduled autonomous workloads, most model calls landed outside the intended
dedicated routes despite lane-level pinning; four disjoint request families
(primary turns, auxiliary inference, plugin LLM calls, delegated/spawned work)
have no single outbound chokepoint.

Consequences: subscription-backed primary models drained by unattended
workloads; unauthorized paid calls via subagents (real-harm precedent:
#128524); provider-side guardrails that hold only on one request path
(#142611).

### Proposed Solution

A named, config-declared inference policy that is enforced pre-send across
every request family, e.g.:

```yaml
inference_policy:
  <name>:
    allowed_models: [...]        # explicit allowlist
    allowed_providers: [...]
    default_action: reject       # fail-closed, pre-send
    fallbacks: disabled          # unless the chain is itself allowlisted
```

- Default action REJECT before the request leaves the client; the error names
  the origin and the attempted route (generalizes the existing per-plugin
  trust-policy pattern in `agent/plugin_llm.py`, which already fails closed
  per call).
- Coverage: primary turns, auxiliary inference, plugin LLM calls, delegated
  children, spawned subprocesses — origin carried via environment and derived
  at card spawn.
- Origin/scope absent ⇒ strictly no-op: zero regression for interactive
  traffic.
- Optional remap table (attempted → permitted model) for soft enforcement.
- Per-origin spend attribution metadata.
- Composes with the request-lease/runtime-seam work in #82235 (and its stage
  issues #82265/#82271) as the enforcement point — this proposal is the
  operator-facing policy layer on top, not a competitor to it.

### Feature Type

Configuration option

### Scope

Large (new module or significant refactor)

### Alternatives Considered

- Prompt/skill instructions ("only use model X") — advisory; #128524 proved
  bypassable by subagents.
- Per-process pinning (`-m`) — does not survive children, fallbacks, or
  helper resolvers.
- `delegation.model` — covers delegated children only.
- Picker display filters (#126996, #111540) — display-only by design;
  `-m <id>` still works.
- Provider-side guardrails (#142611) — hold on the keyed picker path only,
  not auxiliary/fallback lanes.
- Proxy / virtual-key allowlists — outside the client: blind to local models
  and non-proxy paths, weak attribution under shared keys.
- Local source patch (our current stopgap) — fragile across updates; the
  motivation for wanting this natively.

### Relationship to existing issues

- #128524 — subagents bypassed stated model policy; unauthorized paid calls.
- #142611 — guardrail filtering holds only on one path.
- #125989 — model→provider routing pinning, runtime refusal pre-send (PR
  offered by reporter).
- #10729 (open PR) — global banned-provider enforcement (global scope, no
  workload scoping).
- #126996 / #111540 — picker allow/deny + allowed-models config (display
  shaping).
- #94678 — model-scoped auto-approvals (adjacent approvals angle).
- #82235 RFC + #82265/#82271 — request lease / runtime seam; natural
  enforcement seam to compose with.

This proposal is the unifying operator-facing policy layer the above compose
under: origin-scoped (not just model-scoped or provider-scoped), covering all
request families, fail-closed by default, no-op when unset.

### Contribution

- [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

Unchecked — happy to discuss design first; a PR would be a separately
discussed follow-up.

Debug Report omitted (uploads logs to an external paste service). Version:
hermes-agent `27989a2f` (origin/main as of 2026-11-01 verified the same gap at
`9a56be3d`).

issues.title: [Bug]: OpenRouter "show only guardrail approved models" holds for the keyed /model picker but not for its fallback path or the auxiliary/fallback lanes — guardrail-blocked models still get selected

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: provider/openrouter
labels.description: OpenRouter aggregator

labels.name: area/auth
labels.description: Authentication, OAuth, credential pools

labels.name: area/config
labels.description: Config system, migrations, profiles

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
## Bug Description

Hermes documents that, with an OpenRouter credential configured, the `/model` picker is "exactly the account catalog from `/models/user` — OpenRouter filters it by the key's provider preferences, privacy settings and guardrails — and nothing else: no curated snapshot is merged in, so the picker cannot offer a model this account would be denied" (`hermes_cli/models.py::fetch_openrouter_models` docstring).

That guardrail filtering only governs the keyed `fetch_openrouter_models` path. It is **not** applied to the other OpenRouter model-selection surfaces, so models the workspace guardrail blocks still get surfaced and auto-selected, then fail at request time with HTTP 404 "Model blocked by guardrail":

1. **Auxiliary / fallback lane.** `agent/auxiliary_client.py::_try_openrouter` picks its OpenRouter model from config/default, independent of the guardrail-filtered account catalog. In this session it selected `anthropic/claude-fable-5.1`, which the workspace guardrail blocks on every endpoint.
2. **Picker fallback when the credential doesn't resolve.** When `_openrouter_catalog_api_key()` returns empty (key not resolvable in that process/profile), `fetch_openrouter_models` serves the curated manifest path — which is not guardrail-filtered — so the picker can offer models the account is denied.
3. **Cache staleness.** The account catalog is cached for `model_catalog.ttl_*`, so a guardrail change is not reflected until the TTL expires, leaving the picker on a pre-change list.

Net effect: "show only guardrail-approved models" holds for the keyed `/model` list but not for the surrounding selection paths, and the failure mode is a hard 404 rather than a filtered-out model.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an OpenRouter workspace whose guardrail (model allowlist / provider allowlist) blocks a model that is present in the public/curated list — here `anthropic/claude-fable-5.1`, which is "recommended" in the curated manifest but absent from the account's filtered catalog.
2. Trigger an auxiliary task (vision / compression / session search) so the auxiliary client engages its OpenRouter fallback lane.
3. The lane requests the guardrail-blocked model and OpenRouter rejects it.

## Expected Behavior

Every OpenRouter model-selection surface — the `/model` picker, its fallback paths, and the auxiliary/fallback lanes — should be restricted to guardrail-approved models (the `/api/v1/models/user` catalog). A guardrail-blocked model should never be offered or auto-selected.

## Actual Behavior

The auxiliary lane selects the guardrail-blocked model; OpenRouter returns 404 for all 4 candidate endpoints, the client retries 3×, and the auxiliary task fails. The `/model` picker likewise falls back to the unfiltered curated list when the credential does not resolve, and holds a stale list until the catalog TTL expires after a guardrail change.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Linux 6.8.0-146-generic)
- Hermes version: v0.21.7+144.g3f2abce (2026.9.24) · stable
- Install: git — `/opt/clusterfk-ai/.hermes/hermes-agent`
- Python: 3.14.7
- Provider: openrouter

## Error Output

Auxiliary lane engages its OpenRouter fallback with a guardrail-blocked model:

```
agent.auxiliary_client: Auxiliary client: PAID lane engaged for auxiliary task — OpenRouter fallback model 'anthropic/claude-fable-5.1' is not a :free SKU and may incur real spend. Set auxiliary.free_only: true to restrict auxiliary fallbacks to free models, or auxiliary.openrouter_model to a :free model.
```

Then the guardrail rejection — 18 occurrences in `~/.hermes/logs/errors.log`, retried to exhaustion:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "0 endpoints out of 4 requested are available matching your guardrail restrictions and data policy. We removed them for the following reasons (an endpoint may have matched multiple reasons):\nModel blocked by guardrail: 4 endpoints excluded; configurable at https://openrouter.ai/workspaces/default/guardrails\nProvider not allowed by guardrail: 4 endpoints excluded; configurable at https://openrouter.ai/workspaces/default/guardrails",
    "code": 404,
    "metadata": {
      "input_endpoint_count": 4,
      "ineligibility_reasons": [
        {"reason": "model-ignored-by-guardrail", "endpoint_count": 4},
        {"reason": "provider-not-allowed-by-guardrail", "endpoint_count": 4}
      ],
      "routing_funnel": [{"step": "Initial Endpoints", "endpoint_count": 4}],
      "failed_routing_step": "Filter by Guardrails"
    }
  }
}
```

## Additional Context

The credential's guardrail-filtered account catalog already excludes the blocked model — the fallback lanes just don't consult it:

```
~/.hermes/cache/openrouter_account_catalog_<fp>.json   → 3 rows
  deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017   (recommended)
  deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash
  z-ai/glm-5.3-flash

~/.hermes/cache/openrouter_curated_catalog.json        → 62 rows
  anthropic/claude-fable-5.1          (recommended)   ← guardrail-blocked, not in the account catalog
```

Related prior work in this area: the account catalog landed as the authoritative source for the keyed picker (`tests/hermes_cli/test_openrouter_account_catalog.py`), and #122449 is the neighbouring "image 400 misrouted to `format_error`" defect. The remaining gap is extending the same guardrail filter to the fallback/auxiliary selection paths and invalidating the cached filtered list when the guardrail changes.


---

**Related:** #133850 (OpenRouter guardrail 404s retried instead of falling back — the downstream symptom) and its fixes #134325 / #133877. This report is the upstream gap: the guardrail filter is not applied to the fallback/auxiliary selection paths, so the blocked model is chosen before any fallback logic runs.

issues.title: [Bug]: search_files(target="files") discards all matches when find exits 1 on an unreadable sibling directory

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/tools
labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: tool/file
labels.description: File tools (read, write, patch, search)

labels.name: backend/local
labels.description: Local shell execution

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Bug Description

`search_files(target="files", ...)` returns zero results and a hard error whenever the search tree contains **any** directory the invoking user cannot traverse — even though `find` successfully located and printed matches in the readable parts of the tree.

```json
{"total_count": 0, "error": "File search failed while running bounded find traversal."}
```

GNU `find` exits **1** when it fails to descend into *some* directory (EACCES), *even when it has already printed matches to stdout*. `_search_files()` in `tools/file_operations_search.py` treats any exit code outside `{0, 124}` as a total failure and discards results that were in fact returned:

```python
bounded_sigpipe = result.exit_code == 141 and len(raw_files) >= fetch_limit
if result.exit_code not in {0, 124} and not bounded_sigpipe:
    ...
    return SearchResult(error="File search failed while running bounded find traversal.")
```

Failing closed because of a permission problem in an unrelated *sibling* directory means a search of `/tmp` or `$HOME` fails on most real systems, since those routinely contain root-owned directories (`/tmp/systemd-private-*`, `/tmp/snap-private-tmp`, and any root-owned mountpoint under a home directory).

This is **backend-agnostic** — it reproduces on a purely local host and is not specific to remote/SSH backends. `target="content"` is unaffected.

Note the `rg` path (`_search_files_rg`) already tolerates exit 1; only the `find` fallback fails closed, so the bug appears only where `rg` is absent.

## Steps to Reproduce

Any tree with an unreadable directory beside a readable match:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/repro/readable /tmp/repro/blocked
touch /tmp/repro/readable/probe-target.txt
chmod 000 /tmp/repro/blocked
```

Then the exact pipeline the tool builds:

```bash
$ bash -c "set -o pipefail; find /tmp/repro -type f ! -name '.*' -name 'probe-target*' -print 2>/dev/null | head -n 51"
/tmp/repro/readable/probe-target.txt      # <-- the match IS printed
$ echo $?
1                                          # <-- yet the exit code is 1
```

So `search_files(target="files", path="/tmp/repro", pattern="probe-target*")` returns the error above instead of the file. Searching a clean subtree (`/tmp/repro/readable`) succeeds, which is what makes this look intermittent.

Originally observed on `/tmp` and `/home/<user>` where the unreadable directories are `systemd-private-*`, `snap-private-tmp`, and a root-owned mount under the home directory.

## Expected Behavior

A permission error in one directory should be a **partial** result, not a total failure: return the matches that were found, optionally noting that some directories were not readable. This is how `find` itself behaves, and how `_search_files_rg()` already treats exit 1.

## Actual Behavior

All matches are discarded and the caller receives `total_count: 0` plus `"File search failed while running bounded find traversal."`, with no indication that results existed or that the cause was merely a permission boundary.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.21.1 (2026.9.7), upstream `fa756922`, install method: git
- Reproduced on macOS 26.6.2 (arm64) **and** Ubuntu 24.04.4 (kernel 6.8.0-138) — local backend in both cases
- Component: tools / file

## Suggested fix

Treat a non-zero exit **with a usable stdout payload** as partial success, gating on the payload rather than the exit code alone:

```python
partial_permission = result.exit_code == 1 and bool(raw_files)
if result.exit_code not in {0, 124} and not bounded_sigpipe and not partial_permission:
    ...
```

EACCES stderr is already suppressed by the existing `2>/dev/null` on the pipeline, so no extra suppression is needed.

Importantly this must **not** become a blanket amnesty. These stay fatal, and the existing contracts in `tests/tools/test_search_budget_truncation.py` continue to hold:

- exit 1 with an **empty** payload — a genuine failure,
- exit 2 (a real `find` error) with or without partial output,
- SIGPIPE (141) with fewer rows than the fetch bound.

I deliberately did **not** widen the `rg` branch. `rg --files` also exits 2 on an EACCES partial walk, but `test_search_files_engine_selection.py::test_rg_partial_output_with_error_exit_fails_closed` pins rg exit 2 + partial output as fatal on purpose, and `rg --no-messages` suppresses the message without changing the exit code. Relaxing it would break that documented contract, so the `rg` case would need its own decision (e.g. distinguishing EACCES from other exit-2 causes) rather than a widened code check.

I have this running locally with a regression test covering: exit 1 with matches, exit 1 with no payload, exit 2 with partial output, a short SIGPIPE, and an end-to-end case using a real `0000` directory beside a real match. Happy to open a PR if the approach looks right.
