issues.title: Hosted (Team Gateway) agents: Portal agent page gives no link to the shared Hermes Agent bot on Discord/Slack/Teams

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: platform/discord
labels.description: Discord bot adapter

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

labels.name: comp/portal
labels.description: Nous portal / Hermes Pro / hosted-Hermes path

issues.body:
## Context

On a Hermes Cloud instance fronted by the Team Gateway (relay), messaging works through the shared verified bot "Hermes Agent" — the user never runs their own bot. This is documented for Telegram ("Via Team Gateway", QR/link flow) but there's no equivalent discoverable flow for Discord/Slack/Teams.

## Problem

On the Portal's agent page, once a Discord account is linked, the "linked accounts" list shows only the raw snowflake ID (e.g. `784475678322803276`). There is:

- no bot name, invite/profile link, or "how to reach me" instructions
- no indication that DMs must go to the shared "Hermes Agent" bot
- no hint that Discord requires sharing a server with a bot before you can DM it (so the user must also find/join a server the bot is in)

The hosted dashboard's Channels page can't help either — it correctly says "agent's accounts are linked from Nous Portal" and defers to the Portal, which then dead-ends.

## Actual user journey (real case)

1. User tries to add their hosted agent to Discord, assumes a personal bot (self-hosted docs describe exactly that), finds nothing.
2. Dashboard → Channels → "accounts are linked from Nous Portal."
3. Portal → agent page → linked account shows a bare numeric ID.
4. Dead end. The only working path was constructing `https://discord.com/users/<bot_id>` from the relay bot ID — which a normal user has no way to know.

## Suggested fix

On the agent page's Message platforms section (and/or in the hosted dashboard's Channels page when it's relay-fronted), show per platform:

- the shared bot's name + profile/deep link (e.g. `https://discord.com/users/<bot_id>` for Discord)
- a one-line instruction: "DM this bot; you must share a server with it (join the Nous Research Discord: <invite>)"
- ideally a "Get link code" / direct-message CTA like the Telegram card

Even a static "Talk to your agent on Discord →" link would remove the main friction.

issues.title: repair_tool_call cannot bridge a bare MCP catalog name, and its fuzzy step silently mis-routes hallucinated mcp_* names onto different real tools

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: tool/mcp
labels.description: MCP client and OAuth

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
**Summary**

`repair_tool_call` (agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py) ends in
`get_close_matches(lowered, agent.valid_tool_names, n=1, cutoff=0.7)` over ALL valid names. With MCP
tools registered as `mcp_<server>_<tool>` this has two failure modes:

1. **The bare catalog name is never repaired.** Prompts and skills naturally teach the MCP catalog name
   (`entity_search`). The runtime name carries a ~19-char server prefix, so
   `SequenceMatcher("entity_search", "mcp_example_server_entity_search").ratio()` = **0.578** < 0.7 →
   `None` → "Tool 'entity_search' does not exist" — and, because one invalid name voids the WHOLE
   batch (`conversation_loop.py`: "Skipped: another tool call in this turn used an invalid name"),
   every valid sibling call in that turn is discarded and re-issued, plus the full tool catalog is
   appended to the conversation on each miss. Measured on one deployment: ~10% of interactive sessions
   start with exactly this slip; ~25–29 valid calls skipped per 14 days.

2. **Hallucinated prefixed names are silently mis-routed.** The shared prefix inflates every ratio
   BETWEEN `mcp_` tools past 0.7, so a name that does not exist resolves to a *different* real tool.
   Measured against a 51-tool MCP server — **12 of 12** hallucinated names hit a real, different tool:

   | emitted (does not exist) | fuzzy result (real tool) | ratio |
   |---|---|---|
   | `mcp_<s>_entity_delete` | `mcp_<s>_entity_update` | 0.906 |
   | `mcp_<s>_entity_get` | `mcp_<s>_entity_create` | 0.918 |
   | `mcp_<s>_send_email` | `mcp_<s>_read_recent_emails` | 0.818 |
   | `mcp_<s>_drive_write` | `mcp_<s>_drive_read` | 0.915 |
   | `mcp_<s>_calendar_delete` | `mcp_<s>_calendar_update` | 0.912 |
   | `mcp_<s>_contacts_write` | `mcp_<s>_contacts_read` | 0.923 |
   | `mcp_<s>_kanban_list` (a CORE tool, wrongly prefixed) | `mcp_<s>_list_goals` | 0.780 |

   The last row fired in production twice (a cron job wanted the core `kanban_list`; the repaired
   call ran `list_goals` instead). Two BARE catalog names also mis-route today
   (`drive_search → web_search`, `calendar_create → kanban_create`). The repair is announced only via
   `print()` (conversation_loop.py), so it is invisible in file logs and the persisted assistant
   message stores the REPAIRED name — the mis-route cannot be counted after the fact.

**Proposed change** (kept the upstream #14784/#33007/#47967 behavior byte-identical for core tools):

- Before the fuzzy step: if exactly one registered `mcp_` tool equals `<prefix> + normalized` (prefixes
  taken from the tool→server map `_mcp_tool_server_names`, never by splitting names), return it;
  two or more hits → return None (ambiguous), never fall through to fuzzy.
- An `mcp_`-prefixed emission is never fuzzy-matched: exact, or the prefix stripped down to exactly one
  CORE tool name, else None (the existing "does not exist" error, which the model self-corrects).
- The fuzzy step runs over NON-`mcp_` names only, cutoff unchanged.
- Log each repair via the module logger (`logger.info("… %s -> %s normalized=%s")`) instead of `print`.

A reference implementation (as a build-time patch against 0.18.0, with a 17-arm test file whose
fixture carries the verbatim function body) is available on request. Under the 0.19+ `mcp__server__tool`
naming the same rules apply with the new prefix constants (`MCP_TOOL_NAME_PREFIX`, `_MCP_NAME_DELIM`).

prs.title: Declining the gateway service in setup no longer gets it installed by the installer (#157677)
prs.body:
Answering No to "Install the gateway service?" during `install.sh` setup didn't stick: the installer's next step asked again and installed a service anyway, even when you answered No to both of its follow-up questions. Now a No in setup means nothing gets installed, and the installer just tells you how to install it later.

Setup's recorded answer (`gateway.service_install_choice`) now decides `hermes gateway install --if-missing`, the step `install.sh` and `install.ps1` run right after setup.

**Live repro:** real `install.sh` fresh install at main 95a1d228, run as a normal user on a systemd host (Debian trixie, systemd as PID 1 with a running user manager; no container markers visible, so setup offers the service the way it does on a laptop). Same keystrokes on both legs: `hermes setup gateway` → No, then `bash install.sh --stage gateway`.

| | main 95a1d228 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| After No in setup | `Start the gateway now after installing the service? [Y/n]` → n, `…automatically on login/boot…? [Y/n]` → n, then `✓ User service installed!` | `Gateway service skipped (declined in setup). Install it any time: hermes gateway install` |
| `~/.config/systemd/user/` | `hermes-gateway.service` (disabled, inactive) | empty |
| `service_install_choice` | overwritten `decline` → `install` | stays `decline` |
| Yes in setup, then installer stage | `✓ Gateway service already installed` | same: unit `enabled`, `active`, choice `install` |
| Setup never asked (choice `null`), installer stage, answer No | installs a unit (same prompts as row 1) | asks setup's one question `[y/N]`; No → `No service installed. Run: hermes gateway run`, choice `decline`, no unit |

Root cause: `--if-missing` only checked "is a service installed?" and then took the explicit `hermes gateway install` path, which never reads the recorded choice and writes the unit whatever its start-now/start-on-login answers are.

- `--if-missing` delegates to `gateway_setup_service.install_after_setup`: already installed → no-op; recorded decline → one line and exit 0; otherwise setup's own `ensure_gateway_service(context="setup", interactive=True)`, so the question, the recording and the container/no-service-manager guidance are the ones setup uses. (Before this, inside a container the stage failed the install with the user-scope refusal; now it prints setup's container guidance.)
- Plain `hermes gateway install` is unchanged: it stays the explicit opt-in.
- One invariant test on the real config + install path with only the OS supervisor faked (`tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service_choice.py`): red on main (unit file written), green here. The existing `--if-missing` test is re-pointed at the new seam.
- Developer docs (`gateway-internals.md` § Optional service installation) now say what the installer step does.

Not covered: macOS launchd and Windows Scheduled Task legs were not run live. They take the same `ensure_gateway_service` path setup already uses on those OSes; on main the same bug applies to them, because `install.ps1` calls the same `--if-missing`.

Fixes #157677

prs.title: feat(bots): Bot Chat shows a "Waiting on teammates" card for message_agent deliveries
prs.body:
A bot's Bot Chat now shows a **"Waiting on teammates"** card above the composer. It lists every `message_agent` delivery from that bot that hasn't settled: who it went to, where it stands (queued / picked up / working / **waiting on you** / failed with a plain-words reason / outcome unknown), and how long it's been. **Open** jumps to the teammate's chat, where its question or approval card is. **Dismiss** hides a failure.

## Problem

When bot A messages bot B, A's chat goes quiet until B replies or A's wait times out. If B is stuck on a question only the user can answer, nothing in A's chat says so. The user sees a silent bot and either waits or sends the request again. Resending is the risky part: a delivery whose outcome is unknown may already have run on B's side.

## Live evidence (real `hermes serve` + Desktop, two real bot turns)

Rig: native Electron (headless Xvnc, driven over CDP) spawning its own `hermes serve` from each tree, scratch `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`, three Bot Mode profiles: **Launch lead** (default), **Brand designer** (`ada`) and **Offline analyst** (`kai`, whose model endpoint is deliberately unreachable). Real inference on a cheap Nous-hosted model. Every message below was typed into Launch lead's Bot Chat composer, and Launch lead's model called `message_agent` itself. No fixtures, no injected events. Base = `origin/main` 749cb638ff4 (renderer and serve); head = this branch.

| | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| B parked on a clarify, A's chat | nothing above the composer: the last line is "Both messages are queued to @ada" ([1](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/fc9c2c1ce21a753542e2e4a47cc044a6/raw/1-base-sender-nothing.png)), while B's tab holds the question ([2](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/fc9c2c1ce21a753542e2e4a47cc044a6/raw/2-base-teammate-parked.png)) | `Brand designer · Waiting on you — answer its question` ([4](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/fc9c2c1ce21a753542e2e4a47cc044a6/raw/4-head-waiting-on-you.png)) |
| B's turn running | nothing | `Working on it` ([3](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/894cebe6b0086a98a24f616e841db101/raw/e2cae8f61c463463dacb65e7bb6036818d17e71e/bw-1-working.png)), then the row drops once B's reply settles |
| Open | n/a | fronts B's tab with its clarify card ([5](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/fc9c2c1ce21a753542e2e4a47cc044a6/raw/5-head-open-teammate.png)); answering it moved the row to `Working on it`, then off the card |
| Second request behind a parked turn; B's serve killed mid-question; C's endpoint down | nothing | `Queued` / `Waiting on you` / `Outcome unknown` with the never-resent note / `Failed: Connection error.`, ages counting ([6](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/fc9c2c1ce21a753542e2e4a47cc044a6/raw/6-head-queued-waiting-unknown-failed.png)) |
| B's provider rejects its key | nothing | `Failed: its model provider rejected the key` ([7](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/fc9c2c1ce21a753542e2e4a47cc044a6/raw/7-head-failed-reason.png)) |
| Dismiss on that failure | n/a | the card disappears; the id is persisted in `localStorage` ([8](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/fc9c2c1ce21a753542e2e4a47cc044a6/raw/8-head-dismissed.png)) |
| C's endpoint down, retries exhausted | nothing | `Offline analyst · Failed: Connection error.` with Open and a Dismiss (×) ([9](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/894cebe6b0086a98a24f616e841db101/raw/e2cae8f61c463463dacb65e7bb6036818d17e71e/bw-4-recovered.png)) |
| The status poll itself fails (gateway process stopped with SIGSTOP, real request timeout) | n/a | the last rows stay, greyed, with `Couldn't refresh — showing the last known state.` ([10](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/894cebe6b0086a98a24f616e841db101/raw/e2cae8f61c463463dacb65e7bb6036818d17e71e/bw-3-stale.png)); after SIGCONT the next poll restores full opacity and drops the line ([9](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/894cebe6b0086a98a24f616e841db101/raw/e2cae8f61c463463dacb65e7bb6036818d17e71e/bw-4-recovered.png)) |
| Dismiss with a draft typed in the composer | n/a | the card goes, the draft stays in the composer, no turn starts (user-message count unchanged) ([11](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/894cebe6b0086a98a24f616e841db101/raw/e2cae8f61c463463dacb65e7bb6036818d17e71e/bw-5-dismissed-draft-kept.png)) |

### Screenshots, current head (re-shot on 1c217fa1edd, after the card moved to the shared `Button` and theme tokens)

**Working on it** (restyled card: shared ghost `Open`, `--ui-*` tokens)
![head: working](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/894cebe6b0086a98a24f616e841db101/raw/e2cae8f61c463463dacb65e7bb6036818d17e71e/bw-1-working.png)

**Failed: Connection error.** with Open and Dismiss (×)
![head: failed](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/894cebe6b0086a98a24f616e841db101/raw/e2cae8f61c463463dacb65e7bb6036818d17e71e/bw-4-recovered.png)

**Couldn't refresh** — the poll timed out against a SIGSTOPped gateway: last rows kept, greyed, stale line shown (the composer's own "Reconnecting to Hermes…" placeholder is the app's existing reaction to the same outage)
![head: couldn't refresh](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/894cebe6b0086a98a24f616e841db101/raw/e2cae8f61c463463dacb65e7bb6036818d17e71e/bw-3-stale.png)

**Dismiss with a draft typed**: card gone, draft still in the composer, nothing sent
![head: dismissed, draft kept](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/894cebe6b0086a98a24f616e841db101/raw/e2cae8f61c463463dacb65e7bb6036818d17e71e/bw-5-dismissed-draft-kept.png)

**Base**: nothing above the composer
![base: nothing](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/fc9c2c1ce21a753542e2e4a47cc044a6/raw/1-base-sender-nothing.png)

Shots 4, 5, 6 in the table (Waiting on you, Open fronting the teammate's question, the Queued / Outcome unknown mix) are from the first live run, before the restyle; their rows and wording are unchanged, only the button and colour tokens moved. They were not re-shot: Waiting on you needs a teammate turn parked on a clarify, and Outcome unknown needs the teammate's backend killed mid-question.

Every screenshot was vision-checked: no error banners, no toasts, no raw keys, nothing clipped.

### What the live run broke (fixed in this PR)
- **A request queued behind a parked turn showed "Waiting on you" too.** Bot A sent B two requests, B's first turn parked on a clarify, and both rows lit up. The open prompt now marks only the delivery whose admission is the running one (`tools/bot_delivery_status.py`, d740ff03961). The invariant test was red on the previous head and is green now.
- **Failures printed the raw reason code** (`Failed: provider_auth_or_access`). Every typed reason now has plain words in en / ja / zh / zh-Hant. An unclassified failure shows the owner's own error line instead (`Failed: Connection error.`).
- **Ages froze** at their first value ("4s" for minutes), because an unchanged poll result does not re-render. Ages are now computed against the query's last fetch time.

## What changed

**Backend: `bot_delivery.list`, read-only**
- `tools/bot_delivery_status.py` reads the receipts that already exist under each target profile's `runtime/bot_live_delivery/<id>.json`. It keeps the ones stamped `author.id == "bot:<sender>"` and maps each to a strip state:
  - Settled replies drop off.
  - Failed, cancelled and ambiguous receipts stay for 24 h with a typed `reason`. Ambiguous → `unknown_outcome`.
- `gateway/session_teammate_waits.py` is the canonical owner handler, the one the local Desktop talks to. For each target it joins two things, each read under that target authority's own `owner_scope`:
  - the admission row (`queued` vs `started` → working)
  - the open prompts on the target's live session, via a new non-pruning `PendingControls.waiting_kinds()` read, applied only to the delivery whose admission is running
- The sender is the connection's own profile, so a bot only lists its own requests.
- `tui_gateway/methods_bot_relay.py` gets the same method for the legacy sidecar. That transport reports only the durable admission state; it holds no target authority, so it can't show "waiting on you".
- The contract is declared in `tui_gateway/contracts/groups_bot_relay.py`; `apps/shared` was regenerated.
- Nothing is written, claimed, cancelled or resent. A test asserts that receipt bytes and mtimes are unchanged and that no lock file appears.
- A poll re-parses only receipts written since the last one. The cache is keyed per directory on `(inode, mtime_ns, size)`, which works because receipts are replaced atomically. Settled history is cached as its status alone and is never deleted.

**Desktop**
- `hermes-bots/teammate-waits.tsx` renders the card in the `composer.top` slot. It polls on the roster's 5 s cadence. It renders nothing in other chats, when nothing is pending, or on gateways without the method (JSON-RPC method-not-found only). Any other failed poll (timeout, dropped socket) keeps the last rows, greyed, under a quiet "Couldn't refresh" line. It shows the do-not-resend rule as a tooltip, and as an inline line whenever an outcome is unknown. Open and Dismiss are SDK `Button`s. Open is disabled for a teammate the cached roster doesn't list yet, so it never falls back to the sender's own chat.
- New SDK door `useComposerSession()` (via `sdk/areas.ts`; `sdk/index.ts` is untouched). A `composer.top` contribution can now tell which session's composer it sits in, so a tile and the main composer each answer for their own chat. It lives in `composer-top-slot.tsx`, which keeps `ChatBar` within its size and complexity caps.
- Copy ships in en / ja / zh / zh-Hant (`teammate-wait-locales.ts`).

## Tests
- `tests/gateway/test_session_teammate_waits.py`: 3 passed via `scripts/run_tests.sh`.
  - A poll does not re-read unchanged receipts, and it re-reads an atomically rewritten one. This test was red on the pre-fix-round head.
  - Only this sender's unsettled deliveries are listed; settled and stale rows drop; ambiguous → `unknown_outcome`; the mailbox is untouched.
  - The owner join reports `working`, and `waiting_on_you` (clarify) from a real `PendingControls`, without re-publishing the prompt. A delivery queued behind the parked turn stays `queued`. Once the clarify is answered, the row is `working` again.
- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/teammate-waits.test.ts`: 5 passed (vitest).
  - A timeout rejects so the query keeps its rows, while method-not-found is an empty list. An unknown target resolves to no row, never the sender. Both tests were red on the pre-fix-round head.
  - The strip belongs only to a bot's own canonical chat (tip or durable id).
  - Only failures can be dismissed.
  - A failure reads in plain words in every locale and never shows the raw code; an unclassified one shows the owner's error line.
- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/teammate-waits-row.test.tsx`: 1 passed (vitest). Open and Dismiss rendered inside a form never submit it (the strip sits in the composer's form). Red on 9ad3586d2d2 (both clicks submitted), green on 1c217fa1edd; confirmed live in shot 11.
- `tsc --noEmit -p apps/desktop` is clean; eslint and prettier are clean on the touched files; `python scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking.

## Related
- Complements #116440 (@tobenwarrior, the bot-to-bot thread view). This card shows **status**; #116440 shows the **conversation**. The only shared file is a 5-line hunk in `hermes-bots/i18n.ts` (locale wiring).
- Refs #101124: the sender-side delivery still also appears as a background-process row in A's transcript (visible in the screenshots). Hiding that row is left for a follow-up.
- Refs #138313, #91911.

## NOT_COVERED
- **The review-round styling was not re-screenshotted.** The screenshots above predate it. The changes are: SDK `Button`s for Open/Dismiss, no tooltip on the X, defined theme tokens for the card and failure colour, and the stale line.
- Approval answered by Reject / Always allow, Dismiss, several teammates at once, remote/Cloud connections and packaged builds were not driven live on the rebased head.
- **A clarify only parks while someone has the teammate's chat open.** With no viewer attached, the local adapter declines it at once (`gateway/session_local.py::_unanswerable_clarify`, by design), and the teammate carries on. The live run kept B's Bot Chat open in a background tab.
- Cross-connection (relayed) and peer deliveries aren't listed. Their receipts live on another machine, so the card covers local teammates only.
- On the legacy sidecar transport the card can't show "waiting on you".
- Seen in the live run, outside this PR: an unreachable custom endpoint settles with `reason: "unknown"` (the owner's classifier doesn't map `Connection error.`). The card shows the error line for it.

## Live re-run on the rebased head (5d29c5bb, approval kind)

Same rig as above, on `origin/main` fe8b920 and this head. The teammate `arquiteto` has `approvals.mode: manual`, and Launch lead asks it via `message_agent` to run `python3 -c "print('approval-routing-probe')"`. This is the shape of a Cloud support report: an `execute_code` approval timed out after 5 minutes in a teammate's chat nobody had open.

| | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Teammate parked on an approval, sender's chat | nothing above the composer ([shot](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/46dc9981914d9e57e506f145424fe4f4/raw/base-approval-A.png)) | `Arquiteto · Waiting on you — approve or deny · 26s · Open` ([shot](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/46dc9981914d9e57e506f145424fe4f4/raw/head-approval-A.png)) |
| Open | n/a | Arquiteto's chat with the Command card and Reject / Always allow… / Run ([shot](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/46dc9981914d9e57e506f145424fe4f4/raw/head-approval2-B-card.png)) |
| Run, back in the sender's chat | n/a | `Working on it` ([shot](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/46dc9981914d9e57e506f145424fe4f4/raw/head-approval2-working.png)), then the row drops once the reply settles ([shot](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/46dc9981914d9e57e506f145424fe4f4/raw/head-approval2-settled.png)) |
| Approval left to time out | timed out unseen | row stays `Waiting on you` for the whole wait, then clears; the sender relays the timeout ([shot](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/46dc9981914d9e57e506f145424fe4f4/raw/head-timeout-settled.png)) |
| Clarify (regression) | n/a | `Waiting on you — answer its question` ([shot](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/46dc9981914d9e57e506f145424fe4f4/raw/head-clarify-A.png)), Open lands on the clarify card ([shot](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/46dc9981914d9e57e506f145424fe4f4/raw/head-clarify-B-card.png)) |

`state.db` readback: B's terminal rows record the approval (`Command required approval (script execution via -e/-c flag)`, then output `approval-routing-probe-2`, exit 0), and the timed-out one shows `BLOCKED: Command timed out without user response`.

The rebase onto main also moves the teammate-wait reads off the removed old session store and onto the persistence interface (5d29c5bb).

Fixes #149375.

prs.title: fix(gateway): remote-media delivery finds the sandbox the turn registered
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

On a non-docker remote terminal backend (`ssh`, `daytona`, `modal`, `vercel_sandbox`, …), the
remote-media fallback from #466 never ran on a gateway turn: a `MEDIA:` tag pointing at a file the
agent had just written inside the sandbox was always dropped as "not found on this host".

The sandbox is registered under the key `_resolve_container_task_id` builds while the turn's session
vars are bound — `session:<session_key>` for every backend except per-session-isolated docker.
`_active_remote_env` looks it up after `_extract_response_content` has left that context, where
`clear_session_vars` has reset the key to `""`, so the resolver answers `"default"`, the lookup
misses, and `fetch_remote_media` returns before its `try` (no log line, no attempt).

The key is already a parameter one frame above the lookup —
`filter_media_delivery_paths(media_files, session_key=session_key)` → `_validated_delivery_path(…,
session_key, …)` — and was simply not passed down. This threads it and makes it **authoritative**:
the scoped lookup runs first, the context-less one only as a fallback. Order matters beyond the
dropped file — when anything is cached under the `"default"` key (a CLI or cron task's environment),
consulting that first fetches the artifact out of an unrelated session's sandbox, which `main` does
today (see *Lookup order* below).

The key is bound through a new `scoped_session_key` rather than turned into `session:<key>` inside
`media_fetch`, so `_resolve_container_task_id` stays the single place that decides a registry key and
docker's per-session and profile-scoped shapes remain its business.

## Related Issue

Fixes #130875

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/session_context.py` — `scoped_session_key()`, next to the existing
  `scoped_current_session_id()` and with the same contract: task-local, restores on exit, never
  touches `os.environ`.
- `gateway/media_fetch.py` — `fetch_remote_media(path, session_key="")`; a supplied key is looked up
  first with that key bound, and the context-less lookup is the fallback. `_active_remote_env` keeps
  its signature and its behaviour.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py` — `_validated_delivery_path` passes the `session_key` it already
  receives to `fetch_remote_media`.
- `tests/gateway/test_remote_media_fetch.py` — two invariant tests (below).

Nothing in the policy moves: the denylist, `fetch_realpath` symlink screening, the in-sandbox size
cap and the strict-mode early return are all unchanged, and the fetched copy is still validated
before it is delivered.

## How to Test

1. **The regression test is red on `main`** and green with this change:

   ```console
   $ git stash push gateway/      # tests only, on the fix branch
   $ scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_remote_media_fetch.py
   ✗ tests/gateway/test_remote_media_fetch.py (4✓ 1✗, 0.9s)
     FAILED ...::test_sandbox_artifact_is_delivered_after_the_turn_context_is_cleared
     E       AssertionError: assert [] == [b'hello from sandbox']
   $ git stash pop
   $ scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_remote_media_fetch.py
   ✓ tests/gateway/test_remote_media_fetch.py (5✓, 0.5s)
   ```

2. **The two tests assert a relation, not a snapshot.** The first registers a sandbox through the
   real `_resolve_container_task_id` with the turn's session vars bound, clears them (the handler has
   returned), caches an unrelated environment under `"default"`, and then asserts
   `filter_media_delivery_paths(…, session_key=…)` delivers the *session's* bytes and never reads the
   unrelated one — `_active_remote_env` is *not* patched out, which is why the existing tests in that
   file could not see any of this. The second pins the b499ab11 behaviour: a sandbox keyed by session
   id (what per-session-isolated docker does) still resolves with no `session_key` at all.

3. **End to end**, on a deployment with `terminal.backend: ssh`: ask the agent for a file it has just
   written in the sandbox. Before, the gateway logged
   `Skipping MEDIA directive path (not found on this host): /tmp/<file>` and the chat got the text
   with no attachment; after, the file is fetched into the document cache and uploaded.

Platform tested: Amazon Linux 2023 / aarch64 (Python 3.11 for the suite, 3.13 in the deployment).

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Amazon Linux 2023 (aarch64)

On the one unchecked box, so the claim is accurate rather than convenient. With
`scripts/run_tests.sh` (not bare `pytest`), over the files that cover what this touches —
`tests/gateway/test_remote_media_fetch.py`, `test_platform_base.py`, `test_session_env.py`,
`test_session_context_inheritance.py`, `test_media_tag_separator.py`,
`test_async_delivery_capability.py`, `tests/cron/test_media_delivery_parity.py`,
`tests/agent/test_generated_media_durable.py`, `tests/agent/test_session_source.py`,
`tests/plugins/platforms/photon/test_outbound_media.py`, `tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py`:

```
=== Summary: 11 files, 173 tests passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (100% complete) in 2.6s (5 workers) ===
```

I did not claim a clean full-suite run because this environment does not give one: the
`tests/gateway/test_api_*` files fail here on an **unmodified** `main` as well (they bind sockets) —
`test_api_server_jobs.py` + `test_api_notification_outcomes.py` give `9 passed, 14 failed` with my
branch's changes stashed away. Nothing I touched is in their path. Happy to paste more of the
comparison if it is useful.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — docstrings only; the new
  helper and the retry each carry the reason they exist
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A, no new config
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — ContextVar bookkeeping and an existing lookup; no filesystem, process or path handling added
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A, no tool surface change

## Screenshots / Logs

Field evidence from the deployment this was found on — the drop, and the file sitting on the sandbox
host one second earlier:

```
2026-10-01 19:04:44,562 WARNING gateway.platforms.base: Skipping MEDIA directive path
  (not found on this host): /tmp/deep-code-review.md
```

```console
$ ls -l /tmp/deep-code-review.md          # on the ssh sandbox host
-rw-rw-r--. 1 ec2-user ec2-user 29001 Oct  1 19:04 /tmp/deep-code-review.md
```

No `Fetched remote media` line exists in any retained `agent.log` there: the fallback was never
reaching its `try`.

### Deliberately left out

Two things the issue discusses that do not belong in this diff:

- **`ensure_task_env()` instead of `get_active_env()`**, which would also bring a *cold* sandbox up
  during delivery (the fix `tools/image_source.py` took for the same class of miss, #62825). That is
  a behaviour change — an ssh handshake on the delivery path — and deserves its own issue.
- **The lanes that pass no `session_key`**: `gateway/run_turn.py`
  (`_run_background_task_inner`), `gateway/run_notifications.py` (`_deliver_media_from_response`) and
  the two in `cron/scheduler_delivery.py`. They have a session to hand; threading them is a follow-up
  once this shape is agreed.

### One thing a reviewer will reasonably ask about

`_resolve_container_task_id` has a fourth branch for persistent, **profile-scoped** docker that keys
off the session PROFILE — another ContextVar `clear_session_vars` resets and `scoped_session_key`
does not rebind. Measured rather than reasoned, with `TERMINAL_ENV=docker` and
`TERMINAL_CONTAINER_PERSISTENT=true`:

```
docker_profile_scoped            : True
key registered during the turn    : 'profile:tenant-b'
first lookup (today, unchanged)   : 'default'
retry lookup (this PR)            : 'default'
retry changes the key?            : False
```

The retry is a **no-op** for that branch: it computes the same `"default"` key the first lookup
already uses on `main` today, so it cannot reach a container the unfixed lookup would not have
reached. The only branch whose answer changes is `if not scope.docker_profile_scoped: return
f"session:{session_key}"` — the non-docker sandboxes this bug is about. That is why the key is bound
alone, and the retry site now says so in a comment. If you would rather fail closed there explicitly,
gating the retry on the backend is a one-liner — say the word.


### Lookup order

Raised in review, and it was right — with the first revision's ordering an environment cached under
the context-less `"default"` key won over the session the caller named. Worth stating precisely,
because the scenario is **not** something the patch introduced: the same regression test fails on
unmodified `main` the same way, delivering the unrelated sandbox's bytes.

```console
# tests only, against upstream main (c67b0a1d)
E  AssertionError: assert [b'from an unrelated sandbox'] == [b'hello from sandbox']

# tests only, against this PR's first revision (bda0181c, unscoped lookup first)
E  AssertionError: assert [b'from an unrelated sandbox'] == [b'hello from sandbox']

# with the current revision
✓ tests/gateway/test_remote_media_fetch.py (5✓)
```

So the fix is the one the review asked for — an explicitly supplied `session_key` decides, and the
context-less lookup is only the fallback for callers that pass none (`run_turn`,
`run_notifications`, `cron`, the CLI). The regression now carries both registry entries, as
requested.

prs.title: fix(desktop): make guarded model switches commit before reporting success
prs.body:
## Summary

An established Desktop session can report `/model` success from the separate slash worker before the live session has switched. A guarded change, such as a large-context provider switch, can then leave the live agent and persisted route on the previous provider while the user sees “Model switched.”

Route typed `/model <args>` through the existing `config.set model` live-session transaction. Its confirmation, deferred, and error states now reach Desktop. The confirmed retry applies the live provider/model/endpoint before success is reported. Desktop also preserves warnings on confirmed retries and labels deferred canonical picks as queued.

## Evidence and tests

- The new slash confirmation regression fails on clean `fe8b920c` because it enters the separate slash worker, and passes with this patch.
- Focused gateway tests: 34 passed, including large-context confirmation, live provider/base URL, persisted session route, and busy-session deferral.
- Desktop Vitest: 53 passed; Desktop typecheck and targeted ESLint passed.
- Desktop production build passed on Windows with the pinned toolchain.
- `scripts/check --only health` passed.

The full Windows server test file had 611 passes and 23 failures in existing Windows process-reader and POSIX-style SSH path tests; none were changed model-switch tests. The full `scripts/check` run flags an unchanged `.gitattributes` shim-generation mismatch on this Windows checkout. The pre-commit hook itself fails at its shell quoting step on Windows, so the commit was made after running the checks above manually.

This is a draft until a user-facing Desktop run verifies the switch against an established session.

prs.title: fix(tools): select latest cron output by modification time
prs.body:
## What changed and why

This fixes `_latest_job_output_excerpt()` selecting cron output by lexicographic file name rather than by the time the output was last saved. The helper now selects the greatest `st_mtime_ns` value and uses the file name only as a deterministic tie breaker. The selected path is reused in the truncated-output hint so the excerpt and its source reference always match.

## How to test

1. Create two `.md` files for one cron job where the lexicographically later file has an older modification time.
2. Call `_latest_job_output_excerpt()` with a small `max_chars` value.
3. Confirm that the excerpt and the `full output` path refer to the newer file by modification time.
4. Run:
   `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/cron/test_cronjob_output_excerpt.py tests/cron/test_cron_context_from.py`

## Testing

- Passed: 24 tests across `tests/cron/test_cronjob_output_excerpt.py` and `tests/cron/test_cron_context_from.py`.
- Manual model-backed cron execution was not run because this private background-completion helper requires a configured provider and an active cron run. The regression test exercises the real filesystem-backed helper path.

## Platforms

- Tested on Linux under WSL2 with Python 3.11.15.
- Native macOS and Windows were not run. The change uses portable `pathlib.Path.stat()` metadata and does not introduce platform-specific behavior.

## Related issues

None.

prs.title: feat(cli): opt-in weekly_usage status-bar field (wk N%)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in `weekly_usage` field to the CLI status bar (both `display.cli_layout` styles):
`wk 49%`, the share of the provider subscription's weekly allowance already spent. Hermes already
fetches this number for `/usage` (Anthropic's `seven_day` window, Codex's 7-day window, plugin
providers that report one, such as OpenCode Go). The bar never shows it, so checking how much of
the week is left means leaving the conversation for `/usage`.

```
120 cols: ☤ claude-opus-4 │ -- │ wk 49% │ 12m
 60 cols: ☤ claude-opus-4 · -- · wk 49% · 12m
 40 cols: ☤ claude-opus-4 · 12m
```

(Rendered from this branch with `fields: [model, context_pct, weekly_usage, duration]` and a
cached Anthropic snapshot of 12% session, 48.2% week, 61% Opus week. Only the account-wide week
shows, rounded up.)

How it reads the number:

- **Nothing on the render path touches the network.** The bar reads `agent.account_usage_cache`,
  the cache the model picker already uses, and calls `refresh_account_usage_async`, which runs the
  fetch on a daemon thread and throttles it to one try per provider every `REFRESH_AFTER_S` (120 s),
  failed tries included. The reading shows on the next repaint after it lands (a keystroke, a
  running turn, or the idle redraw where `display.cli_refresh_interval` is set). Measured cost per
  repaint: 4–17 µs.
- **Opt-in, like `git_branch` and `total_tokens`.** The default bar never starts a usage fetch: the
  probe runs only when `weekly_usage` is listed in `display.status_bar.fields`.
- **No usable reading means no segment.** That covers a repaint before the first fetch lands, a
  provider without a usage API, and a snapshot past the cache's 15-minute staleness bound
  (`snapshot_is_stale`), so a stale number never shows as live. It also stays hidden for a provider
  with no weekly window, and `/usage` shows why. A provider whose usage API answers with windows but
  no weekly one (an OpenRouter key with a credit limit) is asked again only once that reading goes
  stale. One that answers with no windows at all (an Anthropic API key, which costs no request; an
  OpenRouter key without a limit) leaves the cache nothing to store, so it is asked again every two
  minutes.
- **One login's reading never stands for a pool.** With a credential pool of two or more credentials
  the segment stays hidden, the same rule the `/model` picker applies to its usage gauge: the
  cached reading belongs to one login, not necessarily the one serving the session. The pool is
  the session's in-memory one (the agent's, or the CLI's before an agent exists), so the repaint
  never reads `auth.json`. It counts the pool through a new `CredentialPool.entry_count()`, which
  skips the pool's lock: `select()` holds that lock across token refreshes and `auth.json` writes,
  and a repaint must not wait on those.
- **Only the account-scoped weekly window counts.** Anthropic's Opus and Sonnet weeks are
  `scope="model"` and never stand for the account. The labels the fetchers give that window
  ("Current week", "Weekly") sit in one constant, and two tests run the Anthropic fetcher and the
  Codex labeller to fail if either label drifts. A non-finite reading is skipped.
- **Rounded up**, so 48.2% reads 49%: the question is how close the wall is. Float noise is
  rounded off first, so 7.000000000000001 reads 7%, not 8%. The colour is green, yellow from 50%
  and red from 80%, using the existing `status-bar-good/warn/critical` skin keys.
- **Width tiers like `cache_hit`:** shown at ≥52 columns, dropped below.
- **A failing read never costs the bar.** `weekly_usage_percent` catches, then returns None, so
  the bar renders without the segment. The first failure of each kind per provider logs a warning
  with its traceback; repeats log one debug line, so a lasting failure can't flood `agent.log` or
  `-v` output with a traceback per repaint.

The label is a catalog string (`cli.status_bar.weekly_usage`, `"wk {percent}%"`) in all 17 locales.

## Related Issue

Part of #53306 (show provider quota in the status bar), the account-usage-API half. The
rate-limit-header half for header-only providers is not in this PR.

Overlapping open PRs, both written against the status bar's earlier home in `cli.py`:

- #33836 (weiiqi) adds an opt-in account-usage badge (`5h 94% · Week 86% · Opus 75%`). The
  maintainer sweeper review asked for a port into the current snapshot and renderers plus tests
  for the refresh, single-flight and failure paths. Since then, `agent/account_usage_cache.py` has
  landed with exactly that refresh machinery. This PR builds on it, so the status-bar side is a
  small reader. It is narrower than #33836: one window, not every window.
- #84516 (Isakzvegelj) shows the Codex weekly window behind a `/planusage` toggle. This PR uses
  the existing `display.status_bar.fields` switch instead of a new command, and covers every
  provider with a weekly window.

If maintainers prefer either of those, I'm glad to fold this into it instead.

The contributor-email mapping for this PR's author (`contributors/emails/zkups56@gmail.com`) is
added in #152748; the email check here passes once that lands.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/status_bar_usage.py` (new, beside `status_bar_git.py`): `weekly_window(snapshot)`
  picks the account-scoped weekly window with a finite reading. `weekly_usage_percent(provider,
  credential_pool)` reads the cache, asks for a background refresh, and returns the rounded-up
  percent or None.
- `hermes_cli/cli_status_bar_mixin.py`: the snapshot carries `weekly_usage_percent`, read only when
  the field is listed (`_status_bar_weekly_usage`, which passes the live agent's provider and
  credential pool, or the CLI's before an agent exists). `_status_bar_segments` adds the segment
  after `cache_hit` through `_weekly_usage_segments`. `_weekly_usage_style` holds the colour ladder.
  The logic sits in helpers so `_get_status_bar_snapshot` and `_status_bar_segments` keep their
  code-health complexity caps.
- `locales/*.yaml`: `cli.status_bar.weekly_usage` in all 17 catalogs.
- `agent/credential_pool_admin.py`: `CredentialPool.entry_count()` (on the pool's admin mixin, as
  `credential_pool.py` is at its line cap), the pool's size read without its lock (every writer
  swaps or appends to `_entries` in one step, so the length is always a whole list's).
- `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py` (comment, same line count) and
  `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md`: the new field, its opt-in default, which windows it
  reads, when it stays hidden (and that `/usage` says why), its width tier and how the reading is
  refreshed.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_status_bar_weekly_usage.py` (new, 48 cases in 29 tests, parametrised where
  the cases share an invariant):
  - Reading: rounding up (float noise excluded) and the 0–100 clamp; one table of which window
    counts (the account week, not the session or a model week; a week without a reading or with a
    non-finite one skipped); stale snapshots hidden but re-requested; a provider whose usage API has
    windows but no weekly one re-asked only once its reading goes stale, and one that answers with
    no windows re-asked every interval; a provider without a usage API never asked; a raising cache
    read hiding only the segment while the rest of the bar renders, warning once with its traceback
    and then logging quietly.
  - Refresh: an unlisted field never starts a fetch; an opted-in repaint returns before a blocked
    usage API answers; repaints ask once per refresh interval; a failed fetch is not retried on
    every repaint; an empty answer keeps the last reading.
  - Whose usage: a pool of two or more credentials gets no reading (the agent's pool, or the CLI's
    before an agent exists); a repaint returns while another thread holds a real pool's lock; a
    plugin provider's weekly window reaches the bar; the CLI's provider stands in until an agent
    exists; the live agent's provider wins; a mid-session switch switches the reading. The
    Anthropic and Codex fetchers' labels are the ones the bar reads.
  - Rendering: the colour ladder, the width tiers (drops with `cache_hit`), its place between the
    context gauge and the speed readings, the prompt_toolkit and modern-footer renderers, and the
    plain-text label in three interface languages.

## How to Test

1. Add `weekly_usage` to `display.status_bar.fields` (an explicit list shows only what it holds, so
   list the defaults too), signed in to an Anthropic or Codex subscription. Once the first
   background fetch lands (a second or two), the next repaint (a keystroke is enough) shows
   `wk N%`, matching `/usage`'s weekly line rounded up.
2. Without the field listed, nothing changes, and no usage request is made.
3. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_status_bar_weekly_usage.py`: 48 passed. Each guarded
   behaviour was broken on purpose, 29 mutations in all, and each one turned the test named for it
   red: round down; no clamp at either end; float noise rounded up; model weeks counted; a window
   without a reading, or with a non-finite one, taken; no refresh; a fetch per repaint; stale
   readings shown; no usage-API check; built-in fetchers only; no exception guard; no warn-once; a
   traceback per repaint; no pool check; a pool of exactly two shown; the pool counted under its
   lock (by the bar, or inside `entry_count`); a usage API without a weekly window polled every
   interval; the cache storing an empty answer; the CLI's pool ignored before an agent exists; the
   probe running without the field; the CLI's provider winning over the agent's; the colour
   thresholds; the width tier; the bar position; English hard-coded; and an empty answer erasing
   the last reading (in the cache, which this suite also pins from the bar's side).
4. `scripts/run_tests.sh` on the 109 test files that mention the status bar, account usage or
   `config_defaults`, the credential-pool suites, and `tests/agent/test_i18n.py`: 2,066 passed, 36
   skipped, and 2 failed, the same two that fail identically on untouched `main` on this machine
   (`test_bot_desktop_resources.py::test_start_refuses_and_status_explains_when_memory_is_short`,
   `test_plugin_validate.py::test_portable_validation_fails_orphan_and_reports_availability`).
   `scripts/check` passes.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate (overlaps named above)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this feature
- [x] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass
- [x] `just check` passes
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.7.2 (Ghostty), Anthropic subscription (OAuth)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (`website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md`, the
      `config_defaults.py` comment, docstrings)
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A (no new key; it
      does not list status-bar fields)
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — N/A (no platform-specific code)
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

![wk N% stepping from green to yellow to red, then the terminal narrowing to 60 and 44 columns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZackKuptsow/hermes-agent/pr-152964-assets/weekly-usage.gif)

This branch's CLI, recorded through a pseudo-terminal at its first two commits (the review fixes
since change nothing it shows). A scripted usage API stands in for
Anthropic's and answers 12%, 48.2%, 50%, 79% and 83.6% on successive background refreshes, with the
refresh interval cut to 3 s; the status-bar code is unpatched. The bar repaints on each keystroke.
At 60 columns `wk` stays, and at 44 it drops with `cache_hit`. The three-width sample above is
rendered from the same code.

Known limits, left out on purpose:

- Anthropic readings at or below 1% are scaled ×100 by the existing parser until #139916 lands: a
  1% week reads `wk 100%`, in red. The payload's `utilization` is already a percentage (a live read
  gave `seven_day.utilization` 51.0 beside `limits[].percent` 51 for the same window). This PR
  reads what `/usage` reads and leaves that parser to #139916.
- Two older paths the bar now drives in the background, left for a separate PR so this diff stays
  on the status bar: `fetch_account_usage` swallows every fetch exception without a log
  (`agent/account_usage.py`), and a refresh thread that fails to start leaves its provider marked
  in flight for the rest of the process (`agent/account_usage_cache.py`).
- The CLI, not the Ink TUI: `hermes tui`'s status rule is not changed.

prs.title: Tests that look up a child process no longer fail when an unrelated child just exited
prs.body:
Some tests look for a specific child process by reading each child's command line. If an unrelated child had just exited, that read crashed the test, even though the process it was looking for was fine. Now a child that disappears mid-scan is skipped, so those tests stop failing at random.

Seen on #157669: `tests/gateway/test_managed_worker_launch.py::test_ordinary_owner_launches_tool_worker_and_detach_does_not_cancel[history]` failed with `psutil.ZombieProcess: PID still exists but it's a zombie` at `p.cmdline()` in a `children()` comprehension ([job](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/44463065181/job/135354396886)). That PR does not touch the gateway worker code.

## Changes

- New `tests/process_scan.py`: `children_matching(pid, predicate, recursive=)` and `matching(procs, predicate)` skip a process that raises `NoSuchProcess` / `ZombieProcess` / `AccessDenied` while being read.
- Every test that filtered `children()` by `cmdline()` / `name()` uses it: `test_managed_worker_launch.py`, `test_serve_exit_flush.py` (2 sites), `test_lsp_owned_server.py`, `test_gateway_editor_mcp.py`, `test_fresh_process_entrypoints.py`.

## Verification

- Repro with a real unreaped child of the scanning process: the old comprehension raises `ZombieProcess`; `children_matching` returns the live target.
- The 4 non-E2E files: 24 passed, 0 failed. The E2E file runs only on release/dispatch runs.

Related: #146926 (open) fixes the sibling `pid_gone` check-then-act race in the same test file, at a different line; this PR does not overlap it.

prs.title: Terminal secrets no longer land in the on-disk session snapshot, and commands run ~2x faster (#62336, salvage #148406)
prs.body:
The terminal tool saved every secret the shell could see into a plaintext file on disk (`hermes-snap-*.sh`) after each command, and the file came back every time it was deleted. Now secret values carry between commands in memory instead, the file holds none of them, and each terminal command runs about twice as fast.

A Hermes Cloud user's service credential (client ID and secret) kept landing in `/opt/data/cache/scratch/hermes-snap-*.sh` in plaintext, and so did every key in the profile's `.env`.

## What changes

| Scenario | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Agent runs `export CAROL_CLIENT_SECRET=…`, then reads it in the next call | works, value written to disk | works, value never on disk |
| Profile `.env` holds `PORTAL_CLIENT_SECRET`, `SESSION_COOKIE`, `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDS_JSON` | all 4 in the file | none in the file |
| `github_token` (lower case), readonly `RO_TOKEN`, multi-line `MULTI_TOKEN`, `DATABASE_URL=postgres://u:pw@db` | all in the file | none in the file |
| `KEEP_ME=ordinary`, `PATH`, functions, aliases | in the file | in the file (unchanged) |
| `unset` a secret, delegated child exports, `persistent_shell: false`, `set -o noclobber`, user changes `IFS` / `set -e` | as before | same as main |
| Median `true` on the local backend (100 runs × 5, alternating trees) | 28–32 ms | 14.5–16 ms |

## How

- The `export -p` dump gets the secret exports handed to it over an inherited pipe (`NAME=value\0` records) and drops them before it writes the file (`export -n` also clears readonly exports). The local backend keeps those values per snapshot file and gives them back to the next command as process env, so the shell sees the same variables as before.
- A secret is any name the profile's `.env` / secret sources define (so a custom name needs no naming convention), any credential-shaped name (token, key, secret, password, cookie, webhook, creds, client id, any case), or a URL-shaped name whose value carries `user:pass@`.
- Speed: matching runs inside bash through one `compgen -X` with no per-variable fork; #148406's per-variable `tr` subshell made each command ~25x slower. The PATH each command builds no longer re-reads the tool store per package (`pm/install.py`: ~11 ms → ~1 ms). The wait loop's first poll tick is 1 ms instead of 5 ms.
- Scope: local backend on Linux and macOS. Windows (no `pass_fds`) and remote backends (Docker, SSH, Modal…) keep their snapshot as it was, since dropping the values there would drop the user's exports from later commands.

## Verification

- **Live repro (real `hermes chat -q`, real model `qwen/qwen4-max` on Nous inference, scratch home, snapshot read off disk):** main: the file held all 7 synthetic secrets (2 exported by the agent, 5 from `.env`). This PR: 0 secrets in the file, `KEEP_ME="ordinary"` still there, and the agent's next call printed `secret=[SYNTH-carol-secret] keep=[ordinary] envfile=[SYNTH-client-secret-envfile]` on both trees (tool rows read from each run's `state.db`).
- Component E2E on the real `LocalEnvironment` + bash, main vs head: every row of the table above.
- bash 3.2 (`bash:3.2` image): `compgen -X` with case-folded globs, `export -n` on a readonly export, `\0` records. That run found that 3.2's `compgen -X` ignores `nocasematch`, so each glob ships in both cases.
- Tests: `tests/tools/test_snapshot_secret_handoff.py` (2 invariants on the real backend; the on-disk test is red on main). `test_profile_key_env_scrub.py::test_declaring_a_key_mid_session…` had asserted the secret was IN the snapshot file as its precondition; it now checks the session holds it (the PR's whole point), and the declared-key drop it guards still holds. Snapshot / persistent-shell / pipeline / login-PATH / Windows-msys / pm suites: 90 passed, 17 skipped. A local `tests/tools` + `tests/pm` sweep had 28 red files: 26 fail the same way on `origin/main` here (sudo password, PM toolchain fixtures), `test_profile_key_env_scrub.py` is fixed above, and `test_bot_desktop_idle_self_stop.py` passes 6/6 on the committed head in two clean runs (its earlier reds came from a run taken mid-rebase and from orphaned launchers of an earlier sweep).

## Credit

Salvages #148406 by @paulipopshill01 (fail-closed scrub, readonly handling) and the design from the #62336 thread: @kwchia (take names from the profile's `.env`), @kvnloo (cookie / webhook / creds shapes), @whyyagswhy (fork-free matching).

Fixes #62336

## Infographic

![Secrets stay off disk](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab30c8b/b4mJZ4ZvpOR_jWHk5Dqot_heafvaym.png)

prs.title: fix(desktop): stage large pastes under their .txt basename
prs.body:
Fixes #157667.

## Problem

Pasting more than ~3,000 characters into the desktop composer converts the text into an attachment. When the desktop app is connected to a **remote** gateway, `uploadComposerAttachment` sent `file.attach` with `name: label` — the localized display label (e.g. `粘贴内容 (23.7 KB)`) — so the gateway staged the file under an extension-less name and the preview panel could not resolve it ("Preview unavailable" / 404). The bytes were intact and the model read the content; only the preview failed.

## Root cause

`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/index.ts` (`uploadComposerAttachment`): `file.attach`'s `name` is the staged filename on the gateway side (`gateway/session_ancillary.py` → `tui_gateway/prompt_attachments.py: _stage_session_file_attachment` uses `name` when the bytes arrive as `data_url`, i.e. the remote case). The paste's on-disk file is already correctly named `pasted_content_<stamp>_<hex>.txt` (`electron/composer-paste.ts`), but the display label built in `use-composer-actions.ts` (`${copy.pastedContent} (${pasteSizeLabel(text)})`) was sent as the staged name instead.

## Fix

Stage pasted-content attachments under the basename of their saved path, keeping the display label unchanged:

```ts
const stagedName = isPastedContentPath(path) ? pathLabel(path) : label
```

Scoped to pasted-content paths only (`isPastedContentPath` in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/large-paste.ts`): regular files keep staging under their label, and the image branch is untouched. A side effect of the fix: the returned `ref_text` is now `@file:attachments/pasted_content_*.txt`, so the transcript chip in `directive-text.tsx` matches `isPastedContentPath` again and renders the localized "Pasted content" string instead of the raw label.

## Evidence

Base: `main` @ `52811481bc07b18b073790cd2a168a832c92acd7`.

Repro (new tests in `upload-composer-attachment.test.ts`, mock gateway RPC):

```sh
cd apps/desktop
pnpm exec vitest run --project ui src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/upload-composer-attachment.test.ts
```

Before the fix, the new paste test failed with:

```
- "name": "pasted_content_2026-11-19_12-00-00-000_abc123.txt",
+ "name": "粘贴内容 (23.7 KB)",
```

1 failed / 4 passed. After the fix: **6 passed / 6** (localized-label paste, Windows paste path `C:\...\composer-pastes\pasted_content_....txt`, plus a control case asserting a regular file still stages under its label, plus the 3 pre-existing tests).

Regression scope (all on the fix commit):

- `src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/` — 29 files, **451 passed**
- Paste-adjacent suites (`large-paste.test.ts`, `use-composer-actions.test.ts`, `user-message-text.test.tsx`) — 3 files, **46 passed**
- `tsc -p . --noEmit` — exit 0 (run with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096`; the full `pnpm run typecheck` OOMs on a 6 GB VM, an environment limit, not a code error)
- `eslint` on both changed files — 0 errors (2 pre-existing `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings elsewhere in `index.ts`, untouched code)

## Scope / deliberately unchanged

- Only the staged `name` for pasted-content attachments changes; the chip label, `refText` handling, error messages (still user-facing `label`), and the `image.attach_bytes` path are untouched.
- No change to the preview read path: it already URL-encodes the path (`apps/desktop/src/lib/desktop-fs.ts`), so the issue's secondary suggestion (URL-encode the preview request) needs no separate fix here.
- The browser/webapp paste flow and the bot `file.attach` caller (`group-turns.ts`) do not carry the same bug and are out of scope.

## Limits

E2E preview verification needs a desktop app connected to a remote Linux gateway; this VM has neither, so verification here is the mocked-gateway unit test above plus typecheck. The 404 mechanism itself was not reproduced end-to-end — the unit test pins the exact RPC parameter (`file.attach` `name`) that determines the staged filename.

Closes #157667

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add harness2 (Harness^2 self-improvement loop)
prs.body:
This PR adds the `harness2` plugin to the plugin catalog. The plugin is a native rebuild of the Harness^2 self-improvement loop (arXiv:2610.14224).

## What the plugin does

A harness is the set of files that shape an agent. The set is the system prompt, the configuration, and the skills. The plugin makes the agent better at a class of work. It edits the files of the harness. It re-runs the task in new sessions under the edited files. It keeps only the edits that the evidence supports. It saves the lessons in a library that the next run reads first.

A banked harness is a harness saved in the library. The live profile is the profile you use day to day. The plugin never writes the live profile.

## How one round works

1. The task runs once under the unedited harness.
2. The agent makes two edited harnesses. One changes how the agent works. The other adds what an expert in the field knows.
3. The task runs once under each edited harness, in its own session.
4. The agent merges the edits that the run evidence supports.
5. The task runs once under the merged harness.
6. The agent saves at most one lesson, with its evidence. The harness and the lesson enter the library.
7. The promote stage writes a carry-over report: what the banked harness changed against the unedited base, the evidence for each change, and what to apply to the live profile. The user applies what they approve.

## What the plugin uses in Hermes

The plugin uses these Hermes surfaces:

- `ctx.register_tool` - 9 tools that run the loop (`harness2_init`, `harness2_probe`, `harness2_seed`, `harness2_check`, `harness2_adopt`, `harness2_promote`, `harness2_library`, `harness2_status`, `harness2_gc`). The tool code is plain Python. It makes no model calls.
- `ctx.register_skill` - 5 skills for the judgment stages (`run`, `propose`, `compose`, `select`, `reflect`). They point at the stage prompts from the paper, which ship in `assets/prompts/`.
- `plugins.plugin_storage.plugin_data_dir` - all run state (runs, candidates, library). The installed plugin tree stays read-only.
- `config_schema` - 2 settings: `probe_budget_seconds` (default 900) and `probe_source_tag`.
- `python_dependencies` - 1 declared dependency: `PyYAML>=6,<7`, installed at plugin install time. Hosts without PyYAML use a small ruamel fallback inside the plugin. The docker-managed venv ships ruamel.yaml instead of PyYAML. The declared dependency is a load path, not a hard requirement.

The plugin uses no hooks and no middleware. It has one guarded core import (`hermes_constants`, for home resolution, with a fallback to the `HERMES_HOME` environment variable when the core is not importable). It makes no network calls. In normal operation it reads no settings from environment variables.

## What the plugin does to your machine (Rule 13 disclosures)

Full disclosure of what the plugin does on your machine:

- The plugin runs `hermes profile create --clone` and one-shot `hermes -p harness2-<task>-<probe> chat` sessions. A probe is a fresh agent session under one harness. Each probe is a full agent session billed to the configured model. Each probe has a time limit (900 seconds by default, a per-plugin setting).
- The probe overlay pins `approvals.mode: smart`, `approvals.single_query_mode: deny`, and `approvals.cron_mode: deny`, plus `security.redact_secrets: true`. Probes run as one-shot queries. No human is present to answer a prompt. A user's own `single_query_mode: approve` cannot reach a model-launched probe. The plugin never sets `single_query_mode: approve`, `approvals.mode: off`, or any non-interactive bypass.
- The plugin creates and refreshes Hermes profiles named `harness2-*`. Creation is `hermes profile create --clone`. It pins `HERMES_HOME` to the active profile's home, so a turn in one profile can never clone another profile's configuration. The clone carries the active profile's configuration and `.env` once, under Hermes' own clone policy. Every refresh after the first applies only the overlay keys (plus the run budget) with `hermes -p <probe> config set`. It also replaces `SOUL.md` and `skills/`. It never rewrites the profile's configuration or touches its `.env`. Probes run under the user's own model wiring. `harness2_gc` deletes only the probe profiles the plugin recorded creating for the named task.
- The plugin writes only to its data directory and the probe profile directories. Its read outside them is the task's user-supplied `source_dir` at init. It refuses paths outside the session's working directory, inside the Hermes home or root, under home credential directories, or through dot-dirs. The promote report writes into the run directory only. Applying the report to the live profile is the user's step, not the plugin's. Probes get the same tool access as any profile, including the web. The README shows how to remove the web toolset for offline tasks.
- The plugin sends no telemetry and no usage reports.

## Validation

`hermes plugins validate` passes at the pinned SHA (0000b1b): manifest, declared tools, security scan, and the `python_dependencies` declaration. There is no core override. `scripts/check_yaml_fallback.py` keeps the ruamel fallback path honest in PyYAML-less venvs.
