prs.title: Telegram and Discord replies past 8 messages arrive as one file, nothing cut off (#152012, salvage #152071)
prs.body:
## What

**ELI5:** when Hermes writes a reply too long for chat (more than 8 messages), you now get the whole reply as one `.md` file, and the half-sent messages are cleaned up. Nothing is cut off. If that upload fails, the whole reply still arrives as normal messages, on Telegram and on Discord alike, paced so the bot is not rate-limited. Short and normal replies look exactly as before.

Before, one runaway 415k-character reply went out as 402 Telegram messages and got the bot flood-banned for minutes. The earlier version of this PR stopped the flood by cutting the reply at 8 messages with a "response truncated" notice, which lost the text. Teknium ruled that no text may be lost: past the cap, the reply goes out as a file. A second ruling: Discord must match Telegram when the upload fails, so main's Discord 8-message truncation (#86581) is removed too.

Fixes #152012

## Changes

- **Over the cap, one file.** A reply that needs more than the adapter's `MAX_SPLIT_MESSAGES` (8 on Telegram and Discord) is uploaded whole as `reply-<id>.md` (UTF-8) through the adapter's document send. It carries a localized caption (new key `platform.shared.response_as_file`, all 17 locales: "📎 Long reply: the full text is attached.").
- **Non-streamed replies** (`gateway/platforms/helpers.py::send_long_reply_as_file`, called from `_send_with_retry`, the gateway's final-reply send): the file is the only thing sent. No message goes out first.
- **Streamed replies** (`gateway/stream_consumer_ceiling.py`): the consumer counts every message one reply opens (sealed heads, split-first sends, the final edit, fallback continuations). At the cap it stops opening messages and waits for the complete final text, never a partial. Then it uploads the file, and only after that is confirmed does it delete the messages it already posted for the reply (heads and live preview). The upload is shielded, so the gateway's 5 s flush-window cancel cannot cut it short. `delivered_final_matches` stays True, so the gateway never also sends the text.
- **Upload fails, or the adapter cannot upload:** nothing is deleted. The reply resumes as ordinary messages from where the chat left off, paced by the adapters' existing flood handling, so the full text still arrives. A refused delete (message too old, no permission) leaves that message and moves on.
- **Standalone sends** (`hermes send`, the `send_message` tool, cron) go through the same handoff (`send_rich_standalone`), and the caller gets a warning that the message went as a file.
- **Telegram** uploads through `send_reply_document`: a failed upload is a failed result, never a text notice reported as sent, and a short flood wait is retried inline. Files over 45 MB (the limit is 50 MB) are split into numbered files, never truncated.
- **Discord** uses the same code. It gains `delete_message` and `send_reply_document` (a message Discord accepted without the attachment is deleted again). Files are at most 7 MB each.
- **Discord upload fails: the whole reply as messages** (Teknium's ruling, d90e9fa0). `main`'s `_cap_split_chunks` (#86581: 7 chunks + a "Response truncated" notice, the rest dropped) is removed from `send`, forum posts and the edit-overflow split, along with its copy key `platform.discord.limits.response_truncated` in all 17 locales (it had no other user). Pacing is discord.py's own, so no second pacer: its per-route buckets wait on `X-RateLimit-Remaining`/`Reset-After`, and a 429 sleeps `retry_after` and retries.
- **Removed:** every truncation path this PR had added: `cap_split_chunks`, `capped_raw`, `_split_budget`, `split_capped`/`dropped_chars`, the rich-part cap, the standalone chunk cap, and the Telegram `response_truncated` copy in every locale. `main`'s Discord truncation (#86581) is gone as well (see above).
- Docs: `telegram.md` and `discord.md` say long replies arrive as a file.

Root cause: no delivery path had an upper bound on messages per reply, and the fix that added one threw text away.

## Live probe

Real `hermes gateway run` with the real Telegram and Discord adapters, against the in-repo stand-ins (`tests/fakes/platforms/*_standin.py`; they now record each uploaded file's size and sha256) and `FakeLLMServer`. Base = the previous PR head `e6a846a4`, head = `52f239ca`. "file == reply" means the uploaded document's byte length and sha256 equal the reply's (415,033 B `73bc336bb35b…`, rich `a61987acb54a…`, 60,000 B `37ca037b3f13…`).

| row | base e6a846a4: on screen | base calls | head 52f239ca: on screen | head calls | file | file == reply (bytes + sha256) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tg-streaming-off-415k | 8 msgs (1 truncation notice), 28,516 of 415,033 chars | send 8, rich 0, edit 0, doc 0, del 0 | **1** on screen, 40 chars shown + file | send 0, rich 0, edit 0, doc 1, del 0 | 415,033 B, sha 73bc336bb35b | ✅ |
| tg-streaming-slow-415k | 8 msgs (1 truncation notice), 27,937 of 415,033 chars | send 8, rich 0, edit 3, doc 0, del 0 | **1** on screen, 40 chars shown + file | send 2, rich 0, edit 1, doc 1, del 2 | 415,033 B, sha 73bc336bb35b | ✅ |
| tg-overflow-before-first-preview-415k | 7 msgs (1 truncation notice), 23,978 of 415,033 chars | send 7, rich 0, edit 0, doc 0, del 0 | **1** on screen, 40 chars shown + file | send 0, rich 0, edit 0, doc 1, del 0 | 415,033 B, sha 73bc336bb35b | ✅ |
| tg-rich-streaming-off-415k | 8 msgs (1 truncation notice), 206,571 of 415,033 chars | send 0, rich 8, edit 0, doc 0, del 0 | **1** on screen, 40 chars shown + file | send 0, rich 0, edit 0, doc 1, del 0 | 415,033 B, sha a61987acb54a | ✅ |
| tg-rich-streaming-slow-415k | 8 msgs (1 truncation notice), 47,267 of 415,033 chars | send 7, rich 1, edit 9, doc 0, del 0 | **1** on screen, 40 chars shown + file | send 3, rich 1, edit 6, doc 1, del 4 | 415,033 B, sha a61987acb54a | ✅ |
| tg-cancelled-stream-60k | 7 msgs (1 truncation notice), 23,964 of 60,000 chars | send 7, rich 0, edit 1, doc 0, del 0 | **1** on screen, 40 chars shown + file | send 6, rich 0, edit 0, doc 1, del 6 | 60,000 B, sha 37ca037b3f13 | ✅ |
| tg-standalone-send-415k | 8 msgs (1 truncation notice), 28,516 of 415,033 chars | send 8, rich 0, edit 0, doc 0, del 0 | **1** on screen, 40 chars shown + file | send 0, rich 0, edit 0, doc 1, del 0 | 415,033 B, sha 73bc336bb35b | ✅ |
| tg-document-refused-415k | 8 msgs (1 truncation notice), 27,945 of 415,033 chars | send 8, rich 0, edit 2, doc 0, del 0 | **105** on screen, 416,045 chars shown | send 105, rich 0, edit 2, doc 0, del 0; sendDocument refused ×1 | none | n/a |
| tg-delete-refused-415k | 8 msgs (1 truncation notice), 27,937 of 415,033 chars | send 8, rich 0, edit 3, doc 0, del 0 | **3** on screen, 7,939 chars shown + file | send 2, rich 0, edit 1, doc 1, del 0; deleteMessage refused ×2 | 415,033 B, sha 73bc336bb35b | ✅ |
| tg-control-10k | 3 msgs (0 truncation notice), 9,998 of 10,000 chars | send 3, rich 0, edit 3, doc 0, del 0 | **3** on screen, 9,998 chars shown | send 3, rich 0, edit 3, doc 0, del 0 | none | n/a |
| tg-control-short | 1 msgs (0 truncation notice), 25 of 24 chars | send 1, rich 0, edit 2, doc 0, del 0 | **1** on screen, 25 chars shown | send 1, rich 0, edit 2, doc 0, del 0 | none | n/a |
| dc-streaming-60k | 8 msgs (1 truncation notice), 13,235 of 60,000 chars | msg 8, edit 4, file 0, del 0 | **1** on screen, 40 chars shown + file | msg 8, edit 3, file 1, del 8 | 60,000 B, sha 37ca037b3f13 | ✅ |
| dc-control-short | 1 msgs (0 truncation notice), 24 of 24 chars | msg 1, edit 1, file 0, del 0 | **1** on screen, 24 chars shown | msg 1, edit 1, file 0, del 0 | none | n/a |

- The **document refused** row shows the fallback: the stand-in refuses `sendDocument`, nothing is deleted, and the whole 415k reply arrives as 105 paced messages (416,045 chars shown, counting the `(N/M)` markers).
- In the **delete refused** row, the stand-in refuses both `deleteMessage` calls: those two messages stay beside the file, and the reply is still delivered once.
- Controls: 10k and short replies make the same calls as base.

### Discord upload-refused fallback (d90e9fa0)

Same rig. The stand-in refuses every attachment upload (403 50013). Base = `52f239ca` (previous head), head = `d90e9fa0`. "Whole reply" means the visible messages, with their `(N/M)` markers removed, tile the 60,000-char reply in order with nothing missing (only the split's boundary whitespace differs).

| row | base 52f239ca | head d90e9fa0 |
|---|---|---|
| dc non-streamed 60k, upload refused | **8 msgs, 13,843 of 60,000 chars + truncation notice** | **31 msgs, whole reply**, no notice |
| dc non-streamed 60k, upload refused, 429 (`retry_after` 2 s) on the 5th message | 8 msgs, 13,843 chars + notice | 31 msgs, whole reply; the 429 was waited out and retried, nothing lost |
| dc streamed 60k, upload refused | 33 msgs, whole reply (the stream path already resumed) | 33 msgs, whole reply |
| dc streamed 60k, upload refused, stand-in enforces 5 msgs / 5 s per channel | 33 msgs, whole reply | 33 msgs, whole reply, **never more than 5 in any 5 s**, 0 429s (discord.py paced from the bucket headers) |
| dc streamed 60k, upload works | 1 file (60,000 B, sha256 = reply's), partials deleted | 1 file (60,000 B, sha256 = reply's), partials deleted |
| dc non-streamed 60k, upload works | 1 file, sha256 = reply's | 1 file, sha256 = reply's |
| dc 10k / short controls | 6 / 1 msgs | 6 / 1 msgs (same calls) |
| tg streamed 60k, `sendDocument` refused | 16 msgs, no notice | 16 msgs, no notice (same calls) |

The stand-in gained an opt-in per-channel `create_message` bucket that sends discord.py's `X-RateLimit-*` headers, and a `Via` header on 429s (without it discord.py treats a 429 as a Cloudflare ban and raises instead of retrying).

### Independent review fixes (d75eb12e, 9defb229)

An independent review at `d90e9fa0` found four paths that still flooded. Each is fixed with a test that fails on `d90e9fa0` and passes on head (`tests/gateway/test_reply_file_handoff_paths.py`). Live rows use the same rig:

| row | before | head |
|---|---|---|
| Telegram rich format refused, 86k, streaming off | 22 msgs, 0 files | 1 file, sha256 = reply |
| Finished answer delivered as commentary, 60k | 15 msgs, 0 files | 1 file, sha256 = reply |
| Discord `hermes send` / `send_message`, 60k | 31 msgs, 0 files | 1 file, sha256 = reply |
| Same, upload refused, 5 msgs / 5 s limit | stopped after 5 of 31 on a 429 | all 31 parts, never more than 5 in 5 s |
| Telegram reply crossing a stream segment boundary, 60k | 2 uploads (60,000 + 60,002 B) | 1 upload, sha256 = reply |
| Regression: Telegram streamed 415k / short control | 1 file / 1 msg | 1 file / 1 msg |

- **Rich refused:** the MarkdownV2 fallback recounts against the cap, including after some rich parts landed; over it, the whole reply goes as one file and landed parts are deleted only after the upload is confirmed.
- **Commentary:** the consumer's sends are marked as pieces of one reply, and a complete commentary message goes through the file check.
- **Discord standalone:** the full text is uploaded before splitting (`plugins/platforms/discord/standalone_rest.py`), and the REST fallback waits on 429 `retry_after` and on `X-RateLimit-Reset-After` when the remaining count hits 0.
- **Segment boundary:** after a tool round the agent re-streams the reply with a leading paragraph break, and that second segment uploaded its own file. `_deliver_reply_file` now skips a file whose normalized text was already delivered in this reply and only deletes its preview messages.

Not covered: cron delivery through the running gateway (`gateway/delivery.py::DeliveryRouter._deliver_to_platform`) still sends a long reply as many messages; that is a separate PR. Before the single file lands on a re-streamed reply, two messages briefly appear and are deleted.

## Salvage

The first commit is a cherry-pick of #152071 by @junjuny0227, with authorship kept and the email mapped. The branch is rebased onto `main`. `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` is 6,714 lines (main 6,760), `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py` is 7,244 lines (main 7,268), `gateway/stream_consumer.py` is 1,075 lines (cap 2,000), and `gateway/platforms/base.py` is 3 lines shorter.

## Tests

- New `tests/gateway/test_reply_file_handoff.py`: real consumer and Telegram adapter against a fake Bot. It covers an over-cap streamed reply (slow growth, and overflowing before the first preview), which arrives as one file holding the exact full text with every earlier message deleted; a refused file, which deletes nothing and still shows the full text as messages; an under-cap control; and a non-streamed over-cap reply, which sends only the file.
- The PR's own truncation tests (`test_split_cap.py`, `test_rich_split_cap.py`, `test_stream_reply_ceiling*.py`) are deleted, and `test_telegram_send_message_chunk_mdv2.py` is back to `main`.
- Mirrored dirs (`tests/gateway`, `tests/plugins/platforms/telegram`, `tests/tools`, i18n, boundary lint) pass, except 3 files that fail the same way on base `e6a846a4`: `test_fal_sdk`, `test_plugin_guard`, and the `test_session_mutation_compress_managed` timeout. The e2e contract suites need `python-telegram-bot`, which the local test env lacks, so CI covers them.
- Discord truncation tests on `main` are rewritten under Teknium's ruling (named in the commit): `tests/gateway/test_discord_split_cap.py` and the Discord case in `tests/gateway/test_native_warning_coverage.py` now assert every chunk is delivered with no notice.
- New `tests/e2e/core/platforms/test_discord_long_reply_fallback.py`: real gateway and Discord adapter, upload refused plus a 429 mid-fallback; the 40k reply arrives whole. Red on `52f239ca`, green on head.
- With the `messaging` extra: Discord, split and stream-consumer tests in `tests/gateway`, `tests/plugins/platforms` Discord, the Discord and Telegram e2e contracts and i18n: 939 passed, 0 failed.
- `python scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking. `scripts/boundary_lint.py --check`: rc 0.

## Infographic

![long replies arrive as one file](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab238a7/KvpMbuhy8G-BrGPA7aYga_BGdGtkaa.png)

prs.title: feat(catalog): price models the install ships no rates for from the manifest
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Prices a model released after an install, from the same remote manifest the picker already reads.

**The problem in plain terms.** Hermes ships a table of per-token rates so it can show what a session costs. A new model isn't in an installed release's table, so its cost reads "unknown" until the next release carries the row.

**What changes.** `model-catalog.json` now publishes the rate tables as they are on `main`, under `pricing`:

- `official_docs`: the standard-tier snapshot (`_OFFICIAL_DOCS_PRICING`), keyed by billing provider and model id. 103 rows today across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Bedrock, DeepSeek, Fireworks and MiniMax.
- `anthropic_fast_mode` and `openai_ultrafast`: the two fast-tier snapshots, keyed by model id.

Field names are the ones `PricingEntry` uses and rates are decimal strings, so the builder is a straight dump of the dataclass and there's no second schema to keep in step.

Each lookup consults the manifest only after the bundled table has no row for the model, under the same name normalizing (dotted Anthropic versions, Bedrock region prefixes).

**Three rules.**

1. **A bundled rate is never replaced.** If the install has a row, that row is used even when the manifest disagrees. So for any model a release already prices, nothing changes, and a price correction still ships with a release. Same reasoning as the rest of the stack: a row on `main` is paired with the code on `main`.
2. **A malformed rate is unknown, never a price.** Every rate must be a finite, non-negative decimal and an entry needs both token rates. An entry that fails is dropped whole. That follows the existing sentinel handling for OpenRouter's `-1` rates: a wrong number is worse than no number.

3. **An endpoint's own rate comes first.** With `model.base_url` set, a price that endpoint's `/models` listing advertises for the model is used before the manifest's. A relay's own tariff says more about what it charges than the vendor's list price.

GPT-6.2's fast-tier rates aren't in the tables. They're computed in code from the standard rates and carry a launch discount that ends on a date (`_openai_served_tier_entry`), which doesn't fit a flat table. A later model the manifest adds to that contract goes through the same calculation, from the standard rate the manifest publishes, so a Priority or Ultrafast turn is never shown at the standard rate. Without a published standard rate its tier cost stays unknown.

This is 4 of 4 and builds on #157316, #157318 and #157319. **The diff here includes those PRs' commits; the change to review is the last commit.** It needs #157319's `on_gpt62_contract()` for the tier pricing, so the order matters. Please merge the earlier ones first; I'll rebase this onto `main` as they land.

## Related Issue

Part of #157322 (4 of 4). The stack, in merge order:

1. #157316: picker lists for every provider
2. #157318: context windows and metadata
3. #157319: the id sets that gate request handling
4. #157320: pricing (this PR)

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `agent/usage_pricing.py`: adds `_manifest_pricing_entry()`, which parses and validates one manifest row into a `PricingEntry`. `get_pricing_entry` consults the published standard rate after the bundled table and after the endpoint's own listing. `_anthropic_fast_mode_entry` and the non-contract branch of `_openai_served_tier_entry` fall back to their published tables. The GPT-6.2 branch and the `fast` → `priority` mapping use `on_gpt62_contract()`, and derive the tier rate from the bundled or published standard rate.
- `scripts/build_model_catalog.py`, `website/static/api/model-catalog.json`: publish the three tables (87 KB, was 46 KB).
- `website/docs/reference/model-catalog.md`: documents the section and both rules.
- `tests/agent/test_model_catalog_pricing.py`: 25 tests.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_model_catalog_pricing.py`: 25 pass. The first 12 are the original cases. They seed a manifest into a temp `HERMES_HOME` cache and go through `estimate_usage_cost`. Covered: a model with no bundled rates is priced from the manifest (bare, and with the `anthropic/` prefix and a dotted version), a bundled rate isn't replaced, six malformed entries (negative, `NaN`, `Infinity`, a negative request fee, a missing output rate, a non-number) all come back unknown, a fast-mode response and an Ultrafast response are priced from their tables, and a disabled catalog prices nothing. Without the PR 3 of those 12 fail; the other 9 guard behaviour that already holds.
   The other 13 came out of review: a manifest-added GPT-6.2-contract model served at Priority, Fast and Ultrafast (before and after the discount cutoff), a relay that advertises its own rate, a regional OpenAI host that doesn't, one-sided usage with a missing rate, malformed optional fields, bundled fast-tier precedence for Anthropic and OpenAI, Priority not reading the Ultrafast table, and the committed manifest matching the builder. 5 of the 13 fail on the previous head `52e76d6c`; the rest pin guards that already held.
2. Related suites: the 82 test files that reference usage pricing or the catalog. 1607 passed, 7 failed, 3 errors. Every failing id also fails on `main` (`95a1d228c5`) on this machine (ids diffed). `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py` was left out, as in #157319.
3. `python scripts/check`: 21 of 22 pass. `shims` fails on `main` on Windows as well.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits). It carries the three earlier PRs' commits until they merge.
- [ ] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass. I ran the 18 related files with `scripts/run_tests.sh`; see How to Test.
- [ ] `just check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs). All but `shims`, which fails on `main` on Windows too.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11, Python 3.14

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A (no new keys)
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

Limits worth knowing:

- This is the PR that makes the manifest noticeably bigger (46 KB to 87 KB). Clients refetch it every 20 minutes, and #54792 is still open about the fetch reading the body without a cap. If size is a concern, the fast-tier tables are the cheapest thing to drop.
- A manifest-sourced rate is reported with `source: official_docs_snapshot` and the manifest's `pricing_version`, the same as a bundled one, because it is the same snapshot. Say so if you'd rather it had its own source label.
- The manifest is plain HTTPS from the docs site with a raw GitHub fallback, unsigned, as it is today. With pricing in it, a wrong manifest could show a wrong cost for a model the install doesn't price. It can't change a cost the install already knows, and it doesn't affect what is actually billed.
- On a relay that advertises no rate of its own, a manifest row prices the model at the vendor's list price. A bundled row does the same today for any base URL, and a manifest row is that row arriving early, so I kept the two consistent rather than add a host allowlist that only remote rows obey. Say so if you'd rather remote rows be stricter.

Not tested: macOS and Linux, and a live session against the published manifest (it only exists once this merges).

prs.title: Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT-5.6, Grok 4.7/4.20 and GLM-5.3 get their vendor-documented context windows (salvage #154415)
prs.body:
Hermes thought Claude Haiku 5.5 could only remember 200K tokens, so it started squeezing the conversation down at a fifth of what the model can hold; a few other models had the same kind of wrong number, some too small and some too big. This PR sets each of those numbers to what the model's maker documents.

Fixes #154406

## Credit
- Salvage of #154415 by @suhas-svg: the `claude-haiku-5` key and its tests are cherry-picked as-is, authorship preserved.
- #154515 by @Alexi5000 has the same one-line Haiku fix. Its extra `claude-haiku-5-5` key is redundant once `claude-haiku-5` exists, so no code from it was used; credited here for the same diagnosis.
- @myonza reported the bug and audited the whole table in the issue thread. Every row changed below comes from that audit.

## What changed on top of #154415
`agent/model_metadata.py` `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_LENGTHS`, the hardcoded fallback used when an endpoint publishes no window. Each row was checked against the vendor's own page:

| model | before | after | vendor source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claude-haiku-5-5` (#154415) | 200,000 via `claude` | 1,000,000 | https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview |
| `gpt-5.6` (bare alias) | 400,000 via `gpt-5` | 1,050,000 | https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol ("The `gpt-5.6` alias routes requests to GPT-5.6 Sol", "1,050,000 context window") |
| `grok-4.7` | 256,000 via `grok-4` | 500,000 | https://docs.x.ai/developers/models/grok-4.7 |
| `grok-4.20` (+ `-multi-agent`, `-non-reasoning`) | 2,000,000 | 1,000,000 | https://docs.x.ai/developers/models/grok-4.20, https://docs.x.ai/developers/models/grok-4.20-multi-agent, https://docs.x.ai/developers/models/grok-4.20-non-reasoning |
| `glm-5.3`, `glm-5.3-flash` (incl. NanoGPT `z-ai/glm-5.3`, `z-ai/glm-5.3:thinking`) | 1,310,720 | 1,048,576 | Zhipu documents "1M" (https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-5.3); the exact number is the one every catalog publishes: NanoGPT `/api/v1/models?detailed=true`, Nous Portal and OpenRouter `/v1/models` all list 1,048,576 (output cap 131,072 separate) |
| `glm-5.3-flashx` | 1,048,576 | 1,048,576 (unchanged) | same: Zhipu "1M", OpenRouter/Nous list 1,048,576 |

`claude-haiku-5`, `gpt-5.6` and `grok-4.7` also join `_PRE_CATALOG_STALE_KEYS`. Without that, a user whose older build already cached the catch-all value (200K / 400K / 256K) would keep it forever through the step-1 disk cache.

### Rows checked and left alone
- **`solar-mini4`**: the audit saw 32,768, but on current main it already resolves to 524,288 (= Upstage's documented 512K, https://console.upstage.ai/docs/models/solar-mini-4). The `solar-` family default is boundary-matched since 98f758ae, so `solar-mini` no longer catches `solar-mini4`. No change needed.
- **GLM `:batch` / `:us` rows (1,048,576)**: these are OpenRouter-only slugs, and OpenRouter lists them at 1,048,576. Left alone.
- **GLM 1,310,720 provenance** (4baf4269, comment cited Nous + OpenRouter `/v1/models` on 2026-09-09): both catalogs list `z-ai/glm-5.3` and `glm-5.3-flash` at **1,048,576** today. Nobody serves 1.31M anymore, and Zhipu documents 1M. The reporter also showed a relay silently tail-truncating `glm-5.3` above ~1.02M. OpenRouter and Nous routes are unaffected by this change because they read the live catalog (steps 5b/6) before this table.
- **`grok-4.20` on OpenRouter** still lists 2,000,000, and OpenRouter routes keep reading that live value. This table only serves api.x.ai and custom endpoints, where xAI's docs say 1M.
- The minor (<5%) rows in the audit (gemma-4, qwen3.6/3.7-plus) are out of scope.
- #154594 / #137890 add haiku-5-5 to the Anthropic picker catalog, which is a separate surface. They don't overlap with this PR.

## Tests
`tests/agent/test_model_metadata_haiku5.py` holds #154415's tests plus two invariant tests:
- `test_offline_window_matches_vendor_docs`: a parametrized table of model id → vendor window, run through `get_model_context_length` on a custom endpoint whose `/models` returns no window (the reported route).
- `test_catch_all_value_persisted_before_the_fix_is_dropped`: a catch-all value persisted by an older build is re-resolved.

Red on base (`origin/main` `agent/model_metadata.py`): **18 failed, 4 passed** (every new row plus #154415's haiku cases). Green on head: `test_model_metadata_haiku5.py test_model_metadata.py test_glm_context_window_resolution.py test_bedrock_card_windows.py` 182 passed. Every other `tests/agent` file that references `get_model_context_length` / `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_LENGTHS` also passes, one file at a time. `scripts/check --only health` ok (model_metadata.py stays at its 2613-line cap).

## Live evidence
Real `hermes chat -q "say pong"` in a scratch HOME, `provider: custom` → a local OpenAI-compatible relay whose `/v1/models` rows carry no window (the issue's shape). The resolver's own log line `Using hardcoded context length … (custom endpoint, catalog match on …)`, base = `origin/main` 0d1eb82d vs head:

| model | base | head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| claude-haiku-5-5 | 200,000 (`claude`) | 1,000,000 (`claude-haiku-5`) |
| gpt-5.6 | 400,000 (`gpt-5`) | 1,050,000 (`gpt-5.6`) |
| grok-4.7 | 256,000 (`grok-4`) | 500,000 (`grok-4.7`) |
| grok-4.20 | 2,000,000 | 1,000,000 |
| glm-5.3 | 1,310,720 | 1,048,576 |
| glm-5.3-flashx | 1,048,576 | 1,048,576 |
| solar-mini4 | 524,288 (`solar-`) | 524,288 (unchanged) |

Each turn completed ("pong"). NOT_COVERED: no real-vendor turn above the old window. That would need a paid near-1M-token prompt per vendor; the reporter's issue already measured 975,592 input tokens accepted on Haiku 5.5.

## Rebase + GLM exact number (2026-11-18)
Rebased onto current main (comment-only conflict in the OpenAI rows). GLM-5.3 now lands on **1,048,576**, not 1,000,000: a NanoGPT user reported it on Discord and Gille confirmed it. Zhipu's "1M" is rounded; NanoGPT's detailed model list, the Nous Portal and OpenRouter all publish exactly 1,048,576. NanoGPT's plain `/models` leaves the window out, so its users get this table value.

**Live repro** (real resolver, fresh temp `HERMES_HOME` each, real `https://nano-gpt.com/api/v1` `/models`, `provider: custom`):

| model | main 95a1d228 | head 3dfc7957 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `z-ai/glm-5.3` | 1,310,720 | 1,048,576 |
| `z-ai/glm-5.3:thinking` | 1,310,720 | 1,048,576 |

It also carries @kvnloo's 447d07f (cherry-picked, authorship kept): a 2M `grok-4.20` row that an older build persisted for `api.x.ai` is dropped and re-resolved to 1M, and OpenRouter's legitimate 2M cache row survives.

Tests: `test_model_metadata_haiku5.py` gives 19 failed / 5 passed on main's `model_metadata.py` and passes on head. Every test file that mentions glm-5.3 or grok-4.20 (40 files) gives 2451 passed, 0 failed. `scripts/check --only health` ok.

NOT_COVERED: a persisted 1,310,720 GLM cache row (an overstated value) is not dropped. Hermes only persists live-probed or provider-confirmed windows, never this table's value, so no home should hold one.

## Infographic
![Context windows match the vendor](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab23538/SnWN5emg0YeNsPxnJ2_ps_5vIH38kT.png)

prs.title: feat(catalog): let the manifest add a model to the id sets that gate request handling
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets a new model that behaves like an existing one be driven correctly by an installed release, without waiting for the next one.

**The problem in plain terms.** Some request handling is keyed on an exact list of model ids in the code: which models take the `low`..`max` effort ladder, which accept a fast tier, which go through a different API. When GPT-6.2 came out, none of its behaviour was new. Its two ids only had to be added to lists the code already read. That still took a code change in several files and a release, and it is the part that actually blocks a stable user: a picker row alone isn't enough if the request then goes out with the wrong effort level and gets a 400.

**What changes.** `model-catalog.json` now publishes five of those lists under `model_sets`, and each membership check also accepts an id the cached manifest adds:

| Set | Built-in constant | What an id in it gets |
|---|---|---|
| `openai_gpt62_contract` | `GPT62_MODEL_IDS` | The `low`..`max` effort ladder, the strict request sanitizer on official OpenAI, Codex and US/EU residency routes, account discovery before the Codex picker lists it, no Ultrafast on the EU host |
| `bedrock_openai_responses` | `BEDROCK_OPENAI_RESPONSES_MODEL_IDS` | Treated as a Bedrock-hosted OpenAI model |
| `anthropic_fast_mode` | `_ANTHROPIC_FAST_MODE_MODELS` | Accepts `speed: "fast"` |
| `openai_ultrafast` | `_OPENAI_ULTRAFAST_MODELS` | Accepts `service_tier: "ultrafast"` |
| `openai_fast_eu` | `_FAST_REGION_MODELS` (EU host) | Accepts a fast tier on `eu.api.openai.com` |

So the next model on the GPT-6.2 contract is one line in a JSON file on `main`, and installed releases pick it up within 20 minutes.

**What the manifest can and can't do.**

- It can add an id to a set. It can't add a set: a set only exists because code reads it, so an unknown name is ignored and a model that needs new behaviour still needs a release.
- It can't remove an id an install ships.
- It can't choose a host. A set decides which *model* may use a tier. Which *endpoint* may receive it stays in the built-in route checks (`_fast_mode_route_supported`, `_FAST_REGION_MODELS`). There is a test that no set can make `au.api.openai.com` accept Ultrafast.
- A fast tier is still opt-in. A set only makes `/fast` available for the model, and only for a model and route the built-in family and route checks already allow.
- A set name means one behaviour for good. `requires` checks the name, not a revision of the code behind it, so if a set's request handling ever changes, that release gives it a new name. Older builds then skip the row instead of driving the model the old way.

**The picker gate from #157316 gets its writer here.** The builder now adds `requires` to a picker entry whose model is in a set it can't be driven without (`openai_gpt62_contract`, `bedrock_openai_responses`). A build that doesn't read that set skips the entry. In practice: a release with only #157316 won't list a future GPT-6.2-style model it can't drive, and a release with this PR will list it and drive it.

Pricing keeps its own built-in id set in this PR. `_openai_served_tier_entry` indexes the bundled price table directly for GPT-6.2 ids, so I left `agent/usage_pricing.py` alone. A model added through a set shows an unknown fast-tier cost until #157320 or a release carries its rates.

This is 3 of 4 and builds on #157316 and #157318. **The diff here includes those PRs' commits; the change to review is the last commit.** Please merge those first; I'll rebase this onto `main` as soon as they land.

## Related Issue

Part of #157322 (3 of 4). The stack, in merge order:

1. #157316: picker lists for every provider
2. #157318: context windows and metadata
3. #157319: the id sets that gate request handling (this PR)
4. #157320: pricing

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

prs.title: feat(catalog): add new models to every provider's picker from the remote manifest
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets a model added on `main` show up in the model picker of an already installed release, for every built-in provider and not only OpenRouter and Nous Portal.

**The problem in plain terms.** Each provider's list of models is written into the code. When a provider ships a new model, someone adds it to the list on `main`, and people on the stable release still don't see it until the next release. GPT-6.2 is the recent example: it landed on `main`, and people on stable have to wait for the next release to pick it.

Hermes already has the fix for two providers. Every 20 minutes it downloads a small JSON file (`model-catalog.json`, published from `main` by the docs deploy) and reads the OpenRouter and Nous Portal lists from it. This PR puts the other providers' lists in that same file and teaches the picker to read them.

**How it behaves.**

- The manifest now carries one block per built-in provider row in `_PROVIDER_MODELS` (33 of them: `anthropic`, `openai-api`, `bedrock`, `gemini`, `opencode-zen`, ...).
- On the client the block only adds to the row the install ships: the ids the install doesn't have come first, in manifest order, then the shipped row exactly as it is. It doesn't reorder or respell a shipped id.
- It only adds. Nothing an install lists is removed, and a provider with no built-in row gets nothing from the manifest, so third-party provider plugins stay on their own lists, including a plugin whose name happens to match a published block.
- It only feeds places that *list* models: `/model` on every surface, `hermes model`, and the check for whether a typed id is known. An added id is accepted on a provider whose picker offers it, and not on one whose live listing stands alone.
- It does not feed anything that *chooses* a model. The default for a provider with no model set and the short aliases (`sonnet`, `opus`) read the built-in table. The `default` label is honoured on the OpenRouter and Nous blocks only. The Desktop onboarding recommendation skips added rows. Provider detection for a bare name (`/model some-model`) treats an added row as something to offer, not as proof the current provider serves it: when the only match is an added row, it asks the provider's own listing before deciding to stay. A manifest edit cannot change what an unconfigured install runs, what it costs, or which provider a typed name lands on.
- These rows are read from the disk cache only. They never fetch on their own; the existing fetch points (`/model`, the gateway refresh, `hermes update`) keep the cache warm.

**Two things I was careful about.**

1. The manifest stays at `version: 1`. `_validate_manifest` rejects a higher version, so a bump would cut every existing install off from its OpenRouter and Nous updates. Old clients only look up the `openrouter` and `nous` blocks and ignore the rest.
2. An entry can carry `requires`. A build that doesn't satisfy it skips the entry. Once pickers follow `main`, a stable build could otherwise be shown a model whose request handling it doesn't have yet. Nothing sets the field in this PR; #157319 does. It has to be in the first release that reads these rows, because a release without the check can't be gated later.

I also made the in-process copy of the manifest a single `(path, mtime, manifest)` tuple that is replaced whole. It was three globals written one after another, and with these rows read from more places, two profiles served by one process could pair one profile's manifest with the other's path.

Not published on purpose: `openai-codex` (only the account's live Codex catalog may advertise a model, which is what 444a6b8644 and 864fd57c59 enforce), `xai` / `xai-oauth` (their rows come from the models.dev cache, so they differ per machine) and `moa` (a preset name). The reader ignores a block for any of these as well. On `openai` and `openai-api` it never takes `gpt-6-astra` from the manifest, because only the account's own listing may advertise it.

This is 1 of 4. The later PRs (#157318, #157319, #157320) use the same manifest and the same "only fills what the install doesn't have" rule for context windows and metadata, the id sets that gate request handling, and pricing. Each one works without the ones after it.

## Related Issue

Part of #157322 (1 of 4). The stack, in merge order:

1. #157316: picker lists for every provider (this PR)
2. #157318: context windows and metadata
3. #157319: the id sets that gate request handling
4. #157320: pricing

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/model_catalog.py`: adds `cached_manifest()` (in-process copy, else disk cache, never a fetch; `None` when `model_catalog.enabled` is false), `manifest_provider_models()`, `manifest_additions()` and `merge_remote_models()`. The in-process cache becomes one tuple. A cache file that can't be decoded is a cache miss.
- `hermes_cli/models.py`: the six places that build a provider's curated list (`curated_models_for_provider`, `_stepfun_catalog`, `_anthropic_catalog`, `_openai_catalog`, `merge_profile_catalog`, `_static_catalog`) merge the manifest rows in. `static_catalog()` itself is unchanged, which is what keeps defaults and aliases on the built-in table. `fetch_ai_gateway_models` adds the manifest's rows after the shipped pairs and caches only the gateway's live index. The provider-model cache fingerprint includes the added rows, so a disabled catalog or a changed manifest isn't served from that cache. The file is over the size cap and ends 9 lines shorter.
- `hermes_cli/model_switch_providers.py`: `_build_curated_lists` merges per row, and reads the Nous list first because that call is the one that refreshes the manifest.
- `hermes_cli/model_setup_flows.py`, `model_setup_flows_bedrock.py`: the `hermes model` flows list the merged rows. The "long enough to skip the live probe" cutoff counts the shipped row only.
- `hermes_cli/models_detect.py`: a match on an added row is confirmed against the provider's own list before it keeps a bare name on the current provider.
- `hermes_cli/models_validate.py`: an added id is accepted where that provider's picker lists it.
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/models.py`: the onboarding recommendation skips added rows.
- `hermes_cli/codex_models.py`: `model_requires_account_discovery()`, one predicate for ids only an account listing may advertise. The manifest reader and the picker cache both use it.
- `scripts/build_model_catalog.py`: publishes every built-in row, minus the exclusions it now shares with the reader.
- `website/static/api/model-catalog.json`: regenerated (35 KB, was 12 KB).
- `website/docs/reference/model-catalog.md`: documents the per-provider blocks, the merge rule and `requires`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_model_catalog_provider_rows.py`: 26 tests. `tests/hermes_cli/test_provider_catalog_hooks.py`: one more, for a plugin's static row. `tests/hermes_cli/test_model_cache_swr.py`: two existing tests patched the globals the single cache slot replaced, and failed at setup; they patch the slot now.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_model_catalog_provider_rows.py`: 26 pass. They seed a manifest into a temp `HERMES_HOME` cache and go through the real entry points (`provider_model_ids`, `cached_provider_model_ids`, `detect_provider_for_model`, `validate_requested_model`, the onboarding endpoint, the setup flow, the builder). The first 9 are the original cases: a new model is listed for two unrelated providers, no built-in row is removed, the default and `static_catalog` are unchanged, an entry with an unmet `requires` is skipped, a disabled catalog adds nothing, one profile's cache isn't read for another, a cold-cache picker open lists the new model in the same call. Without the PR 7 of those 9 fail.
   The other 17 came out of review: shipped order and spelling, the four own-source rows, `gpt-6-astra`, a non-UTF-8 cache, the cache slot's path and mtime, the publisher's filters, a disabled catalog against an already-cached picker row, the onboarding recommendation (with and without a `default` label), bare-name detection in both directions, validation on StepFun / GMI / official OpenAI, the setup probe cutoff and the AI Gateway picker. 14 of the 17 fail on the previous head `b655ce9a`; the other 3 pin guards that already held.
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_model_catalog.py`: 30 pass, including the existing check that the committed manifest matches the builder's output.
3. Related suites: the 129 test files that reference the functions this PR touches. 2566 passed. 33 tests fail and 4 error, in 11 files. I ran those 11 files on `main` (`95a1d228c5`) on the same machine and diffed the failing ids: the same 33 and the same 4 (`No module named 'pwd'`, POSIX-only paths, `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py`). My first run of this PR missed two real failures in `test_model_cache_swr.py`, which is why I diffed ids this time instead of matching counts.
4. `python scripts/check`: 21 of 22 pass. `shims` fails on `main` on Windows as well (`.gitattributes` line endings).
5. By hand: add an id to a row in `~/.hermes/cache/model_catalog.json` and open `/model`; the id leads that provider's list.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass. I ran the 308 related files with `scripts/run_tests.sh` rather than the whole suite; see How to Test.
- [ ] `just check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs). All but `shims`, which fails on `main` on Windows too.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11, Python 3.14

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A

- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A

Limits worth knowing:

- `hermes model` reads the cache but doesn't refresh it. A CLI-only install with a cold cache sees the built-in rows until `/model`, the gateway or `hermes update` has fetched the manifest once.
- Six providers (`zai`, `nvidia`, `moonshot`, `deepseek`, `opencode-zen`, `huggingface`) show their plugin's `fallback_models` while their live `/models` probe is unavailable. The manifest rows join when the probe answers. I left that path alone because the list is plugin-owned.

prs.title: feat(catalog): fill in metadata and context windows for new models from the manifest
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Gives a model released after an install the right context window and capabilities, from the same remote manifest the picker already reads.

**The problem in plain terms.** When a model is new, an installed release has no row for it in the hardcoded tables. So it guesses. For the context window it falls back to a family catch-all, or to the generic 256K. For "does it take images, does it reason" it answers "unknown". The right rows are added on `main`, and stable users wait for the next release to get them. A wrong window means compression fires too early or too late.

**What changes.** `model-catalog.json` now publishes those tables as they are on `main`:

- `context_lengths.default`, `.bedrock`, `.codex_oauth`: the three hardcoded context-window tables (`DEFAULT_CONTEXT_LENGTHS`, `BEDROCK_CONTEXT_LENGTHS`, `_CODEX_OAUTH_CONTEXT_FALLBACK`).
- `model_metadata`: the built-in metadata entries (`_BUILTIN_MODEL_METADATA`), keyed by models.dev provider id and model id, in the models.dev entry shape.

Each reader looks at them in the place it already looked at the hardcoded table, at the end of the chain. An explicit `model.context_length`, live provider endpoints and models.dev still come first.

**The rule: it fills gaps, it doesn't correct.** A key or entry the install ships keeps its own value, under any casing, even when the manifest disagrees. What the manifest adds is the row for a model the install has never heard of. So for any model a release already knows, nothing changes. I chose that over "newest wins" because a table row on `main` is paired with the code on `main`, and applying it to older code is the kind of mismatch this stack should not create. Corrections keep shipping with releases.

For the context tables the matching is the same as today (a key is a substring of the model id, longest key wins), so a more specific manifest row beats a built-in family row for the models it names, which is exactly the gap being filled. Added keys are lowercased, because every reader matches against a lowercased id.

A malformed row is dropped rather than half-used: a window that isn't a positive integer, a blank key (as a substring it would match every model), or a metadata entry without a valid `limit.context`. A `cost` field in a metadata entry is ignored, so this table can't put a price on anything.

Metadata is looked up only when models.dev has no entry for the model. That keeps the manifest read off the picker's per-row capability path.

This is 2 of 4 and builds on #157316. **The diff here includes that PR's commit; the change to review is the last commit.** Please merge #157316 first; I'll rebase this onto `main` as soon as it lands.

## Related Issue

Part of #157322 (2 of 4). The stack, in merge order:

1. #157316: picker lists for every provider
2. #157318: context windows and metadata (this PR)
3. #157319: the id sets that gate request handling
4. #157320: pricing

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/model_catalog.py`: adds `manifest_table()`, `manifest_model_metadata()` and `extend_context_lengths()`. The last one returns the built-in table plus the manifest keys it doesn't have under any casing, lowercased; a blank key or a value that isn't a positive int is dropped. `manifest_model_metadata()` returns nothing for an entry without a valid `limit` and strips `cost`.
- `agent/model_metadata.py`: the two hardcoded-default lookups and the Codex OAuth fallback read the extended table. Net zero lines (the file is over the size cap).
- `agent/bedrock_adapter.py`: `bedrock_static_context_length` reads the extended Bedrock and default tables.
- `agent/context_pin.py`: the pin check reads the extended default table.
- `agent/models_dev.py`: `_builtin_model_metadata` falls back to the manifest entry, and `_apply_overrides` only asks for it when models.dev has no entry.
- `scripts/build_model_catalog.py`, `website/static/api/model-catalog.json`: publish the tables (44 KB, was 35 KB).
- `website/docs/reference/model-catalog.md`: documents both tables and the fill-gaps rule.
- `tests/agent/test_model_catalog_metadata.py`: 26 tests.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_model_catalog_metadata.py`: 26 pass. The first 7 are the original cases. They seed a manifest into a temp `HERMES_HOME` cache and go through `get_model_context_length`, `bedrock_static_context_length` and `get_model_capabilities`. Covered: a model with no built-in row gets its window (general and Bedrock) and its capabilities from the manifest, a shipped row and a shipped entry keep their values when the manifest disagrees, and a disabled catalog fills nothing. Without the PR 3 of those 7 fail; the other 4 guard behaviour that already holds.
   The other 19 came out of review: the window reaching the custom-endpoint, pin, Bedrock-family and Codex OAuth fallbacks, a mixed-case published key, a case variant of a shipped key, five malformed context rows, two non-mapping tables, five malformed metadata entries, two `cost` payloads, models.dev precedence and a non-UTF-8 cache. 8 of the 19 fail with this round's fixes reverted; the rest pin guards that already held.

3. `python scripts/check`: 21 of 22 pass. `shims` fails on `main` on Windows as well.

Limits worth knowing:

- `agent/model_metadata.py`, `agent/models_dev.py`, `agent/bedrock_adapter.py` and `agent/context_pin.py` now import `hermes_cli.model_catalog` at module top. That module only pulls in `hermes_cli.version_info` and `utils`, and other `agent/` modules already import `hermes_cli` this way, but say so if you'd rather the readers live elsewhere.

prs.title: search_files tells the model it can search case-insensitively
prs.body:
`search_files` can already search without caring about upper or lower case if the pattern starts with `(?i)`, but its description never said so. This adds that one hint to the `pattern` description so the model doesn't have to guess.

## Why

#157524 (merged as `ba0ccdaa`) made a leading `(?i)` work on every search backend (native rg, shell rg, grep fallback), but the schema still didn't mention it. In Teknium's sessions from Nov 4 to 17 there were **10,181** terminal `grep -i`/`rg -i` commands and only **25** `search_files` calls that used `(?i)`.

## Change

`tools/file_tools.py`, the `search_files` → `pattern` description only:

```diff
-"Regex for content search; glob (e.g. '*.py', '*config*') for file search."
+"Regex for content search (prefix (?i) for case-insensitive); glob (e.g. '*.py', '*config*') for file search."
```

**Token cost:** the full tools list (`json.dumps(get_tool_definitions(quiet_mode=True), ensure_ascii=False)`, cl100k) goes from 7,890 to 7,899 tokens, **+9**. The prompt-surface snapshot's `tool_tokens` goes from 9,464 to 9,473.

## Live check (probe model: Opus 5.5 on Nous, picked for this check)

Each run used its own fresh probe home and a seeded repo where "deprecated" shows up in 4 files with different casing. Counts come from each run's `state.db`. The prompts don't include the #157545 completeness note.

| leg | prompt | runs | `search_files` with `(?i)` | terminal `grep -i` | correct answer | $ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| origin/main | "every line … in any letter case" | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3/3 | 0.27 |
| this branch | "every line … in any letter case" | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3/3 | 0.28 |
| origin/main | "where does this repo mark things as deprecated?" | 3 | 4 | 0 | 3/3 | 0.09 |
| this branch | "where does this repo mark things as deprecated?" | 3 | 6 | 0 | 3/3 | 0.12 |

To be straight about it: in this small check the probe model already reached for `(?i)` without the hint, so the live runs show no change in routing. They show the hint does no harm. Every run was correct, and the `grep -i` calls were second-pass cross-checks after a `search_files` that had already returned all 4 hits, on both legs. The case for the change is the field gap above (10,181 vs 25), which a 12-run probe can't reproduce. Total spend was $0.77.

## Tests

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/ci/ tests/tools/test_search*.py`: 1180 passed, 0 failed, 8 skipped
- `python scripts/check --only health`: ok

## Prompt surface

This edits the stock `tools[]`, so `tests/fixtures/prompt_surface/` is regenerated in this PR (`surfaces.json`, `tools/search_files.json`). Merging needs a **hermes-agent-core approval**. Teknium approved the change itself.

Note: open PR #157545 also edits this schema area but doesn't touch the `pattern` line, so the later rebase should only need the snapshot re-rendered.

## Infographic

![search_files case-insensitive hint](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab30e14/REVRdoRfHnCr_MQMFvgSs_fQJ1I6m6.png)

prs.title: fix(desktop): recover fallback chain after quota reset
prs.body:
## Summary

- share credential-pool exhaustion policy between the live agent fallback walker and Desktop/TUI pre-agent resolution
- skip fallback rungs whose entire credential pool is benched beyond the retry horizon, continuing to later configured providers
- preserve the configured primary when Desktop starts on a pre-agent fallback so a cached gateway agent retries it after quota recovery instead of requiring restart
- publish automatic cooldown clears across processes (`status_cleared_at`) and remove stale `failure_reason`, so an already-running pool observes recovery written by a fresh process

Fixes #119195

## Diagnosis

Desktop/TUI resolves authentication fallbacks before `AIAgent` construction. The report and addendum expose three related gaps:

1. The live agent fallback walker rejected a candidate when every credential for that provider/model was in a long cooldown, but the Desktop pre-agent resolver did not. It could therefore select a quota-benched first fallback and never reach a later healthy rung.
2. When pre-agent resolution selected a fallback, `AIAgent` was constructed from that fallback runtime and snapshotted it as `_primary_runtime`. In a long-lived Desktop session there was then no record of the configured primary to retry after its quota window recovered.
3. Automatic cooldown expiry cleared `last_status` / `last_error_reset_at` on disk, but did not stamp the cross-process clear marker and left `failure_reason` behind. A fresh process could therefore see the row as recovered while an older live pool had no authoritative signal that its in-memory cooldown was stale.

## Verification — October 3, 2026 maintenance

Rebased all five fix commits onto current upstream `main` at `c8301ea6c9` and pushed head `712430f988`. GitHub reports the PR mergeable.

Two conflicts were resolved while preserving both the PR's previously reviewed behavior and newer upstream behavior:
- `agent/credential_pool.py`: preserve upstream live-row handling following an early Codex quota-reopening probe and also publish the PR's `status_cleared_at` marker/remove stale `failure_reason`.
- `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`: retain the upstream early quota-reopening helper alongside the PR's pre-agent configured-primary restoration logic.

**Windows focused regression run at this exact head:** **111 passed**, covering the credential pool, cooldown/rotation and Codex early-reopening cases, primary restore, Nous automatic wire changes, model switching and CLI runtime restoration, plus TUI pre-agent fallback resolution. Focused Ruff and `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed. Worktree clean.

The previously reviewed internal model-switch and one-turn override preservation fixes remain included. No native macOS/Linux matrix, full repository suite, or hosted CI success is claimed for this rebase.

## October 8, 2026 mainline integration

- Merged upstream `origin/main` into the reviewed head `712430f988` without rebasing. Integration merge: `f485560fd7`, pushed to `fork/fix/119195-desktop-fallback-chain`.
- Resolved the single conflict in `agent/credential_pool.py` by preserving `status_cleared_ids` alongside upstream credential pool list handling.
- Exact merged-tree fallback/credential regression suite: **101 passed** across credential pools, cooldowns, exhausted-pool fallback, configured-primary restoration, TUI hot reload, Gateway fallback reload and pre-agent notice.
- Model-switch adjacent tests: **30 passed** for default persistence, reasoning re-resolution, variant tags and user-provided provider switching.
- Ruff on `agent/credential_pool.py`, `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`, `hermes_cli/cli_model_switch_mixin.py`, and `tui_gateway/server.py`: **all checks passed**.
- Local worktree clean after push. Hosted CI and Linux/macOS verification remain outstanding.

prs.title: feat(plugins): expose authenticated embeddings through ctx.llm
prs.body:
Plugins can use Hermes-authenticated completions today, but generating embeddings requires their own provider transport and credential setup. This adds `ctx.llm.embed()` and `aembed()` with Hermes-owned embedding selection, profile-scoped credentials, and existing override trust gates.

The new `auxiliary.embedding` slot selects an embedding model independently of chat routing. Initial support covers OpenAI-compatible API-key routes, including configured custom/OpenRouter shared-space models; chat-only OAuth grants and task-specific models without a supported mapping fail explicitly. The CLI picker asks for an embedding model and requires a shared-space declaration for unknown models. No credentials enter plugin results or errors, and requests never fall back to a chat model or another provider.

Results carry ordered finite vectors, actual provider/model, dimensions, usage, and bounded audit metadata. Validation rejects malformed batches, missing/duplicate vector indices, ragged/nonfinite vectors, and dimension disagreement. Credential recovery stays within the selected provider and preserves model selection. Existing completion APIs are unchanged.

Validation:

- Canonical `scripts/run_tests.sh`: plugin facade and embedding transport, plugin task routing/registration, auxiliary configuration/picker, existing auxiliary-client and credential-pool regression suites.
- Deterministic loopback tests use the real provider resolver, isolated profile configuration, synthetic credential-pool rotation, and concurrent async profile calls. No live provider or user corpus is used.
- `python scripts/check --base a84025ade22d2a4085f575d4353072e5b702635d` and `git diff --check`.

The change is additive and contains no downstream product imports or memory policy.

prs.title: fix(loops): coalesce duplicate same-index /loop wakeups via persisted-transcript dedupe (sys-8xces5)
prs.body:
## Problem

Gateway `/loop` wakeups could fire the same tick twice into a session. The wakeup path in `gateway/run_goals.py` called `abandon_tick()` on ANY injection exception — including a raise that came AFTER the prompt had already persisted as a `role=user` turn. Rolling that tick back made the watcher re-render the identical `#N` prompt on the next pass, producing byte-identical duplicate turns (observed as a 5x duplicate-turn incident). `session_automation` retries never dedupe because the FIFO identity is a fresh `uuid4()` per call.

## Fix

The persisted transcript becomes the dedupe ledger:

- `abandon_tick(payload=...)`: when the caller knows the prompt persisted before the raise, the tick is NOT rolled back; instead `(landed_tick, landed_digest)` (tick index + sha256 of the exact payload) is stamped on `LoopState`.
- `fire_tick()`: re-firing an index whose `(index, digest)` matches the landed record claims the tick and returns `None` instead of re-injecting — one persisted user turn per index.
- Pre-persist failures keep the old rollback semantics (tick is not burned).
- Old `LoopState` rows round-trip: new fields cast to zero defaults.
- Viewer/RPC `abandon_tick` surface gets the same guarantee via the shared manager.

## Tests

`tests/gateway/test_loop_wakeup_coalesce.py` (new, 262 lines): duplicate-turn regression, stale-turn false-land regression, pre/post-persist rollback split, old-state round-trip. Plus the existing `tests/hermes_cli/test_loops.py` suite.

```
python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_loop_wakeup_coalesce.py tests/hermes_cli/test_loops.py -q
72 passed
```

Bead: sys-8xces5

prs.title: The Windows control-pipe identify test no longer fails on a busy runner
prs.body:
When a gateway has just started, the first program that asks it "who are you?" used to wait while the gateway worked out its own version by running git several times. On a busy Windows machine that took longer than the asker was willing to wait (5 s), so it gave up on a gateway that was alive and listening. Now the gateway works that out before it starts listening, so the first answer is instant.

**Root cause:** `GatewayControlServer` built its first `identify` answer lazily, inside the first client's deadline. That answer paid the uncached code-identity git walk (up to seven subprocesses) plus the first psutil process probe in `_build_pid_record`. Under load on Windows that came to more than 5 s, so `run_bounded_sync('control-pipe')` abandoned a live server. This is the flake from main run [44381400294](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/44381400294/job/135074615090).

This is a product bug, not a test race: the fixture already waits for the server's own `SERVER_STARTED` line, printed after `start()` returned and the pipe instances exist. Real clients have the same window, since `hermes update`'s fleet probe, Desktop and `gateway ensure` all identify a just-started gateway with 2–5 s budgets. Raising the deadline would only move the cliff.

### Windows proof (real runner, `blacksmith-32vcpu-windows-2025`)

Same temporary workflow on both sides: `tests/gateway/test_control_socket_windows_live.py` via `scripts/run_tests.sh` with `HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0`, 20 iterations, under 64 Python busy loops + 16 loops spawning git nonstop (the shape of the `-j 16` OS lane). The workflow is not part of this PR.

| | run | result |
|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` (b1db37d2b9) | [44396630943](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/44396630943) | **6/20 pass, 14 fail**, every failure `'control-pipe' timed out after 5.0s` / `identify returned None` |
| this fix | [44406482811](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/44406482811) | **20/20 pass** |

Timing probe on the same runner and load. A cold `build_identify_payload()` in a fresh process took **4.6–6.7 s** (git walk ~5 s, psutil first probe 0.5–1.8 s). With the fix, the server's first answered identify takes **0.000 s** and the client's first round trip **0.033 s**. On main it was 0.6–1.9 s even after the code identity was cached.

An intermediate version that only warmed the code identity reached 13–15/20 ([44396679494](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/44396679494)). The probe then found the remaining cold cost in `_build_pid_record`, so this PR warms the whole default payload.

### What changed

- `gateway/control_socket.py`: `GatewayControlServer.start()` builds one default `identify` payload off the loop (`asyncio.to_thread(build_identify_payload)`) before it binds. That warms every lazy cache, and it also pins the code identity the gateway booted with. Before, if an update swapped the checkout ahead of the first identify, the gateway reported the new code.
- `tests/gateway/test_control_socket.py`: a contract test that the identity is resolved by the time `start()` returns and that `identify` answers from that one resolution (red on main: `assert 0 == 1`). Also fixes two pre-existing Windows footguns in that file (`write_text` without encoding, a BOM-intolerant read).

### Tests

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_control_socket*.py`: 77 passed, 2 skipped (Windows-marked, expected on Linux).
- Every test file that drives `GatewayControlServer` / `_start_gateway_start_control_socket` (37 files): 514 passed, 0 failed.
- `python scripts/check --only health`, `ruff check`, `git diff --check`, `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py` on the touched files: clean.



## Infographic

![Control pipe warms before it opens](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab3039d/qIx7AZx5b5r8C3mvb4Ahe_RVDeSTWb.png)

prs.title: Desktop preview rail plays audio files instead of refusing them as binary (port lobehub#22918, salvage #123274)
prs.body:
When you click an audio file (a `.wav`, `.mp3`, `.ogg`…) in Desktop, the preview rail on the right shows "This looks like a binary file" and has no way to play it. Now it shows a player you can seek, and that works for a clip inside a Docker agent's `/workspace` too.

**Outcome:** audio files play in the Desktop preview rail, streamed from the same session the tab belongs to.

Port of lobehub/lobehub#22918 ("preview and play audio files"). Salvages #123274 by @rsegrest (open since Sep 26, no review yet). Both of their commits are cherry-picked with authorship kept. Our hardening is one commit on top.

## What changes

| Click `take.wav` in the rail | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Local file | "This looks like a binary file · Preview anyway" (Preview anyway shows unreadable bytes) | `<audio controls>` streaming `hermes-media://stream/…` (Range, seekable, no whole-file read) |
| `/workspace/out/take.wav` in a Docker-backed session | refusal screen | player; stream request carries `{path, profile, sessionId}` of the tab's session |
| File rewritten in place by the agent | n/a | player remounts and re-fetches (from #123274) |
| Stream fails | n/a | "Couldn't load this audio file for playback." + Open in external, in all 8 locales |

Screenshots: real renderer components (`AudioFilePreview` / `LocalFilePreview` from each tree), mounted on an untracked Vite probe page with a stubbed desktop bridge. This is not the full Electron app.

| main | head |
|---|---|
| ![main](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/35db5913d5533ed177ac88f88d3455cb/raw/5ea58e74964724250ac758f41591f69abafc9114/audio-preview-main.png) | ![head](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/35db5913d5533ed177ac88f88d3455cb/raw/5ea58e74964724250ac758f41591f69abafc9114/audio-preview-head.png) |

## Changes

- **@rsegrest (#123274):** `electron/preview-kind.ts::previewKindForFile` classifies `audio/*` MIME as `audio` before the binary fallthrough. `lib/media.ts::isAudioFilePath` covers the renderer fallback. The new `AudioPreviewPlayer` streams through `resolveMediaPlaybackSrc` and has loading/failed/ready states plus a `reloadKey` remount.
- **Hardening (ours):**
  - The player passes the tab's `sessionId` to `resolveMediaPlaybackSrc`, the same way the text/image reads in `LocalFilePreview` already do. Without it a sandboxed `/workspace` clip was looked up on the host, while the transcript's inline player (`useMediaPlaybackSrc`) found the same file.
  - `blob:` sources (webapp proxy) are revoked on unmount.
  - Audio tabs are routed in `preview-pane.tsx::PreviewDocumentBody`, which already splits artifact vs file, to a new `AudioFilePreview`. `LocalFilePreview` is unchanged from main. The original placement put `LocalFilePreview` over the health ratchet (CC 59→62, 296→307 lines).
  - `preview.audioUnavailable` is translated into all 8 overlays and `locales/_keys.desktop.json` regenerated.
  - The 8 jsdom cases are cut to 2 invariants: an audio tab plays through a Range stream with no text read, and the stream names the tab's session. The session test fails with the `sessionId` hunk reverted and passes with it. The contributor's `preview-kind`/`media`/`local-preview` unit tests and the Electron e2e spec are kept as they were.

## Comparison with LobeHub

LobeHub routes audio by MIME/extension to an `@lobehub/tts` AudioPlayer that is fed the file URL, and shows a download button when playback fails. We use the native `<audio controls>` element on Desktop's existing Range-capable `hermes-media://` protocol, which needs no new dependency. Ours also handles the remote-gateway and sandboxed-session routing, which LobeHub's single-origin web app doesn't need.

## Verification

- vitest: `src/app/chat/right-rail/`, `src/i18n/`, `src/lib/media.test.ts`, `src/lib/local-preview.audio.test.ts`, `electron/preview-kind.test.ts`: **36 files / 335 tests passed**.
- `npm run check:lint` (typecheck + eslint): 0 errors. `scripts/check --only health`: ok.
- **Live:** the probe page described above, with main and head side by side. On main the target arrives as `binary`, the refusal screen shows, and no stream is requested. On head the `<audio controls>` mounts and the stream call is `{"path":"/workspace/out/take.wav","profile":"docker-coder","sessionId":"sess-docker-42"}`.
- **NOT_COVERED:**
  - Actual decoding in the probe browser: headless Chromium in a hidden tab left `readyState 0` even for a bare `new Audio()` control, so that is the harness, not the player.
  - The contributor's real-Electron `e2e/audio-preview.spec.ts`: on this host the mock-backend boot never makes the composer hit-testable, and `e2e/boot.spec.ts` fails the same way on its own. CI's e2e lane covers it on release/dispatch runs only.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab30da7/RFOHkLeueFY2wyVWOEWUN_OMYISm4Q.png)

prs.title: fix(tts): strip markdown in text_to_speech_tool, with a raw-markup opt-out for command providers
prs.body:
## What

`text_to_speech_tool` (the agent-callable TTS entry point) passed raw markdown to providers, which verbalized the artifacts ("double-asterisk Bold double-asterisk"). The two other TTS call sites (`_send_voice_reply`, the Auto-TTS path) already strip markdown; this aligns the third.

- Text is normalized via the shared `prepare_spoken_text` cleaner **before** provider dispatch and before the provider length budget is applied, so truncation applies to spoken length, not raw markup.
- Command providers that consume raw markup themselves (SSML- or Markdown-aware engines) can opt out per provider with `skip_markdown_strip: true`. The option follows the repository's shared boolean semantics (`is_truthy_value`, like the adjacent `voice_compatible`): false-like strings stay disabled.
- Raw-markup contract: opted-out input is **never split** — it is dispatched as exactly one untouched payload, and input longer than `max_text_length` is refused with a descriptive error instead of being cut into malformed fragments (the plain-text splitter is not XML-aware).
- Documented in `website/docs/user-guide/features/tts.md` (config-key table), limited to the new option.

## Tests

`tests/tools/test_tts_markdown_strip.py`: default stripping (bold/headers/inline-code/list markers), truncation-after-strip, the opt-out passing SSML+markdown through untouched, command-provider default stripping, false-like strings keeping stripping enabled (parametrized), true-like values enabling the opt-out, over-limit raw SSML refused with zero dispatches, under-limit raw SSML arriving as one valid chunk, and plain text still chunking as before.

(Note: this PR previously also carried Telegram/OGG conversion gating; that work is no longer part of this branch and the title/body now describe the current diff.)

prs.title: feat(plugins): add register_background_service() API for long-running services
prs.body:
## Motivation

Plugins that observe an external event source (notification pollers, file-sync watchers, RSS monitors) currently have no sanctioned way to run as long-lived gateway services — the existing surface covers platform adapters (`register_platform`) but not services without `MessageHandler` plumbing. This PR widens the generic plugin surface so such integrations can live **outside** the core tree (per the AGENTS.md standalone-plugin policy) while still getting proper lifecycle management from the gateway.

Context: our Nextcloud integration PRs (#11459, #11460) were closed under the in-tree-provider-integration policy with a pointer to ship them as standalone plugins. This API is the missing enabler — it mirrors the existing `register_platform()` / `platform_registry` pattern one-to-one, so external service plugins are wired up the same way platform plugins already are.

## Components

- `gateway/service_registry.py` — `BackgroundServiceEntry` dataclass + `BackgroundServiceRegistry` singleton (register/get/create_service, same shape as `platform_registry`). `create_service()` gates on `check_fn` (deps), optional `validate_config`, and guards factory exceptions.
- `hermes_cli/plugins.py` — `PluginContext.register_background_service()`, same kwargs shape as `register_platform()`.
- `gateway/config.py` — `GatewayConfig.services` dict populated from the `services:` block in config.yaml; per-service schema stays plugin-owned.

prs.title: fix(agent): route the tool-name repair notice through _vprint so --quiet gates it
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #95803: the tool-name auto-repair notice was emitted with a bare `print()` — the only one in its block, where every neighbouring diagnostic routes through `agent._vprint()`. As a result `--quiet` (and the stricter `suppress_status_output` single-query mode) never gated it, and in headless deployments the notice became the single loudest line in the logs: the reporter measured **4,804 lines / 24h** on one deployment (worst single session: 527), while the properly-gated "Processing N tool call(s)" lines were at zero — the exact inverse of what `--quiet` asks for.

The fix is the one-line routing change: `print(...)` → `agent._vprint(...)`. `_vprint` already implements the full gating contract — suppressed under `suppress_status_output` (`hermes chat -q` machine-readable stdout) and during streaming playback — so the notice now behaves like the diagnostics surrounding it. The repair logic itself (`_repair_tool_call`, the rewritten name) is untouched.

## Related Issue

Fixes #95803

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/conversation_loop.py` — the auto-repair notice in the tool-call validation loop now goes through `agent._vprint(...)` instead of a bare `print(...)`; comment records the #95803 measurement so the next bare-print doesn't reappear here.
- `tests/agent/test_tool_repair_notice_quiet.py` — regression pin: the notice text's enclosing statement routes through `agent._vprint`, and no bare `print(f"Auto-repaired tool name` form remains anywhere in the module.

## How to Test

1. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/agent/test_tool_repair_notice_quiet.py -q` — should pass: 1 passed. Red/green: with the `conversation_loop.py` change stashed, the pin fails (the notice is a bare print); with the change, it passes.
2. Adjacent repair suite should pass: `pytest tests/agent/test_canon_args_memo_parity.py -q` (13 passed). `ruff check` on both changed files should pass.
3. Observed behavior: a `--quiet` run (or `hermes chat -q`) that triggers a tool-name repair no longer prints the notice to stdout; a verbose run still sees it.

prs.title: Catalog self-updater check allows swarm-studio's pinned Godot and asset downloads
prs.body:
swarm-studio passed review (catalog sweep 1117), but CI's self-updater check rejects it. That check rejects any script that both downloads from GitHub and writes files. Five swarm-studio files match that pattern, and none of them can change the plugin's own code. This PR adds them to the maintainer allowlist, the same exception rom-studio got in c711c2efe667.

| File | What it downloads | Where it writes |
|---|---|---|
| `engine/godotinstall.mjs` | Godot 4.7.2 editor + Web export templates, only when the user asks in the game chat; pinned godotengine 4.7.2-stable release, checked for size and against the release's published SHA-512. On macOS with Homebrew the editor instead comes from `brew install --cask godot` (Homebrew's current cask, not pinned) | editor: `<plugin data>/godot/4.7.2/`; the two Web templates: Godot's own `export_templates/` folder, outside HERMES_HOME |
| `engine/library.mjs` | picture assets from the third-party assetrizz repo, pinned to one commit | `<plugin data>/assetrizz/<pin>/`, paths confined to that folder |
| `dyad/makers/MakerAppImage.ts` | AppImage type2-runtime, checked against a fixed sha256 (vendored dyad build tool; the plugin never runs it) | a temp build dir |
| `dyad/scripts/symbolicate-dump.mjs` | Electron debug symbols (vendored dyad dev script; the plugin never runs it) | the user's cache dir |
| `tests/godotinstall.test.mjs` | nothing (injected fake fetch) | test temp folders |

Each row is keyed by repo, the reviewed sha `09326a8d0f28e0b6c7c39392fac6f18323c3fd6c`, the path and the file's sha256, so a re-pin or any edit to one of these files is checked again. I ran the real gate function (`_check_self_updater`) on the pinned tree: it passes with these rows, and the same tree under any other sha is still rejected.

Unblocks #154007.
