## Summary

The desktop preview rail currently refuses audio files (`.mp3`, `.wav`, `.ogg`, etc.) as binary, even though the chat transcript already has an inline audio player for the same file types (see #90435, which notes this exact gap). This PR adds an `audio` `previewKind` alongside the existing `html`/`image`/`pdf`/`text`/`binary` kinds so the rail plays audio instead of showing the binary-file warning.

- Adds `previewKindForFile()` (main process, `apps/desktop/electron/preview-kind.ts`) and `isAudioFilePath()` (renderer, `apps/desktop/src/lib/media.ts`), both deriving from the same extension table `mediaKind()` already uses — so the preview rail and the chat transcript's player can't disagree about what's listenable. Video intentionally answers `false`: it shares the media pipeline but not the player affordances here.
- `PreviewTarget`/`HermesPreviewTarget` gain `'audio'` in their `previewKind` union.
- `LocalFilePreview` renders an audio element for the new kind; added a translated `audioUnavailable` string for the failure state.

prs.title: feat(desktop): search a conversation's full stored transcript, reachable from Cmd/Ctrl+F
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a visible search action beside the open conversation's title. It searches the stored transcript across compression segments, including compacted rows and long tool results, and lets users select or navigate matches to a bounded history window with a highlighted message.

The current page finder only sees rendered messages. The new path reuses the session search query parser and canonical fallback, scopes reads to the conversation's real compression lineage and owning profile, and uses the same display representatives for search and jump. Search responses contain snippets and metadata; a selected result loads at most 120 display rows. Query, owner, session and close transitions fence late responses, and failed or unsupported reads show recovery text.

## Related Issue

Fixes #132677

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_state_transcript_search.py` and `hermes_state_search.py`: reuse the search parser with a scoped display filter, deduplicate retained compression copies, search projected text, and return exact bounded match windows.
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/session_transcript.py` and `sessions.py`: add profile-owned search and match endpoints using the existing read-only session DB path and display projector.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/`: add the header search control, request state and result navigation; reuse the transcript history window and timeline reveal path while keeping the live message store intact.
- `apps/desktop/src/i18n/` and `locales/_keys.desktop.json`: add all bundled locale copy and regenerate the desktop key manifest. Move existing navigation copy and the Japanese language-picker copy to small modules so the oversized catalogs shrink.
- `website/docs/user-guide/desktop.md`: document the search action and keyboard navigation.

## How to Test

1. Open a stored Desktop conversation with older compacted messages. Click the header search icon and search text from an earlier segment, an assistant response, or a long tool result.
2. Select a result, use previous/next or Enter/Shift+Enter, and verify the corresponding history message is loaded and highlighted. Use the thread's return-to-latest control to resume the live view.
3. Switch the query, session or profile while a read is pending. Close the panel, disconnect the backend, or connect an older runtime. Verify stale results stay fenced and failed reads show recovery text.
4. Run the backend regression and related suites through the project runner:

    ```sh
    scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_conversation_transcript_search.py tests/hermes_cli/test_session_timeline.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_session_search.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_session_search_titles.py tests/tools/test_session_search.py tests/hermes_state/test_fts_index_fail_open.py tests/hermes_state/test_search_or_relaxed_fallback.py -j 4
    ```

5. From `apps/desktop`, run the focused conversation-search, history-window, timeline-reveal, runtime-backfill and i18n suites, then `npm run typecheck`, lint/format checks on changed files, `npm run i18n:keys -- --check`, `npm run build`, and `node scripts/assert-dist-built.mjs`.
6. Run `python scripts/check --base origin/main` with the repository's test interpreter.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] My commit message follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/).
- [x] I searched open, closed and merged PRs, issue-number references and the full issue timeline, and inspected adjacent search PRs for overlap.
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this feature and its required checks.
- [ ] I've run the complete Python test suite. The focused backend and related suites were run through `scripts/run_tests.sh`; the full suite was not run.
- [x] I've added behavior-contract tests for the new endpoints and Desktop interaction.
- [x] I've tested on Linux x86_64 and exercised the actual header/thread components in a browser smoke fixture.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated the Desktop user guide.
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A; no configuration keys were added.
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A; contribution workflows are unchanged.
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact: the renderer uses the existing REST bridge and history reveal path, and keeps the existing Ctrl/Cmd+F action.
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas: N/A; no tool contract changed.

## Screenshots / Logs

The two parameterized backend invariants were red on the unmodified base: all 10 cases failed because the stored-search endpoint was absent. The fixed path covers real temporary profile databases, A→B→A routing, default and named pooled launches, compression representatives, CJK/phrase/Boolean queries, long tool tails, hidden handoffs, multimodal text, and foreign-row rejection.

The UI invariants exercise actual `ChatHeader`, `ChatRuntimeBoundary` and timeline reveal behavior under React strict mode, including result paging, stale-response fencing and visible recovery. A browser smoke fixture with the actual `Thread` and a simulated REST bridge verified archived user/assistant jumps, previous/next selection, visible outline and close cleanup.
Final validation on `0895397ff9dfe66fbb4ef3340cd893238a4b5518`, rebased onto `3d304a112b99b9cd56799d3b9f0ba50095fdda8c`:

- Backend: 102 passed across 7 files through the project runner.
- Desktop and i18n: 87 passed across 11 files.
- Complete Desktop typecheck: passed.
- Prettier and desktop translation-key manifest check: passed.
- ESLint on changed files: zero errors; the pre-existing `history` hook dependency warning remains.
- Production renderer/Electron build and `assert-dist-built`: passed.
- `scripts/check --base origin/main`: 11 checks passed, zero code-health findings.

---

## Maintainer salvage (rebased onto current `main` + hardening)

Picked up by the weekly LobeHub scout: [lobehub/lobehub#21530](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/pull/21530) shipped the same capability (find in a topic's full history, Mod+F). This PR already covered the backend and header UI better than a fresh port would, so it is salvaged instead of reimplemented — @Nagisa-3000's commit is kept intact.

**What changed on top**
- `48993382dee` — @Nagisa-3000's commit cherry-picked onto `origin/main` (base was ~10.5k commits behind). Conflicts resolved to main: the i18n locale files are main's (overrides/split modules) plus one `conversationSearch` entry each; the PR's move of `findInPage` copy into `conversation-search.ts` and the `ja_language.ts` split were dropped (main already slimmed those catalogs); `_keys.desktop.json` regenerated (`npm run i18n:keys --check` clean).
- `a30ee2b2a56` — **Cmd/Ctrl+F reaches this search** (the LobeHub part). The find bar only sees rendered turns, so a user hunting an old message with the shortcut got 0/0 and never discovered the header icon. When the scoped chat surface has the transcript search, the find bar now shows a search button that opens it with the typed query and closes the bar. Tiles (no header search) show nothing.
- `1ebdc6ed2ad` — **remote-profile sessions**: Electron's remote-owner router only knew `/messages/around`, so `/messages/search` and `/messages/match` for a session on a remote profile hit the local backend and 404ed. Both now follow the same owner route.

| Scenario | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Long chat, Cmd+F for text from 200 turns ago | `0/0` (not rendered) | find bar offers *Search in chat* → stored-transcript hits → jump + highlight |
| Header search for text in compacted history | no such search | hits in compacted segments, bounded 120-row jump window |
| Same search on a remote-profile session (Desktop) | — | routed to the owning backend |

**Live repro** (real `hermes serve --isolated`, scratch HOME, seeded 300-turn session with the first 200 turns compacted away; turn 7 and turn 150 mention `Zephyr-Orchard`):
- `GET /api/sessions/long-chat/messages/search?q=zephyr-orchard` → rows 16 (turn 7) and 302 (turn 150), both from compacted history; phrase query `"deployment key"` → row 16 only; `GET …/messages/match?row_id=16&limit=3` → window starting at turn 7's answer (`offset 15, total 600, has_older/has_newer true`); unknown session → 404.
- On `main` neither route exists and the find bar has no hand-off.

**Tests run:** `tests/hermes_cli/test_conversation_transcript_search.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_session_timeline.py`, `tests/hermes_state/` (1843 passed), every test referencing the search impl (883 passed); Desktop `npm run typecheck`, eslint (0 errors), vitest `conversation-search`, `find-bar` (+1 hand-off test, red on main), `i18n/`, `assistant-ui/thread/`, `electron/profile-session-routing` (78 passed). `scripts/check --only health` clean.

**Not yet covered:** Desktop screenshots of the header search and the find-bar hand-off in a live Electron window (no isolated display was available to this run without touching the maintainer's session) — needed before merge.

## Infographic

![find-in-full-history](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab0474b/Gd5cV7wbHSSbY94sYR5VR_45Vg5mV9.png)
## Contributor follow-up validation

Rechecked the salvaged head `1ebdc6ed2adfa30b6de68e6bd9dab537f0f787a1` on Windows with Node 26.7.0 and Electron 44.9.3. The three salvaged/hardening commits are unchanged.

- The production renderer/Electron source build passes.
- The canonical frontend entries pass **234 tests across 10 files**: 100 conversation-search/history-window/paging/backfill/sidebar cases, plus 134 find-bar and Electron owner-routing cases. This includes the Ctrl+F hand-off and remote `/messages/search` / `/messages/match` routes.
- Started the built Electron main and renderer with an isolated home/userData and the real canonical gateway; only model inference uses the repository mock provider. The gateway reports ready for `local/default`, and its owner code SHA matches this head.
- Seeded 300 turns using native `SessionDB` compaction: 400 compacted history rows and 201 active rows including the summary. Through the live gateway's existing one-time native HTTP grants, `Zephyr-Orchard` search returns HTTP 200 with five matches, all confirmed to be early compacted rows. The selected match request returns HTTP 200 with a bounded 120-row window, includes the target, and reports `offset=4`, `total=600`, `has_older=true`, `has_newer=true`.
- Source working tree remains clean; `git diff --check` passes.

The requested actual Electron screenshots of the header search and find-bar hand-off are **still pending**. The window starts and responds, but native window capture timed out again after refreshing the target window and retrying. Build, HTTP and behavioral test evidence above does not complete that visual requirement.


## Desktop screenshots (head cd9f3b6e)

Native Electron on a private Xvfb, real gateway in a sealed scratch home, seeded 260-message session (`zephyrquartz` only in turn 4). Default pane layout, no injected styles, no manual anchor overrides, no local edits. Same drivers as the previous round.

**10. The app loads into the seeded chat.**

The popover's left edge is at x=263, which is ≥ composer-bounds x=260, so it no longer overhangs the sidebar. prs.title: catalog: add hermes-make-it-smart (desktop session catalog + pending-approval attribution)
prs.body:
## What this adds

One catalog entry: `plugin-catalog/hermes-make-it-smart.yaml`, pinning `tesla963/hermes-make-it-smart` at `847ee01cfe45bc13f1e653f9c272da771845e655` (v0.25.0).

- **Tier**: `community`
- **Author**: repo owner (submitted under admission rule 5, owner submission)
- **Type**: Desktop plugin (`desktop/plugin.js`) + Python tool layer

## What the plugin does

It builds a canonical catalog over **every** Hermes profile: the tool layer reads the local `state.db` files, names each session `NNN [Subject] MMM [Tag] [Tag] Description · Verb`, and the Desktop page exposes faceted filters (subject, maker, context, intention, theme, year, project).

Two parts are the reason it exists:

1. **Pending approvals, attributed.** The `memory.write_approval` / `skills.write_approval` gate accumulates requests that Desktop has no surface for (#84189, #98330). The plugin lists them split by Memory and Skills, and attributes each id to the session that produced it: exact when the `pending_id` appears in that session's tool result, otherwise by a ±120 s activity window with the confidence method exposed per id.
2. **Reversible rename.** A second tab simulates the canonical renaming in place, writes a mandatory backup first (`commit-backup-TIMESTAMP.json`, each entry carrying `title_before` and `title_after`), and only then commits through the host's `session.title` RPC — with a one-click **Revert** that restores the previous titles. Cron and empty sessions are never touched.

## Declared capabilities match `plugin.yaml`

`provides_tools`: cellar_search, cellar_session, cellar_stats, cellar_series, cellar_rename, cellar_tag, cellar_bateria, cellar_index, cellar_verify, cellar_export · `provides_hooks`: on_session_end · no env vars required.

## Desktop SDK surface

- Imports only `@hermes/plugin-sdk` and `react` / `react/jsx-runtime`.
- No `eval`, no `new Function`, no dynamic `import()`, no script-tag injection, no prototype patching, no `MutationObserver`, and no `data-slot` / `data-tour` / `data-sidebar` / `data-testid` reach-in.
- The only two `document` uses are a temporary `textarea` element it creates itself for the clipboard fallback, and a `querySelector` scoped to its **own** table (`#tb tbody tr.r[data-id=…]`).

## Validation performed at the pinned commit

```
hermes plugins validate .   → Validation passed
node --check desktop/plugin.js
node tests/test_plugin.mjs  → OK
python3 tests/test_invariants.py → 11/11 passed
python3 tests/test_protocol.py   → OK
```

English-first UI (with an ES/EN toggle), docs in English.

## Disclosure

Reads local session titles and message excerpts from the user's Hermes databases on their machine. Nothing is sent over the network. The single write is a session title, and only after the user presses **Commit** in the Testing tab; a backup is written first and Revert undoes it.

## No self-updater

The repo contains no in-app update check, no signed release downloader and no remote `plugin.js` loader. Updates reach users only through a SHA-bump PR here.

prs.title: fix(delivery-ledger): an owed attachment is a ledger row too — record by path+kind, redeliver on boot/reconnect
prs.body:
## The bug

The delivery ledger only ever owed **text**. When a turn's final response carried a `MEDIA:` attachment, the file went out on the adapter that received the message and was never recorded as owed:

- a reconnect mid-turn routes the text onto the *current* adapter (via `send_final_ledgered`) but the file through the *replaced* one — the dead transport returns `SendResult(success=False, error="Not connected")`, and nothing remembers the file existed (#150782);
- a flood-refused or crashed media send logs a warning and the attachment is permanently lost;
- a batch where one image fails is finalized as a whole, so the ledger can't say which file is still owed.

## The fix

Make the ledger speak about attachments directly: two more columns on an obligation row.

* `media_path` / `media_kind` — a row with `content=''` and a `media_path` **owes a file**, replayable through the adapter method its kind maps to (`image`/`video`/`voice`/`document`). Legacy rows and text-only rows are unchanged (the columns are `NULL`, no new keys appear in their claim dicts).
* The live send lanes `record → send → finalize` files in the same bracket text already uses (`BasePlatformAdapter._record_media_obligation` / `_finalize_media_obligation` in `gateway/platforms/base.py`, wired into the post-stream media delivery in `gateway/run_notifications.py`).
* The boot sweep and the reconnect sweep claim those rows and **re-send the file by kind** (`gateway/run_startup.py::_redeliver_claimed_obligations`), with the same profile/thread handling as text. The recovery marker (`RECONNECTED_MARKER` / `FLOOD_MARKER`) rides along as the file **caption** instead of being concatenated onto empty text. A file that vanished from disk is `mark_failed`d with `media file missing` and bounded by the existing `MAX_ATTEMPTS` — recovery never raises.
* The persistence layers (sqlite verbs + the `DeliveryObligationVerbs` / `ClaimedObligation` authority surface) carry the columns through; all signatures stay keyword-only `Optional` with `None` defaults, and the table migration reuses the `adapter_profile` `add_column_if_missing` pattern.

## Tests

* `tests/gateway/test_delivery_ledger_media.py` (new, 6 cases): record → sweep claim carries the media fields (and legacy rows don't grow keys); redelivery dispatches per kind to the right adapter method with the marker as caption; a missing file fails closed into `mark_failed`; the text-only cron lane does not regress.
* `tests/gateway/test_post_stream_media_delivery.py`: the post-stream lane now asserts the file is **ledgered before it is sent**, with ledger isolation updated to the current `_scope()`/store architecture.

Verified locally on `3371c03df6` — the full set of test modules that touch the obligation ledger / delivery sweeps, plus the standalone/reconnect delivery lanes:

```text
585 passed, 3 skipped, 1 xfailed in 336.81s (0:05:36)
```

including `test_delivery_ledger.py` (43), `test_delivery_ledger_media.py` (6), `test_post_stream_media_delivery.py` (5), `test_cron_reconnect_only_rejection.py` (2), `test_cron_live_delivery_confirmation.py` (28), `test_media_resend_dedup.py` (11), and the persistence contracts/conformance/e2e exactly-once suites. `uv ruff --select E9,F` on the touched files shows no findings that don't also exist on the base commit.

## Related work

I know this area has open traffic — this deliberately ships the smallest vertical slice:

* #106709 / #113496 put a JSON `media_manifest` blob on the row; this version stores the two typed columns the sweeps already know how to route (one file per obligation row, which matches how failures mark rows and how the flood timer arms per-row retries).
* #99855 replays `MEDIA:` directives embedded in the text column; that leaves "content='' with an attachment" unrepresentable — the exact shape a failed post-stream send needs to persist.

This closes the reconnect-loss path of #150782 end to end (record before send, replay by kind). It does not touch the content-embedded-directive replay of #99846 or the partial-batch success reporting of #131259, which remain open.

Fixes #150782
Part of #99846
Related #106709 #113496 #99855 #131259 #141585

prs.title: feat(display): diff-aware tool preview truncation
prs.body:
**Diff-aware tool-preview truncation** — full production path, rebased onto current `main`. Fixes #24298.

Show consecutive tool-call previews under the same ~40-char budget by eliding the shared prefix and revealing the **differing tail** (e.g. `cd /p && alpha` vs `… && beta`), instead of a dumb trailing-`...` head-cut that renders distinct commands identically (and then wrongly collapses them into `(×N)`).

### Before / After
Two consecutive distinct commands sharing a long `cd` prefix, at a ~40-char preview cap:

**Before** (dumb head-cut → identical renders → false repeat):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..."
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..." (×2)   ← looks like a stall
```
**After** (diff-aware → differing tail shown, no false collapse):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/…&& run alpha"
💻 terminal: "…&& run beta"
```
A genuine repeat of the *same* command still collapses to `(×2)` — dedup keys on raw identity, not on the rendered string.

### @teknium1's review — both points addressed on the production path
- [x] **Dedup keys on RAW identity, not rendered-truncation equality.** `_progress_emit` (gateway/run_turn_runner.py) now takes a `raw_key` derived from raw inputs (`tool_name` + raw command / preview / args) and dedups on that; truncation can no longer make two distinct commands collapse into `(×N)`. `truncate_middle()` stays presentation-only.
- [x] **The terminal/code-block path no longer head-truncates + bypasses.** `_progress_terminal_blocks` uses `truncate_middle` with a threaded `prev` (same as the ordinary preview path) instead of `cmd[:cap-3]+"..."`.

### Changes
- `agent/display.py`: `truncate_middle` / `_truncate_around_diff` / `_head_tail_truncate`; `prepare_tool_preview` gains optional `prev=`.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py::format_tool_event` **and** `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` (`_progress_build_message` / `_progress_terminal_blocks` / `_progress_emit`) thread `prev` + the raw dedup key via new `gateway/turn_context.py` fields.
- Tests: `tests/agent/test_display_truncate_middle.py` + `tests/gateway/test_run_progress_diff_aware.py` — distinct prefix-sharing commands must NOT collapse to `(×N)`; true repeats must (incl. on the `supports_code_blocks=True` path); covers a non-terminal preview. Stale expectations updated. All green.

The original branch was ~24k commits behind; this is a clean re-application onto current `main`.

prs.title: fix(build): skip npm PATH entries that vanish during resolution
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`npmCommand()` in `scripts/build/node-deps.mjs` probes each `PATH` entry with `existsSync()` and then resolves the hit with `realpathSync()`. An entry can pass the probe and stop resolving before the resolve — a dangling symlink, an entry dropped by a package-manager GC, or a lazily-materialized FUSE entry — and the unhandled `ENOENT` aborts the whole scan, so `hermes update` dies instead of using another npm installation (or the `npm_execpath` fallback).

This resolves defensively: catch the resolution error and keep scanning, and reuse the resolved path for the final candidate instead of calling `realpathSync(bin)` a second time. Missing entries were already skipped at probe time; this extends the same behavior to the resolve step. Motivation and environment details are in #147216.

## Related Issue

Fixes #147216

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `scripts/build/node-deps.mjs` — `npmCommand()` now wraps the per-entry `realpathSync(bin)` in a try/catch and skips the entry on `ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR`/`EACCES`/`ELOOP` instead of aborting the scan; the resolved path is reused for the trailing candidate rather than re-resolved.
- `tests-js/node-deps.test.mjs` — regression test: `realpathSync` throws `ENOENT` for one probed `PATH` entry, and `npmCommand` must still return a working CLI.

## How to Test

1. `node_modules/.bin/vitest run tests-js/node-deps.test.mjs` — 17 tests pass, including the new "npm discovery skips a PATH entry that vanishes during resolution".
2. Reproduce the original crash on `main` by putting a dangling `npm` symlink first on `PATH` and running any command that triggers dependency preparation; the branch survives it and falls through to the next candidate.

Verification note: this change is JS-only (`node-deps.mjs` + its test); the Python suite is untouched by the diff and is validated by CI. My local full-suite runs fail en masse for environment reasons that reproduce identically on a clean `origin/main` worktree (tests launched from a gateway-launched shell trip the real-home `home_io_guard`), so the `pytest` checkbox is deliberately unticked rather than claimed.

prs.title: chore(ci): build Linux AppImages on tag builds without gating releases
prs.body:
## Infographic

![Linux AppImages on canary. Before: Build: dummy jobs; Audit: no floor check; Smoke: never run; Canary: Linux gates it. After: Build: x64 and arm64; Audit: glibc floor audit; Smoke: packaged payload; Canary: never gated. Change: build-linux-<arch> on tag builds, DIAGNOSTIC_JOBS.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6aba972-67fd-4e80-a812-434462402fb3)

## What does this PR do?

`build-linux-x64` and `build-linux-arm64` in `desktop-bundled-release.yml` have been dummy jobs that only print a notice since 5f3f9f3e72 (#102765). Yet `publish-canary` still requires them to succeed, so a real Linux build could only have blocked the canary. This PR makes them real AppImage builds on tag builds (canary tags and stable candidates). They report their result but gate nothing.

Points to review:
- **Gating:** The builds table and canary publisher no longer wait for Linux. An admitted canary can omit either diagnostic group, but still needs all five macOS, Windows and Termux groups. Linux artifacts stay in the tag archive.
- **Floor** (`feat(bundles): audit a packaged Linux app against its glibc floor`): x64 builds in an `ubuntu:22.04` container (Blacksmith has no 22.04 label) and must run on Ubuntu 22.04 / Debian 12. arm64 builds on 24.04 and must run on 24.04 / Debian 13. `scripts/bundles/glibc_floor.py` fails the build when any ELF in the packaged app needs a newer GLIBC/GLIBCXX, or when it can't read an ELF's needs (missing section table, truncated header or section). The packed-relocation ABI marker counts as glibc 2.36. Upstream's x64 llama.cpp CUDA and ROCm engines are allowed up to 2.38.
- **Containers** (`chore(ci): run the desktop build cache action inside a job container`, `fix(ci): install Electron's libraries in the Linux build containers`, `fix(ci): keep the Linux checkout's git exemption under preparation's HOME`): the cache action now finds its script through `$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH`, because `github.action_path` names the host path inside a container (actions/runner#2185). The containers install GTK, NSS, GBM and ALSA, because preparation's native probe starts the downloaded Electron. They install the X11 development headers for the HUD shortcut helper and `rustc` for the native Python cache key, and exempt the runner-owned checkout from git's ownership check in the system config, because preparation runs git under its own HOME.
- The jobs smoke the packaged payload offline and stage the AppImage, plus electron-builder's feed yml when it writes one, to `releases/tag/<tag>/` only. No Linux feed, no download-table rows, no commit or channel builds, and the cache save step refuses commit and channel dispatches the way the native legs' does.

The AppImage packaging (#154493) and complete payload (#154539) prerequisites have merged.

## Related Issue

None filed.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## How to Test

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/ci/test_linux_desktop_builds.py tests/ci/test_protected_canary_publication.py tests/ci/test_tag_builds_summary.py tests/ci/test_commit_build_staging.py tests/scripts/test_bundle_glibc_floor.py tests/scripts/test_render_builds_publication.py tests/scripts/test_desktop_build_cache.py`
- `cd tests-js && pnpm exec vitest run setup-pm-cache.test.mjs`
- After merge, a dry canary-tag run: `gh workflow run desktop-bundled-release.yml --ref main -f tag=<canary tag containing this> -f jobs=linux-x64,linux-arm64 -f upload_release=false`.

Locally (Linux arm64, at `7c4ed8d28a`, before the rebase): those 7 files pass (62 tests) and `setup-pm-cache.test.mjs` passes (13); the floor audit passes the real packaged arm64 app (686 ELF files) and fails it against the x64 floor; the workflow's install step, run in `ubuntu:22.04` and `ubuntu:24.04`, leaves no Electron 44.9.3 library unresolved, starts it as node, and lets git read a uid-1001 checkout under a replaced HOME. The packaged payload smokes offline in `ubuntu:24.04` (on the first head; later commits don't touch the payload). Not run: the jobs on Blacksmith and anything x64, which need a canary tag containing this change.

Rebased onto main `6f929bf85d` as `e60362b3be`. Only the docs commit changed, at the workflows README bullet main had moved; the other 9 commits' patches are identical. On the rebased head, `tests/ci/` plus the three `tests/scripts` files pass (933 tests), `setup-pm-cache.test.mjs` passes (13) and `scripts/check` is clean.

On `a8e6033bc7`, the seven named Python files pass (70 tests). The broader CI and bundle-script set passed 953 tests with 3 skipped. The X11 HUD helper compiled in both Ubuntu containers on arm64. No full x64 AppImage, live tag build or release was run. This branch still conflicts with main in `.github/workflows/README.md`.

prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Closing the tab of a plugin that contributes exactly one pane called `setPluginEnabled(id, false)`. That unloaded the whole plugin, so its sidebar nav row, routes, directives and palette commands vanished along with the pane. Multi-pane plugins already just dismiss the pane. This makes single-pane plugins behave the same way: Close dismisses the pane (persisted in `hermes.desktop.dismissedPanes.v1`), the plugin stays loaded, and turning a plugin off stays an explicit Capabilities -> Plugins action.

Seen with a plugin that has one right-side pane plus a `sidebar.nav` row: after closing the pane tab, the nav row was gone and could not reopen the pane.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/components/pane-shell/tree/store.ts`: `closeTreePane` always takes the `dismissTreePane` path for plugin panes; removed the single-pane disable branch and the unused `setPluginEnabled` import.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/pane-shell/tree/plugin-pane-close.test.ts`: test now asserts the plugin stays registered and only the pane is dismissed.

## How to Test

1. Install a plugin with one pane and a `sidebar.nav` row.
2. Open the pane, click the tab close button.
3. Before: plugin switches off, nav row disappears. After: pane closes, nav row stays, `host.revealPane` reopens it.

`npx vitest run src/components/pane-shell` passes (51 files / 251 tests), `tsc --noEmit` and eslint clean on both files. Tested on macOS.

prs.title: feat(stt): support ElevenLabs Scribe keyterms
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Names and domain terms get mistranscribed by ElevenLabs Scribe. Scribe supports keyterm prompting, but Hermes never sends `keyterms` (and `stt.prompt` is unsupported for `elevenlabs`).

This adds `stt.elevenlabs.keyterms`, a list of strings sent as repeated `keyterms` multipart fields.

```yaml
stt:
  provider: elevenlabs
  elevenlabs:
    keyterms: ["Calliope", "T3 Code", "Outlayr"]
```

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `tools/transcription_cloud.py`: `_elevenlabs_keyterms` validates terms against ElevenLabs' documented limits (max 1000 terms, 50 chars, 5 words, none of `<>{}[]\`), warns and drops invalid ones, and skips `scribe_v1`. `_post_audio_multipart` now also accepts a list of pairs so a field can repeat; with no keyterms the form is the same dict as before.
- `cli-config.yaml.example`, `website/docs/user-guide/features/voice-mode.md`: document the key, limits and the 20% ElevenLabs surcharge on requests that send keyterms.
- `tests/tools/test_transcription_tools.py`: repeated fields (with invalid terms dropped), unchanged form when unset, ignored on `scribe_v1`.

## How to Test

2. `scripts/hermes-python scripts/check`

Results: 108 passed, 1 failed (`test_config_device_and_compute_type_passed_to_whisper`, a local faster-whisper test that fails identically on unmodified main). `scripts/check`: 22 checks ok.

prs.title: Pruned tool results keep their error, task and argument details; archive cleanup works past 20,000 references (salvage #156163)
prs.body:
When Hermes shortens an old tool result to save space, the one-line note it leaves behind now keeps the details that matter (a failed command's exit code and last line, a batch delegation's task count, an MCP call's issue number), and reading an archived result back no longer saves a second copy of it. The archive cleanup now works on homes with any number of stored references, and a failed archive write no longer leaves a half-written file behind.

Salvaged from #156163 by @100yenadmin. #156163 was stacked on #156081, which closed when #156455 superseded it, so these commits are cherry-picked (`-x`, authorship kept) onto `main`'s layout, where the prune archive now lives in `tools/tool_result_storage.py`. Two review fixes from this PR's own thread sit on top.

## Commit mapping

| #156163 commit | Verdict | Where it landed |
|---|---|---|
| `eee9b2a7` keep the details a model needs in tool result stubs | **Kept** (main still had `{line_count} lines output` from the JSON envelope, `'{goal}'` only, and the first two args) | `cd51c1fa`: `agent/context_compressor_prune.py::terminal_stub/delegate_stub/stub_arguments`, `_is_summary_stub` |
| `4569ceaa` point a read-back of an archive at that archive again | **Kept, adapted**: `agent/context_compressor_prune_archive.py` was moved by #156455, so `_readback_archive_path` now lives in `tools/tool_result_storage.py` next to `archive_pruned_originals` | `f257a21f` |
| `d0a0f9d8` clamp the hot-reloaded prune floor; name the real no-op reason | **Kept** (main still had min `0` in `_COMPRESSION_INT_KEYS` and the unconditional `prune:archive_write_failed`) | `ec323911` |
| `a5bed1d2` read every archive reference row, without the 20,000 cap | **Kept, adapted**: on main the cap moved into the persistence verb `MessageRepository.spillover_reference_rows` (`LIMIT 20001`), so the fix makes that verb stream every row in 2,000-row batches (SQLite and in-memory reference backends, contract docstring) and `referenced_archive_refs` folds them into the set; the contract tests that pinned the cap now pin "no cap" | `7ecfb478` |
| `8abb7e3d` clean up failed exclusive archives | **Kept** (main's `_write_to_spillover` still left a partial `xb` file on a write error) | `40db9efd` |
| (ours) | test trim: at most two invariant tests per behaviour | `04d098db` |
| (ours, Greptile P1) | each pruned result is matched to the nearest *preceding* call with its id (`_calls_for_rows`), so a resumed history that reuses a call id cannot hand an older result a later read-back's archive; the streamed reference read is registered in the awaitable-form contract's streamed verbs | `c9c7c838` |
| (ours, Greptile P2) | the three stub helpers join the existing module-top import in `agent/context_compressor.py` (no behaviour change) | `72b3447e` |

Nothing in #156163 was already on main or made obsolete by #156455; two commits needed porting onto the new layout.

## Before → after

| Case | Before (main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Failing `pytest` via `terminal`, pruned | `[terminal] ran `pytest …` -> exit 1, 1 lines output` | `… -> exit 1, 38 lines output \| last: FAILED tests/test_x.py::test_x - AssertionError` (stub stays under the 200-char prune floor) |
| Batch `delegate_task(tasks=[…])` | `[delegate_task] '' (N chars result)` | `[delegate_task] 3 tasks, first: '<goal>' (N chars result)` |
| `mcp_github_get_issue(owner, repo, issue_number)` | `owner=org repo=project` (issue number lost) | all args in order up to 120 chars |
| Model `read_file`s an archive, then a prune runs | a second archive file holding the line-numbered rendering | the stub points at the original archive again |
| Resumed history reuses a call id (older `terminal` result, later archive read-back) | n/a on main (no read-back reuse) | the older result gets its own archive; only the read-back points at the existing one |
| Hot reload `proactive_prune_min_result_chars: 50` / `0` | 50 / 0 (fresh build: 200 / 8000) | 200 / 8000, same as a fresh build |
| Post-archive no-op where no write failed | logs `prune:archive_write_failed` | logs `prune:reclaim_below_minimum` |
| Home with >20,000 rows referencing archives | the capped read answers "unknown", so cleanup KEEPS every `cache/pruned` and `cache/spillover` file, forever | full set read (streamed); unreferenced expired files are swept; a read error still fails closed and keeps everything |
| Reference scan time, Teknium's install (2.66M messages, 7,450 referencing rows) | 11.3 s (capped query) | 11.1 s (full streamed scan): no measurable cost |
| Exclusive archive write fails mid-write | partial file left in `cache/pruned` | the file this call created is removed; an existing file is never touched |

## Tests

- New/changed tests, each red on `origin/main` (0e8e4216) and green here: `tests/agent/test_tool_result_stub_text.py` (5), `tests/agent/test_proactive_prune_readback.py` (3 behaviours: read-back reuses the pointer, a reused call id keeps the older result's own original, a path that is not an existing archive is archived normally; parametrized), `tests/tui_gateway/test_compression_config_hot_reload.py` (2 new), `tests/tools/test_archive_reference_scan.py` (2), `tests/agent/test_proactive_prune_archive_writer.py` (2), `tests/contracts/conversation/test_message_verbs_contract.py::test_spillover_reference_rows_have_no_row_cap`, `tests/persistence_sqlite/conversation/test_message_reference_reads.py::test_spillover_reference_rows_stream_every_referencing_row`; `tests/contracts/core/test_awaitable_form_contract.py` now lists `spillover_reference_rows` as a streamed verb. On main: 22 failed of the new/changed cases before the trim.
- Suites at `04d098db`: `tests/agent/test_compaction*.py`, `test_proactive_prune*.py`, `test_context_compressor*.py`, `tests/tools/`, `tests/tui_gateway/`, `tests/contracts/conversation/`, `tests/persistence_sqlite/conversation/` via `scripts/run_tests.sh`: 21,116 passed, 168 skipped; the 2 failures (`tests/tools/test_sudo_askpass_delivery.py`, one collection error in `tests/tools/`) fail identically on `origin/main`. After `72b3447e`: compressor, stub-text and compaction suites 452 passed.
- CI on the current head (`72b3447e`): 16 checks passed, 21 skipped, 0 failed.
- `ruff` 0.15.22 clean on touched files; `python scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking, 0 advisory.

Trade-off kept from the original: the filter has no index, so the old capped query already read the whole `messages` table; the full scan now runs to the end instead of giving up, streamed in 2,000-row batches so memory is the reference set, not the rows. On Teknium's install (2.66M messages, 7,450 referencing rows) the full scan took 11.1 s against 11.3 s for the capped one, so no measurable cost. @100yenadmin measured ~0.22 s per 100k rows on a synthetic warm-cache `state.db` (#156163 thread).

Refs #156164 (items 2-8 of that issue are still open; this PR does not address them).

Credit: @100yenadmin for all five fixes and their tests; @kvnloo for the review on #156163.

prs.title: Two Windows tests stop failing at random
prs.body:
Two Windows-only tests kept failing at random on busy CI machines. The product code was fine both times: the tests were checking something before it was ready, or stopping only half of the helper program they started.

Outcome: under heavy CPU load on a real Windows runner, both test files went from red in 11/20 and 20/20 copies on main to 0/20 with this fix.

## Windows red/green (real runner, `wine2e/windows-live-flakes`, now deleted)

Each test file was copied 20× and run in parallel with `HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0`, next to 48 CPU-burner processes. These runs used the `windows-venv-e2e.yml` lane, since its stock steps don't include either file.

| | control socket (20 files) | backup recovery (20 files) |
|---|---|---|
| main code — [run 44396228102](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/44396228102) | **11/20 files red** (29 passed, 11 failed) | **20/20 files red** (32 passed, 48 failed, all `owner.lock` FileNotFoundError) |
| this fix — [run 44405378797](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/44405378797) | **40/40 passed** | **80/80 passed** |

Timing probe: [run 44399814363](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/44399814363). Without load, main passed 20/20 ([run 44394217346](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/44394217346)), which is why these only show up on a busy runner.

## 1. `test_control_socket_windows_live.py::test_pipe_gone_after_kill_falls_back`

- **Symptom:** the first line failed, `identify_gateway(home, timeout=5.0) is not None`, with `[deadline] 'control-pipe' timed out after 5.0s` (job 135086459293 on #157533).
- **Cause:** `SERVER_STARTED` only means the named pipe is bound. The server's *first* `identify` also works out its code identity (the uncached git provenance walk). I timed the server-side handler on `blacksmith-32vcpu-windows-2025` under load: **2.8–4.3 s per cold server** (client-side 2.9–4.5 s), then 0.00 s after that. A single 5 s probe lost that race. It never showed up in the first test of the file, and showed up in the second about half the time, because the second test's cold server was the one starting under the most load.
- **Fix (test):** the `live_server` fixture waits for the first real answer (`tests.waiting.wait_until`, 60 s hang bound) before it yields. A server counts as ready when it answers, not when it has bound the pipe. The wait and the `yield` sit inside `try/finally`, so the server is reaped even when the readiness wait itself fails.

## 2. `test_backup_staging_recovery.py::test_killed_backup_recovers_and_preserves_live_peer[True]`

- **Symptom:** `FileNotFoundError` on `<home>\.hermes-backup-stage-<hex>\owner.lock` inside `_await_lease_release` (FLAKY on the same job). The sibling `test_retry_elsewhere_reclaims_…` has the same bug. In the loaded red run the 48 failures split as `test_killed_backup_…[False]` 17, `test_retry_elsewhere_…[False]` 14 and `test_retry_elsewhere_…[True]` 17.
- **Cause:** `_kill()` killed `Popen.pid`. In a Windows venv that is the `python.exe` launcher, not the interpreter running the backup. Probe over 20 spawns: the real PID differed from `Popen.pid` **20/20**, and the backup **survived the kill 13/20**. The orphaned backup then read EOF on stdin, unwound normally and deleted its own stage while the test was inspecting it as abandoned.
- **Fix (test):** `_kill()` kills and reaps the launcher's whole tree with psutil. The "child reached staging" wait goes from 30 to 120 s. It only bounds a hang, and one cold child went past 30 s under the same load.
- **Not a product bug:** a really crashed backup leaves its locked lease for the next reaper, and a backup that unwinds cleanly removes its own stage. On a user machine, `owner.lock` can only disappear when its owner removes it.

## After review

Both Greptile findings were fixed on this branch: the readiness wait now cleans up on failure (8702bce60746), and the new `identify_gateway` and `psutil` imports are at module top (6ee631b74e8e). The green run above was on the code before those two follow-ups. On the head `6ee631b74e8e`, all three Windows-only CI jobs (x64, arm64 1/2 and 2/2) pass.

## Related

#118681 (@JoaoMarcos44) changed a later assertion in this same test (`stale` → `unknown` for the pytest PID). Main has since moved past it: 4adb4d5395fb asserts `unknown`/`code_sha is None` for the pytest PID, plus `stale` for a verified `gateway run` stand-in. Nothing to salvage, so it is closed with credit.

## Infographic

![Two flaky tests, steady](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab302f0/FIt2YPOW4CuEImopfGYOW_4Mfndd7Z.png)

prs.title: Shell exports survive noclobber, and three test files pass on a developer machine, not only in CI
prs.body:
If your shell startup turns on noclobber (`set -C`), anything you exported in one terminal command was lost before the next one, so PATH edits, venv activations and other `export`s quietly stopped carrying over. Exports now survive under noclobber, and two tests that only passed because of how the CI machine is set up now pass on a developer machine too.

Outcome: one real shell bug fixed in product code, plus two tests that no longer depend on the host. All three files that went red locally are green on this head.

## Before / after

Developer machine, `scripts/run_tests.sh`, each file run alone with a fake HOME (main = merge-base `6161a344098f`, head = `7be60cbaf278`):

| Test file | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_sudo_askpass_delivery.py` | 117 passed, **1 failed** (`sudo: Authentication failed`), 1 skipped | 118 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped |
| `test_bot_desktop_idle_self_stop.py` (host with a published launcher) | 1 passed, **5 failed** (idle-stop timeout) | 6 passed |
| `test_fal_sdk.py` (without the `fal` extra) | **collection error** (`No module named 'fal_client'`) | 1 skipped |
| `test_base_environment.py` | 22 passed | 22 passed (assertion updated to `>|`) |

Rows 1, 3 and 4 were re-measured for this description, on both sides. Row 2 is the author's original measurement. Under a fake HOME with no published launcher, main already passes 6/6, which is the CI situation this fix makes the test independent of.

## What changed, per file

**`tests/tools/test_sudo_askpass_delivery.py`**: real product bug, fixed in `tools/environments/base_session_env.py`
- Symptom: `test_live_local_backend_noclobber_startup_keeps_caller_input` fails with `sudo: Authentication failed` on any machine whose real sudo asks for a password. CI's runner has passwordless sudo, so it passed there by accident.
- Cause: when a session shell has `set -C` (noclobber) on, the env re-dump after each command wrote `export -p > "$__hermes_snap_tmp"`. That target is the file `mktemp` just created, and noclobber refuses `>` onto an existing file. The dump failed silently, so **every `export` was lost before the next command**. The test's `export PATH=<fake sudo>:$PATH` disappeared, and the host's real `/usr/bin/sudo` ran. Users whose `BASH_ENV`/profile sets `set -C` hit the same thing.
- Fix: write the dump with `>|`, which is still atomic through mktemp + mv. The test now also checks that the export carries over (`command -v sudo` is the fake), so a regression fails on that line and never reaches the host sudo.

**`tests/tools/test_bot_desktop_idle_self_stop.py`**: host-specific, test-only fix
- Symptom: 5 of 6 tests time out (`waiting for the abandoned screen to be stopped`). The screen's `launcher.log` shows `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'psutil'` from the idle check.
- Cause: the launcher runs the idle check through `installation_command(project_root)`. On a checkout with a published `.hermes/bin/hermes` and a store Python in the account's tool store, that resolves to the launcher. Under the test's temporary `HERMES_HOME` the launcher has no committed dependency generation, so it boots bare and cannot import psutil. CI has no published launcher, so it falls back to `sys.executable`.
- Fix: the test's gateway stub pins `hermes_cli._launchers.resolve_store_python` to `None`, so the idle check runs on the test interpreter. `test_a_screen_started_before_an_update_still_stops_itself` still covers the launcher route through its own prelude.

**`tests/tools/test_fal_sdk.py`**: optional SDK missing, test-only fix
- Symptom: collection error `No module named 'fal_client'` on any env without the `fal` extra (the default test environment).
- Fix: `fal_client = pytest.importorskip("fal_client", ...)`, the pattern the other optional-SDK tests use (boto3, anthropic). CI installs `--extra fal`, so it still runs there.

**`tests/tools/test_base_environment.py`**: `TestAtomicSnapshotWrite` asserted the exact `> ` redirect onto the temp file. It now asserts `>| "$__hermes_snap_tmp"`, and it still asserts that neither `> ` nor `>| ` ever writes the live snapshot directly.

## Verification
- The table above. The author also ran each file alone 3x on the head (same results each time). The snapshot and terminal neighbours (`test_snapshot_*`, `test_terminal_pipeline_status`, `test_docker_mounted_host_session_cwd`, `test_sudo_askpass_sdk_backends`, `test_local_env_blocklist`) gave 183 passed.
- CI on `7be60cbaf278`: every required check passes (Python tests 1–3/3, macOS, Windows x64 and arm64, SSH + Docker backends, lints, repository guards).

## Caveats
- The before/after for the bot-desktop file only shows up on a machine with a published `.hermes/bin/hermes` launcher and a store Python. A clean checkout or a CI runner passes it on main too.

prs.title: A commit in one worktree no longer rewrites another checkout's venv
prs.body:
A dev tree whose `.venv` was a link to another checkout's venv used to re-point that venv at itself on every `git commit`, so the other checkout silently ran this tree's code. Now the git hooks never run `uv run`: they start lefthook directly (or skip with a note), and nothing writes into a venv this tree does not own.

**Root cause:** lefthook's generated hook, when its baked binary path is gone (a deleted worktree's `node_modules`) and no lefthook is on PATH, falls back to `uv run lefthook -h`; `uv run` syncs the checkout's `.venv` and editable-installs the checkout into it, through the symlink, into the other checkout's venv.

**pm was not the writer.** The brief assumed pm was doing this write. On `origin/main`, `scripts/hermes-python` → `pm.cli install --test-environment` in tree A with `A/.venv -> B/.venv` leaves B byte-identical. strace shows every pm `uv sync` targets `installs/<key>/environments/<gen>/venv`; the only pm call that names `A/.venv` is `uv lock --check`, which writes nothing. The write comes from `git commit`: one `uv run lefthook -h` is enough to rewrite B (142 site-packages entries re-synced, `direct_url.json` → A). That matches the incident: the 08:37:23 compat-moves commit printed `Can't find lefthook in PATH` (so `just ruff` never ran), and the hook's `uv run` probe rewrote the runtime `.venv` at 08:37:25.

## Live repro (real `git commit`, no mocks)

Two scratch worktrees per leg, created with `git worktree add --detach` (main = `origin/main`, fix = this branch). B has its own `.venv` with an editable install of B. A has `.venv -> B/.venv`. Hooks are generated by `lefthook install` from each leg's own `lefthook.yml`, and the lefthook binary is then deleted (Teknium's state: the baked path points at a removed worktree). Then `git commit` runs in A with a plain PATH.

| leg | B `direct_url.json` sha256 before → after | B finder MAPPING `agent` before → after | B's venv imports `agent` from | A imports (`scripts/hermes-python`) | hook output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | `71ec216637c2` → `cc46f4ef8500` (url B-main → **A-main**) | `e0ed0e1a96e7` → `60c7f8ac0218` (B-main → **A-main**) | **A-main** ❌ | A-main | `Can't find lefthook in PATH` (after `uv run lefthook -h` re-synced B) |
| fix | `693a26e0c567` → `693a26e0c567` (unchanged) | `d7fd0af6b485` → `d7fd0af6b485` (unchanged) | B-fix ✅ | A-fix ✅ | `✔️ lint python`, `✔️ move shims` (the real hooks ran) |

An independent reviewer re-ran this at `36531817` vs main `6161a344` with real `uv`: main rewrote B; this head left B byte-identical with 0 `uv` calls in all three states (no lefthook → skip note and the commit succeeds; pnpm's native binary plus `just` → jobs run; no `just` → jobs run through `scripts/run-in-hermes-env`).

## Change

How the hook is fixed: lefthook's generated hook runs the top-level `lefthook:` command from `lefthook.yml` when one is set, before its own PATH / `node_modules` / `uv run` search. This PR sets that key, so the search (and its `uv run` fallback) is never reached.

- `lefthook.yml` gets a top-level `lefthook:` command that runs `scripts/run-lefthook`. The command is written so a checkout that predates the script skips the hooks with a note instead of failing. The hook still honours `LEFTHOOK=0` and `LEFTHOOK_BIN` first.
- `scripts/run-lefthook` looks for lefthook in this tree, then in the clone's main checkout (hooks are shared by every worktree), then on PATH. It checks pnpm's isolated layout (`node_modules/.pnpm/lefthook-<os>-<arch>@*/…/bin/lefthook`) and the hoisted layouts lefthook's generated hook searches (npm, `pnpm --node-linker=hoisted`). It uses the native binary, not the `node_modules/.bin` shim, which needs node. It has no package-manager or `uv run` fallback. If it finds nothing it skips with a note, and otherwise it only execs lefthook, with no environment setup.
- The jobs run `{just}` (a `templates:` entry → `scripts/hook-just`). When `just` is not on PATH, that script gets it from `scripts/run-in-hermes-env` (this checkout's own PM environment), and only after lefthook has matched staged files to the job. A docs-only commit never sets up an environment.
- Hooks already installed pick this up on the next `pnpm install` (the `prepare` script re-runs `lefthook install`).

## Tests

- `tests/scripts/test_run_lefthook.py`: 7 behaviour tests, each in a real git checkout whose `.venv` links to another venv, with a recording `uv` on PATH. They cover: the checkout's native lefthook runs with `run pre-commit` and never calls uv; with no lefthook it skips with a message; the hoisted layout is found; a linked worktree uses the main checkout's lefthook; a job without `just` goes through `scripts/run-in-hermes-env`; and two real `git commit`s through the hook that `lefthook install` wrote, whose baked binary was then deleted. In the first, uv is never called. In the second, a docs-only commit with no `just` never runs environment setup. The two `git commit` tests need a pnpm-installed lefthook, so they skip in CI; locally the file is 7/7. Each new test fails on 36531817 or under the mutation it targets.
- Live repro on ae453e10 (strace, plain PATH, hooks generated and then the baked binary deleted, lefthook from the hoisted path, `A/.venv -> B/.venv`): a docs-only commit made 0 execs of uv/just/run-in-hermes-env/setup. A `.py` commit with no `just` ran setup only inside the matched jobs (`✔️ lint python`, `✔️ move shims`). B's `direct_url.json` was unchanged.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` on `test_run_lefthook`, `test_run_in_hermes_env`, `test_hermes_python`, `test_bash_shebangs`, `tests/pm/test_activate_scripts`, `test_activation_setup`, `test_environment_script`: 32 passed, 9 skipped (platform-gated), 0 failed. Run from a worktree with no venv, under a scratch HOME.
- `python scripts/check`: 22 checks ok. CI on `36531817`: 14 checks passed, 22 skipped, 0 failed.

## Caveats

- Windows is not exercised (the Git Bash `uname` mapping is from reading the source); macOS was covered by @kshitijk4poor's generated-hook probes.

prs.title: search_files can search case-insensitively on every backend
prs.body:
When a model asked the file search tool to ignore upper/lower case, it worked on machines with ripgrep installed, but on machines without it the search silently returned nothing. Now the same case-insensitive search returns the same results on every machine and backend.

Outcome: a leading `(?i)` on a `search_files` pattern is turned into `grep -i` on the grep fallback, so models no longer need to fall back to terminal `grep -i`.

## Before / after

Real `ShellFileOperations.search("(?i)RESULT_STORAGE", path=<this worktree>)`, content mode (re-measured on head `b7ffacb` vs its base `f8bbe77`):

| Backend path | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| ripgrep (native / shell) | 58 matches, 32 files | 58 matches, 32 files |
| grep fallback (rg unavailable; plain and find-pruned lanes) | **0 matches** (`grep: warning: ? at start of expression`) | 58 matches, 32 files |

## Why
POSIX ERE has no inline flags, so `grep -E -e '(?i)x'` warns and matches nothing. `_grep_cmd` is shared by both grep lanes (`_search_with_grep` and `_search_with_grep_pruned`), so a leading `(?i)` is stripped there and `-i` is added. ripgrep honours `(?i)` natively and is unchanged. Remote backends go through the same shell grep lane.

Prompted by #157377, whose review noted that search_files had no case-insensitive option and the grep fallback couldn't take `(?i)`.

## Token delta
**0**. No schema change, no new parameter. I measured adding "prefix (?i) for case-insensitive" to the `pattern` description: it costs +9 cl100k tokens, which is over the 8-token budget, so I left the description out. `(?i)` is standard regex syntax that models already reach for, and the rg path already accepted it.

## Tests
- `tests/tools/test_search_pattern_arguments.py::test_inline_ignore_case_prefix_matches_mixed_case_on_every_lane`: real `LocalEnvironment` with real rg/grep, run over rg-native, rg-shell, grep and grep-pruned × content/count/files_only. Red on main (the 6 grep-lane cases), green here.
- `tests/tools/test_search_*.py`: all pass. `python scripts/check --only health`: ok.

## Infographic
![(?i) everywhere](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab2fea8/M8rPU-OWaF88KKmvDd2A9_wdCoSjym.png)

prs.title: feat: add HERMES_DUMP_RETENTION_DAYS to prune old request dumps
prs.body:
Failed-API request dumps (`request_dump_<sid>_*.json`) are written to each profile's sessions/logs directory and never cleaned up. In my profile this grew to **137 dumps / ~26 MB** - and because every dump contains a full prompt mirror, fleet backup jobs end up shipping that unbounded pile along with the profile directory.

This PR adds HERMES_DUMP_RETENTION_DAYS (default **30**,  = keep forever) and prunes equest_dump_*.json older than the cutoff whenever a new dump is written. Pruning at dump-write time keeps the change self-contained (no scheduler/background task) and the directory naturally converges to the retention window. Unrelated files in the logs dir are never touched; prune errors are non-fatal.

### Changes
- gent/agent_runtime_helpers.py: _prune_old_request_dumps(), called right after a new dump is written
- website/docs/reference/environment-variables.md: document HERMES_DUMP_RETENTION_DAYS in both env-var tables
- 	ests/agent/test_request_dump_retention.py: retention pruning,  = keep-forever, and untouched-unrelated-files cases

Closes #157644

prs.title: A chat resumed with fewer tools stops describing tools it no longer has
prs.body:
When you resume a chat with fewer tools than it started with, some of the remaining tools' instructions still told the model to use the tools that were taken away. Now those instructions are rewritten to match the tools the resumed chat actually has. Nothing changes when you resume with the same tools.

## What changed

`tools/mcp_tool_agent.py::restore_agent_tool_prefix` keeps each pinned tool's bytes so `tools[]`, which comes first in every request, stays cached. A few tools build their description from the names of the other tools available (`model_tools._DYNAMIC_SCHEMA_REWRITERS`: `execute_code`'s sandbox helper list, `delegate_task`'s sibling line, `browser_exec`'s `vision_analyze` hint, and after #157517 `terminal`'s file-tools sentence). When a resume dropped pinned tools, those kept their pinned text and still named the dropped tools.

New helper `_refresh_name_dependent_defs`: **only when the restore drops a pinned tool**, every surviving tool that has a dynamic rewriter takes the definition this build just made for it. A survivor carried from the pin (its `check_fn` failed in this process, so this build has no definition for it) is rebuilt through the new `registry.definition_for` (the same builder `get_definitions` uses, runtime overrides included, without the `check_fn` gate), then rewritten against the final tool names and sanitized, the same as a fresh build. If nothing was dropped (same toolsets or more), the function returns early and the pin's bytes are untouched.

Cache: dropping a pinned tool already changes `tools[]` from that slot on, so the cached prefix is broken there anyway. Refreshing the survivors costs nothing extra, and same-toolset resumes are unchanged (shown byte-identical below).

`_merge_preserving_prefix` (the between-turns refresh) is unchanged because it never drops a tool that is still registered. Even when plugin go-live passes a narrower selection, a name missing from the fresh build is carried forward, so no survivor can end up naming a dropped tool. The paths that do narrow toolsets (`/reload-mcp`, Bot Chat capability refresh) use `preserve_prefix=False` and already publish fresh definitions.

## Live run (no mocks)

Real `hermes chat -q` against Nous Portal (probe model: claude-haiku-4.5, picked for cost) in a fresh scratch `HERMES_HOME` with `HERMES_DUMP_REQUESTS=1`. Steps: turn 1 with the default toolsets (18 tools). Turn 2 is `--resume` with the same toolsets. Then `platform_toolsets.cli` is set to `[terminal, code_execution]` and turn 3 is `--resume` again. Each turn runs in a new process. Results come from the dumped request bodies. The "this PR" column was re-run on the current head `9c0bc71a` (3 haiku turns, well under $1); the "+ #157517" column was run on this PR's first commit `2e08f84d` with #157517 applied (the two later commits only touch the carried-survivor path, which this run does not take).

| | main | this PR (`9c0bc71a`) | this PR + #157517 |
|---|---|---|---|
| turn 3 `tools[]` | execute_code, terminal, tool_search, tool_describe, tool_call | same | same |
| turn 3 `execute_code` names absent tools | **patch, read_file, search_files, web_extract, web_search, write_file** | none | none |
| turn 3 `terminal` names absent tools | patch, read_file, search_files, write_file (static text, fixed by #157517) | same (static text) | none |
| turn 2 (same toolsets) `tools[]` vs turn 1 | byte-identical | byte-identical | byte-identical |
| turn 2 cache read | 10662/10682 (100%) | 10666/10686 (100%) | 10659/10679 (100%) |

(`-t` on `--resume` is refused by design for gateway-owned CLI sessions, so the narrowing in the live run comes from a profile change, which is how a real user's resumed session ends up with fewer tools.)

## Tests

- `tests/tools/test_restore_narrowed_tool_descriptions.py`: (1) pin `terminal,file,code_execution`, then restore into `terminal,code_execution`: the file tools are gone, `execute_code`'s description names none of them, and it equals this build's definition. Red on `origin/main` (`assert not ['search_files', 'read_file', 'patch', 'write_file']`). (2) Same selection restored: `tools[]` is byte-identical to the pin, even when the pinned bytes differ from what this process would build.
- Same file, `test_a_carried_survivor_is_rewritten_against_the_final_tool_names`: `execute_code` is carried from the pin (not built here) while the file toolset is gone; its description names no file tool (Greptile finding, red on the first head).
- Same file, `test_a_carried_survivor_keeps_its_runtime_schema_fields`: a carried `delegate_task` keeps the built parameters (its `dynamic_schema_overrides`) and no longer names the dropped `clarify` (second Greptile finding, red on 80caf85).
- `tests/agent/test_oneshot_interactive_surface.py::test_oneshot_resume_keeps_the_pinned_interactive_tool_bytes[True]` now expects the new rule. When config disables `clarify` after the pin, the restored `delegate_task` takes the current definition, which no longer names `clarify`. The `[False]` case (nothing dropped) still requires the pinned bytes.
- CI on the current head: 15 checks passed, 22 skipped, 0 failed.

Raised by @BearHuddleston on #157517.

## Infographic

![resume-narrowed-tool-descriptions](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab30009/p5Ya2bbwlFHkBgdAuO8QI_jwRSvaXP.png)

prs.title: fix(terminal): strip plugin terminal-env strip keys in _make_run_env
prs.body:
## Problem

`_make_run_env` (the foreground terminal environment builder) passes a hardcoded `frozenset()` as the plugin strip-key set, so `register_terminal_environment_provider(...).strip_env_keys` is ignored on the foreground terminal path. Plugin-registered strip keys (e.g. peer/secret keys a plugin wants to keep out of terminal children) still reach every foreground terminal child, while the background `_sanitize_subprocess_env` path already honors the same union.

## Fix

Consult `_plugin_terminal_env_strip_keys()` — the union `_sanitize_subprocess_env` already uses — so plugin-registered strip keys are stripped on the foreground path too.

## Test

Regression test through the real `LocalEnvironment` spawn path: a plugin-registered strip key is absent from the child environment, while an ordinary key is preserved.

prs.title: fix(tools): wrap single-object tasks into a one-entry list in delegate_task
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Updates `delegate_task` batch normalization so passing a single task object (either as a native `dict` or as a JSON-encoded object string) wraps it into a one-element list (`[task]`) instead of being rejected before reaching single-task validation.

## Related Issue

Fixes #157213

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `tools/delegate_tool_tasks.py`: Updated `_recover_tasks_from_json_string()` to wrap parsed `dict` payloads as `[parsed]`, and updated `_normalize_task_list()` to wrap native `dict` inputs into `[tasks]` so normal per-task validation (missing `goal`, placeholders, short-goal exemption) applies consistently.
- `tests/tools/test_delegate_batch_validation.py`: Added 3 unit tests covering native `dict` wrapping, JSON-string object wrapping, invalid single-dict rejection, and scalar JSON string rejection.

## How to Test

1. Pass `tasks={"goal": "..."}` or `tasks='{"goal": "..."}'` to `_normalize_task_list()` / `delegate_task`.
2. Verify it normalizes to a single-element list while invalid single-task fields still produce validation errors.
3. Run `pytest tests/tools/test_delegate_batch_validation.py tests/tools/test_delegate.py -q` (**87 passed**).

issues.title: Security: a failed approval-hook re-initialization during reload leaves the gateway serving with tools ungated
issues.body:
## Summary

PicoClaw supports process approval hooks: before a tool runs, the gateway asks a hook whether the call is approved, and a hook that denies the call produces `exec_skipped`. When the gateway reloads (the `/reload` channel command or a configuration reload), it tears down the old hook and re-initializes the configured hooks. If re-initialization fails, the agent records a warning but the gateway still reports the reload as successful and continues serving with no hooks mounted. Every subsequent tool call then bypasses the approval decision: the built-in `exec` tool runs the command with no approval record, and the operator sees only a warning line followed by "reloaded successfully". The failure is not a transient denial: the gate is absent until the next successful reload or restart.

## Details

### Affected component

`pkg/agent/agent.go` (hook mount and reload), `pkg/agent/hook_mount.go` (hook initialization), `pkg/agent/pipeline_execute.go` (tool execution), `pkg/gateway/gateway.go` (reload completion).

### Vulnerable code

`pkg/agent/agent.go:454-459` and `:485`:

```go
al.hookRuntime.reset(al)
configureHookManagerFromConfig(al.hooks, cfg)
if err := al.ensureHooksInitialized(ctx); err != nil {
    logger.WarnCF("agent", "Configured hooks failed to reinitialize after reload",
        map[string]any{"error": err.Error()})
}
...
logger.InfoCF("agent", "Provider and config reloaded successfully",
    map[string]any{
        "model": cfg.Agents.Defaults.GetModelName(),
```

### Root cause

The reload path treats "hooks failed to reinitialize" as a warning, not as a reload failure. The old hook is already unmounted, the new set is empty, and the gateway publishes a successful reload. The tool pipeline consults the hook manager, finds no approval hook, and proceeds. There is no fail-closed state, no refusal to serve, and no health signal; the warning is the only trace.

### Attack path

1. A deployment uses a process approval hook as its tool gate; the hook denies `exec` calls.
2. The hook becomes unavailable at reload time: its binary is missing, it fails to start, or its configuration is invalid.
3. The operator triggers `/reload`; the gateway unmounts the old hook, fails to mount the new one, logs a warning, and still reports the reload as successful.
4. The gateway continues to accept messages; a user or an agent-driven request causes the LLM to emit an `exec` tool call.
5. The tool pipeline finds no approval hook and executes the command.
6. The operator sees no denial, no `exec_skipped` event, and no error; the command has already run.

### Affected deployments

Deployments that use process approval hooks and reload configuration at runtime. The fault is local (the hook binary or its startup is broken at reload time); the report does not claim a remote way to remove the hook, but the consequence is remote: any user or agent that can drive the gateway can execute ungated tools after the failed reload.

### Remediation

When hook re-initialization fails during a reload, fail closed: keep the previous hook set mounted, abort the reload with an error, or mark the session as degraded and refuse tools that require approval. Surface the failure through the reload response and health/status, not only a log line.

## Proof of concept

Run the gateway with a process approval hook that denies `exec` (`exit 1`), and drive the agent with a scripted LLM that emits:

```json
{"tool":"exec","action":"run","command":"touch /tmp/exec_marker"}
```

Baseline: the hook denies the call; the agent logs `agent.tool.exec_skipped`, and `/tmp/exec_marker` is absent.

```bash
./picoclaw   # gateway with hooks/approval-gate configured
# send: "run the tool"
# expected: exec_skipped; no marker
```

Fault: make the hook unavailable (remove `hooks/approval-gate`, or make it fail to start), then send `/reload` and the same message.

```bash
rm hooks/approval-gate
# send: "/reload"
# gateway log: "Configured hooks failed to reinitialize after reload"
#              "Provider and config reloaded successfully"
# send: "run the tool"
# expected: exec runs; /tmp/exec_marker exists; no exec_skipped
```

Expected difference: with the hook present the call is denied and no marker appears; with the hook unavailable at reload time the same call executes and creates the marker, while the reload reports success. The only changed variable is the hook's availability during reload.

## Impact

Any tool that shares the `ApproveTool` decision point (the observed `exec`; file writes and cron command jobs use the same gate) runs without approval after one failed reload. The gateway keeps serving and reports success, so the operator has no reason to stop or investigate. A user or an agent driven by untrusted content can therefore execute commands the approval hook was meant to block.

## Affected products

- Ecosystem: other (Go binary; GitHub releases)
- Affected versions: `<= 0.3.1`
- Patched versions: (none)

## Weaknesses

`CWE-636` (Not Failing Securely), `CWE-693` (Protection Mechanism Failure).

## Reporting note (why this is a regular issue)

I could not find a `SECURITY.md` or a private vulnerability reporting entry in this repository, so I am filing this as a regular issue rather than a private report. If there is a preferred private channel that I missed, please let me know and I will be glad to move the report there. I have not published this elsewhere, and I am happy to provide any additional detail or to test a patch.

prs.title: Sync with upstream/main (1095 commits) + forward-port magicform customizations
prs.body:
## Summary

- Merges ~1095 commits from `sipeed/picoclaw` `upstream/main` (last sync was at `7ea7bb0`).
- Forward-ports our 6 customization commits onto upstream's restructured layout: agent loop split into `agent_*.go`, tools reorganized into `pkg/tools/{fs,integration}/`, channel config moved to a map+Settings model.
- Drops the launcher subsystem (deps deleted upstream, MagicForm doesn't use it).
- Phase 1 of the multi-tenancy port: tenant hints from `bus.InboundContext.Raw` plumb onto `processOptions`. Phase 2 (effSessions/effProvider/effContextBuilder threading) is deferred to a follow-up PR.
- New `MAGICFORM_CUSTOMIZATIONS.md` indexes the fork's customizations by subsystem so future syncs are predictable.

## Commit shape (deliberately one-customization-per-commit for sync friendliness)

```
763e5690 docs: add MAGICFORM_CUSTOMIZATIONS.md sync index
9a0b2817 forward-port: multi-tenancy hint plumbing on agent processOptions (phase 1)
cd1720f4 forward-port: write size cap + crypto/rand temp suffixes in fs sandbox
94d28c1b forward-port: bound search response size with LimitReader
0c8ebde2 forward-port: register magicform channel in gateway init
93fb7b87 Merge upstream/main into sync/upstream-2026-05-07
```

## Notable upstream changes incorporated

- Agent loop split (#2585) — `pkg/agent/loop.go` → 30+ `agent_*.go` files. Multi-tenancy customization moved into a new isolated `agent_tenant.go` to minimise future conflict surface.
- Tool packages reorganized (`4c133dc2`) — `pkg/tools/{filesystem,web}.go` → `pkg/tools/{fs,integration}/`. Hardening re-applied at the new locations.
- Launcher migrated to `web/backend/` (#1275) — old launcher dropped (see below).
- Channel config switched to map+Settings model — `MagicFormConfig` rewritten as `MagicFormSettings` with `SecureString` token, registered alongside other channels in `config_channel.go`.
- `AgentDefaults.Model` deprecated field removed; `SessionConfig.DMScope` replaced by `Dimensions`; `Config.Bindings` replaced by upstream's legacy bindings migration.

## Things that changed in our fork

- **Launcher dropped.** Half its dependencies were deleted upstream (`auth_config.go`, `process.go`, `server_test.go`, etc.), and MagicForm doesn't use the launcher's HTTP API. Upstream's `web/backend/` is the replacement when an admin UI is needed.
- **Multi-tenancy split into phases.** Phase 1 (this PR) validates and plumbs tenant hints onto `processOptions`. Phase 2 (next PR) wires `effSessions`/`effContextBuilder`/`effProvider`/`effModel` through the turn execution path. Phase 1 is a no-op functionally for current MagicForm traffic (which doesn't yet send webhooks) but locks in the protocol so phase 2 is a clean diff against the agent loop only.
- **Workspace overlays using the deprecated `model` JSON key are now silently ignored.** Migrate them to `model_name`.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./pkg/... ./cmd/...` (excluding matrix, which has a Windows+CGO=0 libolm constraint that's environment-only and pre-existing)

issues.title: [bug] Codex agents lose the ncl and canvas instructions on a default Slack install (AGENTS.md over the 32 KiB cap)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: triage/unresolved
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer triage. Applied by issue forms

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

v2026.11.0-rc.1 (280cae014)

### Host platform

Linux

### What happened?

On an install with Slack and the Codex provider, every container spawn logs the error below (9 times so far, once per spawn). The composed AGENTS.md is 39,393 bytes. NanoClaw caps Codex's project document at 32 KiB, so `fitToCap` drops the two largest sections and writes 27,403 bytes.

So the Codex agent starts with no `ncl` guidance and no canvas guidance. The `scheduling` section is kept and still tells the agent to run `ncl tasks ...`, without the access and approval rules that the `cli` section carries.

Only Codex is affected. A Claude agent on the same install gets every section.

Sizes of the kept sections, in bytes: Runtime Contract 4248, Native Runtime Skills 804, agents 2688, core 1205, create-agent-slack 1791, interactive 3778, rooms 1760, scheduling 1360, self-mod 1833, onecli-gateway 1223, slack-construct 4303, slack-construct-agents 1833. Dropped: cli 6410, canvas 5783.

Cause: 32 KiB is Codex's default `project_doc_max_bytes`, not a hard limit. NanoClaw sets the value itself, in two places in the `add-codex` payload: `src/providers/codex-agents-md.ts` on the host and `container/agent-runner/src/providers/codex-app-server.ts:11` in the container.

### What did you expect?

A default install should give the Codex agent every instruction section, as it does for Claude.

A possible fix: raise both constants to 64 KiB. That keeps every section with room to spare, at about 3k more input tokens per session. Separately, when `cli` has to be dropped, `scheduling` could be dropped with it, since one only makes sense with the other.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. Install with `bash nanoclaw.sh`, choose Slack (setup applies `slack-a2a-rooms` and `slack-agent-flow`) and the Codex provider.
2. Send the agent any message.
3. Check `logs/nanoclaw.error.log` for the line below, and `groups/<folder>/AGENTS.md` for the "Omitted for size" section.

### OS version and CPU architecture

Debian 13 (trixie), x86_64

### Install or update path

Standard setup with nanoclaw.sh

### Docker version

29.10.0

### Channel or interface

Slack

### Agent provider

Codex

### Agent model

None set (Codex default). The cap does not depend on the model.

### Relevant redacted logs

```shell
ERROR Project document exceeded its size cap — dropped the largest instruction sections file="AGENTS.md" group="<group>" bytes=27403 maxBytes=32768 dropped=["NanoClaw Module: cli","NanoClaw Module: canvas"]
```

### Last version that worked

`canvas` was kept up to v2026.11.0-beta.4: there the document was 35 bytes under the cap after dropping `cli`. #4405 added 208 bytes to the OneCLI gateway instructions and pushed `canvas` out too. `cli` was already dropped on v2026.10.0 for this setup.
