### What happened?

An update with `/update-nanoclaw` changed agent-runner source on a host with no Bun, and nothing typechecked the new source before it went live.

Validate skips the check when `bun --version` fails and records that it was deferred (`scripts/update/transaction.ts:519-534`). The image build never runs it: `container/Dockerfile:90` copies only `agent-runner/package.json` and `bun.lock`, and the Dockerfile has no `tsc` step. The source is mounted into the container at spawn (`src/container-runner.ts:1323-1326`), so cutover's `container/build.sh` runs fully from cache and checks nothing.

Bun is not a host requirement, so most installs take this path. The deferral has been there since the transactional updater landed (8772ec977).

### What did you expect?

The skill refresh already runs the pinned Bun through pnpm when the host has none (`scripts/update-skills.ts:60`, version from `pinnedBunVersion`), and validate could do the same for `bun install` before its `tsc` run.

1. On a Linux host with no `bun` on `PATH`, run `/update-nanoclaw` across a range that changes `container/agent-runner/src/` (v2026.11.0-beta.4 to rc.1 does).

29.9.2

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Make OneCLI setup exit non-zero when its gateway readiness check fails.

- **Problem**: `run()` rejects after emitting `STATUS: failed`, but the shared logger handles unhandled rejections without setting a failing exit code. Setup can therefore exit 0 and let the skill driver continue.
- **Fix**: catch rejections at the OneCLI CLI entry point, log the error, and set `process.exitCode = 1`.
- **Coverage**: launch the real setup CLI against loopback fixtures for a 404, a dropped `/v1/health` connection, and a healthy gateway. The tests use a disposable HOME and a fake OneCLI CLI.

## Related work

Closes #4408.

#4303 changes the entry-point path guard and leaves `void run(...)` unchanged. This changes the invocation inside that guard; the adjacent edits may need coordination.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- Against unchanged main at `c0ec12952e8d9a4ebbd869015010daac804d5d11`, `vitest run .claude/skills/add-onecli/scripts/readiness.test.ts` -> 2 failed, 3 passed. Both failing gateways emitted `STATUS: failed` but exited 0.
- With this fix, the same file -> 5 passed. Failed readiness exits 1; healthy readiness exits 0.

- Host `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc` -> pass.

prs.title: fix(add-codex): sign in via the pinned Codex CLI through pnpm dlx, outside /tmp
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Codex ChatGPT sign-in works without a Codex CLI on the host, and no longer warns about `/tmp`.

- **Problem**: with no `codex` on PATH, setup asks for `npm install -g @openai/codex`, which fails with EACCES on a root-owned npm prefix. The throwaway `CODEX_HOME` was in `/tmp`, where Codex refuses its helpers and warns.
- **Fix**: the sign-in runs the image's exact pin from `container/cli-tools.json` through pnpm, the way setup already runs the pinned Bun: `pnpm --package=@openai/codex@<pin> dlx codex login`. pnpm keeps it in its own cache, with no global install and no sudo.
- **Sign-in home**: `data/codex-login/<random>`, git-ignored with mode 0700, and never `~/.codex`. The login runs in its own session. On a signal, setup stops every process group in the login's tree, including the one pnpm 12 gives Codex, and removes the home only once all of them are gone, using SIGKILL after 3 seconds or on a second signal. A killed run's leftovers are swept after an hour. Ctrl-C while pnpm fetches the CLI stops setup with no error.
- **Fails closed**: a pin that isn't strict semver never reaches pnpm. If the pinned sign-in fails, setup names the API-key option and OpenAI's installer (`… | sh -s -- --release <pin>`, no sudo), with npm second. The installer keeps Codex in `~/.codex/packages`, links it into `~/.local/bin` and adds that to the shell profile, so setup says to re-run in a new terminal. Sign-in still uses the throwaway home.

<details><summary>Alternatives considered</summary>

- **Sign in inside the agent image** (OpenCode): Codex binds its browser callback to `127.0.0.1` inside its own process, so a container's port forward can't reach it. Only device pairing would work.
- **npx** (this PR's first heads): works too, but npx runs any `codex` in its project's `node_modules`, so it needed an empty private project, a binary lookup with a version re-check, and npm error parsing to tell Ctrl-C from a failed fetch. `pnpm dlx` needs none of these and matches Cursor sign-in, skill refresh, lockfile regeneration, the provider check and #4461.

</details>

## Related work

Closes #3791
Closes #4449

Replaces closed #3792.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `codex.test.ts` in the composed tree: 46 passed. New cases cover pnpm sign-in, bad pins, a failed or unstartable pnpm and the install commands, the home and its sweep, and Ctrl-C during the probe and during the fetch. The stop tests use real process trees: a wrapper that exits at once on SIGTERM, and a child that outlives it in the wrapper's group or in its own.
- `test-registry-skills.ts add-codex` passes on a fresh clone of HEAD. `skill-pins`, `tsc` and prettier are clean.
- Live test on a Debian 13 LXC with a root-owned npm prefix (`/usr`), no `codex`, and pnpm 10.34.9 through corepack:
  - pnpm fetched the native `@openai/codex@0.169.0-linux-x64` package, and device sign-in showed the URL and code, with no `/tmp` warning
  - Ctrl-C during the download and during device or browser sign-in each exited 130, leaving no process and no home
  - SIGTERM and SIGHUP sent to setup alone during the login, and closing the terminal, each left no process and no home
  - a Codex or pnpm stopped with SIGSTOP kept the home until setup killed it after 3 seconds
  - `~/.codex` stayed absent
- On macOS, pnpm 12 runs Codex in its own process group. A stopped Codex there was gone before setup removed the home.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
**Codex setup no longer needs the Codex CLI installed on your machine.** If `codex` isn't on your PATH, ChatGPT sign-in runs the pinned version through pnpm, from pnpm's cache, with no global install or sudo. It also no longer warns about `/tmp`.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

pnpm fetches the image's exact, reviewed pin with install scripts off (`--config.ignore-scripts=true`), as in the image install; Codex ships none today. pnpm 12 also applies the repo's 3-day `minimumReleaseAge` to this fetch, while 10.34.9 does not. The token goes only to the 0700 home under `data/`, then the gateway vault. If sign-in is killed after login but before the token reaches the vault, the token can stay in that home until the hourly sweep, and an `/update-nanoclaw` snapshot taken in that window copies it along with the rest of `data/` and `.env`, on the same machine.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

The change touches only the add-codex payload's `setup/providers/codex.ts`, its test, and two SKILL.md sentences.

prs.title: feat(setup): new installs choose their update channel
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A new install picks its update channel before setup runs, and starts on that channel's code.

- **Problem**: a fresh clone installs the tip of `main` on the default `stable` channel, so once `main` is past the latest release the first `/update-nanoclaw` stops with ahead-of-release.
- **Question**: on the first run of a fresh clone of the official repo on a terminal, `nanoclaw.sh` asks: stable (latest release, default), beta (release candidates too) or edge (`main`). Stable and beta check out that channel's newest tag, picked as the updater picks it, on a branch named after the channel, and restart from that release's files. Edge stays on `main`.
- **Saved first**: the shell appends the choice to `.env` before the checkout, so a release older than this setting keeps it. If the save or the checkout fails, setup stops before installing anything.
- **No question**: `--update-channel`, `NANOCLAW_UPDATE_CHANNEL` or a channel already in `.env` installs that channel's release, with or without a terminal. Advanced setup has the same field. A bad env value stops setup unless a flag overrides it; uninstall ignores it.
- **Left alone**: existing installs, forks, other branches and local changes. With no channel and no terminal nothing moves; one hint line is printed when `main` is past the release.

## Related work

Follow-up to #3986. No issue: scoped with the maintainers. See [Upgrading](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/operate/upgrading).

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run` -> 5222 passed; the 14 files that failed under full-suite load (timeouts, one timing assertion) pass when rerun on their own. Both typechecks, `format:check`, `skill-pins:check` -> clean.
- `setup/lib/release-checkout.test.ts` (60 tests) runs the real `nanoclaw.sh` in stub official clones, with and without a terminal, against a release older than this setting and one that has it. It checks the shell picks the tags the updater picks and that the updater reads the channel the shell saved. Passes on macOS and Ubuntu 24.04; the shell helpers also pass under `ubuntu:26.04` (uutils, as CI).
- e2e, fresh exe.dev VM, official clone with `main` at this head:
  - Enter -> `v2026.10.0` on branch `stable`; `2` -> `v2026.11.0-rc.2` on branch `beta`; `3` -> `main`. Each saved its channel, reached that code's setup menu, and its first update resolves to the installed tag, with no ahead-of-release stop.
  - Full wizard at an earlier head (`setup/auto.ts` unchanged since): service running, agent replied, channel saved.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
**New installs choose how they get updates.** On a fresh clone, `bash nanoclaw.sh` asks which updates to follow: stable (published releases, recommended), beta (release candidates too) or edge (the newest code from `main`), and installs that version. `--update-channel stable|beta|edge` skips the question, and Advanced setup has the same choice.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Setup can run `git checkout -b <stable|beta> <tag>` in the install folder and then that release's `nanoclaw.sh`. Only for an annotated release tag already in the clone, whose commit is on a branch of the official remote that also contains `HEAD`. It appends one line to `.env`; a new `.env` is created `0600`. No network access or credentials.

prs.title: fix(setup): show the provider image rebuild in the progress window
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup's image rebuild after a non-Claude provider install now runs in the same progress window as the first image build, instead of printing Docker's full output.

- **Problem**: after Codex, Cursor or OpenCode is installed, `container/build.sh` ran on inherited stdio: about 125 lines of build output, and no log in `logs/setup-steps/`.
- **Fix**: `buildContainerImageWindowed()` runs the same script through the existing window (`runWindowedChild`, the windowed twin of `runQuietChild`), with the output in `logs/setup-steps/NN-container-rebuild.log`. Failures keep their messages and hints, the pinned-image refusal included; the Claude failure helper now gets the log.
- **Window fixes, both builds**: a stall prompt still open when the build ends is closed, so it can't take the next prompt's keys. Ctrl-C no longer leaves the cursor hidden.
- **Cancel stops the rebuild**: it runs in its own process group, so Ctrl-C or Esc at the stall prompt, or a signal, stops all of it (SIGKILL after 5 s) before setup exits. On Ctrl-C the window clears the terminal's `^C` echo too, so nothing is left under the shell prompt. The first build is unchanged: its step may need the terminal for sudo.
- **Out of scope**: `--step provider-auth` keeps Docker's output; it has no window, and that output is its progress signal.

## Related work

Closes #4447

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- New `windowed-runner.test.ts` and `container-build.test.ts`, one new `auto.auth.test.ts` case: output goes to the log, not the terminal; failure messages match the old path word for word; a failed rebuild stops setup with its log; the stall prompt closes when the build ends.
- Ctrl-C and Esc at the real stall prompt, and a signal, stop a real child and grandchild before setup exits; a group that ignores the stop is SIGKILLed.
- `vitest run` passes (unrelated `scripts/` timeouts under load pass alone). `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint src/` and `format:check` are clean.
- Live, `bash nanoclaw.sh` in a PTY on fresh exe.dev VMs, Codex with an API key, through a real agent reply: `main` printed 125 lines of build output; this branch prints `Sandbox rebuilt with codex. (1m 1s)` and writes the log.
- Live Ctrl-C on one of those VMs, through the real chain (`bash nanoclaw.sh`, pnpm, tsx, Node): 15 s into the rebuild the shell prompt returns in under a second (exit 130), with the build stopped, the terminal restored and the image tag unchanged. Re-running setup recovers, and the agent replies. Repeated after the `^C` fix: nothing is left under the prompt.

prs.title: skills: add /add-youdotcom-tool for You.com MCP tools
prs.body:
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [x] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [ ] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

Adds `/add-youdotcom-tool`, a host tool-skill that registers You.com's remote MCP server for selected agent groups, modeled on the existing `/add-tavily-tool`. Resolves Linear DX-748.

**What.** Installs the pinned `mcp-remote` bridge in the agent image and registers You.com via `ncl groups config add-mcp-server`, keyless on the free tier by default (`?profile=free` → `you-search`), with an OneCLI-vault API-key upgrade path that unlocks `you-contents`, `you-research`, `you-finance`, `you-balance`, and `you-discover`. Optionally registers You.com's keyless Docs MCP (`searchDocs`) as a second server. Also lists the skill under MCP tools in `/customize`.

**Why.** You.com hosts one MCP server exposing all tools, so a single install skill fits NanoClaw's single-responsibility model and lets the model pick the right tool at runtime. The `youdotcom-oss/agent-skills` `you-web`/`you-research`/`you-finance` split is coding-agent routing guidance and has no NanoClaw target today. Provider-agnostic (Claude/OpenCode/Codex).

**How it works.** Same credential-safe pattern as `/add-tavily-tool`: `--enable-proxy` routes the bridge's HTTPS through the OneCLI gateway (required by egress lockdown), which injects the API key on the wire — the key never enters the args or the container. The single in-tree integration point is the `mcp-remote` entry in `container/cli-tools.json`, guarded by `youdotcom-manifest.test.ts` (copied into `src/` on apply). Per-group MCP registration is runtime `ncl` state with no in-tree line, so there is nothing for a registration test to guard there; the Phase 4 smoke test verifies it instead (this is stated explicitly in the SKILL.md, per the guidelines).

**How it was tested.**
- Directive lint (`pnpm exec tsx scripts/skill-directives.ts`) on the SKILL.md: clean, no problems or warnings.
- Manifest guard verified both ways with vitest: red when `mcp-remote` is absent (2 failed), green when present and exact-pinned (2 passed). The temporary manifest edit and `src/` copy were reverted afterward.
- Test file typechecks.
- Not yet run end-to-end in this environment (no image build / live `ncl` registration) — static guards and lint only. Flagging for maintainer review.

**Usage.** `/add-youdotcom-tool` → pick the agent group(s) → optionally add the Docs MCP. The skill registers the server(s) and installs the free-tier upgrade instructions; `REMOVE.md` reverses every change.

## For Skills

- [x] SKILL.md contains instructions, not inline code (code goes in separate files)
- [x] SKILL.md is under 500 lines
- [ ] I tested this skill on a fresh clone

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): keep context beside a command pending
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stored context no longer starts a turn just because a runner command shares its batch.

- **Problem**: when `/clear` or `/upload-trace` reached the runner in a batch whose other rows were all accumulated context (`trigger=0`), the runner ran the command, then started a turn on the context rows alone. The agent answered messages it was only meant to store, and the command replied in the first context row's thread.
- **Fix**: a batch with no waking non-command row now takes only its waking commands. The context rows stay pending and ride along with the next message that wakes a turn, as the accumulate gate already does for context-only batches.
- **Out of scope**: a context row that itself reads as a command (an admin's `/clear` not addressed to the agent) still runs as a command, as on `main`; whether it should is a separate question. Which thread a turn replies to when context sorts first is https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4159.

## Related work

Split out of https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4159 at review, as a separate behavior change. No issue. Both PRs touch the runner's command block in `poll-loop.ts`, so the second to merge needs a small rebase.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `cd container/agent-runner && bun test --isolate` → 629 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail. `tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json` is clean.
- New `poll-loop.command-context.test.ts`, red on `main`. For `/clear` and for `/upload-trace` batched with one context row, `main` sends two replies to the context row's thread (the command's reply and an answer to the context) and acks the row. Here the command replies in its own thread, no turn starts, and the row stays pending until it reaches the next turn with the next message.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

prs.title: fix(setup): verify linger without interactive polkit prompts
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops setup printing `Failed to execute /usr/bin/pkttyagent` on Linux hosts without polkit, and reports systemd linger as on only when it is.

- **Problem**: on systemd 257.x (Debian 13), `loginctl enable-linger` forks the polkit tty agent whenever setup has a controlling terminal, even with stdin ignored ([systemd 0f81c84](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/0f81c8406f0f47175c699715e84de8291057033c)). Without polkit, its exec error lands under the spinner. Setup also reported `LINGER_ENABLED: true` for every non-root install, even when enabling failed.
- **Fix**: read `Linger` first and change nothing when it is on. Otherwise try `loginctl --no-ask-password enable-linger`, then `sudo -n loginctl enable-linger` (root's `loginctl` starts no agent), re-reading after each. `LINGER_ENABLED` is true only on `Linger=yes`; otherwise the step log keeps each failure reason and the recovery command.
- **Out of scope**: `systemctl --user` and `systemd-run --user` never start the agent, so they are unchanged. A linger warning in the wizard itself would touch `setup/auto.ts`.

prs.title: feat(skills): add add-imessage-summaries
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets an agent group follow chosen iMessage threads as summaries, without the messages ever entering a container or leaving the Mac.

- **Problem**: reading a thread for an agent today means giving a general-purpose process (Node, Python or a terminal) Full Disk Access, which exposes every thread, plus Mail, Safari and the rest, to anything that can run under it.
- **Fix**: a utility skill that ships a small compiled reader, `imsg-reader`, as the only process holding Full Disk Access. It sandboxes itself (no network, no child processes, writes only to its own folder, home-folder reads limited to `~/Library/Messages`). It reads only allowlisted threads, summarizes each message with Apple's on-device model, and writes one JSONL outbox per agent. Each group mounts only its own outbox, read-only.
- **Access control**: the config is root-owned, and every change goes through `sudo imsg-reader-config`, so an agent can't widen its own access. Each thread is bound to the chat name and members the owner picked, and checked against `chat.db` on every run.
- **Untrusted input**: sender and time come from the database, never the model. Bidi, zero-width and Unicode tag characters are stripped. One message per model call. Every record is labeled as third-party data.
- **Out of scope**: sending or replying (that's `/add-imessage`); non-Apple-Silicon Macs; remote agents.

<details><summary>Design notes</summary>

Full design and threat model: `.claude/skills/add-imessage-summaries/docs.md`. Points a reviewer may want up front:

- The model is typed as the on-device `SystemLanguageModel`. macOS 27 also ships `PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel` in the same framework, which sends prompts off the Mac from a system service that a process sandbox can't block.
- Batching several messages into one model call misattributed summaries (every summary after a merge shifted by one sender), so the reader makes one call per message.
- The ad-hoc signature with the hardened runtime ties the Full Disk Access grant to one build. A test proves `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` is ignored.
- A message over 40 words can't come through with a 10-word run of its original wording. Shorter texts can come through close to verbatim, since they can't be paraphrased much.

</details>

## Related work

No issue. Complements `/add-imessage` (a channel that sends and receives) with a read-only path. No overlap with open PRs; #4043 is a Sendblue channel.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `bash .claude/skills/add-imessage-summaries/add/build.sh` on macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon, Command Line Tools only -> builds and signs with the hardened runtime.
- `python3 -I .claude/skills/add-imessage-summaries/add/tests/test_reader.py --real-model` -> 31/31. Covers the allowlist and per-agent scope, a forged chat list, hold, edits and unsends, spoofed lines and hidden characters, a 1.1 MB message, malformed `attributedBody`, bad configs, sandbox path blocking, owner checks, read-only WAL access, locking, schema drift, a tampered state file, `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`, and a real on-device model run that checks each summary matches its own message.
- Mutation check: deleting the chat-binding check, the per-thread SQL filter, the character stripping or the copy rule each turns a test red.
- Live install of this reader (same code, different identifiers) on the author's Mac against a real `chat.db` and one group thread: Full Disk Access applies under launchd, the sandbox is active, the layout check passes, the on-device model runs in the background job, and the batch hash in the unified log matches the file.
- **Not run end to end:** Steps 6–7 (the `add-mount` read-only mount and the `instructions.prepend.md` block) on a NanoClaw install. Untested: whether the container user can read a mode-700 outbox through the bind mount.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New /add-imessage-summaries skill: an agent can follow chosen iMessage threads as on-device summaries, with the messages kept out of the container.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- **Full Disk Access**: granted by the user to `/usr/local/libexec/imsg-reader` only. It's root-owned, hardened runtime, no arguments, ignores the environment, and self-sandboxed.
- **Privilege**: `install.sh`, `uninstall.sh` and every access change run under the user's sudo. Nothing user-writable is executed as root after install.
- **Untrusted input**: other people's message text, chat names and `attributedBody` bytes. Parsing is bounds-checked and never uses a general unarchiver. Text is cleaned before it reaches the model and again before output.
- **Container**: one read-only bind mount of one agent's outbox, through the mount allowlist and `ncl groups config add-mount --ro`. The agent's instructions label records as data, not instructions.
- **Residual**: an admin can change anything; a short message's summary is close to its text; the model can mis-summarize, and refusals become `not_summarized` records.

## Summary Makes the Slack agent DM show its "Get started" prompts, and gives new DM threads a title. - **Problem**: the onboarding module calls `setSuggestedPrompts` and `setThreadTitle`, but the Slack bridge never implemented them. Both did nothing while the module logged `Welcome prompts set`. - **Fix**: the bridge calls the pinned 4.41.1 `setSuggestedPrompts(channel, undefined, prompts, title)` and `setAssistantTitle(channel, threadTs, title)`. Ids decode with the SDK's `decodeThreadId`, as delivery does. `slack-` instances use their own token. Errors still reject, so the module's title retry runs. A DM-level thread id (the welcome session's) has nothing to title and is skipped, as the SDK's `startTyping` does. - **Late welcome**: now that the prompts really land, a welcome delivered after the first DM thread started would pin them again. The welcome now checks for a conversation first, as the DM-open handler does, and clears again if one started while the set was in flight. - **Plain variant** (no `assistant:write`): nothing on the install records whether an app has agent_view, so the bot's first `missing_scope` turns prompts and titles off for that bot, with one info line. No warning per welcome or thread. Other errors still reject. - **DM-open re-assert not needed**: the module re-asserts prompts on `assistant_thread_started`, which agent-view apps never get. Live, the prompts set with the welcome rendered on the first open anyway. - **Out of scope**: the welcome addendum (unchanged). No pin move. On a plain app the module still logs "set" and "cleared" for the skipped calls, as for any adapter without these APIs. ## Related work Closes #4452 ## Change kind - [x] `kind/bug` - [ ] `kind/feature` - [ ] `kind/documentation` - [ ] `kind/cleanup` - [ ] `kind/hardening` ## Validation - `src/channels/slack-agent-dm.test.ts` -> 11 passed. Each new test fails without its fix. - Full `vitest run` -> 5136 passed; 15 load failures in 5 `scripts/` files pass alone (170/170). `tsc`, eslint, prettier clean. - Slack API on the e2e app (plain variant): both calls -> `missing_scope`. - Live, fresh agent-view install (Codex, Linux), on 05596bf: the wizard welcome to a new agent's DM logged `Welcome prompts set`; opening that DM for the first time showed all three prompts at the top, and a new DM thread got its title. prs.title: fix(agent-runner): drop queued turns the provider answered inside another turn
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops reply routing falling behind after the Claude CLI answers several queued inputs in one turn.

- **Problem**: `processQuery` queues one turn per pushed follow-up and advances one per `result`. The CLI answers inputs that are waiting together at a turn boundary in one turn, with one `result`. After such a fold the queue stays behind for the rest of the query, and every later reply carries an earlier message's `in_reply_to`. On a channel that quotes the wrong message. For agent-to-agent replies it picks the wrong session: a downstream install had a peer's verdict for one session of an agent delivered to another session of that agent, and the session that asked waited for ever.
- **Fix**: the provider names each pushed input. The Claude provider sends a fresh UUID as the SDK message `uuid` and returns it from `push`, whose arguments are unchanged, so older provider payloads still fit (`push(message): string | void`). The CLI lists the uuids a turn has consumed on that turn's assistant and result frames (`user_message_uuids`), and the provider reports them as a new optional `ProviderEvent`, `{ type: 'consumed', ids }`. On it, the poll-loop drops the queued turns of the absorbed inputs (by id), so the next turn starts from the right message. The running turn keeps its routing, run mode and retry guards, the same as a batch of several messages already answers under its first message's routing (`extractRouting`). Absorbed prompts are archived with that turn.
- **Absorbed inputs keep what their queued turn would have had**: an absorbed wrap-nudge retry's echo window still suppresses its repeats, checked per window and only on the same thread; and if the turn fails (stream error or error result), each absorbed input's route gets a failure notice, since follow-ups are acked at push and are not redelivered.
- **Why not the `idle` signal suggested in #4033**: `session_state_changed: idle` follows a `result` whenever nothing is queued at that moment, which includes the instant a wrap-nudge retry is pushed while that `result` is handled. Dropping the queue on `idle` would discard the retry's turn and its echo window, and would misroute a follow-up pushed between the CLI going idle and the poll-loop reading the event. The consumed list says exactly which inputs a turn took.
- **Out of scope**: giving each reply in a turn that answered several inputs the route of the input it answers (that needs per-reply attribution from the model; today such a turn answers under one route, as a batch does). Providers other than Claude keep the one-result-per-input assumption until they emit `consumed` (Codex and OpenCode are skill-installed). A provider-neutral alternative (hold follow-ups during a turn and push them as one input at the result) would give up mid-turn folding, which this change keeps.

## Related work

Closes #4033

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- Real CLI, offline: Claude Code 2.1.280 / agent SDK 0.3.280 in the agent image, `--network none`, against a local stand-in Messages API with 3 s replies. Pushing A, then B and C while A answers, gives two results; the second turn's first assistant frame has `user_message_uuids` = [B, C], before its result. Pushing C alone during B's turn gives three turns, reporting [A], [B], [C]. The folded frame is checked in as `providers/__fixtures__/sdk-folded-turn-frame.json`. With the stand-in failing the folded turn (403), the CLI's error result frame still lists [B, C], so absorption and the failure notices hold on the error path; successful result frames carry the list too.
- `bun test src/poll-loop.consumed-inputs.test.ts` -> 18 pass: boundary fold (next turn no longer lags), the same script without `consumed` (today's lag, kept for providers that cannot tell), mid-turn fold (the running turn keeps its routing to the end), absorption by id out of push order, a provider whose `push` returns no id (unchanged behaviour), unknown and repeated ids ignored, folded prompts archived together, a wrap-nudge retry absorbed by a follow-up's turn (one nudge, routing kept), a new message absorbed into a retry turn (one more nudge, bounded), chained retries run or absorbed (earlier nudged turns' sends still suppressed), its echo window (repeat on the same thread suppressed, same text to another thread sent), failure notices to absorbed routes on a stream error and on an error result (including when the running route sends none), and an agent-to-agent replay of the downstream incident, with and without the signal.
- `bun test src/providers/claude.consumed-inputs.test.ts` -> 5 pass: a fresh UUID per input, sent as the SDK `uuid` and returned from `push`, `user_message_uuids` reported as `consumed` from assistant frames and from result frames, the recorded real frame, nothing emitted for frames without a list.
- Full container suite (`bun test` in the agent image) -> 703 pass, 1 fail (`agent mailbox context > treats an unreadable context like a pre-seam host`), the same single failure as unpatched `main` (680 pass, 1 fail) in the same image.
- `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` (after `bun install --frozen-lockfile`) -> clean.
- `/code-review` (high), twice. On the first version it found that adopting the newest consumed input's whole turn state was wrong (a retry pushed behind a follow-up carries the older message's routing; mid-turn it would change run mode and guards), which led to the current design: keep the running turn and only drop the absorbed queued turns. On the whole branch it raised 10 findings: 4 fixed (a new message absorbed into a retry turn can be nudged; one failure-notice helper; the per-thread window check reuses `wasWrittenInWindow`; a dead filter), 1 refuted by the CLI probe above (error result frames do carry the list), 5 declined as unchanged from `main` or deliberate (one route per turn; run mode within a turn; the existing main-route notice write; the thread rule for absorbed windows; query cost when nothing is absorbed).
- CodeRabbit, review-only mirror https://github.com/drsmk238/nanoclaw/pull/3 (10 passes, included allowance, no usage charges): 17 findings in all, 15 fixed in the later commits here (absorb by id; per-thread echo windows kept separately and carried through retry chains; failure notices for absorbed routes on both failure paths, counted only once written, guarded per write, none after a stop; `consumed` from result frames; any string id kept; test fixture seq; stricter test harness and assertions). 2 declined with reasons on the thread: retrying a failed notice write (nothing in `processQuery` retries one; CodeRabbit withdrew it), and per-reply routing within a turn that answered several inputs (predates this PR, listed under Out of scope). The last pass, on the final commit, generated no actionable comments.
- Upstream CI on this PR caught that a positional `push(message, inputId?)` broke the pre-contract OpenCode payload (`push(message, attachments?)`); `push` now keeps its one argument and returns the id. All 50 checks pass on the final commit.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Replies no longer attach to an earlier message (wrong quote, wrong thread, or for agent-to-agent replies the wrong session) after a Claude agent answers several queued messages in one turn.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. The new event carries only ids the agent-runner generated itself; unknown ids are ignored.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change (Claude Code wrote the change, the tests and the real-CLI probe; Claude Code `/code-review` and CodeRabbit reviewed it in a review-only mirror PR on the fork).

## Summary

- **Problem**: OneCLI's ChatGPT stand-in `auth.json` claims a free plan for every login, and Codex hides its `image_gen` tool from free plans (`image_generation_available` in `core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs`, still there in 0.169.0). - **Fix**: the OneCLI adapter drops that made-up plan claim, only when the user id is OneCLI's `onecli-managed` placeholder; Codex then treats the plan as unknown. When Codex saves an image, the Codex provider steers a short note into that image's own turn: where it was saved, that nobody has seen it, and to deliver it the way the request asks. The agent sends it with `send_file` when the asker expects to see it, and leaves it saved for a save-only ask or a task that did not ask to notify anyone. The unused image-folder snapshot and `file` events go. No core change.
- **Out of scope**: Iron Proxy's stand-in already claims `plus`. A sub-agent's image is noted in the sub-agent's own turn; wider sub-agent turn handling is #4165.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Leads the README with what NanoClaw is now, "the always-on agent you own", and makes the rest say what the code actually does.

- **Positioning**: new tagline and a short section before Quick Start. Always-on assistants are a hosted product category now; the README says what's different here: it runs on your machine, you can read and fork it, you pick the harness and model, and credentials stay in a gateway you run. It also says plainly that self-hosted doesn't mean nothing leaves your machine. No competitor names.
- **Harness benefit**: Philosophy now says why running each vendor's own harness matters (full toolset, session handling and model updates as they ship).

- **Privacy**: "your messages never leave your machine" wasn't true as written: they go to the model provider and to every channel you connect. The section now says NanoClaw sends nothing about them to us, and says where they do go.
- **Diagnostics**: described as what they are: step names, timings, status, the error message when setup stops, and platform details, sent to PostHog under a random per-install id. "Anonymous" is gone. The Scarf pixel in the README is mentioned too.
- **Security FAQ**: "credentials never enter the container" becomes "agents never hold raw API keys" (same wording as the feature list). Says egress lockdown is opt-in. Links `SECURITY.md` for private reports.
- **Softer claims**: "Bash access is safe because…" → "Bash commands run inside the container". The gateway "can enforce" policies, since that depends on which gateway is installed.
- **Stale details**: containers are per session, not per agent group. The group folder doesn't hold skills. The channel list was missing Signal, DeltaChat, Mattermost, Dial, Emacs and WhatsApp Cloud. Iron Proxy is named next to OneCLI.
- **Size and config**: "a handful of files" → "one host process, no microservices" (the host is ~245 source files). "Doesn't use configuration files" → "avoids configuration sprawl".
- **Provider-agnostic**: the README no longer reads as Claude-only. Setup's provider picker (Claude, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode) is mentioned in Quick Start, "Best harness, best model" becomes "Your pick of harness and model", and host-side help is "your coding agent" instead of "Claude Code". Claude is still named where it's a fact: the built-in default provider, the skills format, and what `migrate-v2.sh` hands off to.
- **Removed**: the "join the Family Chat group" usage example.
- **Founder's note kept verbatim**: the "Why I Built NanoClaw" text is back word for word, now as a dated quote (Gavriel Cohen, February 2026) under "Where it started" in the new section, instead of a standalone section.
- **Local models**: OpenCode can point at a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so the README no longer implies Ollama is the only local route.
- **Out of scope**: `README_zh.md`, `README_ja.md` and `README_ko.md`. They're about three months behind and link to a doc and a skill that no longer exist. Separate PR.

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): never block or follow links on the Claude settings.json
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops a FIFO (or symlink, or directory) at the group's Claude `settings.json` from wedging every container start.

- **Problem**: `writeMemorySessionHook` read `~/.claude/settings.json` with `readFileSync` and rewrote it with `writeFileSync`. That directory is the group's persistent, agent-writable `.claude-shared` mount, so a FIFO there blocked runner startup forever, on every respawn, before the poll loop started. A symlink was read and written through.
- **Fix**: open with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK` and require a regular file. A refused entry is logged and left alone, as the host's `prepareClaudeMemorySettings` already does, so the session still starts (without the memory hook). Writes go through a sibling temp file and `rename`, never truncating in place, and are skipped when nothing changed.
- **Out of scope**: a size cap on the file; moving hook registration to the host.

## Related work

No issue. Found by an automated review of a downstream fork; the code is unchanged from upstream.

prs.title: fix(mounts): reject extra mounts of paths the driver protects
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops a group mount of a folder NanoClaw keeps for itself from silently stopping that group's agent from starting.

- **Problem**: only NanoClaw may mount its runner code, skills, plugins and instruction files, and its key and certificate folders (`data/session-materials`, `data/gateway-trust`). The driver's guard enforces that. But `ncl groups config add-mount` stores such a mount without complaint, and the guard then refuses every start. The only trace is a once-a-minute warning, and the person gets no reply.
- **Fix**: the guard's rule moves into `requiredMountClass` in `drivers/types.ts`. `validateSpec` and `add-mount` both call it, so there is one rule, not a copy. `add-mount` judges the path the way the mount check resolves it, against the policy the running driver was built with, and refuses a reserved path with the reason. For install content it suggests mounting a copy; for keys and certificates it just refuses.
- **Fix**: a start refused with `denied-by-policy` or `spec-invalid` also logs an error naming the cause, on each attempt (about once a minute per stuck session). The existing retry warning is unchanged, because installed skills anchor on that exact line.
- **Out of scope**: a mount of a parent folder, such as the whole checkout, read-write. That needs a new guard rule and changes behavior for some installs, so it comes as its own PR.

## Related work

No issue. Found in a live install's logs, where two sessions went silent for about 10 minutes after a group mount of the runner code.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- New tests fail on main and pass here: `add-mount` refuses each reserved folder, stores nothing, and suggests a copy only for install content; a policy refusal keeps the warning and adds the error. A retryable failure reaches the driver and logs only the warning, carrying its error. If `NANOCLAW_SESSION_MATERIAL_ROOT` changes without a restart, `add-mount` still follows the driver's policy.
- Existing guard tests (`drivers/`, `mount-composition`) pass unchanged against the shared function.
- Full suite: 331 files pass. 5 files hit 5 s timeouts under load and pass alone; `onecli-detection.test.ts` fails locally on earlier heads too (a local pnpm issue). `tsc`, eslint and prettier are clean.
- No existing line is edited in `wakeContainer`'s failure path or in `groups.ts`'s imports, so downstream skills that patch those lines still apply.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
`ncl groups config add-mount` now refuses folders NanoClaw keeps for itself (runner code, skills, plugins, instruction files, keys and certificates) with a clear reason. A container start refused by the mount guard is logged as an error on each attempt.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

No new permissions. `add-mount` now refuses paths the guard already refuses at start; the guard itself is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(scripts): run CLI entry points from checkouts with spaces or symlinks in the path
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes ten CLI scripts actually run when the checkout path has a space in it or is reached through a symlink.

- **Problem**: they decided whether they were the entry point with ``import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}` ``. `import.meta.url` is percent-encoded and symlink-resolved; `argv[1]` is neither. Under `~/My Projects/nanoclaw` the check is false and the script exits 0 having done nothing: `skill-apply`, `skill-directives`, `skill-driver`, and the OneCLI and Iron Proxy `setup`/`auth`/`control`/`detect` scripts. The detectors then print nothing, so an installed gateway reads as absent.
- **Fix**: `existsSync(argv[1]) && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(realpathSync(argv[1])).href`. The existence check keeps the module importable when `argv[1]` is not a file (`node -e`); `setup/slack-worker.ts` already used `realpathSync` and gets the same guard.
- **Out of scope**: other CLIs that use `pathToFileURL(argv[1])` without realpath (space-safe, symlink-unsafe); a shared `isEntryPoint` helper.

## Related work

No issue. Each changed site is the same one-line expression, so it can be reviewed directly.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`

## Validation

- New `scripts/cli-entry-point.test.ts`: runs `skill-directives.ts` from a directory with a space, and through a symlink; imports it with a non-file `argv[1]`. Each fails against the code it fixes.
- `vitest run scripts/ setup/lib/skill-driver .claude/skills/add-onecli/scripts .claude/skills/add-iron-proxy/scripts` -> pass, except `scripts/update/transaction.e2e`, `scripts/registry-copy.integration` and `scripts/update-skills`, which fail only under full-suite load here and do so on unmodified `main` too; run alone they pass, both before and after.
- Manual: `tsx "<dir with space>/.claude/skills/add-onecli/scripts/detect.ts"` -> `absent` (before: no output).
- Typecheck of the 12 changed files via a tsconfig that includes them (the root one covers only `src/`): the same 24 errors as unmodified `main`, none on a changed line.

prs.title: fix(setup): follow-ups from the #4202 and #4213 reviews
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Daniel's follow-ups from his #4202 and #4213 approvals.

- **Problem**:
  - On a fresh Arch image, `pacman -S jq` fails with "target not found". The jq note then names 5 skills, but 13 run jq.
  - After a provider install on a Mac with no service, "not installed" prints twice.
  - A host build with type errors still writes its JS to `dist/`, and the next restart loads it.
- **Fix**:
  - On a never-synced pacman, jq needs a full system upgrade. Before the sudo ask, `nanoclaw.sh` says so and asks "Run the full system upgrade now? [y/N]". Only `y` or `yes` runs `pacman -Syu --needed jq`. On a no (the default), setup installs nothing and shows the jq note; with no terminal, or for a non-root user without sudo, it doesn't ask and does the same. A host that has synced is never upgraded. The answer goes to `logs/setup.log`.
  - The note names skills as examples; a test keeps it true.
  - `restartHost` drops `restart.sh`'s stderr only on exit 2 (no service).
  - Both host builds in a provider install use `--noEmitOnError`, and so does the rebuild command setup prints when its own fails.
- **Out of scope**: #4213 follow-up 3 (OpenCode needs one more restart after auth).

## Related work

Follow-ups to #4202 ([comment](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4202#issuecomment-6771411298)) and #4213 ([comment](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4213#issuecomment-6771412357)). No issue: found in review. Covers [Zvi's review](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4371#pullrequestreview-5939596461).

## Change kind

<!-- Check exactly one. -->
- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- New tests fail on main's code; 29 mutants each fail only their own tests.
- `setup` plus the verifier, registry and skill-apply tests: 1,044 passed, 14 skipped. `tsc`: no new errors.
- The real `nanoclaw.sh` in a terminal, in the stock never-synced `archlinux` image: Enter and `n` run no pacman command; `y` runs `pacman -Syu` and installs jq. With no terminal, or as a user without sudo: no question, no pacman call.
- Live, earlier: `archlinux:latest` installed jq after one `-Syu`; a type error wrote 0 JS files (428 on main).

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

<!-- Maintainers own CHANGELOG.md — do not edit it in this PR. -->
- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
On an Arch system that has never synced its package lists, setup can now run a whole-system upgrade (`pacman -Syu`, which updates every package) to install jq. It asks first, No is the default, and it never runs without a terminal. During a provider install, setup also shows "not installed" only once, and keeps the last good build when the host build fails.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

On a never-synced pacman host, setup runs `sudo -n pacman -Syu`, a full upgrade, only after the user types `y` or `yes` at the terminal. Otherwise it never upgrades.

- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above
