issues.title: [Feature]: Chat storage lifecycle: recoverable deletion, scoped retention, and visibility

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

- Local: `2.3.0.post1`, Linux, multi-agent, long-running
- Same issue seen on `2.2.x` (#7839)

## Summary

QwenPaw now has several chat-data write paths but no unified lifecycle: `sessions/*.json` stores chat state and feeds `history.db` backfill, `mem_session/dialog/*.jsonl` stores the source of auto-memory, `history.db` stores searchable history, and subagent/cron sessions keep appending. As a result, deleting a chat only removes the registry entry while the files remain; ephemeral sessions never expire; users cannot see per-store usage or reclaim it safely.

Disk is a finite, expensive resource. QwenPaw should move from “write only” to “every store has a defined retention, reclaim path, and visibility” — without indiscriminately deleting user data.

## Current impact

Measured on an agent with frequent subagents and cron jobs:

| Store | Measurement |
|:---|---:|
| `sessions/**/*.json` | **393 files / 658 MB** (subagent 335 / 563.5 MB, cron 50 / 86.5 MB, normal chats 7 / 6.9 MB) |
| `mem_session/dialog/*.jsonl` | **79 MB / 12 files** |
| After manual cleanup | 33 files / 23 MB; back to 38 / 32 MB by 2026-11-19 |

Deleting a chat: `ChatManager.delete_chats()` only deletes `ChatSpec`; delete endpoints clear checkpoints, but the session JSON remains. A maintainer confirmed this in #6299; PR #6536 proposes a tombstone and `.trash/<deletion-id>/` staging, but that staging is for crash recovery, not a user-facing recycle bin with a timeout, and the PR is still unmerged. Agent deletion keeps the whole workspace by default; only `--remove-workspace` runs `rmtree`. The existing CLI only has `qwenpaw clean` (wipes the whole workspace) and `chats delete` (metadata only); there is no per-store cleanup.

Secondary observation: `history.db` is currently a 239 MB file with about 9 MB of live pages, so purge still needs threshold-based compaction; this is not the main thread of the issue.

## Why a blanket cleanup is wrong

The existing designs have good reasons:

- `sessions/*.json` is the source for `history.db` backfill; the docs explicitly say the original session files are not modified or deleted during backfill.
- Retaining an agent workspace after deletion prevents accidental data loss.
- One dedicated session per cron job lets users review history and ask follow-up questions about earlier runs.
- `mem_session/dialog` is the raw evidence behind memory notes’ `source_conversation` links; deleting it would break traceability.

The problem is not these reasons. The problem is that “keep for correctness” and “keep forever, invisible, and unreclaimable” are currently the same state. The fix is a per-data-class lifecycle, not a global delete switch.

## Proposal: define lifecycle by data class

| Data | Role | Default policy | Reclaim path |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Normal chats `sessions/` | User asset | No automatic expiry; archive supported | User delete → recycle bin → timed purge |
| Subagent sessions | Ephemeral execution record | Expiry / count cap (suggest 7–30 days) | Move to trash first; skip running/recent |
| Cron sessions | Per-job review history | Keep one session per job; cap old-run size/count, retain recent N + summary | Archive or move old runs to trash |
| `mem_session/dialog/` | Memory evidence | Keep while referenced by a memory note; expire when unreferenced | Compress/archive; GC after the note is deleted |
| `history.db` | Searchable history | Keep existing retention | Compact when free pages cross a threshold; do not VACUUM on every purge |
| Tool results | Session content | Store a bounded preview in the session | Full output in the tool-result cache with retention |

## Deletion semantics

- One lifecycle service handles registry, session file, `mem_session/dialog`, history/FTS, checkpoints, and `.synced.json`; no per-path ad-hoc deletion.
- Write a tombstone, then move data to the recycle bin; recover unfinished deletions on startup.
- Delete a shared session file only when no other chat references it; deleting a running chat returns a conflict.
- The recycle bin supports restore/empty, keeps items for about 7 days by default (configurable), and purges them automatically.
- After permanent purge, the chat must no longer appear in history search or startup backfill.

## Three surfaces

Expose the same capabilities through three paths, backed by one service and configuration:

- **Periodic maintenance**: daily/weekly cleanup of expired subagent sessions and trash; threshold-based `history.db` compaction; report bytes reclaimed.
- **CLI**: `storage report`, `storage prune --dry-run/--apply`, `trash list/restore/empty`, `storage compact --dry-run/--apply`.
- **WebUI**: Settings → Storage with per-store usage, trash, restore/empty, preview before prune, maintenance settings; confirmation for destructive actions.

## Non-goals

- Do not auto-delete normal user chats.
- Do not change the one-session-per-cron-job design.
- Do not delete `mem_session/dialog` while a memory note still references it.
- Do not change the existing `history.db` retention semantics.

## Implementation order

- Finish #6536’s tombstone + `.trash` deletion flow and extend it to `mem_session/dialog` and checkpoints; it already covers shared references and crash recovery, the riskiest parts.
- #8532’s per-session storage can carry the lifecycle; its author states background retention is out of scope, so it needs a separate track.
- Do not adopt #8557’s per-run session; keep one session per job and cap old-run persistence instead.
- #7839’s orphan sessions need an actionable cleanup/import path, not a silent skip.
- Auto-Memory reads all `mem_session/dialog` files to rebuild its index (#7222); cleanup or archival must update the index instead of triggering another full scan.

## Acceptance criteria

- Deleting a chat/agent moves associated data to the recycle bin; restore makes the chat readable; timed purge removes it; it no longer appears in search or backfill.
- The trash survives restarts; deleting a running chat is rejected; shared files are not deleted accidentally.
- Subagent/cron sessions have configurable expiry or caps; running and recently used sessions are skipped.
- `mem_session/dialog` is retained while a memory note references it, and reclaimable when unreferenced.
- `history.db` can compact at a threshold; `storage report` shows file size, live pages, and reclaimable bytes.
- Periodic maintenance, CLI, and WebUI share behavior and configuration.

## Questions for maintainers

1. Is this per-data-class lifecycle acceptable? Are “no automatic expiry for normal chats” and “caps for subagent/cron” reasonable defaults?
2. Should the recycle bin live in the workspace or at platform level? What default retention would you recommend?
3. Should `mem_session/dialog` be reference-first (keep while a memory note references it) or time-based? If reference-first, should deleting a memory note trigger source cleanup?

issues.title: [Bug]: Scheduled task conversations show no messages until execution completes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body: ## QwenPaw Version 2.3.0 ## Description While a scheduled Agent task is running in the background, its corresponding conversation in the Web Console shows no messages or execution progress: - The message that triggers the task is not visible. - Model response messages are not visible. - All conversation content appears only after the entire task has finished. This prevents users from following the task’s progress during execution. The task uses dispatch mode `final`. I did not encounter this behavior in the previously used version. It appeared after upgrading, but the exact version that introduced the issue has not been identified. **Related PR(s):** Unknown. **Security considerations:** No credentials, tokens, or sensitive configuration are included in this report. ## Component(s) Affected - [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models) - [x] Console (frontend web UI) - [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.) - [ ] Skills - [ ] CLI - [ ] Documentation (website) - [ ] Tests - [ ] CI/CD - [ ] Scripts / Deploy ## Environment - **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0 - **OS:** Windows - **Install method:** Not confirmed - **Python version (if applicable):** 3.13 ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure a multi-step Agent scheduled task with dispatch mode set to `final`. 2. Let the task trigger and open its corresponding conversation in the Web Console while it is executing. 3. Observe that no trigger message, model responses, or execution progress appear. 4. Wait until the entire task finishes. The conversation content then becomes visible. ## Actual vs Expected - **Actual:** The conversation shows no messages or progress during execution. All content appears only after the task finishes. - **Expected:** The conversation displays the task’s trigger message and subsequent model responses as execution progresses. ## Logs / Screenshots ## Additional Notes Preliminary code investigation identified the following relevant paths, relative to the `qwenpaw` package: - `app/crons/executor.py` registers the conversation and directly calls `workspace.stream_query(req)`, without registering the execution with `workspace.task_tracker`. - `app/chats/api.py` obtains conversation execution status from that TaskTracker. - `app/routers/console.py` relies on `tracker.attach(chat.id)` for stream reconnection. - Cron also sets `suppress_console_push=True`, which causes ConsoleChannel to skip the frontend push queue. These findings suggest a missing connection between cron execution and the Web Console’s live conversation tracking. The complete cause and the release that introduced this behavior still need confirmation.

issues.title: [Bug] RESPONSE_SCOPE_LIMIT: active response routes are never evicted, channel silently dies at 128
issues.body:
## Summary

On a long-running deployment, the **WeChat channel silently stopped working in both directions** (inbound and outbound), with no user-visible error. Host logs only showed `-32603 internal error`.

## Root cause

`src/qwenpaw/channel_protocol/shared_response_driver.py:50` defines a hard cap:

```python
_MAX_ROUTES = 128
```

`_persist_route()` only evicts routes where `_evictable(row)` is true. `_evictable()` (in `response_lifecycle.py`) requires **all** of:

- `kind == "terminal"`
- `cleanup_state == "complete"`
- `expires_at_ms` is set and already passed

In our stuck state file (`workspaces/<ws>/channel_state/<sha>.json`, key `wechat.shared.responses`), **all 128 entries had `kind: "active"` and `cleanup_state: null`**. None were terminal, so nothing was ever evictable. Once the count reached 128, `_ensure_capacity()` raised:

```
ResponseStateError: ('RESPONSE_SCOPE_LIMIT', 'response route capacity is exhausted')
```

for every new inbound message **and** every outbound send — the channel became completely unusable while the process stayed healthy.

## Impact

- The entire channel goes **silently dead** (both directions), no alert of any kind.
- Diagnosis is extremely hard because the exception is swallowed twice:
  1. the plugin's inbound handler catches `Exception` and emits a bare `logger.warning(...)` without a traceback;
  2. `src/qwenpaw/plugins/execution/rpc.py` does `except Exception as exc: ... _ = exc` and returns only `-32603 internal error`, discarding the exception entirely.
  We had to patch `rpc.py` locally to `logger.exception(...)` just to see `RESPONSE_SCOPE_LIMIT` at all.
- In our case it took a full day of downtime to identify.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Evict stale `active` routes.** An `active` route that has been open far longer than any legitimate in-flight request should be reclaimable (e.g. by age since creation / `closed_at_ms`, or by a separate cap on concurrent active entries). Right now an `active` entry can never be removed.
2. **Surface capacity exhaustion.** When `_ensure_capacity()` fails, log an actionable error / emit a diagnostic event, and ideally auto-recover by dropping the oldest entries rather than failing all traffic silently.
3. **Do not discard exceptions in `rpc.py`.** The generic `except Exception as exc: ... _ = exc` should log the traceback (or at least keep it in the error `data`), otherwise every worker-side failure is undebuggable.

## Reproduction sketch

1. Run a channel for a long period where some sends fail / some responses never reach a terminal state.
2. `active` entries accumulate in `channel_state` and are never evicted.
3. At 128 entries, all inbound and outbound traffic fails with `-32603 internal error`.

## Environment

- QwenPaw **2.3.0.post1** (self-built fnOS .fpk)
- WeChat channel plugin **0.1.0**
- OS: fnOS (Debian-based NAS)
- Observed state: `wechat.shared.responses` = 128 rows, all `kind: "active"`, `cleanup_state: null`

**Workaround used:** clear `wechat.shared.responses` in the channel_state JSON (backup first), then restart the channel so the worker rebuilds its in-memory route table.

issues.title: [Bug]: 窄屏下整条消息的文字被剪裁，超宽内容（表格 / 代码块）同样被裁切且无法横向滚动

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body: ## 环境 - QwenPaw: `v2.3.0.post1`（升级前为 `v2.3.0`，升级后出现窄屏剪裁问题） - 界面: Console（Web UI） - 桌面端: Chrome / Windows 11，视口宽度约 `1903 px` - 移动端: 手机 Chrome，视口宽度 `375 px`（竖屏） - 设置: 设置中心 → 消息展示 → 消息宽度 = **标准** ## 复现步骤 1. 打开 Console，进入任意会话 2. 设置中心 → 消息展示 → 消息宽度选择「标准」 3. 让 Agent 输出以下任一内容： - 列数较多的 Markdown 表格（本次测试 20 列、30 列） - 超长单行的代码块（`text` 或 `css`，约 490~505 字符） 4. 观察消息气泡右侧 5. 用手机浏览器打开同一个会话，观察同样的消息 ## 实际表现 内容宽度超过气泡宽度时，**右侧被直接裁掉，不出现横向滚动条，也没有任何方式查看被裁掉的部分**。 各内容块表现一致。 ### 1. Markdown 表格 20 列表格只渲染到第 13 列（C13 仅显示一半），C14 至 C20 完全不可见。 - 实测表格渲染宽度：`1421 px` - 外层消息区宽度：`990 px` 30 列表格被裁得更早，实测宽度 `1651 px`。 | 截图 1 · 表格 | |---| | | ### 2. text 代码块 单行 505 字符的 `text` 代码块，只能看到前约 100 字符，其后内容全部不可见。块内每 20 字符放置一个 `` 标尺，用于定位裁切位置。 | 截图 2 · text 代码块 | |---| | | ### 3. css 代码块 单行 489 字符的 `css` 代码块（带语法高亮），表现与 `text` 块完全一致，同样从右侧被裁。 | 截图 3 · css 代码块 | |---| | | ### 4. 手机端（窄屏）：不只是表格和代码块，整条消息的文字都会被裁 375px 视口下打开同一个会话，消息区可视宽度只有 `303 px`，而承载内容的容器实测被撑到 `988 px`： - 一个两列的 Markdown 表格渲染宽度 `987 px`，右侧完全看不到，也无法滑动 - **同一条消息里，表格之后的普通段落文字也会一起被裁掉**，因为整块响应内容都被撑到 988px，超出部分被外层 `overflow: hidden` 静默裁掉 - 表现上就是「这条回复右边的字少了半截」，而且没有任何滚动条提示 ![Screenshot_2026-11-18-23-04-21-633_ai.qwenpaw.shell-edit.jpg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d1a92d9-d241-4ee3-a51a-95835a78e263) ## 补充观察 1. **不是「标准模式特有」**。把「消息宽度」切到「加宽」后，只是可用宽度变大、部分内容刚好能放下；一旦内容宽度超过容器，仍然会被裁且同样没有横向滚动条。标准模式因为容器更窄，所以更容易触发。 2. **同一条消息内的多个内容块全部受影响**。上例中三个块连续排列，每一个都在相同的位置被切断。 3. 通过 Browser 实测，承载消息内容的 `.x-markdown` 元素的实际渲染宽度会被内容撑开（`1651 px`），而外层消息区仍为 `990 px`，超出部分既不可见、也无法滚动到。

issues.title: [Bug]: QQ channel `enabled` flag silently reset to `false` after config reload/restart, breaks message reception with no warning log
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2.post1

## Description

After a system optimization / restart (config reload), the QQ channel's `enabled` flag in `config.json` is **silently set to `false`**, so the bot stops receiving and sending QQ messages entirely — with no startup warning and no log entry explaining why. The channel configuration itself (app_id, client_secret, etc. in `agent.json` / channel config) remains intact and correct; only the `enabled` boolean flips. The user has no way to know the channel was disabled until they notice the bot stopped replying.

**Related PR(s):** none

**Security considerations:** none

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2.post1
- **OS:** Linux (container, NFS-backed persistent disk)
- **Install method:** pip (cloud deployment)
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.11
- **Channel:** QQ (QQ Guild open platform)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a fully working QQ channel configuration (correct app_id / client_secret, `enabled: true`).
2. Trigger a config reload or a framework restart (e.g., routine optimization/restart of the deployment).
3. Observe the QQ channel's `enabled` flag in `config.json`.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** after reload/restart, `enabled` is silently `false`; the bot stops receiving/sending QQ messages; no log line or startup warning mentions the channel being disabled. The channel is effectively dead until someone manually edits `config.json` back to `enabled: true`.
- **Expected:**
  1. The `enabled` flag should be **persisted** and survive config reload/restart without being reset.
  2. If the framework *intentionally* disables a channel during reload, it should emit a **warning log** at startup explaining which channel was disabled and why.
  3. Startup should run a lightweight **health check** over all configured channels' `enabled` state and surface any unexpected changes.

## Logs / Screenshots

No relevant log output exists — this is precisely the bug: the state change happens with zero log signal, so there is nothing to grep for. Confirmed by inspecting `config.json` after restart and comparing before/after values of the QQ channel's `enabled` field.

## Additional Notes

### Root cause hypothesis

The config (re)write path during reload/optimization appears to normalize or reset the `enabled` flag for all channels to a default (`false`) instead of preserving the previously persisted value. The fix likely needs to (a) treat `enabled` as an explicit persisted user preference that must be read back and re-applied rather than re-defaulted on reload, and (b) add a log line whenever a channel's `enabled` state ends up different from the previously persisted value.

### Impact

Any multi-channel deployment where QQ is the primary interaction channel silently loses that channel on every restart/reload, with no alerting. Operators only find out when the bot stops replying, and must manually diff `config.json` to discover the cause.

issues.title: [Bug] Checkpoint service fails on Git long-path prefix + WeChat channel stuck at DEPENDENCY_ENVIRONMENT_AMBIGUOUS (Windows, 2.3.0-beta.2)
issues.body:
## Environment

- QwenPaw Desktop: `2.3.0-beta.2`
- OS: Windows 11 (Build 26300)
- Git: `2.51.0.windows.1`
- `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem\LongPathsEnabled` = `1`
- No `GIT_*` environment variables set at process / user / machine level
- Data dir: `C:\Users\<user>\.qwenpaw`
- Install dir: `D:\工具软件\QwenPaw\QwenPaw Desktop`

---

## Bug 1: Checkpoint service initialization always fails

### Symptom

The checkpoint / workspace snapshot service fails on every startup. Session auto-snapshot, checkpoint rollback and POST_RESPONSE archiving are all non-functional. The failure repeats on each launch (observed 86+ times between 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-08).

### Log evidence

```
git init --bare \\?\C:\Users\<user>\.qwenpaw\workspaces\Satan\checkpoints\shadow.git
exit 128: fatal: unknown error occurred while reading the configuration files
```

`Checkpoint service initialization failed` — latest occurrence `2026-11-08 17:46:57`, target `\\?\C:\Users\<user>\.qwenpaw\workspaces\Satan`.

After failure, the `checkpoints` directory only contains a 0-byte `gitconfig` and a `gitattributes` file. `shadow.git` is never created.

### Root cause

QwenPaw passes a path prefixed with the Win32 extended-length prefix `\\?\` to `git init --bare`. Git for Windows `2.51.0` rejects this form and fails to read its configuration, exiting with code 128.

This is not a local Git or OS configuration issue:
- `LongPathsEnabled=1` is already enabled
- no `GIT_CONFIG_*` variables exist
- setting `core.longpaths=true` does not help

The prefix is injected by the application itself, so it cannot be worked around from the OS or Git side.

### Expected

Checkpoint service should initialize successfully. The `\\?\` prefix should be stripped before being passed to Git, or `os.path.realpath` / `Path.resolve()` results should not be forwarded verbatim to `git`.

---

## Bug 2: WeChat channel stuck at `DEPENDENCY_ENVIRONMENT_AMBIGUOUS`

### Symptom

With `channels.wechat.enabled=true` in `config.json`, the WeChat channel never becomes usable:
- Console channel page never shows a QR code
- `GET /api/config/channels/wechat/qrcode` returns **502 Bad Gateway**
- no `wechat` runner subprocess is spawned
- `GET /api/plugins/wechat` reports `diagnostics: ["channel_validation_pending"]`
- clicking "repair dependencies" in the console returns `DEPENDENCY_ENVIRONMENT_AMBIGUOUS`

`DEPENDENCY_ENVIRONMENT_AMBIGUOUS` appears 49 times in `qwenpaw.log` (latest `2026-11-05 22:18:59`).

### What we observed

1. `~\.qwenpaw\dependency-environments\` accumulated multiple empty hash-named directories (4 at one point), each containing only `.site.dependencies.admission.lock`, `.site.dependencies.lock` and `.site.dependencies-readers\*.lease` — **no `site-packages`, no actual packages** (total size under 1 KB).
2. `~\.qwenpaw\plugin_runtime\py3.11-windows-amd64\site` was completely empty.
3. The WeChat plugin declares dependencies `httpx` and `pycryptodome` (see `requirements.txt`, `Crypto.Cipher.AES` used in `utils.py`), but `~\.qwenpaw\plugin_provisions\` only contains `computer-use.json` — there is **no `wechat.json` provision record**.
4. Plugin manifest: `version 0.1.0.dev0`, `qwenpaw_version.min = 2.2.2b4` (satisfied by host `2.3.0-beta.2`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable the WeChat channel (`channels.wechat.enabled=true`).
2. Restart QwenPaw.
3. Open the console channel page → no QR code is rendered.
4. `GET /api/config/channels/wechat/qrcode` → 502.
5. Click "repair dependencies" → `DEPENDENCY_ENVIRONMENT_AMBIGUOUS`.

### What we already tried (all ineffective)

- Manually installed `httpx>=0.27.0` and `pycryptodome` into the shared dependency site (`plugin_runtime\py3.11-windows-amd64\site`) via `pip --target`; imports verified OK (`import httpx`, `from Crypto.Cipher import AES`).
- Deleted all empty `dependency-environments` directories while the app was fully stopped, then restarted.
- Result: after restart the app **immediately recreated multiple environment directories within the same second** (two dirs created at `20:42:34`, a third at `20:44:06`). The ambiguity therefore returns and cannot be cleared by deleting the directories.
- `POST /api/plugins/wechat/repair-dependencies` returns **409 Conflict** with an empty response body; `reload` / `validate` endpoints return **405**.
- `GET /api/config/channels/wechat` reports `enabled: false` while `config.json` on disk has `channels.wechat.enabled: true` — runtime state and persisted config disagree.

### Expected

- The dependency resolver should converge on a single dependency environment per plugin instead of generating multiple candidates for the same plugin.
- `repair-dependencies` should return a meaningful error body instead of an empty 409.
- If `channels.wechat.enabled=true` is persisted, the runtime channel state should reflect it after restart.

### Additional note

`plugin_provisions` lacks a `wechat` entry, which may cause the validator to treat the plugin dependencies as "unplanned" and refuse to leave `channel_validation_pending`. Whether this is intentional is unclear from the logs.

---

## Impact

- Bug 1: checkpoint / rollback / auto-archive silently broken on Windows with recent Git versions.
- Bug 2: the WeChat channel is completely unusable — no QR code can be obtained, so no login/authorization is possible.

Happy to provide the full `qwenpaw.log` (2.2 MB) and any additional diagnostics if useful.

issues.title: [Discussion]: After updating QwenPaw to 2.3.0.post1, startup_diagnostic floods the output with WARNING lines, and Channels (DingTalk, Feishu) are unavailable by default until manually updated

labels.name: question
labels.description: Further information is requested

issues.body:
# 中文版

**标题：** 更新 QwenPaw 到 2.3.0.post1 后，`startup_diagnostic` 以 WARNING 级别刷屏，且默认情况下 Channel（钉钉、飞书）不可用，需手动更新后才可用

## 背景
更新 QwenPaw 到 **2.3.0.post1** 后，`qwenpaw update` 的输出中出现了大量 **WARNING** 级别日志。这些 WARNING 在**此前历次 QwenPaw 版本更新中均未出现过**，因此怀疑是本次版本引入的日志级别 / 噪音回归。

这些 WARNING 的内容本身并不是错误，而是新版引入的 **startup_diagnostic（启动诊断）** 机制在子进程启动各阶段打印的时序信息：`bootstrap` → `configure` → `dependency_read` → `dependency_admission` → `driver_verify` → `hello`。问题在于子进程把这些信息写到了 **stderr**，父进程捕获 stderr 后**统一按 WARNING 级别记录**，导致正常的启动流程被伪装成大量警告。

## 复现步骤
1. 执行 `qwenpaw update` 更新到 2.3.0.post1
2. 观察输出：`dingtalk`、`feishu` 等插件子进程启动时，每个阶段都会打印一条 `startup_diagnostic` 的 WARNING
3. 更新完成后，日志显示 `Update completed successfully.`
4. 但默认情况下，已启用的 Channel（如钉钉、飞书）**不可用**
5. 必须进入 **Web Console → 频道 / Channels**，手动更新 Channel 版本后，Channel 才能正常使用

## 实际表现 vs 预期
- **实际：**
  - 正常启动流程被记为 WARNING，刷屏严重，容易让用户和维护者误以为出现问题。
  - 虽然主程序更新成功，但默认情况下 Channel（钉钉、飞书）不可用，需要额外手动更新 Channel 版本。
- **预期：**
  - 启动诊断这类时序信息应以 `DEBUG` / `INFO` 级别输出，只有真正的异常（握手失败、依赖不满足等）才使用 WARNING/ERROR。
  - 主程序更新成功后，已启用的 Channel 应可直接使用，或至少给出明确提示，说明需要手动更新 Channel 版本。

## 值得关注的细节
1. **启动偏慢（`startup_slow`）**：`dependency_admission` 阶段在 audit 模式下耗时约 8 秒，接近 10 秒预算阈值。对比明显：
   - `audit` 模式（扫描全局所有 site-packages）→ `dependency_admission` ≈ 8s
   - `probe` 模式（只校验插件直接依赖）→ `dependency_admission` ≈ 1.2–1.5s
   - 说明耗时主要来自 audit 模式需遍历全部已安装包（本环境装有 qwenpaw、anthropic、chromadb、pandas、onnxruntime、playwright 等数十上百个包）。
2. **`returncode: -15`（SIGTERM）**：这是 audit 模式探测完成后主动终止子进程、切换到 `probe` 模式的正常流程，并非崩溃；但因为它同样伴随 WARNING 打印，极易被误读为异常退出。
3. **Channel 默认不可用**：更新到 2.3.0.post1 后，钉钉、飞书等 Channel 在 Web Console 中需要手动更新版本后才能使用，这一行为在历史版本更新时并未出现。

## 建议
- 将 startup_diagnostic 的正常时序日志降级为 DEBUG/INFO，仅对真实异常保留 WARNING/ERROR。
- 或在 stderr 捕获处区分「诊断信息」与「真实错误」，不要一律按 WARNING 记录。
- 可考虑对 audit 模式的依赖扫描做缓存 / 并行，降低 `startup_slow` 发生概率。
- 主程序更新后，若 Channel 版本也需要更新，建议在 `qwenpaw update` 输出中给出明确提示，或自动同步更新已启用 Channel 的版本，避免用户误以为更新已完成却仍无法使用。

## 环境
- QwenPaw 版本：2.3.0.post1
- OS：Linux（aarch64）
- 现象出现在更新后首次启动；日志末尾显示 `Update completed successfully.`，但 Channel 默认不可用，需手动更新 Channel 版本后才恢复正常。
- 完整（已脱敏）日志见附件。

---

# English Version

**Title:** After updating QwenPaw to 2.3.0.post1, `startup_diagnostic` floods the output with WARNING lines, and Channels (DingTalk, Feishu) are unavailable by default until manually updated

## Background
After updating QwenPaw to **2.3.0.post1**, a large number of **WARNING**-level lines appear in the output of `qwenpaw update`. These WARNINGs **never appeared in any previous QwenPaw updates**, which suggests a logging-level / noise regression introduced in this version.

The content of these WARNINGs is not actually errors. They come from the newly introduced **startup_diagnostic** mechanism, which prints timing information for each phase of a worker subprocess startup: `bootstrap` → `configure` → `dependency_read` → `dependency_admission` → `driver_verify` → `hello`. The problem is that the subprocess writes these messages to **stderr**, and the parent process captures stderr and logs it **uniformly at WARNING level**, so a normal startup flow gets rendered as a flood of warnings.

## Reproduction
1. Run `qwenpaw update` to update to 2.3.0.post1
2. Observe the output: during startup of plugin subprocesses (`dingtalk`, `feishu`, etc.), a WARNING line is printed for every phase
3. After the update completes, the log shows `Update completed successfully.`
4. However, enabled Channels such as DingTalk and Feishu are **unavailable by default**
5. They only become usable after manually updating the Channel version in **Web Console → Channels**

## Actual vs Expected
- **Actual:**
  - Normal startup progress is recorded as WARNING, producing noisy output that can easily be mistaken for a problem.
  - Although the main update succeeds, Channels (DingTalk, Feishu) are not usable by default and require a manual Channel version update.
- **Expected:**
  - Startup-diagnostic timing should be emitted at `DEBUG` / `INFO`, not WARNING. Only genuine failures (handshake failure, unsatisfied dependencies, etc.) should use WARNING/ERROR.
  - After a successful main update, already-enabled Channels should work immediately, or at least the CLI should clearly indicate that Channel versions also need to be updated.

## Notable details
1. **Slow startup (`startup_slow`)**: The `dependency_admission` phase takes ~8s in `audit` mode, close to the 10s budget threshold. The contrast is clear:
   - `audit` mode (scans all site-packages) → `dependency_admission` ≈ 8s
   - `probe` mode (validates only the plugin's direct dependencies) → `dependency_admission` ≈ 1.2–1.5s
   - The cost comes from audit mode walking every installed package (this env has dozens/hundreds: qwenpaw, anthropic, chromadb, pandas, onnxruntime, playwright, etc.).
2. **`returncode: -15` (SIGTERM)**: This is the normal flow where audit mode terminates the subprocess after probing and switches to `probe` mode — not a crash. However, because it is also accompanied by WARNING output, it can easily be misread as an abnormal exit.
3. **Channels unavailable by default**: After updating to 2.3.0.post1, Channels such as DingTalk and Feishu require a manual version update in the Web Console before they can be used. This behavior did not occur in previous updates.

## Suggestion
- Demote normal startup-diagnostic timing to DEBUG/INFO, reserving WARNING/ERROR for real anomalies.
- Or distinguish "diagnostic info" from "real errors" at the stderr-capture point instead of logging everything as WARNING.
- Consider caching / parallelizing the audit-mode dependency scan to reduce `startup_slow` occurrences.
- If Channel versions also need updating after a main update, either prompt the user clearly in the `qwenpaw update` output, or automatically sync/update enabled Channel versions, to avoid the impression that the update is fully complete when Channels are still unusable.

## Environment
- QwenPaw version: 2.3.0.post1
- OS: Linux (aarch64)
- Observed on the first startup after update; the tail shows `Update completed successfully.`, but Channels are unavailable by default and only work after manually updating Channel versions.
- Full (sanitized) logs attached.

issues.title: DoomLoopGate never triggers when agentscope accumulates a reply into one assistant message
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0 (Docker image `agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0`). Also reproducible on `main` at `fc1db1a`.

## Description

With the default loop configuration (`window_size=3`, `similarity_threshold=1.0`, stages `after=3 / modify_prompt` and `after=4 / stop`), a turn that repeatedly calls the same tool with identical arguments never triggers either stage.

In a real 9-iteration console session on the default mode (the same failing SQL through `execute_readonly_sql` every round), `--log-level debug` showed `DefaultMode configured 2 gate(s)` and `LoopGate 'doom-loop' activated` on every iteration, but never `Doom loop: sim=`; the turn only ended via `IterationGate`. The persisted `agent.state.context` contained just two messages: the user message and one assistant message with 8 accumulated `tool_call`/`tool_result` block pairs.

**Root cause**

- agentscope 2.0.10 keeps **one assistant message per reply**. `Agent._save_to_context` uses `state.reply_id` as the message id and appends every iteration's blocks (reasoning, tool calls, tool results) to that same message.
- `DoomLoopGate._auto_record_from_ctx` (`src/qwenpaw/loop/gates/doom_loop.py`, around L205) returns as soon as the latest message id matches the last recorded one:

  ```python
  last_msg = context[-1]
  if last_msg.id == state.last_recorded_msg_id:
      return
  ```

  Within a reply the id never changes, so after the first check no further tool calls are recorded, `history_dirty` stays `False`, and `check()` returns `BYPASS` for the rest of the turn.
- Consequence: only a model response whose **first** snapshot already contains at least `window_size` identical tool calls (parallel calls in one response) can trip the window. Even then `consecutive_hits` is seeded to `window_size` and only increments on a later dirty check, so the `after=4 / stop` stage is unreachable in the default mode.

**Related PR(s):** coming in a follow-up PR.

**Security considerations:** none.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0 (`main` at `fc1db1a` also affected)
- **OS:** Debian 12, aarch64
- **Install method:** Docker
- **Python version:** 3.12 (agentscope 2.0.10)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use the default mode (console chat) with the default `agents.running.loop.doom_loop` stages.
2. Ask something that makes the agent call the same tool with exactly the same arguments at least 4 times (for example, the same failing SQL).
3. Observe that no doom-loop warning is injected and the loop is never stopped by the doom gate.

Minimal reproduction without an LLM:

```python
import asyncio
from types import SimpleNamespace

from qwenpaw.config.config import DoomLoopStageConfig
from qwenpaw.loop.gates.doom_loop import DoomLoopGate


async def main():
    msg = SimpleNamespace(id="reply-1", role="assistant", content=[])
    agent = SimpleNamespace(state=SimpleNamespace(context=[msg]))
    ctx = {
        "agent": agent,
        "final_msg": None,
        "iteration": 0,
        "has_tool_calls": True,
    }
    gate = DoomLoopGate(
        window_size=3,
        similarity_threshold=1.0,
        stages=[
            DoomLoopStageConfig(after=3, action="modify_prompt", prompt="warn"),
            DoomLoopStageConfig(after=4, action="stop", prompt="stop"),
        ],
    )
    for i in range(1, 7):
        # Same message id, one more identical tool call per formatting round,
        # exactly like agentscope accumulates blocks into one reply.
        msg.content.append(
            {
                "type": "tool_call",
                "name": "execute_readonly_sql",
                "input": {"sql": "SELECT 1"},
            },
        )
        result = await gate.check(ctx)
        state = gate._ensure_state()
        print(i, len(state.history), state.consecutive_hits, result.action.value)


asyncio.run(main())
```

Actual output on 2.3.0 / `main`:

```
1 1 0 bypass
2 1 0 bypass
3 1 0 bypass
4 1 0 bypass
5 1 0 bypass
6 1 0 bypass
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `history` stays at 1 for the whole reply; both the warning and the stop stage never fire. The `after=4 / stop` stage is unreachable.
- **Expected:** the third identical call produces `INTERRUPT_AND_CONTINUE` with the configured warning prompt, the fourth produces `TERMINATE` with the stop prompt.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
[DEBUG] DefaultMode configured 2 gate(s)
[DEBUG] IterationGate: 1/100
[DEBUG] IterationGate: 2/100
...
[DEBUG] IterationGate: 9/100
(no "Doom loop: sim=" line anywhere)
```

## Additional Notes

The current unit tests only call `gate.record()` directly (`tests/unit/loop/test_doom_loop_gate.py`), so the `_auto_record_from_ctx` path has no coverage and this regression shipped unnoticed. A fix that consumes the tail of the accumulated message (count of already-recorded `tool_call` blocks) restores the intended 3-warning / 4-stop behaviour and keeps the 2.3.0 improvements (recording every tool call in the message, the `has_tool_calls` guard, and warning injection).

issues.title: Repeated identical tool calls are never interrupted: the doom-loop gate records at most one call per reply
issues.body:
## What happens

With `QWENPAW_SHELL_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB=128`, a 400 MB probe process is terminated
correctly and the tool result reads:

```
exit code 15. [resource protection] Shell memory limit exceeded (RSS 134881280 bytes > 134217728 bytes)
```

The same `Bash` invocation was then approved **14 times** between `09:09:10`
and `09:10:22` — one every 6–7 seconds — and the user had to press stop twice.
Nothing in the agent loop noticed that the same call was repeating.

## Correction to the earlier report

The first version of this issue claimed the model never received the result and
therefore retried. That is wrong, and I am correcting it here rather than
leaving a misleading cause in place.

The result did reach the model. The stored turn at `09:11:01` ends with the tool
result carrying the full text shown above plus `state=error`. Draining the same
tool response directly returns it as a normal tool response as well.

So the retries were not caused by a missing result. They were caused by nothing
stopping them.

## Why nothing stopped them

`loop/gates/doom_loop.py` is enabled in the default mode — `window_size=3`,
`similarity_threshold=0.5`, `stop` after 4 hits — but the gate has never fired.
`_auto_record_from_ctx` de-duplicates on the **message** id:

```python
last_msg = context[-1]
if last_msg.id == state.last_recorded_msg_id:
    return
```

Inside a single reply, every assistant message is written with the same
`state.reply_id`: `agentscope` creates one `ReplyContext(reply_id=…)` per reply,
and `AgentState.append_context` either extends the existing message or appends a
new one **with that same id**. From the second iteration onwards `last_msg.id`
already equals `state.last_recorded_msg_id`, the function returns before
recording anything, and the history never grows past **one** entry.

| iteration within one reply | message id | recorded calls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `reply_id` | 1 |
| 2 | `reply_id` | 1 |
| 3 … 14 | `reply_id` | 1 |

A three-entry window can never fill, so `_detect_repetition` cannot return true
and no stage is ever reached.

Reproduced against the real `DoomLoopGate` with two synthetic contexts:

| context shape | history after 8 iterations | fired |
| --- | --- | --- |
| same message id every iteration (actual behaviour) | stays at 1 | never |
| distinct message id per iteration (hypothetical) | reaches 3 on iteration 3 | on iteration 4 |

Production logs agree: `qwenpaw.log` since 11-13 contains no `DoomLoopGate` and
no `Doom loop` line at all.

## Scope

This is not specific to resource-protection terminations. **Any** tool invoked
repeatedly with identical arguments inside a single reply is invisible to the
gate. The shell case only made it visible because each attempt was expensive
and the user was watching.

## Expected

Repeating the same tool call with the same arguments past the configured window
should reach the configured stage, instead of running until the user stops it.

## Proposed direction

Record per tool-call block rather than per message: make the de-duplication key
something that differs between two calls inside the same reply — the tool-call
block id, or `(reply_id, block_id)` — and scan the blocks appended since the
last observation instead of only `context[-1]`.

I am explicitly **not** proposing a change to `_with_shell_guard`. Overriding the
result state with `ERROR` is a separate question, it is not the cause of the
repetition, and changing it would not make the gate work.

## Second observation — explained, not a defect

While reproducing, a bare script that set `QWENPAW_SHELL_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB=96`
before importing `qwenpaw` still ended up with `ShellGuard.from_environment`
returning `None`, and a 300 MB process ran to completion.

The cause is `load_bootstrap_envs()`: at import time it replays
`$QWENPAW_HOME.secret/envs.json` over `os.environ` with `overwrite=True`, and
that file contained `"0"` for this key, so the value set by the script was
replaced (96 → 0). Setting the variable **after** the import creates the guard
as expected (96 MB, kills a 300 MB process).

That is documented behaviour — "persisted values override existing
process/system values" — and the Console path writes through the same store, so
a limit configured there is applied correctly. I am recording it only so the
reproduction in this issue can be run; it is not a defect.

issues.title: [Bug]: Windows auto mode with sandbox off allows inline Office COM Quit() to close the user's PowerPoint

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.1.0 (governance behavior present since the 2.0.1 unsandboxed shell fallback)

## Description

On Windows, with approval level `auto` and the security sandbox turned off, an agent-authored inline Office COM shell command is executed instead of denied. `PowerPoint.Application`, `Excel.Application`, `Word.Application`, and `Outlook.Application` are single-instance COM servers. `Quit()` on that object terminates the user's already-open app, not a private automation instance.

Built-in slide-render scripts that avoid `Application.Quit()` do not cover this path. The command is not in the repo; the model emits it during self-checks, and the shell tool runs it.

Unmatched shell commands are classified as `SANDBOX_FALLBACK` in `GovernancePolicy.evaluate`. When the sandbox is disabled or unavailable, `ResourceGovernor` rewrites that decision to `ALLOW` (`running unsandboxed`). `dangerous_shell_commands.yaml` has no signature for inline Office COM, so nothing flags the command before that rewrite.

**Related PR(s):** none

**Security considerations:** Local impact only. A shell command the agent is already allowed to run can close the user's Office process. No remote code execution or credential exposure.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.1.0
- **OS:** Windows
- **Install method:** from source / desktop package
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Windows, with Microsoft PowerPoint already open on a user file.
2. Set tool approval to `auto` and turn the security sandbox off.
3. Ask the agent to run a PowerShell Office COM self-check, for example `New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application` followed by `Quit()`. The same happens for Excel, Word, Outlook, and a one-liner such as `win32com.client.Dispatch("PowerPoint.Application").Quit()`.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** The command matches no detection rule, becomes `SANDBOX_FALLBACK`, then `ALLOW` because the sandbox is off. PowerShell attaches to the running PowerPoint COM server and `Quit()` closes the user's PowerPoint.
- **Expected:** Inline Office COM automation is denied before the unsandboxed fallback, including when the sandbox is off. The user's PowerPoint, Excel, Word, and Outlook stay open. Ordinary shell commands such as `echo hello` remain allowed.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
ResourceGovernor: sandbox disabled by config, running 'Bash' unsandboxed (ALLOW)
```

Relevant code:

- `src/qwenpaw/governance/policy.py`: unmatched shell returns `GovernanceAction.SANDBOX_FALLBACK`
- `src/qwenpaw/governance/resource_governor.py`: if the sandbox is not usable, that decision is replaced with `GovernanceAction.ALLOW`
- `src/qwenpaw/security/tool_guard/rules/dangerous_shell_commands.yaml`: no Office COM rule

## Additional Notes

Suggested fix: add a CRITICAL shell detection rule for inline Office COM construction (`New-Object -ComObject` / `GetActiveObject` / `CreateObject` / `win32com` `Dispatch` against `PowerPoint.Application`, `Excel.Application`, `Word.Application`, `Outlook.Application`, and the same `Quit()` pattern). CRITICAL findings are denied in Phase 1, so they never reach the sandbox-off ALLOW path.

Please do not treat in-process product scripts that only `Close()` a private temp presentation as the bug. Those scripts never call `Application.Quit()` on an attached user instance. The hole is agent-improvised shell COM plus the unsandboxed fallback.

issues.title: [Bug]: 上下文中出现从未发送过的 user 消息，并驱动 agent 继续执行

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
打个比方，我问一个问题，它执行完工具、得出结论回答完以后，会话没有结束，大概2~3秒后，紧接着又开始执行工具，开始新一轮的工具调用和回复，完毕之后，会话依然没有结束，然后如此循环，但是每一轮不是重复执行相同的内容。给我的感觉是，每轮结论过来以后，agent好像又收到了什么命令又开始执行。具体不知道什么原因，我让agent自行查了好久，也没查到，但是现象可以描述出来，如下。

## 环境

| 项 | 值 |
|---|---|
| QwenPaw | 2.3.0 |
| agentscope | 2.0.10 |
| Python | 3.12.4 / Linux x86_64 |
| 模型 | `workbuddy/cn:deepseek-v4.1-flash` |
| 渠道 | console |
| 已装插件 | 4 个官方 hub + `aw-avatar`、`qwenpaw-openui`、`qq` |
| 相关配置 | `running.loop.rubric.enabled = false`（两个 agent 均为 false）、`defaults.running.loop` 为空、无 `config.gates` 字段、`custom_modes: []` |

## 现象

一次普通的一问一答之后，agent 并没有停下，而是继续执行了约 9 分钟的工具调用。期间用户**没有发送任何消息**。

而 agent 侧确实"收到"了若干条消息，内容都是命令式的。**这些消息用户从未发送，界面上也从未显示过。**

按出现顺序：

**① 你自己看看，你自己用的什么版本**

**② 你上一条回复最后停在「我将…」「我会…」这类承诺句上就结束了，承诺的动作没有执行。请直接执行它：需要查看文件、执行命令或调用工具就直接调用，不要解释为什么停下，不要重复已经写过的内容，不要重新开头。**

**③ 按你说的直接执行，也就是把它加进去。**

**④ 为了健康运行，先确认一下我们现在的状态**

**⑤ 如果确实已经全部完成，请只回复 DONE**

其中第 ② 条在后续轮次中重复出现至少六次，措辞略有差异（例如有时只包含「不要解释为什么停下，不要重复已经写过的内容，不要重新开头」）。

## 证据

### 1. `history.db` 中不存在这些消息

同一 session 的记录序列（时间相邻）：

```
seq=31857  user       context_msg   15:04:20  「插件安装在什么目录里面的？」
seq=31858  assistant  model_turn    15:04:2x  （正常回答）
seq=31859  assistant  tool_result   ...
...
seq=31863  assistant  tool_result   ...
seq=31864  user       context_msg   15:08:36  （用户的下一条，中间约 4 分钟）
```

`seq=31857` 到 `seq=31864` 之间**没有任何 user 记录**，全部是 assistant 的 `model_turn` / `tool_result`。但 agent 在这段时间内确实执行了 5 轮工具调用。

### 2. 上述文本在库中只以 assistant 引用的形式存在

按内容检索这些注入文本，命中项全部是 `assistant`（agent 在分析时把原文贴了出来），**没有一条是 `user`**：

```
seq=31865  assistant  model_turn   （agent 引用）
seq=31926  assistant  model_turn   （agent 引用）
seq=31957  assistant  model_turn   （agent 引用）
seq=31963  assistant  model_turn   （agent 引用）
```

### 3. 不是第二个模型 / 不是另一个 agent

该时间窗口内日志中的全部 LLM 调用：

```
15:20:12  1793455195012-pxcwutx  cn:deepseek-v4.1-flash
15:23:44  1793455195012-pxcwutx  cn:deepseek-v4.1-flash
15:25:00  1793455195012-pxcwutx  cn:deepseek-v4.1-flash
```

同一个 session、同一个模型，没有额外调用。

### 4. 源码中检索不到这些文本

在 `site-packages/qwenpaw/`、`console/assets/`、`@appcenter/my-paw/`（bridge）中检索上述中文原文，0 命中。

### 5. 日志中没有对应的 gate 记录

全量日志中 `Stop handler BLOCKED exit` 出现次数为 **0**。

## 影响

其中一条注入消息（`按你说的直接执行`）**伪装成了用户对某项操作的批准**，agent 据此修改了工作区中的 `MEMORY.md`。

也就是说：一条从未存在过的"用户消息"，成功驱动了一次写操作。

## 已排除的可能

- 不是用户在别的 session 发送 —— 全库（947 条 user 记录）检索该文本，0 命中
- 不是前端渲染问题 —— 用户确认界面上从未出现
- 不是第二个模型 / 第二个 agent —— 日志证据见上
- 不是 `loop.rubric` —— 两个 agent 的 `rubric.enabled` 均为 `false`
- 不是 `custom_modes` —— 该字段为空数组
- 不是持久化污染 —— 这些内容在 `history.db` 中根本不存在（与 #7211 描述的方向相反）

## 一个可能的观察

在同一 session 的后续对话中，agent 多次出现"给出结论后紧接着又发起工具调用"的行为（13 次 `model_turn` 中有 10 次其后紧跟 `tool_result`，约 76%）。但这类轮次**没有**出现注入消息，只有个别轮次出现。

因此该现象是**间歇性**的，不是每轮必现。

issues.title: 📢 [Feature] QwenPaw Is Getting Lighter and Easier to Extend

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Hi everyone! With the release of QwenPaw v2.3.0, we’ve taken the first step toward **making QwenPaw lighter and more extensible**. This will remain an important focus for QwenPaw's future direction. We plan to gradually turn non-core features & modules into plugins, leaving a leaner core harness while continuing to improve harness performance. ## What a Lighter QwenPaw Means for You In our tests, the current development version used about **one-third less memory** and launched speed about **38% faster** than the version before the refactor. The Windows and macOS installers were also roughly **30–40% smaller**. Here’s what we’re working toward in everyday use: + **Installation:** Download and install the components you need, reducing installer size, disk usage, and download requirements. + **Startup:** Keep features you haven’t enabled out of the startup path, so core chat can become available sooner while other capabilities are prepared as needed. + **Runtime:** Reduce the memory and background work associated with unused components, including background processes, file monitoring, and additional model calls. | Metric | Before the refactor | After the refactor | | --- | --- | --- | | Runtime memory usage | 450.31 MiB | 302.66 MiB (−32.8%) | | Time until the core Agent is ready | 5.24 seconds | 3.25 seconds (−38.0%) | | Windows installer size | 871 MB | 533 MB (−38.8%) | | macOS installer size | 1,010 MB | 723 MB (−28.4%) | These are preliminary results comparing a **v2.3.1 test build** with **v2.2.2.post1**, before the plugin refactor. Memory and startup were measured by running the QwenPaw service locally with Python 3.13. Actual results will vary depending on your environment and how you use QwenPaw. ## What We’ve Done in v2.3.0 The first phase of the plugin refactor is now available: + **Improved plugin management.** We’ve updated how plugins are installed, updated, disabled, and removed, as well as how their resources are cleaned up. This makes plugin management more independent, reliable, and secure. + **Introduced a plugin SDK.** Developers now have a more consistent set of interfaces for building and maintaining QwenPaw extensions. + **Turned messaging channels into plugins.** Official QwenPaw channels are now managed as plugins. When you need a channel, QwenPaw can install and load its components, reducing the resources used by channels you don’t need. Your existing channel configurations and enabled status are preserved when you update, so the channels you already use remain available. As other features move to plugins, we’ll explain how to enable them and whether existing users need to take any action when those changes are released. ## What’s Next In future releases, we plan to continue turning optional capabilities into plugins, including third-party harnesses, local speech, local models, the CLI, and MCP. For example, local speech transcription is planned as an optional plugin that users can install from the official plugin marketplace when needed. We’ll also continue improving the plugin SDK: expanding its public interfaces, improving developer documentation, and refining type checking and testing tools. We want developers to be able to build and verify their own plugins more easily using QwenPaw’s capabilities. ## Update and Get Involved You can check the v2.3.0 release notes and installation guide to learn how to update and use the current version. Developers can start with the templates and examples in the new plugin development guide to build and maintain their own extensions using the plugin SDK. [v2.3.0 Release Notes](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/releases/tag/v2.3.0) | [Installation and Update Guide](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/main/README.md) | [Plugin Development Guide](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/main/website/public/docs/plugins.en.md) | [Discussion](https://platform.agentscope.io/community) Making QwenPaw lighter will be an ongoing effort, and we’d love your involving. Whether you have feedback, ideas, or want to contribute a plugin, join us in the [QwenPaw community](https://platform.agentscope.io/community). Let’s make QwenPaw lighter, more useful, and better suited to the way you work. 🐾 --- # QwenPaw 轻量化改造进行时：更轻，也更容易扩展 大家好！QwenPaw v2.3.0 已经发布，**轻量化和插件化重构**也已随这一版本上线，并将会作为 QwenPaw 未来迭代的重要方向之一：我们会逐步把非核心的功能模块插件化，只保留最核心、最精炼的 harness 架构，在继续优化功能的同时，让 QwenPaw 更轻、更容易扩展。 ## 轻量化收益 在我们的测试版本中，我们实测了当前 QwenPaw 相比改造前，运行内存降低约三分之一，启动到核心 Agent 就绪的时间缩短约 38%，Windows 和 macOS 安装包体积均减少约三到四成。在实际使用体验上，减负主要体现在以下几方面： + 安装：**降低首次使用的门槛。** 让用户只为需要的能力下载和安装必要组件，减少安装包体积、磁盘占用和网络要求。 + 启动：**减少开始使用前的等待。** 避免未启用的功能进入启动关键路径，让核心聊天先可用，其他能力按需准备。 + 运行：**降低日常资源占用，保证核心任务稳定。** 减少未使用模块带来的常驻内存、后台进程、文件监听和额外模型调用。 | | 轻量化前 | 轻量化后 | | --- | --- | --- | | 运行内存 | 450.31 MiB | 302.66 MiB
（-32.8%） | | 启动到核心 Agent 就绪 | 5.24 秒 | 3.25 秒
（-38.0%） | | 安装包体大小 | Windows：871 MB
MacOS：1010 MB | Windows：533MB（-38.8%）

issues.title: [Feature]: Plugin-facing theme extension point (semantic token override layer)
issues.body:
## Summary

The Console theme system added in #7741 lets **users** pick a palette (6 built-ins) and customize accent / hover / background / surface / radius. But **plugins** still have exactly one theme knob: `window.QwenPaw.chat.theme.set(pluginId, { colorPrimary })`. Plugin authors who want deeper theming (backgrounds, glass / `backdrop-filter`, full palettes) have no official hook, so they end up injecting CSS.

Proposal (for discussion): add a **plugin-facing semantic token override layer**, built on QwenPaw's *own* semantic tokens rather than the upstream UI library's raw tokens — so plugins can theme deeply **without coupling to upstream upgrades**.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)

## Problem / Motivation

1. **Plugin theming is one-dimensional today.** The plugin theme API only accepts `colorPrimary` (see `plugins/types/qwenpaw.d.ts` and `plugins/hostSdk/install.ts` → `themeFieldMap`). Everything else is unreachable from a plugin.
2. **The marketplace already proves both the demand and the fragility of the workaround.** Appearance plugins such as *QwenPaw Skin Studio*, *background-wallpaper*, and *No Glass (Flat UI)* all describe themselves as "pure frontend, zero-dependency" — i.e. they inject CSS and poke the DOM directly. That breaks whenever the Console's markup or styles change.
3. **Why not simply expose the upstream tokens?** Because `plugins/types/qwenpaw.d.ts` deliberately keeps the public surface stable *"across vendor upgrades"* — exposing the upstream UI library's raw tokens would couple every plugin theme to that library's token names. The layer worth opening is **QwenPaw's own semantic layer**, part of which already exists (see #7682).

## Proposed Solution

Two steps, in order:

1. **Own the layer.** Make the Console's theming go through **QwenPaw-owned semantic tokens** (semantic role names → mapped internally to whatever the underlying UI library expects). #7682 ("use semantic tokens in SettingsCenter") is already a step in this direction.
2. **Open the layer to plugins.** Add a plugin API to override those semantic tokens, with the same disposable / registration semantics as the rest of the plugin SDK, e.g.:

```js
const dispose = window.QwenPaw.chat.theme.overrideTokens("my-plugin", {
  "surface":         { light: "#ffffff", dark: "#1f1f1f" },
  "chat.background": { light: "#fafafa", dark: "#111111" },
  // ...any semantic token; both light & dark required, so an override
  // never goes illegible when the user flips the color scheme.
});
```

Because plugins override **QwenPaw's semantic names**, an upstream library upgrade only changes QwenPaw's internal mapping — plugin themes keep working. That removes the exact risk that motivates keeping the surface closed today.

Happy to start with a **minimal first cut** (e.g. the handful of tokens the Console already uses for surface / background / border / text) and grow from there, rather than a big-bang "full skin system".

## Alternatives Considered

- **Status quo — each plugin injects CSS.** Works, but fragile and duplicated; breaks on Console changes; no clean restore. (This is what marketplace appearance plugins do today.)
- **Expose the upstream UI library's raw tokens directly.** Rejected — couples plugins to upstream token names and contradicts the existing "do not expose vendor config" design intent.
- **Only widen the current scalar list** (accent / surface / radius / …). Helps a little, but still cannot reach backgrounds / glass / full palettes.

## Additional Context

- Related: #7741 (merged — 6 palettes + accent/hover/background/surface/radius), #7406, #5909, #6312 (superseded by #7741), #7287 (external frontend gateway — `not_planned`).
- **Reference design**: DeepSeek Harness ships exactly this — `ctx.theme.overrideTokens(source, tokens)` plus a `ThemeDefinition` type (alias-token overrides, light + dark required), documented as *"Third-party themes can register alias-token overrides through `ctx.theme`."*
- Marketplace plugins currently working around this: `@osier-yi/qwenpaw-dream-skin`, `@levodoubt/background-wallpaper`, `@erickcharles/qwenpaw-no-glass`.

## Willing to Contribute

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this feature (after discussion).

---

### 中文摘要

Console 的主题系统（#7741）让**用户**能换 6 套预设、自定义 accent / 背景 / 表面 / 圆角；但**插件**目前只有一个主题接口 `chat.theme.set(id, { colorPrimary })`。插件想深度定制（背景、毛玻璃、整套配色）没有官方入口，只能注入 CSS —— 市场里的外观类插件（Skin Studio、背景壁纸、去玻璃化）都是这么干的，Console 一改版就失效。

建议：**在 QwenPaw 自己的语义 token 层上加一个面向插件的覆盖接口**（而不是暴露上游 `AgentScope Runtime WebUI` 的原始 token）—— 这样上游升级时插件主题不受影响（只需 QwenPaw 内部重新映射）。愿意在讨论通过后提 PR，可先做最小版本。

issues.title: [Performance]: Base image misses the MALLOC_ARENA_MAX cap from #8654 — main app pins 1.78 GB in 29 glibc arenas (v2.3.0, 112 threads)
issues.body:
## EN TL;DR

#8654 (merged 2026-11-17) capped glibc malloc arenas (`MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4`) in the **Creator** entrypoint, but the **base image** (`deploy/entrypoint.sh`) still has no cap. On a standard v2.3.0 Docker deployment (56-core host, glibc 2.36), the main app reached 2.67 GB RSS, of which **1.78 GB was 29 × 64 MB per-thread arenas** holding freed-but-unreturned memory (112 threads). Adding the same one-line export to `deploy/entrypoint.sh` fixes it; verified locally (arenas stay ≤ 4, fresh RSS ~0.5 GB). Happy to send a one-line PR.

## 现象（实测）

环境：官方 Docker 镜像 v2.3.0（Debian 12，glibc 2.36），宿主 56 核，主进程 `qwenpaw app` 连续运行约 29 小时。

- RSS 2.67 GB，其中 RssAnon 2.63 GB（smaps_rollup），Swap 0
- pmap 可见 **29 个 64MB 级 rw 匿名映射，合计 RSS 1.78 GB**（另有 29 个同尺寸 PROT_NONE 预留区，RSS=0，为 new_heap 对齐预留）
- 线程 112：anyio 工作线程 40 + asyncio 默认池 32（min(32, cpu+4)）+ watchfiles 8 + 轮询/插件伴生若干
- 无泄漏证据：arena 内为已释放未归还内存，Python 侧无对应活对象增长

复现命令（容器内）：

```sh
PID=$(pgrep -f 'qwenpaw app' | head -1)
pmap -x $PID | awk '$1 ~ /^0/ && $2>=60000 && $2<=65536 && $5=="rw---" {n++; r+=$3} END {print n, r/1024" MB"}'
```

## 机制

glibc ptmalloc2 为每个 malloc 线程分配独立 arena（64MB 对齐 heap，`HEAP_MAX_SIZE = 2 × DEFAULT_MMAP_THRESHOLD_MAX`，arena.c:31 / malloc.c:972），默认上限 `8 × 核数`（malloc.c:1935 `NARENAS_FROM_NCORES`，本机 448）。free 仅归还 heap 顶部连续空闲（systrim，M_TRIM_THRESHOLD=128KB，malloc.c:2962），中间活对象钉住整块 → 每池各自滞留高水位，池数越多重复滞留越大。

## 上游先例与缺口

#8654（2026-11-17 合并）在 `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/entrypoint.sh:76` 加入：

```sh
export MALLOC_ARENA_MAX="${MALLOC_ARENA_MAX:-4}"
```

其注释实测：~70 线程钉住 37 arenas = 2.4 GB RSS，而 Python 自身记账仅 125 MB 活对象——与本例同型同量级。

但 main 分支 `deploy/entrypoint.sh` 与 `deploy/config/supervisord.conf.template` 均无此 cap（已逐字核对）→ **基础镜像部署的主应用不受益**。

## 建议修复

`deploy/entrypoint.sh` 在 envsubst 之前加同一行（保留用户 env 覆盖能力，与 Creator 同值）：

```sh
export MALLOC_ARENA_MAX="${MALLOC_ARENA_MAX:-4}"
```

桌面端 / sidecar 启动路径是否同样处理，供维护者定夺。

## 本地验证

supervisord 模板 environment 行加 `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX="4"` + 重启后：

- `/proc/PID/environ` 含 `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4`，子进程继承
- 102 线程下 arena 保持 1（上限 4 = 主池 + 3 mmap）
- 新鲜 RSS ~0.5 GB（对照改前稳态 2.67 GB）

## 代价与边界（诚实披露）

纯 C 对抗基准（16/32 线程紧循环 malloc/free 8KB，绕过 GIL，100% 占空比）：=4 相对不限池吞吐降 11×/43×，=1 降 80–191×；**512B（tcache 路径）零惩罚**（320/338/378 Mops/s）。Python 服务受 GIL 串行化与 pymalloc/tcache 双层缓冲，真实大分配并发约 2–4，日常影响预计低个位数百分比。与 #8654 注释口径一致："raise it only if malloc contention shows up in CPU"；=8/=16 为中间档。cap 不限内存总量、不改分配语义，无正确性风险（官方 tunable，minval=1）。

## 关联

- #7222（长跑内存增长至 20GB+，closed-stale）：同属"RSS 不还 OS"家族，根因侧重索引重建/旧实例保活，与本例 arena 滞留互补
- #8348（replay buffer 优化，closed 未合并）：另一内存源，不在本 issue 范围

愿意提交一行 PR（deploy/entrypoint.sh）。

prs.title: fix(security): require approval for shell-based email sends, HTTP writes, and uploads
prs.body:
## Summary

Shell commands that sent email, made HTTP write requests, or uploaded local files could run without approval in AUTO and SMART modes. Neither Tool Guard nor governance had a detection rule for these operations.

## Changes

Add two `MEDIUM`-severity rules to the ruleset shared by Tool Guard and governance. Both paths use their existing approval logic when a rule matches.

- `TOOL_CMD_OUTBOUND_MAIL` detects `himalaya message send` and invocations of `sendmail`, `msmtp`, `mutt`, and `neomutt`.
- `TOOL_CMD_OUTBOUND_HTTP` detects common write requests and uploads made with curl, wget, and HTTPie, including explicit POST requests, `--data-binary @file`, and multipart file uploads.

## Testing

Added 23 regression cases covering outbound commands, read-only operations, and governance approval decisions. The tests verify that governance returns `ASK` in both AUTO and SMART modes for all three cases reported in the issue.

All 748 related tests passed locally. The tests evaluated approval decisions without sending email or uploading files.

Closes #8513

## Description

Expand the public plugin SDK to version 1.1 so plugins can implement common features through supported APIs, with identity, permissions, coordination, and resource lifecycle managed by the host.

This PR adds or extends:

- Request identity, model selection, scoped conversation history, and run queries.
- Dynamic prompts, stop conditions, scheduled workflows, and pluggable shell execution backends.
- Skill market language/category filters and cancellation during installation.
- Managed threads and interactive processes, file uploads/downloads, workspace paths, and legacy storage import.
- Draft reading and safe replacement, frontend registration, and checkpoint save/preview/restore APIs.
- Process-based channel drivers, structured messages, approvals, delivery tracking, management operations, and HTTP/WebSocket ingress.

Representative plugins were used for local validation. Their implementations and dedicated acceptance tests are excluded from this PR. Shared SDK regression tests remain self-contained.

prs.title: fix(console): repair CJK emphasis boundaries in chat Markdown
prs.body: ## What problem this solves `**中文。**后面` and `__中文！__后面` never parse: CommonMark only accepts a closing delimiter run that is right-flanking, and a run preceded by CJK punctuation and followed by a CJK letter is neither right- nor left-flanking. The renderer therefore shows the raw markers instead of bold text. Earlier commits in this PR repaired the string before parsing. Following the review, this revision drops that approach entirely: the fix is an instance-level marked tokenizer, and the Markdown source is never rewritten. ## Scope Type: C (new renderer behaviour, no data or protocol change) | Input | Stock | This PR | In scope | |---|---|---|---| | `**甲。**乙` | literal markers | `甲。乙` | yes | | `__甲。__乙` | literal markers | `甲。乙` | yes | | `**甲，**乙` … `**甲？**乙` | literal markers | `甲，乙` | yes | | single `*甲。*乙` / `_甲。_乙` | literal | unchanged | no | | ASCII punctuation before the closer (`**甲.**乙`) | literal | unchanged | no | | ASCII follower (`**甲。**b`, `**甲。**1`) | literal | unchanged | no | | nested or unbalanced runs (`***甲。***乙`) | stock result | unchanged | no | | CJK punctuation after the closer (`**甲。**，`) | stock result | unchanged | no | | already-valid emphasis before a CJK span (`**标准** **甲。**乙`) | two spans | two spans | protected | | emphasis spanning a formula (`**甲 $公式。**乙$ 后`) | stock result | stock result | protected | | fenced code, inline code, HTML | verbatim | verbatim | protected | | link label and image alt | verbatim | verbatim | protected (`inLink`) | | link `href` / `title`, image `src` / `alt` / `title` | unchanged | unchanged | asserted | | tables | literal in cells | emphasis in cells | ordinary inline text | Everything outside the rows that change returns the stock tokenizer result, so unsupported shapes keep the stock renderer's behaviour. ## How it works `console/src/utils/markdownCjkStrong.ts` registers one `tokenizer.emStrong` override: - it runs only when the source starts with `**` or `__`; - it inspects exactly one candidate closer — the first following delimiter run. If that run is not the agreed shape (CJK punctuation before it, CJK letter after it) it returns `false` at once and the stock tokenizer owns the span. That keeps already-valid emphasis intact (`**标准** **甲。**乙` stays two spans) and costs one lookup instead of a scan to the end of the paragraph; - `$…$` / `$$…$$` runs are tracked on the masked source, where code spans are already masked. If the opener or the candidate closer sits inside a formula, the span goes back to stock so a formula is never split; - on a hit it returns a `strong` token whose body keeps the punctuation (`甲。`), so no character moves; - the body is limited to 4096 characters. `console/src/components/ChatMarkdown/ChatMarkdown.tsx` is a local counterpart of the SDK's Markdown component. The SDK builds its `config` internally and never forwards one, so the only way to register an instance-level extension without touching global tokenizer prototypes is to compose the same pieces ourselves: math, footnotes, citations, streaming cursor, media, link handling, HTML sanitisation and the code-block slot are all preserved, and the only difference from the SDK is the extra extension. `AssistantMarkdown` renders through it and no longer rewrites the text; `vite.config.ts` inlines the SDK subpaths the wrapper imports so the unit tests resolve them the same way the app does. ## Evidence - `console/src/utils/markdownCjkStrong.test.tsx`: 24 tests through the real renderer — `XMarkdown` for the emphasis cases (agreed punctuation family, follower family, protected regions, repeat-render stability, streamed-versus-complete equality, two-span preservation) and `ChatMarkdown` for the formula cases (one KaTeX node with its payload, and a closer inside a formula producing no emphasis), plus two cost guards. - `console/src/pages/Chat/AssistantMarkdown.test.tsx` and `HostBubbles.render.test.tsx`: 22 tests pass, covering the streamed code-block pipeline that this component reuses. - Benchmark (same process, warm, median of three, stock `marked` versus stock plus the extension): | shape | bytes | stock | this PR | |---|---|---|---| | `"**ok** "` repeated (already valid) | 44,800 | 19.4 ms | 21.3 ms | | `**甲。**乙` repeated (recovery) | 8,400 | 6.1 ms | 4.2 ms | | `**甲。**乙` repeated (recovery) | 32,900 | 27.5 ms | 15.1 ms | | unfinished `**甲。` + prose | 21,004 | 0.9 ms | 0.9 ms | - `tsc -b --noEmit`, eslint and prettier pass on the changed files. ## Test scope - Target: `console/src/utils/markdownCjkStrong.test.tsx` (24 passed) - Neighbour: `console/src/pages/Chat/AssistantMarkdown.test.tsx`, `HostBubbles.render.test.tsx` (22 passed) - `tsc -b --noEmit`, eslint and prettier pass on the changed files.

prs.title: fix(channels): hide internal scaffolding at the display boundary
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Assistant text reaches the user through more than one egress, and two
families of model-facing bytes were being forwarded verbatim on all of them:

1. **Framework-injected context** — `<system-info>` / `<system-notification>`
   and the other `system-*` notes the runtime prepends to a turn. They are
   persisted as ordinary assistant text, so the renderer's structured-block
   switches never match them, a live stream shows them, and `GET /chats/{id}`
   shows them again after a reload.
2. **Reasoning a model inlined into plain text** — a `<thinking>…</thinking>`
   block written into the text block, or a truncated tail ending in a bare
   closing tag. Those bytes are in the same text block, so no display switch
   reaches them either.

## Filtering contract

This section is the definition the previous round asked for: what is
filtered, from which sources, and how incomplete input is treated.

### Sources

- `GET /chats/{id}` history playback (`app/chats/utils.py`).
- The channel renderer used by every structured send
  (`app/channels/renderer.py::message_to_parts`).
- The SSE serializer shared by Console and the web UI
  (`app/channels/base.py::_serialize_event_for_sse`), which also covers
  `console/channel.py` because both call the same method.
- The default reply path (`app/channels/base.py::_response_to_text`) used by
  channels that send the extracted string instead of rendering message parts.
- The streaming hooks (`app/channels/base.py::_on_stream_content_delta` and
  `_on_stream_msg_end`): the raw delta feeds a per-message scanner and only
  its output reaches the display buffer handed to `on_streaming_delta` and
  `on_streaming_end`. The event object and `streaming_buffers` stay raw.

### What is removed

- Reasoning blocks delimited by any of `think`, `thinking`, `analysis`,
  `reasoning`, in either case.
- `system-*` notices, closed by their own tag or by a shortened one
  (`</notification>` closing `<system-notification>`).
- A `<parameter …>` tool shell that opens a line and never closes.
- A bare closing tag with no opening tag: text before it was reasoning, text
  after it is the reply.

### What is never touched

- Text inside fenced code (backtick and tilde), indented code, blockquote
  lines, and inline code spans (single and double backticks).
- A closed `<parameter …>…</parameter>` pair.
- A *reasoning* opening tag that never closes, when the whole text contains
  no closing tag at all — every observed sample of that shape was a reply
  *discussing* the tag, and truncating at the opener deleted real replies.
  Injected `system-*` openers are not exempt: a live stream cannot know the
  closer is missing, so they stay hidden until the message ends.

### Incomplete tags

- **Streaming**: one scanner instance is kept for the whole message (message
  id + block index), not only while a block is being suppressed, so the open
  backtick run and the open fence survive between deltas. Injected `system-*`
  blocks are hidden by the same state — an opener starts hiding, its closer
  or a self-closing tag resumes output — and a partial tag prefix is buffered
  rather than emitted. Each delta is filtered exactly once; whole-message
  snapshots take one stateless pass.
- **Non-streaming**: one scan over the whole text. Whether an unclosed opener
  is reasoning or prose is decided once, from whether any closing tag exists
  in the same text.
- **Line endings**: paragraph boundaries use `\r?\n[ \t]*\r?\n`, so CRLF and
  LF behave identically.

## What is covered, and what is not

Covered: the four egresses above, balanced and bare closing tags, `system-*`
under any name, truncated tool shells, cross-chunk and cross-block splits,
LF and CRLF.

Deliberately not covered (separate discussion, as the review suggested):

- a naked closing tag with no opening tag *and* no surrounding prose — the
  current rule keeps the reply and drops the trailing paragraph, but it is a
  heuristic, not a general Markdown/XML inference mechanism;
- reasoning prose with no tag at all — it has no anchor, so separating it
  requires the parser to keep reasoning out of the text block;
- a scaffold block with no closing tag anywhere — left untouched as damaged
  data.

## Evidence

Targeted:

```
tests/unit/app/channels/test_scaffold_round10.py     29 passed
```

The cases are grouped by the two issues named as merge blockers:

```
fence closes, later reasoning still removed   [` and ~]   2 passed
tags inside a fence stay verbatim             [` and ~]   2 passed
unclosed fence keeps the remainder            ```         1 passed
closing fence split across chunks             5 chunks    1 passed
default reply path filters scaffolding                    1 passed
default reply path filters injected notes                 1 passed
```

Both fixes are load-bearing — reverting either one turns its cases red:

```
fence close reverted        -> 3 failed
                            (test_fence_closes_and_later_reasoning_is_still_removed[`]
                             test_fence_closes_and_later_reasoning_is_still_removed[~]
                             test_fence_state_survives_a_chunk_boundary)
default reply path reverted -> 2 failed
                            (test_default_reply_path_filters_scaffolding
                             test_default_reply_path_filters_injected_context)
```

The three cases from the twelfth review are load-bearing too:

```
inject state reverted       -> 1 failed
                            (test_sse_injected_block_across_three_chunks)
display buffer reverted     -> 1 failed
                            (test_streaming_hooks_show_only_the_public_reply)
state lifetime reverted     -> 1 failed
                            (test_sse_code_examples_survive_chunk_splitting)
```

## Test scope

- Target: `tests/unit/app/channels/test_scaffold_round10.py` (29 passed)
- Neighbouring: `tests/unit/app/channels` (214 passed)
- Context/history: `tests/unit/agents/context` + `tests/unit/app/chats`
  (1115 passed, 3 skipped)
- Pre-commit: all hooks passed (black reformatted two files on the first
  run; clean on the second)

prs.title: fix(skills): keep rollback backups until every workspace is restored
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Rolling back a multi-workspace skill install had five separate weak points. Each one can lose a skill or keep a user waiting, and they sit on the same code path, so they are fixed together.

**1. A restore failure abandons the remaining workspaces.**
`_restore_workspace_skills` used to run every target inside one `try`, so the first failure skipped the targets that had not been undone yet, and the `finally` cleanup then removed their backups as well. A target whose restore failed now keeps its backup, and every target is attempted before the first error is re-raised.

**2. The restore marker is written after the backup has been consumed.**
`_restore_workspace_skill` renames the backup back into place and only then sets `files_restored`. A process killed inside that window leaves a target that looks un-restored while its files are already back, and the next pass would delete the skill as "nothing to put back". A target with no backup but a present skill directory is now counted as restored.

**3. Overwriting an installed skill waits for the old tree.**
`install_staged_skill_dir` deleted the previous tree inline before installing. `rmtree` cannot be interrupted, so cancelling an overwrite had to wait for every file of the old tree. The old tree is now renamed aside first and reclaimed on a daemon thread; cancellation is honoured before anything is replaced.

**4. Pre-existing defect, not introduced by #8477: deleting a skill can lose all three copies.**
`garbage_collection` of the rollback `finally` removed every backup root unconditionally, including the root of a target whose restore had just failed. After a failed restore that backup is the only copy of the previous version on disk, so the cleanup turned a recoverable failure into permanent loss. It is now kept and marked, so a later sweep does not reclaim it either.

**5. New cleanup logic (not a defect fix): reclaim stale rollback roots.**
Backups now live under `skills/` instead of the workspace root, so a restore is a sibling rename rather than a second copy. That move leaves a root in place when a process is killed mid-install, so the next install sweeps the roots that are neither in use nor marked as retained.

## Scope

Type: B (state machine / cancellation / rollback)

Touches `src/qwenpaw/agents/skill_system/store.py`, `src/qwenpaw/app/routers/skills.py` and three test files.

## Self-review

1. **Failure** — `test_restore_continues_after_one_target_raises` (a restore that raises no longer strands the later targets) and `test_failed_restore_keeps_its_backup` (the kept root survives the cleanup and carries the marker).
2. **Cancellation** — `test_cancelled_overwrite_does_not_wait_for_the_old_tree` (measured 6.4s → 0.013s over 12k files) and `test_install_failure_moves_the_old_tree_back`.
3. **Skip / no-op paths** — `test_missing_backup_with_present_skill_counts_as_restored` (the killed-between-rename-and-marker case) and `test_restore_without_a_backup_removes_the_new_copy`.
4. **Concurrency** — the reclaim runs on a named daemon thread and `test_stale_rollback_roots_are_reclaimed_once` covers two installs in one skills directory; the retained marker is what keeps a failed restore's root out of a later sweep.

## Test scope

- Targeted: `test_staged_install.py` + `test_skills_router_pool_ops.py` + `test_skills_router_helpers.py` — **191 passed**
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/agents/skill_system` — **811 passed**; `tests/unit/app/routers -k skill` — **270 passed**
- `pre-commit run --files <the five files>` — all hooks passed

## Evidence

Before this change, injecting one restore failure across three targets left the later targets on the new content with their backups already deleted. After it, the failing target keeps its backup (marked) and the remaining targets are restored.

Overwriting a 12k-file skill took **6.4s** to cancel (the inline `rmtree`) and **0.013s** after the tree is renamed aside.

```
# cancellation timing, 12k files
before: 6.4s   (rmtree of the old tree inside the request)
after : 0.013s (rename aside + daemon reclaim)
```

Refs #8013

## What Problem This Solves

Cron and heartbeat runs drive `workspace.stream_query` directly instead of going through `Channel.consume_one`, so their token usage was never committed to the session's turn records. The console usage panel undercounts all scheduled task consumption: cron jobs (daily digests, reminders) and heartbeat runs make model calls whose usage never lands in the persisted turn records, even though the session data model already distinguishes cron sessions from chat turns.

Failed runs had a second, subtler problem: staged usage was never dropped, so a failed run's tokens could leak into the next run on the same reused session.

## Description

- Extract `commit_turn_usage` / `discard_turn_usage` into `qwenpaw.token_usage.turn_usage`:

prs.title: fix(providers): read a gateway-reported status from the error text
prs.body:
## Description

`extract_status_code()` reads a status from the exception's `status_code`, `code`, `response`, and `body`/`details` fields, and falls back to the message text for one narrow gateway format — `Streaming response failed: [503] ...`.

An OpenAI-compatible gateway that fails mid-stream can instead report the status only inside the message text, for example `status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)`. The OpenAI SDK raises a base `APIError` for such a response: no `status_code`, no `response`. The real status is present in the text, but the fallback does not recognise that shape, so `classify_model_error()` returns `unknown` — no same-model retry, no cross-model fallback, and the turn or scheduled job dies. The same upstream failure wrapped as a real HTTP 502 is `transient` and does fall back, so identical failures behave differently only because of how the gateway phrased them.

This adds one more narrow pattern for gateway error text, keeping the same deliberate narrowness the existing fallback documents: only `4xx`/`5xx` are read, so a success code quoted in a message (`expected status_code=200`) is never mistaken for a failure, and unrelated three-digit numbers in provider messages are still ignored.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8505
