prs.title: feat(mcp): generic OAuth 2.1 authorization-code + PKCE sign-in for remote MCP servers
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Remote MCP HTTP/SSE servers can now authenticate with a real OAuth 2.x authorization-code + PKCE flow via one config opt-in: `oauth = true` (`mcp.servers.<name>`, plus optional `oauth_client_id` / `oauth_scopes`). Before this, remote MCP endpoints were limited to static headers, which fails against real-world MCP gateways fronted by OAuth identity providers.
  - Full RFC stack, provider-agnostic (zero hardcoded provider specifics): RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, RFC 8414 AS metadata, RFC 7591 dynamic client registration (public `none` client), RFC 8707 resource binding, RFC 9207 `iss` validation, RFC 8252 loopback redirects, RFC 6749 §6 refresh-token retention semantics.
  - Grants live in the existing encrypted `auth-profiles.json` store (fail-closed when `secrets.encrypt = false`), single process-wide owner, shared across transport clones and agents; proactive expiry refresh, 401-driven forced refresh, issuer-drift = drop + re-sign-in. A refresh token redeemed after the caller's own tool-call deadline is never dropped with the caller: the exchange finishes in an owned task that holds the single-flight lock until the commit lands; a no-refresh-token grant is retired at its actual expiry edge (a refresh skew is not an expiry) and cleared before the send so the sign-in window (not the handshake timeout) owns the recovery.
  - Interactive posture: an MCP sign-in may run interactively only when the entry point that owns the human DECLARES it (foreground `zeroclaw` run; daemon/gateway/channel/cron/eval/ACP never do) AND both stdin and stderr are terminal-attached. It then waits up to 5 minutes for the browser callback; any other posture never hangs startup: it logs an actionable "connect once from an interactive ZeroClaw" error instead. Sign-in runs OUTSIDE the per-request timeout budgets (`prepare_auth`), so a slow human never has the loopback listener canceled mid-flow.
  - Docs: a full operator section in `docs/book/src/tools/mcp.md` (lifecycle, security posture, Silpo example, troubleshooting shapes).
- **Scope boundary:** does NOT add any OAuth provider specifics, device-code flow, dashboard-hosted redirects, or tool-policy changes. Discovery stays purely spec-driven: the MCP authorization spec's own ordered candidate list (challenge hint, RFC 9728 path then root well-known, an anonymous probe for the promised 401 challenge (GET, plus one anonymous `initialize` POST when the endpoint answers 405), RFC 8414 plus OpenID-Connect metadata forms with issuer verification (endpoints served from another origin than the declared issuer are accepted, as RFC 8414 allows, after the URL policy and pinned-destination checks, with a warning), and the spec's "pre-configured values" branch pinned to the resource origin). Static-header MCP behavior is byte-identical: the SSE advertised-endpoint/redirect confinement is upstream on master (#12149, merged per review), bundles, risk profiles, approvals, and outcome-unknown recovery semantics are untouched, and this PR's changes apply only with `oauth = true`.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-config` schema (three new fields + two new config errors), `zeroclaw-tools` (new `mcp_oauth` module incl. the process-wide manager singleton and its wiring), `zeroclaw-runtime` (interactive-posture decision in the scoped assembly + the daemon heartbeat hookup). Purely opt-in: with no `oauth = true` server, runtime behavior is identical to master. The only non-OAuth-facing addition is the scheme rule layered on #12149's confinement: an `sse` server with `oauth = true` must use a scheme-safe URL (https, or http on exact loopback) so a bearer never rides plaintext.
- **Linked issue(s):** None. The follow-ups this round exposed (RFC 7009 revocation on sign-out, and the interactive paste-fallback sign-in CLI) are tracked as work items after this PR rather than as a linked issue.
- **No open dependency:** #12149 (SSE endpoint/redirect confinement, per review) has merged into master and this branch is rebased onto it, so the confinement is neither carried nor duplicated here. The only confinement rule this PR adds is the OAuth-only scheme requirement.
- **Maintainer question:** ADR-016 disposition for the OAuth wiring placement, resolved in the latest round by moving the process-wide manager singleton and its construction policy into `zeroclaw-tools/src/mcp_oauth/wiring.rs` (state lives beside its owner). The runtime now holds no OAuth state: the scoped assembly keeps only the interactivity decision (entry-declared posture AND terminal fact) and the daemon calls the tools-owned getter. An ADR-016 exception row for the runtime scope is proposed and pending: it is recorded by Core in its own `docs(runtime)` PR ([#12564](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12564)), not from inside this feature PR, and its scope names only the runtime paths this PR changes. Until that row lands on `master`, ADR-016 keeps this PR unmergeable.
- **Design sign-off requested (discovery round):** three judgment calls beyond the letter of the specs, each flagged for disposition: (1) protected-resource documents must declare the exact configured MCP URL as their `resource` on ALL well-known forms, so a root document declaring only the origin is rejected rather than trusted host-wide (keeps the RFC 9728 §3.3/§7.3 impersonation rail; MCP-ecosystem servers ship root docs with the full URL); (2) the PRM-less fallback to the resource origin's own authorization-server/OpenID metadata is an interop heuristic for the legacy same-origin shape (the MCP spec words that branch "abort or use pre-configured values"), kept narrowly: a 401/403 bearer challenge from the anonymous probe required (a non-challenge error status attests that the origin spoke, not that an auth layer exists, and does not unlock the fallback), `issuer` must equal the configured origin, WARN-logged, and the stored-grant issuer binding still drops the grant if a later PRM names a different AS; (3) budgets: 45 s wall clock per discovery pass (needed because `prepare_auth` is deliberately timeout-free and connects are sequential), max 4 issuers probed with the remainder named, and the RFC 9728 §5.2 re-discovery-on-challenge is a one-shot latch per server and process.

### What this does, simply

Many hosted MCP servers (e.g. shopping, banking, SaaS assistants) hide behind a login: they only accept requests carrying an OAuth token that a browser flow obtained. ZeroClaw previously had no way to get such a token, so these servers were unusable. This PR teaches ZeroClaw to knock on the server's door (`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`), discover where the login service lives, register itself as a public client, ask the user's browser to log in once, catch the resulting code on a loopback socket, exchange it for tokens (with PKCE, so no client secret can leak), and inject the token into every request to that server — refreshing it for the user from then on. Tokens are stored encrypted with the rest of ZeroClaw's credentials and are bound to the exact server resource. If sign-in is not possible (a daemon with no terminal), ZeroClaw says so plainly and keeps the server on hold rather than hanging.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes — deterministic, local mocks only, and one optional real-provider check if you have a Silpo account.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` (`cli`, `tui`) + MCP transports (streamable HTTP, SSE) against wiremock servers; gateway/daemon headless paths via unit/integration tests.
- **Setup / preconditions:** any checkout; `secrets.encrypt = true` (default).
- **Steps to run:** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools mcp_oauth` (187 tests, ~37 s — includes the 35 s slow-human connect regression), `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib mcp_` (439), `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib mcp` (62, 1 ignored pre-existing), `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config oauth` (schema/validation/generated-fields). Optional live A/B (account required): config block `[[mcp.servers]] name=... transport="http" url="https://mcp.silpo.ua/mcp" oauth=true` + a bundle grant, then `zeroclaw agent -a <agent> -m "list MCP tools"`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** first connect prints an authorization URL and waits (up to 5 min, interactive); after consent the server's tools appear (`<name>__*`); restart reuses the encrypted grant silently (no browser); `zeroclaw` in a non-TTY environment logs "connect once from an interactive ZeroClaw" instead of hanging.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `McpServerConfig` does not deny unknown fields, so master silently IGNORES `oauth = true`, connects without a token, gets HTTP 401 from the gateway, and the server is skipped with a generic auth error — observed live when the same config ran on a master build. Remote MCP servers were static-header only.

### How I tested

All gates from clean `git worktree` checkouts of the exact SHAs (never the working tree), plus a production smoke against the real `mcp.silpo.ua` authorization server (Docker deployment; no fixtures with personal data).

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                   # 0
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets \
  --features ci-all -- -D warnings                           # 0 warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools mcp_oauth                       # 187 passed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib mcp_                      # 439 passed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib mcp                     # 62 passed, 1 ignored (pre-existing npx)
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config                                # all binaries green
cargo test --workspace                                       # all green except two
                                                             # environment-bound component tests
                                                             # (missing `expect` binary / AppImage
                                                             # smoke), reproduced identically on
                                                             # unmodified master in the same box
DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/tools/mcp.md scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh   # 0 errors
DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/tools/mcp.md scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh     # pass (lychee absent locally; CI runs it)
```

Per-commit verification: every commit in the stack is gated in a detached clean worktree at its exact SHA with `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets` (plain `cargo check` skips `cfg(test)`, which is how an earlier revision of this stack briefly carried an intermediate-only breakage: adding the three schema fields made one exhaustive daemon test struct literal fail the test build two commits before the wiring slice fixed it; the literal completion now rides in the schema commit itself). Result: every commit green workspace-wide including test targets, plus the owning suites re-run by each reviewer at the SHA under review.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the exact gate commands above are the CI strict quality/test surfaces for the touched crates; docs/link gates cover the changed Markdown lines.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** live authorization-server interop is CI-unprovable (no credentials in CI); mitigated by the RFC-strict wiremock matrix + the documented live validation below. `./dev/ci.sh all` not run on the dev box (no Docker); native equivalents were run individually.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A production deployment (Docker on a NAS, real `mcp.silpo.ua` OAuth 2.1 AS) plus a clean-room re-test built from this branch's final tip: fresh sign-in from a wiped grant store — the printed URL survived a multi-minute manual login (listener alive, single token exchange), a second run reused the encrypted grant silently (no browser at all: `enc2:` access+refresh profiles in `auth-profiles.json`), and the headless gateway then exercised real cart, delivery-settings, loyalty, and time-slot reads through the agent (38 tools). NOT verified in CI (no credentials); refresh/rotation paths are proven against mocks only. No PII committed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no layout-bearing surfaces; printed sign-in URL + record lines only).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Docker-based `./dev/ci.sh all` (daemon unavailable on the dev box) — replaced by the native gate commands listed above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes** — a loopback TCP listener on an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port during interactive sign-in only (bind to loopback, host-equality gate on private targets, state + PKCE validation on every callback; RAII-closed after the flow).
- New external network calls? **Yes** — AS metadata/registration/token endpoints discovered from the protected-resource metadata; all HTTPS enforced, DNS answers validated through the crate-wide SSRF guard (`net_guard`, incl. NAT64-embedded addresses under `security.nat64_prefixes`) and pinned to those resolutions, proxy fail-closed when the `tool.mcp` policy applies; no telemetry.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes** — new `mcp:oauth@<hash>` profiles in the existing `auth-profiles.json` (encrypted-at-rest, fail-closed with `secrets.encrypt = false`; each grant also records that requirement in its own profile row, so while a sign-in exists every other write to that file re-seals it with the same key: pasting a provider token, or logging out a different sign-in, cannot expose it); tokens redacted from logs/errors/tool results; resource+issuer-bound grants. Trust-boundary precision to state plainly: a private/loopback CONFIGURED MCP host trusts other ports on that same host for discovered AS/token endpoints (needed for local mock pairs and co-located private IdPs); public configured hosts never reach private ranges. This is host-equality, not origin-equality.
- Grant identity (deliberate): OAuth grants are intentionally bound to the canonical MCP resource URI, not to the configuration name. A configuration name is an operator alias and is not a user or security boundary; multiple aliases for the same resource therefore share the same audience-bound grant. Per-principal grants are out of scope and need a separate design (authenticated principal propagation, cache isolation, storage identity, DCR/client ownership, rate-limit attribution).
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No** — fixtures are synthetic; the docs example names only the public Silpo MCP URL.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.**

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes**, no exceptions within this PR's own scope: every behavioral change requires `oauth = true`. The SSE cross-origin/redirect rejection applies to all `sse` servers but landed with #12149, now on master, and its documented blast radius lives there. The custom-CA https rule for non-OAuth servers is pre-existing and unchanged. Mid-session interactive re-authorization (token revoked while a tool call is in flight) is bounded by that call's timeout, not the full 5-minute browser window; it fails closed and the next attempt re-enters the sign-in with a fresh listener.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes** — three additive fields (`mcp.servers.<name>.oauth|oauth_client_id|oauth_scopes`); two new config validation errors (`oauth` on stdio; `oauth` + configured `Authorization` header). Upgrade steps: none for existing users. Policy freshness: edits to a server's `oauth*`/TLS fields take effect on the next connect without a restart (the manager refreshes its per-resource policy at assembly and re-reads the credential store while it holds no live grant). Known limitations: mid-session interactive re-authorization (token revoked during an in-flight tool call) is bounded by that call's timeout, not the 5-minute browser window — it fails closed and the next attempt re-enters the sign-in with a fresh listener (review-accepted NIT). Sign-in UX for container/remote deployments currently requires a terminal on the host (loopback callback); an operator onboarding follow-up (paste-the-redirect fallback, `zeroclaw mcp signin`, fixed redirect port) is designed and queued as a stacked PR.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No** (one new internal dependency on the `url` crate already used across the ecosystem).

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the PR's commits (stack of eight conventional commits, each independently revertable); or downgrade the binary — older versions silently ignore the `oauth*` fields, so also remove or disable the affected `mcp.servers` entries (their connections would otherwise 401 and be skipped).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** per-server `oauth = false` is the toggle; an unused stored grant is inert for older versions.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** grep records for `mcp_oauth` (`manager-init` errors typically mean `secrets.encrypt = false`; `browser-flow`/`refresh` errors carry the RFC-shaped reason: `invalid_client` → AS without DCR, use `oauth_client_id`; `redirect_uri_mismatch` → AS rejects ephemeral loopback ports; `invalid_scope` → adjust `oauth_scopes`; `issuer-drift` + `store-clear` mean the AS issuer moved and a fresh sign-in is required).

## Supersede Attribution

N/A

---

Privacy contract respected: no real identities/secrets in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs.

prs.title: feat(web): add paired-device voice settings and chat controls
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** master.
- Add opt-in browser dictation and narration in agent chat, with paired-device voice preferences and a localized guide under Config → Other → Browser Voice and Audio.
- Save microphone, recognition mode, language, voice, speed and automatic narration on the authenticated paired-device record, not browser storage. Operators can select another paired device's record without changing the current browser's identity.
- Add one global `gateway.voice_silence_timeout_secs` setting in that same voice screen: default 15 seconds, accepted range 0–300, with 0 disabling automatic submission. It applies to every device/conversation and uses the existing authenticated configuration property API.
- Speak rendered Markdown text rather than hidden delimiters; omit only a trailing crab signature. Preserve meaningful literal code punctuation. Formatting-only replies do not block the continuous reading queue.
- **Scope boundary:** browser speech APIs, paired-device preferences, one gateway configuration field and normal chat submission. No server STT/TTS backend, microphone-audio upload endpoint, new identity or external service is added.
- **Blast radius:** web Config/chat, existing device-registry migration, gateway configuration and same-origin microphone Permissions Policy.
- **Linked issues:** none.

### What this does, simply

A paired browser can enable microphone and speaker controls next to the composer. Recognition starts only when the user clicks the microphone and grants browser permission. Local recognition is the default and never falls back online automatically; browser-service recognition is an explicit choice.

Dictation appends final recognized text to the draft. After the global silence interval, capture stops and final results are accepted before the normal send path is invoked once. Empty captures, hidden/cancelled chats, disconnected/busy sessions and stale conversation requests do not auto-send. A browser ending recognition early still honors the remaining silence interval. Local slash commands remain for manual submission. Set the global value to 0 for manual sending only.

The speaker reads a reply once, stops it, or enables continuous reading through a hold/Shift+Enter gesture. Automatic reading skips restored history and consumes unreadable formatting/signature-only replies so later responses can play. Changing the speech text never changes the displayed/stored response.

<!-- jarvis-validation-update:start -->
## Historical validation update (2026-11-10)

Updated to master a11a5ce5b at 9a9f6a1be. Combined voice controls with scoped chat while retaining operator-only image uploads. Voice submission honors the existing canSend/first-conversation path. A regression drives the actual voice callback through a restricted account's first WebSocket conversation, verifies exactly one message after session_start, and verifies that file uploads remain unavailable. Canonical API generation, the auth suite, all 31 voice tests, and the production build passed. Five gateway voice authorization tests also passed, including revocation during a write. This update was validated locally; earlier installed-browser evidence below describes its recorded revisions.

CI results and maintainer decisions on the published revision remain authoritative.
<!-- jarvis-validation-update:end -->

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interfaces:** web Config and agent chat; authenticated gateway configuration/device APIs.
- **Preconditions:** HTTPS or localhost, a paired browser, browser/OS speech support; select a locally available voice to test playback.
- **Steps:**
  1. Open Config → Other → Browser Voice and Audio. Enable dictation/narration, select language/voice and try the sample.
  2. Change global silence to 15, dictate and pause: verify exactly one send after the interval. Test 0 (manual only), another value, empty capture, manual stop, conversation switch and hidden chat. Confirm the same value appears on another paired device.
  3. Read a response with headings, emphasis, lists, a link and a horizontal rule. Formatting must not be spoken; code such as `apt-get --yes` must retain literal punctuation. A final crab signature is silent, but a crab in the body remains content.
  4. Enable continuous reading; place `---` or a signature-only reply before another readable answer. The latter must play. Restored history and trim notices remain silent.
  5. Reload settings and switch the device selector: per-device choices remain isolated, while the silence timeout stays global. Revoke a technical device and confirm its voice API refuses access. No voice preference storage key is added to browser storage.
  6. Try unavailable local recognition: no online fallback. Browser-service mode and online voices remain explicit choices.
- **Expected after:** documented opt-in controls, durable per-device voice choices, one adjustable global silence deadline and readable narration.
- **Before on master:** these browser speech controls and preference APIs are absent.

### Earlier validation (historical)

- **Earlier layout revision:** 61aeff4bb (global silence, narration fixes and responsive settings/toolbar spacing); the corresponding integrated candidate uses the same feature changes.
- **Latest checks actually run:** 24 voice tests passed; configuration default/range test passed; canonical `cargo run -p xtask --bin web -- gen-api` passed; integrated TypeScript check and production WebUI build passed. The checks exercise the actual component speech-submission callback, global property save, zero-disable, final-results ordering, activity resets, empty/hidden/cancelled capture, early recognition end, signature filtering and continuous queue progress.
- **Historical baseline checks:** gateway paired-device tests (14), security-header tests (5), auth/session/UI tests and format/diff checks passed at earlier documented revisions. These are not reattributed to the new head.
- **CI status:** current head includes master755bc9a4e. Its SQLite exception was approved and merged by maintainers in#12321; this PR does not introduce its own exception. The functional/layout source and installed bundle remain unchanged by that policy-only merge. Current-head CI is authoritative. The independent PR's shared SQLite advisory remains tracked by #12320; the checkout-only #12322 bridge was removed here after its registry-publication limitation was found. No advisory ignore was added. The preceding head's 32-bit check failed during runner `apt install` timeouts, before checking this code.
- **Coverage limits:** component tests simulate speech APIs. Actual microphone hardware, audible OS voice output, language pack downloads and browser-provider network behavior require device testing. New browser validation/deployment results will be reported separately, not inferred from unit tests.
- **Installed-browser validation:** synthetic microphone transcript, actual WebSocket/model completion, exactly one automatic send after **15,131 ms**, technical conversation deleted, global field verified at 15 in Browser Voice and Audio; a nondefault16-second value was saved, verified on disk/after reload, then restored to15. Actual microphone hardware/audio playback are not claimed.
- **Responsive layout follow-up at61aeff4bb:** label above the numeric input (8px gap), separate help and save row (16px gap), and nonshrinking 40px microphone/speaker buttons. Verified the installed UI at 1280px and 390px wide; both controls remain visible. The layout-only static update preserved configuration and binary and did not restart the daemon.

![Historical desktop voice settings before global controls/themed dropdowns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/0cc369ed976c610335df3a05e7fc6db4bfc0b6c1/.pr-evidence/web-voice-layout-desktop.png)

![Historical mobile layout before the global controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/0cc369ed976c610335df3a05e7fc6db4bfc0b6c1/.pr-evidence/web-voice-layout-mobile.png)

- **Earlier functional-field evidence (before the spacing follow-up):** cropped from the installed UI matching the feature changes at3f70b1efc; the evidence branch adds only this image, without changing the reviewed feature head.

![Global browser voice silence setting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/6423d16e3db0b77a369c815b7839f81bbe79d357/.pr-evidence/web-voice-global-silence-live.png)

- **Visual evidence provenance:** the following captures were originally recorded at 6338a726b3297bd18fa3d3a3cc06f5b6a7d109ae and retained at the evidence revision below. They show the prior device selector, guide and controls; they do not show the newly added global field.

![Paired-device selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-devices-other-desktop.png)

![Settings and usage guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-guide-desktop.png)

[Mobile chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-chat-mobile.png) Â· [Portuguese guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-guide-pt.png)

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- **Permissions:** same-origin microphone/on-device recognition is permitted; microphone and narration default disabled per device. Browser consent and user initiation are still required. Global silence defaults to 15 only after dictation is explicitly started.
- **External calls:** optional browser language-pack downloads, explicitly selected online recognition/voices; no microphone audio reaches the gateway.
- **Credentials:** own-device routes resolve the existing paired bearer under the live pairing guard; other-device management uses existing operator authorization. Global timeout reads/writes use the existing config property API and its authorization/validation. No credential is returned or logged by this feature.
- **Personal data in fixtures/docs:** none; synthetic content only.
- **Model-visible text:** recognized text follows the existing user draft/send path; no approval bypass or additional execution capability.

## Compatibility (required)

- **HTTP/config:** existing paired records receive disabled voice defaults; the new global field defaults to 15 when absent. Its range is validated on configuration writes/load. Rust struct-literal callers may need the new field or `..Default::default()`.
- **Config surface:** `gateway.voice_silence_timeout_secs`; existing device preference routes remain per-device. No new environment variable or transport endpoint.
- **Toolchain floor:** unchanged.
- **Upgrade:** build matching gateway/WebUI, enable desired device controls and adjust the global interval in Browser Voice and Audio. Cookie-only sessions without a paired-device identity cannot edit device preferences.

## Rollback

- Disable automatic sending by setting global silence to 0; microphone/narration/continuous reading can be disabled independently in the voice screen.
- For binary rollback, restore a verified prior binary; remove the new configuration key if rolling back to a version rejecting unknown fields. The nullable device-preference column can remain. Preserve state and credentials rather than blindly restoring an old database after accepted work.
- Observable failures: Config save/load errors, browser capture/playback errors or preference-API refusals. Global-setting load failure disables automatic submission rather than guessing a deadline.

### Localization

The existing voice guide/device strings retain their ten-language translations and English fallback. The six new global-setting strings are provided in English and Portuguese; other locales use the existing English fallback.


<!-- followup-20261110-b:start -->
## Additional review follow-up
Continuous reading now checks readiness, listening and speaking before parsing a queued Markdown answer. Added a regression demonstrating no repeated DOM conversion while the parent rerenders during playback; it fails before the fix and passes after. All 32 voice tests pass; the integrated WebUI production build passes.

Local evidence above is from the integrated candidate. Fresh hosted CI will run on the published branch commit; maintainer architecture/merge decisions remain unchanged.
<!-- followup-20261110-b:end -->

## Authenticated browser evidence

A paired Windows operator completed the real spoken-input, single automatic send and audible-reply check in Chrome and Edge on integrated revision `77c0b647d`. The [operator acceptance](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12269#issuecomment-6880263250) and [screenshots](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12269#issuecomment-6880323951) are available. The settings capture shows local dictation selected. The operator did not record browser build numbers or the recognition mode used for each recorded round trip.


## Earlier mobile interface and playback ownership (historical)

The screenshot below renders the production `BrowserVoiceSettings` component and stylesheet from PR commit `610484335` in a headed Chrome viewport at 390 CSS pixels. Device, voice and API data are synthetic. The image shows the reading-voice selector and the speech-speed row. Historical head `1f331f278` changes only the navigation wording in the book relative to the capture.

![Mobile Browser Voice and Audio settings with a reading voice and speech speed control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/850c9a854fb577686c5d6448914df6658ffb8278/.pr-evidence/web-voice-settings-mobile-610484335.png)

For the earlier evidence, integrated build `77c0b647d` used the paired voice changes through `bf0093778`, whose themed-dropdown patch has the same stable patch ID as integrated commit `ec761ae6f`. That build predates `2a70a0f90` and `fec38c9b9`. The older image above is historical. This update removes the nine stale captures from the PR branch and stores the new capture on a separate evidence ref.

```text
npm run test:voice
✔ stopping one pane does not cancel playback owned by another pane
✔ manual playback in a second pane shows the playback busy message

ℹ pass 34
ℹ fail 0
```

The headed browser also opened the authenticated settings route on Jarvis and confirmed it remained accessible after reload. The screenshot is from the isolated PR fixture. The production check verified navigation and rendering.

The shared Security findings are tracked in #12505 (chrono and chrono-tz) and #12101 (zip 9.0.5). This voice PR does not alter the workspace dependency graph or advisory policy.



## Earlier evidence follow-up at 21dec7b (2026-11-18)

Head 21dec7b incorporates master bec292f. The actual production settings component was rendered in headed Chrome at 390 x 844 and 1280 x 1000 with synthetic device/API/voice data. The current mobile reading-voice selector and speed row are visible. At that historical head, 34 voice tests passed. Historical build provenance, screenshots and coverage limits: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12269#issuecomment-6978640606 . These screenshots are kept on a separate evidence branch. Real hardware acceptance from the historical integrated build is not reattributed to the current head.



## Current source follow-up (2026-11-18)

The refreshed source includes master 3773cae2d7 (#12552). The shared page capture/playback owners prevent cross-pane echo. They also allow the same pane to switch its cancelled narration to dictation even when the browser reports stale speaking/pending flags. The base component suite passes 38 tests; the separate OIDC extension passes 39. Exact published heads and test tails are recorded in the follow-up comment. Hosted CI must still validate the refreshed revisions.

The 390 x 844 and 1280 x 1000 component captures at 21dec7b remain applicable to the unchanged settings layout. See https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12269#issuecomment-6978640606 . Real hardware acceptance remains attributed only to the historical integrated build.

prs.title: chore(channels)!: move IRC and Twitch out of the binary into registry plugins
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Remove the compiled-in IRC and Twitch channels. Both now ship as the `irc` and `twitch` WASM plugins, which a stock host installs without a rebuild. Twitch was a thin adapter over the IRC channel, so the two leave together. This takes the raw-TCP IRC channel out of the "retain built-in" list in #8850, now that a compatible, validated package exists.
  - `[channels.irc.*]` and `[channels.twitch.*]` become **retired config keys**, the same mechanism WATI used. Each load drops the section and prints a notice that names the plugin and its install and bind commands. The next save removes it from disk, secrets included.
  - `ChannelKind::Irc` and `ChannelKind::Twitch` stay in the attribution enum so historical records deserialize. They are marked not inbound-capable, so they leave the SOP trigger registry, as WATI did.
  - Keep `OutboundContentFormat::PlainText` for migrated `plugin.<alias>` bindings whose `[channels.plugin.<alias>].package` is `irc` or `twitch` (and fall back to `PlainText` for bare `"plugin"` or unresolved plugin aliases whenever an enabled plain-text plugin binding exists), so Markdown link destinations are still scanned by the outbound leak redactor across drafts, multi-message narration flushes, final replies (including `send_via` redirects), and announcements.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No other channel changes, and no plugin-runtime changes.
  - No automatic conversion of an old section into a plugin binding. The plugin must be installed first, and the encrypted credentials belong to a different config row.
  - The schema version is not bumped (see the reviewer question below).
- **Blast radius:**
  - Release archives never included IRC or Twitch: neither is in the dist feature set. They shipped only in `channels-full` source builds and the `all-features` image. That image and `--preset full` also build the plugin runtime, so every install that had these channels can install the plugins.
  - A plain `cargo build --features channels-full` without `plugins-wasm` loses them, and needs `plugins-wasm` added.
  - Generated installer surfaces (`Containerfile`, `setup.bat`, `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml`) were checked against `cargo generate installers`: no drift.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8850. Depends on zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins#174 (merged and published), which publishes the `irc` and `twitch` 0.2.0 packages this PR points operators to.

### Reviewer decision: `retired_in: 4`, no schema bump

The `RETIRED_KEYS` policy comment asks for a version bump when no pending version covers a retirement. V4 shipped in v0.9.0. I used `retired_in: 4` without a V5 bump because:
- Every load already applies every retired key, whatever version the file declares, so operators see the same thing either way.
- A V5 bump would make every config saved by this binary unreadable by v0.9.0 ("newer than this binary supports"). That's a large side effect for a channel removal, and it would be the first V5 change.

If maintainers prefer the bump, it's a mechanical follow-up: a `MIGRATION_STEPS` entry, `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 5`, and a regenerated fixture.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw used to carry IRC and Twitch support inside its binary, but most installs (every release download) didn't include them, and getting them meant rebuilding ZeroClaw. They are now plugins you install with one command. This PR removes the old built-in copies. If an existing config still has an IRC or Twitch section, ZeroClaw says exactly what to do instead of silently ignoring it, and the rest of the config keeps working.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the upgrade path.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw config`, `zeroclaw plugin`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** a build with `--features plugins-wasm-cranelift,channels-full`, and a config dir whose `config.toml` holds `schema_version = 4`, a provider, `[agents.assistant] channels = ["irc.libera"]`, a `[channels.irc.libera]` section with a `sasl_password`, a peer group on `irc.libera`, and `[plugins] enabled = true`. Both `irc` and `twitch` 0.2.0 are published in the plugin registry (zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins#174).
- **Steps to run:**
  1. `zeroclaw --config-dir D config get agents.assistant.channels`
  2. `zeroclaw --config-dir D plugin install irc`
  3. `zeroclaw --config-dir D plugin bind irc --channel-alias libera`
  4. Set `server`, `nickname`, and `channels` on the printed `plugins.entries.<key>.config.*` paths, and the server on `.egress_hosts`, with `config set --no-interactive`.
  5. `config set --no-interactive agents.assistant.channels '["plugin.libera"]'`
  6. `zeroclaw --config-dir D plugin info irc`
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  - Step 1 prints `warning: dropped retired config key \`channels.irc\` …: the built-in IRC channel moved to the \`irc\` plugin; run \`zeroclaw plugin install irc\` and …`, with no secret value shown.
  - Steps 2 to 5 succeed even though the agent still references `irc.libera`.
  - After the first save, `config.toml` no longer holds `[channels.irc]` or its secret.
  - Step 6 reports `plugin.libera configuration validates against the package schema.`, `The activation plan admits plugin.libera`, and `Loads: yes`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the built-in IRC channel loads from `[channels.irc.libera]`.

### How I tested

At the CI toolchain (Rust 1.98.0), on Linux x86_64:

```text
$ cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check                       # clean
$ cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 45s
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config --all-features
test result: ok. 2009 passed; 0 failed   (zeroclaw-config lib)
test result: ok. 323 passed; 0 failed    (zeroclaw-api lib)
test result: ok. 106 passed; 0 failed    (zeroclaw-config tests/migration.rs)
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --all-features --lib
test result: ok. 3870 passed; 0 failed; 6 ignored (+ 1 passed isolated)
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-features --lib -- sop:: quickstart:: i18n:: plugin_runtime::
test result: ok. 919 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked --features ci-all --test integration --test component --test architecture
test result: ok. 154 passed / 291 passed / 90 passed
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p xtask feature_matrix
test cmd::mdbook::feature_matrix::tests::parity_join_produces_rows_without_stale_keys ... ok
$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh   ->  Summary: 0 error(s)
$ scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh     ->  🚫 Errors...........0
$ scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh  ->  Comment hygiene gate passed.
$ cargo run -p xtask --bin generate -- installers  ->  unchanged dev/ci/docker-tags.toml (Containerfile, setup.bat unchanged)
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:**
  - Lint and the workspace clippy cover the removed features and dead code under `ci-all`.
  - The config migration and fixture tests cover the retirement, including the regenerated `fixtures/v4.toml` (`zeroclaw config generate 4`): the diff is exactly the IRC channel, its agent reference, and its peer group.
  - Channel orchestrator unit and turn tests (`irc_family_plugin_bindings_use_plain_text_outbound_format`, `irc_plugin_outbound_redacts_credentials_in_markdown_link_destinations`) cover plain-text outbound leak redaction for `irc` and `twitch` plugin bindings across replies and announcements.
  - Docs gates and the feature-matrix parity test cover the parity keys, which the docs build treats as a hard error when stale.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known. `scripts/ci/container_build_inputs_gate.sh` fails locally only on an unrelated stray worktree under `.worktrees/`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - The upgrade path above, step by step, with the built binary and the real `irc.wasm`.
  - The plugins themselves were driven through `WasmChannel` against a scripted IRC server and real Twitch (details in zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins#174).
  - Not verified: a daemon soak with both channels running as plugins; the `all-features` container image build.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output (CLI warning shown above, `LC_ALL` default, no width dependence).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `./dev/ci.sh all` in favor of the targeted crates plus the full CI clippy invocation.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No. Removed: the built-in IRC TLS client, including its `verify_tls = false` path that disabled certificate verification.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. Retired sections, secrets included, are dropped from disk on the next save, as for WATI. The notice carries the key path and reason only, never values. The test fixture's sentinel password was confirmed absent from output and from the rewritten file. Outbound leak redaction continues to treat `irc` and `twitch` plugin bindings as `PlainText` so Markdown link destinations are still scanned.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. The `channel-irc` and `channel-twitch` Cargo features are removed, and `[channels.irc.*]` and `[channels.twitch.*]` are retired.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps:
  1. Note the non-secret settings of each `[channels.irc|twitch.<alias>]` section. Secrets are encrypted in the file, so re-enter them from their source.
  2. Build with a WASM plugin backend if this is a custom source build (`--preset full` already has one).
  3. `zeroclaw plugin install irc` (or `twitch`), then `zeroclaw plugin bind irc --channel-alias <alias>` (Twitch: add `--egress declared`).
  4. Set the config keys `plugin info` lists. For IRC, grant the server on the instance's `egress_hosts`.
  5. Replace `irc.<alias>` or `twitch.<alias>` with `plugin.<alias>` in `agents.<agent>.channels` and in peer groups, with lowercase peer names.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` of the commits on this PR restores both channels and their config sections. A config whose retired section was already dropped by a save needs the section re-entered.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `dropped retired config key \`channels.irc\`` / `\`channels.twitch\`` on the CLI and `removed retired config key …` in logs at load; `agents.<agent>.channels[...] = "irc.<alias>" but channels.irc.<alias> is not configured` validation warnings until references are updated.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose ADR-016 exception for plugin wake dispatch
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Proposes a bounded ADR-016 holding-crate exception row in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` for host-mediated WASM tool-plugin wake dispatch (#12416).
  - `zeroclaw-plugins` intentionally does not depend on `zeroclaw-runtime`, while `AgentExecutionCapability`, `TaskRegistry` (`TaskKind::PeerInbox`), `CostTracker`, and `process_message_shared_with_*` still reside in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime` ahead of the planned `zeroclaw-kernel` extraction.
  - Per ADR-016, this exception record is opened separately before the implementation PR merges; the approval cell currently reads `Pending Core Team approval on this pull request` and will be updated with reviewer handle(s) and review link once approved.
- **Scope boundary:** One table row in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`. No Rust code, WIT definitions, config schema, or tests changed. The WIT `dispatch` interface (`wit/v0`), `AgentWakeBackend` trait (`zeroclaw-plugins`), `InternalPrincipal::PluginTool` (`zeroclaw-api`), and `PluginEntryConfig` validation (`zeroclaw-config`) remain outside `zeroclaw-runtime`.
- **Blast radius:** Merge eligibility of the upcoming plugin wake-dispatch implementation under ADR-016; no runtime impact.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12416

### What this does, simply

`crates/zeroclaw-runtime` is a holding crate where new functionality requires a bounded, Core Team-approved exception under ADR-016. This PR records the proposed exception to implement the host-side `AgentWakeBackend` adapter (`src/tools/plugin_wake.rs`) and wire it in `src/tools/mod.rs` alongside `send_message_to_peer.rs` until `zeroclaw-kernel` is extracted. It changes no runtime behavior on its own.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; governance/documentation record only, no behavior changes.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Local diff hygiene and docs gate checks ran on the committed head (`a2f3e92f3f`).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` and `scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh` target `docs/book/src/**` and skip `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, so the table formatting and columns were verified directly via diff inspection.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text
  $ git diff --check
  (exit 0; no output)

  $ bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  No docs files detected; skipping docs quality gate.

  $ bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  No docs files available for link collection.
  No added links detected in changed docs lines.
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Confirmed the single added row matches the 4-column table schema (`Scope`, `Destination`, `Approved by`, `Expires or reviewed`) in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` and includes no secrets, PII, or bot attribution trailers.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `a2f3e92f3f`, repository documentation, `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** `git diff` adds one row to the active-exceptions table and touches no other files.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo fmt`/`clippy`/`test` skipped because only `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` (Markdown) changed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (this PR only records a placement exception; the `agent_dispatch` permission and default-closed `dispatch_agents` controls belong to the follow-up implementation PR).
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert a2f3e92f3f` (note: per ADR-016, if implementation has already landed under an approved exception, coordinate with the Core Team before removing the covering row).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** None at runtime; this is a documentation record.

milestone.description:
Follow-up line after v0.9.0. Work that is wanted soon but is not needed for v0.9.0, or will not be ready in time, moves here instead of holding the v0.9.0 release: v0.9.0 follow-ups and items deferred from v0.9.0 with a plan to pick them up.

prs.title: fix(web): keep the chat input focused through a turn
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The chat message box was `disabled` for the whole turn (the input lock from #6220). Disabling a focused element drops its focus, so every follow-up message needed a click first, and Tab had to cycle through the rest of the page to reach the box.
  - It is now `readOnly` during a turn instead. Typing is still blocked and the "Running…" placeholder and dimming still show (`read-only:opacity-40` alongside `disabled:opacity-40`), but focus stays in the box.
  - `handleSend` now refuses while a turn runs. A read-only field still fires Enter, and an image upload or drag-and-drop can still change the draft mid-turn; the disabled box used to hide that.
  - Stop hands focus to the box as it is clicked, because the Stop button unmounts when the turn ends and would otherwise take focus with it. It does this before the abort request, so the request settling never moves focus: a control the user moves to while it is pending keeps focus.
- **Scope boundary:** nothing can be sent mid-turn, as before. The disconnected and loading states still use `disabled`. The send, upload, and model-picker controls are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** the chat composer in `web/src/pages/AgentChat.tsx` only. During a turn the dimmed box now keeps its focus ring, stays in the Tab order, and is announced as read-only rather than unavailable. On touch devices the on-screen keyboard would likewise stay open through a reply, as before #6220 (not tested).
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11658. Related #6220.

### What this does, simply

While the agent is replying, the chat box is locked so you can't send another message on top of the running one. It was locked in a way that also took the cursor out of the box, so after every reply you had to click back into it before typing. Now the box is locked as read-only, which keeps the cursor where it was: the moment the reply finishes, you can type the next message. You still can't type or send during the reply.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web`
- **Setup / preconditions:** a running gateway with the dashboard and any agent.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Open the agent chat, type a message, press Enter. When the reply finishes, start typing without clicking.
  2. Send another message and press Stop during the reply. Start typing without clicking.
  3. Send another message and, during the reply, open the conversation picker (or click another control).
  4. Delayed Stop: with browser network throttling on (for example Firefox DevTools → Network → Regular 2G), send a message, press Stop, then immediately open the conversation picker.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** 1 and 2: the text goes straight into the message box. 3 and 4: focus stays where you moved it when the reply or the abort finishes.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** 1 and 2: nothing is typed until you click the box, and Tab reaches it only after cycling through the page's other controls.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Web Permission Tests` runs `cargo web check` (API client generation plus `tsc -b`) and `npm run test:contexts`, whose `pretest:contexts` step runs `web/src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts` with both new component tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The component regression runs in Web Permission Tests through `pretest:contexts`; CI does not exercise real browser focus. Firefox on Linux was checked manually as described below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** in a throwaway container (the project's Rust build image, Node v24.20.0), on this branch:
  ```text
  $ cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin web -- check     # gen-api + tsc -b
  ==> npx tsc -b
  exit 0
  $ cd web && npm run test:contexts
  > zeroclaw-web@0.1.0 pretest:contexts
  ✔ the composer stays focusable and read-only during a turn and sends nothing until it ends
  ✔ Stop hands focus to the composer at once and not again when the abort settles
  exit 0   (every suite reports "ℹ fail 0")
  $ npm test
  exit 0   (every suite reports "ℹ fail 0")
  $ npm run build
  exit 0   (only the existing chunk-size warning)
  ```
  Against `master`'s `AgentChat.tsx`, both new tests fail:
  ```text
  ✖ the composer stays focusable and read-only during a turn and sends nothing until it ends
    AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:
    + actual - expected

    + undefined
  ✖ Stop hands focus to the composer at once and not again when the abort settles
    AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Stop focuses the composer before the abort request settles

    0 !== 1
  ```
  The Stop test fails the same way against this PR's first commit (`c2b063c2a`), which focused only after the abort settled.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** In Firefox on Linux, against a daemon built from master `d03325172` with this branch at `d9fe717bd` (plus two of my other open PR branches, neither touching `web/`) and `embedded-web`, I ran the four steps above: focus came back after a completed reply and after Stop. Opening the conversation picker during a reply moved focus to it, and focus stayed there when the reply finished. With Firefox network throttling, opening the conversation picker right after Stop kept focus in the picker when the abort settled, whether I clicked it quickly or a little later. Not verified: Chrome, Safari, touch devices.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `d9fe717bd` merged into master `d03325172`; `web` dashboard; Firefox on Linux.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** in the first comment below: the message box focused, with the caret in it, right after a reply finished, without a click (taken on `c2b063c2a`; the second commit changes only the Stop path).
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** send and wait for the reply → the box keeps focus. Send, then Stop → focus returns to the box. Send, then open the conversation picker during the reply → focus stays on the picker. Throttled send, Stop, then the conversation picker straight away → focus stays on the picker after the abort settles.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** no Rust code changed, so `cargo fmt`, `clippy`, and `cargo test` weren't run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: fix(web): return focus to the chat message box when a turn ends
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `handleSend` focuses the message box, but the textarea is `disabled={!connected || typing || !hydrated}` for the whole turn. Disabling it drops that focus, and nothing focused it again when `typing` went back to false. `AgentChatInner` now arms a refocus when a turn starts. When the turn ends and the box is enabled again, it focuses the box.
  - It only does that when nothing else has focus (`document.activeElement` is the body, missing, or the box itself, which covers Firefox leaving focus on the disabled control) and when the pane is rendered (`getClientRects().length > 0`). That way a turn ending in a hidden chat tab, or after the user moved to another tab, the model picker or a dialog, doesn't steal focus. If the turn ends while the box is still disabled (disconnected or not hydrated), the refocus stays armed until the box is enabled.
  - Pressing Stop leaves focus on the composer's own Stop button, which turns into Send when the turn ends. `chatInputFocusOwner` treats that button as part of the composer, so a stopped turn also gives focus back to the box (found in the browser run below, fixed in 03b7786).
  - The decision is a small pure function in `web/src/pages/chatInputRefocus.logic.ts`, with node tests. A component-level regression test in `sessionLifecycle.test.ts` runs a real `AgentChatInner` turn: send, `done` from the socket, then check the composer's focus calls.
- **Scope boundary:** The input lock during a turn from #6220 stays in place. No other focus behavior changes (the image upload and slash-command focus calls are untouched), and there's no new UI.
- **Blast radius:** The web dashboard agent chat only. The worst case is focus moving to the message box at the end of a turn when nothing else had focus.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11658

### What this does, simply

In the dashboard chat, the message box used to lose the cursor while the agent replied and didn't get it back, so every follow-up needed a click. Now the cursor goes back into the box when the reply finishes, unless you clicked somewhere else in the meantime or the chat is in a background tab.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional. I ran the cases below in headless Chromium; a check in another browser (Firefox/Safari) would still be useful.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web`
- **Setup / preconditions:** A running gateway with a working provider; open an agent chat in the dashboard.
- **Steps to run:** Type a message and press Enter. Wait for the reply to finish, then start typing without clicking. Also try clicking the model picker (or another chat tab) during a reply.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The text goes into the message box. If you moved focus during the reply, it stays where you put it.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Nothing is typed until you click the message box.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The web dashboard checks (`tsc -b` and the `test:contexts` suite) run the new logic tests and the `AgentChatInner` regression test.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None of the CI suites runs a real browser, so CI checks focus against a mocked textarea node (react-test-renderer `createNodeMock`). The browser run below covers real DOM focus.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Node 24.21.0, in `web/`):
  - `JITI_JSX=1 JITI_TSCONFIG_PATHS=1 npx jiti src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts` → `ℹ pass 20` / `ℹ fail 0`. With `AgentChat.tsx` reverted to `master`, the new test fails:
    ```
    ✖ the composer takes focus back when a turn ends, unless hidden or focus moved
      AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: focus returns to the composer
        actual: 0,
        expected: 1,
    ```
  - `node --experimental-strip-types --test src/pages/chatInputRefocus.logic.test.ts` → `ℹ tests 8` / `ℹ pass 8` / `ℹ fail 0` (with `chatInputRefocus.logic.ts` from ae47552 the new Stop test fails: `actual: 'other'`, `expected: 'nothing'`)
  - `npm test` → all suites `fail 0`
  - `npm run test:contexts` (run by web CI; the new logic test lives here since ae47552) → all suites `fail 0`, including the node suite `ℹ tests 40` / `ℹ pass 40` (at 03b7786)
  - `cargo web check` (generates the API files, then `npx tsc -b`) → passed
  - `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` → `Comment hygiene gate passed.`
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A Playwright 1.64.0 run in headless Chromium (Playwright's chromium-1248 build) on Debian 13, 1280×800, English locale, against the dashboard from this branch at 03b7786 (`npm run dev` in `web/`, proxying to a local `zeroclaw` gateway built from the same tree, one agent `local` on a mock OpenAI-compatible provider that answers after ~3 s). Script, full log and screenshots: [proof/11661-chat-focus](https://github.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/tree/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092).
- **Visual interface evidence:** [normal completion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-A-normal-completion.png), [focus moved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-B-focus-moved.png), [Stop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-C-stop.png), [hidden pane](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-D-hidden-pane.png), [offline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-E2-offline.png), [reconnected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-E2-reconnected.png).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 03b7786, web dashboard agent chat (Vite dev server, not the gateway-embedded production bundle), screenshots and log linked above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** see the screenshots above and the results in the next item.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:**
  - Normal completion: after the reply, `document.activeElement` is the visible textarea; typing with no click puts `typed without clicking` in it.
  - Focus moved to the conversation picker during the turn: after the turn, focus stays on the picker button.
  - Stop: right after clicking Stop focus is on the Stop button; after the turn ends it is on the textarea and `after stop` types into it. (At ae47552 it stayed on the button; fixed in 03b7786.)
  - Hidden pane: during the turn I opened a second chat tab; when the hidden tab's turn ended, its composer did not take focus (`hiddenComposerFocused: false`, active element is the body).
  - Disconnected: browser context set offline mid-turn; the composer stayed disabled (`Running…`) and unfocused while offline, including after the mock turn would have finished. After going back online and the composer being re-enabled, focus was on the textarea and `after reconnect` typed into it.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No Rust code changed, so I didn't run `cargo test` / `cargo clippy`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose bounded agent owned-state retirement exception
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Adds one row to the active-exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, proposing a bounded holding-crate exception for the agent owned-state retirement and knowledge-graph scoping in #9745 (which fixes #9647). The crate guide requires the exception to be recorded before the feature merges, and a feature pull request cannot grant itself one, so the row is proposed here on its own. It answers the open review item on #9745 (`src/agent_owned_state.rs:741-745`, 2026-10-25), which found that the knowledge export-and-purge flow has no covering exception.
- **Scope boundary:** Documentation only. The permission covers exactly what #9745 changes in `zeroclaw-runtime` at `123b8396f3`, eighteen files: `src/agent_owned_state.rs`, `src/agent_lifecycle.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/rpc/{context,dispatch,local,types,wss}.rs`, `src/tools/{mod,delegate}.rs`, `src/control_plane/task_store_sqlite.rs`, `src/i18n.rs`, `locales/en/{cli,tools}.ftl` and `locales/{es,fr,ja,zh-CN}/cli.ftl`. Most of it is continued work on a subsystem the crate already holds. On `master`, `src/agent_lifecycle.rs` carries `live_acp_session_count`, `archive_agent_workspace`, `OwnedStateReport`, `cascade_owned_state`, `RenameStateReport` and `cascade_rename_agent`, and the gateway reaches them through a three-line `pub use` shim; #9745 moves them into the new `src/agent_owned_state.rs`, re-exports the four functions from `agent_lifecycle` for compatibility, deletes the gateway shim, and extends them. The additions the row names are: the `PathPresence` classifier `inspect_lifecycle_path`, which re-walks the ancestors of a negative probe so an uninspectable path is residue on Windows as on Unix; the committed delete and rename residue contracts `committed_delete_residue_exists` and `committed_rename_residue_exists`, which probe the workspace, cron, control-plane (through the new read-only `SqliteTaskStore::count_existing_by_agent`), ACP, memory, knowledge and session stores; the shared resolvers that both contracts and both cascades use to reopen the configured memory or session backend when the live handle is absent, or for memory is the `none` placeholder, while config still expects persistence, so a delete or rename cleans or re-points that store instead of skipping it (on `master` the RPC delete substituted `NoneMemory` and warned, and the cascades returned zero for an absent backend); `AgentDeletionArchive`, which replaces `WorkspaceArchiveReport`, with an exclusively created leaf, `create_new` artifact writes and directory syncs up to the data directory, so a successful export gates the memory, knowledge, cron and ACP purges and a failure is reported in `warnings`; `prepare_knowledge_retirement` and `cascade_owned_state_with_retirement`, which export the agent's knowledge rows before the config commit, archive them as `knowledge.json` and purge through `KnowledgeGraph::purge_archived_owner` only while the store still matches the archived snapshot, plus the knowledge rename follower and the knowledge counts on both reports and the manifest; `plan_agent_delete_recovery_with_acp_count`, the recovery-mode preflight for a committed delete; in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`, `run_agent_delete` behind `agents/delete` and `config/map-key-delete` (alias-grammar validation before any probe, so a reserved or malformed alias is now an `INVALID_PARAMS` error on `agents/delete` where `master` returned a `deleted: false` result; config-write authority for `agents.<alias>`, which `agents/delete` did not require before, and for every scrubbed path rechecked inside the commit, which neither method required before; a committed-delete retry that resumes the cascade without a config publication; and, on the map-key adapter only, refusing an agent with active RPC sessions as rename already does and answering `deleted: false` rather than an error for an unblocked alias with neither a config entry nor residue), the rename adapter validating both aliases and probing the old workspace through the classifier, `alias_create_refusal_message` for `config/set`, `config/set-many` and `config/map-key-create` when the alias they would create still owns knowledge or its store cannot be inspected, and the optional `owned_state` field on `ConfigMapKeyDeleteResult`; in `src/tools/mod.rs`, `knowledge_scope_for_agent` and the knowledge tool registration that binds a `KnowledgeScope` from the trusted agent alias, resolved per graph operation through the existing read-only live config handle (it registers no live-config consumer and acknowledges nothing) or from the configured `read_knowledge_from`, assigns unattributed legacy rows to `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent` or the sole enabled agent, and withholds the tool when ownership is ambiguous; in `src/tools/delegate.rs`, `knowledge_tool_for_target`, rebinding the knowledge tool to the delegation target as the memory tools already are; the seven Fluent keys (five in `locales/en/cli.ftl`, two in `locales/en/tools.ftl`), of which `cli-alias-create-knowledge-{retained,uninspectable}` and `delegate-knowledge-init-failed` are translated in `es`, `fr`, `ja` and `zh-CN` with every-locale tests in `src/i18n.rs`; and the tests, including the test-only `pause_knowledge_archive_under` and negative-probe hooks and the `memory` parameter on the test-only `RpcContext::for_persistence_tests` with its call sites in `src/rpc/{dispatch,local,wss}.rs`. The row leaves out, as an implementation detail, the boxed `handle_config_map_key_delete` future that keeps `process_line` inside its stack budget. Everything else #9745 does lives in its owning crate and needs no runtime permission: `KnowledgeScope`, grant resolution, legacy assignment, `export_existing_owner`, the generation-checked `purge_archived_owner` and `rename_owner` in `zeroclaw-memory`; the scoped `KnowledgeTool` and the `model_routing_config` retirement check in `zeroclaw-tools`; the alias admission rule (`create_map_key_checked`, `ensure_knowledge_owner_retired`, `Config::ensure_map_key_for_path`) and the `read_knowledge_from` and `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent` settings in `zeroclaw-config`; the HTTP adapters in `zeroclaw-gateway`; and the CLI paths in the `zeroclaw` binary. The row excludes per-principal ownership, the unwired Postgres graph (`knowledge_graph_pg.rs` is untouched), any new RPC method (the `Method` enum gains no variant), grant source, config key, store or persisted schema in the runtime (the existing archive bundle gains the `knowledge.json` artifact and its manifest counts), the `model_routing_config` tool's `remove_agent` (which still removes an agent without the cascade), the environment-override creation path (applied at config load without the retirement check), and any non-English locale beyond the three keys named. The `remove_agent` and environment-override items are pre-existing gaps #9745's body lists as out of scope. The row also says that it does not ratify the cascade's own landing in the crate (see below).
- **Blast radius:** Contributor placement guidance only. No runtime behavior changes. The row is not active until a Core Team member other than the author approves it; the `Approved by` cell is filled with that review's permalink before merge, so merging this pull request is what records the vote.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9647 and #9745 (head `123b8396f3`). Precedent: #11701, #11963, #12058 and #12062, the four row proposals open at the same table position.

### What this does, simply

`zeroclaw-runtime` is a holding crate: new code there is supposed to move to its own crate, and the Core Team records each deliberate exception in a table so the extraction debt stays visible. #9745 gives every knowledge-graph row an owning agent and makes an agent's delete and rename carry that ownership with the alias: deletion exports the agent's knowledge, archives it next to the memory, cron and ACP exports the cascade already wrote, and purges it only when the archive is durable and still matches the store; rename moves ownership to the new alias; a committed delete or rename whose cleanup failed, or whose stores cannot be inspected, stays retryable on the RPC and gateway surfaces instead of reading as finished (the CLI's committed-rename retry is #10373); and no explicit config write can recreate an alias while its knowledge remains (an environment override that names a new agent is still applied at load, a pre-existing gap #9745 documents). The runtime half of that is the cascade itself, the RPC adapters that run it, and the knowledge tool's binding to the calling agent. This row asks permission for exactly those changes, with the agent-lifecycle owner in the planned kernel extraction as their destination.

### Why a row rather than relocation

Every one of these additions changes code the crate already holds. The owned-state cascade sits in `src/agent_lifecycle.rs` on `master`, next to the delete preflight, and the RPC delete and rename adapters in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs` already call it; the gateway and CLI call the same functions. It landed there on 2026-09-30 through #10621, after this table existed, and has no row of its own; this row covers #9745's changes to it and says so, and does not ratify that landing, which is a separate Core decision if one is wanted. The cascade reaches the cron store (`crate::cron`), the control-plane task store (`crate::control_plane`) and the runtime's Fluent catalogue (`crate::i18n`), all of which the holding crate still contains, so a crate of its own today would either pull those along or invert the dependency the kernel extraction is meant to settle. ADR-016 describes that case: extraction would establish a crate boundary the roadmap does not intend. #11701's proposed row (open, approved) names the agent-lifecycle owner in the planned `zeroclaw-kernel` extraction as this subsystem's destination, and this row uses the same destination. The knowledge-specific logic that can live elsewhere already does: scope, grants, export and purge are in `zeroclaw-memory`, the tool in `zeroclaw-tools`, the admission rule in `zeroclaw-config`. What remains in the runtime is the lifecycle wiring between them.

### Coverage analysis

No row on `master` covers this work. All 47 active rows were read for the paths #9745 touches:

- `src/agent_lifecycle.rs`: no row names it. #11701 (open, approved) is the first row to touch the file, for #11301's rename recovery, and its scope cell excludes exactly this work: "No delete recovery, knowledge-graph follower, new follower store, new lifecycle operation, or non-English locale".
- `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`: named by the #10905, #10407, #11466/#11506, #10911, #11181, #10513/#10522, #11607, #9872/#10391, #11692, #11622, #11513, #11698, #11730, #11221, #11463 and #11286 rows. Each is limited to its own pull request and behavior (compaction, session prompts, config receipts, live-config publication, steering provenance, `sops.run`, the refresh pre-filter, the delegation ceiling call, budget warnings, message times, the profile projection, personality reload, delegate activity, tool selection, diff capture, one WSS regression). None covers the agent delete or rename adapters, alias admission, or the map-key delete response's `owned_state` field and `deleted: false` answer (the #11466/#11506 row covers only that response's `revision` receipt).
- `src/tools/mod.rs` and `src/tools/delegate.rs`: the #9872/#10391 bounded-delegation row covers rebuilding "a bounded delegate's context-sensitive tools for the target workspace", but is limited to #9872/#10391 and the caller ceiling; the #11221 row covers built-in tool selection and name reservation; the #11462 row covers delegate operator approvals; the #11465, #11473, #10331/#11450, #11292, #11730, #11456, #9579, #9447, #11698, #10911 and #10407 rows cover cancellation context, schema deferral, worker-loss recovery, progress, activity forwarding, resident-memory supervision, the docs skill, terminal handling, personality reload, live-config publication and session prompts. None covers binding the knowledge tool to a `KnowledgeScope` or rebinding it for a delegate. The #10911 row excludes a "new live consumer" of the live-config authority; the knowledge scope only reads the existing read-only handle per graph operation and registers nothing, which the row states.
- `src/control_plane/task_store_sqlite.rs`: the #9597 row (task registration and settlement) and the #11292 row (progress persistence) do not cover a read-only residue count.
- `src/i18n.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/rpc/{context,types,local,wss}.rs` and the locale files: each row naming them is limited to its own keys, fields, exports and tests.

The row therefore records the moved cascade and its additions together, so the holding crate's debt for this subsystem is legible in one place.

### Rebase note

Four other row proposals are open and append at the same table position: #11701, #11963, #12058 and #12062. Whichever lands later takes a one-line conflict fix. #11701 (for #11301) is adjacent in subject: it adds the rename recovery contract in `src/agent_rename_recovery.rs` and the path classifier and directory sync helper in `src/lifecycle_path.rs`, and removes the rename follower cascade from `src/agent_lifecycle.rs`, while #9745 adds `inspect_lifecycle_path` and the archive sync chain inside `src/agent_owned_state.rs` and moves and extends `cascade_rename_agent`. The two feature pull requests reconcile that duplication at rebase, whichever lands second, and the row for the one landing second is refreshed to the paths it then uses. This row describes #9745 at its current head.
